title: Fusing Vessel Behavior and Weather Context for Real-time Attribution of AIS Dropouts.
abstract: The Automatic Identification System (AIS) provides real-time vessel identity and kinematics, but abrupt signal dropouts leave operators uncertain whether the cause is a benign equipment failure or deliberate evasion. The majority of existing works detect anomalous maneuvers while transmission is active, overlooking cause attribution at the moment of disappearance and ignoring meteorological context. We propose a three-stage framework that attributes AIS dropouts in real-time by fusing vessel behavior with environmental signals. Stage 1 summarizes the preceding two minutes of motion into maneuver probabilities using a bidirectional LSTM. Stage 2 applies a transparent policy that integrates these probabilities with sustained wind, gusts, traffic density, and channel membership to assign context aware attribution outcomes. Stage 3 compiles this policy into a lightweight Random Forest, producing calibrated risk scores and interpretable decision paths in 0.38 s, well within the 30 s AIS heartbeat. On a held out dataset from the Port of Houston, the system achieves AUROC of 0.834 and accuracy of 0.84. By incorporating weather alongside kinematics, our approach delivers deployable, auditable, and recall oriented attribution precisely when Vessel Traffic Services require actionable intelligence.

title: Edge-Guided ControlNet Synthetic Chest X-ray Augmentation and Ensemble Classification.
abstract: Chest X-ray (CXR) analysis is essential for the early detection of thoracic diseases, but challenges like limited data and class imbalance can undermine model performance. This study introduces a two-phase framework that integrates synthetic image generation with classification. The first phase utilizes a ControlNet-based Stable Diffusion pipeline, utilizing Canny–Sobel edge information to produce realistic synthetic CXRs. Features are extracted using ViT, Swin, ResNet, and handcrafted Gray-Level Cooccurrences Matrix (GLCM) descriptors. In the second phase, the enhanced dataset is classified using ensemble methods, where Extra Tree demonstrates superior effectiveness. Tests on the IU X-Ray and COVID-19 datasets show the framework’s success, achieving SSIM values of 89.53 for COVID and 86.21 for IU X-Ray, along with classification accuracies of 95.01% for COVID and 78.76% for IU X-Ray. These findings underscore the framework’s ability to mitigate data limitations and improve prediction accuracy, suggesting its viability for clinical applications.

title: Cell-Free Massive MIMO for Joint Communication and Proactive Monitoring.
abstract: This paper introduces a novel joint communication and proactive monitoring (JCAM) system that simultaneously monitors multiple untrusted links and serves multiple legitimate users. The system leverages a cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) architecture, where one subset of access points (APs) is dedicated to receiving signals from untrusted links, while another subset transmits data to legitimate users and jamming signals into the untrusted links. This dual functionality not only ensures reliable communication for legitimate users but also degrades the performance of untrusted links, thereby enhancing monitoring effectiveness. Closed-form expressions for the spectral efficiency (SE) of legitimate users and the monitoring success probability (MSP) are derived under partial zero-forcing (PZF) precoding/combining schemes with imperfect channel state information. Leveraging these expressions, we develop a simple yet effective AP mode assignment strategy that determines which APs perform downlink transmission and jamming, and which APs are dedicated to receiving signals from untrusted links. The objective is to maximize the MSP while satisfying predefined quality-of-service (QoS) requirements for all legitimate users. Numerical results show that the proposed mode assignment strategy significantly outperforms the benchmark, achieving up to a $32\%$ improvement in monitoring performance, while maintaining low computational complexity. Moreover, our proposed JCAM framework provides nearly a six-fold improvement in the minimum MSP over the co-located massive MIMO baseline.

title: ARTA: Adaptive Redundancy-aware Telemetry node Activation in 6G Edge.
abstract: Future 6G edge networks must support ultra-reliable and low-latency communication for applications such as autonomous driving and industrial automation, while operating under strict bandwidth and compute constraints. Achieving this balance requires telemetry systems that are adaptive, scalable, and resource-efficient. However, existing telemetry approaches either rely on static deployment or network-wide activation, leading to excessive overhead and redundant measurements in dense edge environments. This paper presents ARTA, an Adaptive Redundancy-Aware Telemetry Node Activation framework that formulates the telemetry activation problem as a redundancy-aware benefit–cost optimization. Each node is evaluated by anomaly likelihood, traffic importance, topological centrality, and context relevance, while redundancy, caused by nearby nodes reporting overlapping telemetry data, and resource limits are explicitly modeled. The resulting submodular objective enables a greedy algorithm with provable optimality guarantees. Simulations on edge–core topologies of up to 1,000 nodes show that ARTA achieves approximately 0.8 normalized accuracy (80% of the maximum achievable accuracy) while activating only 20% of nodes within a few seconds, demonstrating scalability and zero-touch observability.

title: Adaptive Numerology Selection for Beyond-5G/6G using Deep Reinforcement Learning: Breaking the Stability-Performance Trade-off.
abstract: Dynamic numerology adaptation in 5G New Radio (NR) must optimize QoS under varying load and mobility while preserving network stability. Fixed schemes lack flexibility; reactive ones risk excessive reconfigurations. We propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework that reconciles adaptability and stability and empirically shows they need not trade off. Extensive OMNeT++/Simu5G experiments demonstrate consistent gains on latency, MOS, and PLR with controlled reconfiguration, indicating practical deployability for 5G and AI-native 6G RANs.

title: Satellite Constellation Optimization for 6G and Beyond Satellite Networks.
abstract: 6G technology will integrate satellite networks to provide global coverage, support Direct-to-Device communication in coverage gaps, and enable massive IoT connectivity.This paper presents an optimization strategy for designing satellite constellations to minimize the number of satellites while meeting 6G user needs for unmodified handheld devices.Key factors in the optimization include orbital geometry, satellite antenna specifications, and quality-of-service metrics such as signal-tonoise ratio, satellite visibility, and the number of visible satellites.Simulation results indicate that to provide service to a handheld device at any location on Earth's surface, a satellite operating in the S-Band requires 4337 VLEO satellites at an altitude of 183.4 km to achieve a data rate of 18 Mbps and 574 LEO satellites at an altitude of 558.68 km to achieve a data rate of 7.5 Mbps.

title: Flow Fragmentation and Cooperative Scheduling in Time-Sensitive Networking.
abstract: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) enables deterministic data transmission for applications such as factory automation and autonomous driving. However, when applying Time-Aware Shaper (TAS) to large-scale networks where service providers serve numerous customers, conventional methods suffer from significant degradation in network utilization. This paper identifies the root cause as "flow fragmentation due to heterogeneous flow characteristics" and proposes a novel cooperative scheduling method that coordinates flows with different characteristics. The proposed approach combines two complementary strategies: "inter-switch spatial cooperation" between flows with different path lengths and "intra-switch temporal cooperation" between flows with identical transmission periods. Experimental evaluation on ring networks with up to 20 nodes demonstrates that the proposed cooperative scheduling achieves 2.15× improvement in bandwidth utilization compared to conventional methods.

title: Optimal Constellation Design to Combat Equalization-Enhanced Phase Noise.
abstract: In fiber communication systems employing coherent receivers, local oscillator laser phase noise should ideally be compensated prior to dispersion equalization. However, practical limitations in current receiver implementations necessitate reversing this order, such that phase noise compensation is performed after dispersion equalization. This processing sequence amplifies the phase noise, resulting in equalization-enhanced phase noise (EEPN), which has emerged as a critical performance-limiting factor, particularly in high-baud-rate or long-reach transmission systems with significant accumulated dispersion. In this work, recognizing that EEPN-induced impairment is predominantly governed by the phase noise component, we propose a novel distance metric for symbol detection and constellation design that departs from the conventional Euclidean distance. Based on this metric, we optimize the constellation geometry to enhance system robustness against EEPN. Simulation results demonstrate that the optimized constellations achieve lower symbol error rates over extended transmission distances compared to conventional designs. Furthermore, when EEPN is the dominant impairment, the proposed approach enables a 10% increase in baud rate at an equivalent symbol error rate relative to state-of-the-art shaped constellations.

title: Multimodal Wireless Foundation Models.
abstract: Wireless foundation models (WFMs) have recently demonstrated promising capabilities, jointly performing multiple wireless functions and adapting effectively to new environments. However, while current WFMs process only one modality, depending on the task and operating conditions, the most informative modality changes and no single modality is best for all tasks. WFMs should therefore be designed to accept multiple modalities to enable a broader and more diverse range of tasks and scenarios. In this work, we propose and build the first multimodal wireless foundation model capable of processing both raw IQ streams and image-like wireless modalities (e.g., spectrograms and CSI) and performing multiple tasks across both. We introduce masked wireless modeling for the multimodal setting, a self-supervised objective and pretraining recipe that learns a joint representation from IQ streams and image-like wireless modalities. We evaluate the model on five tasks across both modality families: image-based (human activity sensing, RF signal classification, 5G NR positioning) and IQ-based (RF device fingerprinting, interference detection/classification). The multimodal WFM is competitive with single-modality WFMs, and in several cases surpasses their performance. Our results demonstrates the strong potential of developing multimodal WFMs that support diverse wireless tasks across different modalities. We believe this provides a concrete step toward both AI-native 6G and the vision of joint sensing, communication, and localization.

title: SIM-Aided Near-Field Channel and Localization Estimation With Dimensionality Reduction: A Multiport Network Theory Approach.
abstract: The deployment of Extremely Large-Scale Antenna Arrays for 6G enables radiative near-field sensing but poses significant challenges in terms of hardware complexity and interference. Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces (SIMs) address these limitations by enabling wave-domain dimensionality reduction. This paper proposes a rigorous SIM-aided framework for near-field channel and localization estimation based on Multiport Network Theory, which provides an electromagnetically consistent characterization accounting for mutual coupling and non-unilateral inter-layer propagation effects. An indirect estimation approach is adopted, where the SIM is optimized to perform analog spatial filtering by projecting the received signal onto a relevant subspace identified through coarse prior location information. Within this realistic setting, we analytically characterize the impact of SIM approximation errors on channel estimation and quantify the resulting effects on localization performance. The results show that the proposed architecture preserves the essential wavefront curvature information required for accurate near-field localization, achieving performance comparable to fully digital solutions while drastically reducing the number of radio-frequency chains.

title: Non-Convex Over-the-Air Heterogeneous Federated Learning: A Bias-Variance Trade-off.
abstract: Over-the-air (OTA) federated learning (FL) has been well recognized as a scalable paradigm that exploits the waveform superposition of the wireless multiple-access channel to aggregate model updates simultaneously. Existing OTA-FL designs largely enforce zero-bias model updates by either assuming homogeneous wireless conditions (equal path loss across devices) or forcing zero bias updates to guarantee convergence. Under heterogeneous wireless scenarios, however, such unbiased designs are constrained by the worst-channel device and suffer from high variance in the updates. Moreover, prior analyses of biased OTAFL largely focus on convex objectives, whereas most modern machine-learning models are highly non-convex. Motivated by these gaps, we study OTA-FL with stochastic gradient descent (SGD) for smooth non-convex objectives under wireless heterogeneity. We develop novel OTA-FL SGD updates that allow a structured, time-invariant model bias while facilitating reduced variance in the updates. We also derive a finite-time stationarity bound (expected time average squared gradient norm) that explicitly reveals a bias–variance trade-off. To optimize this trade-off, we pose a non-convex joint OTA power-control design and develop an efficient successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithm that requires only statistical CSI of the devices at the base station. Experiments on a non-convex image classification task validate the approach: the SCA-based design accelerates convergence via an optimized bias and improves generalization over prior OTA-FL baselines.

title: Intent2QoS: Language Model-Driven Automation of Traffic Shaping Configurations.
abstract: Traffic shaping and Quality of Service (QoS) enforcement are critical for managing bandwidth, latency, and fairness in networks. These tasks often rely on low-level traffic control settings, which require manual setup and technical expertise. This paper presents an automated framework that converts high-level traffic shaping intents in natural or declarative language into valid and correct traffic control rules. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first end-to-end pipeline that ties intent translation in a queuing-theoretic semantic model and, with a rule-based critic, yields deployable Linux traffic control configuration sets. The framework has three steps: (1) a queuing simulation with priority scheduling and Active Queue Management (AQM) builds a semantic model; (2) a language model, using this semantic model and a traffic profile, generates sub-intents and configuration rules; and (3) a rule-based critic checks and adjusts the rules for correctness and policy compliance. We evaluate multiple language models by generating traffic control commands from business intents that comply with relevant standards for traffic control protocols. Experimental results on 100 intents show significant gains, with LLaMA3 reaching 0.88 semantic similarity and 0.87 semantic coverage, outperforming other models by over 30\. A thorough sensitivity study demonstrates that AQM-guided prompting reduces variability threefold compared to zero-shot baselines.

title: Kubernetes for Satellites: In-Lab Validation of a Mobility-Aware MANO Architecture on the 6GStarLab Engineering Model.
abstract: The rapid evolution of the NewSpace sector has accelerated satellite prototyping and development. Meeting the demands of this dynamic environment requires platforms that can flexibly reconfigure payloads and adapt to evolving protocols. This work presents a Management and Orchestration architecture that integrates mobility awareness and geo-localization with hardware reconfiguration capabilities. This development is implemented on the 6GStarLab mission, a 6U CubeSat designed as an open in-orbit laboratory to investigate novel Non-Terrestrial Networks technologies. The architecture was designed following ETSI Network Function Virtualization (NFV) standards, modified to mitigate the impact of satellite mobility. A geographic information system is used to ensure dynamic service continuity over target regions through proactive, position-based co-scheduling of hardware and software resources. The proposed solution, validated through in-lab experiments with the 6GStarLab engineering model, enables automated remote payload reconfiguration and coordinated service orchestration. Experimental results of the in-lab executions are presented, and they confirm the feasibility of this approach, demonstrating successful geo-triggered service activation in 12 seconds, marking a crucial advancement toward future in-orbit operations.

title: Robust Optical Wireless Positioning With Beam Steering: Pose Estimation and Tilt Robustness.
abstract: Received signal strength (RSS)-based optical wireless positioning (OWP) is attractive but notoriously sensitive to transmitter/receiver tilt. Here, we study three OWP configurations with ceiling-mounted light emitting diodes (LED) under identical optical power, noise, and workspace: conventional multifixed LEDs (MFL), used as benchmark for comparison with new single beam-steerable LED (SBL) and multi beam-steerable LEDs (MBL) methods. For the latter two, we develop closedform estimators that exploit steering diversity. We formulate the SBL position estimator as a singular value decompositionbased ratio method that cancels the incidence angle term, and we introduce an MBL orientation estimator that recovers the receiver pose from steered RSS measurements. Simulations quantify the accuracy/robustness trade-offs across configurations, and hardware experiments with a gimbaled LED and a 6 degreesof-freedom robotic arm validate robustness to uncertainty in receiver tilt up to 20 • over a 0.8×0.8 m 2 area, achieving a root mean square error of 2.66 cm, and a pooled within-position root mean square radius of 4.8 mm. The results consistently favor beam steering-based methods over MFL: SBL maintains centimeter-level accuracy under tilt, while MBL delivers the best absolute accuracy and enables pose estimation.

title: Contrastive Deep Reinforcement Learning for Resource Management in Coexisting Satellite and Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: The coexistence of terrestrial (TN) and non-terrestrial networks (NTN) in the Frequency Range 3 (FR3) spectrum enables wide-area connectivity but also introduces cross-layer interference and dynamic spectrum contention, requiring efficient carrier allocation and beamforming. These challenges stem from mixed discrete–continuous variables, strong interference, and stringent quality-of-service (QoS) constraints. Conventional convex optimization is computationally prohibitive, whereas standard deep reinforcement learning (DRL) struggles with hybrid action spaces and fast channel variations. We propose a contrastive-based generative primal-dual proximal policy optimization (CG-PD-PPO) framework that reformulates resource allocation as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP). A primal-dual PPO backbone enforces QoS guarantees, while a diffusion-based generative module and contrastive learning enhance exploration and stability. The system is modeled under 3GPP and ITU NTN specifications, incorporating Earth station in motion (ESIM) mobility, Loo fading, and Doppler effects, with simulations centered on the Ku-band downlink around 12 GHz. Results show that CG-PD-PPO outperforms successive convex approximation (SCA-MA) and PD-PPO in throughput, QoS satisfaction, and interference robustness, while maintaining lower complexity, making it a practical and scalable solution for TN–NTN coexistence in FR3 scenarios.

title: Hierarchical Federated Learning for Urban Mobility Prediction in VANETs.
abstract: The expansion of 5G networks and Vehicular Ad hoc Networks (VANETs) in smart cities has enabled the development of new distributed approaches for urban mobility prediction. The objective of this work is to develop a hybrid vehicle mobility prediction model for VANETs that combines Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, while preserving the confidentiality of local data. Our prediction model is based on a three-level aggregation architecture integrated into a 5G network infrastructure. At the first level, gNB-DU units aggregate the weights from models trained by connected vehicles. At the second level, gNB-CU units aggregate the weights produced by the gNB-DUs within the same area. Finally, the 5G core network performs a final aggregation to generate a global model. This hierarchical structure adapts the learning process to urban connectivity and mobility constraints. The simulations compared several aggregation strategies (FedAvg, FedProx, and FedNova), and the experimental results show improved convergence stability and prediction accuracy compared to classical federated schemes, with minimal communication overhead that further decreases as the number of vehicles increases.

title: Exploring Small Language Models for Efficient HTTP Traffic Generation.
abstract: Realistic HTTP traces are essential for benchmarking intrusion detection, performance analysis, and traffic engineering in modern communication networks. However, privacy regulations and limited access to real data restrict their availability. Synthetic generation has therefore emerged as a practical alternative. Recent work employs Large Language Models (LLMs) to synthesize protocol-level traffic, but such models are computationally expensive, prone to protocol violations, and exhibit limited portability.This paper presents a lightweight framework for HTTP request generation using a domain-adapted Small Language Model (SLM) based on DistilGPT-2 (82M parameters). The model is fine-tuned on a blended corpus combining CSIC 2010 and CIC-IDS-2018 HTTP samples using a causal language modeling objective with controlled decoding. The generated traffic is evaluated across fidelity, utility, indistinguishability, and privacy.The SLM achieves a Jensen–Shannon Divergence of 0.015, adversarial AUC ≈ 0.5, and Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real accuracy of 0.59—all while running on commodity hardware with an order-of-magnitude lower memory and energy footprint than LLM baselines. The results confirm that compact, protocol-aware SLMs can reliably synthesize high-fidelity HTTP traces, offering a scalable and energy-efficient alternative for privacy-preserving traffic generation and network evaluation in mobile and wireless communication systems.

title: A New Quantum Secure Time Transfer System.
abstract: High-precision clock synchronization is essential for a wide range of network-distributed applications. In the quantum space, these applications include communication, sensing, and positioning. However, current synchronization techniques are vulnerable to attacks, such as intercept-resend attacks, spoofing, and delay attacks. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a new quantum secure time transfer (QSTT) system, subsequently used for clock synchronization, that largely negates such attacks. Novel to our system is the optimal use of self-generated quantum keys within the QSTT to information-theoretically secure the maximum amount of timing data; as well as the introduction, within a hybrid quantum/post-quantum architecture, of an information-theoretic secure obfuscated encryption sequence of the remaining timing data. With these enhancements, we argue that our new system represents the most robust implementation of QSTT to date.

title: Over-the-Air-Assisted Federated Learning with Timing Delays: Convergence and Testing Accuracy.
abstract: Over-the-air computation-assisted federated learning (OTA-FL) exploits the superposition property of the wireless medium to efficiently aggregate the local models of multiple devices to update a global model at the parameter server (PS). We investigate the impact of timing delays on OTA-FL. These delays occur when the devices start their transmissions at different times or due to propagation delays between the devices and the PS. Unlike most prior works that assume known delays and employ a whitening matched filter followed by a high-complexity estimator to recover the global model, we focus on the practically more appealing model in which the PS learns from the output of a conventional matched filter and does not know the delays. We derive a novel recursive upper bound on the optimality gap, which contracts by a factor and increases by an additive residual error in each iteration. We characterize the dependence of the contraction factor and the residual error on the device transmit powers, receiver scaling, and delays. Our experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset using a ResNet-18 model show the extent to which training loss increases and testing accuracy decreases as the delays increase. The impact depends on the transmit power control approach and the choice of matched filter, and is more acute for the heterogeneous dataset.

title: Physical Layer Design and Validation of a Downlink NOMA-QPSK System on Software Defined Radio.
abstract: Next-generation wireless networks are adopting Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) technique in order to achieve improved spectral efficiency and massive connectivity. NOMA has been thoroughly studied in theoretical research works in terms of its theoretical performance, however few research efforts have been devoted to its practical over-the-air implementation. This paper introduces the complete physical layer design, implementation, and validation of a two-user downlink NOMA system based on Software Defined Radio platforms. Specifically, the ADALM-PLUTO platform is used and the Quadrature Phase-Shift Keying modulation, Low-Density Parity-Check forward error correction, and a two-stage channel estimator are implemented in order to achieve reliable communication between the transmitter and the receiver. Detailed testing and validation is performed based on simulations and over the air experiments. The achieved Packet Error Rate (PER) is analyzed under various Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and power allocation factors. The experiments demonstrate that allocating less than or more than of the power to the transmitter with strong channel gain conditions results in a significant performance degradation for the overall system.

title: Design and Validation of a Flexible Satellite IoT Testbed.
abstract: Non-terrestrial networks (NTN) are a key enabler for extending massive Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity beyond the coverage of terrestrial infrastructure. Supporting a large number of low-power and sporadically active devices over satellite links requires scalable and energy-efficient access mechanisms. Investigating and optimizing such mechanisms, as well as evaluating new architectures and protocol designs, requires flexible and realistic experimental environments. In this paper, we present SIMON, a satellite IoT testbed designed to support the evaluation of different scenarios and optimization techniques for NTN IoT systems. Among various IoT technologies, LoRaWAN is selected and implemented as a representative low-power wide-area solution, while the testbed architecture is designed to be extensible to other IoT technologies. SIMON integrates two complementary emulation environments for the satellite backhaul link: a hardware-based emulator and a software-based emulator, enabling controlled experimentation under diverse network, channel, and weather conditions. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed testbed, we implement and evaluate two methods proposed in our prior work: SALSA, a satellite-aware transmission scheduling mechanism that assigns collision-free uplink timeslots based on predicted satellite visibility, and REACT, a lightweight application-layer time-synchronization method providing a time reference for devices. Experimental results show that SIMON provides a reliable and efficient platform for validating access optimization and synchronization mechanisms in NTN-IoT systems, and can serve as a flexible experimental framework for future satellite IoT technologies.

title: Performance Analysis of Sub-band Full-duplex Cell-free Massive MIMO ISAC Systems.
abstract: This paper presents sub-band full-duplex (SBFD) as an alternative to in-band full-duplex (IBFD) for enabling simultaneous wireless communication and sensing in cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems. Unlike IBFD integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems that require self-interference cancellation and the decoupling of mutual interference between uplink communication and radar signals, SBFD employs non-overlapping frequency resources for uplink and downlink or radar transmissions within a predefined SBFD timeslot. In the proposed SBFD CF-mMIMO ISAC system, we demonstrate a multi-target position tracking scheme, where range and angle-of-arrival (AoA) measurements are fused with an extended Kalman filter. We further characterize the joint impact of residual self-interference (SI), access point (AP)-to-AP cross-link interference (CLI), uplink communication interference, and AP-user equipment association on the Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLBs) of range and AoA estimation. Results indicate that, in the high residual SI/CLI power regime, SBFD experiences less degradation in range and AoA CRLBs compared to IBFD due to its inherent frequency isolation. Specifically, increasing residual SI/CLI power from 30 dBm to 50 dBm increases the CRLBs by 3.01 m2 and 0.09 rad2 for SBFD compared to an increase of 12.94 m2 and 0.34 rad2 for IBFD at a residual UL communication interference of -10 dBm. Further, performance analysis reveals a performance dependence on power allocation and the ratio of radar to communication sub-band allocation.

title: Load Balancing in Non-Terrestrial Networks Using Free Space Optical Inter-satellite Links.
abstract: Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) increasingly rely on non-geostationary (NGSO) constellations that combine radio frequency (RF) feeder links (FLs) with free space optical (FSO) inter-satellite links (ISLs). Downlink performance in such systems is often constrained by uneven satellite-gateway visibility, data traffic congestion, and rain-induced FL attenuation, leaving the downlink capacity of some satellites underutilized while others become bottlenecks. To prevent such non-uniform load distribution, this paper presents a fairness-driven load balancing strategy that treats the satellite constellation in space as an anycast multi-commodity flow problem. Then, by solving an equivalent linear programming optimization problem, the proposed algorithm dynamically selects the most convenient ground station (GS) to serve each satellite and, when needed, offloads data traffic to adjacent satellites through FSO ISLs. Using a realistic MEO satellite constellation with 1550 nm FSO ISLs and Ka-band feeder links, the method stabilizes the reverse link data service, maintaining the average data rate but notably improving the worst-case throughput. Our proposed algorithm enhances the minimum downlink data rate by more than 25% in the presence of rain and by over 10% under no-rain conditions. These results demonstrate that the use of an ISL-assisted load-balancing scheme mitigates FL bottlenecks and enhances fairness across the satellite constellation, offering a scalable basis for resource allocation in future NTN systems.

title: Application-Aware Traffic Switching Between 5G and Wi-Fi (and Beyond) for High-Throughput Services.
abstract: The increasing demand for high-throughput and immersive applications in next-generation wireless networks calls for efficient and application-aware Radio Access Technology (RAT) selection. This paper introduces a Heuristic-based Network Selection Algorithm (HNSA), a lightweight and interpretable approach designed to dynamically steer user traffic between WiFi and 5G. Unlike traditional static threshold-based or complex AI-driven techniques, HNSA offers a low-complexity, real-time method that adapts to application-specific Quality of Service (QoS) needs, such as latency, bandwidth, and reliability. Our algorithm uses weighted scoring tailored to three traffic categories: Virtual Reality (VR), 3D video streaming, and mixed traffic. Simulations conducted using NS-3 with 50 user devices show that HNSA can effectively match users to the most appropriate RAT. Notably, 80% of VR users were steered to 5G for its lower latency and higher reliability, whereas 80% of 3D video users remained on WiFi, which provided sufficient bandwidth. These findings demonstrate the strength of our context-aware heuristic in optimizing traffic steering without the complexity of machine learning models, and its potential suitability for real-time deployment in future wireless networks.

title: Utility-Aware Segmented Holographic Video Streaming with Knapsack-Theoretic Optimization.
abstract: Holographic-Type Communication (HTC) promises ultra-realistic telepresence and extended reality (XR), but streaming high-fidelity 3D holograms over bandwidth-limited wireless links remains highly challenging. This paper introduces a utility-aware adaptive streaming framework for segmented holographic video. Each frame is decomposed into semantically meaningful components—face, hands, and pose—encoded segments at multiple resolutions using Draco compression. Segment resolution selection is formulated as a 0–1 Knapsack optimization problem to maximize perceived utility under dynamic bandwidth constraints. Utility is modeled with temporal decay functions (linear, exponential, logarithmic) to capture the varying importance of segments over time. We implement and evaluate the framework in Network Simulator-3.40, integrating realistic wireless traces and application-level utilities. Results show notable improvements in bandwidth efficiency, segment delivery, and Quality of Experience (QoE) compared to non-adaptive and static schemes. The proposed approach provides a practical foundation for real-time holographic streaming in 5G/6G wireless networks.

title: Oblivious Transfer over Discrete Memoryless Broadcast Channels.
abstract: We study the oblivious transfer capacity of discrete memoryless broadcast channels with one sender and two receivers. Both non-colluding and colluding receiver cases are analyzed. We derive general outer bounds on the OT capacity region and propose a secure OT protocol resilient to collusion. These results generalize prior findings on specific channels, such as binary erasure broadcast channels, and reveal fundamental insights into how channel noise enables information-theoretic security.

title: Characterization of FR3 Cellular Vehicle-to-Base Station Links in HighRise Urban Scenarios.
abstract: Driven by the escalating demand for wireless capacity and advancements in 6G research, the new Frequency Range 3 (FR3) referred to upper mid-band (7.125-24.25 GHz) has emerged as a highly compelling spectrum candidate. This range offers a trade-off exploiting the high bandwidth capabilities of millimeter wave frequencies and the superior propagation characteristics of sub-6 GHz bands. As such, the upper mid-band presents an opportunity to enhance both coverage and capacity particularly in the context of 6G and Cellular Vehicle-to-Base Station (C-V2B). Crucially, realizing this potential requires overcoming technical challenges through accurate and realistic channel modeling, especially in dense, high-rise urban environments. To address this, we employ a ray-tracing tool to analyze downlink propagation characteristics, enabling detailed channel modeling for reliable C-V2B communication. Our analysis evaluates the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) across sub-6 GHz, FR3, and mmWave bands using antenna array configurations designed for high-rise urban areas. Results show that, under equal aperture sizes across frequencies, FR3 achieves superior SNR compared to mmWave in interference-free conditions. Moreover, under the full-interference case, FR3 yields higher SINR for cell-edge User Equipment (UEs). This indicates that the increased array gain at mmWave cannot fully compensate for the severe path loss experienced by cell-edge UEs.

title: Uncovering Microservice Faults: A Temporal Graph Approach to Root Cause Analysis.
abstract: Microservices have become the backbone of large IT enterprises due to their ability to scale, recover from failures, and adapt to dynamic workloads within cloud-native architectures. Ensuring the reliability of such systems requires accurate and efficient Root Cause Analysis (RCA) to identify and address faults promptly, minimizing disruptions and maintaining service quality. However, current RCA techniques often focus on isolated levels, such as metrics or services, and rely heavily on predefined thresholds or statistical methods, limiting their effectiveness in complex and interconnected systems. We propose a novel unsupervised RCA method based on Temporal Graph Networks (TGNs) to address these limitations. Our approach models the temporal and structural relationships within microservices through the integrated examination of multimodal data to accurately identify faults. Evaluated on an open-source dataset, our method shows superior accuracy compared to SOTA approaches with at least 2% improvement in PR@1, PR@2, and PR@5.

title: GAEloc: Graph Autoencoder for Attack Localization in Cyber-Physical Water Distribution Systems.
abstract: Critical infrastructures in smart cities such as cyber-physical water distribution systems (WDSs) are exposed to cyber-attacks due to their reliance on Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled sensors, digital communication networks, and automated control components. Cyberattacks can compromise sensor integrity and disrupt operational reliability, potentially leading to severe system failures. Recent studies have investigated machine learning and graph neural network techniques to detect cyberattacks in WDSs. However, existing techniques often struggle to scale efficiently and accurately localize the attacked nodes in large WDS network. Also, their detection is limited a predefined list of attacks. In this work, we propose cyberattack localization via graph autoencoder (GAEloc), a framework designed for effective cyberattack localization in large-scale WDSs. The proposed model learns a compact representation of the WDS topology and temporal flow features, enabling it to reconstruct the expected operational states and identify deviations caused by cyberattacks. Due to its unsupervised nature, GAEloc is only trained on normal operation data and localizes attacks without explicit training on attack patterns. Our experimental results on a large-scale WDS benchmark demonstrate that the proposed GAEloc achieves superior localization accuracy, outperforming baseline models by 7–35%, highlighting the effectiveness of unsupervised graph representation learning for IoT-enabled WDS resilience.

title: Vision Language Models on the Edge for Real-Time Robotic Perception.
abstract: Vision–Language Models (VLMs) enable multimodal reasoning for robotic perception and interaction, but their deployment in real-world systems remains constrained by latency, limited onboard resources, and privacy risks of cloud offloading. Edge intelligence within 6G, particularly Open RAN and Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC), offers a pathway to address these challenges by bringing computation closer to the data source. This work investigates the deployment of VLMs on ORAN/MEC infrastructure using the Unitree G1 humanoid robot as an embodied testbed. We design a WebRTC-based pipeline that streams multimodal data to an edge node and evaluate LLaMA-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct deployed at the edge versus in the cloud under real-time conditions. Our results show that edge deployment preserves near-cloud accuracy while reducing end-to-end latency by 5%. We further evaluate Qwen2-VL-2BInstruct, a compact model optimized for resource-constrained environments, which achieves sub-second responsiveness, cutting latency by more than half but at the cost of accuracy.

title: Distributed Learning for Scalable and Efficient UAV-RIS-Enabled IoT Networks.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle-assisted reconfigurable intelligent surface (UAV-RIS) systems are developing as a key technology for next-generation Internet of Things (IoTs), presenting adaptable coverage, improved connectivity, and intelligent beamforming. Typically, the beamforming decisions are executed in a centralized manner at the base station (BS) using machine learning-based algorithms. Conventional centralized learning is constrained by low processing efficiency, sequential computation, and limited scalability, hindering effective coordination and real-time adaptation in multiple UAV-RIS-assisted IoT deployments. To address this, we propose a novel distributed learning technique that supports parallel local model training on UAV-RIS, asynchronous aggregation across edge and cloud servers, and accessible high-dimensional policy learning. The proposal effectively distributes computation across multiple UAV-RISs to assist IoT devices, achieving faster convergence, improved scalability, and higher training throughput than state-of-the-art decentralized and centralized techniques. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposal, which significantly improves task completion efficiency and throughput for UAV-RIS-assisted IoT networks.

title: Edge Implementation of a Fault-Tolerant Wireless Sensor Network for Environmental Monitoring.
abstract: Environmental sensor networks face significant systemic challenges to sustained long-term operation. These systems must satisfy stringent and often competing design requirements to withstand environmental exposure, node failures, limited energy resources, and prolonged deployment durations. Moreover, the geophysical hazards they monitor can disrupt the communication infrastructure required for continuous operation, while many remote regions may lack such infrastructure altogether. In this paper, we present an edge implementation of a fault-tolerant wireless sensor network. The network is governed by an energy management policy formulated within the Model Predictive Control framework. We implement the proposed system and demonstrate its capability for autonomous, real-time control of sensor nodes during two heavy rainfall events. Our results show that predictive control strategies enable sensor nodes to sustain long-term hazard monitoring and early warning operations under uncertain energy availability, even in the absence of communication infrastructure.

title: AnaQKD: Analytical Modeling of Blocking Probability with Quantum Key Distribution in Spectrally-Spatially Elastic Optical Networks.
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD)-enabled spectrally-spatially elastic optical networks (SS-EONs) using multi-core multi-mode fibers face significant challenges, including inter-core crosstalk, inter-mode crosstalk, and noise from quantum and classical channels, which increase blocking probability (BP) and complicate analytical evaluation. This paper proposes AnaQKD, a novel exact analytical priority-based continuous-time Markov chain model for QKD-enabled SS-EONs. Our approach strategically assigns quantum channels to specific modes based on node connectivity, optimizing placement and resource utilization. AnaQKD calculates BP by accounting for all interference sources while generating every possible state and transition. The model supports uniform slot allocation for single-class requests and variable slot allocation for multi-class requests to accommodate diverse bandwidth requirements. To ensure computational scalability, we developed an iterative approximation model for large-scale single-hop analysis. Numerical evaluation demonstrates that AnaQKD produces BP and resource utilization results closely aligning with Monte Carlo simulations. The approximation model maintains reliable accuracy where exact solutions become computationally prohibitive. Our priority-based approach consistently outperforms the non-priority-based approach, demonstrating significant benefits of strategic mode selection in QKD-enabled SS-EONs.

title: Hetero-Net: An Energy-Efficient Resource Allocation and 3D Placement in Heterogeneous LoRa Networks via Multi-Agent Optimization.
abstract: The evolution of Internet of Things (IoT) into multi-layered environments has positioned Low-Power Wide Area Networks (LPWANs), particularly Long Range (LoRa), as the backbone for connectivity across both surface and subterranean landscapes. However, existing LoRa-based network designs often treat ground-based wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and wireless underground sensor networks (WUSNs) as separate systems, resulting in inefficient and non-integrated connectivity across diverse environments. To address this, we propose Hetero-Net, a unified heterogeneous LoRa framework that integrates diverse LoRa end devices with multiple unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-mounted LoRa gateways. Our objective is to maximize system energy efficiency through the joint optimization of the spreading factor, transmission power, and three-dimensional (3D) placement of the UAVs. To manage the dynamic and partially observable nature of this system, we model the problem as a partially observable stochastic game (POSG) and address it using a multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) framework. An ablation study shows that our proposed MAPPO Hetero-Net significantly outperforms traditional, isolated network designs, achieving energy efficiency improvements of 55.81\% and 198.49\% over isolated WSN-only and WUSN-only deployments, respectively.

title: Vision Language Models for Optimization-Driven Intent Processing in Autonomous Networks.
abstract: Intent-Based Networking (IBN) allows operators to specify high-level network goals rather than low-level configurations. While recent work demonstrates that large language models can automate configuration tasks, a distinct class of intents requires generating optimization code to compute provably optimal solutions for traffic engineering, routing, and resource allocation. Current systems assume text-based intent expression, requiring operators to enumerate topologies and parameters in prose. Network practitioners naturally reason about structure through diagrams, yet whether Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can process annotated network sketches into correct optimization code remains unexplored. We present IntentOpt, a benchmark of 85 optimization problems across 17 categories, evaluating four VLMs (GPT-5-Mini, Claude-Haiku-4.5, Gemini-2.5-Flash, Llama-3.2-11B-Vision) under three prompting strategies on multimodal versus text-only inputs. Our evaluation shows that visual parameter extraction reduces execution success by 12–21 percentage points (pp), with GPT-5-Mini dropping from 93% to 72%. Program-of-thought prompting decreases performance by up to 13 pp, and open-source models lag behind closed-source ones, with Llama-3.2-11B-Vision reaching 18% compared to 75% for GPT-5-Mini. These results establish baseline capabilities and limitations of current VLMs for optimization code generation within an IBN system. We also demonstrate practical feasibility through a case study that deploys VLM-generated code to network testbed infrastructure using Model Context Protocol.

title: Performance Analysis of Cell-Free Massive MIMO under Imperfect LoS Phase Tracking.
abstract: We study the impact of imperfect line-of-sight (LoS) phase tracking on the uplink performance of cell-free massive MIMO networks. Unlike prior works that assume perfectly known or completely unknown phases, we consider a realistic regime where LoS phases are estimated with residual uncertainty due to hardware impairments, mobility, and synchronization errors. To this end, we propose a Rician fading model where LoS components are rotated by imperfect phase estimates and attenuated by a deterministic \textit{phase-error penalty factor}. We derive a linear MMSE channel estimator that accounts for statistical phase errors and unifies prior results, reducing to the Bayesian MMSE estimator when phase is perfectly known and to a zero-mean model when no phase information is available. To address the non-Gaussian setting, we introduce a virtual uplink model that preserves second-order statistics of channel estimation, enabling the derivation of tractable virtual centralized and distributed MMSE beamformers. To ensure fair assessment of network performance, we apply these virtual beamformers to the operational uplink model that reflects the actual physical channel and compute the spectral efficiency bounds available in the literature. Numerical results show that our framework bridges idealized assumptions and practical tracking limitations, providing rigorous performance benchmarks and design insights for 6G cell-free networks.

title: Quantum-Inspired Intelligence for Trustworthy CAN-BUS Protocol Security in Amended Vehicles Communication.
abstract: As connected amended vehicles (CAVs) increasingly depend on GPS and V2X communication, spoofing and DoS attacks threaten system safety and trust. This paper presents Qi2X, a hybrid quantum-classical framework that combines quantum-enhanced learning with explainable AI (XAI) for real-time spoofing detection in CAN-BUS communication. The system integrates three core modules: a Quantum-Inspired Threat (QUIT) detector for encoding spoofing features, an Explainable Hybrid AI $(\hat x{\text{AI}})$ using SHAP and LIME for interpretability, and a Trust-Aware Decision (TAD) engine for dynamic message validation. Evaluated on GPS and CICIoV2024 datasets, Qi2X achieved robust detection of sophisticated (Class 3) spoofing attacks with lower MSE (13.10) and higher trust scores (T = 0.76) than baseline MLP models, ensuring trustworthy and explainable vehicular communication.

title: Secrecy analysis of indoor optical wireless communication for health monitoring.
abstract: We evaluate the physical-layer security of uplink infrared optical wireless communication for indoor health-monitoring applications, with a focus on the impact of user body-induced blockage and environment characteristics on secrecy performance. The scenario considers sensitive data upload from wearable sensors to a ceiling-mounted gateway while a passive eavesdropper occupies a fixed location. Using ray-tracing technique associated to Monte-Carlo method to generate a large dataset of channel realizations, we perform a statistical analysis on the legitimate and eavesdropper optical channel gains. Secrecy is assessed through practically attainable metrics under on-off keying (OOK) modulation, including the achievable secrecy rate and the secrecy area, accounting for target bit error rate (BER) and data rate requirements of representative health sensors. Results show that body presence has a strong influence on secrecy, improving it when the eavesdropper is shadowed, but potentially reducing it when the legitimate link is obstructed. Reducing ceiling reflectivity further improves secrecy by degrading eavesdroppers’ channels more than the legitimate link. These findings highlight the importance of realistic body modeling and environment conscious design in enabling secure uplink infrared (IR) communication, providing a practical baseline for further enhancement through more complex techniques.

title: Control-Oriented Achievable Rates for Continuous-Time Gaussian Channels with Feedback.
abstract: In this work, we revisit the problem of power-constrained transmission over continuous-time (CT) linear, time-invariant (LTI) channels with additive colored Gaussian noise, where channel output feedback is available at the transmitter. Although this model has been studied by several authors, previous work has primarily relied on a stochastic processes framework, which yields explicit achievable rates and capacity characterizations only for a limited class of channel models. Here, we adopt the control-theoretic framework, introduced by Elia in 2004 for the study of discrete-time feedback channels, and extend it to CT settings. We show how CT communications channels can be represented within this formulation, and illustrate the resulting coding scheme with an explicit example. It is observed that the rate achieved by the proposed feedback scheme is 30% higher than the capacity of the channel without feedback, attained by the waterfilling scheme. This work suggests a promising direction for developing communication schemes for additional important CT channel models that have not been studied previously.

title: Enabling Uplink NTN-TN Coexistence via Parametrized Linear Precoding in Upper Mid-Bands.
abstract: The coexistence of terrestrial networks (TNs) and non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) within shared spectrum bands poses significant uplink (UL) interference challenges. While conventional studies assume single-antenna TN terminals, this work investigates UE-side precoding for NTN–TN coexistence using multi-antenna user equipment (UE) operating in upper mid-band frequencies, where larger antenna arrays at the UE become feasible. We develop a parametrized, direction-informed linear UL precoder that leverages antenna directivity and satellite ephemeris information, enabling UEs to shape their radiation patterns without requiring real-time satellite channel state information (CSI). By tuning two design parameters, the precoder can be configured for different practical objectives: an NTN-oriented setting that prioritizes interference suppression toward satellites, and a TN-oriented setting that preserves TN signal quality while adaptively prioritizing the most interference-exposed satellites, reducing the upper tail of the interference-to-noise ratio (INR) distribution and achieving an interference profile closer to uniform.

title: BER Analysis and Optimization of Pinching-Antenna-Based NOMA Communications.
abstract: This paper presents the first bit error rate (BER) analysis of a pinching-antenna (PA)-based non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) communication system. The PA is assumed to be able to be placed anywhere along the waveguide and serves two NOMA user equipment (UEs) in both uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) scenarios. Exact closed-form expressions for the average BER of each user are derived under practical imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). These expressions are then used to optimize the PA location for minimizing the overall average BER of both UEs. In the UL case, the interference between the users' channels introduces phase-dependent fluctuations in the BER cost function, making it highly non-convex with many local extrema. To address this challenge, a smoothing technique is applied to extract the lower envelope of the BER function, effectively suppressing ripples and enabling a reliable identification of the global minimum. In the DL case, a joint optimization of the PA location and NOMA power allocation coefficients is proposed to minimize the average BER. Simulation results verify the accuracy of the analytical derivations and the effectiveness of the proposed optimization methods. Notably, the UL results demonstrate that an optimally positioned PA can create the required received power difference between two equally powered UEs for reliable power-domain NOMA decoding under imperfect SIC.

title: Reliability-Aware Detection of Reactive Jamming in LoRaWAN.
abstract: LoRaWAN is a leading Low-Power Wide-Area Network (LPWAN) protocol designed for scalable Internet of Things (IoT) applications. However, its ALOHA-based Medium Access Control (MAC) scheme renders it highly susceptible to reactive jamming attacks. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to extend the FLoRa/OMNeT++ simulation framework by incorporating a realistic PHY/MAC-level reactive jammer. The proposed jammer leverages Channel Activity Detection (CAD) to synchronize with packet preambles and inject high-power interference using matched transmission parameters. Furthermore, it employs periodic channel hopping to emulate agile attack strategies commonly observed in real-world environments. We then design a unified machine learning pipeline that supports both unsupervised (LSTM/TCN autoencoders) and supervised (LSTM and Transformer classifiers) detection paradigms. Experimental results demonstrate that reactive jamming significantly disrupts LoRaWAN performance. While traditional statistical baselines struggle to balance precision and recall, our Transformer-based classifier achieves 0.939 accuracy, 0.919 precision, 0.895 recall, and 0.907 F1-score outperforming prior approaches. These findings indicate that combining attention-based sequence modeling with realistic adversarial simulation enables accurate and gener-alizable detection of jamming in LPWAN systems.

title: DRL-based AoI Optimization for Energy Harvesting Human Body Communication ECG Networks.
abstract: In energy harvesting (EH) Internet of Bodies (IoB) networks, maintaining information freshness is critical for time-sensitive applications such as electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring. Timely transmissions are essential for reliable ECG analysis, which requires complete and synchronous data from all sensors, as each ECG lead is derived from potential differences between paired sensors. To this end, we leverage model-free deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to learn adaptive scheduling policies that minimize the age of information (AoI) in dynamic and intermittent energy arrival conditions. Specifically, in a human body communication (HBC)-enabled EH-ECG network, wearable ECG sensors transmit data to a central wearable hub acting as the scheduler. The hub implements the DRL scheduling algorithm that selects sensor transmissions based on their battery and AoI levels. Furthermore, we propose an ECG synthesis framework for a 3-lead ECG that mitigates the impact of EH scarcity by reconstructing missing leads from data transmitted by active sensors, thereby ensuring complete signal availability at the hub. Simulation results show that the proposed solution reduces AoI by up to 57% compared to the greedy myopic policy and up to 96% relative to a baseline learning policy.

title: Joint UAV Trajectory and Resource Optimization in UAV-Assisted Networks via Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) play a crucial role in extending wireless network coverage in rural and disaster-affected areas by acting as airborne base stations or communication relays. However, UAV-assisted wireless networks face significant challenges due to limited onboard energy, constrained transmission resources, and strong inter-UAV interference, which jointly degrade flight endurance and communication performance. This paper proposes a novel multiple agent multiple critic deep reinforcement learning (MA-MC-DRL) framework, built upon the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) framework, to enable joint trajectory and resource optimization in a multiple UAV-assisted wireless environment. Unlike conventional single-critic or single-agent approaches, the proposal employs multiple critic deep neural networks (DNNs) to separately evaluate multiple performance metrics, while adopting centralized training with decentralized execution to effectively address the coupling among UAVs. In addition, a fuzzy logic-based adaptive critic-weighting mechanism is proposed, in which each UAV dynamically adjusts the relative importance of individual critic DNNs based on time-varying network conditions, interference levels, and residual energy states, thereby eliminating manual reward tuning and enhancing scalability in dense deployments. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed MA-MC-DRL framework, demonstrating gains of up to 22% in energy consumption, 19% in communication fairness, and 20% in service quality compared to best-performing state-of-the-art algorithms in dense multiple UAV deployment scenarios.

title: Robust Generative-Augmented DRL for Multi-Beam Jamming of Drone Swarms.
abstract: The increasing deployment of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms introduces critical security risks through adversarial surveillance and attacks on infrastructure. Traditional counter-UAV (C-UAV) systems relying on kinetic interceptors or omnidirectional electronic warfare face limitations in scalability, precision, and energy efficiency. While phased-array beamforming enables targeted RF jamming, challenges persist in early detection, spectrum interference, and adaptive responses to evolving swarm tactics. To address these challenges, we propose a generative-augmented adaptive jamming framework grounded in deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and generative AI. Our system model incorporates drone mobility, multi-beam phased-array jamming, and a probabilistic jamming success metric based on the Jamming-to-Signal-plus-Noise Ratio (JSNR). We formulate the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) optimized via Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and integrate three generative modules: a variational autoencoder (VAE) for scenario diversification, a diffusion model for predictive swarm tracking, and a GAN-based adversarial perturbation module. Simulations demonstrate that our method outperforms conventional DRL baselines, achieving 30% higher jamming accuracy, 2x lower latency, 80% less power consumption, and over 4× higher success rates in high-noise environments.

title: Bayesian Network-based Casual Structure Learning for Root Cause Analysis of IoT Network Anomalies.
abstract: Since the Internet of Things (IoT) network’s expansion has significantly increased the complexity of monitoring and debugging systems, there is an urgent need for abnormality diagnosis to ensure stable system operations. However, traditional anomaly detection methods can only find abnormal activities and are not able to perform root cause analysis (RCA) for possible failures. To address this limitation, we introduce a Bayesian Network-based RCA framework, which performs causal structure and parameter learning, and probabilistic reasoning. This framework detect causes and effects by deploying the Peter–Clark algorithm, and can find the model’s parameters (i.e., forward and backwards inference) with Expectation–Maximisation. In this way, we identify how an anomaly transits through the system and uncover root causes. In the feature selection component, one of the main components of the proposed system, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Recursive Feature Elimination methods are employed to reduce model complexity and increase interpretability. We evaluate the framework on the TON_IoT dataset to evaluate diagnostic accuracy and obtain actionable causal insights instead of detection-only baselines. The experimental results reveal that the proposed framework provides a robust diagnosis model with the achieved causal explanations for the anomalies in IoT networks.

title: RCS modeling for ISAC-Enabled 6G Robotic Sensing Using Gaussian Process Regression.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is a key enabling technology for 6G networks, supporting emerging robotic and autonomous systems that require joint high-accuracy sensing and reliable wireless communication. A fundamental challenge in ISAC channel modeling is the accurate characterization of radar cross section (RCS), which directly impacts detection, localization, and classification performance. This paper presents a calibrated RCS measurement and modeling framework tailored for ISAC operation at 28 GHz. Using a controlled quasi-monostatic experimental setup, we measure the RCS of a rectangular metallic target across a wide range of incident angles to simulate a sparse, multistatic ISAC deployment. To reconstruct full 360° RCS profiles from limited data points, Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) is employed, providing both predictive mean estimates and uncertainty-aware bounds. The methodology is experimentally validated through comparison with theoretical RCS expressions for rectangular plates, achieving an accuracy within 0.9 dB. Hyperparameters such as kernel length-scale and signal variance are systematically tuned to ensure high-fidelity interpolation while preserving physical scattering characteristics, with independent testing demonstrating that all predictions fall within the 68–99% confidence bounds of the GPR posterior. Finally, the framework is applied to a security-centric scenario involving the detection of metallic objects concealed beneath fabric. Measurements confirm that while attenuation occurs, the fundamental RCS pattern remains preserved, enabling target identification in obscured conditions and highlighting the potential for 6G-enabled robotics to perform automated object identification in complex, visually degraded environments.

title: A POF-PDMS Matrix Wearable for Multi-Angle Joint Tracking in eHealth Systems.
abstract: Current rehabilitation monitoring devices often rely on electronic strain gauges, inertial measurement units (IMUs), or conductive textiles, which are bulky, power-dependent, and subject to electromagnetic interference (EMI), while offering limited multi-angle tracking. To address these challenges, this paper presents a novel 30 × 30 mm matrix-based sensor consisting of six jacketed plastic optical fibers (POFs) embedded in a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrate. The system employs LEDs and photodiodes for light transmission, with Arduino-based acquisition and MATLAB analysis. Baseline characterization confirmed stable and repeatable signals with minimal noise. Controlled multiangle bending examined the fibers within the deformation, resulting in voltage reductions of up to 32.5%, while unaffected fibers remained stable, validating selective sensitivity. Heatmap visualization further demonstrated directional resolution and spatial mapping capability. These results highlight the proposed POF– PDMS matrix as the first demonstration of a matrix-based wearable optical sensor for physical rehabilitation, offering a lightweight, low-cost, and flexible platform for multi-angle joint monitoring and integration in eHealth architectures.

title: Keyed Compressive Sensing for Efficient and Privacy-aware Distributed ISAC.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables communication nodes to jointly perform sensing and data exchange, allowing radio sensing information to be collected and shared across the network. In OFDM-based systems, this capability allows sensing information to be extracted and distributed using the communication waveform itself, transforming sensing from a single-device capability into an inherently distributed function of the communication infrastructure. To fully realize its potential, however, ISAC must address three key challenges: (i) achieving high-resolution radio sensing under limited radio resources, (ii) enabling efficient data fusion with constrained communication capacity, and (iii) protecting sensing data from unauthorized receivers. In this paper, we show that compressive sensing provides a powerful framework to jointly address these challenges. We propose a keyed variant that simultaneously enables compression, supports efficient fusion, and offers inherent secrecy. Our results show that legitimate receivers can reliably reconstruct the sensed scene even under strong dimensionality reduction, while eavesdroppers are unable to recover meaningful information without knowledge of the secret key.

title: LWM-Temporal: Sparse Spatio-Temporal Attention for Wireless Channel Representation Learning.
abstract: LWM-Temporal is a new member of the Large Wireless Models (LWM) family that targets the spatiotemporal nature of wireless channels. Designed as a task-agnostic foundation model, LWM-Temporal learns universal channel embeddings that capture mobility-induced evolution and are reusable across various downstream tasks. To achieve this objective, LWM-Temporal operates in the angle-delay-time domain and introduces Sparse Spatio-Temporal Attention (SSTA), a propagation-aligned attention mechanism that restricts interactions to physically plausible neighborhoods, reducing attention complexity by an order of magnitude while preserving geometry-consistent dependencies. LWM-Temporal is pretrained in a self-supervised manner using a physics-informed masking curriculum that emulates realistic occlusions, pilot sparsity, and measurement impairments. Experimental results on channel prediction across multiple mobility regimes show consistent improvements over strong baselines, particularly under long horizons and limited fine-tuning data, highlighting the importance of geometry-aware architectures and geometry-consistent pretraining for learning transferable spatiotemporal wireless representations.

title: Dynamic Parameter Scheduling in Soft-Hard BPGD for Lossy Source Coding.
abstract: We investigate lossy source coding based on a soft-decision belief propagation guided decimation (BPGD) encoder for low-density generator matrix (LDGM) codes, referred to as soft-hard BPGD. The performance of this encoder is highly sensitive to the choice of "softness" parameters, typically denoted by (β,µ), which are conventionally tuned via exhaustive empirical sweeps. To reduce this burden and to better align the algorithm with the evolving graphical structure during decimation, we introduce a dynamic scheduling framework in which (β,µ) are not fixed globally but change as decimation progresses. The schedule starts in a softer regime to encourage exploration and gradually hardens toward the end to promote convergence, similar to simulated annealing. We consider linear and exponential schedules, discuss their physical interpretation via an effective temperature view-point, and explain how they integrate with soft-hard BPGD without changing the order of magnitude of its complexity. Numerical experiments with irregular and semi-regular LDGM ensembles indicate improved rate-distortion performance and reduced non-convergence compared to constant-parameter baselines, while largely eliminating expensive grid searches for a single best pair (β,µ).

title: LightTune: Lightweight Online Fine-Tuning for 6G.
abstract: Machine learning (ML) models for mobile devices are often trained offline and deployed in environments that may differ from their training conditions, leading to performance degradation even when real-world data is used for training. To address this training-test mismatch, we propose a lightweight, backpropagation-free online fine-tuning framework termed Light-Tune that refines the ML models using live test-time data. This online fine-tuning mechanism is opportunistically triggered when the model’s performance falls below a desired threshold, ensuring minimal computational overhead and efficient responsiveness.As a practical demonstration, we integrate LightTune into a block error rate (BLER) prediction algorithm for 6G mobiles. This integration enables the model to dynamically adapt to previously unseen channel conditions in real-time. Simulation results show a substantial reduction in the average BLER prediction error up to 43.5% with online fine-tuning. Furthermore, we leverage this BLER prediction algorithm for link adaptation and demonstrate average throughput improvements of up to 9.5% compared to a conventional table-based outer loop link adaptation algorithm.

title: Deep Learning-Driven and Zero-Knowledge Proof-Enhanced Task Offloading for Privacy-Preserving Vehicular Networks.
abstract: In vehicular networks, dynamic topology and limited on-board resources make it difficult for vehicles to execute computationally intensive tasks locally. Machine learning–based task offloading has emerged as a promising solution to optimize resource utilization and network performance. However, rapidly changing network conditions, heterogeneous vehicle capabilities, and the need for privacy-preserving coordination present critical challenges. This paper proposes a deep learning–driven, privacy-preserving task offloading framework for vehicular networks. The proposed approach operates in two stages. First, a deep neural network (DNN) model predicts suitable offloading candidates by learning spatiotemporal patterns and resource availability from historical communication and mobility data. Second, a Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP)-enhanced trust mechanism enables vehicles to verifiably prove their computational capabilities and task completion correctness without revealing sensitive information. This integration allows the task requester to select nodes that are both resource-efficient and trustworthy. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves up to 30% reduction in task latency and 25% improvement in offloading success rate compared to traditional heuristic approaches, while maintaining strong privacy guarantees and low verification overhead. The results validate the potential of machine learning to enable intelligent, secure, and adaptive task offloading in next-generation vehicular networks.

title: Multi-Cluster RIS-Assisted Backscatter Communication Model for Sustainable Interference Mitigation in 6G Industrial IoT Networks.
abstract: Interference mitigation is a critical challenge in future 6G networks, particularly in dense industrial Internet of Things (IoT) environments where massive device connectivity degrades reliability, spectral efficiency, and energy efficiency. To address this challenge, this research proposes a multi-cluster reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted backscatter communication (BackCom) framework for sustainable interference mitigation in 6G networks. The proposed system consists of a gNodeB acting as a carrier emitter, multiple passive backscatter devices, distributed RIS clusters, and backscatter receivers. By jointly optimizing RIS phase shifts and transmit power allocation using fractional programming (FP) and the water-filling algorithm, the proposed approach enhances the effective channel gain while suppressing multi-user interference. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a 36.35% improvement in total sum-rate, a 1.94 dB SINR gain, and an over fourfold reduction in outage probability compared with conventional schemes. In addition, the proposed method significantly improves energy efficiency and reliability under dense device deployment. These results confirm that RIS-assisted BackCom provides a low-power, scalable, and energy-efficient solution for reliable interference mitigation in next-generation 6G industrial IoT networks.

title: Sustainable and Adaptive Resource Allocation for IoT Applications at the Extreme Edge.
abstract: We present SARA, a Sustainable Adaptive Resource Allocation framework for Extreme Edge IoT systems. It guides allocation decisions by jointly considering cost, response delay, and reward-efficiency within a weighted utility formulation. At its core, SARA introduces an Adaptive Efficiency Reward (AER) metric that prioritizes workers offering high computational capacity at reasonable reward expectations, promoting long-term sustainability by maintaining worker participation under budget constraints. The framework is evaluated against a Weighted Fair Assignment (WFA) baseline through an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) formulation. Experiments are conducted in two modes: (i) offline allocation over multiple rounds to analyze sustainability under progressive worker attrition, and (ii) online task arrivals handled through a heuristic version of SARA. In the offline setting, SARA sustains worker engagement by selectively satisfying high-efficiency participants, resulting in improved execution performance across rounds and validating its effectiveness in maintaining long-term participation. In the online setting, we explore adaptive weighting based on task service-level requirements (urgent, elastic, and heavy), demonstrating SARA’s ability to dynamically balance cost, delay, and reward-efficiency. Results show that this adaptability improves task execution rates while better aligning allocation decisions with diverse QoS objectives. These findings demonstrate SARA’s dual capability to maintain long-term sustainability and short-term adaptability in heterogeneous, resource-constrained extreme-edge environments.

title: Estimating Streaming Services Computational Reliability in Extreme Edge Computing.
abstract: Extreme Edge Computing (XEC), which harnesses consumer-owned devices for on-demand service delivery, is pivotal for ultra-low-latency applications. However, providing continuous data streaming services with predictable reliability in such environments is a formidable challenge due to the inherent volatility and limited observability of computational resources at the extreme edge. This paper introduces an analytical framework for quantifying the computational reliability of streaming services operating under uncertainty in XEC. Our framework addresses scenarios with varying information fidelity: firstly, under stationary assumptions using minimal operational bounds, and then leveraging historical data. Analytical expressions are developed, interpreting the complex interplay between QoS requirements and resources availability. We validate the accuracy and efficacy of the derived models, demonstrating their utility in providing robust reliability assessments for continuous streaming services under diverse and dynamic XEC conditions. Our work provides essential theoretical tools for service orchestrators, enabling more informed decisions regarding resilient service placement and dynamic resource management for streaming applications at the network’s extreme periphery.

title: Dynamic Trust-Weighted Federated Learning for Robust Industrial Internet of Things.
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) devices significantly expands the attack surface of modern industrial networks, exposing critical infrastructure to sophisticated cyber threats. Traditional centralized intrusion detection systems face limitations due to data privacy concerns, heterogeneous device capabilities, and delayed threat response. Conventional federated learning approaches often treat all participating nodes equally, making the system vulnerable to unreliable or compromised contributors. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Trust-Weighted Federated Learning (DTW-FL), a novel framework for robust cybersecurity in IIoT networks. DTW-FL assigns a trust score to each device based on reliability in reporting anomalies and contribution to improving detection performance. Devices with higher trust scores exert more influence on the global model, while less reliable or potentially compromised devices have reduced impact.
