Among the methods, Replay-based approaches achieve the best overall performance, while Synaptic Intelligence (SI) delivers near-zero forgetting with high training efficiency, demonstrating strong potential for stable and sustainable IDS deployment in dynamic IoT networks.

title: Pragmatic NTN ISAC: Utilizing Distributed NTN Systems for Sensing and Communication.
abstract: Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) offer promising solutions for extending connectivity to remote and underserved areas, but their potential for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) remains underexplored, particularly in distributed configurations. We show that for distributed NTN systems, owing to their large virtual antenna apertures, Earth’s surface falls within the near-field regime. Hence, it is possible to perform near-field beamfocusing with these systems. The possibility of beamfocusing opens the way for sensing and tracking large metallic objects, such as ships and aircraft. The approach is pragmatic as it repurposes existing RF communication hardware with minimal additional signal processing, eliminating the need for dedicated radar-specific equipment and providing a cost-effective alternative. To overcome the phase and gain impairments from the dynamic nature of the distributed NTN system, we also propose a Kalman filter-based framework to compensate for these impairments. Simulation results demonstrate significantly narrower 3 dB beamwidths (from tens of kilometers to tens of meters) and improved echo signal strength (by 20-50 dB) in distributed NTN systems compared to single-platform NTNs. The framework addresses practical challenges like platform synchronization and handover in dynamic environments, paving the way for resilient, dual-function NTN for the future.

title: LARA-PPO: A Joint Optimization Framework for Success-Energy Trade-off in Vehicular Edge Task Offloading.
abstract: Task offloading to edge servers enables resource-constrained vehicles to run advanced AI services. However, limited edge capacity often leads to overload, especially when traffic surges in specific regions such as during rush hours or major events. Existing vehicular offloading schemes confine cooperation within fixed or neighbor-based scopes, causing severe performance degradation when all servers in a region become saturated. Expanding the cooperation range can alleviate overload but introduces a new cost—system-wide energy consumption. An effective framework must therefore adapt its cooperation scope to real-time network conditions while jointly optimizing the success–energy trade-off. This paper proposes LARA-PPO, a two-layer offloading framework that fulfills both requirements. We first formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize task success while minimizing total energy. The first layer, LARA (Lightweight Adaptive Resource-aware Aggregation), dynamically forms cooperation groups by expanding or shrinking their scope according to real-time resource conditions through decentralized, range-limited message exchanges. Within each group, a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based reinforcement learning agent jointly determines the offloading fraction and task placement to balance success and energy. Simulation results show that LARA-PPO surpasses the success-only scheme with higher task success rates and about 20% lower total energy consumption. Under localized overload, it further outperforms static-region and neighbor-based cooperation by 15% and 25%, respectively, demonstrating robust adaptability through dynamic group expansion.

title: CORE-ML: Compute Optimized Resource Allocation for Cloud-native MLOps Pipelines.
abstract: Efficient resource allocation in cloud-native machine learning (ML) pipelines remains a fundamental challenge, as different pipeline stages exhibit diverse and often imbalanced computational demands. Existing strategies, such as the Kubeflow default allocation (KFDA) and reactive autoscalers like the Kubernetes horizontal pod autoscaler (HPA) and vertical pod autoscaler (VPA), rely on a static provisioning baseline and adjust resources when they exceed a preset threshold. These strategies result in persistent over-provisioning, under-utilization, and higher operational costs. In this paper, we introduce CORE-ML, a unified, stage-aware resource allocation framework for machine learning operations (MLOps). At its core is the CORE-Adaptive strategy, which proactively right-sizes CPU allocations using FLOP-based scaling. Additionally, we propose two complementary policies, CORE-Fixed and CORE-Burst, and evaluate them against the current approaches. Experiments on representative pipelines involving DNN, CNN, and LSTM workloads demonstrate that CORE-ML strategies consistently outperform KFDA and VPA baselines. CORE-Adaptive improves CPU utilization, reduces over-provisioned vCPU-hours, and lowers execution cost by up to 30%, 80%, and 81%, respectively, without compromising training accuracy or runtime. Our findings position CORE-ML as a robust and scalable framework for optimizing resource allocation in cloud-native machine learning environments, delivering both computational efficiency and operational practicality.

title: QoS-Aware Multi-Rate SWIPT for Reliable and Sustainable Industrial IoT Communication.
abstract: Energy harvesting and simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) enable sustainable, low-maintenance industrial communication networks. This work investigates a SWIPT-based system in which an energy-harvesting (EH) relay has multi-rate (MR) selection capability to transmit information to the destination at different rates. Traditional SWIPT and adaptive rate selection considers a broad range of rates, which increases the power consumption and reduces the reliability in real deployments. To address these limitations and improve the reliability of the SWIPT network, we evaluate the performance of the time-switched relaying (TSR) protocol in MR scenarios. Our novel investigation reveals that the proposed MR-SWIPT scheme enhances reliability in terms of throughput over single-rate systems, which supports QoS-aware MR transmission for heterogeneous industrial devices with varying rate requirements. To further improve performance, we jointly optimize TSR parameter (β), and the rate selection parameter (δ) using the 2D golden section search (2D-GSS) method, and reduce computational complexity by transforming the joint optimization into a single-variable problem. The results confirm the effectiveness of SWIPT-enabled MR energy-harvesting relaying for sustainable and resilient industrial networks and next-generation industrial IoT systems.

title: Semantic Knowledge Base Based Dual-mode Video Semantic Communication.
abstract: Semantic communication is a highly promising field designed to boost efficiency by prioritizing the transfer of meaning over raw bit fidelity. Existing research generally focuses on a single transmission mechanism, operating exclusively within either the continuous or discrete semantic space. However, a significant gap remains: there is no unified framework that successfully integrates the benefits of both modes. To overcome this limitation, and specifically targeting video data, this paper introduces a dual-mode video semantic communication (DMVSC) framework that seamlessly combines the continuous and discrete approaches. To further improve transmission efficiency, we design a temporal redundancy compressor based on an attention mechanism. Additionally, we construct a specialized semantic knowledge base (SKB) for video features, enabling efficient semantic feature quantization via index transmission. Experimental results conclusively demonstrate that our proposed DMVSC framework achieves superior video reconstruction performance compared to conventional methods.

title: New Sphere-Packing Bounds for Finite Blocklengths.
abstract: This paper investigates the maximal channel coding rate, denoted by R, with a given decoding error probability ϵ and a finite blocklength n. The existing bounds for this problem are tight for moderate-to-large blocklengths (n ≥ 1000), however, significant disparities persist for n ≤ 100. In this paper, a new achievable bound is derived by employing the sphere-packing tool. Specifically, with an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) P, a concise and explicit asymptotic bound is obtained as ϵ≈ exp {−n[E0(P ) − R + O(n−0.5)]}, where E0is a simple explicit function of only P, whose form bears similarity to Gallager’s error exponent. Numerical results show that the proposed bounds are much tighter compared to existing bounds when n ≤ 100.

title: SWORD: A Secure LoW-Latency Offline-First Authentication and Data Sharing Scheme for Resource Constrained Distributed Networks.
abstract: While many resource-constrained networks, such as Internet of Things (IoT) and Internet of Vehicles (IoV), are inherently distributed, the majority still rely on central servers for fast authentication and data sharing. Blockchain-based solutions offer decentralized alternatives but often struggle to meet the stringent latency requirements of real-time applications. Even with the rollout of 5G, network latency between servers and peers remains a significant challenge. To address this, we introduce SWORD, a novel offline-first authentication and data-sharing scheme designed specifically for resource-constrained networks. SWORD utilizes a proximity-based clustering approach to enable offline authentication and data sharing, ensuring low-latency, secure operations even in intermittently connected scenarios. Our experimental results show that SWORD outperforms traditional blockchain-based solutions while offering similar resource efficiency and authentication latency to central-server-based solutions. Additionally, we provide a comprehensive security analysis, demonstrating that SWORD is resilient against spoofing, impersonation, replay, and man-in-the-middle attacks.

title: Quantum Capacity Analysis of the DNA-to-Protein Channel via Extreme Channel Decomposition.
abstract: Quantum information theory has recently been employed to model biological processes, shedding light on how nature may exploit quantum effects for efficient information transfer. This work explores the potential of quantum channels derived from biological models to advance next-generation communication systems. Focusing on the transfer of genetic information between DNA and proteins, we propose a model that incorporates quantum coherence between synonymous codons, namely, codons encoding the same amino acid. This quantum feature leads to an increase in mutual information compared to classical models. To characterize the resulting communication process, we generalize Birkhoff’s theorem for doubly stochastic matrices, expressing the quantum channel as a convex combination of ten extreme maps, each represented by a sub-permutation matrix. By linking quantum coherence in DNA-to-protein information transfer to channel structure and capacity, this work establishes a theoretical foundation for biologically inspired quantum communication models.

title: On the Feasibility of DRL-Based QUIC Multi-Stream Scheduling.
abstract: The optimization of data transmission and efficient network resource management are key challenges in the evolution of transport protocols, especially in Internet of Things (IoT) environments, characterized by dynamic network conditions and diverse traffic patterns. QUIC, designed to improve both efficiency and security in Internet-based communications, fosters novel packet scheduling schemes. In this context, Machine Learning (ML) techniques, particularly Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), offer the potential to develop schedulers that adapt in real time to varying network conditions, potentially outperforming traditional approaches. This work analyzes the performance of a DRL-based multistream scheduler in QUIC, focusing on its implementation and evaluation under different network conditions. A comparative study with state-of-the-art solutions is conducted, emphasizing fairness and latency metrics, which reflect equality in resource allocation and temporal efficiency in packet delivery. This work not only presents a comparative evaluation but also lays the foundation for future research aimed at optimizing transport protocols, contributing to the development of adaptive networks capable of meeting the growing demands of real-time communication.

title: Lessons Learned from Multi-Vendor O-RAN Open Fronthaul Performance Testing: Scheduler Behavior and TCP Throughput Degradation.
abstract: This paper evaluates commercial multi-vendor 5G Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) deployment performance using standardized O-RAN Test and Integration Focus Group (TIFG) test procedures, testing Open Centralized Unit (O-CU)/Open Distributed Unit (O-DU) equipment from one vendor integrated with Open Radio Unit (O-RU) from another vendor. We document vendor-specific scheduler behavior that deviates from conventional wireless networking assumptions, where fair Radio Conditions (RCs) produce 75% higher Block Error Rate (BLER) than poor RCs due its Throughput (TPUT)-maximizing strategy. Our bidirectional Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) testing reveals 44-64% downlink (DL) TPUT degradation when uplink (UL) Push Rates (PRs) approach theoretical maximums, caused by TCP Acknowledgement (ACK) starvation. We establish RC-specific optimization thresholds through empirical analysis: 210 Mbps for excellent RCs and 120 Mbps for good RCs, achieving 38-55% aggregate TPUT improvements. We provide a methodology that combines 3GPP-defined calculations with O-RAN TIFG standardized testing, offering network operators with vendor-agnostic optimization guidance for TCP performance in multi-vendor O-RAN deployments.

title: Denoising Diffusion Decoding with U-Shaped Error Correction Code Transformers.
abstract: Recent neural decoders substantially improve error correction for short block codes but remain computationally intensive and lack adaptive refinement. This work introduces enhanced U-shaped transformer architectures with two key innovations: (i) double-masked attention from complementary parity-check matrices for improved structural diversity, and (ii) cross-attention message-passing that bridges neural and classical decoding principles. To enable adaptive iterative refinement, we extend these single-shot U-shaped decoders into the denoising diffusion paradigm, where channel corruption is modeled as a forward diffusion process and iteratively reversed based on continuous soft syndrome conditioning. Our key finding demonstrates that U-shaped backbones provide disproportionately larger performance gains under diffusion compared to shallow or deep alternatives, nearly matching deep architectures while utilizing half the parameters. Extensive experiments on LDPC(49,24) and Polar(64,32) codes show that the proposed diffusion-enhanced U-shaped transformers achieve state-of-the-art bit-error-rate performance while achieving superior computational efficiency.

title: Energy-Efficient Dynamic Spectrum Allocation for Massive THz IoT Networks Using Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm.
abstract: The exponential growth of IoT devices in 6G networks poses unprecedented challenges for spectrum allocation in energy-constrained THz communications. We present the first application of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) to energy-efficient spectrum allocation in massive THz IoT networks. Our approach formulates the multi-objective optimization problem as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem, jointly optimizing spectrum assignment, interference mitigation, and energy consumption. Through comprehensive evaluation with up to 36 qubits (representing 9 IoT devices across 4 THz bands), QAOA demonstrates consistent improvements of 7.1-18.9% over classical methods, including greedy allocation, genetic algorithms, and simulated annealing. Statistical validation with 95% confidence intervals confirms quantum advantage across all performance metrics. The favorable scaling behavior and 15.3% average energy reduction establish QAOA as a viable solution for next-generation 6G networks, positioning quantum computing as an essential enabler for massive IoT deployments.

title: Federated Meta-Learning for Ultra-Fast Resource Allocation in Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO 6G Networks.
abstract: Ultra-dense cell-free massive MIMO networks demand resource allocation methods capable of rapid adaptation while maintaining scalability across hundreds of coordinated access points. Traditional centralized approaches face prohibitive computational complexity, while distributed methods lack coordination for optimal performance. This paper introduces a federated meta-learning framework that enables distributed access points to collaboratively learn resource allocation strategies while achieving sub-minute adaptation to dynamic network conditions. The framework combines federated learning for scalable distributed training with meta-learning for rapid few-shot adaptation using only 58 samples. Comprehensive evaluation across varying network densities up to 280 APs/km2demonstrates 87% faster convergence, 94% reduction in adaptation time (38 seconds vs. 10+ hours), and 23% sum rate improvement over state-of-the-art methods while maintaining linear computational complexity.

title: Secure LLM Deployment for IoT-based Agricultural Decision Support with Private Blockchain and E2EE.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) in decision support systems have emerged in industry applications due to the intelligent guidance they provide to user inquiries. Agriculture benefits from integrating LLMs with the Internet of Things (IoT) networks by providing farmers with information on modern farming practices and technologies. However, it also presents security and privacy concerns with its data. This work proposes a platform to address these issues using private blockchain technology and End-to-End Encryption (E2EE) design. It determines the most efficient blockchain and encryption configuration for the platform. The result is a secure platform for deploying LLMs in IoT-based agricultural decision support systems.

title: Physics-Informed Score-Based Diffusion Model for Bio-Nano Communication Channels.
abstract: Probabilistic diffusion models effectively capture complex, multimodal stochastic processes in communications, signal restoration, and physics-informed flow modeling. Bio-nano communication channels remain underexplored despite their stochastic diffusion–advection–reaction dynamics and discrete ligand–receptor interactions, which hinder analytical characterization and simulation. This work introduces a physics-informed probabilistic diffusion framework that learns the conditional distribution of receptor counts given molecular releases and environmental parameters. By combining score-based generative modeling, variance stabilized residualization, and transformer-based conditioning on physical priors, the approach represents both deterministic transport behavior and stochastic fluctuations across diverse channel conditions. The framework enables efficient reconstruction of temporal receptor dynamics without directly solving the governing PDEs. Experiments on synthetic microfluidic datasets show close agreement with numerical simulations in peak amplitude, timing, and cross-correlation structure, which establishes a scalable and interpretable foundation for data driven bio-nano communication system design.

title: Sparse RIS-Assisted Indoor Localization via Offline Environment Shaping and GA-Based Optimization.
abstract: We present a practical RIS-assisted indoor localization framework that shapes the Received Signal Strength (RSS) landscape to improve RSS-fingerprinting accuracy. Unlike user-coupled approaches that reconfigure the RIS per user or query, our method is environment-driven and computed offline, remaining fixed during operation. The design activates only a sparse subset of RIS elements and then optimizes their coefficients to minimize a positioning-loss surrogate. We study three optimizers: (i) a global Genetic Algorithm (GA), (ii) a hybrid GA followed by Sequential Quadratic Programming (GA– SQP), and (iii) a discrete, permutation-based GA that exploits the even-spaced structure of favorable RSS assignments. Simulations show consistent gains over baseline fingerprinting (no RIS) and random RIS settings, with strong robustness to noise. In moderate noise, over 90% of estimates fall within 1 m using the discrete GA, while using substantially fewer active RIS elements than a fully-populated surface.

title: A baseline threat and mitigation model for automotive cybersecurity and privacy.
abstract: This paper investigates the existence and systematic identification of baseline assets, threats, and mitigation measures for automotive cyber-physical systems (CPSs). It introduces the SCAR automotive model, a comprehensive registry integrating 18 high-level asset categories and 124 fine-grained assets across security and privacy domains. Threats are analysed using STRIDE and LINDDUN, while mitigations are grounded in ISO/IEC 27002:2022 and GDPR, ensuring regulatory alignment. The SCAR automotive model provides a well-grounded, scalable, and operationally actionable framework for the engineering of cybersecurity and privacy. It serves as a baseline control framework, bridging threat modelling with compliance. The model is constructed via the SCAR modelling methodology, a domain-agnostic, human–AI (HAI) approach with multi-level refinement, easily adaptable to other automotive sub-domains or other CPS areas such as healthcare and energy.

title: A cGAN Empowered Physical Layer Authentication Against Malicious RIS Attacks.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) have emerged as a transformative technology for next-generation wireless networks, offering unprecedented control over radio propagation environments. However, their passive nature and ease of deployment introduces security vulnerabilities that remain largely unexplored. This paper investigates a spoofing attack where a malicious RIS strategically manipulates its reflection coefficients to impersonate a legitimate RIS, thereby deceiving the base station (BS) and gaining unauthorized network access. To counter this threat, we propose a novel authentication framework that formulates the detection problem as a data-driven binary classification task, leveraging conditional generative adversarial networks (cGAN). The framework employs a U-Net-based generator to synthesize realistic attack scenarios during training, while the discriminator serves as a lightweight authenticator enabling robust authentication without requiring apriori knowledge of attacker strategies. Through extensive simulations across diverse attack scenarios, including co-located and correlated configurations, we demonstrate that the trained discriminator achieves 96.4% detection accuracy against malicious RIS attackers positioned near the BS (co-located) and maintains 86.2% accuracy under correlated attack conditions.

title: End-to-End NOMA with Perfect and Quantized CSI Over Rayleigh Fading Channels.
abstract: An end-to-end autoencoder (AE) framework is developed for downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) over Rayleigh fading channels, which learns interference-aware and channel-adaptive super-constellations. While existing works either assume additive white Gaussian noise channels or treat fading channels without a fully end-to-end learning approach, our framework directly embeds the wireless channel into both training and inference. To account for practical channel state information (CSI), we further incorporate limited feedback via both uniform and Lloyd–Max quantization of channel gains and analyze their impact on AE training and bit error rate (BER) performance. Simulation results show that, with perfect CSI, the proposed AE outperforms the existing analytical NOMA schemes. In addition, Lloyd–Max quantization achieves superior BER performance compared to uniform quantization. These results demonstrate that end-to-end AEs trained directly over Rayleigh fading can effectively learn robust, interference-aware signaling strategies, paving the way for NOMA deployment in fading environments with realistic CSI constraints.

title: Efficient Self-Learning and Model Versioning for AI-native O-RAN Edge.
abstract: The AI-native vision of 6G requires Radio Access Networks to train, deploy, and continuously refine thousands of machine learning (ML) models that drive real-time radio network optimization. Although the Open RAN (O-RAN) architecture provides open interfaces and an intelligent control plane, it leaves the life-cycle management of these models unspecified. Consequently, operators still rely on ad-hoc, manual update practices that can neither scale across the heterogeneous, multilayer stack of Cell-Site, Edge-, Regional-, and Central-Cloud domains, nor across the three O-RAN control loops (real-, near-real-, and non-real-time). We present a self-learning framework that provides an efficient closed-loop version management for an AI-native O-RAN edge. In this framework, training pipelines in the Central/Regional Cloud continuously generate new models, which are cataloged along with their resource footprints, security scores, and accuracy metrics in a shared version repository. An Update Manager consults this repository and applies a self-learning policy to decide when and where each new model version should be promoted into operation. A container orchestrator then performs these decisions across heterogeneous worker nodes, enabling multiple services (rApps, xApps, and dApps) to obtain improved inference with minimal disruption. Simulation results show that an efficient RL-driven decision-making can guarantee quality of service, bounded latencies while balancing model accuracy, system stability, and resilience.

title: Discriminative Siamese Learning for Pilot Spoofing Attack Detection in MIMO Uplink Systems.
abstract: Pilot Spoofing Attacks (PSAs) represent a critical vulnerability in Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) networks. An adversary transmits spoofed pilot signals to disrupt the channel estimation process at the base station, compromising both system performance and data confidentiality. Recent studies have explored deep learning-based detection methods to address this critical problem. However, existing approaches primarily employ conventional Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), which face challenges in generalizing under varying channel conditions, require large labeled datasets, and often fail to detect subtle attacks, particularly when the eavesdropper transmits at low power. In this paper, we propose the first application of Siamese Neural Networks (SNNs) for PSA detection in MIMO uplink systems. Our data-driven approach learns a discriminative embedding space that enables effective differentiation between legitimate and spoofed pilot signals without relying on fixed thresholds or prior channel knowledge. The proposed framework also provides unified detection of both synchronous and asynchronous spoofing attacks. Extensive simulations reveal that our SNN-based framework outperforms state-of-the-art detection techniques, achieving 17% higher accuracy and 2.2 times less inference latency for a base station with 300 antennas and 20 frames per signal, even under low-power PSAs.

title: Quantum-Safe Lattice-Based Authentication and Key Agreement Protocol for Internet of Things.
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices introduces significant security challenges, especially with the advent of quantum computers. This paper proposes a quantum-safe authentication protocol tailored for IoT environments with constrained resources. The protocol leverages lattice based primitives to ensure secure and efficient device authentication. The proposed protocol offers a secure key agreement framework relying on the Module Learning With Errors (MLWE) problem, which resists quantum attacks. It provides resistance against classical and quantum adversaries while minimizing communication and computation overhead. The proposed protocol’s robustness is verified through formal analysis using the Scyther tool. Performance evaluation demonstrates that the protocol has better security features with less computation and communication costs compared to similar protocols.

title: An Automatic Large-scale Tool for X.509v3 Certificate Collection and Analysis.
abstract: Since its introduction in the 1970s, public key cryptography has undergone many changes and updates to meet security, usability, and efficiency. Public-key certificates are important to create trust in the public keys, but they can also be exploited as attack vectors in cyberattacks. To effectively combat the threats associated with the Web Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), it is essential to employ tools or platforms capable of swiftly gathering and thoroughly analyzing large volumes of certificates, including, but not limited to, web domains across defined geographic regions, countries, or pertaining to specific application domains. We introduce DigitalCertiAnalytics, a tool for collecting and analyzing X.509v3 certificates used in the Web PKI. DigitalCertiAnalytics incorporates software tools that may carry out partial analyses, such as Zgrab2 for certificate collection, Zlint for certificate format validation, and SSLyze for certificate chain verification. We validated the proposed tool by examining over 10 million web domains in two lists, containing the most visited web domains in different geographical regions. DigitalCertiAnalytics is accurate, flexible, and fast, making it a useful tool for attack prevention, where early detection of invalid, malformed, or erroneous certificates helps to identify attacks in the early stage.

title: OTFS-IDMA: An Unsourced Multiple Access Scheme for Doubly-Dispersive Channels.
abstract: We present an unsourced multiple access (UMAC) scheme tailored to high-mobility wireless channels. The proposed construction is based on orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation and sparse interleaver division multiple access (IDMA) in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain. The receiver runs a compressive-sensing joint activity-detection and channel estimation process followed by a single-user decoder which harnesses multipath diversity via the maximal-ratio combining (MRC) principle. Numerical results show the potential of DD-based uncoordinated schemes in the presence of double selectivity, while remarking the design tradeoffs and remaining challenges introduced by the proposed design.

title: A Low Complexity Iterative Receiver for OTFS Systems.
abstract: This paper proposes a low-complexity minimum mean square error (MMSE) detection scheme based on the block successive over-relaxation (BSOR) method, which avoids direct channel matrix inversion. By exploiting the circulant and sparse structure of the orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) channel, we employ fast Fourier transform (FFT)-based diagonal block inversion and matrix-vector multiplications to reduce complexity from cubic to near-linear order. Additionally, we introduce an efficient Gram matrix computation and a matched filtering technique using FFTs, and propose a matrix compression scheme that significantly reduces storage from $\mathcal{O}\left( {{M^2}{N^2}} \right){\text{ }}$ to $\mathcal{O}(\alpha MN),$ where α≪M denotes the sparsity level, where M and N are the numbers of delay and Doppler bins, respectively. Simulation results show that the proposed BSOR detector achieves near-MMSE performance with significantly reduced computation complexity.

title: Precoding and Delay Offset Selection Strategies for 3GPP Multi-TRP Coherent Joint Transmission.
abstract: Coherent joint transmission (CJT) from multiple transmission–reception points (TRPs) is regarded by industry as a promising technique for 6G systems, with the potential to improve spectral efficiency and link reliability. However, its performance hinges on the accurate acquisition of channel state information (CSI) across cooperating TRPs. To address this challenge, the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) specified the enhanced Type-II (eType-II) codebook for CJT. The latter enables high-resolution CSI acquisition with a limited increase in feedback compared to single-TRP transmission. This paper provides a detailed study of the codebook design and the reporting modes introduced to accommodate inter-TRP propagation delay differences. It also describes a physical-layer abstraction for precoder selection and analyzes the performance-overhead trade-off. Link-level simulations under 3GPP-compliant conditions demonstrate that multi-TRP CJT achieves notable throughput gains over dynamic point selection, thereby validating the proposed abstraction framework.

title: Energy-Aware and Risk-Averse Multi-Agent Edge AI for Reliable Multi-Interface Wireless Networks.
abstract: AI-aided multi-interface wireless connectivity has shown strong potential for improving the reliability of future IoT networks. However, optimizing multi-interface utilization in dynamic environments while meeting stringent energy constraints remains a major challenge for sustainable Edge AI deployment. To address this trade-off, we propose the Energy-Aware Multi-Agent Risk-Averse Deep Q-Network (EA-MA-RADQN) framework, where each Access Point (AP), equipped by Sub6 GHz/mmWave multi-interface connectivity, optimizes its local risk-averse allocation decisions via limited coordination through a Central Unit (CU). The proposed method is empowered by adaptive pruning that sparsifies the Edge AI models of each AP agent. Numerical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms benchmarks from the multi-objective perspective of communication reliability and Edge AI energy consumption.

title: Mitigating Gradient Inversion Attacks in Federated Learning over Tabular IoT Data.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a cornerstone paradigm for privacy-preserving collaboration across distributed Internet of Things (IoT) environments, enabling multiple devices to jointly train intrusion detection models without exposing local data. Despite these advantages, conventional FL remains susceptible to gradient inversion and reconstruction attacks, which can leak sensitive information from model updates. To address these vulnerabilities, this paper introduces a comprehensive privacy-preserving FL framework that systematically compares Homomorphic Encryption (HE) and Secure Multiparty Computation (SMPC) for securing model aggregation, while integrating user-level Differential Privacy (DP) to bound information leakage. Extensive experiments on tabular IoT traffic datasets, including NSL-KDD, under both near-IID and highly non-IID data distributions, demonstrate that SMPC achieves superior computational efficiency compared to HE, whereas DP, when applied with optimized noise calibration, effectively suppresses feature reconstruction with negligible accuracy degradation.

title: Adaptive Position-Guided Multi-Armed Bandit for Beam Refinement in mmWave RIS.
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) are envisioned as key enablers for future Millimeter Wave (mmWave) networks by providing programmable radio environments with low-cost and energy-efficient beamforming. Fast and accurate beam alignment remains challenging due to the huge training overhead of exhaustive codebook search and the sensitivity of Position Information (PI)-based approaches to localization errors. An adaptive PI-guided multi-level Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) approach is proposed for RIS-assisted mmWave communication. The algorithm refines beam selection by combining PI-based initialization with online MAB learning and hierarchical codebook updates, ensuring robustness against position errors. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves near-optimal SNR and energy efficiency while significantly reducing training overhead. It outperforms conventional PI- and MAB-based baselines and surpasses a dense PI-based sweeping method that uses 450 codewords, achieving similar performance with only 30 codewords. This corresponds to a 15× reduction in beam evaluations. The approach is well aligned with digital twin frameworks for RIS-assisted beam management, where virtual models provide priors and online adaptation enables efficient real-time operation.

title: Post-Decision State-Based Online Learning for Delay-Energy-Aware Flow Allocation in Wireless Systems.
abstract: We develop a structure-aware reinforcement learning (RL) approach for delay- and energy-aware flow allocation in 5G User Plane Functions (UPFs). We consider a dynamic system with K heterogeneous UPFs of varying capacities that handle stochastic arrivals of M flow types, each with distinct rate requirements. We model the system as a Markov decision process (MDP) to capture the stochastic nature of flow arrivals and departures (possibly unknown), as well as the impact of flow allocation in the system. To solve this problem, we propose a post-decision state (PDS) based value iteration algorithm that exploits the underlying structure of the MDP. By separating action-controlled dynamics from exogenous factors, PDS enables faster convergence and efficient adaptive flow allocation, even in the absence of statistical knowledge about exogenous variables. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method converges faster and achieves lower long-term cost than standard Q-learning, highlighting the effectiveness of PDS-based RL for resource allocation in wireless networks.

title: QuantOnion: Quantum assisted Onion Routing for Trusted Data Sharing underlying 6G networks.
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) networks transmit massive traffic over open channels, exposing data to interception that threatens anonymity and confidentiality. Onion routing (OR) addresses these risks by obscuring communication paths and protecting user identities. However, conventional OR frameworks faces the challenge of quantum adversaries. Thus, post-quantum cryptography (PQC) offers quantum-resistant security with improved scalability. Thus, the paper presents a novel framework, QuantOnion that enhances OR key sharing and signing with NIST standardized PQC schemes. The scheme integrates two module lattice (ML) PQC algorithms, namely, the key encapsulation mechanism (KEM) for OR sessions, and the digital signature algorithm (DSA) for message authentication. These algorithms operate over a lightweight blockchain (lightchain) that enforces real-time identity verification and session logging in resource-constrained TOR networks, followed by ethereum smart contracts to enforce tamper-proof policy compliance and access control with the system. The framework is tested for PQC analysis, blockchain network analysis, and computation and communication costs. Our experimental evaluation demonstrated an average improvement of approximately 85-90% in both key generation latency and digital signature operations compared to classical RSA/ECC and traditional DSA schemes while reducing the probability of quantum attacks to negligible levels−6. These results underscore the significant potential of our approach to secure high-volume, low-latency communications in the quantum era.

title: HyperNQ: A Hypergraph Neural Network Decoder for Quantum LDPC Codes.
abstract: Quantum computing requires effective error correction strategies to mitigate noise and decoherence. Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) codes have emerged as a promising solution for scalable Quantum Error Correction (QEC) applications by supporting constant-rate encoding and a sparse parity-check structure. However, decoding QLDPC codes via traditional approaches such as Belief Propagation (BP) suffers from poor convergence in the presence of short cycles. Machine learning techniques like Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) utilize learned message passing over their node features; however, they are restricted to pairwise interactions on Tanner graphs, which limits their ability to capture higher-order correlations. In this work, we propose HyperNQ, the first Hypergraph Neural Network (HGNN)- based QLDPC decoder that captures higher-order stabilizer constraints by utilizing hyperedges-thus enabling highly expressive and compact decoding. We use a two-stage message passing scheme and evaluate the decoder over the pseudo-threshold region. Below the pseudo-threshold mark, HyperNQ improves the Logical Error Rate (LER) up to 84% over BP and 50% over GNN-based strategies, demonstrating enhanced performance over the existing state-of-the-art decoders.

title: AirMIND: Air-Interface Foundation Model in the Delay-Doppler-Angle Domain.
abstract: The success of large foundation models is catalyzing a new paradigm for AI-native 6G network design: wireless foundation models for physical layer design. However, existing approaches often operate on channel state information (CSI) represented in the conventional space-time-frequency domain, where distinct multipath components are superimposed and indistinguishable, preventing the models from learning the underlying channel propagation physics. To address this limitation, we propose AirMIND, an Air-interface foundation Model IN the Delay-Doppler-angle domain. AirMIND transforms CSI into the delay-Doppler-angle domain to explicitly resolve multipath components along physical axes. Building on this, AirMIND is pre-trained from scratch on native wireless modality using a Swin-Transformer-based backbone with frame-structure-aware positional encoding. This architecture aligns local window attention with clustered multipath dependencies and explicitly embeds heterogeneous frame-structure priors. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AirMIND significantly outperforms baselines in channel prediction and estimation tasks, while exhibiting strong generalization across diverse conditions.

title: CRC-Assisted Channel Codes for Integrated Sensing and Communications.
abstract: We propose a novel integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where the base station (BS) passively senses the channel parameters using the information carrying signals from a user. To simultaneously guarantee decoding and sensing performance, the user adopts cyclic redundancy check (CRC)-assisted sparse regression codes (SPARCs) to transmit its information bits. The BS generates an initial coarse channel estimation of the parameters after receiving the pilot signal. Then, a novel iterative decoding and parameter sensing algorithm is proposed, where the correctly decoded codewords indicated by the CRC bits are utilized to improve the sensing and channel estimation performance at the BS. In turn, the improved estimate of the channel parameters lead to a better decoding performance. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed iterative decoding and sensing algorithm, where both the sensing and the communication performance are significantly improved with a few iterations. Extensive ablation studies concerning different channel estimation methods and number of CRC bits are carried out for a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed scheme.

title: Reservoir Computing-Based Detection for Molecular Communications.
abstract: Diffusion-based Molecular Communication (MC) is inherently challenged by severe inter-symbol interference (ISI). This is significantly amplified in mobile scenarios, where the channel impulse response (CIR) becomes time-varying and stochastic. Obtaining accurate Channel State Information (CSI) for traditional model-based detection is intractable in such dynamic environments. While deep learning (DL) offers adaptability, its complexity is unsuitable for resource-constrained micro/nanodevices. This paper proposes a low-complexity Reservoir Computing (RC) based detector. The RC architecture utilizes a fixed, recurrent non-linear reservoir to project the time-varying received signal into a high-dimensional state space. This effectively transforms the complex temporal detection problem into a simple linear classification task, capturing ISI dynamics without explicit channel modeling or complex retraining. Evaluated in a realistic 3D mobile MC simulation environment (Smoldyn), our RC detector significantly outperforms classical detectors and achieves superior performance compared to complex ML methods (LSTM, CNN, MLP) under severe ISI. Importantly, RC achieves this with significantly fewer trainable parameters (e.g., 300 vs. up to 264k for MLP) and ultra-low latency inference (approx. 1 $μ$s per symbol).

title: Digital Twin and AI Driven Multi-Operator Vehicular Networks for Metaverse Applications.
abstract: The emergence of immersive metaverse applications in vehicular environments poses unprecedented challenges for wireless networks due to their stringent quality of service (QoS) requirements, including ultra-high data rates and low latency. Single mobile network operators (MNOs) often struggle to meet these demands, particularly in dynamic vehicular scenarios where network conditions rapidly fluctuate. This paper proposes a novel framework that combines digital twin (DT) technology with multi-agent reinforcement learning to enable intelligent collaboration among multiple MNOs. This collaborative approach optimizes resource allocation, thereby enhancing overall network performance. To support this framework, real-world measurement data from major United Kingdom operators (EE, Vodafone, O2, and Three) are used both to analyze the limitations of individual MNO performance and to construct digital replicas of the network environment. These DTs enable accurate prediction of achievable data rates and support data-driven decision-making. Experimental results demonstrate that collaboration among multiple MNOs is essential for ensuring robust coverage and meeting the demanding QoS requirements of vehicular metaverse applications. These findings highlight the critical role of multi-operator cooperation and artificial intelligence-driven orchestration as foundational components for future 6G networks supporting the metaverse.

title: Dynamic Interference Management for TN-NTN Coexistence in the Upper Mid-Band.
abstract: The coexistence of terrestrial networks (TN) and non-terrestrial networks (NTN) in the frequency range 3 (FR3) upper mid-band presents considerable interference concerns, as dense TN deployments can severely degrade NTN downlink performance. Existing studies rely on interference-nulling beamforming, precoding, or exclusion zones that require accurate channel state information (CSI) and static coordination, making them unsuitable for dynamic NTN scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we develop an optimization framework that jointly controls TN downlink power, uplink power, and antenna downtilt to protect NTN links while preserving terrestrial performance. The resultant non-convex coupling between TN and NTN parameters is addressed by a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)–based reinforcement learning method that develops adaptive power and tilt control strategies. Simulation results demonstrate a reduction up to 8 dB in the median interference-to-noise ratio (INR) while maintaining over 87% TN basestation activity, outperforming conventional baseline methods and validating the feasibility of the proposed strategy for FR3 coexistence.

title: Performance-Driven Strategies for Enhanced Vertical Handover in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks.
abstract: The rapid advancement and proliferation of modern communication technologies have introduced a wide range of protocols, offering a compelling framework for investigating their compatibility and performance. Within this context, this paper presents a comprehensive study on decision-making approaches for Vertical Handover (VHO) in heterogeneous wireless networks. Specifically, we analyze several Multi-Attribute Decision-Making (MADM) methods, namely SAW, WPM, TOPSIS, and FUZZY, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and the criteria required to achieve the Always Best Connected (ABC) paradigm. Furthermore, we examine the integration of optimization techniques, such as hysteresis, threshold margin, and time-to-trigger, with the aforementioned methods, in order to enhance the efficiency and robustness of the VHO procedure in next-generation wireless environments.

title: Optimized Resource Orchestration for LoRa Networks in CS-enabled SHM.
abstract: The growing complexity of infrastructure systems and the demand for sustainable monitoring solutions have positioned Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) and Low-Power Wide Area Networks (LPWANs) as critical enablers for Structural Health Monitoring (SHM). In this work, we propose a centralized optimization framework for LoRa-based IoT systems that jointly tunes the spreading factor, coding rate, and compression factor to balance energy efficiency and data reconstruction quality. Leveraging the principles of Software-Defined Networking (SDN), a centralized controller dynamically adjusts communication parameters based on environmental conditions and application constraints. Using a MATLAB-based simulation platform, we evaluate system performance under AWGN, Rayleigh, and Rician fading channels. Results highlight the trade-offs between energy consumption and signal fidelity, demonstrating the effectiveness of centralized orchestration in adapting to channel variability while minimizing the computational burden on edge nodes. This approach lays the foundation for intelligent, context-aware transmission strategies in scalable and sustainable IoT deployments. Future directions include AI-driven parameter prediction, real-time scheduling, and hardware validation to further enhance the practicality and adaptability of the proposed system.

title: Performance Evaluation of Direct-Detection Mode Vector Receivers in Realistic Data Center Optical Links.
abstract: Mode Vector Modulation (MVM) is a recently proposed multidimensional modulation format that encodes information across spatial and polarization modes simultaneously, providing improved sensitivity over traditional intensity modulation formats such as M-ary Pulse Amplitude Modulation (M-PAM) and over Stokes Vector Modulation (SVM). However, conventional MVM receivers require a number of photodiodes that scales quadratically with the number of modes N, posing significant hardware and cost challenges for short-reach optical systems. To address this limitation, we have previously proposed Mode Vector Direct-Detection (MV-DD) receiver architectures with linear hardware complexity, including an asymmetric optical hybrid receiver that requires only 3N−2 photodiodes. In this paper, we analytically optimize MV-DD receivers for thermal-noise-limited operation, which is critical for cost-sensitive short-haul applications such as intra-data center networks (IDCNs). We achieve this goal by analytically optimizing the power-splitting ratios in conventional, quadratic-complexity MV-DD receivers. Finally, we demonstrate via numerical simulations, for the first time, the feasibility of our proposed reduced-complexity, cost-efficient receiver in the special case of N = 2 (SVM) for realistic 1 km long IDCN links considering the effects of various fiber transmission impairments and different electro-optical noise sources. These findings establish a path toward practical and scalable MVM implementations for next-generation short-reach optical interconnects.

title: Online Active Learning for Adaptive Channel Estimation in Fluid Antenna Systems.
abstract: This paper presents a practical online active learning solution for adaptive channel estimation in fluid antenna systems. We model channel state information (CSI) as a spatiotemporal Gaussian process (GP) and approximate it using a deep dropout neural network (DDNN), transforming the challenge into a deep learning task. By leveraging the expressive power of neural networks, our GP model effectively captures the spatiotemporal characteristics of CSI, thereby reducing the number of ports required for accurate estimation. The DDNN, characterized by its low complexity and ease of training, employs a least-squares loss function based solely on port information and pilot measurements, eliminating the need for true CSI. This facilitates dynamic updates and allows for effective adaptation to environmental changes. Additionally, our solution incorporates a port selection method that maximizes mutual information, focusing on prediction uncertainty to optimize port usage. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed online active learning method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art solutions in CSI estimation accuracy and exhibits robust adaptability in dynamic environments.

title: Channel-Adaptive Post-Quantum Cryptography for Secure and Efficient Non-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs), including satellite systems, are increasingly integrated with 5G/6G to ensure global connectivity. Existing research largely relies on classical cryptography adapted to NTN contexts, but such schemes are vulnerable to quantum-based attacks. Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) offers quantum-safe security, yet its computational and bandwidth overheads challenge resource-limited satellite-IoT networks. This paper introduces Channel-Adaptive Post-uantum NTN Security (CA-PQNTN), an adaptive, channel-aware PQC framework that dynamically tunes cryptographic parameters based on link quality and data sensitivity. A detailed system model combining PQC agility with energy consumption analysis is developed for satellite-IoT environments. Simulation results show that CA-PQNTN improves packet delivery rate by approximately 11.5%, reduces energy consumption by 24.9%, and lowers bandwidth overhead by 26.6% compared to static PQC, with only a modest drop in average security (192-bit vs. 256-bit). The framework maintains quantum resilience while intelligently balancing security and efficiency for future NTNs.

title: A Framework for Evaluation and Comparison of 6G Use Cases and Network Solutions.
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) systems are characterized by diverse service scenarios and heterogeneous architectural approaches. Evaluating and comparing use cases, requirements, and solutions objectively remains challenging, as existing methods rely on qualitative assessments or domain-specific KPIs with limited cross-scenario comparability.This paper proposes a methodological framework for objective 6G analysis based on a multidimensional topological space. Use cases, requirements, and solutions are represented as numerical vectors derived from system-level characteristics, enabling quantitative comparison, distance-based analysis, and clustering. The framework supports alignment assessment between research-driven solutions and 3GPP service scenarios documented in TR 22.870.The approach is independent of specific dimension choices and applicable beyond 6G to other communication systems. We present the mathematical foundations, discuss strengths and limitations, and provide an illustrative application example.

title: Experimental Validation of Reflective Near-Field Beamfocusing using a b-bit RIS.
abstract: This paper presents the first experimental validation of reflective near-field beamfocusing using a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). While beamfocusing has been theoretically established as a key feature of large-aperture RISs, its practical realization has remained unexplored. We derive new analytical expressions for the array gain achieved with a $b$-bit RIS in near-field line-of-sight scenarios, characterizing both the finite depth and angular width of the focal region. The theoretical results are validated through a series of measurements in an indoor office environment at 28 GHz using a one-bit 1024-element RIS. The experiments confirm that beamfocusing can be dynamically achieved and accurately predicted by the proposed simplified analytical model, despite the presence of hardware imperfections and multipath propagation. These findings demonstrate that near-field beamfocusing is a robust and practically viable feature of RIS-assisted wireless communications.

title: Shannon's sampling series has the highest possible arithmetic complexity.
abstract: Shannon’s sampling series constitutes a fundamental pillar of modern digital communication and signal processing. By establishing a rigorous link between analog and digital representations, it provides the theoretical foundation for modern digitalization. In numerous practically relevant applications, particularly in communication systems, reliable reconstruction of the underlying analog signal from digital samples is required. Despite its central role, the computational complexity of this reconstruction does not appear to have been investigated so far. In this work, we demonstrate that the interpolation values obtained from a computable bounded sequence via Shannon’s sampling series are, in general, noncomputable real numbers. We further show that these values belong to the second layer of the Zheng–Weihrauch hierarchy of real numbers, corresponding to the highest arithmetic complexity that can arise in practical settings. This result directly extends to an analogous statement for the values of bandlimited functions.

title: Wireless Channel Modeling for Machine Learning - A Critical View on Standardized Channel Models.
abstract: Standardized (link-level) channel models such as the 3GPP TDL and CDL models are frequently used to evaluate machine learning (ML)-based physical-layer methods. However, in this work, we argue that a link-level perspective incorporates limiting assumptions, causing unwanted distributional shifts or necessitating impractical online training. An additional drawback is that this perspective leads to (near-)Gaussian channel characteristics. Thus, ML-based models, trained on link-level channel data, do not outperform classical approaches for a variety of physical-layer applications. Particularly, we demonstrate the optimality of simple linear methods for channel compression, estimation, and modeling, revealing the unsuitability of link-level channel models for evaluating ML models. On the upside, adopting a scenario-level perspective offers a solution to this problem and unlocks the relative gains enabled by ML.

title: Multi-Band Integrated Sensing and Communication Channel Measurements in the FR3.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) and the Frequency Range 3 (FR3) (upper mid-band) spectrum are among the key enablers of future wireless systems. ISAC promises new sensing functionalities for networks historically designed for communications, while the FR3 spectrum, approximately from 7 to 24GHz, offers large bandwidths and diverse propagation characteristics that significantly extend deployment possibilities. Motivated by the potential synergy between these two paradigms, this work presents an experimental investigation of a multiband ISAC channel in the FR3 range under realistic conditions. Using the Pi-Radio software-defined radio (SDR) platform and superresolution parameter estimation methods, we design a multiband testbed that measures sensing metrics such as the probability of detection (PD), probability of false alarm (PFA), and localization root mean-squared error (RMSE) across sub-bands at 6.5, 8.75, 10, 15, and 21.7 GHz. To analyze how communication performance reacts to environmental dynamics, we introduce the channel update rate gain (CURG), a new metric that quantifies achievable data-rate gains induced by target-dependent channel variations.

title: Fixed-wing UAV relay optimization for coverage hole recovery.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) fill coverage holes as wireless relays during emergency situations. Fixed-wing UAVs offer longer flight duration and larger coverage in such situations than rotary-wing counterparts. Maximizing the effectiveness of fixed-wing UAV relay systems requires careful tuning of system and flight parameters. This process is challenging because factors including flight trajectory, timeshare, and user scheduling are not easily optimized. In this paper, we propose an optimization for UAV-based wireless relaying networks based on a setup which is applicable to arbitrary spatial user positions. In the setup, a fixed-wing UAV flies over a circular trajectory and relays data from ground users in a coverage hole to a distant base station (BS). Our optimization iteratively maximizes the average achievable spectral efficiency (SE) for the UAV trajectory, user scheduling, and relay timeshare. The simulation results show that our optimization is effective for varying user distributions and that it performs especially well on distributions with a high standard deviation.

title: Secrecy-Driven Beamforming for Multi-User Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: This paper proposes a secure integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) framework for multi-user systems with multiple communication users (CUs) and adversarial targets, where the design problem is formulated to maximize secrecy rate under joint sensing and communication constraints. An efficient solution is presented based on an accelerated fractional programming (FP) method using a non-homogeneous complex quadratic transform (QT), which decomposes the problem into tractable subproblems for beamforming and artificial noise (AN) optimization. Unlike conventional artificial noise strategies, the proposed approach also exploits AN to enhance sensing while avoiding interference with legitimate users. Simulation results show significant gains in secrecy rate, communication reliability, and sensing accuracy, confirming the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed framework.

title: Lightweight Preprocessing and Feature Extraction for LoRa RF Fingerprint Identification.
abstract: Deep learning-based radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) achieves strong performance but suffers from high computational demands, limiting its suitability for resource-constrained and real-time scenarios. In this work, we presented a lightweight preprocessing method and machine learning-based framework for LoRa RFFI. In particular, our preprocessing method exploits the instantaneous phase difference of the LoRa signal, enabling fine spectral characterization and revealing residual hardware-dependent patterns. A three-stage framework involves feature extraction training, enrollment and authentication. The feature extraction training is machine learning-based and achieved by extremely randomized trees and linear discriminant analysis. The enrollment is done by distribution matching and the authentication is performed by calculating their probability density. We carried out extensive evaluation using a public LoRa RFFI dataset and compared with the state-of-the-art (SOTA) deep learning-based approach. Our proposed method achieved a comparable classification accuracy and channel robustness with the SOTA approach. In addition, our method required significantly less computation and memory, resulting in an explicit and efficient model across all evaluated scenarios.

title: GTopOpt: Gradient-Based Topology Optimization for Satellite Constellations.
abstract: The growing number of satellites in Geostationary (GEO) and Low Earth Orbit (LEO) requires efficient network management for dynamic topology configuration. We propose a new satellite network optimization framework that optimizes topology over end-to-end latency, in the context of both propagation delay and hop count. This is normally a computationally intense network optimization problem, attributed to the binary nature of connection values, the dimensionality of the possible solution space, and the need for a globally connected topology. We develop Gradient Topology Optimization (GTopOpt), an end-to-end differentiable system utilizing auxiliary logits and functional constraints, enabling optimization of inter-satellite links (ISLs) with respect to the end-to-end objective. A key feature of our solution is a temperature-based cooling method, allowing initially for relaxed constraints and then tightening them over the course of the gradient descent procedure. Comparison against baselines demonstrates a 60% reduction in weighted number of hops in larger constellations and 30% reduction in end-to-end latency in smaller constellations.

title: Reinforcement Learning-based User Association in Sustainable Terrestrial Non-Terrestrial 6G Networks.
abstract: In sixth generation (6G) networks, efficient resource allocation will be pivotal to the viability of three-dimensional (3D) networks. In this paper, we study the online user association problem in an integrated Terrestrial and Non-Terrestrial (TN-NTN) 6G network, with the objective of maximizing energy efficiency subject to capacity and Quality of Service (QoS) constraints. First, we formulate the problem as a Mixed Integer Linear Program (MILP) that minimizes the total power consumption. We then formulate it as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and propose a low complexity reinforcement-learning solution based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to make user association decisions under the same constraints. Extensive multi-scenario simulations show that the proposed DNN-based policy achieves almost 10 times lower power consumption compared to the State-of-the-Art (SoA), while incurring significantly lower computational complexity than the optimal MILP, in a multi-node network with more than 140 base stations.

title: Computer-aided Characterization of Fundamental Limits of Coded Caching with Linear Coding.
abstract: Inspired by prior work by Tian and by Cao and Xu, this paper presents an efficient computer-aided framework to characterize the fundamental limits of coded caching systems under the constraint of linear coding. The proposed framework considers non-Shannon-type inequalities which are valid for representable polymatroids (and hence for linear codes), and leverages symmetric structure and problem-specific constraints of coded caching to reduce the complexity of the linear program. The derived converse bounds are tighter compared to previous known analytic methods, and prove the optimality of some achievable memory-load tradeoff points under the constraint of linear coding placement and delivery. These results seem to indicate that small, structured demand subsets combined with minimal common information constructions may be sufficient to characterize optimal tradeoffs under linear coding.

title: { farm-twin }: an Open Farm-Scale Digital Twin.
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology has emerged as a critical paradigm for the real-time synchronisation and proactive management of complex cyber-physical systems. This paper explores the design, implementation, and evaluation of a digital twin architecture for precision agriculture, grounded in the practical case of the open-source { farm-twin } project. We demonstrate how continuous data streams from in-field sensors, animals, machinery, and drones, processed via edge-fog computing infrastructure, can create a dynamic virtual model of an agricultural farm. A three-layer architecture, centred on data standardisation, a performant API-driven core, and a service layer, effectively addresses the historical problem of agricultural and livestock data silos. A performance evaluation confirms that the implementation meets the key latency and throughput requirements for near-real-time monitoring and management, providing a solid technical foundation upon which more specialised AI and simulation modules can be integrated, accelerating innovation in data-driven farming.

title: Deep Unfolded Fractional Optimization for Maximizing Robust Throughput in 6G Networks.
abstract: The sixth-generation (6G) of wireless communication networks aims to leverage artificial intelligence tools for efficient and robust network optimization. This is especially the case since traditional optimization methods often face high computational complexity, motivating the use of deep learning (DL)-based optimization frameworks. In this context, this paper considers a multi-antenna base station (BS) serving multiple users simultaneously through transmit beamforming in downlink mode. To account for robustness, this work proposes an uncertainty-injected deep unfolded fractional programming (UIDUFP) framework for weighted sum rate (WSR) maximization under imperfect channel conditions. The proposed method unfolds fractional programming (FP) iterations into trainable neural network layers refined by projected gradient descent (PGD) steps, while robustness is introduced by injecting sampled channel uncertainties during training and optimizing a quantile-based objective. Simulation results show that the proposed UIDUFP achieves higher WSR and improved robustness compared to classical weighted minimum mean square error, FP, and DL baselines, while maintaining low inference time and good scalability. These findings highlight the potential of deep unfolding combined with uncertainty-aware training as a powerful approach for robust optimization in 6G networks.

title: Multi-Node Authentication in IoT Networks Using PUF-Assisted CDMA Modeling.
abstract: A Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) is a hardware-based security primitive that acts as a device fingerprint. We propose and evaluate a multi-node authentication framework that binds PUF challenge–response pairs (CRPs) to code-division multiple access (CDMA) parameters in a star-topology IoT system. Each node uses factory-enrolled CRPs to deterministically select orthogonal spreading codes and PUF-derived code permutations, embedding authentication at the physical layer. We formalize this mapping as a challenge-signal PUF (CS-PUF) to reason about CRP exposure and query budgets. The threat model spans passive eavesdropping, message replay, node impersonation, and bounded-query machine-learning (ML) based modeling with partial CRP leakage. Monte Carlo simulations report bit error rate (BER), false acceptance rate (FAR), and false rejection rate (FRR) versus SNR and multi-user loading and quantify attacker advantage for replay/relay attacks and modeling attacks as a function of CRP leakage and acceptance thresholds. The paper also proposes a set of lightweight defense mechanisms and account for their airtime cost in a TDMA schedule. The validation results show that the proposed PUF-assisted CDMA maintains strong resilience to impersonation across a broad SNR range while exposing clear trade-offs among spreading length, threshold choice, challenge cadence, and PUF similarity that govern system-level security and throughput.

title: Data-Driven Power Consumption Models for Wi-Fi Access Points.
abstract: This paper presents a data-driven methodology for modeling the power consumption of off-the-shelf Wi-Fi access points (APs) under realistic traffic and radio conditions. The approach combines non-intrusive alternating current (AC)-input power measurements with synchronized 802.11 monitor-mode captures, to passively gather traffic statistics and controlled traffic generation. The resulting datasets enable regression models that predict AP power consumption from wireless activity features. A compact feature set capturing device model, configuration parameters, and traffic statistics provides accurate and interpretable predictions. Among the evaluated models, histogram-based gradient boosting delivers the most robust performance when compared to a linear regression baseline model. The proposed framework, datasets, and models offer a reproducible foundation for analyzing and optimizing the energy efficiency of modern Wi-Fi deployments.

title: FeedSign: Robust and Communication-Efficient Federated Fine-tuning of Large Models for Edge AI.
abstract: Federated fine-tuning (FFT) attempts to fine-tune a pre-trained model with private data from distributed clients by exchanging models rather than data under the orchestration of a parameter server (PS). To overcome the bottleneck forged by the growing communication and memory overhead for clients in such systems due to the ever-increasing model sizes, we propose FeedSign, an FFT algorithm in which the upload and download payload is exactly 1 bit per aggregation step. Meanwhile, the memory overhead is squeezed to the amount needed for inference. The reduction is realized by utilizing zeroth-order (ZO) optimizers on large models and shared pseudo-random number generators (PRNG) across devices to represent the gradient estimates as seed-sign pairs. We conduct a theoretical analysis of FeedSign and demonstrate that it converges at an exponential rate under the widely used Polyak-Łojaciewicz assumption. Moreover, FeedSign is robust against data heterogeneity and Byzantine attacks due to the 1-bit vague updates. We extensively tested FeedSign on models across different structures and sizes (11M to 13B). We found that the proposed method performs better or closely, depending on the scenario, than its ZO and FO counterparts, despite having an order-of-magnitude lower communication overhead, while adding attractive features for edge AI deployment.

title: Robust Resource Allocation for Age-of-Information Outage: A Comparative Study of FBL-Based and Rayleigh-based Policies.
abstract: Timely status updates are critical for real-time wireless networks. Whil conventional research often focuses on minimizing the average Age of Information (AoI), neglecting the stringent reliability requirements regarding AoI outage events, especially in finite blocklength (FBL) regimes. To address this, this work investigates the AoI outage problem in a multi-device system operating under Orthogonal Multiple Access (OMA). We establish a scalable Discrete-Time Markov Chain (DTMC) framework to characterize system dynamics and derive exact expressions for key reliability metrics, including outage probability, mean outage duration, and mean non-outage interval. By comparing static FBL-based and outage-aware Rayleigh-based allocation policies, we reveal a trade-off between performance optimality and system robustness. Our analysis shows that the FBL-based policy yields superior performance but exhibits high sensitivity to allocation deviations, whereas the Rayleigh-based policy offers inherent robustness. Furthermore, we quantify the impact of resource scarcity, demonstrating that the Rayleigh-based policy becomes increasingly superior for maintaining system reliability as the network scale expands.

title: Joint Activity Detection and Channel Estimation for Massive Connectivity: Where Message Passing Meets Score-Based Diffusion Priors.
abstract: Message passing stands as a powerful Bayesian inference framework for joint activity detection and channel estimation (JADCE) in massive connectivity. The existing message-passing algorithms, however, typically rely on some hand-crafted and oversimplified priors for the wireless channel, which can result in significant errors in channel estimation and also degrade the accuracy of activity detection. In this paper, we propose to incorporate a more accurate channel prior learned by score-based generative models (a.k.a. diffusion models) into message passing, so as to push towards the performance limit of JADCE. Specifically, we develop a novel turbo message passing (TMP) framework that models the entire channel matrix as a super node, enabling the seamless integration of score-based generative models as a minimum mean-squared error (MMSE) denoiser. Our approach, termed score-based TMP for JADCE (STMP-JADCE), takes full advantages of the powerful generative prior and, meanwhile, benefits from the fast convergence speed of message passing. Numerical simulations show that STMP-JADCE substantially enhances the activity detection and channel estimation performance over baseline algorithms.

title: Queue-Aware Online Scheduling for Deterministic TSN with Concurrent Transmissions.
abstract: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) provides a foundation for deterministic industrial communication. However, conventional static scheduling and fixed cyclic forwarding lack runtime adaptability for dynamic online mixed-criticality traffic, leading to resource imbalance and hotspots. Rotating Priority Queue (RPQ) enables slot-level fair transmission via queue rotation without complex configuration, yet existing schemes are limited to single-queue service and ignore resource occupancy. In this work, we propose OCT-RPQ, which supports multi-queue concurrent service per slot under queue-capacity constraints and preserves deterministic delay bounds through precise dual-offset control, while adopting an adaptive minimum-resource enqueueing strategy to mitigate congestion and improve runtime load balancing. Simulation results show that OCT-RPQ consistently outperforms state-of-the-art online baselines across diverse traffic conditions and reduces the maximum resource-occupancy disparity by up to 66%.

title: QoS-Constrained Scheduling in Multi-Cell Multi-User MIMO Networks.
abstract: In 5G and beyond networks, efficient scheduling is essential to exploit the gains of multi-user MIMO (MU-MIMO) equipped with carrier aggregation and joint transmission (JT). However, cross-cell and cross-carrier scheduling under QoS constraints is challenging due to the strong coupling across users, base stations, and carriers. In this work, we address this problem in multi-cell MU-MIMO networks to maximize system throughput for both JT and non-JT users under rate constraints. The optimization is highly complex as scheduling variables and beamforming (BF) vectors are intertwined. To tackle it, we propose an approximate but tractable surrogate by leveraging the eigen-based zero-forcing BF and massive MIMO asymptotics. The reformulated problem has a separable structure and is amenable to efficient solutions by a penalty-based block coordinate descent method. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheduler not only meets the QoS requirements well but also achieves remarkable throughput gains over existing schemes.

title: An Efficient Multi-Action Recognition with Feature Selection Using WiFi Channel State Information.
abstract: This work presents a comprehensive study on WiFi-based human action and gesture recognition, with a particular focus on feature selection and the impact of varying sampling rates while preserving privacy by the inherent nature of wireless signals. Unlike camera or infrared based action recognition, we utilize WiFi signal properties that do not rely on physical images and pose no privacy concern. To support this effort, we introduce a new dataset containing a diverse set of both fine-grained and broader actions, collected under controlled conditions using ESP32-based devices. Beyond data collection, we evaluate the effectiveness of pairwise feature selection in improving recognition performance across a range of common baseline models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Transformer-based encoders. By systematically benchmarking these models under different sampling strategies, we provide an in-depth analysis of how feature relevance and temporal resolution influence recognition accuracy.
