Our contributions include (i) a curated dataset encompassing actions and gestures, (ii) a comparative study of feature selection across deep and traditional baselines, and (iii) empirical insights into the role of sampling rates in WiFi-based sensing systems.

title: Hierarchical Model Compression-Driven Task Offloading and UAV Deployment in SAGIN.
abstract: In remote or disaster-stricken areas where terrestrial networks are unavailable, the Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network (SAGIN) serves as a critical infrastructure for AI-driven services. However, it faces key challenges such as computational asymmetry between resource-rich satellites and latency-sensitive ground devices, topological instability from UAV mobility, and incompatibility between AI models and resource-constrained edge nodes. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel distributed hierarchical model compression framework that integrates pruning and knowledge distillation. Specifically, we develop a Graph Neural Network-enhanced Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (GNN-MAPPO) algorithm to address the joint optimization problem of task offloading, model compression and UAV deployment in SAGIN with varying satellite computing capacities, aiming to minimize latency under resource constraints. The proposed hierarchical compression framework further ensures stable and accurate inference under limited computational resources. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed GNN-MAPPO algorithm and hierarchical model compression framework.

title: Emulation Digital Twin Framework: Case Study on NGAP Attacks in 5G Control Plane.
abstract: The signalling protocols at the 5G network control plane may be exploited to perform Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks. The countermeasures developed have to be evaluated in realistic conditions to validate their effectiveness and performance overhead. However, current emulation frameworks offer limited automation, which prevents large-scale and iterative what-if analysis. To address these needs, we present the Emulation Digital Twin (EDT) Framework, which is a modular three-layered architecture. Here, the Emulation Layer utilises open-source tools of Containerlab, UERANSIM, and an extended Open5GS with designed signalling hooks. Then, the Digital Twin (DT) Layer utilises these to form a graph-based representation and employs the attack detection and mitigation modules. Furthermore, the Orchestration Layer automates scenario generation, deployment, traffic/attack injection, and experiment management. We validate EDT, respectively, with a case study on Next Generation Application Protocol (NGAP) DoS attack performed through the N2 interface between a gNB and Access and Mobility Function (AMF). Here, we showcase how the EDT framework reduces experimental configuration complexity by 81% in lines of code with minimal resource consumption increase.

title: Multi-Agent Emergent Communication for Conflict-Free 6G Network Slicing Orchestration: A Testbed Validation.
abstract: This paper presents a cloud-native multi-agent emergent communication-based orchestration framework for conflict-free resource allocation in 6G network slicing. The proposed architecture deploys communication-augmented reinforcement-learning agents as Kubernetes Pods, each representing an independent slice with dedicated namespaces and dynamic CPU quotas managed through a Slice Manager. Agents exchange discrete messages through an Apache Kafka bus and employ an Information Bottleneck (IB) encoder to compress observations into task-relevant latent representations. This combination of inter-agent communication and representation compression enables cooperative decision-making and efficient resource sharing across slices. Experimental validation on a Kubernetes testbed with realistic traffic traces shows that the enhanced model achieves faster convergence, a ×20 reduction in median latency, and 82% fewer inter-slice conflicts compared with a vanilla MA-DRL baseline. The results confirm that emergent communication can produce self-organized signaling protocols that improve coordination efficiency in distributed cloud-edge systems, paving the way for adaptive, AI-driven orchestration mechanisms in future 6G infrastructures.

title: ReCoopSys: A Cross-Platform Reputation-Aware Middleware for Resilient Opportunistic Mobile Networking.
abstract: Mobile applications often face intermittent connectivity, especially in rural, large-scale, or emergency scenarios. Traditional Delay-Tolerant and Opportunistic Networking (Delay-Tolerant Networking (DTN)) approaches demonstrate store-carry-forward feasibility but rarely reach real mobile ecosystems. This paper presents ReCoopSys, a cross-platform middleware implemented as a Flutter SDK that enables reputation-aware opportunistic cooperation among mobile devices. The system integrates adaptive reputation modeling, selective cooperation policies, and lightweight security while abstracting underlying technologies such as Wi-Fi Direct, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), and WebRTC / libp2p. A real-world deployment with 22 smartphones using a tourism application achieved over 90% delivery probability, 2.5s average delay, 80% cooperation rate, and < 5% energy cost per session. Complementary simulations confirmed comparable reliability to Epidemic and Spray-and-Wait routing with substantially reduced overhead. ReCoopSys bridges theoretical DTN research and practical mobile middleware, contributing to resilient and sustainable connectivity for future mobile ecosystems.

title: Helios: Context-, Energy-, and Periodicity-Aware Orchestration for LEO Compute Clouds.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations have evolved from connectivity providers into a global, in-orbit compute cloud, but orchestrating applications in this environment, where servers move at over 27,000 km/h and power is a finite, harvested resource, presents challenges that existing systems do not address. This paper introduces Helios, a physics-aware LEO cloud orchestrator that co-designs the control plane with the realities of satellite operation through three contributions: (1) a task-aware policy framework via a Domain-Specific Language (DSL) that enables differentiated handover decisions based on application requirements; (2) a physics-based energy model that tracks solar power generation, eclipse cycles, and battery state to ensure constellation sustainability; and (3) a warm-caching mechanism that exploits the predictable, periodic nature of satellite orbits to reduce data transfer and latency for application handovers. Trace-driven evaluation shows that Helios achieves low scheduling latency scaling to thousands of satellites, significantly reduces data transfer through warm caching, and maintains safe battery levels with zero emergency shutdowns.

title: EP-based Spatio-Temporal Channel Estimation for Multi-Frame LEO Satellite MIMO-OTFS Systems.
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation is promising for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite systems to combat mobility-induced channel variations. However, existing researches are confined to single-frame, single-antenna architectures, overlooking the spatio-temporal correlations inherent in the equivalent delay-Doppler (DD) domain channel in multi-frame LEO satellite multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-OTFS systems. Therefore, in this paper, we first establish a multi-frame LEO satellite MIMO-OTFS system with transmitter-windowed under fractional Doppler, derive the input-output relationship, and formulate a structured sparse signal recovery problem. Then, we propose an expectation propagation-based spatio-temporal channel estimation algorithm (EP-ST), which employs a spike-and-slab prior embedded in a hierarchical Gaussian process to exploit the spatio-temporal correlations of the channel, while efficiently tackling high-dimensional posterior intractability via the EP framework. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively captures channel characteristics and substantially improves estimation accuracy.

title: NetAoD: An Energy Efficient AoD-based Network for Large-Scale Items Tracking.
abstract: Angle-of-Arrival (AoA) tracking is widely adopted in warehouse and industrial applications because of its simplicity design on the tag side. However, it requires complex ceiling-deployed locators with wired power and data connections, leading to high installation and maintenance costs, especially at scale. Angle-of-Departure (AoD) approach shifts complexity to mobile tags, which simplifies the infrastructure and reduces its cost. But AoD’s high tag power consumption of continuous listening limits its industrial adoption. This paper presents NETAOD, an energy-efficient AoD-based network for large-scale tracking. To mitigate the tag energy burden, NETAOD establishes a synchronized network between locators and tags. By leveraging scheduled direction-finding packets, tags optimize radio usage and duty cycling. This design preserves locator simplicity for portability while enabling system scalability. Experimental results show that with a 0.5-second update interval and a 2000 mAh AA battery, the system supports up to 0.6 years of locator operation and 0.8 years for tags, while maintaining an angular estimation error within ±5°.

title: Tensor-Based Joint Subarray Channel Estimation for Terahertz Ultra-Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: Channel estimation in ultra-massive MIMO (UM-MIMO) systems with an array-of-subarrays (AoSA) architecture is challenged by high-dimensional channels and spherical-wave propagation caused by terahertz propagation. To address these issues, we propose a novel tensor-based joint subarray (SA) channel estimation method for UM-MIMO systems. Specifically, we model the received signal of each SA as a third-order low-rank tensor under the hybrid spherical-planar wave model (HSPM). Building on this representation, we develop a joint SA processing scheme that leverages inter-SA spatial correlations. The proposed method applies canonical polyadic decomposition to extract path parameters, resolves permutation ambiguities through path matching, and jointly recovers global channel parameters, thereby enabling accurate reconstruction of the full channel. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms baseline methods in estimation accuracy, paving the way for reliable and scalable terahertz UM-MIMO communications in future 6G networks.

title: A QoE-Aware Asynchronous Coded Caching Approach with Economic Incentive.
abstract: Coded caching, which enables coded-multicast transmission, is an emerging technology to reduce the traffic load for content delivery systems. However, in practice, the asynchronous nature of user requests poses significant challenges. To address this, existing work proposes delivery waiting-based asynchronous coded caching (DWACC), which allows delayed delivery. While DWACC can alleviate the traffic load, the introduction of the delivery delay (DD) degrades the quality of experience (QoE) of users. To overcome this trade-off, the economic incentive (i.e., preferential service price) is introduced to improve the QoE of users in this paper. Inspired by the economic incentive (i.e. preferential service price of users), a joint DD and price aware QoE model (JDP-QoE) is proposed in this paper. To balance the profit of the base station (BS) (i.e., operator benefit) and the JDP-QoE, an optimization problem for economic incentive-based ACC (EIACC) is formulated, aiming to maximize the profit with the JDP-QoE constraint. To solve EIACC, the DD candidates satisfying the JDP-QoE constraint are first obtained via threshold based DD candidate set formulation (T-DCSF), then a dynamic programming (DP) based DD candidate optimization (DP-DCO) algorithm is proposed to obtain the optimal DD candidate. Simulations are carried out to evaluate the performance of the proposed EIACC. It is shown that EIACC can improve the profit by 24.6% and 40.6% on average, compared to delivery waiting-based ACC (DWACC) and uncoded caching, respectively. Moreover, EIACC can increase the number of satisfied users by 20.7% compared to DWACC.

title: Deception Against Reactive Jammer: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Anti-Jamming.
abstract: Reactive jamming is a stealthy, highly disruptive threat in wireless networks that evades simple detection by remaining dormant until legitimate transmissions occur. Deception-based anti-jamming strategies can induce premature jammer activation by transmitting deceptive signals. However, existing work has largely overlooked the design of the transmitting window of deception signals, resulting in the waste of channel resources or the failure of deception. To address this gap, we propose a dynamic deception-based anti-jamming scheme, modeling the interaction as a two-phase Markov Decision Process (MDP). Our approach leverages a Deep Q-Network (DQN) to intelligently and adaptively determine the optimal deception window length, then observes the reaction from the jammer to dynamically select the transmission mode, maximizing channel capacity. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with fixed-window strategies, the proposed DQN-based scheme achieves significantly improved anti-jamming performance.

title: SALT-V: Lightweight Authentication for 5G V2X Broadcasting.
abstract: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication faces a critical authentication dilemma: traditional public-key schemes like ECDSA provide strong security but impose 2 ms verification delays unsuitable for collision avoidance, while symmetric approaches like TESLA achieve microsecond-level efficiency at the cost of 20-100 ms key disclosure latency. Neither meets 5G New Radio (NR)-V2X's stringent requirements for both immediate authentication and computational efficiency. This paper presents SALT-V, a novel hybrid authentication framework that reconciles this fundamental trade-off through intelligent protocol stratification. SALT-V employs ECDSA signatures for 10% of traffic (BOOT frames) to establish sender trust, then leverages this trust anchor to authenticate 90% of messages (DATA frames) using lightweight GMAC operations. The core innovation - an Ephemeral Session Tag (EST) whitelist mechanism - enables 95% of messages to achieve immediate verification without waiting for key disclosure, while Bloom filter integration provides O(1) revocation checking in 1 us. Comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that SALT-V achieves 0.035 ms average computation time (57x faster than pure ECDSA), 1 ms end-to-end latency, 41-byte overhead, and linear scalability to 2000 vehicles, making it the first practical solution to satisfy all safety-critical requirements for real-time V2X deployment.

title: NN-Memory: Neural Network Defined Modulator for Modulation with Memory.
abstract: Modulation with memory is a key component of Internet of Things (IoT) communication technologies such as WiFi and Sigfox, enabling reliable data transmission for smart industry, smart homes, and other applications. However, existing modulators with memory rely on platform-specific hardware components, leading to limited extensibility and high adaptation costs when supporting diverse modulation variants. This paper presents NN-Memory, an innovative neural network–defined modulator that can generate signals and their variants for key modulation-with-memory techniques such as DPSK and CPM. NN-Memory realizes the modulation process using basic neural network components with tailored weights, via a Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN)-based memory network to capture inter-symbol temporal dependencies inherent in modulation with memory. Evaluations show that NN-Memory achieves packet reception rates (PRR) exceeding 98% in outdoor and 95% in indoor environments, matching the performance of conventional modulators. Notably, it also provides a 5× speedup in packet generation, reducing processing time to 6 µs per packet.

title: Dynamic Mask Enhanced Intelligent Multi-UAV Deployment for Urban Vehicular Networks.
abstract: Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) play a crucial role in realizing vehicle-road collaboration and intelligent transportation. However, urban VANETs often face challenges such as frequent link disconnections and subnet fragmentation, which hinder reliable connectivity. To address these issues, we dynamically deploy multiple Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) as communication relays to enhance VANET. A novel Score based Dynamic Action Mask enhanced QMIX algorithm (Q-SDAM) is proposed for multi-UAV deployment, which maximizes vehicle connectivity while minimizing multi-UAV energy consumption. Specifically, we design a score-based dynamic action mask mechanism to guide UAV agents in exploring large action spaces, accelerate the learning process and enhance optimization performance. The practicality of Q-SDAM is validated using real-world datasets. We show that Q-SDAM improves connectivity by 18.2% while reducing energy consumption by 66.6% compared with existing algorithms.

title: Generative Learning-Enabled Delay Distribution Prediction and Delay-Bounded User Scheduling.
abstract: Satisfying stringent delay requirements while sustaining acceptable throughput remains a critical challenge for wireless communication systems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a generative learning–enabled delay–bounded scheduling (GLDBS) framework that integrates a conditional variational autoencoder–generalized pareto distribution (CVAE–GPD) model with parameterized resource scheduling. The CVAE–GPD component captures both the main and tail behaviors of packet delay distributions, enabling precise characterization of stochastic delay dynamics. The predicted statistical parameters are subsequently incorporated into a reinforcement learning–based scheduler that adaptively adjusts interpretable control parameters for proactive and risk–aware resource allocation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GLDBS framework effectively reduces delay violation probability while maintaining system throughput, offering a promising solution for wireless services.

title: Values, Acceptance, and 6G: Expanding the Social Sustainability Agenda.
abstract: Social sustainability in 6G discourse is operationalized predominantly through two components: trustworthiness and digital inclusion. This framing, while valuable, overlooks dimensions that acceptance analysis reveals as critical – including mental and physical health and wellbeing, cultural identity and diversity, intergenerational justice, procedural fairness, autonomy, and the right to disconnect. This paper addresses the resulting gap by presenting the Social Acceptance of Technology (SAT) methodology as one approach for systematically identifying the values and legitimacy conditions society may require during 6G development and before its deployment. SAT distinguishes between technologies users can opt out of, and infrastructures that affect everyone regardless of engagement, enabling diagnosis of legitimacy conditions that technical specifications alone cannot capture. The paper proposes how SAT could connect acceptance analysis to human-centric design practice, using e-health within the SUSTAIN-6G project as an indicative vertical to illustrate the potential translation from diagnosed values to system requirements. The contribution is twofold: reframing social sustainability beyond the trustworthiness-inclusion dyad, and proposing a methodology that could bridge value diagnosis to design best practices.

title: AoA Services in 5G Networks: A Framework for Real-World Implementation and Systematic Testing.
abstract: Accurate positioning is a key enabler for emerging 5G applications. While the standardized Location Management Function (LMF) operates centrally within the core network, its scalability and latency limitations hinder low-latency and fine-grained localization. A practical alternative is to shift positioning intelligence toward the radio access network (RAN), where uplink sounding reference signal (SRS)-based angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation offers a lightweight, network-native solution. In this work, we present the first fully open-source 5G testbed for AoA estimation, enabling systematic and repeatable experimentation under realistic yet controllable channel conditions. The framework integrates the NVIDIA Sionna RT with a Keysight PROPSIM channel emulator and includes a novel phase calibration procedure for USRP N310 devices. Experimental results show sub-degree to few-degree accuracy, validating the feasibility of lightweight, single-anchor, network-native localization within next-generation 5G systems.

title: RIS-assisted Cell-Free MIMO with Dynamic Arrivals and Departures of Users: A Novel Network Stability Approach.
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have recently emerged as a hot research topic, being widely advocated as a candidate technology for next generation wireless communications. These surfaces passively alter the behavior of propagation environments enhancing the performance of wireless communication systems. In this paper, we study the use of RIS in cell-free multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) setting where distributed service antennas, called Access Points (APs), simultaneously serve the users in the network. While most existing works focus on the physical layer improvements RIS carry, less attention has been paid to the impact of dynamic arrivals and departures of the users on the system performance. In such a case, ensuring the stability of the network is the main goal. For that, we propose an optimization framework of the phase shifts, for which we derive a low-complexity solution. We rigorously prove that our low complexity solution stabilizes a guaranteed fraction (higher than 78.5%) of the stability region, and all this stability region can be achieved by the optimal solution of our framework. We also provide numerical results that corroborate the theoretical claims.

title: Adaptive Rank Selection in 6G: Curb Your Greediness.
abstract: In 6G network with extreme MIMO a potential misalignment exists between UE-centric rank selection and the internal link adaptation state of the gNB, specifically the outer loop link adaptation offset. Since this misalignment leads to inefficient resource utilization and degraded quality-of-service, it must be avoided. We present a novel adaptive rank selection algorithm that allows the gNB to dynamically influence the rank selection of the UE to bridge this gap. Our solution incorporates a gNB-configurable rank selection margin, α, which imposes a minimum required throughput gain to justify selecting a higher rank. This margin constrains the greedy rank selection by the UE, and helps aligning it with the link adaptation state of gNB. System-level results confirm that our method outperforms the conventional greedy baseline, boosting XR capacity from 14 to 15 users per cell and delivering consistent UE throughput gains across all measured percentiles for best-effort file transfer traffic.

title: Talkative Power Conversion: Tackling Challenging Channels via Reduced-State Equalization.
abstract: Talkative power conversion (TPC) modulates the switching operations of power electronic converters to enable simultaneous information and power transfer. TPC is often applied as a form of power line communications, but it also supports wireless and optical wireless transmission applications. In this paper, we introduce reduced-state sequence estimation (RSSE) for data retrieval at a TPC receiver. Our approach is based on a discrete-time TPC channel model characterized by coupled difference equations, which allows for a flexible trade-off between error-rate performance and computational as well as sampling complexity. We also derive the matched-filter bound (MFB), which is a lower bound on the error rate. Numerical bit-error rate results demonstrate that RSSE can achieve reliable communication with relatively low computational and sampling complexity for equalization. Notably, an RSSE implementation with only eight states comes within about 1 dB of the MFB.

title: Statistics-Aware Low-Overhead Training and Rate Implications for RIS-Aided Systems.
abstract: Channel estimation is essential for a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided system to configure the RIS and achieve a large beamforming gain. We propose a novel scheme that exploits channel correlation statistics to accurately estimate the instantaneous channel gains between the access point, the RIS elements, and the user with a low training overhead. We propose a two-step optimization scheme to jointly optimize the pilot powers and the RIS configurations during training. We also derive a lower bound on the achievable uplink rate that accounts for the training overhead and the channel estimation errors. This leads us to the optimal number of pilots and the pilot and data power allocation that maximize the rate. Our numerical results demonstrate the higher rate achieved by the proposed scheme over several benchmarking schemes. The results show that fewer pilots than the number of RIS elements and even the effective rank of the channel are sufficient.

title: Graph Neural Network-Based Beamforming and User Association for Mixed Near- and Far-Field RIS-Aided mmWave Systems.
abstract: Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) is expected to enhance spectral efficiency in sixth-generation wireless systems but also introduce near-field effects, where far-field transmissions can interfere with near-field users due to energy spread effects (ESEs). This paper considers a multi-base station (BS) XL-MIMO system with mixed near-and far-field users, aided by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). We propose a graph neural network (GNN)-based approach to jointly optimize user association, BS beamforming, and RIS phase shifts for sum-rate maximization, incorporating correlation-based attention and near-field array alignment enhanced training to mitigate energy spread. Simulations show that the proposed method outperforms model-based and codebook-based benchmarks by effectively handling ESEs.

title: Attack Path Inferences for Quantum-Safe FutureG Network Security.
abstract: The looming advent of "Q-Day" is urging standardization agencies to overhaul current cryptographic methods like RSA and Diffie-Hellman in favor of two quantum-safe solutions: post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and quantum key distribution (QKD). FutureG will utilize a hybrid PQC-QKD approach to safeguard data as well as provide quantum computing as a cloud-based service (QCaaS) in this new era of computing. To address the limited literature on quantum-safe FutureG network penetration testing, this paper presents a systematic cybersecurity analysis framework. First, we extend MulVAL, an open source framework for generating logical attack graphs, to include vulnerabilities related to PQC, QKD, and QCaaS within a FutureG context. Next, using the extended MulVAL, we construct an attack graph for a quantum-safe FutureG network, convert it into a Markov Decision Process (MDP), and implement multiple reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms on the resulting MDP model, including Q-Learning, SARSA, DQN, PPO, A2C, and TRPO. Lastly, we evaluate and compare these RL algorithms based on the rolling average reward and cumulative reward metrics, and analyze the inferred attack paths in relation to the shortest attack trace and the RL algorithms.

title: MetaBeam: Learning-Based Predictive Beam Management for Energy-Efficient LEO Satellite Communications.
abstract: Efficient beam management is crucial for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite-to-vehicle communications, where rapid satellite mobility and energy constraints pose major challenges. Traditional exhaustive beam sweeping, while reliable, incurs excessive overhead and energy consumption. To address this, we propose MetaBeam, a predictive beam selection framework that combines meta-learning-enhanced LSTM with knowledge distillation and hierarchical search. The meta-learned LSTM rapidly adapts to SINR variations, while knowledge distillation compresses it into a lightweight student model suitable for resource-constrained satellites. When predictions fail, hierarchical refinement ensures reliable performance. Simulations confirm that MetaBeam delivers superior accuracy, robustness, and energy efficiency under both zero-shot and few-shot adaptation, consistently outperforming traditional methods in dynamic LEO scenarios.

title: MX-AI: Agentic Observability and Control Platform for Open and AI-RAN.
abstract: Future 6G radio access networks (RANs) will be artificial intelligence (AI)-native: observed, reasoned about, and re-configured by autonomous agents cooperating across the cloud-edge continuum. We introduce MX-AI, the first end-to-end agentic system that (i) instruments a live 5G Open RAN testbed based on OpenAirInterface (OAI) and FlexRIC, (ii) deploys a graph of Large-Language-Model (LLM)-powered agents inside the Service Management & Orchestration (SMO) layer, and (iii) exposes both observability and control functions for 6G RAN resources through natural-language intents. On 150 realistic operational queries, MX-AI attains a mean answer quality of 4.1 / 5.0, and 100 % decision action accuracy, while incurring only 8.8 secs end-to-end latency when backed by GPT-4.1. Latency is reduced to 1.3 secs when utilizing lama3.2:3b-q4 approaching near-real-time loops. Thus, it competes human experts performance, validating its practicality in real settings. We publicly release the agent graph, prompts, and evaluation harness to accelerate open research on AI-native RANs. A live demo is presented here https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CEIya7988Ug&t=285s&abchannel=BubbleRAN.

title: Assessing Privacy Preservation and Utility in Online Vision-Language Models.
abstract: The increasing use of Online Vision Language Models (OVLMs) for processing images has introduced significant privacy risks, as individuals frequently upload images for various utilities, unaware of the potential for privacy violations. Images contain relationships that relate to Personally Identifiable Information (PII), where even seemingly harmless details can indirectly reveal sensitive information through surrounding clues. This paper explores the critical issue of PII disclosure in images uploaded to OVLMs and its implications for user privacy. We investigate how the extraction of contextual relationships from images can lead to direct (explicit) or indirect (implicit) exposure of PII, significantly compromising personal privacy. Furthermore, we propose methods to protect privacy while preserving the intended utility of the images in Vision Language Model (VLM)-based applications. Our evaluation demonstrates the efficacy of these techniques, highlighting the delicate balance between maintaining utility and protecting privacy in online image processing environments.

title: NeuroScaler: Towards Energy-Optimal Autoscaling for Container-Based Services.
abstract: Future networks must meet stringent requirements while operating within tight energy and carbon constraints. Current autoscaling mechanisms remain workload-centric and infrastructure-siloed, and are largely unaware of their environmental impact. We present NeuroScaler, an AI-native, energy-efficient, and carbon-aware orchestrator for green cloud and edge networks. NeuroScaler aggregates multi-tier telemetry, from Power Distribution Units (PDUs) through bare-metal servers to virtualized infrastructure with containers managed by Kubernetes, using distinct energy and computing metrics at each tier. It supports several machine learning pipelines that link load, performance, and power. Within this unified observability layer, a model-predictive control policy optimizes energy use while meeting service-level objectives. In a real testbed with production-grade servers supporting real services, NeuroScaler reduces energy consumption by 34.68% compared to the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) while maintaining target latency.

title: Optimal Beam Shape for Resilient FMF-Coupled FSO over Impaired Free-Space Channels.
abstract: Considering the high flexibility of free-space transmission combined with the compatibility of mature fiber-optic devices, fiber-coupled free-space optical (FSO) systems are a promising solution for next-generation communications. Moreover, few-mode fiber (FMF) incorporated with spatial mode multiplexing (SMM) and diversity (SMD) can enhance spectral efficiency and robustness, but atmospheric turbulence introduces modal power degradation and inter-modal crosstalk that substantially limit performance. To address this challenge, we present an end-to-end theoretical framework for FMF-coupled FSO links that jointly accounts for turbulent propagation and fiber coupling. Furthermore, an eigenmode decomposition method is proposed to design the transmission fields aligned with the channel eigenstructure, enabling the optimal power transfer and interference-free spatial channels. To assess communication performance, multiplexing gain is quantified using aggregated data rate, while diversity gain is characterized by outage probability. Simulation results for terrestrial scenarios confirm the effectiveness of the proposed framework, demonstrating substantial improvements in both data rate and reliability under turbulent conditions.

title: Deep Learning-Optimized RIS-Assisted 5G for Underground Mining: Deployment and Performance Insights.
abstract: Underground mining operations face severe wireless communication challenges due to confined geometries, modal propagation effects, and harsh environmental conditions. This paper presents a comprehensive framework for enhancing underground 5G communications through strategic deployment of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) optimized via deep reinforcement learning (DRL). A new framework using DRL helps to adjust RIS settings, beam directions, and resource distribution all at once, even when there is uncertainty about the Channel State Information (CSI). Our deployment strategy analysis addresses critical challenges including hardware specifications, safety compliance, installation procedures, and maintenance protocols. Extensive simulations demonstrate a 120% improvement in sum rate, a 256% enhancement in energy efficiency, and a 53% reduction in outage probability. The suggested framework has a straightforward calculation process O(N), allowing it to quickly adjust in changing underground settings while keeping communication reliable for people, self-driving vehicles, and sensor networks.

title: Analysis of Joint EMF Exposure and Sensing in Large-scale ISAC Network.
abstract: The densification of 6G networks for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) demands a comprehensive framework to jointly evaluate sensing performance and electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure. In this paper, we introduce a novel analytical model for downlink ISAC. Specifically, we first derive a closed-form expression for the beamforming gain under sensing beam misalignment at a maximal ratio combiner (MRC) receiver. Building on this result, we then characterize both the marginal and joint distributions of the sensing signal-to-interference plus noise ratio (SINR) and the associated EMF exposure. Our numerical results validate the analytical findings and shed light on the fundamental trade-offs inherent in ISAC network design, providing three key insights: (i) there exists an optimal base station (BS) density, approximately λb= 3×10−5BS/m2, that maximizes joint performance, cautioning against uncontrolled densification; (ii) the sensing-communication power allocation provides a flexible control mechanism to navigate the trade-off; and (iii) the advantages of large antenna arrays are highly sensitive to beam alignment, as misalignment losses can offset potential gains and increase EMF exposure. The provided statistical characterizations and design guidelines offer essential tools for the sustainable design of EMF-aware ISAC networks.

title: Real-Time Haptic Communication: A Digital-Twin Approach for Low-Latency Model Prediction.
abstract: Haptic communication has garnered significant attention in recent years due to its potential to enable seamless interaction between human operators and remote actuators, with applications spanning remote surgery, virtual reality, and beyond. However, such systems are inherently challenged by communication delays, which are particularly pronounced over wireless links. Notably, excessive delay can severely degrade the quality of experience (QoE) and may even lead to system instability. In this paper, we propose a paradigm-shifting approach to haptic communication by integrating digital twin (DT), a virtual replica of the physical environment, to effectively compensate the communication delays in the feedforward/feedback loop. The DT models the dynamics of the remote environment using differential equations, with their parameters continuously estimated via a recursive least squares algorithm. Furthermore, to address the time-varying nature of remote environments, we introduce an event-triggered transmission scheme combined with the differential pulse-coded modulation, which enables timely and accurate updates of the master-side DT while significantly reducing communication overhead.

title: Acoustic Attacks against MEMS Gyroscope on UAVs.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed in sectors such as agriculture, security, and disaster management. However, they remain susceptible to acoustic interference targeting onboard sensors. Because such attacks require only off-the-shelf ultrasonic devices and no privileged access, they can be readily deployed, posing a realistic threat to the integrity of onboard inertial sensing. This paper investigates the impact of ultrasonic waves on UAV cybersecurity by characterizing sensor-level vulnerabilities in Micro Electro Mechanical Systems (MEMS) gyroscopes. Through controlled experiments, we analyze the effects of frequency, speaker type, distance, and voltage on UAV’s gyroscope outputs. Our findings indicate that acoustic interference can induce a gyroscopic yaw deviation of up to 122 degrees in 10 minutes, with residual effects persisting beyond the interference period. In particular, ultrasonic speakers have the most pronounced impact, especially in higher-frequency bands, underscoring their disruptive potential. Furthermore, increasing the number of speakers or the voltage levels significantly amplifies the attack, doubling the interference at distances of 2-3 meters and increasing it by 20-fold at higher voltages. Finally, we propose potential defense mechanisms to mitigate these vulnerabilities.

title: Continual Reinforcement Learning-Based Social-Aware Resource Allocation for Uncertain Multi-Modal Virtual-Physical Interaction.
abstract: In this paper, we study a social-aware resource allocation problem for multi-modal virtual-physical interaction systems. In the considered system, multiple users interact with each other in a shared virtual model (e.g., a Metaverse or digital twin) hosted on an edge server deployed at a base station. This social interaction creates complex dynamics, leading to highly uncertain and time-varying user behaviors and requirements for multi-modal feedback (including visual and haptic). This social-driven uncertainty poses a significant challenge for resource allocation at the edge server. Our objective is to maximize the long-term quality of experience (QoE) of all users by jointly optimizing the edge server’s bandwidth and CPU frequency allocations, and multi-modal feedback configurations. To tackle this challenge, leveraging the strong generalization capability of continual reinforcement learning (CRL), we propose a novel CRL-based approach, termed CRL-based social-aware resource allocation approach (CRL-SARA). Simulation results show the effectiveness of CRL-SARA and demonstrate its superiority over the existing schemes.

title: Semantic-Guided Generative AI Models for Overcoming Satellite Uplink Limitations in Video Transmissions.
abstract: Satellite communication systems are pivotal for global connectivity by ensuring information exchange when terrestrial connection fails. Traditional satellite uplink transmission suffers from low data rates (e.g., tens of Kbps) due to limited user terminal (UT) power, thus hindering high-quality and data-intensive video transmission. To tackle this problem, in this paper, we introduce semantic communication, which focuses on transmitting semantic information (SI) rather than conventional bits. It can be further empowered by large-scale generative models (LGMs) with powerful generative priors, enabling diverse perceptually high-quality video recovery. However, the limited uplink condition, where traditional video codec schemes fail, makes the effective SI extraction and reliable transmission non-trivial for videos. Besides, inherent random nature of LGMs brings challenge of uncontrollable hallucinations in high-fidelity video recovery. To address these two issues, we propose a semantic satellite communication system featuring a tailored semantic encoder/decoder for effective and reliable SI extraction-transmission, as well as an on-orbit semantic-guided LGM with rich priors. Specifically, the UT transmitter strategically selects key frames, which are mapped into compact continuous semantic space, and then encoded into redundancy-augmented symbols for reliable transmission. On the satellite, the received key SI acts as an explicit semantic guidance that continually anchors the LGM’s generation space toward the target sub-space, thus suppressing generative hallucinations while preserving its creative generation. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperforms the state-of-the-art ones in terms of video quality and transmission efficiency in case of low uplink rate.

title: Trident: Structural-Temporal-Semantic Fusion via GAT-Transformer for Multi-Stage Attack Detection.
abstract: Detecting sophisticated, multi-stage attacks from the massive volume of low-level alerts generated by Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) is a critical security challenge. However, existing methods fail to capture the structural, temporal, and semantic information of attacks simultaneously, leading to suboptimal detection performance. The core challenge lies in synergizing sequence-based and graph-based approaches to model both structural and temporal information, as well as extracting precise semantic information from cryptic and highly condensed alert signatures. To address these problems, we propose Trident, a unified framework that improves comprehensive attack detection by fusing structural, temporal, and semantic information. First, Trident models the structure of attacks by constructing an alert correlation graph and learns node representations using a Graph Attention Network (GAT), which allows each node to gain a global perspective of its position within the entire attack scenario. Second, a novel time-aware pooling mechanism and a Transformer encoder are used to learn a comprehensive vector representation for each attack scenario. This captures the rhythm and long-term evolutionary patterns of attacks. Third, by extracting the semantics of alerts using a pretrained Sentence-BERT (S-BERT), Trident is able to understand the similarities and differences between various alerts. Experiments on a diverse dataset of multi-stage attacks demonstrate that Trident reaches an F1-score of 94.5%, outperforming the leading baseline by 5.7%.

title: Toward LED Fingerprinting in IEEE 802.15.7 VLC via GAF-Attention Spectral Learning.
abstract: With the rapid development of secure and context- aware wireless services, device fingerprinting has become a key technique for physical-layer authentication. It has been extensively explored in RF systems such as Wi-Fi, LoRa, Zigbee, and Bluetooth, but remains largely underdeveloped in visible light communication (VLC), despite its growing prominence as a 6G candidate technology. This work presents a robust fingerprinting method for LED transmitters under IEEE 802.15.7 signaling, addressing the practical challenge that real-world modulated VLC signals exhibit non-ideal spectral properties, rendering traditional circuit-based identification approaches ineffective. We propose a spectral–temporal learning framework that first ap- plies short-time Fourier transform (STFT) to extract narrowband energy time series, then encodes them as Gramian Angular Field (1GADF and 2GASF) images to preserve spectral and temporal structure, and finally employs a dual-channel attention-based convolutional neural network for classification. Experiments show the proposed method achieves 92% accuracy using only 1 MHz of spectrum at 30 dB SNR and 200 mA, with only a 3.5% drop compared to full-spectrum analysis. The model maintains high robustness across varying driving currents and modulation formats (OOK, PPM, PWM, 4-PAM), reaching an average accuracy of 93.67%, thus demonstrating strong generalization under practical VLC conditions.

title: Geometric Cross-Layer NOMA-IRSA Random Access Scheme for GEO HTS Networks.
abstract: Grant-free random access is a key enabler for massive connectivity in geostationary earth orbit (GEO) high throughput satellite (HTS) networks. However, the throughput of conventional schemes is fundamentally limited by packet collisions, whereas existing non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) based approaches often overlook the inherent spatial heterogeneity of satellite spot beams. Specifically, the aggressive antenna gain roll-off from the beam center to the edge creates a severe received power disparity, leading to service starvation for edge users. To address this problem, we propose a cross-layer random access scheme, named geometric non-orthogonal multiple access irregular repetition slotted ALOHA (Geo-NOMA-IRSA), which strategically exploits the beam gain disparity to construct a deterministic power hierarchy. A geometric zone partitioning strategy is executed to classify users into dominant and latent tiers, transforming the gain roll-off into a constructive power difference for reliable successive interference cancellation (SIC). Furthermore, to optimize the interference distribution within the latent tier, a chance-constrained power alignment mechanism is formulated, explicitly accounting for inter-beam interference. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms conventional contention resolution diversity slotted ALOHA (CRDSA) and IRSA in terms of throughput and packet loss rate, effectively mitigating the center-edge inequity under heavy traffic loads.

title: Asymmetric Reliability-Enhanced Scheduler Based on Heterogeneous Cellular Networks in Remote Driving Scenarios.
abstract: Remote driving is crucial for the commercialization of autonomous driving. However, technological and network limitations typically compromise communication reliability in remote driving, thereby undermining control safety and precision. We propose an asymmetric reliability-enhanced (ARE) scheduler based on heterogeneous cellular networks. ARE employs targeted algorithms for uplink and downlink transmissions, which are tailored to their respective traffic characteristics and service requirements. For uplink data, we design an adaptive minimum round-trip time (AE minRTT) scheduling algorithm that leverages buffer overflow awareness to avoid congestion during transmission. For downlink data, given the low traffic volume but high importance, the proposed scheduler uses limited bandwidth to reduce packet arrival latency and packet loss. The simulation results demonstrate that compared with baseline algorithms, AE_minRTT increases uplink aggregated bandwidth by 29%-100%. The field experiments further demonstrate a 14-20 point improvement in video multimethod assessment fusion scores for uplink video transmission and a 10%-20% reduction in downlink one-way latency. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheduler in enhancing reliability in remote driving.

title: Stochastic Geometry Analysis of ELAA-Assisted Near-Field Multi-User Communication.
abstract: As wireless systems evolve toward higher frequencies and larger antenna arrays to meet the growing data rate demand, base stations (BSs) equipped with extremely large antenna arrays (ELAAs) increasingly serve users located in the near-field (NF) region. This paper investigates the performance of a network where an ELAA-assisted BS serves multiple users via NF beamfocusing in the polar domain. To characterize the complicated NF antenna pattern and inter-user interference, which jointly vary with angle and distance, we develop a novel stochastic geometry (SG)-based framework and propose a beam pattern approximation, i.e., NF multi-level antenna pattern (NF-MLAP). We then provide computationally efficient expressions for coverage probability (CP) and area spectrum efficiency (ASE). Numerical results validate the approximation accuracy and show how this framework can guide system design by balancing spatial resource reuse in the polar domain and inter-user interference.

title: Concentration Field Sensing-Based Long-Range Underwater Target Detection and Search.
abstract: Long-range underwater target search plays a crucial role in applications such as aircraft black box recovery, marine resource exploration, and environmental monitoring. Inspired by biological olfactory navigation mechanisms, we propose a divide-and-conquer concentration-gradient adaptive trace (DC-CGAT) algorithm for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). DC-CGAT enables efficient underwater target detection by adaptively tracking concentration gradients. Unlike conventional chemical source positioning methods that overlook the spatial heterogeneity of ocean environments, DC-CGAT explicitly incorporates the depth-dependent variation of the ocean diffusion coefficient within the search process. Through a three-dimensional (3D) spatial decomposition strategy, the algorithm transforms the complex 3D search problem into three independent 1D sub-problems. In the vertical direction, a variable step-size strategy accelerates convergence and mitigates oscillations, whereas in the horizontal plane, Gaussian fitting of concentration profiles enhances both positioning accuracy and search efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that DC-CGAT achieves high precision and efficiency, outperforming existing approaches in long-range underwater target detection scenarios.

title: Collaborative Learning and Resource Scheduling for Decentralized Satellite Federated Learning.
abstract: Benefited from advances in satellite communications and onboard edge intelligence, decentralized satellite federated learning (DSFL) empowers Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites to collaboratively train machine learning (ML) models by periodically exchanging updates over inter-satellite links (ISLs). However, the dynamic topology and constrained onboard resources of LEO satellite networks pose significant challenges to the design of an efficient DSFL strategy. To achieve efficient learning under these conditions, a DSFL strategy should jointly decide when and how to conduct local training and model sharing, and how to allocate the associated computational and communication resources. In this paper, we propose a DSFL framework that jointly optimizes collaborative learning and resource scheduling decisions subject to dynamic ISL connectivity, short ISL duration, and limited onboard energy. With aim of maximizing DSFL model accuracy, the problem is formulated as a long-term optimization and later transformed into a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (DEC-POMDP). Then, we develop a Graph Reinforcement Learning (GRL)-based approach, by incorporating a egnraapbh-attention encoder and a dual Q-network architecture to enable efficient distributed decision-making under observation space with varying dimensionality and high-dimensional decision space. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GRL-based strategy achieves superior performance over several benchmarks in terms of model accuracy and energy consumption.

title: Social-aware Redirected Walking for 5G Networks.
abstract: The development of virtual reality (VR) has accelerated due to the global proliferation of 5G networks and the increasing demand for digital interaction and remote work. Immersion is key to VR’s success, but physical space limitations often degrade VR user experience. To explore a large-scale VR environment within limited physical space, a promising virtual locomotion technique, Redirected Walking (RDW), is introduced to prevent users from running into obstacles. However, previous works did not consider the channel quality and social relations of VR users, which significantly undermines the VR experience of group users. VR users with close social relations usually explore VEs together and share similar experiences, which impacts the RDW path planning. In this paper, we make the first attempt to explore the interplay of RDW, channel quality, and social relations in multi-user VR walking. We propose an approximation algorithm to find the RDW paths and the corresponding physical-to-virtual mapping that jointly reduce the number of RDW resets and maintain good channel quality, considering the impact of social relations. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm against baselines in various scenarios.

title: Energy Efficient and Delay Sensitive Cache Assisted ISTN: MADRL Policy of User Association.
abstract: Integrated satellite-terrestrial network (ISTN) has emerged as a promising architecture to provide seamless global coverage and high-quality services, leveraging its unique advantages of extensive coverage and high reliability. However, despite the application of edge caching technology in ISTN alleviates the transmission pressure on the core network backhaul, challenges such as dynamic channel conditions and low cache hit rates still hinder the improvement of communication service quality. We propose a cache assisted ISTN with a three-layer caching architecture aiming to jointly optimize energy efficiency and delay through user association under service capacity constraints in this paper. Since the competitive learning among multiple users, leading to a non-stationary environment, a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) policy of user association is proposed. Specifically, a multi-agent deep Q network (MADQN) based on value decomposition networks (VDN) is designed to enable centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE), effectively mitigating the non-stationarity of the multi-agent environment. Simulation results demonstrate that in energy efficient scenarios, the proposed algorithm achieves improvements of 17.6% and 172% compared to the benchmark algorithms Proximal Policy Optimization(PPO) and DQN, respectively. In delay sensitive scenarios, it reduces delay by 27% and 30% under two different replacement strategies.

title: Beamforming Design for Pinching-Antenna-Based Integrated Sensing and Communications.
abstract: This paper investigates a pinching-antenna (PA)- based integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where the base station (BS) employs a multi-waveguide PA architecture to serve multiple communication users while detecting multiple sensing targets. Based on this, a joint pinching and baseband beamforming optimization problem is formulated to minimize the angle-estimation Cramer–Rao Bound (CRB), subject to a minimum communication rate constraint and PA deployment constraint. To address the resultant highly coupled and non-convex problem, a Riemannian optimization based method is developed. In particular, the original constrained problem is first reformulated into an unconstrained one on the Riemannian product manifold by invoking the lift technique and exact penalty function. A conjugate gradient method is then employed to explore the manifold space for obtaining high-quality solutions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PA based ISAC significantly outperforms the conventional multiple antenna-array-based ISAC.

title: On the Performance of Tri-Hybrid Beamforming Using Pinching Antennas.
abstract: The Pinching-Antenna System (PASS) reconfigures wireless channels through \emph{pinching beamforming}, in which the active positions of pinching antennas (PAs) along dielectric waveguides are optimized to shape the radiation pattern. This article investigates the performance of PASS-enabled tri-hybrid beamforming, where pinched waveguides are integrated with a hybrid digital-analog beamformer to mitigate path loss and enhance spectral efficiency. The channel capacity of the proposed system is characterized by deriving the optimal tri-hybrid beamformer at both the digital and analog domains, as well as the optimal placement of PAs. Closed-form upper and lower bounds of the channel capacity are obtained, leading to a capacity scaling law with respect to the number of PAs. Numerical results verify the tightness of the derived bounds and demonstrate that applying PASS to tri-hybrid beamforming yields a significant performance gain over conventional hybrid beamforming under the same number of radio-frequency chains.

title: LLM-Guided Reinforcement Learning for OTFS-Enabled Low-Altitude Wireless Networks.
abstract: The evolution of delay–Doppler (DD) domain waveforms provides an effective physical-layer solution for low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs), enabling real-time perception, reliable connectivity, and precise target tracking. This paper proposes a large language model (LLM)-guided reinforcement learning framework, called L2Track, for joint trajectory and resource allocation in orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS)-enabled LAWN systems. The proposed L2Track allows the drone to jointly optimize sensing, tracking, and communication tasks, achieving balanced performance across multiple objectives. To achieve that, L2Track leverages reinforcement learning (RL) to perform real-time decision-making by considering tracking accuracy, communication throughput, and sensing reliability. Furthermore, L2Track utilizes an LLM as a semantic planner to refine reward structures and adjust policy learning. This design results in enhanced adaptability and faster convergence in dynamic environments. The proposed L2Track is evaluated on an OTFS-enabled LAWN system and is shown to outperform state-of-the-art methods in tracking precision, data throughput, sensing SNR, and convergence speed.

title: FDD CSI Feedback under Finite Downlink Training: A Rate-Distortion Perspective.
abstract: This paper establishes the theoretical limits of channel state information (CSI) feedback in frequency-division duplexing (FDD) multi-antenna orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems under finite-length training with Gaussian pilots. The user employs minimum mean-squared error (MMSE) channel estimation followed by asymptotically optimal uplink feedback. Specifically, we derive a general rate-distortion function (RDF) of the overall CSI feedback system. We then provide both non-asymptotic bounds and asymptotic scaling for the RDF under arbitrary downlink signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) when the number of training symbols exceeds the antenna dimension. A key observation is that, with sufficient training, the overall RDF converges to the direct RDF corresponding to the case where the user has full access to the downlink CSI. More importantly, we demonstrate that even at a fixed downlink SNR, the convergence rate is inversely proportional to the training length. The simulation results show that our bounds are tight, and under very limited training, the deviation between the overall RDF and the direct RDF is substantial.

title: Joint Precoding and Phase-Shift Optimization for Beyond-Diagonal RIS-Aided ISAC System.
abstract: Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RIS) can realize interconnections among reflecting elements through an impedance network, thereby providing a new approach to improving the performance of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. This paper investigates the optimization problem in BD-RIS-aided multiuser ISAC system, aiming to enable a flexible trade-off design between communication and sensing performance. Specifically, we propose an optimization framework that jointly integrates multiuser interference management and sensing beam gain approximation. By jointly optimizing the precoding vector and the RIS phase-shift matrix, the proposed framework improves the multiuser communication sum rate through the interference management method and enhances the sensing performance through the beam gain approximation method. For the resulting non-convex weighted optimization problem, we employ an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm to decouple it into two subproblems, namely precoding vector optimization and phase-shift matrix optimization, where each step admits a closed-form solution. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed BD-RIS-aided ISAC system can achieve significant improvement in the tradeoffs between communication and sensing performance than the traditional diagonal RIS, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed optimization framework.

title: Functional WMMSE Algorithm for Multiuser Continuous Aperture Array Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we develop a functional weighted minimum mean-squared error (WMMSE) algorithm for downlink beamforming in multiuser continuous aperture array (CAPA) systems where both the base station (BS) and users are equipped with CAPAs. We first present a closed-form expression for the achievable rate in multiuser CAPA systems, based on which the equivalence between maximizing the sum rate and minimizing the sum of weighted mean-squared errors (MSE) is established. We then employ the orthonormal basis expansion to transform the formulated functional optimization problem into a parameter optimization problem. By deriving the first-order optimality conditions of the parameter optimization problem and mapping them back to the functional domain, we obtain the update equations of the proposed functional WMMSE algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms discretization-based baselines in both sum rate and computational complexity.

title: SeaHCL: Hierarchical Collaborative Learning for Large Models in the Internet of Underwater Things.
abstract: The Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT) enables intelligent marine exploration and environmental monitoring but faces severe communication constraints such as low bandwidth and high latency. Existing federated learning (FL) approaches struggle under these conditions because monolithic model structures overload resource-limited underwater sensors, while knowledge distillation–based methods often reduce model accuracy and training efficiency across heterogeneous nodes. To address these issues, this paper proposes SeaHCL, a hierarchical collaborative learning framework for the IoUT. SeaHCL organizes the network into three layers: underwater sensors, surface buoys, and satellites, and performs model partitioning and collaborative training according to resource availability. Within each buoy-centric cluster, split learning enables feature–gradient interactions between sensors and buoys. Satellites further conduct global aggregation across clusters to achieve system-wide consistency. To further optimize the training efficiency, we design a low-complexity algorithm to efficiently select the split layer to minimize training latency. Extensive simulations using a transformer-based vision model demonstrate that compared with the baselines, the SeaHCL reduce at least 16.6% training delay and 10% memory footprint while maintaining competitive accuracy.

title: Theoretical Analysis and Adaptive Optimization of Random Access for VDE-SAT Systems.
abstract: The rapid development of the Maritime Internet of Things (M-IoT) has driven increasing demand for wide-area, reliable connectivity among ships, sensors, and coastal nodes. As a key component of the M-IoT infrastructure, the Very High Frequency Data Exchange Satellite (VDE-SAT) system supports large-scale maritime data exchange but faces severe access congestion under dense IoT traffic. To address this challenge, this paper presents a theoretical analysis and optimization framework for the random access mechanism in VDE-SAT to enhance scalability and adaptability in M-IoT scenarios. We first analyze the collision characteristics under existing VDE-SAT standards and establish a theoretical model to characterize access throughput and delay. To accommodate the highly dynamic and spatially uneven distribution of IoT nodes, a closed-loop adaptive optimization scheme is designed, consisting of four stages: observation, estimation, optimization, and adaptation. A Bayesian estimation algorithm is employed to infer access load, and a Joint Optimization of Dynamic RSI and ACB (JODRA) algorithm is proposed to maximize throughput under latency and resource constraints. Simulation results show that JODRA significantly improves throughput, resource utilization, and delay performance, demonstrating its effectiveness for massive maritime IoT access management.

title: SPSA-Based Successive Beamforming for Mobile Satellite Receivers with Phased Arrays.
abstract: Efficient and low-complexity beamforming design is an important element of satellite communication systems with mobile receivers equipped with phased arrays. In this work, we apply the simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation (SPSA) method with successive sub-array selection for finding the optimal antenna weights that maximize the received signal power at a uniform plane array (UPA). The proposed algorithms are based on iterative gradient approximation by injecting some carefully designed perturbations on the parameters to be estimated. Additionally, the successive sub-array selection technique enhances the performance of SPSA-based algorithms and makes them less sensitive to the initial beam direction. Simulation results show that our proposed algorithms can achieve efficient and reliable performance even when the initial beam direction is not well aligned with the satellite direction.

title: Transformer-Based Rate Prediction for Multi-Band Cellular Handsets.
abstract: Cellular wireless systems are facing a proliferation of frequency bands over a wide spectrum, particularly with the expansion into FR3. These bands must be supported in user equipment (UE) handsets with multiple antennas in a constrained form factor. Rapid variations in channel quality across the bands from motion and hand blockage, limited field-of-view of antennas, and hardware and power-constrained measurement sparsity pose significant challenges to reliable multi-band channel tracking. This paper formulates the problem of predicting achievable rates across multiple antenna arrays and bands with sparse historical measurements. We propose a transformer-based neural architecture that takes asynchronous rate histories as input and outputs per-array rate predictions. Evaluated on ray-traced simulations in a dense urban micro-cellular setting with FR1 and FR3 arrays, our method demonstrates superior performance over baseline predictors, enabling more informed band selection under realistic mobility and hardware constraints.

title: A Fine-Tuned LLMs-Based Text-Driven Predictive Channel Model for 6G Wireless Communications.
abstract: To address link degradation caused by channel aging, channel prediction provides forecasts of future channel state information (CSI). However, traditional artificial intelligence-based methods, constrained by the number of parameters, lack inherent communication knowledge and environmental awareness. Recently, pre-trained large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant multimodal perception, transfer learning, and generalization ability through fine-tuning limited parameters. In this paper, we propose an LLM-based predictive channel model, which jointly processes channel data and textual information. Specifically, we design a channel alignment encoder and a dual-domain fusion (DDFusion) module to capture the relationship of the CSI in the time and frequency domains, a text-driven encoder to embed textual knowledge into the latent space, and a refined module to map the hidden features to the predicted future CSI. Additionally, we design an angular-coherence loss tailored to the angular power spectrum, thereby extracting structural dependencies in the angular domain. Extensive experiments validate that our algorithm outperforms other state-of-the-art models, achieving superior prediction accuracy and cross-scenario generalization.

title: Joint Resource and Trajectory Design for UAV-RIS-assisted Secure Maritime MEC Systems.
abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle-mounted reconfigurable intelligent surface (UAV-RIS) combines the high maneuverability and deployment flexibility of UAVs with the intelligent reconfiguration of the wireless channel environment by RIS. It can substantially increase the communication coverage, security, and energy efficiency of maritime mobile edge computing (MEC) systems, making it critical for building robust maritime communication infrastructure. A UAV-RIS-assisted maritime MEC secure communication scheme is proposed in this paper, threatened by an offshore ground eavesdropper (OES). The system secure computing capacity is maximized by jointly optimizing the RIS phase shift, resource allocation, and UAV trajectory. The formulated optimization problem (OP) is nonconvex in nature, stemming from the coupling among multiple variables. An efficient solution of RIS phase shift is derived through the Dinkelbach method. Additionally, we reformulate OP via the incorporation of auxiliary variables for the other factors, which is addressed through an iterative framework that leverages successive convex approximation (SCA). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly improves secure computing capacity over baseline schemes.

title: Sensing Performance Analysis for Meta-Backscatter Systems: How Much Information Can It Deliver?
abstract: Meta-Backscatter system, which utilizes metamaterial sensing tags for environmental perception (e.g., temperature or humidity), has emerged as a promising solution for battery-free Internet of Things (IoT) applications due to its cost-effective and maintenance-free nature. These tags alter their resonant frequencies in response to environmental changes, enabling wireless transceivers to sense environmental information by analyzing the reflected signal from tags. In this context, evaluating the sensing performance of meta-backscatter systems remains an open problem, as there is currently no unified theoretical framework available. In this paper, we propose an information-theoretic framework based on mutual information (MI) to evaluate the performance limits of meta-backscatter systems. However, the exact computation of MI is intractable due to the nonlinear sensing models and coupled signals from multiple tags, making it difficult to obtain a closed-form expression. To address these challenges, we derive a tractable lower bound by relating MI to the minimum mean square error (MMSE) estimator for the joint estimation of all tags’ resonant frequencies. This bound reveals that MI is inversely related to the determinant of the MMSE error covariance matrix, thus establishing a relationship between information-theoretic limits and practical estimation performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the derived bound closely approximates the delivered information. In the considered case study, the lower bound of MI reaches 93% of the true MI.

title: A Scalable Big Data Framework for Environmental Sensing Using Commercial Microwave Links.
abstract: Modern communication networks generate massive, high-velocity, and heterogeneous data streams, providing significant opportunities for smart city applications and high-resolution weather monitoring. This paper presents an Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) framework that leverages Commercial Microwave Link (CML) data to unify environmental sensing and communication analysis. The framework uses a convolutional frontend for efficient feature extraction and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) backbone for scalable long-sequence modeling, enabling effective big data analytics of complex network streams. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate its high-accuracy and capability to process high-velocity data streams. The study highlights the potential of modern networks to evolve into intelligent, data-driven infrastructures, supporting sustainable urban management through Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques.

title: Tensor-Based Dynamic Channel Estimation for mmWave Movable Antenna MIMO Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic channel estimation algorithm in mmWave movable antenna (MA) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. To achieve highly accurate channel estimation with lower computational complexity, we propose a tensor decomposition based channel estimation algorithm. First, to fully capture the high-dimensional structural information of the MA MIMO channel, the received signal is constructed as a fourth-order tensor. Then, an alternating least squares based tensor decomposition scheme is adopted to extract the factor matrices. Subsequently, the propagation loss, frequency offset, angle-of-arrival/departure, and time delay are obtained based on these factor matrices. Additionally, the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) is derived as a performance evaluation standard, proving that the proposed algorithm nearly approaches this minimum variance bound. Finally, simulation outcomes reveal a notable reduction in the mean square error obtained by the proposed algorithm when compared to the baseline algorithms, confirming its accuracy advantage.

title: Transciphering of Lightweight Symmetric Ciphertexts for Privacy-Preserving Generative AI Inference in Telecom Systems.
abstract: Resource-constrained devices in future telecom systems, including Narrowband IoT (NB-IoT) deployments and personal IoT networks (PINs), typically rely on lightweight symmetric encryption to satisfy strict communication and latency constraints, but ciphertexts produced by such ciphers do not support computation in the encrypted domain. Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computation over encrypted data, yet its computational and communication overhead makes it impractical to deploy at resource-constrained devices in communication-oriented edge–cloud systems, posing a fundamental challenge for deploying PPML in telecom environments. To bridge this gap, we propose a privacy-preserving generative-AI inference framework based on transciphering of lightweight symmetric ciphertexts. Specifically, the framework transforms symmetric ciphertexts into the homomorphic domain at the server by homomorphically evaluating the decryption circuit, enabling non-interactive inference with low uplink overhead. We evaluate the proposed framework through homomorphic evaluation of the lightweight cipher ASCON. Under a standard 128-bit security setting, our implementation achieves an end-to-end latency of 45.3s for homomorphic ASCON translation, providing a 2.9× improvement over an FHEW-like function-bootstrapping baseline under comparable parameters. These results indicate that lightweight-to-FHE ciphertext translation can be made practical for communication-oriented PPML pipelines.

title: Integrated Sensing and Communication with Tri-Hybrid Beamforming Across Electromagnetically Reconfigurable Antennas.
abstract: Beamforming with a sufficient number of antennas is one of the most significant technologies for both Multi-user (MU) Multiple-input Multiple-output (MIMO) communication and MIMO radar sensing in Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems. However, its performance suffers from limited Degrees of Freedom (DoFs) in conventional hybrid beamforming systems. To overcome this, we propose an Electromagnetically Reconfigurable Antenna (ERA)-aided ISAC system, where transmit ERAs dynamically adjust their radiation patterns to enhance system DoFs and improve overall performance. Specifically, we design a tri-hybrid beamforming optimization framework combining digital, analog, and Electromagnetic (EM) beamforming to jointly maximize communication rate and sensing Signal-to-Clutter-plus-Noise Ratio (SCNR). Furthermore, an integrated Fractional Programming (FP) and Manifold Optimization (MO) approach is developed to transform the problem into tractable subproblems with closed-form updates. Simulation results verify that the proposed ERA-ISAC system achieves almost 10 dB Sensing and Communication (S&C) performance gain compared to its conventional hybrid beamforming counterparts with Omnidirectional Antenna (OA).

title: Lightweight Dual-domain U-shaped Convolutional Neural Networks for PUSCH Channel Estimation.
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated strong potential for improving channel estimation (CE) accuracy; however, their high computational complexity poses a challenge for real-world deployment. This paper presents DdUnet, a lightweight dual-domain U-shaped convolutional neural network tailored for CE in the physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH). DdUnet employs a multi-stage U-shaped architecture with PUSCH-specific downsampling and upsampling schemes to reduce computational complexity while enhancing model capacity. For scenarios involving large numbers of resource blocks (RB), a lightweight sparsity-aware CE solution that estimates the channels in the delay domain is proposed to further reduce complexity with minimal performance degradation. Additionally, a mixed RB training strategy is proposed to improve model generalization across varying RB numbers, a common scenario in PUSCH. Extensive evaluations across different signal-to-noise-ratios levels, RB numbers, and channel profiles show that DdUnet consistently outperforms other CNN-based CE solutions in both estimation performance and computational efficiency.

title: Efficient and Robust Federated Learning via Synergistic Aggregation on Heterogeneous Devices.
abstract: Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL) offers a scalable, privacy-preserving framework for training models on massive End Devices (EDs). However, frequent model parameter exchanges cause excessive communication energy consumption on energy-constrained EDs. Premature dropouts of EDs due to battery depletion slow down convergence, degrade model accuracy, and reduce participant diversity, undermining the integrity and robustness of the federated system. Existing methods save device-side communication energy by adjusting the HFL architecture, but fail to achieve a satisfactory trade-off between energy consumption and global model accuracy, a balance crucial for maintaining the long-term device participation and thus the system’s overall integrity. To address this challenge, we propose HFELAG, a synergistic hierarchical federated learning framework that, for the first time, co-designs inter-group device association and intra-group aggregation to enhance system robustness.
