HFELAG introduces a device metric measurement mechanism to capture both communication capabilities and data distribution impacts. Based on these metrics, it implements an elastic grouping strategy on the cloud server, guided by an adaptive weight to navigate the critical trade-off between communication efficiency and model accuracy. This is complemented by an intra-group hierarchical aggregation mechanism on edge servers, designed to fully leverage the optimized groupings for local energy savings. This integrated approach allows HFELAG to achieve dynamic joint optimization between device communication energy consumption and global model accuracy. Extensive experiments show that HFELAG significantly reduces communication energy consumption while improving model accuracy compared to five strong baselines, demonstrating a practical pathway to bolster HFL’s security through energy-aware optimizations.

title: Quantum-Based Broadband Integrated Sensing and Communication with Rydberg Atomic Receiver.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) demands front-ends that natively support coherent data reception and accurate environmental awareness within a single hardware chain. We present a quantum ISAC receiver that replaces the conventional RF antenna–mixer–LNA cascade with a centimeterscale Rydberg-atom vapor cell, enabling quantum-traceable RF-to-optical I/Q downconversion. Using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and Autler–Townes (AT) physics, the receiver provides a phase-accurate baseband suitable for standard coherent communications, while reusing the same front-end for range sensing via pilot-aided stepped tones. A hybrid tuning strategy—coarse laser-controlled state hopping with fine AC-Stark compensation—realizes non-uniform stepped coverage across 2.6–3.6 GHz. A compact prototype demonstrates centimeter-level range sensing (RMSE = 1.06 cm within 1.6–1.9 m) and resolves 15 cm separations in controlled sparse cases, while preserving stable phase tracking required by coherent demodulation. These results indicate a practical pathway to compact, calibration-free ISAC nodes with simplified RF hardware, where communications pilots can be opportunistically reused for accurate sensing.

title: Receiver-Aware Near-Field Wavefront Engineering for sub-Terahertz Wireless Communications.
abstract: Sub-terahertz and terahertz communication systems have brought practical propagation distances into the near field, where conventional far-field beamforming faces performance degradation. Therefore, various alternative electromagnetic wavefronts have been recently studied for near-field (sub-)terahertz communication systems to enhance the link performance. However, when investigating near-field wavefronts, most works to date focus primarily on the transmitter side (what kind of wavefront or beam type can be generated) but ignore entirely or, at best, notably simplify the receiver model (how this new custom wavefront can be received in practice). To address this gap, for the first time in this work, we derive the mathematical formulation of a wavefront optimization model that leverages additional information on the receiver side. Particularly, we show that receiver capabilities, orientations, and aperture sizes provide profound insights into the choice of wavefront to transmit. We formulate a relevant RX-aware performance metric (conjugate received power) and offer a new intuition for wavefront optimization in end-to-end near-field communication systems. Based on these principles, we present novel RX-aware wavefronts, including quadri-beams that achieve on average a 4.5 dB improvement compared to conventional focused beams –– currently presumed optimal for LOS near-field scenarios –– across 1000 randomly simulated LOS environments, which is further validated by preliminary D-band experiments.

title: Distance-Focusing Property of Sparse UPAs in XL-MIMO Systems.
abstract: This work investigates the distance-focusing property in near-field extremely large-scale MIMO (XL-MIMO) systems that employ sparse uniform planar arrays (UPAs). A closed-form expression is derived for the signal beam power along the radial direction. Based on this result, the length of the main lobe is also formulated in closed form, revealing that it decreases as the antenna spacing increases. Furthermore, a distance criterion referred to as the radial resolution distance is introduced, which defines the boundary for determining whether the XL-MIMO array exhibits the distance-focusing property. Numerical results are provided to validate the main findings of this study.

title: Low-Complexity Pilot-Aided Channel Estimation for OTFS Systems Under Doppler Ambiguity.
abstract: This paper addresses the critical challenge of Doppler ambiguity for Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) systems under extremely high mobility. We first derive the OTFS input-output relation in the presence of Doppler ambiguity, revealing distinct phase rotation along the delay dimension. We then develop a computationally eﬃcient two-stage estimator which utilizes phase differences among pilots to uniquely identify Doppler ambiguity before performing channel estimation. The complexity of ambiguity identification is negligible and independent of the grid size for channel estimation, ensuring scalability. We further investigate two pilot placements, Embedded Pilots with Guard Zone and Data-Surrounded Pilots, to analyze the trade-off between interference suppression and spectral eﬃciency. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively eliminates the error floor caused by Doppler ambiguity, achieving bit error rate and normalized mean squared error performances close to that of the case with perfect channel state information and the high-complexity benchmark with significantly reduced computational overhead.

title: Near-Field IRS Deployment for Channel Decorrelation in Sparse MIMO.
abstract: The rank-deficient nature of the far-field cascaded channel fundamentally constrains the performance of intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) assisted multi-user MIMO systems, precluding effective spatial multiplexing. To overcome this limitation, sparse arrays are introduced at the base station (BS) and IRS to create an expanded near-field region. A deterministic deployment criterion is then established, which strategically positions the IRS to leverage spherical wavefront propagation for channel decorrelation. This approach is shown to fundamentally resolve the rank-deficiency issue. Furthermore, a theoretical performance bound is established, proving that for a sufficiently large number of IRS elements, perfect user channel orthogonality is achievable. Numerical results validate the analytical model for channel correlation and confirm the capability of the proposed deployment to engineer nearly orthogonal user channels.

title: Attribute-Based Bilateral Access Control With Privacy Preservation for IIoT.
abstract: Data sharing in the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) faces significant challenges in simultaneously achieving flexible bilateral access control and preserving data privacy. Existing solutions often struggle to balance these aspects, proving particularly deficient in protecting sender privacy while offering limited expressiveness in access policies, which hinders their use in complex scenarios. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a privacy-preserving data sharing scheme with a flexible access structure, called PP-BAC. The scheme utilizes matching encryption (ME) to enable secure policy matching and employs a Linear Secret Sharing Scheme (LSSS) to construct expressive access structures that support complex policies such as AND/OR and threshold operations. Most critically, by leveraging the properties of bilinear pairing, we enhance existing schemes to effectively protect the privacy of data owners(DOs), ensuring sensitive attributes remain hidden during the matching process. This paper formally proves the scheme's security under bilinear pairing hardness assumptions and validates its effectiveness and computational efficiency through experimental evaluations.

title: Near-Field Channel Estimation for mmWave/THz Communications with Extremely Large-Scale UPAs.
abstract: Extremely large antenna arrays (ELAAs) are widely adopted in mmWave/THz communications to compensate for the severe path loss, wherein the channel estimation remains a significant challenge since the Rayleigh distance of ELAAs stretches to tens or even hundreds of meters and the near-field channel model should be considered. Existing polar-domain based methods and block-sparse based methods are originally devised for Uniform Linear Arrays (ULAs) near-field channel estimation. The polar-domain based method can be applied to Uniform Planar Arrays (UPAs), but it behaves plain since it ignores the specific sparsity structure of the UPA near-field channels. Meanwhile, the block-sparse based method cannot be extended to the UPA scenarios directly. To address these issues, we first reformulate the original UPA near-field channel as an outer product of two ULA near-field channels and we construct a modified two-dimensional DFT (2D-DFT) dictionary for it. With the proposed dictionary, we further prove that the UPA near-field channel admits a 2D block-sparse structure. Leveraging this specific sparse structure, we solve the channel estimation problem with the 2D Pattern-Coupled Sparse Bayesian Learning (2D-PCSBL) algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed approach outperforms conventional existing methods while maintaining a comparable computational complexity.

title: Heterogeneous Satellite Mission Scheduling in Large-Scale Constellations With Transformer-Reptile MAPPO Approach.
abstract: The emergence of sixth-generation (6G) communication technology motivates the evolution of satellite networks from simple single-function and independently operated systems toward hierarchical and intelligent cooperative satellite architectures. Such architectures introduce diverse businesses and heterogeneous missions, each imposing unique requirements on network resources and performance metrics. Traditional monolithic learning policies struggle in these heterogeneous environments due to negative transfer between mission-specific objectives. To address this challenge, we reframe satellite mission scheduling as a multitask learning (MTL) problem, naturally capturing the shared structure across different missions. We propose Transformer-Reptile Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (TRMAPPO), integrating Transformer networks for inter-agent relationship modeling and Reptile for rapid policy specialization. Extensive experiments are conducted based on realistic satellite constellations and authentic ground-user datasets. Results demonstrate TRMAPPO significantly improves the success rate and reduces the latency of overall missions compared to state-of-the-art benchmarks, validating its effectiveness for hierarchical satellite cooperative systems.

title: Robust Waveform Design for MIMO ISAC Systems with Transmit and Receive Channel Uncertainty.
abstract: This work addresses robust waveform design for a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system under imperfect radar transmit/receive (Tx/Rx) array manifolds and communication channel state information. A lower bound for radar signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) is derived using a first-order approximation of the perturbed virtual Tx-Rx array manifold. To ensure robust radar detection and guaranteed communication quality of service, the lower bound of the radar SINR is maximized via dual-use transmit waveform optimization, subject to robust per-user communication SINR constraints. Practical considerations, including per-antenna power and peak-to-average power ratio, are incorporated to facilitate hardware implementation. The robust communication SINR constraints are reformulated into tractable forms using an extension of the S-Lemma, and the resulting nonconvex problem is solved via a customized successive convex approximation. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a guaranteed performance tradeoff between sensing and communication in the presence of radar and communication channel uncertainties.

title: LLM-Aided Physical-Layer Authentication for Maritime Wireless Networks.
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL)-based physical (PHY)-layer authentication enables access points to select hypothesistest thresholds on channel fingerprints to safeguard large language model (LLM) inference against spoofing attacks. However, the accuracy decreases as mobile devices performing inference tasks such as ship hull inspection collect multi-modal sensor data from multiple scenes with varying channel fading in maritime wireless networks. In this paper, we propose an LLM-aided PHY-layer authentication scheme for maritime wireless networks, which incorporates the LLM-derived scene categories such as cabin or deck into the RL state formulation to predict the quality of generated channel fingerprints, thereby guiding the policy optimization, i.e., test threshold. The potential risk of a selected policy is evaluated using multiple thresholds for miss detections, with different penalties imposed to mitigate the selection of high-risk policies that degrade authentication accuracy. Simulation results based on a server running the LLaVA-1.5 model with 7 billion parameters for image-text inference across four mobile devices under spoofing attacks show the performance gain in terms of authentication accuracy.

title: A DRL-Empowered Multi-Level Jamming Approach for Secure Semantic Communication.
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) aims to transmit only task-relevant information, thereby improving communication efficiency but also exposing semantic information to potential eavesdropping. In this paper, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-empowered multi-level jamming approach to enhance the security of SemCom systems over MIMO fading wiretap channels. This approach combines semantic layer jamming, achieved by encoding task-irrelevant text, and physical layer jamming, achieved by encoding random Gaussian noise. These two-level jamming signals are superposed with task-relevant semantic information to protect the transmitted semantics from eavesdropping. A deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm is further introduced to dynamically design and optimize the precoding matrices for both task-relevant semantic information and multi-level jamming signals, aiming to enhance the legitimate user’s image reconstruction while degrading the eavesdropper’s performance. To jointly train the SemCom model and the DDPG agent, we propose an alternating optimization strategy where the two modules are updated iteratively. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with both the encryption-based (ESCS) and encoded jammer-based (EJ) benchmarks, our method achieves comparable security while improving the legitimate user’s peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) by up to approximately 0.6 dB.

title: APTMatch: Empowering Dynamic Rule Updating for Learning-based Packet Classification.
abstract: Learning-based packet classification (LPC) methods reduce the memory consumption by preprocessing the ruleset and utilizing lightweight Recursive Model Index (RMI) structures to make inference. However, existing LPC methods do not support high-speed rule updates due to their static structures. In this paper, we propose APTMatch, a dynamic LPC architecture that tames high-speed rule updates. Our core idea is to replace reconstruction with local updates to the original structure. However, we face a trade-off: local updates achieve lower update time but decline the lookup performance, while reconstruction maintains the lookup performance but spends more time. To break the trade-off between update time and lookup performance degradation, we propose a two-step rule update workflow. First, we design an adaptive distribution adjustment strategy to efficiently preprocess the ruleset by making targeted adjustments to those small but crucial scopes of the original structure that are affected by rule updates. Second, we introduce a method to efficiently update the RMI by using the gapped array, maintaining the inference accuracy of the original data while only retraining the new data. The experiment shows that APTMatch improves update speed by 1.7x and reduces average classification latency growth by 77.97% compared to the TupleMerge-assisted LPC method.

title: Cross-Sparsity Driven Multipath Perception: Enhancing Multi-Target Sensing with Structured Bayesian Inference.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a multi-target sensing system in multipath environment, where inter-target scattering generates first-order non-line-of-sight (NLos) paths, whose angles of departure (AoDs) and angles of arrival (AoAs) coincide with the direct-path angles of different targets. To exploit this property, we propose a novel cross sparsity structure under a three-layer hierarchical structured (3LHS) prior model, which leverages the first-order paths to enhance the prior probability of the direct paths and thereby improve the estimation accuracy. In addition, to reduce the high computational complexity of conventional turbo variational Bayesian inference (Turbo-VBI) algorithms for such problems, we develop a structured fast turbo variational Bayesian inference (SF-TVBI) algorithm, which decreases the frequency of posterior updates for the high-dimensional sparse vector and is able to achieve comparable estimation performance with Turbo-VBI but with much lower complexity. Simulation results verify that exploiting the proposed cross sparsity structure enables much higher target angle estimation accuracy, and that the SF-TVBI algorithm achieves favorable estimation performance.

title: Risk-Constrained PPO with Dual-Stream GAT for Cooperative Routing of Air-Underwater Heterogeneous Communication Networks.
abstract: Space–Air–Ground–Sea Integrated Networks (SAGSINs) are crucial for maritime emergency communications by enabling cooperative networking across heterogeneous domains. In such scenarios, cross-domain communication between aerial and underwater platforms most relies on a combination of radio-frequency and acoustic links. However, the extreme physical disparity between aerial radio-frequency and underwater acoustic links imposes intrinsic challenges on intelligent routing, characterized by prohibitive propagation delays, limited energy budgets, and severe channel uncertainty. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Risk-Constrained Proximal Policy Optimization (RC-PPO) algorithm with dual-stream Graph Attention Network (GAT) for cooperative routing of air-underwater heterogeneous communication networks. Specifically, a dual-stream gat is designed to explicitly decouple heterogeneous physical channels and construct modality-aware state representations. Based on this representation, the routing problem is formulated as a constrained Markov decision process, which is solved by a risk-constrained PPO variant. This algorithm integrates Lagrangian relaxation to strictly enforce energy constraints and employs variance-penalized advantage estimation to mitigate routing risks caused by channel uncertainty. The simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly optimizes routing reliability and energy efficiency in highly heterogeneous air-underwater communication networks.

title: Cache-aware Data Sensing Allocation for Personalized Edge Intelligence.
abstract: In personalized edge learning (PEL), data is essentially a form of labor. Nevertheless, existing resource-scarce edge devices tend to cache the data they sense in isolation. This creates data silos that significantly degrade the quality of edge learning models. To address this impasse, we propose a cache-aware collaborative federated system, where data sensing allocation is optimized based on both local learning requirements and scenario-specific sharing feedback. Specifically, we establish a unified system reward model that explicitly decomposes the overall utility into (i) accuracy gains from local PEL and (ii) data-sharing rewards under two coexisting data sharing paradigms. For the alliance paradigm, we derive an optimal allocation policy by analyzing the properties of sensing allocation rewards. For the reward-feedback paradigm, we further design an asymptotically optimal allocation strategy using the exact penalty method. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithms outperform state-of-the-art approaches.

title: Movable Antenna Enabled Anti-Jamming: A Trust-Region Surrogate Optimization Approach under Unknown Jammers.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a movable antenna (MA) enabled anti-jamming optimization problem, where a legitimate uplink system is exposed to multiple jammers with unknown jamming channels. To enhance the anti-jamming capability of the considered system, an MA array is deployed at the receiver to jointly optimize the antenna positions and the minimum-variance distortionless-response (MVDR) receive beamformer, which aims to maximize the output signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). The main challenge arises from the fact that the interference covariance matrix is unknown and dependent on the antenna positions. To overcome these issues, we propose a surrogate objective by replacing the unknown covariance with the sample covariance evaluated at the current antenna position anchor. Under a two-timescale framework, the surrogate objective is updated once per block (contains multiple snapshots) at the anchor position, while the MVDR beamformer is adapted on a per-snapshot basis. We establish a local bound on the discrepancy between the surrogate and the true objective by leveraging matrix concentration inequalities. Building on this bound, we develop a low-complexity projected trust-region (TR) surrogate optimization (PTRSO) algorithm that maintains the locality of each iteration via TR constraints and enforces feasibility through projection, which is guaranteed to converge to a stationary point near the anchor. Numerical results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed PTRSO algorithm, which consistently achieves higher output SINR than existing baselines.

title: Efficient and Verifiable Data Statistical Analysis via Zero-knowledge Proofs.
abstract: Statistical analysis, which extracts critical insights for evidence-based decision-making, increasingly employs Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) to ensure data confidentiality and process integrity. However, existing ZKP methods suffer from performance bottlenecks, especially when dealing with complex analysis functions. This paper mitigates this limitation by presenting efficient ZKP solutions founded on a novel table lookup approach capable of securely evaluating arbitrary functions. Critically, this approach achieves sublinear communication complexity, a significant improvement over existing alternatives limited to linear complexity. Building upon this core building block, we design new protocols for two critical operations in statistical analysis, i.e., range proof and logistic regression. Our key insight for range proof is a strategic transformation of the verification for an arbitrary target range into a specific, optimized form, thereby maximally leveraging the lookup mechanism. Our logistic regression protocol employs a piecewise polynomial approximation method to simultaneously achieve high accuracy and efficiency. Our protocol outperforms the state-of-the-art work by up to several orders of magnitude in both runtime and communication performance.

title: UAV Mission Planning in Wireless Sensor Networks with Data Freshness and Backhaul Constraints.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology has emerged as an important paradigm for enabling real-time data acquisition in Wireless Sensors Networks (WSNs). Specifically, resource-constrained WSNs operating in urban environments require efficient, scalable, and resilient data collection and offloading mechanisms. However, low-power Wireless Sensors (WSs) often experience non line-of-sight (NLoS) conditions with terrestrial base stations (BSs), leading to unreliable or failed data offloading. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a UAV-assisted WSN architecture, where UAVs act as mobile relays capable of establishing line-of-sight (LoS) links with ground WSs, thereby enabling reliable data aggregation and successful timely offloading while meeting stringent data freshness constraints. An optimization framework is developed to minimize UAV energy consumption while satisfying key constraints, including maintaining high-quality aerial–terrestrial backhaul links for seamless data offloading, and adhering to temporal deadlines for WSs data updates. To address this problem, a reinforcement learning-based algorithm is employed for UAV trajectory optimization, demonstrating superior performance compared to benchmark schemes through extensive simulations. The proposed approach enhances data collection and offloading reliability in dynamic urban environments and offers a scalable solution for heterogeneous WSN deployments within smart city infrastructures.

title: Dyadic-Chaotic Lifting S-Boxes for Enhanced Physical-Layer Security within 6G Networks.
abstract: Sixth-Generation (6G) wireless networks will interconnect billions of resource-constrained devices and time-critical services, where classical, fixed, and heavy cryptography strains latency and energy budgets and struggles against large-scale, pre-computation attacks. Physical-Layer Security (PLS) is therefore pivotal to deliver lightweight, information-theoretic protection, but still requires strong, reconfigurable confusion components that can be diversified per slice, session, or device to blunt large-scale precomputation and side-channel attacks. In order to address the above requirement, we introduce the first-ever chaos-lifted substitution box (S-box) for PLS that couples a $β$-transformation-driven dynamical system with dyadic conditional sampling to generate time-varying, seedable 8-bit permutations on demand. This construction preserves uniformity via ergodicity, yields full 8-bit bijections, and supports on-the-fly diversification across sessions. The resulting S-box attains optimal algebraic degree 7 on every output bit and high average nonlinearity 102.5 (85% of the 8-bit bound), strengthening resistance to algebraic and linear cryptanalysis. Differential and linear profiling report max DDT entry 10 (probability 0.039) and max linear probability 0.648, motivating deployment within a multi-round cipher with a strong diffusion layer, where the security-to-efficiency trade-off is compelling. Our proposed reconfigurable, lightweight S-box directly fulfills key PLS requirements of 6G networks by delivering fast, hardware-amenable confusion components with built-in agility against evolving threats.

title: PhishLumos: An Adaptive Multi-Agent System for Proactive Phishing Campaign Mitigation.
abstract: Phishing attacks are a significant societal threat, disproportionately harming vulnerable populations and eroding trust in essential digital services. Current defenses are often reactive, failing against modern evasive tactics like cloaking that conceal malicious content. To address this, we introduce PhishLumos, an adaptive multi-agent system that proactively mitigates entire attack campaigns. It confronts a core cybersecurity imbalance: attackers can easily scale operations, while defense remains an intensive expert task. Instead of being blocked by evasion, PhishLumos treats it as a critical signal to investigate the underlying infrastructure. Its Large Language Model (LLM)-powered agents uncover shared hosting, certificates, and domain registration patterns. On real-world data, our system identified 100% of campaigns in the median case, over a week before their confirmation by cybersecurity experts. PhishLumos demonstrates a practical shift from reactive URL blocking to proactive campaign mitigation, protecting users before they are harmed and making the digital world safer for all.

title: IFDMA With Low-Complexity Bayesian-Optimal Receiver for High-Mobility Massive Connectivity.
abstract: With the rapid growth of high-mobility communication applications and massive user connectivity, achieving highly reliable and low-complexity multiple access has become a critical challenge. Recently, orthogonal time–frequency space (OTFS) and affine frequency-division multiplexing (AFDM) combined with sparse code multiple access (SCMA) systems have been explored, but their performance is hindered by the lack of efficient detection algorithms and SCMA codebooks that neglect delay–Doppler channel effects. To address these challenges, this paper investigates a novel non-orthogonal interleave frequency-division multiple access (IFDMA) system, where users are efficiently separated by assigning distinct interleaver within individual modulation matrix. Meanwhile, a low-complexity multi-user cross-domain memory approximate message passing (MU-CD-MAMP) detector is proposed. It employs a simple time-domain multi-user memory matched filter to fully exploit the sparsity of time-domain channels, followed by per-user full orthogonalization, cross-domain transformations, and channel decoding. On this basis, MU-CDMAMP fully leverages the right-unitary invariance of each user’s modulation matrix, achieving Bayesian-optimal1detection with extremely low complexity. Numerical results show that, with 5GNR LDPC codes, our proposed IFDMA with MU-CD-MAMP attains a 3 ~ 5 dB bit-error rate performance improvement over existing AFDM-SCMA and OTFS-SCMA schemes.

title: The New Contactless Payment System based on Discovery and Ranging over Ultra-wideband.
abstract: This paper presents NewPay, an Ultra-wideband (UWB) based mobile payment system integrating Samsung Pay and Mastercard’s Digital Secure Remote Payment (DSRP) protocol. The proposed system enables secure, seamless, and contactless transactions through precise UWB ranging and secure channel communication. Implemented on commercial smartphones (i.e., Samsung Galaxy S23+), NewPay achieves an average localization accuracy of 30.34 cm and a transaction latency of 493 ms. Beyond demonstrating feasibility, we discuss deployment cost, scalability, and cross-device calibration for real-world applicability. The results validate the practicality and scalability of NewPay for next-generation contactless payments.

title: HARQ-aided Optical-RIS Communications.
abstract: This paper studies a free-space optical (FSO) link that is assisted by an optical reconfigurable intelligent surface (ORIS), while employing a hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) scheme to enhance the reliability of the overall system. ORIS restores virtual line-of-sight around blockages, while HARQ mitigates turbulence, pointing jitter, and geometric loss via selective retransmissions. We derive a unified statistical model of the transmitter–ORIS–receiver (Tx-ORIS-Rx) end-to-end (e2e) channel and obtain closed-form outage probability (OP) formulas for HARQ with chase combining (HARQ-CC). High-SNR approximations provide valuable insights, including the diversity order for the present scheme. Finally, Monte Carlo simulations for various number of maximum transmissions and weather conditions validate the analysis and demonstrate that only two HARQ rounds achieve substantial performance gains over conventional FSO links.

title: A Synthetic Dataset for Anomaly Detection of RIS-Enabled Jamming Attacks.
abstract: What if a jamming attack could be executed without the need to produce radio signals? How could you detect the attack? Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) are a transformative technology that passively control, or manipulate, radio signals and the channel state through reflection only. Future wireless networks, including sixth-generation (6G) networks, depend upon RIS to improve signal coverage and spectral efficiency by manipulating the channel, but they also enable new security risks, such as passive jamming attacks. In traditional jamming, an attacker actively transmits signals to disrupt a receiver. RIS-based jamming is passive, i.e., the RIS does not transmit a signal but only reflects and manipulates the wireless channel to degrade or deny reception to a receiver. Current approaches to detecting jamming depend upon the active nature of jammers and are not designed to detect a passive adversary. A proposed solution would be to use machine learning (ML) for classification. In order to do machine learning classification, we need training data. In this paper, we present our approach to create artificial jamming data for ML models training. We evaluate the attack effectiveness of the produced jamming data and show that it faithfully reflects power and spectral properties of normal channels and channels under the influence of both an RIS-based jammer and an active jammer. The characteristic differences between active jamming and passive RIS-enabled jamming are analysed across multiple domains (power, spectral, statistical, temporal) providing useful insights into effective features selection for the training of ML-based RIS-enabled anomaly detection models.

title: Performance and Coverage Enhancement with Frequency Diverse STAR-RIS (FD-STAR-RIS).
abstract: Simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) have emerged as a promising technology to achieve full-space coverage. However, existing STAR-RIS schemes primarily rely on angle-domain beamforming. Meanwhile, the frequency diverse RIS (FD-RIS) enables joint distance-angle beamforming, yet its coverage is limited to the half-space. A novel frequency diverse STAR-RIS (FD-STAR-RIS) framework is proposed in this paper by introducing periodic signals for time-modulation on the STAR-RIS. With frequency diversity successfully achieved on the passive STAR-RIS, FD-STAR-RIS enables joint distance-angle beamforming in full-space. In this paper, we first establish the signal processing model for the FD-STAR-RIS. Subsequently, a sum-rate maximization problem is formulated for a dual-user communication system. This is achieved by jointly optimizing the base station (BS) active beamforming, the passive beamforming and time-modulation frequency of the FD-STAR-RIS. To address the formulated problem, an efficient alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed. Specifically, the problem is decomposed into subproblems solved via the minimum mean square error (MMSE) criterion, semidefinite relaxation (SDR), and particle swarm optimization (PSO), respectively. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed FD-STAR-RIS significantly outperforms conventional STAR-RIS by effectively manipulating signals in both distance and angle dimensions.

title: Towards a Sustainable Age of Information Metric: Carbon Footprint of Real-Time Status Updates.
abstract: The timeliness of collected information is essential for monitoring and control in data-driven intelligent infrastructures. It is typically quantified using the Age of Information (AoI) metric, which has been widely adopted to capture the freshness of information received in the form of status updates. While AoI-based metrics quantify how timely the collected information is, they largely overlook the environmental impact associated with frequent transmissions, specifically, the resulting Carbon Footprint (CF). To address this gap, we introduce a carbon-aware AoI framework. We first derive closed-form expressions for the average AoI under constrained CF budgets for the baseline $M/M/1$ and $M/M/1^*$ queuing models, assuming fixed Carbon Intensity (CI). We then extend the analysis by treating CI as a dynamic, time-varying parameter and solve the AoI minimization problem. Our results show that minimizing AoI does not inherently minimize CF, highlighting a clear trade-off between information freshness and environmental impact. CI variability further affects achievable AoI, indicating that sustainable operation requires joint optimization of CF budgets, Signal-to-noise Ratio (SNR), and transmission scheduling. This work lays the foundation for carbon-aware information freshness optimization in next-generation networks.

title: Deep Learning Driven 3GPP-Compliant Scheduler for 6G Networks.
abstract: To provide unprecedented connectivity for sixth-generation (6G) networks, the development of intelligent schedulers has drawn significant attention. These intelligent schedulers, coupled with the massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) network holds the potential to achieve higher performance gains without explicitly increasing the number of antennas. However, the prior developments have often considered scheduling user equipments (UEs) with simplistic parametric assumptions of the network, thereby failing to provide performance guarantees under the stringent control parameters of the third-generation partnership project (3GPP) standard. To address this, in this work, we develop an intelligent 3GPP-compliant scheduler driven by deep learning. Specifically, we construct a hierarchical graph attention (HGAT) network based scheduler adhesive to the 3GPP-compliant system level mMIMO simulator to optimize the scheduling of the UEs in the network by exploiting the inherent interference coupling between the UEs and their traffic demands such that the overall fairness of the network is enhanced. Simulation results substantiate the effectiveness of our proposed deep learning scheduler in achieving enhanced fairness in both uplink and downlink compared to the existing standard schedulers.

title: A Cross-Layer Overlay Architecture for Open RAN-Enabled Integration of Mesh Networks with 5G Private Cores in IIoT.
abstract: The industrial sector is shifting toward Industrial IoT (IIoT) to achieve real-time automation and efficiency. However, traditional hierarchical networks lack the scalability required for dynamic environments, while standalone mesh networks struggle with deterministic latency. This paper proposes a novel Mesh-Enhanced 5G Private Network Architecture that integrates decentralized mesh topologies with centralized 5G Core capabilities. We introduce a cross-layer Overlay Protocol that maps multi-hop mesh traffic onto 5G QoS flows, utilizing Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) for intelligent resource allocation. By defining a logical architecture that bridges Custom Mesh MAC layers with 5G NR interfaces, we address the critical challenges of protocol interoperability and maintaining heterogeneous QoS. The proposed overlay framework aligns with Open RAN principles by decoupling access technologies from core control logic and enabling programmable, cross-layer coordination between non-3GPP mesh access and 5G RAN/core components. Simulation results demonstrate that this hybrid architecture significantly reduces latency variance compared to standard star-topology 5G deployments in dense industrial settings.

title: DRL-Based Beam Positioning for LEO Satellite Constellations with Weighted Least Squares.
abstract: This paper investigates a lightweight deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-assisted weighting framework for CSI-free multi-satellite positioning in LEO constellations, where each visible satellite provides one serving beam (one pilot response) per epoch. A discrete-action Deep Q-Network (DQN) learns satellite weights directly from received pilot measurements and geometric features, while an augmented weighted least squares (WLS) estimator provides physics-consistent localization and jointly estimates the receiver clock bias. The proposed hybrid design targets an accuracy-runtime trade-off rather than absolute supervised optimality. In a representative 2-D setting with 10 visible satellites, the proposed approach achieves sub-meter accuracy (0.395m RMSE) with low computational overhead, supporting practical deployment for resource-constrained LEO payloads.

title: Graphical Causal Reasoning for Root Cause Analysis in Cloud Networks.
abstract: Cloud-computing relies on large-scale networks which are inherently complex systems. In this paper, we present a novel approach to root cause analysis (RCA) of cloud network incidents, leveraging graph-based causal discovery techniques. Our method addresses the limitations of rule-based automation by introducing a spatiotemporal grouping strategy and an automation ontology to reduce the dimensionality of the problem. We construct a causal graph from binary time series data using bivariate Granger causality and conditional independence tests. For inference, we introduce a probabilistic method that assigns edge-specific conditional probabilities as a function of time lag, allowing for interpretable, time-aware root cause scoring via causal graph traversal.We evaluated the system using a labeled dataset of 35 production incidents from a major cloud provider. The model successfully recalled the correct root cause in 85.7% of incidents and produced an exact match in 74.3%. In production, the deployed system has been used in over 800 real-world incidents, with positive qualitative feedback from network engineers. These results highlight the practicality of a data-driven, causal approach to RCA in dynamic and large-scale operational environments.

title: RIS-Aided Self-Interference Cancellation in In-Band Full-Duplex Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is proposed to become a cornerstone of 6G, while in-band full-duplex (IBFD) radios can, in principle, double spectral efficiency by allowing uplink and downlink to share the same carrier. The price of this spectral gain is the severe loop self-interference (LSI) caused by the co-located transmit and receive chains. Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs), which are programmable arrays that reshape impinging wavefronts without active amplification, offer an energy-efficient means of suppressing LSI. This paper investigates RIS-assisted IBFD-ISAC architecture in which the surface is partitioned into sub-arrays dedicated to canceling LSI from multiple transmitters and enhancing desired communication links. We benchmark a suite of convex and meta-heuristic optimization algorithms that jointly allocate resources between sensing and communication while tuning the RIS phase shifts. System performance is then evaluated against stringent data-rate and sensing-rate targets. The results demonstrate that properly optimized RIS partitioning can improve the LSI suppression margin and satisfy simultaneous sensing and throughput requirements across a wide operating range. This highlights the promise of RIS-enabled IBFD-ISAC for next-generation wireless networks.

title: Per-Round Resource Optimization for ISCC-Enabled Vertical Federated Learning in Edge Perception Network.
abstract: This paper investigates an integrated sensing, communication, and computation (ISCC) enabled edge perception network, where multiple distributed edge devices wirelessly sense objects and collaboratively train a learning model under a coordination of an edge server. To address the feature heterogeneity of distributed wireless sensing data at devices, a vertical federated edge learning (VFEEL) framework is adopted, while over-the-air computation (AirComp) is employed to efficiently aggregate local embeddings. Under this setup, we characterize a rigorous convergence analysis to quantify the joint impact of wireless sensing noise and AirComp aggregation errors on the VFEEL performance. Guided by this analysis, we formulate a per-round optimization problem that jointly optimizes the batch size and resource allocation under strict latency and energy constraints. Numerical results on a human motion recognition task demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly enhances learning performance and resource efficiency compared to existing baselines.

title: A New Fine Time Synchronization Scheme for OTFS Systems.
abstract: This paper presents a new fine time synchronization scheme for orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) systems based on an embedded pilot structure in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain. The pilot is formed by a kernel sequence with both cyclic prefixing and postfixing, while the time synchronization scheme is equivalent to a three-stage process for estimating the timing offset (TO) in the delay dimension (θd) and the TO in the time dimension (θt). The first two stages operate in the delay-time domain, but the third stage operates in the DD domain. Stage 1 produces an initial estimate of θdby utilizing the periodicity of the cyclic extensions of the sequence pilot. Stage 2 identifies an estimate of θtby finding the first time bin along which there are sufficient pilot samples. Stage 3 further refines the estimate of θdby checking whether there exists another earlier possible delay estimate. The thresholding mechanisms for stages 2 and 3 are designed appropriately to make the TO estimation process work well. As compared with previous related methods, the proposed one achieves better performance in terms of the probability of perfect time synchronization and the peak-to-average power ratio.

title: Sparse Spike Encoding of Channel Responses for Energy Efficient Human Activity Recognition.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication enables pervasive monitoring, but modern sensing algorithms are often too complex for energy-constrained edge devices. This motivates the development of learning techniques that balance accuracy performance and energy efficiency. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are a promising alternative, processing information as sparse binary spike trains and potentially reducing energy consumption by orders of magnitude. In this work, we propose a spiking convolutional autoencoder (SCAE) that learns tailored spike-encoded representations of channel impulse responses (CIR), jointly trained with an SNN for human activity recognition (HAR), thereby eliminating the need for Doppler domain preprocessing. The results show that our SCAE-SNN achieves F1 scores comparable to a hybrid approach (almost 96%), while producing substantially sparser spike encoding (81.1% sparsity). We also show that encoding CIR data prior to classification improves both HAR accuracy and efficiency. The code is available at https://github.com/ele-ciccia/SCAE-SNN-HAR.

title: Agentic AI-Native Voice Call Quality of Experience Enhancement for 6G Networks.
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) mobile networks are envisioned as AI-native, service-aware systems capable of supporting highly dynamic and immersive applications. Although voice communication is a long-established service, emerging high-fidelity, low-latency, and context-aware voice interactions impose stringent requirements on quality of experience (QoE) in 6G environments. Conventional rule-based and reactive optimization mechanisms are insufficient to address the increasing network complexity and variability. In this paper, an Agentic AI-based voice call quality optimization architecture is proposed for AI-native 6G networks. The proposed approach employs goal-driven intelligent agents operating across radio access, transport, and core network domains to enable continuous, closed-loop optimization of voice services. A multi-dimensional voice quality perception model is introduced to correlate network-level performance metrics with perceptual voice quality indicators, allowing QoE-aware decision-making. Through inter-agent coordination and continuous learning, the agents dynamically adapt key control parameters such as codec selection, scheduling policies, mobility handling, and network slice resource allocation. The proposed architecture provides a scalable and autonomous framework for resilient voice call quality optimization, contributing toward self-optimizing and user-centric voice services in future 6G networks.

title: ISAC-over-NTN: HAPS-UAV Framework for Post-Disaster Responsive 6G Networks.
abstract: In disaster scenarios, ensuring both reliable communication and situational awareness becomes a critical challenge due to the partial or complete collapse of terrestrial networks. This paper proposes an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) over non-terrestrial networks (NTN) architecture referred to as ISAC-over-NTN that integrates multiple uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) and a high-altitude platform station (HAPS) to maintain resilient and reliable network operations in post-disaster conditions. We aim to achieve two main objectives: i) provide a reliable communication infrastructure, thereby ensuring the continuity of search-and-rescue activities and connecting people to their loved ones, and ii) detect users, such as those trapped under rubble or those who are mobile, using a Doppler-based mobility detection model. We employ an innovative beamforming method that simultaneously transmits data and detects Doppler-based mobility by integrating multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) communication and monostatic sensing within the same transmission chain. The results show that the proposed framework maintains reliable connectivity and achieves high detection accuracy of users in critical locations, reaching 90% motion detection sensitivity and 88% detection accuracy.

title: Learning to Save Power: Deep CSI Compression and Neural Antenna Muting for 6G Sustainability.
abstract: Sustainability plays a major role in sixth-generation (6G) mobile technology, making efficient and sustainable use of radio network resources is a top priority in future mobile networks. In this paper, we try to simultaneously improve energy efficiency both at the radio access network (RAN) and user equipment (UE) sides, targeting achieving the sustainability goals of 6G cellular networks. Specifically, the two-sided approach involves a deep learning-based channel state information (CSI) compression at the UE side, and a neural transmit antenna muting (TAM) approach in a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) network. First, we discuss multiple neural architectures to compress and reconstruct CSI, thereby mitigating the substantial feedback overhead associated with high-dimensional CSI in massive MIMO OFDM systems. Exploiting the sparsity and local correlations of CSI in the delay-angle domain, the proposed neural networks based autoencoders effectively capture both local and global dependencies through dynamically learned features. Using the compressed CSI available at the base station, a neural antenna muting solution is then proposed to activate the best subset of antenna elements to maximize energy efficiency. Experiments based on data generated using 3GPP-compliant models were used to evaluate the proposed methodology. It was observed that this method of CSI compression and antenna muting together consistently outperforms existing techniques in achieving high energy efficiency.

title: Learning Compact Representations with Graph Neural Networks for CSI Feedback.
abstract: This paper presents a graph neural network architecture for compressing and reconstructing channel state information (CSI) in cellular systems, aiming to alleviate the significant overhead that high-dimensional CSI feedback poses in massive MIMO and broadband OFDM environments. We observe that the CSI, in the delay-angle domain, is sparser and possesses locally correlated peaks. We propose a graph neural network (GNN) based autoencoder with attention and adaptive quantizer to exploit these structures for CSI compression. The novel GNN-based approach models relational structures among CSI elements using dynamically constructed graphs and attention mechanisms, capturing both local and global dependencies in the delay-angular domain. GNNs can dynamically define relationships (graph edges) based on the similarity or spatial closeness of features (graph nodes, which represent patches or peaks in delay-angle CSI data). Experimental results, based on data generated using 3GPP-compliant models and real-life CSI measurements, demonstrate that the GNN-based architecture consistently outperforms all other neural architectures, offering up to 30x improvement in performance.

title: Secure and Real-Time Data Streaming for Digital Twin Architectures: A Kafka-Based Approach.
abstract: With the rapid increase in data generation from cyber-physical systems, the need for low-latency and high-throughput data exchange has become critical, especially in digital twin applications. The digital twin provides timely and consistent data to reflect the state of physical systems for real-time monitoring, decision-making, and advanced analytics. The effectiveness of a digital twin depends on how accurately and timely it reflects the physical system. However, implementing secure and low-latency synchronization from distributed physical environments to a centralized platform remains a challenge. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a real-time architecture to securely synchronize the digital twin with physical systems using Apache Kafka. Our approach uses Kafka’s high-throughput publish-subscribe model to stream data efficiently under different security configurations to improve Quality of Service (QoS). We design a prototype system and evaluate unencrypted and SSL/TLS-encrypted traffic in terms of latency, and show the impact of encryption overhead under different traffic loads. The results validate Kafka’s potential as a robust middleware for secure digital twin applications.

title: A Road Map for Utilizing SemCom on the Way to Breaking Traditional QoS Boundaries.
abstract: While traditional communication systems focus on the accurate transmission of data at the bit level, today’s increasing data diversity, contextual needs and user-oriented content necessitate a more meaning-centered communication approach. The semantic communication approach, developed in response to these needs, aims to transmit information while preserving its meaning. This paper discusses the building blocks of semantic communication systems, multimodal data processing and the advantages of using Large AI Models (LAMs) in these systems. In particular, large language and visual-language models can be used to semantically represent and compress text, visual and audio data and reconstruct them in a way that minimizes the loss of meaning at the receiver. In this paper, we propose a LAM-based semantic communication framework. The framework utilizes BART and GPT-2 models for encoder and decoder, respectively. Our test results show that our method LAM-SC provides semantically robustness in low and high SNR values. Our results indicate that LAM-SC maintains strong semantic performance over a wide range of SNR values. Even under severe noise at 0 dB, the model preserves meaning, while at 12 dB it achieves BLEU scores of 0.9 (2-gram) and 0.75 (4-gram). The evaluations in this context demonstrate the applicability of semantic communication in different communication environments and show that this approach provides a flexible and meaning-centric communication systems in 6G and beyond networks.

title: Rate-Reliability Tradeoff for Deterministic Identification over Gaussian Channels.
abstract: We extend the recent analysis of the rate–reliability tradeoff in deterministic identification (DI) to general linear Gaussian channels, marking the first such analysis for channels with continuous output. Because DI provides a framework that can substantially enhance communication efficiency, and since the linear Gaussian model underlies a broad range of physical communication systems, our results offer both theoretical insights and practical relevance for the performance evaluation of DI in future networks. Moreover, the structural parallels observed between the Gaussian and discrete-output cases suggest that similar rate–reliability behaviour may extend to wider classes of continuous channels.

title: Scalability and Resilience in Practice: A 24-Month Measurement Study of Congestion Dynamics and Reliability in Production Layer-2 Networks.
abstract: Large-scale distributed applications increasingly depend on Layer-2 optimistic rollups to scale execution while preserving Layer-1 settlement guarantees. Yet, longitudinal evidence on their production behavior under stress remains limited, especially across the EIP-4844 transition. This paper presents a 24-month measurement study of Arbitrum One and Optimism (January 2024–December 2025), covering approximately 457 million user transactions. We evaluate three dimensions: (i) realized throughput and utilization under published capacity baselines, (ii) coupling between Layer-1 execution gas and Layer2 user costs, and (iii) operational resilience during burst events using availability, stress amplification, and recovery-time proxies. Results show major cost reductions versus Ethereum Layer-1 and a clear post-EIP-4844 level shift in fee dynamics, while coupling analysis indicates weakened dependence rather than full independence from Layer-1 execution gas. The two rollups also exhibit distinct stress-response profiles: Arbitrum reaches higher peaks with larger fee volatility, whereas Optimism is more pricestable with lower throughput ceilings. These findings provide reproducible evidence of practical scalability–resilience trade-offs in production rollup systems.

title: Diffusion-Based Data Augmentation and Resource Allocation for Heterogeneous Federated Learning.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a generative AI (GAI)-assisted data augmentation scheme, which can address the heterogeneous data challenge in the data domain of federated learning (FL). Specifically, leveraging the high-quality data generation capability of GAI, data can be generated in accordance with the label distribution of user data to alleviate data heterogeneity, thereby achieving independent and identically distributed (IID) approximation. To efficiently extract features from user-local data without compromising data privacy, we propose a finetuning scheme to enhance the generation performance of the diffusion model. Then, an optimization problem is formulated to minimize the FL training delay by jointly optimizing data augmentation and computing-communication resource allocation. To solve the problem, we decompose it into a data generation management subproblem and a resource allocation subproblem. Then, we propose a joint optimization algorithm for communication resource allocation and augmentation data schedule. To solve the problem, we propose a penalty function-assisted algorithm that enables FL training process resource allocation. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can reduce communication overhead by up to 37.9% and achieve up to 16.1% improvement in model accuracy compared to existing FL schemes.

title: Liquid Digital Twins: Distributed Architecture in the Edge-Fog-Cloud Context.
abstract: In modern cyber-physical systems based on the Internet of Things (IoT), the Digital Twin (DT) paradigm is increasingly adopted to maintain a persistent and synchronized digital counterpart of physical entities. While IoT platforms support monitoring and control functionalities, DT-based systems maintain an explicit and continuously evolving state model of the physical asset, enabling state-aware operation as well as profiling, simulation, and prediction capabilities.However, most existing DT implementations rely on rigid, cloud-centric architectures, which limits their ability to cope with dynamic operating conditions such as network latency variations, fluctuating computational loads, and heterogeneous resource availability across the infrastructure.This paper introduces the Liquid Digital Twin (LDT) paradigm, an architectural approach that exploits the presence of multiple network depth levels, i.e., Edge, Fog, and Cloud, to dynamically reconfigure DT operations and data processing flows. By leveraging this hierarchical infrastructure, the LDT adapts its operating modes to current system conditions while preserving service continuity and state coherence, without requiring full or partial DT migration.The proposed architecture is validated through an experimental prototype based on containerized components and lightweight communication protocols. Experimental results show that the LDT achieves reduced end-to-end latency and improved data flow stability under variable network conditions, confirming its effectiveness as a flexible and resilient solution for distributed DT-based IoT systems.

title: On Extremely Low-Complexity Detection for OTFS via Interference Cancellation.
abstract: In this paper, we focus on orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulated transmissions over doubly-selective channels. Specifically, we investigate the state-of-the-art techniques for effective detection in high-mobility scenarios and introduce an innovative strategy that is based on the Ungerboeck observation model and leverages the principle of interference cancellation. The key advantage of the proposed method lies in its extremely low computational complexity. We evaluated the performance of this algorithm in terms of both pragmatic capacity and bit error rate, comparing it with existing state-of-the-art solutions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach allows to achieve an optimal trade-off between complexity and performance under various channel conditions.

title: Learning-Based Reactive Handover under Line-of-Sight Loss: A UE-Centric NTN Continuity Model.
abstract: The dynamics of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations introduce frequent and unpredictable Line-of-Sight (LoS) interruptions that challenge conventional handover procedures in Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs). Previous analytical work has established that, once the residual LoS interval becomes shorter than the end-to-end control-plane delay, network-assisted preparation loses feasibility and the decision logic must shift toward the terminal. Building on this premise, this paper introduces a learning-based reactive handover model representing a UE-centric continuity mechanism under LoS-limited conditions. The proposed framework employs a lightweight Q-learning agent that selects target satellites based on locally observable indicators such as relative elevation and received signal level. Within a deterministic geometric environment, the agent converges toward stable switching behaviour and reproduces the qualitative trade-offs predicted by the analytical model of reactive continuity. The achieved 25-30% alignment improvement over a geometry-only baseline demonstrates that even simplified reinforcement learning can capture timing dependencies essential to NTN handover robustness. While not intended as a deployment result, the study provides a reproducible benchmark and a methodological foundation for future deep- or federated-learning extensions operating within realistic NTN channel and protocol constraints.

title: Optimal Source Coding of Markov Chains for Real-Time Remote Estimation.
abstract: We revisit the source coding problem for a Markov chain under the assumption that the transmission times and how fast the Markov chain transitions its state happen at the same time-scale. Specifically, we assume that the transmission of each bit takes a single time slot, and the Markov chain updates its state in the same time slot. Thus, the length of the codeword assigned to a symbol determines the number of non-transmitted symbols, as well as, the probability of the realization of the next symbol to be transmitted. We aim to minimize the average transmission duration over an infinite horizon by proposing an optimal source coding policy based on the last transmitted symbol and its transmission duration. To find the optimal policy, we formulate the problem with a Markov decision process (MDP) by augmenting the symbols alongside the transmission duration of the symbols. Finally, we analyze two Huffman-based benchmark policies and compare their performances with the proposed optimal policy. We observe that, in randomly generated processes, our proposed optimal policy decreases the average transmission duration compared to benchmark policies. The performance gain varies based on the parameters of the Markov process.

title: Classification of Hardware Trojan Attacks via model and data based analysis of RF signals.
abstract: The increasing ubiquity of wireless communications has exposed significant security vulnerabilities. This paper addresses the threat of Hardware Trojans (HTs), malicious hardware modifications capable of establishing covert channels within Wi-Fi signals for hidden data transmission. Our primary objective is to automatically detect these attacks by exploiting a public dataset of raw I/Q signals. We propose two different approaches: supervised machine learning, specifically Classification Trees and Random Forests, assuming a labeled dataset of both nominal and attacked data; and one-class learning, assuming only labeled nominal data and exploiting prior knowledge of physical characteristics of Wi-Fi signals and of the attack type. We show that the combined application of both approaches provides quantified substantial improvements with respect to the state-of-the-art results on the same dataset, both for the low and high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

title: Real-Time Inference for Distributed Multimodal Systems under Communication Delay Uncertainty.
abstract: Connected cyber-physical systems perform inference based on real-time inputs from multiple data streams. Uncertain communication delays across data streams challenge the temporal flow of the inference process. State-of-the-art (SotA) non-blocking inference methods rely on a reference-modality paradigm, requiring one modality input to be fully received before processing, while depending on costly offline profiling. We propose a novel, neuro-inspired non-blocking inference paradigm that primarily employs adaptive temporal windows of integration (TWIs) to dynamically adjust to stochastic delay patterns across heterogeneous streams while relaxing the reference-modality requirement. Our communication-delay-aware framework achieves robust real-time inference with finer-grained control over the accuracy-latency tradeoff. Experiments on the audio-visual event localization (AVEL) task demonstrate superior adaptability to network dynamics compared to SotA approaches.

title: Hybrid Channel- and Coding-Based Challenge-Response Physical-Layer Authentication with IRS.
abstract: This paper proposes a new physical-layer authentication (PLA) mechanism that operates in environments where the receiver partially controls the channel conditions. We focus in particular on a channel controlled by an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS). It combines a channel-based challenge-response PLA (CH-CRPLA), which uses instantaneous channel state information (CSI), and a coding-based PLA (CD-PLA), which uses a shared key. The combination allows for reaping the benefits of CD-PLA in a high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the legitimate channel and CH-CRPLA, imposing a high variation of channels even at low SNRs of the legitimate channel, thanks to the increased secrecy (wiretap) capacity. We investigate the trade-off between the pilot symbols for CSI estimation (for CH-CRPLA) and the key bits (for CD-PLA) and evaluate security in terms of the number of secret bits needed by an attacker to succeed. Numerical results confirm the advantage of the proposed hybrid approach over standalone methods.

title: Resource Allocation for URLLC/mMTC in 6G Industrial IoT Networks: Joint Optimization under Mixed-Numerology and SNR Constraints.
abstract: Modern smart factories accommodate numerous heterogeneous devices, making co-scheduling of Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communications (URLLC) and massive MachineType Communications (mMTC) services on shared physical resources are a critical challenge. This paper proposes a resource allocation mechanism for this convergence scenario, combining Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) boosting strategy, flexible numerology configuration, and device priority control. By formulating a multi-objective optimization model that integrates delay constraints, channel conditions, and resource utilization, we design a low-complexity adaptive scheduling algorithm. The simulation results demonstrate that our proposed method improves URLLC schedulability by 19.8% while achieving an average latency of 0.843ms, substantially outperforming the baseline algorithms. This paper provides effective technical support for the establishment of industrial wireless communication systems capable of supporting coexisting Quality of Service (QoS) requirements.

title: Blockage-Aware MmWave OFDM Waveform Design for Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: Millimeter wave (mmWave) based integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables high-speed communication and accurate sensing, yet it is highly susceptible to blockages that could lead to interrupted communication and sensing services. In this paper, we investigate blockage-aware mmWave orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveform design for ISAC, where we exploit multi-base station (BS) collaboration to enhance resilience for dynamic blockage, and leverage dual-functional radar-communication (DFRC) waveform to simultaneously perform data transmission and target localization. To account for the dynamic blockage, the communication and sensing performance is characterized in a probabilistic fashion. Then, we formulate a chance-constrained max-min optimization problem, which can be efficiently solved by the proposed stochastic successive convex approximation (SCA)-based blockage-aware beamforming (SSBAB) scheme. Simulation results verify the robustness of the SSBAB scheme in the presence of dynamic blockage.

title: Large-Small Model Collaboration for Efficient Environment-Adaptive CSI Feedback.
abstract: Large artificial intelligence models (LAMs) have shown strong capability in wireless communications, yet existing works mainly rely on their generalized knowledge across environments while overlooking the potential gains of environment-specific adaptation. Directly fine-tuning LAMs for adaptation is often impractical due to prohibitive training costs, low inference efficiency in multi-user scenarios, and the risk of catastrophic forgetting, in addition to the limited accessibility of model parameters. To address these limitations, we propose LASCO, a large and small collaboration framework for CSI feedback. Unlike prior approaches that either depend solely on LAMs or require direct fine-tuning, LASCO exploits LAMs as a universal channel knowledge base while employing small artificial intelligence models (SAMs) as lightweight plugins to capture environment-specific knowledge. The key idea is to approximate the distribution shift of reconstructed CSI during adaptation through two SAMs, namely a reference SAM and a proxy SAM, and then transfer this shift to the LAM without modifying its parameters. Simulation results demonstrate that LASCO enables LAMs to achieve environment-specific performance gains with significantly reduced training costs, lower data collection requirements, and faster adaptation speed.

title: Optimizing DFT-s-OFDM Waveform for ISAC: A Probabilistic Constellation Shaping Approach.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for future wireless networks. Against this background, this paper proposes a probabilistic constellation shaping (PCS) framework for discrete Fourier transform-spread orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (DFT-s-OFDM)-based ISAC systems. We first derive a closed-form ambiguity function (AF) of DFT-s-OFDM waveforms, which reveals a direct relationship between velocity estimation accuracy and the constellation’s kurtosis. We formulate the PCS design as an optimization problem that maximizes communication throughput while constraining the kurtosis to explicitly control sensing performance. For nonlinear channels with power amplifier distortion, a surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithm is proposed, which efficiently identifies the Pareto-optimal front with low computational complexity. Simulations demonstrate that our framework achieves a superior and highly tunable performance trade-off compared to conventional uniform constellations.

title: Learning-Driven Dual-Line Laser Scanning for Fast and Accurate LEO Satellite Positioning.
abstract: Accurate and low-latency positioning is a key enabler for optical links with Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, where millisecond-level beam alignment is required to maintain reliable high-data-rate communication. This paper presents a learning-driven dual-line laser scanning framework for fast and precise satellite positioning. Unlike conventional Gaussian-beam acquisition systems that rely on multiple sequential beams or mechanical steering, the proposed approach employs two orthogonal line-shaped laser beams to perform structured optical scanning over the ambiguity region without any moving parts. A physics-based model incorporating atmospheric attenuation, turbulence, and MRR-based reflection is developed, and a data-driven neural estimator is trained to map received optical energy patterns to the satellite's two-dimensional position. Simulation results demonstrate that the learning-driven method achieves near-MAP accuracy with typical errors of 7-10 m and deterministic scanning time of 1-2 ms, while conventional two-stage Gaussian-beam schemes exhibit comparable errors but random sensing durations of up to 5 ms. The proposed framework therefore offers a favorable trade-off between positioning accuracy, computational complexity, and sensing latency, making it a practical candidate for next-generation optical LEO tracking systems.

title: MRR-Based Line-Laser Scanning for Reliable Vehicular Positioning and Optical Communication.
abstract: High-speed vehicular environments require optical systems capable of joint sensing, positioning, and communication (JSPC) without mechanical tracking. Existing optical and integrated sensing-communication approaches often rely on point-source emitters or camera-based receivers, limiting spatial coverage and update rate under highway dynamics. This work introduces a new class of tracking-free optical JSPC systems that combine structured line-laser illumination with modulating retroreflector (MRR) arrays on vehicles. Two orthogonal line lasers perform synchronized longitudinal and transverse scanning to provide continuous, wide-area coverage across the roadway. A coverage-driven analytical framework models the coupling between beam divergence, scan geometry, and dwell-time allocation, enabling joint evaluation of sensing reliability and communication quality. An optimization scheme is developed to adapt scanning and divergence parameters for uniform coverage and power efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in spatial coverage uniformity, link stability, and reliability within a fixed scan period. These results establish a practical pathway toward scalable, turbulence-resilient optical architectures for next-generation vehicular JSPC networks.

title: UAV-assisted Anonymous Adaptive Onion Routing Framework for Intelligent Healthcare Communication.
abstract: The evolution of healthcare communication systems demands secure and efficient communication mechanisms to safeguard sensitive medical data. However, conventional wireless and cloud-based communication frameworks remain vulnerable to interception and unauthorized access. To address these challenges, this paper presents an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted Adaptive Onion Routing (AOR) framework designed for intelligent healthcare communication systems. The proposed framework helps to integrate UAVs to help with secure data acquisition and transmission between healthcare entities while implementing an adaptive onion routing network to achieve end-to-end data confidentiality and anonymity. The adaptiveness dynamically chooses optimal relay nodes considering the network conditions and threat probability, and so as a result, this ensures minimum latency and improved route resilience. Artificial intelligence (Al)-driven classification models are incorporated to detect malicious communication in real time. This framework is simulated in the Shadow environment to overview security and performance metrics, anonymity rate, latency, and processing overhead. Experimental results show that the AOR network maintains anonymous communication with very less computational overhead and ensures efficient data protection when compared to conventional OR networks. Therefore, the implementation of adaptive onion routing with UAV-assisted communication establishes an intelligent and secure framework for healthcare systems.

title: CTFANet: Deep Learning for Massive MIMO CSI Prediction using Empirical Data.
abstract: Massive MIMO systems operating in frequency division duplex mode face a critical bottleneck: acquiring accurate downlink channel state information (CSI), especially when antenna counts scale. To overcome this challenge, we introduce CTFANet for CSI prediction, which is a lightweight and data-efficient deep learning architecture that fuses temporal dynamics (Transformer), spatial pattern extraction (ConvMixer), and Fourier-inspired adaptive representations. Unlike prior approaches, CTFANet achieves high precision CSI prediction, maintaining an NMSE of −28.03 dB within 25 epochs and a cosine similarity of 0.99, with as few as 1000 training samples. Despite using only ∼ 1.4 M parameters and 0.23 M FLOPs, the model preserves performance even with aggressive 1-bit quantization per real value, highlighting its robustness and practical deployability. These attributes make CTFANet an ideal candidate for 5G/6G systems, where bandwidth and energy constraints are paramount. Extensive experiments confirm its superiority over state-of-the-art baselines, achieving approximately 12% lower NMSE, 2% higher cosine similarity, while reducing parameter count by about 86% and FLOPs by 91%, particularly in challenging outdoor environments, while maintaining efficient training convergence and minimal complexity at inference.

title: Incremental Decoding for Real-Time Decision Making over Binary Symmetric Channels.
abstract: Low-latency communication has attracted considerable recent attention because it holds the promise of enabling real-time decision making or control in industrial internet-of-things (IIoT), smart grid, factory automation, etc. In conventional real-time applications, a decision is usually made after an entire packet is transmitted and decoded. Owing to the limited bandwidth in practical communication links, however, its sub-packets or even bits have to be transmitted successively, thereby inducing non-negligible delay in decision making. Incremental decoding, a paradigm-shift low-latency transmission technique, allows controllers to make their decisions in real time based on partially received packets. Since there is no need to wait for the whole packet to be decoded, the latency-induced costs can be substantially reduced.
