title: RF Intelligence for Health: Classification of SmartBAN Signals in overcrowded ISM band.
abstract: Accurate classification of Radio-Frequency (RF) signals is essential for reliable wearable health-monitoring systems, providing awareness of the interference conditions in which medical protocols operate. In the overcrowded 2.4GHz ISM band, however, identifying low-power transmissions from medical sensors is challenging due to strong co-channel interference and substantial power asymmetry with coexisting technologies. This work introduces the first open source framework for automatic recognition of SmartBAN signals in Body Area Networks (BANs). The framework combines a synthetic dataset of simulated signals with real RF acquisitions obtained through Software-Defined Radios (SDRs), enabling both controlled and realistic evaluation. Deep convolutional neural networks based on ResNet encoders and U-Net decoders with attention mechanisms are trained and assessed across diverse propagation conditions. The proposed approach achieves over 90% accuracy on synthetic datasets and demonstrates consistent performance on real over-the-air spectrograms. By enabling reliable SmartBAN signal recognition in dense spectral environments, this framework supports interference-aware coexistence strategies and improves the dependability of wearable healthcare systems.

title: Dual Radio Map-Aware Flight Strategy Optimization for UAV-Based Inspection System.
abstract: This paper investigates a dual radio map-aware inspection system that employs a cellular-connected unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in rural environments. The UAV is tasked with executing a series of mission-critical inspection operations while transmitting the collected data in real time under the guidance of pre-constructed radio maps. To enhance inspection efficiency and ensure low-latency data feedback, a joint optimization problem is formulated to simultaneously determine the inspection sequence and flight trajectory, with the objective of minimizing both mission completion time and data transmission delay. To solve this problem, we propose a novel framework that integrates an improved genetic algorithm (IGA) with deep reinforcement learning (DRL). The IGA first derives a near-optimal inspection sequence by jointly considering flight distance, uplink communication throughput, and downlink outage duration based on ground-to-air and air-to-ground radio maps. Subsequently, the DRL module refines the continuous flight trajectory. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DRL-IGA outperforms benchmark schemes, achieving up to a 20% reduction in both total task completion time and transmission delay.

title: Energy Efficiency Maximization for Pinching Antenna Systems.
abstract: A practical power consumption model is proposed for pinching antenna systems (PASS), based on which an energy efficiency maximization problem is formulated in the dual-scale deployment (DSD) framework. Specifically for the pinching antenna (PA) deployment optimization, 1) in the first coarse stage, the PA is transferred over a large-scale range at the waveguide level. 2) The refinement stage performs small-scale relocation of the PA with high precision. In the proposed DSD framework, the transmit precoding, PA radiation power, and PA deployment are jointly optimized to maximize the energy efficiency. To solve this non-convex, highly coupled problem, a low-complexity penalty-based alternating optimization algorithm is proposed. Simulation results validate the accuracy of theoretical results and the convergence of the proposed algorithm. They also demonstrate that PASS delivers about 70% higher energy efficiency than the conventional cell-free architecture and nearly twofold improvement relative to MIMO systems.

title: Large Language Model Assisted Beam Training for Pinching Antenna System (PASS).
abstract: To facilitate intelligent beam training, a large language model (LLM)-empowered beam training framework is proposed for the pinching antenna system (PASS) in downlink multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. A novel LLM-based beam training supervised learning mechanism is developed, wherein multimodal information is encoded into high-dimensional tokens to guide the adaptive probing process. For the multi-user case, a joint codebook generation and beam selection problem is formulated based on the system sum rate under the minimum mean square error (MMSE) transmit beamforming. The training labels for pinching beamforming are constructed by selecting the beam combination that maximizes system performance from each user’s Top-S candidate beams. Based on pretrained Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPTs), the LLM is trained in an end-to-end fashion to minimize the cross-entropy loss. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed LLM-enabled PASS framework significantly outperforms both the LLM-based massive MIMO and conventional PASS beam training, achieving up to 57.14% and 33.33% improvements in sum rate, respectively.

title: Scalable User Admission Control in Large-Scale Cell-Free Massive MIMO.
abstract: IEEECell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) is a promising architecture for 6G wireless networks through distributed access point (AP) cooperation. In large-scale deployments where user demand exceeds system capacity, effective user admission control (UAC) is essential to select users while meeting quality-of-service (QoS) requirements. The UAC problem in CF-mMIMO is inherently challenging, involving both discrete user selection and continuous power allocation variables. To address this challenge, we propose a Graphormer-enhanced Monte Carlo Tree Search (GE-MCTS) method that integrates a Graphormer-based neural network (NN) with Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS). This method leverages the Graphormer’s capability to model the graph-structured AP–user topology and MCTS’s planning proficiency to efficiently explore the vast decision space. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method. With low computational complexity, GE-MCTS admits 26.3–41.7% more users compared to baseline methods across various scales.

title: Seeing Through Walls: Inferring Indoor Layouts from Outdoor Wireless Sensing with PINNs.
abstract: We address wireless inference of unknown indoor layout and materials from sparse path measurements, under severe non-line-of-sight (NLoS) effect and limited viewing angles that hinder geometry-Electromagnetic coupling. We present a physics-aligned dual-branch neural tomography for jointly reconstructing a continuous occupancy field and a per-voxel material map. By integrating a differentiable radio forward model combining volumetric transmission with interface reflection and diffraction, we achieve end-to-end training from path losses. Edge-aware ray sampling and lightweight priors stabilise the learning process and produce sharp interfaces. In synthetic mmWave scenarios, our method produces sharper geometry and materially consistent reconstructions, improving over ray-tracing, fingerprinting, and 3D U-Net baselines, while maintaining the layout fidelity of a geometry-only Physics-informed neural networks (PINN).

title: Secrecy Rate Maximization in NOMA-UAV Enabled ISCC Networks.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a secure integrated sensing, communications and computing (ISCC) network supported by a nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platform, where a full-duplex (FD) UAV acts as an aerial relay to assist secure computation offloading while simultaneously detecting collusive active and passive eavesdroppers. With the goal of maximizing the weighted sum secrecy rate, we jointly optimize the transmit power of communication users (CUs), the UAV’s transmit beamforming, trajectory, and velocity. The formulated non-convex problem is decomposed into two subproblems and solved via an iterative alternating optimization algorithm that incorporates successive convex approximation, semidefinite relaxation, and penalty-based methods. Extensive numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed secure ISCC optimization framework and highlight the important roles of NOMA and UAV trajectory design in enhancing the secrecy performance.

title: Joint Constrained Coding and Iterative Consensus Reconstruction for DNA-Based Molecular Communication.
abstract: DNA-based molecular communication (DNA-MC) faces major reliability challenges. These arise from synthesis to sequencing errors, including insertions, deletions, and substitutions (IDS), as well as from biochemical constraints such as GC balance and homopolymer length limits. These issues directly affect sequence stability and data accuracy. In this paper, we propose two techniques. The first is a biologically constrained coding set that maintains a strict GC balance of 50% and restricts homopolymer lengths to 2–3 bp during DNA synthesis. The second is a multi-copy iterative consensus reconstruction (ICR) algorithm that performs position-wise correction across DNA copies. This method effectively prevents error propagation, a major weakness in traditional majority-voting approaches. Simulation results confirm that the proposed coding scheme enforces the key biological constraints. The ICR algorithm achieves strong error resilience without introducing extra logical redundancy. When combined with a deep learning–based end-to-end DNA-MC framework, the proposed approach improves the Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) by 3.04 dB and the Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) by 0.07 under a nucleotide-to-pixel ratio of 5/12 and a nucleotide error probability of 0.5%.

title: Energy Consumption Optimization for STAR-BD-RIS-Assisted LEO Satellite Collaborative Edge Computing.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) technology can significantly enhance channel conditions in satellite-terrestrial communication and further improve the service quality of satellite networks. Motivated by this observation, we integrate a novel technology called simultaneously transmitting and reflecting beyond-diagonal RIS (STAR-BD-RIS) into the LEO satellite collaborative edge computing (LSCEC) system, where each ground user equipment (GUE) can simultaneously offload task bits to multiple satellites with the aid of STAR-BD-RIS. The energy consumption of the LSCEC system is minimized by jointly optimizing the transmit power, offloading strategy, and STAR-BD-RIS beamforming via an alternating algorithm based on the successive convex approximation (SCA) technique and penalty dual decomposition (PDD) method. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves lower energy consumption than conventional RIS, transmissive beyond-diagonal RIS (T-BD-RIS), full offloading, and single-access schemes.

title: Disentangled Multimodal Semantic Encoding for Task-Oriented Communication.
abstract: Multimodal task-oriented communication has emerged as a promising paradigm for 6G wireless networks. However, existing systems often treat cross-modal aligned representations as semantics, implicitly relying on a multi-view redundancy assumption that may discard modality-unique task-relevant information while transmitting task-irrelevant redundancy. We propose a disentangled multimodal semantic compression framework that factorizes semantics into three orthogonal components: shared semantics capturing cross-modal consistent information, unique semantics preserving modality-specific task-relevant information, and synergistic semantics encoding interaction patterns from joint observations. Inspired by Partial Information Decomposition and the Minimum Necessary Information principle, we derive tractable learning objectives using InfoNCE lower bounds and CLUB upper bounds. Experiments on CMU-MOSI demonstrate consistent improvements over conventional and JSCC baselines under AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels.

title: UP-MC: Privacy-Preserving UAV-based Proximity Detection in Multi-Cloud Environments.
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in commercial applications, there is a growing need for efficient and privacy-preserving collision avoidance systems in dense airspace. Traditional collision avoidance methods face privacy leakage risks, while existing privacy-preserving proximity detection methods, although addressing privacy issues, come with high communication overhead. In this paper, we propose the UP-MC framework, a privacy-preserving proximity detection scheme for UAVs in multi-cloud environments. UP-MC utilizes 3D Z-order encoding, spatial prefix encoding, and additive secret sharing to securely and efficiently manage UAV location data. Through the use of Bloom filters, UP-MC ensures that UAVs can detect potential collisions while preserving the privacy of their positions. The UP-MC achieves constant time complexity O(1) for proximity detection, significantly improving detection efficiency and scalability over state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results show that UP-MC provides sub-millisecond detection latency while ensuring robust privacy protection, even in high-density UAV environments.

title: A ResNet-Decoder Architecture for Classifying OFDM Signals.
abstract: Automatic modulation recognition (AMR) for heterogeneous orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals with varying subcarrier spacing and modulation remains a significant challenge. We propose an architecture based on a GPT-2 decoder, which uses a 2D ResNet feature extractor. This architecture works in several steps. First, it transforms raw In-phase/Quadrature (I/Q) signals into multi-resolution spectral maps using multiple short-time Fourier transforms (STFTs). Next, a 2D ResNet front-end extracts local time-frequency patterns from these maps. These patterns are then tokenized and sent to learn long-range temporal dependencies. Finally, a single linear head is used for classification. To validate our architecture, we performed a comprehensive benchmark against four distinct baseline neural networks. The proposed model achieved a peak accuracy of 99.44%, and significantly outperformed all baseline approaches, regardless of whether they utilized raw time-domain or time-frequency inputs.

title: Generative Al-driven Wireless Semantic Sensing by the Dual-polarized Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface.
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the concept of semantic sensing, which extracts not only spatial features but also high-level semantic information directly from communication signals, playing a critical role in environmental reconstruction that enhances the performance of future wireless communication systems. For practical implementation, semantic sensing remains challenging due to the sparsity of wireless sensing data. To address this issue, we propose and implement a generative AI-driven semantic sensing system where a dual-polarized reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is employed to provide an energy-efficient large-aperture array, thereby enriching the spatial information. The polarization dimension is further exploited by fusing OFDM-based ranging information from multiple polarization channels to reconstruct a more complete and accurate point cloud of the environment. The reconstructed point cloud is then delivered to a semantic recognition network to output the semantic labels of all points. To improve the generalization capability of the recognition network, a diffusion probabilistic model (DPM)-based point cloud generation mechanism is developed to augment the dataset, requiring only 20% of real-world collected data. Finally, the prototype semantic sensing system is evaluated in practical indoor scenarios, and the results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves an average 25% improvement in point-wise semantic recognition accuracy compared with conventional methods when trained on the same limited dataset.

title: Topology-Aware MoE RL for UAV-Oriented MEC Service Migration and DNN Partitioning.
abstract: As a pivotal component of Space-Air-Ground-Sea Integrated Networks (SAGSINs), the Air-Ground integrated layer enables collaborative computing by offloading deep neural network (DNN) workloads from resource-limited aerial nodes such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to ground edge base stations (BSs) via DNN partitioning. However, in highly dynamic integrated networks, the inference service is stateful and the topology is time-varying. The frequent cross-region mobility of aerial nodes necessitates seamless service migration; coupled with topology and load dynamics, the joint service migration, context precaching, and DNN partitioning decisions become large, hybrid, and multi-modal, where suboptimal decisions can trigger long service interruption and queueing delay. We formulate this two-timescale decision problem and propose a topology-aware hard-routed mixture-of-experts (MoE) reinforcement learning algorithm. A pretrained graph neural network (GNN) over the BS graph provides topology-aware BS embeddings, referred to as the base station GNN (BS-GNN), that capture both geographic and handover relations, and a hard-routed MoE head assigns each UAV to a specialized expert to make robust big-slot decisions across heterogeneous topology and load regimes. Trace-driven simulations show that BS-GNN reduces delay by 6.9% and 16.1% compared with Geo-only and No-GNN representations, and hard-routed MoE further reduces delay and migration overhead by 9.9% and 8.1% while enhance the stability of training over the non-MoE baseline.

title: FairVSP: Maximizing Social Welfare through Fair Validators Selection in Permissioned Blockchains.
abstract: Blockchain enables secure information exchange among untrusted parties without intermediaries. In Permissioned Blockchains, Validators are known participants, yet remain susceptible to attacks or mistrust. Existing consensus protocols mainly improve throughput but overlook fairness in transaction confirmation, potentially disadvantaging users. We propose airVSP, a Validator selection algorithm that maximizes Social Welfare through a distributed solution of the Validator Selection problem. The approach leverages α-Fairness as utility and applies Evolutionary Algorithms, Genetic Algorithm, Simulated Annealing, and Ant Colony Optimization, enhanced by a search space division strategy for efficiency. Simulations show FairVSP improves Social Welfare by over 70% compared to existing methods and converges in under 2 seconds. These results demonstrate its efficiency, fairness, and suitability for diverse Permissioned Blockchain applications.

title: SEMIKHORN: Globally balanced affinities for mmWave Localization in MU mMIMO systems.
abstract: This work conceives SEMIKHORN, a semi-supervised channel charting (CC) framework for mmWave localization, which leverages t-SNEkhorn, a doubly stochastic variant of t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) that utilizes entropic optimal transport to construct pairwise similarities. Unlike standard t-SNE, which normalizes affinities independently for each data point, t-SNEkhorn generates globally balanced similarities ensuring consistent neighborhood representation. We consider wireless networks with distributed base stations (BSs) equipped with multiple antennas, where each BS constructs a local dissimilarity matrix from the channel state information (CSI). These local dissimilarity matrices are then fused to obtain a single global dissimilarity matrix, which is processed through manifold learning to embed users onto a geometric map. The performance is evaluated in a simulated outdoor environment, and Bayesian optimization is employed on the framework hyperparameters to minimize the mean localization error (MLE). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an MLE of 6.86% in a circular vicinity of radius 100m, requiring less than 15% of labeled CSI samples.

title: A Novel Relaying-Scheme for Diffusive Molecular Communication Systems.
abstract: This paper elaborates on diffusive wave relaying. This new relaying technique is a scalable alternative to existing strategies, which does not rely on time synchronization. Furthermore, the number of different types of messenger molecules does not scale with the number of used relays. Information propagates in wave-like releases of molecules from the transmitter towards the receiver. We identify the slipstream phenomenon as a fundamental problem resulting in collapses of consecutive waves, prohibiting transmissions of multiple bits. To solve this problem, we propose three relaying strategies, named delay-based separation (DBS), steady-state separation (SSS) and threshold-based separation (TBS), and validate them through computer simulations. Moreover, we derive theoretical limitations in terms of bit rates and robustness.

title: Optimal EPFD-Compliant Power Control for QoS-Aware GEO/LEO Coexistence.
abstract: We introduce a Quality-of-Service-aware optimization framework for the coexistence of GEO and LEO satellites under realistic Equivalent Power Flux Density (EPFD) constraints as part of a Mixed Integer Linear Problem (MILP) formulation of adaptive LEO transmission power within a Cognitive Radio GEO/LEO setting. The EPFD constraints are derived via a generally applicable simulation-based methodology, in terms of satellite antenna capabilities and GEO Ground Station positions, which uses actual satellite orbital data, for improved accuracy, without any static exclusion zones. A polynomial-time complexity Greedy heuristic, named GRE, is also proposed as an alternative to the exact MILP solution and is shown, via simulation, to achieve optimally zero outage for LEO constellation sizes of 800 LEOs, for a LEO Ground User minimum Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) threshold up to 10 dB.

title: RASP: Reliability-Aware SINR Prediction for Realistic Industrial Subnetworks.
abstract: Industrial networks often demand hyper-reliable, low-latency communication (HRLLC) to support closed-loop control and automation. However, performance is severely undermined by dynamic fluctuations caused by unknown interferers, making it difficult to uphold reliability requirements. Channel statistics and mobility of interferers lead to significant variations in perceived signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). To cope with such interference dynamics, predictive resource allocation is required, whereby resource selection must be determined before transmission, making SINR prediction essential. This paper introduces Reliability-Aware SINR Prediction (RASP), a probabilistic framework that predicts the SINR distribution under explicit block error rate (BLER) constraints. RASP employs a Mixture Density Network within a Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR)-based primal–dual optimization scheme to adapt streaming SINR samples while satisfying reliability constraints. Based on real-world industrial measurements with co-subband interferers, we show that RASP achieves the target BLER of 10−6at the 95th percentile across three distinct scenarios, outperforming the baselines by a significant margin.

title: RIS-Enabled Spoofing Against Adversary Sensing: CRB-Maximizing Design and Decoying Analysis.
abstract: This paper studies the capability of a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS), when transparently covering a User Equipment (UE), to deceive an adversary monostatic radar system. A compact RIS kernel model that explicitly links the radar’s angular response to the RIS phase profile is introduced, which enables an analytical investigation of the Angle of Arrival (AoA) estimation accuracy with respect to the kernel’s power. This model is also leveraged to formulate an RIS-based spoofing design with the dual objective to enforce strict nulls around the UE’s true reflection AoA as well as maximize the channel gain toward a decoy direction. In addition, the RIS’s deception capability is quantified using point-wise and angle-range robust criteria, and a configuration-independent placement score guiding decoy selection is proposed. The presented numerical results confirm deep nulls at the true reflection AoA together with a pronounced decoy peak, a fact that eventually renders maximum-likelihood sensing at the adversary radar unreliable.

title: Multi-Periodogram Velocity Estimation with Irregular Reference Signals for Robot-Aided ISAC.
abstract: This paper addresses velocity estimation within robot-aided integrated sensing and communications (ISAC), where mobile robots act as sensing nodes but can only opportunistically reuse irregular 5G/6G reference signals (RSs). We show that the velocity profile induced by such irregular time-domain patterns can be decomposed into a periodic-peak component and an amplitude-shaping (weighting) component. Leveraging this structure, we propose a multi-periodogram velocity estimation algorithm that is standard-compliant and does not require new sensing-dedicated RSs or 3GPP modifications. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared with conventional periodogram processing, the proposed method improves low-SNR robustness by achieving a 3 dB SNR gain at the 10% missed-detection rate and reducing false alarms by 51%.

title: EARL: Energy-Aware Adaptive Antenna Control with Reinforcement Learning in O-RAN Cell-Free Massive MIMO Networks.
abstract: Cell-free massive multi-input multi-output (MIMO) promises uniform high performance across the network, but also brings a high energy cost due to joint transmission from distributed radio units (RUs) and centralized processing in the cloud. Leveraging resource-sharing capabilities of Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN), we propose EARL, an energy-aware adaptive antenna control framework using reinforcement learning. EARL dynamically configures antenna elements in RUs to minimize radio, optical fronthaul, and cloud processing power consumption while meeting user spectral efficiency demands. Numerical results show power savings of up to 81% and 50% over full-on and heuristic baselines, respectively. The RL-based approach operates within 220 ms, satisfying O-RAN’s near-real-time limit, and a greedy refinement further halves power consumption at a 2 s runtime.

title: Instantaneous Risk Minimization for Secure Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: To ensure worst-case physical layer security, this paper proposes a robust beamforming framework for secure integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Different from conventional designs that focus on maximizing the ergodic secrecy rate, the proposed method aims to minimize instantaneous information leakage risk. We formulate a multi-objective optimization problem that jointly suppresses the worst-case eavesdropper signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), improving sensing accuracy, and ensuring the quality of service (QoS) for legitimate users. To address the resulting non-convex problem, we develop a hierarchical iterative algorithm, in which the outer loop refines the continuous uncertainty regions based on the updated sensing performance, and the inner loop optimizes beamforming under the refined uncertainty regions. Theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves per-transmission security guarantees with practical complexity.

title: Towards Optimizing Reinforcement Learning Workload Placement at the Cloud-Edge Continuum in 6G Networks: A Scaled RL Framework.
abstract: With the increasing deployment of Reinforcement Learning (RL) for network optimization at the edge of wirelessnetworks, the RL workload emerges as a significant challenge. While the placement of general Machine Learning workloadsacross the cloud–edge continuum has been widely studied, existing solutions typically exclude RL techniques due to theirdistinct structure and operational requirements. In this work, we propose a framework for RL workload placement in thecloud–edge continuum, enabling the scaling of RL actor processes across both domains. In this framework, agents that interact with the environment through simple feedback loops are deployed at the edge, while training and model storage are performed in the cloud, where sufficient computational resources are available. We implement and simulate a prototype of one scaled RL actor that performs Quality-of-Service-aware resource block assignment with separate threads for environment interaction, inference, buffering/sampling, and the learning process. Finally, we outline the open challenges of the proposed framework.

title: AI-Assisted Next-Gen Outdoor Optical Networks: Camera Sensing for Monitoring and User Localization.
abstract: We consider outdoor optical access points (OAPs), which driven by recent advances in metasurface technology have gained increasing attention. Despite offering high data rates and strong physical-layer security, real-world deployments remain vulnerable to misuse, motivating a dedicated monitoring layer. We propose a user positioning and monitoring system that infers locations from spatial intensity measurements on a photodetector (PD) array. Our hybrid framework combines an optics-informed forward model and sparse, model-based inversion with a lightweight data-driven calibration stage, achieving high accuracy at low computational cost while retaining interpretability, stability, and robustness to nonidealities and device-specific distortions. Under identical hardware and training conditions (both with 5 × 105samples), the hybrid method attains consistently lower mean-squared error than a generic deep-learning baseline while using substantially less training time and compute. Accuracy improves with array resolution and saturates around 60×60–80×80, indicating a favorable accuracy–complexity trade-off for real-time deployment. The resulting position estimates can be cross-checked with real-time network logs to enable continuous monitoring, anomaly detection (e.g., potential eavesdropping), and access control in outdoor optical access networks.

title: Beamforming Design in Dynamic Metasurface Antenna-Assisted Multicarrier ISAC Systems.
abstract: We study a multicarrier integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system where a base station (BS) equipped with a dynamic metasurface antenna (DMA) simultaneously supports multiple users and radar sensing. The subcarriers are divided into two disjoint sets: one for user communications and the other for radar sensing. We consider the frequency response of DMA elements under a Lorentzianconstrained model. The objective is to maximize the minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) among all users, while satisfying radar SINR constraints, the BS transmit power budget, and DMA weight constraints. To this end, we jointly optimize the communication and radar beamforming vectors and the DMA weights. Due to the non-convex nature of the problem, we employ an alternating optimization framework to iteratively solve two decoupled subproblems. Simulation results show that the Lorentzian-constrained DMA design provides about a 80% gain over random DMA weights.

title: Graph-Based Collaborative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for 6G V2X Power and Spectrum Management.
abstract: The advent of sixth-generation (6G) networks is transforming Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications by enabling ultra-low latency, massive connectivity, and high energy efficiency. However, because of interference, mobility, and decentralized decision-making constraints, the dynamic and dense nature of vehicular environments makes power and spectrum coordination particularly challenging. To address these challenges, in this paper, we propose a Graph-based Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (G-MADRL) framework for a collaborative energy-efficient spectrum and power management in 6G V2X networks. By representing vehicles and roadside units as nodes in a dynamic graph, the proposed approach enables agents to share contextual information through graph attention, allowing coordinated and topology-aware resource allocation. The framework jointly optimizes energy efficiency, spectral utilization, and fairness under Quality-of-Service constraints. Simulation results obtained from the MVX co-simulation platform demonstrate that G-MADRL achieves higher spectral and energy efficiency as compared to traditional methods.

title: Foundation Model-Aided Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning for Blockage-Aware Link in RIS-Assisted Networks.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) technology has the potential to significantly enhance the spectral efficiency (SE) of 6G wireless networks. However, practical deployment remains constrained by challenges in accurate channel estimation and control optimization under dynamic conditions. This paper presents a foundation model-aided hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (FM-HDRL) framework designed for joint beamforming and phase-shift optimization in RIS-assisted wireless networks. To implement this, we first fine-tune a pre-trained large wireless model (LWM) to translate raw channel data into low-dimensional, context-aware channel state information (CSI) embeddings. Next, these embeddings are combined with user location information and blockage status to select the optimal communication path. The resulting features are then fed into an HDRL model, assumed to be implemented at a centralized controller, which jointly optimizes the base station (BS) beamforming vectors and the RIS phase-shift configurations to maximize SE. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed FM-HDRL framework consistently outperforms baseline methods in terms of convergence speed, spectral efficiency, and scalability. According to the simulation results, our proposed method improves 7.82% SE compared to the FM-aided deep reinforcement learning (FM-DRL) approach and a substantial enhancement of about 48.66% relative to the beam sweeping approach.

title: Leveraging Analytical TAS Bounds for Latency and Jitter Compliance Evaluation.
abstract: Time Aware Shaper (TAS), defined in IEEE 802.1Qbv, in conjunction with periodic time synchronization, defined in IEEE 802.1AS, is designed to guarantee bounded and deterministic latency and jitter for periodic time-sensitive traffic. However, device clock drift can cause timing misalignments, requiring compensation to preserve determinism. Delay-based scheduling achieves this by deferring frame transmission until frame reception is guaranteed, mitigating the impact of clock drift. Building on previous work that derived analytical latency and jitter bounds for streams, this paper determines the maximum synchronization periodicity that satisfies these timing requirements of all streams while minimizing network overhead due to synchronization. Simulation-based case studies are presented to validate the effectiveness of the framework in realistic networks.

title: Privacy-Preserving 3D Spectrum Sharing for UAVs via Semantic Geo-Indistinguishability and Protection Location Sets.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are emerging as agile secondary users in dynamic spectrum sharing, where real-time coordination with spectrum access systems enables coexistence with incumbent primary users. However, continuous reporting of UAV positions, beam orientations, and interference margins exposes critical vulnerabilities, allowing adversaries to infer flight trajectories, mission objectives, or protected infrastructure. This paper presents a privacy-preserving spectrum-sharing framework that integrates 3D semantic geo-indistinguishability (SemGI) with protection location sets (PLSs) to achieve formally quantifiable location privacy under interference and regulatory constraints. The proposed SemGI+PLS mechanism voxelizes the flyable airspace into spectrum-feasible cells, employs rotated 3D Hilbert indexing to exploit spatial locality, and applies a per-region exponential mechanism over a semantic curved-distance domain. This yields provable differential-privacy guarantees, a tunable distortion floor, and resistance to Bayesian inference attacks. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that the method achieves up to a 5-fold increase in attacker localization error in comparison with 3D-Laplace baselines, with negligible runtime overhead. The results establish a practical pathway toward AI-enabled, privacy-aware cognitive radio networks for UAV operations in 6G and beyond.

title: Assessing the Feasibility of Extended Fronthaul Networks in Centralized Open RAN Architectures.
abstract: One of the key innovations of 5G/6G, in particular in Open Radio Access Networks (RAN), is the openness of the fronthaul (O-FH) interface and its compression through the use of the eCPRI protocol, which boosts the performance between O-RU and O-DU by supporting higher data rates and new transmission schemes. Although it is commonly considered that the extension of O-FH networks is limited by the temporal requirements of the underlying RAN protocols, this study demonstrates that, by adjusting the O-DU transmission and reception intervals, it is possible to extend the distance between O-DU and O-RU beyond what has been considered so far in the state of the art. This would allow moving processing away from the cell site, favoring the adoption of centralized Open RAN architectures and better exploiting their benefits.

title: Network Flow Anomaly Detection using Unrolled Structure-Regularized Tensor Decomposition.
abstract: Anomaly detection (AD) in network flows for resilient communication systems is considered. While deep learning models can achieve state-of-the-art performance in AD tasks, the requirement for large data sets and their black box nature impedes their application in critical systems, where some level of explainability is desirable. To address these challenges, we tackle AD in network flows based on incomplete measurements by robust tensor decomposition and deep unrolling. We first derive a block successive convex approximation algorithm based on a data model that regularizes the normal flows as low-rank and correlated in time, and the anomalous flows as sparse and correlated in time. We subsequently unroll the proposed algorithm by expressing the regularization parameters as learnable weights of the deep network (DN). We extend the DN architecture with a convolutional neural network (CNN) that adapts to each instance of network flows. Simulations on both synthetic and real world data demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed DN architectures.

title: Multi-Slope RSSI-Based Localization for LoRa Transmitters in Avalanche Rescue Scenarios.
abstract: Search and Rescue (SaR) operations in avalanche scenarios rely on rapid and precise victim localization. Traditional ARTVA devices suffer from limited detection range, while LoRa technology has emerged as a promising alternative due to its long-range capabilities. This paper presents, for the first time, multi-slope path loss (PL) RSSI-based localization algorithm to real-world through-the-snow LoRa datasets. Controlled field tests show 75% accuracy within a 7 meters radius using data from a single search axis. Combining data from multiple axes, simulating a multi-operator SaR scenario, enables exact burial localization with zero error. These results underscore the potential of LoRa-based multi-slope localization as a robust alternative to conventional avalanche rescue systems.

title: Enhancing Resilience of Space Communications to Pulsed Jamming through Spatially Coupled Low-Density Parity-Check Codes.
abstract: It is well known that one of the most dangerous attacks against space transmissions is jamming. In particular, space telemetry downlinks are subject to extremely tight power and bandwidth limitations and are hence vulnerable to both accidental and intentional interference. While the Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS) has already standardized Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes for the use in space telemetry communications, we show that their performance is significantly deteriorated by the impact of pulsed jamming. We investigate the use of spatially coupled LDPC (SC-LDPC) codes as a promising alternative for improving reliability of telemetry channels in interference-heavy environments. We perform Monte Carlo simulations to assess the sensitivity of SC-LDPC-coded deep space communications to pulsed jamming, comparing attainable error rate performance with an LDPC code recommended in the CCSDS standard for telemetry synchronization and channel coding issues. Our results show that SC-LDPC codes can achieve improved performance, in terms of reduced bit error rate, under different pulsed jamming conditions.

title: Developing a Private 5G SA Network on a Raspberry Pi: All-In-One or Split RAN and CN?
abstract: The emergence of open-source software and commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware has facilitated new opportunities for private fifth generation (5G) network implementations and deployment. While most such implementations rely on a personal computer (PC) and/or a server, there is a growing interest in investigating the feasibility of running a private 5G standalone (SA) network entirely on low-cost hardware. In this paper, we present a lightweight private 5G SA implementation, which is built solely based on a Raspberry Pi 5 (RPi 5). Two architectures are designed, namely, I) an all-in-one solution where both radio access network (RAN) and core network (CN) operate on a single RPi 5; and II) a distributed setup with CN hosted separately on a PC. Using two open-source software suites, srsRAN and Open5GS, a prototype 5G SA network has been implemented and tested. Experiments with respect to end-to-end connectivity, high data rate demanding services, specifically 4k video streaming, and hardware resource utilization have been performed. Results demonstrate that an RPi 5 can effectively operate both RAN and CN under moderate load, revealing its potential as an affordable private 5G deployment platform.

title: Agentic AI-Driven Dynamic Algorithm Selection for 5G Antenna Tilt Optimization.
abstract: The rapid deployment of 5G networks has introduced unprecedented complexity in Radio Access Network (RAN) optimization, particularly in antenna tilt management, where the choice of algorithm significantly impacts performance. Traditional fixed tilt settings (e.g., 9°) applied uniformly across cells fail to adapt to spatiotemporal variations in user density and traffic, resulting in 30–50% performance deficits compared to optimal configurations, with edge-heavy scenarios suffering over 35% capacity degradation. While recent AI-driven methods improve adaptability, they are limited to a single optimization paradigm, typically deep reinforcement learning or heuristic bargaining, missing scenario-specific algorithmic strengths.This paper presents an agentic AI-driven meta-selector that dynamically chooses the optimal algorithm from a heterogeneous portfolio: Fixed Tilt, Nash Bargaining Solution (NBS), Weighted NBS (WNBS), Kalai-Smorodinsky (KSBS), Shannon Entropy (SEBS), and Deep Q-Network (DQN). In single-cell deployments, it delivers 50.02% capacity gain over fixed tilt and 3.93% over NBS. In multi-cell environments, it maintains 31.80% gain over Fixed and near-perfect fairness (JFI = 1.000). Under extreme loads (10–300 users/cell), the AI agent sustains 2–8% better performance than individual algorithms, with WNBS excelling in coverage and NBS in fairness resilience. The end-to-end pipeline executes in low latency, integrates with O-RAN RIC via E2 interfaces, and reduces manual configuration effort significantly, enabling fully autonomous, scenario-aware optimization.

title: Multivariate Polynomial Codes for Efficient Matrix Chain Multiplication in Distributed Systems.
abstract: We study the problem of computing matrix chain multiplications in a distributed computing cluster. In such systems, performance is often limited by the straggler problem, where the slowest worker dominates the overall computation latency. To resolve this issue, several coded computing strategies have been proposed, primarily focusing on the simplest case: the multiplication of two matrices. These approaches successfully alleviate the straggler effect, but they do so at the expense of higher computational complexity and increased storage needs at the workers. However, in many real-world applications, computations naturally involve long chains of matrix multiplications rather than just a single two-matrix product. Extending univariate polynomial coding to this setting has been shown to amplify the costs—both computation and storage overheads grow significantly, limiting scalability. In this work, we propose two novel multivariate polynomial coding schemes specifically designed for matrix chain multiplication in distributed environments. Our results show that while multivariate codes introduce additional computational cost at the workers, they can dramatically reduce storage overhead compared to univariate extensions. This reveals a fundamental trade-off between computation and storage efficiency, and highlights the potential of multivariate codes as a practical solution for large-scale distributed linear algebra tasks.

title: Multi-Modal Generative Learning Aided Task Scheduling for Satellite Networks.
abstract: Satellite-Ground Integrated Networks (SGINs) represent a promising network architecture designed to enhance access functions for ground users. This approach facilitates the release of additional network resources, reduces loading overhead, and improves channel capacity. Nevertheless, the presence of extensive multi-modal information, including stochastic task types, dynamic satellite locations, and time-varying channel gains, impedes the enhancement of service quality. We propose a multimodal integrated federated quantisation and privacy protection model aimed at reducing network latency and privacy overhead. This study investigates a transformer-based group relative policy optimisation (GRPO) algorithm aimed at optimising CPU cycle frequency, quantisation bit count, and block size, thereby enhancing the integration of communication, computation, and privacy resources. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GRPO algorithm outperforms advanced baseline methods in local execution latency, transmission quantisation latency, and model verification latency.

title: FedSplitKAN: A Federated Split Temporal KAN Framework for Bandwidth-Latency Optimization over Edge-IoT Networks.
abstract: In Smart Cities (SCs), edge Internet-of-Things (IoT) networks often adopt Split Learning (SL) to cope with narrow uplinks. SL allows transmitting smashed activations rather than full Federated Learning (FL) gradients. A federated extension of SL, SplitFed, or Federated SL (FSL) decentralizes aggregation across clients. However, because activation size grows with the sequence horizon and intermediate width, it still encounters bandwidth and latency bottlenecks. To address this limitation, the paper presents FedSplitKAN, which integrates the SplitFed mechanism with Temporal Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (TKANs). TKAN encoders are placed on client devices with a KAN head at the server. It decomposes multivariate streams into sums of univariate spline transforms. The framework assures compact, smooth activations with width directly controllable at the client, where raw features and labels never leave the device. We cast the model training as a bandwidth-latency joint optimization problem. A Learnable Partitioning and Split Activation (LPSA) controller is designed that periodically selects the cut layer and activation width based on validation signals and current link/device conditions. Across smart-city benchmarks, FedSplitKAN reduces average per-round uplink volume by 45.23% versus baseline FL schemes. Compared to FSL, it trims activation size by 30% and lowers training latency by 25%. Relative to vanilla FSL, it cuts cumulative uplink by 35.23% and end-to-end time by 40.12%, while SplitFedKAN-v2 stabilizes at Huber ≈ 0.139, a ≈44% reduction vs v1 and within ≈24% of the centralized KAN reference. Thus, the proposed framework presents a unified bandwidth-aware split control design for real-time resource-constrained and heterogeneous edge-IoT networks.

title: EVM Analysis for Pulse-Shaped SC-FDMA: Evaluation and Implementation.
abstract: Single-Carrier Localized Frequency Division Multiple Access (SC-LFDMA) offers a lower Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR) than OFDM, improving mobile device energy efficiency. However, residual PAPR and nonlinear High Power Amplifiers (HPAs) still degrade signal quality. This work applies pulse shaping to reduce PAPR and spectral leakage, jointly evaluating its impact on Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) and Symbol Error Rate (SER) for SC-LFDMA at a certain roll-off factor, α. Among the pulses considered, the Improved Dual Sinc Pulse (IDSP) shows the lowest PAPR and adequate EVM, while its SER performance is more sensitive to nonlinear effects under LFDMA transmission via computer-based simulations. Hardware tests using a Lime Software Defined Radio (SDR)-based Radio Frequency (RF) setup in an indoor environment confirm IDSP’s advantage, with up to 0.61% EVM improvement in simulations and 6.90% gain in measurements compared to the conventional Raised-Cosine (RC) pulse.

title: Distributed Sensing for Estimating Signal Strengths in Log-Normal Fading.
abstract: Spectrum sharing with an incumbent provider imposes constraints on entrants to limit the associated interference. Existing designs use conservative models of the propagation environment and worst-case entrant power levels for ensuring protection, leading to spectral inefficiency. In this paper, we present a new approach for estimating entrant transmission powers based on real-time distributed sensor measurements. This knowledge is vital information that can then be used to infer aggregate interference at an incumbent receiver location, or for other purposes such as such as spectrum monitoring and enforcement. We propose a computationally efficient two stage estimation algorithm based on a maximum likelihood objective with log-normal fading and exponential noise, and present numerical results illustrating performance.

title: Frame-Aware Resilient ADR for Relay-Connected LoRaWAN IoT Networks.
abstract: In low-power wide-area networks (LPWANs) such as LoRaWAN, Adaptive Data Rate (ADR) mechanisms are essential to balance reliability and energy efficiency. However, conventional ADR relies on gateway-observed PHY metrics, such as RSSI and SNR, which are not directly available to end devices (EDs) communicating via relays in battery-constrained, computation-limited IoT deployments. In addition, the LoRaWAN Relay Specification sets the relay-ED link to SF9, limiting adaptability and resulting in inefficient airtime use in dense networks. To address these limitations, this paper proposes FAFF-ADR, a Network Server (NS)-centric ADR mechanism that adapts the spreading factors (SFs) of relay-connected EDs primarily using delivery ratio inferred from frame counters (WFCnt), without requiring metric computation or reporting from EDs or relays. By comparing expected and received uplink frames over a sliding observation window, the NS indirectly estimates link reliability and triggers SF updates using lightweight application-layer downlink commands. To prevent harmful SF inflation under congestion and collision-driven losses, relay–gateway (GW) RSSI/SNR metadata is used as an auxiliary indicator to suppress unnecessary SF increases. Mathematical validation using SNR–SF decoding thresholds and Q-function-based FER modeling, supported by simulations under varying relay densities and interference conditions, demonstrates that FAFF-ADR converges toward near-optimal SF settings while improving reliability and scalability for relay-enabled LoRaWAN deployments in industrial environments.

title: Optimizing ML-Based Cloud-Native Autoscaling Models with XAI-Driven Variable Selection.
abstract: Autoscaling mechanisms have emerged as essential tools that dynamically allocate resources based on demand. However, traditional autoscaling approaches, which often rely on static thresholds or opaque rule-based systems, lack transparency and can lead to resource inefficiencies. In this paper, we propose a novel SELECTOR-MONITOR framework that embeds explainable AI (XAI) into cloud-native autoscaling by integrating SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) directly into the decision loop. Our design uniquely combines interpretability with operational efficiency, enabling transparent, data-driven scaling decisions in production environments. We present a SHAP-guided, model-agnostic feature selection framework centered on a novel feature efficiency score (FES), defined as a weighted sum of accuracy retention, training-time reduction, and SHAP coverage. FES turns per-feature attributions into an actionable criterion for selecting compact top-k inputs across architectures (XGBoost, LSTM, and BiLSTM). Using the Alibaba cluster traces for resource utilization forecasting, FES identifies smaller feature subsets that preserve fidelity while reducing cost. For CPU forecasting, using k=4 features results in a 3.9% increase in MAE, and a 26.9% reduction in training time vs. the 6-feature baseline. For Memory forecasting with k=3, MAE increases by 4.8%, and training time reduces by 23.6%. XGBoost consistently attains the lowest MAE under comparable feature budgets, while models restricted to bottom-ranked features degrade sharply, underscoring the value of explainable, SHAP-driven selection. The proposed SHAP + FES pipeline yields lightweight, transparent predictors tailored to deployment constraints, offering a practical path to scalable, interpretable autoscaling in production environments.

title: Offline Meta-learning for Real-time Bandwidth Estimation.
abstract: Real-time video applications require dynamic bitrate adjustments based on network capacity, necessitating accurate bandwidth estimation (BWE). We introduce Ivy, a novel BWE method that leverages offline meta-learning to combat data drift and maximize user Quality of Experience (QoE). Our approach dynamically selects the most suitable BWE algorithm for current network conditions, enabling effective adaptation to changing environments without requiring live network interactions. We implemented our method in Microsoft Teams and demonstrated that Ivy can enhance QoE by 5.9% to 11.2% over individual BWE algorithms and by 6.3% to 11.4% compared to existing online meta heuristics. Additionally, we show that our method is more data efficient compared to online meta-learning methods, achieving up to 21% improvement in QoE while requiring significantly less training data.

title: DART: Extending On-Premise K8s via Automated Orchestration of Remote At-scale Testbeds.
abstract: Hybrid infrastructures integrate on-prem clusters, public clouds, and remote testbeds, requiring unified orchestration across heterogeneous platforms. However, Kubernetes’ declarative control plane natively governs in-cluster workloads, leaving external resources outside its scope of reconciliation. This architectural limitation forces operators to rely on fragmented toolchains and imperative APIs that lack Kubernetes’ reconciliation and self-healing capabilities. In this paper, we introduce Dynamic Automated Resource Tethering (DART), a control plane extension that enables Kubernetes to orchestrate heterogeneous external resources. DART leverages a native reconciliation loop to provide comprehensive lifecycle management of heterogeneous external resources, encompassing Chameleon cloud testbeds (OpenStack) and remote Kubernetes clusters. This capability addresses a critical gap in orchestrating distributed infrastructures by enabling consistent, automated control across previously siloed environments. We implement DART using a Crossplane-based controller stack that bridges on-premise Kubernetes environments with at-scale external testbeds such as Chameleon Cloud and Anvil Kubernetes resources. Through cross-provider evaluations on OpenStack and Kubernetes back-ends, DART achieves 100% provisioning reliability and latencies on par with native OpenStack (17–19 seconds for VMs and 12–16 seconds for volumes), while maintaining negligible control-plane overhead (+1.4 percentage points (pp) CPU, +25 MiB memory). DART’s dependency-aware reconciliation engine reduces tail convergence time by ≃80%, enabling robust self-healing and fault recovery even under controller restarts and transient infrastructure failures. DART is the first system to unify declarative lifecycle management across heterogeneous remote substrates, proving that Kubernetes’ control plane can serve as a stable foundation for universal, cross-domain orchestration without compromising performance or fault tolerance.

title: Power-Efficient Edge-Based Keyword Spotting for Remote Patient Monitoring Systems.
abstract: Incorporating Internet of Things (IoT) devices into Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) systems has created new edge-based avenues to improve responsiveness and usability. Speech recognition via neural networks is an example of a strategy to enhance human–machine interactions in RPM systems. However, the current paradigm shift towards edge-based IoT applications has raised concerns about device power consumption. This is due to the high processing requirements of managing the neural network at the edge. In response, we propose a low-power Keyword Spotting (KWS) approach based on dynamic time warping to address the power challenge. We designed a testbed to compare our proposed KWS design with a speech recognition configuration based on a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The accuracy test yielded 75% for our KWS design and 93% for the CNN configuration, while the power consumption test significantly favors our design, demonstrating a 98.4% improvement.

title: SelfAdv-DA: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Framework for Robust Intrusion Detection in IoT Networks.
abstract: The proliferation of IoT devices in 5G/6G networks has significantly expanded the cyberattack surface, challenging Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) due to domain shifts between training and deployment environments. This paper introduces SelfAdv-DA, an unsupervised domain adaptation framework for robust cross-domain intrusion detection without labeled target data. Our approach integrates adversarial training with maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) for feature alignment, and employs confidence-calibrated pseudo-labeling with temperature scaling for reliable self-training. The framework employs a multi-scale feature encoder and progressive adaptation pipeline that systematically combines adversarial learning, distribution alignment, and consistency regularization. Extensive evaluation on NSL-KDD to Bot-IoT adaptation demonstrates state-of-the-art performance with 94.24% accuracy, significantly outperforming existing methods by substantial margins. SelfAdv-DA provides an effective solution for securing IoT ecosystems where labeled training data is scarce or unavailable, offering robust adaptation capabilities for real-world communication networks.

title: Channel Modeling Based on 3D Gaussian Splatting for Outdoor Urban Scenarios.
abstract: Wireless channel modeling in complex environments is crucial for next-generation communication systems. Traditional statistical methods face challenges in prediction accuracy and efficiency. Recent neural network-based approaches, particularly leveraging techniques from computer graphics such as Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), have shown promising results in channel modeling. However, existing methods have two primary limitations: (1) limited physical interpretability; and (2) lack of validation in real-world outdoor scenarios, which stems from insufficient channel data in large-scale outdoor scenarios. In this paper, a channel modeling method based on 3DGS is proposed to improve physical interpretability and enhance effectiveness in real-world outdoor scenarios. To address the challenge of measurement data collection, the model is first trained on a synthetic dataset generated by a ray tracing simulator, then fine-tuned using sparsely collected data from field campaign. The upper mid band (7-24 GHz) is used for both synthetic and real-world data collection, as its large bandwidth and excellent propagation characteristics make it a strong candidate for next-generation communications systems. Experimental results demonstrate that, despite using limited measurement data, the proposed method achieves higher channel prediction accuracy than existing approaches in real-world outdoor scenarios.

title: Universal Costas Matrices: Towards a General Framework for Costas Array Construction.
abstract: Costas arrays are a special type of permutation matrices with ideal autocorrelation and low cross-correlation properties, making them valuable for radar, wireless communication, and integrated sensing and communication applications. This paper presents a novel unified framework for analyzing and discovering new Costas arrays. We introduce Universal Costas Matrices (UCMs) and Universal Costas Frequency Matrices (UCFMs) and investigate their structural characteristics. A framework integrating UCMs and UCFMs is proposed to pave the way for future artificial intelligence-assisted Costas array discovery. Leveraging the structural properties of UCMs and UCFMs, a reconstruction-based search method is developed to generate UCMs from UCFMs. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly accelerates the search process and enhances structural insight into Costas array generation.

title: Secure Low-Altitude Activities: Joint ISAC Beamforming and RIS Phase-Shift Matrix Design.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a promising solution for efficient low-altitude uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) operations. However, the existing works usually lack RIS-enabled anti-eavesdropping mechanisms, making it challenging to ensure secure low-altitude operations. To address this gap, we envision a novel secure low-altitude application scenario, where a ground ISAC platform communicates with aerial UAVs while simultaneously sensing and interfering with malicious eavesdroppers using dedicated artificial noise. Meanwhile, an active RIS is introduced to not only enhance communication performance but also provide supplementary non-line-of-sight (NLoS) links for sensing and security when line-of-sight (LoS) links are blocked. A novel optimization is established to jointly optimize communication/sensing/security precoders and RIS phase-shift matrix, with the goal of maximizing sensing signal-to-clutter-noise ratio (SCNR), under the constraints of communication and security performance. A maximization-minimization (MM) algorithm and a semi-definite relaxation (SDR) are proposed to solve this non-convex complex problem. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms and the superiority of the anti-eavesdropping mechanism, with the SINR of malicious eavesdroppers significantly reduced by 5 dB.

title: Sum-Rate Maximization for Transmissive RIS Transceiver-Empowered SWIPT Systems.
abstract: This paper studies a simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) system empowered by a novel transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surface (TRIS) transceiver. Based on the system model, we consider the design of transmit beamforming at the TRIS transceiver to maximize the sum-rate of all information decoding (ID) users. The design is subject to per-antenna transmit power limits at the TRIS and to a minimum harvested-energy constraint imposed on all energy harvesting (EH) users. The non-convexity of the objective and the EH constraint render the problem hard to solve. To solve this challenging optimization problem, by leveraging the weighted minimum mean squared error (WMMSE) framework and the majorization-minimization (MM) method, we propose an iterative algorithm to obtain a high-quality solution. Numerical results are provided to validate the convergence and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: Optimizing Beamforming for Integrated Sensing and Communications in PASS.
abstract: The joint optimization of pinching antenna positions and transmit beamforming in a pinching antenna system for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is investigated. The optimization problem of maximizing sensing rate (SR) while satisfying minimal communication rate (CR) requirements is first modeled, where the segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna (SWAN) system is adopted to mitigate the impact of in-waveguide attenuation and improve sensing performance. Then, an alternative optimization (AO) algorithm for SWAN-based ISAC (SWISAC-AO) is proposed to solve the problem, where the optimal solution structure of transmit beamforming is derived. The algorithm is efficient by searching PA positions with one-dimensional searching and computing the transmit beamforming matrix with the solution structure. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can achieve higher SR and better satisfy the CR requirements than baseline methods in PASS and conventional antenna systems.

title: Beamforming Design for Beyond Diagonal RIS Assisted Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: Beyond diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS) has emerged as a promising technology for advancing integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. While existing studies primarily focus on communication-centric objectives like sum-rate maximization, the potential of BD-RIS for sensing-oriented optimization remains largely unexplored. We investigate the sensing performance in BD-RIS empowered ISAC under three architectures: fully-, group-, and single-connected. The BD-RIS reflection matrix’s orthogonality and symmetry constraints pose significant optimization challenges. To address these, we develop a penalty dual decomposition (PDD) based algorithm to maximize the radar signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) under communication quality, BD-RIS reflection matrix, and transmit power constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the fully-connected RIS achieves the highest sensing performance compared to traditional RIS, while the group-connected RIS offers a favorable trade-off between complexity and performance, providing valuable insights for future ISAC system design.

title: Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models with LoRA and RSMA-Based Client Scheduling.
abstract: Fine-tuning large language models serves as one of the core technologies for improving LLM performance. To mitigate privacy risks inherent in centralized fine-tuning and the substantial communication burden in wireless distributed settings, we introduce FedRS-LoRA, a Low-Rank Adaptive Federated Fine-Tuning framework. This framework exploits the low-rank structure of model parameters by integrating Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA), thereby significantly reducing communication overhead. By leveraging a Top-k hierarchical parameter selection strategy, the framework addresses client heterogeneity in communication resources to achieve efficient federated fine-tuning and aggregation. Additionally, an iterative client scheduling mechanism is employed to boost fine-tuning performance without incurring extra communication costs. Simulation results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing baseline strategies in both convergence accuracy and speed, while achieving aggregation performance that approaches ideal federated learning benchmarks—thereby striking an effective balance among communication efficiency, scalability, and model performance.

title: CSVAR: Enhancing Visual Privacy in Federated Learning via Adaptive Shuffling Against Overfitting.
abstract: Although federated learning preserves training data within local privacy domains, the aggregated model parameters may still reveal private characteristics. This vulnerability stems from clients’ limited training data, which predisposes models to overfitting. Such overfitting enables models to memorize distinctive patterns from training samples, thereby amplifying the success probability of privacy attacks like membership inference. To enhance visual privacy protection in FL, we present CSVAR(Channel-Wise Spatial Image Shuffling with Variance-Guided Adaptive Region Partitioning), a novel image shuffling framework to generate obfuscated images for secure data transmission and each training epoch, addressing both overfitting-induced privacy leaks and raw image transmission risks. CSVAR adopts region-variance as the metric to measure visual privacy sensitivity across image regions. Guided by this, CSVAR adaptively partitions each region into multiple blocks, applying fine-grained partitioning to privacy-sensitive regions with high region-variances for enhancing visual privacy protection and coarse-grained partitioning to privacy-insensitive regions for balancing model utility. In each region, CSVAR then shuffles between blocks in both the spatial domains and chromatic channels to hide visual spatial features and disrupt color distribution. Experimental evaluations conducted on diverse real-world datasets demonstrate that CSVAR is capable of generating visually obfuscated images that exhibit high perceptual ambiguity to human eyes, simultaneously mitigating the effectiveness of adversarial data reconstruction attacks and achieving a good trade-off between visual privacy protection and model utility.

title: CHASE: Collaborative Hypergraph Task Scheduling for Green Distributed Edge Computing.
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) services drive computation to the edge, Distributed Edge Computing (DEC) has emerged as a key paradigm, where a central logical entity is responsible for decomposing requests into tasks for distributed resource pools. However, global performance is fundamentally limited because the decisions of this entity, which we model as a gateway, are rarely jointly optimized with the local scheduling within each heterogeneous resource pool. Achieving this joint optimization through Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) faces two core challenges: inordinate resource waste from inadequate state representation and excessive energy consumption from inaccurate decision-making. In this paper, we propose a collaborative hypergraph task scheduling framework, namely CHASE. To address inadequate state representation, we employ a hypergraph-based state representation to capture complex, multi-way task relationships for more holistic and energy-aware partitioning. To resolve inaccurate decision-making, we establish a hierarchical collaborative learning architecture with a cross-layer feedback mechanism to dynamically synchronize the gateway’s partitioning plan with the dispatchers’ real-time scheduling actions. Finally, the evaluations using real-world traces demonstrate CHASE significantly improves energy efficiency.

title: Flow Matching for Joint Channel Estimation and Symbol Detection in Massive MIMO.
abstract: Conventional receivers for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems estimate the channel from pilots and then detect payload symbols, a separation that propagates estimation errors and neglects information in the payload. We propose a training-free solver that embeds optimal-transport (OT) flow matching into the joint estimation pipeline. Our method repurposes a single, pretrained score network to generate a channel flow and couples it with a fast Langevin payload refinement loop and a time-gated likelihood correction. This staged approach leverages known pilot information to secure the channel estimate before progressively introducing payload-based gradients. Across a representative signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) sweep, our solver matches the Langevin baseline by the mid-SNR regime and surpasses it at higher SNR or larger payloads, while cutting wall-clock runtime by over 5× through an order-of-magnitude reduction in neural function evaluations.

title: A Visible Light Communication Channel Modeling Approach Based on Ray Tracing in Computer Vision.
abstract: A novel channel modeling framework for visible light communication (VLC) is proposed by introducing ray-tracing operators from computer vision into optical wireless simulations. Built on the NVIDIA Falcor platform, the framework incorporates communication-related physical quantities such as delay, power, and wavelength, while employing next event estimation (NEE) and multiple importance sampling (MIS) to achieve unbiased path estimation with high efficiency. The proposed method is validated against MATLAB simulations, Zemax, and real-world measurements. Results demonstrate that the approach provides accuracy comparable to conventional methods while offering significant computational speedup, highlighting its potential as a scalable tool for realistic VLC channel modeling and simulation.

title: Energy-Efficient Resource Management for Multimodal LAM Inference in Emergency-Response End-Edge-Cloud Systems.
abstract: With the explosive development of large AI models (LAMs), their potential applications in scenarios such as emergency response have attracted increasing attention. At the same time, the unique characteristics and heavy computational demands of LAMs pose new challenges for designing communication networks. In this paper, we propose an end-edge-cloud collaborative inference architecture to support multimodal LAM inference requests generated by heterogeneous agents’ ends in emergency response. An AI-native radio access network (RAN) and a cloud computing center jointly minimize total inference energy consumption through coordinated computing capability allocation and computation offloading, while satisfying end-to-end latency requirements. Concretely, we first develop a multimodal traffic model for LAM inference requests based on real LAM request traffic data. We then analyze the inference characteristics of LAMs in depth, explicitly modeling the impact of token-level length and LAM neural network structures on floating-point operations, and further incorporate GPU batch parallelism into the resulting latency model. To solve the inference energy-minimization problem, we adopt a proximal policy optimization (PPO)-based deep reinforcement learning algorithm and build a computational simulation environment based on an open-source platform to emulate realistic LAM execution. Experimental results show that, compared with baseline schemes, the proposed method achieves 20%–66% reduction in inference energy consumption under various system configurations.

title: Can ChannelLM Serve as Strong Priors for CSI Reconstruction under Extremely Sparse Pilots?
abstract: Accurate acquisition of channel state information (CSI) under extremely sparse pilot measurements remains a critical challenge for future AI-native wireless systems. Traditional deep learning approaches often suffer from severe performance degradation when the pilot overhead is aggressively reduced. In this paper, we investigate whether a channel large model (ChannelLM), instantiated by a frozen foundation LLM backbone, can serve as a strong structural prior for CSI reconstruction under extreme pilot scarcity. By embedding a frozen LLM backbone into an unfolded proximal reconstruction network, we show that foundation-model priors deliver markedly improved robustness over CNN- and GPT-style priors in the ultra-low pilot regime. In particular, under a 1% pilot ratio, ChannelLM improves the reconstruction correlation by 33% and reduces NMSE by 1.6 dB compared with the GPT-style prior. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves high reconstruction fidelity under moderate pilot budgets and maintains strong robustness when pilots become extremely sparse, highlighting the value of high-capacity foundation priors for AI-native channel learning.

title: Channel Prediction-Based Physical Layer Authentication under Consecutive Spoofing Attacks.
abstract: Wireless networks are highly vulnerable to spoofing attacks, especially when attackers transmit consecutive spoofing packets. Conventional physical layer authentication (PLA) methods have mostly focused on single-packet spoofing attack. However, under consecutive spoofing attacks, they become ineffective due to channel evolution caused by device mobility and channel fading. To address this challenge, we propose a channel prediction-based PLA framework. Specifically, a Transformer-based channel prediction module is employed to predict legitimate CSI measurements during spoofing interval, and the input of channel prediction module is adaptively updated with predicted or observed CSI measurements based on the authentication decision to ensure robustness against sustained spoofing. Simulation results under Rayleigh fading channels demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves low prediction error and significantly higher authentication accuracy than conventional benchmark, maintaining robustness even under extended spoofing attacks.

title: Testbed for Time-Frequency Robust Distributed Cooperative Jamming Cancellation in Physical-Layer Security.
abstract: Distributed cooperative jamming (DCJ) is one of the approaches to physical-layer security, which can significantly enhance the security of wireless communication networks. An efficient jamming cancellation (JC) algorithm is a fundamental prerequisite for creating channel disparity and ensuring secure communication. This paper designs a dedicated JC architecture tailored for DCJ scenarios and validates it on a hardware testbed platform. Experimental results show that the proposed architecture achieves a maximum JC capability of 27.86 dB, defined as the suppression of cooperative jamming power at the legitimate receiver, with an associated noise floor increase of approximately 5 dB. Under the DCJ transmission scenario and measured channel conditions, the system achieves a secure achievable rate of 3.75 bps/Hz.

title: OTFS-ISAC Systems with Aerial Targets: Hybrid Precoder Design and Radar Tracking.
abstract: Due to the availability of wide bandwidths in the frequency range 2 (FR2) band, sixth-generation (6G) networks can provide both radar and communication services using shared spectrum and hardware, reducing costs and enhancing efficiency via integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Motivated by the advantages of orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation in high-mobility scenarios, this paper proposes an iterative hybrid precoder design method and a radar tracking algorithm for OTFS-ISAC systems with aerial targets, i.e., drones. Information is sent to the ground user through communication links using the subarray hybrid precoder to balance radar and communication performance through a weighted summinimization framework. The cubature Kalman filter (CKF) is employed for radar prediction and tracking. Simulation results indicate that the proposed hybrid precoder design algorithm effectively balances radar and communication performance, while the CKF-based radar tracking method outperforms other nonlinear Kalman filters.

title: On the Localization Probability of RIS-Assisted Systems: A Stochastic Geometry Perspective.
