abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are envisioned as a key enabler for 6G wireless systems in both communication and localization. Despite recent progress, most existing studies rely on fixed RIS deployments or simplified system settings, leaving the theoretical feasibility of large-scale random deployments insufficiently understood. In this paper, we establish a rigorous analytical framework to quantify the localization performance of RIS-assisted systems under random spatial configurations of both obstacles and RISs. Using stochastic geometry, we characterize the statistical distribution of available propagation paths and derive localizability conditions via Fisher information analysis. Based on these results, a closed-form expression for the localization probability is obtained, enabling tractable performance evaluation under various network parameters. Theoretical analysis, further validated by Monte Carlo simulations, demonstrates the critical impact of RIS density, obstacle distribution, and communication range on localization feasibility. These findings provide a foundational understanding of RIS-enabled localization in large-scale random networks, offering a theoretical benchmark for future system design.

title: SDNR of nonlinearly amplified precoded massive MIMO transmissions in FR3 bands.
abstract: We propose a closed form expression of the Signalto-Distorsion-Noise Ratio (SDNR) for a downlink multi-user massive MIMO system. We consider the influence of the nonlinearity induced by a Rapp Power Amplifier (PA) of the RF chain assuming a perfect Channel State Information (CSI). We set the system power to ensure the PA is efficient and that the Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) is limited.

title: Towards identifying malicious intents using the Grubbs' test.
abstract: Malicious intents, or fraudulent slice requests that pose as authentic in order to interfere with network slicing infrastructures, pose a serious security risk as a result of the move to intent-based networking (IBN). This study examines this new attack vector by classifying malevolent intents into three main groups: Configuration Inconsistency, Quality of Service (QoS) Degradation, and Resource Exhaustion. We provide an AI-based approach that uses cross-domain detection concepts from domains like intrusion detection and social network security to proactively identify these dangers prior to their deployment. We test the model using the IW-IB-5GNET dataset, comparing the Grubbs Statistical Test for anomaly detection with a Fixed Threshold approach. Our findings show that the statistical approach successfully balances the trade-off between detecting a larger range of anomalies and preserving computational efficiency by offering a more sensitive and robust detection mechanism (84% accuracy) than the static rule-based method (62% accuracy). This study emphasizes how important it is to incorporate security at the intent level in order to protect future networks’ automation and dependability.

title: Near-field Extension of Analytical Reflection Model for Large-scale mmWave IRS Geometries in 6G.
abstract: In future 6G networks, large-scale apertures significantly extend the near-field (NF) to tens of meters, especially at millimeter-wave (mmWave) frequencies. This evolution challenges traditional far-field (FF)-centric communications, as users experience propagation conditions that differ markedly from FF model-driven predictions. Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) are anticipated to play a crucial role in 6G mmWave deployments by cost-effectively improving connectivity. Static IRSs, such as passive HELIOS geometries, have demonstrated high maturity levels in field experiments, successfully validating their capabilities. However, as shown in this work, large IRSs optimized for infinite FF behavior exhibit degraded performance in the NF, including reflection beam misalignment, broadening, magnitude reduction, and nulls. These effects can severely compromise the success of IRS-assisted 6G mmWave deployments if left unaddressed during the design phase. For this reason, we extend the analytical reflection model into the NF region. Validation through lab measurements and electromagnetic (EM) simulations confirms its enhanced accuracy in finite FF and radiative NF. The model predicts reflections at distances down to 50cm with up to 46.5%-pt. better correlation between the reflection patterns. These insights pave the way for optimizing NF-centric static-passive IRSs.

title: Cross-Domain Channel Estimation and Equalization For High Diversity Gains.
abstract: The intrinsic channel tap diversity is lost in the frequency domain one-tap channel estimation (CE), where all multipath components collapse into a single equivalent complex coefficient. Therefore, diversity enhancement solutions are typically shifted toward channel coding or multiple input multiple output (MIMO) schemes. In this paper, we propose a cross-domain path diversity aggregation to enhance the effective signal to noise ratio (SNR) of the received signal while maintaining full compatibility with the existing frame structure. Although affine domain can theoretically achieve high diversity order, we first demonstrate the limitations of iterative search based CE under frequency selective channels with fractional spreading. To overcome these issues, we introduce a hybrid-domain processing that employs the frequency-domain pilots-only symbol for CE, followed by a block of data symbols multiplexed in the affine domain. This design enables simple and accurate CE in the frequency domain while harnessing the diversity and equalization benefits of the affine domain, thereby providing inherent SNR enhancement without additional channel coding or MIMO extensions. Simulation results confirm that the proposed method achieves low BER and high achievable rates under severe frequency-selective conditions, approaching the performance of MIMO systems with significantly lower complexity.

title: EXPLoRa: EXP4-based Contextual Bandits for LoRa Networks.
abstract: LoRa is one of the most widely used Low Power Wide Area Network technologies, and its protocol, LoRaWAN, is designed for low energy consumption. However, the efficiency of LoRaWAN in terms of Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) and Energy Consumption (EC) significantly decreases as the number of End Devices (EDs) increases. This paper aims to enhance LoRaWAN performance with respect to PDR and EC using a Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB)-based Reinforcement Learning (RL) approach. In the proposed framework, EDs autonomously adjust their transmission parameters in a distributed manner, leveraging available contextual information to guide parameter selection. To this end, we propose a contextual bandit-based algorithm named EXPLoRa with expert guidance provided by the Distance-weighted eXponential Natural Evolution Strategy (DX-NES). Simulation results demonstrate that EXPLoRa achieves up to a 64% reduction in EC and a 62% improvement in PDR for single-gateway scenarios, and up to a 49% reduction in EC and a 25% improvement in PDR for multi-gateway scenarios, compared to state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, EXPLoRa exhibits faster convergence, stabilizing in nearly half the time required by conventional algorithms.

title: MSE-based Reduced-Dimension Regression for Full-Duplex Interference Estimation.
abstract: Principal Component Regression (PCR) is widely used for reduced-dimension regression, but its component selection based on predictor variance does not necessarily minimize residual error. In this work, we apply PCR to the problem of full-duplex (FD) self-interference cancellation (SIC) and derive a closed-form mean-squared-error (MSE) expression that explicitly characterizes the post-cancellation residual. Building on this analysis, we introduce a bias-aware component selection rule that estimates each component’s contribution to interference suppression without requiring oracle coefficients. This dual contribution, (i) an exact analytical link between discarded components and residual error, and (ii) a practical, low-overhead selection rule, enables near-optimal reduced-dimension regression under strong multicollinearity. In numerical evaluations with realistic IQ imbalance and nonlinearity, the proposed MSE-PCR consistently improves block error rate (BLER) and interference suppression over conventional and supervised PCR, while ensuring low estimation dimensionality, making it a practical solution for next-generation FD transceivers.

title: Explainable and Hardware-Efficient Jamming Detection for 5G Networks Using the Convolutional Tsetlin Machine.
abstract: All applications in fifth-generation (5G) networks rely on stable radio-frequency (RF) environments to support mission-critical services in mobility, automation, and connected intelligence. Their exposure to intentional interference or low-power jamming threatens availability and reliability, especially when such attacks remain below link-layer observability. This paper investigates lightweight, explainable, and hardware-efficient jamming detection using the Convolutional Tsetlin Machine (CTM) operating directly on 5G Synchronization Signal Block (SSB) features. CTM formulates Boolean logic clauses over quantized inputs, enabling bit-level inference and deterministic deployment on FPGA fabrics. These properties make CTM well suited for real-time, resource-constrained edge environments anticipated in 5G. The proposed approach is experimentally validated on a real 5G testbed using over-the-air SSB data, emulating practical downlink conditions. We benchmark CTM against a convolutional neural network (CNN) baseline under identical preprocessing and training pipelines. On the real dataset, CTM achieves comparable detection performance (Accuracy 91.53 +/- 1.01 vs. 96.83 +/- 1.19 for CNN) while training $9.5\times$ faster and requiring 14x less memory (45~MB vs.\ 624~MB). Furthermore, we outline a compact FPGA-oriented design for Zybo~Z7 (Zynq-7000) and provide resource projections (not measured) under three deployment profiles optimized for latency, power, and accuracy trade-offs. The results show that the CTM provides a practical, interpretable, and resource-efficient alternative to conventional DNNs for RF-domain jamming detection, establishing it as a strong candidate for edge-deployed, low-latency, and security-critical 5G applications while laying the groundwork for B5G systems.

title: CLOVER: Collaborative Adversarial Distillation and Budget-Aware Co-Inference for Sensor-Cloud Intelligence.
abstract: Sensor–cloud systems are increasingly critical for health, wearables, and industrial IoT, but face a persistent trilemma: edge-only models meet latency and bandwidth budgets but may lack robustness, cloud-only models offer accuracy yet can violate system constraints and privacy, and split computing inflates bandwidth while exposing sensitive data. We introduce CLOVER (Collaborative training and co-inference between Large and lightWEight models for sensoR-cloud networks), a unified framework that couples collaborative adversarial distillation, trusted execution environments (TEEs), and budget-aware scheduling. CLOVER advances sensor–cloud co-inference in several ways. First, Collaborative Adversarial Distillation (CAD) contracts decision-region divergence between heterogeneous edge/cloud models and transfers robustness to the edge, optionally guided by a Large Language Model (LLM), in our simulator. Second, privacy-preserving collaboration in a TEE with optional differential privacy achieves secure distillation with minimal simulated overheads. Third, a budget-aware router dynamically selects among Edge, Edge+Correction, and Cloud while enforcing explicit P95, energy, and bandwidth constraints under link variability in simulation. Across IMU and physiological modalities, CLOVER (TEE-on) improves robust accuracy by 61.7% over Edge-only and Cloud-only on UCI-HAR (about +62–64% relative), while keeping clean accuracy at cloud parity (about +3.3–3.5% points). Compared to Cloud-only, it cuts P95 latency by 56% (from 105.2 ms to 45.9 ms) and reduces bandwidth by 99.9% (from 337 kB/s to 0.26 kB/s), satisfying budgets of P95≤200 ms and BW≤50 kB/s. TEE deployment adds only +0.31% P95 and +8.3% bandwidth overhead. On MHEALTH, CLOVER attains 99.76% clean accuracy while remaining budget-compliant (P95≈46 ms, BW≈0.26 kB/s). Overall, CLOVER offers a practical path toward secure, real-time sensor–cloud intelligence, with empirical evidence obtained in a system-level simulator; the LLM components are optional and not required for the core results.

title: Adaptive DRL for IRS Mirror Orientation in Dynamic OWC Networks.
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) have emerged as a promising solution to mitigate line-of-sight (LoS) blockages and enhance signal coverage in optical wireless communication (OWC) systems with minimal additional power. In this work, we consider a mirror-based IRS to assist a dynamic indoor visible light communication (VLC) environment. We formulate an optimization problem that aims to maximize the sum rate by adjusting the orientation of the IRS mirrors. To enable real-time adaptability, the problem is modelled as a Markov decision process (MDP), and a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm is developed based on the deterministic policy gradient for real-time mirror-based IRS optimization in dynamic VLC networks. The proposed DRL is employed to optimize mirror orientation toward mobile users under blockage and mobility constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed DRL algorithm outperforms the conventional deep Q- learning (DQL) algorithm and achieves substantial improvements in sum rate compared to random-orientation IRS configurations

title: Intelligent Cross-Layer Management for Robust and Energy-Efficient IoE Communications.
abstract: Ensuring reliable communication and energy efficiency remains challenging in Internet of Everything (IoE) environments, where devices are heterogeneous, mobile, and energy-limited. This paper presents a cross-layer optimization framework that leverages the physical, data link, network, and transport layers to enable adaptive route selection, balanced traffic management, and energy-aware data transmission. Coordinating these layers improves data delivery, reduces latency, and extends device operational lifetime. Experimental results show a 24% increase in delivery rate, 0.85 ns reduction in latency, 37% longer device activity, and up to 35% energy savings. These findings demonstrate the framework’s effectiveness for robust, high-performance, and energy-efficient communication in heterogeneous IoE systems. Overall, this work provides a holistic cross-layer design integrating routing, traffic adaptation, and energy management for reliable and sustainable IoE networking.

title: A Transport Layer-Based Approach for Threat Detection in IoT Networks.
abstract: The rapid proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) has heightened exposure to diverse security threats, particularly Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, which underscore the limitations of traditional security mechanisms in protecting resource-constrained devices. This study introduces a novel threat detection framework that exploits transport layer congestion control features to detect security breaches in real time by monitoring key indicators such as packet loss, round-trip time (RTT), and retransmission rates. The proposed lightweight solution integrates machine learning techniques to effectively distinguish between genuine network congestion and congestion induced by malicious activity. Through extensive IoT simulations, the framework demonstrated a Detection Rate (DR) of 96% with a minimal False Positive Rate (FPR) of 1.2%. It further achieved a Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) of 95%, an average latency of 150 ms, a throughput of 5000 bytes/s, and a Response Time (RT) of 120 ms. These results confirm the framework’s ability to provide reliable, real-time IoT security while preserving high network performance.

title: Quotation-Based Data Retention Mechanism for Data Privacy in LLM-Empowered Network Services.
abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) for next-generation network optimization introduces novel data governance challenges. mobile network operators (MNOs) increasingly leverage generative artificial intelligence (AI) for traffic prediction, anomaly detection, and service personalization, requiring access to users' sensitive network usage data-including mobility patterns, traffic types, and location histories. Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), and similar regulations, users retain the right to withdraw consent and demand data deletion. However, extensive machine unlearning degrades model accuracy and incurs substantial computational costs, ultimately harming network performance for all users. We propose an iterative price discovery mechanism enabling MNOs to compensate users for data retention through sequential price quotations. The server progressively raises the unit price for retaining data while users independently determine their supply at each quoted price. This approach requires no prior knowledge of users' privacy preferences and efficiently maximizes social welfare across the network ecosystem.

title: SynthECN: A Transparent User-Space Mechanism for optimizing CCAs behavior.
abstract: Internet routers often build up queues under load, inflating delay. Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) mitigates this by marking packets as an early "slow down" signal instead of dropping them. Yet in today’s public and edge networks, ECN is often incomplete—many devices lack support—and frequently misaligned with the true bottleneck. In such cases, congestion control algorithms (CCAs) fall back to packet loss or heuristics, leading to persistent queues and poor tail latency.Our method, SynthECN, synthesizes the missing early signal: it monitors per-flow TCP metrics (RTT, loss, CE marks) via extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) and injects short, controlled CE pulses at the sender’s interface. This emulates the effect of a correctly placed ECN/AQM at the bottleneck. The mechanism runs entirely in user space and requires no kernel or CCA changes, ensuring deployability. To the best of our knowledge, no prior work has proposed a deployable endhost mechanism to compensate for absent or misaligned ECN. SynthECN is the first to fill this gap, and it does so in a CCA-agnostic manner.Experiments show that when ECN is absent or misaligned, SynthECN lowers average delay by 20–90% and cuts 95th-percentile latency by up to 50% without throughput loss. When ECN is correctly deployed, SynthECN remains transparent, matching baseline performance.

title: SDN-Blockchain Based Security Routing for UAV Communication via Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network plays important roles in emergency communications. However, it is challenging to design reliable routing strategies that ensure low latency, energy efficiency, and security in the dynamic and attack-prone environments. To this end, we design a secure routing architecture integrating software-defined networking (SDN) for centralized control and blockchain for tamper-proof trust management. In particular, a novel security degree metric is introduced to quantify the UAV trustworthiness. Based on this architecture, we propose a beam search-proximal policy optimization (BSPPO) algorithm, where beam search (BS) pre-screens the high-security candidate paths, and proximal policy optimization (PPO) performs hop-by-hop routing decisions to support dynamic rerouting upon attack detections. Finally, extensive simulations under varying attack densities, packet sizes, and rerouting events demonstrate that BSPPO outperforms PPO, BS-Q learning, and BS-actor critic in terms of delay, energy consumption, and transmission success rate, showing the outstanding robustness and adaptability.

title: Generative-AI-Enabled Onsite Learning Framework for Distribution-Aware Doppler Shift Estimation in AI-Native Wireless Networks.
abstract: Conventional transceiver designs that rely solely on instantaneous input–output relationships fail to leverage site-specific distributions, resulting in suboptimal performance across diverse deployment environments. To address this limitation, we propose a generative-AI-enabled onsite learning framework for site-specific estimator design, demonstrated through Doppler shift estimation as a representative use case. A generative adversarial network (GAN) incorporates local Doppler distributions learned from onsite data into the estimator design process, improving estimation accuracy under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. As GAN training can be unstable and input variability in onsite learning can further complicate this process, a pretrained feature encoder network maps the received signals to latent vectors and stores them as structured inputs to enable stable GAN training. Additionally, a novel onsite adversarial training strategy allows the GAN to generalize across diverse input signals while generating plausible samples conditioned on the instantaneous input. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms optimal analytical and deep learning-based estimators that are distribution-agnostic, achieving substantial gains under low-SNR and complex site-distribution conditions with sufficiently low complexity for real-time operation. These results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed framework as a low-complexity and robust solution for AI-native wireless systems in real-world scenarios.

title: Constellation Design in OFDM-ISAC over Data Payloads: From MSE Analysis to Experimentation.
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) is one of the most widely adopted waveforms for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, owing to its high spectral efficiency and compatibility with modern communication standards. This paper investigates the sensing performance of OFDM-based ISAC for multi-target delay (range) estimation under specific radar receiver processing schemes. An estimation-theoretic framework is developed to characterize sensing performance with random communication payloads. We establish the fundamental limit of delay estimation accuracy by deriving the closed-form expression of the mean-square error (MSE) achieved using matched filtering (MF) and reciprocal filtering (RF) receivers. The results show that, in multi-target scenarios, the impact of signal constellations on the delay estimation MSE differs across receivers: MF performance depends on the fourth-order moment of the zero-mean, unit-power constellation in the presence of multiple targets, whereas RF performance depends on its inverse second-order moment, irrespective of the number of targets. Building on this analysis, we present a ISAC constellation design under specific receiver architecture that brings a receiver-dependent flexible trade-off between sensing and communication in OFDM-ISAC systems. The theoretical findings are validated through simulations and proof-of-concept experiments, and also the sensing and communication performance trade-off is experimentally shown with the proposed constellation design.

title: A Matrix-Pencil Framework Empowering Joint Multi-Dimensional Parameter Estimation in High-Mobility Systems.
abstract: With 6G technologies taking on new roles in the electrical domain, Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation has emerged as a key enabler for integrated sensing and communication. However, parameter estimation in multi-antenna and low-lattice-resolution OTFS (MA-F-OTFS) systems remains underexplored. To address this challenge, this work proposes a hybrid pilot framework based on Chirp structures and Frank sequences, and employs a matrix pencil algorithm to enable efficient joint estimation of multidimensional channel parameters in MA-F-OTFS, including angle, Doppler, and delay. The proposed approach demonstrates fast and accurate estimation performance. The study primarily focuses on Doppler and delay estimation while briefly outlining a joint angle estimation scheme. Simulation results validate the superior performance of the proposed algorithm in parameter estimation.

title: Feedback-Free Precoding for Low-Latency FDD Downlink MIMO for IoT Communications.
abstract: This paper presents a low-latency framework for frequency division duplex (FDD) multi-input multi-output (MIMO) Internet-of-Things (IoT) communications. Our key idea is eliminating feedback associated with downlink channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT) acquisition. Instead, we reconstruct the downlink channel from uplink reference signals by exploiting the frequency invariance of channel parameters. However, the frequency difference between the uplink and downlink bands prevents perfect reconstruction, which in turn results in substantial inter-user interference. To manage this, we formulate a max-min fairness problem and propose an efficient precoding method based on rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA). This robust precoder design is enabled by an error covariance matrix (ECM) approximation technique, a crucial step for operating without feedback. Simulation results demonstrate that our framework significantly enhances minimum spectral efficiency and drastically reduces communication latency compared to conventional feedback-based methods.

title: Spatial-Semantic Attacks and Protection for Trajectory Privacy: From Vulnerability to Defense.
abstract: The rapid expansion of Location-Based Services (LBS) has intensified concerns over trajectory privacy. Existing privacy-preserving models primarily focus on spatial obfuscation and cannot effectively defend against semantic-enhanced attacks. They are particularly vulnerable to the newly proposed Location-Semantic De-Anonymization Attack (LS-DAA), which integrates spatiotemporal dependencies with semantic transition patterns to infer true user locations. This paper introduces LS-DAA to expose the vulnerabilities that arise from spatial aggregation in current approaches. To counter this threat, we further propose the Spatially-Constrained Semantic Anonymization (SCSA) framework. Unlike prior models, SCSA provides protection against LS-DAA by enforcing spatial dispersion while preserving semantic consistency, which jointly mitigates clustering-based and semantic-aware inferences. Extensive experiments on the Geolife dataset show that SCSA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in transfer direction deviation, average identification probability, and semantic transfer entropy. Moreover, SCSA maintains an attack success rate below 5% under Top-5 inference, whereas existing methods remain highly vulnerable to LS-DAA.

title: Collaborative Dynamic Service Function Chain Embedding for Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Networks (ISTN) present significant challenges for Service Function Chain (SFC) embedding due to their heterogeneous resource characteristics and dynamic topological structures. This paper proposes a collaborative dynamic embedding mechanism that achieves efficient coordination between satellite and terrestrial nodes through multi-dimensional resource awareness and adaptive path selection. The core of our algorithm relies on dynamic weight adjustment, comprehensively considering link propagation delay, bandwidth availability, node computational capacity, and VNF deployment status to pre-evaluate resource suitability during path discovery. Distinct from conventional approaches, our scheme introduces VNF sharing potential factors and load balancing constraints, effectively mitigating resource fragmentation issues. Experimental results demonstrate that in dynamic network environments, the proposed mechanism improves SFC request acceptance rate by 20.2% and resource utilization by 16.5% compared to baseline algorithms, while maintaining low computational overhead. This work provides a practical solution for quality of service assurance in ISTN environments.

title: Channel Estimation with Hierarchical Sparse Bayesian Learning for ODDM Systems.
abstract: Orthogonal delay-Doppler division multiplexing (ODDM) is a promising modulation technique for reliable communications in high-mobility scenarios. However, the existing channel estimation frameworks for ODDM systems cannot achieve both high accuracy and low complexity simultaneously, due to the inherent coupling of delay and Doppler parameters. To address this problem, a two-dimensional (2D) hierarchical sparse Bayesian learning (HSBL) based channel estimation framework is proposed in this paper. Specifically, we address the inherent coupling between delay and Doppler dimensions in ODDM by developing a partially-decoupled 2D sparse signal recovery (SSR) formulation on a virtual sampling grid defined in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain. With the help of the partially-decoupled formulation, the proposed 2D HSBL framework first performs low-complexity coarse on-grid 2D sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) estimation to identify potential channel paths. Then, high-resolution fine grids are constructed around these regions, where an off-grid 2D SBL estimation is applied to achieve accurate channel estimation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves performance superior to conventional off-grid 2D SBL with significantly reduced computational complexity.

title: Ownership-Protected Semantic Communication via Signal Processing-Driven Robust Watermark.
abstract: With the rapid evolution of semantic communication (SemCom), embedding ownership protection into transmission frameworks has become crucial for safeguarding intellectual property (IP). In this paper, we present a unified SemCom-watermarking framework, where a fixed watermark image is imperceptibly inserted into all transmitted cover samples via a signal processing embedding module, and reliably extracted at the receiver for ownership verification. By jointly training the semantic codec and a watermark decoder, our system ensures both high-quality SemCom reconstruction and robust watermark recovery under diverse channel models. A statistical hypothesis testing strategy based on paired t-tests validates the presence of the embedded watermark against non-triggered baselines, while the framework also resists adversarial attacks. Experiments on DIV2K show that our method achieves SemCom transmission with 42–45dB PSNR and about 99% SSIM at 30dB SNR across four architectures, while watermark recovery remains around 30dB PSNR and above 86% SSIM at 10–30dB. Paired t-tests yield p-values near 0 over 400 samples, and robustness tests further ensure reliable ownership verification. These findings demonstrate that the framework provides a practical and statistically grounded solution for ownership verification in SemCom, aligning with secure and reliable signal processing for communications.

title: Resource Allocation for Ultra-Reliable and Low-Latency IoT Communications Based on Federated Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: With the rapid development of 5G and upcoming 6G networks, efficient and low-latency wireless resource allocation has become increasingly important. Traditional centralized resource allocation in cellular networks incurs high computational complexity and significant signaling overhead at the base station (BS). This paper investigates a distributed resource allocation scheme for intelligent Internet of Things (IoT) scenarios, aiming to maximize uplink energy efficiency (EE) through joint channel and power allocation while guaranteeing the quality of service (QoS) requirements of ultra-reliable and low-latency communications (URLLC) user equipments (UEs). To enable distributed learning with low communication overhead, we enhance the federated multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (Fed-MADRL) framework and design a QoS model based on effective bandwidth theory for short-packet transmission. Analytical and numerical results show that the proposed framework supports low-overhead collaborative learning and achieves global policy convergence with EE and QoS performance comparable to centralized schemes, while outperforming conventional MADRL methods.

title: Lightweight Task-Adaptive Residual Attention Network for Few-Shot Modulation Classification.
abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) plays a significant role in cognitive radio, military communications, and the Internet of Things. However, existing AMC methods are data-intensive and rely on complex preprocessing. Their reliance on idealized scenarios further limits their ability to generalize to unseen signal formats, hindering their deployment in dynamic spectrum environments. This paper proposes a task-adaptive meta-learning approach to achieve superior classification accuracy and generalization capability in sample-constrained scenarios. By leveraging the self-attention mechanism to capture long-range temporal dependencies and a sequential decoupling strategy for signal representation, the proposed architecture improves adaptability to channel impairments and enhances generalization to unseen modulation classes. Simulation results show that our proposed few-shot learning approach outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Specifically, it achieves 86.7% accuracy in mixed scenarios, and demonstrates strong generalization to both known and novel modulations while reducing the parameter count by 89% compared to Transformer-based models.

title: Wireless and Optical Cooperative Control for virtualized CU live migration with Near RT RIC.
abstract: Flexible and on-demand network service deployment is required to realize low-latency network services. In the Radio Access Network (RAN), the Near Real-Time RAN Intelligence Controller (Near RT RIC) is expected to provide real-time control response within one second. In particular, it is essential that network configuration changes do not impact active services. In order to realize on-demand Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) tailored to each user’s demands, real-time cooperative control between RAN and the optical network is critical. In this paper, we propose a method of wireless and optical cooperative real-time control for live migration of the virtualized central unit (CU) to minimize deployment times and service interruptions. To evaluate the proposed method, we implement the proposed method as xApp running on Near RT RIC. We also use Open-Source Software (OSS)-based RAN functions and 5th Generation Core network (5GC) on several general-purpose servers. Experiments confirm that the proposed method can reduce the deployment time compared to the conventional method. The proposed method achieves rapid reconfiguration with downtimes of less than 1 second regardless of the forwarding bandwidth.

title: Exploiting Skyrmions in Free-Space Optical Communication.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel free-space optical (FSO) communication system utilizing optical skyrmions. We introduce a scheme referred to as skyrmion number modulation (SkM), which employs index modulation by encoding information onto the skyrmion number, a topological invariant preserved during free-space propagation. This topological nature offers the potential for inherent robustness against atmospheric turbulence-induced wavefront distortions, which limit the performance of conventional FSO systems. More specifically, we demonstrate that the fluctuation of the received skyrmion number is mitigated by a proposed intensity-based masking technique. Finally, our performance analysis based on a discrete memoryless channel framework confirms that the proposed system exhibits near-ideal robustness under weak turbulence and supports high-order modulation in moderate regimes.

title: IoT-Enabled Digital Twins for Robotics over Private 5G Networks: Security, Fault Detection, and Environmental Monitoring.
abstract: This paper presents an IoT Digital Twin (DT) frame work for real-time monitoring of robotic systems in Industry 4.0, using a robotic arm as a case study. The framework combines 5G connectivity with SATCOM backhaul to address latency, security, and efficiency challenges in physical-virtual synchronisation. The architecture includes a Jetson Nano processor, a sensor-equipped robotic arm, ROS for control, and Unity for 3D visualisation. Three design objectives guide implementation: (1) real-time syn chronisation between physical robot and digital model; (2) fault detection and environmental response via threshold-based algo rithms; and (3) security through facial recognition. Connectivity uses Vodafone’s 5G mobile private network augmented by Star link SATCOM to ensure consistent data transfer across varied environments. Performance evaluation across 5G standalone, 5G non-standalone, and SATCOM-enhanced configurations shows average latencies of 130-270 ms over 10 iterations per setup, with variations due to deployment location and backhaul factors.

title: Transmit or Idle: Efficient AoI Optimal Transmission Policy for Gossiping Receivers.
abstract: We study the optimal transmission and scheduling policy for a transmitter (source) communicating with two gossiping receivers aiming at tracking the source’s status over time using the age of information (AoI) metric. Gossiping enables local information exchange in a decentralized manner without relying solely on the transmitter’s direct communication, which we assume incurs a transmission cost. On the other hand, gossiping may be communicating stale information, necessitating the transmitter’s intervention. With communication links having specific success probabilities, we formulate an average-cost Markov Decision Process (MDP) to jointly minimize the sum AoI and transmission cost for such a system in a time-slotted setting. We employ the Relative Value Iteration (RVI) algorithm to evaluate the optimal policy for the transmitter and then prove several structural properties showing that it has an age-difference threshold structure with minimum age activation in the case where gossiping is relatively more reliable. Specifically, direct transmission is optimal only if the minimum AoI of the receivers is large enough and their age difference is below a certain threshold. Otherwise, the transmitter idles to effectively take advantage of gossiping and reduce direct transmission costs. Numerical evaluations demonstrate the significance of our optimal policy compared to multiple baselines. Our result is a first step towards characterizing optimal freshness and transmission cost trade-offs in gossiping networks.

title: Enhancing User Throughput in Multi-panel mmWave Radio Access Networks for Beam-based MU-MIMO Using a DRL Method.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication systems, particularly those leveraging multi-user multiple-input and multiple-output (MU-MIMO) with hybrid beamforming, face challenges in optimizing user throughput and minimizing latency due to the high complexity of dynamic beam selection and management. This paper introduces a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach for enhancing user throughput in multi-panel mmWave radio access networks in a practical network setup. Our DRL-based formulation utilizes an adaptive beam management strategy that models the interaction between the communication agent and its environment as a Markov decision process (MDP), optimizing beam selection based on real-time observations. The proposed framework exploits spatial domain (SD) characteristics by incorporating the cross-correlation between the beams in different antenna panels, the measured reference signal received power (RSRP), and the beam usage statistics to dynamically adjust beamforming decisions. As a result, the spectral efficiency is improved and end-to-end latency is reduced. The numerical results demonstrate an increase in throughput of up to 16% and a reduction in latency by factors 3-7x compared to baseline (legacy beam management).

title: Energy-Efficient Federated Learning in Cooperative Communication within Factory Subnetworks.
abstract: This paper investigates energy-efficient transmission protocols in relay-assisted federated learning (FL) setup within industrial subnetworks, considering latency and power constraints. In the subnetworks, devices collaborate to train a global model by transmitting their local models at the edge-enabled primary access (pAP) directly or via secondary access points (sAPs), which act as relays to optimize the training latency. We begin by formulating the energy efficiency problem for our proposed transmission protocol. Given its non-convex nature, we decompose it to minimize computational and transmission energy separately. First, we introduce an algorithm that categorizes devices into single-hop and two-hop groups to decrease transmission energy and then selects associated sAPs. Subsequently, we optimize the transmit power, aiming to maximize energy efficiency. To that end, we propose a Sequential Parametric Convex Approximation (SPCA) method to configure system parameters jointly. Numerical results demonstrate a significant reduction in outage probability and at least a twofold savings in total energy consumption, together with faster convergence, compared with single-hop transmission.

title: Secure Rate-Splitting and RIS Beamforming with Untrusted Energy Harvesting Receivers.
abstract: We consider a reconfigurable intelligent surface(RIS)-assisted heterogeneous network comprising legitimateinformation-harvesting receivers (IHRs) and untrusted energyharvesting receivers (UEHRs). A multi-antenna base station (BS)transmits confidential information to IHRs while ensuring sufficient energy transfer to UEHRs that may attempt eavesdropping.To enhance physical-layer security, we propose a secure ratesplitting multiple access (RSMA) scheme aided by a UAV-mountedRIS. The objective is to maximize fairness-based secrecy energyefficiency (SEE). Owing to the non-convexity of the formulatedproblem, we develop an alternating optimization framework thatjointly designs the common message allocation, active precoders,and RIS phase shifts under transmit power and energy harvestingconstraints, leveraging sequential convex approximation (SCA).Simulation results demonstrate the scalability of the proposedalgorithm and its superior SEE performance compared to spacedivision multiple access (SDMA) and non-orthogonal multipleaccess (NOMA) benchmarks.

title: An Intelligent Framework for Intrusion Detection in Resource-Constrained Wireless Sensor Networks.
abstract: A powerful multi-stage framework is proposed, which includes dimensionality reduction, adaptive sampling, attention-driven learning, and smart query selection. As the first, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) is used to maintain the predictive attributes as much as possible and as the second, Proxy Weighted Random Affine Shadow Sampling (ProWRAS) is used to balance skewed classes artificially. An attention network is then used to focus on meaningful input dimensions in the classification Feature Attention Network (FAN). This system is also improved through the addition of uncertainty-based active learning which gradually extends the labeled dataset through high-entropy queries, and a Bayesian optimization cycle that automatically optimizes hyperparameters by searching through the highest performance points. Empirical results show a marked improvement over traditional methods, with accuracy gains of 39% compared to HighwayNet, 31% over GRU, and 12% over Gradient Boosting. F1-score and AUC-ROC also increased substantially, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed design in delivering high detection reliability. The final model offers a scalable and energy-aware solution, tailored to the unique demands of real-world WSNs.

title: An Adaptive Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Intelligent Intrusion Detection in Internet of Things.
abstract: The exponential proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) has significantly intensified the exposure of connected ecosystems to complex cyber threats, necessitating intelligent and adaptive intrusion detection systems. This study presents a comprehensive hybrid deep learning framework that unifies data balancing, feature normalization, dual-path convolutional fusion, and reinforcement-driven optimization for securing IoT infrastructures. Initially, conditional tabular generative adversarial network is utilized to alleviate severe class imbalance within the canadian institute for cybersecurity IoTs dataset, ensuring equitable representation across intrusion categories. Subsequently, min–max scaling stabilizes gradient propagation, followed by the introduction of the hybrid AS-Net architecture that fuses AlexNet’s hierarchical feature abstraction with ShuffleNet’s efficient grouped convolution through a dual-path fusion mechanism. This integration achieves superior representational diversity while maintaining computational efficiency. Furthermore, the framework is extended to a reinforcement-optimized variant, RAS-Net, wherein the monte carlo policy gradient algorithm dynamically tunes critical hyperparameters such as learning rate and dropout probability. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that AS-Net attains an accuracy of 0.8760, precision of 0.8967, recall of 0.8760, and F1-score of 0.8650, corresponding to an improvement of 3.63% in accuracy and 2.53% in F1-score over AlexNet. The reinforcement-optimized RAS-Net further enhances performance, achieving an accuracy of 0.9059, precision of 0.9267, recall of 0.9160, and F1-score of 0.9050, marking an overall increase of 6.06% in accuracy and 5.63% in F1-score compared to baseline.

title: Ultra-Low-Power ECG Classification Using 2D CNN-based SNN on Neuromorphic Hardware for Wearable Devices.
abstract: Real-time Electrocardiogram (ECG) classification on wearable devices is critical for cardiac monitoring but limited by power and bandwidth constraints. We present the first deployable ECG arrhythmia classification on commercially available neuromorphic Akida AKD1000 hardware, converting a 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) into a 4-bit spiking neural network (SNN). This enables the transmission of only 3-bit semantic alerts over the air, with a decoding rate exceeding 99% in a simulated Rayleigh fading channel. Evaluated on the MITBIH Arrhythmia, our quantization-aware-trained model attains 99.02% accuracy across five heartbeat classes while consuming 2.04 μJ per inference and 1.66 ms latency at 100 MHz. Compared to streaming raw ECG, the proposed system reduces wireless payload by >99%. These results underline the feasibility of battery-powered, always-on cardiac monitoring for 5G/6G telehealth and the potential of neuromorphic computing to enable energy-efficient, accurate, real-time ECG analysis directly on edge devices, paving the way for advanced wearable health monitoring systems and applications in remote healthcare leveraging semantic communication principles.

title: Symmetric-PCGrad: A Conflict-Aware Approach for Multi-Task Learning in RIS-Enabled Networks.
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) provide a fivefold increase in signal power gain compared to traditional approaches, while being easy to deploy and offering cost-effective solutions. A key factor in RIS performance is the intelligent activation of element groups—for instance, enabling only selected elements for reflection while keeping the rest in absorption mode to minimize unnecessary power consumption. Motivated by the need for efficient resource utilization, this study proposes a multi-task deep learning framework based on Symmetric-Projecting Conflicting Gradients (Symmetric-PCGrad). The framework jointly performs two tasks: (i) classifying the active group of RIS elements responsible for producing high signal power at specific azimuth and elevation angles, and (ii) estimating the received signal power at the user end. This dual-task approach is designed to identify the minimal group of elements required to meet a target quality of service—an aspect largely overlooked in existing RIS-assisted wireless communication research. To ensure fair evaluation, we applied the same multi-task learning (MTL) architecture using three strategies: standard MTL (no gradient projection), MTL with Projecting Conflicting Gradients (PCGrad), and the proposed Symmetric-PCGrad, all under identical hyperparameter settings. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms both baseline techniques in terms of individual task performance and overall multi-task effectiveness.

title: Sleep or Transmit: Dual-Mode Energy-Efficient Design for NOMA-Enabled Backscatter Networks.
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices demands communication systems that are both spectrally efficient and energy frugal. Backscatter communication (BackCom) is an attractive low-power paradigm, but its spectral efficiency declines in dense deployments. This paper presents an uplink BackCom design that integrates non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and maximizes system energy efficiency (EE). In a bistatic network where multiple backscatter nodes (BNs) harvest RF energy and alternate between sleep and active modes, we formulate a fractional program with coupled time, power, and reflection variables and develop a Dinkelbach-based alternating optimization (AO) algorithm with closed-form updates. Analysis reveals two operating modes depending on power availability, circuit demands and propagation conditions. Simulations show the proposed design adapts the time allocation, achieving up to 8% higher EE than fixed-power and 68% than no-sleep baselines, and delivering up to 127% EE gains over orthogonal multiple access (OMA). These results establish NOMA-enabled BackCom as a scalable, energy efficient solution for large-scale IoT deployments.

title: RIS-Aided Physical Layer Security in MU-MIMO Communications: MUI-Free Precoding Design and Secrecy Sum-Rate Optimization.
abstract: We study physical layer security (PLS) in a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided multi-user (MU) MIMO downlink, where direct access point (AP) user links are blocked and a multi-antenna eavesdropper is present. A CSI-based precoder is designed to cancel multi-user interference (MUI) at the legitimate users, resulting in an interference-free received signal model that supports reliable maximum-likelihood detection. We then combine RIS-aided beamforming with user power allocation and formulate a secrecy sum-rate maximization problem under a total transmit power constraint. An alternating optimization procedure is developed to iteratively update the user beamforming vectors and power allocation accordingly. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed design and demonstrate consistent secrecy and reliability improvements over representative baseline and beamforming schemes across various SNRs, RIS sizes, and user numbers.

title: Beyond-Diagonal RIS for Wideband NOMA: OFE-REDQ with SIC-Aware Power Allocation.
abstract: Orthogonal multiple access assigns disjoint time-frequency resources and limits reuse in dense 6G settings. Non orthogonal multiple access mitigates this by superposing users and separating streams with successive interference cancellation, but performance is sensitive to SIC errors and channel uncertainty. Many RIS-NOMA studies assume perfect channels and ideal SIC, ignore feedback delay and noise, and restrict RIS to diagonal control, while the wideband joint design of base-station precoding, RIS configuration, and inter/intra-cluster power is nonconvex. In this research we address these gaps with a wideband OFDM downlink that employs beyond diagonal RIS with two-bit eigen-phase quantization, imperfect feedback (delay, noise, random phase flips), MMSE precoding from estimated cluster representatives, and an explicit per-subcarrier SIC feasibility rule. We develop OFE-REDQ, a reinforcement-learning agent that combines an optimized feature encoder with a randomized ensemble of critics and a deterministic actor to jointly control RIS settings, inter-cluster power shares, and intra-cluster splits. Stability is ensured by Polyak target updates, subset-minimum bootstrapping, and target-value clipping. In 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL-D UMi simulations, OFE-REDQ achieves higher sum rate, faster and more stable convergence, and higher SIC success than DDPG and vanilla REDQ, indicating suitability for practical RIS-aided NOMA under realistic hardware and feedback constraints.

title: Alarm Correlation Method for Large-Scale Carrier Network Considering Topology Error Probability.
abstract: Alarm correlation is crucial for understanding network events in large-scale carrier networks since multiple failures can occur simultaneously. Traditional correlation methods commonly rely on topology information, which represents the physical connections between devices. However, discrepancies exist between the topology information stored in the database and the actual device connectivity, because updates in the database are typically manual and occur after network changes, such as device additions or removals. Therefore, existing alarm correlation methods might correlate new alarms using incorrect topology information, resulting in inaccurate clustering. To address this issue, we propose a new alarm correlation method by introducing an estimated Topology Error Probability, which represents the likelihood that topology information is incorrect, to improve correlation accuracy. We evaluate the method using real large-scale network data. The evaluation demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms the baseline approach in terms of clustering completeness and event-level accuracy.

title: FedAR: Adaptive Client Selection Strategy for Heterogeneous Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) allows multiple participants to collaboratively train a shared model without exposing or exchanging their raw data, yet heterogeneous client resources and non-IID data often slow convergence and hurt fairness. We propose FedAR, an adaptive client selection strategy that formulates selection as a similarity-alignment problem between a Global Environmental Vector and per-client Environmental Vectors. FedAR computes cosine similarity and refines it with (i) a communication-efficiency penalty, (ii) an aging mechanism to prevent over-selection, (iii) a dynamic threshold that tightens as training progresses, and (iv) a deadline mechanism that boosts long-unselected clients. We also weight aggregation by client data quality and historical performance. Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 under IID and non-IID partitions demonstrate that FedAR achieves faster convergence, higher accuracy, and lower loss than FedAvg and FedProx, while encouraging fairer and more diverse participation. These gains demonstrate that multi-factor, fairness-aware selection can improve both effectiveness and efficiency in real-world FL deployments.

title: MetaFed: A Novel Aggregation Strategy for Efficient Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables model collaboration across distributed data sources while keeping raw data local, making it a promising solution for privacy-sensitive applications. Despite its advantages, traditional aggregation techniques often perform suboptimally when confronted with heterogeneous client behavior, skewed data distributions, and limited communication budgets. To address these limitations, we introduce MetaFed, a new aggregation framework that models FL aggregation as an optimization problem. Rather than directly averaging client models, MetaFed explores the solution space formed by client updates using a Black Widow Optimization (BWO) algorithm-based evolutionary search, allowing it to adaptively select high-quality model candidates. MetaFed supports flexible fitness objectives, including validation- and norm-based evaluation, enabling use in both accuracy-focused and resource-constrained settings. It also employs various client selection strategies. Experiments on MNIST, FMNIST, and CIFAR-10, conducted under both IID and non-IID distributions, demonstrate that MetaFed accelerates convergence, enhances accuracy, and model performance compared to FedAvg, FedProx, and Pow-d. Overall, MetaFed offers a scalable and adaptive solution for robust and efficient federated learning.

title: LiteTalk: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning via Adaptive Gradient Drift Detection.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed clients without sharing raw data, making it suitable for privacy-sensitive domains. However, frequent communication between clients and the server remains a major bottleneck, particularly in bandwidth-and energy-constrained environments. Existing methods often reduce payload sizes or drop clients but fail to consider whether local updates are truly novel. To address this, we propose LiteTalk, a lightweight methodology that suppresses redundant communication through gradient drift detection. Each client evaluates the novelty of its update via the2distance between consecutive deltas and transmits only if the update is sufficiently different; otherwise, the server reuses its last contribution. LiteTalk incorporates adaptive thresholding strategies, global time-decay, and client-specific exponential moving average (EMA), together with a communication control logic to ensure periodic updates. Experiments on MNIST, FMNIST, and CIFAR-10 under IID and non-IID settings show that LiteTalk improves model performance compared to the baseline, while reducing redundant communication. It offers a practical paradigm for efficient cross-device federated learning.

title: Deep Learning-Based Joint Uplink-Downlink Channel Estimation for Upper Mid-Band Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates channel acquisition challenges under partial antenna probing, which commonly occur in the upper mid-band, also called frequency range 3 (FR3) band, where the number of antennas far exceeds the port capacity defined in current specifications. To address these challenges, we propose a novel channel state information (CSI) acquisition framework that integrates CSI feedback, uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) channel estimation in the FR3 time division duplex (TDD) massive multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems. Specifically, we first develop the Joint UL and DL Channel Estimation Network (JUDCEN) to fuse incomplete observations based on the sounding reference signals (SRSs) and CSI-reference signals (CSI-RSs). By exploiting the complementary characteristics of preliminary UL and DL estimation features, obtained through initial UL estimation and quantized-feedback-assisted DL estimation, it enables full CSI reconstruction in the spatial domain. To mitigate the performance degradation in the feedback process, the feedback process is enhanced by the proposed Transformer-MLP CSI Feedback Network (TMCFN), which employs MLP-based module to jointly exploit angle- and delay-domain features. Simulation results confirm the superior performance in both CSI acquisition accuracy and transmission spectral efficiency of the proposed framework.

title: Understanding the IPv6 Address Usage Strategies of Top Internet Services.
abstract: As IPv6 is deployed at scale around the world, numerous services are beginning to support public IPv6 access as content providers and content distribution networks upgrade to enable IPv6. Since the IPv6 address space is much larger than that of IPv4, the way addresses are used under IPv6 does not need to mirror IPv4; however, we remain unclear about the usage strategies for addresses used by IPv6-enabled services.In this paper, we delve into the IPv6 address usage strategies of top Internet services. We investigate the top 10K domains that support AAAA records and obtain over 3.86 million IPv6 addresses of top Internet services by adding well-constructed EDNS-client-subnet options to DNS queries. By analyzing the IPv6 addresses we have obtained (covering over 3K routing prefixes and 900 autonomous systems), our primary findings are as follows: 1) Approximately 17.5% of the services provided or hosted by the studied ASes are more susceptible to the risk of user inaccessibility in the event of a routing prefix outage or prefix blocking. 2) Over 99% of the addresses in use by top Internet services host only one domain, unlike in IPv4, where addresses host multiple domains. In addition, it is common to host domains with multiple AS IPs, collectively enhancing service survivability. 3) About 17.64% of ASes obliterate the ability of randomized IID to provide resistance to scanning due to the use of strongly correlated randomized IIDs, making them more likely to be detected.

title: Achievable Rate Optimization for Large Flexible Intelligent Metasurface Assisted Downlink MISO under Statistical CSI.
abstract: The integration of electromagnetic metasurfaces into wireless communications enables intelligent control of the propagation environment. Recently, flexible intelligent metasurfaces (FIMs) have evolved beyond conventional reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs), enabling three-dimensional surface deformation for adaptive wave manipulation. However, most existing FIM-aided system designs assume perfect instantaneous channel state information (CSI), which is impractical in large-scale networks due to the high training overhead and complicated channel estimation. To overcome this limitation, we propose a robust statistical-CSI-based optimization framework for downlink multiple-input single-output (MISO) systems with FIM-assisted transmitters. A block coordinate ascent (BCA)-based iterative algorithm is developed to jointly optimize power allocation and FIM morphing, maximizing the average achievable sum rate. Simulation results show that the proposed statistical-CSI-driven FIM design significantly outperforms conventional rigid antenna arrays (RAAs), validating its effectiveness and practicality.

title: Drift-Aware Conditional Diffusion Generative AI for Resource Management in 5G and Beyond Networks.
Dynamic Use of MQTT and HTTP for Transmission of Data in Environments with High Latencies and Low Transfer Rates.
abstract: The rise of IoT has lead to more data being generated worldwide. Very rarely are the data kept directly at the data source. Instead, they are transmitted elsewhere. Depending on where the data will be transmitted, this transmission might be limited by a high latency or a low transmission rate. This research seeks to address such limitations. Therefore, the situation is analyzed, simulated and, optimized with respect to two of the most popular data-transmission protocols in this area: HTTP and MQTT. A detailed comparison of these two protocols is made. Extensive studies have shown that the choice of the right protocol has a major effect on the transmission time that depends on the amount of data to be transmitted, the latency, and the maximum transmission rate. Depending on the circumstances, the transmission time for the same amount of data differs by up to 1300 times for these two protocols. But which protocol to choose under which condition? Therefore, this paper develops a framework of benchmarks, databases, data pipelines, and scripts that dynamically switches between HTTP and MQTT in different QoS configurations depending on the given network performance. Thus, the most efficient protocol is selected automatically for each target IP. In order to validate these findings, a real application test in a world-wide network is performed. As a result, an average up to 2.91 s per transmission can be saved, which also leads to faster reaction times in critical situations.

title: RIS-Assisted Coexistence Design for Radar and Multi-user Communication under NLOS Scenarios.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the joint design for the coexistence of Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar and communication systems aided by a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) in Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) scenarios. To enhance target detection accuracy and resolution, we adopt the Signal-to-Interference-Noise Ratio (SINR) and Integral Mainlobe to Side-lobe Ratio (IMSR) as performance metrics for radar. Meanwhile, the communication system's performance is also considered to ensure reliable operation. To solve this optimization problem, we reformulate the model in an augmented Lagrangian framework, which enables it to be decomposed into easily solvable subproblems. To address the constant-modulus constraints introduced by the RIS, we develop two solution strategies: one based on a combination of the Minorization-Maximization framework and Triple Alternating Direction Penalty Method (MMTADPM), and the other is based on the MM framework and Element-wise Block Coordinate Descent (MMEBCD). Simulation results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

title: Programmable Data Plane Approaches for ML-Based Anomalous Event Classification in Grid Sensor Networks.
abstract: Grid-sensor networks, such as Phasor Measurement Units (PMU) systems, generate high-resolution, time-synchronized measurement data that are critical for detecting voltage and frequency disturbances. Conventional machine learning (ML) classification methods for detecting anomalous voltage events often rely on centralized processing, introducing latency that limits real-time responsiveness. In this work, we explore an in-network classification framework that leverages P4 programmability to support early classification of voltage events in synchrophasor data. We propose two complementary approaches: a data plane (DP)-driven approach that compiles ML logic directly into switch match-action tables for low-latency real-time classification, and a control plane (CP)-driven approach where parsed features by the network switch are exported for more accurate, although slightly higher-latency model inference. Using 27,000 PMU measurements from a campus microgrid, injected with 5% anomalous events, we evaluated multiple ML models, with the DP-and CP-driven approaches achieving on average 96% and 98% accuracy, respectively. Additionally, a hardware-based evaluation of the DP-driven approach using Intel’s Tofino programmable switch demonstrated processing latency between 577 and 610 nanoseconds. Our work illustrates the feasibility of leveraging P4 for real-time, in-network deployment of ML-based security analytics in smart-grid communications.

title: KANC: An Interpretable Network Performance Prediction Model based on KAN and GNN.
abstract: In the hyper-connected era of 5G/6G and IoT, the unprecedented scale and complexity of communication networks make intelligent, proactive performance prediction essential. However, the black-box nature of deep learning models limits their interpretability and trustworthiness. While complex models achieve high accuracy, their inherent opacity creates a trade-off with the interpretability required for operational trust. To address this, we propose the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network-based Graph Neural Network (GNN) for Comprehensible Networking (KANC), an architecture that achieves both high accuracy and deep interpretability by replacing the traditional Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) readout with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN). Experimental results demonstrate that KANC not only surpasses its MLP-based counterpart in prediction accuracy and generalization to unseen topologies but also successfully unlocks the model’s reasoning process. Through a comprehensive analysis combining functional profiling, internal spline visualization, and counterfactual interventions, we show that KANC learns smooth, physically plausible relationships between network state and performance. We can thereby reconstruct the model’s entire decision path, validating that its internal logic aligns with fundamental networking theory. As a transparent and trustworthy predictive tool, KANC represents a significant step towards diagnosable AI for intelligent network operations.

title: Neuromorphic Radar Sensing with the Spiking Locally Competitive Algorithm.
abstract: This paper explores the integration of neuromorphic computing with wireless sensing, focusing on radar processing within the framework of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC). In this context, we propose a neuromorphic signal processing module that employs an extension of the Spiking Locally Competitive Algorithm (S-LCA) to perform delay-Doppler estimation in an OFDM-based sensing setup. As sensing reference signals, we utilize sequences from a finite-dimensional Gabor frame constructed from time-frequency translates of a seed vector. We refer to a Gabor frame construction based on the Alltop seed vector due to its low mutual coherence and hardware-friendly implementation. The proposed system is deployed on the SpiNNaker neuromorphic platform, demonstrating notable power savings compared to traditional hardware.

title: Near-Field Beampattern Analysis of the Sum-Rate Capacity of RIS-aided MIMO Broadcast Channels.
abstract: Future 6G wireless communication systems are exploring advanced technologies such as Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) and Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) to meet the growing demand for ultra-high data rates, improved spectral efficiency, increased coverage, and reliable connectivity. MIMO provides spatial multiplexing and diversity gains while RIS offers control over the wireless propagation environment. This paper examines the sum-rate capacity of a RIS-aided MIMO Broadcast Channel (BC), accounting for both near-field and far-field propagation effects. By leveraging a known duality between BS and multiple-access channels, the input covariance matrix and RIS phase shifts are jointly optimized to address the inherent high dimensionality challenge of the sum-rate maximization problem. Additionally, the beampatterns of the RIS and of the transmitter are analyzed to evaluate how power is allocated across multiple users, under both line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight conditions. Numerical evaluation results highlight the importance of near-field modeling and joint optimization to fully exploit the spatial degrees of freedom offered by BC MIMO and RIS.

title: Deep Learning-Based Maneuvering UAV Tracking in Multi-User Uplink ISAC Systems.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) offers a promising paradigm for low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) surveillance by leveraging existing cellular infrastructure. However, tracking highly maneuvering UAVs using uplink reference signals in multi-user ISAC systems remains challenging. On one hand, conventional motion models often fail to capture complex UAV dynamics, leading to severe motion model mismatch. On the other hand, noisy user equipment positions result in measurement model mismatches and can degrade the performance significantly. To tackle these challenges, we propose a learning-aided extended Kalman filter for robust 3D position and velocity tracking. The method combines a neural prediction module that learns UAV maneuvers and a neural update module that adaptively corrects the innovation covariance to handle parametric uncertainties. Our proposed signal processing pipeline, which incorporates clutter suppression, parameter estimation via MUSIC and the iterative adaptive approach, and the learning-aided tracker, is validated in realistic ray-tracing scenarios with diverse UAV trajectories. Results demonstrate that our scheme significantly outperforms baseline methods in tracking accuracy and robustness while reducing computational complexity.

title: Secure NOMA-Enabled Aerial RIS Networks via Multi-Agent Multi-Stage Curriculum Learning.
abstract: The broadcast nature of wireless channels makes sixth-generation (6 G) networks vulnerable to eavesdropping, necessitating robust physical layer security (PLS). In this paper, we propose a secure non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-enabled unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-mounted reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) architecture to maximize secrecy rates in the presence of eavesdroppers. UAV-mounted RIS enables dynamic repositioning to establish favorable line-of-sight (LoS) links while suppressing signal leakage. However, jointly optimizing UAV 3D trajectory, RIS phase shifts control, base station (BS) active beamforming, and power allocation is challenging due to tightly coupled variables, strict successive interference cancellation (SIC) constraints, and minimum secrecy requirements. We formulate a secrecy rate maximization problem as a highly non-convex mixed-integer nonlinear program (NC-MINLP), intractable for conventional methods. We reformulate it as a Markov decision process (MDP) and propose a multi-agent multi-stage curriculum learning framework with proximal policy optimization (MAMSCL-PPO). The framework progressively expands the secured user set, addressing reward sparsity and enabling knowledge transfer. Two cooperative agents, employing centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE), jointly control the UAV trajectory with RIS phase shifts and the BS beamforming with power allocation. Simulations demonstrate that MAMSCL-PPO achieves a 43% higher sum secrecy rate and faster convergence than single-stage training, validating its effectiveness for scalable PLS in NOMA-enabled aerial networks.

title: Generalizable Pixel-wise 3D Gaussian Splatting enabled Joint Semantic-Channel Coding.
abstract: Despite remarkable advances in immersive communications, current systems often rely on data-intensive three-dimensional (3D) representations. Such heavy data loads impose severe challenges on both spectrum and latency. Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables real-time reconstruction of 3D representations from sparse viewpoints, but little exploration has been made on multi-view image compression and transmission. In this paper, we propose a joint semantic-channel coding scheme to address the aforementioned issues. Specifically, our framework achieves deep compression by extracting multi-view semantic features and leveraging inter-view disparities. Concurrently, it dynamically adjusts the encoder output based on target rate and channel state, ensuring robust transmission under complex conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that our model outperforms existing multi-view image transmission methods in both transmission efficiency and reliability, achieving robust transmission across diverse channel conditions and rates. Compared with approaches combining the key-frame part of multiview high efficiency video coding (MV-HEVC) with 5G LDPC codes and feed-forward 3DGS, our model achieves significant improvements in novel view synthesis (NVS) quality, particularly in poor channel conditions.

title: Communication Bottleneck Analysis for Distributed MoE Training.
abstract: Distributed Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model training requires all-to-all (A2A) communication for dynamic token routing. While it is empirically observed that A2A becomes a bottleneck, no quantitative framework exists to predict when this bottleneck will occur. This paper presents an analytical model of computation and communication time in distributed MoE training that accounts for load imbalance, hierarchical network topology, and hybrid parallelism. We derive a load-imbalance factor as a function of the expert parallelism degree and the number of local experts, and introduce a critical expert parallelism threshold that predicts the transition from compute-bound to communication-bound. Through validation on a real-world GPU cluster, the model achieves prediction errors below 5% for the compute-to-communication ratio. We also discuss how the proposed model guides practitioners in configuring parameters in practice.

title: Margin-Aware Relational Boundary Learning for Imbalanced Incremental Network Fault Diagnosis.
abstract: Modern network infrastructures are inherently dynamic, posing a dual challenge for fault diagnosis. New fault types appear sequentially, framing the problem as Class-Incremental Learning, while real-world operational data is severely imbalanced (abundant normal vs. rare fault instances). This combination biases the model’s decisions toward majority classes, intensifies catastrophic forgetting, and creates unstable decision boundaries, degrading diagnostic reliability. While recent methods aim to address these, they neglect geometric relations in the feature space and fail to handle the dynamic, multi-level class imbalance inherent to real-world network data. We present MARBL-I, a margin-aware relational boundary learning framework for imbalanced incremental network fault diagnosis that addresses these challenges through three synergistic components: (i) Multi-level Relational Knowledge Distillation method preserves learned fault patterns by maintaining similarity, distance/angle relationships, and class-wise statistics through an exponential moving average teacher with progressive warm-up, (ii) MES-driven Boundary Gating mechanism prioritizes boundary exemplars critical for maintaining discriminative power and adaptively scales relational losses based on sample difficulty, and (iii) Hierarchical Balanced Learning mechanism mitigates class imbalance through online prior-calibrated supervision during training and balanced ensemble classification at inference. Extensive experiments on 5G-KPI dataset and TEP dataset show MARBL-I’s state-of-the-art performance. On 5G-KPI dataset, in the challenging final incremental session, MARBL-I achieves a fault recognition accuracy of 67.56%, outperforming the next-best method by 6.85%, and reduces the average forgetting rate to 15.07%, a 5.43% improvement over the strongest baseline.

title: AstroTimer: Rethinking Non-Access Stratum Timers in LEO Constellations.
abstract: Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations play a critical role in expanding 5G coverage to remote and infrastructure-limited regions. They inherit most configurations, such as Non-Access Stratum (NAS), from terrestrial and geostationary (GEO) or medium Earth orbit (MEO) systems. However, they differ fundamentally from terrestrial networks due to rapidly changing topologies, fluctuating delays, and constrained onboard resources. Existing 3GPP NAS timers do not account for these dynamics, leading to signaling storms and inefficiency. This paper introduces AstroTimer, a lightweight and adaptive framework for sizing NAS timers based on LEO-specific parameters, including link variability, processing delays, and network-function placement. AstroTimer derives a closed-form timer model with low computational cost and optimizes both watchdog and backoff timers. We evaluated AstroTimer against the 3GPP defaults in the 5G registration procedure. Simulation results demonstrate that AstroTimer significantly reduces registration time, retry frequency, and user equipment (UE) energy consumption, while preventing signaling overloads. AstroTimer provides an operator-ready foundation for reliable, efficient, and scalable non-terrestrial 5G/6G deployments.

title: Weighted Sum-Rate Maximization for RIS-UAV-assisted Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network with RSMA.
