abstract: In this paper, a rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) based joint optimization framework for the space–air–ground integrated network (SAGIN) is proposed, where the satellite and base stations employ uniform planar array (UPA) antennas for signal transmission, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) relay the satellite signals. Earth stations (ESs) and user equipments (UEs) receive signals from satellite and base stations (BSs), respectively, resulting in mutual interference. We first model the channels and signals in this scenario and analyse the interference at BSs and UEs. Then, We formulate a joint optimization problem aimed at maximizing the weighted sum-rate, involving beamforming, RIS-UAV deployment and phase shifts, and rate splitting. However, this problem is highly non-convex. To tackle this challenge, we apply a block coordinate descent (BCD) approach to decompose the problem and employ the weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) method to transform the non-convex objective function. For the rate-splitting subproblem, a greedy algorithm is proposed and a successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithm is used for beamforming. Besides, the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm is employed for the RIS phase-shift problem with unit-modulus constraints, and an exhaustive search method is adopted for the complex UAV positioning and orientation. Simulation results validate that the proposed algorithm achieves superior performance in terms of user weighted sum-rate.

title: Communication-Efficient Over-the-Air Federated Fine-Tuning with Heterogeneous LoRA.
abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is widely adopted as a parameter-efficient technique for fine-tuning large artificial intelligence models. However, federated fine-tuning faces two challenges: device heterogeneity due to diverse computational capabilities and adaptable LoRA ranks across devices, and communication bottlenecks caused by the frequent transmission of high-dimensional updates in resource-constrained wireless environments. This paper proposes an over-the-air federated fine-tuning framework with heterogeneous LoRA, where singular value decomposition (SVD) projects heterogeneous updates onto a common low-dimensional subspace to reduce model inconsistency, and over-the-air computation (AirComp) enables direct aggregation of LoRA updates in the wireless channel to alleviate communication overhead. We establish a convergence analysis that characterizes the optimality gap in terms of SVD-induced truncation errors and AirComp transmission errors, and develop an alternating optimization algorithm that jointly adjusts device aggregation weights and the AirComp beamforming vector to mitigate error propagation. Simulation results demonstrate faster convergence and higher accuracy than existing baselines under varying LoRA ranks and wireless channel conditions.

title: Computing-Network Integrated Resource Scheduling in Satellite Mega-Constellations: A Hybrid Transfer and RL Framework.
abstract: The development of space-based intelligent computing has advanced space-based Computing-Network Integration based on satellite mega constellations (MSCs), upgrading the traditional communication pipeline to an intelligent computing platform with low-latency and global coverage. However, under the high dynamic topology of MSC, how to reasonably utilize limited communication and computing resources to improve task completion rate and reduce latency and energy consumption is a key issue. To address this, we build a hybrid transfer learning (TL) and reinforcement learning (RL) framework. We first propose a resource allocation strategy based on RL, the ground is divided into multiple domains due to uneven distribution of differentiated task, through satellite-ground collaborative computing, we provide differentiated services for different types of tasks to reduce latency and energy consumption while ensuring task completion rate. Furthermore, based on the task spatiotemporal correlation between adjacent domains, we augment DARLA with transfer learning, proposing DARLA-TL. By exploiting similarities in task structures (eg., arrival distribution, priority), we use minimal training samples to guide the rapid allocation of satellite resources, to adapt to the high dynamic changes of MSCs. Compared with the baseline algorithm A3C, the proposed method can improve task completion rate by 5.2%, and reduce the weighted sum of latency and energy consumption by 6.25% in large-scale tasks.

title: Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Energy-Aware Resource Scheduling in Cloud Environments.
abstract: As cloud computing systems continue to expand in scale and complexity, efficiently allocating heterogeneous computing resources has become a crucial challenge for maintaining high Quality of Service (QoS) and reducing energy consumption. Traditional reinforcement learning (RL)-based scheduling methods often struggle with the curse of dimensionality and poor coordination among multiple resource types. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a heterogeneous multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for energy-aware multi-resource scheduling in cloud environments. In the proposed model, distinct agents are assigned to manage CPU, memory, network, and disk resources, enabling specialized decision-making for each type. To further handle temporal dependencies in dynamic workloads, a temporal fusion module based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks is integrated to capture historical resource states. Additionally, a virtual machine polling strategy is introduced to reduce state-action dimensionality and enhance scalability across varying numbers of VMs. Extensive experiments conducted in a Docker-based cloud testbed demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art RL baselines in terms of QoS stability, resource utilization, and adaptability under high workload variability.

title: Adaptive and Context-Aware Capability Exposure with Digital Twins for Beyond-5G Networks.
abstract: The Network Exposure Function (NEF) is a cornerstone of 5G service openness, enabling third-party applications to access network capabilities via standardized APIs. Current exposure mechanisms, however, remain largely static, offering limited adaptability to real-time network dynamics and diverse vertical requirements. This paper proposes an AI-driven evolution of network exposure by integrating a Network Digital Twin (NDT) as an intelligent companion to the NEF. The NDT continuously mirrors the live network through NEF APIs, learns from its behavior, and proactively optimizes exposure policies and service requests before they reach the operational network. This closed-loop integration enables predictive analytics, context-aware exposure, and adaptive policy enforcement, leading to measurable improvements in resource efficiency and exposure responsiveness. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through an illustrative scenario and a preliminary evaluation, highlighting trade-offs in resource allocation, signaling, latency, and computational overhead.

title: Bayesian Self-Calibration and Parametric Channel Estimation for 6G Antenna Arrays.
abstract: Accurate channel estimation is essential for both high-rate communication and high-precision sensing in 6G wireless systems. However, a major performance limitation arises from calibration mismatches when operating phased-array antennas under real-world conditions. To address this issue, we propose to integrate antenna element self-calibration into a variational sparse Bayesian learning (VSBL) algorithm for parametric channel estimation. We model antenna gain and phase deviations as latent variables and derive explicit update equations to jointly infer these calibration parameters and the channel parameters; the number of multipath components (MPCs) along with their complex amplitudes, delays, and angles-of-arrival (AoA), as well as the noise variance. We assess its performance in terms of the optimal subpattern-assignment (OSPA) metric, demonstrating consistent improvements over conventional VSBL without calibration. Furthermore, we show that integrating the estimation of the calibration parameters into the VSBL algorithm actually increases convergence speed, since a missing or wrong calibration results in the additional estimation of spurious components.

title: LeMon: An eBPF-Driven System Monitoring Framework for Wireless Access Points.
abstract: Wi-Fi has become the primary connectivity medium for modern consumer and IoT devices, yet performance and reliability issues remain poorly understood due to a lack of efficient real-time monitoring tools. Existing approaches rely on coarse Access Point (AP) portal logging, kernel modifications, or packet capture, all of which impose significant overhead or lack sufficient visibility into the network stack. In this paper, we present LeMon, an eBPF-based monitoring framework that performs high-rate, in-kernel aggregation of network statistics and exports them to user-space through a lightweight shared-memory mechanism. LeMon presents a novel map-and-ring-buffer architecture to minimize function calls, reduce copy overhead, and maintain cache locality on APs. As a use case, we demonstrate that LeMon enables real-time flow monitoring with low processor overhead, providing a practical foundation for broader kernel-resident analytics of wireless routers and edge diagnostics.

title: Hybrid Routing with Load-Balanced Resource Allocation in FSO-Assisted Data Center QNs.
abstract: Most existing studies on quantum networks (QNs) focus either on fiber-based transmission or on free-space optical (FSO)-based transmission in isolation. However, little attention has been given to architectures that combine both, which are particularly important for data-center QNs to handle heavy transmission requests. To capture the intrinsic characteristics of hybrid transmission, we formulate a novel optimization problem named HRP, which jointly determines the transmission method for each request and identifies entangled paths while ensuring load balancing across network resources. To address this problem, we propose an approximation algorithm named AHRP. The AHRP leverages linear programming (LP) relaxation and tailored rounding, complemented by a practical heuristic, to provide both provable guarantees and practical adaptability. Simulation results show that the AHRP reduces the maximum network utilization by an average of 36%.

title: AI-based Intrusion Detection Systems for Medical IoT Networks: A Performance Analysis.
abstract: In healthcare, the security challenges created by extensive and varied Internet of Things (IoT) networks directly threaten patient well-being and data confidentiality. This paper compares the intrusion detection performance of Random Forest (RF), RNN-GRU and TabTransformer AI models across real-time (RT-IoT2022), medical (CIC-IoMT2024), general-purpose (CIC-IoT2023) and industrial (Edge-IIoT) IoT datasets. Each algorithm was evaluated for its ability to detect attacks using multiclass and binary classification tasks. Although performance decreased in multiclass tasks, the binary classification results were strong (0.93 average F1 score and 0.96 average accuracy). RF achieved the highest scores (F1 score 0.82 and accuracy 0.97). In contrast, RNN-GRU (F1 score 0.66, accuracy 0.81) and TT (F1 score 0.68, accuracy 0.82) performed less effectively. Within the Medical IoT domain, all models struggled to detect low-intensity, infrequent reconnaissance and distributed attacks. This reveals a significant vulnerability in clinical systems. The conclusion is that complex deep learning models are not inherently superior for IoT security. These findings suggest that a simpler model, paired with domain-specific, high-quality data, may provide solid and effective basis for intrusion detection in healthcare settings.

title: Scaling Up Parallel Decoding of LoRa Channels.
abstract: LoRa is a widely used IoT protocol optimized for long-range, low-power applications. LoRa networks can operate across up to 64 channels and six spreading factors. Since conventional hardware receivers are capable of monitoring only one channel and one spreading factor at a time, mapping networks and identifying devices in a varied LoRa ecosystem is difficult. To address this problem, we present LoRa-MUX, a real-time software-defined radio (SDR) implementation of a LoRa receiver capable of simultaneously processing multiple channels and spreading factors. Our design uses polyphase channelization to isolate each channel, squelch filtering to eliminate noise from inactive channels, and parameter-parallel demodulation to identify and decode packets. We benchmark LoRa-MUX’s performance in a real-world implementation, across varying distances and transmitter gains, using both RTL-SDR and USRP receivers. The USRP receiver maintains a Packet Reception Rate (PRR) above 90% while decoding up to 30 channels in parallel. Even when scaled to 50 channels, the PRR stays above 60%, 30 times better than the PRR of a single-channel receiver under the same conditions.

title: Gradient-Based Service Placement for Capacity-Constrained Edge Computing in DTNs.
abstract: This paper investigates service placement in an edge computing scenario for Delay/Disruption-Tolerant Networks (DTNs), where intermittent contacts, time-varying reachability, and limited on-board resources make conventional placement techniques ineffective. We consider a demand-weighted latency objective in which users are served by the best available service instance at any time. This results in a non-differentiable, combinatorial optimization problem due to binary deployment decisions and hard minimum operators. To enable efficient policy search, we propose differentiable surrogate formulations that relax binary deployments into continuous variables and replace minimum-latency instance selection with a soft-min approximation while enforcing host capacity constraints through smooth penalties. We develop variants for both single-instance deployment (limits exactly one host per service) and multi-instance placement, where the optimizer determines replication levels subject to capacity. The approach is evaluated through a Monte Carlo study using a very large number of randomly generated DTN contact plans considering both statistically homogeneous and disruption-heterogeneous cases. Results show that gradient-based optimization consistently outperforms baselines that use either consolidation or heuristic distribution, with the largest gains observed under disruption variability. Our method provides a scalable optimization framework for DTN edge service placement and is applicable to satellite constellations and integrated terrestrial–satellite networks.

title: LEAD-Drift: Real-time and Explainable Intent Drift Detection by Learning a Data-Driven Risk Score.
abstract: Intent-Based Networking (IBN) simplifies network management, but its reliability is challenged by "intent drift", where the network’s state gradually deviates from its intended goal, often leading to silent failures. Conventional approaches struggle to detect the subtle, early stages of intent drift, raising alarms only when degradation is significant and failure is imminent, which limits their effectiveness for proactive assurance. To address this, we propose LEAD-Drift, a framework that detects intent drift in real time to enable proactive failure prevention. LEAD-Drift’s core contribution is reformulating intent failure detection as a supervised learning problem by training a lightweight neural network on fixed-horizon labels to predict a future risk score. The model’s raw output is then smoothed with an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) and passed through a statistically tuned threshold to generate robust, real-time alerts. Furthermore, we enhance the framework with two key features for operational intelligence: a multi-horizon modeling technique for dynamic time-to-failure estimation, and per-alert explainability using SHAP to identify root-cause KPIs. Our evaluation on a time-series dataset shows LEAD-Drift provides significantly earlier warnings, improving the average lead time by 7.3 minutes (+17.8%) compared to a distance-based baseline. It also reduces alert noise by 80.2% compared to a weighted-KPI heuristic, with only a minor trade-off in lead time. These results demonstrate that LEAD-Drift as a highly effective, interpretable, and operationally efficient solution for proactive network assurance in IBN.

title: Design and Implementation of Multi-Physics Digital Twin Environments for Integrated Nuclear Reactor and Electric Power Systems.
abstract: Critical infrastructure systems are the backbone of modern society and span a variety of sectors, from transportation to health to energy. Energy systems are comprised of diverse generation types, system configurations, and levels of autonomy. These systems are highly interconnected; when system failures or disturbances occur in one part of the system, they can propagate to connected systems. Thus, it is increasingly important to understand and model interconnected critical infrastructure behavior during normal and abnormal operation. With recent advances in automation, artificial intelligence, and overall digitalization, these systems are increasingly cyber-physical with integrated communication and control networking with underlying physics-based processes. To achieve interconnected, cyber-physical critical infrastructure system models, digital twin emulation environments are key. In this paper, we present the design and implementation of a multi-physics digital twin environment for integrated nuclear reactor and electric power systems that enables modeling of diverse cyber-physical disturbances and real-time data collection to assess detection and mitigation performance. The presented multi-physics digital twin modular architecture can be used as a design basis for other interconnected critical infrastructure environments and/or real system models to achieve real-time, cyber-physical operation.

title: Layered Normalized Min-Sum Decoding with Bit Flipping for FDPC Codes.
abstract: Fair-density parity-check (FDPC) codes have been recently introduced demonstrating improved performance compared to low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes standardized in 5G systems particularly in high-rate regimes. In this paper, we introduce a layered normalized min-sum (LNMS) message-passing decoding algorithm for the FDPC codes. We also introduce a syndrome-guided bit flipping (SGBF) method to enhance the error-correction performance of our proposed decoder. The LNMS decoder leverages conflict graph coloring for efficient layered scheduling, enabling faster convergence by grouping non-conflicting check nodes and updating variable nodes immediately after each layer. In the event of decoding failure, the SGBF method is activated, utilizing a novel reliability metric that combines log-likelihood ratio (LLR) magnitudes and syndrome-derived error counts to identify the least reliable bits. A set of candidate sequences is then generated by performing single-bit flips at these positions, with each candidate re-decoded via LNMS. The optimal candidate is selected based on the minimum syndrome weight. Extensive simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed decoder. Numerical simulations on FDPC$(256,192)$ code with a bit-flipping set size of $T = 128$ and a maximum of $5$ iterations demonstrate that the proposed decoder achieves approximately a $0.5\,\mathrm{dB}$ coding gain over standalone LNMS decoding at a frame error rate (FER) of $10^{-3}$, while providing coding gains of $0.75-1.5\,\mathrm{dB}$ over other state-of-the-art codes including polar codes and 5G-LDPC codes at the same length and rate and also under belief propagation decoding.

title: Physical Layer Key Generation for V2X Communications with Doppler Shift Compensation.
abstract: In vehicle to everything (V2X) communications, the high mobility of vehicles makes communication more dynamic and requires fast key agreement. Physical-layer key generation techniques generate symmetric keys for the two communicating parties based on channel reciprocity, without involving the public key infrastructure, thereby reducing the communication overhead and latency of key agreement. However, Doppler shift and channel variations caused by vehicle motion affect the reciprocity of the measured channel state information (CSI). This paper proposes a lightweight Transformer model, named V2Xformer, for CSI reciprocity compensation. A Doppler shift compensation module is introduced to integrate the vehicle speed into the channel feature representation. Hence, the model can dynamically adjust the compensation strategy based on different Doppler shift level. Moreover, the ProbSparse self-attention mechanism is adopted to reduce model parameters and computational requirements. Simulated CSI dataset was generated for model initialization. Based on the open-source real-world V2X CSI dataset, the V2Xformer outperformed the standard Transformer and long short-term memory (LSTM)-Kalman models, resulting a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.998 between compensated CSI of Alice and CSI of Bob. The key agreement rate reached 99.18% with a 3-bit quantization. Moreover, the overall complexity decreased by 22% compared to that of standard Transformer model.

title: Cross-Regional Load Balance in Large-Scale UAV-Assisted Vehicular Fog Computing.
abstract: Spatiotemporal resource imbalance severely hampers the performance of computation offloading in dynamic, large-scale vehicular networks, causing congestion in hotspots and resource underutilization elsewhere. To overcome the inefficiency limitations of static ground infrastructure and resource-constrained unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), we introduce a UAV-assisted cross-regional vehicular fog computing architecture. This architecture leverages UAV swarm to bridge hotspot and idle regions, relaying computational tasks from hotspot to idle regions to balance the network load globally. To address the high-dimensional computing resource matching problem caused by cross-regional collaboration, we propose a two-layer hierarchical scheme. First, in the upper layer, a multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm optimizes UAV trajectories for strategic resource discovery and regional resource allocation. Second, a latency-aware priority queuing mechanism is implemented at the lower layer to prioritize heterogeneous tasks according to their urgency, thereby enhancing task completion. Extensive simulations demonstrate the superiority of our proposed architecture and methods compared to leading baseline approaches, showcasing significant gains in network efficiency and resource utilization.

title: Numerology-Aware Quantum Teleportation Scheduling Considering Data-Qubit Fidelity Decay.
abstract: Entanglement generation and swapping are key techniques for enabling long-distance quantum communication, allowing the creation of end-to-end entangled pairs and making teleportation between non-adjacent nodes possible. However, fidelity loss and decoherence effects must be carefully considered, as they can degrade the quality of the transmitted data. Swapping operations inherently reduce fidelity, while the data to be teleported may also suffer decoherence during the wait for an end-to-end entangled pair to be established. Although the former issue is frequently examined in existing literature, the latter (i.e., decoherence of waiting data) remains largely overlooked. Together, these effects pose significant scheduling challenges. To address this, we formulate a novel optimization problem, termed DAFSP, and propose a separation-oracle-based algorithm, DORA, which achieves a bi-criteria approximation ratio of (O(1),O(log|V||T|)). Finally, simulation results manifest that DORA can notably outperform existing approaches, achieving an average improvement of 495% in the sum of expected overall fidelity.

title: Digital-Twin Assisted Dynamic HAP Deployment and Resource Allocation Using Reinforcement Learning in Air-Ground Integrated Networks.
abstract: Rapid deployment of communication infrastructure is essential for emergency response in disaster and hotspot areas where terrestrial networks may be damaged or inadequate. High-altitude platforms (HAPs) provide flexible aerial coverage but require joint optimization of their three-dimensional (3D) positions and resource allocation under dynamic user mobility and time-varying channels. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a digital twin (DT)-assisted joint optimization framework based on deep reinforcement learning (RL), where deployment and resource optimization occur at two different timescales to reflect practical operations. Our proposed framework integrates a DT layer for deployment optimization using simulated network behaviors with a real-time layer that adapts resource allocation and association strategies based on user locations and channel conditions. To enable this, we employ a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm with customized state and action spaces. Simulation results demonstrate that our framework outperforms existing schemes by achieving higher average throughput and smaller fluctuations.

title: MapViT: A Two-Stage ViT-Based Framework for Real-Time Radio Quality Map Prediction in Dynamic Environments.
abstract: Recent advancements in mobile and wireless networks are unlocking the full potential of robotic autonomy, enabling robots to take advantage of ultra-low latency, high data throughput, and ubiquitous connectivity. However, for robots to navigate and operate seamlessly, efficiently and reliably, they must have an accurate understanding of both their surrounding environment and the quality of radio signals. Achieving this in highly dynamic and ever-changing environments remains a challenging and largely unsolved problem. In this paper, we introduce MapViT, a two-stage Vision Transformer (ViT)-based framework inspired by the success of pre-train and fine-tune paradigm for Large Language Models (LLMs). MapViT is designed to predict both environmental changes and expected radio signal quality. We evaluate the framework using a set of representative Machine Learning (ML) models, analyzing their respective strengths and limitations across different scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed two-stage pipeline enables real-time prediction, with the ViT-based implementation achieving a strong balance between accuracy and computational efficiency. This makes MapViT a promising solution for energy- and resource-constrained platforms such as mobile robots. Moreover, the geometry-pretrained model derived from the self-supervised training in the first stage improves data efficiency and transferability, enabling effective downstream predictions even with limited labeled data. Overall, this work lays the foundation for next-generation digital twin ecosystems, and it paves the way for a new class of ML base models driving multi-modal intelligence in future 6G-enabled systems.

title: MoESEC: A Mixture of Experts Framework for Edge Semantic Communication Networks.
abstract: We present MoESEC, a Mixture of Experts (MoE) framework that unifies sparse MoE coding with resource-aware wireless optimization, enabling reliable and low-latency semantic communication across heterogeneous edge nodes. Unlike monolithic semantic codecs, MoESEC activates a single specialized expert per input, adapting expert ratio (model capacity) to the computational budget of each device. We further introduce the graphics processing unit (GPU) roofline performance model that couples floating-point performance with memory bandwidth to evaluate end-to-end latency. Building on this, we formulate a system-level optimization problem that jointly allocates expert ratios, subcarriers, and transmission power. An iterative heuristic Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) optimization framework is proposed to maximize semantic accuracy under per-user Quality of Service (QoS) requirements. When deployed on heterogeneous edge nodes under varying channel conditions, MoESEC achieves significant latency reduction while preserving high semantic accuracy. By aligning semantic sparsity with communication and hardware constraints, MoESEC offers a scalable and robust foundation for real-time edge intelligence.

title: Fairness Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Multi-User RIS-Aided Networks.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) technology enables programmable wireless environments but faces challenges under user mobility and multi-user interference. In dynamic scenarios, outdated channel state information (CSI) and unbalanced resource allocation can severely degrade performance. This work proposes a deep reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes base station beamforming and RIS phase shifts while addressing both mobility and fairness among users. A fairness-aware reward based on Jain’s index guides the policy toward equitable performance, and a trajectory predictor (Glimpse) estimates near-future user positions to reduce CSI measurement frequency. Simulation results show that, across different fairness weights and update intervals, the proposed method consistently outperforms the conventional and linear-prediction schemes.

title: Chance-Constrained Task Offloading for Reliability Guarantees in Multi-Tenant Networks.
abstract: We study the problem of task offloading under stochastic delays with reliability guarantees. We introduce the Chance-Constrained Multi-Armed Bandit (CCMAB) framework, where each tenant selects a server to minimize cost while ensuring its experienced delay satisfies a probabilistic latency constraint. We propose the Optimal Chance-Constrained (O2C) algorithm, which learns delay distributions and adapts allocation to meet chance constraints with high probability. We establish its admissibility and derive logarithmic regret bounds, proving strong performance guarantees. Experiments on multi-tenant offloading scenarios show that O2C achieves both reliability guarantees and low cost.

title: Towards Edge Intelligence via Autonomous Navigation: A Robot-Assisted Data Collection Approach.
abstract: With the growing demand for large-scale and high-quality data in edge intelligence systems, mobile robots are increasingly deployed to collect data proactively, particularly in complex environments. However, existing robot-assisted data collection methods face significant challenges in achieving reliable and efficient performance, especially in non-line-of-sight (NLoS) environments. This paper proposes a communication-and-learning dual-driven (CLD) autonomous navigation scheme that incorporates region-aware propagation characteristics and a non-point-mass robot representation. This scheme enables simultaneous optimization of navigation, communication, and learning performance. An efficient algorithm based on majorization–minimization (MM) is proposed to solve the non-convex and non-smooth CLD problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves superior performance in collision-avoidance navigation, data collection, and model training compared to benchmark methods. It is also shown that CLD can adapt to different scenarios by flexibly adjusting the weight factor among navigation, communication and learning objectives.

title: Optimal Policy-Based Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation for O-RAN Q&A.
abstract: Open Radio Access Networks (O-RAN) require intelligent automation for real-time optimization, yet general-purpose Large Language Models (LLMs) often lack the specialized knowledge needed for telecommunications tasks. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates this issue by grounding responses in O-RAN specifications and manuals, but existing RAG pipelines typically rely on static retrieval policies that repeatedly query external knowledge regardless of marginal utility. Such indiscriminate retrieval introduces unnecessary latency and compute overhead, conflicting with O-RAN’s strict timing constraints. This paper presents ARGO, an adaptive RAG framework that explicitly optimizes the trade-off between answer utility and inference cost. ARGO models retrieval control as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process and computes the optimal policy via dynamic programming, yielding a provable two-threshold structure for retrieval, reasoning, and termination. Experiments on O-RAN question answering show that ARGO maintains competitive answer quality while substantially reducing retrieval usage and end-to-end latency. By enabling constant-time, cost-aware decision rules with theoretical optimality guarantees, ARGO provides a deployable foundation for latency-critical O-RAN automation.

title: Analysis on Random Linear Streaming Codes in the Gilbert-Elliott Channel.
abstract: Random linear streaming codes (RLSCs) are a class of real-time encoding technologies that eliminate the queuing delay of block codes, thereby enhancing performance in delay-sensitive applications. The performance of Non-systematic RLSCs (NRLSCs) in i.i.d. symbol erasure channels (SEC) has been analyzed in [Pinwen Su et al. 2022]. In this paper, we aim to explore the fundamental limit of large-field-size NRLSCs in Gilbert-Elliott symbol erasure channels (G-ESEC). Compared to i.i.d SEC, the erasure probability of G-ESEC depends on current channel state, thus the transitions between different states should be considered. To deal with the stochastic state transitions, we introduce two novel techniques. (i) To account for the impact of switching states on probability terms, we find and leverage the recursive structure of the state transition traces. (ii) To obtain the expected number of error timeslots, we derive the stationary initial distribution of the states, and formulate iterative equation to characterize the expectation terms. As a result, we characterize the closed-form expression on the exact error probability of NRLSCs in G-ESEC. Simulations are conducted to verify the correctness of our analysis on the exact error probabilities, and compare the performance of NRLSCs with a systematic variant and also existing streaming codes for sliding window erasure channels.

title: A Novel Design of Sparse Vector Coding Aided URLLC With Periodic Quasi-Complementary Pairs.
abstract: Recently, sparse vector coding (SVC) has emerged as a promising coding scheme for short-packet transmission in ultra-reliable and low-latency communications (URLLCs). The encoding and decoding of SVC are jointly formulated as a standard compressed sensing (CS) problem, in which a codebook with low mutual coherence is required to achieve reliable decoding performance. In this paper, we propose the concept of periodic quasi-complementary pairs (PQCPs), based on which we present a novel design of a deterministic spreading matrix with low mutual coherence for efficient SVC encoding. Furthermore, a modified multipath matching pursuit (MMP) decoder for the proposed SVC scheme is developed. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed designs significantly improve the block error rate (BLER) performance of SVC compared with existing approaches.

title: Dual-Layer Index Modulation Aided Multi-Carrier Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access.
Arena: A Kubernetes-based Testbed for Evaluating Application Deployment across the Computing Continuum.
abstract: This paper introduces Arena, a Kubernetes-based testbed for evaluating application deployment across computing continuum environments (IoT/Edge/Cloud). Arena enables the emulation of diverse computing nodes using Docker containers and leverages Kubernetes for testbed management. Arena integrates the Chaos Mesh framework to simulate network characteristics and Prometheus with Grafana tools for monitoring and visualization purposes. Experiments on the Grid’5000 platform with a Google microservice application demonstrate that Arena’s container-based emulation achieves similar resource usage patterns to virtual machine-based nodes, and its network chaos injection effectively enforces network constraints. Results highlight Arena’s capability to provide a practical and reproducible environment for testing containerized applications across diverse computing continuum nodes.

title: Privacy-Driven Probabilistic Constellation Shaping for Federated Sensing in ISAC Networks.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) is recognized as a core application scenario for sixth-generation (6G) systems. With the continuous expansion of wireless network scale, ISAC has naturally evolved toward networked architectures, making the study of cooperative ISAC systems increasingly important. Meanwhile, multi-node cooperation has been shown to significantly enhance sensing performance by exploiting spatial diversity. Motivated by these considerations, this work investigates a federated sensing architecture, in which multiple edge nodes perform lightweight local processing and forward intermediate results to a fusion center for cooperative sensing. Although raw sensing signals are not shared, the exchanged intermediate information may still lead to communication privacy leakage. To quantify this effect, a privacy metric termed privacy entropy is introduced. Based on this metric, a probabilistic constellation shaping (PCS) scheme is proposed to mitigate privacy leakage while preserving both communication and sensing performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PCS approach achieves lower privacy entropy than conventional uniformly distributed constellations without degrading overall system performance.

title: A Universal Prompt-Guided Foundation Model for Multi-band Channel State Information Modeling.
abstract: Accurate channel state information (CSI) is crucial for MIMO-OFDM systems, yet traditional pilot-based estimation becomes inefficient in 6G scenarios with massive antennas. Existing deep learning approaches alleviate pilot overhead but remain constrained, as they are often tailored to a single task or system configuration, limiting their scalability and adaptability. We propose a masked autoencoder-based foundation model for unified CSI modeling, reformulating temporal prediction, spatial estimation, and frequency estimation into a single learning framework. The model incorporates knowledge-guided prompting and multi-strategy masking to exploit intrinsic temporal-spatial-frequency correlations of CSI, enabling robust generalization across diverse settings without retraining. Experiments on a multi-base-station and multi-frequency-band dataset show that our model consistently outperforms existing baselines by around 20%, achieving superior accuracy and adaptability, which demonstrates the potential to provide a unified and efficient paradigm for CSI acquisition in wireless systems.

title: A Pixel-Based FAS with 64-State Reconfigurability Deployed at Both Transmitter and Receiver for Interference Mitigation.
abstract: Reconfigurable antennas for fluid-antenna systems (FAS) have emerged as a powerful solution for adaptive wave manipulation, enabling robust wireless communication and sensing in deep-fading and interference-prone environments. Unlike conventional MIMO architectures that require multiple RF chains and extensive baseband processing, reconfigurable antennas dynamically shape their radiation patterns to provide spatial and temporal diversity with far lower hardware complexity. In this work, we design a sub-7-GHz pixel-based reconfigurable antenna (PBRA) featuring 64 electronically switchable radiation states, offering substantially greater reconfigurability than existing fluid-antenna designs. By deploying the PBRAs at both the transmitter and receiver, we construct a pixel-based fluid antenna system (PB-FAS) that exploits its large state space and single-RF-chain architecture to enhance link reliability and multi-user performance. We present the structural configuration of the PBRA and characterize its S-parameters and state-dependent radiation behavior. We then evaluate a co-channel two-source 16-QAM downlink system using dual-end PB-FAS deployment. Experimental results show that coordinated state selection provides strong interference suppression, achieving up to 11 dB SINR improvement and 13.2% reduction in EVM. Finally, we discuss system-level extensions and identify key research challenges that may guide future developments of PB-FAS–enabled wireless systems.

title: A Lightweight Blockchain-Based Cross-Domain Authentication and Key Agreement Protocol for Industrial IoT.
abstract: To address the security and scalability issues of cross-domain authentication in the IIoT, this paper proposes a lightweight protocol based on blockchain and the Chebyshev chaotic map. The protocol achieves efficient, PKI-less key negotiation through a hybrid trust framework and the Chebyshev map, and adopts a global Merkle tree commitment mechanism to reduce on-chain storage to a constant level, thereby breaking through the scalability bottleneck. Simultaneously, it integrates three-factor authentication using password, biometrics, and device factors, and designs a "validate-then-access" workflow to resist DDoS attacks. Formal verification and performance analysis show that the scheme surpasses existing protocols in terms of both security and efficiency, making it suitable for large-scale cross-domain IIoT environments.

title: Rate-Efficient Perception-Oriented Generative Semantic Video Communication.
abstract: Immersive video services in 6G are expected to impose stringent pressure on wireless bandwidth, while user satisfaction is dominated by perceptual quality rather than exact pixel fidelity. This motivates a generative semantic communication approach that directly transmits compact semantic representations optimized for human perception. In this paper, we develop PVSC, a perception-oriented semantic video transmission framework that avoids explicit motion-vector estimation and instead leverages learned spatio-temporal context from reference buffers for predictive reconstruction. To enable efficient wireless transmission, PVSC integrates a spatio-temporal entropy model with fine-grained variable symbol-length mapping, producing compact channel-symbol streams under a controllable bandwidth budget. Moreover, PVSC adopts a perception-oriented training objective that combines perceptual supervision with GAN-based adversarial learning, encouraging natural textures and realistic details at low transmission cost. Experimental results demonstrate that PVSC achieves up to 70% and 80% bandwidth savings at comparable LPIPS and DISTS, respectively, compared with an engineered baseline using VTM source coding and 5G LDPC with 3GPP-compliant MCS selection.

title: On the Practical Design of IRS-aided LiFi for Generalized Environments with Transfer Learning Positioning.
abstract: This paper proposes a unified framework that seamlessly integrates transfer learning–based optical wireless positioning (OWP) with an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-aided LiFi system. Unlike conventional machine learning approaches that require extensive retraining under environmental changes, the proposed OWP model adapts efficiently to different room geometries and transceiver layouts using limited fine-tuning data, while achieving centimeter-level positioning accuracy. The estimated positions are then utilized to guide IRSs placement configuration and access points (APs) power allocation, enabling energy-efficient and wide-coverage system operation. A generalized APs and IRSs deployment scheme is further introduced to ensure scalable and energy-efficient operation across diverse indoor environments. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves robust and accurate positioning while maintaining reliable communication performance and low outage probability across diverse environments, demonstrating both adaptability and the feasibility of unified positioning and communication in LiFi networks.

title: Multi-Dimensional Parameter Estimation Using a Single-RF Link via VBI-CP Decomposition.
abstract: As the demand for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) continues to grow, multi-dimensional channel parameters—such as polarization information that improves multipath resolution and enhances the accuracy of sensing tasks like target tracking and activity recognition—have become an essential component of wireless sensing systems. Building upon previous research on single-RF-link direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation, this paper proposes a multi-dimensional parameter estimation framework capable of accurately extracting channel features including the angle of arrival (AoA), elevation of arrival (EoA), time of flight (ToF), auxiliary polarization angle (APA), and polarization phase difference (PPD). To address strong parameter coupling and the curse of dimensionality, the problem is reformulated into a tensor-based model, and the parameters are jointly estimated via CANDECOMP/PARAFAC decomposition (CPD). A virtual polarization array (VPA) is incorporated to improve identifiability, while a Variational Bayesian Inference (VBI) framework automatically infers the number of signal paths and enhances robustness against noise and model mismatch. Prototype experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves accurate multi-dimensional parameter estimation and high localization precision using only a single RF link, highlighting its potential for practical ISAC applications.

title: Enhancing Holographic Communication with QoE-Driven Semantic Transmission.
abstract: Holographic communication is a key enabler for 6G immersive services, but its massive data volume poses significant challenges to traditional communication systems. Semantic communication offers a promising solution. However, integrating it with HC, designing a joint source–channel coding (JSCC) model for holographic information extraction and reconstruction, and evaluating the semantic-to-holographic user quality of experience (QoE) remain major challenges. To address these challenges, we propose a QoE-driven semantic transmission framework for holographic communication (ESHC) and systematically optimize its three core components: JSCC module, QoE module, and multimodal resource allocation module. We optimized the design of these three core components individually. First, addressing the limitation that existing JSCC models cannot adapt to a wide range of signal-to-noise ratios with a single model, we developed a voxel importance function and designed a 3D Attention Feature (3D-AF) module based on it. Compared to existing methods, the JSCC model integrated with 3D-AF achieved a 30% performance improvement. Second, we established the first holographic QoE mathematical model incorporating semantic communication factors and proposed a joint optimization problem targeting QoE maximization, involving holographic reconstruction density, computational resources, and semantic communication resource allocation. Finally, for the multimodal resource allocation module, we developed an Online Decision Transformer-based resource allocation algorithm (ODT-RA) to efficiently solve this optimization problem, enabling online optimal resource allocation. Simulation results demonstrate that under identical conditions, ODT-RA achieves 30%-40% higher performance than advanced reinforcement learning methods.

title: Co-Optimization of Satellite Wake-Up and Routing for Lifetime and Delay Balance in LEO Constellations.
abstract: Traditional routing algorithms in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks optimize performance metrics such as delay but are often energy-unaware, leading to constellation energy imbalance and connection lifetime reduction. To address this, we propose a Simulated Annealing-based Hierarchical Satellite Optimizer (SA-HSO), i.e., a hierarchical framework that co-optimizes total service delay and satellite battery lifetime. Specifically, our proposed SA-HSO first formulates an equivalent objective function to minimize the weighted sum of delay and lifetime consumption. Then, it employs an upper-level simulated annealing algorithm to dynamically select the number and set of active satellites, coupled with a lower-level routing optimizer. Simulations show that SA-HSO reduces the normalized objective value by 41.5% and 66.7% compared to the greedy and random activation schemes, respectively. Meanwhile, it improves the energy balance by 33.4% and 48.3%, respectively. Our method effectively balances the energy use and delay reduction, while achieving sustained constellation operation with 99% service reliability.

title: MemeUMPIRE: Zero-Shot Multi-Agent Debate with Judge for Explainable Harmful-Meme Reasoning.
abstract: Memes, which combine text, imagery, and cultural cues in multimodal form, spread fast and shape entertainment, marketing, propaganda, and politics. Their humor-driven virality also enables misuse, smuggling misinformation, hate, and divisive stereotypes past conventional moderation. Prior machine-learning and LLM-based approaches can detect harmful content but often lack interpretability. Recently, prompt-based and debate-style frameworks have emerged to provide richer explanations and more transparent reasoning. Building on this momentum, we propose MemeUMPIRE, a zero-shot, model-agnostic framework using structured, adversarial reasoning. It runs a claim-centric, three-stage pipeline, including Initial Judgment, Structured Debate, and Final Judgment where agents critique a falsifiable harmfulness hypothesis, surface counterevidence, and refine decisions. This judgment-centric design yields auditable rationales, stronger consistency checks, and improved predictions without fine-tuning.

title: Toward Agentic AI: Task-Oriented Communication for Hierarchical Planning of Long-Horizon Tasks.
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is an AI paradigm that can perceive the environment, reason over observations, and execute actions to achieve specific goals. Task-oriented communication supports agentic AI by transmitting only the task-related information instead of full raw data in order to reduce the bandwidth requirement. In real-world scenarios, AI agents often need to perform a sequence of actions to complete complex tasks. Completing these long-horizon tasks requires a hierarchical agentic AI architecture, where a high-level planner module decomposes a task into subtasks, and a low-level actor module executes each subtask sequentially. Since each subtask has a distinct goal, the existing task-oriented communication schemes are not designed to handle different goals for different subtasks. To address this challenge, in this paper, we develop a hierarchical task-oriented communication (HiTOC) framework. We consider a system with an edge server and a robot as an edge device. The high-level planner and low-level actor modules reside on the edge server. The robot transmits only the environmental observation that is relevant to the current subtask to the edge server. We propose a conditional variational information bottleneck (cVIB) approach to train the HiTOC framework to adaptively transmit minimal information required for each subtask. Simulations conducted on the AI2-THOR platform demonstrate that the proposed HiTOC framework outperforms three state-of-the-art schemes in terms of the success rate on MAP-THOR benchmark.

title: ACE-Grouped Neural Min-Sum Decoding with a GRU Hypernetwork for LDPC Codes.
abstract: In 5G New Radio (NR) and toward 6G ultra-reliable use cases, low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoding must balance low complexity with strong performance in both the waterfall and error-floor regions, yet short cycles and low approximate cycle extrinsic (ACE) connectivity often induce trapping sets that form a bottleneck. This paper targets quasi-cyclic LDPC (QC-LDPC) codes and presents an ACE–grouped neural min–sum (NMS) decoder, termed ACE-NMS, and a variant which incorporates the gated recurrent unit (GRU) hypernetwork, termed ACE-NMS-GRU. In ACE-NMS, we compute short-cycle and ACE statistics on the lifted graph, partition variable nodes (VNs) and check nodes (CNs) into good/bad groups, and learn four weights per iteration (good/bad × VN/CN), injecting structural awareness with a low parameter budget. Building on this compact base, ACE-NMS-GRU attaches a lightweight GRU hypernetwork which ingests symmetric per-iteration reliability summaries and then outputs four multiplicative factors to modulate the next iteration's grouped weights. A one-shot gate driven by the change in the ratio of unsatisfied checks activates the GRU only on stagnating frames. The GRU is trained separately with end-to-end loss on hard frames obtained via mining and mild noise augmentation from the error-floor region. Simulation results show that ACE-NMS attains a frame error rate (FER) comparable to degree-based or per-edge schemes with fewer learned weights. ACE-NMS-GRU keeps the error floor aligned with the recent boosted methods, while improving the waterfall and reducing the average incremental complexity.

title: Anchor Topology and Deployment Optimization for Navigation and Data Transmission in Large-Scale Underwater Networks.
abstract: Underwater vehicles are becoming increasingly important in marine environmental monitoring and data collection tasks. To provide accurate navigation and positioning services to underwater vehicles and efficiently collect vehicle data, the optimized deployment of underwater nodes has become extremely critical. In contrast to terrestrial positioning systems, underwater anchor node deployment tends to be sparse. This is primarily attributed to the random distribution of users, alongside the substantial economic costs and the inherent challenges in maintaining underwater equipment. Unlike terrestrial nodes, which can establish ubiquitous backhaul, underwater anchor nodes suffer from a lack of satellite coverage, leaving them unable to achieve this capability. In this paper, we strive to improve the accuracy of perception positioning and navigation as much as possible while ensuring the transmission foundation constraints of communication. Initially, we conduct an analysis of the potential deployment modes applicable to large-scale underwater navigation systems, followed by the formulation of a topology optimization strategy tailored for the deployment of underwater anchor nodes. We then derive a scaling law to quantify the impact of intra-cluster anchors on navigation performance within a specified area, and further prove a service area coverage condition characterized by a high probability of successful destination arrival. Lastly, we evaluate and validate the performance of the proposed optimization approach through a series of experimental findings.

title: Physics-Informed Wireless Imaging with Implicit Neural Representation in RIS-Aided ISAC System.
abstract: Wireless imaging is emerging as a key capability in next-generation integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, supporting diverse context-aware applications. However, conventional imaging approaches, whether based on physical models or data-driven learning, face challenges such as accurate multipath separation and representative dataset acquisition. To address these issues, this study explores the use of implicit neural representation (INR), a paradigm that has achieved notable advancements in computer vision, for wireless imaging in reconfigurable intelligent surface-aided ISAC systems. The neural network of INR is designed using positional encoding and sine activation functions. Leveraging physics-informed loss functions, INR is optimized through deep learning to represent continuous target shapes and scattering profiles, enabling resolution-agnostic imaging with strong generalization capability. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significant improvements over state-of-the-art techniques and reveals the focal length characteristics of wireless imaging systems.

title: Joint Pricing and Scheduling for SLA-aware Serverless GPU Services.
abstract: The growing demand for large-scale AI inference drives the need for elastic and profitable GPU-as-a-Service platforms. However, existing methods often decouple pricing and scheduling, resulting in reactive and inefficient resource utilization. This paper presents HOPS, a hierarchical optimization framework that jointly integrates dynamic pricing and real-time scheduling for SLA-aware serverless GPU services. The upper-level Pricing and Baseline Adjustment (PBA) algorithm adaptively learns per-tier prices and baseline GPU allocations via stochastic gradient updates, while the lower-level Adaptive Reconfiguration and Matching Scheduler (ARMS) manages fine-grained job placement to minimize SLA violations and switching overhead. The two layers form a closed feedback loop to achieve equilibrium between economic and operational objectives. Trace-driven experiments using real workloads show that HOPS improves overall profit by 45–55%, reduces SLA violations by up to 30%, and lowers switching overhead by one order of magnitude, while sustaining over 70% GPU utilization.

title: A Sensing Dataset Protocol for Benchmarking and Multi-Task Wireless Sensing.
abstract: Wireless sensing has become a fundamental enabler for intelligent environments, supporting applications such as human detection, activity recognition, localization, and vital sign monitoring. Despite rapid advances, existing datasets and pipelines remain fragmented across sensing modalities, hindering fair comparison, transfer, and reproducibility. We propose the Sensing Dataset Protocol (SDP), a protocol-level specification and benchmark framework for large-scale wireless sensing. SDP defines how heterogeneous wireless signals are mapped into a unified perception data-block schema through lightweight synchronization, frequency-time alignment, and resampling, while a Canonical Polyadic-Alternating Least Squares (CP-ALS) pooling stage provides a task-agnostic representation that preserves multipath, spectral, and temporal structures. Built upon this protocol, a unified benchmark is established for detection, recognition, and vital-sign estimation with consistent preprocessing, training, and evaluation. Experiments under the cross-user split demonstrate that SDP significantly reduces variance (approximately 88%) across seeds while maintaining competitive accuracy and latency, confirming its value as a reproducible foundation for multi-modal and multitask sensing research.

title: Generative Feature Imputing for Loss-Resilient Semantic Communication.
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) has emerged as a promising paradigm for achieving unprecedented communication efficiency in sixth-generation (6G) networks. However, deploying SemCom over digital systems introduces new challenges in maintaining robustness against packet losses that distort critical content. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel framework, termed generative feature imputing, which comprises three key techniques. First, we introduce a spatial-error-concentration packetization strategy that spatially concentrates feature distortions by encoding feature elements based on their channel mappings. Second, building on this strategy, we propose a generative feature imputing method that utilizes a diffusion model to efficiently reconstruct missing features caused by packet losses. Finally, we develop a semantic-aware power allocation scheme that enables unequal error protection by allocating transmission power according to the semantic importance of each packet. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms conventional approaches, such as Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding (DJSCC) and JPEG2000, under block fading conditions, achieving higher semantic accuracy and lower Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS) scores.

title: Stochastic Optimization based Offloading in Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations constitute a critical component of Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks (SAGIN). However, the inherent uncertainty and orbital dynamics of LEO satellites in satellite-terrestrial channels degrade communication quality, making it difficult to formulate effective offloading decisions to achieve stable, efficient, and sustainable task offloading links. To address these challenges, this paper incorporates LEO satellite orbital dynamics and adopts a Multi-Stage Stochastic Programming (MSSP) approach to characterize the unstable connectivity between space and ground. Based on this formulation, offloading decisions are optimized to enhance the amount of tasks completed cooperatively by satellites and ground computing centers (GC) within limited contact durations. Furthermore, Sample Average Approximation-Particle Swarm Optimization (SAA-PSO) algorithm is employed to achieve a balance between solution optimality and computational tractability, deriving a sub-optimal policy for the MSSP model. Extensive numerical experiments are conducted to validate the performance of MSSP model. Compared with traditional static scenarios that ignore uncertainties, the proposed model and algorithm significantly improve the stability of satellite-terrestrial connections.

title: Joint Caching and Communication Resource Allocation Using Large Language Models in Low-Altitude Edge IoT Networks.
abstract: Low-altitude edge intelligence networks enabled by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) offer a promising platform to enhance traditional terrestrial Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have significantly enhanced IoT service quality, but the complex trade-off between caching and communication resource allocation in low-altitude edge intelligence networks remains insufficiently explored. Recently, large language models (LLMs), pre-trained on vast datasets, have demonstrated strong potential for jointly optimising caching strategies and communication resource allocation in these environments. In this paper, we propose a comprehensive LLM-enabled framework for intelligent low-altitude edge IoT networks, where cellular user equipment (C-UE) can fetch data content from UAV-assisted mobile edge cache (U-MC) nodes. The objective of the framework is to minimise the total data fetching delay of all C-UEs while maximising the cache hit ratio at each U-MC. To achieve this, we design a novel LLM-based caching strategy and resource allocation optimisation algorithm that can jointly optimise the caching decisions of all C-UEs and the communication resource allocation across the network. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing state-of-the-art benchmarks in reducing total data fetching delay.

title: Bayesian Integrated Tracking and Communication with Random Finite Set Observations.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Bayesian integrated tracking and communication (ITAC) framework. By consolidating the time of arrival (ToA) and angle of departure (AoD) measurement models, a robust Bayesian filtering framework is introduced for single-target tracking in dynamic and cluttered wireless environments. By incorporating random finite set(RFS) theory, the method jointly estimates the target’s existence probability and its kinematic state within a unified Bayesian recursion, effectively overcoming the limitations of conventional filters, which assume that the target can always be detected. Furthermore, the paper derives the signal-to-interference-plus noise ratio (SINR) for both communication and sensing links. The proposed RFS-based Bayesian filter is implemented using a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) approach. Numerical simulations demonstrate the framework’s superior performance in maintaining tracking consistency and accuracy even under challenging propagation conditions. Moreover, the results reveal how different network parameters affect the overall communication and tracking performance.

title: Privis: Towards Content-Aware Secure Volumetric Video Delivery.
abstract: Volumetric video has emerged as a key paradigm in eXtended Reality (XR) and immersive multimedia because it enables highly interactive, spatially consistent 3D experiences. However, the transport-layer security for such 3D content remains largely unaddressed. Existing volumetric streaming pipelines inherit uniform encryption schemes from 2D video, overlooking the heterogeneous privacy sensitivity of different geometry and the strict motion-to-photon latency constraints of real-time XR.We take an initial step toward content-aware secure volumetric video delivery by introducing Privis, a saliency-guided transport framework that (i) partitions volumetric assets into independent units, (ii) applies lightweight authenticated encryption with adaptive key rotation, and (iii) employs selective traffic shaping to balance confidentiality and low latency. Privis specifies a generalized transport-layer security architecture for volumetric media, defining core abstractions and adaptive protection mechanisms. We further explore a prototype implementation and present initial latency measurements to illustrate feasibility and design tradeoffs, providing early empirical guidance toward future work on real-time, saliency-conditioned secure delivery.

title: Joint Secure Communication and Over-the-Air Computation via Advanced Multiple Access.
abstract: Joint communication and computation are pivotal for enabling multi-functional 6G networks. This paper investigates secure beamforming for joint communication and over-the-air computation in Internet of Things (IoT) networks. We consider a multiple access scenario where IoT devices concurrently transmit data streams and computation signals to a legitimate base station in the presence of an eavesdropper. To enhance physical layer security without compromising computation accuracy, we propose an artificial noise-aided cooperative beamforming scheme. Our objective is to maximize the sum secrecy rate subject to computational mean squared error and power constraints. For addressing the non-convexity arising from matrix fractions within logarithmic determinants, we develop a low-complexity algorithm based on the matrix-extended generalized Lagrangian dual transformation. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly reduces computational complexity compared to constrained concave-convex procedure baseline while validating the effectiveness of the secure integration scheme.

title: Lightweight Online Meta-Learning for Intrusion Detection under Drift and Adversarial Attacks.
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are essential for securing modern communication networks but face challenges in handling concept drift, the evolving nature of traffic and threats, while resisting adversarial attacks. Conventional IDSs often require computationally expensive full retraining, which limits their real-time deployment in resource-constrained communication environments. This paper presents a meta-learning–driven adaptive IDS framework for attack detection and prevention in dynamic networked systems. The proposed design leverages First-Order Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (FOMAML) to enable rapid online adaptation using a small memory buffer, eliminating the need for complete retraining. To strengthen resilience, adversarial robustness is enhanced by integrating Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM)-based adversarial training directly into the meta-adaptation loop. Furthermore, an adaptive controller utilizes rolling-window accuracy monitoring to trigger updates only when significant performance degradation is observed, minimizing computational overhead. Experiments on the IDSIoT2024 dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework maintains robust detection performance, sustaining an F1-score above 0.93 across varying drift severities and exhibiting rapid recovery under simultaneous multi-class drift and adversarial attack scenarios. Its compact model size of 102.40KB and fast adaptation time of 41.41ms confirm its suitability for real-time, resource-constrained communication scenarios, highlighting the potential of meta-learning for attack detection and prevention in next-generation communication systems.

title: A Novel SNR-Adaptive Fusion Scheme Based on Feature-wise Linear Modulation in Few-Shot AMC.
abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is a critical task for cognitive radio, yet its performance is often challenged by labeled data scarcity in few-shot scenarios. This paper proposes a novel framework, neuro-eye diagram operator and signal-to-noise ratios (SNR)-adaptive fusion scheme (NEDO-SAF). This framework incorporates an SNR-adaptive frequency-domain interpolation (SAFDI) method to mitigate data scarcity, a curriculum-based training strategy for stable learning, and a multi-modal fusion architecture with a hierarchical Transformer to extract highly discriminative features. Evaluated on the RML2016.10a dataset with only 10% of labeled data, NEDO-SAF achieves a state-of-the-art 74.74% overall accuracy. It also demonstrates remarkable data efficiency, requiring only ~5.7% of labeled data to reach 70% accuracy, a task that requires ~28.1% for the suboptimal model. The key innovations of deep multi-modal fusion and adaptive data handling provide a robust foundation for building data-efficient cognitive radio systems, enabling reliable spectrum awareness in practical, data-constrained wireless networks.

title: Detection of Short-Form Video Addiction through Diffusion-Based Graph Augmentation.
abstract: Short-form videos (SFVs) now dominate online entertainment, yet their addictive tendencies correlate with reduced attention, diminished learning motivation, limited psychological support, academic stress, and social anxiety. Current identification of Short-Form Video Addiction (SFVA) relies on manual observation, missing early warning signs. We introduce the first automated, early-detection framework grounded in social network behavior. We collect the first SFVA dataset (3,179 users) capturing users’ social interactions, and propose Heterogeneous Edge Augmentation for SFVA Detection (HEAD). HEAD applies graph diffusion to mitigate sparsity and missing values, converts user traces into multiple feature modalities, and builds a heterogeneous social graph modeling interactions among users and their topics of interest. Extensive experiments show that HEAD outperforms baselines in early SFVA detection, demonstrating the value of integrating heterogeneous graph modeling with graph-based signal propagation for behavioral risk identification.

title: Adaptive Source-Channel Coded Semantic Communication for Collaborative Perception.
abstract: Collaborative perception (CP) has been a promising solution for connected and autonomous vehicles, enabling multi-view sensing to overcome occlusions and extend perception range in vehicular networks. However, conventional CP requires extensive information sharing, which incurs significant communication overhead and is highly sensitive to channel conditions. To address this issue, we propose a novel semantic communication framework with adaptive source-channel coding for CP (ASC-CP), where task-critical features are adaptively extracted, compressed, and protected according to channel conditions and communication bandwidth constraints. To enable joint optimization of source-channel coding, we approximate the end-to-end (E2E) task distortion by deriving an upper bound that decouples source-induced and channel-induced components and formulate the corresponding optimization problem. Building on this formulation, we develop a two-step adaptive optimization strategy to minimize the E2E task distortion through its derived upper bound under given channel conditions and bandwidth constraints. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ASC-CP achieves superior detection accuracy and communication efficiency compared with source-channel-separated schemes and state-of-the-art analog deep joint source-channel coding approaches.

title: Hybrid Spherical- and Planar-Wave Channel Modeling and Jitter Analysis for Multi-UAV Near-field Communications.
abstract: Extremely large antenna array (ELAA), enabled by distributed multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems, is a key technology for future 6G networks. Due to their large aperture, these systems frequently operate in the near-field, rendering the conventional plane-wave assumption invalid. To accurately characterize the channel, this paper first validates the hybrid spherical-plane wave model (HSPWM) as an effective framework that balances modeling accuracy and analytical tractability. However, the practical performance of these collaborative systems is critically limited by the inherent attitude jitter of each UAV, which can disrupt coherent beamforming. To this end, this paper integrates a three-dimensional random attitude jitter model into the multi-UAV near-field channel. Building upon this jitter-aware model, we derive a closed-form analytical expression for the expected array gain. Our analysis reveals that the performance degradation is not only dependent on the jitter intensity but is also critically linked to the UAV swarm’s geometric configuration and average attitude, highlighting the crucial role of attitude control in maintaining system robustness. Numerical simulations validate our theoretical derivations, providing crucial insights for the design of robust multi-UAV communication systems.

title: Robust Beamforming for Multi-UAV Systems under Attitude Jitter via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Multi-Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) collaborative beamforming is a key enabler for future wireless communications, yet its performance is critically degraded by inherent attitude jitter. To address this, we propose a robust beamforming optimization algorithm, Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO)-Transformer. By jointly optimizing UAV positions and attitude angles, our method maximizes the expected lower bound of the received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in the presence of jitter. We formulate this complex optimization task as a Markov game and design a multi-objective reward function to guide the agents’ learning process. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed approach significantly outperforms existing methods in both convergence speed and final performance, offering a novel solution to enhance the reliability of near-field UAV communication systems.

title: Distributed Deep Reinforcement Learning for Hybrid Beamforming in Cooperative UAV-ISAC Networks.
abstract: The Cooperative Integrated Sensing and Communication (C-ISAC) paradigm has emerged as a key enabler of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted sixth-generation (6G) networks, where precise target localization and high-rate data transmission must be achieved simultaneously under mobility, power, and backhaul constraints. The optimization problem is formulated as a multi-objective problem to jointly optimize UAV trajectories, hybrid beamforming strategies, and orthogonal frequency-division multiple access (OFDMA) resource allocation. The resulting mixed-integer non-convex problem is modeled as a cooperative Markov decision process (MDP) with constraint-aware reward shaping. A fusion center orchestrates subcarrier allocation and integrates multi-static echo information to support Extended Fisher Information Matrix (EFIM)-based sensing. To address this complex optimization, a distributed deep reinforcement learning (DDRL) framework is proposed, based on a centralized-training–decentralized-execution multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate improvements of 20%–35% in spectral efficiency and sub-meter localization accuracy compared with centralized DDPG, greedy, and heuristic approaches.

title: Beyond Diagonal RIS Assisted SAGIN for Environmental Monitoring: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks (SAGINs) are emerging as a critical enabler for large-scale, real-time environmental monitoring. This paper proposes a novel SAGIN framework enhanced by Beyond-Diagonal Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (BD-RIS) to address the coverage, reliability, and efficiency demands of 6G-driven environmental surveillance. We present a four-layer architecture comprising satellites, high-altitude platform stations (HAPS), unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with BD-RIS panels, and ground users, forming an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system. To manage the heterogeneous resources and dynamic conditions, we develop a multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm with a hierarchical attention mechanism. This approach jointly optimizes UAV trajectories, transmission powers, BD-RIS phase configurations, and data fusion weights to maximize detection accuracy while minimizing latency and energy consumption under practical constraints. Extensive simulations validate the proposed framework, achieving a forest-fire detection performance with an F1-score of 0.982, a latency reduction of up to 60% compared to terrestrial-only networks, and a 36% improvement in energy efficiency over a 24-hour continuous monitoring mission.

title: Adaptive xApp Architecture for Efficient E2 Interface Management and Near-Time Data Streaming in O-RAN.
abstract: There is a lack of adaptive mechanisms for handling dynamic E2 subscriptions in O-RAN architectures to enable high-volume message processing in near-real-time RIC environments. In this paper, we present the design and implementation of a high-performance xApp for near-real-time RAN control within the O-RAN architecture. The xApp manages E2 subscriptions dynamically, processes incoming KPM indication messages in a multi-threaded manner, and forwards enriched metrics to message brokers for cloud analytics. It employs closure-based callbacks to inject E2 node identifiers into messages without modifying the standard interface, unlike prior studies that break standardization efforts. The system is implemented in C using the libffcall library to enable closure functionality. The xApp is evaluated in a Kubernetes environment with FlexRIC and multiple simulated gNBs. Evaluation shows that the proposed architecture achieves significant performance gains over a single-threaded baseline. The average end-to-end latency decreases from 47 ms to 14 ms, and throughput increases from 820 to 3150 messages per second. These results demonstrate that the proposed design provides lower-latency data handling for near-real-time RIC applications.

title: Array Geometry-Centric Axial Sidelobe Interference Analysis for Near-Field Multi-User MIMO.
abstract: With the deployment of large antenna arrays at high-frequency bands, future wireless communication systems are likely to operate in the radiative near-field (NF). Unlike far-field beam steering, NF beams can be focused on a spatial region with finite depth, enabling user multiplexing in both range and angle. In NF multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems, achievable rates are limited by interference arising from sidelobes in both the axial (range) and lateral (angle) dimensions.
