This work investigates how axial sidelobes (ASLs) vary with array geometry. Closed-form array gain expressions are derived to characterize ASLs for uniform planar arrays. Analytical results show that the uniform square array (USA) yields the lowest ASLs, followed by the uniform concentric circular array (UCCA), uniform linear array (ULA), and uniform circular array (UCA). Specifically, the USA achieves a peak sidelobe level (PSLL) of -17.6 dB versus -7.9 dB for the UCA. Numerical simulations confirm that the USA provides superior sidelobe suppression and highest sumrate performance.

title: Exploratory TEID-Based Defence against Flooding Attacks in 5G Slicing.
abstract: Network slicing, one of the main enablers of 5G networks, is susceptible to flooding attacks. As the case with other types of networks, spoofing the IP addresses of the attackers complicates the tasks of detection and mitigation. Traditional mitigation by blocking the detected source IPs might lead to impacting and blocking legitimate IP addresses.In 5G networks, each traffic stream between the User Equipment (UE) and the Network Core (NC) gets segregated and encapsulated into communication flows utilizing tunnels with distinct Tunnel Endpoint Identifiers (TEIDs) regardless of the inner IPs used in the traffic packets. In this paper, we leverage the TEID of each UE, in addition to traditinal IP and port filtering, to mitigate flood attacks when source IP addresses are spoofed in 5G slicing scenarios. This paper explores a mitigation solution for the 5G network architecture and combines protection layers: 1) IP and port-level filetring layer deployed at the User Plane Function (UPF), and 2) MAC and TEID (Tunnel Endpoint Identifier)-level layer deployed at the gNBs.Our results show the effectiveness of the proposed solution in the hope of expanding research that utilizes new 5G architectural properties to provide defences that may not be possible in earlier architectures.

title: Modeling and Analysis of Collaborative Communications with Multiple LEO Satellites in Non-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites have been widely regarded as a crucial component in emerging non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) to provide global coverage for ground users (GUs). However, traditional LEO satellite communications, relying on individual satellite support, may suffer from poor signal propagation or high failure probabilities. To address this, we focus on a collaborative communication scenario involving multiple LEO satellites in an NTN. Then, we develop a theoretical framework to investigate the signal transmission performance when a GU is served by multiple LEO satellites. We model LEO satellite distribution as a binomial point process (BPP) on a sphere and rank satellites according to their distances to the GU. Our analysis takes into account both uplink and downlink transmissions under shadowed Rician fading and satellite failure probabilities. By employing a collaborative communication scheme, we derive the overall transmission success probability and its corresponding asymptotic expressions. Simulation results are conducted to validate the accuracy of our analysis and demonstrate the impact of network parameters on collaborative communications involving multiple LEO satellites in NTNs.

title: Optimal Array Size Analysis for Reconfigurable Holographic Surface Enabled Ultra-Massive MIMO.
abstract: Reconfigurable holographic surfaces (RHSs) offer a cost-effective implementation of ultra-massive multiple-input multiple-output to support increasing data rate demands in wireless networks. Unlike conventional antenna designs, RHS operates based on sequential element excitation, where an electromagnetic wave travels along the structure while gradually radiating energy and decaying in amplitude. Consequently, there exists a minimum RHS size to meet the data rate requirement, beyond which adding more elements yields diminishing returns in performance and only increases the hardware cost. In this paper, we first develop a serial propagation model of the RHS to characterize the mutual coupling among its radiation elements. Based on this model, we then derive a closed-form expression for the upper bound of the minimum RHS size required to meet a given achievable rate. Simulations verify that this bound serves as an effective guideline for practical RHS design.

title: Bandwidth-Independent Imaging in 6G Integrated Sensing and Communication Systems.
abstract: Imaging is a crucial sensing function that finds wide applications in environmental reconstruction, autonomous driving, etc. However, existing radio imaging techniques require at least Gigahertz-level bandwidth for high-resolution range estimation, and cannot be applied in 6G integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) network with Megahertz-level bandwidth. In this paper, we propose two novel high-resolution radio imaging techniques that can work on the limited-bandwidth 6G signals - bandwidth-independent synthetic aperture radar (BI-SAR), where the aerial base station (BS) moves along a circular trajectory to image the static targets; as well as bandwidth-independent inverse synthetic aperture radar (BI-ISAR), where the BS is static and the targets spin along an axis. Different from conventional SAR and ISAR counterparts that rely on range estimation, our proposed schemes can simply combine the Doppler spectrogram observed over one spin period to perform imaging. We also reveal that the signal model under our BI-SAR and BI-ISAR schemes is related to that under computer tomography (CT), but with an anisotropic scattering function, instead of an isotropic attenuation function as in CT imaging. We design the iterative adaptive approach-based Doppler association (IAA-DA) algorithm to tackle the above issue. Both numerical examples and real-world experiments are provided to show the feasibility and the effectiveness of our proposed BI imaging schemes.

title: PASS-Enhanced MEC: Joint Optimization of Task Offloading and Uplink PASS Beamforming.
abstract: A pinching-antenna system (PASS)-enhanced mobile edge computing (MEC) architecture is investigated to improve the task offloading efficiency and latency performance in dynamic wireless environments. By leveraging dielectric waveguides and flexibly adjustable pinching antennas, PASS establishes short-distance line-of-sight (LoS) links while effectively mitigating the significant path loss and potential signal blockage, making it a promising solution for high-frequency MEC systems. We formulate a network latency minimization problem to joint optimize uplink PASS beamforming and task offloading. The resulting problem is modeled as a Markov decision process (MDP) and solved via the deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method. To address the instability introduced by the $\max$ operator in the objective function, we propose a load balancing-aware proximal policy optimization (LBPPO) algorithm. LBPPO incorporates both node-level and waveguide-level load balancing information into the policy design, maintaining computational and transmission delay equilibrium, respectively. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PASS-enhanced MEC with adaptive uplink PASS beamforming exhibit stronger convergence capability than fixed-PA baselines and conventional MIMO-assisted MEC, especially in scenarios with a large number of UEs or high transmit power.

title: Throughput Maximization for UAV-Aided Networks with STAR-RIS: A Joint Scheduling and Beamforming Approach.
abstract: The combination of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) holds great promise for improving wireless connectivity in urban environments. However, conventional RISs are limited to single-side reflection, restricting coverage and deployment flexibility. To address this, we propose a UAV-assisted communication framework enhanced by a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting RIS (STAR-RIS) deployed on a building facade, enabling seamless service for both indoor and outdoor users. We formulate a joint optimization problem that maximizes the system sum-rate by coordinating user scheduling, active beamforming, and STAR-RIS configuration. The resulting mixed-integer non-convex problem is decomposed into two subproblems: the user scheduling subproblem is tackled using a penalty-based successive convex approximation (P-SCA) method, while the STAR-RIS configuration and active beamforming subproblem is solved via a penalty dual decomposition (PDD) approach with closed-form iterative updates. Simulation results validate the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed framework. Compared to existing benchmarks, our method achieves higher throughput and demonstrates the importance of jointly optimizing user scheduling, active beamforming and STAR-RIS adaptation in dynamic UAV-enabled communication scenarios.

title: High-Reliability Decoupling in Asynchronous UWB ISAC Systems for Rail Shunting Applications.
abstract: This paper investigates a distributed asynchronous integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system for rail shunting scenarios based on impulse radio ultra-wideband (UWB) signals. To address the lack of global time synchronization and severe multipath effects, a reliability-aware differential signal processing framework is proposed. Specifically, a differential decoupling scheme for pulse position modulation (PPM) is developed to eliminate reliance on absolute clock information, with soft amplitude information (SAI) and soft interval information (SII) constructed to quantify pulse reliability and mitigate error propagation caused by clutter and missed detections. Building upon the reliability-filtered measurements, a multi-link Doppler fusion scheme is further designed to reconstruct sensing echoes and estimate train velocity and position. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves robust decoupling and accurate sensing performance in rail shunting scenarios.

title: Convolutional Code Aided Index Modulation for Dual Mode Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing.
abstract: Dual mode aided orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (DM-OFDM) is a promising improvement of conventional OFDM with index modulation (OFDM-IM), which exploits index domain of symbol modes generated from standard constellations to realize IM operation. In DM-OFDM, the minimum Euclidean distance between two symbol modes is smaller than that of two different symbols within same symbol mode, which may lead to error propagation due to the erroneous estimate of DM pattern (DMP). To enhance the reliability of the DMPs in the transmission, we propose a novel convolutional code aided IM for DM-OFDM (CIM-DM-OFDM) in which the symbol mode of each subcarrier is controlled by a binary bit in the obtained code word, which can further improve the robustness of the DMPs. With the aid of convolutional code, the dimension of the subblocks can be much higher than that of conventional DM-OFDM, which can greatly improve the bit error rate (BER) performance in medium and high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) region. Moreover, numerical and computer simulations corroborate that the proposed CIM-DM-OFDM has potential to achieve better BER performance with higher spectral efficiency (SE) due to higher robustness of DMPs.

title: IMU-Based Fusion Localization Algorithm in Multi-Band Networks.
abstract: In Internet of Things (IoT) application scenarios, location-based services (LBS) play a vital role. Single-anchor scenarios are common wireless deployments in indoor environments, where virtual anchors (VAs) provide a solution. However, using VA-assisted positioning requires higher multipath delay resolution to estimate multipath distances. Furthermore, due to the lack of a mapping relationship between multipath and VA, the common approach involves employing highly complex exhaustive algorithms. To address these challenges, this paper first introduces multi-band CSI to enhance multipath delay resolution. We then propose a VA-based localization algorithm for generating candidate user equipment (UE) positions with confidence. Finally, we integrate inertial measurement unit (IMU) motion parameters to select the optimal position. By combining IMU and VA-assisted positioning, we reduce computational complexity compared to VA and path matching-based approaches. and more importantly, utilizing VA-based positioning results eliminates cumulative IMU errors. In real-world tests, the proposed algorithm achieved a 0.35 m mean absolute error (MAE) and a 90th-percentile positioning error of 0.72 m , significantly outperforming traditional geometric methods and validating the effectiveness of the approach.

title: Exploiting Near-field Effect with Spatially Separated Sub-arrays for Upper Mid-band ISAC.
abstract: We propose a novel integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework leveraging spatially separated sub-arrays (SAs) in the upper mid-band. While large-scale arrays in the upper-mid band enable near-field operation, which facilitates joint range-angular estimation in sensing and depth-domain spatial multiplexing in communication, the effective near-field range is constrained by the Rayleigh distance. The proposed SA structure effectively forms a large virtual aperture, enabling near-field-like beam focusing beyond this constraint and enhancing spatial resolution. We develop a joint communication and sensing beamformer to support multiple users and multiple dedicated sensing targets. Additionally, we introduce two methods for joint range-angle estimation using the SA configuration. Numerical results demonstrate that the SA deployment significantly outperforms conventional co-located arrays in both sensing accuracy and communication efficiency, achieving a broader sensing-communication trade-off region. These findings highlight the potential of spatially separated SAs for next-generation ISAC systems, offering improved performance without incurring excessive hardware complexity.

title: Rain-Fading Aware Precoding and Combining for Q/V-Band MIMO Satellite Feeder Links.
abstract: This paper presents a rain-fading aware design of linear precoding and combining strategies for Q/V-band Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) satellite feeder links. We revisit classical schemes—Maximum Ratio Transmission/Combining (MRT/MRC), Regularized Zero-Forcing/Zero-Forcing (RZF/ZF), and Weighted Minimum Mean Square Error/Minimum Mean Square Error (WMMSE/MMSE)—by incorporating first- and second-order channel statistics to capture long-term behavior under spatially correlated rain attenuation. Our framework supports multi-antenna gateway configurations, intra-site fading correlation, and inter-gateway interference, while enabling decentralized implementation based on statistical Channel State Information (CSI). Simulation results over realistic European gateway deployments show that WMMSE/MMSE yields performance gains over RZF/ZF at high power levels and large antenna separations, while MRT/MRC offers low-complexity baselines with limited interference suppression capability.

title: Low-Complexity Data-Driven Stochastic Successive Convex Approximation for Fast and Sustainable Precoding in Wireless Sensor Networks.
abstract: We study stochastic nonconvex optimization with convex nonsmooth regularizers and nonlinear functional constraints, which arises naturally in data-driven resource optimization for modern wireless systems. Such problems are central to large-scale IoT and wireless sensor networks, where energy, computational, and latency constraints demand lightweight and scalable optimization methods. Existing constrained stochastic methods often require solving expensive subproblems, limiting real-time deployment. Building on a penalty linearization and momentum-based recursive updates, we propose SCAMPL (Stochastic Successive Convex Approximation with Momentum and Penalty Linearization). SCAMPL replaces costly constrained surrogates with lightweight strongly-convex subproblems that admit closed-form or fast QP solutions and attains the optimal stochastic first-order oracle complexity ${\mathcal{O}}\left({{\varepsilon ^{ - 3/2}}}\right)$ with adaptive stepsizes, providing theoretical support for its practical efficiency. In a fast precoding experiment for wireless sensor networks, SCAMPL reaches target MSE substantially faster (wallclock time) and with lower per-iteration cost than state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating suitability for latency-sensitive IoT deployments.

title: Entanglement-Based Crossbar for Quantum Routers.
abstract: Classical crossbar routers cannot be directly adopted in the quantum domain, due to the laws of quantum mechanics. In this paper, we propose an entanglement-based crossbar as the quantum counterpart of the classical switching fabric, enabling generalized forwarding solely through local Pauli measurements on a multipartite entangled resource, acting as a switching fabric. We formalize the notions of blocking and non-blocking conditions in the quantum domain by providing the design tenets to achieve a non-blocking switching fabric. Then, we introduce the edge-controlled design principle by identifying the minimal 2 × 2 non-blocking base unit as the fundamental building block for scalable router architectures. The proposed framework provides a hardware-agnostic and scalable foundation for quantum routers, bridging classical network theory with quantum-native forwarding.

title: Random Access with Delayed Feedback: Stability, Delay, and Age of Information.
abstract: We study random access for channels with long propagation delay. In such channels, waiting for feedback requires slotted ALOHA to use large slots, leading to reduced throughput, increased delay and Age of Information (AoI). Various schemes have previously been proposed to handle the propagation delay more effectively, such as the Interleaved Channel Policy (ICP) and the Transmit and Wait Policy (TWP). Extending ideas from framed slotted ALOHA to these schemes, we devise two new schemes, called Framed Interleaved Channel Policy (FICP) and Framed Transmit and Wait Policy (FTWP), to handle propagation delay. We compare ICP, TWP, FICP, and FTWP in terms of stability region, delay, and Normalized Average AoI (NAAoI). We find that all perform similar in terms of NAAoI; TWP and FTWP perform superior to others with respect to stability region and delay, FTWP requiring significantly less frequent feedback than TWP.

title: On the Distribution of Matched Filtering with Continuous Aperture Arrays.
abstract: Continuous aperture arrays (CAPAs) provide a theoretical upper bound on the performance of densely packed antenna arrays, but their analysis is limited by the lack of closed-form signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) distributions under realistic fading conditions. This paper derives accurate analytical expressions for the matched-filter SNR distribution of one-dimensional CAPAs in correlated Rayleigh environments under both the sinc and Jakes correlation models using the Karhunen-Loeve expansion. By applying a truncated hypoexponential model, we obtain accurate approximations for the probability density function and cumulative distribution function of the SNR that closely match simulations, including the outage probability region where precise characterization is critical. Compared to a standard gamma approximation, our approach provides significantly improved accuracy in this regime. Additionally, the CAPA system considered is shown to outperform discrete antenna arrays. The derived expressions enable tractable and accurate evaluation of CAPAs under practical channel models.

title: Secrecy-Aware Beamforming Optimization in RIS-Assisted MIMO Systems using SAC DRL.
abstract: This paper investigates the physical layer security (PLS) in a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) downlink in the presence of multiple eavesdroppers. The joint optimization of base-station precoding and RIS phase configuration is formulated as a continuous-control problem and addressed through deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Specifically, a soft actor-critic (SAC) agent is developed to maximize the secrecy rate by adaptively learning optimal beamforming and phase adjustments under dynamic wireless conditions. The proposed framework accounts for distance-dependent path loss, shadowing, and Rayleigh fading, ensuring realistic modeling and robustness to channel uncertainty. The results illustrate the fast convergence and stable secrecy-rate enhancement of the SAC-based design compared with baseline DRL approaches, highlighting its scalability and practical potential for secure and intelligent wireless systems.

title: Enabling mmWave Communications with VCSEL-Based Light-Emitting Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces.
abstract: This paper proposes a light-emitting reconfigurable intelligent surface (LeRIS) architecture that integrates vertical cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) to jointly support user localization and mmWave communication. By leveraging the directional Gaussian beams and dual-mode diversity of VCSELs, we derive a closed-form method for estimating user position and orientation using only three VCSEL sources. These estimates are then used to configure LeRIS panels for directional mmWave beamforming, enabling optimized wave propagation in programmable wireless environments. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves millimeter-level localization accuracy and maintains high spectral efficiency. These findings establish VCSEL-integrated LeRIS as a scalable and multifunctional solution for future 6G programmable wireless environments.

title: A Dual Belief-Driven Bayesian-Stackelberg Framework for Low-Complexity and Secure Near-Field ISAC Systems.
abstract: Ensuring robust security in near-field Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems remains a critical challenge due to dynamic channel conditions, multi-eavesdropper threats, and the high computational burden of real-time optimization at mmWave and THz frequencies. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a Bayesian–Stackelberg framework that jointly optimizes sensing, beamforming, and communication for secure near-field ISAC in high-frequency regimes (mmWave/THz). The dual-algorithm design integrates (i) Adaptive Hybrid Node Role-Switching between secure transmission and cooperative friendly jamming, and (ii) Belief-Driven detection and Beamforming for confidence-based resource allocation. The proposed unified framework substantially improves robustness against adversarial attacks while maintaining linear computational complexity. Simulation results across carrier frequencies from 28 to 410 GHz demonstrate that the method achieves a 35% increase in secrecy rates and maintains a success rate exceeding 98%, outperforming conventional communication systems with minimal runtime overhead. These findings underscore the scalability of belief-driven ISAC security solutions for low-complexity deployment in next-generation high-frequency communication systems.

title: DDPG-Based Joint Power Allocation and Phase Optimization for Secure STAR-RIS Assisted multi-user MISO Systems.
abstract: This paper presents a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG)-based optimization framework for Simultaneously Transmitting and Reflecting Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (STAR-RIS)-assisted secure multi-user MISO systems. The secrecy-rate maximization problem is formulated as a continuous-control task that jointly optimizes transmit power allocation and RIS phase configurations under practical power and phase constraints. A constraint-aware actor-critic architecture is designed, where sigmoid and phase-mapping activations ensure feasible outputs, and target network updates with experience replay improve convergence stability. The proposed model-free framework effectively learns optimal transmission policies in high-dimensional continuous spaces without explicit channel models. Simulation results demonstrate that the STAR-RIS DDPG achieves faster convergence and higher secrecy rewards about 70% improvement compared with conventional RIS DDPG at Pt= 30 dB highlighting its efficiency, scalability, and strong potential for real-time deployment in secure 6G wireless networks.

title: HCLSensor: Human Comfort Level Sensor.
abstract: Human comfort level sensing, crucial for applications in healthcare and smart home applications, often relies on wired or wireless sensors. However, using these devices poses challenges such as non-subjective feelings, maintenance costs, energy consumption, and negative environmental impact. To tackle these challenges, we for the first time propose a novel approach—Human Comfort Level Sensor. In this system, we leverage existing wireless communication infrastructure to discern the user’s comfort level. The key innovation lies in the fact that wireless signals can capture subtle reactions in the human body that indicate changes in comfort level. By exploring the relationship between wireless signals and human comfort level, our HCLSensor system is designed to gather wireless signals, extract distinctive features, and use a deep learning model to detect human comfort level. More importantly, the HCLSensor can be trained with minimal data from one location, such as a lab, yet applied in another, like a residential home, or trained on one individual’s data and used with another’s. Real-world experiments demonstrate that the HCLSensor system achieves significant accuracy: up to 96% when training and testing occur at the same location, 94% when in different places, and 84% when utilizing data from different individuals.

title: P4 Semantic Steering for Serverless Environments.
abstract: As recent developments have put semantic information in the spotlight, meaning-based communication becomes ever more attractive. In this paper, we take a first step toward our vision of a jointly controlled semantic-aware switching and compute fabric by combining P4 programmable steering and serverless computing. We present a low-latency router that can steer requests to Knative serverless functions by collecting and interpreting application-provided semantic tags from the traffic, node processing capabilities and telemetry on compute node resource usage. Through extensive evaluation, we demonstrate that our BMv2 software switch-based solution can achieve comparable performance to standard IP address-based steering implemented with P4 or leveraging the Linux kernel. Furthermore, we validate our implementation's steering and processing node CPU-utilization-based load balancing features using a representative object recognition application. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Architectural Enhancements for Efficient Sensing Data Utilization in 6G ISAC.
abstract: Current architecture proposals within standards development organizations such as ETSI and 3GPP enable sensing capabilities in mobile networks; however, they do not include a repository for storing sensing data. Such a repository can be used for AI model training and to complement ongoing sensing service provisioning by improving efficiency and accuracy. One way of realizing this is through the fusion of historical sensing data with live sensing data. In this paper, we study historical and live sensing data fusion for Integrated Sensing and Communication in future 6G systems and introduce a Sensing Data Storage Function to store historical sensing data and sensing results. We show how the Sensing Data Storage Function can be used with other network functions in a 6G architecture proposition for Integrated Sensing and Communication. We validate our proposal with a measurement model and show performance improvements in terms of detection probability and false-alarm rate. The network functionality to fuse and process sensing data combines live sensing measurements with previously sensed historical sensing data using a map-aware hard filter that rejects detections consistent with known static structures. Our simulation illustrates that, for a traffic junction scenario, map-aware hard filtering substantially reduces false alarms without degrading detection probability.

title: Coverage-Aware UAV Path Planning for IoT Data Collection.
abstract: This paper proposes an analytical framework for UAV path planning designed to achieve reliable and comprehensive data collection in Internet of Things (IoT) networks. Unlike traditional cluster-based trajectory designs that depend on fixed or statistically known device locations, the proposed approach focuses on scenarios with uncertain or dynamic sensor positions—common in mobile, temporary, or disaster-affected environments. The framework employs mathematically derived spiral trajectories to guarantee full regional coverage while respecting practical constraints on flight curvature and total path length, resulting in energy-efficient flight plans. Additionally, it offers a closed-form analytical method to estimate the minimum number of UAVs needed to satisfy given mission deadlines, thereby avoiding computationally intensive optimization routines and providing a scalable and practical solution for large-scale IoT data collection.

title: Radar Parameter Estimation Using Superimposed Pilots in OTFS-Aided ISAC Systems.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel affine-precoded superimposed pilot (SP) framework for orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation in millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems designed for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). The goal is to jointly estimate radar target parameters (RTPs) and wireless channel with improved accuracy. Initially, separate parameter estimation models are formulated for pilot-assisted radar and data-assisted radar to estimate RTPs. These models are then integrated into a joint pilot-data radar framework, leveraging both data and pilot signals simultaneously to improve estimation accuracy. Additionally, a sparse Bayesian learning (BL)-based technique is developed to effectively exploit the sparsity of the radar scattering environment. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SP-aided BL framework achieves up to 6-10 dB SNR gains and significantly lower normalized mean squared error (NMSE) compared to pilot-only and conventional sparse recovery methods.

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Coverage Optimization for User-Centric 6G Movable Antenna Systems.
abstract: This paper proposes QECOGS (Quantum-Enabled Coverage Optimization via Gradient and Swarm), a hybrid quantum-classical framework for user-centric dynamic antenna configuration in next-generation wireless networks. QECOGS jointly optimizes continuous antenna parameters, including azimuth and tilt, using quantum gradients computed via parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs) and the parameter-shift rule, while performing binary base station activation through particle swarm optimization. The proposed design achieves a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}(2a\log (1/\varepsilon ))$, independent of the number of base stations and spatial sampling points, in contrast to classical binary discrete gradient optimization (BDGO), which scales as $\mathcal{O}\left( {\left( {1/{\varepsilon ^2}} \right)BD{a^2}} \right)$. This quantum-hybrid strategy enables logarithmic precision scaling, accelerated convergence, and improved robustness against local minima in high-dimensional discrete search spaces. Simulation results demonstrate 40-50% fewer iterations in hotspot scenarios, consistent performance under fragmented user distributions, and higher final coverage compared to classical methods. These results establish QECOGS as a scalable and efficient solution for self-organizing wireless networks, with extensions toward multi-cell coordination and hardware-efficient PQC implementations for near-term quantum platforms.

title: Mixture of Inverse Gaussians for Hemodynamic Transport (MIGHT) in Vascular Networks.
abstract: Synthetic molecular communication (MC) in the cardiovascular system (CVS) is a key enabler for many envisioned medical applications in the human body, such as targeted drug delivery, early cancer detection, and continuous health monitoring. The design of MC systems for such applications requires suitable models for the signaling molecule propagation through complex vessel networks (VNs). Existing theoretical models offer limited analytical tractability and lack closed-form solutions, making the analysis of large-scale VNs either infeasible or not insightful. To overcome these limitations, in this paper, we propose a novel closed-form physical model, termed MIGHT, for advection-diffusion-driven transport of signaling molecules through complex VNs. The model represents the received molecule flux as a weighted sum of inverse Gaussian (IG) distributions, parameterized by physical properties of the network. The proposed model is validated by comparison with an existing convolution-based model and finite-element simulations. Further, we show that the model can be applied for the reduction of large VNs to simplified representations preserving the essential transport dynamics and for estimating representative VNs based on received signals from unknown VNs.

title: Framework for Evaluating Fixed-Wing HALE Detection Probability under Hostile Ground-Based Radar Surveillance.
abstract: High-altitude long endurance (HALE), similar to the high-altitude platform station (HAPS), is a non-weaponized aerial drone that operates at high elevations for military applications. In this paper, we introduce a framework for evaluating the detection probability of HALE under multiple ground-based radars, where the non-terrestrial network (NTN) scale and relevant factors, as well as the roll angle of the aircraft body, are rigorously accounted for. To capture the independent and random deployment of radars due to battlefield congestion, simulations based on stochastic geometry (SG) are employed. The results demonstrate that both the circular flight radius and the operational altitude of HALE explicitly influence detectability, with lower values reducing the probability of detection. However, the effect of increasing the flight radius saturates beyond a certain threshold. Moreover, when the number of radars remains fixed throughout the SG processes, fewer radars generally yield a higher average probability of detection due to mutual interference among radars, but also introduce a greater detectability variance, thereby highlighting an inherent trade-off between performance and stability.

title: NYUSIM: A Roadmap to AI-Enabled Statistical Channel Modeling and Simulation.
abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into wireless channel modeling requires large, accurate, and physically consistent datasets derived from real measurements. Such datasets are essential for training and validating models that learn spatiotemporal channel behavior across frequencies and environments. NYUSIM, introduced by NYU WIRELESS in 2016, generates realistic spatio-temporal channel data using extensive outdoor and indoor measurements between 28 and 142 GHz. To improve scalability and support 6G research, we migrated the complete NYUSIM framework from MATLAB to Python, and are incorporating new statistical model generation capabilities from extensive field measurements in the new 6G upper mid-band spectrum at 6.75 GHz (FR1(C)) and 16.95 GHz (FR3) [1]. The NYUSIM Python also incorporates a 3D antenna data format, referred to as Ant3D, which is a standardized, full-sphere format for defining canonical, commercial, or measured antenna patterns for any statistical or site-specific ray tracing modeling tool. Migration from MATLAB to Python was rigorously validated through Kolmogorov–Smirnov (K–S) tests, moment analysis, and end-to-end testing with unified randomness control, confirming statistical consistency and reproduction of spatio-temporal channel statistics, including spatial consistency with the open-source MATLAB NYUSIM v4.0 implementation. The NYUSIM Python version is designed to integrate with modern AI workflows and enable large-scale parallel data generation, establishing a robust, verified, and extensible foundation for future AI-enabled channel modeling.

title: Triarchy-Based for DDoS-Resilient IoT Networks.
abstract: Identifying cost-effective attack scenarios in large-scale IoT networks from an adversarial perspective is vital for proactive defense planning, since protecting even a subset of nodes can significantly improve overall resilience. However, no dedicated algorithm currently pinpoints the most efficient attack paths under realistic cost constraints. In this paper, we introduce a new graph structure, the triarchy graph, to formalize cost-efficient attack-path identification and establish the problem’s NP-completeness. Building on this formulation, we propose CRL-MTD, a cost-effective reinforcement learning (RL)-based moving target defense strategy that learns to identify high-impact attack paths and strategically perturbs them to delay adversaries while minimizing operational burden. We evaluate CRL-MTD on real-world SNDlib-based IoT topologies under simulated Mirai botnet attacks. Experimental results show that CRL-MTD improves solution efficiency by 15%, increases attack execution delay by 111%, and reduces system overhead by 90% compared with representative baseline approaches, demonstrating strong practicality for DDoS-resilient IoT deployments.

title: Autonomous UAV Trajectory Design and Evaluation for Data Muling in AERPAW Digital Twin.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly important for extending wireless connectivity, enabling rapid data collection, and supporting resilient communications in disaster-affected or hard-to-reach environments. This paper presents the design and performance evaluation of autonomous trajectory planning algorithms for UAV operating as a data mule in the Arial Experimentation and Research Platform for Advanced Wireless (AERPAW) Digital Twin (DT) environment. The AER-PAW DT enables realistic real-time emulation of UAV-assisted wireless communication scenarios under controlled conditions. Four trajectory strategies: distance-based, data-driven, SNR-based, and proximity-SNR aware are developed and compared for time-critical data collection from multiple Base Stations (BSs). The proposed proximity-SNR aware approach jointly optimizes communication link quality and travel efficiency by balancing distance and received signal strength. Experiments are conducted in the AERPAW DT which is accessed through VPN. The performance of the algorithms is evaluated in terms of throughput and mission completion time. Emulation results demonstrate that the proposed proximity-SNR aware trajectory consistently outperforms other strategies, achieving the higher throughput and reduced mission completion time under varying data volume cases.

title: A Channel-Adaptive Quantum Transform-Domain Variable-Qubit Encoding for Quantum Image Transmission.
abstract: Reliable image transmission over noisy quantum channels is challenging due to qubit decoherence, channel fluctuations, and resource constraints. Quantum communication in the time domain often fail to maintain high image fidelity under varying channel conditions. To address this, we propose an adaptive quantum image transmission framework using variable-qubit transform-based encoding with the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) and perfect channel state information. The system dynamically selects the optimal qubit size based on real-time channel conditions, balancing resource usage and reconstruction quality. Images are source-encoded (JPEG or HEIF), converted to bitstreams, optionally channel-encoded, segmented by qubit size, quantum-encoded into multi-qubit states, and transformed to the frequency domain via QFT for transmission. At the receiver, inverse QFT, measurement, and decoding recover the bitstreams, followed by source decoding to reconstruct the images. Experiments show the adaptive frequency-domain variable-qubit system outperforms fixed-qubit and adaptive time-domain schemes, achieving Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) up to 58.42 dB, Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) up to 0.9992, and Universal Quality Index (UQI) up to 0.9999 for JPEG, and PSNR up to 70.05 dB, SSIM up to 0.9999, and UQI up to 0.9999 for HEIF. These results demonstrate superior fidelity and noise resilience, highlighting the promise of adaptive frequency-domain quantum encoding for robust image transmission.

title: A Blockchain-Based Data Collection System for EV Networks Using zk-Set Membership Proofs and Ring Signatures.
abstract: The rise in electric vehicle (EV) adoption has created a pressing need for data-driven optimization of the charging infrastructure. While collecting data such as traffic patterns, battery usage, and charging behavior can improve efficiency, it also raises privacy concerns and requires coordination among stakeholders who may not fully trust one another. We propose a blockchain-based data collection system that protects user privacy while enabling on-chain compensation for data sharing. Our approach integrates zero-knowledge set membership proofs, ring signatures, and a probabilistic gossip protocol to hide users identities during registration, data upload, and reward retrieval. We evaluate the system’s network performances through simulations using SUMO and NS2.35, and deploy the core smart contracts on the Sepolia Ethereum testnet to analyze gas consumption. This is, to the best of our knowledge, the first system that combines privacy protection with an on-chain data compensation scheme for vehicular networks, allowing users to share data while receiving direct rewards, without revealing their identity.

title: Agentic AI-Driven Autonomous Wireless Networks via Distributed Sensor Integration.
abstract: Recently, agentic AI systems based on large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for autonomous decision-making across various domains. In wireless communications, agentic AI can serve as an intelligent network orchestrator, which dynamically manages communication resources and adapts to changing conditions. Effective operation of agentic AI requires seamless integration of multimodal sensing data from distributed sensors, which poses significant challenges in communication overhead. In this paper, we propose multimodal agentic wireless network (MAWN), a cooperative agentic AI framework that intelligently selects sensing modalities and autonomously plans computational workflows to address various wireless tasks (e.g., beam management). MAWN consists of two specialized LLM agents: the sensor manager agent (SMA) and the function manager agent (FMA). The SMA minimizes data transmission overhead by selecting only necessary sensors while considering data availability, while the FMA dynamically composes optimal tool execution sequences based on task requirements. By combining two LLM agents, MAWN adaptively gathers information and handles requests with reduced communication overhead and no manual configuration. Simulation results demonstrate that MAWN achieves substantial performance improvements across diverse communication tasks.

title: Wi-Fi-based Detection of GNSS Spoofing Attacks.
abstract: GNSS spoofing is a growing threat to UAV operations, especially in decentralized drone swarms. In this paper, we present both a practical spoofing attack and a lightweight detection algorithm based on Wi-Fi RSSI and GNSS coordinates. The attack selectively compromises drones by transmitting a subset of satellite signals, causing drones to calculate wrong positions. Our detection method leverages geometric consistency checks to validate GNSS-based positions without requiring any infrastructure or additional sensors. Simulation results show that the proposed attack successfully misleads victim drones, and that the detection method reliably helps drones identify such attacks.

title: Beam-Hopping Pattern Design for Multi-Beam LEO Satellite Grant-Free Random Access Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates beam-hopping pattern design for grant-free random access in multi-beam low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems. We formulate a binary optimization problem to design beam-hopping patterns that maximize successful transmission probability under imbalanced traffic demands. To address this problem, we propose a novel algorithm that jointly optimizes collision avoidance and decoding success probability through an alternating optimization framework. Specifically, our algorithm employs a bisection method to determine the number of illuminations for each cell based on traffic demand, while utilizing the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to compute the beam-hopping pattern that maximizes decoding success probability. Simulations with realistic traffic demand models demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms existing beam-hopping methods and exhibits robust performance across different system scales.

title: GAIT-DDRQN: Generative-Augmented RL for UAV-Swarm Anti-Jamming.
abstract: As the low-altitude economy (LAE) accelerates, UAV swarms—its key workhorse—are being deployed at scale. Yet the complex LAE environment dramatically enlarges the state, observation, and interference spaces, aggravating data redundancy and coverage gaps and thereby eroding anti-jamming robustness. To address these challenges, we propose a Generative-Adversarial-Intelligent, fingerprint enhanced Double Deep Recurrent Q-network with Transformer refinement (GAIT-DDRQN) framework, which couples data-centric augmentation with sequential decision making to improve communication reliability under heavy interference. Concretely, a variational autoencoder (VAE) in concert with a Transformer captures cross-channel and cross-jammer dependencies and learns a latent interference manifold from which diverse training samples are synthesized. Building on this refined prior, a double deep recurrent Q-network jointly optimizes channel selection and power allocation, maximizing communication success while explicitly curbing energy consumption and hopping overhead. In a 3GPP TR 38.901 UMa setting, across the baselines, our method improves steady-state return by 25.5% on average, reduces energy consumption by 37.7% on average, and lowers the frequency-hopping rate by 18.2%.

title: EdgeSense FM Foundation Model Driven Collaborative Sensing for IoT and Sensor Networks.
abstract: The next billion sensors will be born networked, mobile, and privacy-sensitive. Meanwhile, the rapid progress of large foundation models makes it possible to reason across heterogeneous modalities and incomplete observations. We present EdgeSense-FM, a unified sensing system for Internet-of-Things (IoT) and sensor networks that combines: (1) a modality-agnostic sensor tokenizer that converts diverse time-series and low-power audio/radar streams into compact tokens; (2) cross-modal masked modeling for representation learning; (3) a diffusion-based semantic completion module that imputes missing sensors and denoises harsh environments; and (4) federated, parameter-efficient adaptation via 4-bit QLoRA on the edge for personalization with strict privacy budgets. A lightweight mixture-of-experts (MoE) gate assigns device-/link-specific experts while an energy-aware scheduler chooses between local inference and collaborative offloading. We empirically evaluate EdgeSense-FM on activity recognition, ambient sensing, and robustness under packet loss, reporting accuracy/F1, imputation error, energy, latency, and uplink. EdgeSense-FM consistently improves accuracy by 2–6% over strong baselines while reducing uplink by > 100× via adapter-only federation.

title: Sum-Rate Maximization for Flexible Intelligent Metasurface Enhanced Multiuser MISO Communications.
abstract: Flexible intelligent metasurface (FIM) has garnered significant attention due to its capability of morphing its three-dimensional (3D) surface shape for achieving flexible electromagnetic wave manipulation. Specifically, an FIM has a soft substrate that can perform surface-shape morphing in 3D space, with multiple elements distributed on its surface for signal transmission and reception. By morphing the FIM’s surface shape, constructive signal superposition can be realized while effectively suppressing interference across the surface. This paper explores a multiuser multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) downlink communication system aided by a FIM, while taking into account limitations on the maximum morphing range of FIM and total transmit power. We examine the potential of FIM in enhancing the sum-rate performance by optimizing its surface shape and transmit beamforming jointly using an effective alternating optimization method. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to traditional rigid uniform planar array (UPA), FIM can significantly improve the system sum-rate even in rich scattering communication environments.

title: VirtSat: Programmable Data Plane Virtualization for Satellite Switching Emulation.
abstract: The rapid expansion of mega-constellation networks demands high-fidelity and large-scale emulation to evaluate satellite switching systems under realistic workloads. However, existing emulators struggle to scale to thousands of satellite switching instances, sustain tens of gigabits of throughput, and efficiently update switching logic for research and validation. This paper presents VirtSat, a scalable emulation architecture that virtualizes the programmable data plane (PDP) to enable constellation-scale switching experiments. At its core, VirtSat introduces a super–sub-pipeline design, allowing thousands of virtual switching instances to share a unified hardware pipeline while ensuring per-packet forwarding integrity through lightweight isolation mechanisms. Implemented on both BMv2 and Tofino platforms, VirtSat supports up to 256 virtual instances on BMv2 and 1584 on Tofino. On the Tofino platform, it sustains over 97% of native throughput with less than 22% latency overhead, and achieves line-rate forwarding on a 40 Gbps port with sub-3.2 µs latency.

title: MAPE-Based Device Activity Detection for Massive Grant-Free Access with Low-Resolution ADCs.
abstract: Existing methods for grant-free access with low-resolution ADCs have unsatisfactory accuracy, mainly due to the heuristic quantization design and approximation. To address these issues, we model low-resolution ADCs as extended uniform quantizers and optimize the quantization step size for a fixed number of quantization bits to minimize the mean square error (MSE) for quantization. Then, we approximate the nonlinear quantization function with a linear one with the minimum MSE for approximation using Bussgang decomposition and build a tractable model for the quantized receive signals with sufficient accuracy. Next, based on this model, we develop a block coordinate descent (BCD)-based algorithm for obtaining maximum a posteriori estimation (MAP)-based device activity detection. Finally, we demonstrate through numerical results that the proposed quantization step size optimization, the approximate quantization model, and the MAPE-based detection method are especially effective for grant-free access with low-resolution ADCs.

title: A Tractable Approach for Power Control in Massive Access.
abstract: Massive access or communication, emerging as one of six usage scenarios in 6G, has attracted considerable recent attention due to its potential to empower next-generation industrial cyber-physical systems such as smart grids, factory automation, industrial internet-of-things (IIoT), etc. However, to guarantee its QoS, the associated power control becomes computationally intractable with a huge number of users. In this paper, we present a tractable algorithm for power control in massive access, based on mean-field approximations. In particular, our aim is to maximize the overall throughput in each scheduling period, at the beginning of which each user has a finite number of backlogged bits. To achieve this goal and overcome the curse of dimensionality, a mean-field game (MFG) is formulated. Unfortunately, the formulated MFG is still a non-convex optimization problem. Enlightened by MAPEL, an efficient solver for non-convex power control problem, we leverage multiplicative linear fractional programming (MLFP) to tackle the non-convexity in our formulated MFG. Furthermore, the mean-field approximation assisted power control strategy requires low signaling overhead consumed for estimation and feedback of channel state information (CSI). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed tractable power control attains substantial performance gains in both the overall throughput and computational complexity.

title: Efficient Pipeline Parallel Edge Inference for Large Language Models in Wireless Networks.
abstract: Edge computing enables distributed inference for computation-intensive applications. However, the autoregressive nature and large model size of large language models (LLMs) pose challenges for their deployment in wireless edge networks. Existing edge inference methods mainly assume an equivalent delay for each token generation step, which is inaccurate in practice. To address these challenges, we propose a pipeline parallel edge inference framework for LLMs, where tasks are grouped into multiple batches and processed in parallel by partitioning the LLM into multiple shards. An accurate latency model is established, where the latency of each token generation step increases during the autoregressive generation process. Building on this model, the end-to-end inference latency is minimized, which is formulated as a joint optimization problem of bandwidth allocation and model partitioning subject to heterogeneous GPU memory constraints. Then, we propose an efficient algorithm that derives a closed-form bandwidth allocation and design a dynamic programming algorithm for model partitioning. Extensive evaluations on BLOOM-3B and LLaMA-2-7B demonstrate that our approach reduces latency by up to 32.0% versus state-of-the-art baselines across diverse edge scenarios.

title: Towards Scalable Service Function Chaining in Software-Defined Wide Area Networks.
abstract: In Software-Defined Wide Area Networks (SD-WANs), diverse applications are typically provisioned through the deployment of Service Function Chains (SFCs), which is inherently complex and NP-hard. Numerous prior works focus on reducing complexity and improving scalability via routing simplification. However, in bandwidth-constrained SD-WANs, such simplification aggravates congestion on critical links, thus degrading the service quality. This creates a fundamental trade-off between routing flexibility and algorithmic complexity. To balance such trade-off, this work presents the Congestion-Aware Scalable Deployment (CASD) algorithm. First, SFC deployment is formulated as a low-complexity ILP problem adopting coarse-grained E2E routing. A parallel deployment framework is then designed, where we propose the graph-embedding-based Traffic Pattern Recognition (TPR) to achieve per-request problem decomposition, innovatively utilizing Node2Vec for SFC request embedding. To alleviate link congestion induced by coarse-grained routing, a congestion-aware path adjustment method is designed, which customizes E2E paths per request through expectation-based iterations, thereby achieving traffic load balancing. Experimental results validate that for centrally distributed SFC requests, CASD achieves 1-2 orders of magnitude efficiency improvement over fine-grained routing approaches, with the benefit loss constrained up to 6%.

title: Asymptotically Optimal Local MMSE Precoding Design for Cell Free Massive MIMO System.
Elimination of Non-Ideal Factors in ISAC Systems Based on Over-the-Air Reciprocity Calibration.
abstract: Time and frequency synchronization in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems pose a critical challenge for both communication and sensing performance. Cell-free communication systems, characterized by the distributed multi-antenna architecture, are well-suited for enabling user-centric cooperative communication and sensing. However, achieving this potential requires eliminating timing and frequency offsets across distributed transmission points. To address this, we propose a time-frequency synchronization algorithm based on over-the-air (OTA) reciprocity calibration, aiming to restore channel reciprocity and eliminate non-ideal factors in sensing. We first model the uplink and downlink channels with consideration of timing advance (TA), and analyze how reciprocity calibration influences the non-ideal factors of sensing systems. Furthermore, we introduce a calibration algorithm that leverages cross transmission reception point (TRP) and cross user equipment (UE) channels to enhance calibration accuracy. Both simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed OTA reciprocity calibration improves the average user spectral efficiency as well as the sensing signal-to-noise-plus-interference ratio (SINR) in cooperative scenarios.

title: Security and Cost Trade-off of Centralized and Distributed Authentication Schemes for Wireless Networks.
abstract: Authentication serves as the cornerstone for establishing trust and securing transmission in wireless networks. As modern wireless networks evolve to support collaboration and sharing among multiple parties and to enable open, diverse, and distributed services and applications, the widely-used centralized authentication scheme struggles to meet requirements for reliability, flexibility, and fault tolerance. In this context, distributed authentication has emerged as a promising solution to these challenges. Yet, it still introduces operational overhead, and thus raises critical concerns in terms of its cost-efficiency in open and dynamic wireless environments. In this work, we establish a mathematical model to characterize both centralized and distributed authentication schemes. We analyze the trade-off between certificate compromise loss and system maintenance cost, and derive the optimal total system costs under authentication-targeted attacks. Furthermore, we determine the condition where the distributed authentication scheme outperforms the centralized one, in terms of attack intensity and loss from attacks, to provide an either-or strategy for enabling cost-efficient and trustworthy authentication for wireless networks. Finally, we validate our model and findings through a lab-built experimental platform that supports both authentication schemes.

title: Sensing Performance Analysis in Cooperative Air-Ground ISAC Networks for LAE.
abstract: To support the development of low altitude economy, the air-ground integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks need to be constructed to provide reliable and robust communication and sensing services. In this paper, the sensing capabilities in the cooperative air-ground ISAC networks are evaluated in terms of area radar detection coverage probability under a constant false alarm rate, where the distribution of aggregated sensing interferences is analyzed as a key intermediate result. Compared with the analysis based on the strongest interferer approximation, taking the aggregated sensing interference into consideration is better suited for pico-cell scenarios with high base station density. Simulations are conducted to validate the analysis.

title: RSMA-Assisted Multi-Functional 6G: Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Powering.
abstract: Integrated sensing, communication, and powering (ISCAP) has emerged as a promising solution for enabling multi-functionality in 6 G networks. However, it poses a significant challenge in the design of multi-functional waveforms that must jointly consider communication, sensing, and powering performance. In this paper, we propose a novel rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA)-enabled multi-functional ISCAP network, where RSMA facilitates the use of communication signals to simultaneously achieve all three functionalities. Based on the proposed system model, we investigate the beamforming optimization problem to explore the performance trade-offs among communication, sensing, and power transfer. To efficiently solve this problem, we develop a novel ISCAP-extragradient (ISCAP-EG) algorithm, which transforms the original problem into a sequence of convex subproblems, reformulates the dual problem as a variational inequality, and solves it using the EG method. Numerical results show that the proposed ISCAP-EG algorithm achieves performance equivalent to that of the conventional successive convex approximation (SCA)-based method, while significantly reducing simulation time. Moreover, the RSMA-enabled multi-functional ISCAP network enhance the performance trade-off compared with the conventional space-division multiple access (SDMA)-based scheme, highlighting RSMA as a promising technique for advancing multi-functional ISCAP development in 6G.

title: Near-Field Beam Routing for Multi-IRS-Reflection Aided Wireless Communications.
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) can be densely deployed in complex environments to establish multi-reflection line-of-sight (LoS) links, thereby enhancing the signal coverage of base stations (BSs). However, to compensate for the severe cascaded path loss, each IRS typically requires a large number of reflecting elements to achieve a sufficient passive beamforming gain. This, in turn, may lead to near-field propagation effects between neighboring nodes along a reflection path. Motivated by this, unlike existing works that focus on far-field signal beam routing via multi-IRS reflections, this paper investigates a new near-field beam routing problem for transmission from a multi-antenna BS to a blocked single-antenna user. Specifically, we aim to maximize the end-to-end BS–user channel power gain by jointly optimizing the reflection path and the active/passive beamforming at the BS and each selected IRS, under an element-wise near-field channel model for all pairwise LoS links in the reflection path. However, due to the complex near-field multi-reflection channel, this problem is inherently challenging to solve optimally. To address this issue, we propose a partial enumeration algorithm, which first identifies a set of candidate reflection paths based on the far-field channel model. Followed by this, we refine the active/passive BS/IRS beamforming for each candidate path based on its actual near-field channels and determine the final reflection path accordingly. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves near-optimal performance, and the conventional far-field beam routing scheme incurs only a small performance loss if the BS/IRS beamforming can be refined.

title: A Heterogeneous Massive MIMO Technique for Uniform Service in Cellular Networks.
abstract: Traditional cellular networks struggle with poor quality of service (QoS) for cell-edge users, while cell-free (CF) systems offer uniform QoS but incur high roll-out costs due to acquiring numerous access point (AP) sites and deploying a large-scale optical fiber network to connect them. This paper proposes a cost-effective heterogeneous massive MIMO architecture that integrates centralized co-located antennas at a cell-center base station with distributed edge APs. By strategically splitting massive antennas between centralized and distributed nodes, the system maintains high user fairness comparable to CF systems but reduces infrastructure costs substantially, by minimizing the required number of AP sites and fronthaul connections. Numerical results demonstrate its superiority in balancing performance and costs compared to cellular and CF systems.

title: Robust Joint Optimization in Fluid Antenna Empowered RIS-Aided Symbiotic Radio Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates an uplink symbiotic radio (SR) system under imperfect channel state information (CSI), integrating reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) and fluid antenna (FA) technologies. In this system, the FA dynamically adjusts its position within a limited region to exploit spatial diversity, while the RIS enhances signal reception quality via passive reflection without additional power consumption. The RIS assists the transmission from user equipment (UE) to the base station (BS) and concurrently embeds its own information through backscatter modulation. To address channel estimation uncertainty, we develop a robust optimization framework based on online successive convex approximation (SCA). Simulation results show that the proposed FA–RIS–SR system outperforms RIS-aided systems with fixed-position antennas (FPA) and backscatter-only systems with either FA or FPA subject to imperfect CSI.

title: An Effective Underwater Acoustic Physical Layer Encryption Communication Mechanism based on Dynamic Spatio-temporal Channel Feature.
abstract: Due to highly dynamic spatio-temporal channel feature, physical-layer key generation (PLKG), which derives keys from the channel’s intrinsic randomness, provides an means of encrypted underwater acoustic communication. To address imperfect reciprocity and the instability of channel features, this paper proposes an efficient PLKG scheme that comprises a spatio-temporally coherent synchronization–probing mechanism and a particle-filtering (PF)-based key-generation technology. With a unique probe signal design, receive array can obtain multiple short-term coherent channel observations of the channel impulse response (CIR). By applying PF to the estimated CIR to track truly stable multipath components (MPCs) and employs their delay information as reliable key material. This design improves probing efficiency and increases key match rate. Field results from both lake and sea trials validate the effectiveness of the proposed method and highlight its promise for secure UWA communications.

title: Secure Federated Fine-Tuning of GenAI in UAV-assisted Vehicular Networks.
abstract: In recent years, the rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has made it possible to provide diverse AI services in vehicular networks to empower intelligent transportation systems (ITSs). However, pre-trained GenAI models struggle to adapt to highly dynamic environments, while federated fine-tuning with vehicles’ perceptual data provides a potential solution. Traditional full-parameter finetuning, however, incurs excessive computational and communication overhead, which is prohibitive for resource-constrained vehicles. Moreover, privacy threats and single points of failure in conventional FL frameworks further compromise the security of ITS. To tackle these challenges, we propose unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted vehicular networks (UVNs), which integrate federated low-rank adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning with a sampling–Laplace–shuffling (SLS) differential privacy mechanism. The federated LoRA framework only transmits LoRA parameter updates to save a large amount of computation and communication costs, and the SLS mechanism also ensures group differential privacy via parameter shuffling. Simulations confirm the effectiveness of the proposed scheme, showing secure federated fine-tuning and enhanced image generation over baseline schemes.

title: MA-HTO: Heterogeneous Task Offloading and Load Balancing in MEC Network.
abstract: Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) is integrated into Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) to form a NOMA-MEC network, enhancing the offloading capability of MEC Server (ES) for latency-sensitive or computation-intensive tasks. However, it is still challenging for User Device (UD) to make independent task offloading decisions in a multi-UD, multichannel, and multi-ES environment, particularly given the highly heterogeneous characteristics of tasks. Moreover, existing methods often focus on task offloading problems within static resource allocation, overlooking the dynamic nature of traffic congestion and the computational workload of ESs. We propose a Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning-based Heterogeneous Task Offloading method (MA-HTO), incorporating queue theory to balance transmission traffic (in bits) and the continuously changing workload (in CPU cycles) of ESs. Besides, the deadline for a task is considered by its input data and CPU cycles required, providing a more comprehensive description of task heterogeneity.MA-HTO method treats each UD as an agent, enabling each agent to decide whether to offload its own task and, if so, which transmission channel and ES to utilize in a decentralized manner. Extensive numerical simulations were conducted, and the results demonstrate that our method outperforms baseline approaches with lower task drop ratios, reduced mean task delays, and lower average energy consumption across the entire system.

title: Pinch Antenna Systems (PASS)-Enabled Predictive Beamforming for Internet of Things (IoT) Networks.
abstract: A sensing-aided predictive beamforming scheme for Internet-of-Things (IoT) networks empowered by pinching antenna systems (PASS) is proposed in this work. Unlike conventional fixed-position antenna systems, PASS dynamically adjusts the positions of pinching antennas (PAs) to flexibly reconfigure the pathloss of wireless channels. To leverage PASS’s advantages for sensing applications, this study examines an IoT network in which an energy-constrained device is tracked over time. To reduce energy consumption caused by frequent reporting from IoT devices, a predictive beamforming framework is introduced for mobility status acquisition in a monostatic configuration. Specifically, an extended Kalman filter (EKF)-based approach is employed to track the target’s current mobility status, including positions and velocities. Based on the tracking results, pinching beamforming is carried out by a two-step process: 1) large-scale pathloss minimization through PA repositioning, and 2) maximum-ratio transmission (MRT)-based beamforming design.

title: A Scheduling Approach to Minimize Peak-Age Violation with Fairness Guarantees in IIoT Systems.
abstract: In the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), where ensuring the timeliness of data delivery is critical, decisions based on outdated information may lead to performance degradation or system faults. To evaluate the timeliness of worst-case fresh information, peak age of information (PAoI) is introduced as a key metric. In this paper, we investigate a scheduling problem that aims to minimize average PAoI violation probability (PVP) while satisfying strict bandwidth constraints and inter-device scheduling fairness in a multi-device IIoT system. The challenge lies in the trade-off conflict between short-term sparse PVP optimization and scheduling fairness with long-term cumulative effect. To address this issue, we integrate the fairness-guided hybrid action selection method and sparse exploration-based random network distillation (RND) into the dueling double deep Q-network, forming a novel RND-based fairness-guided Q-network (RFQN) algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed RFQN approach can effectively minimize the average PVP while guaranteeing long-term scheduling fairness, outperforming existing advanced algorithms.

title: HDAS-SC: A Semantic Communication System for Audio-Visual Streaming in Highly Dynamic Scenes.
abstract: With the advent of 6G, next-generation audiovisual communication demands ultra-reliable, low-latency transmission, challenging conventional bit-level systems. Semantic communication, which transmits the meaning of information rather than raw bits, enhances efficiency and robustness, and has attracted growing research interest. While most existing video semantic communication methods focus on silent scenarios, audiovisual approaches remain limited and struggle with quality and synchronization in dynamic scenes. To tackle this, we propose HDAS-SC, a semantic communication framework for high-quality audiovisual streaming in dynamic scenes. It integrates semantic audio-video coding with facial semantic extraction and generation. A reinforcement learning (RL)-based adaptive group of pictures (GOP) mechanism selects key frames adaptively based on video dynamics, while representing other frames with compact 3D Morphable Model (3DMM) coefficients to balance quality and transmission overhead. An audio-guided lip-sync module further refines lip motion using speech features for more natural articulation. Experiments show HDAS-SC achieves better reconstruction, lower bandwidth, and greater robustness under low SNR compared to existing solutions.

title: Performance Evaluation of Partially Reliable Real-Time Video Transmission over MPQUIC.
abstract: With the rapid growth of real-time video applications, ensuring both transmission efficiency and reliability has become a critical challenge. Traditional transport protocols often struggle to balance latency and reliability, especially in high packet loss network environments. Multipath QUIC (MPQUIC), an extension of Quick UDP Internet Connections (QUIC), offers a promising solution that enables multipath transmission. However, its potential for real-time video delivery remains underexplored. One key issue is the lack of a dedicated evaluation platform to analyze the impact of partially reliable transmission on video quality and network performance. To address this problem, we propose EvalVid-MPQUIC-PR, an extended evaluation framework that supports the partially reliable feature of MPQUIC and is optimized for real-time video transmission. Based on this platform, we evaluated the performance of MPQUIC’s partially reliable transmission under various network conditions and its impact on video quality, focusing on Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), frame jitter, and Mean Opinion Score (MOS). Experimental results demonstrate that EvalVid-MPQUIC-PR effectively supports research on partially reliable transmission strategies, providing valuable insights for further optimizing the reliability and efficiency of MPQUIC in video applications.

title: A Hierarchical Federated Learning based Cloud-Edge-End Collaborative Digital Twin Training Algorithm for Network Intelligence.
abstract: This paper studies an efficient DT training problem in network intelligence and focuses on a cloud-edge-end network scenario. We first propose a hierarchical grouped federated learning framework with knowledge distillation (FedHG-KD) for training a DT model for the network. Then, we consider a sub-global model type deployment (MTD) and hyper-parameters setting (HPS) problem for training a DT model based on the framework. We formulate the problem as a mixed optimization problem with an objective to minimize DT training delay by optimizing the deployment of sub-global model types, the frequencies of local and sub-global model aggregations, and the number of global model updates while satisfying the loss requirement of the DT model. To solve the formulated problem, we first decompose the problem into an MTD subproblem and an HPS subproblem, and then propose an MTD-HPS algorithm, which incorporates an MTD algorithm and an HPS algorithm to solve the two subproblems. Simulation results show that the proposed FedHG-KD framework and MTD-HPS algorithm can significantly improve the DT training performance in terms of model accuracy and DT training delay as compared to several benchmark algorithms.

title: Dimension-Independent Separate Channel Estimation for RIS-Aided Communications.
abstract: Channel estimation in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) assisted communications requires high pilot overhead due to numerous RIS elements incapable of signal processing. Recently, research on sensing RIS has provided a channel estimation scheme with merely three pilots. Nevertheless, it assumes that the BS-RIS channel is known to RIS and remains invariant over a prolonged period. To address this issue, this paper introduces a generalized approximate message passing (GAMP) based channel estimation framework to achieve dimension-independent estimation of separate channels, without the assumption of known BS-RIS channel. Specifically, we first formulate the channel estimation problem as a compressive phase retrieval problem. Based on phaseless power observations, we leverage the GAMP algorithm to retrieve original sparse signals. Furthermore, by exploiting the intrinsic mapping between the sparse representations of the channels and the power observations in the angular domain, we propose a learned GAMP network to enhance the convergence stability and estimation accuracy. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach can efficiently estimate both the BS-RIS and UE-RIS channels with four pilots.

title: A Copula-based Semantics-Structure Minimization Framework for QoS Guaranteed Wireless Communications.
abstract: Current empirically driven research on semantic communication lacks a unified theoretical foundation, preventing quantifiable Quality of Service guarantees, particularly for transmitting minimal structural semantics in emergency scenarios. This deficiency limits its evolution into a predictable engineering science. To address this, we establish a complete theoretical axiomatic basis for this problem. We propose four axioms and rigorously prove that the family of pairwise rank-Copulas is the minimal sufficient representation for minimal structural semantics. Based on this, we construct a semantic distortion metric, centered on the Jensen-Shannon divergence. We then establish the core theoretical boundaries of the framework: sample complexity bounds; rate-distortion bounds; an end-to-end Service Level Agreements theorem; and a semantic source-channel separation theorem, which provides a provable Quality of Service guarantee. Finally, we validate our framework through decoupled experiments, empirically demonstrating that our core metric strictly adheres to our foundational axioms while standard perceptual metrics fail to do so.

title: A Novel Hybrid Time-Frequency Domain Frequency Offset Compensation Method for Coherent Optical Wireless Communication.
abstract: Coherent Optical Wireless Communication (OWC) offers higher spectral efficiency and receiver sensitivity than intensity-modulation/direct-detection (IM/DD) systems, but it remains highly sensitive to carrier-frequency offset (CFO), causing severe phase rotation and bit-error ratio (BER) degradation. Conventional 4th-power method handles large offsets but is limited by Fast Fourier transform (FFT) resolution with coarse compensation. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid time–frequency domain compensation (HTF–FOC) scheme that achieves precise CFO recovery without adaptive equalizers. Simulations show that HTF–FOC restores clear quadrature phase shift keying (QPSK) and 16-Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (16QAM) constellations, reducing residual CFO below 13.7 MHz (vs. > 100 MHz for the 4th-power method). At 10 dB Eb/N0, it achieves BERs of 7.9×10−6(QPSK) and 5.0×10−3(16QAM), making it applicable to high-speed indoor coherent Light Fidelity (LiFi) links.

title: Bandwidth-Efficient Semantic Communication with Training-free Feature Channel Importance Evaluation.
