abstract: This paper examines the transmission efficiency of task-oriented semantic communication systems for image reconstruction, a crucial aspect in real-time unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) monitoring applications that necessitate timely perception and decision-making. Specifically, we focus on exploring the semantic characteristics of feature channels to reveal their intrinsic contributions to image reconstruction. Existing methods for evaluating feature channel importance typically rely on model training, which poses significant constraints in scenarios requiring rapid deployment. To overcome these limitations, we propose a training-free feature channel evaluation module (FCEM) that leverages statistical representations of feature content to identify critical semantic channels. The FCEM can be seamlessly incorporated into pre-trained semantic communication models without incurring additional training overhead. Building upon this, we design the number search module (NSM), which employs a lightweight oracle model to predict reconstruction performance under varying channel conditions, thereby enabling adaptive transmission decisions tailored to the specific requirements of downstream applications. Experimental results on the UCMerced LandUse and VisDrone2019 datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior reconstruction performance, yielding up to 5.41 dB and 6.92 dB improvements over the second-best approaches, respectively.

title: Learning to Unfold Fractional Programming for Multi-Cell MU-MIMO Beamforming with Graph Neural Networks.
abstract: In the multi-cell multiuser multi-input multi-output (MU-MIMO) systems, fractional programming (FP) has demonstrated considerable effectiveness in optimizing beamforming vectors, yet it suffers from high computational complexity. Recent improvements demonstrate reduced complexity by avoiding large-dimension matrix inversions (i.e., FastFP) and faster convergence by learning to unfold the FastFP algorithm (i.e., DeepFP). However, the state-of-the-art DeepFP algorithm relies heavily on FastFP with not-fast-enough convergence and suffers from limited generalization capability. To address these issues, this paper proposes to further accelerate DeepFP through learning to directly unfold the classical FP algorithm with a novel structure-aware graph neural network (GNN) model. The proposed algorithm, named GNNFP, first reformulates the beamforming optimization within the FP alternating iteration framework into a standard single-variable quadratic form, which can be efficiently solved by the GNN model. Numerical experiments show that the proposed algorithm achieves competitive performance while offering substantial advantages over other FP-based algorithms in terms of model size, computational time, and generalization capability.

title: Physics-Aware Tensor Reconstruction for Radio Maps in Pixel-Based Fluid Antenna Systems.
abstract: The deployment of pixel-based antennas and fluid antenna systems (FAS) is hindered by prohibitive channel state information (CSI) acquisition overhead. While radio maps enable proactive mode selection, reconstructing high-fidelity maps from sparse measurements is challenging. Existing physics-agnostic or data-driven methods often fail to recover fine-grained shadowing details under extreme sparsity. We propose a Physics-Regularized Low-Rank Tensor Completion (PR-LRTC) framework for radio map reconstruction. By modeling the signal field as a three-way tensor, we integrate environmental low-rankness with deterministic antenna physics. Specifically, we leverage Effective Aerial Degrees-of-Freedom (EADoF) theory to derive a differential gain topology map as a physical prior for regularization. The resulting optimization problem is solved via an efficient Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)-based algorithm. Simulations show that PR-LRTC achieves a 4 dB gain over baselines at a 10% sampling ratio. It effectively preserves sharp shadowing edges, providing a robust, physics-compliant solution for low-overhead beam management.

title: Distributed Uplink Anti-Jamming in LEO Mega-Constellations via Game-Theoretic Beamforming.
abstract: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations have become vital in emerging commercial and defense Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs). However, their predictable orbital dynamics and exposed geometries make them highly susceptible to ground-based jamming. Traditional single-satellite interference mitigation techniques struggle to spatially separate desired uplink signals from nearby jammers, even with large antenna arrays. This paper explores a distributed multi-satellite anti-jamming strategy leveraging the dense connectivity and high-speed inter-satellite links of modern LEO mega-constellations. We model the uplink interference scenario as a convex-concave game between a desired terrestrial transmitter and a jammer, each optimizing their spatial covariance matrices to maximize or minimize achievable rate. We propose an efficient min–max solver combining alternating best-response updates with projected gradient descent, achieving fast convergence of beamforming strategy to the Nash equilibrium. Using realistic Starlink orbital geometries and Sionna ray-tracing simulations, we demonstrate that while close-proximity jammers can cripple single-satellite links, distributed satellite cooperation significantly enhances resilience, shifting the capacity distribution upward under strong interference.

title: Relay-Aided Distributed Aggregation for Multi-Server FL with Overlapping Clients.
abstract: Multi-server Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising solution to mitigate the communication bottlenecks of single-server FL. In a typical multi-server FL architecture, the regions covered by different edge servers (ESs) may overlap. Under this system, clients located in the overlapping areas can access edge models from multiple ESs. Building on this observation, we propose a cloud-free multi-server FL framework that leverages Overlapping Clients (OCs) as relays for inter-server model exchange while uploading the locally updated model to ESs. This enables ES models to be relayed across multiple hops through neighboring ESs by OCs without introducing new communication links. We derive a new convergence upper bound for loss error bound under non-IID data and an arbitrary number of cells, which explicitly quantifies the impact of inter-server propagation depth on convergence error. Guided by this theoretical result, we formulate an optimization problem that aims to maximize dissemination range of each ES model among all ESs within a limited latency. To solve this problem, we develop a conflict-graph-based local search algorithm optimizing the routing strategy and scheduling the transmission times of individual ESs to its neighboring ESs. This enables ES models to be relayed across multiple ESs by OCs, achieving the widest possible transmission coverage for each model without introducing new communication links. Extensive experimental results show remarkable performance gains of our scheme compared to existing methods.

title: Approximate Proximal Operators for Binary Vector Reconstruction Using Analog Circuit.
abstract: The paper considers the realization of approximate proximal operators of the discrete regularizer for binary-valued vector reconstruction with proximal splitting method using an analog circuit. We propose an analog photonic-electronic convergence circuit for the approximation taking advantage of the voltage-current (V-I) characteristics of the PN-junction diode. Moreover, we derive an analytical expression of the input-output relation of the proposed circuit and show its capability to approximate proximal operator of the discrete regularizer. We have conducted numerical simulations of overloaded multi-input multi-output (MIMO) signal detection with the Douglas-Rachford splitting algorithm using the proximal operator of the discrete regularizer and the proposed approximate proximal operator. The results demonstrate the competitive bit error rate (BER) performance of the proposed operator, indicating the potential for analog realization of binary-valued vector reconstruction using the photonic-electronic convergence approach.

title: Joint Inference-Aware and Resource Allocation Optimization for Drift Adaptation in Edge Intelligence.
abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) on mobile devices holds great potential for enabling intelligent applications, but it also poses significant challenges in inference accuracy, latency, and model robustness. Pre-trained LLMs suffer inference accuracy degradation due to mobile data drift in dynamically changing mobile scenarios, and frequent data uploads for retraining bring substantial communication overhead. Further, resource-constrained mobile edge networks complicate effective system optimization. To address these challenges, we propose AdaInfer, an edge-end collaborative system, to optimize inference accuracy and resource allocation. Specifically, AdaInfer relies on edge servers to continuously retrain and re-compress LLMs with freshly collected data from mobile devices. To overcome resource constraints, we formulate an optimization problem that balances inference accuracy and system efficiency, which is efficiently solved by a self-adaptive global best harmony search (SGHS) algorithm. Experimental results show that AdaInfer achieves high quality inference and efficient resource allocation in dynamic mobile environments.

title: Joint Waveform and Mode Switching Design for RDARS-Aided Integrated Sensing and Communication Systems.
abstract: Reconfigurable distributed antennas and reflecting surface (RDARS) has emerged as a promising architecture for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) recently, thanks to the flexible element mode configurations. However, existing works on RDARS rarely consider the dual-functional (DF) waveform design, which may suffer from a high complexity issue for a RDARS-aided system with a large number of elements and/or antennas. In this paper, we aim to minimize the weighted sum of the waveform discrepancy by regarding the frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) waveform as a reference and the multi-user interference energy, by jointly optimizing the waveform, connection mode switching matrix, absorption mode switching matrix, and passive beamforming for RDARS passive elements. To tackle the mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINP) problem, an alternative optimization (AO)-based penalty dual decomposition (APDD) algorithm is proposed. Finally, simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and demonstrate that the optimized waveform can achieve a better balance between the communication and sensing performance.

title: MASC: A Novel VLM-enabled Semantic Communication Model for Supporting Remote Sensing.
abstract: The growing adoption of multimedia sensing has led to a rapid increase in data volume, urging the development of more efficient communication paradigms to alleviate transmission pressure. Considering the coarse nature of images and videos, only limited portions of them are required to capture key information and perform downstream tasks. Especially under strict bandwidth and latency constraints, compression based on semantic understanding represents a promising solution. However, the potential of leveraging vision–language models (VLMs) to extract image semantics for reducing communication burden remains underexplored. In this paper, we propose mask-aware semantic communication (MASC), a VLM-integrated framework in which a lightweight VLM deployed at the edge extracts a compact semantic representation (e.g., a set of labels or scene elements) under an explicit token/bit budget and transmits compressed data guided by a semantic mask. Experimental results demonstrate that MASC outperforms traditional compression methods and comparable semantic approaches under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, achieving robust reconstruction and high perceptual quality over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels.

title: Near-Field Sensing for UAV-based Virtual Antenna Arrays: Joint Deployment and Waveform Design.
abstract: This paper investigates the target sensing problem within a multi-Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) network, focusing on the construction of a Virtual Antenna Array (VAA) to enhance sensing performance. Due to the limited payload and physical size of individual UAVs, a collaborative VAA is employed to achieve large-scale MIMO gains. Given the expanded aperture of the VAA, the traditional far-field planar wave assumption becomes invalid. Consequently, we establish a sensing model based on the near-field spherical wavefront. Specifically, we adopt Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation and derive the closed-form Cramér-Rao Bound (CRB) for three-dimensional (3D) target localization under the near-field regime. To improve the sensing, we propose a joint optimization that designs the 3D multi-UAV deployment (MUD) and the covariance matrix of the transmit waveform. To solve this non-convex problem, we develop an iterative algorithm based on the Block Coordinate Descent. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed near-field joint design significantly outperforms the fixed Uniform Planar Array (UPA) schemes and far-field approximations.

title: Joint Spectrum and Transmission Adaptation System Under Combat Electromagnetic Environment via Parallel Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Due to the openness and fading characteristics of wireless channels, malicious electromagnetic jamming and channel fading pose severe threats to the stability and quality of wireless links. To address this issue, this paper proposes a joint optimization framework for dynamic spectrum access (DSA) and adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) based on reinforcement learning (RL). Building upon prior DSA-only channel selection works, the proposed approach integrates wideband spectrum sensing with statistical channel estimation to address the time-scale inconsistency between channel switching and rate adaptation. A parallel reinforcement learning algorithm is introduced to decouple the decision space, thereby accelerating convergence and effectively managing the expanded state space. To validate the proposed framework, an intelligent anti-jamming and anti-fading prototype system is implemented on a software-defined radio (SDR) platform. Both simulation and hardware-in-the-loop experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly enhances the resilience and communication quality of the system under complex jamming and fading conditions, achieving a 30.4% throughput improvement over baseline schemes.

title: Planning Oriented Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables simultaneous localization, environment perception, and data exchange for connected autonomous vehicles. However, most existing ISAC designs prioritize sensing accuracy and communication throughput, treating all targets uniformly and overlooking the impact of critical obstacles on motion efficiency. To overcome this limitation, we propose a planning-oriented ISAC (PISAC) framework that reduces the sensing uncertainty of planning-bottleneck obstacles and expands the safe navigable path for the ego-vehicle, thereby bridging the gap between physical-layer optimization and motion-level planning. The core of PISAC lies in deriving a closed-form safety bound that explicitly links ISAC transmit power to sensing uncertainty, based on the Cramér–Rao Bound and occupancy inflation principles. Using this model, we formulate a bilevel power allocation and motion planning (PAMP) problem, where the inner layer optimizes the ISAC beam power distribution and the outer layer computes a collision-free trajectory under uncertainty-aware safety constraints. Compre-hensive simulations in high-fidelity urban driving environments demonstrate that PISAC achieves up to 40% higher success rates and over 5% shorter traversal times than existing ISAC-based and communication-oriented benchmarks, validating its effectiveness in enhancing both safety and efficiency.

title: Navigation and Secure Waveform Design for GNSS-Denied Low-Altitude Wireless Networks.
abstract: With the rapid development of low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs), robust physical-layer security (PLS) and reliable drone navigation are becoming indispensable for practical low-altitude missions. In this paper, we study a LAWN-enabled downlink security framework in which a drone first reaches a designated target under global navigation satellite system (GNSS) denial and then delivers confidential downlink data in the presence of a potential eavesdropper. Specifically, we develop an angle-only guidance strategy for target navigation by exploiting bearing geometry with ground reference anchors, and then design a secure waveform to maximize the worst-case secrecy rate, solved efficiently using successive convex approximation (SCA) and semidefinite relaxation (SDR). Simulations confirm reliable target acquisition with diminishing angle errors and verify the secrecy-rate gains from the proposed waveform scheme.

title: Energy Optimization for Real-Time 3D Reconstruction in Near-Field XR Systems.
abstract: With the emergence of three-dimensional Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) in extended reality (XR), the resulting surge in data volume poses a critical challenge to achieving high-quality rendering under limited communication and computation resources. This paper proposes an innovative distributed rendering framework, establishing a unified paradigm for resource allocation in 3DGS-based XR systems. To overcome the challenges of distributed rendering while simultaneously satisfying user’s stringent requirements of users, we formulate an energy-minimization problem for a near-field XR system. Specifically, by jointly optimizing model selection, downlink transmission precoding, and rendering tasks offloading, we aim at minimizing the total energy consumption of system subject to the constraints of end-to-end latency and rendering quality. To address this mixed-integer and nonconvex design problem, we develop an efficient algorithm capitalizing on the block coordinate descent framework for obtaining an effective solution. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed framework substantially reduces the energy consumption of 3DGS-driven XR systems, providing a paradigm for resource allocation of distributed 3D reconstruction.

title: DL-Aided Super-Resolution Beam Alignment for Low-Overhead mmWave Massive MIMO.
abstract: Although codebook-based beam alignment achieves low training overhead, its limited angular resolution remain critical challenging. To address these issues, we propose a deep learning-enhanced super-resolution beam alignment framework. In particular, we introduce the Quaternary Search-based Super-Resolution (QSSR) algorithm, which exploits the monotonic power ratio property between adjacent Discrete Fourier Transform codebook beams to achieve super-resolution angle estimation without increasing the measurement complexity compared to binary search. Building upon this, we develop QSSR-Net, a gated recurrent unit-based neural network that leverages sequential multi-layer beam measurements to capture angular dependencies, thereby enhancing estimation accuracy and robustness. Simulation results show that QSSR-Net not only outperforms binary search but also surpasses exhaustive search at high signal-to-noise ratios, delivering substantial performance gains with minimal training overhead.

title: 6D Movable Antenna for Internet of Vehicles: CSI-Free Dynamic Antenna Configuration.
abstract: Deploying six-dimensional movable antenna (6DMA) systems in Internet-of-Vehicles (IoV) scenarios can greatly enhance spectral efficiency. However, the high mobility of vehicles causes rapid spatio-temporal channel variations, posing a significant challenge to real-time 6DMA optimization. In this work, we pioneer the application of 6DMA in IoV and propose a low-complexity, instantaneous channel state information (CSI)-free dynamic configuration method. By integrating vehicle motion prediction with offline directional response priors, the proposed approach optimizes antenna positions and orientations at each reconfiguration epoch to maximize the average sum rate over a future time window. Simulation results in a typical urban intersection scenario demonstrate that the proposed 6DMA scheme significantly outperforms conventional fixed antenna arrays and simplified 6DMA baseline schemes in terms of total sum rate.

title: Warm-Start Genetic Algorithm for Region-Constrained User Association.
abstract: This paper proposes a region-constrained association strategy for assisting elements (AEs) and employs a warm-start genetic algorithm (GA) to optimize the region’s shape parameters. Theoretical expressions for the distance distribution and achievable rate are first derived under the Poisson point process model. In the offline phase, the GA is used to determine the optimal shape parameters that maximize the achievable rate under various network conditions, and a knowledge repository is built to store the network condition–shape parameter pairs. A support vector regression-based permutation importance analysis is then applied to identify the most influential network variable. In the online phase, when network conditions change dynamically, the GA is warm-started by searching the knowledge repository according to this key variable and using the corresponding shape parameters as the initial solutions. With only a few iterations, the optimal shape parameters for the new conditions can be obtained. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed strategy further improves the achievable rate.

title: Secrecy Outage Probability of Fluid Antenna-Aided Cooperative Jamming Network.
abstract: Previous studies on uplink physical-layer security (PLS) typically rely on pseudo-random sequences (PRSs) pre-shared between legitimate parties to enable perfect cancellation of jamming signals at the receiver. However, in practical scenarios, the use of pre-shared PRSs may be infeasible due to the associated computational overhead and/or the risk of tracking by intelligent eavesdroppers (Eves). To address these challenges, this work proposes a PLS framework for uplink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access (OFDMA) or single-carrier FDMA (SC-FDMA) networks that leverages fluid antennas (FAs) at user equipments and cooperative jamming under the assumption that no pre-shared key is available. The proposed FA port selection strategy not only effectively mitigates the impact of jamming interference but also enhances the quality of the legitimate link. We derive closed-form expressions for the cumulative distribution functions of the received signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratios at the base station and Eve. Based on these, an exact secrecy outage probability (SOP) expression in integral form is obtained. To further improve analytical tractability and provide clearer insights, a tight approximate closed-form SOP expression is developed for the interference-limited case. Numerical results validate the accuracy of the derived expressions and demonstrate the substantial secrecy performance gains of the proposed framework under the unavailable pre-shared PRS assumption.

title: A Three-Dimensional Path Loss Model for THz Band Aerial Communications.
abstract: Accurate characterization of Terahertz (THz) band path loss is critical for reliable high-frequency communication, especially in aerial networks where transceivers may operate at different altitudes. Existing THz-band path loss models for aerial networks focus on horizontal or vertical transceiver deployments, and fall short at modeling the random 3D geometry of transceiver locations. To address this limitation, we propose a new analytical THz path loss model that incorporates arbitrary 3D geometry of transceiver locations and frequency-selective absorption, obtained through a two-dimensional regression. We validate our proposed model with the propagation data collected via the Atmospheric Model (am) tool for multiple aerial link types, including drone-to-drone (Dr2Dr), medium-altitude aerial communication (MAAC), high-altitude unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV)-to-UAV (U2U) links over varying transceiver separation and sub-THz to low-THz spectrum, i.e., 0.1–1 THz. The proposed framework provides a unified and accurate model for analyzing and designing future high-frequency aerial communication systems.

title: UCB-VG: Virtual-Grid-Based Decentralized Learning for Link Management in LEO Networks.
abstract: Unlike traditional bent-pipe architectures, modern LEO systems employ inter-satellite links (ISLs) to support multi-hop satellite-to-satellite forwarding. These mega-constellations are a key candidate for 6G non-terrestrial networks (NTN), but their rapidly time-varying topology and highly non-uniform, time-dependent traffic demand make efficient link management challenging, often leading to long routes and congestion. We propose UCB-VG, a fully decentralized learning-based scheme that combines an Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) criterion with a Virtual Grid of fixed virtual nodes that satellites temporarily embody. This abstraction enables autonomous link-selection decisions without global topology knowledge and without assuming static ISLs. Using a realistic global simulation based on a Starlink-scale constellation and population-driven traffic, we show that UCB-VG reduces end-to-end penalties by up to 60%, limits delay growth under increasing load, and significantly lowers packet drop rates compared to baseline schemes.

title: EnhanCorr: Stable and Enhanced Flow Correlation under Bursty Traffic.
abstract: With the proliferation of anonymous networks, traffic correlation attacks have become a common means of deanonymization. However, existing methods often rely on regular traffic patterns and exhibit limited effectiveness under bursty traffic conditions typical of web interactions—a critical and unresolved challenge. To overcome this limitation, we propose EnhanCorr, an enhanced flow correlation method based on multimodal convolution, designed to improve de-anonymization performance in bursty traffic environments. Our approach introduces a hybrid input matrix and a window-based weighting mechanism to enhance correlation stability, alongside pre-matching and window-sampling strategies to accelerate training and boost inference efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that EnhanCorr achieves superior correlation accuracy and computational efficiency in bursty traffic scenarios, confirming its practical value and applicability in real-world anonymous communication systems.

title: ENDURE: An Efficient and Lightweight Group Key Generation Scheme Using Sensor Randomness.
Evolving Prediction Models for Radio Access Networks.
abstract: 6G brings expanded use cases, performance requirements, and operational demands of modern Radio Access Network (RAN). AI-native and intent-driven architectures have emerged to support the evolving requirements of RAN. These architectures utilize closed control loops to translate high-level objectives, such as service quality, into network configuration changes with measurable impact on Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Central to these architectures are predictive models, trained on simulation and real-world data, that forecast KPI variations resulting from configuration adjustments to enable proactive and adaptive decision-making. However, robust predictive models for RAN are hindered by the scarcity of datasets as adding new configuration parameter (CP) and/or KPIs to the model implying an exponential growth in the required dataset variety. In this study, we introduce a model evolution paradigm that evolves predictive models for RAN by scaling to new CPs as new data or new specialized models are available. This approach maintains prediction accuracy while managing computational complexity. We conduct thorough experiments on the state-of-the-art (fine-tuning, knowledge distillation and model soup) and two new evolution strategies (chain and mesh), which are benchmarked against an oracle model. Results highlight the chain approach, which embeds domain knowledge to capture additive CP effects, as the most effective strategy as it achieves near-baseline performance with fewer data points compared to other methods. An information-theoretic analysis also corroborates these findings. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first application of model evolution to AI prediction models for RAN, contributing to a data-progressive foundation for intent-driven autonomous RAN management.

title: Federated Mutual Learning for Detection of Diverse-Frequency DDoS Attacks in Social Internet of Things.
abstract: With the increase in Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks effective and early detection has become critical to service providers and users. One of the services being targeted is Internet of Things (IoT), which results in reduced availability for both interaction paradigms-human to human (H2H) and thing to thing (T2T), or worse, potential security risks due to overwhelmed resources. To combat DDoS, conventional Machine Learning (ML) methods were developed which showed promising results, however they raise privacy concerns due to centralized training implementations and were not developed with IoT application in mind. Privacy concerns increase with the extension of IoT called Social Internet of Things (SIoT), which applies social networking concepts to create social networks of interconnected smart objects. SIoT introduces additional interaction paradigm, called human to thing (H2T) which is designed to mimic social behavior of human in everyday life. Federated Learning (FL) has started gaining interest as a mutual model training solution with focus on privacy issues, that can be applied to SIoT applications. However, FL applications often face the Non-Independent and Identically Distributed (non-IID) data problem, which significantly impacts overall performance of finalized model, resulting in worse performance than the centralized approaches. In this paper a framework of Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) is proposed to detect DDoS attacks in SIoT applications that addresses the privacy issues and the FL non-IID problem, while achieving high accuracy and stability across heterogeneous clients with the addition of optimizing for mutual learning, which reduces communication overhead and training time.

title: Towards Secure and Fresh Communications: A New Age Metric for Confidential Information Updates.
abstract: The increasing demand for secure and timely information delivery in short-packet communication systems highlights the need for metrics that jointly capture data freshness and confidentiality. Existing measures, such as the secrecy rate or secrecy age, fail to characterize the freshness of securely received updates. Building upon recent works, we adopt the age of secure information (AoSI) framework and extend it to multi-eavesdropper Rayleigh fading under a retransmission-based policy. We also introduce performance loss metrics to quantify the trade-off between AoI-optimal and AoSI-optimal designs. Numerical results validate the analytical derivations and reveal the secrecy and freshness trade-off through comparative analysis of AoI, secrecy age, and AoSI.

title: Exploring the Viability of Unikernels for ARM-powered Edge Computing.
abstract: The rapid expansion of IoT devices and their real-time applications have driven a growing need for edge computing. To meet this need, efficient and secure solutions are required for running such applications on resource-constrained devices with limited power, CPU, and memory. Unikernel, with its minimalistic design and application-specific approach, offers a promising alternative to traditional virtualization and container technologies in these environments. The existing research does not thoroughly examine the feasibility of using unikernel for edge computing. This paper investigates the potential of unikernel for ARM-powered edge computing by evaluating the performance and efficiency of three prominent unikernel systems such as OSv, Nanos, and Unikraft against Docker container. We experiment with real-world edge computing applications and utilize key metrics such as boot time, execution time, memory usage, CPU overhead, and network performance to determine how unikernel performs under the constraints of edge devices. Our findings reveal the potential advantages of unikernel in terms of reduced resource consumption and faster startup times while highlighting areas where they may need further optimization for edge deployment. This study provides valuable insights for researchers and practitioners considering unikernel as a lightweight, efficient solution for edge computing on ARM architectures.

title: Progressive Latent Refinement for Deadline-Aware Generative AI over Wireless Channels.
abstract: Generative AI, such as diffusion models, faces challenges in real-time applications such as Extended Reality (XR) due to heavy computation and strict deadlines. Standard "compute-then-send" offloading often fails over dynamic wireless channels. We propose a progressive latent refinement strategy that leverages the iterative nature of diffusion models. The core of our solution is a tractable, analytical rate-distortion model, derived from the model’s forward process, that predicts the final quality of any intermediate sample. This model drives a dynamic, online scheduling policy to intelligently selects which intermediate samples to transmit and at what rates. Simulation results show that our policy significantly outperforms baselines, delivering substantially higher sample quality at the deadline.

title: Calibration of IRS Installation Errors via Two-Step Beam Scanning in mmWave Systems.
abstract: The practical deployment of intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) requires calibration techniques to correct angular errors arising during installation. Existing calibration methods either require extensive measurements or fail to fully correct angular errors, highlighting the need for a low-cost, effective approach to ensure reliable IRS-assisted communications. Therefore, this study proposes a two-step beam-scanning method that simultaneously estimates both the positional and angular installation errors of the IRS. By using only two receiving points and relying solely on received power measurements for error estimation, the method significantly reduces the excessive cost and overhead associated with conventional approaches. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, showing an improvement in received power of up to 12 dB after calibration. Moreover, it maintains stable performance even under strong fading conditions and various installation errors. These findings suggest that the method has considerable potential to contribute to the construction of reliable communication infrastructures using IRS.

title: Adaptive Service-Priority and Resource-Tier Offloading at Extreme Edge.
abstract: This paper explores differentiated services in extreme edge computing to address the challenges associated with heterogeneous resources and diverse service requirements. We propose APRTO, an adaptive priority-and tier-aware allocation scheme that formulates the problem as Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP). The formulation optimizes the matching of service priority and device capability while incorporating dynamic perclass minimum guarantees to ensure service continuity and maintain strict service level agreements of critical services. These guarantees allow resource sharing during low demand, while enabling critical services to claim more resources during high demand. Extensive simulations demonstrate that APRTO effectively balances service differentiation with system utilization. The proposed scheme maintains a deadline satisfaction ratio of 97% for critical services, outperforming strict priority and weight fair queuing scheduling schemes under high system loads performance by 10-15%.

title: Toward Long-Range Visible Light Communication: A Chirp Spread Spectrum Scheme.
abstract: Visible light communication (VLC) has emerged as a key technology for the Internet-of-Things (IoT) due to its high speed, inherent security, and immunity to electromagnetic interference. However, VLC is typically limited to short-ranged and controlled environments because visible light suffers from strong attenuation and is highly susceptible to environmental interference. Existing solutions, such as increasing LED transmission power or strictly controlling the VLC environment, are difficult to implement under practical conditions. To enhance link performance for real-world VLC, this paper presents a holistic solution based on chirp spread spectrum to trade bandwidth for long-range and reliable VLC transmissions. Specifically, 1) We adapt chirp spread spectrum to VLC by adjusting the light intensity to a sinusoidal signal. 2) We design and implement a variable-range optical receiver to enable VLC to adapt to changing light conditions. 3) We propose a symbol synchronization scheme and an interval-based signal demodulation strategy to alleviate decoding errors caused by misalignment and signal deviations. We incorporate these innovative designs and build a real-world VLC platform. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach can extend the VLC range by up to 5× while maintaining robustness against shadow fading.

title: Data- and Model-Driven Indoor Localization: Fusion of Trilateration and Deep Learning.
abstract: The widespread deployment of WiFi infrastructure offers a cost-effective opportunity for indoor localization, which is essential for emerging Internet of Things (IoT) applications. While WiFi-based received signal strength indicator (RSSI) methods are widely used, their accuracy is often limited by signal fluctuations, multipath effects, and environmental dynamics. In this paper, we propose a hybrid data- and model-driven localization framework that synergistically combines geometric trilateration with attention-based deep learning. The system first aggregates RSSI measurements over fixed time windows to mitigate noise and extract spatio-temporal features. And a rough position estimate is obtained through trilateration, which provides a geometric prior reflecting the physical layout. An attention-enhanced deep network is then designed to adaptively fuse multi-source inputs—including coarse geometric estimates and RSSI statistics—thereby improving feature discrimination and robustness. A post-processing module based on Mahalanobis distance filtering and signal-quality aware weighting is further introduced to refine the position estimates. Extensive simulations conducted on Wireless Insite validate the proposed method, which achieves an average localization error of approximately 0.15 meters, significantly outperforming conventional trilateration, fingerprinting, and deep learning baselines. This research provides an accurate, robust, and infrastructure-compatible solution for indoor IoT device localization.

title: VR-VFL: Joint Rate and Client Selection for Vehicular Federated Learning Under Imperfect CSI.
authors: José Mairton B. da Silva Jr.
abstract: Federated learning in vehicular edge networks faces major challenges in efficient resource allocation, largely due to high vehicle mobility and the presence of imperfect channel state information. Many existing methods oversimplify these realities, often assuming fixed communication rounds or ideal channel conditions, which limits their effectiveness in real-world scenarios. To address this, we propose variable rate vehicular federated learning (VR-VFL), a novel federated learning method designed specifically for vehicular networks under imperfect channel state information. VR-VFL combines dynamic client selection with adaptive transmission rate selection, while also allowing round times to flex in response to changing wireless conditions. At its core, VR-VFL is built on a bi-objective optimization framework that strikes a balance between improving learning convergence and minimizing the time required to complete each round. By accounting for both the challenges of mobility and realistic wireless constraints, VR-VFL offers a more practical and efficient approach to federated learning in vehicular edge networks. Simulation results show that the proposed VR-VFL scheme achieves convergence approximately 40% faster than other methods in the literature.

title: xApp-Driven Throughput and Demand-Aware Resource Allocation in O-RAN Systems.
abstract: This paper introduces MUMT (minimize-unmet and maximize-throughput), a near-real-time radio access network intelligent controller (near-RT RIC) xApp designed for Open RAN (O-RAN)-compliant beyond 5G (B5G) systems. MUMT operates in a periodic monitor-decide-control loop, computing the allocation of physical resource blocks (PRB) at the end of each reporting interval. The underlying optimization explicitly prioritizes the satisfaction of user rate demands while providing the remaining resources to maximize the aggregate downlink throughput. MUMT is deployed in an O-RAN testbed, relying on open-source tools by Software Radio Systems (SRS) and experimental validation demonstrates that under moderate traffic demands, it consistently surpasses baseline schedulers in both throughput and QoS satisfaction. Furthermore, when traffic demands increase, proportional fair (PF) scheduling can attain slightly higher aggregate throughput. However, MUMT delivers notably better and more stable QoS satisfaction, underscoring its suitability as an effective QoS-aware scheduling xApp.

title: PoLBFT: A Hybrid PBFT-PoL Blockchain Consensus Algorithm for Securing IoT Networks.
abstract: Traditional blockchain consensus mechanisms, such as Proof of Work (PoW), Proof of Stake (PoS), and Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT), face limitations in IoT environments due to high computational costs, scalability issues, and vulnerability to Sybil and Denial of Service attacks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes PoLBFT, a hybrid consensus algorithm that integrates validated physical location via Proof-of-Location (PoL) into the PBFT consensus process. The PoL mechanism ensures that only geographically verified IoT nodes participate in consensus, preventing malicious nodes from exploiting virtual identities. Performance evaluations demonstrate that PoLBFT increases transaction throughput by 12% while reducing consensus latency by 15% and energy consumption by 10−15% compared to standard PBFT. Furthermore, 99.2% of Sybil attacks were successfully mitigated and 98.7% precision was achieved in detecting location spoofing attempts. These results confirm that PoLBFT improves IoT security while maintaining high efficiency and scalability.

title: A Deep Neural Network Codebook Approach for Near-Field Nulling Control Beam Focusing.
abstract: This paper proposes a deep neural network (DNN) codebook approach for multi-user interference (MUI) mitigation in extremely large multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems operating in the near-field region. Unlike existing DNN-based nulling control beamforming (NCBF) methods that face scalability and complexity challenges, the proposed framework partitions the Fresnel region using correlation-based sampling and assigns a lightweight fully connected DNN model to each subsection. Each model is trained on beamforming weights generated using the linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV) method, enabling accurate prediction of nulling control beam-focusing weights that simultaneously optimize the desired signal strength and suppress potential interference for both collinear and non-collinear user configurations. Simulation results show that the trained models achieve average phase and magnitude prediction errors of 0.085 radians and 0.52 dB, respectively, across 75 sample subsections. Full-wave simulations in Ansys HFSS further demonstrate that the proposed DNN codebook achieves interference suppression better than 31.64 dB, with a performance gap within 2 dB of the LCMV method, thereby validating its effectiveness in mitigating MUI while reducing computational complexity.

title: Dual-Side Fluid Antenna Multiple Access for Integrated Sensing and Communications in 6G Networks.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is considered a fundamental building block for achieving high spectrum efficiency in 6G networks. However, conventional fixed-position antenna (FPA) systems face significant performance bottlenecks due to insufficient spatial degrees of freedom (DoF), particularly in interference-limited multi-user scenarios. This paper proposes and analyzes a unique dual-side fluid antenna multiple access (Dual-Side FAMA) architecture where both the base station (BS) and user equipment (UE) are equipped with fluid antenna systems (FAS). A joint optimization problem is formulated that maximizes radar detection and communication quality by leveraging the ability of FAS to change port positions. The proposed dual-sided approach, unlike existing studies that focus solely on configurability at the base station side, creates a broad set of spatial solutions to eliminate multiuser interference (MUI) while simultaneously enhancing target echo strength. Due to the NP-hard nature of the resulting discrete port selection problem, a low-complexity alternating optimization (AO) algorithm has been developed. The simulations conducted within the scope of this study confirm that the dual-sided FAMA architecture significantly expands the ISAC Pareto-optimal region compared to basic FPA and single-sided FAS systems. In particular, the scalability for high-density 6G network deployments has been validated, showing that the proposed method maintains sum-rate even in environments with urban clutter.

title: ZKTrustLLM: IPFS-Anchored Zero-Knowledge Accountability for Secure 5G/O-RAN Edge Multicast.
abstract: Disaggregated 5G/O-RAN edge multicast spans multiple vendors and administrative domains, creating a need for auditable trust signals that do not expose sensitive evidence or disrupt real-time media delivery. This paper presents ZK-TrustLLM, a three-plane architecture that preserves the real-time DTLS/RTP multicast media path while separating evidence retention from trust verification. The evidence plane stores audit artefacts off-chain using the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) via content addressing (CIDs), while the trust plane records commitments, proof outcomes, and policy-triggering events on a permissioned blockchain. Zero-knowledge submissions prove that a reported score lies within an admissible range and is cryptographically bound to an evidence commitment, while raw evidence remains off-chain for authorised audit. Trust outputs can then drive multicast control policies such as Logical Key Hierarchy (LKH) rekeying or subgroup isolation. We implement and evaluate a 10-tenant prototype (50 submissions) on a local chain with co-located IPFS, observing predictable confirmation latency (p50=6 ms, p95=7 ms) with stable gas (mean ≈ 137,783). The released artefact includes executable baselines and NDJSON logs to support reproducible evaluation.

title: Quantum Advantage for Localization.
abstract: Quantum technologies can provide a substantial advantage for sensing, communication, control, and computing, over their classical counterparts. This paper assesses the possible quantum advantage for localization using range measurements. First, we provide a quantum Fisher information analysis for localization, showing the effect of range information and anchor geometry on the fundamental limits of quantum localization. We then demonstrate how the quantum advantage for ranging translates to the quantum advantage for position and orientation estimation. Results, obtained in a scenario with multiple anchors and multiple transmit-receive points for an agent, quantify the extent to which quantum technologies can enhance localization accuracy.

title: A Digital Twin Framework with Field Calibrated Propagation Modeling for Vehicular Network Applications.
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) networks for connected vehicles depend critically on accurate wireless communication models that reflect real-world propagation conditions. This paper presents a field-calibrated DT framework that integrates three-dimensional topography, physical vehicle telemetry, and standardized wireless propagation models to estimate path loss in vehicular network environments. The framework is validated through a case study at the Indian Institute of Information Technology, Sri City (IIITS), where a personal mobility vehicle equipped with sensors and a 4G LTE modem serves as the physical twin. Path loss estimation is performed using the 3GPP Urban Macro propagation model with log-normal shadowing, implemented within a Unity-based virtual environment constructed from OpenStreetMap data. Real-world drive tests along an identical campus route provide ground-truth measurements for calibration and validation. The calibrated model achieves a correlation coefficient of 0.756 and a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 10.95 dB when compared against measured data. The validated framework demonstrates that integrating calibrated propagation models with cyber-physical DT architectures enables reliable radio coverage estimation for infrastructure planning in emerging vehicular and micro-mobility applications.

title: DeepQoE-ST: A Learning-Based Framework for User-Level Video QoE Monitoring under Mobile Network Conditions.
abstract: With the rise of fifth-generation (5G) mobile networks as the backbone of modern multimedia platforms such as Hulu, myCanal, YouTube, and Netflix, accurately measuring Quality of Experience (QoE) from the perspective of the end user has become increasingly complex. Traditional video quality assessment (VQA) methods, whether full-reference or no-reference, typically analyze the digital video stream directly or rely on network-level metrics. Although effective in controlled scenarios, these approaches frequently fail to reflect the genuine visual experience on devices connected via 5G. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Deep Quality of Experience Spatio-Temporal (DeepQoE-ST), a user-centric framework that replicates human perception by evaluating QoE through external recordings of the screen captured by a separate camera. This enables the assessment of the actual visual output observed by users, taking into account distortions induced by compression, bandwidth fluctuations, wireless signal variations, and device-specific display characteristics. DeepQoE-ST combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a temporal attention module to detect visual artifacts and predict Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) consistent with human judgments. A specialized dataset composed of screen captures under diverse 5G conditions was created to train and validate the model.

title: Energy-Efficient Resource Management Optimization Using Programmable Switches.
abstract: The rapid expansion of edge infrastructures in 5G and beyond networks demands solutions that optimize resource utilization while minimizing energy consumption. This work presents an energy-aware resource management framework that dynamically activates or deactivates network switches in the spine layer of data center networks according to real-time traffic conditions. We first provide a formal integer linear programming (ILP) formulation of the resource allocation problem, defining optimal switch activation decisions under energy and performance constraints. Since the exact ILP model becomes intractable for large topologies, we propose an efficient heuristic algorithm that approximates the optimal solution with minimal computational complexity. In addition, we design a data plane algorithm that operates directly on Intel Tofino ASICs, enabling the detection of network condition changes at line rate. A large-scale evaluation using the NetBench network simulator demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves substantial energy savings with only marginal performance degradation compared to the case when all the switches are active all the time in the spine layer.

title: Efficient Quantum Network Synchronization via LOCC.
abstract: This paper investigates quantum network synchronization (QNS) procedures that enable all nodes of a network to synchronize to a common clock with full cooperation and local operations and classical communication (LOCC). The state-of-the-art procedure previously proposed in the literature, referred to as the standard QNS procedure, suffers from sign ambiguity in multi-parameter estimation and requires a number of qubits per node that grows exponentially with the network size. To overcome these limitations, a new procedure is proposed, referred to as the efficient QNS procedure that uses Hadamard matrices and requires a number of qubits per node that grows linearly with the network size. A tactical measurement-time delay is introduced to eliminate sign ambiguity. Results demonstrate that the efficient QNS procedure significantly improves synchronization accuracy over the standard QNS procedure.

title: Lightweight Intrusion Detection Baselines for Open RAN xApps.
abstract: The transition to Open Radio Access Networks (Open RAN) introduces new attack surfaces at the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) and O-Cloud. Securing these interfaces requires Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) that can operate under the strict latency constraints of the Near-Real-Time (NearRT) RIC. However, existing research often prioritizes complex Deep Learning (DL) architectures without justifying their computational cost against the microsecond-level requirements of xApp deployment. This paper establishes a rigorous, reproducible baseline for the NetsLab-5GORAN-IDD dataset, performing a multilayer benchmark on both network flows and radio telemetry. We evaluate twelve algorithms, comparing lightweight machine learning models against complex DL architectures. Our empirical results challenge the assumption that model complexity equates to better security in O-RAN. We demonstrate that lightweight ensemble methods (e.g., Extra Trees, XGBoost) achieve superior detection performance (F1-score > 99%) compared to LSTM and CNN models, while operating at a fraction of the inference latency. Specifically, we identify single Decision Trees as viable candidates for ultra-low latency O-DU filtering, operating orders of magnitude faster than deep learning alternatives. In contrast, DL models like LSTM incurred latencies exceeding 2800 µs (>1000x slower than lightweight models) without yielding performance gains. These findings provide critical design guidance for developing practical, real-time security xApps.

title: Optimization of user-satellite association for LEO networks in a realistic environment.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite megaconstellations enable low-latency global connectivity but suffer from short visibility and frequent handovers due to rapid satellite motion. This work addresses the user–satellite association problem through a centralized optimization framework based on the Kuhn–Munkres algorithm, aiming to maximize aggregate throughput while limiting handovers and enforcing per-satellite capacity constraints. A realistic semi-Markov channel model is considered, based on ITU Recommendation P681-11. Dual connectivity is considered on the user side, with a staggered update scheme of the two links, to reduce the risks of service disruption. Simulation results show the advantages of our approach over a greedy distance-based approach both in an urban and a suburban scenario.

title: Reinforcement Learning-based Resource Allocation in Secure BDRIS-Aided Fluid Antenna Systems.
abstract: The proliferation of network devices has exacerbated the challenge of secure communication in wireless systems. To this end, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) have gained attention for their ability to enhance physical layer security through passive, controllable beamforming that manipulates signal propagation to suppress unauthorized access. Traditional RISs offer limited beamforming gains due to the independent operation of their elements. In contrast, beyond-diagonal RISs promise enhanced resource utilization, which positions them as a key 6G technology. In this paper, we propose a secure design for a novel beyond-diagonal RIS (BDRIS) aided fluid antenna system with multiple communication users and eavesdroppers. We jointly design the antenna position vector and beamforming vectors at the base-station, and the reconfiguration matrix at the BDRIS to enhance secrecy rate performance while meeting the power budget. The formulated problem is non-convex and is solved using proximal policy optimization to obtain a fast-converging solution. Our results demonstrate a 2.5 bps/Hz mean secrecy rate improvement as compared to conventional RIS-aided fluid antenna systems.

title: A Novel Attack-Aware Adaptive Encryption Architecture for Quantum Resilient Networks.
abstract: Next-generation networks, including IoT, edge, vehicular, and 6G systems, require cryptographic schemes that not only resist attacks but also withstand channel degradation without disrupting secure data flows. This paper presents a novel adaptive encryption architecture for quantum-resilient networks that integrates real-time attack detection in quantum channels with per frame key management. A lightweight controller has been designed, which tracks the quantum bit error rate (QBER) via a sliding-window hysteresis and buffer thresholds, deciding per frame whether to derive symmetric keys from Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) or from a post-quantum cryptographic fallback, while maintaining a unified AES–GCM AEAD dataplane. Moreover, a deterministic HMAC-based key derivation function (HKDF) schedule binding eliminates key reuse across modes, retransmissions, and re-encapsulations. Experimental evaluation on image payloads shows: (i) timely QBER-spike detection with 9.5-frame latency and zero misses; (ii) full decryptability and tamper detection across both key sources; (iii) symmetric throughput of ≈ 1.1GB/s with negligible adaptation overhead; and (iv) near-ideal ciphertext metrics including entropy 8.02bits/pixel, NPCR ≈ 99.6%, and UACI ≈ 30.7%. The framework achieves secure, continuous encryption by preventing unsafe QKD use and maintaining authenticated operation under quantum-channel degradation.

title: Dependent Task Offloading in Vehicular Edge Computing Using Trajectory-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) enables latency sensitive applications by offloading computation from moving vehicles to roadside units (RSUs). Scheduling dependent tasks in such environments is challenging because vehicles move quickly through RSU coverage zones and connectivity windows are short. We propose a trajectory aware task offloading framework that unifies short-term mobility forecasting with deep reinforcement learning. A mobility-aware transformer predicts the vehicle’s future trajectory and derives RSU coverage intervals, while a Graph Attention Network (GAT) based actor–critic, trained via Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), decides where each task in a directed acyclic graph (DAG) should execute. Experiments with real highway trajectories and a large synthetic DAG library show that the proposed approach consistently outperforms baselines in terms of delay, and energy.

title: Q-SAFe: Quantum-Safe Agentic Federated Learning Scheme for Telemedicine Edge Networks.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong potential in clinical reasoning, but their scale and cost prevent deployment on resource-constrained telemedicine edge networks. Small language models (SLMs) offer efficiency, yet their limited semantic depth hinders accurate diagnostic support. This gap motivates a Federated Learning (FL) approach, where distributed SLMs collaborate under supervision, while Knowledge Distillation (KD) transfers reasoning from LLMs to sustain accuracy. However, today’s SLM deployments still lack agentic coordination, leaving clinical workflows fragmented. Agentic communication security relies on classical cryptography that cannot withstand quantum adversaries. To address these challenges, we propose Q-SAFe, a four-phase scheme that integrates federated SLM training, agentic orchestration, and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms. Patient and hospital agents are registered, and are collaboratively trained with Federated Proximal (FedProx) and KD strategy. They are connected through authenticated cross-layer handshakes, and protected by Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC) scheme for secure record exchange. Validations show that Q-SAFe sustains clinical-grade responsiveness (≤ 200 ms latency under 300 users), achieves stable convergence (≈ 85% accuracy within 50 rounds), and imposes only 3 KB per-exchange cryptographic overhead, making it suitable for practical edge deployments. The code is available at https://github.com/Mahdiya-Nishat/Q-SAFe.

title: ISAC meets O-RAN: a RIC service to ensure sensing delay requirements.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is a key enabler for 6G technology, expected to drive new services and enhance the quality and efficiency of wireless communications. To this end, this paper showcases the integration of sensing information into the Open RAN (O-RAN) architecture by extending the E2 Service Models (E2SMs) through the FlexRIC implementation. The proposed E2SM aggregates the capability of monitoring both the physical environment and the statistics derived from the sensing data, while also enabling control over the sensing-Radio Unit (sRU). Moreover, since the traffic generated by the sRU may vary depending on the use of the sensing data, it must meet strict latency and freshness requirements defined by each use case. For this aim, we propose the use of a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller to dynamically adjust the capacity assigned to the sensing slice, ensuring that the transmitted information remains timely and up to date.

title: Cross-Modal Phantom: Coordinated Camera-LiDAR Spoofing Against Multi-Sensor Fusion in Autonomous Vehicles.
abstract: Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) increasingly depend on Multi-Sensor Fusion (MSF) to combine complementary modalities such as cameras and LiDAR for robust perception. While this redundancy is intended to safeguard against single-sensor failures, the fusion process itself introduces a subtle and underexplored vulnerability. In this work, we investigate whether an attacker can bypass MSF’s redundancy by fabricating cross-sensor consistency, making multiple sensors agree on the same false object. We design a coordinated, data-level (early-fusion) attack that emulates the outcome of two synchronized physical spoofing sources: an infrared (IR) projection that induces a false camera detection and a LiDAR signal injection that produces a matching 3D point cluster. Rather than implementing the physical attack hardware, we simulate its sensor-level outcomes by inserting perspective-aware image patches and synthetic LiDAR point clusters aligned in 3D space. This approach preserves the perceptual effects that real IR and IEMI-based spoofing would create at the sensor output. Using 400 KITTI scenes, our large-scale evaluation shows that the coordinated spoofing deceives a state-of-the-art perception model with an 85.5% successful attack rate. These findings provide the first quantitative evidence that malicious cross-modal consistency can compromise MSF-based perception, revealing a critical vulnerability in the core data-fusion logic of modern autonomous vehicle systems.

title: On Beamforming for Transmitter Location Privacy in MIMO Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a beamforming framework to ensure transmitter location privacy against sensing-capable MIMO receivers. We propose a novel privacy metric called the direction-of-arrival obfuscation power ratio (DoA-OPR) to design the transmit beamformer. The design approach reshapes the angular power distribution observed at the receiver so that a false direction appears dominant without nulling the line-of-sight (LoS) component. We derive closed-form bounds on the feasible range of DoA-OPR via generalized eigenvalue analysis and formulate an achievable rate-maximization problem under the DoA-OPR constraint. The resulting problem is non-convex but can be efficiently solved using semidefinite relaxation, eigenmode selection, and optimal power allocation. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed DoA-OPR-based beamformer achieves a trade-off between location privacy and communication rate. The proposed design attains higher achievable rates than existing LoS-nulling approaches while maintaining comparable location privacy. A suboptimal design strategy is also proposed with reduced complexity. It achieves a near-optimal communication rate with a reduction of nearly 85% in computation time at a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 10 dB.

title: E-Health: AI based Stroke Prediction with Optimized Active Learning using Fog Computing.
abstract: Stroke continues to be a major global health concern, contributing significantly to mortality and long-term disability. Traditional Artificial Intelligence (AI) and deep learning approaches often face challenges such as data imbalance, weak feature representation, and poor temporal dependency modeling. To address these limitations, this study introduces an advanced AI-based Diagnosis of Stroke (AIDS) framework comprising three novel models, SOFT-Net, SOFTSBS-Net, and SOFTMPA-Net. In this framework, a large volume of patient data, aggregated from multiple hospitals and healthcare centers in form of a comprehensive stroke prediction dataset is utilized, which is processed on a fog computing environment. This distributed architecture enables real-time processing and analysis near the data source, and the processed stroke predictions are subsequently shared back with the healthcare centers and hospitals to support timely clinical decision-making. The framework employs the localized random affine shadows sampling technique to mitigate class imbalance by generating synthetic minority samples. The proposed model, SOFT-Net, integrates shufflenet, overfeat, and a temporal convolutional network to effectively capture intricate dependencies, achieving percentage gains of 5.20% in accuracy, 3.52% in F1-score, and 5.04% in ROC-AUC. The integration of the Stroke-Based Sampling (SBS) active learning strategy leads to the SOFTSBS-Net, which enhances data efficiency and prediction quality, achieving an improvement of 18.00% in accuracy, 23.01% in F1-score, and 4.21% in ROC-AUC. Furthermore, hyperparameter optimization using the Marine Predators Algorithm (MPA) yields the SOFTMPA-Net, which further boosts performance with a 20.00% increase in accuracy, 24.65% in F1-score, and 10.43% in ROC-AUC, while reducing execution time. Overall, the proposed AIDS framework ensures robust and accurate stroke prediction, offering a scalable and intelligent diagnostic solution for modern healthcare ecosystems.

title: Ambiguity Elimination via Successive Estimation in ISAC Systems with Reference Signals.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems can efficiently reuse 5G New Radio (NR) reference signals to enable joint communication and passive target detection. Among these, the Positioning Reference Signal (PRS) is widely adopted for high-performance sensing activities. However, the PRS configuration, given by the comb structure, introduces periodic ambiguities, resulting in ghost targets. Existing approaches mitigate this issue by combining PRS with additional reference signals, such as the DeModulation Reference Signal (DMRS), effectively removing ghosts but at the cost of higher complexity and sensing overhead. This paper proposes a low-complexity successive estimation strategy that initially allows ghost targets but progressively eliminates them using historical ambiguity-free estimations. The method comprises a matching process to associate current detections with historical real targets, and a pattern deviation detection mechanism to trigger a fallback to ambiguity-free estimation when the target set changes. We derive a sufficient condition that guarantees the correct matching as a function of target velocity, PRS comb size, subcarrier spacing, and sensing refresh rate. Using this condition, a parameter selection strategy is proposed to jointly improve sensing and communication performance. Numerical results demonstrate that our method achieves unambiguous detection while significantly reducing sensing resources, thus releasing more resources for communication compared to State-of-the-Art (SotA) approaches.

title: Hybrid Digital Twin Framework for DVB-S2/S2X with Reward-Based Adaptive MODCOD.
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid Digital Twin framework and an adaptive modulation and coding (MODCOD) strategy for satellite-to-ground communication in DVB-S2 and DVB-S2X systems. The framework integrates software-defined radios (SDRs) for physical transmission with a software-in-the-loop channel simulator based on the 3GPP NTN model, capturing satellite propagation effects. By unifying the physical and virtual channels into an effective channel updated with real-time statistical parameters, the system emulates low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite links without requiring on-orbit access. Furthermore, a reward-based meta-heuristic approach for adaptive MODCOD selection is developed, demonstrating superior performance compared to conventional methods.

title: Improvement of DVB-S2/S2X Performance Using External Synchronization.
abstract: Digital Video Broadcasting Satellite, Second Generation and its extension DVBS2X are widely used in modern satellite communications, where synchronization relies on physical layer headers, pilot symbols, and optional superframe structures but lacks defined implementation methods. This work explores the use of external synchronization to enhance DVBS2 performance by using GPS disciplined oscillators, and a hardware software in the loop satellite channel model emulating Low Earth Orbit propagation. We evaluate scenarios with and without Doppler shifts and radio frequency interference, comparing synchronized and unsynchronized cases. Results show that external synchronization significantly improves bit error rate, frame error rate, and signal-to-noise ratio, subsequently reducing the frames required for reliable synchronization and enabling higher throughput in future satellite communication systems.

title: Outage Probability Analysis of NOMA-Enabled Hierarchical UAV Networks with Non-Linear Energy Harvesting.
abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) are expected to enhance connectivity, extend network coverage, and support advanced communication services in sixth-generation (6G) cellular networks, particularly in public and civil domains. Although multi-UAV systems enhance connectivity for IoT networks more than single-UAV systems, energy-efficient communication systems and the integration of energy harvesting (EH) are crucial for their widespread adoption and effectiveness. In this regard, this paper proposes a hierarchical ad hoc UAV network with non-linear EH and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) to enhance both energy and cost efficiency. The proposed system consists of two UAV layers: a cluster head UAV (CHU), which acts as the source, and cluster member UAVs (CMUs), which serve as relays and are capable of harvesting energy from a terrestrial power beacon. For the considered IoT network architecture, the outage probability expressions of ground Internet of things (IoT) devices, each CMU, and the overall outage probability of the proposed system are derived over Nakagami-m fading channels with practical constraints such as hardware impairments and non-linear EH. We compare the proposed system against a non–EH system, and our findings indicate that the proposed system outperforms the benchmark in terms of outage probability.

title: RandModShift: Model and Data Privacy in Federated Inference.
abstract: A key feature of federated learning is to ensure that the data used for distributed model learning stays private. While Differential Privacy (DP) has become a standard approach to mitigate data leakage, there are few solutions to ensure model privacy from an eavesdropper during learning. We extend here our prior work on ModShift, a method to increase model privacy via deterministic shifted model updates, to provide both model and data privacy. The crux of our approach, which we call RandModShift, is to introduce randomized shifts in model updates to ensure DP. The design strategy is based on posing the eavesdropper learning problem as an estimation problem, whose performance is governed by the Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) of the model updates. Our random shift design ensures that the FIM is singular and thus the eavesdropper experiences a provably hard learning problem. We derive technical conditions to ensure FIM singularity. We illustrate our approach with numerical results that show how RandModShift achieves a larger model shift and learning loss compared to a sole DP/noise injection scheme when both methods achieve the same DP levels.

title: Joint Uplink-Downlink Fronthaul Bit Allocation in Fronthaul-Limited Massive MU-MIMO Systems.
abstract: This paper optimizes the fronthaul bit allocation in massive multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems operating with limited-capacity fronthaul links. We consider an advanced antenna system (AAS) controlled by a centralized baseband unit (BBU). In the AAS, multiple antenna elements together with their radio units are integrated into a single unit. In this setup, a key challenge is allocating fronthaul bits between uplink channel state information (CSI) quantization and downlink precoding matrix quantization. We formulate the problem of maximizing the sum spectral efficiency (SE) for a given fronthaul capacity. We develop an SE expression for this scenario based on the hardening bound. We compute the expression in closed form for maximum ratio transmission, which reveals the relative impact of the two types of quantization distortion. We then formulate a bit split optimization problem and propose an algorithm that exactly solves it. Numerical results demonstrate how the relative importance of assigning bits to CSI and precoding varies depending on the signal-to-noise ratio.

title: Optical RIS-Enabled Mixed FSO/UOWC in Space-Air-Ocean Integrated Network.
abstract: Space–air–ocean integrated networks (SAOINs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for achieving seamless global connectivity, particularly in remote maritime and underwater regions. This paper presents an optical reconfigurable intelligent surface (ORIS)-assisted mixed free space optical/underwater optical wireless communication (FSO/UOWC) framework for reliable transmission across multi-domain SAOIN environments. The proposed multi-layer system comprises a satellite source, an ORIS-equipped high-altitude platform station (HAPS), a maritime relay, and a submarine destination, jointly enabling end-to-end optical connectivity from space to the ocean. Closed-form analytical expressions are derived for key performance metrics, including outage probability, asymptotic outage probability, and average symbol error rate, accounting for the combined effects of atmospheric turbulence, pointing errors, and underwater attenuation. Simulation results validate the analytical derivations and demonstrate that integrating ORIS with mixed FSO/UOWC links significantly enhances link reliability and communication efficiency in SAOINs.

title: Robust Optimization and Learning-Based Hide-and-Seek for Resilient Network Design.
abstract: We focus on robust, survivable communication networks, where a signal can only travel a maximum distance before its quality falls below a certain threshold, enforcing regeneration by regenerators installed at network nodes. We assume that both network links and nodes are affected by uncertainty. In this sense, regenerator installation costs at nodes are given through a budgeted uncertainty set. In addition, lengths of network links stem from a newly introduced dynamic budgeted uncertainty set, where each deviation can vary depending on time. Robust optimization seeks a solution with guaranteed performance against all scenarios modeled in an uncertainty set. Thus, the problem is to find a subset of nodes with minimum cost for the placement of regenerators, ensuring that all nodes can communicate even under the worst-case attack of the adversary. To solve the problem, we propose a hide-and-seek game with learning method and compare it with the classical robust static budgeted and deterministic worst-case model. Our theoretical and experimental results show the advantages of our method.

title: PackSwap: A Practical Adversarial Packet Generation Framework against Intrusion Detection Systems.
abstract: As machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) algorithms become integral to modern cybersecurity systems, understanding their vulnerabilities is increasingly critical. Adversarial machine learning (AML) focuses on generating and detecting adversarial examples (AEs), which are inputs intentionally crafted to induce misclassifications. In cybersecurity, such examples can have severe consequences if they enable malicious traffic to evade network intrusion detection systems (NIDSs). This paper presents PackSwap, a practical variational autoencoder–based adversarial attack generation method designed under real-world network constraints. Our experimental results demonstrate that PackSwap effectively crafts adversarial packets that evade multiple target NIDSs, achieving an average Adversarial Success Rate (ASR) of 0.637 and 0.527 for binary classification of adversarial packet headers and of full packets respectively. Furthermore, PackSwap significantly reduces training and execution times compared to state-of-the-art adversarial packet generation techniques. These findings highlight potential vulnerabilities in current ML-based and DL-based NIDSs and provide insights toward developing more robust and resilient intrusion detection systems.

title: Wi-Fi 8 Unveiled: Dynamic Subband Operation (DSO) for Improved Spectrum Utilization.
abstract: Wi-Fi 8 (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.11bn) draft proposes dynamic subband operation (DSO) to mitigate resource underutilization that arises when stations (STAs) with different capabilities share a basic service set (BSS) channel and must synchronize on the primary 20MHz channel. DSO allows an access point (AP) to instruct eligible STAs to temporarily resynchronize to a designated subband within the BSS channel while non-DSO devices continue on the primary. This enables parallel transmissions beyond a station’s operating bandwidth without permanent reconfiguration.
