This article describes the feature based on the latest amendment draft and IEEE 802.11 contributions, and presents a performance evaluation that analyzes potential DSO gains and discusses implementation considerations.

title: Quantum-Secure 5G Sidelink Relay Communication.
abstract: This paper proposes a quantum-resilient message authentication framework for 5G sidelink relay communications, aimed at ensuring end-to-end integrity under computationally powerful adversaries. Current 3GPP sidelink security employs a 32-bit integrity tag that is vulnerable to brute-force and Grover-style quantum search, rendering it unsuitable for long-term or untrusted relay operation. To address this architectural vulnerability, we propose a message-tag decoupling framework that separates authentication delivery from relay forwarding at the physical layer, eliminating relay-controlled forgery and verification-oracle exposure. To realize this decoupling efficiently, we develop a superposition-based transmission strategy that delivers both components within the same time-frequency resources. We evaluate the proposed framework using the metric of authenticated throughput, defined as the number of information bits per channel use that are both correctly decoded and successfully verified, and compare it against the conventional concatenation-based approach.

title: Provenance-Based Detection and Auditing Against Intent Injection Attacks in O-RAN.
abstract: Intent-Based Radio Access Network (RAN) control architectures, such as the Open RAN (O-RAN), enable flexible and declarative network management. Nevertheless, adversaries can exploit intent interpretation gaps to silently broaden the ceiling scope of an originally authorized intent, resulting in unauthorized effects. We propose CeilingChain, a provenance-based detection and auditing framework that enforces a subset-only refinement policy throughout the intent lifecycle, which each refinement step is bound to its predecessor through a cryptographically verifiable token chain. By enforcing that every decomposed scope remains within its ceiling, CeilingChain detects and prevents scope-expanding injections while maintaining interoperability. Using ns3-oran multi-Radio Access Technology (RAT) simulations, we show that when injected throttles are misapplied across RATs, baseline systems suffer up to 78% throughput loss. The proposed provenance-based mechanism provides a path towards verifiable autonomy against intent injection in multi-vendor and autonomous RAN systems.

title: LWM-Spectro: A Foundation Model for Wireless Baseband Signal Spectrograms.
abstract: The received in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) baseband signals inherently encode physical-layer and channel characteristics of wireless links. Learning robust and transferable representations directly from such raw signals, however, remains challenging due to heterogeneous communication systems, diverse propagation environments, and limited labeled data. To address this, we present LWM-Spectro1, a transformer-based foundation model pretrained on large-scale I/Q data represented as time–frequency spectrograms. The model leverages self-supervised masked modeling, contrastive learning, and a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture to learn general-purpose wireless representations. These representations transfer effectively to downstream tasks such as modulation classification and joint SNR/mobility recognition, even with minimal supervision. Across tasks, LWM-Spectro consistently outperforms state-of-the-art deep learning baselines in both few-shot and data-rich regimes, providing a unified foundation for wireless learning.

title: Collaborative Video Caching with Enhanced Privacy Guarantees.
abstract: This paper proposes a privacy-preserving collaborative caching framework that enables coordination between user devices and edge servers (ESs) without revealing request histories, user preferences, or cache states. A personalized federated learning (FL) model based on a variational autoencoder (VAE) jointly learns user-specific popularity and global genre-level trends, while secure aggregation protects model updates. Building on this, a two-stage FL-based caching algorithm allows users and ESs to optimize caching policies under partial knowledge, achieving near-optimal latency without explicit data exchange. Simulation results demonstrate lower latency and stronger privacy guarantees than conventional FL-based and heuristic caching schemes.

title: Joint Beamforming and Space-Time Filtering for Cell-Free LEO Satellite ISAC Networks with Non-Uniform ISAC Demands.
abstract: The low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite system has emerged as a key enabler for supporting global ubiquitous integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) service in 6G. However, prior works have primarily focused on single-satellite ISAC systems, which faces technical limitations such as short service duration caused by satellite mobility and an inability to effectively accommodate non-uniform ISAC demands across the satellite broadband coverage. Motivated by this, we introduce a cell-free LEO satellite ISAC network, where multiple LEO satellites cooperatively transmit ISAC signals, and a dedicated sensing satellite receives echo signals in a bistatic setup. This architecture alleviates the strict dependence of ISAC performance on the geometric positions of satellites and users. In addition, to enhance target detection performance, a space-time (ST) filter is applied at the sensing satellite receiver. To efficiently handle non-uniform ISAC demands, we propose an ISAC demand matching (IsacDM) framework that jointly optimizes the transmit beamforming (BF) and the ST filter to minimize the gap between ISAC demand and achievable performance. Simulation results show that the proposed framework more efficiently manages nonuniform ISAC demands than benchmarks, improving resource utilization and service quality.

title: Explicit LEO Satellite Constellation Design and Coverage Analysis of Clustered Space SDN.
abstract: In this paper, we explore the design of low earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations to ensure seamless global connectivity with clustered software-defined networking (SDN). The key objective of this study is to analyze the impact of clustered space SDN architectures on the constellation design, using the coverage rate as a metric. Existing constellation designs have predominantly relied on trial-and-error–based methods rather than on a theoretical approach. Our methodology then proposes a single-parameterized constellation design by analyzing the critical condition required for seamless coverage. In particular, we focus on minimizing the number of satellites while maintaining the global coverage conservatively. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of satellite altitude on the required number of satellites. This study provides new insights into the interplay between constellation design and SDN architecture, offering a streamlined solution for next-generation global communication networks.

title: Effective Masking Set for False Alarm Mitigation in Blind Detection of Polar Codes.
abstract: False alarms (FAs) may occur during the blind detection of polar-coded systems when a user mistakenly detects a signal intended for another user, where the users are distinguished by unique masking patterns. While previous approaches focused on decoder-side enhancements to mitigate FAs, we propose a transmitter-side strategy that constructs a set of masking vectors systematically and effectively. We analyze the conditions under which a user may erroneously decode another user’s signal, and present a four-step procedure for constructing a masking vector set that mitigates FAs. Experimental results validate our FA-avoidance criteria by demonstrating the high FA vulnerability of identified masking vector pairs, enabling proactive mitigation without decoder changes.

title: A Two-Layer RSMA Framework for Internal Secrecy in Multibeam Satellite Communications.
abstract: This paper proposes a two-layer structural Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) transmission framework to enhance internal secrecy in multibeam satellite communications. Due to the broadcasting nature of satellite communications, confidential signals are inherently exposed to unintended receivers. The framework splits the conventional RSMA common stream into global and group common streams, enabling effective suppression of internal information leakage without increasing transmit power. In this framework, a power minimization problem is solved via an efficient alternating optimization (AO) algorithm integrating weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) reformulation and successive convex approximation (SCA). Simulation results show that it achieves the target secrecy rates with over 500-fold lower transmit power than SDMA, while reducing internal information leakage by approximately 50% compared to one-layer RSMA.

title: Latency-Centric RAN Orchestration with World Model for Satellite-Assisted Mobile Edge Computing.
abstract: As the sixth-generation (6G) network evolves to include low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, it is envisioned to use radio access network (RAN) orchestration for artificial intelligence (AI) task offloading in LEO satellite-assisted mobile edge computing (SAMEC), where satellites serve as relays to forward tasks to ground-based edge servers. However, the realization of efficient orchestration faces fundamental challenges: (i) heterogeneous latency requirements across diverse services, (ii) partial observability stemming from both stale state information caused by propagation delays and low observation resolution, and (iii) stochastic uncertainty such as task arrivals and channel fluctuations. This paper formulates the resource management and load balancing problem as a constrained partially observable Markov decision process (CPOMDP) and proposes a novel hierarchical framework that learns stochastic environmental dynamics via a world model. By combining planning-based imagination for sample-efficient long-term optimization with heuristic scheduling for short-term optimization, our approach maintains latency constraint deviations below 20 ms, significantly outperforming model-free baselines.

title: A Robust and Lightweight Neural Network Design for OFDM Channel Estimation in the Low-SNR Regime.
abstract: This paper proposes a robust and lightweight channel estimation framework for uplink orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems operating in the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regime. The proposed framework, called the denoising transposed attention network (DnTANet), integrates a denoising and downsampling (DDS) block to suppress high-frequency noise and a transposed attention mechanism to efficiently capture joint frequency-antenna correlations. Numerical simulations demonstrate that DnTANet achieves robust performance across various Doppler frequencies and delay spreads, achieving superior normalized mean squared error (NMSE) and required SNR to attain a 10% block error rate (BLER) performance compared with existing attention-based channel estimation methods. Moreover, DnTANet achieves comparable performance while requiring only 14.6 27.3% of the floating-point operations (FLOPs) of conventional−AI-based solutions, demonstrating its suitability for practical low-complexity deployment.

title: Polarization-Multiplexed Massive Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: This paper introduces a polarization-multiplexed massive reconfigurable intelligent surface (PM-mRIS) designed to mitigate link degradation in Ka-band low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite downlinks. While LEO networks are essential for global connectivity, their performance is frequently compromised by polarization mismatch, driven by dynamic factors such as ionospheric Faraday rotation, rapid platform motion, and complex multipath scattering. To address this, we propose a dual-layer liquid crystal (LC) architecture that enables independent phase control for orthogonal linear polarizations, allowing for adaptive polarization conversion to the channel's instantaneous optimum. The proposed 45×50-element PM-mRIS achieves a wide phase-tuning range of over 260° at 27 GHz with high isolation between polarization channels. We experimentally validate the system-level impact of the PM-mRIS in a non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environment, demonstrating successful recovery of high-order modulation signals up to 1024-QAM. Our results confirm that the PM-mRIS significantly enhances the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and spectral efficiency by precisely re-matching distorted polarization states, providing a hardware-efficient solution for robust LEO-to-ground communication.

title: Sidelobe Reduction Using Magnitude-Adaptive Filter Design in DFT-s-OFDM System.
abstract: Discrete Fourier transform-spread orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (DFT-s-OFDM) is a promising waveform for integrated sensing and communications due to its low peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) and compatibility with cellular uplinks. However, DFT-s-OFDM can exhibit high sidelobes in the range profile when a conventional least squares (LS)-based channel-estimation filter is used for sensing. To address this issue, we propose magnitude-adaptive channel-estimation filters. The proposed method determines the filter type for each subcarrier based on the magnitude of the transmitted symbol. In our method, subcarriers with sufficiently large magnitudes are processed by the LS filter, whereas those with small magnitudes are processed with the matched filter (MF). By adaptively combining the advantages of these two filters, the proposed filters can suppress the noise amplification inherent in the LS filter and mitigate the increased sidelobes associated with the MF. Through simulations, we demonstrate that the proposed filters achieve a higher PSLR and a lower range-estimation error than conventional channel-estimation filters. Specifically, the proposed methods achieve up to 5 dB improvement in PSLR over the LS filter at the low SNR value and exhibit the PSLR improvement of 20 dB compared to MF at the high SNR value.

title: Robust Generalization for Multi-Modal Wireless Networks Under Data Scarcity.
abstract: Next-generation wireless networks can potentially employ multi-modal machine learning (ML) models to make network decisions with situation-awareness in dynamic environments. However, trained ML models struggle to generalize to unseen environments because they often become overfitted to training domain due to data scarcity in wireless networks. Such a data distribution change is called domain shift, which occur frequently in practical wireless systems due to dynamic channel statistics, moving obstacles, or variations in hardware configuration. Although one can collect additional data to mitigate domains shifts from various wireless environments, multi-modal data generation is significantly costly without access to target domains. Thus, there is a need for learning frameworks that can achieve robust generalization under scarce multi-modal data in wireless networks. In this paper, a novel physics-based training framework is proposed to improve generalization performance in unseen and unfamiliar wireless environments with minimal amount of multi-modal data. Specifically, a physics-based loss function is employed to enable base station to learn the physics underlying its wireless environment captured by multi-modal data. The data-efficiency of the physics-based loss function is analytically investigated. To validate the proposed framework, a new dataset generation framework is developed by integrating CARLA and MATLAB to predict mmWave received signal strength from LiDAR, RGB, radar, and GPS. Simulation results show that the proposed physics-based training requires only 31% of data samples to achieve the same performance as a state-of-the-art baseline that does not use physics-based training.

title: Multi-Rate Task-Oriented Communication for Multi-Edge Cooperative Inference.
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with the Internet of Things (IoT) enables task-oriented communication for multi-edge cooperative inference system, where edge devices transmit extracted features of local sensory data to an edge server to perform AI-driven tasks. However, the privacy concerns and limited communication bandwidth pose fundamental challenges, since simultaneous transmission of extracted features with a single fixed compression ratio from all devices leads to severe inefficiency in communication resource utilization. To address this challenge, we propose a framework that dynamically adjusts the code rate in feature extraction based on its importance to the downstream inference task by adopting a rate-adaptive quantization (RAQ) scheme. Furthermore, to select the code rate for each edge device under limited bandwidth constraint, a dynamic programming (DP) approach is leveraged to allocate the code rate across discrete code rate options. Experiments on multi-view datasets demonstrate that the proposed frameworks significantly outperform the frameworks using fixed-rate quantization, achieving a favorable balance between communication efficiency and inference performance under limited bandwidth conditions.

title: Liquid Crystal Based Optical STAR-RIS for Enhancing VLC Connectivity in Indoor Workspaces.
abstract: Visible light communication (VLC) presents a promising solution for high-speed indoor connectivity. However, its reliance on line-of-sight (LoS) links makes it susceptible to blockages, which limits its practical deployment. In this paper, we address this issue by utilizing a fully liquid crystal (LC) based optical simultaneous transmission and reflection (OSTAR) reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) that can act as both reflecting and refracting elements, enhancing coverage within the indoor workspaces. Specifically, we formulate a problem to maximize the total system spectral efficiency by jointly optimizing the LED power allocation, user-LED association, and the control voltages of the individual LC elements. Due to the non-convex and non-deterministic polynomial (NP)-hard nature of this problem, we consider an iterative alternating optimization (AO) framework that decouples the problem into three sub-problems, which are solved sequentially using techniques including element-wise search, the majorization-minimization (MM) algorithm, and projected gradient descent (PGD). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed system and optimization framework significantly enhance spectral efficiency and effectively overcome LoS limitations, providing robust coverage across indoor workspaces.

title: FLEX: Joint UL/DL and QoS-Aware Scheduling for Dynamic TDD in Industrial 5G and Beyond.
abstract: Industrial 5G deployments using Time Division Duplex (TDD) networks face a critical challenge: existing schedulers rely on static configuration of Uplink (UL) to Downlink (DL) resource ratios, failing to adapt to dynamic asymmetric traffic demands. This limitation is particularly problematic in Industry 4.0 scenarios where traffic patterns exhibit significant asymmetry between directions and heterogeneous Quality of Service (QoS) requirements. We present FLEX,a novel QoS-aware scheduler that dynamically adjusts the UL/DL ratio in flexible TDD slots while respecting diverse QoS requirements. FLEX introduces DL buffer state estimation to prevent starvation of high-priority DL traffic, exploiting the deterministic nature of industrial traffic patterns for accurate predictions. Through extensive simulations of industrial scenarios using 5G LENA and ns-3, we demonstrate that FLEX achieves similar throughput compared to established scheduling while correctly enforcing QoS priorities in both traffic directions. For deterministic traffic patterns,FLEX maintains minimal latency overhead (less than 1 slot duration), making it particularly suitable for industrial automation applications.

title: A Markov chain model for evaluating GeoNetworking routing performances.
abstract: Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks (VANETs) enable road users and infrastructure to exchange information across a dynamic flow of vehicles, but they present their own challenges. In particular, white areas where there is no cellular network often coincide with low population, low traffic zones. In these situations, there is a need to evaluate whether it is worth installing road side units to allow the communications to go through. This paper presents a model to evaluate an ETSI GeoNetworking routing algorithm performance in different vehicle flow and penetration rates conditions. This model uses a Markov chain to represent the routing of a packet to a destination along a road. Using data collected by us on nearby roads using 802.11p equipment, we can estimate the reception rate based on distance of 802.11p and evaluate, using the model the probability of forwarding a message over long distances. We show that having a good penetration rate as well as quality of service mechanisms are needed to ensure the proper operation of the system.

title: Duplexity Paradigms in Separated Deployment Cell-Free mMIMO ISAC Systems: A Kullback-Leibler Divergence Analysis.
abstract: This paper presents a unified framework for comparing half-duplex (HD) and full-duplex (FD) operation in separated-deployment cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Using Kullback–Leibler divergence (KLD) as a common performance measure, closed-form expressions are derived for downlink (DL) and uplink (UL) communication and for radar detection under both duplexing modes. The analysis explicitly incorporates practical impairments—imperfect channel estimation and imperfect interference cancellation (IC)—and makes the dependence of residual interference on the Tx–Rx coupling coefficients, DL precoder energy, radar waveform energy, and UL power explicit. Monte Carlo evaluations over realistic CF layouts validate the derivations and reveal clear trends: (i) DL performance under FD outperforms the HD; (ii) FD provides a pronounced UL gain when IC error is small and the coupling coefficients are small; (iii) radar KLD (and thus detection probability) remains close to HD under accurate IC and small coupling, but degrades as either the coupling or IC error increases. Power-allocation sweeps further quantify the sensing–communication trade-off: communication symbol-error rate decreases as KLD increases, while radar detection probability increases with KLD. Overall, when effective IC is available, FD is recommended as it delivers a higher end-to-end ISAC utility without time-division overhead.

title: DeepTRX: 6G Physical-Layer Neural Processing with Joint End-to-End Learning under Nonlinearities.
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel physical-layer neural processing solution with joint transmitter-receiver learning, called DeepTRX. Specific focus is on 6G cellular uplink at frequency range 3 (FR3) and the potential relaxation of 6G user equipment (UE) RF transmit signal quality requirements, which allows for operating the UE power amplifiers in the more nonlinear region with increased antenna power. The proposed DeepTRX approach allows for learned bit-to-symbol mapping and PA input waveform shaping, under the constraint of well-bandlimited transmit antenna waveform, while the corresponding receiver stages harness the power of neural processing for efficient data demodulation despite strong nonlinear distortion in the transmit waveform and even without demodulation reference symbols. We provide comprehensive uplink radio link performance results at the future 7GHz 6G FR3 band, highlighting that up to 2-2.5dB of gain can be achieved compared to existing neural or model-based solutions.

title: Experimental Verification of Doppler Shift Correction in the Sub-6 GHz 5G for 500 km/h Train.
abstract: A Sub-6 GHz 5G communication method applicable to ultra-high-speed trains such as Superconducting Maglev has been prototyped and verified. The most significant challenge, Doppler shift correction, has been addressed by detecting phase rotation of the synchronization signals. This eliminates the need for additional reference signals and minimizes any increase in overhead, thereby enabling efficient communication. In prototype experiments on the Yamanashi Maglev Line, 5G downlink communication was successfully achieved on an actual train traveling at 500 km/h. The block error rate (BLER) was confirmed to be less than 0.3% over 5 km using QPSK modulation.

title: LyMARL: Lyapunov-Guided MARL for Energy-Constrained User Association.
abstract: We investigate the joint optimization of user association (UA) and base station (BS) activation in multi-cell wireless networks under finite-horizon energy constraints. This problem is challenging due to the inherent tension between maximizing user throughput and ensuring energy-efficient BS operation. Lyapunov-based control provides a principled and practical approach for distributed stochastic network optimization with strong long-term guarantees; however, energy constraints are enforced only in an asymptotic sense, which may lead to noticeable violations over finite horizons. To address this limitation, we propose LyMARL, a Lyapunov-guided multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes UA and BS activation and scheduling by embedding Lyapunov virtual queues into agent observations and reward design. Unlike conventional Lyapunov-based approaches with passive BS control, LyMARL introduces proactive BS agents for energy-aware decision making while preserving fully decentralized execution. Simulation results demonstrate that LyMARL achieves substantial improvements in throughput, fairness, and energy efficiency.

title: Emergent Cooperation in Quantum Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Using Communication.
abstract: Emergent cooperation in classical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning has gained significant attention, particularly in the context of Sequential Social Dilemmas (SSDs). While classical reinforcement learning approaches have demonstrated capability for emergent cooperation, research on extending these methods to Quantum Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning remains limited, particularly through communication. In this paper, we apply communication approaches to quantum Q-Learning agents: the Mutual Acknowledgment Token Exchange (MATE) protocol, its extension Mutually Endorsed Distributed Incentive Acknowledgment Token Exchange (MEDIATE), the peer rewarding mechanism Gifting, and Reinforced Inter-Agent Learning (RIAL). We evaluate these approaches in three SSDs: the Iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma, Iterated Stag Hunt, and Iterated Game of Chicken. Our experimental results show that approaches using MATE with temporal-difference measure (MATETD), AutoMATE, MEDIATE-I, and MEDIATE-S achieved high cooperation levels across all dilemmas, demonstrating that communication is a viable mechanism for fostering emergent cooperation in Quantum Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning.

title: A Robust Structured-Pruning Based Multimodal Semantic Communication Framework in Wireless IoT Networks.
abstract: Semantic communication is an emerging paradigm for efficient information transmission that prioritizes the accurate understanding of data’s meaning over the bit-perfect replication of the data stream. However, existing semantic communication systems, which typically rely on complex deep neural networks, face significant challenges in deployment on computationally constrained wireless Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Furthermore, the distortion and noise induced by wireless channels pose a serious threat to communication reliability. To address these issues, we propose a novel low-complexity and robust semantic communication framework over wireless IoT networks. Specifically, we design a dynamic pruning strategy at the encoders on devices to reduce redundant neurons based on their contribution, adapting the encoder to the task requirements and significantly improving computation efficiency. Then, to address the semantic degradation caused by pruning and channel noise, we introduce a reconstructive feature enhancement module into the decoder at the base station (BS), leveraging multi-scale fusion to restore lost semantic details and counteract channel noise. Extensive experiments on image, text, and speech tasks demonstrate that our method significantly reduces computation costs while maintaining high task quality, highlighting its effectiveness for resource-constrained and multimodal semantic communication systems.

title: Reinforcement Learning Aided Random Access for Ambient Internet of Things.
abstract: The integration of Ambient Internet of things (A-IoT) into 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) networks enables large-scale deployments of maintenance-free, energy-harvesting devices. Identifying such devices via contention-based random access is challenging due to energy constraints, device heterogeneity, and partial observability. This work proposes a reinforcement learning (RL)-based resource allocation framework that adapts access resources based on slot-level feedback, eliminating the need for explicit backlog estimation. The method accounts for capture effects and heterogeneous device capabilities, learning a policy that balances successful identification and collision reduction. Simulation results show that the RL-based scheme achieves significant device energy savings and reduction in identification time, depending on device type and scenario, compared to relevant conventional baseline schemes.

title: UAV-Enabled Traffic Monitoring Through Semantic Communications and Digital Twinning.
abstract: This paper presents a state-of-the-art approach for traffic monitoring that combines digital twins (DTs) and semantic communication (SemCom) technologies to alleviate traffic in next-generation non-terrestrial networks (NTNs). The presented framework capitalizes on core SemCom principles by transmitting only semantically relevant data through the network to complete the task of creating a DT of the observed scene. It utilizes multiple synchronized video feeds from cameras observing the same scene from different perspectives. To validate the performance of the system, an open dataset was initially employed, while a custom multi-view dataset, consisting of vehicle-, roadside unit-, and UAV-mounted cameras, was additionally created. Experimental results demonstrate that SemCom approach surpasses conventional communication systems in terms of data and energy efficiency, and requires less time to achieve this. In addition, the explainability of the proposed solution is examined by employing the GradCAM library to extract interpretations of the model’s internal logic. Finally, the presented framework achieves substantial significant reduction in network load, while maintaining high accuracy in object detection.

title: A Privacy-Respecting User Activity Classification Method Based on O-RAN E2 Metrics.
abstract: The emergence of fifth-generation (5G) networks and the Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) paradigm aspire to offer more flexible, programmable, and intelligent mobile infrastructures. A key enabler for autonomous resource orchestration in such networks is the accurate and privacy-respecting classification of user activity from RAN telemetry. In this paper, we present the design, deployment, and evaluation of an O-RAN-compliant 5G testbed used to collect near-real-time metrics via the E2 interface. We apply machine learning (ML) techniques on these measurements to classify user activity into three service categories, namely gaming, video streaming, and browsing. Specifically, a deep neural network (DNN) and an extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model were trained to classify the user activity into the aforementioned categories. The evaluation results show a high overall performance for both DNN and XGBoost. Specifically, the precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy values of the DNN are 0.9208, 0.9203, 0.9204, and 0.9204, respectively. On the other hand, the corresponding values for the XGBoost are 0.9801, 0.9794, 0.9791, and 0.9794. The results show that the combination of metrics from the E2 interface and ML can offer insights into the user activity, which are valuable for optimal resource allocation, without having to directly inspect the network packets.

title: NTRU Based Novel Approach to Secure UAV Communications Through MQTT and Blockchain.
abstract: The security of UAV communications is one of the crucial aspects in UAV networks due to the increasing use of UAVs in various applications. In this paper, a novel approach based on Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is proposed to improve the security of UAV communications. The proposed approach utilizes the N-th Degree Truncated Polynomial Ring Unit (NTRU) algorithm, integrated with Blockchain Technology (BT) and the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport Protocol (MQTT). In the proposed approach, UAVs are authenticated by the server, and the BT ledger stores the UAV information, such as its identification number and public key. The encryption and decryption of the message is performed using a securely established secret key between the sender and the receiver UAV. The results of the proposed approach are evaluated and compared with other existing PQC algorithms. The results show that the proposed approach is more computationally efficient and faster than other algorithms.

title: SLA Aware Adaptive Redundancy for Safety-Critical Applications in Wi-Fi.
abstract: Safety-critical industrial applications demand deterministic latency and high availability, which is challenging for Wi-Fi due to interference. We present SAAR (SLA-Aware Adaptive Redundancy), a scheduler that dynamically activates frame replication and elimination for reliability only when application constraints are threatened. Using real-time Service Level Agreement (SLA) feedback and network occupancy, SAAR optimally balances reliability and spectral efficiency across disjoint Wi-Fi paths. Emulation with real industrial safety traffic shows SAAR maintains reliability under heavy load while reducing replication overhead by 97.5% compared to static redundancy.

title: Performance Analysis of One- and Two-way DV-QKD with MIMO FSO Communication Systems.
abstract: This paper considers a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless system wherein two legitimate users attempt to exchange secret keys over free-space optical (FSO) channels. Novel frameworks for the use of the one- and two-way discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD) protocols, employing weak coherent pulses and decoy states, are presented. Focusing on the case where a photon-number-splitting attack is adopted by the eavesdropper and the legitimate multi-antenna receiver using threshold detection for the key extraction, novel expressions for the secret key rate and quantum bit error rate for both one- and two-way protocols are derived. The performance gain with larger MIMO configurations and the tradeoff between the performances with the one- and the two-way protocols with respect to the transmission distance of the legitimate FSO link are numerically assessed.

title: Energy-Aware Federated DRL with Adaptive Differential Privacy for SAGIN Vehicular Networks.
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-agent federated deep reinforcement learning (MA-FDRL) framework for wireless power transfer (WPT)-aided vehicular networks by explicitly accounting for realistic physical impairments and heterogeneous privacy requirements. We introduce three deployment-aware mechanisms: agent-type sensitivity factors that allocate differential privacy (DP) budgets based on data exposure risk across space–air–ground integrated network (SAGIN) tiers, a training-adaptive gradient noise decay strategy that reduces perturbation as model convergence stabilizes, and an energy-aware orchestration policy that aligns privacy-intensive computations with high-coupling WPT intervals. Unlike idealized models assuming continuous power delivery, we incorporate segmented coil topology, magnetic null zones, lateral misalignment-induced power fading, Rayleigh channel fading, and Doppler-induced latency jitter. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations over 100 independent trials demonstrate statistically significant improvements, including a 3.2 percentage-point state-of-charge (SOC) gain and a 37.5% reduction in cumulative privacy budget with an accuracy improvement. In addition, the proposed framework achieves up to 26.2% latency reduction under aligned WPT conditions while maintaining robustness during severe power fading.

title: Finite Blocklength Analysis of Active and Passive STARS-CR-NOMA with Practical Constraints.
abstract: This paper investigates the finite blocklength analysis of an active and passive simultaneously transmitting and reflecting surface (STARS)-assisted cognitive radio (CR) non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system. By employing a transmit antenna selection (TAS) scheme, a multi-antenna secondary source operates in underlay mode to transmit information to two secondary users located in the reflection and refraction regions of the STARS using the NOMA technique. The system performance is analyzed in the finite blocklength regime while considering practical constraints such as hardware impairments (HIs) and imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). We derive novel closed-form expressions for the average block error rate (ABLER), system throughput, and system goodput. To provide deeper insights, asymptotic ABLER expressions are also derived under two power settings: (i) when the transmit power of the secondary source approaches infinity, and (ii) when the maximum interference constraint of the primary network approaches infinity. Finally, Monte Carlo simulations are performed to validate the analytical results. Numerical results confirm the superiority of NOMA over orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and compare the system performance with passive STARS. Moreover, it is shown that the diversity order depends on the number of transmit antennas and reflecting elements. The effects of blocklength, the number of transmit antennas, and HIs on system performance are also examined.

title: Rethinking Network Metrics: User-Centric Lessons from Emerging Cellular Deployments.
abstract: Rapid cellular rollouts in emerging regions promise high-speed connectivity, yet users often experience performance that contradicts operator claims. In this paper, we present a user-centric measurement study from semi-urban India using a portable Android-based framework that emulates real interactions on popular apps such as Amazon and YouTube. Our results show that application responsiveness varies sharply across time and location, frequently falling short of ITU–TRAI benchmarks. Surprisingly, high throughput and strong signal strength do not consistently correlate with better Quality of Experience (QoE). These findings highlight a structural gap between how networks are traditionally measured and how they are actually experienced, underscoring the need for user-centric evaluation frameworks in rapidly evolving deployments.

title: Doppler-Supervised Channel Charting.
abstract: Channel charting is an integrated sensing and communication technique where passively collected channel state information (CSI) at the base-station is used for obtaining a lowdimensional representation of the distribution of all observed CSI samples, referred to as a channel chart.The usage of the channel chart for various applications depends highly on the charting accuracy, which is typically defined by its similarity to the users' geometric positions; an accurate channel chart can be used for a variety of applications like beam selection, beam tracking, radio maps, pilot assignment, signal strength prediction etc.Thus, improving the charting performance is of utmost importance.In this paper, we propose to exploit the delay-Doppler based multipath CSI which occurs naturally in modern techniques such as orthogonal time frequency space modulation as a form of supervision to produce channel charts that more closely match the geometric ground truth of user positions.We use a combination of classical triplet based loss function along with a novel Doppler based loss function to train a deep neural network which provides an efficient charting function.The charting performance for a variety of user trajectories demonstrates the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

title: A Feasibility Study Toward Trustworthy 3GPP NWDAF Closed-Loop Analytics via Distributed MTLF with OpenDaisy.
abstract: AI-native 6G networks require reliable closed-loop analytics that can adapt to traffic distribution drift and non-IID data across geographically distributed sites. While 3GPP NWDAF separates inference (Analytics Logical Function, AnLF) from training (Model Training Logical Function, MTLF), the end-to-end feasibility of distributed closed-loop operation under drift and heterogeneity remains insufficiently validated. This paper presents a system-level feasibility study of NWDAF closed-loop analytics using hierarchical federated learning as a distributed MTLF implementation. Using controlled traffic regime shifts, we evaluate degradation detection, recovery, and robustness under heterogeneous data distributions. Results show that deployed models can suffer catastrophic out-of-distribution failures, with error 52.1% higher than an AR(1) baseline, and that hierarchical federated retraining restores performance, reducing Regime 1 error by 35% and worst-case error by up to 60%. We further quantify two deployment-relevant effects: historical knowledge retention follows a near-linear relationship with historical-data mixing (R2= 0.99), while adaptation to new regimes saturates early; and severe non-IID heterogeneity moderately reduces mean gains but amplifies outcome variance by more than threefold (CV≥0.60). Overall, the results demonstrate the feasibility of NWDAF closed-loop analytics with distributed MTLF and provide operational guidance for deployment under traffic drift and heterogeneous data.

title: AI-Driven Slice-Aware Digital Twin Virtualization in O-RAN for IoV with eMBB and URLLC Traffic.
abstract: Digital-twin virtualization architecture (DTVA) in open radio access networks (O-RANs) provides a promising foundation for artificial intelligence driven service orchestration. However, existing DTVA frameworks treat all traffic uniformly, overlooking the distinct quality-of-service demands of enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB) and ultra-reliable and low-latency communication (URLLC). To address this limitation, we propose a slice-aware (SA) DTVA tailored for real-time (RT) internet-of-vehicles (IoV) traffic, integrating xApp-based control in the near-RT RAN intelligent controller (RIC) with virtualized digital twin (VDT) management in the non-RT RIC. We formulate a multi-objective optimization problem that jointly maximizes slice-specific utility and service response profit while minimizing the operational cost. We develop a SA asynchronous hierarchical reinforcement learning (SA-AHRL) framework to solve this problem. It employs SA action-mapped proximal policy optimization (SA-AMPPO) for high-level VDT orchestration and deep Q-network (DQN) based agents for low-level synchronization. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SA-AMPPO-DQN algorithm significantly outperforms the modified PPO and PPO without generalized advantage estimation, achieving 9.95% and 20.18% higher mean slice utility profit, respectively, under scalable service request loads.

title: Secure and Privacy-Preserving ISAC in RIS-Aided IAB Networks with Delay Alignment Modulation.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) can significantly enhance integrated access and backhaul (IAB) networks, yet their reprogrammable nature and broadcast backhaul also create new security vulnerabilities. To address these challenges, we propose a secure integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework for RIS-aided IAB systems. The framework employs delay alignment modulation (DAM) to synchronize symbol arrivals, thereby mitigating inter-symbol interference under time-selective fading without requiring complex equalization. A dual-function radar–communication base station coordinates with the RIS to enable adaptive beamforming, while a joint optimization of base station precoding, RIS coefficients, and radar receive filters is formulated to maximize secrecy rate. This high-dimensional, non-convex problem is tackled using a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm with a hybrid multilayer perceptron (MLP)-large language model (LLM)-actor design. Results were compared against benchmark schemes that used DDPG with a standard MLP actor and an LLM-enhanced actor. Simulation results demonstrate secrecy rate gains of up to 45% when RIS is integrated compared to non-RIS systems, while within the learning framework, the hybrid actor achieves 35% improvement over the MLP baseline and 28% over the LLM-only approach.

title: Hybrid Actor DRL for Secrecy Optimization in RIS-Aided IAB Networks with DAM.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) and integrated access and backhaul (IAB) enable cost-effective coverage extension and controllable propagation in beyond-5G networks, but secrecy performance is challenged by coupled access–backhaul links, unit-modulus phase constraints, and intelligent eavesdroppers. This paper investigates secrecy rate optimization in a RIS-aided IAB system enhanced with delay alignment modulation (DAM) and dual-beam transmission to synchronize symbol arrivals. The problem is formulated as a joint optimization of transmit power, RIS phase shifts, DAM zero-forcing, per-user and backhaul SNR, access–backhaul splitting, and total backhaul capacity. We propose a Hybrid actor deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework that integrates deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) with a multilayer perceptron (MLP)–large language model (LLM) actor. The proposed Hybrid actor DRL improves efficiency converging 42.8% faster than MLP-based DRL and 27.2% faster than LLM-based DRL, while delivering 13.75% and 8.33% higher steady-state secrecy rates, respectively.

title: Communicating Semantics to an Indecisive Receiver.
abstract: This paper studies semantic communications in a broadcast setting where one of the decoders is indecisive. The reconstruction objective switches between tasks based on the decoder’s intent, which is unknown to the encoder. We formalize the indecisive decoder and analyze it in the multi-decoder source coding framework. We characterize how system design depends on the switching probability p and the per-task distortion constraints. Guided by these insights, we propose a multimodal semantic communication model with an indecisive receiver in a broadcast setting. We train distinct models, each corresponding to a different value of p, and measure their task-oriented fidelities. Simulations over AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels demonstrate that training concentrates fidelity on the more likely task as p varies. The framework yields design insights for next-generation semantic networks with context-driven task selection at the receiver.

title: Average is Good Enough: Low-Complexity UE Receivers for Non-linear Precoded OFDM in Green Networks.
abstract: Power amplifier (PA) non-linearity is a key source of energy inefficiency in 5G and future 6G systems. While reducing input signal backoff improves PA efficiency, it introduces non-linear distortions. These distortions can be mitigated using receiver-side digital post-distortion (DPoD) with near-maximum likelihood detection. Among DPoD methods, Power Amplifier Non-linearity Cancellation (PANC) offers a good trade-off between performance and complexity. PANC, however, was designed for non-precoded single antenna use case and its scalability to multi-antenna and precoded systems is limited. In this work, the PANC framework is extended to support realistic multi-antenna configurations and frequency-selective precoding. Key limitations of the conventional PANC in such settings are identified, and a new variant that leverages statistical averaging of non-linear interference across multiple antennas is proposed. The proposed method makes the computational complexity independent of the number of transmit antennas. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach.

title: Hybrid MIMO Localization with Markov Chain Semi-Analytic Analysis.
abstract: Hybrid antenna arrays are considered as a promising tool for future wireless networks that allows enhanced positioning accuracy with limited number of RF chains. In this paper, we develop an optimization algorithm for analog elements connecting the array elements and the RF chains based on an iterative element-by-element adjustment with controllable convergence behavior for different hybrid architectures. Our algorithm relies on electromagnetic modeling accounting for near/far field and array geometry effects with mutual coupling correction. Assuming random element selection for updates, we apply Markov chain modeling for semi-analytical (analytical for the given scenario realization) investigation of partially connected switched configurations and demonstrate a trade-off between the stationary localization accuracy and the convergence rate. We extend our Markov chain analysis to a hybrid network of spatially distributed sub-systems and show a possibility of significant localization accuracy improvement with joint non-coherent sub-system processing. For higher dimension fully connected architectures, we verify the semi-analytic results by means of simulations with electromagnetic modeling.

title: Experimental Evaluation of Blockchain-Based Collaborative Intrusion Detection on a Virtual 5G Testbed.
abstract: Recent advances in open-source cellular systems enable the deployment of fully virtualized fifth-generation Standalone (5G SA) networks on commodity hardware, creating new opportunities for realistic experimentation with advanced security mechanisms. This paper reports the experimental evaluation of a collaborative intrusion detection system (CIDS) augmented with a permissioned blockchain on such a 5G SA testbed. Our platform integrates the srsRAN Project, Open5GS, GNU Radio and ZeroMQ to emulate an end-to-end mobile network, while the blockchain provides tamper-resistant traceability of alerts. We assess both network and security performance under multiple configurations. Results show that virtualization constraints limit per-UE throughput to 60–80 Mb/s and that consensus operations increase the end-to-end latency by only 1–4 ms. The block commit time averages around 250 ms and collaborative sharing of alerts improves the IDS F1-score from 0.87 to 0.92 with a reduction in false positives. These findings demonstrate that permissioned blockchains can be integrated into virtualized 5G SA networks with minimal overhead and tangible security benefits.

title: Protocol Data Unit Set-based QoS-aware Downlink Scheduling for Extended Reality Applications in 6G.
abstract: This paper presents a downlink scheduling framework for Extended Reality (XR) applications in 6G networks. Building on the 3GPP Release 18 Protocol Data Unit (PDU) Set-based quality of service (QoS) framework, we propose a PDU Set Delay Tracking Queue (PDTQ) mechanism that provides real-time visibility into each PDU Set's remaining delay budget. Unlike existing approaches relying on indirect urgency metrics, PDTQ directly tracks PDU Set aging across queue positions for precise identification of delay-critical data. Leveraging this, we develop the PDTQ-Guided XR (PiXR) scheduler, an adaptive heuristic that allocates resources based on delay criticality and instantaneous channel conditions. Simulations show that PiXR achieves approximately 4--5x higher satisfied user counts than state-of-the-art PDU Set-aware schedulers under limited resources, while maintaining comparable or better performance under adequate conditions.

title: Multi-Hop IoT Network Fault Detection Using Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network.
abstract: Large-scale multi-hop wireless IoT networks are increasingly being deployed to support critical applications with stringent QoS requirements. Robust fault detection in such networks is vital for ensuring normal network operations and enabling proactive maintenance especially in adversarial environments. However, the existing researches primarily focus on data-driven attack detection, leaving natural network fault detection largely unexplored. Due to the absence of dedicated routers, multi-hop IoT networks require network nodes to transmit their own data and also relay data for others, which introduces inherent and cascaded anomalies, making it difficult to locate anomaly sources. Furthermore, the underlying CSMA/CA based communication protocols adopted in IoT networks incur unpredictable delays in transmissions, thereby complicating timely anomaly detection and accurate diagnosis. This paper proposes innovative network fault detection technologies tailored for large-scale multi-hop IoT networks. We introduce a spatio-temporal graph neural network (STGNN) model capable of accurately detecting both node-level and edge-level faults. Our model takes both temporal data and metadata for context-aware forecasting and reconstruction. To address the lack of labeled data, we adopt an unsupervised learning paradigm. We evaluated our model on various large-scale network topologies and transaction log datasets, and results demonstrate that our model consistently outperforms baseline models across most cases.

title: Calibrating Ray Tracing Using Local Phase Error Estimates Enabled Smart Rail Transit.
abstract: In rail transit scenarios, Ray tracing (RT) has modeling errors from environmental reconstruction and electromagnetic parameter uncertainties. And dynamic phase errors caused by coherent multi-path superposition triggered by these modeling errors. Such phase errors decrease prediction precision of channel parameters significantly. We proposes an intelligent RT calibration method based on local phase errors. It builds a phase error distribution model and uses limited measurements to explicitly estimate and correct phase errors in RT-generated channel responses. Firstly, the method applies the Variational Expectation-Maximization algorithm to optimize the phase error model, where the expectation step derives an approximate posterior distribution and the maximization step updates parameters conditioned on this posterior. Secondly, experiments are conducted using differentiable RT implemented in the Sionna library, which explicitly provides gradients of environmental and link parameters with respect to channel frequency responses. Finally, experimental results show that in railway scenarios, compared with calibration methods based on phase error oblivious and uniform phase error, the proposed approach achieves average gains of about 10dB at SNR = 0dB and 20dB at SNR = 30dB.

title: Enabling QoS-Aware Multi-Stage Task Allocation in FANETs: A Hierarchical Learning Approach.
abstract: Flying Ad-Hoc Networks (FANETs) are increasingly deployed to execute multi-stage disaster-relief tasks, such as data collection and rescue, which rely on effective task allocation. Due to the high latency and frequent link disruptions, this allocation is highly sensitive to Quality of Service (QoS) to ensure reliable Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) collaboration. However, existing schemes focus on end-to-end QoS for an entire task rather than the distinct QoS demands of individual task stages. In this paper, we propose HierTask, a hierarchical framework for QoS-aware multi-stage task allocation in FANETs. Specifically, HierTask assigns each task stage to candidate UAV groups through global task-UAV matching, and then dynamically selects the appropriate UAVs within each group based on real-time QoS feedback. To jointly optimize QoS across stages, we formulate the allocation process as a long-term optimization problem and transform it into a hierarchical Markov decision process, enabling sequential decision-making under inter-stage dependencies. To solve this problem, we propose an attention-integrated hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm, where attention modules capture task-UAV feature relevance and hierarchical policies balance global planning with local adaptability. Extensive simulations demonstrate that by satisfying QoS demands at each stage, HierTask significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in task completion rate.

title: Learning-Based Slotted Over-the-Air Computation in Multi-Cluster Networks with Channel Awareness.
abstract: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) enables simultaneous data collection and aggregation from massive devices. However, in the conventional one-slot AirComp approach, signal amplitude mismatches caused by time-varying channel fading inevitably lead to computation errors. In this paper, we propose a multi-slot framework for AirComp tasks with clustered sensors, which leverages time diversity to deal with the instantaneous intra-cluster channel gain disparity caused by time-varying fading, enhancing the performance of a multi-cluster AirComp system. In particular, each aggregation task is assigned across multiple time slots, with only one task served per time slot, and a channel gain threshold is set to guide transmission scheduling. Consequently, we intend to minimize the system computation error by jointly optimizing the transmission and scheduling strategies. The problem is an NP-hard mixed-integer nonlinear program optimization model with intricate coupling among optimization variables, which is solved with a soft actor-critic-based approach. Simulation results validate the convergence and performance of the proposed algorithm, demonstrating the effectiveness of our design.

title: Agentic AI-Enabled Multi-AP Cooperation for Next-Generation Wi-Fi.
abstract: Wi-Fi 8 and future generations strive to develop multi-access point (MAP) coordination to enable advanced performance in terms of throughput, latency, and mobility. Conventional approaches are built upon pre-determined protocol rules and syntax, rendering APs lass capable of interacting and evolving in challenging scenarios. We propose an agentic-AI framework, termed AI-Genie Wi-Fi, to address the challenge. The design principle of AI-Genie Wi-Fi lies in achieving synergy between the efficiency of 802.11 specifications and the intelligence offered by generative AI models. It features an agent management entity (AME) architecture tailored for efficiently bridging and exploiting both the IEEE 802.11 protocol stack and large language models. Specific designs of two critical AME modules, namely Tools and Memory, are materialized for two use cases, (1) channel switch, and (2) load balancing, respectively. The performance of the proposed architecture is validated through a suite of hardware prototypes, where AI-Genie Wi-Fi implements the two use cases and substantially enhances downlink throughput and reduces round-trip time in the downloading and gaming scenarios, respectively.

title: Federated Few-Shot Learning for Internet of Medical Things Applications: Towards Effective AFib Detection.
abstract: The use of data from IoT devices in critical applications, such as atrial fibrillation (AFib) detection in the medical domain, faces significant challenges related to privacy, communication costs, and computational limitations. Moreover, traditional cloud-based AI methods are often unsuitable due to data privacy laws, high data transmission costs, and the statistical differences (non-IID data) across devices and institutions. To overcome these limitations, this work introduces a Federated Few-Shot Learning (FFSL) framework that combines prototypical networks with a lightweight one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) encoder, enabling effective AFib classification with minimal labeled data across distributed healthcare institutions. The proposed framework was evaluated using a real patient ECG dataset, and the results show it achieved a peak accuracy of 91.25% with a high AFib recall of 96% across 1-shot, 5-shot, and 10-shot scenarios, which clearly outperforms all the benchmark models compared to. The results demonstrate the framework’s practicality for privacy-preserving, resource-efficient, and generalizable AFib detection in decentralized clinical settings.

title: Spectral Amplitude Encoding for CEP-Locked Ultrashort Pulse Communication.
abstract: This paper introduces and numerically analyzes the feasibility of a direct spectral amplitude encoding scheme for high-capacity communication using a carrier envelope phase (CEP)-locked ultrashort laser pulses. Leveraging the important, coherent bandwidth of these lasers, our method partitions the pulse spectrum into discrete segments to encode 64 bits of data into a single pulse. We conduct extensive Monte Carlo simulations to characterize the Bit Error Rate (BER) performance of this technique under realistic linear impairments, including adjacent-channel crosstalk and Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN). Our analysis systematically investigates the impact of key design parameters, exploring the trade-offs associated with modulation depth, the performance dependency on the spectral location of the data, and the effectiveness of spectral guardbands in mitigating interference. The results identify that the scheme’s performance is fundamentally limited by the low signal-to-noise ratio of the spectral tails. In this paper we show that a robust, noise-limited performance can be achieved by localizing the encoding to the high-power spectral center. Furthermore, our analysis shows that within this localized scheme, performance can be enhanced by introducing guardbands, establishing a clear trade-off between the required signal noise ratio (SNR) and spectral efficiency. This work provides a foundational performance analysis, establishing the viability of our proposed encoding paradigm.

title: Fast Window Decoding of BMST Codes via Step Adjustment and Universal Parity-Check Termination.
abstract: Block Markov Superposition Transmission (BMST) codes are a class of spatially coupled codes, that achieve excellent error correction performance via superposition of simple constituent codes. A BMST encoder consists of an outer basic code and an inner rate-one block-convolutional shift register. The resulting graph representation of the encoder allows sliding-window decoding, similarly to spatially coupled Low-Density Parity-Check codes. This paper proposes a method to reduce the decoding complexity by adjusting the step size of the sliding window. Furthermore, a low-complexity parity-check-based early termination criterion is introduced, which can be universally applied to recursive BMST structures.

title: Ordered Outage and Capacity Metrics for LEO Satellite Mega-Constellations.
Signature-Aided Early Termination for Ordered Blind Decoding in 6G Control Channels.
abstract: Blind decoding (BD) of the physical downlink control channel is a major barrier to reducing latency and energy use in user equipment, with 6G exacerbating these issues due to larger search spaces. Current methods to reduce BD depend on channel estimation or partial decoding, which restrict early termination. This paper proposes a signature-aided framework for early BD termination through lightweight pre-demodulation filtering, bypassing the need for channel estimation or polar decoding. Two signature types are introduced: signatures using phase rotation patterns for likelihood filtering and signatures in demodulation reference signals for neural network filtering. Both methods are compatible with existing NR receivers. Simulations show over 90% fewer BD attempts at a 1% block error rate. Furthermore, blocking probability decreases by 46–70%, enabling flexible scheduling without added complexity. This framework offers a scalable base for designing energy-efficient 6G control channels.

title: MU-MIMO ISAC Transmit Signal Design for Radar Data Cube Reconstruction.
abstract: Conventional multiuser (MU) MIMO–OFDM signals are rank-deficient when the number of users is smaller than the number of transmit antennas, making reliable MIMO radar processing infeasible. To address this limitation, this paper presents a novel transmit signal design that enables joint MU-MIMO–OFDM communication and MIMO radar sensing. The proposed scheme introduces a radar supplement signal that ensures full-rank transmission and enforces orthogonality to both the communication channel and the data signal, thereby significantly improving radar estimation accuracy while preserving communication performance. Furthermore, the transmission structure divides the time–frequency resource grid into sub-blocks, enabling direct reconstruction of the radar data cube and ensuring full compatibility with conventional MIMO radar processing. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves superior radar detection performance (average precision of 0.95) while maintaining spectral efficiency comparable to the pure communication baseline and outperforming the separate resource allocation method for radar and communication.

title: Advanced Bayesian Channel Estimation for Semi-Passive RIS-Empowered mmWave Systems.
abstract: This paper proposes a channel estimation technique using a Bayesian framework for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-empowered millimeter-wave (mmWave) multi-user equipment systems, where a few semi-passive RIS elements with baseband processing capability are integrated into the RIS. Here, low-resolution analog-to-digital converters are considered to minimize the power consumption of the RIS. Based on additional information sampled from the RIS semi-passive elements, we propose a separate RIS channel estimation technique using the sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) framework, where we use a complex adaptive Laplace prior to effectively capture the angular domain sparsity normally present in mmWave channels. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed technique provides superior estimation performance to baselines, particularly an approach using a Student’s-t prior.

title: A Testbed Implementation of LLM-Based Intent Coordination for Autonomous RAN Management.
abstract: Intent-driven network management enables autonomous RAN operation by expressing high-level objectives without explicit configurations. However, intent conflicts cannot always be resolved at the policy level, as their feasibility often depends on real-time radio conditions. Existing approaches focus on intent translation and policy-level negotiation, leaving execution-layer conflict resolution unaddressed. This paper proposes an LLM-based intent coordination framework operating directly at the RAN execution layer. The framework jointly considers active intents and real-time network measurements to detect conflicts, predict feasibility, and generate executable resolution actions without relying on predefined optimization models. A history reservoir enables learning from past outcomes for more precisely calibrated actions. The proposed approach is validated on a real wireless testbed using srsRAN, Open5GS, and USRP platforms. Experimental findings show that the proposed method outperforms rule-based baselines by effectively coordinating conflicting intents across fluctuating network conditions.

title: CertDNS: Guaranteeing the Integrity of DNS Records Using PKIX Certificates.
Spatially-Adaptive Conformal Graph Transformer for Indoor Localization in Wi-Fi Driven Networks.
abstract: Indoor localization is a critical enabler for a wide range of location-based services in smart environments, including navigation, asset tracking, and safety-critical applications. Recent graph-based models leverage spatial relationships between Wireless Fidelity (Wi-Fi) Access Points (APs) and devices, offering finer localization granularity, but fall short in quantifying prediction uncertainty, a key requirement for real-world deployment. In this paper, we propose Spatially-Adaptive Conformal Graph Transformer (SAC-GT), a framework for accurate and reliable indoor localization. SAC-GT integrates a Graph Transformer (GT) model that captures network’s spatial topology and signal strength dynamics, with a novel Spatially-Adaptive Conformal Prediction (SACP) method that provides region-specific uncertainty estimates. This allows SAC-GT to produce not only precise two-dimensional (2D) location predictions but also statistically valid confidence regions tailored to varying environmental conditions. Extensive evaluations on a large-scale real-world dataset demonstrate that the proposed SAC-GT solution achieves state-of-the-art localization accuracy while delivering robust and spatially adaptive reliability guarantees.

title: A Lightweight Multimodal Beam Prediction Model with Hierarchical Attention for 6G V2X Network.
abstract: The evolution of next-generation communication technologies necessitates accurate and efficient beam prediction to ensure high-quality links in Vehicle-to-Everything networks. Numerous studies have explored beam prediction schemes, which can be categorized into those based on blind beam training, channel state tracking, and side information. While existing schemes suffer from excessive parameters and high latency, this work introduces a lightweight multimodal model centered on a hierarchical attention mechanism. The model employs local attention to capture fine-grained vehicle dynamics and global attention to model long-term scene evolution. Extensive experiments demonstrate the model’s superior robustness and accuracy across diverse traffic scenarios, significantly outperforming existing benchmarks.

title: ADPS-Sat: Adaptive Distributed Patch-Sequence Scheduling for Satellite-Edge Vision Transformers.
abstract: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) constellations provide global coverage and low latency, but individual satellites have limited compute and offloading to ground adds hundreds of milliseconds of delay. Inter-Satellite Links (ISLs) enable collaborative inference to overcome these limits. Existing inter-satellite schemes focus on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), but Vision Transformers (ViT) excel at high-resolution remote sensing through global self-attention, supporting small-object detection, fine-grained change monitoring, and robust occlusion handling. Deploying ViTs across a constellation is challenging due to large parameters and repeated key/value exchanges, imposing heavy bandwidth, synchronization, and scheduling demands. To tackle this issue, we propose ADPS-Sat (Adaptive Distributed Patch-Sequence Scheduling for Satellite-Edge ViT), the first practical system for collaborative ViT inference in LEO constellations. By decoupling NP-hard scheduling into patch enumeration-and-pruning and Particle Swarm Optimization(PSO)-driven sequence-parallel allocation within an alternating-optimization loop, ADPS-Sat adapts to dynamic task arrivals and link topologies. In a 4-satellite simulation using ViT-Base fine-tuned on the MillionAID dataset, ADPS improves average performance over the two state-of-the-art baselines by roughly 31.8%.

title: Byzantine Resilient Federated Multi-Task Representation Learning.
abstract: In this paper, we propose BR-MTRL, a Byzantine-resilient multi-task representation learning framework that handles faulty or malicious agents. Our approach leverages representation learning through a shared neural network (NN) model, where all clients share fixed layers, except for a client-specific final layer. This structure captures shared features among clients while enabling individual adaptation, making it a promising approach for leveraging client data and computational power for personalized federated learning. To learn the model, we employ an alternating gradient descent strategy: each client optimizes its local model, updates its final layer, and sends estimates of the shared representation to a central server for aggregation. To defend against Byzantine agents, we employ two robust aggregation methods for client-server communication, Geometric Median and Krum. Our method enables personalized learning while maintaining resilience in distributed settings. We implemented the proposed algorithm in a federated testbed built using Amazon Web Services (AWS) platform and compared its performance with various benchmark algorithms and their variations. Through experiments using real-world datasets, including CIFAR-10 and FEMNIST, we demonstrated the effectiveness and robustness of our approach and its transferability to new unseen clients with limited data, even in the presence of Byzantine adversaries.

title: Joint Mechanism Selection and Photon Generation Rate Optimization for QKD Military Wireless Networks.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a hybrid quantum key distribution (QKD) scheme to improve the performance and adaptability of QKD applications in dynamic environmental scenarios of military communication systems. Specifically, our proposed hybrid scheme dynamically selects the prepare-and-measure (PM) and entanglement-based mechanisms in QKD to counteract the increase in the quantum bit error rate (QBER) caused by atmospheric loss and turbulence. To efficiently address this issue, we jointly optimize the control of QKD mechanism selection and photon generation rate using a mathematically formulated non-convex mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem. This optimization problem is then solved using advanced techniques, including first-order Taylor approximation and Difference of Convex (DC) programming. To enable fast decision-making for optimal solutions, we design and propose an algorithm based on the deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method. Our numerical results show that the performance of the proposed DRL algorithm is close to that of the classical optimal method, while its time complexity is significantly better. Thus, the DRL algorithm is more applicable in practical tactical scenarios.

title: FedGIA: Personalized Federated Learning via Graph-based Invariant Aggregation.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) can achieve privacy-preserving model training on decentralized data, but due to statistical heterogeneity between clients, its global model often performs poorly. This flaw has given rise to the field of Personalized Federated Learning (PFL). The aggregation strategy adopted by existing PFL methods is relatively simple, and there is a risk of being misled by spurious correlations in the data, thereby weakening the robust generalization ability of the model. To address the aforementioned issues, we propose the innovative PFL framework, FedGIA, which integrates a graph-based aggregation mechanism and an invariant adaptation mechanism. Numerous experiments have shown that FedGIA outperforms existing PFL baseline schemes on multiple datasets, demonstrating excellent accuracy, stability, and adaptability.

title: Adaptive DTN Routing Using Spiking Neural Networks for Services over NTNs.
abstract: Delay-Tolerant Networking (DTN) was developed to address long latency and intermittent connectivity in space communications. The Bundle Protocol (BP) employs a store-carry-forward paradigm, making DTN a viable framework for extending 5G services via Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN). NTN links exhibit intermittent visibility, variable capacity, and weather-induced fading, which invalidate conventional end-to-end assumptions. Contact Space Gateway (CSG) enhances DTN routing by combining path performance prediction with machine learning based on spiking neural networks (SNNs) for adaptive next-hop selection. This approach addresses limitations of Contact Graph Routing (CGR) under congestion and rapidly changing conditions. For critical applications, AI-driven adaptability is essential, as demand spikes, interference, contact plan deviations, and abrupt link degradation can occur unpredictably. Learning from delivery outcomes and evolving telemetry enables CSG to align forwarding decisions with observed network behavior rather than nominal schedules. This work introduces two enhancements to improve robustness and responsiveness: (1) periodic reporting, in which nodes disseminate network state at fixed intervals and fuse local and peer metrics to approximate a global network view despite intermittent connectivity; and (2) loop avoidance integrated into SNN training, which penalizes predecessor selection to reduce routing loops while preserving beneficial path reversals. Experimental results obtained using a prototype CSG implementation within NASA’s High-Rate DTN (HDTN) framework demonstrate significantly reduced response times without loss of delivery success, supporting NTN service extension under uncertainty.

title: Measurement and Characterization of Terahertz Reflections from Common Indoor Materials.
abstract: Terahertz communications is an emerging candidate for future 6G wireless systems because of the potential to deliver terabit/sec data rates. However, it suffers from many impairments such as high path loss, severe reflection/scattering loss, and blockage by many materials. In order to design communication systems and protocols, it is important to be able to model the channel accurately. To that end, in this paper, we describe results of a measurement campaign where we characterize the reflections of 325-500 GHz from 11 different materials. These materials are what one would find in most indoor environments and thus will help with constructing accurate channel models.Prior work on characterizing reflection coefficients of materials for terahertz is quite limited. In most cases, results are reported for a small frequency range and for just a few materials. Indeed, none of the prior studies consider common materials like paper, cotton cloth, keyboards, etc. that we study. We collect measurements in our terahertz testbed and fit a reflection channel model to the collected data and show a very good fit. Using the fit we derive parameters including reflection coefficient, complex permittivity, loss tangent, and roughness. We observe a frequency dependence for many materials such as cardboard, paper, cotton, and plastic. Many other materials such as glass, keyboard, plywood, and wood show less of a frequency dependence. We discuss the implication of these results for three frequency bands 327-333 GHz, 356-368 GHz, and 391-433 GHz that are being considered by ETSI (European Communications Standards Institute) for industrial applications.

title: Constrained MARL for Coexisting TN-NTN Resource Allocation: Scalability and Flexibility.
abstract: This paper considers the joint TN-NTN constrained resource allocation, where terrestrial base stations and non-terrestrial base stations coexist in the spectrum. We focus on large-scale and practical scenarios characterized by large numbers of transmission channels and users, alongside highly dynamic user behaviors. As common learning solutions fail to address these challenges, we propose a decomposition solution based on the special properties of the cross-segment interference, and then tackle the original problem via solving subproblems in a sequential learning manner.
