Furthermore, to enhance the flexibility of the learned policies, we design a stochastic training environment that captures the key characteristics of real-world systems. Simulation results tested on the full 20MHz bandwidth with various numerologies show that our solution significantly improves scalability compared to existing solutions and remains robust in highly dynamic scenarios.

title: Joint Optimization for Security and Reliability in Round-Trip Transmissions for URLLC services.
abstract: Physical layer security (PLS) is a potential solution for secure and reliable transmissions in future Ultra-Reliable and Low-Latency Communications (URLLC). This work jointly optimizes redundant bits and blocklength allocation in practical round-trip transmission scenarios. To minimize the leakage-failure probability, a metric that jointly characterizes security and reliability in PLS, we formulate an optimization problem for allocating both redundant bits and blocklength. By deriving the boundaries of the feasible set, we obtain the globally optimal solution for this integer optimization problem. To achieve more computationally efficient solutions, we propose a block coordinate descent (BCD) method that exploits the partial convexity of the objective function. Subsequently, we develop a majorization-minimization (MM) algorithm through convex approximation of the objective function, which further improves computational efficiency. Finally, we validate the performance of the three proposed approaches through simulations, demonstrating their practical applicability for future URLLC services.

title: Collaborative Multistatic Integrated Sensing and Communications-Part I: Radar Sensing = Communication Channel Estimation?
Collaborative Multistatic Integrated Sensing and Communications-Part II: Autofocus via Message Passing in Tanner Graphs.
abstract: The technology of integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) improves the efficiency of spectrum and power by sharing the same waveform and harvesting reflected electromagnetic (EM) waves. In ISAC networks, different nodes can collaborate in sensing by exchanging information related to their measurements, while communications and sensing can collaborate due to the similarity between communication channel estimation and radar sensing. However, the collaboration for sensing is challenged by the imperfection in time and frequency synchronizations among the nodes. In the second part of this paper, an autofocus algorithm is proposed to mitigate the time/frequency synchronization errors based on common targets, similarly to parity check nodes in error correction codes. The inference of sensing information is accomplished by message passing in Tanner graphs, which is similar to the decoding of low density parity check (LDPC) codes. The validity of the proposed collaborative ISAC scheme is demonstrated by numerical simulations.

title: A New Analytical Framework for BER Evaluation of Cross-Link NOMA in Vehicular Networks.
abstract: This paper investigates a cross-link non-orthogonal multiple access (XNOMA) system with two sources and two destinations, where each destination receives a superposition of four streams through direct links and cross links. Closed-form bit error rate (BER) expressions are derived under Rayleigh fading, which accounts for imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). To model SIC imperfections and the resulting error propagation, a projection-based residual method is adopted, enabling the derivation of effective SNR expressions at each decoding stage. Feasibility conditions for power allocation (PA) and a fixed decoding order are established to ensure successful message decoding. We formulate a PA optimisation that minimises the average BER of the system under SIC feasibility and fairness constraints. Both average and per-message BER are obtained for the 4-BPSK scenario. Our Monte Carlo simulations show excellent agreement with the analytical results, which validates the proposed model and analysis. A comparative analysis of downlink NOMA (DNOMA) and orthogonal multiple access (OMA) highlights the effects of multiuser interference and residual SIC errors on reliability. The system-level comparison shows that XNOMA delivers a trade-off between throughput and BER. The findings provide tractable performance predictions and practical design insights for XNOMA links under realistic SIC constraints.

title: Theoretical Explanation and Upper Boundary of Model Extraction Attacks.
abstract: Existing research has demonstrated that model extraction attacks infringe commercial value and privacy security. The attackers only need to query the black-box victim model with the attack data. Then they use the prediction to locally train a clone model with a similar function to the victim model. However, the current model extraction attacks generally stay in the method stage, focusing on the selection of attack data, and lacking the explanation of attack principle. Therefore, we theoretically explain the principle of model extraction attacks based on decision boundary theory, thus providing reliable guidance for the optimization of future attack and defense methods. In addition, we investigate the upper boundary of model extraction attacks independent of attack data, acting as a measure of model extraction difficulty. Finally, we design a specific and feasible experimental method to test the theory.

title: ASTSC: An Asymmetric Swin Transformer-Based Efficient Semantic Communication System for Remote Sensing Images.
abstract: With the advancement of remote sensing (RS) imaging, high-resolution images are increasingly available. However, efficient transmission under resource-constrained on-orbit conditions remains a challenge. Existing neural networks (NN), mostly designed with symmetric architectures, fail to fully exploit the computational resources at ground stations, thereby limiting semantic extraction and image reconstruction performance. To address this, we propose an asymmetric Swin Transformer-based semantic communication system (ASTSC) for RS images, enabling orbit–ground collaborative transmission. Specifically, the satellite encoder is kept shallow to reduce on-orbit computation, while the ground decoder is deeper, incorporating multi-level feature fusion and a generative adversarial network (GAN) for semantic and fine-detail reconstruction. Experimental results show that ASTSC outperforms three representative categories of methods in both compression efficiency and image reconstruction quality: conventional schemes (JPEG + LDPC), an advanced CNN-based model, and an advanced symmetric Transformer-based model. Ablation studies indicate that the asymmetric architecture achieves approximately 0.8 dB PSNR gain over its symmetric counterpart. Furthermore, the "universal model + fine-tuning" strategy further enhances system performance and facilitates model updates in air–ground integrated networks.

title: Joint Downlink and Uplink Pilot Exploitation for Multi-User 4D Parameter Estimation in Aerial MIMO-ISAC.
abstract: Most existing integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems rely solely on either downlink or uplink pilot signals. While jointly leveraging both types of pilots is expected to improve sensing performance and reduce power consumption, this approach has rarely been explored. To bridge this gap, we investigate a multi-input multi-output (MIMO)-based aerial ISAC system that uses both downlink and uplink pilots. First, we derive the Cramér–Rao lower bounds (CRLBs) for jointly estimating multi-user 4D parameters—including 2D angle, range, and velocity—using both pilot types, and provide a closed-form CRLB expression for the single-user case to offer design insights. Next, we propose a low-complexity estimation method based on chirp z-transform (CZT)-accelerated block coordinate descent (BCD). Numerical results validate the benefits of joint pilot utilization and show that the proposed algorithm achieves high estimation accuracy with low computational complexity and low transmit power. These findings highlight the practical value and effectiveness of the proposed framework for aerial MIMO-ISAC applications.

title: Differential Privacy for Free: Wireless Federated Learning over Multiple-Access Fading Channels.
JIMI: A Hierarchical Partition-Refinement MIQP Framework for Jitter Minimization in PONs.
abstract: Jitter mitigation is pivotal for maintaining high quality of service (QoS) in Passive Optical Networks (PONs). However, existing PON systems lack the capability for global jitter optimization and exhibit limited generality across diverse bandwidth scheduling algorithms and traffic loads. This paper presents JIMI, a multi-stage optimization framework that formulates system-wide jitter minimization as a Mixed-Integer Quadratic Programming (MIQP) problem, offering global optimality guarantees and strong adaptability across different PON configurations and traffic conditions. Besides this, JIMI leverages hierarchical decomposition to effectively reduce computational complexity. Moreover, JIMI incorporates a partition-refinement mechanism to further enhance its scalability in large-scale PON deployments. Experimental results demonstrate that JIMI achieves high solution quality across diverse application scenarios in 50G-PONs, with average jitter reductions of 7.3× and 2.9× at the coarse-grained and fine-grained optimization levels, respectively. Moreover, JIMI maintains robust performance and high efficiency as the network scales up. These results collectively indicate the efficacy, generality, and scalability of JIMI, establishing it as a promising solution for next-generation PONs.

title: Pilot-Free Channel Inference via Multimodal Flow Matching.
abstract: Accurate channel state information (CSI) is fundamental to reliable and efficient wireless communication. However, traditional pilot-based channel estimation introduces considerable overhead, particularly in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. This paper investigates pilot-free channel inference to estimate complete CSI directly from multimodal sensing observations, including camera images, LiDAR point clouds, and GPS coordinates. Specifically, we propose a multimodal flow matching framework that fuses heterogeneous sensing modalities into a latent distribution in the channel space, and learns a velocity field that continuously transports samples from the source latent distribution toward the target channel distribution. To shorten and straighten the transport trajectory, we introduce a modality alignment loss that not only regularizes the encoded source distribution but also encourages it to align with the target channel distribution. During inference, the learned flow is efficiently approximated using a second-order numerical integrator. For evaluation, we construct a multimodal simulation dataset with Sionna and Blender, enabling realistic modeling of sensing scenes and wireless propagation. System-level experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms both pilot-based and sensing-aided baselines in channel estimation accuracy under dynamic environments.

title: DoA Estimation Based on Deep Learning-MUSIC Hybrid Algorithm with Fluid Antenna for Closely Spaced Signals.
abstract: Fluid antenna (FA) has emerged as a highly promising candidate in wireless communications, attributed to its exceptional design flexibility and enhanced degrees of freedom (DoFs). This paper addresses the challenge of direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation for closely spaced signals under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and limited snapshot conditions. To tackle this issue, a dual-driven FA system is proposed, which synergistically integrates data-driven and model-driven paradigms. Drawing inspiration from the Toeplitz algorithm, a deep neural network (DNN)-based multi-layer perceptron (MLP) architecture is developed to learn the mapping relationship between input covariance matrices and labeled covariance matrices. To ensure the output covariance matrices are compatible with subsequent subspace-based search procedures, a constrained forward computation function is designed. Furthermore, a dual-constrained loss function is formulated to balance the numerical precision and structural consistency of the output covariance matrices. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significant performance improvements over conventional DoA estimation algorithms in terms of estimation accuracy.

title: Privacy-Preserving Verification of Secure Aggregation for Hierarchical Peer-to-Peer Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed data sources without sharing raw data to enhance privacy, accuracy, and scalability. However, FL remains vulnerable to dishonest aggregators that may tamper with or misuse client model updates, compromising model integrity and privacy. A very natural manner is to authenticate that the aggregated weight is from the individuals’ weights. To address this, we propose a verifiable hierarchical peer-to-peer federated learning (P2PFL) framework integrating collaborative zk-SNARKs (proof-size efficient and non-interactive zero knowledge proofs) and multi-party computation. It enables clients to jointly generate a proof that verifies correct aggregation without revealing individual parameters. Also, no single node can access another’s plain weights, while allowing multiple clients to efficiently verify the aggregation outcome. Our P2PFL strengthens trust and privacy in federated learning by decentralizing verification and eliminating reliance on a single honest aggregator.

title: Coordination of Physical AI in a Wireless-Connected Smart Factory.
abstract: Smart factories represent a typical use case of Physical AI, where collaborative transportation multi-robot systems execute just-in-time material pickup and delivery based on real-time multi-robot task allocation from the edge server, enabling flexible production flows. However, dynamic task patterns and partial observability suggest a challenge in coordinating such distributed AI. This paper studies how wireless communication can fundamentally enhance collaborative Physical AI systems. Instead of optimizing existing communication for AI, we disruptively investigate how wireless communication improves AI execution. We identify two key pieces of information for AI decision-making, namely belief maps and predictive reward maps, to periodically exchange and fuse them via robot-to-infrastructure-to-robot communication. The fused belief maps are fed into the event-triggered planner and Q-learning, while the fused reward maps provide predictive guidance to assist Q-learning. Together, they enable a wireless-connected coordination scheme that integrates learning-based decision-making and dynamic event-triggered planning. Extensive simulations demonstrate that communication significantly improves scalability and efficiency, reducing task completion time and alleviating the computational burden. The results further reveal that timely information sharing can effectively compensate for limited local computation, highlighting the importance of integrated communication and computing for Physical AI and 6G communications.

title: Rethinking Mutual Coupling in Movable Antenna MIMO Systems.
abstract: Movable antenna (MA) systems have emerged as a promising technology for future wireless communication systems. The movement of antennas gives rise to mutual coupling (MC) effects, which have been previously ignored and can be exploited to enhance the capacity of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. To this end, we first model an MA-enabled point-to-point MIMO communication system with MC effects using a circuit-theoretic framework. The capacity maximization problem is then formulated as a non-concave optimization problem and solved via a block coordinate ascent (BCA)-based algorithm. The subproblem of optimizing MA positions is challenging due to the presence of the analytically intractable MC matrices. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a trust region method (TRM)-based algorithm to optimize MA positions, wherein Sylvester equations are employed to compute the derivatives of the inverse square roots of the MC matrices. Simulation results show significant capacity gains from leveraging MC effects, primarily due to customizable MC matrices and superdirectivity.

title: A Phase-Parameterized Frank-Sequence-Based CAZAC Waveform for Doubly Selective Channels.
abstract: Reliable communications over doubly selective channels require waveforms that are robust to both delay and Doppler spreads while maintaining low-complexity reception. Constant-amplitude zero autocorrelation (CAZAC) sequences provide attractive correlation properties and implementation advantages, yet their direct use in doubly selective channels is often suboptimal due to limited design flexibility. In this paper, we propose a phase-parameterized Frank sequence construction that preserves the CAZAC property while introducing an additional phase-parameter vector. Building on this construction, we develop a CAZAC waveform family tailored to doubly selective channels and propose two associated orthogonal modulation schemes. Compared with the fixed-structure Frank-sequence-based construction, the proposed waveform family can provide improved error-rate performance under doubly selective fading. Furthermore, simulation results show that, with linear MMSE reception, the proposed waveform achieves BER performance comparable to two representative high-mobility waveforms, namely, OTFS and AFDM. More importantly, in high-Doppler regimes, when combined with an MMSE-initialized iterative maximum-ratio combining (MRC) receiver, the proposed waveform provides a clear performance gain over OTFS and AFDM, indicating its suitability for high-mobility links.

title: HYDRA: A Hybrid Synthesizer for Asymmetric Mixture-of-Experts Communication Scheduling.
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models form a cornerstone of scaling language models to trillions of parameters, yet training efficiency is hampered by asymmetric Alltoallv communication. Existing schedule synthesizers face an impasse: (i) MILP-based synthesizers lack scalability; (ii) heuristic-based synthesizers trade global optimality for scalability; and (iii) symmetry-based synthesizers are scalable and near-optimal in symmetric settings, but this assumption fails under asymmetric MoE traffic. To address this impasse, we propose HYDRA, a hybrid synthesizer based on traffic decomposition. We observe that MoE traffic can be decomposed into two components: a stable, high-volume base and a dynamic, low-volume delta. In the first phase, HYDRA extracts from the base traffic a symmetric core for synthesis by symmetry-aware algorithms, and optimizes the small asymmetric residual using a multi-commodity flow (MCF) approximation. In the second phase, HYDRA schedules delta traffic with SRPT over the residual bandwidth remaining after the base schedule. Our evaluation shows that HYDRA reduces end-to-end MoE communication time by up to 34.4% compared with state-of-the-art synthesizers.

title: LAB: Integrating Deep Reinforcement Learning and Bayesian Optimization for Task-Oriented Computation Offloading.
abstract: In this paper, we consider an edge inference (EI) system where multiple edge devices (EDs) transmit visual data to an edge server (ES) for object detection. While degrading data (e.g., reducing video resolution from 4K to 720p or 480p) before transmission can reduce transmission delay, it often compromises inference accuracy. To balance the accuracy-latency tradeoff, we formulate a black-box mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) which maximizes long-term accuracy of all EDs while minimizing inference latency. The problem is challenging due to its implicit objective and combinatorial degradation action space. To address this problem, we propose LAB, a novel learning framework that effectively integrates deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and Bayesian optimization (BO). Within LAB, a DRL actor maps the input system state to discrete degradation actions directly, tackling the combinatorial complexity. In parallel, a BO critic employs a Gaussian process surrogate for model-based action evaluation. For each selected action, optimal bandwidth allocation is then efficiently solved via convex optimization. Experiments on real-world datasets show that LAB achieves near-optimal accuracy-latency tradeoff, exhibiting only 1.22% accuracy degradation and 0.07s latency increase compared to exhaustive search. It also outperforms conventional DRL with 3.29% higher accuracy and 42.60% lower latency, demonstrating its effectiveness for complex black-box optimization in EI systems.

title: LLM-driven Algorithm Composition and Optimization for TPE Design in OCS-based DCNs.
abstract: Nowadays, optical circuit switching (OCS) has been considered as a key building block for AI-centric data-center networks (DCNs), primarily due to its power efficiency, capacity, and capability of dynamic topology adaption (i.e., topology engineering (TPE)). However, the TPE design for OCS-based DCNs is challenging, especially when TPE should be optimized together with traffic engineering. In this work, we, for the first time to the best of our knowledge, propose a large language model (LLM) empowered approach, namely, Evol-TPE-LLM, to compose and optimize the procedure of TPE design. Specifically, we first formulate an integer linear programming (ILP) model to define the problem, and then architect Evol-TPE-LLM based on an LLM core that can understand the task of TPE design by digesting the ILP and leverage an evolutionary optimization loop to achieve automatic code generation and refinement. Extensive simulations verify the robustness and generalizability of Evol-TPE-LLM, and its superiority over the state-of-the-arts.

title: SemiRoot: A Semi-Supervised Deep Learning Framework for Root-Cause Analysis of QoE Degradations in Mobile Networks.
abstract: As modern mobile networks strive to meet the growing demands for low latency and high throughput, accurate root-cause analysis (RCA) of Quality of Experience (QoE) degradations has become essential for ensuring service reliability of radio access networks (RAN). While deep learning offers strong potential for automating this task, its effectiveness often hinges on large-scale, high-quality labels, which are costly to obtain. In contrast, rule-based labeling can be generated automatically but often suffers from low accuracy and semantic ambiguity. To address these limitations, we propose SemiRoot, a two-stage semi-supervised learning framework that integrates weak rule-derived labels with scarce expert supervision for intelligent RAN operation and diagnosis. In the first stage, we formulate a rule-guided contrastive learning objective to induce a semantically structured representation space, where latent clusters reflect degradation-related patterns encoded by domain heuristics. In the second stage, we employ expert-guided fine-tuning to calibrate decision boundaries with high precision. This decoupled design explicitly disentangles representation learning from decision-making and maintains the respective strengths of rule and expert supervision in a complementary manner. Extensive experiments on a real-world mobile network dataset demonstrate that Semi-Root consistently outperforms strong baselines, offering a label-efficient solution for QoE-oriented RCA in operational wireless systems.

title: Joint Channel and CFO Estimation From Beam-Swept Synchronization Signal Under Strong Inter-Cell Interference.
abstract: Complete awareness of the wireless environment, crucial for future intelligent networks, requires sensing all transmitted signals, not just the strongest. A fundamental barrier is estimating the target signal when it is buried under strong co-channel interference from other transmitters, a failure of which renders the signal unusable. This work proposes a maximum likelihood (ML)-based cross-preamble estimation framework that exploits carrier frequency offset (CFO) constancy across beam-swept synchronization signal (SS), coherently aggregating information across multiple observations to reinforce the desired signal against overwhelming interference. Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) analysis and simulation demonstrate reliable estimation even when the signal is over a thousand times weaker than the interference. A low-altitude radio-map case study further verifies the framework’s practical effectiveness.

title: RIS-Assisted Survivable Backhaul Recovery in Small-Cell Systems.
abstract: The increasing densification of small-cell networks substantially expands cable-based backhaul infrastructure, creating heightened vulnerability to cable link failures. This paper proposes a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted backup framework that exploits a key insight: during backhaul cable failures, base station (BS) radio components remain functional, enabling wireless backhaul traffic redistribution. Our framework maintains network connectivity by redistributing disconnected BS backhaul traffic to neighboring BSs through RIS-assisted wireless links. To maximize survivability across varying traffic conditions, we formulate a joint optimization problem that maximizes total resolvable backhaul traffic by jointly deciding BS selection, RIS phase shifts, and precoding vectors. The inherent non-convexity arising from coupling and quadratic fractional term is addressed through an alternating optimization algorithm that iteratively solves tractable convex subproblems via quadratic transformation. Comprehensive numerical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed RIS-enhanced framework significantly improves survivability from 58% to 72% under challenging high-intensity hotspot traffic conditions. Moreover, RIS provides the greatest gains for antenna-constrained systems by extending coverage to access more spare capacity of the distant BSs as well as enhancing the signal strength. Consequently, high survivability is achieved even with only two antennas per BS under moderate traffic intensity.

title: Secure Cell-free ISAC Systems with Limited Fronthaul Capacity: Centralized versus Distributed Processing.
abstract: This paper investigates secure cell-free integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems with limited-capacity fronthaul. To address the multi-static sensing challenges under fronthaul constraints, two processing architectures, namely centralized and distributed, are proposed and analyzed. For both architectures, the maximum a-posteriori ratio test (MAPRT) detection statistics and their distributions are derived, where the sensing signals are also served as artificial noise (AN) for interfering with potential eavesdroppers. In the centralized case, the central processing unit (CPU) jointly designs beamforming to maximize the detection probability under security constraints; however, since the sensing echoes must be transmitted to CPU via fronthaul links, the performance is limited by the fronthaul capacity. In contrast, the distributed approach performs local target detection and secure beamforming design at each AP, which avoids fronthaul limitations. Simulation results reveal the respective operating regions of the centralized and distributed approaches, providing insights into future design of secure cell-free ISAC systems under fronthaul limitations.

title: Learnware-Enabled Deployment for Deep Learning-based CSI Feedback.
abstract: Channel state information (CSI) feedback is essential for realizing high-capacity and spectral-efficiency goals of future 6G systems, yet existing deep learning solutions face a trade-off between model generalization and scene-specific performance. Large neural networks generalize well but incur high computational and tuning costs, whereas small models excel in particular environments but require repetitive end-to-end training for each base station (BS). To address these challenges, we introduce a model repository-based deployment framework in which a centralized AI data center maintains a catalog of scene-specific CSI models. The repository is enhanced with a Learnware-based framework, where each model is associated with a specification including a semantic part (network architecture parameters) and a statistical part (codebook-fingerprint embeddings of training-data distributions). A BS submits only its local statistical specifications to retrieve the most relevant pretrained model, preserving data privacy and drastically reducing retrieval latency and communication overhead. We further develop a data-driven search strategy that matches codebook fingerprints to model performance. In simulations, our scheme yields 19%–24% performance improvements over benchmarks while reducing local fine-tuning by 500 samples and 50 epochs. This approach minimizes redundant training, maximizes model reuse, and supports rapid, privacy-preserving deployment of CSI feedback models.

title: PUVC: A Novel Position-based VANET Caching Framework Built Upon UAVs Association.
abstract: The rapid adoption of vehicular communication technologies has driven the development of the Vehicular Ad Hoc Network (VANET), which supports applications such as congestion control and resource allocation and serves as a critical component of automotive cyber-physical and industrial communication networks. Despite enhanced On- Board Units (OBUs), the VANET faces challenges from limited communication range, storage capacity, and highly dynamic topology, which collectively degrade Quality of Service (QoS) and increase network link load. In-network caching improves QoS by distributing content closer to vehicles. Meanwhile, recent advancements have refined VANET caching methodologies by enhancing traditional strategies, such as probabilistic caching, and integrating innovative communication frameworks, including Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and Named Data Networking (NDN). However, existing schemes often suffer from limited coverage and redundant rebroadcasts. To address these challenges, this paper proposes PUVC, a position-based UAV-assisted VANET caching framework in which a Central UAV disseminates popular content and Sub-UAVs maintain backups based on vehicle location and received signal strength. Road-constrained UAV mobility further improves transmission efficiency and mitigates topology-induced QoS degradation. Simulations in urban and highway scenarios show that PUVC reduces link load by over 74%, increases local satisfaction by more than 77%, and decreases data retrieval latency by 55%, demonstrating its effectiveness for QoS-aware industrial vehicular communication systems.

title: UAV-RIS-Assisted Secure Space-Time Interference Management for SAGINs.
abstract: In space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGIN), the interference generated in the communication process poses a significant challenge to both information security and communication reliability. To address these issues, we first introduce the unmanned aerial vehicle carrying the reflecting intelligent surface (UAV-RIS) to enhance network performance. Then, a UAV-RIS-assisted secure space-time interference management scheme (SSTIM) is proposed for maximizing system capacity while ensuring that user information remains secure. In the proposed scheme, low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite actively participates in the space-time coding design under strict security constraints, while the UAV-RIS provides flexible signal reflection and interference shaping, enabling secure transmission and effective suppression of multi-domain interference. The simulation results show that the UAV-RIS-SSTIM scheme improves network capacity, safeguards information, and enhances communication reliability.

title: Efficient Joint Resource Allocation for Wireless Powered ISAC with Target Localization.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables 6G networks to share radio resources for sensing and data transmission. For energy-limited ISAC systems, wireless power transfer (WPT) can be integrated as a power supply, which also introduces tradeoffs among harvested energy, communication throughput, and sensing accuracy. Motivated by this, we study a wireless powered multi-user ISAC system for multi-target localization, where a base station (BS) broadcasts a WPT signal for energy harvesting and users then transmit data with the harvested energy to the BS sequentially. Meanwhile, both the WPT signal and the users’ data signals are exploited for target localization at the BS. By imposing Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) constraints to guarantee localization accuracy, we formulate a minimum user throughput maximization problem that jointly optimizes the WPT duration, per-user transmission durations, and user transmit powers. To address the variable coupling and inherent nonconvexity of the problem, we derive a more tractable reformulation via variable substitutions and logarithmic objective transformations. Since the CRB constraints remain nonconvex, we further develop a successive convex approximation (SCA)-based iterative algorithm and finally obtain an efficient suboptimal solution. Numerical results demonstrate the algorithm convergence and significant performance gains of the proposed scheme over benchmark schemes, highlighting the importance of joint resource allocation design for wireless powered ISAC systems.

title: Joint Compression and Resource Allocation for Semantic Communication Based Image Transmission.
abstract: In industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments, high-resolution images captured by cameras are frequently transmitted to edge servers for analysis. However, constrained wireless bandwidth and real-time requirements pose challenges for raw image delivery. To address this, we propose a three-stage framework comprising local compression, wireless transmission, and edge reconstruction. Specifically, each device locally compresses the image data using lightweight neural networks and then transmits the compressed data to the edge server for semantic reconstruction. A joint compression and resource allocation problem is formulated to minimize the total energy consumption of devices, subject to the constraints of bandwidth, delay tolerance, computing and power capacities, and reconstruction quality. An alternating optimization algorithm is developed for effectively solving the formulated mixed-integer non-convex problem. The simulation results demonstrate our proposed scheme can reduce total energy consumption by up to 17.1% compared to the benchmarks, while maintaining recovery fidelity and satisfying delay requirements.

title: Latency-aware Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning for Semantic Communications.
abstract: Semantic communication promises task-aligned transmission but must reconcile semantic fidelity with stringent latency guarantees in immersive and safety-critical services. This paper introduces a time-constrained human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning (TC-HITL-RL) framework that embeds human feedback, semantic utility, and latency control within a semantic-aware Open radio access network (RAN) architecture. We formulate semantic adaptation driven by human feedback as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) whose state captures semantic quality, human preferences, queue slack, and channel dynamics, and solve it via a primal–dual proximal policy optimization algorithm with action shielding and latency-aware reward shaping. The resulting policy preserves PPO-level semantic rewards while tightening the variability of both air-interface and near-real-time RAN intelligent controller processing budgets. Simulations over point-to-multipoint links with heterogeneous deadlines show that TC-HITL-RL consistently meets per-user timing constraints, outperforms baseline schedulers in reward, and stabilizes resource consumption, providing a practical blueprint for latency-aware semantic adaptation.

title: Pareto-Optimal Sampling and Resource Allocation for Timely Communication in Shared-Spectrum Low-Altitude Networks.
abstract: Guaranteeing stringent data freshness for low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in shared spectrum forces a critical trade-off between two operational costs: the UAV’s own energy consumption and the occupation of terrestrial channel resources. The core challenge is to satisfy the aerial data freshness while finding a Pareto-optimal balance between these costs. Leveraging predictive channel models and predictive UAV trajectories, we formulate a bi-objective Pareto optimization problem over a long-term planning horizon to jointly optimize the sampling timing for aerial traffic and the power and spectrum allocation for fair coexistence. However, the problem’s non-convex, mixed-integer nature renders classical methods incapable of fully characterizing the complete Pareto frontier. Notably, we show monotonicity properties of the frontier, building on which we transform the bi-objective problem into several single-objective problems. We then propose a new graph-based algorithm and prove that it can find the complete set of Pareto optima with low complexity, linear in the horizon and near-quadratic in the resource block (RB) budget. Numerical comparisons show that our approach meets the stringent timeliness requirement and achieves a six-fold reduction in RB utilization or a 6 dB energy saving compared to benchmarks.

title: Non-Cooperative Interference Cancellation with Auxiliary Antennas: Analysis and Experiments.
abstract: Amidst the surge in wireless device usage, the intrinsic vulnerability of wireless channels has become a critical concern, particularly due to the escalating issue of non-cooperative interference—whether intentional or unintentional—which severely compromises channel security by degrading spectral efficiency, disrupting legitimate communications, and undermining the reliability of wireless networks. This paper proposes a novel non-cooperative interference cancellation (NCIC) method that utilizes auxiliary antennas. Unlike other auxiliary antenna-assisted interference cancellation (AAAIC) techniques, the proposed method does not rely on spatial domain information to extract the target signal and suppress interference. Instead, it exploits the uncorrelation between the transmitted data of interference and target sources, as well as the inactive period of the target signal. The optimal weight vector is determined by applying the maximum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (MSINR) criterion. Simulation and experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a SINR gain (SG) of about 15dB, validating its feasibility and effectiveness in restoring communication integrity under hostile or uncoordinated interference.

title: MCKD: A Modality Compression Knowledge Distillation Model for Efficient Beam Prediction in V2X Communications.
abstract: Beam prediction plays a pivotal role in enabling reliable and low latency communication for Vehicle-to-Everything systems. It typically requires high capacity models trained on multimodal data to achieve accurate and robust performance. However, roadside units face strict computational limits and often have access to only a single sensing modality. These constraints hinder the deployment of heavy multimodal fusion models. To address these challenges, we propose MCKD, a modality compression knowledge distillation model that transfers multimodal representations to a single student model for efficient beam prediction. Specifically, MCKD maintains performance comparable to multimodal models while significantly reducing parameter complexity. Extensive experiments across various weather conditions demonstrate that MCKD achieves high accuracy and adapts robustly to environmental variations.

title: Energy Efficient Sensing-Communication-Computation Resource Allocation in RSMA-Assisted Vehicular Networks.
abstract: In the integration of sensing, communication, and computation (ISCC) vehicular networks, the collection, transmission and processing of diverse application data lead to significant energy consumption and resource conflict for autonomous vehicles. However, existing resource allocation works on energy efficiency optimization often overlook the time dependencies and the coupled resource constraints among wireless sensing, communication, and computation tasks. Moreover, although rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) has been investigated to assist data transmission in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, the joint optimization of RSMA-assisted vehicleto-vehicle (V2V) communication and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) computation offloading in the multi-vehicle ISCC scenario remains unexplored. To address these challenges, this paper investigates a time-division (TD) ISCC energy efficiency maximization problem jointly considering sensing, RSMA-assisted transmission, and data processing. An iterative energy efficiency maximization algorithm based on the Dinkelbach and successive convex approximation (SCA) methods is proposed. Numerical results illustrate that the proposed algorithm achieves higher energy efficiency compared to existing ISCC benchmarks, and the advantage of RSMA in enhancing energy efficiency for data transmission is also demonstrated.

title: MMSense: Adapting Vision-based Foundation Model for Multi-task Multi-modal Wireless Sensing.
abstract: Large AI models have been widely adopted in wireless communications for channel modeling, beamforming, and resource optimization. However, most existing efforts remain limited to single-modality inputs and channel-specific objec- tives, overlooking the broader potential of large foundation models for unified wireless sensing. To bridge this gap, we propose MMSense, a multi-modal, multi-task foundation model that jointly addresses channel-centric, environment-aware, and human-centered sensing. Our framework integrates image, radar, LiDAR, and textual data by transforming them into vision- compatible representations, enabling effective cross-modal align- ment within a unified feature space. A modality gating mecha- nism adaptively fuses these representations, while a vision-based large language model backbone enables unified feature align- ment and instruction-driven task adaptation. Furthermore, task- specific sequential attention and uncertainty-based loss weighting mechanisms enhance cross-task generalization. Experiments on real wireless scenario datasets show that our approach outper- forms both task-specific and large-model baselines, confirming its strong generalization across heterogeneous sensing tasks.

title: Measurement-Uncertainty-Aware Control for ISAC-Enabled UAV Tracking.
abstract: This paper studies joint sensing and control for trajectory tracking of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) using an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) base station (BS) under explicit measurement uncertainty. Departing from the common practice of designing sensing/communication and control in isolation, we develop a measurement-uncertainty–aware control (MUAC) framework grounded in model predictive control (MPC) that (i) explicitly ties controller design to state-estimation accuracy, (ii) incorporates the posterior Cramér–Rao bound (PCRB) into the control objective to penalize future estimation error, and (iii) enforces communication-rate constraints for reliable control signaling. The resulting nonconvex cost function is addressed via a successive convexification program (SCP) with trust-region backtracking. Simulations with two UAVs demonstrate 3D tracking accuracy over horizons and improvements around high-curvature segment over classical model predictive control (MPC) that ignores measurement uncertainty.

title: A Low-Feedback-Overhead Uplink-Downlink Cooperative Channel Extrapolation Scheme.
abstract: In time division duplexing (TDD) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, acquiring channel state information (CSI) has always been a challenging and critical issue. User Equipments (UEs) typically transmit low-power uplink (UL) pilots only on a narrow band, making it extremely difficult to accurately extrapolate the wideband channel from these constrained UL observations. Against this backdrop, exploiting downlink (DL) observation information to aid uplink channel inference has emerged as a promising research direction. However, effectively exploiting DL observation information remains challenging due to several practical impairments, including prohibitively high feedback overhead, the limited number of DL observations (pilot symbols), and inconsistencies between UL and DL channel parameters (such as delay offset). To overcome this challenge, this paper proposes a low-feedback-overhead UL-DL Cooperative Channel Extrapolation (UD-CCE) scheme. The scheme leverages limited UE resources: the UE processes few downlink observations via smooth multiple signal classification (Smooth MUSIC) to extract and feed back only low-dimensional delay information, drastically reducing overhead. At the Base Station (BS), a robust parameter refinement mechanism is employed. First, the BS cooperatively estimates and compensates for the UL-DL delay offset. Second, it uses complementary subspace projection to recover paths missed by the UE’s limited observations. Accurate delay estimates are achieved at the BS with only a very small amount of feedback from the user, enabling efficient wideband channel reconstruction. Simulations show the UD-CCE scheme significantly outperforms baselines, offering a practical and efficient solution for TDD CSI acquisition with substantial accuracy gains.

title: Dual-Offset Chirp-Based Random Access Preamble Design and Detection for AFDM-Enabled LEO Satellite Communication Systems.
abstract: This paper focuses on the affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM)-enabled low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication, which can not only achieve seamless global coverage but also guarantee reliable multi-user access in high-mobility scenarios. On this basis, we put forward a discrete affine Fourier transform (DAFT)-domain random access preamble design scheme based on a dual-offset chirp, which concatenates asymmetric frequency-shifted chirps to significantly enlarge the available preamble pool. In particular, we reveal that, in the presence of timing offsets, the magnitude spectrum of the received preamble after matched filtering exhibits equidistant and oppositely directed peak shifts, presenting a predictable signature that enables accurate multi-user timing advance (TA) estimation. Building on this property, we further develop a segmented correlation and index reorganization-aided orthogonal matching pursuit (SCIR-OMP) algorithm for joint user identification and TA estimation. Theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves superior multi-user detection performance compared with state-of-the-art ones.

title: Performance Analysis of Self-Interference Cancellation for Transmit Beamforming with Quantization Errors in FD Phased Array Systems.
abstract: When transmit beamforming (TxBF) is implemented for self-interference (SI) cancellation (SIC) in simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) phased array systems, the finite-resolution attenuators and phase shifters (FRAP) will introduce quantization errors, leading to a loss in SIC capability and beam gain. In this paper, we build an orthogonal error perturbation model to demonstrate the effects of quantization errors. Further, we derive the closed-form expression of the performance degradation bounds for the TxBF with the FRAP, in terms of the equivalent isotropically radiated power (EIRP), the SI power and the isolation. In addition, an angle search algorithm is proposed to improve the isolation with the FRAP. Theoretical and test results results validate the effectiveness and accuracy of the derived bounds and show that the isolation with the FRAP under the proposed angle search algorithm is close to that with the ideal infinite-resolution attenuators and phase shifters.

title: Dynamic Cross-Domain Network Slicing for Teleoperation: A Real-World Proof-of-Concept.
abstract: Teleoperation is increasingly used to complement Level-4 autonomous driving, but it depends on strict network requirements i.e., latency below 5 ms, uplink throughput exceeding 25 Mbps, and reliability of 99.999%. To meet such requirements Network Slicing has emerged as a key paradigm to allocate and isolate network resources. However, in current 5G Standalone (5G SA)networks, Network Slicing faces fragmented orchestration. 3GPP mechanisms govern the 5G Core (5GC), O-RAN manages Radio Access Network (RAN) resources, while Transport Network (TN) operates separately, limiting end-to-end Quality of Service (QoS) guarantees.In this work, we propose a Cross-Domain Controller (CDC) that establishes synergy between network domains i.e., 5GC, TN, and RAN, through policy-driven coordination. The CDC implements a closed-loop, threshold-based mechanism that monitors slice Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and triggers runtime network resource reconfigurations when the Teleoperation slice requires additional capacity to meet its QoS targets. Experimental validation on a real-world 5G SA testbed demonstrates that the CDC maintains strict slice isolation while dynamically expanding allocated network resources.

title: Security Assessment of Deep Learning-Based RF Fingerprinting for Wireless IoT Standards.
abstract: Radio-frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) exploits device-specific hardware impairments for authentication, yet most prior studies focus on a single protocol, limiting cross-protocol understanding. This paper presents a preamble-based comparative study of WiFi, LoRa, and Bluetooth on a unified USRP X310 software-defined radio (SDR) platform using three neural models. To balance fairness and realism, we introduce two evaluation schemes: one with unified length and sampling, and another with native protocol parameters. Results show that WiFi achieves the highest separability, LoRa offers superior robustness under low SNR, and Bluetooth remains constrained by its short preamble. These findings establish a re-producible fair-comparison baseline and a realistic supplement, highlighting the decisive role of preamble design in fingerprint robustness and informing scalable, multi-protocol authentication in the 2.4 GHz band.

title: UrMap: UAV-assisted Spatio-Temporal Radio Mapping using Sparse Cellular Samples.
abstract: The rapid development of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and wireless communication technologies has fueled the rise of the low-altitude economy, supporting applications such as logistics delivery, precision agriculture, and disaster response. Reliable UAV communication and navigation rely on accurate radio maps that characterize the spatial distribution of signal strength and channel quality. However, constructing such radio maps is challenging, as extensive data collection in complex 3D environments is constrained by flight regulations and energy limits. In addition, pre-constructed radio maps may degrade over time due to environmental dynamics. To address these challenges, this work presents UrMap, a radio map estimation system based on multi-task spatio-temporal modeling. In UrMap, a Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) model is developed to jointly model spatial and temporal correlations, enabling the generation of complete radio maps that remain robust under time-varying environmental conditions. Furthermore, the proposed GPR model generates diverse connectivity maps by exploiting their cross-modality correlations, thereby providing a comprehensive understanding of the radio environment. Extensive experiments show that UrMap outperforms baseline methods, achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.1 dB in the best case and maintaining 4.2 dB even in the worst case for radio map estimation.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Wireless CSI Feedback.
abstract: Channel state information (CSI) feedback is critical for high-performance transmission in modern wireless systems, but the massive dimensionality of CSI creates prohibitive feedback overhead. Existing deep learning-based methods address this by treating CSI as an image for compression. Such a data-driven "black-box" approach is agnostic to the underlying physical structure, fundamentally limiting its efficiency and interpretability. To address this issue, we propose PINN-CFnet, a Physics-Informed Neural Network for CSI Feedback that departs from the vision-inspired paradigm. By embedding a differentiable signal propagation model into the network architecture, we reframe the high-dimensional CSI "image" reconstruction task into a low-dimensional physical parameter estimation problem. PINN-CFnet features a multi-layer convolutional encoder for multi-path feature extraction, and a hetero-architecture decoder tailored to recover distinct physical parameters of each path (e.g., gain, angle). Moreover, a two-step training strategy is proposed to guide and fine-tune the network’s physical model learning process. Experiments show that PINN-CFnet outperforms the state-of-the-art method, while requiring only 9.9% of its computational complexity.

title: Environment Map-Assisted Positioning Using a Single Receiver in Mixed LoS/NLoS Environments.
abstract: Positioning in complex propagation environments remains a fundamental yet challenging problem, particularly when only a single receiver (Rx) is available. This paper re-visits received signal strength (RSS)-based localization in mixed line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) environments, leveraging prior knowledge of the physical environment map. Compared to conventional methods that treat NLoS disturbances as non-Gaussian random variables, we explicitly model NLoS RSS measurements through first-order reflection paths, thereby providing a more physically grounded characterization of NLoS propagation. Based on this model, a closed-form solution is then developed to accurately estimate the target position. Simulation results reveal that NLoS measurements contain additional useful information that can be exploited to improve localization accuracy, while the proposed scheme can approach the optimal performance given by the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB).

title: Randomized Scheduling for PAoI Violation Guarantees in Periodic Multi-Source Systems.
abstract: We study peak Age of Information (PAoI) violation guarantee in a periodic multi-source status update system. The system is served by a shared base station, which requires scheduling. Our main contribution is a randomized scheduling framework that targets heterogeneous PAoI requirements. To that end, we derive numerically trackable upper bounds on the PAoI violation probability in two traffic regimes (long and short period) by leveraging the multivariate noncentral hypergeometric Wallenius distribution and the geometric distribution, respectively. Guided by these bounds, we design two low-complexity randomized scheduling schemes that meet diverse PAoI violation probability targets without the traffic assumption. Simulations validate the bounds and demonstrate feasible operation across a wide range of configurations.

title: Optimal input distribution of M-PAM over IM-DD optical channel with non-linear capacitive LED.
abstract: In channels with a wide available bandwidth, M-ary pulse amplitude modulation (M-PAM) with a small number of signal levels is a popular modulation method. The capacity of such optical channels has been investigated before as a function of the energy per bit and a limitation in average or peak optical power. However, in practice, the transmit energy consumption can be a complicated function of the signal waveform. In this work, we study a channel in which, firstly, the power associated with radiating a signal level is not a quadratic function of the signal amplitude, because the emitter may not act as a linear ohmic resistor. Secondly, level transitions consume additional power, for instance, because an intrinsic capacitance in the emitter diode junction needs to be charged up quickly. Light-emitting diodes (LED)s or lasers used in optical wireless communications are prime examples. We optimize their source entropy for a limited power budget. This not only leads to asymmetric probabilities for signal levels, as known from previous theory, but also introduces a dependency on previous signal probabilities. For example, our results show that in an energy-constrained system that employs on-off keying (OOK), the conditional probability of transmitting a logical 1 following a logical 0 should be lower than that of transmitting a second 1 after an initial 1.

title: Knowledge-Aware ISAC for UAV Swarms: Two-Timescale Co-Design of Sensing Reliability, Latency, and Energy.
abstract: This paper presents DKA-ISAC, a knowledge-driven ISAC co-design for UAV swarms operating under tight latency, energy, and reliability constraints. A dynamic knowledge graph and a Knowledge-aware Sensing Confidence (KC) metric jointly couple sensing geometry, link reliability, and knowledge quality into a system-optimizable signal. DKA-ISAC adopts a dual-timescale architecture: a slow loop for knowledge-guided task/trajectory planning with a (1 − 1/e) approximation guarantee, and a fast loop using Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty with the classical O(1/V) optimality–O(V ) backlog trade-off. Large-scale simulations and a 125-node hardware-in-the-loop testbed show consistent gains: mean KC ≈ 0.751, latency 28.36 ms at 124.89Mbps, energy 14.68J/s, and Service Level Agreement (SLA) violations 3.2% (vs. 7.4–14.4%). Knowledge priors warm-start optimization and shrink feasible sets, cutting convergence to 15.0s. DKA-ISAC offers a unified, scalable, engineering-ready solution for high-confidence sensing and stable communications.

title: Sensor Data Transmission Optimization in Infrastructure-Assisted Cooperative Perception.
abstract: The rapid advancement of connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) has improved intelligent transportation systems, but managing real-time data transmissions among vehicles and roadside infrastructures under stringent latency and bandwidth constraints remains challenging. This paper proposes two scheduling algorithms: an offline data transmission scheduling (DTS) algorithm using Integer Linear Programming (ILP) for stable conditions, and an online data transmission scheduling (O-DTS) algorithm employing a heuristic approach for dynamic environments. Evaluations against broadcast and best-effort strategies show that DTS and O-DTS achieve superior scalability and lower latency, enhancing CAV network efficiency while balancing computational and communication costs.

title: Cross-Band Channel Impulse Response Prediction: Leveraging 3.5 GHz Channels for Upper Mid-Band.
abstract: Accurate cross-band channel prediction is essential for 6G networks, particularly in the upper mid-band (FR3, 7-24 GHz), where penetration loss and blockage are severe. Although ray tracing (RT) provides high-fidelity modeling, it remains computationally intensive, and high-frequency data acquisition is costly. To address these challenges, we propose CIR-UNext, a deep learning framework designed to predict 7 GHz channel impulse responses (CIRs) by leveraging abundant 3.5 GHz CIRs. The framework integrates an RT-based dataset pipeline with attention U-Net (AU-Net) variants for gain and phase prediction. The proposed AU-Net-Aux model achieves a median gain error of 0.58 dB and a phase prediction error of 0.27 rad on unseen complex environments. Furthermore, we extend CIR-UNext into a foundation model, Channel2ComMap, for throughput prediction in MIMO-OFDM systems, demonstrating superior performance compared with existing approaches. Overall, CIR-UNext provides an efficient and scalable solution for cross-band prediction, enabling applications such as localization, beam management, digital twins, and intelligent resource allocation in 6G networks.

title: MADRL-Based Edge Offloading and Resource Allocation for Vehicular LLM Inference.
abstract: With the powerful capabilities of large language models (LLMs) poised to empower vehicular networking, resource-limited vehicles struggle to meet low-latency inference requirements on-board, motivating collaborative inference via edge offloading. This paper proposes a cooperative offloading and resource allocation framework for vehicular edge computing, where LLM inference is partitioned between resource-limited vehicles and nearby MEC servers and transmitted via RSMA-based uplink. Specifically, a split-point traversal method with delay estimation is developed for fast hierarchical partitioning of LLM inference tasks, and RSMA is integrated to reduce uplink latency under heavy traffic and fast time-varying channels. In addition, a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework with a server-side shared critic and vehicle-side distributed actors is designed to jointly optimize task offloading and resource allocation under heterogeneous constraints. Simulation results show that the proposed approach significantly outperforms the baseline schemes in terms of system reward, which is defined as a weighted sum of task latency and energy consumption with an additional timeout penalty, and the task timeout rate.

title: Lossless-SR: Towards Non-Disruptive Source Routing for Topology-Varying LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: By embedding path information within packet headers, Source Routing (SR) allows source nodes to flexibly customize traffic paths while exempting forwarding nodes from complex route lookups. However, applying SR to Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks faces packet loss issues due to high topological dynamics. Specifically, at the instant of a topology handover, inflight packets carry routes calculated from the previous snapshot, which may become invalid in the current topology, triggering transient packet loss. Furthermore, storing SR information for every snapshot lacks scalability as constellation sizes increase.To address these issues, this paper proposes Lossless-SR, a reliable and memory-efficient SR framework that ensures seamless end-to-end connectivity during topology handovers. By leveraging the multi-path characteristics of LEO satellite topologies, Lossless-SR designates SR paths as stable backup paths that span adjacent snapshots during handovers, thereby reducing transient packet loss to zero. Concurrently, a routing table compression framework is introduced to eliminate redundant snapshots containing identical or potentially equivalent paths, reducing the on-board memory footprint by 95.7% to 96.8%. Experimental results demonstrate that Lossless-SR achieves high reliability and resource efficiency in dynamic LEO environments.

title: Towards a Theoretical Framework for Robust Node Deployment in Cooperative ISAC Networks.
abstract: This paper investigates node deployment strategies for robust multi-node cooperative localization. First, we establish a multi-node localization system, in which the target is randomly distributed in a two-dimensional area. By discretizing the coverage area into uniform grids, we reveal a key insight: the worst-case localization error is dominated by the maximum distance-weighted steering vector correlation among all grid pairs. Based on this insight, we propose a deployment optimization framework that jointly optimizes node positions and array orientations to minimize the maximum weighted steering vector correlation, thereby enhancing the worst-case localization robustness of the network. A genetic algorithm (GA) is subsequently developed to solve this non-convex optimization problem. Extensive simulations based on multiple signal classification (MUSIC) and neural network (NN)-based localization methods validate that the proposed approach significantly improves the localization robustness, demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Unleashing Uplink Potential: AI-Driven Channel Selectivity Matching via Compressed Channel State Information.
abstract: The uplink (UL) throughput stands as a critical KPI for wireless communication network. Various technologies have emerged to improve the UL throughput, such as high-order modulation and high-layer transmission. Additionally, sub-band precoding has gained recognition as a crucial enabling technology for UL Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) transmission due to its potential to achieve substantial throughput gains. This work introduces an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven UL high-resolution precoding scheme featured by neural network-powered engine. Our aim is to leverage the performance benefits of sub-band precoding and non-codebook precoding while minimizing the signaling overhead associated with UL precoding control. Furthermore, the proposed precoding scheme addresses the practical implementation challenge, power balancing across antenna ports. The link-level simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves 2dB and 5dB SNR gains at 70% of maximum throughput over the legacy schemes with acceptable control overhead in 4Tx and 8Tx cases, respectively. Field-measurement-based evaluation further proves the effectiveness of proposed scheme

title: Channel Estimation using 5G Sounding Reference Signals: A Delay-Doppler Domain Approach.
abstract: Delay-Doppler multicarrier modulation (DDMC) techniques have been among the central topics of research for high-Doppler channels. However, a complete transition to DDMC-based waveforms is not yet practically feasible. This is because 5G NR based waveforms, orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) and discrete Fourier transform-spread OFDM (DFT-s-OFDM), remain as the modulation schemes for the sixth-generation radio (6GR). Hence, in this paper, we demonstrate how we can still benefit from DD-domain processing in high-mobility scenarios using 5G NR sounding reference signals (SRSs). By considering a DFT-s-OFDM receiver, we transform each received OFDM symbol into the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, where the channel is then estimated. With this approach, we estimate the DD channel parameters, allowing us to predict the aged channel over OFDM symbols without pilots. To improve channel prediction, we propose a linear joint channel estimation and equalization technique, where we use the detected data in each OFDM symbol to sequentially update our channel estimates. Our simulation results show that the proposed technique significantly outperforms the conventional frequency-domain estimation technique in terms of bit error rate (BER) and normalized mean squared error (NMSE). Furthermore, we show that using only two slots with SRS for initial channel estimation, our method supports pilot-free detection for more than 25 subsequent OFDM symbols.

title: Uplink Performance of Fluid Antenna-Aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO With Imperfect CSI.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the uplink spectral efficiency (SE) of FA-aided cell-free massive MIMO (FA-CF) systems with imperfect channel state information (CSI). We design a minimum mean-square error (MMSE)-based channel estimation scheme to estimate the aggregated channels between access points (APs) and user equipments (UEs). We further derive achievable SE expressions for both large-scale fading decoding (LSFD) and equal-gain decoding processing (EGDP) schemes. Moreover, we formulate a mean-square error (MSE) minimization problem based on the signal transmission model. To solve this problem, we develop an efficient algorithm that combines orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) with binary search to jointly optimize FA positions and the combining matrix. Numerical results demonstrate that FA-CF significantly outperforms conventional cell-free systems in terms of SE, even with a limited number of antennas, and maintains strong robustness under imperfect CSI or heavy UE loads by adaptively adjusting antenna positions.

title: Graph Neural Network Based Federated Wideband Spectrum Sensing with Sub-Nyquist Sampling.
abstract: Wideband spectrum sensing (WSS) is crucial in cognitive radio, enabling efficient utilization of idle licensed spectrum bands. However, Nyquist-rate sampling over a wide frequency range incurs prohibitive hardware cost, while sub-Nyquist sampling leads to incomplete and noisy observations that severely degrade sensing performance, especially for non-cooperative schemes. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Graph Neural Network-based federated WSS scheme (GNN-FWSS) with sub-Nyquist sampling. By exploiting the inherent relationships between the sampling patterns and the spatial diversity among sensing nodes, the proposed approach significantly enhances detection reliability without requiring strict sparsity in spectrum occupancy. Simulation results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional non-cooperative and cooperative schemes across a wide range of signal-to-noise ratios and spectrum occupancy ratios, as evaluated by label-wise accuracy and the receiver operating characteristic(ROC) curve.

title: Capacity of Cooperative Networks with Local Traffic Patterns.
abstract: Revealing the asymptotic relationship between the number of cooperative relays and network capacity is crucial for ensuring capacity scalability and enhancing the robustness of network topology, especially when the network experiences frequent node or link failures. Towards this objective, we first prove that the upper bound of network capacity is $O\left( {\frac{m}{n}} \right)$1only when the number of relay nodes satisfies $\frac{c}{l}\sqrt[3]{{\frac{{n{V^2}}}{{\log n}}}} < m \leq \frac{n}{{\log n}}$, where n is the number of nodes, V is the network volume and $\bar l$ is the average path length. To capture the spatial locality of traffic patterns, furthermore, we employ the power-law distance distribution. Based on this model, we have identified the conditions for ensuring that network capacity grows linearly with the number of nodes: for dense networks (V = Θ(1)), α ≤ −2, and for extended networks (V = Θ(n)), α < − 1. α is the traffic spreading exponent, which serves as a key metric to measure the spatial locality of traffic patterns. These results reveal that network capacity is scalable only when the traffic spreading exponent is below a certain threshold.

title: Capacity Limits of LEO Satellite Constellations with Link Failures.
abstract: In this study, we model the LEO satellite constellation with link failures as the -random regular graph, where (≥ 3) is the number of antennas per satellite, i.e, each satellite can establish at most inter-satellite links (ISLs). It is found that the critical link failure probability at which the constellation structure connectivity collapses is pc(Δ) = Δ - 2/Δ - 1. We show that the capacity upper bound is proportional to Δ γ (p)L(α,D) at p < pc(Δ).L(α,D) is the average hop distance without link failures under traffic decay factor α ∈ (0,1). γ(p) < ∞ is the hop stretch factor measuring the extra hops to overcome link failures. D is the diameter of constellations. To achieve this bound, furthermore, we propose the distributed shortest-hop routing framework based on local link states (DSR-L), which uses prior geometric knowledge of the constellation structure. These results can provide effective guidance for resilience strategies regarding redundant satellites and ISL configurations.

title: Flexible-Sector 6DMA: Joint Sector Rotation and Antenna Allocation Optimization.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cost-effective six-dimensional movable antenna (6DMA)-enhanced base station (BS) architecture, termed the flexible-sector BS, which allows the deployed antennas to flexibly rotate and move along a circular track, thus enabling common sector rotation and flexible antenna allocation across sectors to adapt to the spatial user distribution efficiently. In particular, we focus on the uplink transmission in a single-cell system, where the flexible-sector BS receives independent messages from multiple users. We introduce an angular-domain user distribution model, which captures the users’ spatial clustering or hot-spot distribution effectively. Assuming the zero-forcing (ZF) based receiver applied at the BS to decode the multiuser signals, we derive the average sum rate achievable for the users as a function of the common rotation of sectors and the antenna allocation over sectors. Moreover, we develop a two-step algorithm to jointly optimize the common sector rotation and antenna allocation to maximize the average sum rate of all users. It is shown that the optimal antenna number in each sector linearly increases with the number of users in it. Numerical results also show that the proposed flexible-sector BS outperforms other benchmark schemes, such as the traditional fixed-sector BS as well as the BS with sector rotation or antenna allocation optimization only.

title: Statistically Robust Energy Efficient Transmit Beamforming for Block-Fading URLLC Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the energy efficiency maximization based statistically robust beamforming design for a multiuser ultra reliable and low-latency communication (URLLC) system under block fading channels, where the random channel uncertainty is explicitly taken into account. To tackle the difficult problem, we first obtain a problem reformulation via the sample average approximation (SAA) method. Then, we decouple the beamforming vector of each user into a normalized transmit beamformer and a transmit power, and develop a minorization-maximization (MM)-based algorithm to find an efficient solution. Specifically, by performing a careful investigation, we achieve a closed-form solution to the normalized transmit beamformer and a semi-closed-form solution to the transmit power in each MM iteration. Simulation results validate the superiorities of the proposed solutions compared with the existing benchmarks.

title: Online Adaptive Resource Allocation for Dynamic Stream Processing in Cloud Environments using Deep Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Dynamic stream processing in cloud environments presents unique challenges due to fluctuating data rates, heterogeneous workloads, and constrained resource availability. Traditional static and heuristic-based resource allocation techniques often fail to adapt effectively to these real-time dynamics, leading to suboptimal throughput, excessive latency, and violation of service-level agreements (SLAs). In this paper, we propose a Hierarchical Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (H-MADRL) framework to address these limitations through autonomous, data-driven adaptation. Our system integrates Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agents with Kubernetes orchestration and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for topology-aware scaling decisions. Experiments under simulated and live workloads demonstrate the PPO agent’s ability to maintain stable performance during load surges up to 5,000 events/sec without over-provisioning. Comparative evaluation with heuristic rule-based methods shows that the proposed DRL-based framework improves elasticity and responsiveness by up to 35% lower latency and 22% higher throughput, particularly under bursty or deceptive low-CPU workloads where heuristics fail to detect overload. Furthermore, the DRL agent consistently optimizes resource utilization, reducing unnecessary replica scaling while maintaining SLA targets. The system’s reward function jointly balances throughput maximization, latency reduction, and cost efficiency, providing a robust alternative to traditional methods.

title: On Resilient OCS-based Data Center Networks.
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) models is driving a transition from electrical packet switching to optical circuit switching (OCS) in data center networks (DCNs). The boosting capacity introduces heightened reliability concerns, as frequent device failures can severely disrupt long-running distributed training jobs. In response, this paper introduces a resilient OCS-based DCN scheduling (ROS) scheme that co-designs job scheduling with failure recovery by leveraging redundant device deployment. We propose a novel resilient flow completion time (rFCT) metric, which jointly optimizes performance and failure impact, enabling proactive resilience-aware scheduling. The ROS problem is formulated as a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) model, and a scalable heuristic is developed to efficiently solve it in practical settings. Simulation results demonstrate that ROS significantly reduces overall flow completion time up to 35.5% under switch/link failures.

title: Projecting to Consensus: Communication-Efficient Collaborative Learning Across Heterogeneous Networks.
abstract: Collaborative learning across heterogeneous networks faces a fundamental tension between communication efficiency and architectural flexibility: conventional federated approaches require extensive parameter transmission while enforcing strict homogeneity constraints across client devices. Although knowledge distillation and compression techniques have been proposed to address these limitations individually, existing solutions fail to simultaneously achieve drastic communication reduction and native support for heterogeneous client architectures without compromising learning performance. To overcome this challenge, we introduce Federated Latent Space Consensus (FeLSC), a principled collaborative framework that fundamentally reframes distributed optimization from parameter-space aggregation to semantic-space alignment. Our key insight lies in decoupling local feature extraction from global knowledge fusion: clients maintain their diverse, frozen backbone networks while learning lightweight projection heads that map heterogeneous features into a unified semantic space. Rather than aggregating full model parameters, the server orchestrates collaborative learning through a compact set of learnable semantic anchors that serve as class-wise prototypes, enabling consistent representation alignment across architecturally diverse clients. By transmitting only these minimal projection components, FeLSC achieves over 92.8% communication reduction. Moreover, our approach natively accommodates mixed client architectures (ResNet and MobileNet) and demonstrates enhanced robustness under challenging nonIID settings, establishing a new solution for practical, scalable collaborative learning in heterogeneous environments.

title: Enhancing Collaborative Learning Efficiency via Control-Theoretic Merit Gating in Federated Networks.
abstract: Collaborative learning has emerged as a fundamental paradigm for enabling distributed machine learning across heterogeneous networks, with federated learning serving as a prominent implementation framework. However, most existing federated learning frameworks rely on uniform client participation protocols, mandating all selected participants to transmit model updates regardless of their contribution quality. This rigid approach results in substantial communication overhead and collaborative learning degradation, as low-quality updates from participants with poor data distributions or converged local models consume bandwidth without providing meaningful improvements to the collective intelligence.
