To address these challenges, we propose AdaptiveGate, a novel merit-driven federated learning framework that incorporates control-theoretic mechanisms to intelligently filter client communications based on learning progress. AdaptiveGate employs a client-side merit gating mechanism that evaluates local training progress using normalized loss reduction metrics, ensuring only high-impact updates are transmitted to the server. Furthermore, AdaptiveGate features a server-side proportional controller that dynamically adjusts participation thresholds to maintain target network activity levels, creating a self-regulating system that balances update quality with participant diversity. The framework eliminates the need for manual threshold tuning while maintaining stable network operation across varying client heterogeneity conditions. Extensive experimental results on three datasets demonstrate that AdaptiveGate improves accuracy by up to 2.68%, reduces communication costs by 45.1%, and accelerates convergence by 1.34× compared to standard federated averaging approaches.

title: Bayesian Based Algorithm for Optimizing Space Interferometric Constellation Design.
abstract: Space Very Long Baseline Interferometry (SVLBI) extends VLBI baselines beyond Earth by placing radio telescopes in space. In practice, imaging performance is governed by the constellation geometry, and the induced mapping from orbital parameters to imaging metrics is highly nonlinear and must be evaluated through computationally expensive simulations. However, existing constellation design methods are often tailored to small arrays and rely on heuristics or single-objective formulations; as the number of satellites increases, the search space grows rapidly, making it difficult to efficiently expose trade-offs among competing imaging requirements. This paper develop a Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization (MOBO) framework for SVLBI constellation design to efficiently expose Pareto-optimal trade-offs under expensive function evaluations. First, a compact symmetric Walker-like orbit model is proposed for an Nsat-satellite SVLBI array, under which the constellation design problem is formulated as a constrained multi-objective expensive black-box optimization over (u, v)-coverage Filling Factor (FF), Angular Resolution (AR), and Point-Source Sensitivity (PSS). Second, this paper solve the resulting problem using MOBO with uncertainty-aware surrogates to refine the non-dominated archive toward the attainable Pareto boundary. Observational data from the real source M87*validate stable convergence across random seeds and improved Pareto approximation in the metric space, yielding a representative knee solution for mission configuration.

title: Tomlinson-Harashima Precoding for MU-MISO ODDM-Based Satellite Communications.
abstract: The high mobility in low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite communications results in severe Doppler spreads, for which orthogonal delay-Doppler (DD) division multiplexing (ODDM) modulation has emerged as a promising solution. In this paper, we investigate the Tomlinson-Harashima precoding (THP) scheme for downlink multi-user (MU) multiple-input single-output (MISO) ODDM transmissions. This scheme facilitates simplified equalization, and numerical results confirm its superior performance in mitigating the inter-symbol coupling in the DD domain. In addition, we characterize the achievable sum-rate of the proposed scheme by establishing an information-theoretic equivalent model. In particular, we derive the scaling laws for the achievable rate with respect to the number of antennas and users. Numerical simulations corroborate the accuracy of our theoretical derivation.

title: Perceive to Generate: High-Fidelity Channel Generation via Multimodal Conditional Diffusion.
abstract: Future networks demand high-fidelity yet low-overhead acquisition of channel state information (CSI), posing a significant challenge to conventional pilot-based methods. To address this, we embrace a "perceive-to-generate" paradigm that promotes direct synthesis of wireless channels through a deep understanding of physical environments. While leveraging multiple sensing modalities offers enriched environmental representation, their heterogeneity could also lead to feature contamination that undermines generation quality. Motivated by these challenges, we propose MM-CDiff, a multimodal conditional diffusion framework characterized by two novel mechanisms: an adaptive cross-attention mechanism that fuses encoded environmental features in a selective manner, and a dual-path conditioning mechanism that incorporates both environmental context and temporal embeddings to enable robust channel generation. Experiments on a digital twin dataset of a real-world urban scenario show that MM-CDiff consistently outperforms other generative baselines in terms of generation fidelity, and exhibits superior robustness over pilot-based methods under diverse conditions. Moreover, it achieves favorable tradeoff between accuracy and efficiency, with reduced inference latency and compact model footprint.

title: Orthogonal Space-time Block Codes with Frequency Index Modulation for MIMO-ISAC.
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has emerged as a key enabling technology for future sixth-generation (6G) networks and the low-altitude economy. In a MIMO-ISAC system, classical multiplexing/diversity schemes in communication can achieve high data rates/reliability; however, they suffer from degraded sensing performance due to the lack of orthogonality across transmit antennas. In contrast, traditional orthogonality schemes in radar ensure orthogonality across transmit antennas but are limited by low communication rates. Therefore, this paper proposes a space-time block coding scheme with frequency index modulation (FIM-OSTBC) scheme for MIMO-OFDM ISAC, which utilizes FIM to achieve high spectral efficiency and leverages OSTBC with specifically designed parameters to enhance communication reliability and ensure orthogonality across transmit antennas, thus improving sensing performance. We then provide a theoretical performance analysis of the proposed scheme in communication and sensing. Finally, simulation results validate the superior performance of the proposed scheme in both communication and sensing.

title: A Zero-Key-Exchange OFDM based Positioning Reference Signal Authentication Approach.
abstract: Location Based Services (LBS) constitute a pivotal function in next generation mobile communication networks. Since Release 16, 3GPP has standardized the Positioning Reference Signal (PRS) within the Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) framework. Similar to GNSS, PRS adopts a one-way broadcast mechanism, making it vulnerable to spoofing. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel implicit authentication architecture based on a self-adaptive fingerprint generation approach. By integrating Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) with a deep residual learning framework, the proposed architecture does not require key exchange over the air. At the transmitter, an autoencoder leverages time-frequency texture features of the raw OFDM spectrum to adaptively generate nonlinear artificial noise as "endogenous fingerprints." At the receiver, a Blind Residual Prediction Network accurately predicts and removes these embedded fingerprints, enabling high-fidelity signal restoration and authentication. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves imperceptibility for noncooperative detectors, with recognition rates approaching 50%. Furthermore, it constrains the signal restoration Mean Squared Error (MSE) to the order of 10−5. it provides a forward compatible, zero interaction, and low distortion physical layer security solution for PRS signals.

title: Non-Reciprocal Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Assisted Covert Communications.
abstract: Covert communication is essential for cognitive radio to prevent its dynamic spectrum access from being detected. In this paper, we propose a covert communication scheme aided by a non-reciprocal reconfigurable intelligent surface (NR-RIS) with a legitimate receiver that also emits artificial noise (AN). Non-reciprocity enables directional coordination of the desired signal and AN, mitigating friendly-jammer penalties at the receiver while suppressing the warden. First, we conduct a comprehensive theoretical analysis of the system and derive the closed-form expressions, i.e., the minimum detection error probability (DEP) of the warden and the outage probability of the legitimate receiver. Then, we formulate an optimization problem that aims to maximizing the covert rate at the legitimate receiver while satisfying the covertness constraint. Due to the complexities arising from the non-reciprocal and block-diagonal properties of the NR-RIS and the non-convex optimization problem, we finally propose an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm to optimize the proposed scheme. Specifically, the semidefinite relaxation (SDR) method is employed for the transmit beamformer design, while a Dinkelbach-based SDR method is developed for optimizing the NR-RIS coefficients. Numerical results show that NR-RIS consistently achieves higher covert rates than a diagonal (reciprocal) RIS, highlighting how non-reciprocity benefits covert communications in the proposed scheme.

title: A Framework for Robust Network Traffic Prediction Using Multi-Scale Adversarial Training and an Online Adaptive Mechanism.
abstract: Deep learning-based network traffic predictors are highly vulnerable to small input perturbations, which can induce significant forecast errors. To address this, we propose a defense framework that integrates multi-scale adversarial training with an online adaptive mechanism. First, multiple submodels are trained across a range of perturbation strengths to avoid overfitting to a single attack budget. Then, the online adaptive mechanism dynamically adjusts ensemble weights based on recent predictive performance. Evaluated on real-world network traffic datasets, this framework substantially reduces errors under attack while maintaining competitive accuracy on unperturbed inputs, outperforming other adversarial training methods.

title: Joint Visibility Region Detection and Beam Training for XL-MIMO.
abstract: Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) operating at millimeter-wave frequencies is a key enabling technology for next-generation wireless networks. However, the large array aperture in XL-MIMO introduces two fundamental challenges: near-field propagation and spatial non-stationarity (SnS). While near-field beam training has been extensively studied, the SnS effect characterized by visibility regions (VRs) remains largely unexplored in beam training design. To address this gap, we propose a joint visibility region detection and beam training (JVRDBT) framework in spatially non-stationary XL-MIMO systems. Exploiting a hybrid precoding architecture, the proposed scheme enables multi-beam sweeping to obtain compressive measurements for VR detection and candidate angle set determination, which subsequently guides fine beam search with significantly reduced pilot overhead. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed JVRDBT scheme achieves substantial performance gains over conventional methods, highlighting the importance of jointly designing VR detection and beam training for practical XL-MIMO systems.

title: Clustered Agent-driven Task Scheduling for Resource-Efficient Computing Power Networks.
abstract: Vehicular computing power networks (VCPNs) have emerged as a key infrastructure for processing vehicular data by providing unified and on-demand computing capabilities. However, the fragmentation of computing resources, the imbalance in task scheduling, and the conflict between centralized scheduling bottlenecks and the instability of real-time distributed decision-making pose challenges to efficient data processing and adaptive task scheduling. In this paper, we propose an agent-driven clustered scheduling mechanism that leverages clusters to achieve distributed autonomy and global coordination. A new metric termed task utility is defined to capture the synergy between task execution quality and resource consumption. An optimization problem is formulated as a task utility maximization problem that jointly considers the cluster formation of VCPN nodes and task scheduling decisions. To address the problem, a clustered agent-driven two-stage method is developed. Specifically, a similarity-based adaptive fast clustering algorithm is designed to form VCPN clustered agents without predefined cluster numbers dynamically, enabling efficient organization of heterogeneous VCPN nodes. On this basis, a clustered agent-driven scheduling algorithm is developed, where each cluster acts as an agent to perform task scheduling and collaborative optimization. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method improves total task utility and convergence speed compared with baselines, achieving intelligent and resource-efficient task scheduling.

title: Mobility-Aware Energy-Efficient Design for Wireless Agent Network.
abstract: In energy-constrained wireless agent networks, delivering massive sensed data over fading channels requires a sophisticated balance between physical movement and computational overhead. This work investigates a synergistic approach that integrates source node trajectory, on-device data compression, and transmission power control to enhance overall energy efficiency. We consider a scenario where a mobile agent can actively reduce its distance to a base station (BS) and compress data before transmission. A joint optimization problem is formulated to maximize the effective information rate under a total energy budget and a minimum Quality-of-Service (QoS) requirement. To solve the resulting non-convex problem, we provide a vectorized grid search (VGS) as a global benchmark and develop a penalty-based genetic algorithm (P-GA) as an efficient optimizer. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed joint strategy significantly outperforms conventional mobility-only and compression-only baselines.

title: A Gridless Two-Stage Localization Algorithm and Its Performance Analysis for Near-Field Sources Based on Non-Circular Noise Theory.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a two-stage localization framework, termed two-dimensional off-grid (2DOG) algorithm, for the localization of near-field sources. To relax stringent array-spacing requirements and reduce the complexity of conventional methods, we construct an equivalent virtual far-field signal model (EVFSM) by extracting sub-diagonal entries of the covariance matrix. Based on this model, the 2DOG algorithm achieves efficient two-stage estimation of near-field position parameters. Unlike existing studies, our work further reveals the impact of non-circular noise embedded in the EVFSM on both the Cramér–Rao bound (CRB) and the estimation algorithm. To mitigate this effect, we introduce the BONE algorithm, which leverages augmented-domain whitening to suppress non-circular noise. Simulations verify the adaptability of the proposed algorithms to array-spacing and the importance of incorporating EVFSM noise and its non-circularity to avoid performance degradation. Moreover, the two proposed methods also achieve low complexity while maintaining superior localization performance.

title: G2FL: Robust Federated Learning for GNSS Spoofing Detection.
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) are vulnerable to spoofing attacks that can compromise critical infrastructure and safety-critical applications. While Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising paradigm for collaborative GNSS spoofing detection, with privacy preservation, existing proposals remain vulnerable to Data Poisoning Attacks (DPAs), by malicious clients manipulating local training labels to degrade global model performance. This paper presents G2FL, a robust FL framework that detects and mitigates label-flipping attacks in GNSS spoofing detection. Our approach integrates two complementary mechanisms: a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM)-based cluster analysis that distinguishes poisoned model updates from benign contributions, through validation prediction statistics, and a score-based client management system that maintains reliability assessments to exclude persistently malicious participants. Experimental evaluation using a real-world GNSS spoofing dataset demonstrates that G2FL effectively mitigates DPAs, achieving 84.29% Area Under the Curve (AUC) compared to undefended FL (56.42%) and state-of-the-art defense, FoolsGold (65.80%), while maintaining performance close to attack-free scenarios (88.77%).

title: Near-Field Channel Estimation for XL-RIS-Assisted Terahertz OFDM Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of near-field channel estimation in extremely large reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS)-assisted terahertz (THz) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. By utilizing the sparsity of multi-user channels, we design a training protocol and formulate channel estimation as a low-rank tensor recovery problem. A canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD)-based method is then developed to estimate the channel parameters across different tensor dimensions. Moreover, based on the second-order Fresnel approximation of the near-field array response, we propose a two-stage residual fitting (TSRF) algorithm for the angular parameter estimation at the RIS side, which effectively reduces the computational complexity. Simulation results indicate that the proposed tensor-based algorithm significantly enhances estimation accuracy, while the TSRF algorithm is superior to traditional algorithms in both accuracy and complexity.

title: CRA-Enabled Secure ISAC Systems with Joint EM-BB Precoding.
abstract: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, dual-functional signaling may leak confidential messages during sensing, especially when the sensing target acts as an eavesdropper. Existing physical-layer security solutions mainly operate in the baseband (BB) via directional beamforming or artificial noise, but their effectiveness is limited by finite spatial resolution and correlated channels. To address this, we propose a secure ISAC framework enabled by compound reconfigurable antenna (CRA) arrays that jointly reconfigure radiation patterns and polarization in the electromagnetic (EM) domain. We develop a unified channel model capturing virtual angular-domain features, spatial propagation, and depolarization, and formulate a mixed-binary optimization problem to jointly design EM- and BB-domain precoders. We derive an efficient iterative algorithm leveraging majorization–minimization (MM), second-order cone programming (SOCP), and penalty methods. Simulations show that the proposed CRA-enabled joint EM– and BB-domain design substantially enhances sensing performance while preserving communication secrecy, achieving up to 11 dB sensing gain over conventional BB-only beamforming.

title: An Intelligent Spectrum Map Construction and Signal Source Localization Scheme Enabled by DSSTP-Net.
abstract: Spectrum map construction and signal source localization constitute essential components of dynamic spectrum management. However, the high implementation cost of the sampling infrastructure and the high complexity of signal source mobility pose significant challenges for the generation of continuous spectrum maps and the reconstruction of signal source trajectories. To address these challenges, a data and semantic dual driven spatio-temporal perception network (DSSTP-Net) is proposed. Semantic priors in the form of binary city maps and sampling location maps are incorporated to provide spatial structural guidance, which enhances the inference capability in regions with limited observations. Moreover, a spatio-temporal fusion module with a transformer-based architecture is designed to capture long-range dependencies across temporal dimensions, enabling better modeling of dynamic signal behavior. Furthermore, a motion compensation mechanism and a convolutional block attention module are introduced to ensure temporal consistency and to enhance the discriminability of feature representations. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves accurate reconstruction of continuous spectrum maps and reliable estimation of signal source trajectories. Compared with baseline methods, the DSSTP-Net demonstrates improved performance in both spectrum construction and localization accuracy, particularly under sparse sampling conditions.

title: Secure Task Offloading and Transmission via Homomorphic Encryption for Marine IoT Networks.
abstract: To address the privacy leakage risks, high energy consumption, and excessive latency inherent in task offloading and data transmission within marine Internet of Things (IoT) environments, this paper proposes a secure and efficient task offloading and transmission scheme based on homomorphic encryption (S2THE). Specifically, we construct a three-tier heterogeneous network architecture comprising low earth orbit (LEO) satellites, buoy nodes (BNs), and underwater sensor nodes (USNs), and formulate an optimization model that jointly considers privacy preservation, energy efficiency, and latency constraints for task offloading. To further ensure data transmission security, a Paillier homomorphic encryption mechanism is developed, in which keys are centrally managed and distributed by a key management center (KMC), thereby achieving end-to-end privacy protection of task data. Experimental results demonstrate that, in high-threat scenarios with a large number of eavesdropping nodes, the proposed S2THE method reduces energy consumption and latency by approximately 44.8% and 57.9%, respectively, compared to existing approaches, while decreasing the frequency of privacy leakage events by about 85.7%. These results highlight the significant advantages of S2THE in terms of both system performance and data security.

title: A Locally Differential Private Coding-Assisted Succinct Histogram Data Collection Protocol.
abstract: The increasing demand for large-scale data collection in emerging systems, such as 6G networks, presents significant challenges regarding user privacy. While local differential privacy (LDP) is a crucial framework for protecting sensitive data, existing coding-based LDP protocols for constructing succinct histograms, which identify heavy hitters and estimate their frequencies, have remained theoretical, lacking practical implementations and thorough analysis. This paper introduces the first practically implementable (ϵ, δ)-LDP coding-assisted protocol for succinct histogram data collection. We leverage polar codes for efficient encoding and utilize the Analytic Gaussian mechanism to perturb the data, which, critically, enables efficient soft decoding via a successive-cancellation list (SCL) decoder at the server. This approach is appealing because it can be integrated with existing reliable communication mechanisms. We provide theoretical bounds on the frequency estimation error and demonstrate through experimental validation that our protocol significantly improves robustness in the item decoding errors, particularly when the true frequency of the heavy hitter is low, compared to prior work. By supporting soft decoding, our design achieves greater versatility and lower decoder complexity, making it highly suitable for real-world deployment in large-scale data systems.

title: Causal Graph Transformer for Microservices Anomaly Detection.
abstract: As next-generation networked systems increasingly adopt microservice architectures to support scalable, intelligent, and cloud-native applications, the need for next-generation anomaly detection mechanisms becomes critical. However, the complexity of microservice architectures and the dependencies among services pose significant challenges for anomaly detection tasks. Anomalies such as high CPU usage, memory leaks, and unexpected network latency can severely impact system performance. Existing statistical-based methods often fail to accurately capture the dependency relationships between microservice modules, leading to low detection accuracy. To tackle this issue, we propose a Causal Graph Transformer (CGT) model for microservice anomaly detection, which transforms the anomaly detection problem into a graph classification task by representing microservice modules as nodes and service interactions as edges based on the system architecture. The model integrates Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Transformer, and Causal Attention Learning (CAL). Specifically, GNNs are employed to extract local features, Transformer is utilized to model global relationships, and CAL serves to filter out shortcut features while retaining causal features pertinent to anomaly propagation. Experiments on three popular benchmark microservice system datasets show that the CGT model outperforms other methods and achieves higher anomaly detection accuracy. The average anomaly detection accuracy of the CGT model reaches 95.87%, which is at least 2.87% higher than that of the baseline models.

title: Incremental Learning-Based Open-Set Classification of Unknown UAVs via RF Signal Semantics.
abstract: The proliferation of civilian and commercial unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has heightened the demand for reliable radio frequency (RF)-based drone identification systems that can operate under dynamic and uncertain airspace conditions. Most existing RF-based recognition methods adopt a closed-set assumption, where all UAV types are known during training. Such an assumption becomes unrealistic in practical deployments, as new or unknown UAVs frequently emerge, leading to overconfident misclassifications and inefficient retraining cycles. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a unified incremental open-set learning framework for RF-based UAV recognition that enables both novel class discovery and incremental adaptation. The framework first performs open-set recognition to separate unknown signals from known classes in the semantic feature space, followed by an unsupervised clustering module that discovers new UAV categories by selecting between K-Means and Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) based on composite validity scores. Subsequently, a lightweight incremental learning module integrates the newly discovered classes through a memory-bounded replay mechanism that mitigates catastrophic forgetting. Experiments on a real-world UAV RF dataset comprising 24 classes (18 known and 6 unknown) show effective open-set detection, promising clustering performance under the evaluated noise settings, and stable incremental adaptation with minimal storage cost, supporting the potential of the proposed framework for open-world UAV recognition.

title: BlindFuse: A Unified Framework for Active-Passive Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: In future 6G networks, integrated sensing and communication is vital to enable high-resolution situational awareness. However, fusing data from multiple base stations operating in heterogeneous active and passive sensing modes poses significant challenges to the communication backhaul and processing pipeline. These include high overhead from transmitting complex multitarget densities, resolving data association ambiguities in a distributed network, and managing dynamic sensor coverage. To address these hurdles, we propose a novel, communication-efficient fusion framework based on random finite set theory. Our framework first utilizes a lightweight Gaussian mixture representation to drastically reduce the required backhaul bandwidth. Second, we introduce a dynamic coverage partitioning algorithm that enables opportunistic fusion at the central processor without prior knowledge of each BS’s field of view, adapting to network dynamics. Finally, a robust fusion and global relabeling scheme generates a consistent and unified environmental map. Simulations show that our framework reduces the multitarget localization error by 33.3% and improves trajectory continuity by 70%, demonstrating a scalable solution for network-level cooperative perception.

title: Service-Oriented Dynamic Computing Resource Allocation in Software-Defined B5G/6G Systems.
abstract: Software-defined (SD) B5G/6G technology is gradually becoming a popular option for network deployment due to its flexibility and minimal dependence on dedicated hardware. However, SD-B5G/6G systems face the challenge of extremely high demand for general-purpose computing resources, especially in service-oriented scenarios focusing on end-to-end user requirements. As a result, SD-B5G/6G systems are highly prone to resource contention with user applications, which can adversely affect radio access network (RAN) performance. Most existing research only considers wireless resource competition among multiple users, while ignoring the computing resource demands of SD-B5G/6G systems in real-world scenarios. To address this gap, this study first develops a practical 5G platform integrating the SD-RAN, core network, and application service pipeline, enabling end-to-end user communication and controllable experimental evaluation under realistic deployment conditions. A layered architecture is further designed to jointly manage the application layer, control layer, infrastructure layer, and SDB5G/6G layer, so that computing resources can be monitored and dynamically coordinated across communication functions and user applications. Within this framework, a contextual bandit-based decision module is implemented as a case study to illustrate that the proposed framework can effectively mitigate resource contention and improve the stability of both application processing and SD-B5G/6G network performance.

title: Foundation Models for Generalizable Semantic and Goal-Oriented Communication.
abstract: Semantic and goal-oriented communication is increasingly studied for 6G, but generalization beyond seen data remains a key weakness under tight rate budgets. Many existing systems overfit their training data and degrade sharply at very low bit rates because they attempt to compress the entire signal. We introduce Foundation Model-Guided Semantic and Goal-Oriented Communication (FMSGOC), a framework that uses broad visual-linguistic Foundation Model priors to mitigate overfitting. It further improves rate efficiency by concentrating bits on sparse, goal-aligned anchors and relying on generative foundation-model priors to reconstruct the masked regions. By decoupling what to send from how to reconstruct, a vision-language foundation model selects and transmits a sparse set of semantic anchors, while a pretrained diffusion model, fine-tuned for masked completion, reconstructs the image at the receiver. In our experiments, FMSGOC reaches 0.039 bits per pixel (BPP), maintains high semantic fidelity (cosine similarity 0.87-0.90 on CIFAR-10), remains robust on previously unseen inputs (0.83-0.86 on ImageNet), and shows good perceptual similarity (0.1278/0.1558, CIFAR-10/ImageNet), outperforming strong end-to-end baselines at lower bit rates.

title: Flag-Preamble-Based Delay-Doppler Channel Estimation for Next-Evolution Waveforms.
abstract: Accurate delay-Doppler channel estimation is critical for next-evolution waveforms (NEWs) to enable reliable signal detection. This paper proposes a robust channel estimation algorithm that integrates Flag sequences optimized via an adaptive accelerated parallel majorization-minimization (AP-MM) algorithm with a proposed channel estimation algorithm. To enable efficient, low-complexity parameter extraction and further overcome the robustness issues of conventional greedy estimation, we introduce two key enhancements, i.e., a candidate selection strategy to mitigate spurious sidelobe peaks, and a global least squares (LS) refinement stage to eliminate error propagation caused by sidelobe masking effects. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms traditional existing algorithms, achieving the desired estimation accuracy.

title: HMS-RWKV: A Hybrid Multi-Scale Model with Spatial-Temporal Adaptive Fusion for Efficient WiFi Sensing.
abstract: WiFi-based human activity recognition (HAR) offers privacy-preserving sensing for smart environments, yet AI-based methods face a critical trade-off: Transformers achieve high accuracy with quadratic complexity, while Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are efficient but struggle with long-range dependencies. In this paper, we propose Hybrid Multi-Scale RWKV (HMS-RWKV), a lightweight dual-branch architecture featuring lightweight spatial extraction and linear-complexity RWKV temporal modelling. Our Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF) mechanism dynamically balances features from temporal and spatial branches, marking the first application of Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) in WiFi sensing. HMS-RWKV can consistently achieve over 99% accuracy across three main-stream public datasets and reach a new accuracy level on the more challenging Widar dataset, while reducing parameter and computational overhead by up to 90% compared to Transformer-like models, making it an ideal candidate for resource-constrained edge deployment. Ablation studies also validate each component’s contribution across four datasets.

title: Hardware-Efficient Distributed MIMO: Relaxing Power Amplifier Linearity Constraints.
abstract: Massive MIMO is a key enabler for next-generation wireless networks; however, it faces scalability challenges due to power amplifier (PA) nonlinearity. This paper establishes a theoretical foundation for the inherent advantage of the distributed MIMO (D-MIMO) architecture in relaxing PA linearity requirements. While our prior indoor measurements empirically demonstrated reduced nonlinear power leakage in distributed topologies, this work develops a generalized analytical model that captures the fundamental geometric principles underlying these benefits. Through rigorous analysis, we show that D-MIMO’s spatial distribution provides higher effective channel gain, enabling identical performance targets to be met with substantially lower transmit power compared to co-located architectures across diverse propagation environments. This power reduction allows PAs to operate in more linear regions with higher output backoff, thereby tolerating more severe nonlinearity without performance degradation. Simulation results validate the analysis, demonstrating that D-MIMO achieves up to an 89% transmit power reduction and maintains superior output back-off (OBO) performance across rural to urban environments, confirming its dual advantage of enabling cheaper PAs and lowering energy costs.

title: Enhancing In-Network Distributed Traffic Analysis Models with Implicit Topology Embedding.
abstract: Distributed traffic analysis on programmable network elements is challenged by the dual constraints of limited on-device resources and model compatibility. Existing learning frameworks for streamlined models often overlook the crucial influence of a node’s network role, leading to suboptimal performance when aggregating models from heterogeneous data sources. This paper introduces DisITE, a novel framework for enhancing in-network ML/DL models using implicit topology embedding. DisITE first learns node-specific, topological representations directly from local traffic in a self-supervised manner. These embeddings then guide a location-aware collaborative training framework to effectively manage data heterogeneity. Finally, knowledge distillation produces lightweight, efficient models for on-device deployment. Extensive experiments on simulated network topologies and public datasets demonstrate that our approach not only accurately infers network fabric but also significantly outperforms traditional topology-agnostic methods, including improvements in F1-Score and a huge reduction in resource usage.

title: Toward Resilient Channel Estimation in Wideband High-Mobility Scenarios: A Non-Uniform Pilot Pattern Design.
abstract: In wideband high-mobility scenarios, reliable channel estimation is challenged by strong Doppler effects and frequency-dependent channel variations. Conventional pilot designs based on uniform frequency-domain patterns become increasingly inefficient, as they fail to adapt to heterogeneous channel statistics, such as coherence bandwidth and Doppler spread, across the spectrum. In this paper, exploiting the sparsity of delay–Doppler channel representation, we first establish an explicit analytical relationship between frequency-domain pilot spacing and the mutual coherence of the sensing matrix in compressed sensing (CS), revealing the fundamental subband-dependent coherence constraints on channel estimation performance. Then, we derive the closed-form of the upper bound of mean squared error (MSE) performance, as a function of the mutual coherence and delay-Doppler paths. Finally, we formulate a pilot pattern optimization problem under coherence and frequency domain sampling constraints, and develop a low-complexity Adaptive Subband Pilot Allocation (ASPA) algorithm. Simulation results confirm that the proposed non-uniform pilot design achieves significantly lower MSE than conventional uniform schemes under the same pilot overhead in wideband high-mobility scenarios.

title: Smaller is Better: Generative Models Can Power Short Video Preloading.
abstract: Preloading is widely used in short video platforms to minimize playback stalls by downloading future content in advance. However, existing strategies face a tradeoff. Aggressive preloading reduces stalls but wastes bandwidth, while conservative strategies save data but increase the risk of playback stalls. This paper presents PromptPream, a computation powered preloading paradigm that breaks this tradeoff by using local computation to reduce bandwidth demand. Instead of transmitting pixel level video chunks, PromptPream sends compact semantic prompts that are decoded into high quality frames using generative models such as Stable Diffusion. We propose three core techniques to enable this paradigm: (1) a gradient based prompt inversion method that compresses frames into small sets of compact token embeddings; (2) a computation aware scheduling strategy that jointly optimizes network and compute resource usage; and (3) a scalable searching algorithm that addresses the enlarged scheduling space introduced by scheduler. Evaluations show that PromptStream reduces both stalls and bandwidth waste by over 31%, and improves Quality of Experience (QoE) by 45%, compared to traditional strategies.

title: High-Fidelity Semantic Transmission and Reconstruction for Task-Oriented Spatial Perception Codec in 6G.
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence and spatial perception technologies, specialized robots have been increasingly applied in complex environments. To address the challenges of computational complexity, network transmission efficiency, and high–fidelity semantic reconstruction faced by specialized robots in large–scale real–time scene reconstruction, a semantic–enhanced spatial perception codec technology is proposed. First, Bird’s–Eye–View (BEV) feature mapping is adopted to convert point clouds into structured tensors. Second, binary semantic masks are generated based on semantic information to achieve key region localization and data sparsification. Third, a hierarchical entropy coding framework is constructed to realize efficient compression through learnable quantization and hyper–prior probability models. Finally, decoding adopts embodied intelligent scene semantic alignment reconstruction to ensure high–fidelity restoration of geometry and semantics. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves efficient data transmission while maintaining good reconstruction quality, which fully validates the effectiveness and robustness of the approach.

title: An Intelligent Traffic Estimation Approach to 6G Networks for Industry Applications based on Time-Frequency Features.
abstract: Industry applications landing is one of the important visions of 6G networks. The flexibility and scalability of network architectures is one of the most important factors since massive industrial User Equipments (UEs) access network randomly and their Quality of Service (QoS) requirement is extremely diversity. The maturity of software defined networking and network function virtualization bring new opportunities to 6G networks. In 6G networks, massive industrial UEs share information with each other to enable automatic control, recognition, and decision-making. Due to the task-orientation and timeliness characteristics of industry applications, the network traffic engineering becomes an important issue that should be considered. Network traffic prediction is very important for load balancing and network planning. The prediction results can be used to improve the QoS of industrial UEs. In this paper, we propose an intelligent approach to obtain network traffic in 6G networks. Firstly, the wavelet decomposition theory is used to extract the time-frequency features of network traffic. We consider network traffic as a time serials at different moments. Then we refine the dynamic time-frequency features at different moments and frequencies, based on the wavelet decomposition. Secondly, We utilize the Elman neural network to build the intelligent learning model for network traffic features. A mul-input and mul-ouput feature extraction model is proposed. Thirdly, we build a mulconstraints optimization model to estimate network traffic in 6G networks. Finally, simulation results show that our approach is promising.

title: Pinching-Antenna-Aided Localization and Tracking: A Bayesian Perspective.
abstract: Pinching-Antenna Systems (PASS) have attracted considerable attention, since they are capable of beneficially reconfiguring the wireless environment by establishing powerful line-of-sight paths. In this paper, a Bayesian localization and tracking framework is developed for uplink PASS, which explicitly exploits propagation delay information enabled by orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM). The delay-dispersed received signals are modeled in the frequency domain, and a Bayesian localization tracking algorithm is proposed by jointly leveraging variational inference and belief propagation to extract path delays, infer user locations, and exploit the temporal correlation across consecutive time slots. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed PASS-based tracking scheme achieves a user tracking performance comparable to that of a conventional multi-base-station system, while requiring significantly fewer RF chains. Moreover, it consistently outperforms conventional baselines when the number of RF chains is aligned.

title: Attention-Enhanced-PPO-based Multi-UAV Cooperative Sensing for Heterogeneous Tasks.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) cooperative sensing shows strong promise for environmental monitoring, emergency response, and smart-city applications. However, under tight energy budgets and heterogeneous sensing requirements, achieving efficient multi-UAV cooperation remains challenging. In this paper, we propose a multi-UAV cooperative sensing scheme for wireless networks that explicitly models the correlation between UAV capability levels and the heterogeneous sensing demands of Points of interest (PoIs). We formulate a makespan-minimization problem that accounts for sensing requirements, task duration (and optional deadlines), and propulsion energy consumption. To handle the tight coupling among assignment and scheduling decisions in the problem, we develop a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) policy that integrates multi-head attention with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), enabling the policy to focus on salient UAV-PoI interactions and improving decision quality and training stability. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme consistently outperforms baseline methods in both makespan and energy efficiency, and maintains strong scalability in complex multi-task environments.

title: Near-Field Line-of-Sight Communication with Massive Movable Antennas.
abstract: The proliferation of the sixth generation (6G) networks demands innovative antenna technologies to fully unlock spatial degrees of freedom. Large-scale position-reconfigurable antenna (PRA) arrays have emerged as a promising solution, while existing antenna position design approaches often suffer from high computational complexity and neglect the near-field effect. In this paper, we propose efficient methods to determine the antenna positions for near-field line-of-sight communication. Specifically, by transforming the antenna positions into the angular domain, we reformulate the achievable rate maximization problem as a Vandermonde matrix determinant maximization problem, which is known as a weighted Fekete problem, whose optimal solution can be obtained by off-the-shelf solvers. To further reduce the computational complexity, we propose a greedy algorithm to find the asymptotically optimal antenna positions accommodating practical physical constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme yields a considerable achievable rate gain compared to the conventional uniform linear array scheme in the near-field region with up to 35× reduction in design complexity.

title: NS-D3QN Enhanced Sensing and Communications for Emergency UAV Networks.
abstract: In post-disaster rescue operations, although emergency communication vehicles (ECVs) can temporarily replace destroyed base stations, their limited deployment often results in poor signal link quality, making it difficult to meet high-speed emergency sensing and communication (ESAC) requirements. To address this challenge, we establish an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted ESAC system to search and rescue survivors. The UAV flies along the selected direction based on the distress signal strength of survivors. Meanwhile, it uploads the disaster information to the ECV, ultimately reaching the centroid of survivor distribution to serve as a communication relay. To maximize the weighted sum of the system’s communication information rate and sensing estimation rate while minimizing the flight time, we formulate the objective problem by jointly optimizing UAV trajectory and power allocation subject to constraints of UAV velocity, accessible airspace boundaries, start and end positions, UAV transmit power limits, minimum sensing estimation rate thresholds, and the requirement to detect all survivors. To tackle this highly coupled non-convex problem, we propose the Noisy-Scheduled Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (NS-D3QN) algorithm, enabling real-time joint optimization of UAV trajectory and power allocation without prior knowledge of the full environment. Simulation results demonstrate that NS-D3QN significantly outperforms other baseline algorithms.

title: Adaptive Online Decision Transformer for Fault-Tolerant DAG Service Orchestration in Dynamic 6G Edge Networks.
abstract: The 6G edge networks are experiencing a growing demand for compute-intensive services that exhibit complex dependencies, typically modeled as Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs). However, dynamic resource fluctuations and node state variations pose significant challenges to the robustness of task orchestration and deployment. Existing solutions often inadequately address task dependencies and environmental dynamics in 6G edge environments. This paper proposes an Adaptive Online Decision Transformer (AODT) that leverages Reinforcement Learning (RL)-generated trajectories for supervised training and and performs online fine-tuning through environment interaction to enhance adaptability in dynamic 6G edge networks. Experimental evaluation is conducted in a high-fidelity 6G edge simulation system featuring dynamic resource adjustments and time-varying node states. Results demonstrate that AODT achieves an average improvement of 89.94% in DAG completion time and reduces the task redeployment rate by 72.31%, validating its efficacy in dynamic edge networks.

title: Transformer-Based Integrated Sensing and Semantic Communication for Low-Altitude Wireless Networks.
abstract: Emerging low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs) provide a promising aerial platform for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) due to the high mobility and flexible deployment. Nevertheless, dynamic environment and limited infrastructure support pose significant challenges for achieving high-accuracy ISAC services. To address these issues, we propose a Transformer-based integrated sensing and semantic communication (T-ISSC) framework that transmits task-relevant semantic tokens in distributed sensing networks. In particular, inspired by recent advances in generative large models, the proposed T-ISSC framework integrates the Transformer-empowered joint source-channel coding architecture with a task head for target state estimation. Moreover, transfer learning is leveraged to enhance the framework’s adaptability to diverse communication environments in LAWNs. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed T-ISSC framework achieves a 52.35%-73.66% reduction in root mean square error compared with benchmark schemes.

title: An Analytically Tractable Cox Point-Process Model for LEO Mega-Constellation Mobility Management.
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, mobility management has become a critical challenge for maintaining seamless connectivity. Simulation-based tools such as satellite tool kit (STK) provide accurate assessments of satellite motion but are computationally intensive for large constellations, while conventional analytical models often treat satellite positions as static and fail to capture the dynamic visibility geometry inherent in mobility scenarios. To address these limitations, this work develops a Cox point process–based analytical framework that jointly models the random distribution of orbital planes and the along-track movement of satellites. This dual-layer stochastic geometry captures both the spatial hierarchy and temporal dynamics of LEO constellations, enabling tractable analysis of mobility behavior. Closed-form expressions are derived for key metrics, including access probability, service-time distribution, and handover probability, revealing how orbital altitude, constellation density, and elevation constraints jointly determine link continuity and handover frequency. Analytical results closely match high-fidelity STK simulations while reducing computational complexity by more than two orders of magnitude, demonstrating that the proposed Cox framework provides an effective and scalable foundation for mobility management analysis in next-generation LEO mega-constellations.

title: Max-min Fairness Optimization for UAV-assisted Mobile Relay Communication Systems with SLIPT.
abstract: The endurance of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is usually restricted by their limited onboard energy, thus posing challenges to sustainable operations. To address this challenge, we investigate a UAV-assisted mobile relay system enabled by simultaneous lightwave information and power transfer (SLIPT), where free-space optical links jointly provide high-speed data transmission and energy replenishment. Moreover, considering the diverse spatial distribution of users, a max–min fairness optimization problem is formulated to balance communication performance, energy harvesting efficiency, and UAV mobility. Then, the resulting mixed-integer nonlinear problem is decomposed into three more tractable subproblems and solved iteratively. In addition, simulation results demonstrate the convergence of the proposed algorithm, and highlight its superior fairness performance compared with existing schemes in the literature.

title: Adaptive Resource Allocation under Time-varying Traffic in Optical IRS-assisted VLC Networks.
abstract: In practical visible light communication (VLC) networks, traffic demand exhibits strong temporal variations, necessitating the adaptive resource allocation to ensure both efficiency and fairness among users. Therefore, the dynamic resource optimization in an optical intelligent reflecting surface (OIRS)-assisted VLC network is investigated in this paper, considering time-varying user demands across time slots. The optimization is formulated as minimizing the long-term average total transmit power, and then is addressed via the per-slot power allocation and OIRS configuration with the Lyapunov optimization framework. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves substantial power savings, while the deployment of OIRS units further reduces the energy consumption and enhances the network adaptability.

title: Mitigating Inter-user Interference in Mixed Near-field and Far-field Communications.
abstract: In mixed near-field and far-field systems, the non-orthogonality between near-field and far-field channels may lead to severe inter-user interference and hence degraded rate performance, when the analog beamforming is designed based on full-array maximum ratio transmission (MRT). To tackle this issue, we propose a new scheme that employs the antenna selection technique to effectively suppress mixed-field interference. Specifically, we first consider a typical two-user mixed-field case and show that the strong mixed-field interference can be greatly reduced by deactivating a small portion of antennas only, yet without compromising array gains too much. Then, a sum-rate maximization problem is formulated for the general case, where the antenna selection and power allocation are jointly optimized based on MRT beams in analog beamforming. Although this problem is non-convex and difficult to solve, we propose an efficient penalty dual decomposition (PDD)-based double-layer framework to obtain its high-quality solution by using the block coordinate descent (BCD) and successive convex approximation (SCA) techniques. Last, numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves a favorable trade-off between interference suppression and array gain loss, hence achieving significant performance gains over various benchmark schemes.

title: Robust Spatial Anti-Jamming Based on Steering Vector Estimation and Orthogonal Projection.
abstract: In this paper, a robust spatial anti-jamming algorithm capable of jamming suppression in mismatch scenarios is proposed. Firstly, the Capon spectral peak search is performed in the jamming angular sector and the directions-of-arrival (DOAs) of the jamming signals are initially filtered out. Then, the power spectrum is integrated in the neighboring range of each estimated jamming signal DOA to construct matrices, and the principal eigenvectors of these matrices are utilized to estimate the steering vectors (SVs) of jamming signals. Similarly, Capon spectrum integration is performed in the intended signal angular region, and the expected signal SV is approximate through principal eigenvector extraction. Finally, the proposed beamforming weight is obtained through orthogonal projection and the estimated SVs of jamming signals and desired signal. Numerical results confirm that the presented algorithm exhibits better jamming suppression performance and lower sensitivity to mismatch environments than the comparison algorithms. In addition, the presented beamforming weight is capable of keeping the peak of the beampattern main lobe aligned with the practical incoming direction of the intended signal and the beampattern notches aligned with the practical DOAs of jamming signals.

title: N2V: A Lightweight Image-Based Model for Predicting Extreme Regions in Network Traffic.
abstract: Accurate traffic prediction is critical for achieving low latency and high Quality of Service (QoS) in edge networks. However, existing time series forecasting models often struggle to capture sudden fluctuations, particularly extreme peaks and troughs, and their high computational overhead limits real-time deployment on resource-constrained edge servers. To address these challenges, we propose N2V (Numerical to Visual), a lightweight forecasting framework that converts numerical time series into image representations to enhance the modeling of extreme regions. By visualizing traffic dynamics, N2V captures distinctive patterns associated with peaks and troughs, providing richer contextual information than conventional numerical inputs. The framework employs an efficient Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) architecture to ensure fast inference and minimal resource consumption, enabling seamless real-time deployment at the network edge. Extensive experiments on four real-world network traffic datasets show that N2V reduces mean squared error (MSE) by 12% and improves peak and trough prediction accuracy by 28% and 31%, respectively, compared with state-of-the-art baselines. These results demonstrate that N2V offers a practical and scalable solution for real-time traffic forecasting and intelligent resource management in edge environments.

title: LiReS IDS: A Lightweight, Real-time, and Secure Intrusion Detection System for RISC-V Edge Devices.
abstract: As edge devices take on greater responsibility for processing sensitive data, they also face escalating risks from sophisticated cyberattacks. Machine learning-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs) are a key defense mechanism, but deploying IDS on edge devices poses three challenges: models must remain lightweight, inference must operate in real-time, and the IDS itself must be secured against adversarial manipulation. In this paper, we present LiReS IDS, a lightweight, real-time, and secure IDS tailored for RISC-V edge devices. First, we introduce a genetic algorithm-driven structured pruning method that reduces the size of CNN-based IDS by up to 80% while preserving detection accuracy, enabling deployment on memory-constrained RISC-V edge platforms. Second, we design a TEE-secured IDS architecture using Keystone enclaves to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the IDS. Finally, we implement and evaluate LiReS IDS on the SiFive HiFive Unmatched RISC-V board using multiple benchmark datasets (NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, and CICIDS-2018), achieving real-time detection performance with a latency of 50 ms, demonstrating its practical feasibility for next-generation RISC-V edge computing environments.

title: Network Slicing Migration for Satellite Network Failures: A GraphToken-Assisted LLM Approach.
abstract: The rapid deployment of Ultra-Dense Low Earth Orbit Satellite Networks (UD-LSNs) is expected to play a critical role in future 6G. However, the dynamic topologies and stochastic inter-satellite link (ISL) failures caused by space environmental effects in UD-LSNs present significant challenges for reliable service delivery. Network slicing with virtual network embedding has emerged as a key technique to support heterogeneous services, yet ISL disruptions may compromise the stability of mapped virtual networks, necessitating effective migration strategies. In this paper, we investigate the problem of slice migration in UD-LSNs under ISL failures and formulate it as a long-term optimization problem to maximize slice utility, jointly considering virtual network request (VNR) acceptance rate and migration cost. To address the stochastic and diverse failure conditions, we propose a GraphToken-assisted LLM migration (GTLM) algorithm that integrates Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) with large language model (LLM). This hybrid architecture leverages graph-based network state representations and the generalization capability of LLM to adaptively select migration strategies under varying ISL failure scenarios. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed GTLM consistently outperforms baselines in terms of VNR acceptance rate and total utility across different failure probability and VNR arrival rate scenarios, thereby ensuring robustness and scalability in dynamic UD-LSN environments.

title: Early Traffic Accident Prediction for Connected Vehicles: A Multi-Source Data Fusion Scheme.
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of intelligent vehicles and the consequent intensification of traffic density, traffic accidents have emerged as a pressing safety concern for contemporary society. The World Health Organization (WHO) has identified vehicle blind spots as one of the primary causes of traffic accidents. Consequently, there is an urgent need to research new technologies to expand the perception range of automobiles, thereby safeguarding users’ safety. In response to this, some researchers have proposed a traffic accident prediction scheme based on Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X), which predicts upcoming collisions and issues timely warnings by sharing data from surrounding vehicles and Road Side Units (RSUs). However, existing schemes either only use Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) data or utilize Vehicle-to-Road (V2R) data, which limits the prediction accuracy. Additionally, these works do not discuss Time-to-Accident (TTA) in detail, which is directly related to whether drivers have sufficient reaction time to avoid traffic accidents. Therefore, we propose a novel early-warning scheme that, by fusing multi-source data, integrates a multi-channel attention architecture and a Probabilistic Occupancy Map (POM) to enhance prediction accuracy and quantify spatial risks towards earlier prediction. Extensive experiments on the INTERACTION dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves 99.97% prediction accuracy and 3.06 seconds advance warning time in straight carriageway scenarios, confirming its advantages in prediction accuracy and timeliness.

title: Spatial-Temporal Dual-Branch Learning for Anomaly Detection in Software-Defined Networks.
abstract: The unique architecture of Software-Defined Networking (SDN) offers enhanced management flexibility but also introduces new security threats, especially as 6G networks further expand the scale and complexity of network environments, making traditional intrusion detection methods difficult to apply directly. Although existing research has attempted to solve these problems by combining spatial and temporal features, there remains considerable room for improvement in detection accuracy and generalization capability, especially in practical scenarios with limited labeled data. To address these limitations, this paper proposes the Spatial-Temporal Dual-Network (STD-Net), a small-sample anomaly detection framework designed for SDN environments. The framework begins by dynamically grouping raw flow data into a hierarchical "user–time point" structure through adaptive user identification and temporal aggregation, followed by automated feature selection using Information Value (IV) analysis. Architecturally, STD-Net employs a dual-branch design, a temporal branch using a Transformer encoder to capture long-term dependencies, and a spatial branch leveraging a Graph Attention Network (GAT) to model structural relationships among time points. These two branches are integrated through an adaptive gated fusion module. By explicitly modeling spatiotemporal characteristics and incorporating built-in inductive biases, the design significantly improves performance under conditions of incomplete data and scarce annotations. Experimental results demonstrate that STD-Net outperforms other baseline methods in both detection accuracy and robustness in low-resource settings.

title: Transmit Beamforming Design for Integrated Sensing and Multicast Communication based on Distribution Information.
abstract: In this paper, we study an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where a multi-antenna base station (BS) simultaneously estimates the unknown angle parameter of a point target using the echo signals received at the BS with prior distribution information, and serves a group of single-antenna communication users in the downlink via multicast transmission. We aim to minimize the posterior Cramér-Rao bound (PCRB) of the target angle parameter by optimizing the multicast beamformer and potential dedicated sensing beamformers, subject to a multicast rate constraint. We propose a successive convex approximation (SCA) based algorithm to effectively solve the non-convex problem, and obtain a stationary solution that satisfies Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions. Through analysis, we derive a specific structure of the proposed KKT solution across different rate regimes, and characterize the number of dedicated sensing beams needed in a multicast ISAC system for the first time. Our analytical results hold for any KKT point solution, including the optimal one. Numerical results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed design and the theoretical analysis.

title: Learning-Based Joint Communication and Control Design for Wireless Networked Control Systems.
abstract: This paper studies a multi-loop wireless networked control system (WNCS), in which a base station (BS) centrally coordinates multiple nonlinear subsystems over fading wireless channels. Due to unknown plant dynamics and uncertainties in the transmission of state information and control signals, traditional model-based control-communication co-design methods may not work well in such WNCS systems. To address these issues, we propose a data-driven control-communication co-design approach that leverages deep learning and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to maximize the cumulative reward across all subsystems. Specifically, we first employ long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks to estimate missing observations and control inputs resulting from transmission losses. We then apply a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm with prioritized experience replay to jointly optimize the control inputs and wireless resource allocation, thereby enhancing the overall control performance. Finally, simulations conducted on the OpenAI Gym platform demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms several benchmark schemes.

title: Gradient-Aware High-Resolution Pathways for Tiny UAV Object Detection.
abstract: Detecting ultra-small targets in UAV imagery is hindered by (i) gradient washout on fine details, (ii) resolution loss from downsampling, (iii) dilution during cross-scale fusion, and (iv) the cost/misfocus of global attention. We present Gradient-Aware High-Resolution Pathways (GA-Pathways), which tackles these issues with three cooperating parts: a GHRP block that maintains well-conditioned gradient routes along high-resolution paths, an HR-PentaPath (HRPP) fusion pathway with lightweight content-aware merging, and localized CGA applied only at shallow levels for targeted enhancement. Under a single-scale, no-TTA FP32 protocol at 6402, GA-Pathways-s delivers 56.2% Precision, 40.3% Recall, 44.5% AP50, and 27.1% AP0.5:0.95on VisDrone2019-DET with 5.24M parameters and 25.7 GFLOPs; on AI-TOD it attains 36.8% AP50and 17.5% AP0.5:0.95at the same complexity. A nano variant reaches 36.7%/22.8% (AP50/AP0.5:0.95) with 1.94M parameters and 7.83 GFLOPs. On VisDrone, GA-Pathways-s improves over YOLOv12s/13s by +4.2∼+4.6 (AP50) and +2.7∼+3.3 (AP0.5:0.95) while using ∼42% fewer parameters; GA-Pathways-n exceeds YOLOv13n by +2.3/+2.8 with ∼20% fewer parameters. Ablations indicate that safeguarding shallow gradients and favoring high-resolution fusion, complemented by localized attention, yields a strong accuracy–efficiency balance and reliably localizes targets down to 4×4 pixels.

title: O-RAN Slicing Deployment over Jittery Clouds: A Stochastic Network Calculus Approach.
abstract: O-RAN disaggregation enables flexible deployment of O-DU/O-CU functions over heterogeneous edge and regional clouds, but Service Level Agreement (SLA) guarantees become difficult under bursty slice traffic and time-varying server performance. This paper develops a stochastic network calculus (SNC) model for the O-RAN service chain by combining an On–Off MMPP arrival model with a jitter-aware drift service model whose computation jitter increases with load. From the resulting delay-violation bound, we derive a sufficient per-node CPU allocation condition to meet slice-specific delay and reliability requirements. Building on these SNC constraints, we jointly optimize user association, O-DU/O-CU placement, and CPU allocation under radio and server capacity limits, and propose an SNC-guided hybrid genetic algorithm. Simulations show that the proposed method satisfies the target violation probabilities and substantially reduces CPU consumption compared with peak-rate provisioning, while providing practical guidance for deploying sliced O-RAN over multi-tier clouds.

title: Multi-Agentic AI for Conflict-Aware rApp Policy Orchestration in Open RAN.
abstract: Open Radio Access Network (RAN) enables flexible, AI-driven control of mobile networks through disaggregated, multi-vendor components. In this architecture, xApps handle real-time functions, whereas rApps in the non-real-time controller generate strategic policies. However, current rApp development remains largely manual, brittle, and poorly scalable as xApp diversity proliferates. In this work, we propose a Multi-Agentic AI framework to automate rApp policy generation and orchestration. The architecture integrates three specialized large language model (LLM)-based agents, Perception, Reasoning, and Refinement, supported by retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and memory-based analogical reasoning. These agents collectively analyze potential conflicts, synthesize intent-aligned control pipelines, and incrementally refine deployment decisions. Experiments across diverse deployment scenarios demonstrate that the proposed system achieves over 70% improvement in deployment accuracy and 95% reduction in reasoning cost compared to baseline methods, while maintaining zero-shot generalization to unseen intents. These results establish a scalable and conflict-aware solution for fully autonomous, zero-touch rApp orchestration in Open RAN.

title: A Lightweight Framework for Integrated Sensing and Communications with RIS.
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have been recognized as a promising technology to enhance both communication and sensing performance in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems for future 6G networks. However, existing RIS optimization methods for improving ISAC performance are mainly based on semidefinite relaxation (SDR) or iterative algorithms. The former suffers from high computational complexity and limited scalability, especially when the number of RIS elements becomes large, while the latter yields suboptimal solutions whose performance depends on initialization. In this work, we introduce a lightweight RIS phase design framework that provides a closed-form solution and explicitly accounts for the trade-off between communication and sensing, as well as proportional beam gain distribution toward multiple sensing targets. The key idea is to partition the RIS configuration into two parts: the first part is designed to maximize the communication performance, while the second introduces small perturbations to generate multiple beams for multi-target sensing. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and demonstrate that it achieves performance comparable to SDR but with significantly lower computational complexity.

title: Full Domain Resource Programming in Wideband MIMO Systems: A Step Towards 6G.
abstract: In this work, we consider a wideband full resource domain programming for multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wideband systems. Focusing on a practical dense scenario where the number of multiple users exceeds the scheduling capability of the base station (BS), we formulate a non-convex mixed integer non-linear programming (MINLP) problem towards sum rate maximization. Exploiting the inherent connections of time, frequency, space, and power resources, we provide a novel routine for joint design of user scheduling, subcarrier allocation, and hybrid precoding, which outperforms classic decomposition-based design and convex-concave programming (CCP)-based joint design. Finally, capturing the unique upper triangle analog structure, we propose a wideband distributed successive subtraction (WDS) decomposition method to decompose the obtained optimal hybrid precoder to digital and analog precoder. Results show our scheme considerably outperforms the benchmarks while ensuring a fast convergence.

title: LLM-Aided UAV Routing Against Jamming Attacks.
Agentic Open RAN: A Deterministic and Auditable Framework for Intent-Driven Radio Control.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) open new possibilities for agentic control in Open RAN, allowing operators to express intents in natural language while delegating low-level execution to autonomous agents. We present A1GENT, an agentic RAN control stack that decouples reasoning from real-time actuation. A non-RT agentic rApp compiles operator goals into typed A1 policy instances, and three task-oriented near-RT agentic xApps enforce them through a deterministic loop with plane-scoped actuation—E2 for mobility and load steering, and O1 for energy orchestration. This agentic reasoning–execution split ensures auditable coordination between RAN intelligent controller (RIC) tiers, supported by encoded guardrails and a fixed-priority action merger for conflict governance. A training-free adaptive policy tuner then refines bounded parameters using KPI memory without retraining, sustaining predictable adaptation. By integrating intent-driven planning with deterministic nearRT execution, A1GENT advances Open RAN toward verifiable, self-governing, and reproducible agentic intelligence.

title: SNC-Based Delay Analysis for RIS-Aided URLLC Systems in IIoT-Enabled Factory Automation Scenarios.
abstract: B5G/6G communication facilitates intelligent and flexible factory automation (FA) through ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) technology where short packet transmission via Finite Blocklength Coding (FBC) is used to reduce latency. Due to the vulnerability of wireless links caused by severe blockage in FA, Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) is regarded as a promising technology to ensure high reliability. In this paper, we analyze the statistical delay performance in RIS-aided URLLC systems via stochastic network calculus (SNC) for the first time, facing challenges of the dynamic wireless channel environment and the randomness of packet arrivals. Specifically, we derive the upper bounds for the delay violation probability (DVP), considering two critical URLLC scenarios under FBC: given decoding error probability (DEP) and given transmission rate. Furthermore, we develop an efficient rate adaptation scheme to minimize the DVP. Simulation results validate both our theoretical analysis and the proposed scheme, which can balance the rate-DEP trade-off. Our findings emphasize the significance of deploying RIS to ensure deterministic URLLC services. Increasing the number of RIS elements can enable better DVP performance even with stricter DEP and rate requirements.

title: LBFT: A Low-latency Blockchain and Fabric-based Trust Scheme for Efficient IoT Cross-Domain Authentication.
abstract: Cross-domain authentication in the Internet of Things (IoT) faces challenges of incompatibility with Certificate Authority (CA) Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) systems and interoperability across heterogeneous blockchains. Existing solutions often require entirely new trust infrastructures or impose excessive overhead, limiting their applicability to resource-constrained IoT devices. This paper proposes an efficient blockchain-based cross-domain authentication scheme built on Hyperledger Fabric. The scheme integrates a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) for secure key generation and storage, and a Physically Unclonable Function Identifier (PUFID) for tamper-resistant device identity. A nonce- and timestamp-based mechanism prevents replay attacks, while credential batch processing improves scalability by grouping multiple operations into single blockchain transactions. Security analysis under the Dolev–Yao adversary model confirms strong guarantees of authenticity, integrity, anti-replay, and unforgeability. Experimental results show the scheme achieves 253 transactions per second (TPS) with 10–30 ms authentication latency, outperforming comparable approaches. Overall, the proposed framework provides a compatible, scalable, and hardware-assisted solution for secure IoT cross-domain interoperability.

title: Sensing-assisted Predictive Hybrid Beamforming for Low-Altitude Communication Networks.
abstract: This paper proposes a sensing-assisted predictive hybrid beamforming scheme for low-altitude communication networks (LACN). Specifically, we consider that a base station transmits data to multiple unmanned aerial vehicles. Without the estimation of historical state parameters, i.e., angle-of-arrival, channel state information (CSI), we establish a direct mapping between reflected echo signals and hybrid beamforming (HBF) matrices through an end-to-end framework. To enhance the communication quality of service, the predictive HBF design problem is formulated by maximizing communication sum-rate subject to power and hardware constraints. A novel sensing-assisted network architecture is proposed to predict HBF for LACN. This architecture combines Transformer and convolutional modules to jointly extract rich spatio-temporal features from the reflected echoes. We compare our proposed PHBFNN with existing deep learning-based methods and the extended Kalman filtering approach. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed PHBFNN scheme achieves a higher sum-rate, validating its feasibility for realizing LACN without CSI.

title: Near-Field ISAC with Location Division Multiple Access: A Secure Beam-Scanning Framework.
abstract: This paper investigates a secure beam-scanning framework for near-field integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, enabled by location division multiple access (LDMA). An ISAC base station performs robust full-map beam-scanning within each transmission cycle to detect potential eavesdroppers (Eves) while ensuring secure communication for legitimate users (Bobs). Using Bobs’ channel state information (CSI) at the cycle’s start and Eves’ CSI estimated from prior sensing, we formulate a robust optimization problem that jointly designs hybrid analog Cdigital precoding and time allocation to maximize the worst-case secrecy rate. To reduce complexity, we eliminate semi-infinite constraints via convex hull representation, construct an azimuth Cdistance LDMA codebook for ideal radar beampatterns, and design efficient analog precoders. Furthermore, a low-complexity alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed under the convex hull model. Simulation results show that the proposed framework effectively enables full-map Eve detection while guaranteeing secure Bob transmission.

title: Deep Learning Enabled Direct Multiuser Hybrid Beamforming for XL-MIMO Communications.
abstract: This paper presents a pilot-efficient direct hybrid beamforming framework for multiuser near-and far-field XL-MIMO systems that operates without downlink channel state information.
