We design a fully complex-valued end-to-end architecture comprising a grouped complex-convolution sensing frontend, a shared complex multilayer perceptron, and a constant-modulus normalization head that outputs the analog precoder directly from a small set of uplink measurements. A variant minimum mean-squared error surrogate eliminates the digital precoder in closed form during training, providing stable gradients while respecting hybrid hardware constraints. At inference, the learned analog combiner is reused to estimate the equivalent channel from a few additional pilots, enabling a regularized zero-forcing digital precoder computed via Cholesky-based linear solves. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed method delivers up to 3 bps/Hz sum-rate gains over sparse-recovery pipelines and strong deep learning baselines under identical pilot budgets, while approaching ideal hybrid beamforming performance with an order-of-magnitude lower complexity than iterative schemes. The framework remains robust across wide SNR ranges, various multipath levels, and mixed near-/far-field deployments, highlighting its suitability for scalable XL-MIMO implementations.

title: IU-GUARD: Privacy-Preserving Spectrum Coordination for Incumbent Users under Dynamic Spectrum Sharing.
abstract: With the growing demand for wireless spectrum, dynamic spectrum sharing (DSS) frameworks such as the Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS) have emerged as practical solutions to improve utilization while protecting incumbent users (IUs) such as military radars. However, current incumbent protection mechanisms face critical limitations. The Environmental Sensing Capability (ESC) requires costly sensor deployments and remains vulnerable to interference and security risks. Alternatively, the Incumbent Informing Capability (IIC) requires IUs to disclose their identities and operational parameters to the Spectrum Coordination System (SCS), creating linkable records that compromise operational privacy and mission secrecy.We propose IU-GUARD, a privacy-preserving spectrum sharing framework that enables IUs to access spectrum without revealing their identities. Leveraging verifiable credentials (VCs) and zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs), IU-GUARD allows IUs to prove their authorization to the SCS while disclosing only essential operational parameters. This decouples IU identity from spectrum access, prevents cross-request linkage, and mitigates the risk of centralized SCS data leakage. We implement a prototype, and our evaluation shows that IU-GUARD achieves strong privacy guarantees with practical computation and communication overhead, making it suitable for real-time DSS deployment.

title: SPDMA: A Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access in Uplink Channels for 6G ISAC Systems.
abstract: This paper proposes sensing parameter diversity multiple access (SPDMA), a novel air-interface paradigm for the sixth-generation (6G) communications leveraging integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). By exploiting distinct user-specific sensing parameters—distance-induced delays and velocity-induced Doppler shifts—SPDMA enables signal separation without additional resource allocation. A rigorous mathematical model is developed for an uplink orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing scenario in which two users share the same subcarrier. A separation algorithm based on the least-squares criterion is formulated, and its effectiveness is assessed through cross-correlation coefficients and Cramér–Rao bounds. The derivation of bit error rates demonstrates that SPDMA maintains low error levels under various conditions, achieving superior performance compared with conventional multiple access methods in ISAC scenarios. Our analytical results are validated through numerical simulations, which evince that the proposed multiple access technology outperforms conventional methods in terms of bit error rate (BER) and spectral efficiency in doubly dispersive channels.

title: Proactive Channel-Semantic Adaptive JSCC for Robust Image Transmission in High-Mobility OFDM System.
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) has demonstrated strong potential to enhance spectral efficiency and communication robustness by transmitting task-relevant meaning rather than bit-level representations. However, in high-mobility multi-carrier systems, Doppler-induced inter-carrier interference (ICI) and rapidly outdated channel state information (CSI) cause severe degradation in semantic fidelity and reconstruction accuracy. To overcome these challenges, we propose channel–semantic joint adaptive JSCC (CSJA-JSCC), an end-to-end predictive framework that adaptively aligns semantic feature transmission with time-varying channel conditions. The proposed design jointly optimizes a transmitter with semantic-to-subcarrier and power allocation guided by predicted CSI, and a receiver that performs integrated channel estimation and semantic decoding. These modules are jointly trained through a differentiable prediction feedback mechanism, allowing the entire system to co-adapt to channel dynamics and prediction uncertainty. Extensive simulations over high-Doppler channels show that CSJA-JSCC consistently achieves higher peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and semantic similarity than baselines, which demonstrates its effectiveness and robustness in dynamic wireless environments.

title: ACE-HVD: A Multi-Agent Collaboration Approach for Interpretable Hate Video Detection.
abstract: The prevalence of video-sharing platforms also facilitates the propagation of hate content, which poses significant threats to individuals’ mental health and societal harmony. However, current detection methods often rely on black-box models, which lack interpretability—a crucial factor for trustworthy AI. To address this challenge, we propose ACE-HVD, a novel multi-Agent Collaboration framework for interprEtable Hate Video Detection. ACE-HVD designs three Large Multimodal Model (LMM) agents: two agents independently analyze the multimodal content of videos from opposing perspectives, one identifying evidence supporting the presence of hate content and the other identifying evidence supporting its absence. A third agent synthesizes and reconciles these contrasting pieces of evidence to produce a comprehensive explanation. This explanation is then combined with the original multimodal features of the video to produce the final prediction, enabling the detection of subtle hate patterns. Extensive experiments conducted on three video datasets demonstrate that ACE-HVD not only achieves state-of-the-art performance but also provides reliable rationales for its predictions.

title: Hyperbolic Pattern-Based Beam Training in Near-Field Communications.
abstract: Extremely large-scale arrays (XL-arrays) are a promising technology for significantly enhancing spectral efficiency and spatial resolution for future 6G mobile networks. However, XL-arrays considerably extend the near-field region, which is characterized by spherical-wave propagation and may span hundreds of meters. Such a spherical-wave nature of the near field leads to substantially higher beam training overhead compared with conventional far-field methods, as the training complexity scales with the spatial dimensionality. To address this challenge, in this paper, we exploit the geometric structure of the near-field beam pattern and observe that its high-energy region follows a hyperbolic trajectory, along which the optimal codeword resides. Motivated by this geometric insight, we propose a novel three-stage hyperbolic beam training method to effectively reduce beam training overhead. Specifically, in the first stage, the curvature parameter is searched to determine the hyperbolic trajectory that contains the optimal codeword. Then, in the second stage, a constrained search is performed along this hyperbolic path to identify the codeword corresponding to the highest received signal strength. Finally, in the third stage, a localized rectangular fine search is conducted around the selected codeword to compensate for residual deviation and further refine the beam alignment. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method approaches the performance of perfect channel state information-based beamforming while drastically reducing the training overhead.

title: CRB minimization for PASS Assisted ISAC.
abstract: A multiple waveguide PASS assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system is proposed, where the base station (BS) is equipped with transmitting pinching antennas (PAs) and receiving uniform linear array (ULA) antennas. The PASS-transmitting-ULA-receiving (PTUR) BS transmits the communication and sensing signals through the stretched PAs on waveguides and collects the echo sensing signals with the mounted ULA. Based on this configuration, a target sensing Cramér–Rao Bound (CRB) minimization problem is formulated under communication quality-of-service (QoS) constraints, power budget constraints, and PA deployment constraints. An alternating optimization (AO) method is employed to address the formulated non-convex optimization problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PASS assisted ISAC framework achieves superior performance over benchmark schemes.

title: Automatic Network Planning with Digital Radio Twin.
abstract: Network planning seeks to determine base station parameters that maximize coverage and capacity in cellular networks. However, achieving optimal planning remains challenging due to the diversity of deployment scenarios and the significant simulation-to-reality discrepancy. In this paper, we propose \emph{AutoPlan}, a new automatic network planning framework by leveraging digital radio twin (DRT) techniques. We derive the DRT by finetuning the parameters of building materials to reduce the sim-to-real discrepancy based on crowdsource real-world user data. Leveraging the DRT, we design a Bayesian optimization based algorithm to optimize the deployment parameters of base stations efficiently. Using the field measurement from Husker-Net, we extensively evaluate \emph{AutoPlan} under various deployment scenarios, in terms of both coverage and capacity. The evaluation results show that \emph{AutoPlan} flexibly adapts to different scenarios and achieves performance comparable to exhaustive search, while requiring less than 2\% of its computation time.

title: Performance Analysis of RIS-Aided MISO URLLC Systems with Channel Aging and EMI.
abstract: This study investigates a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided multi-user multiple-input single-output ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) system, taking into account the joint effects of channel aging and electromagnetic interference (EMI). We develop a comprehensive model that integrates the impact of EMI and channel aging. Using linear minimum mean square error estimation, we characterize the system’s channel state and evaluate system performance using maximum ratio transmission precoding. We derive a closed-form expression for the URLLC rate based on the use-and-then-forget lower bound and analyze the block error rate (BLER) using Gaussian Chebyshev quadrature approximations. Our findings reveal that, while increasing the number of RIS elements enhances the URLLC rate, it also exacerbates the EMI-related performance loss. Notably, increasing the number of antennas at the base station initially reduces BLER but may exacerbate it when channel aging effects dominate the spatial diversity gains. Furthermore, under a fixed RIS total area, systems with larger RIS elements achieve higher URLLC rates and greater EMI resilience compared to those with a larger number of smaller RIS elements. These insights provide valuable guidance for optimizing RIS-aided URLLC systems in practical urban environments.

title: Applying Fiber-to-the-Room (FTTR) with RFID for Next-Generation Smart Warehouse Networking.
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid network architecture that integrates Fiber-to-the-Room (FTTR) with Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) for next-generation smart warehouse networking. FTTR provides deep fiber penetration to enable precise synchronization of time, phase, and frequency across distributed Sub Fiber Units (SFUs). Based on this capability, we propose a scheme that applies distributed transmit beamforming (DTB) among SFUs for cooperative RFID transmission. The synchronization inherent in FTTR allows cooperative beamforming to improve signal quality, addressing a longstanding limitation of conventional RFID deployments. A field trial was conducted jointly by a leading system vendor and a top service provider. It demonstrated the benefits of the proposed architecture. Results confirm that automated inventory can be achieved with a 100% success rate, and that SFU cooperation significantly enhances coverage and inventory time. These findings indicate that the integration of FTTR and RFID provides a viable pathway toward high-performance networking in digitalized warehouse environments. The network architecture is promising for the industrial Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications.

title: Toward TinyML-Based Robust Visible Light Positioning under Aging LEDs.
abstract: Due to the dual functionality of lighting and localization, received signal strength (RSS) based visible light positioning (VLP) has become a promising high-precision indoor positioning method in industrial environments by leveraging pervasively available lighting infrastructure. However, its widespread deployment is hindered by two key challenges: 1) the need for densely sampled fingerprint datasets, and 2) performance degradation due to LED aging in a long-lasting deployment. To address these limitations, we develop a data-efficient VLP method with an online calibration strategy that automatically compensates for gradual light intensity decay caused by LED aging, maintaining robustness without manual re-fingerprinting. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains centimeter-level precision across varying LED usage durations. A lightweight on-device model deployed on the Raspberry Pi Pico microcontroller achieves 1.62 cm mean positioning error with 8.39 ms inference latency, demonstrating the practicality of our approach for long-lasting indoor positioning in industrial and IoT scenarios. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/joeywli/VLP.

title: Information-Theoretic Capacity of Decentralized Secure Aggregation with Groupwise Keys under Collusion.
abstract: This paper investigates decentralized secure aggregation (DSA) under the presence of groupwise keys and potential user collusion. In a fully-connected network of K users, each user holds a private input and aims to compute the sum of all inputs without revealing additional information, even when colluding with up to T users. We focus on the symmetric groupwise key setting, where each group of G users shares an independent key. We characterize the capacity region by specifying the minimum communication and groupwise key rates required for secure aggregation. We show that DSA is infeasible when G = 1 or G > K −T − 1. In the feasible regime, securely computing one symbol of the sum requires each user to transmit at least one symbol, and each groupwise key should contain at least $(K - T - 2)/{\binom {K - T - 1} {G }} $ independent symbols. Our results establish the fundamental limits of DSA and provide insights for designing secure and efficient aggregation protocols in decentralized learning systems.

title: Asynchronous Satellite Federated Learning with Intermittent Ground-to-Satellite Links.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate federated learning (FL) in space–ground networks composed of large-scale low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites equipped with communication, computation, and storage capabilities. Satellite federated learning (SatFL) faces distinct challenges due to the highly dynamic network topology, heterogeneous data distributions, and varying computational resources. On the one hand, the sparse and time-varying coverage of ground-to–satellite links (GSLs) makes model aggregation at ground stations intermittent and incomplete. On the other hand, asynchronous connectivity and statistical heterogeneity introduce inherent model drift, hindering global convergence. To address these challenges, we propose GSL asynchrony-aware satellite federated learning (GaaSFL), an algorithm that manages aggregation among currently connected satellites while mitigating drift through staleness-aware constraints in both local training and global updates. Extensive simulations demonstrate that GaaSFL significantly reduces the negative effects of intermittent GSLs and data heterogeneity, achieving faster convergence and higher predictive accuracy compared with baseline methods.

title: Performance Analysis of Flexible Duplex Inter-Satellite Links in LEO Networks.
abstract: This paper investigates energy-efficient inter-satellite communication in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) networks, where satellites exchange both buffered and newly generated data through half-duplex inter-satellite links (ISLs). Due to orbital motion and interference-prone directional asymmetry, the achievable ISL capacities in opposite directions vary dynamically, leading to inefficient utilization under conventional fixed or alternating duplex modes. To address this, we propose a Flexible Duplex (FlexD) scheme that adaptively selects the ISL transmission direction in each slot to maximize instantaneous end-to-end sky-to-ground throughput, jointly accounting for ISL quality, downlink conditions, and queue backlogs. A unified analytical framework is developed that transforms the bottleneck rate structure into an equivalent SINR domain, enabling closed-form derivations of throughput outage probability and energy efficiency under deterministic ISLs and Rician satellite-to-ground fading. The analysis reveals distinct operating regions governed by ISL and backlog constraints and provides tractable bounds for ergodic rate and energy efficiency. Numerical results confirm that FlexD achieves higher reliability and up to 30% improvement in energy efficiency compared with conventional half- and full-duplex schemes under realistic inter-satellite interference conditions.

title: Blind Channel Estimation Based Positioning Enhancement for ACO-OFDM Integrated Visible Light Communication and Positioning.
abstract: The integrated visible light communication and positioning (VLCP) allows simultaneous communications and the received signal strength (RSS)-based positioning, using identical signals. However, light emitting diode (LED)’s limited bandwidth and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) channels cause inter-symbol interference (ISI), having significant impact on the RSS-based positioning for VLCP systems. Therefore, we propose a blind symmetry-based channel estimation (BSCE) approach to realize high-performance communications and high-accuracy positioning, requiring no pilot. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first work to investigate blind channel estimation to enhance the RSS-based positioning for asymmetrically clipped optical-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (ACO-OFDM) VLCP systems. The symmetry structure of ACO-OFDM signals in time domain is utilized to estimate LED’s limited bandwidth, line-of-sight (LoS) and NLoS channels, separately. This is different from the previous channel estimation methods that only realize the purpose of communications, estimating LED’s limited bandwidth, LoS and NLoS channels together. Thus, the proposed BSCE approach enhances the RSS-based positioning accuracy much higher than the previous channel estimation works, as the RSS variation caused by LED’s limited bandwidth and NLoS is mitigated. Simulation results show that the proposed BSCE approach can effectively mitigate the impact of LED’s limited bandwidth and NLoS channels on positioning, and provide positioning performance higher than existing channel estimation methods.

title: Energy Harvesting and Reflection Control in Self-Sustainable RIS: A Dynamic Activation Design.
abstract: Self-sustainable reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (S-RISs) integrate energy-harvesting (EH) capabilities into traditional RIS architectures, eliminating the need for external power wiring and facilitating large-scale deployment. However, existing S-RISs often suffer from inefficient EH operation, as the RIS can assist communication only after harvesting sufficient energy to activate all reflecting elements (REs), thereby reducing communication efficiency. To address this issue, we propose a dynamic activation design that allows the S-RIS to adaptively activate REs and assign phase shifts or amplitude amplification based on the currently harvested energy. This flexible design shortens EH duration and enhances reflection efficiency. A rate-maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize the EH duration and RIS reflection coefficients. To solve it efficiently, an ℓ1-norm relaxation combined with fractional programming is employed to realize dynamic activation, followed by an RE reassignment procedure that determines whether each RE operates in active or passive mode. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed dynamic activation strategy effectively balances EH and reflection durations, significantly improving the achievable rate of S-RIS-assisted wireless systems.

title: Robust Edge Inference with Graph Neural Networks under Channel Aging.
abstract: One of the key missions of sixth-generation (6G) networks is to deploy artificial intelligence (AI) at the network edge. The widely recognized paradigm, edge inference, is envisioned to enable diverse IoT applications such as autonomous driving, industrial automation, and human activity recognition. However, its efficient deployment is hindered by two major challenges: 1) the communication bottleneck from uploading high-dimensional features under limited resources, and 2) performance degradation due to outdated channel estimation, known as channel aging. This work addresses these challenges to enable robust edge inference via efficient resource allocation. In particular, we theoretically characterize the effects of channel aging on end-to-end (E2E) performance by linking inference accuracy to a surrogate metric, termed effective discriminant gain. An efficient resource allocation strategy adaptive to channel aging is realized by leveraging the permutation invariance of a graph neural network (GNN) to maximize the proposed surrogate metric. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework over benchmarks that either assume perfect CSI or employ uniform resource allocation.

title: SGCNet: Scenario-Generalizable CSI Feedback Compression via Residual Vector Quantization.
abstract: The rapidly increasing number of antennas in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems has significantly raised the feedback burden of channel state information (CSI), highlighting the need for efficient CSI compression. While recent learning-based methods outperform classical approaches such as compressive sensing in both accuracy and efficiency, they typically require dedicated models for different channel scenarios, substantially increasing training complexity and deployment cost. This paper introduces SGCNet (Scenario-Generalizable CSI Compression Network), a neural network designed for scenario-generalizable CSI feedback compression. SGCNet employs multi-stage residual vector quantization (RVQ) to learn stage-wise codebooks, which are shared between the user equipment (UE) and the base station (BS). By composing multiple codewords as building blocks, the latent representation is reconstructed in a coarse-to-fine manner from the sum of stage-specific codewords. This approach produces a regularized representation that demonstrates increased robustness to scenario shifts. Extensive simulations indicate that SGCNet attains superior reconstruction fidelity with low computational complexity. In particular, under cross-scenario evaluation at η = 1/16, SGCNet trained exclusively on the COST2100 Indoor and Outdoor scenarios sustains a worst-case NMSE of −8.83 dB on ten unseen DeepMIMO scenarios, whereas state-of-the-art baselines such as AiANet and TransNet degrade to −0.94 dB and −0.98 dB, respectively.

title: FALCON++: A Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection and Localization Framework for Resilient O-RAN Deployments.
abstract: Fault detection is a critical problem in Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) observability, but the availability of labeled fault data is extremely limited, and enumerating all possible fault scenarios is costly and often infeasible. Therefore, it is essential to rely on normal network behavior to enable effective fault detection. In this work, we propose FALCON++, a tailored semi-supervised anomaly detection and localization framework. Specifically, we use a specialized contextual autoencoder that fuses feature-wise gating and hierarchical temporal encoding for the effective reconstruction of normal network behavior. Furthermore, we combine a causal decoder with residual skip connections to improve robustness to data deemed anomalous due to their higher reconstruction error. FALCON++ also addresses scalability issues by shifting from a monolithic system model to CU-DU pairwise inferencing. Through experimental results on synthetic faults generated using STRESS-NG and TC, we show that FALCON++ achieves a high-precision and high-recall operating point with an F1-score of 0.77, thereby enabling anomaly detection and localization.

title: Transfer to Sky: Unveil Low-Altitude Route-Level Radio Maps via Ground Crowdsourced Data.
abstract: The expansion of the low-altitude economy is contingent on reliable cellular connectivity for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). A key challenge in pre-flight planning is predicting communication link quality along proposed and pre-defined routes, a task hampered by sparse measurements that render existing radio map methods ineffective. This paper introduces a transfer learning framework for high-fidelity route-level radio map prediction. Our key insight is to leverage abundant crowdsourced ground signals as auxiliary supervision. To bridge the significant domain gap between ground and aerial data and address spatial sparsity, our framework learns general propagation priors from simulation, performs adversarial alignment of the feature spaces, and is fine-tuned on limited real UAV measurements. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset from Meituan show that our method achieves over 50% higher accuracy in predicting Route RSRP compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Resource Allocation of Cooperative ISAC Networks with Codeword Splitting and Data-Aided Sensing.
abstract: Efficient resource allocation in wireless networks is evolving with the advent of the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) paradigm, a key enabler for systems requiring high-quality data transmission and sensing capabilities. A comprehensive investigation of resource allocation in ISAC networks is therefore of paramount importance. In this paper, we optimize the joint sensing and communication (S&C) performance of an cooperative ISAC network with broadcast communication and relative localization. We establish a theoretical model for this ISAC network, with the transmission capacity and the relative squared position error bound (rSPEB) introduced as the network S&C metrics, and present the resource allocation problem. In particular, we develop a cooperative ISAC scheme based on codeword splitting (CS) and data–aided (DA) sensing. In this cooperative scheme, we propose an optimization algorithm to solve the resource allocation problem. Numerical results demonstrate the performance gain of joint S&C resource allocation over S&C decoupled designs.

title: Enabling Flying MIMO System with Low-Altitude UAV Swarm for Near-Field Communication.
abstract: By leveraging the intrinsic three-dimensional (3D) mobility and swarm cooperation, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm serves as an ideal platform for implementing flying multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system. Compared to existing terrestrial MIMO and massive MIMO systems, flying MIMO system facilitates an extremely large-scale array aperture, and thus the conventional far-field uniform plane wave (UPW) model may no longer be valid for aerial-to-ground links. This paper considers the near-field communication enabled by flying MIMO under the non-uniform spherical wave (NUSW) model, with a focus on the dual impact of UAV swarm trajectory on channel amplitude and phase. Subject to practical constraints on UAVs, we formulate a general optimization problem to maximize the minimum average communication rate over user equipments (UEs), by jointly optimizing the receive beamforming for all UEs and the 3D UAV swarm trajectory. Subsequently, an alternating optimization algorithm is proposed to efficiently tackle the highly non-convex optimization problem. Simulation results demonstrate the significant performance gains of the proposed scheme compared with the benchmark schemes.

title: Delay Alignment Modulation for Secure ISAC Systems.
abstract: This paper introduces delay-alignment modulation (DAM) for secure integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). Due to the broadcast nature of multi-user downlinks, communications are vulnerable to eavesdropping. DAM applies controlled per-path symbol delays at the transmitter to coherently align the multipath components at the intended user, enhancing the received signal power, while simultaneously creating delay misalignment at the eavesdropper (Eve). To mitigate sensing degradation caused by multipath propagation, we propose a two-stage protocol that first estimates the angle and then the delay of the line-of-sight (LoS) path after suppressing multipath interference. We derive the secrecy spectral efficiency (SSE) and the Cramer-Rao (CRB) of the target delay. Finally, we develop a path-based zero-forcing (ZF) precoding framework and formulate a max-min SSE design under CRB and power constraints. Simulation results show DAM significantly outperforms the strongest-path (SP) benchmark in terms of SSE, while meeting sensing requirements, since intentional delay alignment at legitimate users degrades reception at Eve.

title: Intelligent Trajectory Planning and Channel Selection of Interference-Aware Multi-UAV.
abstract: The deployment of multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) may lead to excessive congestion of spectrum resources, further resulting in mutual interferences. Therefore, this article investigates an online decision-making trajectory planning and channel selection system for interference-aware multiple UAVs. To deal with the uncertainty of interference and the dynamics of UAVs, the markov decision process is modeled for the combinatorial optimization problems, and then an interference-aware trajectory planning and channel selection (IA-TPCS) algorithm is proposed based on multi-agent actorcritic (MAAC). Considering the sparsity of interference rewards, the IA-TPCS algorithm utilizes the prioritized experience replay (PER) mechanism to help propagate rewards faster and optimize learning strategies. Simulation results show that the proposed IA-TPCS algorithm outperforms other benchmark algorithms in terms of learning strategies such as accumulative rewards, trajectory length, and network communication utility.

title: Cooperative Distributed Memory AMP Detection for Oversampled Random Multiplexing Systems.
abstract: Doubly-selective fading continues to challenge wireless communication in high-mobility scenarios. Random multiplexing (RM) with approximate message passing (AMP)-type detectors address it while achieving maximum a posteriori bit-error rate performance. In this paper, we consider oversampled RM systems to further improve the performance. To overcome the limitations of conventional oversampling detectors, including their centralized processing of high-dimensional data and need for noise whitening, we propose a cooperative distributed memory AMP (CD-MAMP) algorithm. We derive the input-output relationship for the distributed oversampled RM and analyze the correlation induced by the shared random transform matrix and the oversampling noise. By leveraging the correlation, we design the CD-MAMP that consists of an inner-iteration cross-domain memory AMP (MAMP) and an outer-iteration optimal fusion strategy. Simulation results show that RM outperforms other modulation schemes. CD-MAMP outperforms both the centralized MAMP and the Nyquist-sampling detectors. After sufficient inner iterations, only one outer iteration is needed to achieve nearly identical gains, reducing communication overhead.

title: Cross-Modal Semantic Communication for Heterogeneous Collaborative Perception.
abstract: Collaborative perception, an emerging paradigm in autonomous driving, has been introduced to mitigate the limitations of single-vehicle systems, such as limited sensor range and occlusion. To improve the robustness of inter-vehicle data sharing, semantic communication has recently further been integrated into collaborative perception systems to enhance overall performance. However, practical deployment of such systems is challenged by the heterogeneity of sensors across different connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs). This diversity in perceptual data complicates the design of a unified communication framework and impedes the effective fusion of shared information. To address this challenge, we propose a novel cross-modal semantic communication (CMSC) framework to facilitate effective collaboration among CAVs with disparate sensor configurations. Specifically, the framework first transforms heterogeneous perceptual features from different sensor modalities into a unified and standardized semantic space. Subsequently, encoding, transmission, and decoding are performed within this semantic space, enabling seamless and effective information fusion. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CMSC achieves significantly stronger perception performance than existing methods, particularly in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regimes.

title: Digital Twin Aided Millimeter Wave MIMO: Site-Specific Beam Codebook Learning.
abstract: Learning site-specific beams that adapt to the deployment environment, interference sources, and hardware imperfections can lead to noticeable performance gains in coverage, data rate, and power saving, among other interesting advantages. This learning process, however, typically requires a large number of active interactions/iterations, which limits its practical feasibility and leads to excessive overhead. To address these challenges, we propose a digital twin aided codebook learning framework, where a site-specific digital twin is leveraged to generate synthetic channel data for codebook learning. We also propose to learn separate codebooks for line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight users, leveraging the geometric information provided by the digital twin. Simulation results demonstrate that the codebook learned from the digital twin can adapt to the environment geometry and user distribution, leading to high received signal-to-noise ratio performance. Moreover, we identify the ray-tracing accuracy as the most critical factor in digital twin fidelity that impacts the learned codebook performance.

title: Low-Complexity Digital Twin for CSI Acquisition in MIMO Communications.
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications will continue to be a cornerstone of modern wireless networks, thanks to the spatial multiplexing and beamforming gains enabled by large antenna arrays. However, acquiring precise downlink channel state information (CSI)—essential for effective precoding for large-scale antenna systems—involves substantial signaling overhead. In this paper, we propose a CSI acquisition framework that leverages digital twin to generate user-specific channel prior at the base-station, and reduces the CSI acquisition overhead. To achieve a low-complexity operation, we propose a multi-tiered digital twin architecture and complexity reduction methods, which reduce the ray-tracing runtime with minimal performance loss. Through comprehensive evaluations in an urban scenario, we demonstrate that the proposed framework can effectively reduce CSI acquisition overhead, and decrease the digital twin compute requirement by 56% while maintaining healthy cell coverage and spectral efficiency at the user.

title: Generative Decoding of Compressed CSI for MIMO Precoding Design.
abstract: Massive MIMO systems can enhance spectral and energy efficiency, but they require accurate channel state information (CSI), which becomes costly as the number of antennas increases. While machine learning (ML) autoencoders show promise for CSI reconstruction and reducing feedback overhead, they introduce new challenges with standardization, interoperability, and backward compatibility. Also, the significant data collection needed for training makes real-world deployment difficult. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose an ML-based, decoder-only solution for compressed CSI. Our approach uses a standardized encoder for CSI compression on the user side and a site-specific generative decoder at the base station to refine the compressed CSI using environmental knowledge. We introduce two training schemes for the generative decoder: An end-to-end method and a two-stage method, both utilizing a goal-oriented loss function. Furthermore, we reduce the data collection overhead by using a site-specific digital twin to generate synthetic CSI data for training. Our simulations highlight the effectiveness of this solution across various feedback overhead regimes.

title: DRL-Enhanced Intelligent Frame Aggregation and Rate Selection for Next Generation Wi-Fi Networks.
abstract: The IEEE 802.11 family continues to evolve to provide high throughput and reliable connectivity in dense indoor deployments. However, widely deployed rate-control algorithms such as MinstrelHT react slowly to rapid channel variations and intermittent interference, and existing learning-based designs often exhibit limited generalization and value overestimation. This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning framework that jointly selects the A-MPDU aggregation length and transmission rate for IEEE 802.11ax uplinks. The agent observes link-quality and contention indicators and outputs joint decisions at each transmission opportunity. We adopt an enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) formulation with a multi-dimensional action space and train the agent using realistic indoor ray-tracing channel models. The problem is modeled as a Markov decision process (MDP) with a reward that captures the throughput– latency trade-off. Simulation results in ns3-ai show that the proposed method achieves higher throughput and lower one-hop delay than MinstrelHT and Thompson Sampling in both static and dynamic scenarios, and it converges within 150–200 training episodes.

title: Continuous Angular Power Spectrum Recovery from Channel Covariance via Chebyshev Polynomials.
abstract: This paper proposes a Chebyshev polynomial expansion framework for the challenging problem of continuous angular power spectrum (APS) recovery from channel covariance. By exploiting the orthogonality of Chebyshev polynomials, we derive an exact series representation of the covariance matrix, enabling the inherently ill-posed APS inversion to be reformulated as a finite linear regression problem through truncation. We show that the truncation error is governed by the tail coefficients of the APS’s Chebyshev series and decays rapidly with increasing APS smoothness. By further enforcing the non-negativity of the APS at the zeros of the Chebyshev polynomial, we develop a computationally efficient convex formulation for APS estimation. Simulation results demonstrate the robustness and high accuracy of the proposed framework across a variety of APS models.

title: Joint Beamforming for Active RIS-Aided Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Power Transfer.
abstract: This paper proposes a promising framework of multi-functional service incorporating single sensing target (ST), multiple information receivers (IRs), and multiple energy receivers (ERs) in an active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided integrated sensing, communication, and power transfer (ISCPT) system. In the proposed system, we aim to maximize the received radar signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) by jointly optimizing the transmit beamforming at the multi-functional base station (MFBS), the coefficients of active RIS, and the radar receive filter coefficients, while meet the requirements of signal-to-interference-plus-noise-ratio (SINR) for IRs and energy harvesting (EH) for ERs. The formulated problem is tackled by developing an efficient alternating optimization (AO) algorithm combined with Schur complement and majorization-minimization (MM) techniques. Finally, the numerical results reveal that active RIS is remarkably superior to passive RIS for ISCPT systems by over 40 dB, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: Dynamic Weighted Graph Partitioning for Resource Allocation in Massive MIMO LEO Satellite Communication.
abstract: Low earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations with massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology are poised to deliver global broadband connectivity, but face a critical challenge in managing severe co-channel interference, which is fundamentally a computationally complex resource allocation problem. To address this, we propose a novel framework that quantifies inter-user interference based on their angular separation, derived from geographical coordinates. This angle-based interference model enables us to reformulate the allocation task as a maximum L-cut problem on a complete graph, where users are vertices and dynamic edge weights represent their symmetric interference cost. Building on this graph formulation, we introduce the dynamic weighted graph partitioning (DWGP) algorithm, which uses a feedback loop to refine these weights based on physical-layer performance, progressively steering the user partition towards the global optimum. Extensive simulations validate our approach, showing that the DWGP algorithm achieves near-optimal performance, substantially outperforms conventional greedy methods, and exhibits rapid convergence.

title: A Resource Allocation Strategy Based on Static Beam Layout and Dynamic Auction Mechanisms for LEO Satellite Communication Systems.
abstract: In low earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems, achieving efficient and equitable resource allocation has become a critical research issue. This paper proposes a resource allocation strategy based on static beam layout and dynamic auction mechanisms. After user grouping and beam layering based on geometric location and link budget, the strategy achieves dynamic balancing of hierarchical resources through adaptive optimization of layer shares and user migration. Within the beam, user demands, channel conditions, and priorities are quantified as bidding weights. An iterative auction process is proposed to maximize the overall system utility by integrating a three-stage algorithm, which comprises proportional fairness allocation, equitable compensation, and max-min fairness-based residual allocation. Simulation results demonstrate that compared to traditional methods, the strategy proposed in this paper exhibits significant advantages in terms of increased total throughput, enhanced user fairness, and improved quality of service (QoS) assurance.

title: LoRaWAN vs. IEEE 802.11p: A Reproducible Comparative framework under Realistic V2I Conditions.
abstract: Today, the main communication technologies driving Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) are IEEE 802.11p and 5G NR-V2X, both designed for high-throughput, low-latency vehicular applications. However, these technologies face coverage and cost limitations, particularly in rural and low-infrastructure environments. In contrast, Low Power Wide Area Networks (LPWAN)—and especially LoRaWAN—offer long-range, low-energy connectivity but remain insufficiently explored in dynamic vehicular contexts. This paper presents a rigorous and reproducible comparative study of LoRaWAN and IEEE 802.11p under realistic Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) conditions. Using a unified NS-3 framework coupled with synchronized SUMO mobility traces and a calibrated HybridBuildings propagation model, both technologies are evaluated within identical spatial, temporal, and physical contexts. Results show that LoRaWAN maintains a high packet delivery ratio (up to 85% within a range of 4 km) and strong resilience under mobility (up to 72 km/h), making it suitable for delay-tolerant periodic V2I communications. Conversely, IEEE 802.11p achieves sub10 ms latency and higher throughput but experiences sharp reliability degradation beyond 800 m under non-line-of-sight conditions. The proposed framework and the open simulation dataset establish a reproducible foundation for future research on adaptive radio access and cross-technology optimization in vehicular networks.

title: Angular Metasurface Design Paradigm Based on Constitutive Parameters.
abstract: In this work, we propose a universal "angular performance-constitutive parameter-structure" design paradigm for angular metasurface design. Theoretical formulas are derived to establish the analytical relationship between angular performance and constitutive parameters and to obtain the physical boundary of angular performance. Then, based on the known mapping between metasurface resonators and their constitutive parameters in the Drude-Lorentz dispersion, periodic folded resonators are employed to stimulate the desired dispersion response for pre-calculated constitutive parameters, thereby achieving a metasurface with an angular bandwidth of 30° and angular selectivity of 1.6. The good agreement between the calculated and simulated results demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed design paradigm of angular metasurfaces.

title: An RGB-Optical Flow Fusion Scheme for Proactive Vehicle Accident Risk Prediction.
abstract: Driver distraction is one of the primary causes of road traffic accidents, so there is an urgent need for new approaches to reduce such accidents. With the widespread adoption of low-cost dashcams, researchers develop dashcam-based vehicle risk prediction methods to anticipate high-risk situations earlier and warn drivers in time. However, vehicle accident prediction methods based on images and depth maps fail to effectively capture the motion characteristics of moving objects, leading to low prediction accuracy. Meanwhile, existing RGB-optical flow based methods do not dynamically adjust the weights of image features and object motion features, which restricts the early warning window. To address this limitation, we propose the RGB-Optical Flow Fusion Scheme for Proactive Vehicle Accident Risk Prediction (ProVAR) that aligns and dynamically fuses appearance features from RGB images with motion features from optical flow images. Specifically, we design a Cross-Modal Feature Fusion (CMFF) module that models interactions between appearance and motion features and performs effective fusion. On the Dashcam Accident Dataset (DAD), our scheme achieves 90.10% Average Precision and 4.47 seconds mean Time-to-Accident, outperforming existing methods and supporting onboard deployment in intelligent vehicles for earlier warnings.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Beamforming Design in UAV-enabled NOMA ISAC System.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) enabled non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) empowered integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where the UAV is introduced as the ISAC base station providing services to multiple users employing NOMA, while communication signals is simultaneously exploited for target sensing. To maximum the communication sum-rate while satisfying the maximum Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) requirement, a beamforming design problem is formulated. The optimization problem is inherently non-convex, which makes it challenging to find the optimal solution through traditional optimization algorithms. To address this challenge, we adopt an online decision-making framework based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to solve the problem. Numerical results indicate that the proposed NOMA-ISAC outperforms conventional ISAC in terms of sum-rate.

title: Parameter-efficient Large AI Model Co-inference at Multi-cluster Edge Networks.
abstract: The increasing scale and computational demands of large artificial intelligence models (LAIMs) pose significant challenges for efficient inference among distributed devices in resource-constrained environments. This paper presents a multi-cluster LAIM co-inference framework in which an edge server, equipped with multiple graphics processing units (GPUs), coordinates user clusters to fulfill inference requests. We assume that devices within each cluster capture data from different perspectives, and then use on-device lightweight LAIMs to generate local features. The edge server collects and fuses these features to produce a more accurate inference result. To capture the fundamental trade-off between model pruning and co-inference performance under multi-device scenarios, we theoretically characterize the impact of pruning ratio and device contribution based on the rate-distortion analysis and partial information decomposition. Guided by the analysis, we then jointly optimize the pruning ratio, task scheduling, and transmit power to minimize inference distortion subject to the latency, energy, and capacity constraints. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior performance in comparison to existing baselines, offering improved inference quality and resource efficiency in multi-cluster edge environments.

title: Dual-Branch Residual U-Net for Phase Noise Compensation in Terahertz Inter-Satellite Communications.
abstract: Inter-satellite communication (ISC) is essential for future 6G space-air-ground integrated networks, providing seamless global connectivity. The terahertz (THz) band (0.1-10 THz) offers ultra-wide bandwidth for high-throughput ISC links but suffers from severe phase noise and multipath distortion caused by hardware limitations and spacecraft structures. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a dual-branch residual U-Net (DBR-UNet) for joint phase noise and multipath compensation in THz ISC systems. The proposed DBR-UNet employs a residual learning framework with a joint loss function to effectively recover clean signals while estimating the corresponding noise components. Simulation results at 130 GHz and 1.02 THz verify that the proposed DBR-UNet consistently outperforms conventional LS-BEM, LMMSE, and DNN-based approaches, yielding lower bit error rates (BERs) and enhanced robustness under increasingly severe phase noise conditions. The optimal weighting coefficients are found at λ = 0.1 for 130 GHz and λ =0.3 for 1.02 THz, respectively.

title: Customized User Plane Processing via Code Generating AI Agents for Next Generation Mobile Networks.
abstract: Generative AI is envisioned to have a crucial impact on next generation mobile networking, making the sixth generation (6G) system considerably more autonomous, flexible, and adaptive than its predecessors. By leveraging their natural language processing and code generation capabilities, AI agents enable novel interactions and services between networks and vertical applications. A particularly promising and interesting use case is the customization of connectivity services for vertical applications by generating new customized processing blocks based on text-based service requests. More specifically, AI agents are able to generate code for a new function block that handles user plane traffic, allowing it to inspect and decode a protocol data unit (PDU) and perform specified actions as requested by the application. In this study, we investigate the code generation problem for generating such customized processing blocks on-demand. We evaluate various factors affecting the accuracy of the code generation process in this context, including model selection, prompt design, and the provision of a code template for the agent to utilize. Our findings indicate that AI agents are capable of generating such blocks with the desired behavior on-demand under suitable conditions. We believe that exploring the code generation for network-specific tasks is a very interesting problem for 6G and beyond, enabling networks to achieve a new level of customization by generating new capabilities on-demand.

title: Stacked Flexible Intelligent Metasurface Design for Multi-User Wireless Communications.
abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) have recently emerged as an effective solution for next-generation wireless networks. A SIM comprises multiple metasurface layers that enable signal processing directly in the wave domain. Moreover, recent advances in flexible metamaterials have highlighted the potential of flexible intelligent metasurfaces (FIMs), which can be physically morphed to enhance communication performance. In this paper, we propose a stacked flexible intelligent metasurface (SFIM)-based communication system for the first time, where each metasurface layer is deformable to improve the system's performance. We first present the system model, including the transmit and receive signal models as well as the channel model, and then formulate an optimization problem to maximize the system sum rate under constraints on the transmit power budget, morphing distance, and the unit-modulus condition of the meta-atom responses. To solve this problem, we develop an alternating optimization framework based on the gradient projection method. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SFIM-based system achieves significant performance gains compared to its rigid SIM counterpart.

title: Securing Smart Grids against PSSE FDI attacks.
abstract: Cyberattacks such as false data injection (FDI) attack have increased substantially following the digitalization of electric power and energy systems (EPES) and smart grids (SGs). Resilient protection measures are necessitated for these critical infrastructures due to the direct, immediate, and serious effects of FDI, such as generators tripping, transmission lines overloading, and cascading blackouts that cause equipment damage, financial losses, and threat to life. In this paper, we present a deep learning-enabled (DL) in-network FDI attack mitigation strategy using extended berkley packet filtering (eBPF)-based network programmability. Complex algorithms must be approximated to reduced instruction set when implementing cybersecurity solutions in eBPF, however, these approximations lead to precision losses. We present an architecture that integrates non-BPF deep leaning-based network functions into the eBPF data processing pipeline. For an EPES use case, we test the architecture on a proof-of-concept. A stealthy and sparse FDI attack is modelled on the power state system estimations (PSSE). To counter these attacks, we propose a feasible feature extraction and a robust detection and mitigation mechanism. In comparison to the legacy operational technology software-defined networking (OTSDN), performance evaluation reveals a reduction in detection latency of 54.6% and accuracy of up to 99% and F1–score of 0.93. In compliance with society’s growing reliance on the electricity grid network’s continuity, the proposed methodology mitigates disruptive impacts of FDI attacks in a timely manner.

title: Impact of Topological Parameters on the Super C+L-Band Optical Networks Throughput via Machine Learning.
abstract: A possible medium-term solution to mitigate the capacity crunch in optical networks is the use of Super C+L-band transmission. Network throughput is a key metric for analyzing the performance of such networks. However, evaluating this metric is a complex task due to the interplay between physical and network layer aspects, with additional complications arising from the presence of SRS (stimulated Raman scattering). To address these challenges, we propose a machine learning (ML) approach to evaluate the impact of network topological parameters on both Shannon and real throughput. The approach relies on an artificial neural network (ANN) model, whose predictions are interpreted using the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method to identify the importance of various topological parameters. The analysis provides valuable insights for designing future ultra-high-capacity optical networks.

title: A Reinforcement Learning Approach for Dynamic Latency-Energy Trade-off in Multi-UAV Mobile Edge Computing Systems.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-aided Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) systems have emerged as a promising solution for providing computational services in dynamic environments with user mobility and intermittent connectivity. However, achieving an optimal balance between latency and energy consumption remains a fundamental challenge in these systems. Conventional approaches typically rely on fixed weighting parameters that fail to adapt to varying network conditions and available resources. In this paper, we propose an intelligent framework that leverages Q-learning to dynamically adjust the latency-energy trade-off parameter during operation. Our solution incorporates this adaptive mechanism within a Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) optimization scheme that simultaneously addresses UAV trajectory control, task offloading decisions, user association, and communication-computation resource allocation. Extensive simulations with realistic user mobility traces show that the proposed method significantly outperforms static schemes, achieving lower latency and energy consumption while maintaining a high offloading ratio. These results demonstrate the potential of our adaptive framework to enable intelligent and flexible MEC systems capable of meeting the dynamic and heterogeneous demands of future wireless networks.

title: Neural Network-Based Dynamic Antenna Weight Optimization Scheme for Robust Coverage Fixation in Multi-Cell HAPS Systems.
abstract: High-altitude platform stations (HAPSs) are widely recognized as key enablers of seamless global coverage across space–air–ground networks. Although a single HAPS can offer a coverage radius of up to 100 km, accommodating large numbers of users requires increasing its service-link capacity, which in turn motivates the development of multi-cell architectures with universal frequency reuse. In multi-cell systems, the service-link capacity is highly sensitive to the cell configuration, and the aircraft’s motion and attitude variations shift the cell shapes projected onto the ground (footprints), causing frequent handovers. To address this issue, we propose a neural network (NN)-based beamforming method that explicitly accounts for the implemented array antenna architecture rather than relying on beam-pattern models and directly optimizes the antenna weights to jointly configure the cells, allocate inter-cell power, and maintain fixed footprints. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves a higher footprint-fixation rate than conventional beamforming methods and improves the median spectral efficiency by at least 21% in representative HAPS operating environments.

title: AIRTwin: AI-Assisted Real-Time Digital Twin for Proactive High-Fidelity Radio Map Prediction in Vehicular Networks.
abstract: Reactive radio map construction methods generate outdated and invalid results for highly dynamic vehicular networks. This paper presents a real-time digital twin (DT), called AIRTwin, for proactive radio map prediction in vehicular networks. To enable proactive radio map prediction, vehicles’ trajectories are predicted, and ray tracing is performed for predicted positions ahead of time. 3D buildings, roads, and vehicles are considered to represent the real-world environment and objects. The two main engines of the AIRTwin are vehicle trajectory prediction and radio map prediction. A Transformer-based AI model is designed for vehicle trajectory prediction, and continual learning is performed online to fine-tune the model. The radio map prediction engine is powered by NVIDIA Sionna, an open-source library for link-level simulations. Predicted trajectories are integrated with 3D vehicles, representing realistic mobility of vehicles. For performance evaluation, the AIRTwin is compared with ground truth DT, a state-of-the-art proactive DT for vehicular networks called PRISM DT, and the stochastic 3GPP channel model. The evaluated parameters were the path gain, root mean square error (RMSE), latency, and time. Numerical results and visualized online radio maps show the impact of vehicles on wave propagation and the advantage of the AIRTwin over PRISM DT and the 3GPP model, where the AIRTwin provides 7.23 dB and 11.62 dB lower RMSE compared to PRISM DT and 3GPP, respectively. Furthermore, the simulation results show that while AIRTwin increases the accuracy compared to PRISM DT and the 3GPP model, it maintains real-time performance.

title: Stochastic Analysis of Low Earth Orbit Satellite Connectivity for Land Transportation.
abstract: This paper develops a tractable stochastic-geometric framework for analyzing low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite connectivity to ground users moving along deterministic terrestrial routes. Satellites are distributed on multiple inclined circular orbits with random right ascensions, while users follow real-world trajectories extracted from geographic data. A geometry-driven two-stage association policy is proposed, whereby the network initially selects the closest orbital plane and then associates the terminal with the nearest visible satellite on that plane. The analysis yields exact expressions for the line-of-sight serving distance, coverage probability, and ergodic capacity in a noise-limited downlink scenario. Numerical results, validated via Monte Carlo simulations, demonstrate excellent agreement with the analytical model and reveal how orbital inclination, constellation density, and user latitude jointly shape performance. Route-based case studies over example Helsinki-Kolari and Paris-Dakar corridors highlight the fundamentally different roles of inclination at high and mid latitudes, providing design insights for inclination selection in next-generation LEO constellations.

title: Mutual Coupling-Aware 3D Non-Stationary Channel Modeling for TRIS Transceiver Systems.
abstract: Transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (TRIS) are regarded as a promising solution for energy-efficient multi-stream transceivers in next-generation wireless communication systems, yet accurate channel modeling remains a significant challenge. Recent studies have shown that large arraybased communication channels exhibit near-field propagation characteristics and non-stationary behavior in both spatial and temporal domains. Moreover, the mutual coupling (MC) effect among array elements has a significant impact on channel characteristics. In this paper, an MC-aware three-dimensional (3D) non-stationary channel modeling framework is proposed for TRIS transceiver systems in the near-field regime. A visible-region-based clustering evolution approach is developed to capture spatiotemporal non-stationarity, while multiport network theory is employed to characterize the MC effects in TRIS arrays. Results of the spatial cross-correlation function (SCCF) and temporal autocorrelation function (TACF) demonstrate spatiotemporal consistency and reveal that MC enhances subchannel correlations. Furthermore, simulations of the root mean square (RMS) delay spread incorporating the MC effect demonstrate excellent agreement with empirical channel measurements, validating the effectiveness of the proposed channel model.

title: Composite Index Modulation for Pinching Antenna Systems.
Resource Allocation in Semantic Communication: A Trade-off Between Transmission and Knowledge.
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom), a paradigm central to the next generation task-oriented vision, relies on a shared Knowledge Base (KB) between the transmitter and receiver. However, the prevalent assumption of a static KB is frequently invalidated in dynamic real-world environments, where KB "staleness" precipitates a collapse in semantic efficiency. This introduces a critical trade-off: either continue transmission with a suboptimal, stale KB, or allocate scarce wireless resources to a knowledge consensus protocol to update the KB, thereby incurring a significant opportunity cost. This paper addresses this dynamic resource allocation problem. We are the first to establish a system model that explicitly quantifies knowledge staleness K(t) as a state variable and models the update procedure as a resource-consuming consensus task. We formulate this trade-off as a complex, NP-hard 0-1 Mixed-Integer Non-Linear Program (MINLP), which uniquely incorporates the fixed activation costs associated with initiating the consensus protocol. To solve this intractable problem, we propose a low-complexity online control framework based on model predictive control (MPC), which embeds a novel heuristic algorithm termed iterative marginal cost allocation (IMCA). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MPC-IMCA framework significantly outperforms static Greedy and Periodic Update baselines in long-term cumulative semantic utility, exhibiting robust adaptability to varying environmental dynamics (δd) and update workloads (DKB).

title: Performance Analysis of Cooperative Service Caching in Integrated Ground-Air-Space Networks.
abstract: In order to support the ever-increasing computation demand of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in low-altitude economy (LAE), the information infrastructure needs to provide service caching and computation offloading capabilities for the storage- and computation-limited UAVs, in addition to radio coverage. In this paper, we propose an integrated ground-air-space network architecture, in which the UAVs’ service requests can be satisfied via either their local computation capabilities or task offloading to the low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites and ground base stations (GBSs) equipped with service caching functionalities. In the proposed architecture, we consider a practical-yet-challenging issue that each UAV can only offload its computation tasks to a limited number of LEO satellites and GBSs, due to its constrained visible range and mobility. Under this constraint, we leverage the tools from stochastic geometry and derive compact expressions of the successful transmission probability (STP) and successful service probability (SSP), showing how they are determined by key system parameters, including the densities of GBSs and LEO satellites, as well as the task offloading strategy of the UAVs. Through numerical results, we validate the effectiveness of our proposed framework even when the LEO satellites and GBSs adopt the random service caching strategy, and demonstrate that the SSP can be significantly improved by judiciously deploying the GBSs, and selecting the task offloading strategy of the UAVs. The results reported in this work provide valuable insights into the design of future integrated ground-air-space wireless networks for LAE.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Interference Suppression in RIS-Aided Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks.
abstract: Future 6G networks envision ubiquitous connectivity through space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs), where high-altitude platform stations (HAPSs) and satellites complement terrestrial systems to provide wide-area, low-latency coverage. However, the rapid growth of terrestrial devices intensifies spectrum sharing between terrestrial and non-terrestrial segments, resulting in severe cross-tier interference. In particular, frequency sharing between the HAPS satellite uplink and HAPS ground downlink improves spectrum efficiency but suffers from interference caused by the HAPS antenna back-lobe. Existing approaches relying on zero-forcing (ZF) codebooks have limited performance under highly dynamic channel conditions. To overcome this limitation, we employ a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided HAPS-based SAGIN framework with a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm. The proposed DDPG framework optimizes the HAPS beamforming weights to form spatial nulls toward interference sources while maintaining robust links to the desired signals. Simulation results demonstrate that the DDPG framework consistently outperforms conventional ZF beamforming among different RIS configurations, achieving up to \(11.3\%\) throughput improvement for a \(4\times4\) RIS configuration, validating its adaptive capability to enhance spectral efficiency in dynamic HAPS-based SAGINs.

title: Security Analysis of NOMA-Based STAR-RIS: Near and Far Users Under Colluding vs. Non-Colluding Eavesdropping.
abstract: To ensure robust connectivity in environments affected by signal blockage, simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (STAR-RIS) are introduced to provide seamless coverage to both indoor and outdoor users. Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is incorporated to increase spectral efficiency and serve multiple users. Under this configuration, the objective of this paper is to analyze the physical layer security (PLS) performance of STAR-RIS-assisted NOMA systems in scenarios involving multiple eavesdroppers. Specifically, the STAR-RIS reflects and transmits signals to near and far users for both indoor and outdoor propagation environments, which exposes the communication to potential interception by external adversaries. To assess the system’s vulnerability, closed-form intercept probability expressions are derived for both near and far users under colluding and non-colluding eavesdropping scenarios. The analysis further examines the influence of critical design parameters, including the number of transmitting and reflecting elements, multi-eavesdropping conditions, power allocation strategies, and fading characteristics, on the overall security performance.1

title: FiSH: Feature-informed Similarity Hashing for Edge-based Traffic Fingerprinting.
abstract: Edge-based Network Traffic Fingerprinting (NTF) enables the identification and classification of Internet of Things (IoT) communications without complex monitoring infrastructure. Yet, performing NTF directly on edge gateways is challenging due to limited computational and storage resources, constraining the use of complex Machine Learning (ML) methods. This paper presents Feature-informed Similarity Hashing (FiSH), a lightweight framework for efficient traffic fingerprinting and classification at the network edge. FiSH employs the Nilsimsa similarity hash on selected protocol-level features to generate compact, noise-tolerant fingerprints of network behavior. Experimental results demonstrate that FiSH accurately distinguishes heterogeneous IoT traffic types with minimal computational overhead, achieving real-time classification accuracy above 87%. The proposed approach highlights similarity hashing as a practical and scalable alternative to traditional ML-based NTF techniques for resource-constrained edge environments.

title: Multimodal-Wireless: A Large-Scale Dataset for Sensing and Communication.
abstract: This paper presents Multimodal-Wireless, a large-scale open-source dataset for multimodal sensing and communication research. The dataset is generated through an integrated and customizable data pipeline built upon the CARLA simulator and Sionna framework, and features high-resolution communication channel state information (CSI) fully synchronized with five other sensor modalities, namely LiDAR, RGB and depth camera, inertial measurement unit (IMU) and radar, all sampled at 100 Hz. It contains approximately 160,000 frames collected across four virtual towns, sixteen communication scenarios, and three weather conditions. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the dataset, outlining its key features, overall framework, and technical implementation details. In addition, it explores potential research applications concerning communication and collaborative perception, exemplified by beam prediction using a multimodal large language model. The dataset is open in https://le-liang.github.io/mmw/.

title: Learning-Based Resource Management and Bitrate Adaptation for UAV Video Streaming over Low-Altitude Wireless Networks.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) video streaming scheme to enhance video quality in low-altitude wireless networks. Unlike the existing fifth-generation (5G) scheduling algorithm, which relies on a fixed priority level, we propose a dynamic priority scheme that enhances video quality by adaptively adjusting the priority level based on real-time UAVs’ channel conditions and bitrate feedback. Furthermore, we formulate a long-term video quality maximization problem, which jointly optimizes resource block (RB) allocation, modulation and channel coding scheme (MCS) selection, and bitrate adaptation. Due to the coupled decision variables and nonconvexity, we design a learning-based two-layer scheduling algorithm. In the outer layer, the long-term optimization problem is reformulated as a Markov decision process, and then a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm is proposed to determine the priority level in each time slot. In the inner layer, given the determined priority level, the optimal RB allocation, MCS selection, and bitrate adaptation decisions are derived in closed forms, thereby reducing computational complexity. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm averagely improves the video quality by 15.67% as compared to the existing 5G scheduling benchmarks.

title: A Real-time RGB-D SLAM based on Semantic and Geometric Information in Dynamic Environments.
abstract: Visual simultaneous localization and mapping (vSLAM) presents significant potential in the field of intelligent mobile robots. However, the strong assumption of SLAM systems is that the environment is static, which leads to significant pose estimation errors in real-world scenarios where dynamic objects are present. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Red Green Blue-Depth (RGB-D) SLAM system based on semantic and geometric information in dynamic environments, which aims to accurately estimate the camera pose. More specifically, this method utilizes semantic information combined with a depth-based clustering approach to accurately and efficiently identify dynamic objects. Besides, a depth consistency check between the reference frame and the current frame is implemented using the chi-square test to further identify dynamic feature points. Experiments performed on the public Technical University of Munich (TUM) RGB-D dataset and real-world scenarios show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art RGB-D SLAM systems in terms of trajectory accuracy. Additionally, the proposed SLAM system demonstrates high real-time performance.

title: IND-MAC: A Stratified MAC Protocol for Differentiated Services in IRS-Enhanced Industrial IoT Networks.
abstract: Industrial internet of things (IIoT) networks face a core challenge in simultaneously managing mission-critical services and massive data streams, compounded by signal blockages from dense machinery. While intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) are effective in creating reliable communication links to overcome these blockages, the fundamental task of efficiently allocating these reconfigured resources to services with vastly different requirements falls to the multiple access control (MAC) layer. This paper proposes IND-MAC, an IRS-enhanced non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) -based differentiated MAC protocol featuring a stratified access mechanism. The time frame of IND-MAC is logically partitioned into a guaranteed-access period (GAP) for critical services and an efficiency-oriented period (EOP) for routine services. During the GAP, a QoS-aware optimization strategy is employed to jointly optimize IRS phase shifts and transmit power of IIoT devices, whereas during the EOP, an efficiency-driven allocation strategy leverages contention-based NOMA to maximize throughput. Simulation results demonstrate that IND-MAC achieves higher spectral and temporal efficiency than state-of-the-art benchmark protocols. This stratified approach enables IND-MAC to adeptly manage the trade-off between overall system efficiency and guaranteed service quality for heterogeneous IIoT applications.

title: Digital Twin-Based Framework for Behavioral Modeling and Activity Recognition in Smart Homes.
abstract: Ambient Assisted Living (AAL) systems, which combine digital healthcare technologies with Smart Home environments, play an important role in supporting independent living, especially for elderly individuals and people with physical impairments. However, the growing need to continuously monitor users, collect large and heterogeneous data streams, and anticipate abnormal or dangerous situations, has highlighted the necessity of advanced analytical frameworks capable of adapting to dynamic daily contexts.To address this necessity, this paper proposes a framework that integrates the Digital Twin (DT) paradigm with a fully implemented simulation platform. This simulator provides the required analytical capabilities by modeling user interactions with domestic objects and environmental sensors, enabling context-aware understanding of daily activities, behavioral modeling, and the generation of alternative scenarios.Experimental results show that the simulated activities closely reflect real-world patterns, producing distinctive temporal and contextual signatures that can be effectively recognized by classification algorithms. These findings underline the potential of combining DT concepts with simulation-based approaches to enhance situational awareness, adaptability, and user assistance in AAL environments.

title: Bridging IoT and the Metaverse: Policies for the Synchronization of Digital Twins.
abstract: The convergence of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the metaverse creates systems where a Digital Twin (DT) sits between physical and virtual worlds. Keeping them in sync is hard when actions arrive at the same time with different priorities and delays. We present a DT template that supports two-way, asynchronous interactions and a stack of three policies: confirm matching intents, resolve conflicts with context (domain weights and timeliness), and rollback on invariant violations. We validate the approach in a smart building with DTs representing doors, windows, and lights operating within policy domains that include security, comfort, and energy efficiency. Without policies, conflicting windows already reach 33-56% with only two users for different request rates. With the policy stack, the share of conflicts resolved by policy increases with the reliability gap and can approach all the conflicts, reducing rollbacks.
