Finally, under asymmetric placement, by simulating the DT at different points in the network (e.g., edge close to physical devices and cloud close to the metaverse), rollbacks shift to the slower side but leave the overall resolution essentially unchanged.

title: Trust Beyond Perfection: Managing Uncertainty in the Internet of Digital Twins.
abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are increasingly adopted in IoT systems as autonomous agents capable of providing services and interacting within distributed ecosystems. However, most trust management solutions rely on overly idealized assumptions: service evaluations are always accurate, and benevolent nodes never make mistakes. These assumptions limit the applicability of such models in realistic scenarios, where uncertainty and imperfection are the norm. This paper proposes a trust management model tailored to more realistic DTs, where both service providers and requesters may introduce errors. Providers may fail due to physical or software limitations; requesters cannot rely on objective ground truth to evaluate outcomes. To capture this complexity, we introduce a feedback mechanism based on divergence from aggregated results, rather than binary correctness. We define an IoT scenario where DTs dynamically offer and request services. A trust computation model is applied to distinguish truly malicious nodes from those affected by faults, reducing false positives. Simulations confirm improved trust accuracy and system resilience under realistic conditions.

title: 6G OFDM Communications with High Mobility Transceivers and Scatterers via Angle-Domain Processing and Deep Learning.
abstract: High-mobility communications, which are crucial for next-generation wireless systems, cause the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveform to suffer from strong intercarrier interference (ICI) due to the Doppler effect. In this work, we propose a novel receiver architecture for OFDM that leverages the angular domain to separate multipaths. A block-type pilot is sent to estimate direction-of-arrivals (DoAs), propagation delays, and channel gains of the multipaths. Subsequently, a decision-directed (DD) approach is employed to estimate and iteratively refine the Dopplers. Two different approaches are investigated to provide initial Doppler estimates: an error vector magnitude (EVM)-based method and a deep learning (DL)-based method. Simulation results reveal that the DL-based approach allows for constant bit error rate (BER) performance up to the maximum 6G speed of 1000 km/h.

title: GreenTent: an Intent-based Framework for Sustainable Network Orchestration.
abstract: Video streaming dominates global Internet traffic and contributes significantly to worldwide greenhouse gas emissions, making network orchestration a key lever for sustainability. However, current orchestration mechanisms remain largely performance-driven, optimizing traditional key performance indicators while neglecting sustainability dimensions, spatio-temporal variations in grid carbon intensity, and performance-driven rebound effects. This paper presents GreenTent, an intent-based orchestration framework that integrates sustainability by design into video streaming service delivery. GreenTent leverages Intent-Based Networking (IBN) to translate high-level service requests into joint performance and sustainability objectives, and a Digital Twin Network (DTN) to enable carbon-aware orchestration by combining Software-Defined Networking (SDN) state with external energy and emission indicators. A two-phase orchestration logic jointly optimizes topology activation and request-level routing while explicitly accounting for rebound effects. Experimental evaluation shows that GreenTent improves carbon efficiency compared to throughput-optimized and energy-aware baselines, without degrading user-perceived performance, demonstrating the feasibility of sustainability-aware orchestration for future 6G networks.

title: FairEnergy: Contribution-Based Fairness meets Energy Efficiency in Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed devices while preserving data privacy. However, balancing energy efficiency and fair participation while ensuring high model accuracy remains challenging in wireless edge systems due to heterogeneous resources, unequal client contributions, and limited communication capacity. To address these challenges, we propose FairEnergy, a fairness-aware energy minimization framework that integrates a contribution score capturing both the magnitude of updates and their compression ratio into the joint optimization of device selection, bandwidth allocation, and compression level. The resulting mixed-integer non-convex problem is solved by relaxing binary selection variables and applying Lagrangian decomposition to handle global bandwidth coupling, followed by per-device subproblem optimization. Experiments on non-IID data show that FairEnergy achieves higher accuracy while reducing energy consumption by up to 79% compared to baseline strategies.

title: From GNNs to Symbolic Surrogates via Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Delay Prediction.
abstract: Accurate prediction of flow delay is essential for optimizing and managing modern communication networks. We investigate three levels of modeling for this task. First, we implement a heterogeneous GNN with attention-based message passing, establishing a strong neural baseline. Second, we propose FlowKANet in which Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks replace standard MLP layers, reducing trainable parameters while maintaining competitive predictive performance. FlowKANet integrates KAMP-Attn (Kolmogorov-Arnold Message Passing with Attention), embedding KAN operators directly into message-passing and attention computation. Finally, we distill the model into symbolic surrogate models using block-wise regression, producing closed-form equations that eliminate trainable weights while preserving graph-structured dependencies. The results show that KAN layers provide a favorable trade-off between efficiency and accuracy and that symbolic surrogates emphasize the potential for lightweight deployment and enhanced transparency.

title: Energy-Efficient Power Control in Single-User M-MIMO-OFDM System with PA Nonlinearity.
abstract: Although multiple works have proposed energy-efficient resource allocation schemes for Massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (M-MIMO) system, most approaches overlook the potential of optimizing Power Amplifier (PA) transmission power while accounting for non-linear distortion effects. Furthermore, most M-MIMO studies assume narrow-band transmission, neglecting subcarrier intermodulations at the non-linear PA for an Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) system. Therefore, this work investigates the energy-efficient power allocation for a single-user equipment (UE) M-MIMO downlink (DL) system employing OFDM with nonlinear PAs. Unlike prior works, we model wide-band transmission using a soft-limiter PA model and derive a closed-form expression for the signal-to-distortion-and-noise ratio (SNDR) under Rayleigh fading and Maximal Ratio Transmission (MRT) precoding. Next, the Energy Efficiency (EE) function is defined considering two PA architectures and a distorted OFDM signal. We then propose a low complexity root-finding algorithm to maximize EE by transmit power adjustment. Simulation results demonstrate significant EE gains over a fixed PA back-off baseline, with over $100\%$ improvement under both low and high path loss. Our findings reveal how the optimal operating point depends on the antenna count, the PA model, and the propagation conditions.

title: Joint Beamforming and Channel Assignment via Complex-Valued Graph Neural Networks in MU-MISO Systems.
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have demonstrated promise for resource allocation in wireless networks by taking into account the topological structure of the network. However, a common approach processes channel state information (CSI) as real-valued features, thus discarding critical phase relationships governing interference patterns in multi-user systems. We propose Complex-Valued Graph Neural Networks (CV-GNN) for joint beamforming and channel allocation in MU-MISO systems, which preserve complete complex CSI throughout the optimization process. Our approach introduces complex-valued message passing through native complex graph convolutions, uses modReLU activation to maintain phase structure while providing non-linearity, and leverages Wirtinger calculus for efficient gradient computation in the complex domain. By embedding channels as complex-valued graph features and jointly optimizing beamforming vectors and channel assignments in the complex domain, CV-GNN naturally captures interference relationships that real-valued methods cannot represent. The joint optimization framework enables CV-GNN to learn coordinated resource allocation strategies where channel assignment decisions are informed by complex interference patterns, while beamforming design accounts for multi-channel interference coupling. The results of our simulations on MU-MISO systems with multiple resource blocks demonstrate that CV-GNN achieves superior performance as compared to other optimization approaches and real-valued baselines.

title: Collective Grid: Privacy-Preserved Multi-Operator Energy Sharing Optimization via Federated Energy Prediction.
abstract: Electricity consumption in mobile networks is increasing with the continued 5G expansion, rising data traffic, and more complex infrastructures. However, energy management is often handled independently by each mobile network operator (MNO), leading to limited coordination and missed opportunities for collective efficiency gains. To address this gap, we propose a privacy-preserving framework for automated energy infrastructure sharing among co-located MNOs. Our framework consists of three modules: (i) a federated learning-based privacy-preserving site energy consumption forecasting module, (ii) an orchestration module in which a mixed-integer linear program is solved to schedule energy purchases from the grid, utilization of renewable sources, and shared battery charging or discharging, based on real-time prices, forecasts, and battery state, and (iii) an energy source selection module which handles the selection of cost-effective power sources and storage actions based on predicted demand across MNOs for the next control window. Using data from operational networks, our experiments confirm that the proposed solution substantially reduces operational costs and outperforms non-sharing baselines, with gains that increase as network density rises in 5G-and-beyond deployments.

title: Beyond Arbitrary Thresholds: Conformal Prediction for Trustworthy CAN Bus Intrusion Detection.
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) for in-vehicle Controller Area Network (CAN) traffic increasingly employ data-driven models to detect abnormal communication patterns. These systems learn normal behavior and trigger alarms when reconstruction errors exceed a predefined threshold, which is typically chosen heuristically without statistical justification. This paper reinterprets this threshold-based approach through the lens of conformal prediction, establishing a rigorous theoretical foundation for anomaly detection in CAN traffic. We demonstrate that selecting a percentile of benign reconstruction errors is equivalent to conformal calibration under exchangeability assumptions. Violations of this assumption caused by attacks or abnormal behavior are detected when nonconformity scores exceed the calibrated quantile, reframing anomaly detection as a test for distributional shift. We evaluate multiple nonconformity measures (MSE, MAE, and MaxAE) and propose an online calibration mechanism with an adaptive threshold for handling drift. This post-hoc update adapts the decision cutoff at inference time without retraining the base detector, improving F1-scores from 0.70 to 0.91 on DoS/Fuzzing attacks while reducing false alarms from benign drift. Experimental validation on the HCRL Car-Hacking dataset confirms that our conformal framework delivers statistically principled and reliable CAN bus intrusion detection.

title: NHAR: Orbit-Aware Lightweight Elevation-Angle Prediction in 6G NTNs.
abstract: Accurate elevation angle prediction is critical for proactive decision-making in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks, enabling mobility management, handover planning, and resource allocation in 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs). This paper presents a lightweight framework for real-time elevation prediction that integrates autoregressive memory, nonlinear correction, and harmonic periodic features to capture short-term dynamics and structured orbital cycles. Unlike deep learning methods, the model employs closed-form regression via ordinary least squares (OLS), ensuring fast inference and interpretability suitable for edge deployment. Simulation results in dense urban canyon scenarios demonstrate high accuracy with minimal complexity, confirming its practicality for proactive and scalable NTN operations.

title: Strategic Decoy Deployment for Mitigating Poisoning Attacks in Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed devices while preserving data privacy by keeping raw data localized. However, this decentralized paradigm introduces significant vulnerabilities to coordinated poisoning attacks, where adversaries compromise multiple clients to inject malicious updates that systematically degrade global model performance. To counter these threats, this paper proposes a novel game-theoretic defense framework employing strategic deception through the optimal deployment of decoy clients. Our approach formulates the security challenge as a non-zero-sum Bayesian game that captures the asymmetric information between attackers and defenders in FL systems. By analyzing Nash equilibrium strategies, our method enables the defender to probabilistically identify and protect high-value clients while minimizing the attacker’s influence on the global model. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our approach maintains model accuracy within 5-8% of attack-free performance even under intense poisoning scenarios, reducing attack success rates from 95% to below 20% while introducing minimal computational overhead. This work establishes a principled foundation for strategic defense in FL, demonstrating the efficacy of game-theoretic deception against large-scale adversarial threats in decentralized learning environments.

title: On Channel Correlation-Based Jamming Detection.
abstract: As we increasingly rely on wireless infrastructure for enabling critical applications, e.g., from Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) or healthcare, we must ensure resilience, which includes robustness against both accidental and intentional jamming attacks. Hence, awareness of the potential jamming attack information is crucial to the resilience of a fully automated system. However, channel estimation within modern communications remains highly vulnerable to such attacks. The jamming signal is considered to be projected onto the captured channels, which enables the jamming detection through channel analysis. In this work, we consider the detection of a jamming source within an indoor environment. Narrowband white Gaussian noise (WGN) is employed to jam the communications. The impact of the jamming signal on the channel measurements is analyzed by examining the correlation between the jammed and unjammed channels. Based on the correlation pattern, the presence of interference is detected through a comparative suite of statistical thresholding and machine learning algorithms. An overall detection accuracy of 99.31% is achieved, demonstrating the feasibility of jamming detection through the proposed framework.

title: Energy Efficient Design for Self-Sustainable Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface-Aided MIMO SWIPT.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a novel self-sustainable reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) enhanced simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) system, where the RIS harvests energy from the incident signal by adjusting the reflection amplitude coefficient to sustain its operation. Our goal is to minimize the transmit power while considering the data rate requirements of information users (IUs), as well as energy harvesting requirements of both energy users (EUs) and RIS. The formulated problem is highly non-convex due to the variables coupling. To tackle the power minimization problem, we first reformulate the problem by adopting the minimum mean square error (MMSE) technique. Subsequently, we proposed an alternating optimization (AO) framework to decompose the reformulated problem into two sub-problems. Furthermore, we utilize successive convex approximation (SCA) method to approximate the non-convex constraints. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and verify the benefits of implementing self-sustainable RIS for reducing the transmit power compared to other baseline schemes.

title: Uplink-Driven Multistatic ISAC with Distributed Base Stations.
abstract: This work investigates a multistatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system based on single-input multiple-output (SIMO)-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), where spatially distributed base stations (BSs) cooperate to detect and localize targets by exploiting the uplink signals transmitted by a user equipment (UE). In particular, the UE transmits communication signals towards its serving BS, while echoes are simultaneously captured by other BSs in the area, either in stand-by mode or engaged in communication with different UEs. The collected measurements are then processed at an fusion center (FC), where we compare two target localization approaches: a data fusion strategy and a weighted nonlinear least squares (WNLLS) estimator. System performance is evaluated, in a single-target scenario, in terms of target position root mean squared error (RMSE), considering different UE transmit powers and localization uncertainties. Numerical results show that the data fusion method achieves superior robustness and accuracy, particularly under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and UE position uncertainty, whereas the WNLLS estimator performs better in favorable bistatic geometries.

title: Robust and Predictable Orchestration of Distributed Multiuser AI-Powered Applications.
abstract: Modern AI-powered applications demand predictable orchestration across the edge-cloud continuum under stringent quality of service (QoS) requirements. State-of-the-art optimization methods, including the recent IDAGO algorithm, provide probabilistic performance guarantees but remain inherently stochastic, requiring repeated randomized rounding tries and lacking deterministic customization. We introduce IDAGO-SANE, a deterministic extension of IDAGO that advances the state of approximation algorithms for AI service orchestration. IDAGO-SANE builds upon refined probabilistic analysis and provide a principled derandomization strategy that produces high-quality embeddings in a single deterministic step. Experiments leveraging real data from AWS infrastructure and AI extended reality applications shows that IDAGO-SANE consistently delivers solutions with lower and more stable capacity utilization under increasing service loads, obtaining up to 2.5X gains in total cost and resource usage with respect to the baseline methods.

title: Autoencoder-based Constellation Learning for Unified SWIPT Receivers.
abstract: Unified receivers (URs) for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) exploit rectified signals to perform both information decoding (ID) and energy harvesting (EH). This work investigates amplitude constellation designs, tailored for UR-SWIPT architectures, that jointly optimize ID reliability and EH efficiency. The nonlinear behavior of rectifying circuits, however, makes optimal constellation design analytically intractable. We address this by modeling the UR-SWIPT link as an autoencoder, allowing us to learn constellations that minimize symbol error rate while satisfying average transmit power and EH constraints. Towards optimizing decoding accuracy, we further present an algorithmic approach that pre-compensates for the rectifier nonlinearities and yields the optimal information-only constellation. Numerical results validate the efficacy of the proposed framework, demonstrating its adaptability across various energy requirements and operating power levels. The learned constellations consistently outperform conventional modulation schemes and approach near-optimal rate-energy tradeoff. A key feature is a high-amplitude symbol, enabling the system to meet the EH requirements while allowing for reliable decoding.

title: An Ambiguity-Function-Assisted Newtonized Channel Estimation Method for Pulse-Shaped AFDM Under Fractional Delay and Doppler.
abstract: Accurate channel estimation for pulse-shaped AFDM systems over doubly selective channels with fractional normalized delay and Doppler remains challenging. This paper proposes a low-complexity ambiguity-function-assisted newtonized channel (AFNC) estimation method. Specifically, we first present a closed-form input-output relation for pulse-shaped affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) under fractional normalized delay and Doppler. As a further step, we demonstrate that the input-output relation admits a low-complexity representation by offline precomputing and storing the discretized ambiguity function of the shaping pulse, followed by tailored cyclic-shift and stacking operations. Building on this representation, AFNC performs fractional delay-Doppler channel estimation through Newtonized refinement, where the required Jacobian and Hessian updates are computed efficiently using the low-complexity input-output representation. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Phase-Retrieval-Inspired Deep Learning Estimation of Downlink Channel State Information.
abstract: Accurate downlink channel state information (CSI) in the next-generation NodeB (gNB) is essential to enable high-performance precoding in massive multiple input multiple output (MIMO) systems. Many existing works have utilized deep learning for efficient downlink CSI feedback from user equipment (UE) in massive MIMO. However, in practice, UEs can only estimate partial downlink CSI from sparsely distributed CSI-RS. To address the deleterious effects of sparse CSI-RS and UE feedback delay on downlink CSI estimation, we leverage the strong correlation between magnitudes of uplink-downlink CSIs and the dense CSI available from common downlink signals of PBCH/PSS/SSS. We generalize a classic phase retrieval framework to propose a deep learning-enhanced Gerchberg–Saxton (GS) algorithm that reconstructs dense downlink CSI from sparse RB-domain feedback. We develop a neural network architecture that unfolds the iterative GS process to effectively improve phase estimation accuracy and robustness. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms conventional and baseline learning-based models in terms of both normalized mean square error and achievable rate under various downsampling scenarios.

title: Designing Profile-Based Deep Learning Models for Massive MIMO Precoder Forecast.
abstract: UE feedback of downlink precoder to the base station (gNB) is important for achieving high spectrum efficiency in massive MIMO wireless networks. Considering the delay of precoding matrix (PM) feedback, rapid channel change due to UE mobility can lead to a mismatch between PM from UE feedback and the current downlink channel. To mitigate performance degradation due to such outdated PM feedback, we propose a profile-based deep learning framework for PM forecast by incorporating radio environment information. Our method models PMs as temporally correlated sequential frames across Transmission Time Intervals (TTIs) and designs a gNB-side DL network to forecast the current PM based on historical feedback. To improve adaptability and generalization, we extract Doppler and multipath delay spread variables to implement environment-aware clustering and to customize a DL model for each cluster. The gNB selects the appropriate DL model in real time according to the current propagation profile. Test results under a Uniform Planar Array (UPA) configuration demonstrate the performance enhancement. This framework provides a scalable and practical solution for robust precoding in dynamic and high-mobility radio environments.

title: Can Multi-Satellite Cooperation Always Improve Electromagnetic Stealth?
abstract: Electromagnetic stealth prevents signals from being detected, identified, and located, which is typically achieved by covert communication technologies, and has become a critical capability for satellite communications. Recently, multi-satellite cooperation has been extensively studied for covert communications, yet whether it can effectively enhance covert transmission performance remains to be verified. This paper investigates the precise conditions for achieving the optimal covert performance of multi-satellite cooperation with respect to the number of deployed satellites. We first introduce a new metric termed the covert radius, which integrates covertness and transmission reliability. Using hierarchical optimization, we derive its closed-form expression through a joint analysis of the time, frequency, spatial, and energy domains. Building on this framework, we theoretically determine the optimal number of cooperative satellites that minimizes the covert radius by employing an asymptotic expansion of implicit functions. The main results reveal that indiscriminately increasing the number of cooperative satellites does not continuously improve covert communication performance. Simulations validate the correctness of the theoretical closed-form solution and provide intuitive results for the covert radius and the optimal number of satellites under typical system parameters.

title: Energy Profiling of Secure MQTT over WiFi on ESP32-Based IoT Devices.
abstract: This paper investigates the energy impact of Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol on an ESP32-based IoT system for ambient intelligence applications. The prototype integrates inertial and electrocardiogram (ECG) sensors and transmits data over WiFi using MQTT, with and without TLS. Current consumption is profiled using an INA219 sensor under varying payload sizes (158 to 4096 bytes) and transmission intervals (1 to 600 seconds). Results show that TLS introduces negligible overhead (below 2%) on average current consumption, even under frequent transmissions and large payloads. Transmission interval remains the dominant factor shaping energy consumption. Deep Sleep mode significantly extends battery life, yielding up to 75% reduction in average current for low-duty-cycle settings. The findings provide guidance for designing secure, energy-efficient IoT systems in constrained environments.

title: Accelerating DPI Using Domain-Specific Hardware Accelerator for Dynamic Programming.
abstract: Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) is a critical component of modern network security and traffic analysis, enabling applications such as intrusion detection, malware identification, and policy enforcement. Conventional DPI engines typically rely on exact signature-matching algorithms, which are efficient but susceptible to evasion via polymorphism and obfuscation. Polymorphic malware attacks on Industrial Control Systems (ICS) can easily bypass traditional DPI engines. To overcome these limitations, more robust methods based on sequence alignment and partial pattern matching have been explored; however, their high computational cost renders them impractical on general-purpose CPUs. This paper investigates the use of GPUs equipped with Domain-Specific Dynamic Programming Accelerators (DPAs) to accelerate partial signature matching in DPI. The proposed approach reformulates DPI as a sequence alignment problem and implements the Smith–Waterman algorithm while exploiting both GPU parallelism and DPA hardware capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system can process 10K signatures in the order of hundreds of microseconds and scale to 1M signatures within 4 milliseconds.

title: LEO-Based Positioning Under Orbital Errors.
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites hold considerable promise for providing accurate positioning services; however, their low altitudes also induce significant orbital perturbations that can degrade positioning accuracy. We study the LEO-based positioning under orbital errors within a signals-of-opportunity framework based on downlink communication signals. Initially, we present a realistic LEO orbit model that captures Earth’s non-sphericity, and combine it with a wideband communication model that captures fast satellite dynamics and multipath propagation. Subsequently, we derive the misspecified Cramér-Rao bound (MCRB) to analyze the impact of the orbit mismatch on positioning accuracy. Finally, we design a two-stage scheme to ensure accurate positioning under orbital errors by first calibrating the satellite orbit and then positioning the user. The MCRB analysis reveals that typical orbital errors can cause kilometer-level position errors. Our simulation results show that this positioning error can be effectively reduced with the proposed orbit calibration method.

title: SubFormerNet: Transformer Fusion with Subarray Tokenization for DOA Estimation.
abstract: Reliable direction of arrival (DOA) estimation is essential for wideband orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in realistic multipath environments. This paper proposes SubFormerNet, a Transformer based subarray fusion network that estimates angles from covariance measurements. A lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) encoder maps each subarray covariance block to a compact token, and a Transformer fusion module models global interactions for angle classification. Experiments on a realistic ray-tracing dataset show that SubFormerNet consistently outperforms model driven and learning baselines, especially under strong multipath, and generalizes well to signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) beyond the training range.

title: A Reconfigurable RFSoC-Based Spectrum Sensing Platform Using a Polyphase Channeliser and Distributed Publisher-Subscriber Framework.
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a reconfigurable wide-band spectrum-sensing platform developed within the Open Network Shared Spectrum Innovation and Design Environment (ON-SIDE) project. Most existing implementations lack integration between modern SDR wide-band capture and reconfigurable cognitive spectrum management. The proposed platform addresses this by implementing a fully custom real-time wide-band monitoring directly on AMD Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC 670 DFE hardware, targeting the 3.8–4.2 GHz shared-access band in the UK. The system monitors up to 400 MHz of instantaneous bandwidth, tunable from 0 to 4.9 GHz. The 400 MHz span was selected to cover the full n77 shared-access band (3.8 - 4.2 GHz) allocated by Ofcom, while the 3.84 MHz per-channel resolution aligns with the smallest 5G NR OFDM sub-carrier spacing. A polyphase channeliser and energy detection pipeline implemented on the FPGA fabric provides 106 parallel channel outputs, enabling real-time energy monitoring. An embedded PYNQ-based control dashboard allows configuration and live visualisation, and a Python ZeroMQ publisher-subscriber framework distributes sensing data to multiple remote clients. Field trials on live 5G NR signals in the n77 and n78 bands verified accurate, low-latency energy detection and remote operation. The platform demonstrated an efficient and reconfigurable hardware foundation for future cognitive radio and dynamic spectrum management applications.

title: Comparison of OTFS and OFDM for RIS-aided Systems in the Presence of Phase Noise.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the performance of RIS-aided orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) and orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems in the presence of oscillator phase noise. OFDM is known to be sensitive to phase noise, which could limit the potential gains promised by RIS systems. OTFS, on the other hand, is a compelling potential waveform for RIS-aided systems in the presence of phase noise due to it’s resilience to time-varying channels. However, the effect of phase noise on OTFS has not been fully analyzed in the literature as of yet. Additionally, no existing works in the literature consider the effect of phase noise on an RIS-aided OTFS system. Hence, we propose a joint RIS channel and phase noise estimation technique using a Wiener filtering approach. Our proposed method exploits the statistical nature of both the phase noise and the Doppler spread channel in a setup with RIS. Our numerical analysis demonstrates the significant gain of RIS-aided OTFS offers compared to RIS-aided OFDM in the presence in the presence of phase noise. Additionally, our results demonstrate the superiority of our proposed estimation technique, with gains of up to 3 dB in terms of bit error rate (BER), over existing methods in the literature.

title: Effect of Full Common Randomness Replication in Symmetric PIR on Graph-Based Replicated Systems.
abstract: We revisit the problem of symmetric private information retrieval (SPIR) in settings where the database replication is modeled by a simple graph. Here, each vertex corresponds to a server, and a message is replicated on two servers if and only if there is an edge between them. To satisfy the requirement of database privacy, we let all the servers share some common randomness, independent of the messages. We aim to quantify the improvement in SPIR capacity, i.e., the maximum ratio of the number of desired and downloaded symbols, compared to the setting with graph-replicated common randomness. Towards this, we develop an algorithm to convert a class of PIR schemes into the corresponding SPIR schemes, thereby establishing a capacity lower bound on graphs for which such schemes exist. This includes the class of path and cyclic graphs for which we derive capacity upper bounds that are tighter than the trivial bounds given by the respective PIR capacities. For the special case of path graph with three vertices, we identify the SPIR capacity to be $\frac{1}{2}$.

title: Game-Theoretic Security Orchestration for Cross-RIC Policy Conflicts in O-RAN.
abstract: In Open Radio Access Network (Open RAN), disaggregated network components can interact through specialized xApps or rApps from multiple vendors. Despite the flexibility of operations and the dynamism of functions enabled by the open architecture, this openness can cause conflicts in security policy enforcement (e.g., encryption levels, key rotation, firewall restrictiveness), formally defined as thresholded divergences on shared or interdependent security parameters, where one app wants to set a stricter rule while another wants a more lenient policy simultaneously. The current solutions of "first-come" or "last-write" make the change one-sided for the benefit of a single app, while other apps may be harmed by the result, and at a network level, security and stability can be compromised. In this paper, we propose a novel Game-Theoretic Security Orchestrator (GTSO) that operates at the Service Management and Orchestration (SMO) layer, with cross-RIC scope, and is responsible for resolving parameter conflicts across xApps and rApps. GTSO treats xApps/rApps as strategic players and negotiates convergent solutions using game-theoretic models such as non-cooperative Nash games, cooperative bargaining, and leader-follower (Stackelberg) that guide competing control applications toward stable equilibrium points, while exchanging strategy summaries over secure channels to protect sensitive details and enhance overall network security.

title: Breaking the Link: Head-Motion Effects on VR Wi-Fi Connectivity Across 5 GHz and 6 GHz.
Causal-AI for Explainable and Robust KPI Prediction in 6G.
abstract: Accurate prediction of key performance indicators (KPIs) such as end-to-end (E2E) latency is essential for the management and optimization of sixth-generation (6G) networks. Nevertheless, the presence of dynamic environments and distribution shifts between training and inference data introduces uncertainty and data mismatches, making precise KPI prediction particularly challenging in 6G networks. In this study, we propose a framework that combines a causal discovery algorithm for time series with artificial intelligence (AI)-based time series prediction to improve KPI prediction in dynamic wireless networks. Unlike traditional deep recurrent neural networks (DRNNs), which rely on correlation-based features and often struggle with distribution shifts, our approach selects only causally relevant parameters for prediction. This focus on causal drivers reduces the input dimensionality by approximately 60% in our setup and slightly reduces trainable parameters, improving robustness and explainability.

title: Layer-Reuse Aware Optimization for Efficient Microservice Migration in UAV Edge Systems.
abstract: The integration of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) with edge computing enables latency-sensitive services such as real-time video analytics and object detection. However, UAV mobility causes frequent network changes, requiring efficient microservice migration to maintain Service Level Agreements (SLAs). Existing strategies often overlook the layered structure of containers and the impact of layer reuse on provisioning time. This paper introduces a layer-aware optimization model for microservice migration in UAV-assisted edge environments. Using an optimization solver, the model jointly minimizes provisioning time, the number of migrations, and SLA violations by considering Docker layer reuse, registry selection, and end-to-end latency constraints. It provides optimal placement decisions that serve as a reliable baseline for future heuristic and learning-based approaches. Experimental results in UAV mobility scenarios demonstrate that the proposed model significantly reduces provisioning overhead through intelligent, layer-aware placement.

title: Constellation Selection and Power Allocation for OFDM ISAC: Optimization and Experiments.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) techniques can leverage wide-coverage communication networks to perform sensing tasks, enabling large-scale and low-cost target sensing. However, the inherent randomness of communication data payloads introduces undesired sidelobes in the ambiguity function that may degrade target detection and parameter estimation performance. This paper develops a communication-centric ISAC framework that is standards-compliant and compatible with existing devices. Specifically, we propose a low-complexity constellation selection scheme over a finite, off-the-shelf alphabet, achieving an efficient sensing–communication trade-off without custom waveforms or frame-structure changes. To this end, we analyze the sensing performance of matched filtering receiver for ranging measurements, and derive closed-form sensing laws that link constellation statistics to sensing performance. Under any finite-alphabet constellation combination, the receiver sidelobes depend on the weighted sum of the kurtosis values of the per-subcarrier constellations, providing a tractable expression for tuning the sensing-communication trade-off. A bilevel algorithm with closed-form inner updates attains near-optimal performance while sharply reducing computational complexity. We validate the entire theoretical pipeline with experimental results.

title: TGCL: Target-aware Graph Contrastive Learning for Stance Detection.
abstract: Stance detection aims to identify users’ attitudes toward specific targets. Existing methods based on graph neural networks have attracted significant attention due to their high applicability in social networks and their remarkable performance. However, these methods commonly overlook the critical role of target information and the issue of node representation over-smoothing. This paper proposes a novel Target-aware Graph Contrastive Learning (TGCL) framework for stance detection, which primarily consists of a Target-aware Graph Attention Network (TGAN) and a Stance-aware Multi-granularity Contrastive Network (SMCN). The TGAN introduces a target-aware attention mechanism to capture target-related node representations, effectively overcoming the neglect of significant target information in existing methods. SMCN integrates global context contrast, local neighborhood contrast, and stance-aware semantic contrast, together with graph reconstruction and stance detection tasks, to learn highly discriminative node representations. SMCN effectively alleviates the over-smoothing of node representations and significantly improves the performance of TGCL in stance detection. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that TGCL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

title: Efficient Clustered Channel Estimation via Channel Knowledge Map Constructed with Tensor Decomposition.
abstract: To address the complexity and accuracy challenges in channel estimation for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems, conventional channel knowledge map (CKM) approaches that store multipath parameters are prone to model mismatch under clustered multipath propagation. Moreover, their reliance on fine-grained geographical grids results in high construction and storage overhead. To mitigate these issues, we propose a low-complexity CKM construction and utilization framework that leverages historical channel estimates acquired over a relatively large geographical area. A two-layer hierarchical structure is learned via tensor decomposition to characterize both the spatial and frequency subspace structures of the channel and the power distribution in the shared subspaces within this area. We further design a two-stage channel estimation scheme, which utilizes the low-rank subspaces and preprocessed correlation characteristics provided by the CKM. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves significantly improved estimation accuracy while reducing computational complexity across various conditions, offering an efficient solution for high-performance wireless communications.

title: PrivFly: A Privacy-Preserving Self-Supervised Framework for Rare Attack Detection in IoFT.
abstract: The Internet of Flying Things (IoFT) plays a vital role in modern applications such as aerial surveillance and smart mobility. However, it remains highly vulnerable to cyberattacks that threaten the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of sensitive data. Developing effective intrusion detection systems (IDS) for IoFT networks faces key challenges, including data imbalance, privacy concerns, and the limited capability of traditional models to detect rare but potentially damaging cyber threats. In this work, we propose PrivFly, a privacy-preserving IDS framework that integrates self-supervised representation learning and differential privacy (DP) to enhance detection performance in imbalanced IoFT network traffic. We propose a masked feature reconstruction module for self-supervised pretraining, improving feature representations and boosting rare-class detection. Differential privacy is applied during training to protect sensitive information without significantly compromising model performance. In addition, we conduct a SHapley additive explanations (SHAP)-based analysis to evaluate the impact of DP on feature importance and model behavior. Experimental results on the ECU-IoFT dataset show that PrivFly achieves up to 98% accuracy and 99% F1-score, effectively balancing privacy and detection performance for secure IoFT systems.

title: Towards Network Design-to-Impact: RAN Pruning for Sustainability.
abstract: This paper investigates long-term energy sobriety in 5G networks by selectively decommissioning base stations under Quality of Service (QoS) constraints. Unlike conventional sleepmode schemes that temporarily switch off BSs, the proposed approach permanently redefines the network topology, allowing deactivating sites for permanent energy savings, under relaxed coverage and throughput requirements. The network is modeled using stochastic geometry and flow-level dynamics captured via M/G/1/PS queues coupled to massive-MIMO SINR distributions. A load-aware Bernoulli p-thinning retains each BS with probability derived from its stationary load, yielding a scalable and analytically tractable thinning. Simulations under realistic channel models show substantial energy savings with minimal QoS relaxation.

title: A Digital Twin Framework for Multi-Hazard Risk Assessment in Telecommunication Infrastructure.
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology offers a practical and intuitive way to represent complex physical infrastructures in a continuously evolving digital form. In this study, a Digital Twin–based simulation framework is presented to jointly model and analyze the multi-hazard risk conditions of a telecommunication company’s mobile base stations and fixed domain stations within a unified Digital Twin environment. The proposed framework brings together risk information related to earthquakes, hydrological and geotechnical hazards, meteorological conditions, wildfires, planned power outages, and road accessibility. For each risk type, real-time data provided by relevant authorities at predefined update intervals are processed and spatially linked to infrastructure assets using their geographic locations. These periodically refreshed inputs are coherently integrated within the Digital Twin to describe how risk levels evolve at both site and network scales, using a weighted multi-criteria aggregation approach. Rather than relying on continuous data streams, the proposed model adopts a time-stepped update structure that reflects realistic operational practices and data availability. The resulting Digital Twin provides a coherent and scalable representation of infrastructure risk dynamics and illustrates how real-world Digital Twin simulations can support systematic risk mapping, resilience assessment, and informed decision-making for large-scale telecommunication networks operating under diverse natural and operational risk conditions.

title: Channel Extrapolation based Downlink Precoding using 5G NR Uplink SRS in LEO Satellite.
abstract: In frequency division duplexing (FDD)-based low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite non-terrestrial networks (NTN), the downlink (DL) channel state information (CSI) feedback from user equipment (UE) often becomes outdated due to the high mobility of the satellite and the long propagation delays. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a multiuser (MU) DL precoding scheme for the FR1 NR-NTN band that utilizes 5G New Radio (NR) sounding reference signals (SRS). The proposed framework derives DL CSI by extrapolating uplink (UL) CSI obtained from SRS measurements, thereby removing the need for explicit CSI feedback from the UE. Based on the extrapolated CSI, the gNB performs MU precoding to suppress inter-user interference and improve overall link efficiency. Performance evaluations in terms of normalized mean squared error (NMSE) and average spectral efficiency (ASE) under diverse CSI scenarios, including perfect, imperfect, extrapolated, and outdated CSI, validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The findings demonstrate that SRS-based CSI extrapolation enables practical and fast MU precoding for LEO satellite systems while maintaining full compatibility with existing 5G NR specifications.

title: An Efficient Subtree-based Mutual Authentication Technique for Secure Fuzzy User Data Exchange in Healthcare Applications.
abstract: Given the fact that Wireless Body Sensor Networks (WBSNs) are employed in healthcare service delivery, it is necessary to protect patients' data and ensure proper data exchange. Therefore, this study provides and recommends a secure subtree-based mutual authentication scheme suitable for optimized fuzzy data exchange in healthcare applications. This technique is designed to address data security, confidentiality, and integrity while simultaneously satisfying the energy-constrained environment inherent in WBSNs. When the proposed authentication protocol employs a subtree structure, it enhances only those devices and clients that can access and share patient data, and its fuzzy logic increases the flexibility of client authentication while simultaneously adapting to changes in biometric data. The technique not only guarantees high security against attacks such as impersonation, eavesdropping, and data tampering, but also reduces energy consumption and extends the lifetime of sensor nodes. Based on simulation and theoretical analysis, we show that this authentication mechanism significantly reduces computational and communication costs relative to existing mechanisms and is suitable for real-time applications, such as patient health monitoring. Overall, the findings highlight the enhanced performance of the proposed technique in improving the dependability and effectiveness of WBSNs, thereby supporting practical solutions for the secure and sustainable storage of large healthcare datasets.

title: LLM4Imp: Leveraging Frozen Large Language Models with Spectral Prompts for Time-Series Imputation.
abstract: Multivariate time-series imputation is essential for preserving data integrity in healthcare, finance, and industrial monitoring. Deep learning methods such as recurrent networks, autoencoders, attention models, and graph neural networks have advanced the task but still face high training cost, limited handling of missingness, and weak semantic reasoning. Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities but typically require expensive fine-tuning, blur temporal detail through coarse tokenization, and fail to encode missing-value patterns. LLM4Imp is introduced as a parameter-efficient framework that reprograms a frozen GPT-2 for multivariate imputation. It integrates prompt-based statistical and temporal cues, spectral-aware prompts via Fourier analysis, PatchTST-style embeddings, and a cross-domain attention layer. Experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate that LLM4Imp improves imputation accuracy while avoiding LLM fine-tuning costs.

title: Behaviour-Aware Vehicle Prioritization for Bandwidth-Efficient Cooperative Perception in Constrained V2V Communication.
abstract: Cooperative perception enables vehicles to extend situational awareness beyond on-board sensing through vehicleto-vehicle (V2V) knowledge sharing, but its practical deployment is constrained by limited bandwidth and packet loss. Most existing approaches focus on reducing message size while implicitly assuming uniform participation by all vehicles. Under constrained communication conditions, this assumption introduces transmitter-level redundancy, increases congestion-induced loss, and can suppress timely delivery of safety-critical information. In this paper, we address the complementary problem of determining which vehicles should transmit under bandwidth-limited and lossy V2V conditions. We propose a behaviour-aware vehicle prioritization framework that uses interpretable driving features together with a lightweight learning-based scoring model (XGBoost) to selectively enable knowledge sharing from vehicles more likely to observe emerging safety-relevant events. The framework is evaluated through frame-level simulations using real-world highway trajectories from the NGSIM dataset, combined with a communication model inspired by 3GPP TR 37.885. Results show that behaviour-aware transmitter selection improves detection stability (macro F1 from approximately 0.60 to 0.70) while reducing average communication cost by up to 25% compared to conventional methods, particularly under congested network conditions.

title: Communication-Efficient Hierarchical Federated Learning via Graph-Based Edge Server Clustering.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed clients without sharing raw data, but the conventional flat architecture often suffers from excessive communication cost and latency, particularly when scaling to large and heterogeneous networks. To address this challenge, we propose a hierarchical FL framework that organizes edge servers into clusters, with each cluster coordinated by an edge-server head to communicate with the cloud. The edge-server clustering problem is formulated as a graph partitioning optimization task, aiming to simultaneously minimize inter-cluster communication cost and preserve intra-cluster model similarity. To solve this problem, we design a spectral clustering based strategy that exploits the monotonicity property of the constraint function to automatically determine the optimal number of clusters and employs eigen-decomposition to perform partitioning. The effectiveness and improved efficiency of the proposed scheme are demonstrated through the theoretical analysis and extensive experiments.

title: Interference-Robust Non-Coherent Over-the-Air Computation for Decentralized Optimization.
abstract: Non-coherent over-the-air (NCOTA) computation enables low-latency and bandwidth-efficient decentralized optimization by exploiting the average energy superposition property of wireless channels. It has recently been proposed as a powerful tool for executing consensus-based optimization algorithms in fully decentralized systems. A key advantage of NCOTA is that it enables unbiased consensus estimation without channel state information at either transmitters or receivers, requires no transmission scheduling, and scales efficiently to dense network deployments. However, NCOTA is inherently susceptible to external interference, which can bias the consensus estimate and deteriorate the convergence of the underlying decentralized optimization algorithm. In this paper, we propose a novel interference-robust (IR-)NCOTA scheme. The core idea is to apply a coordinated random rotation of the frame of reference across all nodes, and transmit a pseudo-random pilot signal, allowing to transform external interference into a circularly symmetric distribution with zero mean relative to the rotated frame. This ensures that the consensus estimates remain unbiased, preserving the convergence guarantees of the underlying optimization algorithm. Through numerical results on a classification task, it is demonstrated that IR-NCOTA exhibits superior performance over the baseline NCOTA algorithm in the presence of external interference.

title: Probabilistic end-to-end quality of service in networks of quantum repeaters.
abstract: We model a multihop quantum repeater network for establishing high fidelity entanglement link between non-neighboring quantum repeater nodes. We have used random times for quantum and classical communication instead of slotted time concept widely used in literature. We model a single repeater using theory of M/G/m + r queues, and apply the Jackson network principle to model the network over repeater nodes. This model allows derivation of distribution of end-to-end entanglement delivery time and probability of decoherence.

title: Age of Job Completion Minimization with Stable Queues.
abstract: We consider a time-slotted job-assignment system with a central server, N users and a machine which changes its state according to a Markov chain (hence called a Markov machine). The users submit their jobs to the central server according to a stochastic job arrival process. For each user, the server has a dedicated job queue. Upon receiving a job from a user, the server stores that job in the corresponding queue. When the machine is not working on a job assigned by the server, the machine can be either in internally busy or in free state, and the dynamics of these states follow a binary symmetric Markov chain. Upon sampling the state information of the machine, if the server identifies that the machine is in the free state, it schedules a user and submits a job to the machine from the job queue of the scheduled user. To maximize the number of jobs completed per unit time, we introduce a new metric, referred to as the age of job completion. To minimize the age of job completion and the sampling cost, we propose two policies and numerically evaluate their performance. For both of these policies, we find sufficient conditions under which the job queues will remain stable.

title: Nucleolus-Based Incentive Mechanism for V2X Cooperative Perception toward Road Safety.
abstract: Cooperative perception represents an underutilized but promising resource for enhancing traffic safety in future smart cities. At urban intersections, vehicle-mounted and infrastructure cameras could be used to provide complementary viewpoints. Sharing their data could eliminate blind spots and improve recognition accuracy at the edge server. To sustain such accuracy, continuous cooperation among organizations and sensors would be required, and would rely on the willingness of data holders to share it. One mechanism to increase propensity to share is using incentive. The success of any incentive mechanism would be dependent on the acceptance of incentive allocation by the data providers, one mechanism to quantify incentive is using recognition accuracy, however, traditional approaches to this are limited because of a reliance on the mathematical averaging of individual contributions across coalitions. In this paper, we introduce a transformed characteristic function that enables cooperative game-theoretic incentive design for incentive mechanism. We compare two allocation strategies: the Shapley value, which ensures fairness, and the nucleolus, which minimizes dissatisfaction and guarantees stability. Experimental results demonstrate that the nucleolus achieves lower excess and greater long-term stability than the Shapley value, providing a robust foundation for sustainable cooperative perception in smart cities.

title: Bidirectional Communication-Aware Offloading for Federated Prompt Learning at the Edge.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) has been increasingly applied to smart city applications to enable distributed model training while preserving data privacy. However, conventional weight-sharing FL still incurs high communication costs in bandwidth-constrained edge environments. Recently introduced Federated Prompt Learning (FPL) significantly reduces communication bandwidth usage to alleviate this issue. Nevertheless, performance degradation persists due to the coexistence of inference and training tasks and communication overhead, defined as delays arising from the transfer of tasks and associated data. Managing priorities between latency-sensitive inference and delay-tolerant training tasks is a critical challenge.This paper models the offloading of inference and training tasks in FPL environments using queuing theory. Compared to the Task-Type Separation (TTS) method, we expand the control model and propose an improved offloading scheme that minimizes the mean sojourn time of training tasks while meeting delay requirements for inference tasks. This scheme allows for bidirectional offloading among multiple edge servers, reducing inference latency while maintaining training continuity. Analytical evaluations show that the proposed method satisfies inference delay requirements while maintaining acceptable training delays. This provides an automatic, scalable task control mechanism for FPL-based edge systems.

title: Secrecy-Driven ISAC Optimization in mmWave via Twin Delayed DDPG and RIS-Assisted Beamforming.
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of secure and efficient joint beamforming and reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) phase shift optimization in an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system. We consider a downlink scenario where a multi-antenna base station (BS) serves multiple single-antenna legitimate users and simultaneously senses a target in the presence of an eavesdropper, assisted by a passive RIS. The optimization objective is to maximize the secrecy sum rate of legitimate users while ensuring sufficient power delivery to the sensing target and adhering to the BS power budget and RIS constraints. Due to the non-convex nature of the problem, we reformulate it as a Markov decision process (MDP) and propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) solution based on the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed TD3-based approach significantly outperforms conventional DRL (DDPG) and heuristic optimization methods, achieving faster convergence and higher secrecy sum rates across varying system configurations. The proposed framework provides valuable insights for designing secure and efficient RIS-assisted ISAC systems.

title: Improving Energy Sustainability of Multi-RAT IoT Coexistence Networks in the Presence of Adjacent Channel Interference and Hardware Impairments.
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices operating across heterogeneous radio access technologies (RATs) poses major challenges to energy sustainability. In practical multi-RAT deployments, adjacent channel interference (ACI) and hardware impairments (HWI) arising from low-cost transceivers significantly degrade energy efficiency (EE), while conventional optimization and learning-based approaches often fail to scale or adapt reliably under such impairments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a digital twin (DT)-assisted continual multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (CMADRL) framework for sustainable resource allocation in multi-RAT IoT networks. The problem is formulated as a two-level hierarchical optimization model. At the upper level (UL), the DT–physical interaction frequency is optimized to balance synchronization overhead and model fidelity. At the lower level (LL), transmit power, modulation, and coding rate are jointly optimized to maximize long-term weighted EE under realistic ACI and HWI conditions using decentralized learning with local observations. The UL problem is solved via bisection search, while the LL problem is modeled as a Markov game and addressed using a DT-assisted CMADRL algorithm enhanced with prioritized experience replay (PER) for stable, sample-efficient, and continual learning. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves substantial gains in EE, convergence speed, and robustness compared with conventional schemes, particularly under severe ACI and HWI.

title: Deep Multi-Task Learning for Joint Estimation of Impulsive Noise Parameters.
abstract: Impulsive noise poses a significant challenge to the reliability of wireless communication systems, necessitating accurate estimation of its statistical parameters for effective mitigation. This paper introduces a multitask learning (MTL) framework based on a CNN–LSTM architecture enhanced with an attention mechanism for the joint estimation of impulsive noise parameters. The proposed model leverages a unified weighted-loss function to enable simultaneous learning of multiple parameters within a shared representation space, improving learning efficiency and generalization across related tasks. Experimental results show that the proposed MTL framework achieves stable convergence, faster training, and enhanced scalability with modest computational overhead. Benchmarking against conventional single-task learning (STL) models confirms its favorable complexity–performance trade-off and significant memory savings, indicating the effectiveness of the MTL approach for real-time impulsive noise parameter estimation in wireless systems.

title: Detecting Sentiment Steering Attacks on RAG-enabled Large Language Models.
abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that enhances the accuracy and reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs), enabling them to answer questions about data they weren’t trained on by fetching relevant documents and adding them as context to the prompts sent to an LLM. As companies are incorporating RAG in their LLM applications at a large scale, the technique opens a new attack surface, and sentiment-steering data poisoning attacks are becoming one of the most critical vulnerabilities in RAG, where an attacker can inject biased data to influence the sentiment of an LLM towards an open-ended topic. However, there is a lack of research detecting sentiment-steering attacks. This work lays a foundation towards this by developing a novel detection model to identify poisoned biased passages before they can make their way into databases. From the results, we observe that the detection model achieves a high recall score of 97.75%.

title: Transformer-Based Sparse CSI Estimation for Non-Stationary Channels.
abstract: Accurate and efficient estimation of Channel State Information (CSI) is critical for next-generation wireless systems operating under non-stationary conditions, where user mobility, Doppler spread, and multipath dynamics rapidly alter channel statistics. Conventional pilot aided estimators incur substantial overhead, while deep learning approaches degrade under dynamic pilot patterns and time varying fading. This paper presents a pilot-aided Flash-Attention Transformer framework that unifies model-driven pilot acquisition with data driven CSI reconstruction through patch-wise self-attention and a physics aware composite loss function enforcing phase alignment, correlation consistency, and time frequency smoothness. Under a standardized 3GPP NR configuration, the proposed framework outperforms LMMSE and LSTM baselines by approximately 13 dB in phase invariant normalized mean-square error (NMSE) with markedly lower bit-error rate (BER), while reducing pilot overhead by 16 times. These results demonstrate that attention based architectures enable reliable CSI recovery and enhanced spectral efficiency without compromising link quality, addressing a fundamental bottleneck in adaptive, low-overhead channel estimation for non-stationary 5G and beyond-5G networks.

title: HiPMD: Hierarchical Prompting meets Multi-Layer Distillation for Incomplete Multimodal Learning.
abstract: Recently, prompt learning and knowledge distillation have become mainstream for missing-modality learning in multimedia systems. However, existing approaches face two major limitations: static prompts struggle to capture inter-modal relations and adapt to individual instances; and knowledge transfer relies on complete modalities and high-level alignment, limiting cross-modal generalization. We propose Hierarchical Prompting with Multi-Layer Distillation (HiPMD), a unified framework enabling robust and adaptive semantic modeling under missing modalities. HiPMD (i) employs scenario-level prompts to capture diverse missing-modality patterns and inter-pattern relations, (ii) uses instance-level adaptive prompts to refine scenario priors with sample-specific features for fine-grained reasoning, and (iii) applies multi-layer distillation to transfer modality-shared and task-specific knowledge across feature layers. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that HiPMD consistently outperforms prior methods, achieving a 3.62% improvement on the Hateful Memes dataset and demonstrating strong potential for adaptive multimodal learning in multimedia systems. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Hipmd-76B3.

title: Not all who wander are lost: Industrial Network Topology Inference via Tomography Probing.
abstract: Understanding the topology of, and interconnectivity within a computer network is fundamental to enabling security, optimising performance, and ensuring digital resilience. This is particularly challenging in the context of Industrial Control Systems (ICS) where networks use alternative topological structures and comprise legacy equipment that is often poorly documented. In this paper, we investigate how network tomography techniques can be used to achieve topology inference in ICS environments. Topology inference through network tomography enables the network topology to be identified without direct monitoring of the internal network elements, making it a promising technique for use in ICS networks which can be difficult to monitor due to being highly physically distributed or difficult to access. Through experimental analysis of active measurement techniques, we evaluate Round Trip Time (RTT) probes and the efficacy of different inference algorithms such as Rooted Neighbour Joining and Maximum Likelihood Tree to achieve topology discovery. The results highlight that existing topology inference approaches achieve average accuracies between 59.7% and 88.6%. Furthermore, we identify that topology structure has the greatest impact on inference accuracy, with PLC vendor and traffic volumes providing lower variation in performance.

title: Active RIS-Aided Mixed FSO-THz NOMA Network: Performance and Statistical Analysis.
abstract: We analyze the performance of a dual-hop mixed free-space optical (FSO)–Terahertz (THz) downlink system employing non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), where the THz transmission is assisted by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). The FSO link follows the Fisher–Snedecor $\mathcal{F}$ distribution to model moderate-to-strong turbulence, while the THz link is characterized by the α − µ distribution to capture severe fading. The probability density function of the individual THz channel with pointing errors and its generalized moments are derived. Subsequently, the cascaded THz channel via the RIS is approximated by a Gamma distribution, from which the end-to-end outage probability is obtained. The impacts of atmospheric turbulence, pointing errors, imperfect channel state information (CSI), and imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC) are examined. Moreover, an asymptotic outage expression is derived to reveal the influence of key parameters on the outage slope. The analytical results are validated through Monte Carlo simulations.

title: Bridging Cloud and Edge for Digital Twins: A Qualitative and Quantitative Study of WASM, Unikernels, and Containers.
abstract: The Digital Twin (DT) technology is gaining increasing relevance across various domains, enabling real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and closed-loop control in mission-critical scenarios. As DTs deployments evolve toward large-scale distributed architectures spanning the cloud-edge continuum, the adoption of modern DevOps practices becomes essential to ensure DT continuous integration, automated delivery, and operational resilience. These environments are inherently heterogeneous, combining resource-constrained edge nodes with high-performance cloud infrastructures, which introduces significant challenges in choosing suitable execution environments for DT services. In this paper, we conduct a systematic comparative analysis of two emerging technologies, WebAssembly and unikernels, against the current state-of-the-art container-based approach, represented by Containerd, that underpins widely adopted platforms, such as Docker and Kubernetes. Our study combines quantitative benchmarks and qualitative assessments to evaluate critical dimensions, including startup latency, resource efficiency, isolation, portability, and DevOps integration capabilities. The proposed analysis aims to uncover the trade-offs associated with adopting each execution environment for DT workloads, providing actionable insights to guide both operational decisions and the design of next-generation automation and orchestration frameworks.

title: Sequential BP-based Decoding of QLDPC Codes.
abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are a leading approach to quantum error correction, yet conventional belief propagation (BP) decoders often perform poorly, primarily due to non-convergence exacerbated by stabilizer constraints, which induce short cycles and degeneracy. We propose two scheduling variants, sequential check node scheduling (SCNS) and sequential variable node scheduling (SVNS), that improve BP’s error-correction ability by processing check nodes (CNs) or variable nodes (VNs), respectively, in a fixed order, stabilizing message updates and reducing stalls. We also employ this technique to an improved BP-variant called BP guided decimation (BPGD), where symbols are progressively fixed during decoding iterations. Here, we demonstrate that the sequential BPGD (SBPGD) decoder can further improve the convergence properties and performance of the decoder. On standard QLDPC benchmarks under a Pauli-X noise model, our sequential schedules are shown to lower the block error rate relative to conventional BP, and SBPGD outperforms BPGD while using significantly fewer decimation rounds, translating to lower computational cost. These results demonstrate that changing the update schedule, without altering the code, can improve both the reliability and efficiency of BP-based decoding for QLDPC codes. For the [[1922, 50, 16]] C2 hypergraph-product code with independent X errors, SVNS-BP surpasses BP–OSD–0 in error correction at roughly the same complexity as standard BP.

title: Contextual Bandits and Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces for Predictive LTM Handover Decisions.
abstract: This article addresses the challenge of optimizing handover (HO) in next-generation wireless networks by integrating Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS), predicting received signal power, and utilizing learning-based decision-making. A conventional reactive HO mechanism, such as lower-layer triggered mobility (LTM), is enhanced through linear prediction to anticipate link degradation. Additionally, the use of RIS helps to mitigate signal blockage and extend coverage. An online trained non-linear Contextual Multi-Armed Bandit (CMAB) agent selects target gNBs based on context features, which reduces unnecessary HO and signaling overhead. Extensive simulations evaluate eight combinations of these techniques under realistic mobility and channel conditions. Results show that CMAB and RSRP prediction consistently reduce the number of HO, ping-pong rate and cell preparations, while RIS improves link reliability.

title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Unsupervised Log Anomaly Detection on Logs from Real Network Systems.
abstract: Log anomaly detection is an essential component in maintaining the reliability of industrial and production network systems. While many unsupervised LSTM-based methods have been evaluated on open datasets, their behavior on logs collected from actual network systems remains unclear. In this paper, we conduct a comparative evaluation of five unsupervised log anomaly detection models—DeepLog, DeepLog with Word2Vec embeddings, DeepLog with BERT embeddings, LogAnomaly, and LogAnomaly with BERT embeddings—using both public datasets (HDFS and OpenStack) and three proprietary datasets collected from actual network systems. The results show that detection performance depends more strongly on dataset characteristics than on architectural differences or embedding options.

title: Proactive SFC Provisioning with Forecast-Driven DRL in Data Centers.
abstract: Service Function Chaining (SFC) requires efficient placement of Virtual Network Functions (VNFs) to satisfy diverse service requirements while maintaining high resource utilization in Data Centers (DCs). Conventional static resource allocation often leads to overprovisioning or underprovisioning due to the dynamic nature of traffic loads and application demands. To address this challenge, we propose a hybrid forecast-driven Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework that combines predictive intelligence with SFC provisioning. Specifically, we leverage DRL to generate datasets capturing DC resource utilization and service demands, which are then used to train deep learning forecasting models. Using Optuna-based hyperparameter optimization, the best-performing models, Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network, Temporal Graph Neural Network, and Long Short-Term Memory, are combined into an ensemble to enhance stability and accuracy. The ensemble predictions are integrated into the DC selection process, enabling proactive placement decisions that consider both current and future resource availability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method not only sustains high acceptance ratios for resource-intensive services such as Cloud Gaming and VoIP but also significantly improves acceptance ratios for latency-critical categories such as Augmented Reality increases from 30% to 50%, while Industry 4.0 improves from 30% to 45%. Consequently, the prediction-based model achieves significantly lower E2E latencies of 20.5%, 23.8%, and 34.8% reductions for VoIP, Video Streaming, and Cloud Gaming, respectively. This strategy ensures more balanced resource allocation, and reduces contention.

title: BYOD-Gait: Spoofing Proof Gait Authentication with User-Owned Device.
abstract: Gait-based user authentication is a promising biometric approach that leverages the unique motion patterns of individuals for identity verification. With the rise of mobile and wearable technologies, personal devices can utilize their inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensors to collect motion patterns of the users, enabling low-cost authentication in a Bring-Your-Own-Device (BYOD) setting. However, this scheme blindly trusts whatever motion data the device uploads, making them vulnerable to replay or synthesized traces. We close this gap with a liveness check that compares each untrustworthy IMU stream with co-located Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) captured by trustworthy pre-deployed "authentication stations". When a person walks, their body rhythmically disturbs the wireless channel; we estimate a per-second speed trace from CSI and require it to agree with the IMU's per-second speed trace. Genuine walks align; replays, GAN-generated deep-gait signals and treadmill attempts do not. After a segment passes liveness, we perform user identification using only the IMU stream, keeping CSI solely for liveness evidence. Built with low-cost, off-the-shelf personal devices and WiFi-routers, we prototyped our idea and evaluated the performance, reliability, and overhead of the system. Our experiments achieve a 97% true-accept rate at under 1% false accepts, reject every attack in under ≈5 seconds, and add negligible bandwidth and energy overhead, turning ordinary personal devices into secure, low-cost keys for doors, and IoT services—without cameras, badges, or extra wearables.

title: Just-in-time Restoration with Distributed Fiber Sensing in Metropolitan Optical Networks.
abstract: Distributed Fiber Sensing (DFS) leverages optical backscattering signals to predict failure events and enable just-in-time restoration in metropolitan optical networks, i.e., without optical amplifiers.
