In this paper, we study the effectiveness of proactive restoration based on DFS information in all-optical networks, while considering different sensing devices' capabilities. We evaluate whether restoration can be provisioned just-in-time before a failure happens, and its impact on key performance metrics, including the number of affected and suspended optical circuits, bandwidth blocking rate, and service downtime. Simulation results demonstrate that just-in-time restoration enabled by DFS with a prediction time capability of 15~ms can reduce circuit disruptions by more than 90\% compared to restoration without sensing and ensure optical service continuity in optical networks comparable to resource-intensive protection schemes, at a fraction of the spectral resources.

title: An Intelligent Traffic Steering Framework for Hybrid Terrestrial-Non-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: Enabling seamless traffic steering between terrestrial networks (TN) and non-terrestrial networks (NTN) is a key requirement for future 6G systems to ensure service continuity, resilience, and global coverage. This paper presents the design and simulation-based validation of an intelligent Traffic Steering (TS) xApp for hybrid TN-NTN operation within an Open RAN architecture. The proposed xApp operates in a near-real-time control loop and selects the serving access by aggregating radio-and network-level key performance indicators (KPIs) collected from the terrestrial RAN together with representative NTN metrics. Rather than relying on offline-trained machine learning (ML) models, the xApp exploits network intelligence derived from real-time telemetry and a configurable, service-aware weighting framework. To ensure stable operation under fluctuating network conditions, hysteresis margins and decision dwell-time mechanisms are explicitly incorporated into the steering logic. Simulation results over a 300 s evaluation window with 1 sec resolution show that, in the absence of stability controls, frequent access oscillations occur, whereas introducing hysteresis margins up to 20% and dwell times up to 3 s reduces steering events by up to 80% without persistent access bias. The results validate the functional behaviour of the proposed xApp and provide practical insights into telemetry-driven traffic steering for hybrid TN-NTN 6G deployments.

title: MEGA-Fence: Multi-metric Entropy-based GMM Aggregation to Defend Poisoning Attacks in FL.
abstract: The exponential growth of Big Data generated by Internet of Things (IoT) devices is foundational to intelligent applications, but its utilization is often hindered by critical privacy concerns. Federated Learning (FL) emerges as the key paradigm to address those concerns by enabling collaborative model training while preserving data locality. However, FL’s collaborative nature makes it highly vulnerable to poisoning attacks, which mainly manipulate gradients or data labels to degrade model performance. Existing robust aggregation techniques struggle with the sensitivity of non-IID data distributions, and traditional cluster-based strategies often fail to correctly distinguish between benign and poisoned model updates, particularly against adaptive attacks like HidAttack. To overcome these limitations, we propose MEGA-Fence, a novel adaptive poisoning attack-resilient aggregation framework. MEGA-Fence automatically discriminates malicious updates using a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) to estimate dynamic thresholds which eliminates the need for manual hyperparameter tuning. It incorporates a robust, multi-metric similarity assessment combining cosine similarity, L2-distance, and Jaccard similarity of gradient signs, coupled with threshold-aware leaky sigmoid weighting for robust aggregation. Comprehensive evaluations on the Human Activity Recognition (HAR) dataset show MEGA-Fence achieves 1-27% higher accuracy and superior F1-score than state-of-the-art FoolsGold, Krum, SignDefence, FedAvg, and Flame techniques.

title: Federated LLM Framework for the Metaverse: Joint VNF Placement and SFC Routing.
abstract: Network Function Virtualization (NFV) is a key enabler for 6G and metaverse applications, supporting flexible service delivery through dynamic placement of Virtual Network Functions (VNFs) and their interconnection via Service Function Chains (SFCs). Most existing deep learning–based solutions for VNF–SFC management rely on centralized training and static models, limiting adaptability to dynamic traffic and heterogeneous infrastructures. These limitations create operational bottlenecks that degrade Quality of Experience (QoE), including suboptimal VNF placement and inefficient SFC routing that increases end-to-end (E2E) latency. To address these challenges, Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising alternative due to their semantic reasoning and contextual awareness. This paper proposes a Federated Learning–based LLM (FL–LLM) framework that guides a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) agent to jointly optimize VNF placement and SFC routing in metaverse systems while preserving data privacy and reducing communication overhead. Built upon the Large Language Model Meta AI (LLaMA) architecture with parameter-efficient Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), the framework enables scalable adaptation across distributed edge–cloud nodes. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed FL–LLM framework consistently outperforms benchmark methods under varying E2E delay budgets and target bitrate requirements, achieving up to a 36% higher QoE score than DRL in high-bitrate scenarios. These gains stem from context-aware, bandwidth-efficient joint VNF placement and SFC routing decisions that sustain service quality under constrained network resources.

title: Dynamic Downlink-Uplink for Spectrum Sharing in Non-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: 6G networks are expected to integrate low Earth orbit satellites to ensure global connectivity by extending coverage to underserved and remote regions. However, the deployment of dense mega-constellations introduces severe interference among satellites operating over shared frequency bands. This is, in part, due to the limited flexibility of conventional frequency division duplex (FDD) systems, where fixed bands for downlink (DL) and uplink (UL) transmissions are employed. In this work, we propose dynamic re-assignment of FDD bands for improved interference management in dense deployments and evaluate the performance gain of this approach. To this end, we formulate a joint optimization problem that incorporates dynamic band assignment, user scheduling, and power allocation in both directions. This non-convex mixed integer problem is solved using a combination of equivalence transforms, alternating optimization, and state-of-the-art industrial-grade mixed integer solvers. We show numerical results for simple setup to demonstrate the effectiveness of the the proposed approach over conventional FDD, achieving up to 94% improvement in throughput in dense deployments.

title: From Ghosts to Beams: Radar-Guided LoS/NLoS Beam Alignment for 60 GHz Communication.
abstract: This paper proposes and experimentally validates a radar-guided beam alignment scheme for 60 GHz indoor communication. The proposed scheme uses azimuth estimates from a co-located low-power FMCW radar to reduce beam-training overhead and sustain connectivity under blockage. The scheme is path-agnostic in the sense that all radar-detected directions, including multi-bounce ghost points, are treated as candidate transmit communication angles without requiring explicit LoS/NLoS identification. During alignment, the transmitter probes only the radar-indicated angles and selects the first beam whose received power exceeds a preset threshold, thereby, avoiding exhaustive or hierarchical beam searches. A prototype integrating a Texas Instruments IWR6843AOP radar system-on-chip (SoC) with 60 GHz phased-array radios was evaluated in laboratory, hallway, and classroom environments. Experimental results show that coarse radar azimuth estimates provide effective angular priors, and that ghost directions often correspond to usable reflected paths that support NLoS links. Across six deployments, radar guidance reduces the number of probed beams by 82–90% in lab/hallway settings and by 42% in a cluttered classroom relative to an exhaustive beam sweep. The proposed scheme offers a low-complexity and energy-efficient approach to robust mmWave connectivity for XR, Industry 4.0, and autonomous robotic networks.

title: Distributed Continuous Aperture Arrays for Multiuser SWIPT.
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed continuous aperture array (D CAPA) to support simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) to multiple information users (IUs) and energy users (EUs). Each metasurface supports continuous surface currents that radiate electromagnetic (EM) waves for information and energy transmission to the users. These waves propagate through continuous EM channels characterized by the dyadic Green function. We formulate a system power consumption (PC) minimization problem subject to spectral efficiency and energy harvesting quality of service (QoS) requirements, where the QoS requirements are derived under the equal power allocation (EPA) scheme. An efficient two layer optimization algorithm is developed to solve this problem by optimizing the power allocation subject to the QoS violation penalties using augmented Lagrangian transformation. Our numerical results show that well optimized current distributions over each metasurface in the proposed D CAPA achieve up to 65% and 61% reductions in overall system PC compared to the EPA and colocated CAPA (C CAPA) cases, while maintaining the same total aperture size and transmission power.

title: Slepian-based Type-2 Codebook Design for 3GPP.
abstract: The third generation partnership project (3GPP) employs an oversampled discrete Fourier transform (OS-DFT) codebook approach to feedback channel state information (CSI) in frequency division duplex massive MIMO systems. However, the large number of antennas envisioned presents challenges for OS-DFT, resulting in excessive feedback overhead due to spectral leakage issues. To address this, we propose using a Slepian basis codebook for CSI feedback. Our approach involves modifying the Slepian sequences, which are bandlimited, to better represent the spatial channel, which resembles a multiband channel. Additionally, since the spatial channel with a uniform planar array is two-dimensional, we utilize two-dimensional Slepian sequences. We propose an algorithm for modeling the spatial channel with these appropriately modified Slepian bases. Our observations indicate that using the Slepian basis requires fewer basis vectors, resulting in reduced CSI feedback overhead. While our primary focus is on the spatial domain, we also briefly discuss the potential for development in the frequency and time domains, highlighting the evolution of codebook design from spatial to frequency and time domains in 3GPP.

title: SENTRY: Saving Energy through Neural Network-based Receiver Systems.
abstract: AI-native receivers have been proven to demonstrate a lower bit error rate (BER) compared to classical receivers under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Our approach, called SENTRY, offers a decision framework to switch between AI-native and classical receivers, specifically to serve Massive Machine-Type Communication (mMTC) traffic for IoT devices that are constrained by transmission power limits. First, through a convolutional neural network (CNN) encapsulated in an xApp and implemented within the Open RAN cellular deployment, SENTRY determines if mMTC traffic is present. If yes, then the xApp activates the AI-native receiver, thus allowing the UE to transmit at lower powers, while relying on the AI-based decoding at the base station to maintain the same BER. We validate SENTRY on an OAI 5G network stack (i) after model quantization through Qualcomm’s AI Model Efficiency Toolkit (AIMET) for increased execution speed, and (ii) under realistic urban microcell (UMi) and site-specific ray-traced mMTC channel conditions. Experiments show that SENTRY-RX achieves BER comparable to high-power classical receivers while reducing transmit power by 3 – 4 dB per UE, yielding up to 50% energy savings with an inference latency of 1.2 ms per OFDM slot for mMTC traffic compared to a classical receiver. This demonstrates its practicality as an energy-efficient solution for enhancing reliability in large-scale mMTC deployments.

title: Precoding Design for Multi-User MIMO Joint Communications and Sensing.
abstract: We investigate precoding for multi-user (MU) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) joint communications and sensing (JCAS) systems, taking into account the potential interference between sensing and communication channels. We derive indicators for the sensing and communication performance, i.e., the detection probability and the communication signal-to-interference-and-noise ratio (SINR) for general input signals. Our results show that the use of the communication signal for sensing can prevent a loss in communication performance if channel interference occurs, while the kurtosis of the transmit alphabet of the communication signal limits the sensing performance. We present simulation results of example setups.

title: InKubeator: Pre-warming In-Memory KV Caches from Disk for Elastic LLM Serving.
abstract: Serving large language models (LLMs) in distributed, cloud-native environments requires dynamic, elastic autoscaling to manage fluctuating demand. This paradigm, however, introduces a critical cold-start problem: new instances created by an autoscaler begin with an empty key-value (KV) cache, forcing the first user request to incur a severe Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) latency penalty from the compute-intensive prefill phase. Existing caching systems focus on runtime, queue-based optimizations, but fail to address the initialization bottleneck. We introduce InKubeator, a novel architecture that eliminates cold-start latency via proactive, disk-based KV cache prefetching. InKubeator extends vLLM with a three-phase architecture: (i) an offline phase persists canonical KV caches to a shared disk; (ii) a startup-time prefetcher loads the cache from disk into CPU RAM before the pod is ready to process prompts; (iii) at runtime, a cache hit entirely bypasses the prefill computation, paging the required cache blocks from host RAM to GPU High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) on demand. A comprehensive evaluation on NVIDIA A100 (with DDR4 RAM) and H100 (with DDR5 RAM) platforms validate this approach. Results show a dramatic reduction in user-facing latency, with the Llama 3.1 70B Instruct model on an A100 platform seeing an 82.3% decrease in TTFT, from 3.67 to 0.65 seconds. InKubeator incurs a predictable, one-time, I/O-intensive initialization phase overhead constrained primarily by host memory bandwidth rather than storage throughput. InKubeator successfully transforms a critical, user-facing, compute-bound latency into a non-user-facing, I/O-bound initialization cost, enabling truly elastic LLM serving.

title: Lightweight Keplerian Prediction of Remaining Visibility Duration of LEO Satellites.
abstract: We propose a computationally efficient method for a ground-based terminal such as a user equipment (UE) to predict the remaining visibility duration of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, crucial for handover. Using a Two-Body-Keplerian model under the circular orbit assumption, we derive an analytical expression for the squared distance between the UE and a satellite. Solving for the stationary point of its derivative directly yields the time of closest approach which corresponds to the maximum elevation. Consequently, the UE performs orbit propagation only once, at this specific instant, to determine the maximum elevation angle and the remaining visibility duration. Analysis using real-world ephemeris data from Starlink and OneWeb constellations demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves over 97% prediction accuracy with significantly reduced computational overhead. Moreover, results also reveal that the proposed method optimizes handover performance making it practical to realize for energy-efficient UE operation.

title: Task Offloading and Handover in Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks.
abstract: The integration of mobile edge computing (MEC) into space–air–ground integrated networks (SAGIN) has emerged as a promising solution to meet the growing demand for computation-intensive and latency-sensitive applications. This paper considers MEC offloading in an SAGIN network, in which a set of ground users offload tasks to a set of non-terrestrial MEC servers embedded at unmanned aerial vehicles and low Earth orbit satellites. Each user offloads its tasks and receives the computed results. A framework is developed, in which as the users move, each user is associated with the same server or handed over to another server that could provide better service at each time slot. An optimization problem is formulated to maximize the size of the completed tasks per user. An ant colony optimization (ACO) algorithm is developed to solve the optimization problem, and an ACO with prediction (ACOP) solution is also developed to further improve the solution quality. Simulation results show that the considered framework enables the users to offload more tasks when compared to a baseline approach, where the users are randomly associated with the servers. Results also illustrate that the ACO and ACOP solutions provide performance close to that obtained through exhaustive search approaches.

title: Privacy-Aware Agent Collaboration for Dynamic VR Slice Management in 6G SD-RAN.
abstract: Ultra-low latency and high throughput are required for Virtual Reality (VR) services in 6G networks, which presents critical challenges for Software-Defined Radio Access Networks (SD-RANs) dynamic resource management. This work propose a mobility-driven, privacy-aware Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for VR slice management, in which cooperative agents maximize resource distribution over end-to-end VR links while protecting the privacy of user data. Our approach incorporates mobility prediction and an information bottleneck encoder to facilitate effective and secure agent collaboration. In simulations, comparisons with traditional methods are studied which show up to 34% throughput improvement, 28% fewer resources, and 85% less privacy leakage, guaranteeing dependable immersive VR experiences in future 6G environments.

title: A Lightweight AI-Driven Framework for Rapid Intrusion Detection in IoT.
abstract: IoT systems are notoriously susceptible to network attacks, given their ubiquity and often resource-constrained Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). While various IDS solutions have been proposed to secure IoT systems, machine learning (ML) and deep neural network (DNN) based techniques are of recent focus in this field, given their ability to adapt to newer attacks. However, such ML and DNN based IDSs are typically classified as heavyweight or lightweight based on their resource footprint. While lightweight IDSs are often chosen for deployment on IoT and edge devices due to their limited resource requirements, their accuracy is typically limited, and improving it typically impacts the speed of detection, and vice versa. In remedy, we introduce a framework that provides an effective tradeoff between accuracy and speed, while keeping AI-based IDS models lightweight for IoT Edge deployment. By merging Edge and cloud support, with tunable offloading based on the complexity of the attacks, our self-improving framework provides measurable reliability, rapid detection, while maintaining lightweight operation, making it a practical framework for real-world deployments.

title: Feasibility Study of VLC-Based Collective Perception for Vehicular Communication.
abstract: This study explores the use of Visible Light Communication (VLC) in Collective Perception (CP) — a technology that enables vehicles and infrastructure to share sensor information to help reduce traffic accidents. Recent advances in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication have spurred growing research interest in CP. However, in regions such as the United States and Japan, only 30 MHz of radio spectrum is allocated for V2X, which is insufficient to effectively support CP.In this paper, we propose integrating VLC into V2X systems to enhance CP, complementing the existing 5.9 GHz band for V2X communications. VLC can coexist with wireless systems that use radio waves, providing an additional optical channel for data exchange. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first study to investigate VLC for CP.We evaluate the feasibility of VLC-based CP through three experiments. First, we measured the application-level delay of a VLC-based CP system in a stationary indoor environment. Next, we evaluated its communication range in a stationary outdoor setting. Finally, to assess robustness under realistic conditions, we conducted driving experiments at vehicle speeds up to 90 km/h. The results demonstrate that VLC-based CP is feasible and could serve as a promising solution to spectrum scarcity in the 5.9 GHz band for future V2X communications.

title: Distributed Multi-Agent Teacher-Student DDPG for Autonomous RIS-Assisted HSR mmWave Communication.
abstract: This paper presents the novel distributed multi-agent teacher-student deep deterministic policy gradient (MATS-DDPG) framework for autonomous transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surface (ATRIS) phaseshift optimization to maximize the weighted sum-rate of users in high-speed railway (HSR) millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication systems. The frame-work features a teacher agent at the base station (BS) with MBSantennas performing beamforming optimization for C carriages each containing Kcusers, while distributed student agents located at each carriage autonomously control NcATRIS elements phaseshift through a feedback system using only a fraction of the BS-to-ATRIS channel power locally measured. The teacher shares minimal global knowledge of the environment with each student: beamforming vector and weighted sum-rate of all Kcusers per carriage. This shared information generates a $\mathcal{O}\left( {2{M_{BS}} + 1} \right)$ communication overhead for every iteration per student agent, instead of $\mathcal{O}\left( {{N_c}} \right)$ direct control signals received at each ATRIS carriage for the centralized approach. The proposed distributed MATS-DDPG with information sharing architecture achieves an optimization complexity scaling of $\mathcal{O}\left( {{{\left( {{M_{BS}}C} \right)}^2}} \right) + C \cdot \mathcal{O}\left( {{{\left( {{N_c}} \right)}^2}} \right)$ compared to centralized complexity scaling of $\mathcal{O}\left( {{{\left( {{M_{BS}}C + {N_c}C} \right)}^2}} \right)$. Extensive simulations demonstrates that MATS-DDPG achieves performance within 98% of centralized benchmarks while outperforming no information sharing variants by up to 15% in global reward, validating its effectiveness for scalable ATRIS deployment in dynamic HSR environments.

title: CGFormer: A Cross-Attention Based Grid-Free Transformer for Radio Map Estimation.
abstract: Radio map estimation (RME), which predicts wireless signal metrics at unmeasured locations from sparse observation measurements, has attracted growing attention as a key enabler of intelligent wireless networks. The majority of existing RME techniques employ grid-based strategies to process sparse measurements, where the pursuit of accurate RME results in significant computational inefficiency and inflexibility for off-grid prediction. In contrast, grid-free approaches directly exploit coordinate features to capture location-specific spatial dependencies, enabling signal prediction at arbitrary locations without relying on predefined grids. However, current grid-free approaches demand substantial preprocessing overhead for constructing the spatial representation, leading to high complexity and constrained adaptability. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel cross-attention grid-free based transformer model for RME. We introduce a lightweight spatial embedding module that incorporates environmental knowledge into high-dimensional feature construction. A cross-attention transformer is then developed to model the spatial correlation between target and measurement points. Simulation results indicate that our proposed RME method reduces RMSE by up to 6%, outperforming the existing grid-based and grid-free baselines.

title: Behavioral Game-Theoretic Resource Allocation for IoT Security under Jamming Attacks.
abstract: This paper introduces a behavioral game-theoretic framework to model strategic interactions between a defender and a jammer in Internet of Things (IoT) networks. We extend the classical Colonel Blotto game by integrating Prospect Theory to capture human cognitive biases in resource allocation under uncertainty. The defender, modeled as a fusion center, allocates limited monitoring bits across heterogeneous IoT nodes based on their connectivity and importance, while a behavioral jammer strategically distributes its jamming power to maximize disruption while evading detection. A behavioral fictitious play algorithm is developed to compute the mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium under prospect-theoretic utility distortions. Simulation results across various network topologies demonstrate that incorporating cognitive biases significantly alters equilibrium strategies and improves the robustness of anti-jamming defense mechanisms in realistic IoT scenarios.

title: Structured Latent Dynamics in Wireless CSI via Homomorphic World Models.
abstract: We introduce a self-supervised framework for learning predictive and structured representations of wireless channels by modeling the temporal evolution of channel state information (CSI) in a compact latent space. Our method casts the problem as a world modeling task and leverages the Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) to learn action-conditioned latent dynamics from CSI trajectories. To promote geometric consistency and compositionality, we parameterize transitions using homomorphic updates derived from Lie algebra, yielding a structured latent space that reflects spatial layout and user motion. Evaluations on the DICHASUS dataset show that our approach outperforms strong baselines in preserving topology and forecasting future embeddings across unseen environments. The resulting latent space enables metrically faithful channel charts, offering a scalable foundation for downstream applications such as mobility-aware scheduling, localization, and wireless scene understanding.

title: Real-Time Encrypted Traffic Classification with P4-DPDK.
abstract: Classifying encrypted traffic remains a significant challenge in network management and security. Accurate identification of encrypted traffic is essential for various applications, including traffic profiling, threat detection, and quality of service optimization. Hardware-based approaches (e.g., P4 switches) are high performing but not available in most operational networks. Existing software solutions are often deployed offline or struggle to handle high-rate traffic efficiently. Their reliance on packet processing through the kernel stack introduces overhead, limiting real-time performance. This work presents an Encrypted Traffic Classification (ETC) system implemented using Programming Protocol-Independent Packet Processors (P4) and Data Plane Development Kit (DPDK) technology, enabling high-speed packet processing by bypassing the kernel stack and eliminating kernel overheads. The system is deployed on the P4-DPDK target running on multicore CPUs of the host. The ETC utilizes a Random Forest (RF) model trained offline on features extracted from packet headers and timing, achieving a classification accuracy of over 90% on a publicly available encrypted traffic dataset. The results highlight that the system can classify encrypted traffic accurately, even in the presence of 100Gbps of background traffic, while also addressing the latency and throughput limitations of traditional packet processing methods.

title: Experimental Validation of Coordinated Machine Learning for Radio Resource Management.
abstract: Efficient radio resource management (RRM) in wireless networks is challenging due to mutual dependence among various RRM parameters. In this paper, we provide a proof-of-concept of coordinated machine learning framework designed to enhance RRM in a realistic network environment. For this purpose, we employ two lightweight deep neural networks (DNNs) that interact through bi-directional feedback, allowing each DNN to refine the prediction of other DNN. The coordination mitigates error propagation and accumulation, leading to improved predictions and more efficient RRM. We implement the framework to open-source OpenAirInterface (OAI) platform, providing a practical proof-of-concept and releasing the corresponding datasets and platform modifications to facilitate reproducibility and further research. We conduct extensive real-world experiments to demonstrate that the coordinated machine learning significantly outperforms both conventional machine learning-based and traditional RRM techniques, with gains ranging from 3.4% to 11.5% and from 4.1% to 20.1%, respectively.

title: Semantic Communication with Hopfield Memories.
abstract: Traditional joint source-channel coding employs static learned semantic representations that cannot dynamically adapt to evolving source distributions. Shared semantic memories between transmitter and receiver can potentially enable bandwidth savings by reusing previously transmitted concepts as context to reconstruct data, but require effective mechanisms to determine when current content is similar enough to stored patterns. However, existing hard quantization approaches based on variational autoencoders are limited by frequent memory updates even under small changes in data dynamics, which leads to inefficient usage of bandwidth.To address this challenge, in this paper, a memory-augmented semantic communication framework is proposed where both transmitter and receiver maintain a shared memory of semantic concepts using modern Hopfield networks (MHNs). The proposed framework employs soft attention-based retrieval that smoothly adjusts stored semantic prototype weights as data evolves that enables stable matching decisions under gradual data dynamics. A joint optimization of encoder, decoder, and memory retrieval mechanism is performed with the objective of maximizing a reasoning capacity metric that quantifies semantic efficiency as the product of memory reuse rate and compression ratio. Theoretical analysis establishes the fundamental rate-distortion-reuse tradeoff and proves that soft retrieval reduces unnecessary transmissions compared to hard quantization under bounded semantic drift. Extensive simulations over diverse video scenarios demonstrate that the proposed MHN-based approach achieves substantial bit reductions around 14% on average and up to 70% in scenarios with gradual content changes compared to baseline.

title: AI-Driven Fuzzing for Vulnerability Assessment of 5G Traffic Steering Algorithms.
abstract: Traffic Steering (TS) dynamically allocates user traffic across cells to enhance Quality of Experience (QoE), load balance, and spectrum efficiency in 5G networks. However, TS algorithms remain vulnerable to adversarial conditions such as interference spikes, handover storms, and localized outages. To address this, an AI-driven fuzz testing framework based on the Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) is proposed to systematically expose hidden vulnerabilities. Using NVIDIA Sionna, five TS algorithms are evaluated across six scenarios. Results show that AI-driven fuzzing detects 34.2% more total vulnerabilities and 5.8% more critical failures than traditional testing, achieving superior diversity and edge-case discovery. The observed variance in critical failure detection underscores the stochastic nature of rare vulnerabilities. These findings demonstrate that AI-driven fuzzing offers an effective and scalable validation approach for improving TS algorithm robustness and ensuring resilient 6G-ready networks.

title: Encoders, Roll Out! A Digital-Twin Enabled Multi-Modal Sensor Transfusion for Proactive I2V Beam Prediction.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication is a key enabler of high-capacity wireless networks, particularly in infrastructure-to-vehicle (I2V) scenarios. However, mmWave links are highly susceptible to blockages, rapid channel variations, and beam misalignment, making fast and reliable beam selection essential. Conventional beam alignment based on channel estimation and exhaustive beam sweeping incurs prohibitive overhead in dynamic vehicular environments. We propose a transformer-fusion (TransFusion) architecture that functions as a Digital Twin–enabled intelligence module for proactive beam prediction in I2V mmWave networks. In utilizing synchronized multi-modal sensing, the Digital Twin maintains a virtual representation of the physical communication environment, enabling candidate beam configurations to be evaluated in the digital domain before physical actuation. TransFusion integrates camera frames, LiDAR and radar point clouds, and GPS data using modality-specific encoders and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, followed by early fusion and transformer-based refinement. Self-attention mechanisms capture long-range spatiotemporal dependencies and cross-modal interactions, enabling accurate and latency-aware beam selection in dynamic urban settings. Evaluation on real-world multi-sensor data demonstrates that Digital Twin–assisted multi-modal fusion substantially improves beam prediction performance, with the camera-GPS-lidar configuration achieving a top-3 accuracy of 90.0% and-0.009552 average actual power loss (APL). These results highlight trade-offs among predictive accuracy, computational cost, and sensing complexity, and showcase the importance of selective modality fusion for real-time, Digital Twin–enabled wireless operation.

title: ORACLE: Reconciling Next-G Cellular Core Operations for Correctness.
abstract: The decomposition of the cellular core into distributed Network Functions (NFs) introduce critical correctness issues due to non-deterministic delays, message reordering, and races. Our analysis show that: (i) 5G control-plane NFs execute messages on a first come, first served basis. They fail to maintain session correctness when these messages arrive out of the order; (ii) 5G core executes operations based on individual message priority. If two procedures have a common message (e.g., session modification message is common in both handover and policy update procedure), the low-priority procedure (policy update) can block the execution of a higher-priority procedure (handover); (iii) races occur when two messages collide, where the core network function arbitrarily executes one of the messages, resulting in an arbitrary outcome. To this end we introduce ORACLE a 5G standard compliant cellular control-plane, that reconciles message execution according to operational context and causal order of messages. It preserves 5G state consistency despite delayed, re-ordered, or re-transmitted messages in distributed deployments. Using real 5G control-plane traces, we show that ORACLE avoids failure-induced recovery and latency spikes under conflicts. As a result, ORACLE improves throughput and latency over state-of-the-art cores specifically when failures occur (e.g., stragglers, retries, and collisions). We further demonstrate that these improvements translates into better end-user performance for latency-sensitive edge applications.

title: Improved Twisted Convolution Precoding for Zak-OTFS.
abstract: Recently, a novel twisted convolution (TC) based precoding scheme that enabled single-tap equalization at the Zak-OTFS receiver has been proposed. This precoder maximized the per-carrier signal-to-interference plus noise ratio (SINR) at the receiver. In this paper, we extend this work in two useful directions. First, we propose a TC precoder that maximizes the correlation between the actual precoded channel response vector and a desired target precoded channel response vector. The proposed correlation-maximizing precoder achieves a better localized response at the receiver, and hence achieves improved symbol error rate (SER) performance. Second, we propose a deep neural network (DNN)-based ‘denoiser’ at the transmitter that enhances the accuracy of the read-off based model-free channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT) estimate, which further improves the SER performance. Heatmaps of the precoded channel response and SER simulation results using Vehicular-A channel model with fractional delays and Dopplers demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed precoder for different delay-Doppler pulse shaping filters.

title: Mobility-Aware Power Control for VCSEL-Based Indoor OWC.
abstract: Optical wireless communication (OWC) is a promising technology for supporting data-intensive services in indoor environments due to its large unregulated spectrum, high spatial reuse, and potential for multi-gigabit data rates. In particular, vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) based systems enable highly directional transmission, allowing efficient spatial separation of users and improved link performance. However, the use of narrow optical beams also makes system performance highly sensitive to user mobility and device orientation, as movement directly affects beam alignment and optical channel gain. Consequently, power allocation strategies that ignore mobility dynamics often provision excess optical power to maintain reliable connectivity, resulting in inefficient energy use. In this work, a power control framework for dynamic indoor OWC networks that explicitly accounts for mobility-driven channel variation is developed. It uses a hybrid Gauss–Markov and learning-based approach that captures both user movement continuity and behaviour-driven orientation changes. The mobility states are then used to guide power allocation decisions. Simulation results show that incorporating mobility-aware channel prediction enables more accurate power allocation, and improves energy efficiency compared with conventional power control schemes in dynamic indoor environments.

title: Robust Beam Codebooks for mmWave/THz Systems: Toward a Stochastic RL Approach.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) and terahertz (THz) massive MIMO systems often rely on predefined beamforming codebooks, which are usually suboptimal in Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) conditions and for hardware-limited transceivers. Reinforcement Learning (RL) enables adaptive, data-driven codebook design without explicit Channel State Information (CSI), but the robustness of such algorithms in practical conditions is underexplored. This paper introduces a robust multi-agent RL framework that learns beam codebooks directly from environmental feedback, eliminating the need for prior channel knowledge. Our method is well-suited for real-world deployments facing unpredictable propagation and hardware constraints. We conduct a comprehensive analysis of three off-policy algorithms, Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3), and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), evaluating their resilience to hardware impairments and feedback noise. Simulations show that SAC consistently outperforms deterministic methods, achieving superior beamforming gains and stability in NLoS scenarios, even under severe impairments. These results demonstrate the promise of RL-based codebook design for robust mmWave/THz massive MIMO systems.

title: NOMA-based Joint Mode Selection and Time Allocation for Wireless Powered D2D Social Users Networks Scenarios.
abstract: Device-to-Device (D2D) social communication represents a technique having potential to tackle the challenge of the doubly-near-far scenario in wireless powered social networks (WPCN) through the utilization of social communication techniques. A framework is presented in this paper for a wireless powered communication system in which cell center users (CCUs) initially harvest energy from the radio frequency signals of the hybrid access point (HAP) before communication with cell edge social users (CEUs) through either cellular connections or D2D communication. To boost the overall throughput of the network, CCUs make use of the innovative non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) approach for interactions with CEUs. The issue is mathematically formulated as a mixed integer nonlinear programming challenge and is subsequently split into two distinct sub-problems. The primary sub-problem sets forth an optimal strategy for selecting the mode to enable effective communication between CCUs and CEUs based on the energy harvested from the HAP. Following this, the ideal allocation of time for energy harvesting and data transmission in either cellular or D2D mode is determined using the Hessian and Lagrangian techniques to enhance the performance of CCUs and CEUs, respectively. The results of the numerical analysis demonstrate that the proposed technique produces superior results in comparison to conventional NOMA and orthogonal multiple access (OMA) approaches.

title: An Energy-Efficient Resource Allocation in UAV STAR-RIS Aided Vehicular Cooperative Road Systems.
abstract: The rapid evolution of Vehicle Road Cooperative Systems (VRCS) demands high energy-efficiency to support seamless and immersive vehicular experiences to the end users. However, the emergence of Simultaneously Transmitting and Reflecting Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (STAR-RIS) offers a transformative approach to enhancing wireless communication by intelligently controlling the propagation environment. Motivated from this, in this paper, we present a framework which integrates UAV-mounted STAR-RIS with VRCS and employs Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to optimize energy-efficient resource allocation. Specifically, a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm is designed to dynamically allocate beamforming vectors and phase-shift coefficients, thereby, maximizing system energy-efficiency while ensuring reliable quality of service. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed DRL driven STAR-RIS assisted VRCS achieves up to 38% improvement in energy-efficiency compared to baseline systems without STAR-RIS and approximately 18% improvement over conventional RIS-based approaches. These findings emphasize the potential of intelligent surface technologies combined with adaptive learning algorithms to enable sustainable, energy-efficient resource allocation in next-generation vehicular communication systems.

title: BER Analysis of All-QPSK PD-NOMA: An Experimental Study with up to Five Users.
abstract: Power Domain NOMA (PD-NOMA) enhances spectral efficiency in wireless systems by enabling multiple users to share the same orthogonal resource. However, the need for interference cancellation at the receivers creates complex Bit Error Rate (BER) dependencies. This paper bridges theory and practice by comparing analytical BER predictions for a specific scenario with experimental results obtained with Universal Software Radio Peripherals (USRPs).

title: Tertiary-Mode STAR-RIS for Secure NOMA: Integrating Transmission, Reflection, and Jamming.
abstract: This paper investigates the physical layer security of a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system assisted by a tertiary-mode simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS), which can perform transmission, reflection, and jamming simultaneously. The system comprises a base station (BS) serving two users located on opposite sides of the STAR-RIS, assuming perfect channel state information (CSI) at the transmitter. To enhance secrecy performance, a subset of STAR-RIS elements is adaptively configured for jamming. A penalty-based alternating optimization algorithm is developed to jointly optimize the BS's active beamforming and the STAR-RIS's passive beamforming and mode selection. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed design substantially improves the achievable sum rate and secrecy performance compared to conventional RIS-assisted and no-RIS benchmarks, highlighting the potential of tertiary-mode STAR-RIS for secure and efficient next-generation wireless communications.

title: Transformer-Based CSI Prediction for FDD Wireless Backhaul Links Under Antenna Vibration.
abstract: In frequency-division duplex wireless backhaul links, feedback and processing latency can cause severe CSI mismatch under weather-induced antenna vibration (AV), where rapid antenna gain fluctuations render commonly used least-squares (LS) estimation unreliable. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a vibration-robust transformer-based CSI predictor (VRTP) that forecasts future CSI using only the transmit–receive training samples within a single frame. The key insight is that, although AV corrupts delayed CSI, the fine-grained temporal structure embedded in the training sequence itself remains informative and can be exploited for prediction. VRTP captures this structure through time-major Transformer encoding and incorporates explicit delay awareness via feature-wise linear modulation, enabling a single model to operate reliably across a wide range of prediction horizons without retraining. To further improve the estimation of low-power channel components, a lightweight mixture-of-experts (MoE) regression head with tap-dependent routing is introduced. Numerical results for a realistic mmWave backhaul scenario demonstrate that VRTP substantially reduces the CSI prediction mean-squared error compared with LS using outdated CSI, achieving gains exceeding 15 dB at long delays and maintaining strong performance advantages even at low SNR. The MoE-enhanced model provides additional improvements of nearly 2 dB at modest computational cost.

title: LLM-Based Net Analyzer rApp for Explainable and Safe Automation in O-RAN Non-RT RIC.
abstract: Modern 5G/6G radio access networks are increasingly programmable through O-RAN, yet their operational complexity has grown with disaggregation, open interfaces, and fine-grained control parameters. While RAN-side analytics and telemetry mechanisms, such as KPI-based monitoring and mobility event reporting, provide visibility into network behavior, operators still face challenges in correlating heterogeneous events and safely translating observations into actionable configuration changes. This paper presents an LLM-based Net Analyzer rApp for the O-RAN Non-RT RIC that enables explainable and safe, human-in-the-loop automation for RAN operations. The proposed rApp adopts an event-informed, batch-triggered reasoning framework in which mobility events are first interpreted, anomalies are confirmed through targeted log inspection, configurations are inspected via tool-gated access, and minimal configuration changes are proposed only after explicit operator approval. The architecture enforces a strict separation between reasoning and actuation, ensuring auditability and operational safety. The system is implemented and demonstrated on a real O-RAN testbed using a reproducible ping-pong handover scenario, illustrating how large language models can function as reasoning co-pilots that transform raw RAN telemetry into structured explanations and controlled remediation workflows, complementing existing analytics-only approaches in the Non-RT RIC.

title: Microsecond Federated SVD on Grassmann Manifold for Real-time IoT Intrusion Detection.
abstract: This paper introduces FedSVD, a novel unsupervised federated learning framework for real-time anomaly detection in IoT networks. By leveraging Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and optimization on the Grassmann manifolds, FedSVD enables accurate detection of both known and unknown intrusions without relying on labeled data or centralized data sharing. Tailored for deployment on low-power devices like the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the proposed method significantly reduces communication overhead and computational cost. Experimental results show that FedSVD achieves performance comparable to deep learning baselines while reducing inference latency by over 10x, making it suitable for latency-sensitive IoT applications.

title: DualSense: WiFi Sensing and Segmentation of Signal Scatterers For Object Reconstruction.
abstract: Wi-Fi sensing for 3D reconstruction faces fundamental challenges such as multipath interference, limited spatial resolution, and signal distortion. These limitations highlight the need for robust models capable of accurately capturing geometric information from commodity wireless signals. This work introduces DualSense, a novel framework addressing the limitation through two distinct pipelines: (i) high-accuracy localization, and (ii) high-fidelity 3D volume reconstruction. Both are built on segmentation of signal scatterers, applying phase-linking techniques to ensure signal coherence across the synthetic aperture. The localization pipeline (i) utilizes bistatic ellipsoidal back-projection to generate a physical map. This is fed into a two-stage cascade: a light re-ranker first filters candidates, which are then refined by a GDN processing 3D patches to achieve centimeter-level accuracy. Concurrently, the reconstruction pipeline (ii) transforms a dense aperture synthesis method wavefield into a structured graph voxel dataset. And then a graph deep network (GNN) is proposed to learn complex spatial relationships and estimate high-fidelity occupancy volumes. Evaluation demonstrates the success of both independent pipelines in DualSense. The localization model achieves a 3D Euclidean distance error of 0.080m, approaching our validation limits, while the reconstruction model produces sharp, high-fidelity volumes of intersection-over-union (IoU) of 0.450 with superior image quality. DualSense thus enables robust 3D object imaging in complex indoor environments, paving the way for non-camera human monitoring.

title: Efficient Quantum Soft Actor-Critic Model for Dynamic Spectrum Sharing in Intelligent O-RAN.
abstract: The Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) architecture enables intelligent Dynamic Spectrum Sharing (DSS), although state-of-the-art deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods have demonstrated remarkable practical results, their integration with quantum computing brings greater potential for enhancements in performance. In this study, we present Quantum Soft Actor-Critic (QSAC), a novel hybrid quantum-classical methodology aimed at tackling barren plateaus and demonstrating enhanced performance compared to conventional DRL benchmarks, including Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) and Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3), achieving a higher demand satisfaction ratio and markedly improved ϵ-band compliance rates under demanding conditions. Additionally, we present a comprehensive architectural design for the effective integration of our framework into the O-RAN non-real-time and near-real-time RICs. Our quantum-enhanced actor significantly reduces the number of trainable actor parameters by over 99% compared to its conventional SAC equivalent (from around 73,000 to merely 377), indicating an important improvement in model efficiency. To promote repeatability and facilitate future research, we offer the open-source implementation of our study.

title: UAV-Assisted Downlink Satellite Covert Communication.
abstract: This paper investigates the use of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to assist covert communication between a low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite and a ground user under the surveillance of a passive warden. The UAV simultaneously serves its own ground network and acts as a friendly jammer to enhance the covertness of satellite transmissions. We derive a closed-form lower bound on the warden's average minimum detection error probability which is then used to define the covert constraint. Building on this, we formulate an optimization problem to jointly design the UAV's 3D placement, its power allocation, and the satellite's transmit power to maximize the system's covert rate. To solve the resulting non-convex problem, we propose an algorithm based on the block coordinate descent (BCD) and successive convex approximation (SCA) techniques, and further develop a Dinkelbach's algorithm for a special case. Numerical results validate the tightness of the derived bound and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms in configuring optimal system parameters.

title: A Joint JSCC-Resource Allocation Framework for QoS-Aware Semantic Communication in LEO Satellite-based EO Missions.
abstract: In Earth observation (EO) missions with Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, high-resolution image acquisition generates a massive data volume that poses a significant challenge for transmission under the limited satellite power budget, while LEO movement introduces dynamic systems. To enable efficient image transmission, this paper employs semantic communication (SemCom) with joint source-channel coding (JSCC), which focuses on transmitting meaningful information to reduce power consumption. Under a quality-of-service (QoS) requirement defined by image reconstruction quality, this work aims to minimize the total transmit power by jointly optimizing the JSCC encoder-decoder parameters and resource allocation. However, the implicit relationship among JSCC parameters, link quality, and image quality, coupled with the presence of mixed integer-continuous variables, makes the problem difficult to solve directly. To address this, a curve-fitting model is proposed to approximate the JSCC compression-SNR-quality relationship. Then, the joint compression ratio-resource allocation (JCRRA) algorithm is proposed to address the underlying problem. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves substantial power savings compared to both greedy algorithms and conventional transmission paradigms.

title: Triple-Layered Anti-Interception Security Framework for Ground Combat Vehicular Networks.
abstract: Tactical Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (TVANs) face significant challenges in ensuring secure and reliable communications. State-of-the-art security solutions for TVANs mainly focus on a single anti-interception technique, sacrificing quality of service (QoS) to prevent energy-based eavesdroppers. We propose a triple-layered anti-interception strategy for TVANs, integrating passive, active, and AES-based encryption defense mechanisms to address this issue. We formulate a non-convex optimization problem that jointly optimizes jamming allocation (JA), power allocation (PA), and key length assignment (KA). We approximate this problem using first-order Taylor approximation and then solve it using an iterative method combined with the difference of convex (DC) functions. To further reduce the computational complexity in the high-mobility environment of ground combat vehicles, we reformulate the problem using a Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL) framework. Simulation results show that the MADRL framework achieves near-optimal performance in real time and outperforms the state-of-the-art baselines in terms of both Low Probability Interception (LPI) and throughput.

title: Hybrid Transformer-based Learning For Enhancing Malware Detection in Cloud-Based Services.
abstract: In recent years, the rise of malware and ransomware has posed significant threats to information security and software-oriented applications, particularly in the cloud-based and virtualized environments. This study explores a novel transformer-based model to enhance malware detection through dynamic analysis of portable executable (PE) files. By applying API hooking techniques, it is possible to track traces of viruses, such as call addresses, API names, input parameters, and return values. The features can be used in a transformer learning to identify the behavior of either virus-infected or benign files. This work also enhances the combination of data augmentation and the transformer-based learning model to detect ransomware, even with imbalanced datasets or excessive data similarity. The proposed model achieved a remarkable detection accuracy of 93.42% for binary classification and 87.56% for multi-class classification, outperforming traditional methods. This study highlights the effectiveness of transformer-based approaches in addressing the evolving context of malware threats and provides a foundation for developing robust security solutions in cloud-based services.

title: Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative UAV Relay Networks Under Jamming Attacks.
abstract: The deployment of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms as dynamic communication relays is critical for next-generation tactical networks. However, operating in contested environments requires solving a complex trade-off, including maximizing system throughput while ensuring collision avoidance and resilience against adversarial jamming. Existing heuristic-based approaches often struggle to find effective solutions due to the dynamic and multi-objective nature of this problem. This paper formulates this challenge as a cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) problem, solved using the Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE) framework. During the offline training phase, a centralized critic utilizes global state information (available in the simulation environment) to guide decentralized actors. Crucially, during online execution, agents operate solely based on local observations, requiring no global communication. Simulation results show that our proposed framework significantly outperforms heuristic baselines, increasing the total system throughput by approximately 50% while simultaneously achieving a near-zero collision rate. A key finding is that the agents develop an emergent anti-jamming strategy without explicit programming. They learn to intelligently position themselves to balance the trade-off between mitigating interference from jammers and maintaining effective communication links with ground users.

title: Fusion of Ultra-Wideband Radar and Bioelectrical Impedance for Subcutaneous Fat Assessment.
abstract: We propose a high-performance algorithm for estimating abdominal subcutaneous fat thickness using personal mobile devices: a smartwatch with an embedded body impedance analysis function and a smartphone with an integrated ultra-wideband radar. Knowing subcutaneous fat thickness provides insight into an individual's overall body composition and health status, helping to assess risks associated with obesity or malnutrition. It is an indicator for evaluating the effectiveness of diet, exercise, or medical interventions aimed at improving health. The proposed algorithm was validated in clinical trials with 90 subjects, representing a uniform distribution of ages and body mass indexes. It achieves high performance in subcutaneous fat thickness estimation, with a coefficient of determination of 0.92 and a root mean square error of 2.51 mm.

title: AdaptiveOnline-IDS: Efficient Intrusion Detection via Lifelong Learning and Knowledge Distillation.
abstract: Traditional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) often struggle to adapt to the evolving nature of network threats and the changing distribution of data. This paper presents a novel intrusion detection framework that leverages state-of-the-art Lifelong Learning (LL) algorithms to continuously and effectively detect network anomalies while addressing the critical issue of catastrophic forgetting. The proposed approach begins by extracting network flows from raw Packet Capture (PCAP) files and organizing them into sequential tasks that represent different time periods or attack types. A Teacher-Student model is employed, in which knowledge distilled from the Teacher network guides the Student network through the initial learning phases. By utilizing advanced LL techniques, the framework ensures the preservation of previously learned information while maintaining adaptability to emerging threats. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly improves detection accuracy over time and achieves high computational efficiency. This adaptive and scalable solution highlights the potential of combining flow-based analysis with LL strategies to enhance the resilience and effectiveness of modern intrusion detection systems.

title: On the Performance Analysis of Optical Wireless Integrated Sensing and Communications.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has been identified as a key paradigm for future wireless networks by enabling spectrum and hardware-efficient coexistence of data transmission and environmental sensing, utilizing shared waveforms. On the other hand, by leveraging the large unregulated bandwidth, high spatial resolution, and inherent security of optical wireless links, optical wireless ISAC (O-ISAC) is attractive for high-accuracy indoor sensing and communication applications. While existing literature largely explores O-ISAC through resource allocation or architectural design, this paper provides a waveform-level analysis, focusing on the sensing performance of direct-current-biased optical OFDM (DCO-OFDM). More specifically, we derive closed-form expressions for the ambiguity function (AF) of the DCO-OFDM waveform as well as its mean and variance to characterize the ranging performance. Our analysis reveals that the required DC bias and the imposed Hermitian symmetry for intensity modulation/direct detection (IM/DD) fundamentally alter the AF compared to its conventional radio-frequency counterpart. Furthermore, we show that the AF variance is inherently linked to the fourth-order moment of the employed signal constellation. Finally, numerical results obtained with Monte-Carlo simulations validate the accuracy of the derived analytical expressions, providing a theoretical foundation for the design of optimized waveforms and constellations in O-ISAC systems.

title: Where is My Drone Delivery? Towards Multi-Actor Threat Modelling for Autonomous Delivery Systems.
abstract: Autonomous uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly proposed for the last-mile delivery, where security, safety, and environmental effects interact in a single operational setting. Such deployments are inherently multi-actor with crossdomain interactions. Current threat-modelling formalisms provide structured views of attacks, failures, and countermeasures but are often applied in isolation and rely on assumptions that may not hold in open, dynamic environments. In this paper, we present an initial step towards a unified semantic basis for interpreting such models via a risky world, a labelled transition system populated by interacting originators (actors) with potentially conflicting objectives. Threat models are interpreted as partial views by restricting world paths to selected originators, yielding a validity relation that characterises when a model describes the world behaviour. This enables principled comparisons of threat models across domains and makes explicit the assumptions under which their conclusions hold. Using a drone-delivery scenario, we illustrate how attacker, defender and environmental models relate to the same world and show that a threat model validated in isolation can be invalidated by cross-interactions. These results motivate joint representation. We do not provide a new threat-modelling paradigm, but a semantic bridge for future exploration connecting multiple methods.

title: Quantum PUF and Quantum Biometric-Based Identification Supporting Authentication.
abstract: The fundamental information-theoretic limits of secure identification and authentication protocols that leverage Quantum Physical Unclonable Functions (QPUFs) and Quantum Biometrics are established in this paper. A unified theoretical framework is developed for enrollment-based identification systems with key generation that encompasses both QPUF-based device fingerprinting and quantum biometric modalities. This framework extends classical models of identification and key generation to both classical-quantum (c-q) and quantum-quantum (q-q) settings. The primary contribution of this work is the derivation of the complete, single-letter capacity region for the c-q model, which characterizes the ultimate trade-offs between the identification rate, secret-key rate, privacy-leakage rate, and public-storage rate. Furthermore, we establish a tight achievable region for the more general q-q model, quantifying the potential performance gains achievable with coherent quantum correlations. These results are also shown to hold for secret-key binding protocols, demonstrating an equivalence between key generation and secure storage. These findings provide comprehensive information-theoretic foundations for the design and analysis of secure, scalable, and privacy-preserving identification systems.

title: Low-Overhead Phase-Based Ranging for Sub-GHz Wireless Systems Using Fractional-N PLL.
abstract: Remote keyless entry (RKE) systems are widely adopted in modern vehicles for their convenience, but they remain vulnerable to relay attacks that exploit wireless channels. Wireless ranging between the key fob and the vehicle has been recognized as an effective countermeasure. We have previously proposed a bidirectional sub-GHz ranging technique based on phase detection. However, implementing such phase-based ranging on existing transceiver System-on-Chips (SoCs) typically requires redesigning the transmitter and receiver architectures, which leads to increased development time and the loss of established design advantages. This paper proposes a novel phase-based ranging method that requires no modification to the RF/analog architecture of the existing transceiver. The key idea is to estimate and compensate for the initial phase variation of the internal local oscillator (LO) caused by switching between transmission and reception frequencies. The proposed method introduces a duplicated integrator within the delta-sigma modulator of a fractional-N phase-locked loop (PLL). The duplicated integrator continues operating independently of frequency changes, enabling accurate estimation of the initial LO phase variation by comparing its integral value with that of the original integrator. The proposed approach preserves the proven transceiver design, leveraging its established advantages while significantly reducing development time while maintaining low power consumption and compact SoC implementation. Simulation results demonstrate that accurate phase-based ranging can be achieved without architectural redesign, making the proposed method well-suited for secure and efficient wireless ranging in RKE and similar IoT applications.

title: Transcriber: A Lightweight Dynamic Trigger Filter for Securing LLM-enabled Robots.
abstract: Large language Models (LLMs) have been widely applied in robotics such as executable code generation. The transferability and convenience offered by in-context learning (ICL)-based embodied artificial intelligence (EAI) significantly enhance efficiency but also introduce security risks, particularly backdoor attacks. Although several security mechanisms have been proposed, such as incorporating additional prompts for risk analysis or requiring LLMs to perform multi-round reasoning on the generated code, these approaches substantially increase computational overhead and costs while still exhibiting high false positive rates. In this paper, we propose a plug-and-play framework named Transcriber, which functions as a trigger filter to defend against backdoor attacks in ICL-based EAI. Transcriber effectively reduces both the false positive rate and trigger survival rate across various types of triggers compared with a wide adopted lightweight detection methods. Furthermore, we introduce a dual trigger filter mechanism to mitigate false positives and enhance overall filtering performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach preserves task executability for benign instructions, while effectively removing triggers from malicious ones, thereby defending against backdoor attacks in EAI.

title: Quantum-Channel Matrix Optimization for Holevo Bound Enhancement.
abstract: Quantum communication holds the potential to revolutionize information transmission by enabling secure data exchange that exceeds the limits of classical systems. One of the key performance metrics in quantum information theory, namely the Holevo bound, quantifies the amount of classical information that can be transmitted reliably over a quantum channel. However, computing and optimizing the Holevo bound remains a challenging task due to its dependence on both the quantum input ensemble and the quantum channel. In order to maximize the Holevo bound, we propose a unified projected gradient ascent algorithm to optimize the quantum channel given a fixed input ensemble. We provide a detailed complexity analysis for the proposed algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed quantum channel optimization yields higher Holevo bounds than input ensemble optimization.

title: SOCP-Embedded DRL for Low-Energy Hybrid Beamforming in Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems with Imperfect CSI.
abstract: As a key technology for future 6G networks, the dense deployment of access points (APs) with digital beamforming (DBF) architecture in cell-free massive MIMO systems significantly enhances user throughput but also leads to substantial energy consumption. Hybrid beamforming (HBF) provides an effective trade-off between performance and energy consumption by reducing the number of RF chains. In practical applications, it is challenging to acquire accurate channel state information (CSI) for HBF, especially due to the large antenna arrays. Moreover, the precoder dimension of HBF becomes strongly coupled with the number of active RF chains. In this paper, the total system energy consumption is reduced in cell-free massive MIMO systems with a partially connected HBF architecture, while simultaneously satisfying user QoS requirements. Specifically, a closed-form expression for the downlink user capacity is derived based on the estimated CSI, decoupling the precoder dimension from the RF-chain configuration. Using the derived capacity expression, a low-energy optimization problem is developed, where the number of activated RF chains and the transmit power are jointly optimized. To efficiently solve the resulting mixed-integer nonlinear programming problem, a second-order cone programming–embedded DRL framework is proposed, which integrates the stability of traditional optimization and the fast decision-making of DRL, achieving faster convergence and superior performance compared with conventional DRL. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves 27.2% faster convergence and 75% higher performance than conventional DRL, and further saves 85.4% and 90.4% energy compared with the full RF-chain activation and DBF schemes, respectively.

title: Delay Outage Constrained Precoding Design for RTBC via A Rate-penalty Approach.
abstract: In this paper, an efficient precoding design is proposed to guarantee quality-of-service (QoS) for more users in 6G real-time broadband communication (RTBC) applications. The weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization problem under delay outage constraints and total transmit power constraint is revisited for a downlink multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) system. Initially, the intractable delay outage constraints are transformed into minimum rate constraints by employing stochastic network calculus theory. Subsequently, two penalty terms, including QoS relaxation penalty term and QoS guarantee penalty term, are introduced into the optimization problem, which can increase the number of users satisfying their QoS requirements. By applying difference-of-concave programming and semidefinite relaxation method, the optimization problem is transformed into a tractable convex one. Then, a precoding algorithm via a rate-penalty approach (RPA) is proposed based on successive convex approximation to find a solution to the problem. Through numerical results, the superiority of the proposed scheme is demonstrated under the key performance evaluation metric defined by 3GPP, i.e., user satisfaction ratio.

title: Dynamic Security Resource Allocation in V2X Edge Computing via Attention-BiGAN and DRL.
abstract: To address the security defense challenges arising from constrained computational resources and highly dynamic network threats in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) edge computing nodes, this paper proposes a closed-loop dynamic resource scheduling and intrusion detection framework based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). First, a Bidirectional Generative Adversarial Network (BiGAN) integrated with a channel attention mechanism serves as the core detection engine to capture concealed attack features within high-noise communication environments through feature recalibration. A risk-adaptive dual-stream scheduling mechanism is designed, wherein a Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent is employed to dynamically regulate the allocation ratio of security detection resources based on real-time perceived threat levels and communication queue backlog states. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves an F1-score of 0.9389 on the NSL-KDD dataset while attaining a Pareto optimal balance between detection accuracy and communication latency. Compared with static high-resource strategies, the proposed approach significantly reduces queuing latency, thereby guaranteeing the real-time performance and security of critical V2X services.

title: A Spatio-Temporal Diffusion Approach for Communication-Efficient Digital Twin Synchronization.
abstract: Digital twin (DT) provides an effective paradigm for modeling and monitoring large-scale spatio-temporal traffic sensing systems by constructing real-time virtual replicas of geographically distributed roadside sensing entities. However, practical deployment of DT is challenged by the excessive uplink communication overhead incurred by continuous real-time state synchronization. To fill this gap, we propose a communication-efficient DT synchronization framework that combines selective uplink reporting at the base station with diffusion-based state completion at the DT server. Leveraging the uncertainty estimation capability of diffusion models, we quantify reconstruction uncertainty by measuring the variability of spatio-temporal states across multiple diffusion-based completion samples, and jointly incorporate node importance derived from the underlying geographic connectivity to capture spatial redundancy. Numerical results show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms random masking in DT reconstruction accuracy under the same communication budget, demonstrating its effectiveness for communication-efficient DT synchronization.

title: Improving Key Randomness in Physical-Layer Wireless Security via Semi-Synchronized RSSI and Cubic Spline Projection.
abstract: Robust security methods are crucial in wireless networks to protect sensitive data transmission and physical-layer key generation provides a novel solution for short-term session key encryption in wireless communication systems. This paper presents a new approach to key generation at the wireless physical layer using Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI). We propose a semi-synchronized algorithm to make the synchronization process less dependent on time. To enhance the randomness of generated keys, particularly in low mobility or low entropy scenarios, we introduce the Cubic Spline Projection (CSP) technique to increase the inherent randomness and range of RSSI measurements. Finally, to tackle reconciliation challenges in key generation, we employ an extended version of the Jules Sudan algorithm for error code correction. With the increased randomness from cubic spline projection, we effectively eliminate the need for a high degree of motion in physical layer-based key generation. Numerical results demonstrate that our scheme achieves high bit entropy, low bit disagreement, and reliable key generation even in environments with minimal inherent randomness.

title: On-Device AI/ML Codebook Self-Learning for Enhanced Beamforming of Network-Controlled Repeaters.
abstract: We propose a standards-compliant, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML)-enabled codebook self-learning method for network-controlled repeaters (NCRs) that preserves the 3GPP Release-18 signalling chain while updating the NCR beam codebook entirely on-device. Our machine-learning pipeline converts discrete precoding matrix indicator (PMI) histories into a high-resolution spatial probability mass function (PMF) via kernel density estimation (KDE), then applies spherical k-means++ to extract representative directions and synthesize a new uniform planar array (UPA) codebook. Because learning runs inside the NCR, no new messages or gNodeB (gNB)–NCR codebook synchronization are required. Using a Hongdae 3D urban digital twin with ray-tracing channels, we quantify gains over a conventional discrete fourier transform (DFT) codebook: the ML-updated codebook produces beams that consistently improve beamforming gain and throughput across codebook sizes, with pronounced sum-rate increases when indoor users dominate. These results show that PMI-driven, ML-based NCR adaptation can significantly enhance the indoor coverage and system sum-rate without any air-interface changes, offering a practical building block for next-generation repeater-assisted deployments.

title: Phase-Based Bit Commitment Protocol.
abstract: With the rise of artificial intelligence and machine learning, a new wave of private information is being flushed into applications. This development raises privacy concerns, as private datasets can be stolen or abused for non-authorized purposes. Secure function computation aims to solve such problems by allowing a service provider to compute functions of datasets in the possession of a a data provider without reading the data itself. A foundational primitive for such tasks is Bit Commitment (BC), which is known to be impossible to realize without added assumptions. Given the pressing nature of the topic, it is thus important to develop BC systems and prove their security under reasonable assumptions. In this work, we provide a novel quantum optical BC protocol that uses the added assumption that the network provider will secure transmission lines against eavesdropping. Under this added assumption, we prove security of our protocol in the honest but curious setting and discuss the hardness of Mayer’s attack in the context of our protocol.

title: Generative Resource Allocation for 6G O-RAN with Diffusion Policies.
abstract: Dynamic resource allocation in O-RAN is critical for managing the conflicting QoS requirements of 6G network slices. Conventional reinforcement learning agents often fail in this domain, as their unimodal policy structures cannot model the multi-modal nature of optimal allocation strategies.
