This paper introduces Diffusion Q-Learning (Diffusion-QL), a novel framework that represents the policy as a conditional diffusion model. Our approach generates resource allocation actions by iteratively reversing a noising process, with each step guided by the gradient of a learned Q-function. This method enables the policy to learn and sample from the complex distribution of near-optimal actions. Simulations demonstrate that the Diffusion-QL approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art DRL baselines, offering a robust solution for the intricate resource management challenges in next-generation wireless networks.

title: Constructing Quantum Convolutional Codes via Difference Triangle Sets.
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a construction of quantum convolutional codes (QCCs) based on difference triangle sets (DTSs). To construct QCCs, one must determine polynomial stabilizers X(D) and Z(D) that commute (symplectic orthogonality), while keeping the stabilizers sparse and encoding memory small. To construct Z(D), we show that one can use a reflection of the DTS indices of X(D), where X(D) corresponds to a classical convolutional self-orthogonal code (CSOC) constructed from strong DTS supports. The motivation of this approach is to provide a constructive design that guarantees a prescribed minimum distance. We provide numerical results demonstrating the construction for a variety of code rates.

title: LLM-Guided Digital Twin for Network Experimentation: Fidelity, Robustness, and Optimization.
abstract: Evaluating communication networks traditionally requires costly simulations or physical testbeds. This work presents a closed-loop framework that combines a Large Language Model (LLM) for scenario generation, a Random Forest (RF) surrogate for rapid prediction of key performance indicators (KPI), and an NS-3 digital twin (DT) for validation.The LLM produces schema-constrained scenarios, the RF filters scenarios by predicted throughput, latency, and loss, and high-value cases are executed in the DT with results fed back to refine the RF model and guide subsequent exploration.Experiments demonstrate three outcomes: fidelity, with the digital twin consistently reproducing baseline KPIs across batches (e.g., Cubic-FQ-CoDel maintains 71.13±0.01 Mbps); robustness, with accurate capture of degradation and recovery under failures and identification of resilient protocol-queue combinations (NewReno-CoDel: 95%+ retention); and optimization, with Pareto analysis highlighting Westwood+RED for lowest latency ( 13 ms) and Cubic+RED as overall best (performance score: 23.48).The framework achieves near-perfect prediction accuracy (R2 ≈ 0.99), reduces simulation overhead, and offers interpretable insights for multi-objective optimization. These results position LLM-driven DTs as a practical tool for efficient, data-driven network experimentation.

title: Standard Condition Number-Based Detection for MIMO ISAC Systems under Noise Uncertainty.
abstract: This paper presents a unified analytical and optimization framework for Standard Condition Number (SCN)–based detection in MIMO Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems operating under noise uncertainty. Conventional detectors such as the Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT) and Energy Detector (ED) suffer from false-alarm inflation when interference or jamming alters the noise covariance. To overcome this limitation, the SCN detector, defined as the ratio of the largest to smallest eigenvalues of the sample covariance matrix is analytically characterized for the first time in an ISAC setting. Closed-form expressions for the false-alarm and detection probabilities are derived using random matrix theory for a two-antenna sensing receiver and generalized to arbitrary MIMO dimensions. The analysis proves that the SCN maintains a constant false alarm rate (CFAR) property and remains resilient to covariance mismatch, providing theoretical justification for its robustness in dynamic environments. Leveraging these results, a tractable ISAC power-allocation problem is formulated to minimize total detection error subject to communication rate and power constraints, yielding an interpretable sequential solution. Numerical evaluations verify the theory and demonstrate that the proposed SCN detector consistently outperforms LRT and eigenvalue-based benchmarks, particularly under strong interference and jamming typical of modern multiuser networks.

title: Learning During Inference: Adapting Neural Wireless Receivers Via Demodulation Pilots.
abstract: We propose a zero-overhead online learning framework for orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) neural receivers that directly detect the soft bits of received signals. Unlike conventional fine-tuning methods that rely on dedicated training intervals or full resource grids, our approach leverages existing demodulation pilots to simultaneously enable signal demodulation and model adaptation. We introduce two pilot designs: fully and partially randomized pilots that flexibly support joint demodulation and learning. To accommodate these pilot designs, we develop a receiver architecture, which is a parallel design that separates inference and fine-tuning for uninterrupted operation. The simulation results show that the proposed method effectively tracks the channel distribution variations effectively without additional overhead, service interruption, or catastrophic performance degradation under distribution shift.

title: Energy-Efficient Digital Baseband Design for 3GPP Rel.19 5G NR LP-SS.
abstract: This paper investigates efficient correlator design for the newly released 3GPP 5G NR Rel. 19 Low Power Synchronization Signal (LP-SS) standard. Rel.19 introduces a spectrally efficient wake-up signal, which significantly decreases power consumption for user devices while retaining low latency. The proposed correlator takes advantage of inherent symbol-length integration, minimizing power consumption. Tradeoffs between sequence length, analog-to-digital converter resolution, and sample rate are evaluated against timing accuracy after synchronization. An example design is implemented in a commercial 22nm CMOS process with simulated power for required radio resource management (RRM) measurements.

title: Proof of Concept of QCSP Frames in Earth-to-LEO Satellite Transmission.
abstract: In this paper, we report on a multi-site experiment involving the transmission of a new type of frame for IoT, called Quasi-Cyclic Short Packet (QCSP). QCSP frames are characterized by the combination of a q-ary modulation using Cyclic Code Shift Keying (CCSK) and a q-ary non-binary Error Correction Code (ECC). A QCSP frame does not contain a preamble, making it energy-optimal since no resources are wasted for signaling. However, this absence poses a significant challenge for detection and synchronization, particularly in the case of a LEO satellite, which is subject to strong and fast-varying Doppler shifts. Our experiment demonstrates that such transmission can be successfully recovered.

title: Highly Correlated Feature Elimination Algorithm Based Feature Selection for the Internet of Drones Security.
abstract: Although the Internet of Drones (IoD) and the Internet of Things (IoT) are increasingly integrated into mission-critical applications, they remain highly vulnerable to cyberattacks due to their large-scale, heterogeneous, and resource-constrained nature. Designing efficient intrusion detection systems (IDS) requires not only robust machine learning algorithms, but also effective feature selection methods to reduce redundancy, computational overhead, and overfitting. In this work, we propose the Highly Correlated Feature Elimination Algorithm (HCFEA), a novel feature selection approach that systematically removes redundant features while retaining the most informative attributes for intrusion detection. The method employs correlation-driven elimination and iterative filtering to balance dimensionality reduction with predictive performance. Experiments conducted using the recent CIC-IoT2023 dataset demonstrate that HCFEA consistently outperforms classical filter and wrapper-based approaches, achieving competitive accuracy, precision and recall, while requiring fewer features and reducing inference time. Compared with existing methods, HCFEA improves generalization and computational efficiency, making it well-suited for lightweight IDS deployment in both IoD and IoT environments. These findings highlight the potential of correlation-aware feature elimination to enhance the practicality of ML-based IDS in next-generation cyber-physical networks.

title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning with Local-Reconstruction Error-Feedback-Based Rescaled 1-Bit Compressive Sensing.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is well-suited for the next-generation networks, but it is often constrained by the communication cost of repeatedly transmitting high-dimensional updates. Compressive sensing (CS) alleviates this limitation by utilizing a short measurement vector; however, low-dimensional projection and coarse quantization, especially the 1-bit CS (1BCS), can lead to reconstruction errors that slow down convergence. Therefore, we propose local reconstruction error feedback (LREF), where each device performs 1BCS reconstruction locally to feed back not only the sparsification residual but also the reconstruction discrepancy, and introduce the rescaled 1BCS (R1BCS), which uses a magnitude scalar to rescale the unit sparse gradient estimated from the 1-bit measurement vector. We provide upper bounds on the convergence rate, along with the required constraints to ensure the performance of the proposed design. In experiments, R1BCS-LREF approaches the ideal case (i.e., no reconstruction error) while significantly reducing the cost, confirming that the proposed design effectively counters the reconstruction error.

title: A Novel Detector under Generalized Hardware Impairments.
abstract: This paper presents, for the first time, a maximum-likelihood detection framework that jointly mitigates hardware (HW) impairments in both amplitude and phase. By modeling transceiver distortions as residual amplitude and phase noise (PN), we derive the approximate phase-and-amplitude distortion detector (PAD-D), which operates in the polar domain and effectively mitigates both distortion components through distortion-aware weighting. The proposed detector performs reliable detection under generalized HW impairment conditions, achieving substantial performance gains over the conventional Euclidean detector (EUC-D) and the phase-noise oriented Gaussian assumption for phase noise detector (GAP-D), which is primarily designed to address phase distortions. In addition, a closed-form high-SNR symbol error probability (SEP) approximation is derived, offering a generic analytical expression applicable to arbitrary constellations. Simulation results demonstrate that the PAD-D reduces the error floor by up to an order of magnitude relative to EUC-D and GAP-D for both high-order quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) and optimized super-APSK (SAPSK) constellations, while the analytical SEP provides an accurate and practical tool for system performance evaluation and optimization under realistic transceiver impairments.

title: An Adaptive Grouping and Masking-Based Collaborative Training Framework for Federated Digital Twin Networks.
abstract: Federated digital twin networks (DTNs) continue to face many challenges arising from heterogeneous data distributions across diverse physical twins (PTs), as well as communication and computation imbalances among PTs, further complicated by privacy-preserving constraints. Although traditional federated learning approaches have proposed various solutions, maintaining scalable, secure and real-time synchronization between physical and virtual entities remains difficult. To address these challenges, this paper presents a new collaborative training framework enhanced by a token-based dynamic masking technique to improve synchronization under heterogeneous network and computational conditions. An effective adaptive group formation scheme is introduced to enable efficient and context-aware PTs grouping, while the dynamic masking mechanism ensures robust privacy preservation during communication and aggregation processes. Furthermore, a proximal policy optimization algorithm is employed to learn optimal dynamic grouping policies and maximize long-term system performance. The obtained results demonstrate that the proposed framework supports more frequent model updates, achieves higher learning accuracy, while effectively preserving privacy in federated DTNs.

title: A Federated and Self-Adaptive Generative Adversarial-Based Framework for Real-Time Sensor Anomaly Detection in Human Digital Twins.
abstract: This paper introduces a new federated and self-adaptive generative adversarial network (GAN)-enabled framework, called FedSAGE, for real-time anomaly detection in human digital twin (HDT) networks. Designed for sensor anomaly detection within such distributed environments, FedSAGE adopts federated multi-task learning (FML) to facilitate a self-adaptive GAN, necessary to support local representation learning, data generation and robust anomaly detection. The framework operates in two phases: a collaborative federated adversarial training phase, where local autoencoders and GANs learn from decentralized sensor data without raw data exchange; and an anomaly detection operation phase, where real-time anomaly detection is performed using enhanced local models. Extensive performance evaluations conducted on multivariate sensor data demonstrate FedSAGE’s superiority over commonly adopted traditional methods. Results show significant improvements, including better accuracy, high sample quality and communication efficiency. Overall, FedSAGE is shown to be capable of supporting real-time decision-making in dynamic HDT environments while ensuring low overhead and enhanced privacy. The proposed framework proves highly effective for scalable and decentralized anomaly detection in this emerging cyber-physical system.

title: Queue-Aware Age of Information Optimization Framework for Large-Scale Digital Twin Networks.
abstract: In large-scale digital twin networks (DTNs), maintaining timely synchronization between physical entities and their digital counterparts is crucial for accurate real-time representation. While many communication and computation optimization frameworks have been suggested to enhance such physical-to-virtual synchronizations, heterogeneous update generation rates, limited edge resources, and fluctuating network conditions can cause information delays that degrade system freshness and efficiency, making the overall system very challenging to analyze. This paper, therefore, proposes a queue-aware age of information (AoI) optimization framework that jointly minimizes AoI, latency, and energy consumption within a multi-queue and multi-server DTN environment. Using a discrete-time Geo/Geo/n queuing model, we develop a priority-based scheduling policy that dynamically allocates edge servers based on queue states and AoI. The performance of the proposed framework is compared with other related scheduling policies and evaluated under different generation rates and service-time conditions. Simulation results show that the proposed policy consistently delivers optimal efficiency by balancing information freshness and resource use, while maintaining queue stability and reducing overall system time and energy costs.

title: Two-Phase Routing with Source-Dependent Traffic Distribution Ratios.
abstract: Two-phase routing (TPR) is a routing strategy based on segment routing that aims to balance traffic load in two phases. In TPR, a source node distributes traffic to intermediate nodes in the first phase, and each intermediate node forwards it to a destination node in the second phase. Previous studies addressed two models of TPR: TPR-C and TPR-SD. TPR-C distributes traffic to intermediate nodes with a common set of distribution ratios regardless of each source and destination node pair. TPR-SD distributes traffic to intermediate nodes with distribution ratios depending on each source and destination node pair. TPRSD reduces the network congestion ratio compared to TPR-C, but TPR-SD requires higher deployment complexity. This paper proposes a TPR-based model that enables distribution ratios dependent on each source node but independent of different destination nodes, called TPR-S, to minimize the network congestion ratio under a given traffic matrix. Since TPR-S does not require destination information, it is easier to deploy in an IP network than TPR-SD. We formulate the problem to determine distribution ratios in TPR-S as a linear programming problem. Numerical results show that TPR-S reduces network congestion by up to 53.4% compared to shortest path routing and achieves a comparable network congestion with other baseline models.

title: Type-Based Unsourced Federated Learning With Client Self-Selection.
abstract: We address the client-selection problem in federated learning over wireless networks under data heterogeneity. Existing client-selection methods often rely on server-side knowledge of client-specific information, thus compromising privacy. To overcome this issue, we propose a client self-selection strategy based solely on the comparison between locally computed training losses and a centrally updated selection threshold. Furthermore, to support robust aggregation of clients' updates over wireless channels, we integrate this client self-selection strategy into the recently proposed type-based unsourced multiple-access framework over distributed multiple-input multiple-output (D-MIMO) networks. The resulting scheme is completely unsourced: the server does not need to know the identity of the clients. Moreover, no channel state information is required, neither at the clients nor at the server side. Simulation results conducted over a D-MIMO wireless network show that the proposed self-selection strategy matches the performance of a comparable state-of-the-art server-side selection method and consistently outperforms random client selection.

title: Experimental Analysis of a Bidirectional Air-to-Ground Optical Communication Link.
abstract: Under the German QuNET initiative, Key Exper iment 3 investigates the integration of dynamic mobile nodes into future quantum networks using airborne optical links as an intermediate step to satellite-based scenarios. The experiment aims to demonstrate the applicability of different quantum key distribution (QKD) technologies over long-distance mobile links. The German Aerospace Center (DLR) contributes with the Free-Space Experimental Laser Terminal 2 (FELT-II) and a bidirectional classical optical link, which is essential for both data transmission and tracking operations. This paper presents a preliminary experimental analysis of the classical communication channel during the flight campaign conducted in Erlangen in September and October of 2025. Performance metrics at both the physical layer (received signal strength indicator (RSSI), signal to-noise ratio (SNR)) and data layer (raw and coded bit error rate (BER), round trip times (RTT)) are evaluated under varying day-time and night-time conditions. The results are in line with the expected performance for scientific data transmission and these are subject to limitations arising from the pointing, turbulence and ambient light. These factors particularly affect the stability required for reliable bidirectional communication in air-to-ground link scenarios.

title: Synthetic Graph Data Augmentation for Generative Digital Twins.
abstract: Digital twin systems rely heavily on high-fidelity data to simulate, analyze, and optimize real-world processes. In domains such as communication networks, power grids, transportation systems, and industrial automation, these systems are naturally modeled as graphs, where nodes represent entities (e.g., routers, vehicles, sensors) and edges represent relationships (e.g., data flows, road links, control dependencies). However, collecting large-scale, structurally diverse graph data for training and experimentation remains a major bottleneck, especially in networked systems where real deployments are expensive or impractical. To address this challenge, we propose a scalable, generative graph learning framework that synthesizes larger, structurally consistent graphs from smaller input samples, called GraphSynTwin. Our method captures latent structural patterns using permutation-invariant embeddings and generates synthetic node representations through probabilistic modeling. Connectivity is reconstructed via a geometric decoding scheme that preserves topological characteristics such as community structure and degree distribution. Beyond standalone generation, we demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach for graph-based data augmentation. Through experiments on benchmark datasets, including node classification tasks, we show that augmenting training sets with synthetically generated graph data consistently improves downstream model accuracy. These results highlight the potential of generative graph learning as a powerful tool for enhancing digital twin simulations and enabling robust, data-efficient learning in graph-centric domains.

title: Spatiotemporal Semantic V2X Framework for Cooperative Collision Prediction.
abstract: Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) demand real-time collision prediction to ensure road safety and reduce accident severity. Conventional approaches rely on transmitting raw video or high-dimensional sensory data from roadside units (RSUs) to vehicles, which is impractical under vehicular communication bandwidth and latency constraints. In this work, we propose a semantic V2X framework in which RSU-mounted cameras generate spatiotemporal semantic embeddings of future frames using the Video Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (V-JEPA). To evaluate the system, we construct a digital twin of an urban traffic environment enabling the generation of d verse traffic scenarios with both safe and collision events. These embeddings of the future frame, extracted from V-JEPA, capture task-relevant traffic dynamics and are transmitted via V2X links to vehicles, where a lightweight attentive probe and classifier decode them to predict imminent collisions. By transmitting only semantic embeddings instead of raw frames, the proposed system significantly reduces communication overhead while maintaining predictive accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework with an appropriate processing method achieves a 10% F1-score improvement for collision prediction while reducing transmission requirements by four orders of magnitude compared to raw video. This validates the potential of semantic V2X communication to enable cooperative, real-time collision prediction in ITS.

title: A Lightweight Digital-Twin-Based Framework for Edge-Assisted Vehicle Tracking and Collision Prediction.
abstract: Vehicle tracking, motion estimation, and collision prediction are fundamental components of traffic safety and management in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). Many recent approaches rely on computationally intensive prediction models, which limits their practical deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. This paper presents a lightweight digital-twin-based framework for vehicle tracking and spatiotemporal collision prediction that relies solely on object detection, without requiring complex trajectory prediction networks. The framework is implemented and evaluated in Quanser Interactive Labs (QLabs), a high-fidelity digital twin of an urban traffic environment that enables controlled and repeatable scenario generation. A YOLO-based detector is deployed on simulated edge cameras to localize vehicles and extract frame-level centroid trajectories. Offline path maps are constructed from multiple traversals and indexed using K-D trees to support efficient online association between detected vehicles and road segments. During runtime, consistent vehicle identifiers are maintained, vehicle speed and direction are estimated from the temporal evolution of path indices, and future positions are predicted accordingly. Potential collisions are identified by analyzing both spatial proximity and temporal overlap of predicted future trajectories. Our experimental results across diverse simulated urban scenarios show that the proposed framework predicts approximately 88% of collision events prior to occurrence while maintaining low computational overhead suitable for edge deployment. Rather than introducing a computationally intensive prediction model, this work introduces a lightweight digital-twin-based solution for vehicle tracking and collision prediction, tailored for real-time edge deployment in ITS.

title: A Digital Twin-enabled Swarm Intelligence Approach to Distributed Processing in IoT Networks.
abstract: With the increasing use of Internet of Things (IoT) devices to generate and process data in industry, offices, homes and more, there has been a big shift towards digital twins (DTs). DTs help mimic real computing architectures to manage data generated from edge devices and IoT sensors in order to see the impact of different policies on various performance metrics such as bandwidth requirements and latency. This paper aims to design a DT of the real IoT-edge communication and test a policy for offloading tasks when an edge device is computationally overloaded. We achieved this by balancing the additional tasks between the under-utilised edge devices on the same layer using Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) to dynamically create an efficient Distributed Architecture within the IoT network. The DT was built using a system of Docker containers networked over MQTT, mimicking IoT and Edge devices, connected to a central edge device and a user-interactive ‘manager’ which gives and processes container simulation metrics from cAdvisor. With the help of this DT, we found that using PSO, networks of variety of sizes can efficiently reduce their reliance on the central edge devices whilst maintaining good performance and energy usage across the individual nodes – relieving the need to offload data processing to the cloud.

title: Diffusion-Based Generative Priors for Efficient Beam Alignment in Directional Networks.
abstract: Beam alignment is a key challenge in directional mmWave and THz systems, where narrow beams require accurate yet low-overhead training. Existing learning-based approaches typically predict a single beam and do not quantify uncertainty, limiting adaptive beam sweeping. We recast beam alignment as a generative task and propose a conditional diffusion model that learns a probabilistic beam prior from compact geometric and multipath features. The learned priors guide top-k sweeps and capture the SNR loss induced by limited probing. Using a ray-traced DeepMIMO scenario with an 8-beam DFT codebook, our best conditional diffusion model achieves strong ranking performance (Hit@1 ≈ 0.61, Hit@3 ≈ 0.90, Hit@5 ≈0.97) while preserving SNR at small sweep budgets. Compared with a deterministic classifier baseline, diffusion improves Hit@1 by about 180%. Results further highlight the importance of informative conditioning and the ability of diffusion sampling to flexibly trade accuracy for computational efficiency. The proposed diffusion framework achieves substantial improvements in small-k Hit rates, translating into reduced beam training overhead and enabling low-latency, energy-efficient beam alignment for mmWave and THz systems while preserving received SNR.

title: LLMs meet Federated Learning for Scalable and Secure IoT Management.
abstract: The rapid expansion of IoT ecosystems introduces severe challenges in scalability, security, and real-time decision-making. Traditional centralized architectures struggle with latency, privacy concerns, and excessive resource consumption, making them unsuitable for modern large-scale IoT deployments. This paper presents a novel Federated Learning-driven Large Language Model (FL-LLM) framework, designed to enhance IoT system intelligence while ensuring data privacy and computational efficiency. The framework integrates Generative IoT (GIoT) models with a Gradient Sensing Federated Strategy (GSFS), dynamically optimizing model updates based on real-time network conditions. By leveraging a hybrid edge-cloud processing architecture, our approach balances intelligence, scalability, and security in distributed IoT environments. Evaluations on the IoT-23 dataset demonstrate that our framework improves model accuracy, reduces response latency, and enhances energy efficiency, outperforming traditional FL techniques (i.e., FedAvg, FedOpt). These findings highlight the potential of integrating LLM-powered federated learning into large-scale IoT ecosystems, paving the way for more secure, scalable, and adaptive IoT management solutions.

title: Mitigating Network Uncertainty in Rural Telesurgery: A Satellite-Driven Digital Twin Approach.
abstract: The delivery of telesurgical services to rural areas is hindered by unpredictable connectivity and limited infrastructure. While Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites offer promising low-latency coverage, their performance is vulnerable to visibility loss, handoffs, and link failures. To address this, we propose a Satellite Robotic Telesurgery Digital Twin (SRTDT) framework that integrates causal forecasting with a proxy-surgeon failover mechanism to ensure surgical continuity under network disruptions. Using twelve hours of simulated LEO data, we demonstrate: (i) a multitask deep learning model that predicts satellite visibility and failure types with 88% accuracy; (ii) a causal analysis linking orbital dynamics, such as: elevation, slant range, and path loss to the network KPIs including latency, jitter, throughput and packet loss; and (iii) an interpretable XGBoost+SHAP model that identifies elevation as a dominant driver of end to end delay, supported by Granger causality tests. In a simulated two-hour surgical procedure, our proactive failover mechanism recovered 57% of the execution time lost to network outages, enabling either a safe resumption or a controlled termination of the operation. These results underscore the potential of integrating causal forecasting with autonomous failover to mitigate the risks of satellite dependent telesurgery in remote settings.

title: Against Unreliable Communication in Federated Learning: A Generative Gradient Method.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) over wireless networks frequently suffers from intermittent client unavailability due to time-varying channel conditions and limited power budgets, leading to biased aggregation and performance degradation. To address this challenge, we propose a novel framework termed generative gradient-aided federated learning (GGAFL). Specifically, GGAFL employs server-side gradient generation networks (GGNs) to capture the temporal dependencies of gradient trajectories and generate surrogate gradients for unavailable clients. We rigorously analyze the convergence behavior of GGAFL and reveal that a key term in the convergence rate, referred to as the gradient generation error, is closely related to the adopted resource allocation strategy. Guided by this theoretical insight, we formulate a joint bandwidth allocation and power control problem to minimize the long-term generation error subject to instantaneous latency and long-term power constraints. To solve this stochastic optimization problem, we develop an efficient online algorithm based on Lyapunov optimization and Lagrange dual decomposition. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed GGAFL framework compared with benchmark schemes.

title: Capacity Region of Pinching-Antenna Systems.
abstract: This article characterizes the capacity region of a multiuser Pinching-Antenna System (PASS), in which a single pinched waveguide supports both uplink and downlink communications. The analysis begins with the uplink channel, for which closed-form expressions are derived for the optimal antenna activation position, the corresponding capacity region, and the achievable rate regions under time-division multiple access (TDMA) and frequency-division multiple access (FDMA). It is proven that the capacity region of PASS strictly contains that of conventional fixed-antenna systems, and that the FDMA rate region encompasses the TDMA rate region. The analysis is then extended to the downlink case using the uplink-downlink duality framework. Numerical results confirm that PASS achieves a substantially enlarged capacity region compared with conventional fixed-antenna systems.

title: Fingerprinting AI Applications and Phases in Edge-Assisted Distributed Learning and Inference using Side-Channel Data.
abstract: Edge computing has enabled users to experience ubiquitous artificial intelligence (AI) through distributed learning and inference. Continuous efforts to reduce computing burden from the edge devices and increased preservation of privacy have popularized remote inference and federated learning (FL). However, network-level side-channel information can still expose sensitive operational states. In this paper, we demonstrate that network-level telemetry data can be used to fingerprint edge-assisted learning and inference workflows and reveal their operational phases. We propose a hierarchical classification framework, where the first stage separates learning from inference, and the second distinguishes learning phases. In addition, we develop a testbed with convolutional and recurrent neural network-based FL and remote inference systems, alongside an attacker device collecting network sniffing data. Using features derived from flow volumes, transfer speeds, ratios, and latency, the system achieves fingerprinting accuracy of 100% between learning and inference tasks, and 95.9% across different learning phases. These results highlight the vulnerability of edge-assisted distributed AI systems to network-based side-channel fingerprinting.

title: Multi-Layered Explainable AI for Handover Management in 5G and Beyond Networks.
abstract: The latest developments in 5G and beyond networks have the potential to provide a wide range of new services. Among these, the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has emerged as a key area of application to enable intelligent transportation and enhanced connectivity between vehicles and infrastructure. However, inefficient handover management may lead to unacceptable communication interruptions, which can degrade the overall Quality of Service (QoS) and lead to safety risks. To maintain service reliability and user experience under high-speed mobility, seamless connectivity with strict latency control is required to minimize spatio-temporal fluctuations during handover. This can be achieved with a QoS prediction and "what-if" analysis in handover management. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a multi-layer explainable AI (XAI) framework for 5G and beyond networks to predict spatio-temporal peaks and handover triggers. We present a multi-layered deep learning model by combining temporal features of Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) network and static attributes in a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP). The proposed multi-layered XAI consists of (i) SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for diagnosing peaks, (ii) Diverse Counterfactual Explanations (DiCE) for prescriptive what-if analysis and (iii) Policy Extraction for handover triggering. In the simulation results, the number of critical latency peaks and total mobility interruption time are reduced by 45.08% and 20.95%, respectively. This study highlights the critical role of XAI in transitioning from reactive analysis to measurable, proactive and automated decision support systems.

title: Joint Data and Network Heterogeneity in Edge ML: Experiments on Asynchronous Parameter Server.
Confidential Edge Architecture for Network-Augmented Vehicles.
abstract: The transition towards 6G enables new architectural paradigms integrating communication and computation to support data-intensive vertical applications. In the mobility domain, vehicles are increasingly acting as mobile sensors, allowing to maintain digital twins of urban infrastructure and another avenue for monetizing vehicle data. However, realizing this in practice is challenging due to limited on-board computing resources, high data transmission costs, and regulatory compliance constraints. We present a network-augmented edge architecture for privacy-preserving processing of vehicle sensor data, aligned with emerging 6G architectural principles. Our approach combines lightweight on-board pre-processing with confidential edge computing in the mobile network. We leverage confidential computing to ensure security and privacy of workloads while augmenting the on-board vehicle compute capacity. We practically demonstrate a use case where vehicles collect sensor data in a live urban setting and transmit selected data points to confidential edge nodes updating the digital representation of road signage. To ensure regulatory compliance, the approach was assessed as part of a personal data protection regulatory sandbox. In this paper, we discuss design choices, practical deployment aspects, and privacy considerations to support such capabilities in upcoming mobile networks

title: Lightwave Power Transfer-Enabled Underwater Optical ISAC Systems under Ship Attitude Variation.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a lightwave power transfer-enabled underwater optical integrated sensing and communication (O-ISAC) system, where an access point (AP) mounted on a seasurface ship transmits lightwave signals to two nodes, namely ($i$) a seabed sensor that harvests energy and transmits uplink information to the AP, and ($ii$) a sensing target whose position is estimated by the AP using an array of pinhole cameras. To capture practical deployment conditions, the ship attitude variation is modeled through its roll, pitch, and yaw angles, each following a Gaussian distribution under low-to-moderate sea states. Closed-form approximations are derived for the mean squared error (MSE) of target localization and the achievable uplink data rate. Analytical and simulation results demonstrate excellent agreement, validating the proposed models and derived expressions, while revealing the fundamental communication-sensing tradeoff in the O-ISAC system. The results further provide valuable design insights, including the optimal camera placement on the ship to minimize localization error, achieving a minimum MSE of $10^{-2}$ $\text{m}^2$ with multiple cameras under roll, pitch, and yaw angle variation of $10^{\circ}$, and the optimal harvest-use ratio of $0.55$ for the considered setup.

title: AFDM-guided Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding for Satellite Communication.
abstract: As a key technology for next generation networks, satellite communication faces challenges due to constrained spectrum and interference. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding framework guided by Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing (AFDM-JSCC). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to seamlessly integrate the AFDM waveform into an end-to-end JSCC architecture. This integration leverages JSCC to improve transmission efficiency while specifically mitigating the performance degradation observed in conventional OFDM-based semantic systems over time-frequency robustness against such channel effects, we further design a channel state information encoder and a novel deep learning-based channel compensation module. We conduct extensive simulations in satellite channels. Results demonstrate that the proposed AFDM-JSCC maintains superior performance compared with benchmarks and demonstrating significant resilience under high Doppler conditions.

title: UPQ-RV: A Unified Peripheral Event Queue Architecture for Low-Power and Parallel Communication on RISC-V.
abstract: Ultra-low-power (ULP) RISC-V systems face growing challenges in managing communication from multiple peripherals, as traditional CPU-centric interrupt handling leads to frequent wake-ups, increased latency, and reduced energy efficiency. Existing approaches such as dedicated event interconnects or general-purpose I/O processors offer partial solutions but often involve trade-offs in latency, scalability, or integration complexity. To address these limitations, we introduce UPQ-RV, a Unified Peripheral Event Queue architecture designed for low-power and parallel communication in RISC-V platforms. UPQRV consolidates peripheral-generated events via an event descriptor unit, a dynamic priority scheduler, and low-power controller that enables autonomous event exchange through a unified programmable queue. This design minimizes CPU intervention and leverages Wait-For-Interrupt (WFI) states for energy-aware execution. Synthesized on an FPGA, UPQ-RV demonstrates up to 2.5× reduction in dynamic power compared to conventional CPU-mediated handling, while supporting scalable and concurrent peripheral communication. The architecture is lightweight, modular, and readily integrable into next-generation ULP RISC-V IoT processors.

title: Energy-Efficient Design for Robust UAV Wireless Networks Using Dual-Timescale Statistical Uncertainty Learning.
Energy-Efficient UAV Trajectory and Beamforming Optimizations for mURLLC-Driven AirComp Over ISAC-Enabled Networks.
abstract: To meet the stringent latency and reliability demands of future 6G networks, this paper presents a communication-efficient and energy-aware optimization framework for UAV-assisted over-the-air federated learning (Air-FL) systems under massive ultra-reliable and low-latency communication (mURLLC) constraints. The proposed system enables distributed AI/ML at the edge by integrating UAV-enabled cellfree MIMO access with ISAC-based channel estimation and model aggregation via over-the-air computation (AirComp). We formulate a joint resource management problem involving UAV trajectory control, mobile users (MUs) transmit power allocation, and UAV access points (APs) receive beamforming design, aiming to minimize a weighted sum of AirComp aggregation error and UAV energy consumption, while satisfying mURLLC delay and reliability constraints. To tackle the resulting non-convexity, an alternating optimization strategy is adopted: closed-form solutions are derived for power control and beamforming, while UAV trajectories are predicted using a lightweight Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) model. Simulation results show that the proposed framework significantly improves accuracy of FL task and energy efficiency over benchmark methods, demonstrating its potential for scalable and communication-efficient edge intelligence in time-critical wireless learning scenarios.

title: Resource and Power Optimizations for Multi-Task Air-FL With Digital Twin Assisted ISAC Over OFDM-Based Mobile Networks.
abstract: In 6G edge intelligent networks, Over-the-Air Federated Learning (Air-FL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for distributed model training while protecting user data privacy. However, communication overhead and energy consumption pose serious challenges, especially in multi-task scenarios. This paper proposes a digital twin (DT)-assisted, multi-task Air-FL framework utilizing massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) and Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC). Using an OFDM-based schemes, each sub-carrier corresponds to a learning task, enabling parallel aggregation of multiple devices. We incorporate downlink radar sensing at the base station to obtain accurate channel estimates and user states, and continuously synchronize them with a virtual replica of the physical wireless environment for predictive optimization. We formulate a weighted objective that jointly minimizes the mean-square error and energy consumption under non-convex constraints, and develop an alternating optimization method that iteratively updates transmit precoders and receive combiners. We prove our schemes’ convergence to a local optimum with feasible complexity in massive MIMO settings. Experiments on representative image-classification workloads show higher efficiency and robustness than conventional methods, highlighting the potential of DT-assisted ISAC multi-task FL.

title: An Efficient IID-Based Routing Table Aggregation Algorithm for Large-Scale Load-Sharing Networks.
abstract: The increasing scale of network dimensions necessitates effective solutions for routing table management to meet escalating demands. In this paper, we propose a solution tailored for load-sharing networks that maintain comprehensive next-hop records, importantly extendable to conventional networks. We introduce a novel routing table aggregation algorithm designed to minimize modifications by predicting fluctuations. This algorithm leverages Indirect Identifiers (IIDs) to achieve aggregation. Additionally, we develop an innovative pruning technique that reduces runtime and enhances the algorithm’s efficiency in updating the Shortest Path Tree (SPT) while preserving essential path information. Computational complexity analysis validates the efficacy of our approach. Extensive simulations demonstrate its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art techniques, consistently reducing computation time and routing table modifications across diverse network scales and configurations.

title: Toward Energy-Efficient mmWave Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems: A Hierarchical Hybrid Precoding Framework.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate energy-efficient hybrid precoding for cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems at millimeter-wave (mmWave) frequencies. We propose a hierarchical hybrid precoding (HHP) framework to tackle the energy efficiency (EE) optimization problem with two sequential subproblems: fully digital EE optimization and hybrid precoding decomposition. Firstly, by exploiting rate-MMSE equivalence, the central processing unit (CPU) optimizes the fully digital precoder with a Dinkelbach-based weighted minimum mean square error (D-WMMSE) algorithm. Secondly, the access points (APs) perform row-wise parallelized hybrid precoding decomposition via a parallel alternating direction method of multipliers-based alternating minimization (P-ADMM-AltMin) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed HHP framework achieves substantial EE improvements (up to 193.9% higher at most) with computational complexity reduced by a factor proportion to the number of antennas per AP compared with the baselines.

title: Rethinking On-Device LLM Reasoning: Why Analogical Mapping Outperforms Abstract Thinking for IoT DDoS Detection.
abstract: The rapid expansion of IoT deployments has intensified cybersecurity threats, notably Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, characterized by increasingly sophisticated patterns. Leveraging Generative AI through On-Device Large Language Models (ODLLMs) provides a viable solution for real-time threat detection at the network edge, though limited computational resources present challenges for smaller ODLLMs. This paper introduces a novel detection framework that integrates Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), tailored specifically for IoT edge environments. We systematically evaluate compact ODLLMs, including LLaMA 3.2 (1B, 3B) and Gemma 3 (1B, 4B), using structured prompting and exemplar-driven reasoning strategies. Experimental results demonstrate substantial performance improvements with few-shot prompting, achieving macro-average F1 scores as high as 0.85. Our findings highlight the significant advantages of incorporating exemplar-based reasoning, underscoring that CoT and RAG approaches markedly enhance small ODLLMs’ capabilities in accurately classifying complex network attacks under stringent resource constraints.

title: SCALER: Self-Consistent Assessment for SLA Explanation and Resolution in 6G Networks.
abstract: In emerging 5G and beyond (B5G) network architectures, ensuring service-level objectives (SLOs) requires more than reactive monitoring. It demands systems capable of interpreting behavioral deviations and reasoning about compliance with operational intent. This paper introduces a framework that combines unsupervised behavior modeling with large language model (LLM)–driven reasoning to explain potential service level agreement (SLA) non-compliance. By leveraging a multi-sample zero-shot prompting strategy to generate contextual explanations for observed service degradations, the system aligns intent expression with network observations. To assess the reliability of these explanations, it introduces a self-consistency mechanism based on semantic similarity among multiple LLM responses. This mechanism acts as both a proxy for explanation confidence and a signal for semantic drift. The architecture is deployed in a cloud native pipeline, in line with zero-touch service management and scalable orchestration. Evaluations on real-world traffic datasets demonstrate the system’s ability to support trustworthy and interpretable SLA assurance in machine learning (ML)-based telecommunication environments.

title: CP-Free ODDM: Modeling and Design.
abstract: This paper studies the modeling and design of a new orthogonal delay-Doppler division multiplexing (ODDM) system that can operate without using a cyclic prefix (CP) in the transmitted signals. The CP-free ODDM architecture is enabled by exploiting the unique structures of the ODDM prototype pulses, which are constructed through repetitions of finite-duration elementary pulses. The CP-free ODDM system eliminates the need of CP by designing a new receiving filter that temporally extends the transmission prototype pulse. The elementary pulse repetition at the transmitter along with the temporal filter extension at the receiver introduces a wrap-around effect in the equivalent channel spreading function in the DD domain. The wrap-around effect leads to a block-circulant-like structure of the DD-domain channel matrix that is the same as conventional ODDM systems with CP. Thus CP-free ODDM can employ the same receiver as conventional ODDM systems, yet it yields a higher energy efficiency as no energy needs to be allocated for CP symbols. The wrap-around effects are theoretically demonstrated by deriving the exact analytical expressions of the cross-ambiguity functions of practical transmission and receiving prototype pulses. Simulation results demonstrate that the CP-free ODDM system outperforms other delay-Doppler communication systems.

title: Physics-Aware RIS Codebook Compilation for Near-Field Beam Focusing under Mutual Coupling and Specular Reflections.
abstract: Next-generation wireless networks are envisioned to achieve reliable, low-latency connectivity within environments characterized by strong multipath and severe channel variability. Programmable wireless environments (PWEs) address this challenge by enabling deterministic control of electromagnetic (EM) propagation through software-defined reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs). However, effectively configuring RISs in real time remains a major bottleneck, particularly under near-field conditions where mutual coupling and specular reflections alter the intended response. To overcome this limitation, this paper introduces MATCH, a physics-based codebook compilation algorithm that explicitly accounts for the EM coupling among RIS unit cells and the reflective interactions with surrounding structures, ensuring that the resulting codebooks remain consistent with the physical characteristics of the environment. Finally, MATCH is evaluated under a realistic EM framework incorporating mutual coupling and secondary reflections, demonstrating its ability to concentrate scattered energy within the focal region, confirming that physics-consistent, codebook-based optimization constitutes an effective approach for practical and efficient RIS configuration.

title: RIS-Assisted D-MIMO for Energy-Efficient 6G Indoor Networks.
abstract: We propose an alternating optimization framework for maximizing energy efficiency (EE) in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) assisted distributed MIMO (D-MIMO) systems under both coherent and non-coherent reception modes. The framework jointly optimizes access point (AP) power allocation and RIS phase configurations to improve EE under per-AP power and signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints. Using majorization-minimization for power allocation together with per-element RIS adaptation, the framework achieves tractable optimization of this non-convex problem. Simulation results for indoor deployments with realistic power-consumption models show that the proposed scheme outperforms equal-power and random-scatterer baselines, with clear EE gains. We evaluate the performance of both reception modes and quantify the impact of RIS phase-shift optimization, RIS controller architectures (centralized vs. per-RIS control), and RIS size, providing design insights for practical RIS-assisted D-MIMO deployments in future 6G networks.

title: Switch-DFT: Adaptive Waveform and MIMO Switching for Energy-Efficient Base Stations.
abstract: Energy efficiency has emerged as a critical challenge in modern base stations (BSs), as the power amplifier (PA) consumes a substantial portion of the total power due to its limited efficiency. We investigate waveform and mode adaptation to enhance the energy efficiency of BSs. We propose Switch-DFT, an adaptive switching framework that selects between cyclic prefix orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CP-OFDM) and discrete Fourier transform-spread-OFDM (DFT-s-OFDM) waveforms, as well as between single-input multiple-output (SIMO) and multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) modes. Switch-DFT improves efficiency by reducing PA backoff with DFT-s-OFDM and achieves the target rate at lower power by leveraging higher MIMO throughput. This results in superior energy efficiency over a wide range of the spectral efficiencies compared with static configurations.

title: Importance-Driven Resource Management for MIMO-OFDM Semantic Communications.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel importance-aware quantization, subcarrier mapping, and power allocation (IA-QSMPA) framework for semantic communication in multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems, powered by a pretrained Vision Transformer (ViT). The proposed framework leverages attention-based importance extracted from a pretrained ViT to jointly optimize quantization levels, subcarrier mapping, and power allocation. To this end, an optimization problem is formulated which maps semantically important features to high-quality subchannels, while allocating resources according to their contribution to task performance and transmission latency. To solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, a block coordinate descent algorithm is developed. Simulation results on multi-view image classification demonstrate that IA-QSMPA consistently outperforms conventional baselines in ideal transmission settings, offering superior task performance and reduced communication latency.

title: A Unified AI-Native 6G Architecture for 3GPP AI Use Cases: Systematic Categorization and Identification of Gaps in Specifications.
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks require a fundamental transformation of the traditional connectivity-oriented design into an intelligence-centric blueprint, in anticipation of a plethora of upcoming artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities and applications to be offered, such as those described in the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) Technical Report (TR) 22.870. This paper performs a systematic categorization of the 61 AI use cases in 3GPP TR 22.870 (v1.0.1) into 10 functional domains based on their primary AI function, deployment characteristics, and network requirements. The analysis gives rise to a unified AI-native architecture for 6G networks, for which the following seven architectural components are considered to be essential for the studied use cases: Service Hosting Environment (SHE) for distributed AI execution, Network Data Analytics Function (NWDAF) for predictive analytics, Network Knowledge Exposure Function (NKEF) for third-party AI integration, Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) function for network-native processing of sensing information, AI agent framework (AAF) for autonomous service orchestration, federated learning infrastructure for privacy-preserving collaboration, and semantic communication protocol implementation for bandwidth efficiency. Finally, with respect to the future standardization activities deemed imperative for fully realizing this architecture, we identify four critical gaps in the current specifications: (1) lack of a standardized agent authentication framework affecting 15 use cases, (2) undefined privacy guarantees for federated learning affecting 10 use cases, (3) missing semantic communication protocols limiting cooperative perception, (4) incomplete explainability requirements vital for safety-critical systems.

title: Dynamic Edge Server Placement in Vehicular Edge Computing Using Metaheuristic Approach.
abstract: Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) supports intelligent transportation services by enabling computation to be performed closer to vehicles, thereby reducing service delay and improving energy efficiency at the network edge. In VEC, the emerging challenges are the optimal deployment of edge servers in highly fluctuating vehicular environments. Unlike the conventional approaches that rely on static server placements. This paper formulates the dynamic edge server placement problem using the real-world vehicular mobility traces and proposed an improved Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)-based metaheuristic mechanism that jointly reduces the communication latency and energy consumption. An adaptive mechanism that restricts the unnecessary server relocations by considering the displacement threshold, inter-server proximity, and heterogeneous server capacity constraints, thereby improving the system stability even in the high dynamic vehicular networks. The comprehensive results show that the improved PSO with an adaptive mechanism approach achieves better performance in terms of communication latency and energy consumption compared to state-of-the-art approaches. The proposed approach is a feasible and scalable solution for edge server placements in advanced networks.

title: Volumetric Near-Field Beamfocusing via Zernike Phase Tapering.
abstract: This paper develops the foundational framework for three-dimensional (3D) near-field beamfocusing, termed as volumetric near-field beamfocusing, using uniform rectangular arrays (URAs). We first analyze matched filter (MF) beam-forming, and derive closed-form expressions for the lateral and axial resolutions around a target focal point. The analysis reveals that MF achieves strong lateral intensity but inherently produces an axially elongated focal region, which limits its compact volumetric energy concentration. This demonstrates that existing beamfocusing techniques in literature are primarily two-dimensional (2D) beamfocusing or spot beams, not truly 3D focused beams. To overcome this, we introduce a novel Zernike-based phase tapering approach, inspired by optical aberration correction. By incorporating fourth-order Zernike modes, the extended axial structure is reshaped into a sharper volumetric focus. Both analytical derivations and numerical simulations with URAs of practical dimensions confirm that Zernike-based tapering enhances volumetric focusing and reduces focal depth (approximately up to 73 times) and incurs only a moderate reduction in peak intensity (approximately 1.5 dB) compared to conventional MF. These findings establish phase-domain tapering via Zernike polynomials as a foundational tool for compact volumetric beamfocusing. It also opens up a plethora of promising applications for near-field wireless communications, sensing, and localization systems that require precise energy confinement in three dimensions.

title: CTMap: LLM-Enabled Connectivity-Aware Path Planning in Millimeter-Wave Digital Twin Networks.
abstract: In this paper, we present CTMap, a large language model (LLM)-empowered digital twin framework for connectivity-aware route navigation in millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless networks. Conventional navigation tools optimize only distance, time, or cost, overlooking network connectivity degradation caused by signal blockage in dense urban environments. The proposed framework constructs a digital twin of the physical mmWave network using OpenStreetMap, Blender, and NVIDIA Sionna’s ray-tracing engine to simulate realistic received signal strength (RSS) maps. A modified Dijkstra’s algorithm then generates optimal routes that maximize cumulative RSS, forming the training data for instruction-tuned GPT-4-based reasoning. This integration enables semantic route queries such as "find the strongest-signal path" and returns connectivity-optimized paths interpretable by users and adaptable to real-time environmental updates. Experimental results demonstrate that CTMap achieves up to tenfold improvement in cumulative signal strength compared to shortest-distance baselines, while maintaining high path validity. The synergy of digital twin simulation and LLM reasoning establishes a scalable foundation for intelligent, interpretable, and connectivity-driven navigation, advancing the design of AI-empowered 6G mobility systems.

title: FedChain: Blockchain-assisted Federated Learning Framework for Secure Resource Allocation in Device-to-Device Communication.
Joint Beamforming and Telescopic STAR-RIS Design for NOMA-ISAC: A WMMSE Approach.
abstract: We study an integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) system assisted by a novel telescopic simultaneous transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (TSTAR-RIS). This surface features per-element height control, providing an additional physical degree of freedom to jointly tune the effective aperture and phase response across its transmit and reflect halves. We consider a RIS-only (no direct BS-UE link) scenario using downlink power-domain NOMA and passive echo-based sensing. We formulate a constrained utility maximization to jointly optimize the communication sum-rate and a sensing-SINR-based utility, subject to hardware constraints including finite-bit quantization, passive energy splitting, and mechanical height limits. To tackle the nonconvex couplings, we propose a three-block alternating optimization (AO) algorithm: (i) the downlink data precoder is updated via the weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) method to maximize sum-rate; (ii) the dedicated sensing beamformer is updated via projected gradient (PG) to maximize the sensing utility; and (iii) the TSTAR-RIS coefficients and element heights are jointly optimized via PG with Armijo backtracking to maximize the total ISAC utility. Simulations are conducted for a fair comparison where both TSTAR and a conventional non-telescopic (NTSTAR) baseline use the same random, uneven user distributions and channel realizations. Results demonstrate that the proposed TSTAR-RIS consistently outperforms the NTSTAR baseline.

title: Joint Rendering Quality and Encoding Type Selection for Edge-Assisted Extended Reality.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel scheme to jointly select rendering quality and encoding type for an edge-assisted extended reality (XR) system to enhance user quality of experience (QoE) in terms of visual quality and quality variation. Specifically, XR service delivery requires a series of interdependent tasks, including frame rendering, encoding, and transmission, to be completed within a time latency. To cope with network dynamics, the rendering quality of frames can be dynamically adjusted, which in turn triggers intra-frame encoding and leads to a sudden transmission burst. To capture such task interdependency, we formulate a long-term QoE maximization problem under edge computing and communication resource constraints, which jointly selects the rendering quality and either intra- or inter-frame encoding for each frame. To solve this problem, we theoretically analyze the impact of per-frame decisions on long-term QoE and present an online algorithm for decision-making. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed scheme outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of long-term QoE.

title: Efficient Early Network Intrusion Detection based on Sub-Flow Segmentation.
abstract: With the increasing complexity of network traffic and the diversification of cyber attacks, traditional intrusion detection systems based on full-session analysis face challenges in real-time performance and computational efficiency. To enhance early detection capability, recent research has explored using only partial flows or the first few packets for rapid classification. The few proposed approaches rely mainly on time-driven flow segmentation, making it inefficient to capture the full flow context. This paper introduces a novel framework (named Hybrid Prefix N) that combines both time-based features as well as other crucial flow features (e.g., SYN/FIN/RST) to better capture flow contextual, bidirectional and boundary features. In particular, as we shall see, the flow segmentation strategy significantly affects feature distributions and model overall performance. The Experimental results show that although the time-driven approach achieves slightly higher numerical metrics, it suffers from class imbalance and high false positive rates. On the other hand, the proposed Hybrid segmentation model provided high accuracy while providing a more reliable and semantically consistent foundation for real-time intrusion detection.

title: Adaptive Feature Selection for Efficient Task-Oriented Semantic Communications.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate point-to-point (P2P) task-oriented semantic communication (SemCom) for image classification using joint source-channel coding (JSCC) with deep neural networks (DNNs). Unlike existing methods, our joint source-channel encoder at the transmitter employs a novel feature map selector enabled by attention mechanism-based learnable pruning functions, allowing for dynamic pruning of feature maps according to both their semantic importance and the channel signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The proposed approach not only efficiently reduces the overall transmitted data volume without degrading classification accuracy but also supports flexibly adjustable feature pruning under varying channel conditions. Simulation results of an ablation study on two public datasets verify the advantages of the learnable pruning function over its non-learnable counterpart in selecting semantically important features. In addition, our proposed approach consistently outperforms several baseline schemes in terms of classification accuracy, adaptability to channel variations, generalizability of the model, and data transmission efficiency.

title: Knowledge Base-Aware Resource Allocation for Semantic Communication-Enabled Multi-Cell Networks.
SLayer: Secure and Scalable Smart Contract Sharding via Layered Encoding.
abstract: Blockchain scalability remains constrained by the limited throughput. Sharding offers a practical path forward, yet existing smart contract sharding approaches exhibit two fundamental weaknesses. First, inter-shard contract dependencies can form call chains, allowing a single shard failure to cascade into system-wide disruption. Second, cross-shard smart contract execution involves multiple rounds of inter-shard communication and requires locking entire contract states, resulting in significant overhead and limited concurrency. To overcome these challenges, we propose SLayer, a sharding system that achieves both shard-fault resilience and high-performance contract execution. SLayer introduces Repairable Fountain Codes (RFCs) to organize the blockchain into a raw layer and an encoded layer, enabling detection and recovery of faulty shards with low storage and computational overhead. To reduce inter-shard synchronization cost, SLayer further employs Consensus Hub, a set of nodes from different shards that stores contract states likely to be invoked across shards, reducing inter-shard communication and state synchronization overhead. It adopts fine-grained state locking at the variable level, further improving parallel execution efficiency.Experiments demonstrate that under identical security guarantees, SLayer delivers up to 1.7× higher throughput than Jenga, the state-of-the-art smart contract sharding system, validating its scalability and fault-tolerance advantages.

title: LB-Decider: Runtime-Adaptive Load Balancing for All-to-All Communication in MoE Training.
abstract: As large language models drive massive AI training clusters, network interconnects have emerged as critical performance bottlenecks. Existing load balancing (LB) schemes are typically static and fail to adapt to heterogeneous topologies and phase-varying traffic in distributed Mixture of Experts (MoE) training. Through theoretical modeling and large-scale experiments, we show that LB performance exhibits strong scenario dependence, and no single strategy remains optimal across all cases. We formalize three dominant bias mechanisms underlying performance deviation: collision, splitting, and coordination, and empirically validate their effects. To address this limitation, we propose LB-Decider, a lightweight online framework that extracts observable scenario features and dynamically selects the optimal LB strategy at iteration granularity. LB-Decider achieves 96.1% of the best-static improvement on average, approaching the perscenario best-static envelope across sixteen Mixture of Experts training scenarios. These results show that adaptive, data-driven selection links topology cost reductions with algorithmic performance, improving end-to-end MoE training efficiency.

title: Multicast Routing Algorithm Based on Local State and Source Routing Probing for LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: Multicast routing algorithms for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks commonly suffer from inadequate adaptability to dynamic networks and a tendency to cause network congestion. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Multicost Routing Algorithm Based on Local State and Source Route Probing (MRA-LS). Specifically, this algorithm constructs a multicast tree through the source routing probing mechanism and can update the tree in real time based on network topology changes, thereby effectively adapting to the highly dynamic characteristics of satellite networks. For path probing, a shortest path algorithm based on a Double Depth Q-Network (DDQN) is employed, which can realize efficient path probe relying solely on local network states, significantly enhancing routing flexibility and adaptability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms baseline algorithms in key performance metrics such as average end-to-end delay and packet loss rate. Particularly in scenarios with non-uniformly distributed traffic, the algorithm exhibits significant advantages.

title: Robust Multimodal Semantic Communications with Semantic Fusion and Compensation.
abstract: Semantic communication has demonstrated significant potential to improve communication network performance. However, ensuring robustness in multimodal semantic communication remains challenging due to both physical and semantic impairments, with the latter largely underexplored. In this paper, we investigate multimodal semantic impairments and propose a novel framework for robust multimodal semantic communications. We introduce a performance metric to quantify semantic impairments and construct a corresponding dataset for validation. Moreover, we design DeepSC-RM, a deep learning enabled semantic communication system, which integrates an adaptive multimodal semantic fusion module to dynamically combine information across modalities, a multimodal joint semantic–channel codec for symbol-level transmission, and a cross-modal semantic compensation module at the receiver to enhance accurate semantic interpretation. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed DeepSC-RM, confirming its effectiveness in mitigating semantic impairments and achieving robust multimodal transmission.

title: Pinching Antenna Multiple Access With Optimal Antenna Placement.
abstract: Pinching antenna systems, which dynamically reconfigure antenna positions along dielectric waveguides, have emerged as a promising technology for future wireless networks. Currently, most existing works on pinching antennas are confined to single-waveguide scenarios and combined with orthogonal multiple access (OMA) schemes, which restrict the full potential of pinching antenna systems. In this paper, we propose a novel pinching antenna multiple access (PAMA) scheme that can support multiuser transmission in the same time-frequency resources, without complex signal processing. In particular, by adjusting the pinching antenna placement, PAMA can reduce or even eliminate the inter-user interference and allow each waveguide to serve its corresponding user independently, thereby fully exploiting the spatial gain provided by the multi-waveguide architecture. Specifically, we prove that inter-user interference can be perfectly cancelled through carefully designed antenna placement. Based on this key insight, we then propose an optimal antenna placement method, with low computational complexity, to achieve higher user channel gains with suppressed interference. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PAMA scheme achieves superior spectral efficiency and fairness compared with the existing schemes.

title: Error-Aware Super-Resolution Channel Estimation for RIS-Aided Multi-User mmWave Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we propose an effective two-stage error-aware super-resolution channel estimation method for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided multi-user (MU) millimeter wave (mmWave) systems based on the ambiguity and correlation of the cascaded channel matrices. From the estimation framework perspective, in Stage I, the method estimates the ambiguous RIS-base station channel by exploiting the MU diversity gain, while in Stage II, it not only estimates the ambiguous user-RIS channels with reduced pilots, but more importantly, explicitly and adaptively estimates and compensates for the estimation errors propagated from Stage I, thereby improving the estimation accuracy of channel parameters in Stage I and consequently enhancing the overall estimation performance. Accordingly, to achieve error-aware super-resolution estimation within the framework, the proposed method introduces the smooth approximation of the lpnorm and dynamic grids to formulate the channel parameter estimation in Stage II as tractable joint sparse recovery and perturbed dictionary adaptation problems, which are iteratively solved using a developed majorization-minimization-based alternating minimization algorithm. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Group Relative Policy Optimization for Robust Blind Interference Alignment with Fluid Antennas.
abstract: Fluid antenna system (FAS) leverages dynamic re-configurability to unlock spatial degrees of freedom and reshape wireless channels. Blind interference alignment (BIA) aligns interference through antenna switching. This paper proposes, for the first time, a robust fluid antenna-driven BIA framework for a K-user MISO downlink under imperfect channel state information (CSI). We formulate a robust sum-rate maximization problem through optimizing fluid antenna positions (switching positions). To solve this challenging non-convex problem, we employ group relative policy optimization (GRPO), a novel deep reinforcement learning algorithm that eliminates the critic network. This robust design reduces model size and floating point operations (FLOPs) by nearly half compared to proximal policy optimization (PPO) while significantly enhancing performance through group-based exploration that escapes bad local optima. Simulation results demonstrate that GRPO outperforms PPO by 4.17%, and a 100K-step pre-trained PPO by 30.29%. Due to error distribution learning, GRPO exceeds heuristic MaximumGain and RandomGain by 200.78% and 465.38%, respectively.

title: Ripple-Inspired In-Context Learning for Radio Map Estimation.
abstract: Accurate and cost-effective radio map estimation (RME) is critical for a wide range of wireless applications such as coverage planning, localization, and wireless network deployment. However, most existing methods still follow a supervised learning mindset that relies on costly labeled datasets and delicate model training. Inspired by the remarkable generalization ability of large language models, we make the first attempt to formulate RME as an in-context learning (ICL) problem, where a pretrained large autoregressive vision model (LAVM) is prompted by a few input–output demonstrations to predict the radio map for a new scene (e.g., a new transmitter (Tx) position or building layout) without requiring model updates. We propose Ripple, a physically inspired ICL framework that integrates visual tokenization with a novel ripple autoregressive modeling strategy to explicitly capture the causal structure of wireless signal propagation from the Tx outward. Besides, we develop a two-stage generation strategy for coarse-to-fine prediction and provide theoretical analysis from an implicit optimizer view. Extensive experiments under two different ICL scenarios demonstrate that RIPPLE consistently outperforms three baselines, highlighting its promising capability for RME.

title: Soft Actor Critic-Based Adaptive Routing for QoS-Driven Post-Disaster Networks.
abstract: Quality of Service (QoS) assurance is critical for maintaining reliable communication in post-disaster environments where fixed infrastructure is often damaged or unavailable. In such scenarios, routing must rely on mobile and ad hoc nodes that face frequent topology changes and unstable links. Conventional routing protocols such as AODV, OLSR, and GPSR depend on static metrics and are unable to adapt to these dynamic conditions. This paper presents a reinforcement learning-based routing framework built on the Soft Actor Critic (SAC) algorithm to enable adaptive QoS-aware communication. The model observes network states, including link delay, packet reliability, and node energy, and learns routing policies that maintain stable multi-hop connectivity under varying mobility. The framework is evaluated in a simulated post-disaster network that includes mobile edge devices, UAV relays, and temporary gateways. Results show that the SAC-based model reduces average round-trip time by about 18% compared with PPO and achieves nearly 95% of the throughput upper bound under static conditions. When 60% of nodes are mobile, it retains over 90% of baseline throughput and maintains a stable success rate. These findings suggest that SAC offers a robust and adaptive approach for QoS-driven routing in dynamic networks.

title: FLASH: A Hierarchical Federated Learning Framework for Sustainable Smart Home Networks.
