title: Optimally Deployed Multistatic OTFS-ISAC Design With Kalman-Based Tracking of Targets.
abstract: This paper studies orthogonal time-frequency space (OTFS) modulation aided multistatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in vehicular networks, whereby its delay-Doppler robustness is exploited for enhanced communication and high-resolution sensing. We present a triangulation-based deployment framework combined with Kalman filtering (KF) that enables accurate target localization and velocity estimation. In addition, we assess the ISAC performance in the multistatic topology to determine its effectiveness in the dynamic environment. Further, a suboptimal placement strategy for the multistatic receivers is devised to reduce the targets’ localization error. Numerical results demonstrate significant reductions in the sensing error and bit error rate (BER) performances.

title: Equitable Multi-Task Learning for AI-RANs.
abstract: AI–enabled Radio Access Networks (AI-RANs) are expected to serve heterogeneous users with time-varying learning tasks over shared edge resources. Ensuring equitable inference performance across these users requires adaptive and fair learning mechanisms. This paper introduces an Online-Within-Online Fair Multi-Task Learning (OWO-FMTL) framework that ensures long-term equity across users. The method combines two learning loops: an outer loop updating the shared model across rounds and an inner loop re-balancing user priorities within each round with a lightweight primal–dual update. Equity is quantified via generalized α-fairness, allowing trading-off efficiency and fairness. The framework guarantees diminishing performance disparity over time and operates with low computational overhead suitable for edge deployment. Experiments on convex and deep-learning tasks confirm that OWO-FMTL outperforms existing multi-task learning baselines under dynamic scenarios.

title: Reliable LLM-enabled Intent-driven Management: A Validation pipeline for Network Automation.
abstract: To democratize zero-touch network automation, we need to connect natural language user intents with formal, standards-compliant specifications. Large Language Models (LLMs) are promising but unreliable. We propose a hybrid AI-symbolic framework that uses LLMs for translation but enforces correctness with deterministic "guardrails". Our Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline generates TM Forum-compliant intents and then validates them to ensure syntactic, semantic, and policy compliance. We benchmark our solution using three open-source LLMs, demonstrating the framework’s high reliability. It achieved a 93.8% pipeline success rate with Mistral-7B, where intents were correctly processed to a definitive conclusion. The results suggest that a hybrid architecture with symbolic guardrails offers the safety and reliability necessary for deploying generative AI in network orchestration, overcoming the limitations of using isolated LLMs.

title: PQ-TabNet: A Post-Quantum Secure Framework for Intrusion Detection in UAV Networks.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are used in various civilian applications to collect data. Security is a major issue in UAV networks. To securely transmit the data from the UAVs to the base station, the data must be sent in encrypted form. Cryptography techniques are used for encryption and decryption. Classical cryptography schemes do not provide protection against quantum attacks. To secure the data from quantum threats we use post quantum cryptography(PQC) techniques. In this paper, a post-quantum secure intrusion detection model named the PQ-TabNet model is proposed to address these challenges. The proposed model integrates N-th Degree Truncated Polynomial Ring unit (NTRU) lattice-based encryption with a transformer-based deep learning model to ensure confidentiality and resilience against both classical and quantum attacks. The proposed model was trained on the CICIDS2018 data set, where PQ-TabNet achieved better performance than the Kyber-based configuration in terms of energy efficiency and latency. Experimental analysis demonstrated that NTRU provided faster encryption and reduced energy consumption while maintaining strong quantum resistance.

title: On the Minimum Distances of Finite-Length Lifted Product Quantum LDPC Codes.
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is critical for the practical realization of fault-tolerant quantum computing and quantum communication systems. Recently proposed families of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are prime candidates for advanced QEC hardware architectures. This paper focuses on finite-length QLDPC code design criteria, specifically aimed at constructing degenerate quasi-cyclic symmetric lifted-product (LP-QLDPC) codes with high minimum distances. We describe necessary conditions to ensure that the designed LP-QLDPC codes have a minimum distance strictly greater than the minimum weight stabilizer generators, thus ensuring superior error correction performance. The focus of the paper is on LP-QLDPC codes built from quasi-cyclic base codes belonging to the class of type-1 protographs, and the necessary constraints are efficiently expressed in terms of row and column indices of the base parity check matrix. This gives us combinatorial constraints - termed as Row-Column Partition Constraints (RCPC) - on classical quasi-cyclic base matrices to construct degenerate LP-QLDPC codes. For type-1 protographs, RCPC constraints provide an efficient certification approach to designing good codes, and we also give exhaustive search evidence on small base matrices. Simulations with BP+OSD decoding demonstrate significant logical error-rate gains when RCPC is avoided. We discuss extensions to circuit-level noise and outline sufficient conditions and research directions for exact distance preservation.

title: CE-FedAvg: A Communication-Efficient Federated Learning Framework for LoRaWAN-Based Edge AI.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralizing data, yet deployment over low-power wide-area networks (LPWANs), such as LoRaWAN, remains challenging due to severe bandwidth, payload, and duty-cycle constraints. This work examines the feasibility of FL on LoRaWAN by designing and implementing a communication-efficient framework tailored to constrained Internet of Things (IoT) environments. CE-FedAvg is introduced as a communication-efficient variant of FedAvg that restructures client-server exchanges to comply with standard LoRaWAN operation. In addition to sparsification, quantization, and lightweight compression, CE-FedAvg incorporates seed-based initialization for deterministic synchronization and explores model improvements optimized for ultra-low-throughput communication environments. The framework is fully compatible with the LoRaWAN specification and is implemented across heterogeneous edge devices and a low-power gateway, demonstrating end-to-end feasibility under realistic IoT conditions.

title: Comparison of Purely MPR-based and IRSA Random Access: Spectral Efficiency versus Energy Expenditure.
abstract: Grant-free random access enables massive Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity in Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs), where a large number of low complexity devices intermittently transmit short packets under tight energy and reliability constraints. Repetition based coded random access schemes, such as Irregular Repetition Slotted ALOHA (IRSA), achieve near-optimal throughput under idealized collision channel assumptions, while successive interference cancellation based multi-packet reception schemes attain high spectral efficiency under more realistic physical-layer models. Nevertheless, a consistent comparison between these approaches under unified reliability and energy constraints is still missing.This paper provides a unified analytical and simulation based comparison of MPR Adaptive Slotted Access (MASA) and IRSA under a common physical-layer model, using the same frame structure, channel assumptions, and packet-level reliability constraint. The analysis explicitly links packet-level reliability to replica-level decoding in repetition-based access and captures the resulting impact on required decoding thresholds and energy expenditure. Results show that although IRSA can asymptotically approach the spectral efficiency of adaptive multi-user decoding, doing so under a common outage constraint entails a rapidly increasing energy cost. In contrast, MASA maintains high spectral efficiency with a significantly lower energy expenditure by exploiting multi-user decoding over the full data interval, thereby delineating when the throughput gains of coded random access remain energy-efficient in non-terrestrial massive IoT systems.

title: Quantum Graph Neural Network for Joint Optimization of Pinching and Fluid Antenna Systems.
abstract: This work optimizes a flexible antenna environment, that incorporates both pinching antenna systems (PASS) and fluid antenna systems (FAS) at the transmitter and the user sides. Optimizing PASS and FAS presents a non-trivial challenge, as the wireless network exhibits a highly dynamic topology and an extensive solution search space. To address this, this work proposes a quantum graph neural network (QGNN)based solution workflow designed to optimize the user’s quality of service by learning the spatial and structural dependencies between the pinching antenna elements and user ports as a quantum state. The QGNN approach encodes the wireless network topology, encompassing both edge and vertex relationships, into the quantum state space, and performs optimization through a tunable single-qubit rotation gate. Overall, the QGNN-based solution shows a faster loss reduction, especially during the early learning episodes, compared to the benchmark model. The QGNN achieves an average training loss approximately 3.4× lower than that of the typical parameter quantum circuit model during model training. In summary, this work points out the feasibility of applying graph-based, data-driven learning, realized through the quantum graph neural network workflow, to the problem of flexible antenna optimization.

title: TransfoREM: Transformer aided 3D Radio Environment Mapping.
abstract: Providing reliable cellular connectivity to unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is a key challenge, as existing terrestrial networks are deployed mainly for ground-level coverage. The cellular network coverage may be available for a limited range from the antenna side lobes, with poor connectivity further exacerbated by UAV flight dynamics. In this work, we propose TransfoREM, a 3D Radio Environment Map (REM) generation method that combines deterministic channel models and real-world data to map terrestrial network coverage at higher altitudes. At the core of our solution is a transformer model that translates radio propagation mapping into a sequence prediction task to construct REMs. Our results demonstrate that Trans-foREM offers improved interpolation capability on real-world data compared against conventional Kriging and other machine learning (ML) techniques. Furthermore, TransfoREM is designed for holistic integration into cellular networks at the base station (BS) level, where it can build REMs, which can then be leveraged for enhanced resource allocation, interference management, and spatial spectrum utilization.

title: Signal Rise-Fall Time Based Fingerprinting in CAN Networks.
abstract: The Controller Area Network (CAN) bus is widely used in automotive and industrial automation systems. Since CAN pursues a broadcast protocol without built-in authentication mechanism, it is highly vulnerable to spoofing attacks. A common defense is to apply voltage-based fingerprinting, where physical-layer features are used to verify the transmitting node. However, existing methods depend on absolute voltage levels, which are easily influenced by noise, bus load changes, and environmental conditions, causing fingerprint instability. In this work, we present SRF-CAN, a new fingerprinting framework that relies on the rise and fall times of CAN voltage signals instead of their absolute values. By leveraging an implicit differential method of measuring voltage, SRF-CAN captures device-specific process variations in transient behavior and remains robust against voltage fluctuations and varying operating conditions. Experiments on a real CAN testbed show that SRF-CAN achieves 100% attack detection accuracy and 99.99% node identification accuracy, demonstrating its effectiveness as a lightweight and resilient solution for protecting CAN networks.

title: BER Analysis of Zak-OTFS Using Zero-Forcing Equalization Under Perfect and Imperfect CSI.
abstract: The bit error rate (BER) of Zak orthogonal time-frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation using zero-forcing (ZF) equalization over doubly dispersive wireless channels is analyzed. A closed-form BER expression is derived by exploiting the block-circulant structure of the Zak-OTFS channel matrix in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, enabling an eigenvalue-based representation through discrete Fourier transform diagonalization. To assess its robustness under practical conditions, the analysis is further extended to account for imperfect channel state information (CSI) using an estimation error model. Increasing the number of paths enhances the diversity gain and strengthens effective eigenvalues, hence improving BER performance. In the crystalline regime, the eigenvalue spread narrows, yielding stable and predictable BER. The results demonstrate that Zak-OTFS outperforms the multicarrier OTFS (MC-OTFS) and maintains consistent BER in high-mobility scenarios. However, the channel estimation errors reduce the effective SNR and distort the DD-domain eigenvalues, hence causing higher error floors at high SNR.

title: A Practical AI-Driven Strategy for Cell On/Off Switching under Adaptable QoS Constraints.
abstract: The rapid expansion of 5G networks has intensified concerns over their sustainability, as denser Radio Access Network (RAN) deployments have increased overall power consumption. Although numerous studies have examined energy-efficient cell on/off switching, few have focused on approaches capable of dynamically adapting to operator-defined Quality of Service (QoS) requirements. In this paper, we propose a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)–based strategy, trained using a dataset from a European Mobile Network Operator (MNO), that enforces both target throughput levels and outage-tolerance constraints. Unlike previous approaches, our model adapts to different QoS requirements by tuning a decision threshold at inference time, enabling operators to balance energy savings and service guarantees without retraining. Across an unseen week, the method attains 63–96% of an oracle’s energy savings while largely meeting operator-specified constraints. We also provide CO2and OPEX estimates under representative scenarios to quantify potential operator benefits.

title: Mobile Webpage Phishing Detection through Model Distillation and Stacking.
abstract: The widespread diffusion of smart mobile devices has made them a primary target for various types of phishing attacks, among which webpage phishing is one of the most common and dangerous. In response to this threat, academic and industrial research have increasingly focused on developing lightweight solutions that can detect fraudulent content, though with minimal attention being given to the structure and content of the HTML page. In this context, we introduce PROTEGE: a stacking approach to phishing webpage detection that leverages metadata extracted from URLs and HTML code, as well as the full page structure. To achieve this, a resource-efficient LLM is employed and trained using a Teacher–Student framework through knowledge distillation. Experimental results confirm the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed approach compared to techniques currently available in the literature.

title: Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Low-Carbon P2P Energy Trading among Self-Interested Microgrids.
abstract: Uncertainties in renewable generation and demand dynamics challenge day-ahead scheduling. To enhance renewable penetration and maintain intra-day balance, we develop a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for self-interested microgrids participating in peer-to-peer (P2P) electricity trading. Each microgrid independently bids both price and quantity while optimizing its own profit via storage arbitrage under time-varying main-grid prices. A market-clearing mechanism coordinating trades and promoting incentive compatibility is proposed. Simulation results show that the learned bidding policy improves renewable utilization and reduces reliance on high-carbon electricity, while increasing community-level economic welfare, delivering a win–win situation in emission reduction and local prosperity.

title: Enhancing User Fairness in Pinching-Antenna Systems-Enabled Multi-User Communications.
abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) facilitate flexible and strong line-of-sight communication links by reconfiguring the positions of pinching antennas (PAs) along waveguides. A PASS-enabled multi-user communication system is considered by exploiting the newly introduced waveguide division multiple access (WDMA). A resource allocation problem is formulated to maximize the rate fairness via the joint optimization of pinching beamforming and power allocation. The problem is decomposed within a majorization-minimization (MM)-based alternating optimization (AO) framework, where a MM surrogate function is constructed, and an element-wise update is derived for the pinching beamforming. The transmit power allocation is then obtained through MM-based optimization. Numerical results demonstrate that: 1) PASS significantly improve communication rate performance over conventional fixed antenna systems; 2) WDMA scheme efficiently exploits spatial decoupling between users in the waveguide domain enabled by pinching beamforming to support multi-user communications.

title: Over-the-Air Synchronization of Large-Scale Cooperative ISAC Networks.
abstract: This paper investigates the over-the-air (OTA) synchronization problem in large-scale cooperative integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. We propose an access point (AP) cluster classification strategy according to the synchronization requirements. Within each cluster, orthogonal pilots are assigned to APs, while pilot reuse is permitted among different clusters. The Cramér–Rao lower bounds (CRLBs) for symbol timing offset (STO) and carrier frequency offset (CFO) estimation are derived. An iterative K-means-based algorithm is designed for AP cluster classification, and the pilot reuse problem is formulated as a graph coloring task. Building on the Dsatur algorithm, we further develop a simulated annealing (SA)-based scheme with pilot exchange to enhance performance. For multipath scenarios, a robust STO and CFO estimation algorithm based on the space-alternating generalized expectation-maximization (SAGE) method is proposed. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: Hardware-Impairment-Aware RIS Deployment Optimization for Vehicular Networks under Time-Varying Rician Fading.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) can enhance vehicular networks by creating controllable reflected links to mitigate blockage, extend coverage, and improve reliability in highly dynamic environments. However, most existing RIS-assisted vehicular studies assume ideal hardware and time-invariant channels, which can substantially overestimate practical performance. In particular, residual hardware impairments distort phase alignment and introduce additional distortion noise, while mobility-induced line-of-sight (LOS)/non-line-of-sight (NLOS) switching yields fast time-varying channels. As the link distance increases, the cascaded path loss and the mismatch between idealized assumptions and practical conditions become more pronounced, leading to non-negligible spectral-efficiency (SE) degradation and potentially larger delay spread than predicted by ideal models. To address these issues, we propose a hardware-impairment-aware RIS deployment model for vehicular networks under time-varying Rician fading with a distance-dependent K-factor. We derive a closed-form expression for an SE upper bound and jointly optimize RIS placement and phase configuration to minimize propagation delay while maximizing SE. Monte Carlo simulations show that hardware impairments incur about 7% SE reduction compared with ideal hardware, and optimized RIS placement improves SE by about 19.4% over random deployment, highlighting the importance of impairment-aware modeling and deployment optimization in practical vehicular networks.

title: D2SC: A Personalized Semantic Communications Framework for IoT via Federated Learning.
abstract: By integrating advanced semantic communications (SC) into Internet of things (IoT) devices, we can greatly enhance task execution efficiency and deliver high-quality services to users. However, with the widespread adoption of personalized services, providing customized intelligent communications presents a new challenge. In this paper, we introduce a two-stage SC framework for image transmission. In the first stage, SC is innovatively integrated into a federated learning (FL) framework, which enables the extraction of personalized knowledge while preserving privacy. Furthermore, to accommodate edge IoT devices, knowledge distillation is employed to obtain a small student model with strong semantic understanding capabilities. In addition, the intrinsic value of unlabeled data, which is often overlooked, is fully exploited through the self-supervised scheme in this phase. In the second stage, the global model in FL is deployed in wireless communications to activate specific SC functions. To mitigate channel interference, a signal-to-noise ratio modulation module is designed to achieve adaptive channel coding for semantic representation. We denote the proposed framework as distillation-to-SC (D2SC) and demonstrate its superior performance across diverse tasks through extensive simulation experiments.

title: Spectrum-Weighted Instantaneous Frequency Estimation Empowering Real-Time Drone Detection.
abstract: Existing radio frequency (RF)-based drone detection methods usually rely on time-frequency spectrum (TFS) because drones adopt frequency-hopping spread spectrum (FHSS) communication. However, the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) to obtain TFS and the detection based on TFS bring high computational complexity. On the other hand, instantaneous frequency (IF) is a feature available for drone detection, but IF estimation methods suitable for drone signals also rely on STFT, limiting their real-time capability. To address this challenge, we propose a drone signal detection algorithm based on spectrum-weighted IF (SWIF) estimation. Specifically, the algorithm estimates the amplitude-weighted average frequency of multi-tone signals by constructing the trajectory of the differential I/Q signals. Beyond the existing TFS-based feature extraction methods, the proposed method achieves linear computational complexity. Using the SWIF estimation results as input, the temporal detection network achieves only 2% of the parameters of the TFS network while maintaining detection accuracy, making real-time drone detection possible. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm using simulations and real Radio Frequency data with drone signals.

title: Hybrid Precoding for Multi-User MIMO-OFDM Systems with Phase Shifter Impairments.
abstract: Millimeter wave (mmWave) technology operates at high frequencies to provide dramatically increased bandwidth for next-generation networks. mmWave multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems require hybrid precoding—a combination of digital and RF techniques—rather than purely digital precoding due to hardware constraints. This approach balances performance with cost while addressing limitations of signal mixers and analog-to-digital converters. These systems operate in wideband channels with frequency selectivity, requiring OFDM (orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing) to handle dispersive channels. We study the problem of robust digital-RF precoding optimization for the downlink sum-rate maximization in hybrid multi-user (MU) MIMO-OFDM systems under maximum transmit power and unit modulus constraints, where phase shifters (PSs) are possibly impaired at the transmitter and users. The formulated maximization problem is non-convex and difficult to solve. We propose a weighted minimum mean squared error (WMMSE) based block coordinate descent (BCD) method to iteratively optimize digital-RF precoders at the transmitter and digital-RF combiners at the users. Low-cost and scalable optimization approaches are proposed to efficiently solve the BCD subproblems. Extensive simulation results are conducted to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed approaches and exhibit their superiority relative to well-known benchmarks.

title: Molecular Communication in Multi-Layered Parallel Channels with an Ocean Surface Case Study.
abstract: Molecular transport through heterogeneous layered structures is fundamental to biological, environmental, and engineered systems, yet molecular communication models typically assume uniform diffusivity or apply averaging approximations that mask interlayer effects. We present an analytical frame-work for multi-layered Cartesian channels that preserves layer-specific diffusion coefficients while accommodating arbitrary source positioning and diverse interface conditions. Application to oceanic stratified systems demonstrates how sea surface microlayer properties and air-water interface permeability control molecular transport behavior. Particle-based simulations validate these analytical findings.

title: Optimizing Receiver Field-of-View for OISLs in LEO Constellations.
abstract: Optical inter-satellite links (OISLs) have become a key technology for next-generation low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, offering ultra-high data rates, reduced latency, and immunity to radio frequency (RF) spectrum congestion. However, their performance strongly depends on optical alignment, transmit beam divergence, and receiver field-of-view (FOV), which together determine both received signal strength and exposure to interference. This paper investigates the impact of receiver FOV on the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) of OISLs in large-scale LEO constellations. A constellation-wide simulation framework is developed to compute SINR across thousands of OISLs while accounting for geometric visibility, beam divergence, and interference between neighboring satellites. By sweeping the receiver FOV while keeping the transmit beam divergence angle fixed, the analysis reveals a critical trade-off between the effective SINR of OISLs in a LEO constellation and the establishment time of the OISLs. Larger FOV reduces the OISL establishment time but also increases exposure to interference causing lower SINR. An optimization problem is formulated to determine the optimal receiver FOV that maximizes the product of receiver FOV and the (minimum or mean) SINR in a given constellation. This problem is then solved for three different constellations: Starlink, OneWeb, and Kuiper, yielding the optimal receiver FOV that jointly maximizes the OISL performance and minimizes the OISL establishment time. A comparison is also made between fixed and variable receiver FOVs, showing that the variable FOV model yields better performance in terms of SINR. These results provide quantitative design guidelines for adaptive optical receiver architectures in LEO satellite networks.

title: The Role of Excitation Schemes in the Functionality of Metasurface-based Antennas.
abstract: Using metasurface (MTS) antennas in wireless communication networks offers a promising way to achieve both high-quality connections and low power usage. In this paper, we study a setup where a transmissive MTS is integrated into the basestation antenna. We explore how the type of electromagnetic wave used to illuminate the MTS affects communication performance, assuming all other system parameters remain fixed. Our results show that using a cylindrical wave improves downlink performance compared to a plane wave. Although a plane wave might seem ideal due to its uniform illumination, our findings highlight the benefit of a richer set of wavevectors in the illuminating field.

title: Electromagnetically Consistent Modeling of Near-Field Channels With Metasurface Antennas.
abstract: Reliable and energy-efficient indoor wireless communication is increasingly important as user demand and device density continue to grow. Transmissive metasurface-based (TMTS) antennas have emerged as a promising solution for meeting these demands. In indoor environments, users often operate in close proximity to the basestation (BS), placing them within the near-field region of the antenna. In this work, we employ an electromagnetic integral-equation (IE) formulation to deterministically model the wireless channel in such scenarios, capturing the interactions among all objects in the environment and the TMTS antenna deployed at the BS. Our study shows that, beyond the expected spherical wavefronts and reactive fields that characterize the near-field, the electromagnetic interaction between the BS antenna and the users’ antennas plays a critical role in accurately estimating system performance. These interactions must therefore be explicitly incorporated into near-field channel models, and the IE framework offers a rigorous and effective way to achieve this goal.

title: ALIGN: 1 Gbps Optical Inter-Satellite Link Demonstration on 6U CubeSats with the FOCUS Terminal.
abstract: Free-space optical (FSO) inter-satellite links (OISLs) offer dramatically higher data throughput than traditional radio-frequency (RF) systems for satellite constellations. This paper presents the Free-space Optical Communications Unit for Satellites (FOCUS), a compact 2U payload for 6U CubeSats—the 6U form factor referring to a ∼10×10×30cm nanosatellite platform—demonstrating autonomous >1Gbps optical links at ranges up to 1000km in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). The terminal employs non-return-to-zero on-off keying (NRZ-OOK) modulation at 1.25Gbps. Component-level characterisation using an arbitrary waveform generator (AWG) test setup demonstrates receiver sensitivity below −37dBm, measured bit error rate (BER) as low as 10−8under laboratory conditions, closed-loop pointing accuracy below 50μrad using a fast-steering mirror (FSM), and AWG-based end-to-end throughput characterisation at 1.25Gbps. Compared with prior CubeSat-class OISL demonstrations, FOCUS achieves the highest reported ISL data rate at equivalent or better receiver sensitivity within a 2U payload volume. Two 6U CubeSats are planned to launch, subject to funding confirmation, as part of the Autonomous Laser InterSatellite Gigabit Network (ALIGN) mission, funded by the UK Space Agency, to validate optical ISL performance at orbital ranges from 100km to 1000km.

title: Large-Dataset Empirical Characterization of SNR, Outage, Capacity, and Modulation Reliability in 851 MHz Cellular Channels.
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive empirical analysis of wireless channel performance at 851 MHz using a dataset of one million real Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) measurements collected from a cellular base station in an indoor environment. High-fidelity data acquisition was ensured using a dual-marker measurement protocol on a Keysight MXA N9020B spectrum analyzer. The study includes statistical characterization of SNR via probability density functions (PDFs) and cumulative distribution functions (CDFs), empirical evaluation of channel capacity using Shannon’s formula, symbol error rate (SER) assessment for multiple M-PSK and M-QAM modulation schemes, and outage probability analysis for M-PSK based on an information-theoretic threshold. All analyses employ empirical methods, with results validated by agreement between direct sample computations and PDF/CDF-based integrals, ensuring reliable performance predictions for system design. The evaluation shows significant performance variations across modulation schemes and provides practical guidelines for balancing spectral efficiency and reliability in the 851 MHz band.

title: Exploiting MQTTv5 Request-Response for Traffic Amplification Attack: Detection and Mitigation.
abstract: IoT proliferation and the resulting high-volume and heterogeneous traffic are putting 5G under severe pressure; consequently, 6G aims to meet density and latency/energy requirements while embedding security-by-design practices across network and protocol layers to address a broader attack surface. At the IoT application layer, MQTT is a representative example: its latest specification (MQTTv5) introduces features that support key 6G goals, notably improved scalability and flexibility. Among these, the Request–Response pattern enables lightweight request/reply interactions via the Response Topic and Correlation Data. Despite its benefits, this paper unveils a severe security vulnerability related to such feature that leads to undermine the communication channel availability through an Amplification Attack. Specifically, a request carrying a Response Topic delivered to N subscribers may trigger up to N replies; if that topic is broadly subscribed or matched via wildcards, the traffic can grow further, enabling amplification attacks against brokers and clients. A broker-side defense is proposed to counteract such attack exploiting a statistical detection technique through sliding-window Median Absolute Deviation (MAD). Then, a mitigation mechanism that combines adaptive access-control rules with rate limiting is introduced to throttle accepted responses while preserving normal operations. Experiments on increasingly large deployments with realistic IoT traffic demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposal in detecting and mitigating the uncovered vulnerability.

title: Learning to Separate RF Signals Under Uncertainty: Detect-Then-Separate vs. Unified Joint Models.
abstract: The increasingly crowded radio frequency (RF) spectrum forces communication signals to coexist, creating heterogeneous interferers whose structure often departs from Gaussian models. Recovering the interference-contaminated signal of interest in such settings is a central challenge, especially in single-channel RF processing. Existing data-driven methods often assume that the interference type is known, yielding ensembles of specialized models that scale poorly with the number of interferers. We show that detect-then-separate (DTS) strategies admit an analytical justification: within a Gaussian mixture framework, a plug-in maximum a posteriori detector followed by type-conditioned optimal estimation achieves asymptotic minimum mean-square error optimality under a mild temporal-diversity condition. This makes DTS a principled benchmark, but its reliance on multiple type-specific models limits scalability. Motivated by this, we propose a unified joint model (UJM), in which a single deep neural architecture learns to jointly detect and separate when applied directly to the received signal. Using tailored UNet architectures for baseband (complex-valued) RF signals, we compare DTS and UJM on synthetic and recorded interference types, showing that a capacity-matched UJM can match oracle-aided DTS performance across diverse signal-to-interference-and-noise ratios, interference types, and constellation orders, including mismatched training and testing type-uncertainty proportions. These findings highlight UJM as a scalable and practical alternative to DTS, while opening new directions for unified separation under broader regimes.

title: Normalized Ambiguity Function Characteristics of OFDM, OTFS, AFDM, and CP-AFDM for ISAC.
abstract: This paper presents a unified and system-agnostic analysis of the ambiguity function (AF) characteristics of four representative multicarrier waveforms, orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS), affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM), and chirp-permuted AFDM (CP-AFDM), which are considered as key candidates for enabling integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) in future sixth generation (6G) networks. The AF of each waveform is obtained directly from its discrete-time definition and enhanced via ideal fractional interpolation, enabling precise characterization of its continuous-time delay-Doppler response. Two signaling modes are examined: a communication-oriented case with random information symbols suitable only for monostatic scenarios, and a sensing-oriented case with fixed unimodular symbols suitable for general multi-static scenarios. Furthermore, the AFs and the ambiguity metrics including the 3dB mainlobe width, peak-to-sidelobe ratio (PSLR), and integrated sidelobe ratio (ISLR), are evaluated in normalized delay-Doppler units, enabling direct translation to any physical system configuration defined by bandwidth, sampling frequency, or symbol duration, while ensuring straightforward and consistent comparison across waveforms. The results establish a consistent benchmark for comparing waveform sensing capabilities in ISAC design, consolidating known behaviors: OFDM exhibits excellent delay resolution and sidelobe behavior but poor Doppler response, whereas advanced waveforms achieve improved balance between delay and Doppler resolution with varying sidelobe characteristics. The simulation code of the smooth AFs, is openly shared to promote reproducibility and support future ISAC waveform research.

title: Low Complexity Compression for Challenged Wireless Environments.
abstract: Under severe resource limitations, as exemplified by wireless sensor nodes, and under communication-challenged environments, e.g., long-distance, low-power, low-bitrate communication, a low complexity compression scheme is needed for the streaming of sensor data. While the compression scheme may have to be, inevitably, lossy, such loss should only be employed when it is clear that lossless communication is not possible. We compare three different strategies that are of low complexity, and apply lossy compression only when necessary, and to the extent necessary. In the interest of keeping complexity low, all three schemes rely on piece-wise linear approximation/compression albeit with totally different logic on how this approximation is applied. We demonstrate that a scheme based on explicit minimization of the maximum error performs better than the other two strategies.

title: SLA-Driven Adaptive FL policy with Real-Time Visualization for Zero-Touch 6G Network Slicing.
abstract: 6G paradigm enables massive network slicing for pervasive digitization across vertical industries, demanding scalable, sustainable, AI-driven zero-touch automation, particularly under non-IID conditions in live networks. This work introduces a cloud-native service-level agreement (SLA)-driven stochastic policy to guarantee a scalable and fast operation of constrained federated learning (FL)-based analytic engines (AE) that perform statistical slice-level resource provisioning at RAN-Edge domain, deploying on the kubernetes platform with real-time visualization capability. The key novelty lies in an SLA-aware adaptive learning rate policy to tune the local model’s learning rate dynamically during FL local training to enhance stability and convergence. Besides, to sustain scalability under massive slicing, we leverages SLA-driven stochastic AE selection policy in each FL training round, maintaining computational efficiency while reducing computational overhead. Extensive experiments in both simulated and emulated environments demonstrate significant reductions in SLA violations, enhanced convergence stability, and improved scalability compared to conventional FL approaches.

title: RIS-Assisted Near-Field ISAC for Multi-Target Indication in NLOS Scenarios.
abstract: Enabling multi-target sensing in near-field integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems is a key challenge, particularly when line-of-sight paths are blocked. This paper proposes a beamforming framework that leverages a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) to achieve multi-target indication. Our contribution is the extension of classic beampattern gain and inter-target cross-correlation metrics to the near-field, leveraging both angle and distance information to discriminate between multiple users and targets. We formulate a problem to maximize the worst-case sensing performance by jointly designing the beamforming at the base station and the phase shifts at the RIS, while guaranteeing communication rates. The non-convex problem is solved via an efficient alternating optimization (AO) algorithm that utilizes semidefinite relaxation (SDR). Simulations demonstrate that our RIS-assisted framework enables high-resolution sensing of co-angle targets in blocked scenarios.

title: Serial Polar Automorphism Ensemble Decoders for Physical Unclonable Functions.
abstract: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) involve challenging practical applications of error-correcting codes (ECCs), requiring extremely low failure rates on the order of $10^{-6}$ and below despite raw input bit error rates as high as 22%. These requirements call for an efficient ultra-low rate code design. In this work, we propose a novel coding scheme tailored for PUFs based on Polar codes and a low-complexity version of automorphism ensemble decoding (AED). Notably, our serial AED scheme reuses a single successive cancellation (SC) decoder across multiple decoding attempts. By introducing cascaded and recursive interleavers, we efficiently scale the number of AED candidates without requiring expensive large multiplexers. An aggressive quantization strategy of only 3 bits per message further reduces the area requirements of the underlying SC decoder. The resulting coding scheme achieves the same block error rate of $10^{-6}$ as our baseline based on Bose-Ray-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) codes while requiring 1.75x fewer codeword bits to encode the same K = 312 payload bits. This reduction translates directly into 1.75x less helper data storage and, consequently, a smaller overall chip area.

title: TraPos: A Transformer-Based Localization Framework for Next-Generation Mobile Networks.
abstract: In multipath-rich indoor environments, accurate localization remains a challenging task, as bandwidth-limited signals require high-resolution algorithms for precise parameter estimation. To address this challenge, we introduce TraPos, a transformer-based framework for indoor localization. The network is trained and evaluated on 5G channel measurements collected with a software-defined radio (SDR) platform. The datasets were acquired using an automated guided vehicle (AGV), with spatial uniformity ensured through grid-based filtering. As a baseline, TraPos is compared to a state-of-the-art joint angle-delay Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm. Results show that TraPos outperforms the super-resolution method in both angle of arrival (AOA) and time difference of arrival (TDOA) estimation. When trained directly on two-dimensional coordinates, TraPos achieves decimeter-level accuracy, demonstrating competitive performance for unfiltered position estimates.

title: Performance Analysis of Containerized Microservice Architectures for 360° Video Web Delivery Within an Edge-Cloud Infrastructure.
abstract: Immersive content provides engaging experiences to users, with 360° videos being a prominent example. Such videos allow users to remotely explore events as if they were physically present. However, delivering these experiences incurs high computational costs. This challenge can be alleviated by distributing processing and communication tasks across an edge-cloud infrastructure. When combined with heterogeneous hardware and microservice architectures, this approach enables a scalable system for streaming 360° videos. In this paper we introduce a modular 360° video web streaming system deployed with various microservice architectures on an edge-cloud infrastructure. Our analysis reveals that edge-based architectures can cope with small-scale deployments, before hitting performance bottlenecks, by improving both delay and resource consumption. In contrast, when the video platform is stressed by adding more users, edge-cloud and microservice-assisted deployments become more efficient, improving both CPU and memory utilization, while providing similar delays as with a pure edge-based deployment.

title: QoE Benchmarking of Resilient 6G Teleoperation: VR Digital Twin vs. Video Streaming.
abstract: Teleoperation of robots is a key enabler for operations in complex and unpredictable environments such as rescue robotics or urban automated driving. Next-generation 6G networks target immersive teleoperation as a core service, using Virtual Reality (VR) interfaces that offer more intuitive control and a comprehensive perception of the environment through Digital Twins(DTs), which provide a virtual representation of the remote system. We present a testbed that combines two industrial robotic arms with a virtualized air hockey game, enabling interactive real-time control under different visual feedback modes. Four distinct modes were studied: high-quality 6G VR Video and 6G VR DT, and their degraded counterparts, impaired VR Video and impaired VR DT, under emulated wireless impairments. Players control the robots via hand gestures in VR, ensuring consistent interaction while isolating the impact of visual feedback. Our results show that the VR DT is significantly more robust to packet loss than video streaming. While the impaired VR DT mode remained close to optimal performance, impaired VR Video breaks down due to severe artifacts and interruptions, leading to a breakdown in playability and player confidence. In fact, players using the digital twin feedback achieved up to 70% better offensive and defensive gameplay performance compared to the degraded video mode. Overall, transmitting only state data using semantic communication instead of an entire video stream reduced bandwidth requirements drastically while maintaining or even improving controllability. This work demonstrates how immersive teleoperation over digital twins can enhance both Quality of Experience (QoE) and reliability in future 6G networks and provides a platform for systematically studying human–robot interaction under adverse network conditions.

title: Game-Theoretic Over-the-Air Computation for Socially Coupled Crowdsensing Systems.
abstract: The device heterogeneity, uncertain wireless channels, and the strategic behavior of socially connected participants introduce major challenges to the socially-coupled crowdsensing in order to aggregate large-scale, real-time information. This problem is addressed in this paper by introducing a game-theoretic distributed power control framework for over-the-air computation (AirComp) in socially coupled crowdsensing systems. The proposed framework jointly integrates the users’ physical-layer channel conditions characteristics and their peer effects into the data aggregation process by formulating a distributed power control problem as a socially-aware non-cooperative game and analytically proving the existence and uniqueness of a pure Nash equilibrium. A low-complexity best response dynamics algorithm is designed to enable the users to adapt their transmission powers in a fully distributed manner in order to ensure the efficient and stable data aggregation without requiring perfect channel state information. Detailed results demonstrate the energy efficiency of the proposed approach, its scalability in large-scale networks, and its energy consumption benefits compared to centralized power control approaches.

title: DepthPulse+: A Depth and Vital Sign Based Method for Face Presentation Attack Detection.
abstract: Face Presentation Attacks (FPA) are a widespread threat against face authentication systems. FPA are performed by presenting face representations of the authorized user to the camera for authentication, e.g., by displaying printed photos (photo attacks), displaying images or videos on a screen (video attacks), or wearing a face mask (mask attacks). In this paper, we propose an ensemble method that combines depth-based and vital-sign based (using remote photoplethysmography) FPA detection (FPAD). DepthPulse+ achieves state-of-the-art attack classification error rate (ACER) on all four evaluation protocols of the widely-used OULU-NPU benchmark dataset (achieving reductions of 35%, 44%, 84%, and 10% in Protocols 1 to 4, respectively, compared to the benchmark method), highlighting improved generalizability to conditions not encountered in training.

title: Q-Learning for 3D Coverage in VCSEL-based Optical Wireless Systems.
abstract: Beam divergence control is a key factor in maintaining reliable coverage in indoor optical wireless communication (OWC) systems as receiver height varies. Conventional systems employ fixed divergence angles, which result in significant coverage degradation due to the non-convex trade-off between optical power concentration and spatial spread. In this paper, we introduce a reinforcement learning (RL)–based framework for dynamic divergence adaptation in vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL)–based OWC networks. By continuously interacting with the environment, the RL agent autonomously learns a near-optimal mapping between receiver height and beam divergence, thereby eliminating the need for analytical modeling or computationally intensive exhaustive search. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves up to 92% coverage at low receiver heights and maintains robust performance under challenging conditions, enabling scalable, real-time, and energy-efficient beam control for dense VCSEL array deployments in next-generation OWC systems.

title: ReFLect: A Reputation-based Client Selection for Federated Learning in Mobile Networks.
abstract: Mobile networks increasingly rely on the data driven intelligence, however, most of the mobile and edge devices cannot support continuous model training due to limited computational and energy resources. This challenge has accelerated the adoption of Federated Learning (FL), wherein devices train local models and only the trained model parameters are thus sent to a central server, thereby preserving data privacy. A significant drawback of this approach is that some mobile devices may behave maliciously and disrupt the training process since the local training cannot be fully controlled. Such behaviour can degrade the overall quality of the final global model. To address this, this research introduces a reputation based client selection framework so as to measure the trustworthiness of each participant in FL task. The envisaged framework employs the adaptive metrics, i.e., historical accuracy, data quality, resource availability, willingness to participate, and consistency of behaviour, in a bid to compute a reputation score. We evaluate the framework using LEAF benchmark datasets, i.e., FEMNIST and Synthetic, to measure reliability and effectiveness. Experimental results show around 6% improvement in detection rate and an approximately 30% increase in accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods.

title: Location-aware Channel Prediction via Digital Radio Twin.
abstract: Digital twin (DT) is crucial for accurately modeling and simulating wireless propagation environments in next-generation (xG) networks. However, its use in real-time channel prediction remains limited due to the high computational cost of ray tracing (RT)–based emulations. This paper introduces the digital radio twin (DRT), a lightweight and real-time implementation of a DT designed to predict channel state information (CSI) efficiently. The core idea of the DRT lies in exploiting the coherence of specular reflections, a property ensuring that small variations in user equipment (UE) positions cause continuous shifts in reflection points along smooth surfaces. Building on this property, we develop a perturbation-based propagation path estimation (PPE) framework that updates CSI by perturbing previously computed reflection paths rather than performing full RT. Extensive emulations demonstrate that the proposed method achieves lower normalized mean square error (NMSE) and reduced runtime compared to conventional methods, including dynamic RT. The proposed DRT maintains accuracy across diverse geometries and frequency bands, paving the way for intelligent and proactive wireless network operation.

title: A Novel CSI-RS Reporting Scheme for RIS Optimization in O-RAN-based NextG Networks.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) technology is a promising enabler for next-generation (NextG) wireless systems, capable of dynamically shaping the propagation environment. Integrating RIS within the open radio access network (O-RAN) architecture enables flexible and intelligent control of wireless links. However, practical RIS-assisted operation requires efficient acquisition and reporting of channel state information (CSI) to support real-time control from the base station side. This paper proposes a CSI reference signal (CSI-RS)-based reporting scheme for downlink complex channel information (CCI) to facilitate RIS optimization in an O-RAN-compliant environment. The proposed framework establishing CCI extraction and CSI-RS reporting procedures is experimentally validated on a real-world testbed integrating an open-source O-RAN system with an RIS prototype operating in the n78 frequency band. Existing channel estimation-based RIS optimization algorithms, including Hadamard and orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP), are tailored for integration into the O-RAN architecture. Experimental results demonstrate notable improvements in received signal power for both near and far users, highlighting the effectiveness and practical viability of the proposed scheme.

title: MAS-Replay: A Hybrid Continual Learning Framework for Evolving IDSs.
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are essential for safeguarding network infrastructures, particularly in dynamic environments where attack patterns evolve continuously. How-ever, traditional machine learning models struggle with catastrophic forgetting when trained sequentially on non-stationary data, limiting their effectiveness in real-world scenarios. To ad-dress this, we propose a novel continual learning framework that integrates a Modified Temporal Fusion Transformer (M-TFT) with Memory Aware Synapses (MAS) and a replay buffer. The M-TFT architecture captures complex temporal dependencies and attention patterns, MAS regularization preserves important weights across tasks, and the replay buffer reinforces previously learned knowledge. Evaluated on the CSE-CIC-IDS2018 dataset across five sequential tasks, our method achieves a state-of-the-art average accuracy of 99.12% with zero forgetting, significantly outperforming a strong baseline using Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), which attained only 82.31% accuracy and a forgetting score of 0.17. These results demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of our approach in maintaining high IDS performance over time in continually evolving cyber-threat environments.

title: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Sub-Array Design for D2D Interference Channel.
abstract: This paper investigates the utility of reconfigurable intelligent surface-sub-array (RIS-SA) design to optimize the power-domain array factor (PDAF) of device-to-device (D2D) interference channel. We exploit an additional design degree of freedom–namely sub-array element selection– provided by RISSA to enhance the desired PDAF and suppress interfering PDAFs so as to maximize the sum-rate of D2D networks. To achieve this goal, we generate directional beamwidth PDAFs that exhibit significant power towards intended users while minimizing PDAF towards unintended users. To this end, the joint optimization of the RIS-SA element selection and phase shifts is formulated, subject to the interfering PDAFs ratio constraints of users, as a non-convex mixed integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem. To address the non-convex optimization problem, we propose solving it using binary differential evolution (BDE) that creates notches at the interference angles and directional beamwidth PDAFs where the intended receiving users might reside. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed joint optimization using BDE enabled D2D interference network outperforms its conventional counterparts, which enhances the performance and reduces the complexity of the beamforming design.

title: AAV-Assisted SWIPT in MU-mMIMO IoT Networks: A Joint Optimization Framework.
abstract: Autonomous aerial vehicles (AAVs) equipped with simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) offer a promising solution to sustain energy-limited and data-driven Internet-of-Things (IoT) networks. This paper presents J-HBF-PSOLPA, a particle swarm optimization (PSO)-based framework for jointly optimizing AAV location, power allocation (PA), and hybrid beamforming (HBF) in a decode-and-forward (DF) multi-user massive MIMO (MU-mMIMO) system over geometry-based millimeter-wave (mmWave) channels. The goal is to maximize the total harvested power (HP) for ground IoT devices while ensuring a minimum user-wise rate threshold for information decoding (ID). Further, we investigate two SWIPT protocols, power splitting (PS) and time switching (TS), for distributing received radio frequency (RF) signals between HP and ID. To evaluate the proposed J-HBF-PSOLPA algorithm for AAV-assisted SWIPT, we benchmark it against a fixed-location, equal-PA scheme (J-HBF-FL-EQPA). Simulation results show that J-HBF-PSOLPA significantly outperforms the benchmark, improving both total HP and achievable rate (AR), and PS yields superior energy–rate trade-offs. By enforcing the rate constraint, user-wise AR is further improved with negligible effect on HP, emphasizing the importance of dynamic resource allocation in emerging AAV-assisted IoT applications.

title: CoBA: Integrated Deep Learning Model for Reliable Low-Altitude UAV Classification in mmWave Radio Networks.
abstract: Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly used in civilian and industrial applications, making secure low-altitude operations crucial. In dense mmWave environments, accurately classifying low-altitude UAVs as either inside authorized or restricted airspaces remains challenging, requiring models that handle complex propagation and signal variability. This paper proposes a deep learning model, referred to as CoBA, which stands for integrated Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), and Attention which leverages Fifth Generation (5G) millimeter-wave (mmWave) radio measurements to classify UAV operations in authorized and restricted airspaces at low altitude. The proposed CoBA model integrates convolutional, bidirectional recurrent, and attention layers to capture both spatial and temporal patterns in UAV radio measurements. To validate the model, a dedicated dataset is collected using the 5G mmWave network at TalTech, with controlled low altitude UAV flights in authorized and restricted scenarios. The model is evaluated against conventional ML models and a fingerprinting-based benchmark. Experimental results show that CoBA achieves superior accuracy, significantly outperforming all baseline models and demonstrating its potential for reliable and regulated UAV airspace monitoring.

title: PPIR: A Privacy-Preserving and Intrusion-Resilient decentralized gossig-based trajectory prediction framework for VANETs.
abstract: Security breaches in Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) pose significant threats by compromising sensitive data and endangering the physical safety of road users and their property. This issue becomes particularly critical when the vehicle trajectory prediction process is compromised. Thus, ensuring the security of autonomous vehicles has become a significant challenge. In this context, we introduce PPIR (Privacy-Preserving and Intrusion-Resilient decentralized gossig-based trajectory prediction framework for VANETs) , a lightweight and robust framework to detect and mitigate malicious behavior, reinforced by privacy-preserving mechanisms for distributed and collaborative trajectory prediction in VANETs. The proposed approach integrates a data-driven misbehavior detection and mitigation algorithm, coupled with a unified elliptic curve-based encryption and signature process. This algorithm relies on innovation errors computed through an extended Kalman filter to assess the consistency and plausibility of the parameters received by each vehicle from peers. The system is fully decentralized and operates using a gossip-based communication protocol, making it wellsuited for highly dynamic vehicular environments. Experimental results demonstrate that PPIR achieves superior performance compared to existing data-centric misbehavior detection systems, while remaining efficient under the computational constraints inherent to vehicular networks.

title: A Network-Aware Digital Twin Architecture for Dual-Mode Transition to IATA Modern Airline Retailing.
abstract: IATA Modern Airline Retailing (MAR) represents a fundamental transformation of airline commercial systems by shifting from ticket-centric passenger service system architectures to "offer and order" based retail models. It represents a unique opportunity to improve the customer experience and create more value. Although MAR enables personalization, dynamic pricing, and flexible fulfillment, airlines operating traditional passenger service systems (PSS) owned by the airline face significant technical and operational challenges during the transition period. In practice, MAR adoption rarely occurs in a single cut-over and instead requires prolonged dual-mode operation, with legacy systems and MAR workflows coexisting.This coexistence increases system complexity and exposes airline retail transactions to network-induced risks, including latency variability, partial service degradation, and workflow instability. This paper proposes a network-aware Digital Twin architecture designed to support a controlled dual-mode transition to MAR. The proposed approach integrates digital twins of structural, behavioural, and network to model retail workflows and their network dependencies jointly. A policy-driven control layer employs what-if analysis and multi-criteria operational assessment rather than rigid analytical formulations. Scenario-based evaluation demonstrates that Digital Twin–guided routing improves transaction stability and reduces failure propagation under adverse network conditions.

title: Defense Against Membership Inference Attacks on Deep Learning-based RF Fingerprinting.
abstract: Deep learning (DL) models have shown promise as radio signal classifiers, including those for radio frequency (RF) fingerprinting. However, they have been found vulnerable to adversarial machine learning (AML) attacks such as member inference attacks (MIA). In this paper, we investigate the vulnerability of RF fingerprinting binary classifiers used for device continuous authentication (i.e., to classify a device as either authorized or unauthorized) to MIA attacks. We consider a threat actor who eavesdrops on transmitted radio signals and queries their labels to train multiple surrogate models. Then, they feed a membership inference classifier with (i) features: the signal waveforms used (members) and held out (non-members) during the training of the surrogate models, and (ii) labels: the surrogate models’ responses to the eavesdropped waveforms. After training the membership classifier, the threat actor is able to predict the membership of new waveforms and the fingerprints contained in them. MIA is designed to be aware of radio channel distortions and explainable. We compare this MIA to a baseline attack and show that it achieves higher accuracy. To mitigate MIA of this kind, we designed a three-layer defense mechanism that (i) regularizes the training, (ii) sanitizes the model output at inference, and (iii) mitigates repetitive queries on the legitimate model. The results show that the proposed defense technique successfully mitigates MIA, reducing its accuracy.

title: Neural Network Compression for Video Transmission Using Semantic Communications and VVC.
abstract: This paper introduces a hybrid video codec that integrates semantic communications with Versatile Video Coding (VVC) to enhance neural network compression in video transmission systems. The proposed approach focuses on reducing bandwidth usage by transmitting optimized Deep Neural Network (DNN) parameters tailored to each video scene. The codec leverages autoencoders (AEs) to encode semantic information from video frames into low-dimensional latent space representations (LSRs), significantly lowering the bitrate required for DNN transmission. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid codec outperforms the state-of-the-art NNCodec, achieving a lower bitrate while maintaining comparable video quality. This work presents a promising solution for efficient video transmission, particularly for bandwidth-constrained applications, and lays the groundwork for further exploration of video coding systems optimized for emerging content formats such as 360° and extended reality (XR) videos.

title: Error Resilient Rate-Scalable Image Compression Using Semantic Communications.
abstract: Scalable image compression and transmission is a capability that underpins a wide range of consumer technologies, ranging from large-format displays to remote sensing cameras. A major challenge in it is that current scalable image compression techniques are inadequately equipped to handle very small bandwidths and very noisy communication channels, which are increasingly common in many consumer electronic applications. A solution for this is proposed using the concept of semantic communications, where an autoencoder-based codec augmented with a residual coding system is used to improve the compression ratio and noise resilience of image transmission over error-prone communication channels. The system is tested with residual coders based on widely accepted and state-of-the-art image codecs, and its performance is evaluated under equal error protection and unequal error protection scenarios. Experimental results show that the proposed systems demonstrate up to 27 dB improvement in the peak signal-to-noise ratio and up to 0.90 improvement in the structural similarity index measure for a given image quality compared to conventional scalable image codecs, in addition to demonstrating superior error resilience against noise distortions for a given level of compression.

title: Consensus-Driven Fuzzy Handover Decision with PureChain Privacy-Preservation in 6G Satellite Networks.
abstract: Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) satellites at 300-1200 km altitude promise revolutionary 6G connectivity with 5-15 ms propagation delays, but their high orbital velocity (7.5-7.8 km/s) necessitates frequent handovers every 30-120 seconds while preserving user privacy. We propose a consensus-driven fuzzy handover framework for seamless integration with PureChain, a privacy-preserving credential management system. Our Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system processes signal quality (RSSI: -110 to -60 dBm), satellite elevation angles (5°-90°), user mobility (0-1000 km/h), and network load to compute handover priority scores with 94.7% accuracy in under 1µs. PureChain leverages certificateless cryptography to eliminate key escrow vulnerabilities, uses consortium-based Merkle Patricia Trees for logarithmic authenticated lookups, and employs chameleon-hash pseudonyms to ensure session unlinkability. The four-layer distributed architecture achieves over 90% local verification through Bloom filter caching, reducing authentication latency to 45-75 ms. Extensive simulations across 5000 handover scenarios demonstrate a 91.8% success rate with 96.7% privacy preservation, 42% faster than traditional public key infrastructure, while maintaining robustness against replay attacks, man-in-the-middle threats, token forgery, Sybil attacks, and Byzantine validator compromises.

title: Movable Antenna Enhanced Near-Field Velocity Estimation.
abstract: Accurate velocity estimation is essential for wireless sensing applications. Conventional fixed-position antenna (FPA) arrays are limited by their static configurations, which constrain their estimation accuracy. To tackle this challenge, this paper proposes a new movable antenna (MA) enhanced near-field velocity estimation method, where antennas can be flexibly repositioned to enable multi-view sensing of the target’s velocity. To characterize its performance limit, we first derive the Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLBs) for both radial and transverse velocity estimation of the target. A joint optimization problem is formulated to minimize the sum of the CRLBs by optimizing the antenna positions. However, this optimization problem is non-convex due to the intricate expression of the sum CRLB. To tackle this challenge, we propose an efficient suboptimal algorithm by discretizing the antenna movement region into a set of sampling points and employing a sequential update (SU) search over them. To avoid low-quality local optima, a Gibbs sampling process is also invoked following each SU iteration. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed sensing method can achieve substantially lower sum CRLB than conventional FPAs and draw new insights.

title: USRP-based mmWave SDR Testbed for UAV-to-UAV Experiments.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication offers high data rates and inherent spatial security, but its directional nature poses significant challenges for mobile platforms such as Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). In this paper, we develop a low-cost portable Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP)-based mmWave Software-Defined Radio (SDR) testbed for UAVs. Our testbed integrates compact USRP-based airborne nodes with Ka-band up/down-conversion front-ends, supports interchangeable antenna configurations including K-band horn antennas and a Sivers EVK02004 beam-steerable patch array, and provides a Python API for real-time beam control. The design enables rapid deployment of UAV-to-UAV as well as UAV-to-ground mmWave links within a portable and extensible aerial research framework. This testbed provides a flexible and open framework for researchers to prototype and evaluate advanced UAV-based mmWave communication strategies, including machine learning–driven beam alignment, neighbor discovery, and secure link acquisition. We present UAV-to-UAV and UAV-to-ground measurements under various scenarios and using different antennas.

title: WiRD-Gest: Gesture Recognition In The Real World Using Range-Doppler Wi-Fi Sensing on COTS Hardware.
abstract: Wi-Fi sensing has emerged as a promising technique for gesture recognition, yet its practical deployment is hindered by environmental sensitivity and device placement challenges. To overcome these limitations we propose Wi-Fi Range and Doppler (WiRD)-Gest, a novel system that performs gesture recognition using a single, unmodified Wi-Fi transceiver on a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) laptop. The system leverages an monostatic full duplex sensing pipeline capable of extracting Range-Doppler (RD) information. Utilizing this, we present the first benchmark of deep learning models for gesture recognition based on monostatic sensing. The key innovation lies in how mono-static sensing and spatial (range) information fundamentally transforms accuracy, robustness and generalization compared to prior approaches. We demonstrate excellent performance in crowded, unseen public spaces with dynamic interference and additional moving targets even when trained on data from controlled environments only. These are scenarios where prior Wi-Fi sensing approaches often fail, however, our system suffers minor degradation. The WiRD-Gest benchmark and dataset will also be released as open source.

title: Multi-Agent System for Dynamic Wavelength and Bandwidth Allocation in TWDM-PONs for Mobile Fronthaul.
abstract: The deployment of 5G and beyond networks requires high-capacity, low-latency fronthaul solutions. Time and Wavelength Division Multiplexing Passive Optical Networks (TWDM-PONs) offer high capacity but face challenges in dynamically managing bandwidth and wavelength resources under bursty mobile traffic. This paper proposes a Multi-Agent System (MAS) framework using goal-oriented agent modeling to optimize resource management, integrating two agents: a Resource Management Agent allocating wavelengths/timeslots and a Traffic Distribution Agent ensuring fair bandwidth distribution. Simulations demonstrate the framework’s ability to meet stringent latency requirements and maintain efficiency as the number of ONUs increases.

title: Physics-Informed Compressed Sensing: Incorporating Rotor Dynamic Equations for High-Fidelity State Estimation from Sub-Nyquist Samples.
abstract: This paper introduces a Physics-Informed Compressed Sensing (PICS) framework for high-fidelity condition monitoring of rotating machinery in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments. Classical compressed sensing methods rely solely on generic signal priors like sparsity, often producing reconstructions that are mathematically plausible but physically in-consistent, especially in low-measurement or high-noise regimes. Our proposed method fundamentally enhances the reconstruction process by embedding the governing differential equations of rotor dynamics directly into the optimization problem as a regularizer. This is achieved by introducing a "physics-residual" penalty term that forces the reconstructed signal to conform to the system’s known Lagrangian dynamics. We validate our framework using simulated data from a Jeffcott rotor model under various fault conditions, including mass unbalance and stiffness asymmetry. Experimental results demonstrate that our PICS approach significantly outperforms standard compressed sensing in both reconstruction accuracy (up to a 10 dB SNR improvement) and downstream fault diagnosis, especially at compression ratios below 30%. This work paves the way for more robust and data-efficient monitoring systems that reduce communication overhead in critical IIoT applications.

title: Sign of the Times: Ultra-Low-Power Rotor Fault Diagnosis using 1-Bit Compressed Sensing.
abstract: The proliferation of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) requires the deployment of massive-scale wireless sensor networks for real-time condition monitoring of critical machinery. However, the operational lifetime of these sensors is severely limited by power consumption, with the analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and wireless transmitter being the primary bottlenecks. This paper challenges the conventional high-resolution sensing paradigm by proposing an ultra-low-power framework for rotor fault diagnosis based on 1-bit compressed sensing. In our approach, high-frequency vibration signals are projected into a low-dimensional space and severely quantized to a single bit per measurement, effectively replacing the power-hungry ADC with a simple comparator. We then develop a deep neural network that performs fault classification directly on these binary measurements, bypassing the ill-posed and computationally expensive signal reconstruction step. Through extensive simulations on a high-fidelity rotor dynamics model, we demonstrate that complex gyroscopic fault signatures can be accurately identified from these minimalist data streams. Our proposed method achieves classification accuracy comparable to systems using unquantized data, while requiring only a fraction of the measurements and enabling an order-of-magnitude reduction in sensing power. This work paves the way for a new generation of long-lifetime, cost-effective sensors, making pervasive and truly autonomous predictive maintenance a feasible reality.

title: DQN-Driven Adaptive Neighbor Discovery for Directional Aerial Networks.
abstract: Directional antenna systems are gaining substantial traction for aerial networks due to their higher gain, extended transmission range, and enhanced security. However, the requirement of beam alignment makes the task of finding and reaching neighbors challenging, particularly in a mobile setting. For wireless networks, privacy concerns play an equally critical role. However, the problem of ensuring network-wide connectivity while maintaining limited exposure when probing around is still unexplored. We address this trade-off by proposing an adaptive transceiver selection protocol based on the Deep Q-Network (DQN) framework. Each node acts as an independent DQN agent and interacts with the environment to learn how to balance the trade-off. Since the directional nodes operate only based on local observations, we adopt a weighted mechanism that guides them in prioritizing either high reachability or privacy by adaptively tuning the probing patterns. Results show that DQN framework surpasses the Random and Q-Learning baselines. Weights favoring discovery provide higher probing efficiency and reachability, while weights prioritizing privacy ensure limited exposure at the cost of low reachability, eventually attaining higher objective value.

title: Network Slicing Resource Management in Uplink User-Centric Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: This paper addresses the joint optimization of per-user equipment (UE) bandwidth allocation and UE-access point (AP) association to maximize weighted sum-rate while satisfying heterogeneous quality-of-service (QoS) requirements across enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB) and ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) slices in the uplink of a network slicing-enabled user-centric cell-free (CF) massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) system. The formulated problem is NP-hard, rendering global optimality computationally intractable. To address this challenge, it is decomposed into two sub-problems, each solved by a computationally efficient heuristic scheme, and jointly optimized through an alternating optimization framework. We then propose (i) a bandwidth allocation scheme that balances UE priority, spectral efficiency, and minimum bandwidth demand under limited resources to ensure fair QoS distribution, and (ii) a priority-based UE-AP association assignment approach that balances UE service quality with system capacity constraints. Together, these approaches provide a practical and computationally efficient solution for resource-constrained network slicing scenarios, where QoS feasibility is often violated under dense deployments and limited bandwidth, necessitating graceful degradation and fair QoS preservation rather than solely maximizing the aggregate sum-rate. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves up to 52% higher weighted sum-rate, 140% and 58% higher QoS success rates for eMBB and URLLC slices, respectively, while reducing runtime by up to 97% compared to the considered benchmarks.
