title: Priority-Based Bandwidth Allocation in Network Slicing-Enabled Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: This paper addresses joint admission control and per-user equipment (UE) bandwidth allocation to maximize weighted sum-rate in network slicing-enabled user-centric cell-free (CF) massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) systems when aggregate quality-of-service (QoS) demand may exceed available bandwidth. Specifically, we optimize bandwidth allocation while satisfying heterogeneous QoS requirements across enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB) and ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) slices in the uplink. The formulated problem is NP-hard, rendering global optimality computationally intractable. We decompose it into two sub-problems and solve them via computationally efficient heuristics within a sequential framework. We propose (i) a hierarchical admission control scheme that selectively admits UEs under bandwidth scarcity, prioritizing URLLC to ensure latency-sensitive QoS compliance, and (ii) an iterative gradient-based bandwidth allocation scheme that transfers bandwidth across slices guided by marginal utility and reallocates resources within slices. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves near-optimal performance, deviating from an interior point solver-based benchmark by at most 2.2% in weighted sum-rate while reducing runtime by 99.7%, thereby enabling practical real-time deployment. Compared to a baseline round-robin scheme without admission control, the proposed approach achieves up to 1085% and 7% higher success rates for eMBB and URLLC slices, respectively, by intentionally sacrificing sum-rate to guarantee QoS. Sensitivity analysis further reveals that the proposed solution adapts effectively to diverse eMBB/URLLC traffic compositions, maintaining 47-51% eMBB and 93-94% URLLC success rates across varying load scenarios, confirming its robustness for resource-constrained large-scale deployments.

title: Closed-loop Uplink Radio Resource Management in CF-O-RAN Empowered 5G Aerial Corridor.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the uplink (UL) radio resource management for 5G aerial corridors with an open-radio access network (O-RAN)-enabled cell-free (CF) massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) system. Our objective is to maximize the minimum spectral efficiency (SE) by jointly optimizing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-open radio unit (O-RU) association and UL transmit power under quality-of-service (QoS) constraints. Owing to its NP-hard nature, the formulated problem is decomposed into two tractable sub-problems solved via alternating optimization (AO) using two computationally efficient algorithms. We then propose (i) a QoS-driven and multi-connectivity-enabled association algorithm incorporating UAV-centric and O-RU-centric criteria with targeted refinement for weak UAVs, and (ii) a bisection-guided fixed-point power control algorithm achieving global optimality with significantly reduced complexity, hosted as xApp at the near-real-time (near-RT) RAN intelligent controller (RIC) of O-RAN. Solving the resource-allocation problem requires global channel state information (CSI), which incurs substantial measurement and signaling overhead. To mitigate this, we leverage a channel knowledge map (CKM) within the O-RAN non-RT RIC to enable efficient environment-aware CSI inference. Simulation results show that the proposed framework achieves up to 440% improvement in minimum SE, 100% QoS satisfaction and fairness, while reducing runtime by up to 99.7% compared to an interior point solver-based power allocation solution, thereby enabling O-RAN compliant real-time deployment.

title: CSI Prediction Using Autoregressive Conditional Diffusion Models.
abstract: Acquiring accurate channel state information (CSI) is critical for reliable and efficient wireless communication, but challenges such as high pilot overhead and channel aging hinder timely and accurate CSI acquisition. CSI prediction, which forecasts future CSI from historical observations, offers a promising solution. Recent deep learning approaches, including recurrent neural networks and Transformers, have achieved notable success but typically learn deterministic mappings, limiting their ability to capture the stochastic and multimodal nature of wireless channels. In this paper, we propose a novel CSI prediction scheme based on diffusion models. We decompose the CSI prediction task into two components: a temporal encoder, which extracts channel dynamics, and a diffusion-based generator, which produces future CSI samples autoregressively. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our diffusion-based models significantly outperform state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Channel Charting for Secure Massive MIMO Communications With Flexible Exclusion Area.
abstract: This paper deals with secure transmission in massive MIMO systems where malicious users compromise the network integrity. Without explicit positional information of the possible threat, a self-supervised manifold learning method called channel charting (CC) is employed to pseudo-localize the suspicious users, which are subsequently excluded from reception via secure precoding. Unlike existing approaches requiring positional knowledge and channel state information (CSI) of the exclusion region, CC derives a chart of the coverage area from offline-collected CSI samples. This enables suppression of the transmitted signal not only at the positions of users suspected to be malicious, but also within an extended area around possible eavesdropper. Secrecy performance is evaluated through coverage maps and secrecy rate analysis. Comparisons against position-aware and no-charting baselines in a realistic multipath propagation environment highlight the effectiveness of the proposed approach with a substantial gain of 9 bps/Hz over the artificial noise scheme.

title: A Hardware-Aware Performance Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Sensor-Aided Millimeter-Wave Beam Prediction.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mm-wave) and sub-terahertz communication are cornerstones for 6G networks, but are hindered by their reliance on highly directional beams and the high latency of conventional beam alignment and beam management procedures. Sensor- and machine learning (ML)-based beam prediction offers a low-latency alternative, but remains constrained by hardware limitations at the wireless edge. This paper presents a systematic, hardware-aware analysis of ML models for sensor-aided beam prediction, specifically focusing on LiDAR, spanning deep learning, classical ML, and a novel class of proposed hybrid models that combine a CNN-based feature extractor with lightweight classical classifiers. Using the public DeepSense 6G dataset, models are benchmarked on accuracy, inference latency, memory footprint, and computational complexity. Our results show that classical ML models, particularly linear and tree-based methods, deliver strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, achieving up to 95× lower inference latency and 67× smaller memory footprint than CNNs with minimal accuracy loss. The proposed hybrid models further enhance this trade-off, maintaining CNN-level top-5 accuracy while drastically reducing re-training time by up to 20× and enabling fast, environment-specific adaptation. These findings establish classical and hybrid models, supported by efficient preprocessing, as promising candidates for real-time, resource-efficient beam prediction in future 6G edge systems.

title: Time-Slot-Aware Transmission in 5G TDD for Edge-Controlled Robotics.
abstract: Future 6G networks are expected to support net-worked collaborative robotics with stringent requirements on latency determinism, synchronization, and reliability. In current 5G systems, end-to-end latency can vary substantially because packet transmissions are not coordinated with the Time Division Duplexing (TDD) frame timing, and experimental evidence from reproducible hardware testbeds remains limited. This paper presents a testbed-based evaluation of time-slot-aware transmission in a standalone 5G system. We align packet dispatch with the 5G TDD frame structure without modifying the radio scheduler. Measurements on an OpenAirInterface-based testbed show that slot-aligned transmission improves latency determinism, reducing mean latency by up to 39.0% and jitter by up to 89.5% compared to baseline operation. These results support timing alignment as a practical mechanism for more predictable communication in cellular networks targeting collaborative robotic workloads.

title: Causal Inference for Quantifying Noisy Neighbor Effects in Multi-Tenant Cloud Environments.
abstract: Resource sharing in multi-tenant cloud environments enables cost efficiency but introduces the Noisy Neighbor problem, i.e., co-located workloads that unpredictably degrade each other’s performance. Despite extensive research on detecting such effects, there are no explainable methodologies for quantifying the severity of impact and establishing causal relationships among tenants. We propose an analytical that combines controlled experimentation with multi-stage causal inference and validates it across 10 independent rounds in a Kubernetes testbed. Our methodology not only quantifies severe performance degradations (e.g., up to 67% in I/O-bound workloads under combined stress) but also statistically establishes causality through Granger causality analysis, revealing a 75% increase in causal links when the noisy neighbor activates. Furthermore, we identify unique "degradation signatures" for each resource contention vector (i.e., CPU, memory, disk, network), enabling diagnostic capabilities that go beyond anomaly detection. This work transforms the Noisy Neighbor from an elusive problem into a quantifiable, diagnosable phenomenon, providing cloud operators with actionable insights for SLA management and smart resource allocation.

title: Radio Channel Measurements of D2X Communication in a Running Industrial Factory.
abstract: The trends associated with Industry 4.0 are fundamentally dependent on wireless communication technologies to facilitate a mobile and flexible factory floor. Consequently, comprehensive radio channel measurements are necessary for understanding the challenges and characteristics of the propagation environment. This paper presents a channel measurement campaign conducted within an operational industrial factory utilizing both static and mobile nodes to emulate device-to-everything (D2X) communications. An analysis is performed by first computing the distribution of node distance, followed by a conditional characterization of received power. Moreover, the spatial correlation properties of both device-to-infrastructure (D2I) and device-to-device (D2D) links are evaluated, revealing shorter decorrelation distances for D2D links, which highlight their deployment challenges in industrial environments.

title: Empirical Evaluation of Multihop DECT-2020 NR in a Factory Environment.
abstract: As Industry 4.0 drives the shift to flexible wireless automation, novel technologies such as DECT-2020 NR present promising capabilities designed to support ultra-reliable and low latency communication. However, the performance of this technology under realistic industrial traffic conditions and multihop operation remains insufficiently characterized. Consequently, a comprehensive evaluation is necessary to assess its suitability for dependable factory deployments. This paper presents an empirical study conducted in an operating factory, focusing on a two-hop communication where an operational automated guided vehicle serves as a mobile relay. The testbed setup applies hardware timestamping and a traffic pattern derived from real industrial applications. The measurements enable a detailed assessment of key performance indicators such as one-way delay, packet delay variation, and packet error rate under realistic network load and mobility. Results show consistently low latency and jitter across two hops. However, the packet error rate is increased under the specified network load, which may be attributed to current hardware limitations that will improve in future DECT-2020 NR implementations.

title: Influence of Antenna Height on Fading Effects Inside the Factory Floor.
abstract: Modern automated manufacturing facilities increasingly rely on a growing number of devices that require dependable wireless connectivity. Future communication systems are anticipated to integrate device-to-device communication, enabling nodes to exchange data directly at similar antenna elevations. However, the impact of the antenna height on the performance of radio channel parameters in industrial environments remains insufficiently characterized. This study aims to address this gap by conducting a statistical analysis of large-scale and small-scale fading parameters derived from an extensive measurement dataset collected within an operational factory, where an automated guided vehicle is used as mobile transmitter. The results indicate that antennas positioned at elevations exceeding the surrounding environmental clutter consistently outperform those situated at lower heights in terms of path loss as well as spatial and temporal signal correlation properties. In contrast, antennas situated at intermediate heights exhibit reduced performance regarding path loss and fading. This is attributable to their comparable elevation to obstructing structures, which enhances multipath propagation of the received signal. Interestingly, the receiver antenna positioned at a height comparable to that of the transmitter exhibits unexpectedly favorable behavior in the probability distributions of key channel parameters, including the Rician K-factor, coherence bandwidth, and coherence time. This phenomenon is likely attributable to the predominance of ground-reflected multipath components, which exhibit greater attenuation compared to reflections from adjacent metallic structures. Overall, this paper provides further insights into propagation conditions within industrial environments.

title: Data Augmentation and Attention for massive MIMO-based Indoor Localization in Changing Environments.
abstract: The demand for high-precision indoor localization has grown significantly with the rise of smart environments, industrial automation, and location-aware applications. While massive Multiple-Input and Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems enable millimeter-level accuracy by leveraging rich Channel State Information (CSI), most existing solutions are optimized for static environments, where users or devices remain fixed during data collection and inference. Real-world applications, however, often require real-time localization in changing environments, where rapid movement, unpredictable blockages, and dynamic channel conditions pose significant challenges. To address these challenges, we introduce two data augmentation techniques designed to resemble blocked antennas, enhancing the generalizability of localization models to dynamic scenarios. Additionally, we enhance an existing Deep Learning (DL) model by incorporating attention modules, improving its ability to focus on relevant channel features and antennas. We train our model on data from a static scenario, augmented with the proposed techniques, and evaluate it on a dataset collected in changing scenarios. We investigate the performance enhancements achieved by the data augmentation techniques and the Attention modules, and observe a localization accuracy improvement from a mean error of 286 mm, when trained without Attention and without data augmentations, to 66 mm, when trained with Attention and data augmentation. This shows that high localization accuracy can be maintained in changing environments, even without training data from those scenarios.

title: Forward-Forward Autoencoder Architectures for Energy-Efficient Wireless Communications.
abstract: The application of deep learning to the area of communications systems has been a growing field of interest in recent years. Forward-forward (FF) learning is an efficient alternative to the backpropagation (BP) algorithm, which is typically used as the training procedure for neural networks. Among its several advantages, FF learning does not require the communication channel to be differentiable and does not rely on the global availability of partial derivatives, allowing for an energy-efficient implementation. In this work, we design end-to-end learned autoencoders using the FF algorithm and numerically evaluate their performance for the additive white Gaussian noise and Rayleigh block fading channels. We demonstrate their competitiveness with BP-trained systems in the case of joint coding and modulation, and in a scenario where a fixed, non-differentiable modulation stage is applied. Moreover, we provide further insights into the design principles of the FF network, its training convergence behavior, and significant memory and processing time savings compared to BP-based approaches.

title: QSFL-ID: Quantum-Split Federated Learning for Intrusion Detection in IIoT Networks.
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is reshaping industrial automation through interconnected, intelligent systems. However, this evolution increases exposure to sophisticated cyber threats, especially given the constraints of IIoT devices such as limited processing power, bandwidth, and heterogeneous protocols. Traditional machine learning methods often fail to meet these security demands due to their computational intensity and centralized data requirements. To address this, we propose a hybrid quantum-classical Split Federated Learning (SFL) framework for intrusion detection in IIoT networks. Our method integrates Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs) to model complex, non-linear data relationships, enhancing detection accuracy while preserving data privacy through decentralized learning. The architecture assigns lightweight preprocessing to edge devices and complex analysis to a quantum backend, ensuring efficiency and scalability. To evaluate the proposed framework, we conduct extensive experiments on the real-world EDGE-IIoT dataset; the experimental results demonstrate that the model attains 95.5% training accuracy, significantly surpassing classical SFL (85.7%). In addition, the quantum model’s enhanced entanglement properties and expressibility strengthen its generalization performance. This approach offers an efficient and privacy-preserving solution for securing IIoT systems.

title: Evaluating Event-Based Synchronization Techniques for Network Digital Twins Operation.
abstract: With the advent of 6G, mobile networks are becoming more cognitive and self optimizing. In this context, Network Digital Twins (NDTs) have emerged as a key enabling technology for supporting real-time monitoring, enhancing service management, and performing predictions. However, for efficient operation of Digital Twins (DTs), a primary requirement is to possess accurate and timely synchronization with the Physical Twin (PT). While many synchronization techniques have been proposed, many result in redundant updates and wasteful usage of computing and communication resources. Synchronization which is activated only during substantial variations, provides a more resource-efficient approach especially under the bandwidth limitations, and resource constraints that characterize mobile network environments. In this paper, we study and present the technique of event-based synchronization, which is fundamental in the operation of Network Digital Twins. Our work offers novelty in evaluating different techniques including Adaptive event-based synchronization, Model Predictive Control (MPC), Kalman filters, and Reinforcement Learning (RL). Our investigation takes into account how critical these approaches are in achieving accurate synchronization and efficient resource utilization. The results obtained highlight that MPC achieves the highest synchronization accuracy reflected by a lowest MAE of approximately 0.067, while the RL and Kalman filters offer a strong balance between accuracy and complexity.

title: SIR Analysis for Affine Filter Bank Modulation.
abstract: The signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) of the Affine Filter Bank Modulation (AFBM) waveform is analyzed under minimum mean square error (MMSE) equalization in two domains; namely, the affine domain and the filtered time-domain (TD). Due to the incorporation of the discrete affine Fourier transform (DAFT) and despreading/mapping, an interesting and counter-intuitive cancellation of the unwanted combination of the channel induced interference with the orthogonality approximation error is seen in the filtered TD, a process which does not occur in the affine domain. The direct impact on bit error rate (BER) provides a thorough validation of the proposed analysis and explains the substantial gains in performance of the filtered TD detection scheme as opposed to its affine domain equivalent

title: Infra-free Indoor Localization via On-demand Wi-Fi Aware FTM with Extended Particle Filter.
abstract: Traditional indoor localization remains costly and impractical at scale due to the need for dense infrastructure, limiting its widespread adoption in real-world environments. We propose an infrastructure free indoor localization system that leverages on-demand Wi-Fi Aware discovery and fine timing measurement (FTM) ranging, combined with pedestrian dead reckoning (PDR), to enable accurate localization using only smartphones. the system triggers Wi-Fi Aware sessions and FTM measurements adaptively, activating them only when the reliability of PDR degrades, and fuses theses measurements using an extended particle filter optimized for low computational and energy overhead. Simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate substantial improvements in correction frequency, localization accuracy, and energy efficiency compared to baseline methods, highlighting the system’s practicality for unified outdoor-to-indoor navigation on smartphones.

title: Cylindrical Receiver Grids for Resilient mmWave Communication and Sensing.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication at 73 GHz is fundamental to beyond-5G networks but faces severe challenges in dense urban environments due to blockage and dynamic obstructions. This paper presents a comprehensive ray-tracing analysis of mmWave propagation in urban intersections, introducing cylindrical receiver grids as a novel methodology for complete 3D spatial channel sampling. Through high-fidelity simulations using Wireless InSite, we compare cylindrical (360° coverage) and planar (120° field-of-view) receiver configurations under varying traffic conditions. Our results demonstrate that cylindrical grids capture 10-20% additional received power from diffuse scattering in non-line-of-sight scenarios, reduce signal variability by 48% under vehicular blockages, and reveal direction-dependent vulnerabilities invisible to planar arrays. When seven vehicles occupy 42% of an intersection area, cylindrical receivers experience up to 13.6 dB directional power loss, while the coefficient of variation increases by 112% at transition points. Critically, omitting diffuse scattering in simulations increases standard deviation by 90% (from 12.3 to 23.4 dB), confirming its essential role in link resilience. These findings position cylindrical receiver grids as dual-purpose infrastructure for smart cities, enhancing communication robustness while enabling passive vehicular sensing through angular power variations.

title: PACDiff: Protocol-Aware Diffusion-Based Anomaly Detection for Next-Generation Vehicular Networks.
abstract: In-vehicle Controller Area Network (CAN) security in next-generation vehicular networks requires anomaly detection mechanisms that achieve high detection fidelity under normal-only training while preserving sensitivity to protocol-level deviations. This paper proposes PACDiff, a generative AI–driven, protocol-aware diffusion-based anomaly detection framework for in-vehicle networks that explicitly incorporates CAN identifier (CAN-ID) conditioning into the generative modeling process. By conditioning both the encoder and the diffusion denoiser on CAN identifiers, PACDiff learns ECU-specific normal traffic distributions rather than a single homogeneous representation of CAN traffic, enabling protocol-aware modeling for intelligent and next-generation in-vehicle network monitoring. Anomalous CAN messages are identified using multi-timestep diffusion-based reconstruction errors computed under a normal-only training regime. In addition, a model-driven attribution mechanism enables localization of anomalous behavior at both the CAN-ID and payload-byte levels without requiring signal decoding or labeled attack data. Experimental evaluation on CAN datasets demonstrates high anomaly detection performance, achieving an F1-score of 0.99 with zero false positives. Beyond binary detection, the framework provides interpretable localization by ranking anomalous CAN identifiers and attributing deviations to specific payload bytes.

title: Physics-Aware Joint Optimization for Embodied Agents via LLM-Based Decision Correction.
abstract: This paper studies the optimization of data-intensive task execution by intelligent mobile agents under energy constraints. Traditional communication paradigms treat the mobile terminal as a passive receiver, ignoring its potential to actively reshape the wireless environment through mobility. In this paper, we propose a framework that synergistically optimizes physical mobility and semantic compression of the mobile agent to maximize the effective transmission rate. Unlike conventional static systems, our agent can utilize embodied intelligence to autonomously adjust its spatial displacement to seek superior channel conditions while dynamically calibrating its semantic compression ratio to balance computational energy and transmission overhead. Specifically, we formulate a joint rate-maximization problem that optimizes the effective semantic throughput by concurrently tuning the agent’s spatial displacement and semantic compression ratio, subject to a unified power budget that couples communication, mechanical, and computational energy. We develop an efficient algorithm based on the block coordinate descent (BCD) strategy, deriving a closed-form solution for displacement and utilizing the Lambert W function for optimal semantic compression ratio. Furthermore, a Validation Agent is introduced to ensure the physical feasibility and robustness of the decisions in dynamic environments via a Large Language Model (LLM) based decision layer. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed joint optimization framework significantly outperforms baseline strategies, achieving up to a 50% increase in transmission efficiency and providing a "Graceful degradation" capability for energy-starved agents in far-field scenarios.

title: CATS: Predictive-Feedback Adaptive Load Balancing for Computing-Aware Traffic Steering.
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed load balancing algorithm for computility networks, aiming to address load balancing challenges in both observable and implicit computing resource scenarios. Under observable computing resource conditions, the Predictive PI Feedback algorithm (PIRF-LB) performs task scheduling through online learning and prediction combined with a PI controller. Under implicit resource conditions, the Adaptive Iterative algorithm (AIRF-LB) iteratively estimates the effective relative load capacity of computing nodes through adaptive adjustment. Simulation tests on six service types and four combined scenarios demonstrate that when node capacities are known, the algorithm achieves over 6% performance gain improvement. When capacities are unknown, it achieves over 30% performance gain improvement and approximately 17% stability enhancement. These results validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed algorithm across different scenarios and conditions.

title: Robust Semantic Communication via Dimension-Selective Fading Analysis and Repair.
abstract: Semantic communication is envisioned as a key enabler for 6G networks, yet its deployment remains hindered by semantic distortion caused by wireless channels that vary over time. This paper presents a robust semantic communication framework for text transmission to enhance both robustness and semantic accuracy. An interpretable semantic embedding is first developed, where each vector dimension encodes a distinct semantic attribute, enabling explicit analysis of semantic variation induced by the channel. Based on this embedding, a theoretical model of semantic dimension-selective fading is established to quantify semantic distortion through sensitivity gradients. Furthermore, a semantic domain repair mechanism is proposed, combining distortion estimation weighted by sensitivity and semantic reconstruction adaptive to the channel to prioritize critical semantic dimensions. Simulation results over Rayleigh fading channels demonstrate significant improvements in semantic fidelity and robustness compared with conventional methods operating at the bit level, showing promising potential for practical 6G semantic communication systems.

title: 3-D Velocity Estimation in OFDM-Based Bistatic Near-Field ISAC via Spatial Focusing.
abstract: Near-field communications and sensing with large-aperture arrays are promising for safety-critical smart-factory coordination of automated guided vehicles (AGVs), autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), and human operators. However, dense indoor scenes contain many reflectors whose structured echoes can corrupt high-resolution estimators. This paper develops a bistatic OFDM near-field integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework for full 3-D motion recovery under spherical-wave propagation and multi-object clutter. Motivated by Release-19 industrial ISAC studies and 3GPP channel-modeling directions, we adopt a deterministic Tx–target–Rx formulation for FR3 and large arrays using the channel frequency response (CFR) over OFDM grids. We spatially focus a 64 × 64 planar receive array processed on an 8 × 8 subsampled aperture onto target 3-D points to enhance the desired echo and suppress background reflections. A joint spatial–Doppler MUSIC estimator applied to the focused CFR recovers the complete velocity vector while treating other objects as structured interference, and we analyze degradation due to target–background subspace leakage. Ray-traced factory-hall simulations achieve around 1 m/s median 3-D velocity error per-axis at 5–30 m and approximately 2–3 m/s median error up to 60 m, demonstrating the potential of FR3 bistatic near-field ISAC for scalable localization-aware motion sensing.

title: Doppler-Precoded OTFS with Frequency-Domain Shaping and Extension.
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation has emerged as a promising waveform for high-mobility wireless communications due to its inherent robustness against severe Doppler effects. However, the multicarrier structure of OTFS leads to a high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), which degrades power amplifier efficiency and poses challenges for practical deployment. To mitigate the high-PAPR issue, this paper proposes a low-PAPR OTFS waveform design by jointly exploiting Doppler-domain Zadoff–Chu (ZC) precoding and frequency-domain spectral shaping (FDSS) with symmetric spectral extension (SE). By appropriately adjusting the spectral extension ratio while preserving the original spectral efficiency, the proposed scheme is capable of reducing the instantaneous PAPR to approximately 3 dB at the 10−4complementary cumulative distribution function (CCDF) level, with only negligible degradation in block error rate (BLER). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed waveform design method achieves significant PAPR reduction without compromising error-rate performance, rendering it a promising solution for practical high-mobility OTFS systems.

title: Integrated Sensing, Computation and Communications Using Continuous-Aperture Array.
abstract: This paper presents a continuous-aperture array (CAPA)-enabled integrated sensing, computation and communications (ISCC) framework. In this architecture, a CAPA-based base station (BS) performs continuous receive beamforming to collect sensing information from distributed ISCC nodes, while simultaneously supporting communications and over-the-air computation (AirComp) via the waveform superposition property of the wireless multiple access channel (MAC). The computation error minimization (CEM) problem is formulated under sensing performance constraints and subsequently addressed within an alternating optimization (AO) framework. In particular, closed-form minimum mean-squared error (MMSE) CAPA receivers for sensing and computation are derived, and the transmit beamforming subproblem is efficiently tackled using a semidefinite relaxation (SDR)-based method. Extensive numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed design. The proposed ISCC algorithm achieves significant reductions in computation error while maintaining reliable sensing performance compared with conventional zero-forcing (ZF) and MMSE schemes; and ii) the CAPA architecture consistently provides substantial performance advantages over the traditional spatially discrete array (SPDA).

title: DRAD-AIM: Dynamic Region Anomaly Detection Based on Intersection-Level Anomaly Mining.
abstract: Accurate anomaly detection in dynamic regions plays a crucial role in intelligent transportation systems. However, most existing methods are designed for static regions and struggle to adapt when regional boundaries and data distributions change over time. To address these challenges, we propose DRAD-AIM, which reformulates region-level anomaly detection as an intersection-level problem. Specifically, the centrality of roadway intersections is calculated to identify a set of hotspot intersections that remain structurally stable despite dynamic boundary variations. A BiLSTM network is then trained on historical traffic flow and speed data from these intersections to model normal spatiotemporal patterns. Intersection-level anomaly scores are computed using the Local Outlier Factor (LOF) algorithm and subsequently aggregated to infer regional anomalies. Experimental results on both simulated and real datasets demonstrate that DRAD-AIM effectively detects anomalous incidents in dynamic regions, achieving an average precision improvement of 40.6% over the best-performing baseline methods.

title: On Leveraging Digital Twins for Training and Validation of Reinforcement Learning in 6G.
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) demonstrates significant potential for mobile network optimization, but training or deploying RL algorithms on live networks risks degrading Quality of Service. Alternatively, Digital twins (DTs) offer safe, high-fidelity environments for RL development and validation. This paper presents a framework for training and validating RL-based network management algorithms using a DT. We demonstrate the framework through a network slicing case study, where a Proximal Policy Optimization agent dynamically allocates radio resource blocks among eMBB, URLLC, and Vehicle-to-X slices. Our results show that the pretrained RL agent outperforms baseline algorithms and highlight the critical advantage of DT-based pretraining over online training. Additionally, we demonstrate how DTs enable testing what-if scenarios under varying network conditions. This work showcases the essential role of DTs in enabling reliable RL deployment in future 6G networks.

title: Explainable TinyML for Intrusion Detection in Automated Manufacturing Communication Systems.
abstract: As manufacturing systems rapidly evolved into intelligent and interconnected ecosystems, the threat of sophisticated cyber intrusions grows exponentially. In order to overcome this problem, we present a novel XAI-based TinyML model that can be used to perform real-time, safe intrusion detection in automated manufacturing and IIoT communication systems. Our solutions integrate the effectiveness of TinyML to deploy on edge devices with the explainable AI (XAI) methods, such as SHAP and LIME, and guarantee that they are accurate and have an interpretable usefulness. The framework is trained on the large-scale X-IIoTID data set in a pre processing step and adversarial training step to be robust to lightweight performance. Our model has a high rate of detection ( 98 percent) using the compremensive experimentation and has a small memory footprint, meaning that it is a dependable service to implement resource bound industrial environments, leading to reliable, efficient, and transparent cybersecurity in the age of Industry 4.0.

title: Federated Learning-Based Beamforming Design Towards CRLB Minimization in RIS-Assisted ISAC.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems jointly utilize wireless resources for high-rate data transmission and accurate environmental sensing. Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) enable dynamic control of propagation, enhancing both communication reliability and sensing precision. This paper proposes a full-duplex (FD) RIS-assisted ISAC framework integrated with federated learning (FL) for distributed, privacy-preserving optimization of beamforming and RIS phase shifts. Using a realistic Rician channel model, the Fisher information matrix and Cramér-Rao lower bound are derived to assess sensing accuracy. The FL-based algorithm jointly maximizes sum rate and minimizes localization error under power and QoS constraints through local training and global aggregation. Simulations show that the proposed method achieves up to 8% higher throughput and 20% lower CRLB than centralized SGD, demonstrating the effectiveness of combining RIS and FL for scalable, privacy-aware ISAC systems.

title: Robust Split Federated Learning Against Multi-Vector Poisoning in Semantic Communication Networks.
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) semantic communication systems rely on distributed intelligence across edge and cloud layers, but their openness also exposes them to adversarial manipulation. This paper investigates the robustness of split federated learning (SFL) under multi-vector poisoning attacks in a semantic communication environment. Three attack modalities, namely label poisoning, weight poisoning, and representation-space (smash) poisoning, are modeled and evaluated using the MNIST dataset as an image-semantic proxy for edge sensing. A multi-k Krum aggregation scheme with L2-norm clipping is proposed to enhance Byzantine resilience while preserving communication efficiency. Comparative experiments under conservative (30% malicious clients) and strong attack scenarios show that the proposed defense achieves near-clean accuracy (95.52% and 98.19%) and bounds semantic deviation within ±robust aggregation effectively mitigates semantic corruption in1% of the benign baseline. The results demonstrate that distributed learning, offering a secure and resource-efficient foundation for AI-native 6G networks.

title: Uncertainty-Guided Dynamic Precoding for Cell-Free ISAC without Prior Target Information.
abstract: This paper investigates the precoding optimization problem in cell-free integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems under the practical scenario where no prior information about target locations is available. The absence of such prior knowledge poses a major challenge for conventional precoding designs that rely on known target directions to focus sensing energy for better sensing performance. To address this issue, we propose a dynamic uncertainty-aware precoding framework that adapts precoding based on the posterior covariance of regional scattering coefficients obtained via Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves significantly improved multitarget identification accuracy compared with baseline precoding schemes.

title: Variational Bayesian Learning Estimator for NF gMIMO-OTFS with Spatial Non-Stationarity.
abstract: Near-field propagation and spatial non-stationarity in gigantic multiple-input multiple-output (gMIMO) orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) systems introduce unique challenges for channel estimation. We propose a novel channel model, which captures spatial non-stationarity in spatial dimension and fractional Doppler shift in delay Doppler domain. These aspects lead to a structured two-dimensional (2D) sparsity in the delay-Doppler-spatial domain. To exploit this 2D sparsity, we propose a novel 2D Gaussian mixture prior, where each Gaussian component models a different sparsity pattern in the channel. Using this 2D prior, we develop a variational Bayesian learning (2DGVBL) framework to approximate the channel posterior distribution. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed 2DGVBL algorithm achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art algorithms under high-mobility conditions.

title: Variational Learning with 2D Coupled Prior for Fractional-Doppler Aware mMIMO-OTFS Systems.
abstract: We consider a massive multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal time-frequency space system with practical fractional Doppler, which induces block sparsity in the DD domain, and burst sparsity in the angular domain. This leads to a structured two-dimensional (2D) burst-block sparse channel. To efficiently estimate the channel, we capture its 2D sparsity by constructing a novel user equipment (UE)-coupled 2D Gaussian mixture prior. The prior also captures the DD domain shared sparsity across UEs by considering the influence of non-zero entries of channels of all UEs. We develop a variational Bayesian learning algorithm to exploit these sparsities by employing the proposed prior. We show that our algorithm, due to its novel prior and variational learning, outperforms existing algorithms by a margin of 8 − 10 dB, for a given number of antennas.

title: Electromagnetically Coupled Near-Field Uplink Holographic MIMO Channel and Beamforming.
abstract: This paper investigates uplink near-field holographic MIMO (HMIMO) systems operating in the radiating Fresnel region, where dense apertures and electromagnetic (EM) coupling invalidate conventional far-field models. A hybrid EM-statistical channel model is proposed that jointly captures deterministic mutual coupling and stochastic non-line-of-sight (NLoS) scattering, enabling physically grounded yet tractable near-field analysis. Within this framework, uplink receive beam-forming is studied via a max-min fairness design and an analytical characterization of maximum-ratio combining (MRC). To address the resulting nonlinear signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) expressions, an equivalent-in-distribution SINR model and a mean-equivalent approximation are developed, yielding closed-form SINR and achievable-rate approximations. The analysis is further extended to imperfect channel state information (CSI) through an error-aware SINR formulation. Simulation results validate the analysis and show that MRC provides a robust complexity-performance tradeoff in near-field HMIMO uplinks, remaining stable under EM-coupling and CSI mismatch, while zero-forcing (ZF) and max-min beam-formers are more sensitive to estimation errors.

title: RSMA-Assisted Downlink Service Provisioning for Aerial Users.
abstract: In this paper, we provide guidelines on ground base station (GBS) service provisioning for aerial users (AUs) in a non-terrestrial network (NTN). Considering a multi-antenna GBS infrastructure, we study the downlink transmission to AUs using rate splitting multiple access (RSMA) with a single layer of imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). Assuming an interference-limited, line-of-sight (LoS)-only air-to-ground channel, we derive expressions for the successful transmission probability (STP) and successful area throughput (SAT) metrics. Numerical and simulation results show that the optimum operating point in terms of common stream power allocation lies near the boundary between common-stream-dominated and private-stream-dominated transmission, revealing a fundamental balance between interference mitigation through the common stream and desired signal enhancement via the private stream in high altitude LoS propagation. Furthermore, the optimum SAT-STP trade-off exhibits non-monotonic behaviour under infrastructure densification, indicating that the same SAT can be achieved either in a reliability-favoured moderately dense regime or in a ultra-dense interference dominated regime.

title: A Hardware-Based Adaptive Power Updating System for Ultraviolet Communication.
abstract: To address varying environmental conditions, this paper proposes a transmitter-side adaptive power updating mechanism for ultraviolet (UV) communication. The receiver performs channel estimation on the forward link and sends back the signal and background radiation components to the transmitter via the feedback link. We begin by generating a bit error rate (BER) performance map via offline simulation for various signal and noise conditions. The transmitter combines real-time channel information from the feedback link with this performance map to dynamically update the number of active transmitting elements (LEDs), ensuring the signal strength required for an ultra-low BER. Furthermore, to reduce power consumption, we have also defined a power-saving threshold, which is intended to proactively limit and decrease the number of active LEDs when the channel conditions are favorable, such as in short-range communication, thereby avoiding unnecessary energy loss. Outdoor experiments are conducted to verify the performance in long-range scenarios where the transceiver distance increases. Experimental results demonstrate the dual advantage of the proposed mechanism: it ensures high power efficiency by operating at low power in favorable channel conditions, while also guaranteeing communication reliability and robustness by increasing power in long-distance, weak-channel scenarios.

title: Bruxism Recognition via Wireless Signal.
abstract: Bruxism is an oromandibular movement disorder involving teeth grinding and clenching, which severely impairs sleep quality and dental health. However, its diagnosis remains challenging, as existing methods often cause discomfort or compromise user privacy. To address these limitations, we establish a contactless bruxism recognition system based on millimeter-wave radar. First, we analyzed the potential impact of the movement patterns of teeth grinding on radar echo signals. Based on this analysis, 11 features were extracted. Subsequently, using these features, we performed classification with a Random Forest model on the dataset constructed via millimeter-wave radar. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 96.1% on the test set, with precision, recall, and F1-score all remaining at a relatively high level. This study validates the effectiveness of millimeter-wave radar for Bruxism recognition, providing a non-invasive and privacy-friendly alternative to existing recognition techniques. Future research will focus on enhancing the robustness of the method across diverse populations and environments, as well as striving to mitigate the interference of other facial micro-movements on teeth grinding recognition.

title: Feature-Coupling-Based Non-Orthogonal Transceiver Design for Multi-Image Semantic Transmission.
abstract: This paper proposes a feature-coupling-based non-orthogonal transceiver (FC-NON-TS) design method for multi-image semantic transmission. Especially, the semantic feature extractor, feature coupling and transmission selection module of the proposed FC-NON-TS are designed based on a lightweight network. The semantic feature extractor extracts the semantic feature information of each image, and adjusts the feature information according to the noise level. The feature coupling module combines the features of multiple images, reducing the amount of data for feature transmission. A transmission selection module further enhances the effectiveness of feature transmission by ignoring some of the invalid features. Unlike single-image or multi-view transmission, their main purpose is to extract useful information. We reduce the amount of transmitted data and improve transmission efficiency in three aspects: data characteristics, feature coupling, and transmission selection. The proposed FC-NON-TS can be flexibly adapted to different image transmission systems with varying loads. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets and real-device implementation on the Huawei Ascend Atlas 200I DK A2 platform verify that the proposed FC-NON-TS maintains stable reconstruction quality and efficient bandwidth utilization across diverse channel conditions, confirming its effectiveness and practicality for real-time multi-image transmission under constrained bandwidth resources.

title: A DRL-Based Method for Improving the Reliability of 5G-TSN Systems Employing HARQ Mechanism.
abstract: With the development of emerging mission-critical applications like industrial Internet of things (IIoT) and vehicleto-everything (V2X) communication, their requirement for deterministic communication continues to grow. The convergence of the fifth generation (5G) mobile communication and time-sensitive networking (TSN), introduced in 3GPP Release 16, is regarded as an effective approach for realizing end-to-end (E2E) deterministic communication. This paper investigates a practical wireless IIoT scenario employing a 5G-TSN integrated network with moving industrial devices. The entire transmission procedure using hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) mechanism is thoroughly analyzed and how to ensure deterministic delay is explained. Then, closed-form formulas of E2E latency and reliability are derived, and an optimization problem is formulated to maximize successful data delivery by jointly configuring output gate timing and retransmission counts. An artificial intelligence scheme based on proximal policy optimization (PPO) is designed to solve the problem and simulation results illustrate that our PPO-based method outperforms the other methods.

title: Task-Driven Semantic Networking Coding for Image Transmission in Low-Altitude Communication Network.
abstract: Semantic communication is considered as a promising solution for low-latency transmission in low-altitude communication networks. Nevertheless, existing methods for semantic image transmission all focus on the link level, while ignoring the image semantic fusion among multiple nodes at the network level, resulting in inefficient bandwidth utilization. This paper introduces an efficient Combined-and-Forward Relaying framework with Task-Driven Semantic Networking Coding (TD-SNC) for real-time object detection from multiple unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) views. By fusing semantic features into a single compact representation, TDSNC significantly enhances transmission efficiency while preserving essential task semantics. Driven by the goal of balancing detection accuracy and transmission efficiency, we implement a task-oriented optimization that combines object detection loss with L1-norm sparsity, allowing the model to discard irrelevant data effectively. A two-stage training strategy—initial pre-training for stable reconstruction followed by end-to-end fine-tuning—ensures reliable convergence in this complex system. Evaluations on the MDMT dataset show that TDSNC achieves superior transmission efficiency and noise resilience compared to existing benchmarks.

title: Low-complexity Frequency Domain Equalization for filtered-AFDM over General Physical Channels.
abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) has emerged as a promising waveform for high-mobility communications. However, its equalization remains a practical challenge under general physical channels with off-grid delay and Doppler effects. In this paper, we investigate frequency domain equalization for AFDM by considering a practical filtered-AFDM waveform. We analyze the input–output relations of filtered-AFDM across various domains and show that off-grid effects lead to severe inter-symbol interference in the DAFT domain, limiting the effectiveness of DAFT domain equalization. Motivated by the compactness of the frequency domain channel matrix in wideband systems, we propose a low-complexity two-stage frequency domain equalization scheme. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves performance close to full-block LMMSE equalization with significantly reduced computational complexity, and offers clear advantages over time domain equalization in wideband scenarios.

title: Radio-Frequency Sensor for Skin Moisture Monitoring.
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for the development of radio-frequency (RF) biosensors. The proposed sensor design is very sensitive to content of water in biological tissues that makes it very appropriate for measurement of moisture level of the human skin. An operation principle of the sensor is based on the dielectric spectroscopy technique and the effect of change of dielectric parameters of epidermis layer depending on the water content. In contrast to most of known RF biosensors, the human skin is considered as a part of sensor that provides a good interaction of electromagnetic field into the testing object and, as a result, very high accuracy and repeatability of the measured results. Operating on 24 GHz, it analyzes deep layers of epidermis that is important for beauty care industry: application of the sensor provides a feedback to user about skin condition and effectiveness of cosmetics products that can be used for continuous monitoring of user skin health. The paper demonstrates the experiment results for in-vivo measurements that are in good agreement with the simulation. The developed sensor is very compact (less than 5mm x 5mm) and can be integrated in wearable or standalone devices.

title: Trust Aware Federated Learning for Secure Bone Healing Stage Interpretation in e-Health.
abstract: This paper presents a trust aware federated learning (FL) framework for interpreting bone healing stages using spectral features derived from frequency response data. The primary objective is to address the challenge posed by either unreliable or adversarial participants in distributed medical sensing environments. The framework employs a multilayer perceptron model trained across simulated clients using the Flower FL framework. The proposed approach integrates an Adaptive Trust Score Scaling and Filtering (ATSSSF) mechanism with exponential moving average (EMA) smoothing to assess, validate and filter client contributions.Two trust score smoothing strategies have been investigated, one with a fixed factor and another that adapts according to trust score variability. Clients with low trust are excluded from aggregation and readmitted once their reliability improves, ensuring model integrity while maintaining inclusivity. Standard classification metrics have been used to compare the performance of ATSSSF with the baseline Federated Averaging strategy. Exper imental results demonstrate that adaptive trust management can improve both training stability and predictive performance by mitigating the negative effects of compromised clients while retaining robust detection capabilities. The work establishes the feasibility for adaptive trust mechanisms in federated medical sensing and identifies extension to clinical cross silo aggregation as a future research direction.

title: Agentic Trust Coordination for Federated Learning through Adaptive Thresholding and Autonomous Decision Making in Sustainable and Resilient Industrial Networks.
abstract: Distributed intelligence in industrial networks increasingly integrates sensing, communication, and computation across heterogeneous and resource constrained devices. Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training in such environments, but its reliability is affected by inconsistent client behaviour, noisy sensing conditions, and the presence of faulty or adversarial updates. Trust based mechanisms are commonly used to mitigate these effects, yet most remain statistical and heuristic, relying on fixed parameters or simple adaptive rules that struggle to accommodate changing operating conditions.This paper presents a lightweight agentic trust coordination approach for FL in sustainable and resilient industrial networks. The proposed Agentic Trust Control Layer operates as a server side control loop that observes trust related and system level signals, interprets their evolution over time, and applies targeted trust adjustments when instability is detected. The approach extends prior adaptive trust mechanisms by enabling context aware intervention decisions, rather than relying on fixed or purely reactive parameter updates. By explicitly separating observation, reasoning, and action, the proposed framework supports stable FL operation without modifying client side training or increasing communication overhead.

title: Physical Layer Integrity Test for Full Duplex Decode and Forward Relays at a NOMA Receiver.
abstract: Decode-and-forward (DF) relays in power-domain NOMA can silently rewrite forwarded payloads while matching power and timing, evading conventional energy and timing checks. We present a receiver-only, physical-layer integrity method to detect payload rewriting by a full duplex DF relay that runs online within NOMA reception and requires no cryptographic tags, side information, or helper nodes. The detector examines two consecutive slots in which the relay should forward the prior symbol and integrates cleanly with standard Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC). It adapts to four decoding outcomes: when any stream decodes, the receiver verifies by direct equality or correlation; when both fail, a covariance-based likelihood test detects the cross-slot signature of honest forwarding. We derive closed-form single-slot failure probabilities under residual cancellation leakage, show that the probability of the dual-failure event factorizes across slots, and provide exact finite-sample expressions for false alarm and miss together with Bayes-optimal and Neyman–Pearson thresholds. Decoding the stronger stream first consistently reduces risk, and a modest power tilt further suppresses errors. Residual leakage harms integrity by increasing time spent in the dual-failure regime. With practical leakage, total detection error falls below five percent once either hop is near 10dB and decreases rapidly with short averaging windows. Because the decision hinges on relative cross-slot correlation rather than absolute power, the approach is robust to CSI bias and slow drift, enabling practical, tag-free policing of untrusted relays in future NOMA systems.

title: Leveraging Multi-Agent System (MAS) and Fine-Tuned Small Language Models (SLMs) for Automated Telecom Network Troubleshooting.
abstract: Telecom networks are rapidly growing in scale and complexity, making effective management, operation, and optimization increasingly challenging. Although Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been applied to many telecom tasks, existing models are often narrow in scope, require large amounts of labeled data, and struggle to generalize across heterogeneous deployments. Consequently, network troubleshooting continues to rely heavily on Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to manually correlate various data sources to identify root causes and corrective actions. To address these limitations, we propose a Multi-Agent System (MAS) that employs an agentic workflow, with Large Language Models (LLMs) coordinating multiple specialized tools for fully automated network troubleshooting. Once faults are detected by AI/ML-based monitors, the framework dynamically activates agents such as an orchestrator, solution planner, executor, data retriever, and root-cause analyzer to diagnose issues and recommend remediation strategies within a short time frame. A key component of this system is the solution planner, which generates appropriate remediation plans based on internal documentation. To enable this, we fine-tuned a Small Language Model (SLM) on proprietary troubleshooting documents to produce domain-grounded solution plans. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly accelerates troubleshooting automation across both Radio Access Network (RAN) and Core network domains.

title: Deterministic Multicast Using Temporal Graph-based Routing and Scheduling in Non-terrestrial Networks.
abstract: The rapid advancement of non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) has greatly enhanced the service capabilities of traditional terrestrial Internet infrastructures, enabling potential "one-to-many" real-time interactive applications on a global scale. However, inherent network dynamics and resource constraints pose critical challenges for deterministic multicast (DM), including: i) high-complexity scheduling, where large-scale topologies and non-negligible propagation delays degrade time efficiency and scalability; and ii)low service performance, where frequent multicast routing failures and forwarding-cycle conflicts cause excessive delay, unpredictable jitter, and packet loss. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an efficient DM solution for NTNs based on temporal graphs. We rigorously formulate the DM problem as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model under key constraints such as forwarding timing, link capacity, and delay, thereby establishing a robust yet time-consuming performance upper bound. To improve time efficiency, we introduce a time-expanded graph (TEG) to accurately capture dynamic network topology and resource variations in a time-slotted manner, reformulating the original MILP into the identification of a time-featured (TF) tree. Through further TEG pruning and enhancement, we develop a low-complexity algorithm that jointly conducts multicast routing and scheduling within a reduced solution space, efficiently deriving the optimal TF tree. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly reduces run-time compared with the MILP-based solution, while achieving substantial improvements in traffic acceptance and resource utilization ratio over conventional satellite multicast schemes.

title: A Transformer Decoder with Tanner Graph-based Positional Encoding.
abstract: Error correction codes (ECCs) are essential for reliable communication over noisy channels. While Transformer-based decoders surpass traditional methods on short and medium-length codes, they insufficiently exploit the structural information of Tanner graphs. In this paper, we propose a novel Transformer decoder with Tanner Graph-Based Positional Encoding (TGPE) which introduces a dual-level positional encoding mechanism to effectively integrate graph topology into the attention process. The intra-type encoding utilizes a distance matrix to embed shortest-path relationships among nodes of the same type, thereby enhancing the modeling of intra-group dependencies. Meanwhile, the inter-type encoding extends the differential attention mechanism by combining mask-based edge connectivity—derived from the parity-check matrix—with a distance-modulated attention term that captures distance-aware dependencies between variable and check nodes while suppressing background attention noise. This dual encoding enables the decoder to capture both global and local, indirect and direct topological dependencies. Extensive experiments on standard ECC benchmarks demonstrate that TGPE consistently outperforms previous methods including BP, ECCT and CrossMPT. Moreover, interpretability analysis confirms that the learned distance encodings reflect theoretical coding principles, with smaller graph distances corresponding to stronger correlations, highlighting TGPE’s robustness and theoretical soundness.

title: Think Less, Label Better: Multi-Stage Domain-Grounded Synthetic Data Generation for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models in Telecommunications.
abstract: The success of large language models (LLMs) depends heavily on large-scale, high-quality instruction-following and reinforcement datasets. However, generating such data through human annotation is prohibitively time-consuming particularly for domain-specific tasks like telecom network troubleshooting, where accurate responses require deep technical expertise and contextual understanding. In this paper, we present a fully automated, retrieval-augmented pipeline for generating synthetic question-answer (QA) pairs grounded in structured domain knowledge. Our multi-stage framework integrates a retriever, base generator, and refinement model to synthesize and enhance QA pairs using documents retrieved from a domain-specific knowledge graph. To ensure data quality, we employ customized RAGAS-based scoring to filter low-quality samples, producing a high-quality dataset suitable for reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT). We demonstrate our approach in a real-world telecom scenario focused on radio access network (RAN) troubleshooting. The resulting pipeline generates complex, context-rich troubleshooting solution plans without human intervention. This work offers a scalable solution for building instruction and reinforcement datasets in specialized domains, significantly reducing dependence on manual labeling while maintaining high technical fidelity.

title: Machine Learning-based Dynamic Spectrum Sharing and Traffic Classification with dApp.
abstract: The growing demand for wireless communication in 5G and Next-Generation (Next-G) is placing significant strain on the commercial spectrum. Spectrum reserved for incumbent users, such as government and military, is often under-utilized and can be shared with commercial/civil users via spectrum sharing as extra spectrum resources. However, existing centralized spectrum sharing schemes suffer from high latency and significant administrative overhead. Within decentralized frameworks like O-RAN, the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) cannot directly observe User Plane parameters, such as I/Q samples. While dApps provide the capability to acquire I/Q samples, few studies have focused on intelligent spectrum sharing schemes that leverage dApps. To address this gap, this paper proposes a dApp-based scheme that extracts I/Q samples for machine learning-based signal classification, which in turn informs dynamic spectrum management policies. In the experiment, the proposed scheme achieves a 99.66% recall in incumbent protection, significantly outperforming the baseline (63.80%), thereby reducing interference risk to high-priority users.

title: Parameter-Adaptive Channel Prediction for 6G Upper Mid-Band Communications.
abstract: Upper mid-band (7.125–24.25 GHz) massive MIMO is recognized as a pivotal technology for future 6G communication systems, providing wide bandwidth while maintaining reliable coverage. To fully unlock the beamforming potential of massive MIMO antenna systems, acquiring accurate channel state information (CSI) at the base station (BS) is paramount. However, this task is challenging in the upper mid-band systems, where channels vary rapidly within the uplink sounding reference signal (SRS) interval, causing a significant mismatch between the estimated and actual CSI. To mitigate the performance degradation caused by such channel aging, accurate channel prediction is indispensable. In this paper, we propose parameter-adaptive channel prediction (PACP), which decomposes the uplink SRS into multipath geometric channel parameters (GCPs), such as angle, delay, and path gain, and predicts each parameter according to its own temporal dynamics. Using the predicted multipath GCPs, BS proactively generates a proactive beamforming matrix for downlink data transmission. Numerical results demonstrate that PACP provides an 8 dB channel normalized mean square error (NMSE) gain over the conventional schemes and nearly matches the data rate of perfect CSI.

title: Multi-Agent Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Remote IoT in the Space-Edge Cloud.
abstract: Traditional terrestrial computing facilities, i.e., Edge Computing (EC) and Cloud Computing (CC), have limited applicability for remote Internet of Things (IoT) applications due to connectivity challenges. These challenges can be addressed through a Space-Edge Cloud continuum that leverages computing facilities enabled by Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites and terrestrial cloud facilities. We aim to minimize the joint latency and energy cost for processing remote IoT data in this continuum by formulating a complex optimization problem. Specifically, our goal is to optimize the complete offloading process by jointly selecting optimal routes, computation nodes, and buffering policies. We develop a Multi-Agent Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (MA-HRL) solution to solve this problem. The proposed solution is developed in a Python environment and compared with several benchmark methods, demonstrating significant performance gains in terms of reduced latency and energy demands.

title: KEF-Transformer: A Kalman EMA Fusion Transformer for Robust Automatic Modulation Classification.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel transformer-based architecture called Kalman exponential moving average fusion transformer (KEF-Transformer) with Kalman augmented weighted multi-head self-attention (KA-WMHSA), which incorporates temporal variation into the attention mechanism. We introduce an additional attention mechanism based on a steady-state Kalman exponential moving average (EMA) filter which computes the high-frequency components of the query, key, and value vectors by subtracting the low-pass filtered version of each vector. In addition, we apply attention with linear biases (ALiBi), a parameter-free relative positional encoding technique, to enhance generalization across varying sequence lengths and unseen signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Our experiments show that the proposed model outperforms recent baselines by improving the minimum accuracy across modulation types, achieving robust classification for challenging types to distinguish.

title: Wireless Memory Approximation for Energy-efficient Task-specific IoT Data Retrieval.
abstract: The use of Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) for storing Machine Learning (ML) models plays a critical role in accelerating ML inference tasks in the next generation of communication systems. However, periodic refreshment of DRAM results in wasteful energy consumption during standby periods, which is significant for resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices. To solve this problem, this work advocates two novel approaches: 1) wireless memory activation and 2) wireless memory approximation. These enable the wireless devices to efficiently manage the available memory by considering the timing aspects and relevance of ML model usage; hence, reducing the overall energy consumption. Numerical results show that our proposed scheme can realize smaller energy consumption than the always-on approach while satisfying the retrieval accuracy constraint.

title: KAN-Pointformer: Hierarchical Learning for Covert ISAC in Pixel Reconfigurable Fluid Antenna Systems.
abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) based on pixel reconfigurable antennas (PRA) provide enhanced spatial degrees of freedom (DoF) to improve physical layer security in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. However, the inherent coupling between discrete port selection and continuous beamforming under stringent sensing and covertness constraints leads to a challenging mixed-integer non-convex optimization problem. To address this, we propose a hierarchical learning framework that decouples the optimization variables via a constraint-aware collaborative mechanism. Specifically, a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) serves as the inner beamformer to accurately approximate the non-linear mapping from irregular array manifolds to optimal weights, replacing traditional Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP). Guided by KAN-evaluated rewards, a Pointformer-based reinforcement learning policy is developed to efficiently optimize the large-scale combinatorial port selection by capturing global spatial correlations. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms fixed-position antenna (FPA) and achieves near-optimal covert rates. Moreover, numerical results confirm that the Pointformer policy achieves an order-of-magnitude reduction in training overhead compared to the Pointer Network baseline, demonstrating its superior scalability for practical deployment.

title: LLM-SuSA: A Semantic-Enhanced Framework for Scenario-Adaptive Spectrum Utility Situational Awareness in Dynamic Satellite Constellations.
abstract: The proliferation of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations demands effective Spectrum Utility Situational Awareness (SuSA). However, traditional Artificial Intelligence models exhibit poor performance when applied to new scenarios, as they fail to capture the relationships between non-quantifiable data. To address this limitation, we propose a novel semantic-enhanced framework, dubbed LLM-SuSA, which uses a Large Language Model (LLM) fine-tuned with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) as a domain-specific semantic encoder. This LLM converts heterogeneous textual inputs into rich semantic vectors. Then the vectors were concatenated with numerical data and processed by an enhanced Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) pipeline to predict key performance indicators (KPIs). Experiments show that our model significantly outperforms both numerical-only baselines and semantic baselines without domain-specific fine-tuning. Our work validates that a domain-adapted LLM encoder effectively enhances the accuracy and generalization of SuSA models for dynamic satellite environments.

title: Unified Far-Field and Near-Field Cascaded Channel Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Systems.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) can significantly enhance wireless coverage, yet their gains rely on accurate cascaded channel state information (CSI). In large-aperture systems, a non-negligible portion of users operate in the radiative near field, where spherical wavefronts invalidate conventional far-field, angle-domain estimation. This paper develops a unified cascaded channel model in the wavenumber domain (WD) using electromagnetic information theory and the Weyl expansion. The model characterizes the physically admissible WD support and reveals a sparse structure applicable to both far-field and near-field users. Based on this representation, cascaded channel estimation is cast as a compressed-sensing problem and solved by two algorithms: wavenumber domain-least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (WD-LASSO) and a greedy wavenumber domain-orthogonal matching pursuit (WD-OMP). Numerical results demonstrate improved normalized mean square error (NMSE) and robustness, with WD-OMP achieving the best performance under short pilots.

title: Distributed Multi-UAV Collaborative Computing in Dynamic MEC Networks.
abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled mobile edge computing (MEC) provides rapid and flexible on-demand computing services for mobile terminals (MTs) in industrial settings and mission-critical operations. This paper studies a distributed multi-UAV MEC system with dynamic UAV participation, where UAVs may join or leave over time and can cooperatively migrate workloads to mitigate load imbalance. We model the coupled interactions between UAV pricing and MT offloading as a Stackelberg game. In the leader level, UAVs optimize their mobility and cooperative computing decisions together with service pricing to maximize their benefits. In the follower level, MTs choose offloading ratios and computing resource requests to minimize the overhead combining task completion time and payment. We develop a hierarchical distributed solution in which UAV policies are learned via a multi-agent proximal policy optimization, and MT responses are computed using a two-stage iteration with closed-form updates. Simulation results demonstrate stable convergence under time-varying UAV participation and show consistent gains over benchmarks, including about 33.77% lower average MT overhead than full offloading and up to 22.50% higher average UAV benefit than the non-collaborative baseline.

title: Sparse Precoder Design for Massive MIMO LEO Satellite Communications.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate precoder design for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite communication (SATCOM). We first establish a beam based channel model that characterizes the spatial single path property of the LEO SATCOM channel, and reveal its sparsity in the beam domain. Based on this channel model, we prove that the design of the space domain precoder can be simplified into that of a lower-dimensional beam domain precoder. More importantly, we introduce a sparsity constraint on the beam domain precoder and propose a novel sparse precoder, achieving a flexible trade-off between transmission performance and computational complexity. Simulation results demonstrate the satisfactory performance of the proposed sparse precoder with low complexity.

title: Agentic AI for Intent-driven Optimization in Cell-free O-RAN.
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a key enabler for autonomous radio access networks (RANs), where multiple large language model (LLM)-based agents reason and collaborate to achieve operator-defined intents. The open RAN (O-RAN) architecture enables the deployment and coordination of such agents. However, most existing works consider simple intents handled by independent agents, while complex intents that require coordination among agents remain unexplored. In this paper, we propose an agentic AI framework for intent translation and optimization in cell-free O-RAN. A supervisor agent translates the operator intents into an optimization objective and minimum rate requirements. Based on this information, a user weighting agent retrieves relevant prior experience from a memory module to determine the user priority weights for precoding. If the intent includes an energy-saving objective, then an open radio unit (O-RU) management agent will also be activated to determine the set of active O-RUs by using a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm. A monitoring agent measures and monitors the user data rates and coordinates with other agents to guarantee the minimum rate requirements are satisfied. To enhance scalability, we adopt a parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) method that enables the same underlying LLM to be used for different agents. Simulation results show that the proposed agentic AI framework reduces the number of active O-RUs by 41.93% when compared with three baseline schemes in energy-saving mode. Using the PEFT method, the proposed framework reduces the memory usage by 92% when compared with deploying separate LLM agents.

title: Multi-band Carrier Phase Positioning toward 6G: Performance Bounds and Design Insights.
abstract: Carrier phase positioning (CPP) is widely used in satellite system applications, enabling centimeter-level localization accuracy.
