Recently, CPP is gaining attraction also in terrestrial mobile networks, particularly in 5G New Radio (NR) evolution toward 6G. One key challenge is to resolve the so-called integer ambiguity problem, as carrier phase provides only relative position information. This work introduces and studies a multi-band CPP scenario with intra- and inter-band carrier aggregation (CA) opportunities across FR1, mmWave-FR2, and emerging 6G FR3 bands. Specifically, we derive multi-band CPP performance bounds, showcasing the superiority of multi-band CPP for high-precision localization in current and future mobile networks. A wide collection of numerical results is provided, covering the impacts of the available carrier bandwidth, number of aggregated carriers, transmit power, and the number of network nodes. The offered results highlight that only two carriers need to be aggregated to substantially facilitate resolving the integer ambiguity problem.

title: Edge Resilient Agent (ERA) : An Edge AI-Driven Framework for B5G and Wi-Fi 6 Heterogeneous MEC Networks.
abstract: The rapid growth of digitization and Internet of Things (IoT) applications exposes the limitations of cloud-centric architectures in meeting stringent latency reliability, and compliance requirements. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the Edge Resilience Agent (ERA), a containerized framework that leverages Sensing, Learning, and Adaptivity (SLA)-driven for resilient edge services. A multi-dimensional serviceability model is introduced to unify reliability, availability, and performability for quantitative resilience evaluation. Proof-of-concept experiments validate ERA across communication and computation: millisecond-scale seamless handover via Socat, sustained Quality of Service (QoS) through slicing and dynamic bandwidth control, and AI-driven auto-scaling that reduces failures from 789 to 46 while lowering response time to 0.91 s. Results show that ERA achieves a Serviceability score of 90%, significantly outperforming native Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA) at 60%. These findings highlight ERA’s practicality for enabling highly reliable and low-latency services in heterogeneous Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) environments.

title: Task-Oriented Multi-Tier Computing in NOMA-Enabled Cell-Free Networks: A Conditional Hybrid Action Masked DRL Approach.
abstract: Cell-free networks have emerged as a promising paradigm for 6G communication, offering enhanced user-centric service quality by eliminating the limitations of cell boundaries. In this paper, we consider a multi-tier computing framework for NOMA-enabled cell-free networks, integrating hierarchical task offloading across local, edge, and cloud layers. By leveraging NOMA, this framework facilitates efficient user multiplexing, mitigates inter-user interference, and improves spectrum utilization. We then formulate a task-oriented optimization problem under delay constraints, jointly optimizing multiple communication-related decisions. However, resource management in these systems remains challenging, since offloading, link scheduling, and power allocation are conditionally coupled and cannot be optimized independently. To tackle the difficulty of dependency-aware communication decisions in hybrid conditions, we introduce an innovative Conditional Hybrid Action Masked-PPO (CHAM-PPO) algorithm. CHAM-PPO incorporates several coordinated mechanisms to ensure effective coordination between discrete and continuous actions, addressing training instability caused by inconsistent update rates. Simulation results demonstrate that CHAM-PPO achieves more stable convergence and exhibits strong robustness under high task loads and severe interference, consistently outperforming existing hybrid action learning methods.

title: PHANTOM: PHysical ANamorphic Threats Obstructing Connected Vehicle Mobility.
abstract: Connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) rely on vision-based deep neural networks (DNNs) and low-latency (Vehicle-to-Everything) V2X communication to navigate safely and efficiently. Despite their advances, these systems remain vulnerable to physical adversarial attacks. In this paper, we introduce PHANTOM (PHysical ANamorphic Threats Obstructing connected vehicle Mobility), a novel framework for crafting and deploying perspective-dependent adversarial examples using anamorphic art. PHANTOM exploits geometric distortions that appear natural to humans but are misclassified with high confidence by state-of-the-art object detectors. Unlike conventional attacks, PHANTOM operates in black-box settings without model access and demonstrates strong transferability across four diverse detector architectures (YOLOv5, SSD, Faster R-CNN, and RetinaNet). Comprehensive evaluation in CARLA across varying speeds, weather conditions, and lighting scenarios shows that PHANTOM achieves over 90% attack success rate under optimal conditions and maintains 60-80% effectiveness even in degraded environments. The attack activates within 6-10 meters of the target, providing insufficient time for safe maneuvering. Beyond individual vehicle deception, PHANTOM triggers network-wide disruption in CAV systems: SUMO-OMNeT++ co-simulation demonstrates that false emergency messages propagate through V2X links, increasing Peak Age of Information by 68-89% and degrading safety-critical communication. These findings expose critical vulnerabilities in both perception and communication layers of CAV ecosystems.

title: Towards Scalable, Low-Latency Volumetric Streaming: A Hybrid Predictive Synchronization Framework.
abstract: Volumetric video is emerging as a cornerstone for multi-user Extended Reality (XR) and metaverse applications. However, achieving synchronous playback across distributed clients remains challenging under heterogeneous network conditions (such as varying latency, jitter, packet loss, and asymmetric bandwidth). Existing synchronization approaches, such as state synchronization and fixed-frame buffering, struggle with scalability and often trade off latency for playback continuity. We present a predictive synchronization framework that combines lightweight time-series latency forecasting with adaptive buffering control. Our framework incorporates a hybrid predictor that adaptively selects the most suitable model (including EWMA, ARIMA, LSTM) for each client, escalating to heavier predictors only when residual errors exceed thresholds. This design balances accuracy with computational overhead, enabling lower latencies at larger scales. Our experimental results show that predictive synchronization reduces average inter-client skew by up to 76% compared to baselines, while also decreasing the average buffer size by 40% in a controlled multi-client testbed. The average per-frame latency remains below 20 ms and the 95th-percentile latency below 70 ms for up to 100 concurrent clients. These results demonstrate that prediction-aware, hybrid synchronization substantially improves quality of service while maintaining lightweight per-client overhead.

title: Multi-Modal Quantum Reinforcement Learning for Entanglement Routing in Quantum Satellite Networks.
abstract: Efficient entanglement routing in quantum satellite networks directly affects quantum communication reliability, which is reflected by entanglement fidelity. However, due to dynamic topologies of the satellites and limited quantum resources, the entanglement routing optimization problem remains an open challenge. Classical routing methods are inefficient to solve the problem due to their limited serial processing capability in handling such high computational complexity. To address this problem, this paper proposes a multi-modal quantum deep reinforcement learning (QDRL) model, capable of processing time-varying and complex features. Here, the multi-modal refers to leveraging heterogeneous data from multiple environmental features, rather than relying on homogeneous data, to improve performance. QDRL is then used to optimize the entanglement routing to achieve maximum entanglement fidelity. To evaluate performance, extensive simulations are conducted to compare the proposed multi-modal QDRL framework with a multi-modal classical DRL (CDRL) approach and a homogeneous QDRL scheme that relies on homogeneous data. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed multi-modal QDRL framework achieves significantly faster convergence, outperforming the CDRL scheme by 99.71% and the homogeneous QDRL scheme by 5.06%. Furthermore, the proposed multi-modal QDRL framework achieved higher entanglement fidelity as compared to the CDRL and homogeneous QDRL schemes by 6.73% and 2.40%, respectively.

title: Enhancing IoT Connectivity in NTN: A Machine Learning Approach for Packet Detection in Grant-Free Access.
abstract: Non-terrestrial networks (NTN) are key to the 6G-Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem, providing broader coverage and reliable connectivity. As IoT adoption grows, the demand for scalable communication solutions increases. IoT communications, relying on grant-free random access protocols, face challenges in packet detection due to uncoordinated transmissions. Traditional detection methods struggle in NTN environments, especially due to interference and Doppler shifts. This paper proposes a convolutional neural network for efficient packet detection in IoT-NTN scenarios. The method outperforms a traditional correlator-based approach, showing superior detection performance under harsh conditions. Our results highlight the potential of machine learning for enhancing IoT connectivity over NTN.

title: Profit Maximization for Service Placement in Multi-Access Edge Computing Considering Locational Marginal Prices of Electricity.
abstract: Multi-access edge computing (MEC) is a promising paradigm for next-generation wireless networks, including emerging 6G networks. It is designed to support services such as virtual and augmented reality, which require low latency, high bandwidth, and fast computation. In MEC, service placement refers to the process of deploying service instances close to the users to meet their demands. Although MEC has been studied extensively from a technical perspective, models that evaluate the economic sustainability of MEC deployments are largely underexplored. Economic sustainability involves the profitability of such deployments, requiring the balancing of operational costs of infrastructure, including electricity expenses, with revenue generation. In this work, we propose a techno-economic model of the service placement problem. The model accounts for region-dependent electricity costs, which can fluctuate significantly over time and location due to factors such as variations in renewable energy generation. Furthermore, the interactions between service providers (SPs) and infrastructure providers (IPs) and their individual costs and revenues are modeled. For the users, we consider service demands such as latency and quality of service (QoS). To solve the formulated service placement problem, we provide an optimization-based algorithm, which is evaluated using real-world data sets from 22 SPs and 5 IPs. Our results show that our proposed approach yields up to 5% more total profit by optimizing the service placement to lower the cost for procuring electricity by 10%, while maintaining the provided QoS in comparison to the state-of-the-art benchmark algorithms.

title: LLM Based Policy Generation for IoMT Device Access Control: A Context-Aware Approach.
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices in healthcare environments has introduced significant security challenges, particularly in managing dynamic access control policies across heterogeneous IoMT devices. Traditional access control mechanisms struggle to adapt to the complex, context-dependent nature of clinical workflows where access requirements vary based on patient conditions, emergency situations, and clinical roles. This paper presents a novel approach leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to automatically generate and verify context-aware access control policies for IoMT devices using natural language descriptions of clinical scenarios and device metadata. We fine-tuned Mistral 7B on a carefully constructed dataset of IoMT device access patterns, clinical contexts, and Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) compliant device metadata for accurate policy generation. Our evaluation in simulated hospital environments shows that LLM-generated policies achieve high accuracy in matching expert-defined policies while significantly reducing policy configuration time. We further analyze the safety applications of automated policy generation, identifying cases where human oversight remains critical, and propose a hybrid human-in-the-loop validation framework for deployment in production clinical environments.

title: Provisioning 6G Services in Edge-Core Continuum.
abstract: Enhanced mobile broadband with reliable and massive machine type with ultra-reliable, low-latency communication are new 6G services to be provisioned with 5G-legacy services. Even though the network slicing technology can provision logical virtualized networks with distinct quality of service (QoS) demands, we need enhanced orchestration strategy to meet the more complex resource and performance requirements posed by these new class of 6G-services. Accordingly, we have developed iACRA6, an intelligent admission control and resource allocation solution to provision 6G network slices in the edge-core continuum. The iACRA6 is based on deep reinforcement learning and considers the QoS requirements of 6G use-cases, differentiates the network core from edge nodes, and processes slice requests in a prioritized manner to favor the service provider's profit and resource utilization. Results show that iACRA6 provides an improved acceptance ratio, profit, and resource utilization for 6G heterogeneous services as compared to the existing schemes.

title: Agentic AI for Ultra-Modern Networks: Multi-Agent Framework for RAN Autonomy and Assurance.
abstract: The increasing complexity of Beyond 5G and 6G networks necessitates new paradigms for autonomy and assur- ance. Traditional O-RAN control loops rely heavily on RIC- based orchestration, which centralizes intelligence and exposes the system to risks such as policy conflicts, data drift, and unsafe actions under unforeseen conditions. In this work, we argue that the future of autonomous networks lies in a multi-agentic architecture, where specialized agents collaborate to perform data collection, model training, prediction, policy generation, verification, deployment, and assurance. By replacing tightly- coupled centralized RIC-based workflows with distributed agents, the framework achieves autonomy, resilience, explainability, and system-wide safety. To substantiate this vision, we design and evaluate a traffic steering use case under surge and drift conditions. Results across four KPIs: RRC connected users, IP throughput, PRB utilization, and SINR, demonstrate that a naive predictor-driven deployment improves local KPIs but destabilizes neighbors, whereas the agentic system blocks unsafe policies, preserving global network health. This study highlights multi- agent architectures as a credible foundation for trustworthy AI- driven autonomy in next-generation RANs.

title: Intent-Aware Federated GNN-MAPPO for URLLC V2X Resource Allocation.
abstract: This paper proposes G-FEDMAP, a graph-based federated multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) framework designed for semantic- and intent-aware resource allocation in 6G-enabled vehicular networks. Unlike conventional centralized or single-domain learning models, G-FEDMAP integrates a GraphSAGE-based encoder with multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) under a centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) paradigm, enabling vehicles to make distributed yet coordinated spectrum and power allocation decisions. A federated coordination layer is introduced to aggregate model updates across multiple vehicular domains without raw data exchange, enhancing scalability and privacy. Furthermore, an intent-aware reward design dynamically adjusts learning priorities to ensure ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) and semantic message retention. Simulation results in urban vehicle-to-everything (V2X) scenarios demonstrate that G-FEDMAP significantly improves vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) delivery success, intent satisfaction, and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) throughput compared to baseline methods such as MAPPO, GNN-MAPPO, and federated PPO. These findings establish G-FEDMAP as a robust and adaptive solution for trustworthy 6G vehicular communication systems.

title: AI-Augmented Multi-Factor Subnet Selection for Dynamic Network Slice Creation in 3GPP Networks.
abstract: Network slicing in 5G/6G demands dynamic selection and composition of RAN, Core, and Transport subnet instances. Current orchestration mechanisms rely on MDAS (Management Data Analytics Service) outputs. However, MDAS primarily reports performance- and fault-centric KPIs, which are insufficient for advanced orchestration decisions. We introduce a novel interface between MDAS and the Orchestrator, incorporating proactive, geo-resilience, energy, and security-aware metrics to enable explainable and sustainable subnet selections. A multi-factor scoring system enables explainable, risk- and sustainability-conscious subnet selections. Evaluations show significant improvements in SLA adherence, geo-resilience, and resource utilization. Our framework provides a standards-compatible path to next-gen, proactive network slicing.

title: Performance Analysis of Movable Antenna Arrays.
abstract: This paper provides a thorough mathematical analysis of continuous movable antenna (MA) arrays. Focusing on the multiple antenna case, we consider a linear antenna array with multiple fixed antenna elements that moves along a line. We assume a full, spatially coherent correlation model and continuous positioning of the array. We provide asymptotically exact approximations to the upper tail of the cumulative distribution function (cdf) of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), considering both correlated and uncorrelated antenna elements in the array. We also obtain a novel closed-form expression for the level crossing rate (LCR) of the SNR under correlated array elements, where a non-separable two-dimensional correlation is present. The analysis is validated through simulations, confirming both the accuracy of the LCR expressions and the tightness of the cdf bounds in the upper tail. Numerical results show that the proposed MA array outperforms single fluid antenna and fixed-array systems, with reduced inter-element spacing providing further performance gains.

title: DOA Estimation for Tri-Polarized Continuous Aperture Array.
abstract: This paper addresses direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation using tri-polarized continuous aperture arrays (CA-PAs). By leveraging electromagnetic (EM) information theory, the spatially continuous signals received by the tri-polarized CAPA are modeled to enable accurate DOA estimation. To facilitate subspace decomposition for continuous operators, a continuous-discrete transformation technique is developed. Furthermore, both self- and cross-covariances of the tri-polarized signals are exploited to construct a tri-polarized spectrum, thereby significantly improving DOA estimation performance. In particular, the computationally intensive integral operations involved in the spectrum formulation are efficiently approximated using Gauss-Legendre quadrature, which substantially reduces the computational burden. Numerical results validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework.

title: Entanglement Generation via Spatial Path Superposition.
abstract: Entanglement generation and distribution is a core functionality of quantum networks. Traditional approaches to this functionality rely on chains of quantum repeaters or on manipulation of multipartite states. In this work, we explore an alternative paradigm that explores quantum coherence at propagation level, by enabling genuine quantum instantiations of communication channels, existing in superposed configurations. We demonstrate that this mechanism can be harnessed to generate both bipartite and multipartite entangled states from separable inputs. Specifically, we show that Bell states can be obtained from initially separable two-qubit states, through the superposition of two unitary quantum channels. The proposed approach is further extended to multipartite systems, by generating n-qubit GHZ and W states and thereby revealing the constructive role of superposed quantum operations in entanglement creation. Moreover, we analyze the robustness of the proposed scheme against noise, showing that the resulting states retain high fidelity and concurrence even under realistic imperfections. Our results suggest that, under appropriate quantum control, noisy superposed paths can be effectively harnessed to engineer entanglement generation and distribution in quantum networks.

title: Integrating Bandit Learning into xApps for BLER-Driven Link Adaptation.
abstract: Open Radio Access Networks expose standardized interfaces that enable external applications (xApps) to influence radio scheduling decisions. One of the most critical decisions is modulation and coding scheme (MCS) selection, which directly governs spectral efficiency and error performance. Conventional schedulers in systems such as OpenAirInterface (OAI) use fixed threshold rules based on block error rate (BLER), adapting MCS by only 1 step. While simple, this method reacts slowly to dynamic environments and lacks coordination with slower supervisory policies. This paper presents a BLER-driven control architecture that augments the OAI gNB with a narrow policy hook and an external xApp. The gNB executes per-transmission time interval scheduling using a logarithmic BLER-tracking controller whose aggressiveness is governed by a tunable gain parameter. A reinforcement learning xApp based on Thompson Sampling learns this gain online from aggregated throughput and BLER statistics, while a baseline xApp cycles through fixed gain values for comparison. We implement the framework using OAI with USRP B205mini-i radios and evaluate it in a wireless laboratory environment with two user equipment and controlled interference. Results show that the approach is feasible on commodity hardware and enables more flexible MCS adaptation than fixed threshold rules, demonstrating the potential of lightweight ML-driven xApps for real-time RAN control.

title: Performance of NIST Post-quantum Cryptography Additional Digital Signature Algorithms.
abstract: NIST post-quantum cryptography (PQC) project selected three digital signature algorithms (Dilithium, Falcon, and SPHINCS+) to standardize as PQC digital signature standards. In addition to the PQC digital signature standards, for diversity and to address the concerns on the overheads including key/signature sizes and computational performances, NIST is considering 14 additional digital signature algorithms for further standardization. One or more algorithms from these 14 algorithms can be selected for further standardization. However due to the dynamic nature of the NIST standardization process and cryptanalysis, all these candidate algorithms go through continuous changes and updates. The latest updates in Oct 2025 outdated the previous performance analyses of these algorithms. In this paper, we study the computational performance overheads of the NIST PQC additional signature candidates (round 2 - latest submission packages) in terms of key generation time, signing time, and verification time. Our results show that additional signature candidate algorithms including Hawk, CROSS, and SNOVA are competitive and computationally outperform the PQC standards on several occasions.

title: Threshold-based Wavelet Decomposition for 3D Point Clouds in Digital Environments.
abstract: This paper proposes a compressed sensing method based on threshold-driven multi-level wavelet decomposition to reduce storing and processing of 3-dimensional point cloud data. The approach is evaluated on 3D point clouds of rural and urban terrains and compared to an approach based on the discrete cosine transform. Our results show that mountainous landscapes can be effectively reconstructed from a compressed set of wavelet coefficients, achieving a lower mean absolute error and higher visual fidelity than DCT-based reconstructions while more work needs to be done for urban environment to achieve similar accuracy. The proposed method can be applied to larger, high-resolution point clouds and other higher dimensional datasets, such as hyperspectral images, for digital environments.

title: AI-enabled Adaptive PHY-Layer Authentication for Integrated TN-NTN IoT-5G Healthcare.
abstract: The combined terrestrial network (TN) and Non-terrestrial Networks (NTN) with satellite and UAV-driven Communication is the crtical and major role player for the pervasive and reliable connectivity. Fifth Generation (5G) empowers and revolutionizes the IoT by enhancing and extending the connectivity between portable devices for supporting various applications for instance, healthcare, smart cities, and hospital management. Due to diverse and profound impact of the IoT there are various potential benefits in parallel with the insightful challenges. The heterogenous platform, diverse connectivity, and dynamic features of IoT-5G there are more risks and security vulnerabilities by intruders and attackers. In addition, security particularly authentication is the paramount for implementation, management, and monitoring of the IoT and 5G platforms. A joint adaptive, continuous and reliable (ACR) mechanism for IoT-5G authentication is in demand to be developed. Due to heterogenous technological trends, and lack of uniform interoperable standard and solution, and restricted computing and networking capacity of IoT devices there is need of lightweight and adaptive, continuous, reliable and authenticated data exchange solution. Up to now there are less efforts from research community dedicated to developing an adaptive solution with lower-latency fast and continuous authentication, and high reliability to IoT-5G by adopting the PHY-layer parameters. Our proposed ACR authentication mechanism follows the multi-authentication behavior with soft notion of trust instead of hard flag of binary sequences. Moreover, we aim to detect the intruders with suspicious behavior at PHY-layer, because it is difficult to prevent the access of such illegitimate entities to higher layers.

title: LIME: Lightweight Multi-head Early-exit Transformer for Network Intrusion Detection.
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) is a critical component of modern network security, yet its effectiveness is hindered by several factors, such as class imbalance, feature heterogeneity, and the need for low-latency operations. In this direction, transformer-based architectures have gained significant attention over the past couple of years, such as Vision Transformer, TabTransformer, etc. These models employ multi-head self-attention to capture long-range feature dependencies and contextual relations in sequential network data. However, the majority of these designs remain computationally expensive and unsuitable for resource-constrained and real-time settings. Thus, to address these gaps, this paper presents LIME, a Lightweight Multi-Head Early-Exit Transformer for flow-based intrusion detection. LIME integrates efficient feature encoding along with lightweight self-attention and adaptive Early-Exit (EE) inference to advance the practicality of transformer-based IDS for modern-day networks. The proposed model introduces a Record Projection Encoding (RPE) layer to unify heterogeneous numerical and categorical features into a compact latent space, reducing sparsity and enhancing representation of minority attack classes. Further, a shallow three-block transformer is also employed, with block-wise classification heads that provide intermediate supervision and enable a mechanism, allowing inference to halt once prediction confidence surpasses a given threshold. In addition to this, we also mitigate class imbalanceaware optimization strategies, including label smoothing and class-weighted training. Extensive experiments on the NSL-KDD and CICIDS-2017 datasets demonstrate that the LIME achieves up to 99.9% F1-score while considerably reducing inference latency and computational complexity compared to the baseline.

title: Zero-Shot Pruning Using Weight Compensation for Energy Efficient Inference in Responsible Artificial Intelligence.
abstract: Zero-Shot Redistributive Pruning (ZSRP) introduces an innovative algorithm for neural networks that optimizes inference models by removing the traditional post-pruning fine-tuning phase. Fine-tuning after model pruning typically increases training time, leading to higher computational necessity and energy consumption. ZSRP addresses this issue by compensating for removed weights during pruning. The removed weights are redistributed proportionally among the remaining weights. The experimental results show that our algorithm outperforms the baseline in terms of energy consumption while achieving slightly better accuracy and comparable inference latency, providing an efficient approach to deploying responsible artificial intelligence in cellular networks.

title: IntAgent: NWDAF-Based Intent LLM Agent Towards Advanced Next Generation Networks.
abstract: Intent-based networks (IBNs) are gaining prominence as an innovative technology that automates network operations through high-level request statements, defining what the network should achieve. In this work, we introduce IntAgent, an intelligent intent LLM agent that integrates NWDAF analytics and tools to fulfill the network operator's intents. Unlike previous approaches, we develop an intent tools engine directly within the NWDAF analytics engine, allowing our agent to utilize live network analytics to inform its reasoning and tool selection. We offer an enriched, 3GPP-compliant data source that enhances the dynamic, context-aware fulfillment of network operator goals, along with an MCP tools server for scheduling, monitoring, and analytics tools. We demonstrate the efficacy of our framework through two practical use cases: ML-based traffic prediction and scheduled policy enforcement, which validate IntAgent's ability to autonomously fulfill complex network intents.

title: Scenario-Oriented Multi-Task And Multi-Objective Optimization for Resource Allocation in 5G/6G.
abstract: In 5G/6G networks, the expanding service diversity, stringent quality-of-service (QoS) demands, and rapid user growth call for advanced radio resource allocation (RA) schemes. Conventional RA solutions, which rely on task-independent methodologies, often fail to achieve system-level optimization across multiple objectives, such as system throughput, spectral efficiency, and delay. In this paper, we propose a joint-optimization agent for RA, abbreviated as RA-JOA, that fuses multiple correlated tasks into a single reinforcement-learning (RL) network to harvest joint gains across multiple performance objectives. Initially, we introduce an asynchronous RL network to accommodate varying policy update periods and a preference pruning scheme to optimize multitask losses during updates. Additionally, we design a practical scenario-oriented framework, which trains dedicated RL models per scenario group, grouping by key features, to reduce complexity and leverages transfer learning to boost online performance. System-level simulations on a full-stack platform show that RA-JOA achieves up to a 6.15% increase in system throughput, an 11.37% improvement in user spectral efficiency, and a 17.94% reduction in packet delay, along with a 40% faster convergence rate.

title: Movable Antenna-Assisted UAV-to-UAV Communication: Joint Beamforming and Antenna Position Optimization.
abstract: This paper investigates a movable antenna (MA)-assisted uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm communication system. Each UAV is equipped with an MA array deployed on two hemispherical surfaces at the head and tail, significantly expanding the spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs). A far-field line-of-sight (LoS) channel model is adopted to characterize the UAV-to-UAV (U2U) communication links. We formulate a sum rate maximization problem by jointly optimizing the antenna position vectors (APVs) and transmit/receive beamforming vectors, subject to constraints on maximum transmit power, limited antenna moving region, and minimum inter-antenna spacing. To tackle this non-convex and highly coupled problem, we propose a two-loop iterative optimization algorithm that effectively combines the Spider Wasp Optimizer (SWO) for APV optimization and alternative optimization (AO) for beamforming design. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MA-assisted scheme outperforms traditional fixed position antenna (FPA) systems and other benchmark algorithms under different settings.

title: Energy Efficiency Optimization of STAR-RIS Assisted MIMO-NOMA Networks.
abstract: Simultaneous transmission and reflection reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) extends coverage beyond conventional RIS by enabling full-space signal manipulation. This paper investigates a STAR-RIS assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) network. We aim to maximize the energy efficiency (EE) of this system, which is modeled to include the direct link between the base station (BS) and the reflection-user (R-user), which mostly exists in practice. We jointly optimize the active and passive beamforming, respectively at the BS and STAR-RIS, by decomposing the original non-convex problem into two tractable subproblems, which are then efficiently solved via an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm. The non-convexity is addressed by integrating the Dinkelbach method, quadratic fractional programming (QFP), semidefinite relaxation (SDR), and successive convex approximation (SCA) to convert each subproblem into a convex form. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme can substantially improve overall EE over existing STAR-RIS assisted MIMO-NOMA networks.

title: Receiver-Agnostic Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification via Supervised Contrastive Learning and Parametric Wasserstein Barycenters.
abstract: Radio frequency fingerprint (RFF) has emerged as a promising approach for physical-layer authentication. While recent advances in machine learning have enabled high-accuracy RFF identification in controlled environments, performance substantially degrades in cross-receiver scenarios. To address this limitation, we propose a domain generalization framework that integrates supervised contrastive learning (SCL) with Wasserstein distance for robust RFF identification across heterogeneous receivers. Specifically, SCL fosters discriminative feature learning and promotes invariance to receiver-specific perturbations, yielding receiver-agnostic feature representations. Concurrently, class-wise Wasserstein barycenters are estimated across receivers to align class-conditional feature distributions, thereby mitigating inter-receiver distributional discrepancies. To make barycenter estimation tractable, we introduce parametric class-wise prototypes that serve as differentiable proxies for Wasserstein barycenters, thus alleviating the computational burden of conventional Wasserstein solvers. Experimental results on the public WiSig dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving an improvement of at least 7% in identification accuracy. Our code is available at https://github.com/SONGzyyyyyy/WASS.

title: Enabling Practical 6G Extreme Massive MIMO: Block Krylov-Nyström Beamspace Processing.
abstract: Extreme massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) in the upper mid-band spectrum (7-20 GHz) is a key enabler for 6G. In orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems, two-stage beamforming is essential for practical deployment, but most existing works rely on simplified channels and do not consider real-time processing constraints. Current methods require full-dimensional covariance computation and/or eigenvalue decomposition (EVD), resulting in prohibitive memory use and computational complexity. We propose a block Krylov-Nyström framework for beamspace beamforming that avoids full covariance storage and reduces complexity compared to EVD counterparts. The proposed scheme reconstructs full beamforming weights from low-rank channel information using the block Krylov-Nyström subspace, ensuring numerical stability and efficiency. To capture real-time constraints, we further introduce two evaluation methodologies: a complexity-to-delay conversion integrated with channel aging, and a spectral efficiency-to-complexity ratio (SECR) metric. Simulations with 3GPP 38.901 channel models demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves benchmark spectral efficiency with significantly lower latency and complexity, offering up to 15-30 higher SECR than baseline methods. These results establish the block Krylov-Nyström framework as a practical and robust solution for real-time massive MIMO-OFDM beamforming in 6G networks.

title: Detection in Bistatic ISAC with Deterministic Sensing and Gaussian Information Signals.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) is a disruptive technology enabling future sixth-generation (6G) networks. This paper investigates target detection in a bistatic ISAC system, in which the base station (BS) transmits superimposed ISAC signals comprising both Gaussian information-bearing and deterministic sensing components to simultaneously provide communication and sensing functionalities. First, we develop a Neyman-Pearson (NP)-based detector that effectively utilizes both the deterministic sensing and random communication signals. Closed-form analysis reveals that both signal components contribute to improving the overall detection performance. Subsequently, we optimize the BS transmit beamforming to maximize the detection probability, subject to a minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraint for the communication user (CU) and a total transmit power budget at the BS. The resulting non-convex beamforming optimization problem is addressed via semi-definite relaxation (SDR) and successive convex approximation (SCA) techniques. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed NP-based detector, which leverages both types of signals, over benchmark schemes that treat information signals as interference. They also reveal that a higher communication-rate threshold directs more transmit power to Gaussian information-bearing signals, thereby diminishing deterministic-signal power and weakening detection performance.

title: Buffer-Constrained Expert Gating for Large-Scale MoE Inference in Distributed Edge Systems.
abstract: The deployment of distributed Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)-based Large AI Models (LAMs) at the wireless edge is challenged by stringent buffer constraints, dynamic channel conditions, and heterogeneous resource availability. Existing greedy gating strategies fail to adapt to time-varying congestion and wireless distortions, leading to unbalanced expert utilization and high sample drop rates. This work formulates the gating problem in distributed MoE as a constrained Markov Decision Process (MDP) and introduces a Deep Q-Network (DQN)-based intelligent routing mechanism that jointly optimizes expert specialization, queuing latency, and transmission reliability. Our approach uniquely integrates real-time environment statistics, including buffer occupancy, estimated waiting time, and channel state, with label-free sample-expert affinity features such as confidence, entropy, and classification margin. To address instability and overestimation in deep reinforcement learning (RL), we employ Double DQN (DDQN) with target network synchronization and experience replay. The system is trained under a two-stage protocol: supervised pre-training for expert specialization followed by constraint-aware RL for dynamic adaptation. Extensive evaluations on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 demonstrate that our method outperforms a congestion-aware greedy baseline, achieving higher end-to-end accuracy while reducing the total drop rate by a significant margin. Moreover, the proposed framework promotes equitable expert workload distribution and mitigates buffer congestion, validating its efficacy in real-world edge inference scenarios.

title: Optical Feeder Link Scheduling in Space-Ground Networks with Multiple Transceivers on Each Node.
abstract: Optical feeder links (OFLs) are a key enabler for high-capacity satellite-ground integrated optical networks (SGIONs), but their performance in geostationary earth orbit (GEO) systems is strongly limited by cloud-induced outages and long acquisition and handover times. This paper investigates predictive OFL scheduling in GEO SGIONs where both satellites and optical ground stations are equipped with multiple transceivers, enabling enhanced spatial diversity. We propose a centralized link scheduling framework that exploits short-term cloud forecasts to maximize network capacity while maintaining operational stability under multi-aperture constraints. The resulting scheduling problem is formulated as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) and incorporates a link-retention mechanism to reduce handovers across scheduling epochs. Simulation results based on real cloud coverage data show that multi-transceiver architectures significantly improve average capacity and robustness. Moreover, achievable capacity scales nearly linearly with the number of transceivers per node, revealing a tunable trade-off between capacity and stability.

title: Space-to-Ground Entanglement Downlinks: When to Transmit - and When Not.
abstract: The study considers when a low Earth orbiting (LEO) satellite should transmit or hold entangled photons to a ground station in a rapidly varying free-space optical (FSO) channel. A channel-aware observable scheduler is developed that uses time-tag statistics to develop per-slot transmission decisions. The study compares the performance of the scheduler under six environmental conditions and the algorithm delivers secure-key totals providing similar results to an always-transmit scenario, yet allowing for considerable resource efficiency by reducing activity under harsh channel conditions. The system has higher conditional success among used slots and shows a higher avoidance of infeasible and high-error windows. The controller converges faster under normal conditions while longer convergence times are taken only under harsh environmental conditions. The study proposes a practical, drop-in scheduling layer that allows to achieve resource-efficient key delivery by considering the volatile atmospheric conditions for a LEO-to-ground transmission system.

title: EdgeNeXt: A Lightweight Model for UAV-Based Gesture Recognition from Aerial Perspectives.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) increasingly collaborate with humans in scenarios requiring rapid, robust nonverbal communication, such as public safety, inspection, and logistics. Aerial gesture recognition faces key challenges: small and blurred subjects, cluttered backgrounds, and varying viewpoints, distances, and orientations. Prior work largely focuses on controlled or close-range settings, limiting real-world applicability. We introduce a novel outdoor dataset of five practical gestures (direction, acknowledge, land, stop, inspect) across eight orientations (0°–315°), altitudes up to 40m, and diverse conditions, totaling 1,000+ RGB images, far exceeding prior datasets in scale and variability. We benchmark four state-of-the-art (SOTA) lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) (MobileNetV2 (M2), MobileNetV3-large (M3L), EfficientNet-D0 (E0), VGG16 (V16)) and propose EdgeNeXt (ENx), a custom lightweight architecture optimized for embedded UAV deployment. On gesture classification, M2 and M3L achieve 90.5% accuracy, E0 89.5%, and ENx 81.0% with 40× memory savings (0.87MB vs. 33MB) and 7× fewer FLOPs. For orientation estimation, ENx attains 97% accuracy, nearing the 100% of larger models. Our results enable efficient, real-time aerial gesture recognition for on-board UAV operation.

title: Outdoor Accuracy Evaluation of DecaWave's DWM1002 PDoA Kit Measurements.
abstract: Accurate localization in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) is critical for applications such as emergency response, traffic monitoring, and industrial process control. Range-based methods generally outperform range-free ones, and Ultra Wideband (UWB) technology is particularly promising due to its high bandwidth and robustness against multipath effects. This paper evaluates the DecaWave DWM1002 Phase Difference of Arrival (PDoA) kit, an experimental commercial UWB platform extending the earlier DWM1001 Time Difference of Arrival (TDoA) boards, through a real-world outdoor test-bed spanning multiple distances and angles. Our objective is not to propose a new localization algorithm, but to characterize and correct structured, repeatable PDoA bias that affects outdoor deployments. The raw measurements show systematic errors, with short ranges often underestimated and longer ranges increasingly overestimated, deviating significantly from the centimeter-level accuracy claimed by the manufacturer. The observed bias is highly consistent across repetitions, indicating good precision but poor accuracy and motivating lightweight calibration. To mitigate these biases, we explored regression- and Machine Learning (ML)-based calibration models. The best-performing ML approach reduced the average error to around 12cm, achieving an improvement of roughly 70% over the uncalibrated data. These results indicate that while the kit is unsuitable for safety-critical localization in its raw form, lightweight calibration makes it viable for non-critical tasks such as tracking or crowd monitoring.

title: Model-Aware UAV Trajectory Planning for Efficient Radio Environment Mapping.
abstract: Accurate Radio Environment Mapping (REM) is essential for wireless network optimization and performance analysis. However, conventional data acquisition and REM construction methods face practical challenges, particularly in complex or inaccessible urban areas. Model-driven approaches such as ray tracing (RT) offer a promising alternative but are often limited by unknown electromagnetic (EM) parameters that reduce their accuracy. To overcome this, we propose a model-aware UAV trajectory planning framework for efficient REM generation in challenging environments using limited measurements. The problem is formulated as a joint UAV path planning and REM generation as an inverse modeling problem to collect informative data for inferring unknown EM parameters, thereby improving RT-based REM reconstruction. Simulations in an urban setting demonstrate that the proposed method improves REM estimation accuracy by up to 40% compared with baseline approaches. This work presents the first model-aware UAV trajectory optimization framework for EM parameter learning, enabling accurate and data-efficient REM construction in inaccessible regions.

title: Precoder Design Using Local CSI for Full-Duplex Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: This article addresses an interference management challenge in an integrated satellite-terrestrial network (ISTN) amidst spectrum sharing and full-duplex (FD) operational drawbacks. In particular, a beamforming optimization problem is formulated to maximize network throughput while minimizing the adverse effects of interference. To address the non-convex and non-smooth nature of the optimization problem, we first relax it into a product of Rayleigh quotients and then reformulate it into a smooth function using the LogSumExp technique. Next, the resulting problem is split into two subproblems to guarantee distributed beamforming for the satellite (SAT) and base station (BS), respectively, without sharing channel state information (CSI). Going forward, each subproblem is solved using the generalized power iteration (GPI) algorithm to obtain solutions for the respective SAT and BS beamforming vectors. The simulation results presented in this article affirm that the proposed strategy performs better than the existing schemes.

title: Network Slicing and Edge-Driven UAV Surveillance in 5G Private Networks for Industrial Digital Transformation in the Aerospace Sector.
abstract: This paper presents a 5G-enabled private network solution designed to support industrial digital transformation within the aerospace sector. Building upon prior research that identified 5G adoption challenges in the Ayrshire region of Scotland, this work introduces a practical use case demonstrating an integrated 5G and edge computing system for autonomous aerial surveillance. The proposed system employs a 5G private network with network slicing to guarantee ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) even under network congestion. A fleet of 5G-enabled Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) form a resilient mesh network using the Better Approach To Mobile Adhoc Networking (BATMAN) protocol to maintain continuous connectivity. At the network edge, a Human Detector AI module performs real-time intruder detection using a custom deep learning model, UWS-YOLO. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that network slicing ensures service continuity for mission-critical applications, highlighting the potential of 5G MPNs as a key enabler of digital transformation for the aerospace sector and the wider industrial landscape.

title: Hybrid Wireless Network Architectures for Resilient Communication in Seismic Zones.
abstract: Reliable communication is vital during seismic events, yet traditional cellular networks are prone to complete failure. This paper proposes a hybrid architecture integrating conventional cellular systems with cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) to enhance resilience. We model a catastrophic base station failure and leverage the distributed nature of neighboring access points to prioritize the affected zone through fractional power control. Simulation results show that this hybrid approach maintains 70-85% of the pre-disaster per-user rate, preventing the total outage typical of traditional networks. Furthermore, we introduce a proactive disaster identification mechanism using Gradient Boosting Regression to predict network instability. This machine learning component is tightly coupled with the physical layer, triggering recovery actions early to ensure continuous, end-to-end communication in extreme failure scenarios.

title: Enhancing Physical Layer Security with Tree-connected Beyond Diagonal Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface.
abstract: Beyond diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface(BD-RIS) offers promising potentials for improving secrecy performance in wireless environments, due to its additional degree of freedom and higher flexibility in manipulating wireless channels compared with its conventional counterpart. However, a fully connected BD-RIS requires a considerable amount of hardware components and incurs a significant increase in circuit complexity. In this paper we investigate Physical Layer Security(PLS) performance in a multi-input-single-output(MISO) system with the aid of a tree-connected BD-RIS, whose tunable admittance components are connected to form a tree topology. The ensuing joint optimization of the transmit covariance matrix and RIS’s scattering matrix is nonconvex. Additionally, the tree topology maps the scattering matrix to a symmetrical and tridiagonal susceptance matrix. To solve this problem we decompose it into two subproblems, and then we employ the Dinkelbach method and convex approximation to handle nonconvexities in the problem formulation, and propose a Riemannian conjugate gradient algorithm to ensure that symmetry and tridiagonality are maintained throughout the iterative process. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed scheme achieves secrecy performance comparable to the fully connected BD-RIS while significantly reducing circuit complexity.

title: Beyond Retraining: Source-Free Adaptation for Generalizable Intrusion Detection.
abstract: Machine learning (ML)–based intrusion detection systems (IDS) often degrade when deployed across heterogeneous networks due to domain shifts in traffic and configuration. To mitigate this degradation, conventional domain adaptation (DA) methods aim to align source and target data distributions; however, they require access to source data during deployment—an impractical constraint that undermines scalability and reusability. To overcome this limitation, we propose TRANSFA-IDS (Transformer Source-Free Adaptation for IDS), which removes the need for source data during adaptation while preserving the knowledge encoded in the source-trained model. TRANSFA-IDS transforms tabular flow records into structured color image embeddings and employs a compact Vision Transformer with a Deep Support Vector Data Description (Deep-SVDD) head to learn domain-invariant representations of benign behavior. During deployment, it adapts to new environments using only a small portion of unlabeled target traffic by fine-tuning the last Transformer block, efficiently realigning feature distributions without retraining. Experiments across cross-dataset settings (CICIDS2018↔UNSW-NB15) show that TRANSFA-IDS achieves AUROC scores up to 0.908 and 0.873, outperforming traditional non-adaptive unsupervised baselines by over 40% while adapting more than twice as fast as conventional adaptive unsupervised. These results demonstrate that source-free adaptation can deliver both high accuracy and deployment practicality for scalable IDS across diverse network environments.

title: SLIPT-Enabled Ground-to-UAV FSO Systems with Optical Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces.
abstract: This paper proposes an optical reconfigurable intelligent surface (ORIS)-assisted ground-to-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) free-space optical (FSO) communication system empowered by simultaneous lightwave information and power transfer (SLIPT). To overcome the line-of-sight (LoS) limitation of FSO-based SLIPT systems, we introduce an ORIS that reflects the laser beam towards a non-LoS UAV receiver. We model and analyze the combined channel characteristics, incorporating atmospheric loss, turbulence-induced fading, pointing error, and angle-of-arrival fluctuations due to UAV hovering. We derive closed-form expressions for harvested energy, outage probability, and symbol error rate (SER). Numerical results show that integrating ORIS improves EH efficiency while maintaining manageable outage and SER performance.

title: FAST: Floating AI Service for Time-Varying Mobile Mixed Reality Networks.
abstract: Mobile Mixed Reality Network (MMRN) is an emerging decentralized, infrastructure-free system that enables users to interact in a shared space blending real and virtual worlds via mobile Head-Mounted Devices (HMDs). These immersive experiences increasingly rely on Artificial Intelligence (AI) services such as gaze tracking to deliver responsive interactions. However, the limited computational and communication capabilities of HMDs make it challenging to support AI services locally, while the mobility and dynamic data distributions of HMDs hinder device-to-device collaboration. To address such issues, we propose FAST, a fully decentralized framework for scalable and resource-efficient AI service provisioning in MMRN. FAST performs online prediction with a time-varying loss function to enable model adaptation to evolving data streams, and exploits pairwise proximity constraints to identify shared interests among nearby HMDs, enabling selective device-to-device model sharing for improved local performance. We propose a decentralized online saddle-point algorithm that dynamically adjusts model complexity to balance accuracy and resource usage, with theoretical guarantees of sublinear regret and constraint violations under time-varying topologies. Simulations on real-world datasets show that FAST outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by up to 28% in accuracy and reduces computation and communication costs by 39% under user mobility and data heterogeneity.

title: Latency Minimization in AirComp-Assisted Split Federated Learning with Layer-Wise Aggregation.
abstract: This paper proposes an over-the-air computation (AirComp)-assisted split federated learning (SFL) framework for mobile edge networks. Specifically, heterogeneous devices are assigned device-specific split points, such that each device executes the layers up to its split point locally and offloads the remaining layers to the edge server, while the split submodels are aggregated over the air. To guarantee reliable learning under noisy aggregation, we impose a mean-squared error constraint to control the aggregation distortion. We formulate a joint optimization problem over split-point selection, communication and computation resource allocation, and develop an efficient alternating algorithm that combines Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT)-based updates with the interior point method to convex subproblems. Simulation results demonstrate that, under various signal-to-noise ratios, data distributions, and computing capabilities, the proposed scheme consistently achieves faster convergence and higher test accuracy than baselines.

title: Covert and Efficient DNS Traffic Loop Attacks Based on Intermediate Devices.
abstract: DNS traffic loop is an efficient application-layer DDoS attack method. By constructing circular query-response interactions across multiple nodes, such attacks not only continuously consume network bandwidth and computational resources along the path but also direct amplified traffic toward arbitrary targets. However, existing attack methods often struggle to balance deployment simplicity with loop concealment. To address this, we propose a novel DNS traffic loop attack. This method leverages widely deployed intermediate devices (e.g., DNS proxies, ISP middleboxes) and their associated DNS resolvers. By exploiting mechanisms that trigger unexpected DNS responses, our method achieves covert attack loops without complex configuration. Furthermore, the attack leverages the DNS protocol’s retry mechanism to achieve exponential traffic amplification, significantly enhancing its destructive potential. To validate the feasibility and effectiveness of this method, we implement the attack in a controlled experimental environment and test its performance. Concurrently, through large-scale scanning experiments, we identify 286,223 intermediate devices exhibiting such behavior and 29,011 associated DNS resolvers, analyzing their distribution characteristics and potential threats.

title: An Evaluation of the Remote CX Protocol under Noise in Distributed Quantum Computing.
abstract: Quantum computers connected through classical and quantum communication channels can be combined to function as a single unit to run large quantum circuits that each device is unable to execute on their own. The distributed quantum computing paradigm is therefore often seen as a potential pathway to scaling quantum computing to capacities necessary for practical and large-scale applications. Whether connecting multiple quantum processing units (QPUs) in clusters or over networks, quantum communication requires entanglement to be generated and distributed over distances. Using entanglement, the remote CX protocol can be performed, which allows the application of the CX gate involving qubits located in different QPUs. In this work, we use a specialized simulation framework for a high-level evaluation of the impact of the protocol when executed under noise in various network configurations using different number of QPUs. We compare naive and graph partitioning qubit assignment strategies and how they affect the fidelity in experiments run on Grover, GHZ, VQC, and random circuits. The results provide insights on how QPU and network configurations or naive scheduling can degrade performance.

title: Joint Pilot Muting and 3D U-Net Reconstruction for Inter-Cell Pilot Contamination in 6G UDNs.
abstract: Pilot contamination is a fundamental bottleneck in 6G ultra-dense networks (UDNs), where static pilot reuse cannot adapt to irregular user-centric topologies and spatially non-stationary channels. We propose a joint optimization framework combining binary pilot muting and deep learning-based channel reconstruction. Network layouts are modeled by a Matérn hard-core process (HCP) derived from a Poisson point process (PPP), and small-scale fading is generated using a 3D non-stationary geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM). Pilot muting is formulated as a binary combinatorial optimization that minimizes network-wide pilot-domain normalized mean square error (NMSE) and is solved efficiently via an Estimation of Distribution Algorithm (EDA). To compensate for sparsified observations, a compact 3D U-Net performs channel inpainting to recover full resource blocks from muted pilots. Simulations show faster convergence than greedy heuristics and notable gains in Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) and channel estimation accuracy, especially for edge users in dense network environments.

title: Spectral Efficiency Maximization in Pinching-Antenna-Enabled CR Networks.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a cognitive radio (CR) network underpinned by pinching antennas (PAs), in which both the primary transmitter (PT) and secondary transmitter (ST) employ a single waveguide and multiple PAs to support simultaneous spectrum sharing. A sum spectral efficiency (SE) maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize the pinching beamforming at both the PT and ST, under constraints on the PA deployment. To solve this non-convex problem, a two-stage optimization algorithm is developed, which sequentially optimizes the PT and ST pinching beamforming. For each pinching beamforming optimization, the coarse positions of the PAs are first determined at the waveguide level, followed by wavelength-level refinements to achieve constructive signal combining at the target user and destructive superposition at the non-intended users. Simulation results demonstrate that PAs yield substantial SE gains compared to conventional fixed-position antennas.

title: Secure Beamforming for Pinching-Antenna Systems.
abstract: Recently, pinching-antenna systems (PASS) have demonstrated pronounced advantages in mitigating large-scale path loss. This paper investigates their performance advantages in downlink secure transmission. We consider a scenario with multiple waveguides, one legitimate user, and one eavesdropper. The goal is to maximize the secrecy rate by jointly designing the baseband beamformer and the positions of pinching antennas (PAs). To handle the coupled optimization problem, we first exploit a generalized Rayleigh quotient structure to derive the optimal baseband beamformer. This step converts the coupled problem into a single-variable optimization over PAs' positions. Then, an efficient gradient-based method is proposed to achieve PA position updates. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm converges rapidly and stably, and that PASS achieve substantial secrecy rate gains over the fixed-antenna baselines.

title: Joint Age of Information and Energy Minimization in Two-hop Status Update Systems.
abstract: We consider a relay-assisted status update system, where each relay is responsible for transmitting updates from a cluster of sources to a base station (BS). The relays harvest energy from the environment to sustain the operations. To avoid collisions, only one relay is scheduled to transmit updates to the BS at a time. To this aim, the relays send update proposals to the BS, and the BS greedily selects the one that minimizes the overall age of information (AoI). Our goal is to design an update proposal policy for the relays that jointly minimizes their average AoI and energy consumption. Considering that each relay can only access its local information, i.e., its own AoI, buffer and battery status, and that the energy harvesting and update arrival processes are stochastic, we first model the update scheduling problem as a partially observable Markov game. Then, we propose a decentralized multi-agent proximal policy optimization (DMAPPO) algorithm at each relay to solve it. Our results show that the proposed DMAPPO algorithm outperforms baseline schemes in terms of AoI and energy consumption.

title: Optimization of Sparse VLSF Codes for Short-Packet Transmission via Saddlepoint Methods.
abstract: In this work, we present an optimization framework for sparse variable-length stop-feedback (VLSF) codes based on a saddlepoint approximation, which jointly optimizes the decoding configuration parameters. Thanks to the analytical tractability of the saddlepoint approximation, the framework enables efficient gradient-based optimization of such parameters for common memoryless channels, including the additive white Gaussian noise, binary symmetric, and binary erasure channels. We further propose a refined decoding rule that extends the conventional fixed-threshold rule and leads to a tighter achievability bound. Numerical results demonstrate that our framework provides near-optimal decoding configurations at low computational cost. Moreover, the results from our refined rule demonstrate that the fixed-threshold decoding rule is restrictive and that achievability bounds can be further tightened.

title: Joint Power Allocation and Positioning Optimization for Multi-Satellite Cooperative Transmission.
abstract: The rapid evolution of multi-satellite cooperative transmission (MSCT) systems has enabled unprecedented improvements in global broadband connectivity. As the deployment density of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites increases, the short inter-satellite distances allow MSCT systems to exhibit array-like behaviors, where spatial geometry and relative positioning critically affect coherent signal transmission and interference management. This paper studies a downlink MSCT system, where multiple LEO satellites collectively function as a large-scale distributed antenna array. By flexibly adjusting their relative positions, the array geometry can be reconfigured to enhance coherent transmission and mitigate inter-user interference. To fully exploit this geometric flexibility, we develop a joint power allocation and position optimization framework to maximize the weighted sum rate under power, displacement, and collision avoidance constraints. The system is modeled as a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output network with Rician fading. To address the strong coupling between power allocation and spatial configuration, an alternating optimization framework is proposed. Specifically, the transmit power is optimized through a Lagrangian dual-based algorithm that introduces auxiliary variables and employs a bisection search to satisfy power constraints, while the satellite positions are refined using a particle swarm optimization procedure within feasible spatial domains. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed optimization framework.

title: Channel Gain Map Reconstruction Based on Virtual Scatterer Model.
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient method for modeling and reconstructing the channel gain map (CGM) based on virtual scatterers. Specifically, we develop a virtual scatterer model to characterize the channel power gain distribution in three-dimensional (3D) space, by capturing the multi-path propagation environment structure and exploiting the angular-domain spatial correlation of scatterer response. In this model, the CGM is represented as a function over a set of tunable parameters for virtual scatterers, including their number, positions, and scatterer response coefficients (SRCs), which can be estimated from a limited number of channel power gain measurements at a given set of locations within the region of interest. This new representation offers a flexible and scalable modeling framework for efficient and accurate CGM reconstruction. Furthermore, we propose a progressive estimation algorithm to acquire the scatterers’ parameters. In this algorithm, we gradually increase the number of virtual scatterers to balance the computational complexity and estimation accuracy. In addition, by exploiting the spatial correlation of scatterer response, we propose a Gaussian process regression (GPR)-based inference method to predict the SRCs that cannot be directly estimated. Finally, ray-tracing-based simulation results under realistic physical environments validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, demonstrating that it achieves higher reconstruction accuracy compared to conventional CGM estimation approaches.

title: Energy-Efficient Resource Management for MEC-Assisted VR Systems: A D3QN-IL Approach.
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) enables immersive experiences for remote monitoring, guidance, and control, improving operational efficiency across Internet of things-enabled and other cyber-physical applications. However, VR services characterize with ultra-high resolution, ultra-low latency, and frequent computation-intensive viewport rendering, posing stringent requirements on wireless communication and computation. In this paper, we propose a mobile edge computing assisted VR streaming transmission scheme to improve quality of experience (QoE) and alleviate computing burden of VR devices. A joint optimization problem is formulated to minimize the weighted energy consumption under QoE constraints. To solve the high-dimensional mixed integer non-convex problem, we propose a hierarchical optimization framework. The upper layer leverages convex optimization methods, while the lower layer uses dueling double Q network enhanced with imitation learning for binary decisions. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can achieve lower energy consumption and adapts faster to dynamic environments.

title: LLR-Based Attention-Weighted Projection Decoding for Sparse Vector-Coded Short Packet Transmissions.
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced sparse vector coding scheme tailored for short-packet communication over noisy wireless channels. Conventional SVC often uses random (Gaussian, Bernoulli) or structured (partial Hadamard) spreading/projection matrices with baseline decoding based on naive projection scores to recover the sparse signal support, which may suffer from reliability degradation under fading conditions. To address this, we introduce an enhanced decoding approach leveraging LLR-based attention-weighted projection, which dynamically reweights received signal measurements according to their reliability, giving more importance to more reliable measurements. Simulation results over both Rayleigh flat fading and 3GPP TDL-C/TDL-D frequency-selective channels show that the proposed LLR-based attention-weighted projection decoding outperforms baseline projection decoding with both structured and random projection matrices. Moreover, we extend our analysis to a short-packet (3–11 bits) transmission framework over the 3GPP PUCCH. The results highlight that the proposed SVC scheme, employing a partial Hadamard spreading matrix combined with LLR-based attention-weighted projection decoding, can competitively rival 3GPP RM codes under optimal maximum likelihood (ML) decoding at very low BLER targets, while offering significant computational complexity advantages, making it a promising short-packet coding candidate for ultra-reliable, low-latency 6G short-block-length uplink/downlink channels.

title: A Linearly Convergent Distributed Algorithm for Robust Multi-Sensor Fusion via Sinkhorn Barycenters in ISAC Networks.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) networks face communication bottlenecks when fusing high-dimensional sensing data across distributed nodes. This paper addresses this challenge through a communication-efficient federated algorithm for computing entropy-regularized Wasserstein barycenters, enabling robust fusion of non-Gaussian posteriors under sensor uncertainties. To reduce overhead, we develop a compressed alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) scheme that exchanges only sparsified probability vectors between base stations and a fusion center. Theoretical analysis provides convergence guarantees under practical bounded-delay asynchronous operation. Simulations demonstrate improved tracking accuracy and order-of-magnitude communication reduction compared to classical fusion baselines, supporting deployment in bandwidth-constrained ISAC fronthaul networks.

title: Stealth in Sight: Model-Free Assessment of LiDAR Vulnerabilities in Autonomous Vehicle Systems.
abstract: Industrial networks increasingly support safety-critical Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) such as Autonomous Vehicles (AVs), where reliable sensor data and real-time perception are essential for resilient operation. However, LiDAR-based perception, widely used for its high spatial accuracy, introduces vulnerable attack surfaces. The compromise can propagate downstream to planning and control modules, jeopardizing systems’ safety and reliability. To assess the vulnerability, this paper presents a model-free adversarial framework that injects stealthy perturbations such as, occlusion, point removal, and, noise into LiDAR data via malicious software into the LiDAR preprocessing stage of Robot Operating System (ROS) middleware. A Proximal Policy Optimization-enabled with Long Short Term Memory (PPO-LSTM) agent under an Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) learns these perturbations without access to perception models or hardware. Experiments on the KITTI dataset show an 85% attack success rate, with 67.8% and 61.5% drops in recall and precision for 3D object detection, demonstrating both effectiveness and stealth. These results reveal critical vulnerabilities in LiDAR-enabled CPS and emphasize the need for resilient industrial networks, secure middleware, and robust perception defenses.

title: Quality-Cost-Security Trade-off via Semantic Feature Importance Aware Adaptive Transmission.
abstract: Although semantic communication offers superior transmission efficiency, it simultaneously brings new security vulnerabilities. To address this challenge, we propose a Feature-Importance Guided Selective Masking-Encryption (FISME) scheme to balance the semantic communication tasks quality, transmission cost and security performanc, where an eavesdropper conducts the model inversion attack by exploiting intercepted semantic information. First, we define a composite system cost function that integrates channel decoding iterations and encryption processes. Second, we jointly optimize feature masking, encryption, and channel coding parameters to minimize the composite system cost while ensuring robust and secure transmission. Third, we propose a dynamic Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) coding-rate selection mechanism to adjust coding parameters based on real-time SNR, ensuring a balance between reliability and redundancy. Moreover, we propose a Bayesian optimization of semantic transmission parameters via the Sequential Model-based Algorithm Configuration (BOST-SMAC3) algorithm to dynamically optimize masking feature set, encryption feature set, LDPC coding rate and LDPC decoding iterations. Simulation results show that the proposed FISME scheme achieves a flexible trade-off among cost, quality, and security by dynamically adapting communication, encryption, and channel coding costs to varying SNR.

title: Handover-Enabled Multi-Timescale Service Offloading in Vehicular Edge Computing.
abstract: Vehicular edge computing (VEC) is a critical enabler of low-latency and computation-intensive vehicular applications by offloading tasks from vehicles to edge servers. However, the dynamic nature of vehicular networks poses significant challenges to task offloading schemes. In particular, efficient schemes should address the migration of tasks due to vehicle handover in a mixed-timescale manner, as the computational and radio resources need to be allocated in different timescales. This paper proposes a robust task offloading scheme for VEC within the open radio access network (O-RAN) architecture. The proposed scheme integrates large timescale computational resource allocation (CRA) with moderate timescale task partitioning and small timescale radio resource allocation (RRA) using O-RAN’s hierarchical control framework. Our scheme minimizes the network-wide resources under latency constraints that are subjected to demand uncertainty. Large timescale CRA proactively compensates for the migration overhead to maintain the tasks’ deadlines. Simulation results show that our robust scheme provides a trade off between resource consumption of non-robust solutions and outage probability of conservative robust solutions.

title: Frequency-Aware Passive Beamforming for Shared IRS-Aided Communications.
abstract: In a system in which a single intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is shared among multiple communication systems (CSs) operating at different frequency bands with jointly controlled phase shift, optimizing the phase shift for specific frequency may result in limited coverage for certain CSs across the communication area. This is because of the frequency-dependent reflection characteristics of the IRS, which cause variations in performance across different CSs. This study proposes an IRS control scheme that maximizes the minimum signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in order to prevent unfairness in IRS shared systems. In particular, we designed the phase-shift control of the IRS to maximize the minimum SNR in the coverage area of the IRS, considering the frequency characteristics. The results show that the proposed method improves the SNR and ensures fairness among CSs, compared to the control that considers only a single frequency. The results show that the proposed method maximizes the minimum SNR, thereby ensuring fairness among CSs. This method contributes to optimizing communication performance when multiple CSs operating at different frequencies simultaneously employ an IRS.

title: On the Impact of Densification in Near-Field Downlink mmWave Cellular Networks.
abstract: In this work, we present an analytical framework for a dense mmWave network consisting of base stations (BSs) with extremely large antenna arrays (ELAA) where users may fall within the near-field region of electromagnetic wave propagation. Near-field channels enable BSs to beamform using complete user-location information. We first analyze the location-based beamforming (LBF) to provide a simplified beamforming gain model that can be incorporated in large-scale analysis. We show that near-field beamforming may lead to loss of directivity in some regions. By leveraging stochastic geometry tools, we derive the coverage probability of the typical user while incorporating the near-field effects in the presence of random blockage. Through numerical investigations, we compare near-field LBF and far-field direction-based beamforming (DBF).
