Our analysis reveals many interesting insights, including the impact of densification and the existence of multiple critical BS densities due to near-field effect, blockages, and noise-interference trade-off. We show that near-field effects may lead to degradation in coverage probability, thus requiring a more careful design.

title: GO-GenZip: Goal-Oriented Generative Sampling and Hybrid Compression.
abstract: Current network data telemetry pipelines consist of massive streams of fine-grained Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) from multiple distributed sources towards central aggregators, making data storage, transmission, and real-time analysis increasingly unsustainable. This work presents a generative AI (GenAI)-driven sampling and hybrid compression framework that redesigns network telemetry from a goal-oriented perspective. Unlike conventional approaches that passively compress fully observed data, our approach jointly optimizes what to observe and how to encode it, guided by the relevance of information to downstream tasks. The framework integrates adaptive sampling policies, using adaptive masking techniques, with generative modeling to identify patterns and preserve critical features across temporal and spatial dimensions. The selectively acquired data are further processed through a hybrid compression scheme that combines traditional lossless coding with GenAI-driven, lossy compression. Experimental results on real network datasets demonstrate over 50% reductions in sampling and data transfer costs, while maintaining comparable reconstruction accuracy and goal-oriented analytical fidelity in downstream tasks.

title: Distributed Model Predictive Control-Based Trajectory and Resource Optimization for Aerial Base Stations.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with aerial base stations (ABSs) have gained considerable attention for their ability to enhance coverage and capacity in the beyond 5G era. However, optimizing ABS trajectories is challenging due to limited battery capacity and inter-cell interference in multi-ABS scenarios. Existing ABS trajectory control methods are mostly offline and centralized, relying on the assumption of perfect knowledge about future channel states and user locations, rendering them impractical in real environments. In this paper, we propose an online and distributed ABS trajectory and resource optimization method based on distributed model predictive control (MPC). We formulate a problem that jointly optimizes ABS trajectories, user association, and power control to minimize flight time and power consumption while satisfying users’ data reception requirements. In the proposed method, each ABS solves its own local MPC problem to achieve the overall objective through local computation and communication. Because each local problem is non-convex, we develop an efficient algorithm using successive convex approximation. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Topology-aware Scheduling for Efficient Federated Learning in Computing Power Networks with Graph Neural Networks.
abstract: With the growing demand for intelligent services, computing power networks (CPNs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for collaborative computing across heterogeneous and distributed resources. Federated learning (FL) can be integrated into CPNs to enable large-scale model training across diverse devices while preserving data privacy. However, heterogeneous client capabilities and multi-hop communication topologies pose significant challenges to FL, leading to high latency and energy consumption. To address these issues, we propose G2S, a graph neural network-based method for efficient client scheduling in CPNs under a FL setting. G2S employs a message-passing graph neural network to model physical network characteristics and a graph attention network to capture client communication dependencies. A differentiable multi-layer perceptron scorer with Gumbel-Softmax relaxation then generates assignment scores to minimize the overall system cost. Numerical results on multiple real-world topologies demonstrate that G2S improves system efficiency and accelerates model convergence compared with baseline algorithms.

title: Personalized Federated Learning via Label-Level Feature Enhancers.
abstract: To counter the degraded personalization caused by client heterogeneity, we propose FedLFE. Each client inserts a distribution layer that reparameterizes latent features as Gaussians, yielding implicit augmentation and regularization. A label-level feature enhancer (LFE) builds per-class Gaussian mixtures from local statistics; the server aggregates these with smoothing to produce global label distributions. During aggregation, classifier heads are merged via similarity-weighted averaging, while an alignment loss forces local latent features to match samples drawn from the global LFE. FedLFE avoids the generators/selectors and extra communication of methods such as FedGen and FedCP, offering lightweight augmentation. Comprehensive experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and AG News show FedLFE surpasses state-of-the-art personalized federated learning (FL) baselines across diverse non-IID settings.

title: Fully-Activated GSSK with LFM Waveform for Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: This paper proposes a fully-activated generalized space shift keying (FA-GSSK) modulation scheme for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems to address the difficulty of simultaneously satisfying communication and sensing requirements. Unlike conventional GSSK, FA-GSSK activates all transmit antennas at the base station (BS) within each symbol period, enabling multi-user communication while achieving high-precision sensing tasks. To further enhance sensing capability, the communication symbols are embedded into a linear frequency modulated (LFM) waveform, enabling the ISAC system to exploit the pulse compression gain of LFM signals for coherent target sensing. Under this framework, a joint transmit–receive beamforming optimization problem is formulated to maximize the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the target echo received at the ISAC BS, subject to the constraints of correct FA-GSSK demodulation at each communication user (CU) and a total transmit power budget. The resulting nonconvex problem is efficiently solved using semidefinite programming (SDP). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed FA-GSSK with LFM waveform achieves a superior communication–sensing trade-off compared to conventional orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) based benchmarks.

title: Joint BS Clustering and Resource Allocation for High-Accuracy, Low-Latency 6G Positioning.
abstract: The demand for high-accuracy and low-latency positioning for large-scale user equipment (UEs) is critical for emerging 6G applications such as intelligent rescue. However, the following challenges for positioning accuracy and latency are attracting increasing attention. Firstly, due to the limitation of computational resource at base stations (BSs) and wireless transmission resource, numerous measurements caused by a surge in positioning requests will increase computation and transmission delays. Secondly, the positioning accuracy will degrade if the topology of measurable BSs cluster and the UE form a poor Position Dilution of Precision (PDOP). Nevertheless, we find no discussion on the joint optimization for positioning accuracy and latency in existing research. To address this limitation, a novel joint optimization framework is proposed in this paper, concurrently minimizing positioning error that is characterized by PDOP and positioning latency comprising that of both transmission and computation. Our solution, the Greedy-Cooperative Game-based joint Strategy and Resource optimization algorithm (GCGSR), creatively employs greedy search-based cooperative game to jointly resolve both the BSs clusters measuring with each UE and the central BSs computing the UE’s location, where convex optimization ensures the optimal solution for bandwidth allocation. Simulation results with up to 1000 UEs verify that GCGSR outperforms the benchmarks in optimization capability with an acceptable implementation latency, which implies that GCGSR can be deployed in 6G dynamic large-scale positioning systems.

title: Analysis of SINR Coverage in LEO Satellite Networks through Spatial Network Calculus.
abstract: We introduce a new analytical framework, developed based on the spatial network calculus, for performance assessment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks. Specifically, we model the satellites' spatial positions as a strong ball-regulated point process on the sphere. Under this model, proximal points in space exhibit a locally repulsive property, reflecting the fact that intersatellite links are protected by a safety distance and would not be arbitrarily close. Subsequently, we derive analytical lower bounds on the conditional coverage probabilities under Nakagami-$m$ and Rayleigh fading, respectively. These expressions have a low computational complexity, enabling efficient numerical evaluations. We validate the effectiveness of our theoretical model by contrasting the coverage probability obtained from our analysis with that estimated from a Starlink constellation. The results show that our analysis provides a tight lower bound on the actual value and, surprisingly, matches the empirical simulations almost perfectly with a 1 dB shift. This demonstrates our framework as an appropriate theoretical model for LEO satellite networks.

title: Concatenated error-correcting codes for the interference channel with multi-antenna reception.
abstract: Error correcting codes (ECCs) such as low-density parity check (LDPC) codes and polar codes can operate close to Shannon capacity, especially in the low-noise regime. However, ECCs are not designed to mitigate high levels of interference – a task usually relegated to signal processing at the physical layer. For channels with strong interference, recent work has shown that packet repetition at the transmitter with dual antenna reception and canonical correlation analysis (CCA) signal alignment at the receiver can significantly improve the bit error rate under strong and unpredictable interference. Inspired by this, this paper proposes the use of concatenated high-rate LDPC - repetition codes with combined CCA and belief propagation (BP) decoding. Our numerical results show that concatenating a high-rate LDPC code and a repetition code can significantly reduce the block error rate (BLER) compared to LDPC codes with the same code rate when interference is present; and, interestingly, even for interference-free channels with multi-antenna reception. Furthermore, adjusting the code rate of the LDPC codes and the repetition codes can further optimize the BLER performance.

title: Multi-Sensor Scheduling for Remote State Estimation over Wireless MIMO Fading Channels with Semantic Over-the-Air Aggregation.
abstract: In this work, we investigate multi-sensor scheduling for remote state estimation over wireless multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) fading channels using a novel semantic over-the-air (SemOTA) aggregation approach. We first revisit Kalman filtering with OTA aggregation, highlighting its sensor power limitations. To balance power efficiency and estimation performance, we formulate the scheduling problem as a finite-horizon dynamic programming (DP) problem. Analyzing the optimal Q-function structure, we show that the scheduling policy exhibits a semantic structure that dynamically adapts to real-time error covariance and channel variations. To efficiently learn the solution, we derive an upper bound on the Q-function via a positive semidefinite (PSD) cone decomposition, allowing for an approximate scheduling policy and an efficient algorithm for remote state estimation. Numerical results confirm that our scheme outperforms existing methods in both estimation accuracy and power efficiency.

title: Doppler-Resilient LEO Satellite OFDM Transmission with Affine Frequency Domain Pilot.
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) based low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication system suffers from severe Doppler shifts, while the Doppler-resilient affine frequency-division multiplexing (AFDM) transmission suffers from significantly high processing complexity in data detection. In this paper, we explore the channel estimation gain of affine frequency (AF) domain pilot to enhance the OFDM transmission under high mobility. Specifically, we propose a novel AF domain pilot embedding scheme for satellite-ground downlink OFDM systems for capturing the channel characteristics. By exploiting the autoregressive (AR) property of adjacent channels, a long short-term memory (LSTM) based predictor is designed to replace conventional interpolation operation in OFDM channel estimation. Simulation results show that the proposed transmission scheme significantly outperforms conventional OFDM scheme in terms of bit error rate (BER) under high Doppler scenarios, thus paving a new way for the design of next generation non-terrestrial network (NTN) communication systems.

title: Alleviating Budgetary Challenges in Machine Unlearning Services Through Insurance.
abstract: Machine unlearning as a service offers data contributors the opportunity to withdraw their data from the trained model. Yet, the number of upcoming requests may be too large for the service provider’s budget to cover, which prevents these requests from responding in time as ruled out by regulations. The insurance for the unlearning service offers the provider a chance to respond to more unlearning requests in time, especially for those requests that are difficult to process because of budget limitation. The risk of overloaded unlearning requests is transferred to the insurer, but the price and strategy of insurance in such a market is under exploration. We explore the problem by designing a Stackelberg game-based pricing model to locate the best response of service provider’s decisions and insurance premium, along with a general unlearning scenario that is complied with GDPR. Our theoretical analysis shows that the Stackelberg equilibrium exists and is unique, and the numerical simulation further visually verifies the results and demonstrates the performance in the unlearning market.

title: KP-A: A Unified Network Knowledge Plane for Catalyzing Agentic Network Intelligence.
abstract: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) and agentic systems is enabling autonomous 6G networks with advanced intelligence, including self-configuration, self-optimization, and self-healing. However, the current implementation of individual intelligence tasks necessitates isolated knowledge retrieval pipelines, resulting in redundant data flows and inconsistent interpretations. Inspired by the service model unification effort in Open-RAN (to support interoperability and vendor diversity), we propose KP-A: a unified Network Knowledge Plane specifically designed for Agentic network intelligence. By decoupling network knowledge acquisition and management from intelligence logic, KP-A streamlines development and reduces maintenance complexity for intelligence engineers. By offering an intuitive and consistent knowledge interface, KP-A also enhances interoperability for the network intelligence agents. We demonstrate KP-A in two representative intelligence tasks: live network knowledge Q&A and edge AI service orchestration. All implementation artifacts have been open-sourced to support reproducibility and future standardization efforts.

title: CT-LSTM: Cluster-based Classification of Irregular Time-series Medical Data.
abstract: In clinical practice, time-series models are crucial for intervention and individualized treatment, as they can predict the progression of a patient’s condition. However, existing models often assume uniformly spaced time intervals, ignoring variable sampling differences and patient heterogeneity, which leads to reduced predictive performance and the omission of potential clinical patterns. To address this, the Time-aware LSTM (T-LSTM) was designed to handle irregular time intervals, but it still struggles to capture differential features across patients. In this paper, we propose a novel time-aware predictive framework, the Cluster-based Time-aware LSTM (CT-LSTM). The method first partitions patients into subgroups based on their representations, thereby capturing heterogeneous characteristics across populations; it then incorporates a time-decay mechanism within each subgroup to model the dynamics of irregularly sampled sequences. Experiments on a real-world ICU dataset demonstrate that CT-LSTM significantly outperforms traditional models such as ARIMA and VAR in irregular time-series classification tasks, and is able to identify clinically meaningful patient subtypes. These results show that CT-LSTM not only improves predictive performance but also enhances interpretability, offering potential support for individualized treatment.

title: Expansion-Aware Design Model for Optical-Circuit-Switched Data Center Networks Suppressing Fiber Link Rewiring.
abstract: The rapid growth of data center traffic has intensified the need for scalable and cost-efficient network architectures. Optical circuit switching (OCS) has emerged as a promising technology for this purpose, offering high bandwidth, low latency, and energy efficiency compared to traditional electrical packet switching. Among OCS-based architectures, the twisted and folded Clos network (TF-Clos) is particularly attractive due to its structural simplicity and modular scalability. However, conventional TF-Clos design models primarily address one-time network construction and do not explicitly consider incremental expansions, during which extensive optical fiber link rewiring may be required. Such reconfiguration increases operational complexity and risks service disruption, underscoring the need for expansion-aware design approaches. This paper proposes an expansion-aware OCS-based TF-Clos design model that incorporates multiple steps of network expansion while balancing two conflicting objectives: maximizing the switching network size and suppressing fiber link rewiring operations. We formulate the design problem as an optimization problem, and we introduce a pruning-based search algorithm to approximately solve it with reduced computation time. Numerical results show that the proposed model can reduce the number of fiber link rewirings at the expense of network size. These results highlight the practical advantages of the proposed model for designing scalable and reliable OCS-based TF-Clos networks in real data center environments.

title: Low-Complexity Joint 4D Estimation for Aerial Targets in MIMO-ISAC via BCD and CZT.
abstract: Current multi-target estimation methods in aerial MIMO-ISAC struggle to balance estimation accuracy and computation time, fail to utilize the resolution gain from virtual antenna arrays, and cannot fully handle multi-target joint 4D (2D angle, distance, and velocity) estimation. To address these issues, this paper investigates 4D estimation of multiple aerial targets using a MIMO-ISAC system with code-division orthogonal pilot sequences and two receive uniform planar arrays (UPAs), including standard and sparse ones. We formulate the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) problem as a challenging nonconvex optimization problem and propose a low-complexity algorithm to solve it by leveraging ESPRIT, block coordinate descent (BCD), and chirp-z transform (CZT). Numerical results validate the sparse receive UPA’s significant resolution gain and the proposed algorithm’s superior tradeoff between estimation accuracy and computational complexity. These findings highlight the practical value of the proposed framework for aerial MIMO-ISAC.

title: Meta-Learning-Driven GFlowNets for 3D Directional Modulation in Mobile Wireless Systems.
abstract: In our prior work we have proposed the use of GFlowNets, a generative AI (GenAI) framework, for designing a secure communication system comprising a time-modulated intelligent reflecting surface (TM-IRS). However, GFlowNet-based approaches assume static environments, limiting their applicability in mobile wireless networks. In this paper, we propose a novel Meta-GFlowNet framework that achieves rapid adaptation to dynamic conditions using model-agnostic meta-learning. As the communication user is moving, the framework learns a direction-general prior across user directions via inner trajectory-balance updates and outer meta-updates, enabling quick convergence to new user directions. The approach requires no labeled data, employing a pseudo-supervised consistency objective derived from the learned reward by GFlowNet and the actual sum-rate reward of the TM-IRS system. Simulation results show that the proposed method attains faster adaptation and higher secrecy performance than retrained GFlowNets, offering an efficient GenAI framework for dynamic wireless environments. Although the scenario considered here focuses on directional modulation–based physical-layer security, the proposed framework can also be applied to other mobile wireless systems, such as joint sensing–communication networks, that utilize GFlowNets.

title: FairMoE-FL: A Communication-Efficient and Fair Federated Mixture-of-Experts Framework.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed clients without sharing raw data but suffers from communication overhead and unfair performance due to client heterogeneity. We propose FairMoE-FL, a novel FL framework that integrates a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture with fairness-aware optimization. FairMoE-FL employs sparse expert activation and dual-level routing with lightweight local adapters, reducing communication while preserving personalization. To ensure equitable outcomes, we introduce fairness-regularized objectives that penalize accuracy disparity, balance expert usage, and incorporate communication cost constraints. Extensive experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 show that FairMoE-FL consistently improves accuracy and fairness across clients while transmitting fewer parameters than baseline methods. These results highlight the potential of conditional computation with fairness-aware optimization for scalable, efficient, and equitable FL in heterogeneous environments.

title: When Critics Disagree: Adaptive Reward Poisoning Attacks in RIS-Aided Wireless Control System.
abstract: Reward-poisoning attacks present a significant risk to learning-based wireless control systems. Given this, we propose a Disagreement-Guided Reward Poisoning (DGRP) adaptive attack on a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) agent. In a Cognitive Radio Network (CRN) environment assisted by Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS), the SAC agent is tasked with maximizing the long-term secondary users’ (SUs) rate by simultaneously optimizing the transmission power of the SU transmitter and the RIS phase shifts. DGRP corrupts rewards, particularly when the SAC dual critics exhibit substantial disagreement—especially in high-leverage, high-uncertainty states—resulting in distorted value estimations and guiding the policy towards suboptimal actions. Our findings demonstrate that DGRP substantially diminishes the performance improvements typically provided by RIS and degrades transmission quality. We further investigate key attack parameters and determine their impact on learning. In comparison to periodic-timing and exploration-triggered baselines, DGRP consistently causes greater damage, highlighting the necessity of considering disagreement-aware threats when evaluating the robustness of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) in RIS-assisted networks.

title: Unsupervised Out-of-Distribution Sample Selection for Reliable ML in Wireless Systems.
abstract: Incorporating Machine Learning (ML) approaches within wireless systems hinges on their ability to handle real-world variability. In practice, data will inevitably deviate from the training distribution due to new devices, changing environments, and unforeseen interference. Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection provides a safeguard by identifying these shifts before they lead to unreliable model behavior. To address this challenge, we develop a multi-stage OOD detection algorithm and evaluate it on the publicly available 3GPP NR CSI Compression dataset, which contains high-dimensional Channel State Information (CSI) representative of realistic wireless propagation. First, we perform coarse OOD detection by measuring the distance of incoming samples to in-distribution class centers, flagging those that lie beyond a threshold. We then apply fine OOD detection using density-based clustering to filter spurious anomalies and isolate dense clusters that representing meaningful shifts. While these stages identify OOD samples, retraining on all of them is inefficient. Instead, we rank the selected OOD samples by discriminativeness (distance from the ID distribution) and diversity (feature dissimilarity), ensuring that retraining incorporates only the most informative examples. In our analysis, coarse detection led to a 6.93% increase in reconstruction Mean Squared Error (MSE), fine detection raised it to 37.6%, and incorporating discriminativeness–diversity ranking further increased it to 45.5%. While MSE is typically minimized during training, a higher reconstruction error for detected samples indicates stronger deviation from the learned manifold. This increase confirms that the detected OOD samples reflect realistic wireless variations, reinforcing the framework’s value for reliable ML deployment in dynamic environments.

title: Advancing Responsible AI in 6G: Toward Trustworthy and Sustainable Predictive Handover.
abstract: The evolution to 6G brings widespread intelligence across the cloud–edge–device continuum and places AI at the core of autonomous network control. Predictive handover is a key use case in the radio domain that enables seamless connectivity and mobility in next-generation networks. Yet, using AI for such systems demands a careful balance between accuracy, energy efficiency, robustness, and explainability. This paper describes how Responsible AI aspects can be considered when designing a concrete use case like Predictive Handover, supported by responsibility-related metrics and integrating them into both development and monitoring processes. These metrics enable continuous evaluation to ensure trustworthy and sustainable operation while maintaining service-level performance. Our goal is to guide the design, deployment, and oversight of AI models in 6G while delivering both technical excellence and ethical accountability for future wireless networks. Evaluations of the LSTM, CNN, and Transformer architectures show that the CNN’s compact inference path yields strong energy-efficiency gains, while the LSTM and Transformer exhibit complementary strengths—high attribution concentration for the LSTM and a well-balanced combination of robustness and explainability for the Transformer.

title: Robust Composite DNA Storage under Sampling Randomness, Substitution, and Insertion-Deletion Errors.
abstract: DNA data storage offers a high-density, long-term alternative to traditional storage systems, addressing the exponential growth of digital data. Composite DNA extends this paradigm by leveraging mixtures of nucleotides to increase storage capacity beyond the four standard bases. In this work, we model composite DNA storage as a multinomial channel and draw an analogy to digital modulation by representing composite letters on the three-dimensional probability simplex. To mitigate errors caused by sampling randomness, we derive transition probabilities and log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) for each constellation point and employ practical channel codes for error correction. We then extend this framework to substitution and insertion-deletion (ID) channels, proposing constellation update rules that account for these additional impairments. Numerical results demonstrate that our approach achieves reliable performance with existing LDPC codes, comparing prior schemes designed for limited-magnitude probability errors, whose performance degrades significantly under sampling randomness.

title: Improved Data Rates for Radar-centric ISAC with Index and Phase Modulations.
abstract: This work presents a radar-centric integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system that employs both index modulation (IM) and phase modulation (PM) to enable simultaneous data transmission and radar sensing. Frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) chirps are modulated using IM and PM, forming IM-PM-FMCW signals that carry communication data while maintaining radar functionality. The proposed design enables the dynamic reconfiguration of waveform parameters (e.g., chirp duration, bandwidth, and phase coding), allowing for a flexible trade-off between communication throughput and sensing performance, depending on the specific application requirements. Simulation results demonstrate that the system can achieve reliable radar performance while efficiently transmitting data to the users. The approach provides a flexible and adaptive framework for future radar-centric ISAC applications, particularly in vehicular scenarios where both high-resolution sensing and efficient communication are essential.

title: Edge Learning via Federated Split Decision Transformers for Metaverse Resource Allocation.
abstract: Mobile edge computing (MEC) based wireless metaverse services offer an untethered, immersive experience to users, where the superior quality of experience (QoE) needs to be achieved under stringent latency constraints and visual quality demands. To achieve this, MEC-based intelligent resource allocation for virtual reality users needs to be supported by coordination across MEC servers to harness distributed data. Federated learning (FL) is a promising solution, and can be combined with reinforcement learning (RL) to develop generalized policies across MEC-servers. However, conventional FL incurs transmitting the full model parameters across the MEC-servers and the cloud, and suffer performance degradation due to naive global aggregation, especially in heterogeneous multi-radio access technology environments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes Federated Split Decision Transformer (FSDT), an offline RL framework where the transformer model is partitioned between MEC servers and the cloud. Agent-specific components (e.g., MEC-based embedding and prediction layers) enable local adaptability, while shared global layers in the cloud facilitate cooperative training across MEC servers. Experimental results demonstrate that FSDT enhances QoE for up to 10% in heterogeneous environments compared to baselines, while offloading nearly 98% of the transformer model parameters to the cloud, thereby reducing the computational burden on MEC servers.

title: Flexible Intelligent Metasurfaces for Enhancing MIMO Integrated Sensing and Communications.
abstract: This paper explores the application of flexible intelligent metasurfaces (FIMs) in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Unlike conventional rigid antenna arrays (RAAs), FIMs can actively reshape their surface shapes by adjusting the vertical displacements of elements, thereby enabling real-time geometric reconfiguration. Such flexibility provides additional degrees of freedom for joint communication and sensing design. Focusing on point target sensing, we adopt the trace of the Cramér–Rao bound (CRB) matrix as the primary measure of estimation accuracy, while MIMO channel capacity serves as the communication metric. To balance the two objectives, we formulate a weighted optimization problem and develop an efficient block coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm to alternately update the transmit covariance matrix and the FIMs geometry. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed FIM-assisted ISAC system achieves superior performance compared with RAAs, offering significantly reduced CRB for a given capacity level.

title: Quantum-secured Explainable TinyFL for Military Battlefield Space Stations over NTN Satellite RAN.
abstract: The enhanced complexity and importance of military communication infrastructure in space has forced the necessity to develop solutions to can ensure security, low latency, interpretable, and intelligent threat detection solutions. The present paper introduces a framework Rationale AI-Driven Quantum-secured Lightweight Federated Learning that can be deployed to categorize the DDoS attacks in 5G-enabling non-terrestrial Networks (NTN) Radio Access Networks in the high-level military space stations. The framework consists of TinyML that are enabled in the satellite nodes to help develop privacy enhancing federated learning by way of Federated Learning (FL). The E91 protocol, particularly, Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) offers security to the model update transmissions at the best possible system performance (latency and energy efficiency). Moreover, Explainable AI methods like SHAP and LIME are incorporated in the model to grant transparency and interpretability of the model predictions, which will increase faith and understanding of the workings to make mission-critical choices. As experimental findings indicate, after Round 5 of training, the suggested structure has a global classification accuracy of 99.87% and a loss of 0.0461, which is much lower than communication overhead but has guaranteed quantum-secured model integrity. These results confirm the feasibility of the framework in critical military spaceborne IoT network and defense applications in battlefield.

title: Low-Complexity Port Selection for Fluid Antenna Systems.
abstract: This paper focuses on the port selection problem of a discrete fluid antenna system (FAS). We consider the uplink of a multi-user setup where an FAS is employed at the receiver. The objective is to maximize the overall sum rate based on a linear minimum mean squared error (LMMSE) combiner. Identifying the complexity of optimal selection, we propose a maximum distance-based sub-optimal low-complexity port selection algorithm, where ports are selected such that the minimum Euclidean distance between selected ports is maximized. We also propose two other sub-optimal algorithms, namely sequential selection, where ports are selected sequentially, and orthogonal selection, where ports that maximize the orthogonal user power are selected. Comparing with several benchmark methods, we demonstrate that the proposed sub-optimal low-complexity algorithms effectively reduce computational cost while maintaining performance close to optimal selection. In particular, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed maximum distance-based method enables a flexible performance–complexity trade-off through appropriate selection of its design parameter.

title: Robust Semantic Transmission for Low-Altitude UAVs: Predictive Channel-Aware Scheduling and Generative Reconstruction.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) downlink transmission facilitates critical time-sensitive visual applications but is fundamentally constrained by bandwidth scarcity and dynamic channel impairments. The rapid fluctuation of the air-to-ground (A2G) link creates a regime where reliable transmission slots are intermittent and future channel quality can only be predicted with uncertainty. Conventional deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) methods transmit coupled feature streams, causing global reconstruction failure when specific time slots experience deep fading. Decoupling semantic content into a deterministic structure component and a stochastic texture component enables differentiated error protection strategies aligned with channel reliability. A predictive transmission framework is developed that utilizes a split-stream variational codec and a channel-aware scheduler to prioritize the delivery of structural layout over reliable slots. Experimental evaluations indicate that this approach achieves a 5.6 dB gain in peak signal-to-noise (SNR) ratio over single-stream baselines and maintains structural fidelity under significant prediction mismatch.

title: Energy-Accuracy Tradeoff-Aware Adaptive Collaborative Inference.
abstract: Driven by the rapid proliferation of edge inference, collaborative inference among edge devices has emerged as a promising paradigm for addressing resource constraints in computationally intensive tasks. However, existing approaches often suffer from inefficient utilization of heterogeneous resources and lack dynamic adaptation to varying device capabilities and network conditions. To address these challenges, we present a novel collaborative inference framework that prioritizes energy-accuracy co-optimization through workload partitioning and resource-aware model pruning. Specifically, we first design a workload partitioning strategy aimed at maximizing resource utilization efficiency in heterogeneous environments. Dynamically distributes image slices to edge devices by closely matching tasks with their specific computational, energy, and network profiles, ensuring balanced load and minimized latency. Moreover, we propose an adaptive pruning method that is aware of energy-accuracy tradeoffs. It is equipped with dual predictors that model the accuracy and energy consumption under different pruning rates in real-time, enabling dynamic pruning rate selection to optimally balance performance with energy efficiency. The experimental results on the VisDrone2019 dataset demonstrate that our method achieves significant improvements over existing approaches, improving detection accuracy by up to 1.3% in mAP50 while increasing inference speed by 5.3× compared to slicing methods. Furthermore, our adaptive pruning strategy reduces energy consumption by up to 32% while maintaining comparable accuracy across various edge devices, such as the NVIDIA AGX Orin and Jetson TX2.

title: Satellife: Lightweight and Fast Traffic Data Estimation in LEO Mega-constellation Networks.
abstract: The proliferation of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) mega-constellations has revolutionized global connectivity, but the dynamic network topologies and constrained satellite resources pose significant challenges in achieving fast, accurate, and resource-efficient traffic data measurement. Traditional traffic estimation methods, such as tensor decompositions, struggle to capture nonlinear spatio-temporal dependencies, while machine learning approaches face computational complexity and limited on-board resources in satellite environment. To address these challenges, this paper introduces Satellife, a lightweight and fast traffic data estimation framework. Our compression module employs Lagrange interpolation to achieve dimensionality reduction, effectively alleviating computational burdens. The core innovation is an AdamGCN co-tuning mechanism that ensures robust data estimation while maintaining a lightweight neural network architecture. Experiments on large-scale datasets demonstrate that Satellife achieves high estimation accuracy, comparable to state-of-the-art schemes, while offering superior inference time and memory usage performance.

title: Policy-Guided MCTS for near Maximum-Likelihood Decoding of Short Codes.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a policy-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) decoder that achieves near maximum-likelihood decoding (MLD) performance for short block codes. The MCTS decoder searches for test error patterns (TEPs) in the received information bits and obtains codeword candidates through re-encoding. The TEP search is executed on a tree structure, guided by a neural network policy trained via MCTS-based learning. The trained policy guides the decoder to find the correct TEPs with minimal steps from the root node (all-zero TEP). The decoder outputs the codeword with maximum likelihood when the early stopping criterion is satisfied. The proposed method requires no Gaussian elimination (GE) compared to ordered statistics decoding (OSD) and can reduce search complexity by 95\% compared to non-GE OSD. It achieves lower decoding latency than both OSD and non-GE OSD at high SNRs.

title: Blockchain-Enabled Secure Traffic Rerouting in P4-based Computing Systems.
Efficient Shaping Modulation using Circular Symmetric Hexagonal Constellation and Nonbinary Polar Coding.
abstract: This paper proposes a coded modulation scheme that utilizes circular symmetric hexagonal constellations and nonbinary polar coding. Hexagonal constellations are known as the most efficient 2-dimensional constellations in terms of signal point density. However, a major drawback of hexagonal constellations is their unsuitability for bit-based transmission. To address this issue, our scheme directly maps coded symbols obtained using q-ary polar coding to points on a q-ary hexagonal constellation. This allows us to leverage the advantages of the circular symmetric hexagonal constellations, namely higher coded modulation capacity and a larger minimum Euclidean distance compared to square constellations. Furthermore, by applying probabilistic shaping to this scheme, we demonstrate that the proposed coded modulation scheme achieves performance close to the random coding bound.

title: Beyond-Diagonal RIS for MIMO Systems: Boosting Block-Level Interference Exploitation Precoding.
abstract: The constructive interference (CI)-based block-level precoding (CI-BLP) approach reduces computational complexity compared to conventional CI-based symbol-level precoding (CI-SLP) method and provides additional design flexibility due to its relaxed block-level power budget. However, employing a constant precoding matrix within each block restricts the system’s degrees of freedom (DoFs), leading to performance degradation for large block lengths. To overcome this limitation, we propose the use of a beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS) to increase the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system’s design DoFs. Specifically, we jointly optimize the BLP matrix and the block-level BD-RIS reflection matrix using an alternating optimization (AO) framework. The BLP matrix optimization subproblem admits a closed-form solution and can be reformulated as a quadratic programming (QP) problem, while the BD-RIS reflection subproblem is solved via an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results show that BD-RIS aided CI-BLP approach substantially outperforms conventional designs, achieving significant CI gains owing to its enhanced design flexibility.

title: On the Ambiguity Functions of Delay-Doppler Domain Multicarrier Modulation (DDMC).
abstract: Delay-Doppler (DD)-domain multicarrier modulation (DDMC) is a recently proposed DD-domain modulation technique. Ambiguity functions (AFs) of their prototype pulses provide a useful tool for analyzing the communication and sensing performance of DDMC. In this paper, we study the auto-ambiguity functions (AAFs) and cross-ambiguity functions (CAFs) of DDMC prototype pulses. We demonstrate their quasi-periodic properties and the influence of the subpulse, system parameters, and cyclic extension (CE). We also present an AF-based analysis of monostatic sensing using random DDMC frames and examine the resulting sensing resolution and ambiguity characteristics.

title: Towards an ontology for the governance of secure, resilient and interoperable digital twins.
abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) rely on continuous, real-time or near-real time data exchange, often spanning organisational and, increasingly sectoral boundaries, thereby increasing security, resilience and interoperability requirements (SRI). This paper reports preliminary findings that aim to inform the design of a proof-of-concept SRI governance ontology for DTs. The study follows an iterative workflow that integrates (i) a standards-informed approach to capturing relevant requirements and shared terminology, and (ii) interview-derived socio-technical themes to address practical governance concerns that are under-specified in formal documentation. These sources are consolidated into a structured set of candidate SRI governance themes, which are then used to inform subsequent ontology modelling. Overall, the work highlights some design considerations for more integrated SRI governance in DTs and provides a starting point for future ontology development and evaluation in an operational DT environment.

title: Experimental Performance of Deterministic Identification for Goal-Oriented Communications in AWGN Channels.
abstract: In this paper we investigate the performance of deterministic identification (DI) in additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels by implementing a constructive DI code designed for AWGN channels in order to demonstrate both experimentally and via simulations performance advantages of using DI codes instead of a classical Shannon transmission model in goal-oriented communications. In order to optimize the verification process, we present a procedure to find optimized radii of the decoding regions at each analyzed signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) level for the worst case, when the Hamming distance between two codewords is minimal. At the receiver, such radii are used to define the decoding regions for reliable verification of the DI hypothesis test. We compare the performance of DI against Shannon transmission both in simulations and hardware experiments using software-defined radios, and show the advantages of using DI to ensure goal-oriented communications even in low-SNR scenarios, where uncoded classical communication fails.

title: Multiuser Physical-Layer Key Generation for FDD Wireless Systems.
abstract: This paper presents a novel group secret key generation (GSKG) protocol for multiuser wireless FDD systems with a star topology. While most existing GSKG schemes are tailored to TDD systems, their counterparts for FDD systems remain largely unexplored due to the inherent lack of reciprocity between uplink and downlink channels. To address this limitation, we exploit the reciprocity of the scattering matrix parameters S12and S21within the same frequency range and utilize amplitude, absolute phase, and phase differences between neighboring antennas as reciprocal features for pairwise key generation. Furthermore, we propose a novel group key construction method based on the concatenation of pairwise keys, combined with a secure group key distribution mechanism that enhances security and increases the effective key length compared to conventional XOR-based approaches. Extensive indoor experiments confirm that the proposed scheme achieves low key disagreement rates, strong randomness, and high robustness against eavesdropping.

title: Bidirectional Information Forwarding in LDPC-Coded Binary Markov Sources.
abstract: This paper addresses the decoding of Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes for correlated binary Markov sources transmitted over AWGN channels. Conventional decoders typically assume independent bits, failing to exploit the memory inherent in practical data sources. We propose a bidirectional information forwarding algorithm that dynamically updates a-priori log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) through a specialized message-passing schedule along the variable nodes. Unlike standard joint source-channel decoding structures, our approach integrates Markov dependencies without the structural complexity of static graph expansion. By utilizing recursive forward and backward updates, the proposed scheme refines the inputs to the LDPC decoder iteratively. Simulation results confirm that the proposed bidirectional approach consistently outperforms standard belief propagation and the proposed unidirectional approaches, achieving coding gains of up to 2.17 dB and approaching the Shannon limit within 3.75 dB for highly correlated sources.

title: LUT-GenNet: Target-PSNR- and Input-Guided Neural Lookup Table for Adaptive Rate Control in Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding.
abstract: Deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) is a promising technology for high efficiency wireless image transmission, but many existing models adopt a fixed compression rate. To address this problem, this paper proposes a DeepJSCC with lookup table generation network (LUT-GenNet), a novel scheme that provides peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) guaranteed adaptive compression rate control. Conventional adaptive rate control approaches determine the compression ratio after encoding, which makes a processing bottleneck. Furthermore, since the encoder requires channel SNR information, if the channel SNR changes after it is obtained and encoding is performed, the image quality can degrade significantly. The proposed LUT-GenNet is a neural network that generates an image-specific LUT directly from the input image. This LUT instantaneously determines the optimal compression rate based on the target PSNR and channel SNR. This approach enables parallel processing of encoding and rate determination and avoids the SNR mismatch problem because the encoder does not rely on SNR feedback. A comparison with the conventional method under SNR mismatch conditions showed that while the conventional performance degrades significantly as the mismatch increases, the proposed method maintains stable.

title: Resilience Optimization in 6G and Beyond Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Networks: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: Ensuring network resilience in 6G and beyond is essential to maintain service continuity during base station (BS) outages due to failures, disasters, attacks, or energy-saving operations. This paper proposes a novel resilience optimization framework for integrated satellite-terrestrial networks (ISTNs), leveraging low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites to assist users when terrestrial BSs are unavailable. Specifically, we develop a realistic multi-cell model incorporating user association, antenna downtilt adaptation, power control, heterogeneous traffic demands, and dynamic user distribution. The objective is to maximize of the total user rate in the considered area by optimizing the BS’s antenna tilt, transmission power, user association to neighboring BS or to a LEO satellite with a minimum number of successfully served user satisfaction constraint, defined by rate and Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP) requirements. To solve the non-convex, NP-hard problem, we design a deep Q-network (DQN)-based algorithm to learn network dynamics to maximize throughput while minimizing LEO satellite usage, thereby limiting reliance on links with longer propagation delays and prolonging satellite operational lifetime. Simulation results confirm that our approach significantly outperforms the benchmark one.

title: FTA-NTN: Fairness and Throughput Assurance in Non-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: Designing optimal non-terrestrial network (NTN) constellations is essential for maximizing throughput and ensuring fair resource distribution. This paper presents FTA-NTN (Fairness and Throughput Assurance in Non-Terrestrial Networks), a multi-objective optimization framework that jointly maximizes throughput and fairness under realistic system constraints. The framework integrates multi-layer Walker Delta constellations, a parametric mobility model for user distributions across Canadian land regions, adaptive K-Means clustering for beamforming and user association, and Bayesian optimization for parameter tuning. Simulation results with 500 users show that FTA-NTN achieves over 9.88 Gbps of aggregate throughput with an average fairness of 0.42, corresponding to an optimal configuration of 9 planes with 15 satellites per plane in LEO and 7 planes with 3 satellites per plane in MEO. These values align with 3GPP NTN evaluation scenarios and representative system assumptions, confirming their relevance for realistic deployments. Overall, FTA-NTN demonstrates that throughput and fairness can be jointly optimized under practical constraints, advancing beyond throughput-centric designs in the literature and offering a scalable methodology for next-generation NTN deployments that supports efficient and equitable global connectivity.

title: Learning-Based Sensor Scheduling for Delay-Aware and Stable Remote State Estimation.
abstract: Unpredictable sensor-to-estimator delays fundamentally distort what matters for wireless remote state estimation: not just freshness, but how delay interacts with sensor informativeness and energy efficiency. In this paper, we present a unified, delay-aware framework that models this coupling explicitly and quantifies a delay-dependent information gain, motivating an information-per-joule scheduling objective beyond age of information proxies (AoI). To this end, we first introduce an efficient posterior-fusion update that incorporates delayed measurements without state augmentation, providing a consistent approximation to optimal delayed Kalman updates, and then derive tractable stability conditions ensuring that bounded estimation error is achievable under stochastic, delayed scheduling. This conditions highlight the need for unstable modes to be observable across sensors. Building on this foundation, we cast scheduling as a Markov decision process and develop a proximal policy optimization (PPO) scheduler that learns directly from interaction, requires no prior delay model, and explicitly trades off estimation accuracy, freshness, sensor heterogeneity, and transmission energy through normalized rewards. In simulations with heterogeneous sensors, realistic link-energy models, and random delays, the proposed method learns stably and consistently achieves lower estimation error at comparable energy than random scheduling and strong RL baselines (DQN, A2C), while remaining robust to variations in measurement availability and process/measurement noise.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Dynamic Resource Allocation in Cell-Free Massive MIMO.
abstract: In this paper, we consider power allocation and antenna activation of cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CFmMIMO) systems. We first derive closed-form expressions for the system spectral efficiency (SE) and energy efficiency (EE) as functions of the power allocation coefficients and the number of active antennas at the access points (APs). Then, we aim to enhance the EE through jointly optimizing antenna activation and power control. This task leads to a non-convex and mixed-integer design problem with high-dimensional design variables. To address this, we propose a novel DRL-based framework, in which the agent learns to map large-scale fading coefficients to AP activation ratio, antenna coefficient, and power coefficient. These coefficients are then employed to determine the number of active antennas per AP and the power factors assigned to users based on closed-form expressions. By optimizing these parameters instead of directly controlling antenna selection and power allocation, the proposed method transforms the intractable optimization into a low-dimensional learning task. Our extensive simulations demonstrate the efficiency and scalability of the proposed scheme. Specifically, in a CFmMIMO system with 40 APs and 20 users, it achieves a 50% EE improvement and 3350 times run time reduction compared to the conventional sequential convex approximation method.

title: Evaluation of EMF Exposure to Throughput Ratio for Sustainable 5G Networks.
abstract: This paper builds stochastic geometry frameworks for analyzing downlink electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure and efficiency in 5G multi-connectivity networks, using 5G E-UTRAN New Radio - Dual Connectivity (EN-DC) configuration as a representative use case. The Poisson point process (PPP) and the β-Ginibre point process (β-GPP) are used to model the spatial distribution of base stations (BSs), where β-GPP effectively captures the repulsion observed in real deployments. We derive tractable expressions for the distribution of EMF exposure and validate the framework through both Monte Carlo simulations and real BS data from Paris. In addition to conventional metrics, we introduce the Radiated Energy per Bit Transmitted in the Downlink (REBT-DL), which accounts for throughput and received power. Results show that network configuration significantly affect exposure and REBT-DL, highlighting the relevance of energy-aware deployment strategies and confirming the proposed approach as a comprehensive tool for sustainable network evaluation. The results also confirm that β-GPP provides a more accurate fit to practical deployments than PPP.

title: O-RAN 7.2x Deployment: Insights from Laboratory Integration to Field Trials.
abstract: Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) enables flexible, multi-vendor cellular networks through open interfaces and hardware-software decoupling. The 3GPP Option 7.2x intra-PHY split separates PHY-high processing in the Open Distributed Unit (O-DU) from PHY-low and RF processing in the Open Radio Unit (O-RU), and is realized through the O-RAN 7.2x Open Fronthaul (OFH) specification. Although open-source 5G Radio Access Network (RAN) and Core stacks support such deployments, few studies provide detailed accounts of End-to-End (E2E) integration, Radio Frequency (RF) tuning, synchronization, and lab-to-field performance evaluation. In this work, we present an E2E O-RAN 7.2x deployment that integrates open-source Open Centralized Unit (O-CU)/O-DU and Core components with a commercial O-RU. The system is evaluated with a Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) User Equipment (UE) in indoor and outdoor environments, including distances up to 1.2 km. The measured downlink (DL) and uplink (UL) throughput reaches the maximum achievable for the given RAN configuration under optimal channel conditions. Practical insights from laboratory integration to field trials are provided, covering hardware/software configurations, Lower-Layer Split (LLS) selection, synchronization, RF tuning, and benchmarking methodology, with detailed integration and tuning procedures made available on GitHub. This work serves as a reference for reproducible O-RAN 7.2x deployments with open-source RAN stacks and commercial O-RUs.

title: Robust Wireless Resource Allocation Against Adversarial Jamming.
abstract: We study the problem of bandwidth allocation in a wireless network in the presence of adversarial jamming. Specifically, we consider a setting in which the network designer acts first and allocates bandwidth to users, before an adversary applies a jamming strategy to reduce the bandwidth of a subset (or all) of the access points. We consider a strong adversary who has complete information and can optimize the jamming strategy, subject to power budget constraints. In turn, the network designer must allocate resources in anticipation of the adversary’s actions.We explain that our model gives rise to a special network interdiction model, which differs from the standard setting in two ways: The first is that the interdictor is given the benefit of responding, rather than leading the game. The second is that the interdiction is fractional and performed at the node level of the network. The interdiction then propagates to all edges incident to the access point.In terms of technical results, we provide a bandwidth allocation algorithm that is based on linear programming duality and show that the algorithm can solve the problem optimally, assuming knowledge of the adversary’s budget constraints. We conduct experiments on synthetic data to show the extent to which the algorithm improves the total utilized bandwidth over the algorithm that optimizes bandwidth allocation while being oblivious to the adversary’s existence. Evaluating our algorithm on a data set with realistic instance parameters, we observe improvements in the range of 10 − 50% as the adversary’s jamming budget increases.

title: User-Centric Hardware Acceleration for Energy-Efficient Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: The rapid increase in mobile data traffic necessitates a highly energy-efficient radio access network (RAN) architecture. In cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) systems, hardware accelerators (ACCs) for physical-layer signal processing consume considerable static power because they must remain active to support control functions even during low-traffic periods. To address this inefficiency, we propose a user-centric hardware acceleration (UC-HA) architecture that separates signal processing into control-channel and per-user data-channel, and dynamically activates per-user ACCs according to user activity. A 5G outdoor testbed implementing UC-HA validates its feasibility and shows comparable throughput performance to conventional acceleration. Large-scale simulations in a 1 km2urban network calibrated by real power measurements demonstrate up to a 37% reduction in daily energy consumption compared with network-centric architectures. These results indicate that UC-HA constitutes a scalable and sustainable hardware platform for future green CF-mMIMO deployments.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Friendly Jamming for Secure ISAC Under Channel Uncertainty.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication enables efficient spectrum sharing by jointly performing radar sensing and wireless transmission. This paper proposes a deep learning–driven framework for secure ISAC under imperfect channel state information (CSI) and unknown eavesdropper (Eve) locations. Unlike conventional friendly jamming (FJ) methods requiring Eve’s CSI or precise angle-of-arrival (AoA), the proposed approach leverages radar echo feedback to guide directional jamming without explicit Eve information. To ensure robustness against sensing uncertainty, we introduce a radar-aware neural network that jointly optimises beamforming and jamming using a nonparametric Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) estimator based on f-divergence. The design satisfies Cramér–Rao lower bound constraints under noisy AoA. A quantised tensor-train encoder reduces model size substantially while maintaining performance. A non-overlapping secure subband scheme further isolates communication channels. Simulations demonstrate higher secrecy rates, reliable BLER, and robustness to CSI and angular errors, confirming the practicality of learning-based secure ISAC.

title: Ergodic Rate Analysis of Two-State Pinching-Antenna Systems.
abstract: Flexible Antenna Systems (FAS) are a key enabler of next-generation wireless networks, allowing the antenna aperture to be dynamically reconfigured to adapt to channel conditions and service requirements. In this context, pinching-antenna systems (PASs) implemented on software-controllable dielectric waveguides provide the ability to reconfigure both channel characteristics and path loss by selectively exciting discrete radiation points. Existing works, however, typically assume continuously adjustable pinching positions, neglecting the spatial discreteness imposed by practical implementations. This paper develops a closed-form analytical framework for the ergodic rate of two-state PASs, where pinching antennas are fixed and only their activation states are controlled. To quantify the impact of spatial discretization, pinching discretization efficiency is introduced, characterizing the performance gap relative to the ideal continuous case. Finally, numerical results show that near-continuous performance can be achieved with a limited number of pinching points, providing design insights for scalable PASs.

title: Joint Beamforming and Resource Allocation for ISAC-Enabled UAV Networks in Disaster Response.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is becoming an important approach in modern wireless networks by combining sensing and communication within shared hardware. However, deploying such systems in complex scenarios like disaster environments, where infrastructure is often damaged, remains challenging. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) enhance ISAC capabilities due to their mobility, flexibility, and cost efficiency, making them well-suited for time-critical operations. In this study, an ISAC-enabled UAV framework is proposed for disaster response, where UAVs simultaneously perform environmental sensing, such as survivor detection and debris mapping, while maintaining reliable communication with ground stations. A unified system model is developed to jointly optimize beamforming, power allocation, and resource partitioning between sensing and communication while ensuring a minimum communication quality of service (QoS). Additionally, an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM)-based dual-functional waveform is introduced to balance sensing accuracy and communication performance. Simulation results demonstrate improved sensing coverage and communication reliability compared to conventional schemes, along with reduced hardware complexity and more efficient spectrum utilization.

title: Supporting Over-the-Air Updates over Urban 5G Networks: Insights from a Real-World Study.
abstract: Over-the-Air (OTA) updates constitute a fundamental service for modern vehicles, providing the critical capability of update-ability upon which many other use cases depend. While previous studies have investigated technological advancements to improve their efficiency and adoption, such as ad-hoc communication schemes and edge caching, few have evaluated their actual impact on production communication networks. This study presents the first comprehensive numerical evaluation of how large-scale automotive OTA updates affect network congestion at the radio-access network (RAN) level in urban environments. Leveraging empirical network data and simulated urban vehicle mobility data from the city of Barcelona, Spain, a numerical evaluation is provided to determine the impact of massive OTA updates in physical resource block (PRB) usage and temporal network congestion variations. Specifically, a massive OTA update scenario to thousands of vehicles in an urban environment is considered. Evaluation results demonstrate substantial variations in PRB usage during OTA updates, both across cells and over time. In the worst affected cells, PRB load increases by up to 30%, while other cells with similar vehicle densities remain largely unaffected. Moreover, the temporal distribution of vehicle connectivity shows that peak-hour usage of vehicle and background traffic is highly correlated, further increasing the load on already congested cells. These findings demonstrate the need for adaptive OTA update planning strategies to alleviate network congestion while ensuring timely updates for all vehicles.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Implicit Hate Speech Detection.
abstract: Implicit Hate Speech (IHS) is proliferating exponentially on all social platforms, including X, 4Chan, Telegram, GAB, among others. IHS language is used to evade AI content moderation policies on social platforms, since these policies aim to mitigate hate speech and create a safer online space. However, current AI models rely solely on Explicit hate speech and n-words directed at a particular group or community. In this work, we introduce a Pragmatic Analysis Framework (PAF) that consists of four linguistic components in the context of hate speech in Islam. Semantic Field Activation (SFA), Lexical Manipulation Detection (LMD), Presuppositional Bias Analysis (PBA), and Pragmatic Inference Detection (PID). We first defined coding statements for Explicit hate speech using defined slurs and terms, which are toxic, and current AI techniques can easily flag them, such as semi-coded terms pislam and muzrat; including general cursing terms such as f**k and b**ch. Next, we use Large Language Model (LLM) prompts to categorize posts as explicit or implicit, and then use PAF to classify them into four linguistic categories. Our analysis shows that both GPT and Claude treat lexical manipulation differently, and both architectures show strength in PAF analysis. Moreover, to better understand Islamophobic discourse, we also perform topic modeling of these explicit and implicit terms and find that Islamophobic discourse is often linked to political tensions and events.

title: Propagation and Rate-Aware Cell Switching Optimization in HAPS-Assisted Wireless Networks.
abstract: Cell switching is a promising approach for improving energy efficiency in wireless networks; however, existing studies largely rely on simplified models and energy-centric formulations that overlook key performance-limiting factors. This paper revisits the cell switching concept by redefining its modeling assumptions and mathematical formulation, explicitly incorporating realistic propagation effects such as building entry loss (BEL) and atmospheric losses relevant to non-terrestrial networks (NTN), particularly high-altitude platform station (HAPS). Beyond proposing a new cell switching strategy, the conventional energy-focused problem is reformulated as a multi-objective optimization framework that jointly minimizes power consumption, unconnected users, and data rate degradation. Through this reformulation, the proposed methods ensure that energy-efficient operation is achieved without compromising user connectivity and data rate performance, thereby inherently supporting sustainability objectives for sixth-generation (6G) networks. To solve this reformulated problem, two complementary approaches are employed: the weighted sum method (WSM), which enables a flexible and adaptive weighting mechanism, and the -constraint-inspired method ( CM), which converts connectivity and rate-related objectives into constraints within the conventional energy-focused problem. Moreover, unlike prior work relying only on simulations, this study combines system-level simulations with Sionna–OpenAirInterface (OAI) based emulation on a smaller network to validate the proposed cell switching concept under realistic conditions. The results show that, compared to the conventional approach, WSM reduces rate degradation for up to 70% for high-loss indoor users and eliminates the 44% drop for low-loss indoor users.

title: 3D Depth-Sensing Framework for Hand-Object Interaction in Microgravity Environments.
abstract: -Understanding human interaction and object manipulation in microgravity is essential for effective astronaut training and mission design. The absence of gravitational cues introduces unique challenges in motion control, perception, and coordination. Although real microgravity experiments conducted through parabolic flights or orbital missions provide valuable data, they remain costly and infrequent. To address these limitations, this work proposes a depth-based simulation framework that replicates 3D hand-object interaction in various gravity environments. The system employs an active infrared stereo sensing module to capture synchronized color and depth data in real time. Then, the video stream is processed to estimate the hand position and calculate its coordinates in 3D space. These coordinates are transmitted to a physics-driven simulation engine built on Open3D, which represents the hand and controls its interaction with free-floating objects through a discrete Newtonian motion model. In addition, the visualization environment includes adjustable gravity parameters, hand tracking, and gravity-responsive object motion. The experiments are conducted under a range of gravity scenarios to evaluate the tracking accuracy and interaction robustness. Moreover, the observed results confirm that the proposed framework provides stable depth-based tracking and realistic hand-object interaction that offers a cost-effective and accessible platform for astronaut training and microgravity research.

title: Towards Green O-RAN: A QoS-Aware Energy Optimisation Framework for Network Slicing.
abstract: Making Energy Efficiency (EE) gains is a critical priority for Mobile Network Operators (MNOs). New open and disaggregated architectures such as Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) with Intelligent RAN Controllers (RICs) provide opportunities for optimised energy efficient control and management of radio resources. In this paper, we propose a Quality of Service (QoS) aware energy optimisation framework based on reinforcement learning (RL)-informed Advanced Sleep Modes (ASMs) to dynamically manage RF channels. Our proposed framework specifically addresses the unique QoS characteristics of diverse network slices by dynamically applying ASMs to RF channels for a single O-RU based on each slice traffic pattern. Simulation results exhibits up to 64% energy savings under low traffic without any QoS violations. Even under high URLLC and medium eMBB loads, URLLC QoS violations of less than 0.5% are reported with 25% energy savings. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in achieving substantial energy efficiencies while preserving service-level performance in multi-slice 5G networks.

title: Neural Beamforming with Doppler-Aware Sparse Attention for High Mobility Environments.
abstract: Beamforming has significance for enhancing spectral efficiency and mitigating interference in multi-antenna wireless systems, facilitating spatial multiplexing and diversity in dense and high mobility scenarios. Traditional beamforming techniques such as zero-forcing beamforming (ZFBF) and minimum mean square error (MMSE) beamforming experience performance deterioration under adverse channel conditions. Deep learning-based beamforming offers an alternative with nonlinear mappings from channel state information (CSI) to beamforming weights by improving robustness against dynamic channel environments. Transformer-based models are particularly effective due to their ability to model long-range dependencies across time and frequency. However, their quadratic attention complexity limits scalability in large OFDM grids. Recent studies address this issue through sparse attention mechanisms that reduce complexity while maintaining expressiveness, yet often employ patterns that disregard channel dynamics, as they are not specifically designed for wireless communication scenarios. In this work, we propose a Doppler-aware Sparse Neural Network Beamforming (Doppler-aware Sparse NNBF) model that incorporates a channel-adaptive sparse attention mechanism in a multi-user single-input multiple-output (MU-SIMO) setting. The proposed sparsity structure is configurable along 2D time-frequency axes based on channel dynamics and is theoretically proven to ensure full connectivity within p hops, where p is the number of attention heads. Simulation results under urban macro (UMa) channel conditions show that Doppler-aware Sparse NNBF significantly outperforms both a fixed-pattern baseline, referred to as Standard Sparse NNBF, and conventional beamforming techniques ZFBF and MMSE beamforming in high mobility scenarios, while maintaining structured sparsity with a controlled number of attended keys per query.

title: CSIT-Driven Spectral Precoding for Sidelobe Suppression in Multicarrier Modulation.
abstract: We propose a channel-aware spectral precoding scheme for multicarrier modulation with channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT) that minimizes out-of-band radiation (OBR) under transmit power and mutual information constraints. The precoder is obtained by solving a constrained optimization problem via a fixed-point algorithm that incorporates reverse waterfilling and spectral shaping through a semi-unitary front-end. The spectral invariance under unitary rotations is leveraged to embed CSIT without altering the transmit power spectral density. This enables low-complexity receiver designs based on zero-forcing (ZF) or successive interference cancellation (SIC) strategies. Numerical results over block-fading multipath channels show that the proposed design achieves better OBR reduction and improved symbol error rates compared to existing schemes such as pre-equalized and spectrally precoded OFDM (PSP-OFDM) and null-subcarrier precoding. The SIC receiver achieves the best performance in the medium-to-high SNR regime, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Semantic-Aware Rate-Splitting Multiple Access for Meaning-Aware Multiuser 6G Communication.
abstract: This paper presents a unified framework that integrates semantic communication with rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) for sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks. Unlike traditional bit-level transmission, semantic communication focuses on conveying task-relevant meaning, reducing redundancy, and enhancing spectral efficiency. RSMA, with its flexible message-splitting structure, effectively mitigates multiuser interference and adapts to heterogeneous channel conditions. The proposed semantic–RSMA framework jointly optimizes semantic encoding and physical-layer transmission using a penalty-based successive convex approximation (SCA) approach. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme achieves up to 25% improvement in sum rate and a 12% increase in semantic similarity over conventional non-RSMA systems, establishing RSMA as a key enabler for intelligent, meaning-aware 6G communications.

title: Practical Low-Weight Codes for Energy-Efficient Bus Encoding.
abstract: We consider the transmission of data encoded into binary messages, with the goal of minimizing the Hamming distance, i.e., the number of bit-flips, between consecutive messages. This problem is relevant for enhancing the longevity of Non-Volatile Memories and reducing transition-induced energy consumption in data buses. Known as Write-Efficient Memory coding in the literature, this challenge has traditionally been addressed using optimal but complex schemes. In low-power computer systems the same topic is known as bus encoding. In this paper, we derive closed-form expressions to evaluate the average number of bit-flips for practical, sub-optimal encoding schemes, and propose two new schemes assisted by predefined random codebooks. We demonstrate that low-complexity solutions achieve performance very close to the optimal schemes, making them attractive for implementation in energy-sensitive and memory-critical applications. For instance, by adding 8 extra bits to 64-bits data, sub-optimal schemes can achieve a bit-flip reduction (related to energy saving) of approximately 24.7%, compared to the 26.4% reduction offered by the significantly more complex optimal scheme.

title: Compressible Tasks in Green Data Centers as Grid-Forming Support Assets.
abstract: Renewable microgrids can help data centers cope with the increasing demand for cloud-based services, but they pay the price of the double uncertainty of workload and renewable resource availability. The mismatch between demand and renewable supply prevents microgrid-based data centers from achieving full autonomy, requiring connection to the main grid. However, while imports from the main grid could increase environmental impact, the massive export of excess renewables, when injected into the grid, can cause serious instability in the system. This work addresses both issues using compressible tasks, whose concave utility functions allow for the adaptation to the available resources, reducing or increasing the task size with negligible impact on the quality provided to the user. By absorbing surplus renewable energy, they help maintain frequency stability in the main grid, thereby supporting grid-forming operations.
