We cast this problem as an optimization problem that dynamically adapts the task size based on renewable availability. We devised Online- REATA, an online heuristic able to manage tasks arrivals on the fly. Tested in a live video transcoding case study and compared to a solution without task compression, Online-REATA achieves the same average QoE and self-sufficiency, as well as higher self-consumption, while reducing storage requirements by up to 35.3%.

title: User Acceptance Model for Smart Incentives in Sustainable Video Streaming towards 6G.
abstract: The rapid growth of 5G video streaming is intensifying energy consumption across access, core, and data-center networks, underscoring the critical need for energy and carbon-efficient solutions. While reducing streaming bitrates improves energy efficiency, its success hinges on user acceptance—particularly when lower bitrates may be perceived as reduced quality of experience (QoE). Therefore, there is a need to develop transparent, user-centric incentive models that balance sustainability with perceived value. We propose a user-acceptance model that combines diverse environmental awareness, personalized responsiveness to incentives, and varying levels of altruism into a unified probabilistic framework. The model incorporates dynamic, individualized incentives that adapt over time. We further enhance the framework by incorporating (i) social well-being as a motivator for altruistic choices, (ii) provider-driven education strategies that gradually adjust user acceptance thresholds, and (iii) data-driven learning of user traits from historical offer–response interactions. Extensive synthetic-data experiments reveal the trade-offs between provider cost and network flexibility, showing that personalized incentives and gradual behavioral adaptation can advance sustainability targets without compromising stakeholder requirements.

title: Limitations and Enhancements for Network Energy Savings Towards 6G: Time Domain Adaptations.
abstract: Network Energy Saving (NES) techniques are becoming increasingly important for the radio access networks towards 6G, considering the high demand for beamforming due to higher frequency bands in 6G. This indicates even higher energy consumption and motivates further NES enhancements in 6G. Although cell discontinuous transmission (DTX) has been standardized to reduce energy consumption, its effectiveness is constrained by the time-domain occupancy of mandatory common signaling (e.g. SIB1), particularly when multiple beams are used. In this paper, we investigate the impact of beamforming on cell DTX performance and analyze how periodic transmission of common signals limits energy savings. To address this limitation, we evaluate a standalone on-demand System Information Block (SIB1) mechanism, in which system information is transmitted only upon explicit user equipment request. Simulation results show that, while beamforming improves interference, reducing periodic SIB1 transmission is necessary to decrease time-domain occupancy. In a standalone configuration, on-demand SIB1 reduces energy consumption and delay in beamforming deployments particularly for future 6G deployments using frequency bands of FR3 (7.125 GHz to 24.25 GHz).

title: Energy-Efficient Uplink-Downlink Decoupling for 6G TN-NTN Multi-Connectivity.
abstract: In 6G, LEO satellites complement terrestrial networks by extending coverage and offloading downlink services. However, direct satellite access faces a severe uplink energy bottleneck: required transmit power far exceeds handheld device capabilities. We propose decoupling uplink and downlink associations: uplink via short-range infrastructure (TN, UAV, HAPS) and downlink via satellite. Using 3GPP-compliant link budget analysis, we quantify substantial uplink power gaps and demonstrate order-of-magnitude battery lifetime extension with over 90% energy savings versus satellite-only operation. We address protocol feasibility through disaggregated RAN that eliminates inter-BS HARQ coordination overhead, and evaluate adaptive HARQ strategies (HARQ-less, independent, bundled). Results show bundled HARQ achieves substantial power reduction while maintaining high reliability with minimal delay overhead.

title: Simultaneous Source Separation, Synchronization, Localization and Mapping for 6G Systems.
abstract: Multipath-based simultaneous localization and map-ping (MP-SLAM) is a promising approach for future 6G net-works to jointly estimate the positions of transmitters and receivers together with the propagation environment. In cooperative MP-SLAM, information collected by multiple mobile terminals (MTs) is fused to enhance accuracy and robustness. Existing methods, however, typically assume perfectly synchronized base stations (BSs) and orthogonal transmission sequences, rendering inter-BS interference at the MTs negligible. In this work, we relax these assumptions and address simultaneous source separation, synchronization, and mapping. A relevant example arises in modern 5G systems, where BSs employ muting patterns to mitigate interference, yet localization performance still degrades. We propose a novel BS-dependent data association and synchronization bias model, integrated into a joint Bayesian framework and inferred via the sum-product algorithm on a factor graph. The impact of joint synchronization and source separation is analyzed under various system configurations. Compared with state-of-the-art cooperative MP-SLAM assuming orthogonal and synchronized BSs, our statistical analysis shows no significant performance degradation. The proposed BS-dependent data association model constitutes a principled approach for classifying features by arbitrary properties that persist over time, such as reflection order or feature type (scatter points versus walls).

title: Adversarial ML for Channel-Based Key Agreement for Underwater Acoustic Communications.
abstract: With the growing interest in underwater acoustic networks (UWANs), such as in the Internet of underwater things, we need mechanisms that guarantee communication security. In turn, security mechanisms often require legitimate devices to share secret keys. In this paper, we propose a physical-layer key generation (PKG) scheme for UWANs where a pair of legitimate users process the respective channel observation by two neural networks (NNs) to extract a raw key. Inspired by the lower bound on the secret key capacity, we train key extractors to maximize reciprocity and uniformity while minimizing the information leakage to the eavesdropper. Specifically, a custom architecture and loss function have been designed to accomplish these tasks. The performance of the proposed PKG mechanism based on machine learning (ML) has been evaluated considering both additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and UWAN scenarios, with the latter using measurements extracted from an experimental dataset. The results highlight the benefits of the proposed mechanism over the state-of-the-art solutions.

title: Performance Evaluation of Private 3GPP-Based Industrial Network Deployments.
abstract: Private cellular networks are a key enabler for industrial automation, yet their performance depends critically on network architectural choices such as the number of base stations (BSs) and the frequency assignment, especially under realistic blockage conditions. This work presents the first unified analysis of BS deployment configurations, frequency assignment, and blockage density in 3GPP indoor industrial deployment sub-scenarios (which differ in clutter density and BS height) under different performance requirements. The results reveal that the best design strongly depends on the performance target. Stringent performance goals require an increase in the number of channels demanded for interference mitigation, although excessive partitioning may reduce spectral efficiency. Blockers reshape these trade-offs by attenuating interference and reducing reuse requirements. Across deployment models, sub-scenarios where BSs are positioned above the clutter require aggressive frequency reuse to control interference, whereas sub-scenarios in which BSs are located amid the clutter favor fewer BSs and moderate reuse.

title: Digital Twin-Enabled Proactive Resource Management for Connected Robotics.
abstract: Industrial connected robots depend on reliable wireless communication to meet mobility and quality of service requirements. Conventional wireless network management approaches are mostly reactive and become inadequate in dynamic factory environments, particularly when high-frequency technologies such as millimeter wave and LiFi are used. This paper presents digital twin-enabled proactive wireless resource management for connected robotics. A proof-of-concept digital twin of an industrial environment is developed, capturing robot states, trajectories, and line-of-sight link characteristics, and enabling predictive interaction with the network. By exploiting future-aware information from the digital twin, network decisions such as resource allocation and handovers are performed proactively to prevent connectivity degradation. Two representative use cases are investigated. The first considers line-of-sight-aware resource management in heterogeneous LiFi-RF networks, achieving around 16 percentage improvement in the robot’s experienced data rate. The second addresses proactive handover management in 5G mobile networks, significantly reducing service interruption time due to handovers. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of network digital twins in enhancing wireless performance and ensuring seamless connectivity for industrial robots.

title: Intelligent UAV Path Planning for Ergodic Rate Maximization of MIMO Multipath Channels.
abstract: Reliable communication between ground control stations and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is fundamental for safe, autonomous, and coordinated flight operations. This work presents a decentralized model predictive control (MPC) framework that jointly optimizes UAV trajectory planning and high-frequency MIMO communication performance, explicitly accounting for multipath channel effects. The proposed framework incorporates ergodic spectral efficiency, derived from realistic location-dependent channel modeling, into the control cost function, thereby enabling UAV trajectories to dynamically balance three key objectives: (i) minimize travel time to assigned targets, (ii) maintain probabilistic safety through minimum separation constraints under stochastic disturbances, and (iii) maximize the achievable uplink ergodic rate to the ground station. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the approach, showing that ergodic rate–aware path planning leads to improved trade-offs between communication quality, safety, and mission efficiency under practical channel conditions.

title: Under the Hood of Mobile Roaming: Measuring IPX Network Latency on a Global Scale.
abstract: Global mobile connectivity depends on international roaming, which enables subscribers to use their service abroad through agreements ensuring traffic exchange between home and visited networks. Poor interconnect performance over the IPX network can degrade user experience and cause revenue loss, yet roaming remains underexplored due to proprietary systems and limited transparency. We present a large-scale study based on nine months of active probing from gateways across seven global regions, yielding nearly four billion latency measurements spanning 173 countries and 399 operators. This dataset enables the analysis of temporal trends, regional disparities, anomalies, and routing inefficiencies in IPX-based roaming. Our findings show how interconnection choices, carrier selection, and routing detours impact performance, advancing our understanding of global roaming trade-offs and allowing future optimization.

title: Coverage Enhancement through Network Controlled Repeaters: An XR perspective.
abstract: eXtended Reality (XR) is expected to be one of the most demanding and socially impactful application categories for future 6G networks. As 6G moves toward supporting immersive experiences with ultra high data rates and low latency, it becomes essential to explore novel radio access network (RAN) enhancements. In this context, this paper investigates the potential of network controlled repeaters (NCRs) as a scalable RAN element to support XR deployments. NCRs differ from conventional repeaters by enabling network driven beamforming and resource management, allowing the base station (gNB) to coordinate beam selection and direct signal relaying for more efficient coverage extension. We evaluate the performance of NCRs in simple (with single gNB and NCR) and complex (multiple gNB’s and NCR’s) urban XR scenarios. Users are placed indoor and outdoor and we investigate for two representative frequency ranges: FR1 (4GHz) and FR2 (28GHz). XR applications are emulated by considering their appropriate traffic models with the traffic parameters set from experimentally collected XR traffic. Key performance indicators such as signal to noise interference ratio (SINR), block error rate (BLER) and throughput heat maps are analyzed. In both simple and complex configurations, NCRs achieve substantially higher throughput and SINR, while reducing BLER for improved reliability. In scenarios with multiple base stations and NCRs, coverage is significantly expanded, making NCRs highly effective for large scale deployments. These improvements in link reliability, coverage, and XR quality of experience demonstrate the practical value of NCR enabled architectures for meeting the growing demands of 6G XR applications.

title: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Adaptive Handover Control Optimization for O-RAN.
abstract: Handover optimization in O-RAN faces growing challenges due to heterogeneous user mobility patterns and rapidly varying radio conditions. Existing ML-based handover schemes typically operate at the near-RT layer, which lack awareness of the mobility-mode and struggle to incorporate a longer-term predictive context. This paper proposes a multi-modal mobility-aware optimization framework in which all predictive intelligence, including mobility mode classification, short-horizon trajectory and RSRP forecasting, and a PPO Actor–Critic policy, runs entirely inside an rApp in the non-RT RIC. The rApp generates per-UE ranked neighbour-cell recommendations and delivers them to the existing handover xApp through the A1 interface. The xApp combines these rankings with instantaneous E2 measurements and performs the final standards-compliant handover decision. This hierarchical design preserves low-latency execution in the xApp while enabling the rApp to supply richer and mode-specific predictive guidance. Evaluation using mobility traces demonstrates that the proposed approach reduces ping-pong handover events and improves handover reliability compared to conventional 3GPP A3-based and ML-based baselines.

title: Optimizing Sensor Placement for Estimating Radio Occupancy Maps.
abstract: Radio maps show a radio characteristic of interest over a region and are used in applications from wireless network optimization to emitter localization. Radio map estimation often employs sensor measurements of signal power, where the sensors’ locations play a large role in the accuracy of the maps. In this work, we consider occupancy where signal power is above a given power threshold in a region, and propose two approaches for optimizing sensor placement. The first approach assumes that the joint probability distribution of the sensor measurements is known and maximizes sensor joint entropy. The second approach additionally assumes that the conditional probability distribution of the radio map occupancy given the sensor measurements is known, and minimizes expected occupancy estimation error. The second approach outperforms the first, but the first approach performs surprisingly well in estimating radio occupancy maps.

title: Distributed Pilot Framework for OTFS: Achieving Interference Whitening and PAPR Reduction.
abstract: Pilot design for Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation has evolved from embedded pilots to block, superimposed, and continuous pilots, progressively improving spectral efficiency and estimation accuracy. Yet, the deeper implications of pilot geometry, such as inter-symbol interference structure and spectral energy distribution, have not been systematically investigated. This paper advances this evolution by proposing a novel Distributed Pilot (DP) framework. By embedding pilots sparsely throughout the delay-Doppler grid, the DP structure achieves interference whitening, which decorrelates data interference into Gaussian-like white noise and yields a tighter estimation bound. Additionally, the dispersed placement prevents spectral energy concentration, achieving significant PAPR reduction. We develop a unified PAPR analytical model and an advanced message passing receiver to validate the framework. Simulations confirm that the DP scheme consistently outperforms state-of-the-art benchmarks in both estimation accuracy and PAPR.

title: Joint Near-Field/Far-Field Beam split-based Allocation in Multi-User THz Wideband Systems.
abstract: Wideband TeraHertz (THz) networks are anticipated to provide extremely high data rates and massive device connectivity, catering to the needs of 6G applications. While THz systems have demonstrated strong performance in the Far-Field (FF), recent research has highlighted the importance of accounting for Near-Field (NF) conditions. However, NF communications may suffer severe degradations due to the beam split effect. In this work, we address the weighted sum-rate maximization problem with NF-FF multi-user coexistence, for which we propose a two-step beamforming and resource allocation approach. In the first step, we design a low-complexity subarray–group assignment that leverages NF-FF spatial multiplexing. In the second step, given the selected subarray–group matching, we perform a beam split–aware intra-group resource allocation method that exploits multi-user diversity in NF-FF. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms benchmarks in terms of sumrate, while improving user fairness.1

title: Statistics Approximation-Enabled Distributed Beamforming for Cell-Free Massive MIMO.
abstract: We study a distributed beamforming approach for cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output networks, referred to as Global Statistics & Local Instantaneous information-based minimum mean-square error (GSLI-MMSE). The scenario with multi-antenna access points (APs) is considered over three different channel models: correlated Rician fading with fixed or random line-of-sight (LoS) phase-shifts, and correlated Rayleigh fading. With the aid of matrix inversion derivations, we can construct the conventional MMSE combining from the perspective of each AP, where global instantaneous information is involved. Then, for an arbitrary AP, we apply the statistics approximation methodology to approximate instantaneous terms related to other APs by channel statistics to construct the distributed combining scheme at each AP with local instantaneous information and global statistics. With the aid of uplink-downlink duality, we derive the respective GSLI-MMSE precoding schemes. Numerical results showcase that the proposed GSLI-MMSE scheme demonstrates performance comparable to the optimal centralized MMSE scheme, under the stable LoS conditions, e.g., with static users having Rician fading with a fixed LoS path.

title: R.S.D: A Regulatory Anonymity System with Decentralized Identity.
abstract: Decentralized Identity (DID) systems promise self-sovereign privacy but face a critical problem: effectively preventing anonymous misconduct without stripping user anonymity. Existing solutions predominantly rely on accountability via deanonymization (e.g., traceable signatures) or inefficient revocation lists, forcing a zero-sum decision problem where governance necessitates privacy loss or significant scalability bottlenecks. In this work, we solve this problem by introducing R.S.D (Regulatory Anonymity System with Decentralized Identity). Our core breakthrough is achieving blocking without revealing: enabling service providers to penalize specific malicious actors without learning their real-world identities. Unlike prior schemes relying on identity disclosure, R.S.D leverages zero-knowledge dynamic ticketing to enforce governance purely through cryptographic non-membership proofs. Experiments confirm its scalability, achieving 76.8 ms verification and sub-220 ms blocklist proofs (1,000 entries), making it a practical alternative to heavy revocation lists.

title: Synergizing Global Pattern Learning and Time Order Characterization in Mobile Channel Prediction: An RWKV-Based Approach.
abstract: Owing to the potential to reduce pilot overhead and mitigate channel aging, channel prediction is emerging as an important research topic in wireless communications. Meanwhile, deep neural networks are becoming a foundational technology for high-precision prediction thanks to their excellent non-linear representation capabilities. In this paper, we conceive a task-driven prediction network, which aims to deeply synergize the following two functions: learning global patterns for shareable features across adjacent time slots and structurally encoding time order to characterize the inherent causality within the channel dynamics. To implement channel prediction accuracy, we employ RWKV (receptance weighted key value) as network backbone and adapt it to the task’s specific characteristics, utilizing its deep interleaved learning architecture to extract global patterns across multiple channel samples and leveraging its unique exponential decay to characterize temporal order. These task-driven unique designs significantly improve the learning efficiency of prediction network. Comprehensive experimental evaluations demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over current data-driven methods, such as long short-term memory and Transformer, in the channel prediction task, including 1.84~4.29 dB gains in normalized mean squared error and 2.6~10.5 percentage point gains in cosine correlation.

title: Joint Trajectory and Resource Optimization for Secure UAV Communications Based on Graph Attention Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: UAV communications have been a vital technology for 5G and the forthcoming 6G wireless communications. However, the realization of secure communication remains a critical challenge due to the broadcast nature of UAV links. In this paper, we investigate a UAV-assisted framework, where the UAV is deployed as a flying base station (BS) to serve multiple user equipments (UEs) against eavesdropping threats. We propose a Graph Attention Reinforcement Learning for Secure Communications (GARL-SC) algorithm, where the complex relational features among UAV and UEs are extracted by Graph Attention Network (GAT) for jointly optimizing the UAV trajectory. We further develop Secure Hierarchical Bandwidth Allocation (SHBA) algorithm and Adaptive Hybrid Power Allocation (AHPA) algorithm for optimizing transmission power control and bandwidth allocation, aiming at maximizing the overall throughput and secrecy rate. From the experimental results, the proposed algorithm has considerable performance gains over existing traditional and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based baselines in terms of the optimization objective.

title: HS-TSA: Avoidance of Deanonymization Attacks in Unstructured DAG-based DLTs with Light Nodes.
abstract: Distributed ledger technology (DLT) provides a decentralized and tamper-resistant platform for secure data management. However, blockchain-based DLTs suffer from limited scalability due to their sequential block structure, making them unsuitable for large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) environments. Directed acyclic graph (DAG)-based DLTs overcome this limitation by enabling high throughput and concurrency. In particular, unstructured DAGs offer greater flexibility, allowing transactions to freely attach to existing unapproved transactions (tips), and are widely adopted in IoT-oriented systems. However, light nodes with limited resources often depend on full nodes to perform the tip selection algorithm(TSA), exposing them to deanonymization attacks. Existing countermeasures only mitigate but cannot avoid this risk. This paper proposes a Highest Similarity Tip Selection Algorithm (HS-TSA) that enables light nodes to select tips without revealing their identities. The proposed method formulates the selection as an optimization problem that maximizes intersection with full-node candidate sets while remaining distinct from each of them. Both theoretical analysis and simulations confirm that the proposed algorithm achieves the optimal solution efficiently.

title: A High-Performance and Scalable sFlow Scheme with Zero Control-Plane Overhead.
abstract: sFlow, defined in RFC 3176, is an industry standard supported by almost all managed network switches/routers for network traffic monitoring. Due to the complexities of forming and sending sFlow sample packets to a remote collector, commercial switches implement sFlow in the control plane by using the switch CPU. However, when the frequency of generating sFlow sample packets is high, the resulting sFlow sample packet loss rate will be very high due to a lack of switch CPU resources. In this work, we design and implement a high-performance and scalable sFlow scheme in a Programming Protocol-Independent Packet Processors (P4) switch. No matter how high the link speed (and the traffic arrival rate on the link) is, since our scheme performs sFlow packet formation and encapsulation entirely in the data plane of a switch, it always has zero control-plane overhead.We compared the performance of our data-plane-based scheme with that of control-plane-based schemes on a P4 switch. Experimental results show that the sample packet loss rate was always 0% in our scheme, no matter how high the traffic arrival rate increased. In contrast, when the conventional single-process control-plane-based scheme was used, the sample packet loss rate increased from 0% to 70% when the traffic arrival rate increased from 1 Gbps to 9 Gbps.

title: AirBreath Sensing: Toward Robust and Spectrum-Efficient Over-the-Air Distributed Sensing.
abstract: The natural integration of distributed sensing and edge artificial intelligence (AI), termed integrated sensing and edge AI (ISEA), is envisioned to be a key enabler of sixth-generation (6G) networks. In this context, leveraging over-the-air computing (AirComp) for simultaneous feature fusion in ISEA systems has attracted growing research interest. Despite its advantages, AirComp-based distributed sensing still faces two challenges: 1) the vulnerability of AirComp to interference resulting from uncoded transmission, and 2) communication bottleneck due to high-dimensional feature uploading. To tackle these challenges, we propose AirBreath sensing, a spectrum-efficient framework that cascades feature compression and spread spectrum to mitigate interference without bandwidth expansion. This work reveals a fundamental tradeoff between these two operations under constrained spectrum resources: a more aggressive compression may reduce sensing accuracy but allows for more aggressive interference suppression via spread spectrum, and vice versa. This tradeoff is regulated by a key variable called breathing depth, defined as the feature subspace dimension and is optimized by designing a tractable surrogate for sensing accuracy, measured by classification discriminant gain (DG). Experiments on real datasets show that AirBreath sensing effectively suppresses interference in ISEA systems, with the proposed algorithm achieving near-optimal performance.

title: 6G-PATH Open Experimentation Platform for B5G Enablers and Diverse Vertical Applications.
abstract: To prepare Europe for the 6G era with an open experimentation platform, the EU 6G-PATH project aims to help foster the further development and integration of new and improved 5G/6G enablers from EU collaboration, whilst facilitating the deployment and testing of a wide spectrum of vertical applications. To this end, the project establishes a uniform experimentation platform that is able to accommodate nine highly heterogeneous and geographically distributed testbeds from the project consortium, and is leveraging this platform for 10 diverse use cases across four key verticals including Farming, Education, Health, and Smart Cities. This paper presents the architectural design and prototyping of the 6G-PATH experimentation platform, highlighting its essential building blocks and advanced features, primary workflows, and example vertical application use of the platform.

title: Dual-Timescale MoE for Resource Management in Space-Air-Ground-Sea Integrated Networks.
abstract: The growing demand for maritime broadband services exposes the limitations of conventional satellite–ground systems, which often fail to jointly optimize spatial–temporal resources, computation costs, and the trade-offs between energy and information freshness. To address these challenges, we develop a physics-aware system model for near-shore Space-Air-Ground-Sea Integrated Networks (SAGSIN), capturing realistic maritime channels, Poisson task arrivals, Age of Information (AoI), and energy consumption. Based on this model, we propose a AI-enabled dual-timescale framework based on heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts (MoE). Specifically, the framework operations are formulated as a two-agent Markov decision process: the long-slot agent determines satellite beam-hopping coverage, while the short-slot agent jointly optimizes per-slot task offloading, UAV deployment, and resource allocation. Both agents employ MoE policies with Top-K gating. Simulation results validate that the proposed framework achieves superior AoI–energy trade-offs compared with baseline methods, highlighting the potential of AI-driven autonomy in next-generation network orchestration.

title: Clock Parameters Estimation for Inactive Nodes Under Arbitrary Distributed Delays in Multi-UAV Networks.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks are increasingly deployed in dynamic, large-scale missions such as environmental monitoring, cooperative sensing, and disaster response. Reliable coordination among network elements in multi-UAV networks strictly depends on precise time synchronization. Owing to its high energy efficiency achieved by enabling inactive nodes to passively synchronize without packet transmission, receiver-only synchronization (ROS) has been widely adopted for time synchronization in multi-UAV networks. However, accurate clock parameters estimation for ROS in high-dynamic multi-UAV networks remains challenging due to rapid mobility and communication delays with arbitrary distribution. To address these issues, we develop a robust invariant estimator for inactive nodes in energy-limited multi-UAV networks, capable of accurately estimating clock skew and offset under arbitrary distributed delays without relying on specific delay models. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves synchronization accuracy and robustness over existing approaches.

title: Joint Communication, Computation and Control Design for Wireless Agent Network (WAN).
abstract: This paper studies max-min fair effective semantic rate optimization for the Internet of Agents (IoA). We propose a joint resource allocation framework that integrates communication, computation, and control. For mobile intelligent agent networks, we establish a system model including bandwidth allocation, semantic compression, power control, and active mobility, where agents can improve channel conditions through position adjustments and reduce transmission load via semantic compression. To balance channel gain enhancement and additional energy consumption, this paper aims to maximize the minimum user energy rate, formulating a non-convex fractional optimization problem. By decomposing the original problem into four subproblems. We design an alternating iterative algorithm based on bisection to solve the problem effectively. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to the traditional fixed-position, non-compression, and three-variable optimization schemes, the proposed joint optimization framework achieves a maximum performance gain of up to 325% in worst-user energy efficiency and improves overall system fairness by up to 27% across diverse network scenarios, confirming its significant enhancement in both energy efficiency and user fairness.

title: Incentive Mechanism for Distributed Learning in Heterogeneous Networks: A Multi-Leader Multi-Follower Stackelberg Approach.
abstract: Incentive mechanisms are crucial for achieving efficient and sustainable distributed learning, especially when considering individual rationality and heterogeneity of distributed learning participants. However, existing incentive mechanisms are predominantly designed for federated learning (FL), overlooking split learning (SL), another significant distributed learning paradigm. Meanwhile, the heterogeneity of participants in terms of resources and demands is not well addressed. In this paper, we design an incentive mechanism for a distributed learning framework that integrates FL and SL. Specifically, we classify distributed learning participants into requesters and workers based on their model training demands. Requesters employ workers for collaborative model training, while requesters pay rewards to workers in exchange for their participation with computing and data resources. Requesters aim to maximize their utility by optimizing the offered rewards, whereas workers seek to maximize their payoffs by adjusting their participation levels. We employ the Multi-Leader Multi-Follower (MLMF) Stackelberg game to model the complex strategic interactions among requesters and workers. We prove the existence and uniqueness of the Stackelberg equilibrium for the proposed MLMF Stackelberg game using variational inequality theory and derive its closed-form solution via backward induction. Numerical results demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness of our proposed incentive mechanism, which significantly enhances the performance of model training compared to centralized model training.

title: Cross-DMRS RF Fingerprint Identification for LTE-V2X using Autocorrelation Features.
abstract: In vehicle to everything (V2X) communications, the high mobility of vehicles requires fast authentication. Radio frequency fingerprint (RFF) identification has emerged as a lightweight physical layer authentication method without involving the certificate authority. Existing RFF extraction methods are mostly based on fixed reference signals. However, in V2X communications, group hopping causes the demodulation reference signal (DMRS) to change every physical sidelink shared channel (PSSCH) subframe. The variation of DMRS sequences severely interferes the identification model to learn the subtle RFF features. This paper proposes a cross-DMRS RFF extraction framework for long term evolution (LTE)-V2X. Based on the property that reference DMRSs have identical autocorrelation function, triplet features of abnormal peaks in the autocorrelation of the received DMRS are extracted as RFF features. The experimental system are implemented using four on-board units (OBUs) and an universal software radio peripheral (USRP), to collect the PSSCH signals. Seven datasets are collected including line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) channels, both static and moving scenarios, and traverse nearly all of the 240 possible DMRS sequences. Using a deep learning network that combines convolutional neural network (CNN), squeeze-and-excitation (SE) and bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM), the average identification accuracy reaches 93.97%.

title: Bandwidth Enhanced Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receivers for Wireless Communication and Sensing.
abstract: Rydberg atomic quantum receivers (RAQRs) have emerged as highly sensitive receivers for future communication and sensing systems. However, conventional RAQRs are primarily effective for single-carrier and narrowband reception, typically with an operational bandwidth of only a few hundred kilohertz. To enable the reception of multi-carrier signals with larger bandwidth, we propose a multi-carrier Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (MC-RAQR) architecture based on a five-level quantum system model. We analyze the amplitude and phase of the output laser in MC-RAQR and extract the baseband electrical signal for signal processing. Furthermore, we quantify the performance of MC-RAQR in multi-carrier communication and sensing by studying the channel capacity and distance estimation, respectively. Numerical results show that the MC-RAQR is capable of achieving a bandwidth of $7.2$ MHz, which is an order of magnitude larger than conventional RAQRs. Besides, compared to conventional receivers, MC-RAQR can improve the capacity and distance estimation by $18$-fold and $10^3$-fold, respectively. This validates the superiority of MC-RAQR in receiving multi-carrier signal, and demonstrates its compatibility in detecting waveforms such as orthogonal frequency‐division multiplexing.

title: On the Fundamental Tradeoff of Sensing Accuracy, Outage Capacity and Information Freshness in ISAC Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates the fundamental tradeoff of sensing, communication, and information freshness in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. In particular, to evaluate the system performance, we adopt the age of information (AoI) as a key metric for data freshness, the outage capacity as the communication performance metric and the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) as the sensing performance metric. Through theoretical analysis, we derive two classes of extreme optimal designs, corresponding to the communication and sensing perspectives, respectively. Based on these designs, we construct several outer and inner bounds connecting these two extreme points by integrating the AoI into the multi-objective optimization framework, thereby highlighting the inherent mutual tradeoff between the three key performance metrics. Finally, through numerical simulations, our theoretical analysis is validated.

title: Hybrid CI-BLP Design in ISAC Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a multi-user, multi-target integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system and propose a fully-digital block-level precoding (BLP) scheme based on constructive interference (CI). Within the considered block, the optimization objective is the minimum CI scaling factor, with constraints on target illumination power, 3dB mainlobe width, and peak sidelobe ratio. Based on the fully-digital CI-BLP scheme, an optimal hybrid CI-BLP scheme is proposed. The required number of radio frequency (RF) chains depends only on the block length. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed fully-digital CI-BLP scheme in terms of the ISAC performance and validate the optimality of the proposed hybrid CI-BLP scheme.

title: Enhanced Multi-Target Detection and Range-Angle Estimation via RIS Space-Time Beamforming.
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-enabled multi-target sensing using communication waveforms. We propose to leverage both space-domain and time-domain RIS beamforming gains to further enhance the sensing performance. To this end, we propose a signal processing framework for multi-target sensing under RIS space-time beamforming, which jointly processes echo signals received under multiple time-varying RIS spatial beams. The framework consists of delay-domain signal processing for multi-target detection and range estimation, as well as space-time-domain signal processing for super-resolution angle estimation. We reveal that orthogonal RIS space-time beamforming codebook is optimal for the proposed signal processing method and design the RIS space-time beamforming by using the discrete Fourier transform matrix or the Hadamard matrix as the space-time codebook. The simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed space-time processing method in detection and super-resolution estimation performance compared to the traditional method under RIS spatial beamforming.

title: ScaleDL: Towards Scalable and Efficient Runtime Prediction for Distributed Deep Learning Workloads.
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) form the cornerstone of modern AI services, supporting a wide range of applications, including autonomous driving, chatbots, and recommendation systems. As models increase in size and complexity, DNN workloads such as training and inference tasks impose unprecedented demands on distributed computing resources, making accurate runtime prediction essential for optimizing development and resource allocation. Traditional methods rely on additive computational unit models, limiting their accuracy and generalizability. In contrast, graph-enhanced modeling improves performance but significantly increases data collection costs. Therefore, there is a critical need for a method that strikes a balance between accuracy, generalizability, and data collection costs. To address these challenges, we propose ScaleDL, a novel runtime prediction framework that combines nonlinear layer-wise modeling with graph neural network (GNN)-based cross-layer interaction mechanism, enabling accurate DNN runtime prediction and hierarchical generalizability across different network architectures. Additionally, we employ the D-optimal method to reduce data collection costs. Experiments on the workloads of five popular DNN models demonstrate that ScaleDL enhances runtime prediction accuracy and generalizability, achieving 6 times lower MRE and 5 times lower RMSE compared to baseline models.

title: DRL-Based Mitigation Against Nonreciprocal RIS-Aided Channel Reciprocity Attacks.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) technology enhances wireless communication performance, but it also introduces new vulnerabilities. This paper investigates channel reciprocity attack (CRACK) threats in multi-antenna wireless systems operating in time-division duplexing mode using a physically consistent nonreciprocal RIS (NR-RIS) model. CRACK can degrade the communication rate by distorting the downlink precoding, without requiring any additional signal transmission or channel state information (CSI). Unlike conventional RIS jamming strategies, the NR-RIS does not need synchronization with the legitimate system and thus can operate with slow or fixed configurations to implement CRACK, complicating corresponding defensive precoding designs. To counter this threat, we develop "SecureCoder," a deep reinforcement learning-based framework that can mitigate NR-RIS CRACK by determining an improved downlink precoder matrix using the estimated uplink CSI. Simulations confirm the severe degradation caused by NR-RIS CRACK and demonstrate the effectiveness of SecureCoder in improving the system throughput.

title: A Snorkel-Guided GAN-Based Framework for Robust Traffic Data Imputation in Sparse IoT Traffic Environments.
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) plays a pivotal role in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) by enabling large-scale data collection from sensors and supporting real-time services through fifth-generation (5G) and emerging sixth-generation (6G) networks. These IoT-enabled infrastructures are critical for incident detection, dynamic routing, and congestion mitigation, yet their performance is often undermined by missing data caused by sensor failures, unreliable wireless links, and bandwidth limitations. Existing imputation methods typically overlook semantic information related to traffic incidents, reducing their effectiveness in latency-sensitive IoT applications. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a Snorkel-Guided Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based Data Imputation (SKGAIN) framework that integrates weak supervision with adversarial learning to jointly capture spatiotemporal dependencies and incident-aware semantics. By leveraging Snorkel-guided soft labels and GAN-based reconstruction, SKGAIN enhances imputation quality under sparse conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach improves data reliability in traffic monitoring, thereby supporting low latency and resilient decision making in connected transportation systems.

title: Mitigating Heterogeneity in Personalized Federated Learning with Local Pruned Generative AI.
abstract: Generative AI is widely applied in Federated Learning (FL) to mitigate heterogeneity, with proven success in scenarios like the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). However, most existing methods deploy generative models on a central server, which risks privacy leakage by exposing local data distributions. Consequently, it is crucial to deploy the generative model locally. In this paper, we propose Per-PDiff, a framework that ensures secure generative AI integration in Personalized FL (PFL) through the local deployment of a pruned diffusion model. Due to resource constraints on devices selected by a heterogeneity-aware strategy, we introduce Tailor-Pruning with ratios tailored to each device’s computational capacity, ensuring the successful deployment and inference of on-device Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs). Data generated by pruned DDPMs are paired with their corresponding labels and integrated into the device-oriented data augmentation process. Further, we incorporate a personalized meta-learning algorithm during FL training to balance global generalization and local personalization. Experiments were conducted on several datasets from multiple perspectives to validate the feasibility and superiority of our framework. The results demonstrate that Per-PDiff significantly outperforms advanced baseline models, improving global convergence accuracy.

title: Attention-Aided Boundary Equilibrium GAN for Wideband Power Amplifier Predistortion.
abstract: Digital predistortion (DPD) is an essential technique for linearizing power amplifiers (PAs) in wideband wireless communication systems. Neural networks (NNs) have become a mainstream solution for DPD due to their nonlinear approximation capabilities. However, as escalating signal bandwidths intensify memory effects, the efficacy of conventional models is limited by the point-wise error minimization objective, which tends to learn a deterministic average mapping that cannot fully capture the complex statistical distribution of the PA’s inverse characteristics. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a novel DPD method that leverages a boundary equilibrium generative adversarial network (BEGAN) for robust distributional learning of the PA’s inverse characteristics. An integrated attention mechanism further identifies and weights critical temporal features to address long-term memory effects. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed method outperforms existing NN-based approaches for a 100 MHz input signal, achieving approximately 2 dB enhancements in both normalized mean square error (NMSE) and adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR).

title: Offloading IP Packet Fragmentation from CPU to SmartNIC Using P4.
abstract: CPU offloading of complex packet processing to Network Interface Card (NIC) is an important technique commonly used on the servers in today’s data center networks. The CPU cycles saved by this technique can be used by the servers to execute crucial network functions to increase productivity. A common example is offloading the checksum computation and verification of TCP packets from CPU to NIC.In this work, we design and implement a scheme to offload the task of fragmenting a large IP packet into multiple MTU-sized packets from the CPU to a SmartNIC using the P4 language. Such a work has not been reported in the literature. Unlike using traditional ASIC-based NICs, which have fixed hardware pipelines with limited flexibility, our approach leverages the programmability of P4-based SmartNICs to achieve these functionalities with greater adaptability. Experimental results show that when the packet payload size is 4000 bytes, our scheme can reduce the CPU usage from 200% to 62%, achieving a saving of 138%.

title: Mutual Coupling Kernel Approximation for Continuous Aperture Beamforming.
abstract: A mutual coupling aware beamforming design is proposed for continuous aperture arrays (CAPAs), a paradigm that features continuous electromagnetic (EM) radiating surfaces. The optimal uni-polarized continuous aperture beamforming is derived as a function of the inverse of the mutual coupling kernel. To address the non-trivial kernel inverse, a kernel approximation method is proposed based on the Fourier transform and Gauss-Legendre quadrature, resulting in a closed-form optimal beamforming solution. Numerical results validate the rapid convergence of the proposed approximation. It also reveals the anisotropic nature of mutual coupling in uni-polarized CAPAs, demonstrating that its effect can be either constructive or destructive depending on the direction of radiation relative to the polarization direction.

title: Adaptive Video Streaming in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks with Mixture of Experts.
abstract: Adaptive video streaming is a fundamental technology for modern video delivery, especially in cellular networks. However, the dynamic nature of mobile environments and the varied preferences of users pose significant challenges for adaptive bitrate (ABR) algorithms. Current methods frequently struggle to achieve a balance between high performance in specific conditions and robust generalization across diverse network environments personalized Quality of Experience (QoE) demands. To address these challenges, we propose NMoEABR, a unified ABR decision-making framework that integrates a nonlinear Mixture-of-Experts (NMoE) architecture with preference-aware meta-reinforcement learning. Specifically, we design an NMoE-based actor network that adaptively aggregates expert policies through dynamic convolution conditioned on real-time network states, thereby enhancing robustness and cross-network generalization without incurring additional computation overhead. Furthermore, we introduce a preference-aware meta-RL strategy that incorporates user preference embeddings and virtual preference synthesis to stabilize meta-policy updates. Comprehensive evaluations on real-world traces demonstrate that NMoEABR consistently outperforms mainstream ABR benchmarks, particularly under unseen wireless networks and user preferences.

title: Joint Optimization of Communication and Sensing Performance for ISAC Systems Under Jamming.
abstract: This paper investigates the communication and sensing performance of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems under constrained energy consumption and malicious jamming, with imperfect channel state information (CSI). We formulate a problem of maximizing the minimum communication performance (MCP) under the sensing constraint by jointly optimizing base station (BS) beamforming, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) transmit and receive beamforming. To address this coupled non-convex problem, we develop an alternating optimization (AO)-based scheme. Specifically, we first transform the BS beamforming problem into a semidefinite program (SDP) problem and solve it using the semidefinite relaxation (SDR) method. Second, auxiliary variables are introduced to solve the UAV beamforming problem by employing the successive convex approximation (SCA) method. Subsequently, the UAV receive beamforming optimization problem is transformed into a Rayleigh quotient problem, thus yielding a closed-form solution for the receive beamforming vector. Extensive simulation results validate that the proposed scheme exhibits excellent convergence properties and outperforms benchmarks.

title: Channel-Adaptive Generative Semantic Communication with Dynamic Bandwidth Allocation for Future 6G Systems.
abstract: Deep learning-based semantic communication (SemCom) has emerged as a key technology for 6G networks to improve information transmission efficiency. However, existing adaptive-rate frameworks typically operate as black boxes, failing to jointly optimize semantic distortion and bandwidth consumption under dynamic channel conditions. To address this, we propose an Ordered Variational Autoencoder-based Generative SemCom (OVAE-GSemCom) framework guided by semantic rate-distortion (SRD). By enforcing a strict ordering in semantic confidence via nested dropout training, the framework transforms the VAE latent space into an importance-ranked semantic representation, enabling efficient semantic feature selection. Building on this ordered representation, a learnable semantic water-filling mechanism is designed to dynamically allocate bandwidth, jointly optimizing semantic reconstruction and channel resource usage. The simulation results demonstrate that OVAE-GSemCom achieves superior semantic rate-distortion performance, requiring only approximately $\frac{1}{6}$ of the bandwidth required by conventional methods while maintaining high perceptual quality.

title: Learning to Jointly Optimize Antenna Positioning and Beamforming for Movable Antenna-Aided Systems.
abstract: The recently emerged movable antenna (MA) and fluid antenna technologies offer promising solutions to enhance the spatial degrees of freedom in wireless systems by dynamically adjusting the positions of transmit or receive antennas within given regions. In this paper, we aim to address the joint optimization problem of antenna positioning and beamforming in MA-aided multi-user downlink transmission systems. This problem involves mixed discrete antenna position and continuous beamforming weight variables, along with coupled distance constraints on antenna positions, which pose significant challenges for optimization algorithm design. To overcome these challenges, we propose an end-to-end deep learning framework, consisting of a positioning model that handles the discrete variables and the coupled constraints, and a beamforming model that handles the continuous variables. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior sum rate performance, yet with much reduced computation time compared to existing methods.

title: Energy Saving for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Networks: A Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: This paper focuses on energy savings in downlink operation of cell-free massive MIMO (CF mMIMO) networks under dynamic traffic conditions. We propose a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) algorithm that enables each access point (AP) to autonomously control antenna re-configuration and advanced sleep mode (ASM) selection. After the training process, the proposed framework operates in a fully distributed manner, eliminating the need for centralized control and allowing each AP to dynamically adjust to real-time traffic fluctuations. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm reduces power consumption (PC) by 56.23% compared to systems without any energy-saving scheme and by 30.12% relative to a non-learning mechanism that only utilizes the lightest sleep mode, with only a slight increase in drop ratio. Moreover, compared to the widely used deep Q-network (DQN) algorithm, it achieves a similar PC level but with a significantly lower drop ratio.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Active Learning for Data Completion in Sparse Crowdsensing.
abstract: Mobile CrowdSensing (MCS) relies on sparse data completion to infer missing information. However, centralized approaches require uploading raw data to a central server, which entails significant privacy risks. Moreover, under limited sampling budgets, random or fixed sampling is often ineffective at improving completion accuracy. Therefore, we proposes a privacy-preserving framework for sparse data completion based on Federated Learning (FL), which avoids raw data transmission while maintaining inference accuracy. We instantiate the framework with three models: Federated Deep Matrix Factorization (FDMF), Federated Recurrent Neural Network–enhanced Deep Matrix Factorization (FRDMF), and Federated Active Learning–enhanced Deep Matrix Factorization with Differential Privacy (FRDMF-DP-AL). To mitigate privacy risks in model updates, we add Laplace noise to the uploaded parameters to achieve ϵ-differential privacy. Experimental results indicate that the framework delivers a strong privacy–utility–efficiency trade-off, supporting city-scale MCS deployments.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-based Multi-parameter Adaptation for Meteor Burst Communication.
abstract: Meteor Burst Communication (MBC) has emerged as a pivotal beyond-line-of-sight propagation technique for next-generation wireless networks, offering a resilient solution for massive Internet of Things (mIoT) backhaul in remote areas. By leveraging ionized meteor trails as reflective media, MBC provides high-security, low-cost connectivity independent of satellite infrastructure. However, the inherent intermittency and rapid decay of these trails pose significant challenges to energy efficiency and throughput. Existing methods often rely on reactive, stationary models that fail to capture the complex, non-linear dynamics of the meteor-scatter channel. To overcome these hurdles, this paper proposes MoE-SAC, a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) and soft actor-critic (SAC)-based framework for joint optimization of transmit power and antenna orientation to maximize energy efficiency of the MBC system. MoE-SAC allows for expert specialization on distinct trail characteristics, which can significantly improve the convergence and robustness in time-varying environments. Furthermore, we develop a high-fidelity, data-driven environment based on real-world trajectory data from the Global Meteor Network (GMN), ensuring the model reflects authentic physical propagation behaviors. Numerical results demonstrate that our enhanced approach achieves up to 11.2% and 19.2% improvements in delivered data volume and energy efficiency, respectively, over vanilla SAC schemes.

title: MEC Caching for Spatial Audio with Immersive Soundfield Reconstruction.
abstract: Spatial audio streaming for 6 DoF virtual reality (VR) applications presents new challenges in MEC, as it requires a large amount of high-resolution ambisonic audio recordings to satisfy user requests. Unlike traditional audio streaming, 6 DoF spatial audio requires position-dependent interpolation using nearby subsets of microphone signals to satisfy geometric validity constraints. In this paper, we formulate a new problem, Joint Soundfield Reconstruction and Cache Control (JSRCC), for 6 DoF spatial audio streaming under network constraints and prove it NP-Hard. We design an online algorithm EMSCR with a performance bound and propose Maximum Covering Tree (MCT) and Quality-Bandwidth Efficiency (QBE) to dynamically select, evict, and fetch ambisonic recordings in the cache based on user movement. EMSCR minimizes the total cost of cache operation, transmission overhead, and audio degradation while ensuring interpolation validity and efficient bandwidth utilization, dynamically balancing spatial coverage and perceptual fidelity under varying network conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms the baselines in cache efficiency and perceptual quality with reduced transmission redundancy.

title: PHY-aware TCP BBR in Wi-Fi Networks.
abstract: Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication over WLAN technologies can support variety of applications in intelligent transportation systems. Due to the potentially large volume of data transmissions, congestion control in wireless network has been a compelling challenge that gained considerable interest in the research community. Traditional congestion control algorithms, such as TCP CUBIC, often misinterpret wireless signal loss as congestion, leading to degraded throughput and unstable delay. Recently, the Bottleneck Bandwidth and Round-trip propagation time (BBR) algorithm, a model-based approach that estimates bottleneck bandwidth and minimum RTT, has been shown to outperform CUBIC in dynamic wireless networks. However, BBR’s reliance on delayed end-to-end feedback limits its responsiveness under fast channel variations. In this paper, we proposes a PHY-aided BBR modification that dynamically adjusts pacing gain using real-time physical layer measurements. By smoothing PHY data rates and integrating them into BBR’s phase-dependent control, the proposed scheme improves BBR’s ability to track available channel capacity in wireless network. To validate the proposed approach, we developed our own custom Wi-Fi testbed and conducted experiments under different channel blockage scenarios corresponding to V2V communications. Experimental results show that when dynamic channel fading/blockage appears, the PHY-aided BBR achieves a faster recovery time and lower number of retransmission compared to baseline BBR, making it a promising approach for next-generation vehicular networks.

title: Frequency-Hopping Based Co-Located LoRa Sensing for An Aerial Target Using BCD and CZT.
abstract: The primary challenges for co-located LoRa sensing of aerial targets include the limited bandwidth of LoRa signals, carrier frequency offsets (CFOs) caused by unsynchronization between transceivers, and signal leakage from the transmitter to the receiver. This paper attempts to fill the gap. Specifically, we consider a co-located LoRa sensing system to estimate the distance and velocity of an aerial target using unsynchronized transceivers with signal leakage from the transmitter to the receiver. We expand the bandwidth by transmitting multiple narrowband up-chirp or down-chirp signals over different subcarriers via frequency hopping (FH). We analyze the Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLBs) and optimize the FH pattern to minimize the CRLBs against all possible unknown parameters using robust optimization. We also propose a low-complexity method to solve the challenging nonconvex maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) problem by jointly using Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC), block coordinate descent (BCD), and chirp z-transform (CZT). Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed FH patterns effectively reduce CRLBs, and the proposed low-complexity algorithm achieves high estimation accuracy with a short computation time.

title: ISAC-Enabled Multi-UAV Collaborative Target Sensing for Low-Altitude Economy.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has attracted growing research interests to facilitate the large-scale development of the low-altitude economy (LAE). However, the high dynamics of low-altitude targets may overwhelm fixed ISAC systems, particularly at the edge of their coverage or in blind zones. Driven by high flexibility, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted ISAC can provide more freedom of design to enhance communication and sensing abilities. In this paper, we propose an ISAC-enabled multi-UAV dynamic collaborative target sensing scheme, where UAVs can dynamically adjust their flight and resource allocation for cooperative sensing of mobile target through communicating with the terrestrial cellular network with ISAC signals. To achieve the precise sensing of the dynamic target, the posterior Cramér-Rao bound (PCRB) for the target state is derived. Subsequently, the PCRB minimization problem is formulated by jointly optimizing the UAV-BS association, UAVs’ trajectories and bandwidth allocation, subject to the communication requirements for the UAVs. However, the problem is challenging since it involves non-convex and implicit objective function with coupled optimization variables. For a fast implementation of sensing and tracking, we propose a low-complexity iterative algorithm that can efficiently obtain a sub-optimal solution to the problem. Specifically, the UAV-BS association is first determined by the communication-optimal solution. Then the UAVs’ trajectories and bandwidth allocation are alternatively optimized based on the descent direction search algorithm. Finally, numerical results are provided to validate the superiority of our proposed designs as compared to various benchmarks.

title: ForeQast: Structuring Forward Looking Delay Guarantees in QUIC.
abstract: For many real-time applications, such as video conferencing, the end-to-end latency is a critical metric to the user experience. While the latency over the Internet has been significantly reduced in recent days, we find that the delay at the sender has been increasingly critical and dominant. We identify that the delay comes from the socket buffer at the sender. Specifically, the gap between when the application writes data and when packets are actually transmitted. The existing socket buffer lacks active management and is not optimized for low latency. To solve this, we propose a predictive thresholding approach, ForeQast, that integrates active queue management directly at the end host. We introduce an adaptive buffer threshold to actively manage the socket send buffer to reduce the latency. We carefully design the threshold to maintain throughput in different network conditions. We implement the ForeQast over QUIC protocol and evaluate it using trace-driven emulation. Evaluations on synthetic and real network traces show that the algorithm meets percentile-based delay guarantees across traces, targets, and RTTs, without throughput loss or noticeable CPU overhead, delivering a controllable delay for the socket send buffer.

title: Joint Communication and Computation in Optical System with Mach-Zehnder Modulator.
abstract: 6G requires intelligent computations in the communication networks. Conventional scheme is to compute in a standalone processor after receiving the raw data transmitted through the communication system. In this paper, we present a technique of processing image classification tasks during data transmission through optical fiber communication systems instead of processing after transmission in the classical networks, which complies with the joint communication and computation (J2C) scheme. The Mach-Zehnder modulators (MZM) in optical system exhibit behaviors of Bessel functions when the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) of the transmitted signal is large, which imposes a limitation in modern communication system. In this paper, we demonstrated that this unwanted Bessel-function behavior can be turned useful if the signal is computed during transmission. Simulation results with Cifar-10 datasets show that the proposed MZM-based J2C scheme outperforms the classical scheme in both accuracy and efficiency.

title: Near-Field Channel Tracking With Fractional-Domain Sparsity Awareness.
abstract: In extremely large-scale MIMO (XL-MIMO) systems, the user’s mobility and angular spread caused by the near-field effect render conventional tracking schemes either ineffective or prohibitively expensive. To address this, we propose a low-overhead channel tracking scheme that exploits fractional-domain sparsity. Specifically, leveraging the Fractional Fourier Transform (FrFT), we first construct a dynamic subspace based on trajectory prediction to significantly reduce observation dimensionality. Subsequently, we propose a closed-form fractional order correction method utilizing spectral width and phase curvature to resolve energy spreading to avoid exhaustive search, thereby ensuring high energy concentration for precise channel tracking. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves an 11 dB NMSE gain over polar-domain benchmarks in high-mobility scenarios under strict pilot overhead constraints.

title: UAV-Enabled Joint Sensing and Communication in Spatially Correlated Environments.
abstract: This paper investigates a joint sensing and communication system enabled by an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), where the UAV simultaneously performs environmental sensing and communicates with ground users (GUs) in a target area. We consider spatially correlated sensing environments modeled as a spatial autoregressive (SAR) process and employ joint entropy to quantify the information contained in the sensing data. Due to the spatial correlation, maximizing the sensing information encourages the UAV to widely explore the target area, potentially degrading communication performance, which uncovers a previously unexplored tradeoff between sensing and communication in UAV trajectory design. To balance sensing and communication performance, we jointly optimize the trajectory of the energy-constrained UAV and the bandwidth allocation among the GUs for maximizing the weighted sum of sensing information and the minimum data volume received from the GUs. To tackle the resulting mixed-integer nonconvex optimization problem, we first reformulate it into an equivalent dynamic programming (DP) problem and further propose a One-Step Lookahead Rollout (OSLR) algorithm for a low-complexity approximate DP solution. The OSLR algorithm adopts a novel base policy, designed by leveraging the submodularity and convexity of the underlying subproblems, to approximate the optimal value function of the DP problem. Simulation results show that the proposed OSLR-based scheme significantly outperforms the baseline methods in both sensing and communication objectives.

title: Dynamic and Autonomous Deployment of Mobility-Aware Aerial Base Stations in Low-Altitude Emergency Network.
abstract: Driven by the low-altitude economy representing emerging productive forces, the Low-Altitude Internet of Intelligences (LAIN) emerges as an intelligent airspace architecture. Addressing poor adaptability and slow response in traditional strategies under dynamic distributions, this paper proposes a dynamic node deployment method based on the Actor– Critic deep reinforcement learning framework to maximize throughput. The established system model comprises ground stations, communication nodes, and users, adopting power-domain Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) to enhance spectrum efficiency and multi-user transmission. Formulating the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), the proposed AC-based algorithm enables efficient decision-making in continuous action spaces, adaptively optimizing node positions and power. Simulations demonstrate throughput improvements of 38.18% and 50.38% over heuristic and DQN algorithms, respectively. Furthermore, the method exhibits superior stability under uniform and Gaussian distributions, maintaining performance advantages in high-density scenarios up to 40 users/km2.

title: Augmented Edge-Cloud Service Orchestration: A Twin-Driven Coupling approach.
SRDiffC: Ultra-Low-Bitrate Visual Communication with Generative Reconstruction.
abstract: Recent advances in generative AI and large multimodal models are motivating AI-native visual communication over open and disaggregated RAN architectures, calling for programmable control to meet tight latency–bandwidth budgets in cloud–edge deployments. While diffusion-based learned image compression can achieve photorealistic reconstruction at ultra-low bitrates, it remains difficult to deploy in communication systems due to high decoding latency from multi-step denoising and limited content fidelity, where perceptually plausible reconstructions may drift from the source, undermining reliable transmission and downstream semantics. In this paper, we propose a multimodal generative compression framework that is explicitly designed for low-latency and bandwidth-adaptive visual communication. For real-time decoding in cloud–edge settings, we build on SD-Turbo and tailor it to compression via parameter-efficient LoRA fine-tuning, enabling high-quality reconstruction with only a few denoising steps. To enhance fidelity across variable rate budgets, we introduce a residual-guided multi-grained textual coding scheme that explicitly conveys semantic residuals missed by a baseline autoencoder. Specifically, the residual semantics are extracted and verbalized into variable-length text tokens using large pre-trained vision–language models, refined through differential prompt optimization, and transmitted as lightweight side information to guide the diffusion decoder. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach substantially reduces decoding steps while producing photorealistic yet faithful reconstructions, and it preserves fine details more consistently across a wide bitrate range. This highlights the potential of large-model-assisted, semantic-aware generative compression for next-generation communication networks.

title: Channel Knowledge Map-aided Hierarchical Beam Training for Massive MIMO Systems.
abstract: Channel knowledge map (CKM) emerges as a promising framework to acquire location-specific channel information without consuming wireless resources. Despite its potential, the practical application of CKM in beam training faces severe challenges. Most importantly, the user’s precise location is typically unavailable prior to beam training, which limits the utility of CKM. In this paper, we present a framework for CKM-aided beam training. We propose a reward-motivated beam-potential hierarchical strategy which integrates partial position information and CKM. This strategy models the user equipment (UE) position uncertainty and formulates the hierarchical searching process as a pruned binary search tree. An optimal hierarchical searching strategy with minimal overhead is derived by evaluating the weights and rewards of potential codewords. Furthermore, a low-complexity two-layer lookahead scheme is designed to balance overhead and computational demands.

title: A Novel Channel Estimation Scheme for OTFS MIMO Systems Assisted with Double IRSs.
abstract: Intelligent-reflecting-surfaces (IRSs) cooperation is an available way to enhance signal coverage for Internet of Things by dynamically adjusting the phases of the elements on the IRSs. This paper investigates the channel estimation of a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system in orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) assisted by double IRSs to enable reliable communication in high-mobility environments, and a novel channel estimation scheme is developed to overcome the hybrid-channel estimation challenge introduced by double IRSs. Specifically, to reduce computational complexity and improve estimation efficiency, three orthogonal subcarrier subsets are used to implement channel estimation for the three cascaded channels respectively. Furthermore, to induce linearly varying frequency offsets for different links, the phases of the elements on the two IRSs are rotated dynamically, which endows each cascaded channel with unique spectral characteristics and enhances multipath separability. Meanwhile, each individual link is efficiently estimated in the delay-Doppler domain via the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm. Simulation results are presented to validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed scheme in channel estimation for double-IRS assisted MIMO systems.

title: Extended Target Tracking for Contour-Aware Predictive Beamforming in ISAC Systems.
abstract: Recent advances in massive multiple-input multiple-output and millimeter-wave technologies have enabled target sensing with sub-degree angular and decimeter-level range resolution. Consequently, conventional point-target models become inadequate for capturing the detailed spatial characteristics of targets during tracking. In this work, we introduce the concept of target contour, which is modeled by the truncated Fourier series to capture the spatial extent of the target, for extended target tracking within an integrated sensing and communication framework. A predictive beamforming design is developed, where each tracking period is divided into a sensing block and a data block. During the sensing block, the base station (BS) performs beam scanning and applies maximum likelihood estimation to extract scatterer measurements along the target contour. These measurements are then processed by an extended Kalman filter to jointly estimate the target’s kinematic states and contour parameters, which are further used to predict the direction of the target-mounted communication terminal (CT). In the subsequent data block, the BS steers an adjustable narrow beam towards the predicted CT direction to establish reliable communication link. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves robust target tracking performance and high communication rate under complicated target trajectories.

title: Energy-Efficient Resource Management via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning in O-RAN.
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks are expected to meet all the demands of the next decade, a feasibility that is only possible with advances in network design and management. This paper first proposes a unified resource management framework for a 6G-based network architecture that includes an Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) deployment and then defines a hierarchical network energy control and resource management approach. Leveraging the openness of O-RAN, the proposed novel Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL)-based scheme provides two-level centralized agent policy evaluation and decentralized agent real-time scheduling optimization, thereby minimizing system energy consumption while ensuring Quality of Service (QoS). To validate the performance of this management approach, we propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)based algorithm for each level. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of this solution in terms of throughput, user-experienced data rate, and energy consumption.

title: Age of Information Minimization for Buffer-Aided Uplink Systems via Movable Antennas.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate an uplink multiple-access system assisted by movable antennas (MAs), with the objective of minimizing the long-term average weighted Age of Information (LAW-AoI). To tackle the resulting nonconvex mixed-integer programming problem from the joint optimization of MA positioning and user scheduling, we develop an adaptive transmission policy under a Lyapunov optimization framework. An alternating optimization approach incorporating successive convex approximation (SCA) is introduced to efficiently update the MA positions, while a dynamic time-division multiple access (TDMA)-based scheduling strategy is designed to maintain queue stability and information freshness. Simulation results confirm that the proposed scheme achieves a significant reduction in average AoI compared to conventional benchmark methods, demonstrating the effectiveness of MA-assisted optimization in time-sensitive wireless communication systems.

title: Outage Performance of PASS Under Random LoS Blockage.
abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) offer considerable potential for wireless communications due to their unique ability to dynamically reconfigure radiation positions along a waveguide. However, the performance of PASS remains a critical challenge in the presence of random line-of-sight (LoS) blockage, leading to significant attenuation and even communication outages. In this paper, the outage performance of PASS in the presence of LoS blockage is investigated from the perspective of stochastic geometry.
