Obstacles are modeled as a homogeneous Poisson point process that captures the randomness in their spatial distribution and geometric dimensions. Based on the proposed blockage model, closed-form analytical and asymptotic expressions for the outage probability are obtained. The numerical results reveal that denser obstacle environments or statistically larger obstacles substantially increase the outage probability of PASS.

title: CRB-Constrained Sum Secrecy-Rate Maximization for 6DMA-Enabled MU-MISO ISAC Systems.
abstract: Reusing integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) waveforms for sensing can induce information leakage exploitable by eavesdroppers, thereby jeopardizing physical-layer security (PLS). In this paper, we studied a six-dimensional movable antenna (6DMA)-assisted multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) ISAC system for secure transmission, where a 6DMA-enabled base station serves multiple single-antenna legitimate users in the presence of eavesdroppers. Under a worst-case eavesdropper assumption, we formulate a sum secrecy rate maximization problem subject to a Cramér–Rao bound (CRB) threshold, a transmit power constraint, and feasible 6DMA pose constraints. To tackle the highly coupled and non-convex optimization problem, we employ successive convex approximation (SCA) to construct consistent convex surrogates for the non-convex terms, and adopt an alternating optimization (AO) framework to iteratively obtain approximate solutions for the optimization variables. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can significantly improve the sum secrecy rate while satisfying sensing requirements.

title: Multiple-Cyclic-Basis GCD for BCH Codes.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a Gaussian-elimination-free (GE-free) multiple-cyclic-basis guessing codeword decoding (MCB-GCD) algorithm for BCH codes. Unlike conventional ordered statistics decoding (OSD), which selects a single most reliable basis via GE, MCB-GCD employs multiple cyclic bases, each consisting of k consecutive bits that serve as the re-encoding basis. By leveraging the cyclic structure of BCH codes, the proposed algorithm completely eliminates online GE and supports parallel list decoding through multiple re-encoding bases. A local-constraint (LC) mechanism together with trivial and dynamic approximate ideal (DAI) stopping criteria is employed to reduce the average number of searches. We prove that, with unlimited searches and tailored early stopping, the proposed algorithm is a non-exhaustive-search ML decoding algorithm. Furthermore, a saddlepoint-based numerical method is derived to estimate the upper bound on frame error rate (FER) and the average number of searches for the proposed decoding algorithm, confirming that MCB-GCD closely approaches maximum-likelihood (ML) performance with dramatically reduced average number of searches. Simulation results over BPSK-AWGN channels demonstrate that the BCH codes decoded by the proposed MCB-GCD closely approach the finite-length capacity across all supported code rates, while outperforming that with OSD, GCD and LC-GCD under certain parameters.

title: Energy Consumption Modeling and Optimization for Hybrid PLC/WLC Systems.
abstract: Hybrid Power Line Communication (PLC) and Wireless Communication (WLC) technology provides a reliable and cost-effective communication framework for applications such as smart grids and the Industrial Internet of Things (IoT), by synergistically leveraging the complementary strengths of both PLC and WLC. However, most existing energy efficiency studies have focused on a single communication medium, and the energy efficiency of hybrid PLC/WLC systems has not yet been systematically modeled or analyzed. To address this issue, closed-form expressions for the energy consumption per bit (bEC) of PLC and WLC are derived, providing a theoretical foundation for subsequent energy efficiency evaluation. Furthermore, a low-complexity Delay-Constrained Energy Consumption Optimization (DC-ECO) algorithm is proposed to minimize the overall system energy consumption through dynamic allocation between PLC channels and WLC channels. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DC-ECO algorithm reduces the total energy consumption by more than 50% compared with the conventional single WLC scheme. Under low-load conditions, the performance gap from the theoretical lower bound is <5%, significantly improving the energy efficiency while satisfying the transmission delay requirements, thereby providing an effective and practical solution for future energy-efficient hybrid communication systems.

title: From Detectors to Decisions: Probabilistic Fusion for Multiple Target Tracking.
abstract: Modern tracking systems parallelize numerous pretrained deep detectors to deliver multi-dimensional detection for each individual target. These detectors operate asynchronously, and exhibit heterogeneous, target-specific accuracy. An efficient, training-free probabilistic fusion framework is a key enabler for turning outputs from a bank of detectors into coherent trajectory. In particular, we model soft detector responsibilities with a factor graph, and loopy sum–product algorithm (SPA) on the association subgraph produces soft assignment posteriors that feed back into the responsibility chain and drive the state updates. The proposed drop-in pipeline adapts detector responsibilities online to shifting conditions, delivering robust data association and state estimation across diverse multi-detector scenarios. A closed form Gaussian realization is presented, and numerical result including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) validate the superior performance of our proposed algorithm compared with alternative approaches.

title: VN-Dict: Lightweight Authenticated Spatial Queries over Hybrid-Storage Blockchain.
abstract: Blockchain technology, with its decentralized, tamper-proof, and traceable properties, offers a promising foundation for trusted data management. Its potential is being explored for various applications, including spatial data storage, where applications like logistics tracking demand guarantees of authenticity, traceability, and secure multi-party cooperation. However, the direct integration of large-scale spatial data is hindered by prohibitive on-chain storage costs and the complexity of managing spatial indexes. To address the storage bottleneck, hybrid-storage architectures have emerged, where data is stored off-chain with cryptographic digests maintained on-chain to guarantee data integrity for queries. Existing solutions that employ R-tree indexes for this purpose suffer from large verification objects and inefficient on-chain updates, leading to significant resource consumption. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a lightweight authenticated data structure for spatial k-nearest neighbor (kNN) queries. Our method combines vector commitment with a Voronoi diagram to construct an authenticated Voronoi dictionary. This structure generates compact verification objects and enables gas-efficient on-chain maintenance that supports arbitrary updates. Security analysis verifies the security of authenticated queries and the correctness of updates. Experiments demonstrate that our approach reduces transmission overhead by up to 90% compared to state-of-the-art methods, and the cost of ADS updates on-chain remains constant, independent of the database size.

title: A Physical Layer Security Method Based on Multi-AAV Collaborative Beamforming.
abstract: With the development of the low-altitude economy, a large number of autonomous aerial vehicles (AAVs) will be deployed in low-altitude environments, capable of effectively performing data collection and relay tasks. Unlike non-line-of-sight transmission environments on the ground, the line-of-sight transmission of AAVs offers greater channel gain while facing a higher risk of data interception. Although the traditional encryption method can decrease the risk of data being cracked, it cannot diminish the probability of data being intercepted by eavesdroppers. In this paper, we propose a physical layer security method based on the distributed collaborative beamforming for the multi-AAV networks, in which both scenarios of known and unknown eavesdropper locations are considered. Then, two beamforming algorithms are designed for these scenarios. Besides, the theoretical performance is derived for the case where the location of the eavesdropper is known, while for the unknown-location case, a beamforming scheme based on the generalized Rayleigh quotient is introduced to substantially improve the secure transmission performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a substantial improvement in average secrecy rate without increasing the payload of AAVs compared with the conventional methods.

title: 6G-Enabled Heterogeneous Multi-Scale Transformer for Cooperative Multi-Agent Traffic Signal Control.
abstract: Urban traffic congestion has become an enduring challenge in metropolitan transportation systems, leading to severe travel delays, energy waste, and environmental impact. Reinforcement learning (RL)–based traffic signal control (TSC) has shown great promise in addressing this issue; however, its performance is constrained by limited sensing coverage and the absence of global situational awareness. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces a 6G-enabled Decentralized Actor–Centralized Critic framework with a Heterogeneous Multi-Scale Transformer (HMST) module for cooperative multi-intersection traffic signal control. The proposed framework jointly leverages fine-grained local observations from infrastructure sensors and aggregated large-scale traffic states inferred from 6G base stations. Using localization and channel state information from mobile users, the system estimates vehicle density and speed within each road segment, enabling agents to coordinate efficiently under a unified multi-scale representation. Experiments on real-world urban networks in Shanghai and Paris demonstrate that our approach significantly improves control performance, achieving up to a 33.7% reduction in average waiting time and a 30% improvement in average speed compared with other baselines.

title: iRadioDiff: Physics-Informed Diffusion Model for Indoor Radio Map Construction and Localization.
abstract: Radio maps (RMs) serve as environment-aware electromagnetic (EM) representations that connect scenario geometry and material properties to the spatial distribution of signal strength, enabling localization without costly in-situ measurements. However, constructing high-fidelity indoor RMs remains challenging due to the prohibitive latency of EM solvers and the limitations of learning-based methods, which often rely on sparse measurements or assumptions of homogeneous material, which are misaligned with the heterogeneous and multipath-rich nature of indoor environments. To overcome these challenges, we propose iRadioDiff, a sampling-free diffusion-based framework for indoor RM construction. iRadioDiff is conditioned on access point (AP) positions, and physics-informed prompt encoded by material reflection and transmission coefficients. It further incorporates multipath-critical priors, including diffraction points, strong transmission boundaries, and line-of-sight (LoS) contours, to guide the generative process via conditional channels and boundary-weighted objectives. This design enables accurate modeling of non-stationary field discontinuities and efficient construction of physically consistent RMs. Experiments demonstrate that iRadioDiff achieves state-of-the-art performance in indoor RM construction and received signal strength based indoor localization, which offers effective generalization across layouts and material configurations. Code is available at https://github.com/UNIC-Lab/iRadioDiff.

title: Joint Device Pairing and Bandwidth Allocation Optimisation for Semantic Feature Multiple Access Networks.
abstract: This paper presents a Semantic Feature Multiple Access (SFMA) framework for multi-user semantic communication in downlink wireless systems. By extending SwinJSCC to a two-user superimposition paradigm, SFMA enables simultaneous semantic transmission to multiple users over shared time-frequency resources. A key innovation is the Cross-User Attention (CUA) module, which facilitates controlled semantic feature exchange between paired users by leveraging inter-image similarity while mitigating interference. We formulate a joint user pairing and resource allocation problem to minimize global semantic distortion under constraints on bandwidth, end-to-end latency, and energy. This mixed-integer non-convex problem is decomposed into a Minimum-Weight Perfect Matching (MWPM) sub-problem and a convex bandwidth allocation feasibility check, with semi-closed-form bandwidth bounds derived from a strictly concave rate expression. A polynomial-time algorithm based on Blossom matching and bisection search is proposed. Extensive simulations on ImageNet-100 show that SFMA significantly improves reconstruction quality across pairing modes, and the proposed optimization effectively reduces overall distortion while satisfying physical-layer constraints.

title: Edge Heterogeneous LLMs Collaborative Reliable Inference Based on Adaptive Repeat Query.
abstract: Deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) at the network edge is crucial for ubiquitous Artificial Intelligence (AI). Compared to a single LLM, collaborative inference with multiple LLMs can significantly enhance robustness, but strict resource constraints pose challenges for reliable inference. This paper proposes the Gating Adaptive Repeat Query (G-ARQ) framework, which enhances robustness by transforming collaborative inference into a semantics-driven closed-loop process. A fact-checking engine triggers an intelligent gating mechanism to dynamically select the next LLM for the query. In G-ARQ, the Semantic-Space Alignment and Error-Guided Retransmission (SEMAR) mechanism aligns heterogeneous LLM outputs into a unified semantic space and uses inference errors information to guide next LLM selection, while a trajectory optimizer jointly manages LLM gating and resource allocation without explicit system dynamics. Experiments on the hybrid dataset of SQuAD and TriviaQA show that under stringent latency constraints, the accuracy can be improved by up to 5.3%, establishing a Pareto boundary for the G-ARQ framework to characterize the trade-off between accuracy and latency, offering a practical path for reliable Sixth-Generation (6G) edge intelligence.

title: Data Fusion for Multi-Band Zadoff-Chu OFDM Based Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: To enhance sensing accuracy in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, this paper proposes a multi-band Zadoff–Chu sequence based orthogonal frequency division modulation (ZC-OFDM) ISAC framework with an overlapped resolution based data fusion strategy. Specifically, a prediction-based data selection method is developed to exploit the overlapped resolution grids among multiple sensing bands and incorporates target motion information to identify the most reliable detections. In addition, a conventional weighted-average fusion method is also formulated based on fitted resolution error distributions for comparison. As a benchmark, an ideal selection scheme assuming perfect target range knowledge is introduced to evaluate the upper bound of performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms single-band baselines in multi-target ISAC scenarios, achieving lower optimal sub-pattern assignment (OSPA) metrics.

title: Exploiting Submodularity for Efficient Discrete Movable Antenna Placement.
Mitigating Intent Inference Errors in Large-Model-Assisted SLO-Aware Routing.
abstract: In this paper, we study an intent-driven service level objective (SLO)-aware routing problem for cloud-edge multi-domain networks, in which service intent signals are provided by an upstream large-model-assisted intent inference component to guide automated routing and orchestration. The key challenge is that inferred intents can be uncertain and directly acting on hard (top-1) intent predictions may mislead the closed-loop controller, causing unnecessary SLO violations and performance instability, especially when the network operates near congestion. To address this issue, we propose a lightweight and deployable Soft-Intent Guard (SIG) framework that sits between intent inference and control to make intent usage more reliable, without changing the underlying routing policy. The proposed framework consists of two simple mechanisms: 1) soft intent usage, which treats inferred intents as graded signals to avoid abrupt control changes, and 2) confidence-based guarding, which triggers a safe fallback behavior when the intent signal is unreliable. SIG is designed to mitigate intent uncertainty propagation in closed-loop control, where small inference errors can be amplified into large performance degradation. Simulation results in a multi-domain routing setting with controlled intent error rates show that SIG can consistently enhance robustness: at a critical load point, SIG improves SLO satisfaction by up to 6.13 percentage points for the most affected service class, while keeping tail latency and packet drop behavior comparable to benchmark schemes.

title: An Alternating Directional Dual-RBF Approach for Joint Multi-BSs and Multi-RISs Deployment.
abstract: The deployment of sixth-generation (6G) networks must overcome the spatial mismatch between network capacity and traffic demand caused by heterogeneous traffic patterns, all while managing high energy consumption. To achieve sustainable network deployment, this paper investigates the joint deployment of base stations (BSs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) to maximize Integrated Relative Energy Efficiency (IREE). We propose an Alternating Directional Dual-Radial Basis Function (ADD-RBF) framework, which models BSs and RISs as two distinct classes of radial basis neurons within a unified architecture. This framework enables the alternating optimization of active beamforming, bandwidth allocation, and node locations for BSs, alongside the passive beamforming and placements for RISs, to enhance capacity while mitigating spatial traffic mismatches. Simulation results demonstrate that the ADD-RBF scheme effectively mitigates the traffic-capacity mismatch while achieving reduced energy consumption, confirming the complementary roles of both components: RISs efficiently resolve localized traffic hotspots, while BSs address systemic capacity shortages. These findings offer practical guidelines for green 6G network design.

title: Bistatic Passive Tracking via CSI Power.
abstract: Accurate object tracking for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) remains challenging due to limited bandwidth, sparse antenna arrays, and clock asynchronism in bistatic deployments. Although channel state information (CSI) phase carries fine-grained sensing information, it is often severely distorted by time-varying phase offsets and therefore requires complex compensation procedures that may introduce artifacts. This work proposes WiDFS 2.5, a real-time passive tracking framework that operates directly on CSI power. While discarding CSI phase, WiDFS 2.5 shows that CSI power still implicitly pre-serves the motion-related phase evolution that is crucial for object tracking and sensing. To exploit this implicit phase information, WiDFS 2.5 employs a cascaded fast Fourier transform (FFT) pipeline to extract delay, angle of arrival (AoA), and Doppler features, and mitigates symmetry-induced mirror components via single-sided delay processing. The resulting measurements are then used for target detection, outlier suppression, and extended Kalman filter (EKF) tracking to enable accurate real-time trajectory estimation. Moreover, using the estimated target positions as a spatiotemporal filter, WiDFS 2.5 produces refined micro-Doppler signatures for fine-grained motion sensing. Experiments with 3.1 GHz LTE and 5.8 GHz WiFi bistatic signals (20 MHz bandwidth) achieve a median tracking error of 0.52 m, without requiring prior antenna calibration for AoA estimation, while extracting clear micro-Doppler signatures of the tracked target.

title: Pruned Causal Inference Enabled Active Deception for Covert Internet of Things (IoT).
abstract: In this paper, the problem of covert wireless communication in Internet of Things (IoT) systems under passive eavesdropping attacks is investigated. In the considered model, an IoT system intents to transmit a confidential signal from an origin to a destination under time and energy limitations. Meanwhile, a group of eavesdroppers attacks the IoT system by only passively listening to the confidential transmission without transmitting any signals. By detecting the oscillator leakage, the IoT devices can perceive the existence of nearby passive eavesdropping attacks. In this case, we propose an active deception scheme, with which the IoT devices will strategically transmit fake signals to distract and expose the passive eavesdroppers. Then, the passive eavesdroppers have to carefully choose the signal to intercept while avoiding exposure. The complex interaction among IoT devices and passive eavesdroppers is captured using tools from dynamic deception game, within which the conflicting goals of IoT system privacy and eavesdropping attacks are captured in multi-attribute utilities. Considering the challenges on searching the perfect bayesian equilibrium (PBE) in the partially observable, large-scale wireless IoT system, a pruned causal inference based approach is proposed. Simulation results show that the proposed method yields an up to 63.6% improvement in the convergence speed as compared to the traditional Bayesian-inference algorithm, while exhibiting an up to 229% improvement in security performance as compared to a traditional deception strategy that is designed by an open-loop algorithm.

title: Coordinated Movable Antennas Assisted Covert ISAC for Low-altitude Systems.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel coordinated movable antennas (MA)-assisted covert integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) strategy for low-altitude systems, where the transmitter not only emits ISAC signals, but also generates artificial noise (AN) to increase the uncertainty of the warden’s detection and enhance the sensing performance. We aim to maximize the sensing signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio (SCNR) by jointly optimizing the covariance matrix of the transmit signal/AN, positions of transmit/receive MA, and the receive filter. To solve the highly coupled nonconvex problem efficiently, a Dinkelbach–block successive upper-bound minimization (BSUM) algorithm is developed, which guarantees tractable block-wise updates and monotonic convergence. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed strategy, showing that coordinated MA arrays achieve an up to 3.6 dB sensing SCNR gain over the conventional fixed-position antenna scheme.

title: A Reconfigurable Dual-Port, Triple-Band Antenna System Enabling Seamless, on-Demand Wake-Up, Wireless Power Transfer, and Data Telemetry in IoMT Applications.
abstract: This paper presents a dual-port reconfigurable antenna system designed for on-demand wake-up, wireless power transfer, and data communication. The proposed system pairs with smart implantable devices for cardiovascular disease monitoring within Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) networks. Integrating RF switching circuit using PIN diodes, the antenna can dynamically reconfigure among three operational bands at 868 MHz, 915 MHz, and 2.45 GHz for wake-up, power, and data transmission, respectively. The influence of the on-board circuitry on antenna performance is analyzed through reflection coefficient (S11) simulations, showing stable impedance characteristics under different configurations. In addition, transmission between the external and implantable antennas demonstrates coefficients of -41.589 dB and -53.819 dB, indicating reliable power transferring and data acquisition.A proof-of-concept prototype is fabricated and experimentally validated, demonstrating efficient signal transmission with integrated control circuitry. Furthermore, a custom mobile application is implemented for real-time closed-loop control via user equipment (e.g., smartphone, tablet, or laptop). The design proposed a multi-functional antenna system that provides the feasibility for future IoMT-based healthcare monitoring applications.

title: Triad-GAN: Feature-Level Generative Adversarial Network for Multi-Receiver Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification.
An Augmented GNSS-DAS Architecture for Continuous and Robust Positioning.
abstract: Accurate and resilient positioning is essential for Internet of Things (IoT) applications, including smart transportation, urban navigation, and logistics tracking. While GNSS provides ubiquitous outdoor coverage, it can fail in challenging environments such as urban canyons and tunnels. To address this, we propose a hybrid framework that integrates GNSS with Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) and validate it through real-world experiments, achieving consistently accurate positioning under adverse conditions. By leveraging existing fiber-optic cables as vibration sensors, DAS offers a complementary and interference-resistant source of spatial information when GNSS is unreliable. Experimental results show that the Joint DAS and GNSS (JDG) substantially outperforms conventional imputation and prediction methods, enhancing positioning robustness for IoT-enabled smart transportation and urban navigation.

title: Delay-Constrained Multiuser MISO Downlink: Performance Analysis and Power Allocation.
abstract: The increasing demand for ultra-reliable and low-latency communications (URLLC) has motivated research on transmission strategies under delay constraints. The access delay, i.e., the time from a codeword becoming the head-of-line to being successfully transmitted, constitutes a major portion of the overall transmission latency. This paper investigates a multiuser multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) downlink system with mean access delay. We first derive analytical expressions for the system information output rate (IO-Rate) as explicit functions of the mean access delay threshold and per-user average power constraint, under heterogeneous large-scale path loss. The analysis considers two representative power allocation schemes: truncated channel inversion and waterfilling. To gain further insight, we then analyze a special case with identical path loss among users, which reveals the fundamental rate-delay trade-off and its scaling behavior with respect to the degrees of freedom of the effective channel and transmit power. Furthermore, an optimal average power allocation strategy is formulated to maximize the IORate of the system under a total average power constraint.Simulations validate the theoretical analysis, showing that: 1) The IO-Rate saturates under loose delay constraints and increases linearly with transmit power (in dB) in the high signal-to-noise ratio regime. 2) When the number of base station antennas scales proportionally with the number of users, the IO-Rate of the system scales linearly with user count. 3) The proposed delay-aware power allocation achieves 25% higher IO-Rate than equal power allocation and outperforms the ergodic capacity maximizing allocation under stringent delay constraints while the gap increases as the constraint tightens.

title: Index Packet Error Correction in Digital Semantic Communications Through Vector-Quantized Diffusion Models.
Deep Unfolding Supported Cell-free Anti-jamming Coordinated Multipoint Beam Pattern Synthesis.
abstract: Traditional cell-free anti-jamming beamforming faces high complexity, poor adaptability, and limited scalability. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel two-stage deep unfolding-assisted coordinated multipoint beam pattern synthesis (DUCoMP-BPS) scheme, which seamlessly integrates model-based optimization with data-driven learning. In the first stage, each access point (AP) independently determines analog beamforming using local angle information with deep unfolding accelerating computation, eliminating the need for real-time central processing unit (CPU) communication. Then, the CPU aggregates analog beamforming weights from multiple APs to perform cooperative digital beamforming. The proposed scheme possesses excellent scalability with complexity increasing linearly with the number of APs. Simulations show that DUCoMP-BPS shows strong anti-jamming communication robustness and reduces single-AP analog beamforming runtime by about 67% compared to model-driven methods and outperforms the data-driven approach in beam pattern performance. For example, under the configuration of 10 APs and 64 antennas per AP, < 1 dB mainlobe ripple can be achieved while maintaining ≤ -15 dB sidelobe and two 8°/-30 dB nulls.

title: Dual-Active Handover-Based Resource Allocation for GEO-LEO Heterogeneous Satellite Networks.
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of link instability and dynamic network topology encountered during the Dual Active Protocol Stack (DAPS) handovers in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks. It investigates joint optimization of handover and resource allocation in heterogeneous Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO)–Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks. A multi–time–scale frame structure is designed to harmonize the differences in resource–scheduling cycles between GEO and LEO satellites. A joint optimization model that integrates handover strategy, beam–hopping illumination, power control, and subcarrier allocation is formulated to minimize the downlink–latency gap between the source and target satellites during user handover. To address the strong coupling among variables, a problem–decomposition strategy is adopted to divide the problem into two subproblems: resource scheduling and handover decision–making, solved using the Distributed Proximal Policy Optimization (DPPO) algorithm and the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), respectively. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively adapts to link–state fluctuations in dynamic heterogeneous satellite–network environments, improving handover–latency stability and enhancing resource–scheduling efficiency.

title: RF-Vision Fusion Non-Cooperative UAV Detection and Identification for Low-Altitude Security.
abstract: Precise non-cooperative unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) detection and identification are of crucial importance for the low-altitude network security. Although various single-sensor solutions have been explored, their performance degrades under the sensor-specific noise, resulting in limited robustness and performance. To address these limitations, we propose a radio-frequency (RF)–vision fusion-based method that exploits both the time-frequency features of RF signals and the high spatial resolution of visual data to achieve precise UAV detection and identification. Moreover, a novel unified RF-Vision fusion Network (RFViNet) is designed to fully exploit the RF-vision cross-modal complementarity and semantic synergy. Specifically, by leveraging the RF-informed proposal generation, RF-enhanced feature modulation, and RF-guided semantic query, RFViNet effectively integrates the RF and visual information at the proposal, feature, and semantic levels, respectively. Furthermore, the performance of the proposed RFViNet is evaluated in our developed practical RF–vision system. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed RFViNet achieves a competitive 85.8% average precision under various challenging scenarios, including the complex electromagnetic interference and nighttime.

title: Reducing ORBGRAND Latency via Partial Gaussian Elimination.
abstract: Guessing Random Additive Noise Decoding (GRAND) is a universal framework for decoding all block codes by testing candidate error patterns (EPs). Ordered Reliability Bits GRAND (ORBGRAND) facilitates parallel implementation of GRAND by exploiting log-likelihood ratio (LLR) rankings but still suffers from high tail latency under unfavorable channel conditions, limiting its use in real-time systems.We propose an elimination-aided ORBGRAND scheme that reduces decoding latency by integrating the Rank of the Most Reliable Erroneous (RMRE) bit with a partial Gaussian-elimination (GE) filtering mechanism. The scheme groups and jointly verifies EPs that share the same RMRE, and once a valid EP is identified, the ORBGRAND search is resumed. By leveraging prior GE steps to filter out unnecessary guesses, this approach significantly reduces the number of EPs to be tested, thereby lowering both average and worst-case latency while maintaining error-correction performance.Simulation results show that compared to the original OR-BGRAND, the elimination-aided ORBGRAND filters out more than 50% of EPs and correspondingly reduce overall computational complexity, all with no loss in block error rate. This demonstrates that this approach is suitable for ultra-reliable low-latency communication scenarios.

title: Unified Channel Estimation Framework for Flexible Sparse DMRS Patterns via Transformer-based Point Cloud Neural Operator.
abstract: In current mobile communication systems up to 5G, orthogonal demodulation reference signals (DMRS) are inserted per resource block (RB) and for each layer of spatial multiplexing. However, as we move to increase the number of layers in 6G, DMRS overhead potentially limits the expected benefits of capacity growth. While CNN channel estimation methods under sparse DMRS allocation (such as ReEsNet and ChannelNet) have been proposed, these existing models are trained for specific DMRS patterns and cannot handle practical systems with resource schedulers, where RB allocation patterns vary dynamically over time slots. This configuration fragmentation requires massive dedicated model libraries, limiting scheduling flexibility. To address these fundamental issues, this paper proposes a unified channel estimation framework based on Transformer architecture inheriting the concept of point cloud neural operator, enabling a single model to handle arbitrary DMRS patterns and densities flexibly. Extensive simulations across 5 distinct configurations demonstrate that the proposed unified model achieves 5.0 to 5.5 dB improvement over dedicated ReEsNets and up to 11.0 dB improvement over classical LS estimation at 50% DMRS density, while enabling 50 to 75% overhead reduction. The unified approach eliminates the need for massive model libraries and does not limit the potential gains of scheduling operations, providing a practical solution for next generation wireless systems.

title: The Asymptotic Vector Witsenhausen Counterexample: When Optimal Transport Meets the Hypersphere.
abstract: Implicit communication has attracted considerable recent attention because it holds the promise of enabling decentralized decision-making or control with nonclassical information in next-generation industrial internet-of-things and other cyberphysical systems. The Witsenhausen counterexample plays a vital role in understanding implicit communication based decentralized control. Unfortunately, computing the optimal solution of the scalar Witsenhausen counterexample has been shown to be NP-complete. In this paper, we are interested in an asymptotic vector Witsenhausen counterexample with sufficiently large dimension, which also sheds light on the performance upper bound of its scalar version. In this context, the sphere hardening effect allows us to build a unified framework based on optimal transport from the surface of a high-dimensional sphere to a target domain in Euclidean space. Both the target domain and transport plan are judiciously conceived in order to minimize the mean-square error (MSE) in estimating variables distributed in the target domain, given a constraint on the transport cost. By leveraging the sphere packing and covering theorems in high-dimensional geometry, we obtain the closed-form MSE. Numerical results not only validate our theoretical analysis, but also demonstrate the performance gain of the optimal transport-based policy over the information theory-based policy inspired by dirty-paper coding and joint source-channel coding.

title: RF Impairments Compensation for OFDMA System with Model-based Machine Learning Approach.
abstract: In this paper, we propose two model-based learnable multi-layer structures for joint frequency domain equalization and radio frequency (RF) impairments compensation in orthogonal frequency-division multiple access (OFDMA) systems. Our approach uses transmitter (Tx) pre-compensation to address user-specific RF imperfections, particularly carrier frequency offset (CFO). The first structure employs Tx pre-compensation for CFO and receiver (Rx) post-compensation for Tx/Rx in-phase/quadrature-phase imperfections (IQIs), offering reduced Tx complexity. The second structure implements Tx pre-compensation for both CFO and Tx IQI, with Rx post-compensation for Rx IQI, providing more accurate compensation but higher Tx complexity. Simulation results show that both structures require only small training samples for effective learning, and the second structure achieves ideal case performance when RF imperfection parameters are known.

title: Field Trials of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces for Coverage Enhancement in Urban Transportation Infrastructures.
abstract: The integration of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) into commercial networks is a pivotal step towards realizing the vision of the sixth generation (6G) network. However, field trials in large-scale, complex urban environments remain scarce, leaving a gap in understanding their practical performance under real-world constraints. This paper presents field trial results from a commercial network deployed in the challenging, mountainous city of Chongqing, focusing on three critical transportation infrastructure scenarios: tunnels, river-crossing bridges, and riverside roads. Contrary to idealized setups, our trials demonstrate that RIS delivers substantial performance gains even under non-optimal deployment conditions with large incident angles and long distances. This work goes beyond conventional downlink-centric trials by providing a comprehensive uplink-downlink joint analysis and introducing fine-grained physical-layer metrics, the channel quality indicator (CQI) and the modulation and coding scheme (MCS), which collectively reveal the performance gains of RIS in dynamic environments. Our work offers invaluable empirical evidence and deployment insights for integrating RIS into future wireless networks.

title: Joint AMC and Power Control for HARQ-Enabled Uplink SCMA in LEO Satellite Communications.
abstract: This paper investigates SCMA-enabled uplink transmission with hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) and adaptive modulation and coding (AMC), referred to as SCMA-HARQ, for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite communications. We first formulate the expected throughput of the proposed SCMA-HARQ by decoupling the multiuser interference among SCMA users. The resulting problem is formulated to maximize the expected system throughput, leading to a mixed discrete-continuous optimization with per-user throughput and reliability constraints. To address the inherent nonconvexity and the large interference-coupled decision space, we propose a federated hybrid soft actor-critic (FH-SAC) framework, in which each TU learns a decentralized policy for joint modulation and coding scheme (MCS) selection and transmit power control, while periodic parameter aggregation enhances learning stability and scalability. By incorporating HARQ-aware throughput modeling into the soft actor-critic learning process, the proposed approach explicitly accounts for retransmission effects in the control loop. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed FH-SAC scheme in SCMA-HARQ systems in terms of convergence speed, robustness with respect to the number of supported users, and overall throughput improvement.

title: A Capacity-Aware Task Allocation Scheme in Internet of Agents.
abstract: As large language model (LLM)–driven agents proliferate, the Internet of Agents (IoA) is emerging as a decentralized ecosystem of heterogeneous, autonomous agents. Achieving large-scale cooperation in such systems requires reliable agent capability modeling and adaptive task allocation. However, existing approaches often rely on self-reported capabilities and overlook the workflow-dependent nature of coalition capability. This paper presents a capacity-aware task allocation framework for IoA that addresses these gaps through three components: i) a dynamic capability verification model that transforms self-declared skills into empirical quality and throughput metrics; ii) a topology-aware coalition capability aggregation method that models intra-coalition workflows as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) and computes coalition capabilities via both serial (multiplicative) and parallel (additive) reductions; and iii) a many-to-one stable matching formulation with a low-cost two-sided iterative algorithm to obtain optimal and stable task assignments under coalition capacity constraints. Extensive simulations demonstrate the proposed framework’s effectiveness and scalability compared with baseline methods.

title: DeepJSCC-LZ-MI: A Mutual Information Driven Framework for Task-Oriented Distributed Semantic Communication.
abstract: Distributed semantic communication systems often underutilize side information, as existing fusion schemes either operate at a single scale or ignore the information-theoretic correlation between the received and side-information features, leading to limited robustness under varying channel conditions. To address this gap, we propose DeepJSCC-LZ-MI, a task-oriented distributed JSCC framework for Wyner–Ziv scenarios. The core is a Mutual-Information-Guided Multi-Scale Fusion module that selectively injects complementary side-information features based on estimated cross-stream mutual-information relevance, while preserving spatial details with negligible overhead. In addition, a task-oriented end-to-end training strategy with progressive SNR scheduling aligns the optimization with semantic objectives and enhances cross-SNR robustness. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet32 show that DeepJSCC-LZ-MI achieves 0.5–2.1 dB Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and 3.0–15.8% classification accuracy improvements while reducing floating-point operations (FLOPs) by 59.3% compared with DeepJSCC–WZ. The model further generalizes well to large-scale datasets (1000 classes) and remains robust under Rayleigh fading, demonstrating its effectiveness for practical 5G/6G semantic communication.

title: Transform-Domain M-PSK Constellation Design for RIS-Enabled Backscatter Systems.
When Guidance Turns Poisonous: Backdooring the SAR-guided Cloud Removal Model.
abstract: Models for optical-image cloud removal guided by Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) have made remarkable progress in addressing cloud occlusion in remote sensing. However, the vulnerability of such models to backdoor attacks remains unexplored. To fill this gap, we present the first backdoor attack on SAR-guided optical-image cloud removal models. Unlike previous approaches that embed triggers into optical images, we embed triggers into SAR images. By exploiting the inherent speckle-like texture of SAR imagery, we design a frequency-aware speckle trigger that is both stealthy and robust against common data augmentations. After training on poisoned data, the backdoored model generates manipulated cloud-free outputs that faithfully reconstruct an attacker-specified target scene when the trigger is present, while preserving high-quality restoration performance on clean inputs. We evaluate three commonly used SAR-guided optical-image cloud removal models on public datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms other triggers designed for optical images.

title: Coding-Enforced Resilient and Secure Aggregation for Hierarchical Federated Learning.
abstract: Hierarchical federated learning (HFL) has emerged as an effective paradigm to enhance link quality between clients and the server. However, ensuring model accuracy while preserving privacy under unreliable communication remains a key challenge in HFL, as the coordination among privacy noise can be randomly disrupted. To address this limitation, we propose a robust hierarchical secure aggregation scheme, termed H-SecCoGC, which integrates coding strategies to enforce structured aggregation. The proposed scheme not only ensures accurate global model construction under varying levels of privacy, but also avoids the partial participation issue, thereby significantly improving robustness, privacy preservation, and learning efficiency. Both theoretical analyses and experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our scheme under unreliable communication across arbitrarily strong privacy guarantees.

title: Rotatable Antenna Array-Enhanced Null Steering: Performance Analysis and Optimization.
abstract: Conventional fixed-orientation antenna (FOA) arrays offer limited degrees of freedom (DoF) for flexible beamforming such as null steering. To address this limitation, we propose a new rotatable antenna array (RAA) architecture in this paper, which enables three-dimensional (3D) rotational control of an antenna array to provide enhanced spatial flexibility for null steering. To characterize its performance, we aim to jointly optimize the 3D rotational angles of the RAA, to maximize the beam gain over a given desired direction, while nulling those over multiple interference directions under zero-forcing (ZF) beamforming. However, this problem is non-convex and challenging to tackle due to the highly nonlinear expression of the beam gain in terms of the rotational angles. To gain insights, we first examine several special cases including both isotropic and directional antenna radiation patterns, deriving the conditions under which full beam gain can be achieved over the desired direction while meeting the nulling constraints for interference directions. These conditions clearly indicate that compared with FOA arrays, RAAs can significantly relax the angular separation requirement for achieving effective null steering. For other general cases, we propose a sequential update algorithm, that iteratively refines the 3D rotational angles by discretizing the 3D angular search space. To avoid undesired local optimum, a Gibbs sampling (GS) procedure is also employed between two consecutive rounds of sequential update for solution exploration. Simulation results verify our analytical results and show superior null-steering performance of RAAs to FOA arrays.

title: A Digital Twin-Enabled Approach for Resource Allocation in Cross-Domain Network Slicing.
abstract: Network Digital Twin (NDT) and network slicing are key technologies for the next-generation mobile networks (6G), enabling a transformation in network planning, construction, and operation. However, existing 5G networks face issues such as heterogeneous resource types, differing management strategies among operators, and cross-domain data privacy constraints, which hinder the interoperability of node resources and state information. This paper proposes the use of a DT network to create virtual counterparts of physical nodes, enabling cross-domain information exchange and collaborative optimization across Radio Access Network (RAN) and Core Network (CN) domains. The main contributions are: (1) a DT-based cross-domain heterogeneous network slicing architecture, using Software Defined Network (SDN) to mirror the operating states of physical nodes for interaction and collaboration between slices and twins; (2) a physical network model for pretraining resource scheduling strategies at the physical network layer; (3) a transfer learning mechanism to migrate pretrained strategy parameters from the physical to the virtual twin network, establishing collaborative resource allocation between the twin and physical networks. This mechanism further supports coordination between AI-RAN and the CN. Simulation results show that the proposed solution outperforms the baseline in multi-agent resource scheduling tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in cross-domain collaboration and joint resource scheduling in a multi-slice heterogeneous environment.

title: Channel Capacity Bounds and Asymptotic Analysis for FMCW-based Optical Wireless ISAC.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a foundational usage scenario for the sixth-generation (6G) mobile communication system, with optical wireless (OW)-ISAC rapidly advancing as a compelling alternative to its radio-frequency counterpart. Among OW-ISAC technologies, frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW)-based light detection and ranging (LiDAR) gains significant attention for its ability to achieve direct velocity estimation. In this paper, the channel capacity of FMCW-based OW-ISAC is analyzed to evaluate the influence of the sensing constraint on the communication performance. Firstly, the channel model of FMCW-based OW-ISAC is recast into an information-theoretic formulation, where an additional harmonic-mean constraint is imposed to ensure the sensing performance. Subsequently, the lower bound for channel capacity is given by the entropy-power inequality and the max-entropy distribution. In addition, the dual expression provides an upper bound for channel capacity, which converges to the same asymptotic expression as that of the lower bound in the high-signal-to-noise-ratio region. Numerical results illustrate the performance metrics of OW-ISAC and highlight the trade-off between its communication and sensing functionalities.

title: Epistemology-Inspired Bayesian Games for Distributed IoT Uplink Power Control.
abstract: Massive number of simultaneous Internet of Things (IoT) uplinks strain gateways with interference and energy limits, yet devices often lack neighbors' Channel State Information (CSI) and cannot sustain centralized Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) or heavy Machine Learning (ML) coordination. Classical Bayesian solvers help with uncertainty but become intractable as users and strategies grow, making lightweight, distributed control essential. In this paper, we introduce the first-ever, novel epistemic Bayesian game for uplink power control under incomplete CSI that operates while suppressing interference among multiple uplink channels from distributed IoT devices firing at the same time. Nodes run inter-/intra-epistemic belief updates over opponents' strategies, replacing exhaustive expected-utility tables with conditional belief hierarchies. Using an exponential-Gamma SINR model and higher-order utility moments (variance, skewness, kurtosis), the scheme remains computationally lean with a single-round upper bound of $O\!\left(N^{2} S^{2N}\right)$. Precise power control and stronger coverage amid realistic interference: with channel magnitude equal to $1$ and a signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) threshold of $-18$ dB, coverage reaches approximately $60\%$ at approximately $55\%$ of the maximum transmit power; mid-rate devices with a threshold of $-27$ dB achieve full coverage with less than $0.1\%$ of the maximum transmit power.Under $80\%$ interference, a fourth-moment policy cuts average power from approximately $52\%$ to approximately $20\%$ of the maximum transmit power with comparable outage, outperforming expectation-only baselines. These results highlight a principled, computationally lean path to optimal power allocation and higher network coverage under real-world uncertainty within dense, distributed IoT networks.

title: Digital Twin-Assisted Measurement Design and Channel Statistics Prediction.
abstract: Prediction of wireless channels and their statistics is a fundamental procedure for ensuring performance guarantees in wireless systems. Statistical radio maps powered by Gaussian processes (GPs) offer flexible, non-parametric frameworks, but their performance depends critically on the choice of mean and covariance functions. These are typically learned from dense measurements without exploiting environmental geometry. Digital twins (DTs) of wireless environments leverage computational power to incorporate geometric information; however, they require costly calibration to accurately capture material and propagation characteristics. This work introduces a hybrid channel prediction framework that leverages uncalibrated DTs derived from open-source maps to extract geometry-induced prior information for GP prediction. These structural priors are fused with a small number of channel measurements, enabling data-efficient prediction of channel statistics across the entire environment. By exploiting the uncertainty quantification inherent to GPs, the framework supports principled measurement selection by identifying informative probing locations under resource constraints. Through this integration of imperfect DTs with statistical learning, the proposed method reduces measurement overhead, improves prediction accuracy, and establishes a practical approach for resource-efficient wireless channel prediction.

title: RIS-assisted Maximum-SNR mmWave Communications via Stochastic Approximation.
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have emerged as a solution to enhance the performance of millimeter wave (mmWave) wireless links by dynamically tuning the phase shift of a large number of reflecting elements. In this paper, we propose a practical framework to maximize signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for RIS-assisted mmWave Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) links. We first optimize the RIS phase shifts to maximize the received signal strength (RSS) by adopting Kiefer-Wolfowitz Stochastic Approximation (KWSA) where the gradient is approximated through RSS measurements. Upon optimizing the RIS configuration, we design the transmit and receive beamforming vectors based on the estimated channel and noise covariance matrices at the receiver. We implement the proposed method in a RIS-assisted mmWave software-defined radio (SDR) testbed based on USRP® and TMYTEK® platforms in an indoor laboratory environment. We demonstrate that the proposed RIS optimization approach achieves the highest RSS with almost half of the amount of RSS measurements required by the exhaustive grid search approach. Upon RIS optimization, we show that Tx/Rx beamformer optimization offers an additional 7 dB gain in SNR. Given an RSS-optimized RIS configuration, the proposed optimization of Tx/Rx beamformers to maximize SNR requires 51x less computations than exhaustive search.

title: Evaluating AFDM-Based Integrated Sensing and Communication in Vehicular Scenarios.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is envisioned as a key enabler for 6G networks, empowering devices with enhanced environmental perception capabilities. In this paper, we explore the application of Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing (AFDM) in vehicular scenarios under realistic raytracing channels. We develop a low-complexity on-grid sensing algorithm that directly extracts delay and Doppler shifts. By selectively processing dominant delay bins and incorporating maximum ratio combining (MRC), the proposed method provides an efficient sensing solution while significantly reducing computational overhead. Simulation results demonstrate that AFDM-based sensing attains superior or comparable accuracy to OFDM with lower complexity, offering an efficient and scalable solution for high-mobility environments.

title: Fair Energy Efficient Resource Allocation for Wireless Agent Network (WAN).
abstract: This paper investigates fairness-oriented energy efficiency optimization for semantic communications in a satellite–air–ground integrated network (SAGIN) assisted by uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs), where relay UAVs are explicitly modeled as intelligent agents capable of autonomous displacement decisions. By actively adjusting their two-dimensional positions, relay agents can reshape the communication environment to improve system performance. Considering direct, relay-assisted, and satellite–relay-assisted transmission paths, we formulate a max–min energy efficiency optimization problem that jointly optimizes path selection, semantic compression ratios, and relay UAV displacement under latency and mobility constraints. To avoid decision coupling and double counting of mobility energy, an exclusive source–relay association mechanism is adopted, in which each relay agent executes a single-step displacement per decision period. An alternating optimization framework is developed, combining path-wise energy efficiency evaluation via one-dimensional compression search with constrained relay position updates. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed agent-based scheme consistently achieves superior max–min energy efficiency and robustness compared with baseline approaches across varying task sizes, mobility budgets, and delay thresholds.

title: Harnessing LLMs with Graph Representation Learning for Anomaly Detection in Microservices.
abstract: Large-scale microservice systems, characterized by distributed and complex architecture, pose substantial challenges for anomaly detection. Existing approaches operating at the trace or service level often fail to capture intricate and fine-grained dependencies between services, leading to suboptimal detection performance. To address these limitations, we propose a novel graph-based anomaly detection framework MAD-LLM, which takes advantage of the rich knowledge of Large Language Models (LLMs). Our approach consists of three key steps. First, we design a unified data model that integrates heterogeneous observability data, including traces, logs, and metrics, into a structured representation. Second, inspired by graph neural networks, we introduce a self-supervised neighbor aggregation module to fine-tune LLMs by incorporating local topological context from service dependency graph. Finally, we employ a fine-tuned LLM to generate node embeddings that encode the semantic and structural properties of a metric-aware events graph, which are leveraged for anomaly detection. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of our approach. MAD-LLM achieves an average F1-score improvement of 9.1% over the best-performed baseline, with a maximum gain of 22.9% on the TraceBench dataset. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of our design and highlight its necessity for achieving optimal performance. The source code can be available at https://github.com/wz-01/MAD-LLM.

title: Joint Antenna Position and Rail Radius Design for Circular Pinching Antenna Systems.
abstract: Pinching-antenna systems have emerged as a promising technology for next-generation networks by enabling continuous aperture reconfiguration via translating a dielectric perturbation along a guided-wave structure. With this structure, pinching antenna systems can provide line-of-sight (LoS) propagation and avoid deep fading, yielding a strong and highly predictable channel for reliable communication. However, most existing studies focus on linear waveguide configurations, which introduces a topological mismatch when serving two-dimensional user distributions. This paper proposes a circular rail architecture for circular coverage regions. We first develop a pinching antenna positioning algorithm that maximizes the instantaneous rate. Subsequently, we derive the rate-optimal radius of the circular rail. Simulation results confirm that the proposed circular architecture outperforms diameter-aligned linear benchmarks in terms of achievable throughput.

title: Joint Optimization of Multi-UAV Trajectory and User Association for Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: Multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platforms with integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) technology will see increasingly widespread application in the future. However, for multi-UAV ISAC networks to achieve desired performance, challenges such as higher user mobility, time-varying channels, resource competition among multiple users, and multi-UAV trajectory design must be addressed. For the problem of user mobility in multi-UAV multi-user scenarios, we apply a real-time user tracking and prediction strategy based on an extended Kalman filter, with its performance bound derived from the Cramér–Rao bound. Then, to achieve high-rate communication and high-accuracy location tracking, this paper proposes an optimization framework based on clustering, coalitional games, and successive convex approximation. Simulations verify the superior communication rate and tracking accuracy of the proposed scheme over conventional approaches.

title: Availability of Aerial Heterogeneous Networks for Reliable Emergency Communications.
abstract: We investigate network availability (NA) in aerial heterogeneous networks (AHetNets) for effective emergency rescue, where diverse delay-constrained communication services must be provided to user equipments (UEs) with varying mobility. The heterogeneity in delay constraints and UE mobility introduces resource allocation conflicts and imbalances, which undermine communication reliability and challenge NA. Although unified resource allocation (URA) can mitigate these issues, it remains unclear whether NA can be sustained under such diverse conditions. To address this, we derive expressions for the lower bound (LB) on NA in AHetNets under URA. Our analysis reveals that extended heterogeneity significantly degrades the LB due to resource limitations—even when the heterogeneity stems from additional services under less stringent delay constraints (LSDC) or from UEs with lower mobility. To overcome this degradation, we formulate and solve a joint optimization problem for the number of UEs sharing time-frequency resources (K) and pilot length (ξ), aiming to enhance the LB by improving spatial, frequency, and temporal resource efficiency. Simulation results validate our analysis and demonstrate that jointly optimizing K and ξ enables AHetNets to achieve the target NA under greater heterogeneity, outperforming existing resource allocation policies.

title: MOR-GenREH: A Multi-Stage Nonlinear Rectifier Model with Generalized Statistical Rectification for Radio Frequency Energy Harvesting.
abstract: This paper presents a detailed modeling and simulation study of a multi-stage nonlinear rectifier for radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting. The rectifier is modeled analytically using the multi-stage nonlinear energy-harvesting (EH) formulation that extends the generalized statistical rectifier (GSR) concept by incorporating higher-order nonlinearities and inter-stage attenuation effects. A MATLAB-based implementation of the analytical and circuit models reproduces the rectifier behavior, capturing the nonlinear dependence of output voltage, power conversion efficiency (PCE), and harvested DC power on input RF power, load resistance, and the number of stages. The simulated results demonstrate that the proposed rectifier achieves high normalized efficiency and voltage scalability, validating the model as an effective analytical tool for designing RF EH circuits.

title: Impairment Leakage Attention-Based Denoising for 5G NR RF Fingerprinting Under Low SNR.
abstract: Radio Frequency Fingerprinting (RFF) identifies transmitters via hardware impairment, which is promising for enhancing air interface access security in future mobile communications. However, RFF is an inherently weak feature that can easily be masked in noise under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, such as at 5G New Radio (NR) cell edges, and current denoising techniques are prone to distorting RFF characteristics. To fill this gap, this paper proposes an impairment leakage attention-based denoising (ILA-D) method for 5G NR RF fingerprinting. This denoising method is built on the diffusion model, and a new impairment leakage attention (ILA) mechanism is proposed to optimize the design of the noise prediction network, thereby reducing the damage to RFF features while denoising. Specifically, according to the theoretical model of RFF, three distinct impairment leakage patterns generated by hardware impairment in 5G NR transmitted signals are derived first to form a set of attention positions. Then, the attention weight is designed according to the correlation between the source subcarrier signal and the target subcarrier leakage corresponding to different leakage patterns. By enhancing attention to these subcarriers, the RFF features are no longer blurred during the denoising process, thus achieving the goal of improving RFF recognition performance under low SNR conditions. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed ILA-D enhanced RFF method in low SNR environments. At -10dB SNR, it outperforms existing denoising-based RFF schemes by 35.47% in identification accuracy, while preserving RFF discriminative features and enhancing 5G NR RFF robustness.

title: Cross-Application Key Abuse Attack against Hardware-backed Android Keystore.
abstract: The Android Keystore is a cornerstone of mobile security, providing application developers with hardware-backed protection for cryptographic keys. While hardware isolation prevents direct key extraction, it cannot stop malicious applications from misusing keys. We systematically analyze the Keystore’s access control model and reveal its strong reliance on the untrusted Rich Execution Environment (REE), which exposes protected keys to cross-application abuse. We demonstrate the feasibility of such attacks on real devices through a two-step process: UID spoofing and user authentication bypass. Since the latter depends on application-level Keystore authentication settings, we analyzed 160 Android applications, including the top 100 most-downloaded apps on Google Play and 60 two-factor authentication (2FA) apps. Among the 2FA apps, 32 used the hardware-backed Keystore, yet most misconfigured authentication: 21 lacked it entirely, six used long validity windows, and eight misused biometric binding, leaving hardware-protected keys exposed.

title: Joint Communication and Sensing Beamforming for Secure Transmission in 6G SAGINs.
abstract: In 6G space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs), integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables terrestrial devices to support secure computation offloading via simultaneous uplink transmission and eavesdropper detection using shared spectrum resources. However, non-orthogonal access induces severe multi-terminal interference (MTI), while limited angular resolution leads to uncertainty in eavesdropper localization—posing significant challenges to physical-layer security. To address this, we propose a joint ISAC beamforming design that maximizes communication performance while guaranteeing robust secrecy against directional eavesdroppers despite angular estimation uncertainty. To solve this non-convex, dynamic problem, we propose a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based deep reinforcement learning framework under the centralized-training-decentralized-execution (CTDE) paradigm, which learns adaptive beamforming policies in a model-free manner while enabling low-overhead online execution. Simulations show the method significantly improves communication performance and effectively resists worst-case eavesdropping, demonstrating its potential for securing future 6G ISAC-enabled SAGINs.

title: Carbon-Aware Computing and Communication Resource Optimization in Edge-Cloud Networks.
abstract: With the increasing demands of computing and communication resources for wireless network, the relevant carbon emissions have rapidly increased. However, the study of carbon-aware optimization for mobile edge computing (MEC) networks is still far from complete. To address this, this work presents a novel computing and communication resource optimization approach that dynamically adjusts computing and communication resources, task offloading, task migration among edge nodes, user association, and edge node ON/OFF at two different timescales of the network for reducing carbon emissions. To develop the approach, we formulate a problem that minimizes long-term carbon emission subject to network stability, queue length and novel end-to-end (E2E) latency constraints. By exploiting the two-timescale Lyapunov technique, a solution framework for the problem is devised. Simulations show that our proposed approach can obtain effective tradeoff between the carbon emission and average latency and outperform the reference schemes.

title: Trade-off Frontier of the OCDM-Based ISAC System with Pilot Arrangements.
abstract: The severe Doppler effects in high-mobility scenarios pose critical challenges for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC), motivating the development of next-evolution waveforms (NEW). Therefore, this paper investigates orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) waveform for ISAC, leveraging its inherent robustness derived from the time–frequency duality of chirp modulation. First, a compact Fresnel-transform representation is adopted to establish an analytical signal and channel model for OCDM over multipath Doppler channels. Based on this model, we characterize the communication performance under Doppler-induced interference and develop a range–velocity estimation method via FFT-based processing. Furthermore, closed-form expressions for the achievable rate and the Cramér–Rao bounds (CRBs) are derived for adjustable pilot density and placement. These expressions quantify the OCDM-specific resource trade-off and reveal how pilot arrangement determines the performance boundary. Simulation results validate that the proposed OCDM scheme with optimized pilot arrangements achieves a lower bit error rate and higher sensing accuracy in high-mobility environments.

title: Contribution-Aware Coalition Federated Learning in Edge-Assisted Healthcare Monitoring Systems.
abstract: Healthcare digital transformation has driven an explosion in electronic medical data, which holds great potential for improving diagnostic precision and healthcare quality. Yet, it is confronted with the issue of data privacy sensitivity. Federated edge learning (FEL) addresses this challenge by enabling privacy-preserving collaborative global model training and integrating edge computing’s near-source processing, while enhancing privacy and adapting to healthcare’s resource-constrained environments. However, device mobility causes delayed and inconsistent data updates, which slows global model convergence and may prevent models from reaching the desired performance within limited training rounds. To address these complexities, We propose a coalition federated edge learning (CFEL) framework for FEL Healthcare Monitoring, with two specialized calculation strategies (optimized for large/small-scale user mobility) addressing mobility-induced data inconsistency and delayed updates in the healthcare device ecosystem. We design a tailored CFEL algorithm and defined the coalition Shapley value (CSV) to compute contributions within the framework. In small-scale user mobility scenarios, CSVs act as reliable aggregation weights, ensuring accurate reflection of each user’s contribution in model updates. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed algorithm by comparing it with different weight generation methods in different scenarios.

title: Movable-Antenna Position Optimization with Partial CSI via RACOS.
abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) are recognized as a promising technology for enhancing the performance of wireless communication by enabling local antenna movement. However, optimizing MA positions requires full channel knowledge within a continuous movement region, which incurs excessively high training overhead. To tackle this problem, this paper proposes a new antenna position optimization framework for MA systems without explicit channel state information (CSI). Unlike existing partial-CSI-based MA position optimization algorithms limited to point-to-point scenarios, the proposed framework can be applied to a broader range of problems involving more constraints and design variables. Its basic idea is to transform the constrained position optimization problem into a black-box problem with an unknown objective function. This problem is then solved by combining a penalty-based method and the randomized coordinate shrinking classification (RACOS) method. As a case study, we investigate a joint power control and antenna position optimization problem for an MA-enhanced cognitive radio system by applying the proposed framework. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed framework can significantly outperform the conventional fixed-position antennas (FPAs) and other baseline schemes with or without explicit CSI.

title: Movable Antenna Position Optimization for Energy Efficient Secure Communications.
abstract: Movable antenna (MA) can be employed to enhance physical-layer security by reconfiguring wireless channel conditions for both legitimate users and eavesdroppers via local antenna movement. However, to achieve accurate and fast antenna movement, MA drivers entail non-negligible power consumption, rendering secure energy efficiency (SEE) optimization more critical compared to conventional fixed-position antenna (FPA) systems. To tackle this problem, this paper develops a new mechanical power model for two-dimensional (2D) MA arrays. Based on this model, we formulate a new SEE maximization problem, aiming to jointly optimize the MAs’ 2D moving velocities, 2D positions, and their transmit beamforming vector. Due to the complex mechanical power consumption model, this SEE maximization problem is difficult to solve optimally. To overcome this difficulty, we first uncover that the SEE always monotonically increases with the velocity of each MA in each dimension. For the remaining joint position and beamforming optimization, we develop a two-layer optimization framework. In the inner layer, the Dinkelbach algorithm is employed to derive the optimal beamforming solution in a generalized Rayleigh quotient form for any given MA positions. In the outer layer, a sequential update algorithm is proposed to iteratively refine the MA positions based on the optimal values obtained from the inner layer, jointly with Gibbs sampling to avoid local optimality. Numerical results show that the SEE of the considered system can be significantly improved compared with FPAs and other baseline schemes.

title: Optimizing Security Performance of LEO Satellite Communications with IRS against Mobile Diverse Eavesdroppers.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite communication can complement to terrestrial networks by providing extended Internet access to remote regions, especially those in harsh environments. However, some operational satellites may work as Eavesdroppers (Eves), referred to as ESats, intercepting confidential signals during communication between the Ground Station (GS) and the Serving Satellite (SSat). Besides, Eavesdropping Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (EUAV) also poses a potential threat to satellite-ground communication along the extended propagation paths. In view of this, this paper deploys an Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) near the GS within the satellite system, where several ESats and EUAV coexist and the satellite follows a predictable trajectory. We discuss the optimal transmit beamforming vector and IRS configuration to maximize the Ergodic Secrecy Rate (ESR) and minimize the Secrecy Outage Probability (SOP). Besides, to mitigate the multipath effect induced by the satellite mobility, the Doppler spread is taken into consideration, which is to be minimized. A Genetic Algorithm (GA) is introduced to solve this intractable non-convex multi-objective problem. To evaluate the efficiency of IRS deployment and IRS phase shift optimization, we compare our proposed scheme against benchmark strategies, including systems without IRS, with random IRS, and with Artificial Noise (AN). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves enhanced security and communication performance and outperforms baselines.

title: A Comprehensive Comparison of Two Resource Allocation Schemes in DCNs under the Hose Model.
abstract: The joint allocation of virtual machines (VMs) to servers and network bandwidth have long been major challenges in data center networks (DCNs). The hose model was introduced to simplify VM and network bandwidth allocation without requiring pairwise traffic demands between VMs, as needed in the pipe model. In Oktopus, a virtual cluster V C(N,B) can be quickly constructed to guarantee a bandwidth B between N VMs under the hose model. A more recent approach, Elastic, defines V C(−,B), where − corresponds to the maximum number of VMs the current DCN can support. In this way, Elastic determines the largest slice, called the max C (for the cluster), and supports scheduling that offers maximum elasticity for future VM growth through a scaling-down approach. In this paper, we critically compare these two approaches in scheduling a sequence of batched VM requests and releases. We introduce a new approach, called Tailor, which is based on Elastic. Tailor first applies Elastic to generate the max C, and then subsequent VC requests are tailored and cut from this max C. Tailor also incorporates garbage collection after a sequence of releases and before constructing the next maximum VC. Comparisons in both simulation and testbed DCN show that Tailor outperforms Oktopus in terms of total execution time, by approximately 40%–80%, including scheduling and garbage collection.

title: Linkability-Resistant Decentralized Identity Scheme with Verifiable Pseudonym Credentials.
abstract: The rapid expansion of diverse, open, and dynamic network services and applications has made identity authentication a necessity for maintaining security and reliability in massive and frequent inter- and intra-domain interactions. Among existing identity authentication schemes, decentralized identity (DID) has become a prevalent self-sovereign paradigm to ensure privacy and autonomy. However, existing DID schemes often rely on persistent identifiers, which leads to residual linkability and suffers from correlation attacks by colluding verifiers. To tackle these issues, we propose a blockchain-based verifiable pseudonym credential (VPC) scheme using BBS+ signatures, where the holder can cryptographically derive independent pairwise pseudonyms from a persistent root DID. We decouple interactions from the root DID by enabling the issuance and presentation of VPCs under distinct pseudonyms to mitigate linkability risks from collusion. Furthermore, we facilitate selective disclosure through non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs to enable minimal disclosure of necessary attributes to verifiers and privacy protection. We introduce a credential session mechanism to achieve real-time proof-of-possession and resist against impersonation and replay attacks.
