We also conduct a concise security and performance analyses of our proposed scheme. Finally, we validate through simulations the risk-resistance and computational efficiency of our design.

title: Scalable Fluid Antenna Systems for Mixed-Field Source Localization.
abstract: Existing antenna array-based localization methods rely on fixed-position arrays and strict field assumptions (near-field or far-field), limiting their effectiveness in complex scenarios. This paper introduces a scalable fluid antenna system (SFAS) that dynamically adjusts its aperture for different localization tasks. We develop a two-stage strategy based on exact spatial geometry: a compressed aperture for initial direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation, and an expanded aperture for enhanced DOA and range estimation. This approach eliminates the need for source classification and achieves high accuracy without field-specific assumptions or approximations. Simulations demonstrate superior performance in localization accuracy and robustness across mixed-field environments.

title: Goal-oriented Semantic Communication for Joint Vehicle and License Plate Recognition.
abstract: Recently, video-based vehicle and license plate (LP) recognition have become a core requirement in city-scale traffic monitoring. However, constrained wireless resources have imposed a severe video transmission bottleneck, degrading its performance. To address the challenge, we propose a goal-oriented semantic Communication (GSC) framework for the joint vehicle and LP recognition task, which extracts semantic information, compresses, and protects each region based on its importance to the task. Specifically, we design a semantic information extraction module to remove spatial and temporal redundancy in the input video, which is irrelevant to the task. Then, we design an importance ranking module that ranks the importance of various semantic information regions based on the shapley value. Guided by the importance, the designed semantic-based encoding module allocates higher compression quality and stronger protection to regions critical for the task. Simulation results validate that our proposed GSC framework significantly outperforms H.264/H.265+LDPC, achieving a 250.02% and 133.32% increase in joint recognition accuracy, and a 99.26% and 98.87% reduction in communication cost, respectively.

title: Hierarchical Rate-Splitting Multiple Access for Layered Security.
abstract: In future 6G networks, multiuser systems face the challenge of layered message confidentiality. This paper investigates a secure transmission scheme tailored for a layered physical layer security (PLS) model, in which users are exposed to intra-layer and cross-layer eavesdropping threats. We propose a hierarchical rate-splitting multiple access (H-RSMA) scheme that partitions and combines transmitted signals based on their respective security layers. The proposed design exploits the dual functionality of the common stream serving simultaneously for interference management and artificial noise, so that the decoding capability of higher layer users is enhanced while eavesdropping attempts from lower layer users are suppressed. We formulate an optimization problem that jointly designs the precoding and rate-splitting matrices to maximize the worst-case sum secrecy rate (WCSSR). Numerical results show that the proposed scheme achieves superior WCSSR performance compared with 1-layer rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) and no rate-splitting (NoRS) baselines.

title: DoSMitigation: Mitigating DoS Attacks in Software Defined Networking.
abstract: The separated control and data planes in SDN introduce a more flexible way to manage and control network traffic. However, the limited data-to-control plane communication channel can be jammed by massive table-miss packets incurred by DoS attackers, resulting in high packet loss rate and long transmission delay. To defend against the SDN-aimed DoS attack, we propose DoSMitigation, a DoS attack mitigation framework which utilizes the idle resource of neighbor switches to confront the attack traffic. It works as an extension of the SDN switch in the data plane. Each switch collects the its neighbor switches’ idle resource information (data-to-control plane communication channel throughput, flow rule replacement rate, available bandwidth, etc.). When the DoS attack occurs, the overloaded switch distributes packets to the selected neighbor switches with idle resources in time to confront the SDN-aimed DoS attack cooperatively. The experiment results show that our strategy can prevent packet loss and reduce delay between hosts.

title: Efficient Privacy-Preserving Genetic Analysis via Distributed Function Secret Sharing.
abstract: Genetic research is pivotal for personalized medicine and understanding disease mechanisms, yet this field faces a critical privacy challenge due to the inherent sensitivity of genomic data. General Secure Multi-Party Computation protocols offer confidentiality but suffer from prohibitive communication and computational overheads, hindering their practical deployment. Function Secret Sharing (FSS) provides exceptional online efficiency, but its practicality is limited by reliance on trusted dealers or high offline costs in dealer-less constructions. To address these bottlenecks, this paper proposes an efficient privacy-preserving genetic analysis framework centered on distributed FSS. The core of our framework is a novel Dealer-less Compressed Full Domain Key Evaluation protocol. This protocol successfully adapts the early termination optimization to the dealer-less setting, reducing GGM tree traversal depth and PRG invocations without requiring a trusted dealer, which may be of independent interest. Furthermore, we leverage FSS-based primitive to construct efficient lookup tables and a secure division protocol. These building blocks are then applied to implement secure protocols for three crucial genetic analysis tasks including Secure Genomic Predicate Analysis, Secure Hamming Distance Evaluation, and Secure Bayesian Classification. Experimental results show our compressed full domain evaluation achieves up to a 3.99× latency reduction over prior FSS work. Compared to a SOTA general MPC framework, our full framework provides up to 31.03× less communication and 263.71× lower latency in both LAN and WAN environments.

title: MICS: Min-cost Joint 3C Scheduling with Asymmetric Routing.
abstract: The rapid rise of computation- & data-intensive applications, such as machine learning training and inference, poses significant challenges for joint communication, computation, and caching (3C) scheduling over the network. In this work, we study a cache-enabled computation network in which each node can forward packets, cache data, and execute compute tasks. Each task produces non-cacheable results and requires two types of input data: (i) cacheable data orchestrated by the cloud server and (ii) non-cacheable, user-specific data uploaded together with the request from the user. Existing joint 3C scheduling approaches either assume restrictive network topologies or neglect the size of user-specific input data, thereby relying on the widely used symmetric routing assumption, in which computation results always return to the user along the reverse path of the corresponding requests. We propose MICS, a distributed framework that incorporates user-specific data size into the model and jointly schedules network operations to minimize convex flow and computation costs across arbitrary network topologies. By breaking the symmetric routing, MICS significantly reduces system costs. In MICS, a dual subgradient-based control plane ensures ergodic convergence of the 3C variables under the Slater condition, while the data plane executes practical 3C operations. Simulations demonstrate up to a 32.1% improvement in average request satisfaction time compared to baseline methods.

title: Auditing Method of Private Data Unauthorized Access for Differential Privacy Model.
abstract: As machine learning models become widely deployed, ensuring that third-party models have not used sensitive datasets without authorization is critical for privacy protection. Even with differential privacy (DP) guarantees, auditing a model is challenging when the training data and parameters are inaccessible. To address this, we propose a distribution-based auditing method that compares the outputs of the target model with two auxiliary models. A query model is trained on the dataset of interest, while a calibration model is trained on a disjoint dataset sampled from the same data domain. For shared inputs, the output probabilities are used to construct empirical cumulative distribution functions (CDFs), and a noise-corrected Kolmogorov–Smirnov (K-S) distance is computed. An indicator ratio derived from these distances provides probabilistic evidence determines whether the target model incorporates the query dataset, accounting for different DP mechanisms (DP, zCDP, RDP, AC) and privacy budgets. Experiments on MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10, and ISIC datasets show that our method reliably detects unauthorized dataset usage while avoiding false positives on unrelated domains, demonstrating both its accuracy and robustness under defined assumptions and limitations.

title: Resource Allocation Strategy for AUVs-Assisted UWSN with MI Communication in Multi-Layer Ocean Current Environments.
abstract: Aiming at the challenges of low network coverage and limited battery power in underwater wireless sensor network (UWSN) operating within ocean currents, resource allocation strategy for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs)-assisted UWSN with magnetic induction (MI) communication in multi-layer ocean current environments is investigated in this paper. Specifically, the target monitoring area is divided into multiple ocean current layers at unequal intervals. First, sensor nodes (SNs) are deployed in these ocean current layers. The effect of ocean currents on SNs is analyzed. An improved virtual force algorithm (I-VFA) is employed to enhance the network coverage of the UWSN. Then, AUVs navigate to specific ocean current layers and collect data from SNs via MI communication. A genetic algorithm (GA) is adopted to optimize the navigation trajectories of AUVs. The transmitting power of SNs and the distance between SNs and AUVs are jointly optimized to minimize the energy consumption of SNs under the constraints of energy causality, transmitting power, distance, and transmission time. The suboptimal solution to the formulated optimization problem is obtained by adopting the global search whale optimization algorithm (GSWOA). Simulation results show that the GSWOA has a faster convergence speed and better global search capability than other benchmark methods.

title: Extended k-u Fading Model in mmWave Communication: Statistical Properties and Performance Evaluations.
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel small-scale fading model, named the extended k-u model, which incorporates the imbalance of multipath clusters by adding a new parameter based on the original k-u model. The extended k-u model has more accurate modeling capability than the extended η-u model in scenarios with line-of-sight (LoS) paths. Additionally, it is mathematically more tractable than the a-k-η-u model. The extended k-u model provides an effective channel modeling tool for millimeter (mmWave) LoS scenarios. Through theoretical derivations, we obtain closed-form expressions for the key statistical characteristics of this model, including the probability density function, the cumulative distribution function, moments of arbitrary order, and the moment generating function. Based on these statistics, this study further derives and analyzes the expressions for some performance metrics of the communication system, including the amount of fading, the probability of outage, the average bit error rate, and the effective rate. Using the measured fading data extracted from literature, which cover communication scenarios at 28 GHz, 65 GHz, and 92.5645 GHz with LoS paths, we apply the proposed model in mmWave scenarios and compare it with the k-u model and the extended η-u model. The results show that the extended k-u model has better capability in characterizing such fading than the other two models, verifying that this extension enhances its ability to model LoS mmWave scenarios.

title: Air Strike Task-Oriented Intelligent Communication System Based on Diffuse Reflection Visible Light.
abstract: As an important technology for 6G, Visible Light Communication (VLC) is highly suitable for internal cabin communication amid the current trend of cable-free and modular communication. This paper proposes a VLC system implementing "OOK + Manchester coding" based on deep learning. The system combines two neural networks to extract signal features and adopts a classification method for signal demodulation, adapting to the characteristics of high occlusion and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) paths in the missile interior. The "train-first-then-use" characteristic of artificial intelligence aligns well with the task features of air-to-ground missiles—long mounted flight time and short autonomous flight time. It can utilize the pre-launch time to complete data training, thereby supporting in-missile signal transmission after launch. Practical tests have shown that a communication rate of 1 Mbps can be achieved in a 1.2-meter-long channel with numerous internal obstacles, and the bit error rate (BER) is lower than 10−4.

title: MERCATOR: A Geography-Aware Structured Broadcast Protocol for Blockchain Networks.
abstract: Blockchain systems aim to achieve security and high-performance. These characteristics depend on efficient data broadcast mechanisms. However, existing mechanisms often suffer from inefficiency, primarily because they fail to consider geographic proximity in network topology construction and rely on redundant gossip-based transmission. We introduce Mercator, a geography-aware structured data broadcast protocol. It enables fast and robust data propagation through two techniques: (i) region division strategy based on geographic proximity, and (ii) an efficient and robust broadcast method covering inter-region and intra-region. Extensive simulations show Mercator significantly outperforms current broadcast schemes, reducing propagation latency by up to 61.94% and message redundancy by up to 73.03%. Moreover, Mercator maintains robustness and low latency even in the presence of 30% malicious nodes.

title: Location-Informed Edge Server Selection in Integrated Access Backhaul-Enabled 6G Networks.
abstract: With the advent of the Rel. 16 of the 5G system (5GS), 3GPP introduced the feature of integrated access and backhaul (IAB), which enables multi-hop cellular communications for coverage extension at the radio access network (RAN). 3GPP and ETSI have also worked towards the tight integration of 5G-Advanced and Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) infrastructures, targeting at seamless offloading of computation loads in the near area of user equipments (UEs). In this work, we present a benchmark analytical model that leverages the enhanced measurement capabilities of next-generation (NG)-RAN base stations (BSs) and the user equipments (UEs) towards location-informed MEC host selection in IAB-enabled 6G systems. We focus on the scenario where the UE selects between two candidate MEC hosts by pulling knowledge from the Location Management Function (LMF) on the relative positions of IAB donor BSs. Using as a key metric the aggregate length of the end-to-end IAB path separating the UE and the candidate MEC hosts, we derive exact and approximate expressions on the IAB path length distribution and assess the performance of a simplified yet location-informed MEC host selection strategy in IAB-enabled NG-RAN setups.

title: Robust Vision-Aided mmWave TDMA Hybrid Beamforming With Low-Resolution Phase Shifters.
abstract: Vision-aided beamforming is emerging as a key enabler for Next-Generation Multiple Access (NGMA), where multi-modal sensing and intelligent signal processing jointly enhance communication efficiency. However, extending vision-aided techniques to hybrid millimeter-wave (mmWave) architectures with limited-resolution phase shifters and ensuring robustness under dynamic environments remain challenging. This paper proposes a Vision-aided Hybrid Beamforming Network (VHBN) that explicitly embeds hardware constraints into a neural network trained with a physics-informed loss function. To enhance robustness, a Hierarchical Visual–Wireless Beamforming (HVWB) framework is further developed, where coarse visual predictions guide refined channel estimation through dictionary-based sparse reconstruction. Numerical results based on the DeepSense6G dataset demonstrate that: (i) the proposed approach achieves spectral efficiency nearly identical to that of conventional CSI-based schemes; (ii) VHBN offers greater hardware compliance for low-resolution phase shifters than existing CSI-free approaches; and (iii) HVWB exhibits superior robustness compared with existing vision-aided techniques in previously unseen environments. These results demonstrate the potential of vision-aided hybrid beamforming as a practical and intelligent solution toward NGMA realization.

title: An Adaptive Multimodal Integrated Sensing and Communication Framework for Embodied Agents.
abstract: Embodied agents (EAs) are expected to serve as key enablers in future human–machine societies by tightly integrating cyber intelligence with physical actuation. To achieve robust cognition and interaction in dynamic and uncertain environments, EAs are typically equipped with heterogeneous sensing modalities, such as cameras, LiDAR, and radar. This diversity underscores the significance of multimodal integrated sensing and communication (MISC), which exploits complementary sensing capabilities to overcome the inherent limitations of conventional single-modality integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Nevertheless, most existing MISC approaches are designed for fixed single-modality devices and lack adaptability to dynamically varying modality combinations or modality mismatches, thereby constraining the cognitive capability and robustness of EAs. To address these limitations, we propose an adaptive MISC (AMISC) framework that incorporates a multimodal adaptive fusion architecture (MaFA) for dynamic feature fusion across heterogeneous modality inputs, together with a neighbor-based feature enhancement (NeFE) strategy that enables cooperative perception among neighboring EAs via wireless links. The proposed framework allows each EA to utilize complementary features from its peers to compensate for missing modalities and enhance sensing reliability. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that AMISC can flexibly adapt to arbitrary multimodal combinations, achieving higher beam prediction accuracy with minimal communication overhead. Furthermore, by leveraging the NeFE strategy, the proposed framework effectively preserves sensing and communication performance even when certain critical modalities are unavailable, thus providing a scalable and resilient solution for next-generation embodied intelligence networks.

title: Distributed Covert Communication Under Imperfect Synchronization.
abstract: Covert communication offers a highly undetectable framework for wireless transmission in scenarios demanding secrecy and resilience by concealing the communication existence. However, centralized covert communication systems may achieve a heightened detectability when the eavesdropper and intended receiver are geographically co-located. Distributed multi-antenna systems provide a promising solution, upon leveraging spatial diversity to enhance coverage flexibility. Nevertheless, synchronization imperfections among distributed antennas critically degrade system performance, posing a fundamental challenge to covertness. To address this problem, we investigate joint beamforming and transmit power control for distributed covert communication, aiming at maximizing the covert capacity with the consideration of frequency-phase synchronization offsets. By employing Lagrange decomposition, we derive an analytical upper bound of asymptotic covert capacity and obtain a near-optimal beamforming solution. Simulation results validate our theoretical findings.

title: Collusion-Resistant and TTP-Free Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning via Dynamic Functional Encryption.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is widely used in privacy-sensitive domains, as it enhances privacy by exchanging model updates instead of raw data. However, studies have shown that model parameters can still leak private information. To address this, many privacy-preserving FL (PPFL) schemes adopt cryptographic techniques, but they often rely on trusted third parties (TTPs) and remain vulnerable to collusion. Decentralized multi-client functional encryption for inner product (DMCFE-IP) is a promising approach for these two issues. However, existing DMCFE-IP schemes require fixed weight vectors tightly bound to client keys. This limits flexibility and causes decryption failure if any client drops out. We propose a new DMCFE-IP scheme called DDMCFE-IP that supports dynamic aggregation weights and tolerates client dropout. Based on this scheme, we design SecFL, a TTP-free and collusion-resistant PPFL framework. Moreover, we have identified and proven that our DMCFE-IP scheme possesses the quasi-additive homomorphism. This property has potential applications in FL, as it may enable the server to perform computations directly on ciphertexts, thereby better supporting scenarios with specific requirements for aggregation weights. We analyze model performance on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10. Experiments show that SecFL achieves high model accuracy with moderate computational overhead in both IID and non-IID settings.

title: FedEG: Towards Fair Federated Learning via Expert-Guided Knowledge Transfer.
Dynamic Differential Strategy-Based Multi-proxy MTD for Low-Rate DDoS Attack Detection.
abstract: Low-rate Distributed Denial-of-Service (LDDoS) attacks present a significant threat to online web services due to their ability to mimic legitimate traffic patterns, making them difficult to detect with conventional methods. Traditional single-point traffic detection-based defense mechanisms often demonstrate limitations in accurately and promptly distinguishing between legitimate traffic and distributed low-rate attacks, primarily due to their singular perspective and reliance on historical and current behavioral data from a single point. This often results in low accuracy and high latency. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel detection scheme based on a multi-proxy moving target defense (MTD) framework. The core innovation of our approach is a novel multi-proxy differential collaborative detection mechanism. This mechanism enhances detection by analyzing state discrepancies across multiple proxy nodes in the spatial domain, building upon single-point temporal analysis, thereby identifying subtle, coordinated attack patterns that are indistinguishable from a single-point perspective. Validation through experiments conducted in real-world network environments and on the SUEE8 dataset demonstrates the effectiveness of our scheme. It achieved accuracy rates of 98.96% and 98.49%, and missed detection rates of 0.34% and 0.55%, respectively, outperforming existing state-of-the-art solutions. Furthermore, the detection latency was merely 15 ms, which is lower than that of existing LDDoS mitigation schemes.

title: Movable Antenna-Enabled Region-Oriented Wireless Sensing.
abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) have emerged as a promising technology to enhance wireless sensing in sixth-generation (6G) networks. The design of MA arrays typically relies on the precise prior knowledge of the target’s position, which is rarely satisfied in practice. To address this limitation, we introduce a region-oriented design that concentrates sensing resources over a predefined angular range. In this paper, we propose an MA-enabled wireless sensing system, focusing on optimizing the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) within the region of interest (RoI) for target direction estimation while suppressing the received energy outside the RoI. Then, we formulate a joint optimization problem, considering both antenna positions and sensing waveform design. To tackle this problem, we develop an alternating optimization algorithm to find the closed-form solution by iteratively optimizing the position of each transmit MA and sensing waveform with other variables being fixed. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed MA-enabled wireless sensing system significantly outperforms conventional fixed-position antenna (FPA) systems.

title: A Hierarchical Model for Ephemeris Extrapolation Towards Transmission Enhancement for SAGIN.
abstract: The integration of satellite and terrestrial systems in the space-air-ground integrated network (SAGIN) introduces new challenges in maintaining reliable communication due to high satellite mobility and dynamic channel variations. This paper proposes a hierarchical model that systematically exploits ephemeris information for orbital extrapolation to enhance communication performance in SAGIN. The proposed model establishes a global correlation framework linking orbital dynamics to communication functionalities across three planes: the Ephemeris Plane (E-Plane), the Mapping Plane (M-Plane), and the Communication Plane (C-Plane). By mapping orbital parameters to communication layers, the model enables efficient utilization of ephemeris data for optimizing key network functions. Three representative case studies are presented-cell selection, hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ), and Doppler frequency offset (DFO) estimation-demonstrating how ephemeris-driven enhancement improves mobility management, link reliability, and frequency synchronization. Simulation results validate that the proposed approach significantly enhances coverage continuity, throughput, and synchronization accuracy, providing a promising framework for robust integration of non-terrestrial and terrestrial networks in future 6G systems.

title: Joint Secure Task Offloading and Trajectory Optimization via Deep Reinforcement Learning for UAV-assisted Internet of Vehicles.
abstract: Computation-intensive vehicular applications, such as autonomous driving, are increasing task offloading demands in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). In its open wireless environment, frequent transmissions risk the leakage of sensitive data. Although encryption and blockchain mitigate such threats, they incur high computational overhead and latency, making them unsuitable for low-latency scenarios. Physical Layer Security (PLS) provides a lightweight alternative by exploiting channel characteristics, yet most existing approaches assume single or static eavesdroppers, limiting their applicability in dynamic settings. We propose a UAV-assisted secure offloading framework for environments with multiple mobile eavesdroppers. Using high mobility and line-of-sight links, UAVs serve as dynamic offloading nodes and proactive jamming sources, countering eavesdroppers while providing computational resources. We jointly optimize UAV trajectories and vehicle offloading decisions, modeling the process as a Markov Decision Process solved via a Proximal Policy Optimization-based deep reinforcement learning algorithm. Simulations demonstrate that our scheme outperforms A2C, DQN, and greedy baselines, reducing energy consumption while satisfying latency and security constraints, and improving adaptability in dynamic IoV.

title: Topology Reconfiguration for Vulnerability Optimization in Damaged LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks, as a key component of the next-generation (6G) mobile communications infrastructure, hold great promise to provide global connectivity and massive throughput. However, it is susceptible to the complex and dynamic space environment. For instance, sun outages induce transient link disruptions, and geomagnetic storms together with space-weather perturbations can lead to node failures and connectivity degradation, which in turn heightens network fragility and jeopardizes the reliability of the constellation. To enhance the resilience and robustness of LEO satellite networks, a vulnerability optimization framework based on topology reconfiguration is proposed, which dynamically rebuilds inter-satellite links (ISLs) to alleviate topological vulnerabilities and preserve connectivity under damaged conditions. To quantify vulnerability and guide reconfiguration, an improved hop–plane–node (IHPN) method is developed, and the feasible reconfiguration space is explored using a soft actor-critic–augmented hyperplane-assisted evolutionary algorithm (SAC-hpaEA). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces network vulnerability across diverse impairment scenarios and lowers communication cost, achieving superior robustness compared with conventional multi-objective optimization (MOP) algorithms.

title: Resilient Hierarchical Split Federated Learning over Resource-Limited Wireless Communication Systems.
abstract: As machine learning models escalate in size and wireless networks expand, deploying federated learning (FL) in edge environments encounters challenges, including increased transmission failures and constrained wireless resources. Although split federated learning (SFL) framework is proposed to mitigate these challenges by shifting workload from clients to a central server, the single-server suffers from limited capability to manage extensive communication workloads. To tackle these challenges, we design a Resilient Hierarchical Split Federated Learning (RHSFL) framework that ensures reliable, resource-efficient communication across a three-tier system by adopting a novel sub-model gradient recycle technique. Based on our analysis, we reformulate the joint optimization problem as minimizing the squared Age of Information (AoI) to indirectly reduce global training loss, and subsequently derive an equivalent linear programming formulation. To efficiently address this optimization, we propose an adaptive algorithm for client orchestration and resource block (RB) allocation. Simulation experiments conducted on the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets demonstrate that the proposed RHSFL framework outperforms baselines in terms of accuracy and convergence speed.

title: SemAID: Zero-Shot Semantic-Aware Image Communication with Adaptive Sampling and Diffusion-based Signal Recovery.
abstract: The paradigm of semantic communication prioritizes the recovery of semantically meaningful information over pixel-level fidelity, which is crucial for bandwidth-constrained and extreme environments such as deep-space exploration and disaster response. However, existing deep learning-based approaches often rely on task-specific training and struggle with the compound distortion of aggressive compression and severe channel noise. In this paper, we formulate semantic-aware image transmission as a signal recovery problem from incomplete and noisy measurements, guided by semantic importance. We propose SemAID, a novel framework that integrates an adaptive, semantic-driven non-uniform sampler at the transmitter and a generative diffusion-based Bayesian estimator at the receiver. The transmitter dynamically masks pixels based on saliency and edge information, effectively implementing content-aware compression. The receiver, leveraging a pre-trained diffusion model as a strong generative prior, solves the corresponding inverse problem via posterior sampling without any retraining. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SemAID achieves superior performance in both perceptual quality and reconstruction fidelity under low-SNR conditions, showcasing remarkable generalization across varying channel states and unseen data distributions. This work validates the potent efficacy of generative priors for semantic signal recovery under the compound challenge of non-uniform sampling and channel noise, offering a practical zero-shot solution for extreme communication environments.

title: Joint Discriminative Generative Semantic Communications via MLLMs.
abstract: Deep learning-based joint source-channel coding has recently demonstrated strong potential for semantic communication (SemComm). However, most existing approaches focus on optimizing visual-fidelity metrics, which can lead to reduced perceptual quality. Generative model-based SemComm leverages rich prior knowledge from large-scale pre-training to enhance perceptual quality, but often at the cost of increased distortion and unreliability. This paper addresses above issues by proposing a two-stage semantic image transmission framework, integrating a multimodal large language model (MLLM) for generative editing. In the first stage, a JSCC-based discriminative transmission selectively prioritizes semantically important regions, preserving scene layout and object integrity under limited bandwidth. In the second phase, MLLM-driven generative editing refines missing details based on the textual descriptions, enhancing semantic fidelity and perceptual quality. Extensive experiments show that the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in semantic preserving, perceptual quality, and visual fidelity across a wide range of channel conditions, specially in low-SNR regimes.

title: Unlocking Bistatic Target Detection for ISAC: Synergizing Deterministic Pilots and Unknown Random Data Payloads.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) is a key enabler for 6G applications such as drone surveillance, urban air mobility, and low-altitude logistics. However, the hybrid ISAC signal, which comprises deterministic pilots and random data payloads, poses challenges for target detection, since 1) these components jointly affect both the mean and variance of the received signal, and 2) the random data payloads are typically unknown to the sensing receiver in bistatic systems. To address these, we develop a generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT)-based detector that exploits the known pilots and the statistical properties of the unknown payloads. Given the exact performance is analytically intractable, an asymptotic analysis of the false alarm probability is conducted. Simulation results validate the theoretical derivations and demonstrate the superiority of the proposed detector, which highlights the importance of tailored ISAC detection that fully leverages data payload resources.

title: Edge Transciphering: A Practical Framework for Future Telecom Privacy Computing on Data Processing.
abstract: As future telecom networks evolve toward the integration of sensing, communication, and computing, data-driven services are becoming increasingly prevalent. However, there are security concerns regarding Over-The-Top (OTT) servers accessing user data from the User Equipment (UE). Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) allows data to be processed in ciphertext and is considered one of the necessary ways to guarantee secure privacy computing in telecom networks. Nevertheless, the inherent ciphertext expansion of FHE results in massive data volumes, imposing significant overhead on resource-constrained wireless air interfaces. To address the issue of enabling UE privacy computing in the future telecom network, this paper proposes an edge homomorphic transciphering framework. We deploy the transciphering function within edge computing nodes, such as the User Plane Function (UPF). UE only needs to transmit symmetrically encrypted data at low expansion rates, and the network edge computing node converts this into FHE ciphertext and forwards it to the OTT server. We validated the framework using multi-modal payloads. Our scheme reduces transmission overhead in air interface and enables the telecom network to apply FHE while mitigating the impact of ciphertext expansion. Furthermore, we tested the system by integrating two representative block ciphers, AES and HIGHT, verifying the framework’s flexibility for future telecom devices.

title: Distributed Learning for Low-Altitude Economy: A Collaborative Adaptation Approach.
abstract: Distributed learning is pivotal for enabling local raw-data processing in the low-altitude economy (LAE), given the surging demand for localized data processing. In this paper, we propose a novel distributed learning algorithm for LAE, in which some unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) act as edge servers and perform distributed learning with multiple UAV clients. Considering the heterogeneity of the LAE, in the proposed algorithm, we exploit the clustering UAV architecture to locally train the model with distributed data. We formulate the resource-abundant UAVs to perform backpropagation-based knowledge programming learning process. We further introduce resources-limited UAVs to conduct test-time adaptation (TTA)-based collaborative knowledge aggregation process after downloading all the domain knowledge vectors. Compared to various benchmark schemes, we validate the efficiency of our proposed collaborative distributed learning algorithm, and show how it can achieve better convergence performance with reduced communication cost and training cost.

title: SMART: A Sparse MoE-Transformer Framework for Environment-aware Channel Prediction.
abstract: Accurate channel prediction is essential for addressing the channel aging issue without introducing additional signaling overhead in wireless communication systems. Most existing works rely on a general, static model to handle highly diverse wireless environments, suffering from poor generalization, limited adaptability, and suboptimal performance in real-world deployments. Although large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated promising sequence modeling capabilities for channel prediction, their massive computational costs hinder real-time deployment, especially for latency-sensitive communication scenarios. To address these limitations, we propose SMART, a novel Sparse MoE-trAnsformer framework for enviRonment-aware channel predicTion, which achieves both personalized prediction and computational efficiency. SMART replaces the standard feed-forward networks in each Transformer sub-layer with a sparse mixture of experts (MoE) module, consisting of one shared expert capturing environment-invariant features and multiple specialized experts, each tailored to distinct environmental conditions. A lightweight routing network is trained to dynamically activate only the most relevant experts for each input, enabling adaptive inference pathways for different channel characteristics of different environments. Our proposed SMART only activates a small subset of experts during each forward process, thereby significantly improving computational efficiency while preserving high model capacity. Extensive experiments have been conducted to compare the performance of SMART with state-of-the-art solutions. Our experimental results suggest that SMART provides up to 14.02% and 41.77% improvement in multi-environment channel prediction accuracy, compared to Transformer and LLM-based solutions, respectively.

title: BMPrune: Bidirectional Magnitude-based Backdoor Pruning with Clean Preservation and Malicious Penalization.
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, posing serious risks to their secure deployment. Recent research reveals that backdoors can be erased from infected DNNs by pruning a specific group of neurons, while how to effectively identify and remove these backdoor neurons remains an open challenge.In this paper, we found that backdoor neurons exhibit abnormal magnitude-saliency correlations distinct from benign neurons. Building on this observation, we propose BMPrune, a bidirectional pruning framework that includes: (1) exposing backdoor behavior by amplifying malicious neurons’ abnormal magnitude patterns, (2) eliminating backdoor triggers through deviation-aware pruning, and (3) preserving model functionality by stabilizing clean neurons’ magnitude-saliency alignment. This bidirectional strategy enables BMPrune to achieve state-of-the-art defense performance across diverse attacks using minimal clean data, conclusively demonstrating neuron magnitude’s pivotal role in trustworthy model repair.

title: Dual-Hop Joint Visible Light and Backscatter Communication Relaying under Finite Blocklength.
abstract: This paper investigates a dual-hop joint visible light communication (VLC) and backscatter communication (BC) relaying framework under the finite blocklength (FBL) constraint, aiming at energy-neutral Ambient Internet of Things (A-IoT) deployments. In the proposed system, indoor LED access points are used to simultaneously provide illumination and transmit information over light to a backscatter device (BD), which harvests optical energy and backscatters the received messages to user equipments (UEs) equipped with radio frequency (RF) front ends. This forwarding of the information from VLC to RF channels is implemented without the need for carrier synthesizers and power amplifiers at the IoT node. By modeling the end-to-end communication link with short-packet IoT traffic and realistic levels of interference between adjacent VLC coverage areas, we analyze the outage performance and achievable data rate of the proposed system. Simulation results demonstrate that key factors, such as placement and orientation of the BD, as well as the selected code rate of the system affect reliability and data rate that can be achieved for communication purposes. The insights gained from this study pave the way for ambient power-enabled IoT solutions and future hybrid VLC/RF network designs.

title: Multi-hop Parallel Image Semantic Communication for Distortion Accumulation Mitigation.
abstract: Existing semantic communication schemes primarily focus on single-hop scenarios, overlooking the challenges of multi-hop wireless image transmission. As semantic communication is inherently lossy, distortion accumulates over multiple hops, leading to significant performance degradation. To address this, we propose the multi-hop parallel image semantic communication (MHPSC) framework, which introduces a parallel residual compensation link at each hop against distortion accumulation. To minimize the associated transmission bandwidth overhead, a coarse-to-fine residual compression scheme is designed. A deep learning-based residual compressor first condenses the residuals, followed by the adaptive arithmetic coding (AAC) for further compression. A residual distribution estimation module predicts the prior distribution for the AAC to achieve fine compression performances. This approach ensures robust multi-hop image transmission with only a minor increase in transmission bandwidth. Experimental results confirm that MHPSC outperforms both existing semantic communication and traditional separated coding schemes.

title: Dynamic Clustered Federated Learning for Distributed Channel Prediction.
abstract: Accurate channel state information (CSI) prediction is crucial for optimizing performance in modern communication systems, such as Wi-Fi and 5G. However, the performance of data-driven prediction is challenged by the significant variations in channel statistics across users, which stem from their diverse wireless environments. Traditional centralized prediction schemes that centrally collect users’ data are usually impractical due to prohibitive communication overhead. Federated learning (FL) is a distributed training framework that addresses this overhead by enabling collaborative model training while keeping users’ data locally. Nevertheless, training a single global model via FL struggles to capture the distinct channel characteristics of individual users. To address this challenge, we propose Contribution-aware Clustered Federated Learning (CCFL), a novel framework that groups users with similar wireless channel characteristics to encourage intra-group collaboration. It enables the training of cluster-specific prediction models, each tailored to the unique data distribution of its cluster. CCFL first directs each user to learn a low-dimensional feature embedding from their local CSI data, then dynamically clusters users by assigning them to a group where their data contributes most significantly, measured by the alignment between their feature embedding and a learnable cluster prototype. Experiments show that CCFL significantly outperforms local-only training and reduces the prediction error by 45.2% compared to the single-model benchmark.

title: Physical Embedding for Radio Map Construction.
abstract: Constructing radio maps traditionally requires extensive site surveys with precise location labels, making the calibration process costly and time-consuming. Existing methods often rely on inertial measurement units (IMUs) to provide location information, but such approaches are constrained by hardware dependencies and device-level access restrictions. In this paper, we propose a label-free radio map construction method that relies solely on Channel State Information (CSI), completely eliminating the need for location labels. The key idea is to embed CSI into a two-dimensional physical space via training a neural network, while preserving the real-world topology. To achieve this, we introduce a Physical Embedding (PE) framework that integrates CSI-derived angle-of-arrival (AoA) and time-of-arrival (ToA) information with power-angle-delay profile (PADP)-based spatial proximity, ensuring that the learned embedding is geometrically consistent with the physical environment. Experiments conducted in a real industrial environment demonstrate that PE achieves an average localization error of 0.821 m and a relative beam-estimation error of 5.02%, outperforming state-of-the-art label-free localization methods.

title: Submodularity-Driven Communication-Efficient Distributed Reinforcement Learning for Wireless Networks.
abstract: With the continuous growth of access terminals, the uplink bandwidth of wireless networks is becoming increasingly scarce, and latency and energy consumption constraints are becoming more and more prominent. Simultaneous parameter exchange among all terminals will rapidly increase communication overhead and cause idle waiting, resulting in diminishing marginal returns on performance gains per unit of communication overhead. Therefore, in order to allocate a fixed communication budget to the update containing the most information, this paper presents a communication-efficient distributed policy gradient method (CE-DPG) for distributed reinforcement learning under fixed communication budgets. The scheme designs a submodularity-driven agent selection rule that balances gradient strength and diversity, thereby reducing redundancy while maintaining representativeness. Unselected agents maintain lightweight local statistics and a cached summary that is reused only for candidate evaluation. A periodic full refresh limits the staleness of cached information. In theory, we prove that the proposed set objective follows the law of diminishing returns. Under the assumptions of standard smoothness and bounded variance, CE-DPG guarantees the expected decrease in each step and achieves near-linear selection costs per round. Simulation experiments show that in Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) tasks, CE-DPG achieves almost the same returns as full participation with 55% of the communication rounds.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Persistent UAV Swarm Network Planning for Emergency Communications.
abstract: In recent years, UAVs have become a key support for emergency communication due to their rapid and flexible deployment. However, individual UAVs are limited by coverage range and endurance, making it difficult to meet the continuous communication needs in large-scale post-disaster scenarios. We develop a persistent UAV swarm task planning model that accounts for both long-term coverage of persistent communication regions and periodic visits to intermittently accessed regions. To minimize the required number of UAVs, we first propose a periodic rotation path method that reduces problem complexity and transforms the original formulation into an extended vehicle routing problem. Subsequently, a Transformer-based reinforcement learning framework is developed to handle the reformulated problem, with a multi-constraint reward design ensuring energy efficiency and network connectivity. Simulation results show that the proposed method significantly reduces the number of UAVs while meeting the service demands of both region types.

title: Balancing Flow and Memory: Context-Aligned Streaming Knowledge Graph Reasoning.
abstract: Streaming knowledge graph reasoning aims to infer emerging relations from continuous event streams, enabling real-time understanding and decision-making in dynamic environments. Existing approaches often rely on periodic retraining or replay mechanisms to preserve temporal information, but they suffer from semantic drift and unstable reasoning under streaming constraints. To address these issues, we propose CASR, a Context-Aligned Streaming Representation framework for temporally consistent knowledge graph reasoning. CASR maintains adaptability and stability by anchoring entities to their recent historical context and aligning semantic representations across time without replay. The framework integrates a context-aligned retrieval unit that constructs temporally weighted subgraphs to capture essential historical semantics, a semantic fusion gate that balances historical anchors and current representations through a self-gated alignment mechanism, and a temporal evolution encoder that incrementally refines entity states for real-time prediction. Experiments on multiple temporal knowledge graph benchmarks demonstrate that CASR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving stable and temporally consistent reasoning under realistic streaming conditions.

title: MIMO-OTFS Transceiver Design Based on Stream-Level SINR.
abstract: This paper investigates a wideband linear transceiver architecture for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal time frequency space (MIMO-OTFS) system. By examining the input–output relationship in the delay–Doppler–beam (DDB) domain, the stream-level signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) is validated to be approximately equivalent to the OTFS symbol-level SINR under ideal delay–Doppler (DD) domain equalization. This gives rise to a novel framework for designing MIMO-OTFS transceivers by formulating the optimization problem based on the stream-level SINR, which is more mathematically tractable, instead of the symbol-level SINR. Particularly, a MIMO-OTFS transceiver employing zero-forcing (ZF) as well as maximum ratio transmission (MRT) and maximum ratio combining (MRC) is simulated to evaluate the system’s average achievable rate under the given channel conditions, thereby validating our conclusions.

title: Joint Transceiver Beamforming and IRS Phase Shift Design for mmWave MIMO with Modulo ADCs.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) has accelerated the efficiency of modern wireless systems, yet its performance is constrained by the propagation blocking effect and the receiver analog-to-digital converters (ADC) saturation. Motivated by these, this paper first attempted to study an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-aided downlink mmWave MIMO system equipped with a modulo ADC front end at the receiver and explicitly models receiver-side quantization error. We propose spectral efficiency (SE) maximization under total-power and constant-modulus constraints and develop a real-valued genetic algorithm-based scheme that, in each generation, (i) explores the IRS reflection matrix and (ii) updates the transceiver beamformers by performing singular value decomposition on the cascaded channel, updated with the IRS reflection matrix. Experimental results demonstrate that the modulo ADC achieves higher SE and lower bit error rates with fewer bit resolution, effectively mitigating saturation-induced clipping and outperforming conventional ADCs.

title: Hierarchical Structured Massive Access for Scalable Distributed Cell-Free Radio Access Network.
abstract: Existing studies on cell-free radio access networks (CF-RANs) have primarily focused on physical-layer aspects, leaving the scalability of medium access control (MAC) functions insufficiently addressed, particularly in wide-coverage scenarios with large-scale access points (APs) and dense user equipments (UEs). In this paper, we decentralize the tasks of the structured massive access to individual user-centric distributed units (UCDUs), each coordinating a finite number of APs and UEs, thereby enabling scalable distributed MAC-layer coordination. Each edge distributed unit (EDU) can be coordinated by multiple UCDUs, ensuring strong network coverage capability. However, since each UCDU relies solely on its own local information, this approach not only complicates the massive access but also inherently leads to resource conflicts and additional interference. To address these challenges, we propose a hierarchical framework for structured massive access in CF-RAN. Firstly, a universal UCDU-EDU association deployment scheme is introduced, followed by a UE-UCDU association scheme based on a competition mechanism. We further design distributed pilot assignment and AP-UE association strategies executed locally at each UCDU, and enhance them via global fine-tuning for partial UEs. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves superior spectral efficiency, validating its effectiveness in large-scale networks.

title: Analyzing Discovery Dynamics in Zigbee IoT Networks.
abstract: This paper addresses a key challenge in passive Zigbee network reconnaissance – the ability to determine the completion of a network scan. While prior work has focused on device identification and traffic fingerprinting, the question of when a scan can be confidently terminated has remained unaddressed. We formulate this as a progress-tracking problem and propose a passive inference method, called ZigSweep, based on traffic analysis of encrypted Zigbee Link Status packets. By extracting neighbor-count information from observed control-plane exchanges, the method derives a dynamic lower bound on the network size, which serves as a stopping criterion for discovery. We formally prove the bound and evaluate its tightness through experimental measurements in a typical residential Zigbee deployment, showing that it reliably converges to the true device count. In all tests conducted, the method correctly determines the network size and yields actionable outcomes. In 75% of the cases, it identifies all the network devices, and in the remaining 25%, it identifies all but one device (with the scanner correctly assessing the outcome as incomplete). These results demonstrate that formal network reconnaissance can be accomplished through passive scanning, without requiring packet decryption or intrusive probing.

title: Function-Aligned Nonuniform Quantization Graph Coloring for Distributed Functional Compression.
abstract: We study distributed functional compression for computing a target Z = f (X,Y) from separated sources and found that strict graph coloring wastes bits in nearly homogeneous regions when rare contexts along the other source create conflicts; a single conflicting context blocks merging globally. We propose a function-aligned design that (i) places nonuniform axis cuts via grid-guided one-dimensional dynamic programming (DP) in a coordinate-descent loop and (ii) applies τ-tolerant characteristic-graph coloring with a lookup-table decoder. Rates are accounted for by length-weighted color entropy, which is sampling-invariant and matches separate entropy coding. On Temperature–Humidity Index (THI) classification, the proposed scheme shifts the bits– accuracy Pareto frontier: the method we propose saves about 15% bits above the same accuracy where there are more levels to classify. On the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) task, nonuniform quantization with τ-tolerant coloring achieves up to 37% fewer bits at accuracies above 95%. The design is distribution-free and function-aware, scales by per-axis DP with majority votes of grid cells. Results indicate that once the task surpasses a binary label or moves to higher dimensions, grid-guided nonuniform partitioning with strict or τ-tolerant coloring is a strictly better operating point for graph coloring.

title: AdaMo: Adaptive Multimodal Policy Learning for Joint Coverage Optimization via Deep Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Adaptive management of increasingly complex wireless environments is essential for future 6G networks. A core challenge lies in the joint optimization of weak and overlapping coverage: reducing coverage holes often exacerbates inter-cell interference and thus increases overlap. To address this antagonistic trade-off, we propose AdaMo, a deep reinforcement learning algorithm for large-scale joint coverage optimization in 6G networks. AdaMo employs a discrete-to-continuous curriculum learning strategy that combines the fast convergence of discrete action learning with the fine-grained control achievable in continuous action spaces. The policy is parameterized by a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) to enable multimodal decision-making, and an entropy regularization term is incorporated to preserve component diversity and prevent collapse. Experimental results show that AdaMo achieves superior decision quality and the best joint coverage performance, outperforming both learning-based and heuristic baselines with an average improvement of 32.94%. These results demonstrate that AdaMo is an efficient, robust, and scalable solution for adaptive joint coverage optimization in future 6G wireless systems.

title: 3D Cooperative User Tracking for Distributed Integrated Sensing and Communication.
abstract: As integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) becomes an integral part of 6G networks, distributed ISAC (DISAC) is expected to enhance both sensing and communication performance through its decentralized architecture. This paper presents a complete framework to address the challenge of cooperative user tracking in DISAC systems. By incorporating a global probability hypothesis density (PHD) filter and a field-of-view-aware access point (AP) management strategy, the framework enables accurate user tracking using radio signals while optimizing AP scheduling. In addition, a real-world distributed MIMO channel measurement campaign is performed to evaluate the effectiveness of the framework. The results demonstrate that a centimeter-level root mean-square trajectory error can be achieved. Furthermore, the results show that it is not necessary to keep APs active at all times to maintain high tracking accuracy, indicating the need for robust and efficient AP management. These findings provide valuable insights into practical deployments and the further development of cooperative user tracking techniques in DISAC systems.

title: Distributed MIMO Single Snapshot Environment Mapping via Spatial Filtering.
abstract: Radio-based environment mapping is a key aspect in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). This paper presents a spatial Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (PMBM)-based filter to address environment mapping with distributed multiple-input multiple-output (D-MIMO). Using the spatial diversity provided by D-MIMO architectures, the filter performs Bayesian recursive estimation over spatially distributed access points (APs) using only a single snapshot of measurements. We consider a challenging scenario in which measurements convey limited bearing information. The angles of the multipath component (MPC) on the user side are not available, in contrast to previous PMBM mapping studies where this angle information has been crucial. Furthermore, a unified measurement model is incorporated into the filter to exploit MPCs with different interaction orders (single-bounce and multi-bounce) and various interaction mechanisms (reflections, scattering, and their combinations). Through numerical simulations, the proposed filter is evaluated in various system configurations and is shown to outperform the benchmark method. When applied to real-world D-MIMO channels, the consistency between the mapping results and the physical environment further validates the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Understanding In-Waveguide Attenuation in Pinching-Antenna Systems under LoS Blockage.
abstract: Existing studies on pinching-antenna systems often ignore in-waveguide attenuation, leaving its impact under practical LoS blockage conditions insufficiently understood. In this work, we develop a channel model that jointly accounts for in-waveguide attenuation and probabilistic LoS blockage. By deriving an approximate but accurate solution for optimal antenna placement, we provide an analytical characterization of the average data rate loss incurred when in-waveguide attenuation is neglected. The results show that this loss remains negligible in blockage-prone environments, even over large coverage areas. Simulations further confirm that pinching antennas consistently outperform fixed antennas, underscoring their robustness for future wireless networks.

title: A Multi-Round Voting Consensus Framework via Evolutionary Game Theory and Score Completion.
abstract: As distributed systems grow more complex, traditional consensus algorithms such as Raft and PBFT exhibit fundamental limitations in supporting joint decision-making among heterogeneous nodes with diverse preferences and incomplete information. Their focus on uniform agreement, rather than collaborative optimization, restricts their effectiveness in modern environments. To address these challenges, we propose EGSCN, a novel framework that integrates evolutionary game theory with multi-round voting. EGSCN enables autonomous proposal evaluation through normalized local scoring and leverages a deep learning-based Score Completion Network to infer missing evaluations. A static performance-based leader election strategy coordinates score aggregation with minimal overhead. By modeling strategy adaptation as an evolutionary game, EGSCN enhances decentralization, captures individual preferences, and preserves node privacy. Simulations demonstrate that EGSCN achieves rapid convergence and reliable consensus even under partial observability and agent heterogeneity.

title: On the Impact of In-Waveguide Attenuation on Pinching-Antenna Systems.
abstract: Pinching-antenna systems enable highly flexible deployment by dynamically adjusting antenna positions along a dielectric waveguide. In this work, we investigate their performance for practical channels with in-waveguide attenuation. We first introduce a channel model that captures both in-waveguide and free-space propagation, based on which the optimal antenna placement is derived. Building on this result, we further characterize the average data rate loss incurred when in-waveguide attenuation is ignored. Our analytical results show that in-waveguide attenuation can be safely neglected without causing significant performance degradation, provided that the communication region is not excessively large. Simulation results further demonstrate the performance gains of pinching-antenna systems compared with conventional fixed-antenna baselines.

title: Pinching-Antenna-Assisted ISAC Based on the Reflection Law.
abstract: We propose a novel pinching-antenna-assisted integrated sensing and communication (PAA-ISAC) framework, where the dielectric waveguide enables the downlink transmission and the reflected signal is collected at the base station (BS) for radio sensing. Due to the asymmetrical propagation between the waveguide → sensing target (ST) and the ST → BS, the reflection law is exploited to model the radio sensing propagation. The sensing degree of freedom (SDoF) and Cramér–Rao Bound (CRB) of the estimated angle are first analyzed, where the qualitative relationship between the CRB and the antenna design is revealed. Capitalizing on this finding, a weighted CRB and transmit power minimization problem is formulated subject to dual-functional requirements. A low-complexity alternating optimization algorithm is proposed to jointly optimize the location of the activated pinching antenna (PA) and the transmit power towards the waveguide by invoking the Lagrange duality theory. Our simulation results showcase that: 1) the derived performance approximation is close to the exact CRB; 2) the SDoF is independent of the waveguide deployment; 3) the proposed algorithm outperforms the fixed antenna design in the context of radio sensing performance and the transmit power consumption.

title: Doppler Shift Based Multiple Base Stations Cooperative ISAC System in Low-Altitude FD-RAN.
abstract: Low-altitude electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) plays an important role in the future low-altitude economy and requires robust communications and precise localization capabilities. Fully decoupled radio access network (FD-RAN), leveraging coordinated multi–base station (BS) architectures, is envisioned to meet these requirements. In this paper, we propose a cooperative integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system for eVTOL with FD-RANs. By leveraging the uplink Doppler shift inherently captured during carrier frequency offset (CFO) compensation at each BS, the proposed ISAC system enables accurate vehicle localization without additional sensing resources. Specifically, the localization problem is formulated as a set of Doppler-based equations without the vehicle’s position and velocity information. For high-accuracy trajectory tracking, we further design a learning-based adaptive double filter (LADF) algorithm that exploits temporal correlations in Doppler measurements and vehicle dynamics. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed ISAC system not only enhances communication coverage, but also provides highly accurate localization for eVTOL.

title: Sensing-Assisted Low-Complexity Beamforming for Dual-RIS ISAC Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates a multi-user integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system that leverages semi-passive reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) equipped with sensing elements to enhance both communication and sensing performance. To ensure the quality of service and fairness for all users, a max-min signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) optimization problem is formulated, involving the joint design of base station (BS) transmit beamforming and RIS discrete phase shifts. However, for large-scale RIS, conventional optimization methods typically suffer from high computational complexity. To this end, we first utilize the RISs to perform user angle estimation, thereby simplifying the solution process of the formulated problem. Building on this, an efficient alternating optimization algorithm is subsequently proposed. Specifically, semi-definite relaxation and the bisection method are employed to solve the BS beamforming optimization subproblem. For optimizing the RIS phase shift matrices in multi-user scenarios, a low-complexity algorithm is developed that leverages a sensing-assisted approach to constrain the discrete search space. Numerical simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves performance that closely approaches that of the ideal continuous phase shift configuration.

title: Advancing Wireless Differentially Private Distributed Learning for 6G Applications: A Digital Transmission Design and Analysis.
abstract: Differentially private distributed learning (DPDL) is essential for secure and efficient 6G systems that predominantly rely on digital transmission. However, existing studies mainly focus on analog transmission, which is sensitive to synchronization errors and severely affected by stragglers, leading to degraded overall performance. To overcome these limitations, we propose the first digital transmission-based DPDL framework, termed D-DPDL. By integrating orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) and Lagrange encoding, D-DPDL enables digital transmission with improved tolerance to synchronization errors and inherent resilience to stragglers, while preserving privacy. We further provide theoretical analysis on its privacy protection level and convergence, and validate the results through simulations. The results show that D-DPDL outperforms existing schemes in both accuracy and training time, and highlight the impact of different parameters on performance.

title: Spot Pilot Scheme for AFDM under Fractional Delay-Doppler Channel.
abstract: Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing (AFDM) has recently attracted considerable attention owing to its strong resilience against multipath delay and Doppler dispersion, making it a promising candidate for next generation wireless communication systems. However, accurate channel estimation under multipath channels with fractional delay–Doppler shifts remains a major challenge that limits the performance of AFDM. In this paper, a novel spot pilot scheme is proposed for AFDM. By exploiting the banded and quasi-static structure of the affine domain channel matrix, multiple sparsely distributed pilots are inserted within a single frame to capture the channel responses at selected positions. The complete channel matrix is then reconstructed at the receiver through interpolation. Furthermore, a neural network is developed to mitigate the pilot interference caused by fractional delay–Doppler effects and to refine the estimated channel matrix. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed spot pilot scheme achieves significantly improved estimation accuracy compared with single embedded scheme pilot under fractional delay–Doppler conditions.

title: Denoising-Autoencoder-Assisted Physical Layer Secret Key Generation.
abstract: In this paper, we propose denoising autoencoder (DAE)-assisted secret key generation (SKG), where channel noise reciprocity imperfections induced due to wireless channel measurements are suppressed, hence significantly enhancing the reliability and efficiency. More specifically, the DAE is capable of capturing the intrinsic structure of input distributions, reconstructing the original data structure, and removing additive noise while preserving the essential structure of signals. In our analysis, it is demonstrated that the proposed SKG scheme exhibits higher performance than the conventional schemes in terms of key disagreement rate (KDR), secret key capacity (SKC), and randomness of the generated keys.

title: Optimal Self-Interference Cancellation with Generalized Analog Least Mean Square Loop.
abstract: This paper develops a theoretical framework for optimal filter design in the generalized analog least mean square (GALMS) loop to improve analog self-interference cancellation (SIC). We derive the minimum modeling error condition and show that orthogonal filter banks maximize captured channel power, ensuring an optimal representation of the self-interference (SI) channel. The theoretical cancellation limit is established through analysis of the excess mean-square error (EMSE), showing that orthogonal basis filters achieve optimal performance when adapted to channel characteristics. For multipath delayed channels, tapped delay lines (TDLs) with delay matching attain the bound, and their closed-form expressions relate it to channel power and loop gain. Power spectral density (PSD) simulations confirm that delay-matched TDLs converge faster and suppress SI more effectively than mismatched ones. Simulations of exponentially decaying channels show that the Laguerre basis filter achieves optimal performance with only a single tap, validating the framework. Moreover, increasing loop gain enhances the cancellation capability of the GALMS loop.

title: Network Slicing in Integrated Sensing and Communication: A Flexible Multi-Domain Resource Allocation Scheme.
abstract: Performing network slicing in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is an essential task to enhance the performance of dual functionalities. However, the existing works merely consider a single resource domain and neglect the sensing capabilities. Motivated by this, we propose a flexible network slicing framework that leverages resources in multiple domains. We formulate a joint optimization problem for beamforming and frequency allocation to maximize the sum communication rate, subject to constraints on the sensing beam pattern, transmit power, and total bandwidth. To solve this problem, we formulate it as a Markov decision process (MDP) and apply the Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3) algorithm. To further improve convergence, we propose a Lagrangian duality-based TD3 algorithm. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms, and they outperform baseline methods in terms of sensing accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, we analyze the trade-off between the two functions (sensing and communication) and examine the impact of key system parameters.

title: A Federated Trust Modeling Framework for Anomaly Detection in Zero Trust Edge Networks.
abstract: Edge networks are increasingly vulnerable to sophisticated cyber-attacks, yet conventional security approaches struggle to balance robust threat detection with user privacy preservation. In this paper, we propose a Federated Trust Modeling framework, a solution for secure anomaly detection in Zero Trust edge networks. By integrating multi-modal anomaly detection, Byzantine-resilient federated learning, and context-aware trust scoring, the framework addresses critical gaps in existing IoT security approaches. The framework employs a three-layer architecture: Device-Level Trust Learning for local anomaly detection using ensemble methods (Enhanced VAE, Isolation Forest, LSTM, and Statistical Process Control), Federated Aggregation Layer for Byzantine-resilient model aggregation with differential privacy, and Trust Scoring & Decision Layer for context-aware access control using Subjective Logic. Comprehensive evaluation on synthetic IoT data demonstrates high precision, near-linear scalability, and privacy preservation with high accuracy even under strict differential privacy. The multi-modal anomaly detection achieves high accuracy while generating zero false alarms. Statistical validation confirms sub-linear time complexity and significant trust score differentiation across security contexts. The framework provides a practical, deployable solution for edge networks requiring strong security with privacy guarantees.

title: Jamming Elimination and Parameter Estimation for Integrated Sensing and Communication System.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the jamming elimination and parameter estimation in mmWave MIMO integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system in presence of jamming attack. The sensing ability of the ISAC base station is exploited to discriminate and eliminate the jamming signals to enhance the performance of parameter estimation. A joint angle estimation and successive signal elimination algorithm is proposed to mitigate the jamming impact on the parameter estimation, where the signal of the strongest propagation path is successively estimated, discriminated, and eliminated from the received signals until the angles of all the users have been successfully estimated. Furthermore, to enhance the performance of parameter estimation, we propose an off-grid angle estimation algorithm, where the angle is first coarsely estimated with the on-grid projection, and then the estimation accuracy is further improved by the iterative gradient descent (IGD) approach. Besides, we propose an off-grid distance and velocity estimation algorithm, where the distance and radial velocity of users are first estimated by two-dimensional fast Fourier transform, and then the estimation accuracy is enhanced with the IGD approach. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms and show their robustness against the strong-power jamming.

title: DP-DyLoRA: Fine-Tuning Transformer-Based Models On-Device under Differentially Private Federated Learning using Dynamic Low-Rank Adaptation.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) allows clients to collaboratively train a global model without sharing their local data with a server. However, clients' contributions to the server can still leak sensitive information. Differential privacy (DP) addresses such leakage by providing formal privacy guarantees, with mechanisms that add randomness to the clients' contributions. The randomness makes it infeasible to train large transformer-based models, common in modern federated learning systems. In this work, we empirically evaluate the practicality of fine-tuning large scale on-device transformer-based models with differential privacy in a federated learning system. We conduct comprehensive experiments on various system properties for tasks spanning a multitude of domains: speech recognition, computer vision (CV) and natural language understanding (NLU). Our results show that full fine-tuning under differentially private federated learning (DP-FL) generally leads to huge performance degradation which can be alleviated by reducing the dimensionality of contributions through parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). Our benchmarks of existing DP-PEFT methods show that DP-Low-Rank Adaptation (DP-LoRA) consistently outperforms other methods. An even more promising approach, DyLoRA, which makes the low rank variable, when naively combined with FL would straightforwardly break differential privacy. We therefore propose an adaptation method that can be combined with differential privacy and call it DP-DyLoRA. Finally, we are able to reduce the accuracy degradation and word error rate (WER) increase due to DP to less than 2% and 7% respectively with 1 million clients and a stringent privacy budget of $ε=2$.

title: Throughput Optimized Channel Smoothing.
abstract: A throughput-oriented optimization strategy using a residual neural network (ResNet) within convolutional neural network (CNN), enabled by a fully differentiable receiver chain, is proposed. Unlike conventional training with known channel conditions, the proposed method directly maximizes throughput. It is then evaluated under typical 5G channel models. Results show consistent improvements for block error rate (BLER) and uncoded bit error rate (BER) when compared against least squares estimation. Comparisons with conventionally trained neural networks are inconclusive. However, some scenarios demonstrate improvements in throughput optimized neural networks over those trained under ideal channel conditions. In addition to improved performance, the proposed approach also enables training applications in which ideal channel conditions are not available. The proposed training method can be used as long as transmitted bits are known. These findings highlight the practical value of a throughput-oriented optimization strategy in channel smoothing and indicate its feasibility as a direction for AI-enhanced receivers without relying on ideal channel conditions.

title: SEPS: Secure and Efficient Proximity Search for Encrypted Cloud Storage.
