abstract: Proximity search enables data owners to outsource their datasets to the cloud servers that respond to clients who submit queries with proximity conditions. However, existing privacy-preserving solutions for proximity search suffer from limitations: (1) they incur statistical information leakages and thus are vulnerable to leakage-abuse attacks, or (2) entail significant client bandwidth/computation costs and thus are undesirable for large-scale outsourced databases with resource-constrained clients. In this paper, we present a strongly Secure and concretely Efficient Proximity Search scheme, named SEPS. In the scheme, we first convert proximity query into keyword query followed by proximity computation, which supports flexible proximity queries with self-defined proximity boundaries. Then, we achieve oblivious keyword query by adopting distributed point function (DPF)-based private information retrieval (PIR) technique, which provides adaptive security against semi-honest adversaries and statistical attacks. Moreover, we introduce lightweight and oblivious proximity computation, which achieves user-driven efficiency while concealing search, access, and size patterns. Our experimental results demonstrate that SEPS outperforms in comprehensive evaluations, achieving microsecond-level query generation time, and up to two orders of magnitude faster in server retrieval and 29× lower overall communication costs than the state-of-the-art with the same security level and search functionality.

title: Hiding in FR3: Sensing-Secure OFDM-ISAC Design Against Multi-Intercept Threats.
abstract: The upper mid-band frequency range 3 (FR3) has attracted significant attention for 6G due to its ability to strike a balance between coverage and capacity. As integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems are expected to operate extensively in this band, their vulnerability to increasingly sophisticated interception attacks becomes a critical concern. To this end, this paper studies the sensing security of FR3-based orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM)-ISAC systems under multi-intercept threats. Specifically, to hide ISAC signals from an electronic reconnaissance aircraft employing power detection and cyclostationary analysis, we propose a joint transmit beam-forming and receive filtering design to achieve a low probability of intercept. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme effectively realizes ISAC while significantly enhancing sensing security against multi-intercept threats in FR3 scenarios.

title: MB-HGAN: A Hierarchical Graph Attention Network for Indoor Localization with 5G NR Multi-Beam Signals.
abstract: Accurate indoor localization is crucial for applications like smart navigation and asset tracking, but it remains challenging in complex indoor environments. This paper presents a localization framework based on 5G new radio (NR) multi-beam signals, leveraging a Multi-Scale Beam-aware Hierarchical Graph Attention Network (MB-HGAN) to enhance positioning accuracy and robustness. MB-HGAN combines implicit spatial encoding, multi-scale graph modeling, and a hierarchical attention mechanism to capture both local signal dynamics and global topological patterns. Specifically, beam index embedding and activation pattern encoding are used to learn spatial features without relying on angle information. A hybrid strategy based on signal similarity and motion constraints is also introduced to ensure realistic movement behavior. Field experiments conducted in factory and office environments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves mean absolute errors (MAE) of 2.56 m and 0.74 m, and root mean square errors (RMSE) of 2.61 m and 0.82 m, respectively. Compared to existing 5G NR fingerprinting methods, MB-HGAN significantly improves both accuracy and stability, highlighting its effectiveness in complex indoor scenarios.

title: Diffusion Posterior Sampling with Channel Feedback for Adaptive Semantic Communication.
abstract: Diffusion-aided deep joint source–channel coding (DeepJSCC) has shown strong potential for semantic communication (SemCom) under challenging wireless conditions. However, existing diffusion-based JSCC schemes lack adaptivity in three key aspects: (i) task-specific fine-tuning, (ii) channel and rate adaptation, and (iii) instance-level generalization. We propose FPS-SemCom, a feedback-guided diffusion posterior sampling framework that unifies posterior-based decoding and feedback-driven progressive encoding. FPS-SemCom achieves instance-, channel-, and rate-adaptive image transmission via a training-free sampler and a lightweight feedback-guided linear encoder. Built entirely on frozen pre-trained diffusion models, FPS-SemCom refines the posterior toward high-fidelity reconstructions while preserving semantic consistency across varying channel conditions. Remarkably, our results reveal that under strong generative priors, even a simple linear encoder can achieve competitive performance, underscoring the representational power of diffusion priors for SemCom. Extensive experiments based on a pre-trained diffusion model show that FPS-SemCom outperforms the existing diffusion-based JSCC baseline, achieving up to a 33.3% improvement in LPIPS and a 1.56 dB gain in MS-SSIM.Project page: https://eedavidwu.github.io/FPS-SemCom/

title: Cross-Data Center Training with Heterogeneous Accelerators: Protocols and Evaluation.
abstract: Training at production scale increasingly spans multiple datacenters, where heterogeneous accelerators operate over long-haul networks with non-trivial latency and variable bandwidth. We study cross-datacenter training under a single, reproducible evaluation protocol that fixes model version, optimizer, precision, and data order, and that reports medians and dispersion over repeated short windows. We compare two deployable strategies. The first is a shallow cross-site pipeline that preserves synchronous semantics with at most one boundary and concentrates traffic into a small number of predictable exchanges. The second is asynchronous aggregation that lets each site advance for a configurable number of local steps before parameters are averaged; a monotone learning-rate reduction accompanies longer aggregation periods to control drift. A measurement-driven selection rule uses the observed share of time spent in communication and the variability of the wide-area link to choose between these paths. On both a dense model and a sparse expert model, the pipeline approach improves or preserves relative efficiency on stable links with modest communication cost, while aggregation sustains throughput on constrained or volatile links without violating predefined tolerance bands on validation metrics. A compact tuning workflow and a manifest make configurations repeatable across hardware mixes and network conditions, providing a practical template for Big-Data deployments.

title: Orthogonal Additive Inverse EP Codes over GF(5m) for Overloaded FFMA Systems.
abstract: The finite-field multiple-access (FFMA) framework effectively addresses the multiuser finite blocklength problem by inverting the conventional processing order of channel coding and multiplexing. In this architecture, element-pairs (EPs) function as virtual resources to separate users directly in the finite-field domain. The algebraic structure of EPs, which can be constructed over different finite fields, plays a crucial role in determining system characteristics and performance advantages. This paper focuses on orthogonal additive inverse EP (AI-EP) codes constructed over GF(5m), enabling an overloaded FFMA scheme that achieves both enhanced spectral efficiency and reliable error performance. The superimposed signals from J users collectively form a structured channel codeword, for which we develop a dynamic programming q-ary sum-product algorithm (DP-QSPA) that ensures effective multiuser signal separation while maintaining tractable decoding complexity. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GF(5m)-based FFMA system achieves superior error performance compared to conventional power-domain NOMA and SCMA systems.

title: Utilizing Meta-Learning to Enhance the Transferability of GAN-Based Adversarial Traffic Generation.
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) play a vital role in cybersecurity infrastructures by monitoring network traffic and system activities to identify malicious behavior. To address the growing complexity of cyberattacks, IDS have evolved from traditional signature-based approaches to machine learning (ML)-driven models. Unlike signature-based methods, ML-based IDS automatically learn patterns from data, enabling superior generalization to previously unseen threats. Despite their effectiveness, ML-based IDS remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks that exploit model weaknesses. This paper presents High-Transferability IDS-GAN (HT-IDS-GAN), a novel framework that integrates Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) into IDS-GAN to improve both the transferability and realism of generated traffic samples. By enabling rapid adaptation to unseen IDS models, HT-IDS-GAN achieves strong transferability and high sample authenticity, providing a robust tool for evaluating IDS resilience in adversarial scenarios and supporting the development of more effective cyber defense mechanisms. Experimental results demonstrate that HT-IDS-GAN outperforms existing methods in terms of transferability and sample realism.

title: Fluid Antenna Relay (FAR)-assisted Communication with Hybrid Relaying Scheme Selection.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a fluid antenna relay (FAR)-assisted communication system with hybrid relaying scheme selection. By leveraging statistical channel state information (CSI) and distribution characteristics of fluid antenna system (FAS), we approximate the outage probability (OP) with different relaying schemes utilizing a Gaussian copula-based method. Each relay node follows the OP-minimized principle to choose the forwarding schemes. To reduce self-interference and avoid multi-user interference, half-duplex relays and frequency division multiple access schemes are considered, respectively. On this basis, we formulate a sum-rate maximization problem to mitigate the rate loss introduced by the half-duplex mode. To solve this problem, we first transform the original nonconvex problem into a power control optimization problem by obtaining the closed form of bandwidth allocation and substituting it into the original problem. Then, we solve the power control optimization problem with a low complexity method. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of our proposed algorithm to improve the sum rate of the system.

title: Experimental Validation of SBFD ISAC in an FR3 Distributed SIMO Testbed.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a key enabler for future radio networks. This paper presents a sub-band full-duplex (SBFD) ISAC system that assigns non-overlapping OFDM subbands to sensing and communication, enabling simultaneous operation with minimal interference. A distributed testbed with three SIMO nodes is implemented using USRP X410 devices operating at 6.8 GHz with 20 MHz bandwidth per channel. A total of 2048 OFDM subcarriers are partitioned into three subbands: two for sensing using Zadoff–Chu sequences and one for communication using QPSK. Each USRP transmits one subband while receiving signals across all three, forming a 1×3 SIMO node. Time synchronization is achieved through host-server coordination without external clock distribution. Indoor measurements, validated against MOCAP ground truth, confirm the feasibility of the SBFD ISAC system. The results demonstrate monostatic sensing with a velocity resolution of 0.145 m/s, and communication under NLoS conditions with a BER of 3.63×10−3. Compared with a multiband benchmark requiring three times more spectrum, the SBFD configuration achieves comparable velocity estimation accuracy while conserving resources. The sensing and communication performance trade-off is determined by subcarrier allocation strategy rather than mutual interference.

title: Deep Learning-Based Waveform Learning for Superimposed Pilot Systems.
Multi-Task Semantic Communication with Sparsely Activated Mixture-of-Experts.
abstract: Multi-task semantic communication (MTSC) employs a unified semantic encoder or decoder capable of executing multiple tasks, such as semantic segmentation and depth estimation. However, existing MTSC systems focus on either extracting the correlations or distinguishing the heterogeneity of multiple tasks, unable to balance generalization and specialization. Due to the inherent conflict between the optimization objectives of leveraging task correlations and heterogeneity, it is non-trivial to achieve both simultaneously in a single framework. In this paper, we propose a mixture of experts (MoE)-based MTSC system that consists of a shared expert pool and task-specific routers to jointly leverage task correlation and heterogeneity, thereby improving the execution accuracy of diverse tasks. The expert pool serves as a shared knowledge base, allowing routers to capture correlations by learning to reuse the same experts for similar tasks. Simultaneously, the routers capture heterogeneity by directing conflicting tasks to different, specialized experts within this pool. This routing strategy ensures that the conflicting optimization objectives of these tasks are applied to distinct experts, thus eliminating interference. In the simulations, three semantic tasks are considered. The proposed scheme achieves improvements of at least 10% on semantic segmentation, 20% on surface normal estimation, and 5% on depth estimation compared to existing multi-task schemes.

title: Boosting Near-Field User Tracking via Channel Map-Aided Movable Antenna Optimization.
abstract: Near-field user tracking is a key challenge in sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks. Conventional fixed-position antennas (FPAs) lack the deployment flexibility needed for robust tracking. For example, when the user is nearly collinear with the array, the geometry can be ill-conditioned due to reduced Fisher information. Movable antennas (MAs) mitigate this limitation by dynamically repositioning array elements to introduce additional spatial degrees of freedom and enrich the observation geometry. Specifically, we first derive the posterior Cramer-Rao lower bound (PCRLB) for near-field tracking and analyze the Fisher information matrix (FIM). Our analysis motivates decomposing the Bayesian inference problem by first optimizing MA placements to shape the log-likelihood landscape and then estimating the user’s position within the resulting well-conditioned geometry. Based on this insight, we propose a hierarchical algorithm that employs sequential convex programming (SCP), aided by channel-map priors to optimize the MA placements, followed by a two-stage tracking method that exploits the well-conditioned landscape to achieve rapid and accurate UE tracking. Simulation results show that our solution substantially outperforms existing benchmarks and closely approaches the PCRLB.

title: Dual Time-Constrained UAV Routing for Reward Maximization Under Joint Multi-PoI Capture.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are widely used in various applications, such as surveillance and disaster response. These missions often involve video recording of multiple spatially distributed points-of-interest (PoIs). However, limited battery capacity imposes a strict dual time constraint, making efficient route planning essential. A green effective strategy is to capture multiple PoIs simultaneously from a single capture point, where the required capture time at that point is determined by the longest duration among the captured PoIs. Moreover, PoIs may carry different reward values that reflect their priority or importance in the mission. Therefore, it is critical to jointly select the PoIs to be captured and their associated capture points, such that the UAV visits each selected point within the tour and capture time budget while maximizing the total collected reward. The paper formulates an optimization problem and proposes an approximation algorithm. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms other baselines by up to 67%.

title: Trajectory and Latency-Aware DNN Task Offloading in Vehicular Edge Computing: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) play a crucial role in enabling a wide range of vehicular intelligent applications. However, the limited computational capacity of individual vehicles makes it necessary to process DNN tasks by computation offloading. Considering the inherent mobility of vehicles and the dynamic nature of computation resources, designing efficient computation offloading strategies remains highly challenging. To this end, this paper proposes a Trajectory and Latency-Aware Collaborative Offloading scheme (TLATO). Firstly, a multi-scale attention Transformer is employed to predict vehicle trajectories, supporting the selection of reliable computation nodes. Secondly, a pre-trained two-stream network is introduced to predict the required latency for task execution across different computing nodes, thereby facilitating efficient task offloading by abstracting the heterogeneity of computing resources. Finally, the task offloading and resource allocation optimization problem is formulated, which is solved by a Dueling DQN-based algorithm that integrates predictive results and real-time states. Experiments demonstrate that TLATO significantly reduces task latency and energy consumption while achieving better task success rate compared to baseline algorithms.

title: Neural Bits Recovery for FDMA-based Large-coverage Ambient-IoT Network.
abstract: Due to the large coverage and low deployment cost, Ambient Internet of Things (A-IoT) has a significant potential to penetrate passive IoT markets such as asset inventory. However, extremely low-end A-IoT tags cannot integrate advanced technologies such as efficient multiple access schemes and forward error correction (FEC) coding. This inferiority is magnified by the increase in access demand and the more adverse channel conditions of the broad coverage, resulting in severely degraded system performance. To address the aforementioned issues, this paper presents two A-IoT-friendly designs: (1) an uplink frequency domain multiple access scheme based on subcarrier modulation and (2) a low-complexity uplink bits recovery algorithm based on Hopfield network that does not require FEC. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed designs increase the inventory efficiency of the A-IoT system by more than 100 times in certain scenarios, providing unparalleled market competitiveness.

title: Latency Minimization toward Communication-Sensing-Computing Integration for C-AEB in Internet of Vehicles.
abstract: Connected Autonomous Emergency Braking (C-AEB) must complete collision detection and issue a braking command within one second. Traditional Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) architectures, however, often fail to satisfy collision-protection requirements in complex traffic scenarios. In this paper, we propose a trace-driven Integrated Communication-Sensing-Computing (ICSC) joint optimization framework for vehicular networks. First, we establish a high-fidelity system model grounded in the real-world pNEUMA dataset and 3GPP TR 38.901 channel models, explicitly formulating the trade-off between sensing beamforming gain and transmission delay. Based on Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3), we propose TD3-ICSC, a robust joint optimization framework to solve this non-convex problem. Unlike standard Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approaches, we leverage the Twin Critic mechanism to explicitly mitigate the Q-value overestimation caused by high-mobility channel stochasticity, ensuring that the agent learns a stable policy that simultaneously optimizes active sensing duration and computation offloading ratios. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TD3-ICSC achieves the lowest average latency of 113.8 ms, reducing latency by 61.0%, 38.7%, 37.0%, and 31.7% compared to Random, Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) baselines, respectively. Furthermore, ablation studies verify that the proposed joint optimization of sensing duration and offloading ratio is essential for enhancing the reliability of C-AEB services.

title: Proportional-Integral-Based Distributed Nesterov Gradient Methods for Distributed Optimization.
abstract: This paper investigates the distributed constrained optimization problem, where participating agents cooperatively minimize the average of individual cost functions through local computation and information exchange. To address this problem, we develop a proportional-integral-based distributed algorithm from a new dynamic average consensus perspective, and further incorporate Nesterov momentum to accelerate convergence. The algorithm requires communication of only a single intermediate variable. Based on a spectral-radius-based analysis framework, we demonstrate a linear convergence of the proposed algorithm, and numerical simulations validate its effectiveness.

title: Energy-Efficient End-to-End Resource Allocation, Computing, and Pairing for UAV-Assisted Mobile Crowdsensing Networks.
abstract: This paper investigates an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted mobile crowdsensing (MCS) end-to-end (E2E) system designed to support computation-intensive and energy-constrained intelligent services. In this architecture, UAVs fly to the vicinity of sensors for data collection, perform necessary computations, and then move to paired actuators to transmit the results. To minimize the total E2E energy consumption across this entire sensing-communication-computation-actuation process, we formulate an optimization problem that jointly optimizes user pairing alongside communication and computation resource allocation. Given the non-convex nature of this problem, which makes it intractable for traditional methods, an effective deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach is proposed. Specifically, our algorithm integrates a genetic-initialized algorithm for extensive global exploration of the solution space and the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm for precise local optimization. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme performs significantly better than existing baselines in reducing the overall E2E system energy consumption.

title: MAD3QN-Enabled Handover Optimization in Integrated GEO-Multibeam and LEO-UAV Networks.
abstract: The integrated geostationary Earth orbit (GEO)-multibeam and low Earth orbit (LEO)-uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) network has emerged as a promising paradigm to enhance the coverage and capacity of terrestrial networks. However, due to the high dynamics of the network, handover becomes a critical yet challenging problem. In this paper, we model the handover problem as a decentralized Markov decision process (DEC-MDP), aiming to maximize throughput while minimizing energy consumption and handover cost. A multi-agent dueling double deep Q-network (MAD3QN) algorithm is then designed to solve it, where the centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) method is utilized to share intelligent information, and an offline training approach is adopted to support practical deployment. Simulation experiments with real-world satellite deployments demonstrate that MAD3QN effectively converges and significantly outperforms the existing baselines.

title: Computation Reuse and Imitation Learning for Task Offloading in 6G-Enabled VEC Networks.
abstract: Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) is considered as a key technology in the Internet of Vehicles, enabling resource-constrained vehicles to offload computation-intensive tasks to roadside units (RSUs). However, frequent offloading of similar tasks to RSUs can generate redundant computations, resulting in resource wastage. In addition, the dependencies among tasks complicate the design of task offloading strategies, thus limiting the overall system performance. To address these issues, we first design a computation reuse mechanism with an adaptive locality-sensitive hashing algorithm to efficiently identify and reuse historical calculation results. Then, we propose a reuse-assisted graph attention network-based imitation learning (REUSE-GATIL) algorithm to minimize the system cost that consists of task execution latency and energy consumption. Specifically, we utilize GAT to extract dependencies among tasks and employ imitation learning to train the GAT with expert policies generated offline by a branch-and-bound algorithm. Furthermore, we integrate a continual learning approach that utilizes elastic weight consolidation to ensure the model’s adaptability in dynamic vehicular environments and prevent catastrophic forgetting. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed algorithm’s effectiveness and superiority over benchmark schemes. Notably, it achieves a 56% gain in system cost compared to the GAT-IL algorithm without computation reuse, and a 17% gain compared to the deep reinforcement learning-based dependent task offloading algorithm.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Joint Network and Computing Load Balancing for Industrial Networks.
abstract: Industrial digital twin and metaverse applications, such as VR/AR-assisted operations, impose strict end-to-end latency requirements on industrial networks. However, traditional network-centric traffic engineering approaches often overlook edge computing workloads, resulting in resource imbalance and unstable service latency. To address this fundamental challenge, this paper proposes a traffic orchestration framework based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL). By deploying an agent at the controller, the framework jointly perceives the global network state and edge computing workloads, and learns traffic orchestration policy for network and computing load balancing. We introduce a multi-head Proximal Policy Optimization (MPPO) algorithm to support discrete path selection and continuous weight allocation, enabling intelligent traffic scheduling and resource load balancing under dynamic conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared with baseline approaches, the proposed solution significantly improves overall system load balancing and robustness while ensuring Quality of Service (QoS) guarantees.

title: OTFS-based Integrated Positioning and Communication Systems with Low-Resolution ADCs.
abstract: This paper proposes a two-phase orthogonal time–frequency space (OTFS)-based integrated positioning and communication (IPAC) framework under realistic low-resolution analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). In the uplink phase, the positioning signal is used to estimate channel parameters, which are subsequently used to determine the user’s position. The spatial smoothing-multiple signal classification algorithm is introduced to estimate the angle-of-arrival, whereas an iterative interference cancellation scheme is conceived for the remaining parameters’ estimation. The corresponding Cramer–Rao lower bounds of channel parameters and user position are also derived. During the downlink communication phase, the estimated parameters are exploited to improve beamforming at the base station. Simulation results evaluate the impact of ADC quantizer resolutions. Specifically, it is shown that enhanced downlink bit error rate performance can be achieved with improved uplink positioning, while the use of low-resolution ADCs induces noticeable performance degradation in the OTFS-IPAC system.

title: An Immersive Image Transmission System with Mutual Information based Feature Separation.
abstract: The emergence of immersive 360-degree image applications in 6G networks presents new challenges for multi-user semantic communication. Existing multi-user approaches, such as those incorporating multiple access or broadcast technologies, have successfully enhanced transmission efficiency from unicast approaches. However, they still fail to address the inherent redundancy of overlapping field-of-view regions among various users. To address this issue, we investigate a multi-user wireless communication system for immersive 360-degree image transmission, respectively extracting both shared and personalized semantic feature from overlapping and non-overlapping regions. Specifically, we propose a mutual information based feature separation regularization (MI-FSR) to formulate an optimization objective that achieves complementarity between personalized and shared semantic features while eliminating redundancy. Furthermore, we design a personalized semantic extractor integrated with a joint importance-redundancy attention module to efficiently extract semantic information from non-overlapping regions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves significant performance gains over both the modern broadcast semantic communication and conventional unicast joint source-channel coding baseline.

title: Low-Latency Federated Learning via Adaptive Batch-Size Control under Device Heterogeneity.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) plays a vital role in privacy-preserving collaborative intelligence for sixth-generation (6G) networks, supporting mission-critical, time-sensitive Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications. To achieve low-latency FL under heterogeneous communication-and-computation (C2) device capabilities, this paper proposes a C2-aware framework for optimal batch-size control that minimizes end-to-end (E2E) learning latency while ensuring convergence. The framework is designed to balance a fundamental C2tradeoff as revealed through convergence analysis. Specifically, increasing batch sizes improves the accuracy of gradient estimation and thus reduces the number of communication rounds required for convergence, but results in higher per-round latency, and vice versa. The associated problem of latency minimization is intractable; however, we solve it by designing an accurate and tractable surrogate for convergence speed, with parameters fitted to real data. This approach yields two batch-size control strategies tailored to scenarios with slow and fast fading, while also accommodating device heterogeneity. Experiments on real datasets demonstrate that the proposed strategies outperform conventional batch-size adaptation schemes that do not consider the C2tradeoff or device heterogeneity.

title: Collaborative LLM Fine-Tuning over Mobile Networks via Sparse-and-Orthogonal LoRA.
abstract: Distributed federated learning (DFL) enables mobile devices to fine-tune a large language model (LLM) collaboratively by directly sharing local updated parameters on a device-to-device (D2D) network through wireless connections. However, the local fine-tuning and updated parameters aggregation impose a significant burden on devices with limited computational and communication resources. Furthermore, aggregating parameters from heterogeneous datasets can lead to catastrophic knowledge interference, thereby degrading the overall performance of LLM. To address these issues, we formulate an optimization problem whose goal is to maximize LLM’s overall performance under resource constraint. To address this problem, we employ a sparse-LoRA method that reduces both computational and communication overhead by decomposing parameters into low-rank and sparse activated matrices. To further enhance the DFL performance, we impose a parameter-orthogonalization constraint on the LoRA matrix on each device to mitigate knowledge interference. Finally, we analyze the relationship between D2D topology and DFL performance, and propose a cluster-based topology design for efficient parameter aggregation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively reduces communication resources consumption by 55% and enhances DFL performance by 22% compared to baselines.

title: Finite-Length E-I Region Analysis and a Polar-Coded PAS Scheme for Nonlinear-EH SWIPT.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) system with nonlinear energy harvesting (EH) over both additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and fast-fading channels. We derive and characterize the finite-blocklength energy-information (E–I) region that captures the fundamental tradeoff between information rate and harvested energy. By employing the random coding union (RCU) bound, we obtain a computable inner bound on the finite-length capacity. Furthermore, we propose a novel polar-coded probabilistic amplitude shaping (PAS) SWIPT framework, in which a constant-composition distribution matcher (CCDM) optimizes the transmit distribution to maximize wireless power transfer (WPT) efficiency, while a cyclic redundancy check-aided (CA)-polar code ensures reliable wireless information transfer (WIT). Numerical results confirm that the proposed polar-coded PAS SWIPT scheme achieves over 70% (AWGN) and 55% (fast-fading) gains in harvested power compared with uniform-input polar-coded modulation at equivalent WIT reliability. Notably, its operating points lie close to the RCU-based finite-blocklength capacity boundary, validating both its theoretical optimality and practical effectiveness.

title: PCF: Proactive Communication Framework for Edge Collaborative Perception.
abstract: Collaborative video perception leverages pervasively deployed cameras to expand coverage, reduce occlusions, and enhance perception in domains such as transportation, community safety, and robotics. However, analyzing large-scale video streams is data-intensive and strains network and computation resources, especially when only a small region of interest (ROI) is relevant. To address this challenge, we propose PCF (Proactive Communication Framework), with a task-oriented method that incorporates ROI awareness into the detection task objective during training and inference, and an ROI-aware efficient camera selection policy at run time. Evaluations on a public dataset demonstrate up to a 7.5-percentage-point improvement in detection accuracy, while reducing communication cost by 56% without sacrificing performance. These results highlight PCF’s potential to enable efficient, ROI-aware perception for battery-powered mobile robots and other resource-constrained edge systems.

title: Separate the Wheat from the Chaff: A Machine Unlearning Method based on Gradient Decoupling and Purification.
abstract: As privacy protection and regulatory compliance demands grow, machine unlearning has become crucial for safeguarding user privacy. However, existing methods often struggle to separate forgettable information from retained knowledge, making the process difficult to interpret and less robust. In this paper, we propose a novel method, Gradient Decoupling and Purification (MU-GDP), which enhances unlearning effectiveness and interpretability by decoupling forgetting targets from retained knowledge through gradient direction decomposition. MU-GDP consists of three modules: (1) forgetting gradient construction to mislead classification and suppress confidence, (2) orthogonal decomposition to minimize interference with retained knowledge, and (3) gradient sign-space partitioning to improve precision by applying orthogonal decomposition only to conflicting dimensions. Extensive experiments show that our method achieves strong unlearning performance while maintaining model utility and robustness.

title: Empowering Deterministic-Delay MEC via Intelligent Network Slicing.
abstract: Deterministic demand of mission-critical applications is essential in edge computing systems for realizing Industry 4.0. However, the conventional average-based network slicing schemes incur unexpected long-tail delay, resulting in the failure to meet strict deterministic delay guarantee. To resolve this issue, in this paper, we construct a two-scale network slicing framework for multi-access edge computing (MEC), aiming to meet deterministic delay requirements of multiple users with minimal resource usage. To derive the closed-form delay distribution, we decompose the offloading process and employ the weighted approximation to address the multi-UE coupling. Then we propose an iterative two-scale network slicing (TNS) algorithm to guarantee deterministic delay, and construct a TNS-based deep-unfolding neural network, called TNS-Net, to improve the solution in presence of inaccurate channel statistics. Moreover, for the training of TNS-Net with deterministic delay as the network input, we apply extreme value theory (EVT) to analyze the distribution characteristic of delay bound violation. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that our theoretical analysis provides a relatively accurate estimate and the proposed TNS-Net ensures better delay guarantee with lower resource consumption.

title: FM-RME: Foundation Model Empowered Radio Map Estimation.
abstract: Traditional radio map estimation (RME) techniques fail to capture multi-dimensional and dynamic characteristics of complex spectrum environments. Recent data-driven methods achieve accurate RME in spatial domain, but ignore physical prior knowledge of radio propagation, limiting data efficiency especially in multi-dimensional scenarios. To overcome such limitations, we propose a new foundation model, characterized by self-supervised pre-training on diverse data for zero-shot generalization, enabling multi-dimensional radio map estimation (FM-RME). Specifically, FM-RME builds an effective synergy of two core components: a geometry-aware feature extraction module that encodes physical propagation symmetries, i.e., translation and rotation invariance, as inductive bias, and an attention-based neural network that learns long-range correlations across the spatial-temporal-spectral domains. A masked self-supervised multi-dimensional pre-training strategy is further developed to learn generalizable spectrum representations across diverse wireless environments. Once pre-trained, FM-RME supports zero-shot inference for multi-dimensional RME, including spatial, temporal, and spectral estimation, without scenario-specific retraining. Simulation results verify that FM-RME exhibits desired learning performance across diverse datasets and zero-shot generalization capabilities beyond existing RME methods.

title: Robust Streaming Tensor Train Completion for Dynamic Space-based Spectrum Situation Map Construction.
abstract: Leveraging the broad coverage and collaborative sensing capabilities of low Earth orbit satellite constellations, space-based spectrum monitoring enables the construction of spectrum situation map (SSM) for dynamic interference tracking and precise spectrum management. However, the limitations of predetermined satellite orbits and long satellite-to-ground transmission result in spectrum measurements highly incomplete and contaminated with unexpected anomalies. To better explore spatio-temporal-frequency correlations, tensor train (TT) decomposition is exploited in this paper to capture subspace information within high-order correlations for accurate SSM construction. As space-based spectrum measurements are incrementally collected with a large scale and high rate, conventional batch-based optimization limits real-time analysis and time variation tracking in dynamic changing spectrum environments. To address this issue, we propose a robust streaming tensor train completion framework that decomposes high-order incomplete streaming spectrum into the TT format and performs online tensor factor tracking and outlier removal to construct the SSM over time. Moreover, by exploiting the latent temporal structure extracted through TT format, the proposed scheme can further forecast future SSM evolution. Numerical analyses demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves better accuracy and scalability than state-of-the-art schemes in dealing with dynamic space-based SSM construction and prediction.

title: HypCC: A Hyperbolic Congestion Control Approach for Heterogeneous Flows in Datacenters.
abstract: Modern datacenters handle both latency-sensitive short flows and throughput-sensitive long flows, posing significantly different performance requirements. However, existing congestion control algorithms focus on inter-flow fairness, neglecting flow diversity and resulting in suboptimal performance. This paper presents HypCC, a congestion control scheme that combines flow size and network status to optimize short and long flows. Specifically, HypCC dynamically classifies short flows and long flows based on the bandwidth-delay product and the concurrent number of flows. On this basis, HypCC uses a hyperbolic rate control function based on the shortest-remaining-processing-time policy to prioritize short flows, reducing the corresponding flow completion time. Furthermore, HypCC leverages a ternary state machine to respond to network congestion. The state machine transitions between states based on the real-time bottleneck queue length and adjusts the position of the asymptote of the control function accordingly. Experimental results demonstrate that HypCC reduces the 99th percentile flow completion time of short flows by 58.24% and 13.01%, and the 99th percentile flow completion time of long flows by 28.61% and 17.39% compared to HPCC and FNCC, respectively.

title: Joint Channel and CFO Estimation for Chirped-OFDM-Based ISAC.
abstract: To address the performance degradation induced by inter-carrier interference (ICI) in multicarrier ISAC systems and investigate the sensing characteristics of chirped-OFDM waveforms, this paper proposes a chirped-OFDM-based ISAC framework. By strategically performing sensing prior to demodulation, the approach circumvents the ICI-induced distortions. The sensing task is then formulated as a joint estimation of channel parameters and carrier frequency offset (CFO), for which the modified Cramér-Rao lower bound and maximum likelihood estimator are derived. The CFO in chirped-OFDM helps improve sensing accuracy, while the obtained estimates facilitate low-complexity frequency synchronization. Simulation results validate that the proposed framework offers sensing accuracy comparable or superior to interference-free OFDM models, and illustrate the effects of chirp rate and time-frequency configuration on sensing performance.

title: Hiding Information Under Overt Signals: A Partially Covert Communication Framework Based on Generative Adversarial Networks.
abstract: As the demand for data privacy and wireless security continues to grow, covert communication has attracted increasing attention for its ability to transmit information without revealing its existence. However, practical covert transmission often suffers from low data rates, fragile signal recovery, and degraded covertness under time-varying fading channels. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes CAMO, a novel framework that integrates covert adversarial mimicry into the DeepJSCC paradigm for robust image transmission. CAMO employs a dual-antenna architecture: one antenna transmits legitimate QPSK signals as an overt channel, while the other emits covert signals or pseudo noise. Through adversarial training, the transmitter learns to generate covert signals that are statistically indistinguishable from background noise. Quantitatively, the Jensen-Shannon divergence between the covert and pseudo noise signals is as low as 0.003267, confirming their extreme statistical similarity. Experimental results on wireless image transmission demonstrate that CAMO maintains reliable image reconstruction quality and near-random detection accuracy (around 0.5) across varying channel conditions (AWGN, Rayleigh, Rician) and signal-to-noise ratios.

title: Deep Graph Unfolding for QoS-Aware Distributed Beamforming in Cell-Free Massive MIMO.
abstract: This paper investigates low-latency downlink beamforming design for cell-free massive multi-input multi-output (CF-mMIMO) systems with user quality of service (QoS) requirements. To address the high computational complexity and slow convergence of conventional distributed weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) algorithms, we propose a graph-based deep unfolding architecture, termed GUPD-WMMSE, which integrates parallel distributed WMMSE updates with graph neural networks (GNNs). By unfolding the iterative WMMSE procedure into a multi-layer GNN and introducing a gated recurrent unit (GRU) to exploit historical state information, the proposed approach avoids explicit matrix inversion and step-size search in each iteration. Simulation results demonstrate that GUPD-WMMSE achieves near-optimal sum rate performance with significantly reduced computational complexity and fast convergence. Moreover, the proposed architecture generalizes well to different network scales without retraining, making it suitable for real-time distributed beamforming in large-scale cell-free networks.

title: LEO-DPSL: An Efficient Split Learning Framework for AI Tasks over LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: The increasing deployment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites has enabled seamless global coverage, positioning satellite networks as critical infrastructure for intelligent applications such as remote sensing and disaster monitoring. To empower these applications, Artificial Intelligence (AI) models are widely deployed to process massive sensing data. However, conventional centralized training paradigms, which require transmitting raw data to a central server, face severe communication bandwidth and energy consumption bottlenecks over resource-constrained links. To address this, we propose a Low Earth Orbit Dual-Partitioning Split Learning framework (LEO-DPSL), a novel framework designed to overcome these limitations. By implementing a dual partitioning strategy across both model and data dimensions, LEO-DPSL enables the parallel execution of computation and transmission, significantly improving the overall pipeline efficiency. Furthermore, we formulate a joint total latency and energy consumption minimization problem and utilize an Enhanced Simulated Annealing algorithm to efficiently explore the complex solution space and determine the optimal model splitting strategy and collaborative satellites. Experimental results demonstrate that compared with the federated learning baseline, LEO-DPSL reduces training time by approximately 75.3% and energy consumption by 38.7% while maintaining model accuracy.

title: Reading Radio from Camera: Visually-Grounded, Lightweight, and Interpretable RSSI Prediction.
abstract: Accurate, real-time wireless signal prediction is essential for next-generation networks. However, existing vision-based frameworks often rely on computationally intensive models and are also sensitive to environmental interference. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel, physics-guided and light-weighted framework that predicts the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) from camera images. By decomposing RSSI into its physically interpretable components, path loss and shadow fading, we significantly reduce the model’s learning difficulty and exhibit interpretability. Our approach establishes a new state-of-the-art by demonstrating exceptional robustness to environmental interference, a critical flaw in prior work. Quantitatively, our model reduces the prediction root mean squared error (RMSE) by 50.3% under conventional conditions and still achieves an 11.5% lower RMSE than the previous benchmark’s interference-eliminated results. This superior performance is achieved with a remarkably lightweight framework, utilizing a MobileNet-based model up to 19 times smaller than competing solutions. The combination of high accuracy, robustness to interference, and computational efficiency makes our framework highly suitable for real-time, on-device deployment in edge devices, paving the way for more intelligent and reliable wireless communication systems.

title: Computationally Efficient Structure-Aware Cascaded Anti-Jamming Architecture for SWaP-Constrained Integrated Space-Air-Ground Vehicular Networks.
abstract: In modern integrated space-air-ground vehicular networks, vehicular terminals face severe co-channel interference across heterogeneous layers. To achieve effective interference cancellation in the main receiving channel, obtaining high-fidelity interference reference signals via auxiliary antennas is imperative. However, the highly dynamic multipath environment and strict Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) constraints limit the applicability of traditional reference acquisition methods relying on substantial CSI feedback or computationally intensive deep learning. Addressing this challenge, this paper proposes a computationally efficient "Identification-Separation-Equalization" cascaded blind processing architecture. This architecture utilizes a group of auxiliary antennas to capture mixed interference signals and precisely reconstruct high-fidelity interference waveforms. First, a lightweight power-tiered feature extraction mechanism is designed to rapidly identify interference modulation types. Second, a structure-aware hybrid Blind Source Separation (BSS) algorithm is proposed, which leverages signal geometric priors and the Riemannian natural gradient to achieve fast spatial decoupling without CSI. Finally, a dual-mode blind equalizer is cascaded to eliminate residual Inter-Symbol Interference (ISI) caused by convolutive mixtures. Simulation results show that the proposed method accurately reconstructs interference waveforms, improving the Interference-to-Noise Ratio (INR) by 8-10 dB and the Peak-to-Second-Peak Ratio (PSR) by approximately 30 dB. This architecture provides high-quality reference samples for the subsequent main antenna interference cancellation filter and is a key enabling technology for SWaP-constrained platforms.

title: GDiffLinQ: A Graph Diffusion Approach to Device-to-Device Spectrum Sharing.
abstract: Spectrum sharing is one of the most crucial problems for device-to-device (D2D) communications, for which link scheduling and power control are the most common approaches for large-scale D2D networks. While both optimization-based and learning-to-optimize approaches in the literature yield high-quality solutions for link scheduling and power control, there remains a challenging task to achieve near-optimal performance, low-latency, and cross-scenario adaptivity simultaneously. This paper proposes a novel D2D spectrum sharing approach, named GDiffLinQ, leveraging graph neural networks and diffusion models for generating high-quality solution distributions, and simultaneously enhancing scalability and generalization. By an extensive set of simulations, GDiffLinQ demonstrates superior sum rate performance to the best FPLinQ solutions that were believed to be numerically optimal, and more remarkably, possesses strong scalability and generalizability in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution large-scale network scenarios.

title: Congestion-Aware Ant Colony Optimization for Time-Varying Networks in All-Optical Satellite Systems.
abstract: As the commercialization of terrestrial 6G technology accelerates, ground-based 6G networks impose increasingly stringent requirements on performance metrics such as transmission rates and latency control for backhaul links. Against this backdrop, laser communication has effectively transcended the bandwidth limitations inherent in traditional satellite systems, emerging as a key technological direction in the field of space communication. The advent of all-optical single-wavelength multi-hop networks has further broken through the efficiency bottlenecks associated with electro-optical conversion processes. However, existing path planning algorithms for all-optical single-wavelength networks remain inadequate, struggling to efficiently address network congestion and thereby constraining overall performance enhancement. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a congestion-aware ant colony optimization algorithm. By dynamically sensing real-time network congestion states and optimizing path selection strategies accordingly, the proposed algorithm demonstrates significant optimization effects across three critical dimensions: reducing network congestion, minimizing path hop counts, and controlling transmission costs.

title: Network-Aware Intelligent Task Distributor for Edge-Assisted Generative AI.
abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) models in mobile and Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems poses significant challenges due to their high computational demands and the resulting latency on resource-constrained devices. While edge computing provides additional computational support, the performance of edge-assisted GenAI still depends heavily on communication delays and dynamic computational resource conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel network-aware Intelligent Task Distributor (NA-ITD) that reduces end-to-end inference latency for edge-assisted GenAI through adaptive, sub-model-level task allocation. To evaluate the performance of the proposed NA-ITD, we use a Stable Diffusion model, where NA-ITD dynamically decides, before starting the inference process, which sub-models of Stable Diffusion (encoding, denoising, and decoding) should be executed locally on the user device or offloaded to the edge server. This decision is guided by a lightweight latency predictor that estimates per-sub-model delays across both domains based on real-time network conditions, transmission latency, and edge server graphics processing unit (GPU) utilization. Unlike conventional offloading approaches, NA-ITD adapts its task allocation policy to current network and system conditions, supporting efficient utilization of communication and computation resources. Experimental results conducted under diverse network scenarios show that NA-ITD achieves up to a 38.78% reduction in average end-to-end latency compared with all-on-user and all-on-server baselines. The proposed approach demonstrates the feasibility and efficiency of communication-aware, fine-grained task distribution for real-time edge-assisted GenAI systems, paving the way for more responsive and latency-efficient edge intelligence architectures.

title: Temperature-Controlled Quantization-Aware CSI Feedback via a Multi-Value Transformer.
abstract: Practical deployment of deep learning-based CSI feedback in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems is constrained by the limited feedback-bit budget and the mismatch between training in floating-point and inference with quantized bitstreams. This paper presents a CSI feedback framework that integrates a multi-Value Transformer (MVT) with a temperature-controlled non-uniform quantization-aware training (TQ) scheme. The proposed MVT shares a single Query-Key map across multiple heads and introduces a sharpening branch to preserve high-magnitude channel components, reducing attention computation. The TQ module enables stable end-to-end optimization under low-bit feedback through a temperature-controlled surrogate and denser quantization thresholds near zero. Simulation results show that MVT achieves a better accuracy-complexity trade-off than high-performance counterparts, with up to 22.2% higher reconstruction accuracy and 89.19% lower computational complexity under the same compression ratio. The TQ maintains stable accuracy even at 3 bit quantization and offers a practical path toward deployable, bit-efficient CSI feedback for future massive MIMO systems.

title: System Design and Convergence Analysis for Decentralized Federated Fine-Tuning on LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: With low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellites emerging as edge nodes for Federated Learning (FL), their high deployment cost and limited onboard resources make efficient model training crucial. This paper addresses the challenge of global weather forecasting using a network of LEO satellites, where individual satellites have limited regional coverage and insufficient access to global data. To overcome this, we propose a Decentralized FL (DFL) framework that incorporates both observed and self-generated data for training. Each satellite locally fine-tunes its weather forecasting model using its own observations and synthetic data generated from its model, and then collaboratively updates model parameters across the network using DFL to achieve global knowledge sharing without transmitting raw data. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical convergence bound for the proposed framework, and simulation results demonstrate that it achieves accurate forecasting while ensuring robust convergence.

title: A Low-Complexity Unified Error Correction Transformer.
abstract: Channel coding is vital for reliable sixth-generation (6G) data transmission, employing diverse error correction codes for various application scenarios. Traditional decoders require dedicated hardware for each code, leading to high hardware costs. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven approaches, such as the error correction code Transformer and its enhanced version, the foundation error correction code Transformer, have been proposed to reduce the hardware cost by leveraging the Transformer to decode multiple codes. However, their excessively high computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left( {{N^2}} \right)$ due to the self-attention mechanism in the Transformer limits scalability, where N represents the sequence length. To reduce computational complexity, we propose a unified Transformer-based decoder that handles multiple linear block codes within a single framework. Specifically, a standardized unit is employed to align code length across different code types, while a redesigned low-rank unified attention module, with computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left( N \right)$, is shared across various heads in the Transformer. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed unified Transformer-based decoder outperforms existing methods and provides a high-performance, low-complexity solution for next-generation wireless communication systems.

title: Unlocking High-Fidelity Analog Joint Source-Channel Coding on Standard Digital Transceivers.
abstract: Analog joint source-channel coding (JSCC) has demonstrated superior performance for semantic communications through graceful degradation across channel conditions. However, a fundamental hardware-software mismatch prevents deployment on modern digital physical layers (PHYs): analog JSCC generates continuous-valued symbols requiring infinite waveform diversity, while digital PHYs produce a finite set of discrete waveforms and employ non-differentiable operations that break end-to-end gradient flow. Existing solutions either fundamentally limit representation granularity or require impractical white-box PHY access. We introduce D2AJSCC, a novel framework enabling high-fidelity analog JSCC deployment on standard digital PHYs. Our approach exploits orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing’s parallel subcarrier structure as a waveform synthesizer: computational PHY inversion determines input bitstreams that orchestrate subcarrier amplitudes and phases to emulate ideal analog waveforms. To enable end-to-end training despite non-differentiable PHY operations, we develop ProxyNet—a differentiable neural surrogate of the communication link that provides uninterrupted gradient flow while preventing JSCC degeneration. Simulation results for image transmission over WiFi PHY demonstrate that our system achieves near-ideal analog JSCC performance with graceful degradation across SNR conditions, while baselines exhibit cliff effects or catastrophic failures. By enabling next-generation semantic transmission on legacy infrastructure without hardware modification, our framework promotes sustainable network evolution and bridges the critical gap between analog JSCC’s theoretical promise and practical deployment on ubiquitous digital hardware.

title: Capacity Maximization for FAS-Enhanced MIMO Systems: A Low Complexity Approach.
abstract: In this paper, the problem of fluid antenna system (FAS)-enhanced multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) capacity maximization is studied. Different from conventional MIMO systems equipped with fixed-position antennas (FPAs), we consider fluid antennas (FAs) can be flexibly repositioned in a fixed region, such that the MIMO channel between them is reconfigured to achieve higher capacity. We aim to jointly optimize the beamforming matrix and FA positions of the transmitter to maximize the MIMO capacity. First, we develop an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm to find a locally optimal solution by iteratively optimizing the transmit beamforming matrix and the positions of each FA with the other variable being fixed. For the beamforming matrix optimization, we adopt the conventional eigenmode transmission scheme, and the optimal power allocation is calculated by water-filling method. For the FA positions optimization, we identify a small set of promising candidates that can be exhaustively searched efficiently. Next, we analyze two special cases in which the MIMO-capacity maximization reduces to maximizing the sum of eigenvalues with respect to the FA positions. The proposed candidate set can then be directly applied to these cases as well. Numerical results show that the performance of the proposed method is close to that of the successive convex approximation (SCA)-based method, while consistently outperforming other benchmarks up to 30% in achievable rate. Most importantly, the proposed algorithm requires only 16.9% of the simulation time compared to the SCA-based method. This highlights its potential for practical and efficient position optimization of FAs, paving the way for real-world applications in 6G.

title: Heterogeneous Personalized Federated Learning with Mixture-of-Experts for Intrusion Detection in the Internet of Vehicles.
abstract: With the widespread adoption of intelligent connected vehicles, safeguarding the Internet of vehicles (IoV) against cyberattacks has become increasingly critical. However, existing IoV intrusion detection systems (IDSs) encounter two major challenges: (1) vehicular mobility leads to highly heterogeneous data distributions across nodes, causing model drift and degraded detection performance, and (2) resource-constrained vehicular nodes are often incapable of supporting the computational demands of diverse heterogeneous models under federated learning. To address these issues, we propose HPFedMoE, a novel heterogeneous personalized federated intrusion detection framework tailored for the IoV. The framework leverages the mixture-of-experts (MoE) paradigm to balance generalization and personalization. Specifically, each client is equipped with a shared lightweight feature extractor and a local gating network, thereby forming a locally heterogeneous MoE. Through weighted representation fusion, the framework integrates global generalized features with client-specific patterns, enhancing fine-grained intrusion detection while accommodating model heterogeneity. Experiments on public datasets demonstrate that HPFedMoE outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of detection accuracy. Furthermore, it effectively reduces computational overhead while preserving data privacy in IoV environments.

title: Power Allocation for Efficient Decentralized Federated Learning over Cell-Free Massive MIMO.
abstract: Cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CFmMIMO) and federated learning (FL) are key enablers for distributed intelligence in future sixth-generation (6G) networks. However, the uplink transmission of high-dimensional local models in FL over wireless networks incurs significant communication overhead, which limits training efficiency under practical latency and energy constraints. In this paper, we study decentralized federated learning (DFL) over CFmMIMO networks, where interconnected access points collaboratively aggregate models and focus on uplink power allocation to enable efficient model training. We formulate a joint uplink latency and energy optimization problem by incorporating the achievable uplink rate. Based on the derived analytical expressions, an efficient coordinate descent-based power allocation algorithm is developed to balance the latency-energy trade-off in DFL global training. Simulation results show that our proposed method improves the final model accuracy by up to 32% compared with benchmark schemes under various resource budget constraints. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of latency and energy considered power allocation for efficient DFL over CFmMIMO networks.

title: SMARTWIN: Smart Reinforcement Learning Based Digital Twin for Resource Optimization in O-RAN.
abstract: The exponential increase of heterogeneous devices and vertical applications in 5G and Beyond 5G (B5G) networks has catalysed a paradigm shift in cellular network design, fostering a transition towards disaggregated, fully virtualized, and programmable architectures. To meet these demands, the Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) architecture standardized by the O-RAN Alliance enables hardware independence, while the use of Digital Twins (DTs) for network emulation and validation is becoming increasingly popular. Although O-RAN introduces new technologies and opportunities, advances in Machine Learning (ML) based network automation remain limited, mainly because of insufficient large-scale datasets and experimental testing environments. To address the challenges of accurate network modelling and efficient resource management in O-RAN, this paper introduces SMARTWIN, a Smart Reinforcement Learning based Digital Twin framework. SMARTWIN enables precise network modelling and intelligent resource allocation and scheduling, with the objective of optimizing the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) of eMBB, mMTC, and URLLC network slices. It also implements a Conservative Q-Learning (CQL) algorithm to learn from data generated by the DT, where the performance comparison with the baseline Implicit Q-Learning (IQL) algorithm shows an improvement of approximately 41% across all slices. This indicates that the proposed SMARTWIN framework can generalize well beyond the behaviour policy, enabling more efficient and intelligent resource allocation decisions within the DT.

title: Software-Defined Optics for UAV Laser Communications.
abstract: Laser-based optical wireless systems have immense potential to increase the capacity and security of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) communication. However, UAV-induced vibrations and dynamic instabilities severely degrade optical beam alignment, resulting in significant link losses. This paper presents a Software-Defined Optics (SDO) framework that integrates machine learning–based predictive control with real-time inertial feedback for resilient UAV laser communications. A Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) is trained on inertial measurement unit (IMU) telemetry to forecast UAV motion and predictively steer a micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS)-based laser transmitter, thereby compensating for latency in the sensing–processing–actuation loop. The framework is validated through experimental testing for motion predictions and Zemax OpticStudio (ZOS) simulations for optical link performance.

title: Practical RIS Gain without the Pain: Randomization and Opportunistic Scheduling in 5G NR.
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the performance gains achieved by an in-house built reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) integrated with a real-time 5G new radio (NR) system implemented using the OpenAirInterface (OAI) framework. We first quantify the gain in throughput achievable by integrating an RIS with a 5G system. Next, we show that randomly setting the RIS phase configuration and leveraging the inherent proportional fair (PF) scheduling mechanism of 5G NR can yield near-optimal throughput, provided the throughput averaging window of the PF scheduler is chosen judiciously. This occurs because, in each time slot, the PF scheduler naturally prioritizes data transmission to the user equipment (UE) that experiences the best channel conditions, namely, the UE to which the randomly configured RIS is aligned. Subsequently, we experimentally evaluate key performance metrics, including the reference signal received power (RSRP), block error rate (BLER), modulation and coding scheme (MCS) index, and throughput, under random RIS configurations. These results confirm that even a randomly configured RIS with negligible overhead can deliver performance comparable to optimized RIS designs, in real-world 5G NR wireless communication systems.

title: SmartIA: Context-Aware Feedback-Free Beam Discovery for Efficient Initial Access.
abstract: Future wireless networks leveraging millimeter-wave and sub-Terahertz spectra rely on highly directional beamforming to counter severe path loss. However, identifying the optimal beam, specially during the Initial Access (IA) procedure, remains challenging due to the lack of feedback between the Base Station (BS) and User Equipment (UE). In this paper, we present SmartIA a context-aware feedback-free hierarchical beam scanning framework for efficient IA. We design an optimized sequence of transmitted beam patterns that uniquely encode spatial directions, enabling all UEs to identify the best beam by aggregating multi-stage information. This achieves logarithmic-complexity beam discovery with reduced acquisition time while preserving high spatial resolution. We further introduce a novel analog antenna weight vector design that achieves the required spatial coding with full power amplifier utilization. We develop an adaptive Synchronization Signal Block (SSB) transmission strategy that leverages contextual information on link conditions across the user distribution to minimize BS radio resource utilization, while preserving cell coverage under power-constrained multi-directional transmissions. Simulation results show 50% lower IA acquisition time and BS energy consumption, with 3 dB gains in both coverage and link quality compared to standard approaches, validating SmartIA as an scalable solution for beam discovery and IA in future high-frequency networks.

title: Trajectory-Adaptive Beam Shaping: Towards Beam-Management-Free Near-field Communications.
abstract: The quest for higher wireless carrier frequencies spanning the millimeter-wave (mmWave) and Terahertz (THz) bands heralds substantial enhancements in data throughput and spectral efficiency for next-generation wireless networks. However, these gains come at the cost of severe path loss and a heightened risk of beam misalignment due to user mobility, especially pronounced in near-field communication. Traditional solutions rely on extremely directional beamforming and frequent beam updates via beam management, but such techniques impose formidable computational and signaling overhead. In response, we propose a novel approach termed trajectory-adaptive beam shaping (TABS) that eliminates the need for real-time beam management by shaping the electromagnetic wavefront to follow the user's predefined trajectory. Drawing inspiration from self-accelerating beams in optics, TABS concentrates energy along pre-defined curved paths corresponding to the user's motion without requiring real-time beam reconfiguration. We further introduce a dedicated quantitative metric to characterize performance under the TABS framework. Comprehensive simulations substantiate the superiority of TABS in terms of link performance, overhead reduction, and implementation complexity.

title: Transmit Beampattern Design for Continuous Aperture Array (CAPA)-aided Sensing Systems.
abstract: In this paper, a continuous aperture array (CAPA)-aided sensing system is investigated, and a corresponding beampattern design framework is designed. Unlike conventional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) arrays, CAPAs are capable of generating continuous source currents, enabling full amplitude and phase control across the aperture. In the proposed system, the directional beampattern is first derived based on the free-space electromagnetic response and the far-field Green’s function approximation. Then, a minimal beam gain maximization problem is formulated for CAPA-based multi-target sensing, in which the continuous source current is optimized. Since the source current is a continuous function, the problem is an integral-based functional optimization, where conventional discrete methods are not directly applicable. To address this issue, a Fourier-based algorithm is proposed to transform the functional optimization into a discrete form, whereafter the successive convex approximation is employed to solve the non-convex problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed CAPA-aided system achieves enhanced beam gains and reduced sidelobe levels compared to the conventional MIMO systems.

title: Three-Stage Channel Estimation for Active RIS-FAS-Assisted Millimeter-Wave Systems.
abstract: This paper investigates the channel estimation problem in millimeter-wave systems assisted by an active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) and fluid antenna system (FAS). A three-stage estimation scheme is proposed by strategically controlling the RIS on/off states and the FAS position switching. Stage I deactivates the RIS to enable channel estimation for the user equipment (UE)-base station (BS) link. Stage II activates the RIS while fixing the FAS position, thereby avoiding strong channel coupling to enable RIS cascaded channel estimation. Stage III activates the RIS while allowing the FAS to switch positions; despite the resulting strong coupling between cascaded angles and UE-RIS link angles of departure (AoDs), an alternating iterative projection method, leveraging prior-stage estimates, is proposed to achieve accurate UE-RIS link AoD estimation. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

title: TwinPot-Gen: A Generative Semantic Digital-Twin Honeypot Framework for Adaptive and Explainable Defence in 6G Networks.
abstract: The security of emerging 6G small-cell networks increasingly depends on intelligent deception mechanisms, where honeypots serve as proactive defence components. However, conventional honeypots lack semantic and behavioural realism and often risk leaking sensitive data when emulating complex network states. Existing systems remain limited by static personas, weak sanitisation, and unexplainable reactions, making them ineffective against adaptive attackers. To address this challenge, we propose TwinPot-Gen, a digital-twin-assisted honeypot framework that integrates semantic communication , graph-based knowledge modelling, and generative AI to achieve realistic and privacy-preserving deception. The framework establishes two isolated domains-the Digital-Twin Network and the Honeypot Network-connected through two secure gateways: the Generative Knowledge Gateway (GKG) and the Defence-Orchestration Gateway (DOG). GKG performs semantic sanitisation and persona generation using a large language model, while DOG enforces adaptive, policy-driven responses. Experimental results on a Kubernetes-based 6G testbed show that TwinPot-Gen improves persona realism by 35-50%, achieves a 0.94 F1-score in attack detection, and maintains sub-100 ms orchestration latency, confirming its efficiency and trustworthiness in dynamic 6G environments.

title: Conditional Generative AoA/AoD Estimation: A Pilot-Free and System-Agnostic Approach.
abstract: Accurate angle of arrival (AoA) and angle of departure (AoD) estimation underpins spatial precision, efficient beamforming, and the overall Quality of Service (QoS) and Quality of Experience (QoE) of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). This paper introduces a generative AI (GenAI) framework that synthesizes the complete set of multipath 2D AoA/AoD parameters directly from transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) locations, overcoming the limitations of traditional model-based and current data-driven learning methods. The proposed classifiers-guided conditional generative adversarial network (CG-CGAN) offers a system-agnostic approach that removes the need for pilot signals and operates effectively under challenging coherent multipath conditions. Its three-stage architecture integrates classification and conditional generative modeling to jointly infer line-of-sight (LoS) status, number of propagation paths, and angular parameters. Simulations on the DeepMIMO dataset demonstrate over 99.5% classification accuracy and 92% angle generation accuracy, significantly outperforming classical techniques while reducing computational complexity and enhancing the QoS/QoE of ISAC-enabled systems.

title: Benchmarking Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks for Airborne Network Performance Prediction.
abstract: Airborne networks present unique challenges due to their dynamic nature, requiring more research than stationary networks. While Graph Neural Networks in Machine Learning have advanced performance modelling for stationary networks, existing Graph Neural Networks algorithms developed for performance modelling do not fully capture the dynamism of airborne networks. To address this, we developed a Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network for performance modelling in airborne networks, demonstrating its performance improvement over Graph Neural Network models in the state of the art.

title: Priority Assignment of Packets in Sensor Nodes for Goal-Oriented Semantic Communications.
abstract: The power and bandwidth demands of massive machine-type communications (mMTC) are expected to notably grow in beyond 5G (B5G) networks, thereby straining network resources and operators [1]. In response, semantic communication frameworks are proposed to reduce communication overhead in B5G. Transmission of resulting semantic information over prioritized random access channels (RACH) thus emerged. In this work, we propose a content-centric priority assignment procedure at the sensor level for this paradigm. We define an information gain metric using reinforcement learning nomenclature that relates sensor observations to a goal. We propose a novel objective function that maximizes information retrieval at the base station while adhering to the given RACH configuration. It is shown that state sequences reconstructed at the BS follow actual sequences more accurately, measured using the proposed metric. We further demonstrate the feasibility of our proposal in a case study of distributed control in heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), and show that it achieves a smaller tracking error compared to non-prioritized RACH.

title: Task Offloading for Stacked Intelligent Metasurface enabled MEC in Millimeter-Wave Communications.
abstract: Millimeter-Wave (mmWave) communications enable ultra-high data rates but suffer from severe path loss and blockage, which significantly limits reliability and coverage. Mobile edge computing (MEC) has been recognized as a promising paradigm to reduce latency and enable computation-intensive applications by bringing cloud capabilities closer to end users. However, the performance of MEC systems is still constrained by unfavorable propagation conditions.
