Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) offer a cost and energy-efficient technology to enhance link quality; however, conventional single-layer RISs provide limited capabilities in interference suppression and beamforming flexibility. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel stacked intelligent metasurface (SIM) architecture integrated with MEC in mmWave communications. By jointly leveraging multilayer wave-domain processing and edge computing resources, the proposed SIM-MEC framework enables efficient task offloading in multi-user mmWave systems, effectively increasing the total computing task size under strict latency constraints. We formulate a joint optimization problem of SIM phase shifts and time allocation for transmission and computing, which is solved using a combination of projected gradient ascent and active-set algorithms. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SIM-enabled MEC framework significantly outperforms benchmark schemes, including direct transmission without SIM, single-layer RIS, and equal-phase configurations, in terms of maximization of the computing task size.

title: Enhancing Text-to-Image Generation via End-Edge Collaborative Hybrid Super-Resolution.
abstract: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content (AIGC) has made significant strides, with high-resolution text-to-image (T2I) generation becoming increasingly critical for improving users’ Quality of Experience (QoE). Although resource-constrained edge computing adequately supports fast low-resolution T2I generations, achieving high-resolution output still faces the challenge of ensuring image fidelity at the cost of latency. To address this, we first investigate the performance of super-resolution (SR) methods for image enhancement, confirming a fundamental trade-off that lightweight learning-based SR struggles to recover fine details, while diffusion-based SR achieves higher fidelity at a substantial computational cost. Motivated by these observations, we propose an end-edge collaborative generation-enhancement framework. Upon receiving a T2I generation task, the system first generates a low-resolution image based on adaptively selected denoising steps and super-resolution scales at the edge side, which is then partitioned into patches and processed by a region-aware hybrid SR policy. This policy applies a diffusion-based SR model to foreground patches for detail recovery and a lightweight learning-based SR model to background patches for efficient upscaling, ultimately stitching the enhanced ones into the high-resolution image. Experiments show that our system reduces service latency by 33% compared with baselines while maintaining competitive image quality.

title: RL-Based Multi-Modal Semantic Transmission in Bandwidth-Constrained Vehicular Networks.
Conditional Diffusion Model-Driven Massive MIMO Iterative Detection.
abstract: To ensure future high-quality and reliable massive communication during 6G uplink transmissions, we propose a conditional diffusion model-driven massive MIMO detector, which can iteratively estimate channels and detect data for the uplink multiuser access. This approach utilizes a generative diffusion model to learn the score function of the joint posterior by integrating the prior distribution with the likelihood derived from the transmission model. The prior distribution is obtained either by learning from channel statistics or through analytical derivation from the symbol constellation. By employing noise matching initialization and an asynchronous annealed Langevin dynamics (ALD) sampling scheme, the receiver alternates efficiently between score-based channel estimation and data detection, thus avoiding traps of local minima. Simulation results demonstrate that this iterative diffusion process outperforms Bayesian-based and existing synchronous ALD channel estimation and data detection schemes in multiuser uplink scenarios.

title: Reliability-Aware Multi-Agent Resource Scheduling for Vehicular Network Slicing under RSU Failures.
abstract: The convergence of network slicing and edge computing in vehicular networks enables customized, low-latency services for diverse applications. However, most orchestration schemes assume reliable roadside infrastructure, overlooking stochastic RSU failures caused by hardware faults, software crashes, or connectivity loss. Such failures interrupt slice services and degrade QoS but are rarely modeled alongside dynamic resource demands. This paper proposes a resilient resource orchestration framework for vehicular network slicing under RSU failures. The problem is formulated by modeling RSU states and optimizing joint communication–computation allocation with multi-path offloading to improve task completion rate and processing latency. A Reliability-Aware Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (RA-MADDPG) algorithm is developed, integrating real-time RSU reliability into agents’ observations for adaptive and distributed decision-making. Simulation results show that the proposed approach significantly enhances service continuity and reduces end-to-end latency compared with baseline methods, validating its effectiveness in maintaining resilient IoV services under infrastructure disruptions.

title: HoRAMA: Holistic Reconstruction with Automated Material Assignment for Ray Tracing using NYURay.
abstract: Next-generation wireless networks at upper mid-band and millimeter-wave frequencies require accurate site-specific deterministic channel propagation prediction. Wireless ray tracing (RT) provides site-specific predictions but demands high-fidelity three-dimensional (3D) environment models with material properties. Manual 3D model reconstruction achieves high accuracy but requires weeks of expert effort, creating scalability bottlenecks for large environment reconstruction. Traditional vision-based 3D reconstruction methods lack RT compatibility due to geometrically defective meshes and missing material properties. This paper presents Holistic Reconstruction with Automated Material Assignment (HoRAMA) for wireless propagation prediction using NYURay. HoRAMA generates RT-compatible 3D models from RGB video readily captured using a smartphone or low-cost portable camera, by integrating MASt3R-SLAM dense point cloud generation with vision language model-assisted material assignment. The HoRAMA 3D reconstruction method is verified by comparing NYURay RT predictions, using both manually created and HoRAMA-generated 3D models, against field measurements at 6.75 GHz and 16.95 GHz across 12 TX-RX locations in a 700 square meter factory. HoRAMA ray tracing predictions achieve a 2.28 dB RMSE for matched multipath component (MPC) power predictions, comparable to the manually created 3D model baseline (2.18 dB), while reducing 3D reconstruction time from two months to 16 hours. HoRAMA enables scalable wireless digital twin creation for RT network planning, infrastructure deployment, and beam management in 5G/6G systems, as well as eventual real-time implementation at the edge [1].

title: A Nonlinear Testbed for Terahertz PAs: Revealing the Limitations of Polynomial-Based DPD.
abstract: Terahertz (THz) communication is a key technology for sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems, promising to support unprecedented data rates and capacity. In this paper, we construct a real nonlinear test platform for characterizing power amplifiers (PAs) operating in THz band. Utilizing this platform, we experimentally analyze distortion characteristics of THz PAs, revealing significant nonlinearity and pronounced memory effects, especially under wideband scenarios. In addition, a conventional memory polynomial model-based digital predistortion (DPD) is applied. Experimental results show that the polynomial-based DPD provides only limited linearization for the THz PA, revealing the heightened complexity of nonlinear behaviors in the THz regime. In summary, our findings demonstrate a clear need for more sophisticated behavioral modeling and linearization techniques in future THz communication systems.

title: Cluster-Aware Structured Pruning for Robust and Sustainable Edge Intelligence.
abstract: Edge intelligence for sustainable 6G must operate under strict constraints on latency, energy, and computational availability, motivating structured pruning for efficient on-device inference. However, at high pruning ratios, current global magnitude-based channel pruning solutions remove entire feature groups, leading to severe accuracy collapse. To cope with this, we present PKPrune (PCA-KMeans Pruning), a data-free cluster-aware structured pruning method that groups convolutional filters in weight space and prunes within each group while keeping at least one representative per cluster. Ablation study reveals that clustering granularity plays a dominant role in preserving robustness under extreme pruning, while the PCA variance retention ratio has a comparatively minor impact on post-pruning accuracy. To assess practical deployment feasibility, we further study the impact of the fine-tuning budgets, showing catastrophic accuracy collapse without adaptation and rapid recovery with lightweight retraining, which enables explicit accuracy and energy trade-offs under constrained edge resources. Finally, we evaluate PKPrune on CIFAR-10 using ResNet-18 with pruning ratios up to 90%. At 90% pruning, PKPrune achieves 72.94% Top-1 accuracy after lightweight fine-tuning, compared to 63.72% with conventional L2-norm structured pruning, while exhibiting competitive efficiency behavior relative to a dependency-aware structured pruning baseline in our measurement setting.

title: Impact of UAV 3D Posture and Wobbles on the Non-Stationary Air-to-Ground Channels.
abstract: Accurate modeling of UAV-to-ground (U2G) channels is essential for the design and evolution of future wireless systems. This paper introduces a three-dimensional (3D) non-stationary multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel model that accounts for both UAV posture variations and wobbling dynamics. The model characterizes fuselage posture changes, represents internal UAV vibrations as a sinusoidal random process, and describes wobbling induced by random airflow using a Gaussian distribution. By integrating these 3D posture and wobbling effects within the air-to-ground (A2G) channel framework, this study examines how the temporal auto-correlation function (ACF) varies with different postures,wobble angle amplitudes, and carrier frequencies. The findings indicate that even minor UAV posture adjustments and wobbles can substantially influence the channel’s temporal correlation. Numerical analysis further demonstrates a rapid decline in the ACF as wobble angle amplitudes and carrier frequency increase.

title: LPPFS: A Lightweight and Privacy-Preserving Feature Selection for Vertical Federated Learning.
abstract: Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm that preserves the privacy of participants’ raw data while enabling entities with fully overlapping sample spaces to collaboratively train a shared model. Feature selection plays a pivotal role in the data preprocessing phase of VFL. However, existing works often suffer from inefficiency and excessive interactions, which hinder their practical deployment. To address these deficiencies, we propose a lightweight and privacy-preserving feature selection scheme. Our scheme adopts a filter-based method and, for the first time in the VFL setting, employs the Fisher criterion as the scoring metric. Feature selection can be completed in only three rounds of interaction between the label holder and other participants, with communication costs kept within a practical range. Privacy preservation is ensured through the integration of Fully Homomorphic Encryption and a random masking mechanism, thereby removing the need for a trusted third party. We evaluate the proposed scheme on three real-world datasets, and the results demonstrate notable accuracy improvements and superior efficiency compared to existing filter-based secure feature selection methods for VFL.

title: DP-MADDPG: Dual-Path Redundant Routing for UAV Swarms via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Node failures in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm networks significantly impact communication reliability. This paper proposes Dual-Path Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DP-MADDPG), a novel redundant routing algorithm that applies the MADDPG framework to UAV swarm networks and introduces a dual-output training scheme capable of generating two communication paths simultaneously. Unlike traditional approaches that compute backup paths after determining primary routes, our method employs a dual-output network architecture where each agent learns to select both primary and backup next-hop nodes during training. Through passive switching mechanisms, the system enables immediate failover upon link failures without route recomputation. We conduct extensive evaluations under various scenarios including different UAV mobility speeds, Constant Bit Rate (CBR) traffic loads, and node failure patterns. Simulation results demonstrate that DP-MADDPG significantly outperforms both single-path MADDPG and MADDPG with Loop-Free Alternate (LFA) in terms of packet delivery ratio and average delay in failure scenarios, validating the effectiveness of our dual-path training scheme for intelligent redundant routing in dynamic UAV environments.

title: EPGAT: Graph Attention Aided Expectation Propagation for MU-MIMO Detection.
abstract: In multiuser Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems, reliable symbol detection is a significant challenge due to severe Multi-User Interference (MUI). Model-based methods like Expectation Propagation (EP) are effective in low-interference conditions but struggle as MUI increases. While deep learning detectors like the Graph EP Network (GEPNet) can handle high MUI, their computational complexity and slow convergence limit practical use. To address these limitations, we introduce EPGAT, a lightweight, model-driven detector that embeds a Graph Attention Network (GAT) into the EP algorithm. EPGAT leverages the GAT’s attention mechanism to effectively model and mitigate MUI, and incorporates iteration-invariant node features to facilitate faster convergence. Simulations demonstrate EPGAT’s primary advantage in its rapid convergence. With few iterations, it achieves a much lower Symbol Error Rate (SER) than GEPNet, and its performance becomes comparable to that of GEPNet as iterations increase, effectively addressing the high-MUI weakness of the model-based EP algorithm. EPGAT also demonstrates generalization capability to channel model mismatch. It maintains viable performance on NLoS-dominant Rician channels (low K-factors) even when trained exclusively on Rayleigh channels. This makes EPGAT a practical detector that effectively balances performance, computational cost, and fast convergence.

title: On the Impact of Pilot Power Allocation in Pilot-Aided ISAC Systems with Synchronization Errors.
abstract: Pilot-aided simultaneous communication and localization (PASCAL) provides a promising foundation for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. However, most existing studies assume uniform pilot power allocation and perfect synchronization, overlooking the higher temporal importance of early pilots, particularly under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions and hardware imperfections. This paper proposes a pilot power-allocation strategy that front-loads early pilots and keeps a uniform tail for later pilots, under a fixed total pilot-energy budget. The framework is further extended to account for integer synchronization errors, which degrade pilot correlation and cause leakage among overlapping pilots. Under synchronization errors, we model integer-delay timing misalignment and characterize performance degradation using RMSE-CRLB analysis for localization and Sum Data Rate (SDR) for communication. To evaluate performance, we derive the analytical Cramér–Rao lower bound (CRLB) and validate the analysis with Monte-Carlo simulations by reporting the root-mean-square error (RMSE). The results show that the proposed allocation significantly reduces angle-estimation RMSE, leaves Doppler RMSE nearly unchanged, and preserves SDR relative to uniform power allocation, especially at low-to-medium SNRs.

title: Enhancing Heatmap Generation for WiFi-Based Human Pose Estimation via Trajectory-Guided Joint-Aware Temporal Weighting.
Virtualized GPU Offloading for AI Inference: Enabling Deep Learning Frameworks on GPU-less Devices.
abstract: The deployment of Deep Learning (DL) inference on resource-constrained endpoint devices is often hampered by the absence of Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) creates performance bottlenecks for real-time applications. This paper presents a virtualized GPU offloading framework that enables devices to execute demanding AI workloads by transparently leveraging a remote, high-performance GPU. Our system is based on an enhanced version of the GVirtuS framework, updated to support CUDA 12.6 and integrated with DL libraries, including PyTorch, Caffe, and OpenCV DNN. We validated our framework on representative AI tasks, including human pose estimation and image classification. The experimental results demonstrate substantial performance gains, achieving up to a 17.8x speedup over CPU-only execution while maintaining ease of deployment. This work confirms that transparent remote GPU acceleration is a practical and effective solution for unlocking high-performance AI capabilities on the vast ecosystem of GPU-less devices.

title: Zero-Shot Wireless Blockage Detection via Foundation Models.
abstract: Wireless blockage detection (WBD) is crucial for ensuring stable communication services, yet traditional methods and deep learning (DL)-based approaches face limitations that conventional techniques struggle to distinguish line-of-sight (LoS) blockage from complex channel dynamics, while DL models rely heavily on large-scale labeled wireless data, which are costly and difficult to annotate. To address these challenges, this paper proposes FM-WBD (Foundation Model-based Wireless Blockage Detection), a zero-shot WBD framework leveraging the cross-modal reasoning and generalization capabilities of foundation models (FMs). We design a custom wireless encoder to extract semantic features from received power measurements, and employ contrastive learning to align wireless features with image features from pretrained FMs. Zero-shot detection is achieved by measuring the similarity between aligned wireless features and text prompt embeddings representing blocked/unblocked states. Additionally, a few-shot enhancement strategy is introduced to refine detection accuracy using a small number of labeled samples. Evaluations on the DeepSense 6G dataset demonstrate that FM-WBD achieves competitive performance with fully supervised baselines, and exhibits superior generalizability to unseen scenarios. Although its zero-shot performance is inferior to that of few-shot learning, the zero-shot capability enables label-free WBD, which is of significant practical and research value in scenarios where labeled data are unavailable or prohibitively costly to obtain.

title: Multi-User Semantic and Data Communications with Adaptive Source-Channel Coding.
abstract: This paper considers a multi-user semantic and data communication (MU-SemDaCom) system, where a base station (BS) simultaneously serves users with different semantic and data tasks through a downlink multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) channel. We propose a multi-user adaptive source-channel coding (MU-ASCC) framework that adaptively optimizes deep neural network (DNN)-based source coding, digital channel coding, and superposition broadcasting according to the channel conditions. First, we employ a data-regression method to approximate the end-to-end (E2E) semantic and data distortions. Then, based on the derived formulas, we formulate a weighted-sum E2E distortion minimization problem that jointly optimizes the source-channel coding rates, power allocation, and beamforming vectors for both the data and semantic users. Finally, an alternating optimization (AO) framework is developed, where the adaptive rate optimization is solved using the subgradient descent method, while the joint power and beamforming is addressed via the uplink-downlink duality (UDD) technique. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MU-ASCC scheme achieves simultaneous improvements in both the data recovery and semantic task performance compared with conventional schemes.

title: Online Scheduling in Pinching Antennas Assisted Vehicular Communication Networks.
abstract: Traditional cellular-oriented vehicular communication systems often struggle with limited connectivity and rigid infrastructure, leading to coverage gaps, reduced throughput, and poor adaptability in highly dynamic transportation scenarios. Recently, pinching antennas, with its inherent capability to support line-of-sight paths and flexible antenna configurations, has emerged as a promising candidate for next generation multiple access (NGMA), offering new degrees of spatial and structural freedom for vehicular communication networks. In this paper, we consider a queuing-theoretic framework for pinching antennas assisted vehicular communication networks, which aims to minimize queue backlogs and achieve optimal throughput by designing pinching antenna activation strategies. The problem is hard to solve due to the stochastic nature of traffic arrivals, the discrete and spatially constrained set of feasible antenna activation patterns, and the unknown service rates under dynamic network conditions. To overcome these challenges, we propose a schedule-as-you-learn (SYL) based pinching antenna activation approach that employs dual-averaging based online learning to estimate feasible service rates and derive dynamic pinching antenna activation patterns. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SYL-based pinching antenna activation approach strikes a balance between the optimal throughput and low latency compared with the conventional max-weight approach.

title: RIS-Aided Near-Field Target Localization via Decoupled Atomic Norm Minimization.
abstract: In this paper, a gridless near-field (NF) localization method based on reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is proposed for non line of sight (NLOS) target using SIMO transmission model. To fully utilize the spatial-temporal information of the signal source, cross-correlation operation with multiple pseudo-snapshots is performed to eliminate the influence of NF range term with Fresnel approximation, which extends the array aperture of RIS. Then, a single-snapshot decoupled atomic norm algorithm based on virtual aperture is proposed for two-dimensional direction of arrival (DOA) with a pairing procedure, followed by a subspace method for range estimation. Finally, the total least squares (TLS) method is used to alleviate the systematic error on the estimated parameters. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Distributed Optimization for Secure Task Offloading in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks.
abstract: Low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs) provide a promising platform for delivering high-throughput and low-latency connectivity in mission-critical operations. However, the security of task offloading in drone-assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) systems remains a key challenge, especially when eavesdroppers can exploit favorable propagation conditions. In this paper, we propose a secure task offloading framework based on cooperative jamming and power control, using a dual-drone architecture with dedicated service and jamming drones. We formulate the system’s total weighted energy consumption minimization as a mixed integer nonconvex problem, addressing secrecy rate, latency, and power constraints. To solve this problem, we develop a distributed optimization algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), incorporating successive convex approximation (SCA) for secure power control. The proposed framework enables decentralized coordination under strong security coupling without requiring full global information. Simulation results show that the proposed distributed scheme achieves an objective value close to that of centralized optimization, validating its effectiveness.

title: GPT4RAN: A GPT-powered Framework Towards Unified Wireless Resource Scheduling.
abstract: Efficient wireless resource scheduling is fundamental to next-generation radio access networks (RAN). Traditional methods and deep reinforcement learning struggle with non-convexity, inflexibility, and poor generalization. This work investigates the application of Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPT) to RAN control, proposing GPT4RAN — a sequence modeling-based framework for unified cross-layer wireless resource scheduling. It operates through three core stages: RAN tokenization, offline imitation learning, and online reinforcement learning. The RAN tokenizer first transforms high-dimensional RAN state information into token-based, flexible, and efficient sequences. This is followed by offline imitation learning, which leverages extensive expert trajectories to achieve rapid warm-starting and near-expert performance. Finally, online reinforcement learning further elevates the model’s capability through task-specific interaction via RLOOwE algorithm. Experiments demonstrate that GPT4RAN rapidly attains expert-level performance after imitation learning and consistently surpasses it after reinforcement learning, while maintaining strong generalization across diverse scenarios. This work illustrates the significant potential of GPT-powered frameworks in building next-generation intelligent RAN.

title: RIS-aided Far-field NLOS Target Localization in Bistatic EMVS-MIMO Radar.
abstract: In this paper, a non-line-of-sight (NLOS) localization method is proposed for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided bistatic MIMO radar, where both the transmitter and receiver employ arbitrarily configured electromagnetic vector sensor (EMVS) arrays. By exploiting the inherent multi-dimensional structure of the received data, we construct a third-order parallel factor (PARAFAC) model and solve it using the trilinear alternating least squares (TALS) algorithm to recover the parameters of interest. Two-dimensional (2-D) direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation is then obtained through the rotational invariance property combined with the normalized vector cross-product (VCP) method, followed by a disambiguation procedure to address angle ambiguities caused by arbitrary receiver geometries. A least squares approach is further applied to estimate 2-D polarization parameters. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate and unambiguous estimation of direction-of-departure (DOD), DOA, and polarization angles, with root mean square error (RMSE) performance close to the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB). Moreover, the approach enables reliable localization and parameter pairing of multiple targets in challenging NLOS scenarios, confirming both its effectiveness and robustness.

title: Copot-2025: Six-month Observation of Honeypots.
abstract: Publicly available datasets from long-term honeypot deployments remain scarce. We release Copot-2025, a six-month dataset collected from January to July 2025, comprising 1.6 million sessions across diverse honeypot types. By analyzing this dataset and comparing it with prior measurements and external data sources, we characterize recent trends in attack traffic and interaction depth. Using workflow-level abstraction and unsupervised sequence modeling, we show that complete post-compromise attack workflows form a statistically negligible tail. Cross-session and cross-honeypot analysis further indicates that correlated attack activity persists for only a small fraction of sources and is dominated by tool-driven automation rather than operator-level coordination.

title: A Future-Aware Cognitive Semantic Communication System via Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models.
abstract: Cognitive semantic communication (SemCom) system is envisioned as a promising paradigm for enhancing traditional semantic communication by incorporating semantic inference and error correction enabled by knowledge graphs (KGs). However, existing KG embedding models are typically static or rely solely on historical data, limiting their ability to capture the temporal evolution of entities and relationships. To address this challenge, we propose a future-aware cognitive SemCom system named FAC-SemCom. In this system, large language models (LLMs) are first employed to generate enhanced quadruple datasets incorporating a time stability index, extending conventional KG datasets that consist of triples like (head, relation, tail) with future-oriented semantic information. A novel loss function is then defined by taking into account the temporal stability with future awareness during model training. In addition, a relation-sensitive classification transmission strategy is introduced to improve communication energy efficiency. To mitigate the errors introduced by this classification-based approach, an LLM-driven triple correction module is further designed to reduce transmission error rates and enhance semantic accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate that FAC-SemCom achieves approximately 45.2% higher transmission accuracy than baseline methods under low signal-to-noise ratio while significantly lowering total energy costs for large-scale triple transmission.

title: Beamwidth-Adaptive Reconfigurable Holographic Surfaces Enabled ISAC Systems.
abstract: The performance of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-based integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems is often constrained by the high power consumption of phase shifters and the complexity of spatial-domain waveform design. To address these challenges, we employ reconfigurable holographic surfaces (RHS), a type of metamaterial surface, as the transceiver antenna for MIMO-ISAC, eliminating the need for phase shifters. By leveraging the element-wise amplitude-tuning feature of RHS, we present a low-complexity RHS spatial-domain waveform design that directly generates multi-lobe beam patterns via a linear superposition of closed-form single-beam holographic beamformers. Moreover, the element-wise amplitude-tuning feature is also utilized to realize effective aperture tuning, yielding beam patterns with adaptive beamwidth and flat gain, which outperforms antenna arrays with a fixed aperture size. Based on this design, we develop a two-stage ISAC scheme enabled by a beamwidth-adaptive RHS, where the holographic and digital beamforming is jointly optimized for improved ISAC performance. Simulation results show that the proposed beamwidth-adaptive ISAC scheme achieves a higher weighted sum rate than schemes based on RHSs with a fixed beamwidth or phased arrays, given the same power consumption and sensing signal-to-noise ratio constraint.

title: OECaaS: Towards Serverless Computing for LEO Multi-Satellite On-Orbit Processing.
abstract: Fresh and high-quality satellite imagery is critical for applications such as disaster response, agricultural monitoring, and environmental observation. However, Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites face a severe downlink bottleneck, with only about 2% of acquired data typically transmitted to the ground, leading to significant resource waste. Existing onboard processing schemes often rely on static strategies that cannot adapt to dynamic fluctuations in computational capacity, energy availability, and image content. To address this limitation, this paper introduces OECaaS, a serverless computing-based scheduling system for multi-satellite on-orbit image processing. OECaaS decomposes tasks into fine-grained functions and employs an intelligent scheduler that dynamically selects suitable satellites, constructs optimized processing pipelines, and performs energy-adaptive task priority scheduling based on real-time resource states and task requirements. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that OECaaS achieves an average 61.2% improvement in task completion rate and reduces average task completion latency by 36.1% under the same energy constraints compared to existing baselines

title: Characterizing ISCI in Multi-carrier ISAC Systems over Doubly Dispersive Channel: Joint Sensing and Communication Performance Analysis.
abstract: This paper presents a systematic analysis of inter-symbol and inter-carrier interference (ISCI) modeling in doubly dispersive channels for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. We propose a generalized OFDM (Weyl-Heisenberg) framework to evaluate four ISCI treatment approaches: (1) explicit estimation and compensation, (2) complete ignorance, (3) uncorrelated colored noise approximation, and (4) correlated colored noise modeling. Through continuous delay-Doppler channel characterization, we derive LMMSE channel estimators and corresponding estimation errors (as sensing metrics) for both pilot-assisted and fully-known symbol scenarios. The communication performance is quantified via ergodic capacity bounds under imperfect CSI. Our theoretical analysis and numerical results reveal fundamental performance-complexity trade-offs, providing insights for practical ISAC waveform and receiver design in doubly dispersive channels.

title: Diffusion-Aided DRL for Joint Scheduling of Computing and Network Resources.
abstract: With the growing demand for low-latency and reliable processing, computing services are moving closer the network edge. However, existing scheduling frameworks focusing solely on either computing or network resources fail to achieve effective global coordination. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a diffusion-aided soft actor-critic (DASAC) algorithm for joint scheduling of computing and network resources. The approach leverages the powerful distribution modeling and generative capabilities of diffusion models to enhance policy generation in deep reinforcement learning (DRL). By employing multi-dimensional state modeling and a multi-head action output mechanism, the approach minimizes both network and computing loads under latency constraints, achieving collaborative scheduling and dynamic optimization of computing and network resources, thereby effectively ensuring overall quality of service (QoS). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms baseline methods in terms of average reward and task failure rate.

title: Topology-Aware Integrated Communication, Sensing, and Power Transfer for SAGIN.
abstract: The space-air-ground integrated network (SAGIN) has garnered significant attention in recent years due to its capability to extend communication networks from terrestrial environments to near-ground and space contexts. The application of SAGIN enables to achieve a high-quality, multi-functional, and complex communication requirements, which are essential for sixth-generation communication systems. This paper presents a topology aware (TA) framework to leverage the topological structure in SAGIN to address the multi-functional communication challenge, particularly the integrated sensing, communication, and power transfer (ISCPT) problem. To take advantage of the topological structure, we initially establish the topology according to the criteria of visibility and channel strength. The ISCPT problem can be reformulated into a topological structure as a mixed integer linear program, providing valuable insights from the objectives and constraints. Results demonstrate the superior performance of our solution compared to the benchmarks.

title: Terrain-Driven Uplink Localization in Mountainous Environments Based on Moving UAV Anchors.
abstract: In complex mountainous areas, global navigation satellite system (GNSS) signals suffer severe degradation due to multipath and non-line-of-sight propagation. Although unmanned aerial vehicles, as part of Non-terrestrial Networks, can enhance Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled emergency localization through line-of-sight connectivity, current approaches often neglect the influence of terrain on signal behavior in machine-type communication scenarios. To address this, we propose a Terrain-Driven Uplink Localization (TDUL) framework that integrates a high-fidelity channel model based on digital elevation models and ray tracing. By simulating 5G New Radio uplink, TDUL extracts terrain features and multipath characteristics to train a Terrain-Driven XGBoost (TD-XGBoost) model, which guides a particle filter using a Student’s t-distribution for robust outlier resistance. Simulation results show substantial performance gains over baseline methods across diverse altitudes and ranges, with cross-terrain evaluation demonstrating strong generalization.

title: Resilient Cell-Free Massive MIMO Networks.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel optimization framework for enhancing the security resilience of cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) networks with multi-antenna access points (APs) and protective partial zero-forcing (PPZF) under active eavesdropping. Based on the main principles of absorption, adaptation, and recovery, we formulate a security-aware resilience metric to quantify the system performance during and after a security outage. A multi-user service priority-aware power allocation problem is formulated to minimize the mean squared error (MSE) between real-time and desired security efficiency, thereby enabling a trade-off between the target user's secrecy performance and multi-user quality of service (QoS). To solve this non-convex problem, a security-aware iterative algorithm based on the successive convex approximation (SCA) is employed. The proposed algorithm determines the optimal power allocation strategy by balancing solution quality against recovery time. At each iteration, it evaluates the overall resilience score and selects the strategy that achieves the highest value. Simulation results confirm that the proposed framework significantly improves the resilience of CF-mMIMO networks, allowing flexible adaptation between rapid recovery and high-quality recovery, depending on system requirements.

title: On the Achievable Rates of Faster-than-Nyquist Signaling with Nyquist Receiver Sampling.
abstract: Faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling is a classic signaling scheme for improved spectral efficiency compared to the conventional Nyquist signaling at the cost of increased complexity. In this paper, we investigate the FTN transmission with Nyquist receiver sampling (a.k.a. FTN-NR transmission), in order to simplify the receiver processing. Particularly, we derive a closed-form expression on the achievable rates of the FTN-NR transmission with arbitrary shaping pulses and Gaussian constellations. Our analysis reveals that this achievable rate relates closely to both the folded spectrum and folded squared spectrum of the pulse, which incorporate the folding effect of the signal spectrum due to the receiver sampling. Furthermore, we prove that the achievable rate of FTN-NR transmission is no better than that of Nyquist signaling despite the pulse shapes, when Gaussian constellation is applied. However, we then provide a numerical study on the rate with finite-alphabet constellations, and verify that FTN-NR transmission can outperform Nyquist signaling in terms of the achievable rate, especially when the modulation order is low. Our numerical results confirm our conclusions and report a noticeable achievable rate improvement of the FTN-NR transmission compared to Nyquist signaling under QPSK signaling.

title: A Queuing Theory-based Dynamic Adaptive Energy Sustainability Algorithm in Battery-free Sensor Networks.
abstract: Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) technology enables the realization of Battery-free SWIPT-enabled Sensor Networks (BSSN). However, existing SWIPT energy efficiency optimization schemes typically rely on static traffic models, making them ill-suited for dynamic and large-scale network conditions. To this end, a Queuing Theory-based Dynamic Adaptive Energy Sustainability Algorithm (QT-DAES) is proposed. Specifically, the data transmission process of BSSN was modeled as an M/M/1/K queuing model based on queuing theory to capture its dynamic characteristics. Based on these characteristics, an energy efficiency optimization problem is formulated, which is proven to be a non-convex optimization problem. Finally, by adopting QT-DAES to address this optimization problem, the adaptability and scalability of BSSN in dynamic scenarios were significantly enhanced. Experimental results demonstrate that QT-DAES achieves rapid convergence, requiring only 5 iterations on average. Moreover, in high-load scenarios, QT-DAES achieves network throughput improvements of 37%, 57.1%, and 80.6% over DSNRA, MRMEE, and MTE-EHWSN respectively.

title: SemCast: One Representation Semantic Communication for Multi-task Receivers.
abstract: Traditional wireless transmission prioritizes bit-perfect transmission, wasting bandwidth on details irrelevant to downstream tasks. Existing semantic communication methods train task-specific encoders from scratch for each application or channel condition, limiting scalability and requiring extensive retraining. To overcome these limitations, we present SemCast, a semantic communication system that leverages frozen pretrained encoders to enable multi-task visual transmission over diverse wireless channels without task-specific encoding or retraining. A unified transmitted representation, extracted by a frozen Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) encoder via joint source–channel coding (JSCC), supports concurrent decoding for multiple tasks, including classification, object counting, attribute recognition, depth estimation, and segmentation. The transmitter employs a learned mapper with unequal error protection (UEP) to automatically prioritize task-critical feature dimensions. At the receiver, PRISM-Rx introduces a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and pilotless vector-quantized channel tokenization for blind adaptation to diverse channels without Channel State Information (CSI). JEPA’s masked prediction pretraining provides superior spatial and compositional representations for multi-task semantic communication compared to contrastive and pixel-reconstruction baselines. PRISM-Rx achieves near CSI-known performance without CSI, while achieving significantly lower latency than CSI-based approaches.

title: A Low-Complexity Receiver Design for Uplink ISAC.
abstract: Uplink integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems have recently emerged as a promising research direction, enabling simultaneous uplink signal detection and target sensing. In this paper, we propose the flexible projection (FP)-type receiver that unify the projection-type receiver and the successive interference cancellation (SIC)-type receiver by using a flexible tradeoff factor to adapt to dynamically changing uplink ISAC scenarios. With adjustable tradeoff factors, the FP-type receiver can balance the enhancement of the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) with the reduction of correlation in the reconstructed signal for communication signal detection. A homotopy optimization framework is first applied for the FP-type receiver with a fixed trade-off factor. This framework is then extended to develop the dynamic FP (DFP)-type receiver, which iteratively adjust the trade-off factor for improved algorithm performance. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed receiver designs is verified via simulations.

title: Experimental Integration of Quantum Key Distribution for Secure 5G Networks.
abstract: The rapid advancement of quantum computing fundamentally threatens 5G network security by undermining conventional public-key cryptography. This paper presents an experimental integration of quantum key distribution (QKD) into operational 5G environments. Through three representative use cases spanning midhaul, backhaul, and backbone segments, we deploy commercial QKD systems with ETSI-compliant key management interfaces to evaluate performance impacts on latency and throughput. Experimental results demonstrate that QKD-based encryption maintains the stringent low-latency and high-throughput requirements of 5G applications. The proposed quantum cryptography function further enables flexible application of QKD-generated keys to selective data flows, providing fine-grained security control. These findings validate the technical feasibility and operational practicality of QKD in realistic 5G settings, highlighting its crucial role in building future-proof, quantum-resistant communication infrastructures.

title: Multi-Tiered Shuffling with User Stratification for QoS-Stable DDoS Defense in Online Services.
abstract: Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks remain one of the most severe threats to online services. Moving Target Defense (MTD) [1] mitigates such attacks by frequently remapping clients to proxies through shuffling. However, existing shuffling strategies face a fundamental trade-off: accelerating attacker isolation often comes at the cost of degrading the Quality of Service (QoS) experienced by benign users. Most prior approaches emphasize isolation speed and effectiveness while neglecting the QoS impact during the shuffling process. To balance isolation speed and QoS, we propose a multi-tiered rapid isolation shuffling algorithm. The algorithm stratifies users based on multi-dimensional security scores and assigns them to corresponding proxy domains to access target services. In high-risk domains, a Score-Guided Rapid Isolation (SGRI) is applied to accelerate security score convergence and achieve faster attacker containment. We implement multiple shuffling strategies and conduct comprehensive comparisons in terms of defense effectiveness and QoS. Experimental results show that our method improves attacker isolation speed by over 40%, while maintaining QoS degradation within approximately 2%. This ensures that online services such as cloud gaming can sustain smooth and continuous user experiences even under DDoS attacks.

title: A Multi-agent Proximal Policy Optimization-Driven Resource Allocation in Cognitive Smart Cities.
abstract: With the rapid development of cognitive smart cities, the number of smart devices and communication demands has surged, making efficient resource allocation a core challenge. This paper proposes a multi-agent proximal policy optimization-based resource allocation (MAPRA) strategy. First, the resource allocation scenario in cognitive smart cities is modeled as a multi-agent system, where unauthorized communication devices (UCDs) are treated as independent agents that collaborate and compete to utilize the idle spectrum resources of cellular communication devices (CCDs). Each agent perceives local environmental information and makes decentralized decisions regarding channel selection and transmit power control. Second, to enhance coordination among agents and the stability of strategy learning, the MAPRA algorithm is improved by designing a hybrid reward mechanism that combines local throughput and global resource utilization, and by optimizing the agents’ state observation space to reduce redundant information. Experimental results demonstrate that the MAPRA algorithm outperforms comparison algorithms in system throughput, providing robust support for the efficient operation of cognitive smart cities.

title: Beyond Post-Hoc: A SHAP-Based Feature Selection Framework for High-Accuracy, Class-Aware Intrusion Detection.
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) has gained prominence in Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) to address the opacity of black-box models. However, existing efforts have largely confined XAI to post-hoc interpretability, with limited exploration of its potential for driving data refinement and model optimisation. To the best of our knowledge, SHAPRefine is the first model-agnostic feature selection framework that systematically integrates class-wise SHAP value aggregation with automated refinement to produce lightweight and high-performing IDS models. Unlike existing SHAP-based methods that repeatedly recompute Shapley values for each candidate subset—often requiring excessive retraining and parameter tuning—SHAPRefine introduces a performance-driven iterative selection strategy that minimizes redundant computations while explicitly accounting for minority-class contributions. Comprehensive evaluations across diverse IDS datasets and classifiers demonstrate that SHAPRefine consistently reduces feature dimensionality by up to 90%, cuts training time and energy consumption, and improves detection accuracy across all attack types, with F1-score gains of up to 95% for minority classes. These results establish SHAPRefine as a robust and resource-efficient solution for accurate IDS deployment in Beyond 5G (B5G) and 6G networks.

title: Joint Delay, Doppler, and Phase Noise Tracking for Distributed Inter-Satellite Synchronization.
abstract: Inter-satellite networks require tight synchronization to support coherent links, cooperative processing, and distributed beamforming.In low Earth orbit, fast relative motion causes perlink delay and Doppler to drift over a synchronization burst, while independent oscillators introduce relative phase noise.Limited link budgets further lead to sparse connectivity, so each receiver observes only a subset of neighboring links.We develop an OFDM pilot-based, motion-aware synchronization approach that jointly models propagation and oscillator impairments and links them to an SINR-type reliability metric.A unified frequency-domain observation model is derived in which delay, Doppler, and phase noise appear explicitly, and intra-symbol phase-noise leakage contributes a self-interference term in the despread pilot statistic.Coupled delay-Doppler dynamics yield an EKF-ready state-space model, and a two-stage tracker combining EKF updates, RTS smoothing, and Doppler compensation refines delay and phase estimates.Simulations show that the proposed processing improves delay and phase tracking across SINR, providing a consistent basis for synchronization under stochastic drift and sparse connectivity.

title: ASSENT: Learning-Based Association Optimization for Distributed Cell-Free ISAC.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is a key emerging 6G technology. Despite progress, ISAC still lacks scalable methods for joint AP clustering and user/target scheduling in distributed deployments under fronthaul limits. Moreover, existing ISAC solutions largely rely on centralized processing and full channel state information, limiting scalability. This paper addresses joint access point (AP) clustering, user and target scheduling, and AP mode selection in distributed cell-free ISAC systems operating with constrained fronthaul capacity. We formulate the problem as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) that jointly captures interference coupling, RF-chain limits, and sensing requirements, providing optimal but computationally demanding solutions. To enable real-time and scalable operation, we propose ASSENT (ASSociation and ENTity selection), a graph neural network (GNN) framework trained on MILP solutions to efficiently learn association and mode-selection policies directly from lightweight link statistics. Simulations show that ASSENT achieves near-optimal utility while accurately learning the underlying associations. Additionally, its single forward pass inference reduces decision latency compared to optimization-based methods. An open-source Python/PyTorch implementation with full datasets is provided to facilitate reproducible and extensible research in cell-free ISAC.

title: Domain Aware Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network and Multi-Head Attention based Modulation Classification.
abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is essential for spectrum awareness, cognitive radio, and electronic intelligence. While classical likelihood- and feature-based methods degrade under channel impairments, deep learning models, though powerful, often ignore domain knowledge and treat frames independently. We propose a Domain Aware Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-Head Attention (DSTCN–MHA) that integrates statistical signal features with learned temporal embeddings and aggregates multiple frames to emphasize informative segments. Two variants are introduced: a light model optimized for efficiency and a heavy model targeting accuracy. Experiments on the RML22.01A dataset show that even at K=1 frames, both models outperform CNN and ResNet baselines, while at K=6 they achieve over 20% gains at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and near-perfect accuracy above 10 dB, with significantly fewer parameters than prior models.

title: AoI-Aware Machine Learning for Constrained Multimodal Sensing-Aided Communications.
abstract: Using environmental sensory data can enhance communications beam training and reduce its overhead compared to conventional methods. However, the availability of fresh sensory data during inference may be limited due to sensing constraints or sensor failures, necessitating a realistic model for multimodal sensing. This paper proposes a joint multimodal sensing and beam prediction framework that operates under a constraint on the average sensing rate, i.e., how often fresh sensory data should be obtained. The proposed method combines deep reinforcement learning, i.e., a deep Q-network (DQN), with a neural network (NN)-based beam predictor. The DQN determines the sensing decisions, while the NN predicts the best beam from the codebook. To capture the effect of limited fresh data during inference, the age of information (AoI) is incorporated into the training of both the DQN and the beam predictor. Lyapunov optimization is employed to design a reward function that enforces the average sensing constraint. Simulation results on a real-world dataset show that AoI-aware training improves top-1 and top-3 inference accuracy by 44.16% and 52.96%, respectively, under a strict sensing constraint. The performance gain, however, diminishes as the sensing constraint is relaxed.

title: Bridging the Reality Gap in O-RAN Networks: Designing Robust RL-based xApps for Heterogeneous Real-World Deployments.
abstract: The deployment of Reinforcement Learning (RL) within the Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) framework promises to enable intelligent and adaptive control of network functions. However, the transition from simulation-based environments to real-world deployments introduces a significant reality gap that can compromise the effectiveness and robustness of RL-based xApps. This paper investigates the impact of real-world data heterogeneity on the performance of RL algorithms in the O-RAN Service Network. By analyzing two real deployment datasets collected from O-RAN–compliant testbeds based on OpenAirInterface (OAI) and srsRAN, we empirically quantify how discrepancies in data distributions and measurement scales create fundamental challenges for RL-based decision-making. To address this issue, we propose a data normalization and preprocessing strategy that enhances model generalization across heterogeneous environments. Results confirm that the approach aligns the OAI and srsRAN distributions, with PCA capturing 90.3% of the variance and a 0.05 Silhouette Score. This yields a platform-agnostic state-space-preserving protocol-level semantics, enabling portable RL xApp development across heterogeneous O-RAN deployments.

title: Predictable and Exposed: Eavesdropping and Exploitation of Positioning Reference Signals.
abstract: The Positioning Reference Signal (PRS) is a cornerstone of 5G New Radio localization, enabling precise timing and ranging. As PRS configurations parameters (e.g., timing, periodicity, and identifiers) are exchanged through encrypted control-plane messages, a lazy observer might reasonably assume that the positioning plane inherits the same level of protection. In reality, such confidence in control-plane encryption neglects what remains directly in plain sight at the physical layer. To demonstrate this point, we develop a PRS reconnaissance technique that learns key PRS configuration parameters by exploiting the deterministic and predictable scheduling of PRS slots, allowing an attacker to infer when and where positioning signals occur simply by observing the 5G spectrum. Using both simulations and real-world traces collected with commercial Software-Defined Radios (SDRs) (e.g., USRP B210) and open-source software, we explore the feasibility of multiple attack types, i.e. smart jamming, store-and-replay, and selective spoofing. Such attacks can bias time-of-arrival estimates or deny positioning service, even without altering communication KPIs. The root cause lies in the absence of PHY-layer integrity and unpredictability: current 5G protections secure only upper-layer signaling (NAS/RRC), leaving PRS transmissions exposed once on air. These results show that the design of reference signals for positioning (and likewise for sensing now under standardization) cannot rely solely on upper-layer encryption, yet security must be incorporated into the PHY and configuration mechanisms to prevent over-the-air reconnaissance and exploitation.

title: Auction-Based RIS Allocation With DRL: Controlling the Cost-Performance Trade-Off.
abstract: We study the allocation of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) in a multi-cell wireless network, where base stations compete for control of shared RIS units deployed at the cell edges. These RISs, provided by an independent operator, are dynamically leased to the highest bidder using a simultaneously ascending auction format. Each base station estimates the utility of acquiring additional RISs based on macroscopic channel parameters, enabling a scalable and low-overhead allocation mechanism. To optimize the bidding behavior, we integrate deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents that learn to maximize performance while adhering to budget constraints. Through simulations in clustered cell-edge environments, we demonstrate that reinforcement learning (RL)-based bidding significantly outperforms heuristic strategies, achieving optimal trade-offs between cost and spectral efficiency. Furthermore, we introduce a tunable parameter that governs the bidding aggressiveness of RL agents, enabling a flexible control of the trade-off between network performance and expenditure. Our results highlight the potential of combining auction-based allocation with adaptive RL mechanisms for efficient and fair utilization of RISs in next-generation wireless networks.

title: From Monitoring to Prediction: Hands-on Experience on Building a Cloud-Native Network Digital Twin for 5G Core.
A Source-Channel Tradeoff in Ultra-Low-Latency Edge Intelligent Sensing.
abstract: The upcoming 6G mobile network is set to extensively integrate edge artificial intelligence (AI) with integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), giving rise to the new paradigm known as edge intelligent sensing (EI-Sense). This paradigm leverages ubiquitous edge devices for environmental sensing while deploying AI algorithms on edge servers to interpret observations through remote inference on wirelessly uploaded features. A critical challenge in designing EI-Sense systems for 6G mission-critical applications lies in achieving high performance under stringent latency constraints. To address this, we focus on the end-to-end performance of EI-Sense and characterize a source-channel tradeoff in terms of source distortion and channel reliability. This work establishes a theoretical foundation for the source-channel tradeoff by quantifying the impact of source coding on feature discriminant gains and channel reliability on packet loss. We further validate our theoretical insights through experiments, demonstrating significant sensing performance improvements when optimizing this tradeoff compared to traditional reliability-centric approaches.

title: Toward UAV-Terrestrial BS Coordinated ISAC Transmission: Optimal Power Allocation and Trajectory Design.
Graph Reinforcement Learning based Resource Allocation Method in RIS-aided Heterogeneous IoV.
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS)-assisted vehicular networks entail formidable challenges in resource allocation due to Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) and Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communications. However, the heterogeneous roles of vehicles and the spatial correlations among network entities are often overlooked in resource allocation schemes, leading to unstable convergence and suboptimal decisions. To address these issues, we propose a Graph Neural Network (GNN)-enhanced Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) framework for joint optimization of power allocation, channel selection, and RIS phase configuration. A Graph Attention Network (GAT)-based encoder extracts topological dependencies and generates structured state representations for policy learning. Extensive simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The results show that GNN-TD3 achieves faster convergence, higher reward stability, and superior robustness across varying learning rates, vehicle densities, and transmission powers. Moreover, it significantly improves Age of Information (AoI) and V2V success probability, demonstrating strong adaptability to fine-grained heterogeneous vehicular environments.

title: Secure Storage Optimization: How to Deduplicate Multi-media Data without Dependent Server.
abstract: Deduplication for encrypted data is a good way to optimize the cloud storage with data privacy. However, it meets the challenges such as how to effectively and securely check large-scale similar encrypted data. In this work, we present a Secure Batch Fuzzy Deduplication (SBFD) for fast checking the similar data (i.e., redundant multi-media data) in encryption form. Moreover, our approach does not depend on any assistant servers to resist against the brute-force guessing attacks (inherent problem existed in conventional encrypted deduplication). Our work provides a methodology to achieve fast and secure duplicates check to realize secure storage optimization.

title: Performance Analysis of Data-Aided Sensing in Cellular ISAC Systems.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is recognized as one of the core objectives in sixth-generation (6G) networks. Compared to conventional reference signal (RS)-based sensing, data-aided sensing may enhance the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), but would also introduce undesirable inter-target interference. In this paper, we present a systematic performance analysis of the data-aided sensing scheme using stochastic geometric arguments. In particular, we demonstrate that the data-aided scheme can extend sensing coverage when the interference suppression capability is sufficient. In addition, when the number of users is large, we show that the inter-target interference can be viewed as emitted from an effective interference region. When the number of users is small, we show that the non-line-of-sight (NLoS) paths help improve the target detection performance.

title: Unseen Cost of Space Computing: Quantifying LEO Battery Aging via Physics-Driven Modeling.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations in the 6G era are evolving into intelligent in-orbit computational platforms, forming Space Computing Power Networks (SCPNs) to deliver global-scale computing services. However, the intensive computation within SCPN incurs a significant ``unseen cost'': the frequent charge-discharge cycles accelerate the physical degradation of satellites' life-limiting and high-cost batteries, thereby threatening the long-term operational viability of such a system. Existing approaches, often relying on indirect metrics like Depth of Discharge (DoD) and neglecting the complex, nonlinear degradation process of battery aging, fail to accurately quantify this cost. To address this, we introduce a high-fidelity, physics-driven model that quantitatively links computational workload parameters to the nonlinear battery degradation. Building on this model, we formulate a degradation-aware scheduling problem and analyze heuristic policies across different energy regimes. Simulations reveal that the optimal strategy should be adaptive: in solar-rich conditions, a myopic policy maximizing instantaneous solar utilization is superior, whereas under energy scarcity, a reactive policy leveraging real-time battery state significantly extends lifetime.

title: Bridging Theory and Practice: Linux Kernel Native Implementation of UBS-TBE for Industry 5.0.
abstract: The emergence of Industry 5.0 is transforming manufacturing, logistics, and automation, introducing highly interconnected smart factories and cyber-physical systems. These environments rely on real-time data exchange between sensors, controllers, and actuators, where delays or jitter can directly impact productivity, safety, and operational reliability. Consequently, ensuring low-latency and deterministic communication has become a fundamental requirement for modern industrial networks. While specialized hardware solutions exist to achieve predictable performance, the integration of time-sensitive mechanisms into widely used software platforms remains limited. Linux, as a flexible and widely deployed operating system, offers an ideal foundation for building practical solutions that can operate at the network edge, bridging the gap between theoretical scheduling algorithms and real-world deployment. In this paper, we present an Urgency-Based Scheduler (UBS) based on Token Bucket Emulation (TBE), implemented as a Linux kernel queuing discipline. By deploying this mechanism directly in Linux, we enable smart factory networks to maintain ultra-low latency and fair service across multiple industrial applications.

title: An Architectural Framework for Open and Interoperable Web 4.0 and Virtual Worlds.
abstract: Web 4.0 and virtual worlds represent a new stage in the evolution of the Internet toward open, interoperable, and user-centered digital ecosystems. This paper presents a structured architectural framework for Web 4.0, based on open standards, open source, and digital commons, and aligned with regulatory requirements. We present a layered reference architecture that unifies immersive applications, identity and trust services, interoperability middleware, open hardware infrastructures, and governance mechanisms into a single ecosystem. This framework systematically maps the five priority areas of the Virtual Worlds Partnership, identity management, software supply chain security, open hardware, decentralized alternatives to centralized platforms, and Virtual Worlds demonstrations, highlighting their cross-layer interactions. In addition, we define evaluation criteria and key performance indicators that connect architectural design choices to measurable technical, socio-economic, and regulatory outcomes. The proposed architecture offers a common baseline for early Web 4.0 demonstrations and interoperability-driven virtual worlds, supporting scalable, secure, and sustainable deployment.

title: Security Evaluations of Post-Quantum Cryptographic Primitives Against Quantum and AI-Based Attacks.
abstract: The emergence of quantum computing poses an existential threat to conventional cryptographic systems, prompting the development of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) based on quantum-resistant mathematical problems. However, the long-term security of these primitives remains uncertain, especially under realistic quantum and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven attack scenarios. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of the security of PQC primitives with a dual focus: (i) analyzing advances in quantum algorithms that target the underlying hardness assumptions of lattice-based, code-based, and other post-quantum schemes; and (ii) leveraging AI-based methodologies for identifying cryptographic vulnerabilities. We survey the current state of quantum cryptanalysis, propose a unified insights for evaluations. Our findings offer updated parameter recommendations and highlight both strengths and potential fragilities in leading PQC candidates. The results contribute actionable insights toward the design and standardization of resilient cryptographic systems for the post-quantum era.

title: OAM Shift Keying in LDPC-Coded Free-Space Optical Communication via Vision Mamba.
abstract: Orbital angular momentum shift keying (OAM-SK) encodes symbols as discrete vortex charges in free-space optical (FSO) links. However, atmospheric turbulence (AT) distorts ring structure and vortex cores, inducing inter-mode crosstalk and decoding errors. In this work, we address OAM-SK demodulation in a low-density parity-check (LDPC)-coded FSO link under turbulence with a Vision Mamba (Vim)-based decoder. The proposed Vim-based decoder adopts a selective state-space model architecture and performs bidirectional scans to aggregate context over long ranges without the ${\mathcal{O}}\left({{N^2}}\right)$ cost of attention. It uses input-gated state updates to adapt the effective kernel to local evidence. We identify that these mechanisms are well matched to AT-induced ring warping, core wandering, and orientation jitter. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed Vim-based decoder outperforms the Swin Transformer and a convolutional neural network baseline in symbol-decoding accuracy across the training, validation, and test sets, with the advantage becoming more pronounced as turbulence increases. When the predicted symbols feed the LDPC chain, the proposed Vim-based decoder can bring significant link-level performance gains in terms of lower bit error rate and higher peak signal-to-noise ratio across turbulence. Furthermore, the proposed Vim-based decoder improves accuracy and stability under turbulence while retaining linear time complexity.

title: Enhancing Hypernetwork Integration with VAE for Data Augmentation of Small Tabular Datasets.
abstract: We introduce VAE-HyperNetFusion, an innovative framework that integrates variational autoencoders (VAEs) with interpolation-based data augmentation to enhance hypernetwork training on small tabular datasets. Using VAE-HyperNetFusion we initially focused on a prostate cancer dataset to address the critical challenge of limited sample size by generating augmented data that substantially enriches the training environment for hypernetwork integration models. The hypernetwork adopts a multi-head design and generates the parameters of an ensemble of differentiable soft decision trees, improving training stability and reducing sensitivity to random initialization. Beyond the prostate cancer dataset study, we validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach on several published tabular datasets. It demonstrates that VAE-HyperNetFusion can be generalized and is robust across different domains. By incorporating VAE for data augmentation within the VAE-HyperNetFusion framework, the risk of overfitting, a common pitfall when handling small datasets, is substantially reduced through the introduction of a more diverse and enriched pool of training samples. This innovation extends the applicability of deep learning methods to problems traditionally dominated by shallow learning techniques, particularly in fields requiring precise and reliable analysis of limited data, such as medical diagnostics and personalized healthcare. Experimental results show that VAE-HyperNetFusion consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in small dataset settings highlighting its potential as an important advance in applying deep learning to tabular data with severe sample constraints. This work provides the deep learning community with a new approach for analyzing small tabular datasets and establishes a strong benchmark for future research.

title: Joint Resource Allocation and Beamforming for STAR-RIS-aided Multicast OAM systems.
abstract: This paper investigates orbital angular momentum (OAM) multicast transmissions aided by a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS). In dense networks, OAM mode orthogonality is easily compromised by transceiver misalignment, leading to severe inter-mode interference. To address this, we leverage STAR-RIS to provide full-space wavefront control, effectively compensating for misalignment and suppressing crosstalk. We formulate a weighted sum capacity (WSC) maximization problem and propose a joint resource allocation and beamforming algorithm. By applying Lagrange-dual and quadratic transform methods combined with semidefinite relaxation (SDR), the algorithm effectively coordinates active base station resources and passive STAR-RIS phase shifts. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed system significantly outperforms conventional MIMO and reflective RIS-aided benchmarks, particularly by restoring mode orthogonality in misaligned scenarios. Furthermore, the system achieves superior network energy efficiency, supporting next-generation green communication objectives.

title: Detection Performance Analysis of ISAC Systems with Practical Heavy-Tailed Clutter: A Bayesian Likelihood Ratio Perspective.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) aims to support both high-rate communication and high-precision sensing within a unified framework. Although considerable progress has been made to evaluate ISAC performance, most existing studies assume clutter-free or ideal Gaussian clutter environments. These assumptions fail to capture the heavy-tailed characteristics of real-world clutter and may lead to inaccurate performance assessments. To address this limitation, we model the clutter as a compound-Gaussian process that accounts for realistic amplitude fluctuations. Based on this model, a Bayesian likelihood ratio test (BLRT)-based detector is developed, and closed-form expressions for the detection probability (DP) and false alarm probability (FAP) are derived. In addition, we investigate the effect of input distribution parameters on the average sensing signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio (SCNR), a key metric for characterizing detection quality. Leveraging this relationship, we formulate a joint optimization of pilot power and symbol statistics to enhance sensing performance under communication rate constraints. Simulation results validate the theoretical analysis and the performance advantage over conventional Gaussian-based detectors.

title: QFMapNet: A Query-Based Temporal Fusion Network for Efficient Online Vectorized HD Map Construction.
abstract: Autonomous driving requires real-time high-precision semantic mapping, as high-definition maps provide accurate positioning and rich semantic information such as lane markings and road topology. Existing methods typically rely on multimodal sensors to construct vectorized maps in real time, but most are limited to single-frame processing, which reduces robustness in complex scenarios. In this paper, we propose QFMapNet, a simple yet effective temporal fusion network that leverages long-term temporal information for vectorized high-precision map construction. We introduce a lightweight Temporal Query Aggregation Module (TQAM) that incorporates historical contextual information to enhance current-frame predictions, thereby improving mapping accuracy. Experiments on the NuScenes dataset demonstrate that QFMapNet effectively exploits temporal information and achieves superior performance in semantic map construction tasks.

title: Collaborative Hierarchical Decision-making Framework for Multi-AUV Search and Hunt.
abstract: Multi-AUV (Autonomous Underwater Vehicle) systems are increasingly vital for complex maritime missions like cooperative searching and hunting. However, coordinating AUV swarms presents significant challenges in dynamic underwater environments characterized by constrained physics, turbulent currents, and imperfect communication networks. Many existing multi-agent reinforcement learning approaches overlook these complexities, leading to inefficient team collaboration, such as redundant target pursuit and suboptimal exploration patterns. To address these issues, we proposed the Collaborative Hierarchical Decision-making Framework (CHDF), a novel multi-agent hierarchical reinforcement learning approach. The framework decomposes the complex mission into a high-level strategic policy and two specialized, physics-aware low-level policies for searching and hunting. The high-level policy leverages a shared team knowledge base and action masking to enable effective role assignment and mitigate redundancy. Meanwhile, the low-level search policy uses the Age of Information (AoI) and knowledge of local currents to perform energy-efficient exploration. Simulation results validate the framework’s superior performance, showing marked improvements in overall mission execution and collaborative efficiency when compared to several baseline approaches.

title: Symbol Rate Maximization in Rolling-Shutter OCC: Design and Implementation Considerations.
abstract: Optical Camera Communication (OCC) systems can take advantage of the row-by-row scanning process of rolling-shutter cameras to capture the fast variations of light intensity coming from Visible Light Communication (VLC) LED-based transmitters. In order to study the maximum data rate that is feasible in such kind of OCC systems, this paper presents its equivalent digital communication system model in which the rolling-shutter camera is modeled as a rectangular matched-filter whose time width is equal to the exposure time of the camera, followed by a sampling process at the pixel row sweep rate of the camera. Based on the proposed rolling-shutter camera model, the maximum symbol rate that such OCC systems can support is experimentally demonstrated, and the impact of imperfect time synchronization between the VLC transmitter and the rolling-shutter OCC receiver is characterized in the form of Inter-Symbol Interference (ISI). The equivalent three-tap channel model that results from this process is experimentally validated and the generated ISI is compensated with the use of linear equalization in reception. Simulation and experimental results show a strong correlation between them, demonstrating that the proposed approach can be used to make the OCC system work at the Nyquist sampling rate, which is equivalent to the pixel row sweep rate of the rolling-shutter camera used in reception.

title: Ghost-LSNet: See Large, Focus Small for WLANs.
abstract: The Wi-Fi Alliance (WFA) has incorporated 4096-QAM into the 802.11be protocol, enabling Wi-Fi 7 to achieve a 20% increase in peak throughput over its predecessor. However, due to cost constraints, most chip vendors rely on Wiener-based channel estimators even as rising Modulation and Coding Scheme (MCS) indices demand far greater precision. Such methods are prone to channel estimation distortion caused by over-smoothing from fixed receptive fields, which is especially severe in deeply faded subcarriers.
