To address this, we propose Ghost-LSNet (GLSNet), a channel estimation algorithm tailored for Wi-Fi 7 receivers supporting 4096-QAM demodulation. Particularly, inspired by the "See Large, Focus Small" strategy of LSNet, which captures wide-context features using large kernels and refines local details via small-kernel aggregation, and Ghost-Net’s efficient convolution mechanism, we design a novel 1D convolutional architecture. Additionally, it adopts a separate training strategy for edge/central band to address edge band accuracy loss, another key cause of high-order MCS performance degradation. Simulation results under standard channel models show GLSNet outperforming Wiener-filter estimators and even state-of-the-art neural network-based methods, with substantially lower computational overhead.

title: AI Agent-Driven Client Selection and Pricing for Reliable D2D Computing Power Service in Wireless Computing Power Networks.
abstract: Device-to-Device (D2D)-assisted wireless computing power networks enhance overall system capability by leveraging idle computing resources from end-user devices. However, the highly mobility of these devices poses significant reliability challenges to edge computing service. Furthermore, as this service often occur among mutually untrusted devices, a critical challenge lies in designing effective incentives to motivate computing resource contribution while maintaining allocation efficiency. This paper propose a novel D2D wireless computing power network framework for reliable computing service by utilizing AI agent to joint design client selection and pricing scheme. Specifically, we first propose an AI agent-based framework for D2D-enabled wireless computing power networks. Subsequently, we design a reliability evaluation model and a dynamic pricing model for devices, integrating them into a joint optimization problem. Finally, by leveraging the deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm within the AI agent, we cooperatively optimize the client selection and resource pricing strategy, thereby ensuring service reliability while effectively incentivizing device participation in computing services. Simulation results demonstrate the significant effectiveness and performance improvement of the proposed scheme in reliable computing service environments.

title: Quantum Takes Flight: Two-Stage Resilient Topology Optimization for UAV Networks.
abstract: Next-generation Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) communication networks must maintain reliable connectivity under rapid topology changes, fluctuating link quality, and time-critical data exchange. Existing topology control methods rely on global optimization to produce a single optimal topology or involve high computational complexity, which limits adaptability in dynamic environments. This paper presents a two-stage quantum-assisted framework for efficient and resilient topology control in dynamic UAV networks by exploiting quantum parallelism to generate a set of high-quality and structurally diverse candidate topologies. In the offline stage, we formulate the problem as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model and leverage quantum annealing (QA) to parallelly sample multiple high-quality and structurally distinct topologies, providing a rich solution space for adaptive decision-making. In the online stage, a lightweight classical selection mechanism rapidly identifies the most suitable topology based on real-time link stability and channel conditions, substantially reducing the computation delay. The simulation results show that, compared to a single static optimal topology, the proposed framework improves performance retention by 6.6% in a 30-second dynamic window. Moreover, relative to the classic method, QA achieves an additional 5.15% reduction in objective value and a 28.3% increase in solution diversity. These findings demonstrate the potential of QA to enable fast and robust topology control for next-generation UAV communication networks.

title: Gambling Account Detection for Social Network Security.
Multi-Waveguide Pinching Antenna Placement Optimization for Rate Maximization.
abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) have emerged as a technology that enables the large-scale movement of antenna elements, offering significant potential for performance gains in next-generation wireless networks. This paper investigates the problem of maximizing the average per-user data rate by optimizing the antenna placement of a multi-waveguide PASS, subject to a stringent physical minimum spacing constraint. To address this complex challenge, which involves a coupled fractional objective and a non-convex constraint, we employ the fractional programming (FP) framework to transform the non-convex rate maximization problem into a more tractable one, and devise a projected gradient ascent (PGA)-based algorithm to iteratively solve the transformed problem. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed scheme significantly outperforms various geometric placement baselines, achieving superior per-user data rates by actively mitigating multi-user interference.

title: LLM-Aided UAV Anti-jamming Communications Based on Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL)-based unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) anti-jamming communication schemes optimize transmit power and channel, but have communication reliability degradation due to delayed feedback under dynamic environment. In this paper, we propose a large language model (LLM)-aided RL-based UAV anti-jamming communication scheme to optimize transmit power and channel based on the environmental features extracted by LLM including terrain layout and weather conditions that cause channel fading, as well as jamming features including the received jamming power and jammed channel. The risk function formulated based on the bit error rate (BER) and inference latency to avoid communication outage or even task failure. In addition, a long-short-term memory network is employed to predict channel variation based on the historical channel gain sequences to mitigate feedback delay in channel estimation. The proposed scheme is implemented based on a UAV and a control center running the 7-billion-parameter LLM, LLaVA, for detecting nets and kites on power lines. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme reduces BER and energy consumption and improves inference accuracy compared with the benchmarks.

title: RBS-UPSCA: Optimal Random Frequency Band Selection for Multi-Cell IoT Networks over Unlicensed Spectrum.
abstract: The optimization of frequency band selection of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in multi-cell IoT networks over an unlicensed spectrum is crucial for effectively supporting massive IoT devices but has yet to be closely studied. This paper investigates optimal random frequency band selection for a multi-cell IoT network operating on an unlicensed wideband and adopting ALOHA random access. Optimizing frequency band selection probabilities is a challenging, large-scale, non-convex problem. We propose a parallel iterative algorithm called RBS-PSCA to find the stationary points of the non-convex problem by using equivalent transformations and parallel successive convex approximation (PSCA). Additionally, we introduce a deep unrolling neural network for RBS-PSCA, named RBS-UPSCA, to optimize RBSPSCA’s algorithm parameters based on data samples to accelerate convergence and to leverage the parallelizable neural network architecture for efficient parallel computation. Numerical results confirm the significant benefits of RBS-PSCA and RBS-USCA in the average achievable rate and computation time.

title: Deep Learning-Based Cooperative UAV Detection With CPE-Assisted Sensing.
abstract: The rapid growth of the low-altitude economy (LAE) has intensified safety concerns caused by unauthorized unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), or black flights. Detecting such UAVs requires methods that are accurate, cost-effective, and capable of wide-area coverage. To address this need, we exploit fixed wireless access (FWA) customer premises equipment (CPEs), which are static, densely deployed, and can serve as wireless cameras for the radio environment. We propose a deep learning (DL)-based two-stage cooperative UAV intrusion detection framework that leverages uplink channel state information (CSI) from multiple base station (BS)-CPE pairs. In the first stage, neural networks analyze per-pair CSI to predict UAV presence. In the second stage, binary outputs are fused at a central server using a thresholding rule to declare UAV detection. This two-stage design minimizes transmission overhead between sensing nodes and the server while preserving substantial cooperative gains. Simulation results show that the proposed cooperative scheme significantly reduces the missed detection probability to 0.22%, well below the 3GPP 5% requirement, highlighting the effectiveness of CPE-assisted ISAC sensing for UAV monitoring in the LAE.

title: Resource-Efficient Large-Scale Service Placement with Online Adaptation in Vehicular Edge Networks.
abstract: The rapid proliferation of time-sensitive applications, exemplified by autonomous driving, imposes latency targets that exceed on-board and remote-cloud capabilities. Vehicular edge computing (VEC) mitigates these limits by moving computation to roadside units (RSU), yet system performance hinges on mobility-aware, module-level placement. Existing strategies typically assume small modules and static topologies, which is incompatible with large language model (LLM) services under high mobility and tight storage budgets. We address these gaps with a two-timescale framework that performs long-timescale deployment and replication of service modules at RSUs and short-timescale task routing and offloading, while explicitly accounting for resource budgets, latency constraints, and vehicle mobility. We introduce a composite quality-of-service (CQS) metric that balances deadline satisfaction with RSU compute utilization, and propose a decentralized Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Based RSU Module Placement Algorithm (MA-DMPA) in which each RSU learns from local observations, outputs storage-feasible binary placements for the next long slot, and coordinates implicitly via a shared global reward derived from CQS. Experiments on an urban RSU grid with varied density, storage, and mobility demonstrate that MA-DMPA approaches the quality of an exhaustive scheme while outperforming a game-theoretic baseline in end-to-end timeliness, resource utilization, and load fairness.

title: Planar Gaussian Splatting with Bilinear Spatial Transformer for Wireless Radiance Field Reconstruction.
abstract: Wireless radiance field (WRF) reconstruction aims to learn a continuous, queryable representation of radio frequency characteristics over 3D space and direction, from which specific quantities—such as the spatial power spectrum (SPS) at a receiver given a transmitter position—can be predicted. While Gaussian splatting (GS)-based method has surpassed Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF)-based method for this task, existing adaptations largely transplant vision pipelines, limiting physical interpretability and accuracy. We introduce BiSplat-WRF, a planar GS framework that retains the expressiveness of 3D GS while removing unnecessary projections and incorporating global EM coupling and mutual scattering among primitives. Each primitive is a 2D planar Gaussian with 3D coordinates, rendered directly on the angular domain of the SPS. A bilinear spatial transformer (BST) aggregates inter-primitive relations on an angular grid and, via attention, captures long-range electromagnetic dependencies, thereby enforcing globally aware EM interactions that reflect the complex physics of the wireless environment. On spatial spectrum synthesis task, BiSplat-WRF surpasses NeRF-based and prior GS-based baselines with respect to the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM); comprehensive ablation studies validate the contribution of BST. We also provide a larger BiSplat-WRF+ variant that further increases SSIM at a higher computation cost, serving as a strong reference for future studies.

title: Staleness-Control Semi-Asynchronous Satellite Federated Learning via Flexible Aggregation.
abstract: Satellite Federated Learning (SFL) has emerged as a viable approach for deploying distributed machine learning in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks, enabling timely processing of space-acquired data without the need to transmit raw data back to ground. However, in the constellations with ground-satellite links, intermittent visibility windows and Non-IID data distributions significantly exacerbate both the occurrence and negative impacts of staleness in semi-asynchronous SFL. Specifically, outdated local models uploaded by satellites may compromise convergence stability. To address these challenges, we propose a staleness-control semi-asynchronous SFL framework. By leveraging Lyapunov optimization, it maintains staleness below a predefined threshold while dynamically adjusting the number of fresh models aggregated per round, thereby maximizing communication window utilization and enhancing training efficiency. To further mitigate the impact of staleness, the staleness-aware weights are applied during aggregation. Additionally, a gradient compensation strategy is incorporated, which leverages historical models from non-updated satellites to mitigate the impact of Non-IID data. Experimental results on MNIST and CIFAR-10 show that our method speeds up training by 1.25× to 1.95× over baseline approaches.

title: Perceptual Audio-Visual Quality Assessment for Compressed Professionally-Generated Content: A New Dataset and An Effective Method.
abstract: With the rapid advancement of multimedia technologies, assessing the perceptual quality of audio–visual content has become increasingly important for ensuring users’ Quality of Experience (QoE). While Video Quality Assessment (VQA) has achieved remarkable progress, most methods focus solely on the visual modality. Deep learning-based Audio–Visual Quality Assessment (AVQA) addresses this limitation by modeling perceptual interactions between audio and video. However, existing datasets and methods mainly target Non-distinctive Source Content (NSC) or User-Generated Content (UGC) and may not generalize well to high-quality Professionally-Generated Content (PGC). To address this issue, we introduce PGC-AVQ, the first compressed PGC AVQA dataset annotated with Mean Opinion Scores (MOS), and propose a cross-attention-based effective AVQA method. Experiments on PGC-AVQ show that our method consistently outperforms existing baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness for perceptual quality prediction on professionally generated content. The dataset and code are publicly available at: https://github.com/Handvery/PGC-AVQ.

title: TTD3-Enhanced Reliable Downlink Communication in Multi-UAV Networks Supported by 6DMA-Assisted Symbiotic Radio.
abstract: Reliable communication in multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks faces challenges due to link gain fluctuations caused by UAV mobility and limited spectrum resources. To address these issues, we propose a multi-UAV network supported by six-dimensional movable antennas (6DMA)-assisted symbiotic radio (SR), in which a 6DMA-assisted UAV serves as an aerial auxiliary node. By flexibly adjusting their three-dimensional (3D) positions and orientations, 6DMA enables precise beam alignment and controllable signal reflection, thereby enhancing link stability and communication reliability. Meanwhile, SR technology facilitates efficient spectrum sharing and energy reuse, effectively alleviating spectrum scarcity and improving overall spectral efficiency. Based on this framework, a spectral efficiency maximization problem is formulated by jointly optimizing active/passive beamforming and 6DMA posture. To efficiently solve the resulting high-dimensional problem, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based twin-twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TTD3) algorithm is developed, which decomposes the task into beamforming and six-dimensional posture control subproblems. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms conventional baseline schemes in terms of spectral efficiency.

title: Movable-Antenna Array-Enhanced Energy-Efficient RSMA Communication Networks.
abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) are increasingly recognized as a promising technology for emerging next-generation communications due to their unique capability to dynamically adapt their positions and satisfy service demands. In this paper, we investigate an MA-enhanced rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) network, aiming to maximize overall energy efficiency through joint optimization of antenna positioning, data transmission, and repositioning durations, beamforming, and common-rate allocation under a shared-energy source and non-linear motor power model. Since the formulated problem is highly non-convex, we develop an alternating optimization-based framework to decouple the original design problem into three subproblems, which are addressed iteratively. Simulation results unveil that the proposed MA-enhanced RSMA system achieves significant energy efficiency gains over conventional fixed-position antenna networks and consistently outperforms all benchmarks.

title: Beam Prediction and Tracking for UAV Millimeter Wave Communications: Identify and Exploit Information from PID Controller.
abstract: In recent years, the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications have become an important part of the space-air-ground integrated network. However, the high mobility of UAV poses a great challenge in aligning narrow high-gain beams. To tackle this challenging issue, in this paper we propose efficient beam prediction and tracking solutions from the view of control. First, for an important and typical UAV flight mode in practice, i.e., the mission flight mode which assigns a series of targets in advance and then fly from one target to the next one in turn, we analyze in-depth the underlying control principle and reveal important properties and relationships between beam direction and controlled variables. To exploit the properties and relationships revealed, we further develop an efficient learning model, together with offline training and online inference algorithms. Simulation results from open-source software (including UAV environment) confirm the superiority of our control-assisted approach.

title: Theoretical Analysis for Control-Assisted UAV Millimeter Wave Communications.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications have been an important part of space-air-ground integrated networks, thanks to the flexible coverage and line-of-sight (LoS) propagation. But the goal of high-speed data transmission relies on efficient alignment of narrow high-gain beams between the UAV and base station (BS), which is highly challenging due to UAV mobility. To tackle this issue, the idea of control-assisted communications was recently proposed, where UAV-control signalling is exploited for efficient beam prediction and tracking. The developed approaches to date are heuristic, because no analytical framework exists to characterise the dependence of UAV beam direction variation on the parameters of control system. In this paper, we fill this gap by first deriving a model for beam direction dynamics, with control signal as model input. Then, we reveal theoretically how parameters like proportional gain of the control system affect the performance of beam tracking, by studying the rise time metric of the controller. We also analyze and reveal the important tradeoff between performance metrics for control and communications.

title: Dynamic DoF Allocation for Energy-Efficient ISAC via Element-Grouping Extremely Large-Scale IRS.
abstract: The convergence of high-throughput communications and high-precision sensing in sixth-generation (6G) networks is a key driver for Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) frameworks. A fundamental challenge in ISAC stems from a spatial trade-off: communication performance benefits from rich scattering and high spatial Degrees of Freedom (DoFs), whereas sensing often requires a dominant Line-of-Sight (LoS) path, treating non-target reflections as clutter. This paper proposes a novel element grouping-based extremely large-scale Intelligent Reflecting Surface (EG-XL-IRS) architecture to proactively manage this trade-off. The core idea involves strategically manipulating the inherent spatial DoFs of the IRS-reflected channel by partitioning its elements into groups, guided by statistical channel state information. This grouping enables the sensing channel to operate with lower effective DoFs while allocating higher DoFs to the communication link. We formulate a joint optimization problem to minimize the total transmit power at the ISAC base station (ISAC-BS) by co-designing the active beamformers and passive EG-XL-IRS phase shifts, subject to both communication signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) and sensing signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio (SCNR) constraints. To address this non-convex problem with coupled variables and constant modulus constraints, we develop a semidefinite relaxation (SDR)-based alternating optimization (AO) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves substantial energy efficiency gains with low resource overhead compared to benchmark methods, validating the efficacy of the EG-XL-IRS in harmonizing sensing and communication functionalities.

title: Resource and Trajectory Optimization for STAR-RIS Enhanced Secure UAV-MEC Systems.
FinGAN: An Interpretable RSS Generation Network for Scalable Fingerprint Localization.
abstract: This work introduces FinGAN, a robust received signal strength (RSS) data generator designed to expand RSS fingerprint datasets. Compared to existing generative adversarial models that either rely on known reference positions (RPs) or depend on predefined priors, FinGAN learns the latent information between RPs and RSS values by maximizing the mutual information between the generated RSS data and the RPs, enabling an end-to-end RSS generation directly from RPs. This allows us to accurately generate RSS data for previously unmeasured RPs. Both quantitative and qualitative evaluations demonstrate that FinGAN produces synthetic RSS data closely aligned with real RSS sample collected from the on-site experiment, preserving localization performance comparable to that achieved with complete real-world datasets. To further validate its generalizability, FinGAN is also trained and evaluated on open-source datasets from three typical office environments,and the results demonstrate consistent performance across different scenarios.

title: Movable Antenna Optimization for Multi-User MIMO Systems in Realistic Ray-Traced Propagation Environments.
abstract: To meet the growing data traffic demand in future wireless systems, novel transmission architectures capable of adapting to complex propagation environments are required. Movable antenna (MA) systems have recently emerged as a promising approach, enabling the physical repositioning of antenna elements to exploit spatial degrees of freedom. However, existing studies largely rely on idealized or simplistic channel models, leaving open the question of whether the performance gains of MA systems persist under realistic propagation conditions. This paper investigates the performance of downlink multi-user MIMO systems with movable antennas using deterministic ray-traced channel models. A simulation framework combining three-dimensional ray tracing and field-response channel modeling is developed, and antenna positions are optimized using particle swarm optimization and genetic algorithms. Simulation results reveal that while simplified distance-based channel models predict large performance disparities between competing array configurations, realistic ray-traced channels significantly compress these differences, indicating that propagation effects dominate over pure array geometry optimization. Nevertheless, movable antenna systems retain strong effectiveness over conventional fixed arrays across different user distributions, array sizes, and multipath conditions, even in geometry-constrained propagation environments.

title: Toward Interference Mitigation for Wi-Fi 8 Coordinated Beamforming in Multi-AP network.
abstract: Next-generation Wi-Fi 8 (IEEE 802.11bn) targets Ultra-High Reliability (UHR) by introducing Coordinated Beamforming (CoBF). In dense networks with many access points (APs), simultaneous downlink multi-user MIMO (MU-MIMO) transmissions from multiple APs can cause severe interference, both within a basic service set (intra-BSS) and between BSSs (inter-BSS). CoBF is envisioned to allow multiple APs to transmit concurrently without mitigated interference. This paper proposes a coordinated beamforming nulling strategy that completely cancels all intra-AP and inter-AP interference when sufficient spatial degrees of freedom are available. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed CoBF approach significantly mitigates interference and achieves substantial throughput gains in dense AP scenarios.

title: A Model Driven Optimization Toward Next-Generation Multi-AP Coordinated Spatial Reuse.
abstract: Wi-Fi 8 (IEEE 802.11bn) targets Ultra-High Reliability (UHR) by introducing a key technology - Coordinated Spatial Reuse (CoSR) passed in the TGbn motion list. In dense networks with many access points (APs), CoSR is envisioned to enable simultaneous Downlink (DL) transmissions for multiple APs. Hence, compared to the pre-UHR SR technology, CoSR is able to achieve reduction in frame deliver delay and increased throughput as a result of concurrent multi-AP DL transmission with moderately increased overhead. However, the optimization for CoSR is under-investigated for intelligent power control and network topology in terms of minimizing the interference and maximizing the network throughput in overlapping basic service set (OBSS). To this end, this paper firstly formulates a network throughput maximization problem to optimize the transmit power, constrained by network topology formed by following IEEE 802.11 DCF method. This problem is solved by the proposed block coordinate descent (BCD) with the corresponding improvised W-MMSE method that is of an optimized time complexity. The proposed methods are evaluated using a link-level simulator against the standard SR method and CoSR with maximum transmit power in terms of the network throughput, Jain’s index, time complexity, and the average number of active APs. The results demonstrates that the proposed CoSR outperforms the SR baseline by up to 63.64% in terms of network throughput.

title: Environment-Aware Path Loss Prediction Using Panoramic Images for Vehicular Communications.
abstract: The integration of communications and artificial intelligence is a key driver of the 6G evolution. Accurate channel prediction is fundamental to system design and optimization; however, traditional prediction approaches struggle to balance accuracy, efficiency, and generalization, making them insufficient for increasingly complex and dynamic 6G scenarios. The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, particularly computer vision, provides a promising pathway for intelligent channel prediction due to its zero spectrum cost, low deployment overhead, and mature algorithmic foundation. In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based path loss prediction model leveraging panoramic visual information for vehicle-to-infrastructure communication scenarios. We first conduct comprehensive channel measurements and environmental awareness in urban scenarios, building a multi-modal dataset comprising synchronized channel, panoramic image, and GPS data. Subsequently, a panoramic segmentation and depth estimation network is employed to extract environmental features, such as the location, scale, and distance of scatterers, from panoramic images. An enhanced ResNet-based architecture is then developed, jointly incorporating segmented and depth images, and transceiver geolocation data to predict path loss. Experimental results from both scenario self- and cross-validation demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high prediction accuracy and strong generalization. This study provides an effective and scalable framework for intelligent channel prediction in vehicular communication systems.

title: Spectrum-Efficient Ranging for Chirp-Based ISAC Systems with Triangle FMCW.
abstract: Chirp-based waveforms are emerging as a cornerstone for future Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems due to their robustness in the Delay-Doppler domain. However, achieving high-precision ranging in these systems traditionally requires increasing the signal bandwidth, which imposes a significant strain on the already scarce spectrum resources. To address this bottleneck, this paper proposes a novel signal processing technique that doubles the ranging resolution of triangle FMCW signals without occupying additional bandwidth. Unlike conventional methods that rely on bandwidth expansion, our design exploits the unique phase consistency observed in the beat signal effectively bridging the up-chirp and down-chirp segments. This approach allows for the extraction of finer delay information beyond the standard Fourier limit while maintaining a high spectral Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR). Theoretical analysis and model-based simulations validate that the proposed technique successfully breaks the conventional resolution barrier, offering a spectrum-efficient solution for high-accuracy sensing in bandwidth-constrained communication networks.

title: FedTGR: Topology-Guided Byzantine Robust Federated Learning for Trustworthy AI-Native RAN.
abstract: Open and disaggregated AI-native Radio Access Networks (RANs) increasingly rely on federated learning to support distributed intelligence across heterogeneous and potentially untrusted edge components. In such open settings, Byzantine or poisoned updates can compromise learned models and the reliability of model-driven network functions. Most existing defenses emphasize aggregation or cryptographic mechanisms, while overlooking how the participant coordination topology can be used to improve robustness. In this work, we present FedTGR, a topology-guided grouping overlay for standard server-client federated learning. FedTGR overlays a virtual topology at the server by grouping clients, performing group-level robust aggregation, and enforcing an ADMM-based two-tier consensus to suppress adversarial influence. Extensive experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 under typical poisoning attacks show that grouping improves test accuracy by about 20% on MNIST and 15% on CIFAR-10 on average. Even when paired with state-of-the-art robust aggregation rules, FedTGR consistently boosts accuracy and stabilizes convergence, demonstrating that topology-level programmability provides a practical trustworthiness layer for open, programmable AI-native RAN deployments.

title: DRL-MCR: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Multi-Modal Communication Routing Scheme for Multi-Domain Integrated Networks.
abstract: Next-generation networks envision ubiquitous multi-domain integrated networks, extending into challenging environments like remote ocean and deep-sea regions. To overcome the limitations of single-modal communication, the multi-modal communication emerges as a promising solution by leveraging the complementary strengths of diverse modalities such as radio frequency (RF), underwater acoustic communication (UAC), and optical wireless communication (OWC). However, conventional routing approaches designed for single-modal or homogeneous networks are inadequate to manage the network complexity. To address these challenges, we propose a deep reinforcement learning-based multi-modal communication routing (DRL-MCR) scheme for multi-domain integrated networks (MDINs). The DRL-MCR enables decentralized network nodes with decision-making capability through the trial-and-error learning process, to exploit multi-modal communication cooperation and learn the optimal routing policies for path and modality selections. Moreover, we design an algorithm that employs double deep Q-network, dueling network structure, and prioritized experience replay mechanism, to efficiently evaluate the value of routing actions, thereby improving decision-making effectiveness and learning convergence. The simulation results demonstrate the superiority of our proposed scheme compared with benchmarks in both latency and packet delivery ratio in various scenarios.

title: Leakage-Aware Sparse Subcarrier Allocation for AFDM-Based Integrated Sensing and Communications.
abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) provides a natural delay–Doppler (DD) representation for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC), but practical fractional delays and Doppler shifts destroy the ideal DD sparsity and induce structured leakage across the DD domain. This leakage degrades both the reliability of data detection and the sensing performance. This paper proposes a leakage-aware sparse subcarrier allocation strategy for AFDM-based ISAC systems. Instead of redesigning the waveform or suppressing leakage through complex processing, a deterministic on–off mask is applied in the subcarrier domain to activate only a subset of subcarriers for data transmission. Although allocation is performed in the subcarrier domain, it effectively reshapes the induced DD-domain coupling caused by fractional delay–Doppler effects. Simulation results show that the proposed allocation significantly improves bit error rate performance and enhances sensing robustness against leakage-induced sidelobes. The results further reveal an allocation-dependent communication–sensing trade-off, where sparser subcarrier activation suppresses leakage more effectively at the cost of reduced delay resolution.

title: Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation in Decentralized Networks.
abstract: Motivated by the increasing demand for data security in decentralized federated learning (FL) and stochastic optimization, we formulate and investigate the problem of information-theoretic decentralized secure aggregation (DSA). Specifically, we consider a network of K interconnected users, each holding a private input, representing, for example, local model updates in FL, who aim to simultaneously compute the sum of all inputs while satisfying the security requirement that no user, even when colluding with up to T others, learns anything beyond the intended sum. We characterize the optimal rate region, which specifies the minimum achievable communication and secret key rates for DSA. In particular, we show that to securely compute one bit of the desired input sum, each user must (i) transmit at least one bit to all other users, (ii) hold at least one bit of secret key, and (iii) all users must collectively hold no fewer than K−1 independent key bits. Our result establishes the fundamental performance limits of DSA and offers insights into the design of provably secure and communication-efficient protocols for distributed learning systems.

title: Fractional Doppler Shifts Channel Estimation for OTFS Systems Based on the Novel CBAM Network.
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation is a promising waveform for sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks, offering robustness to severe Doppler effects through its operation in the sparse delay-Doppler (DD) domain. However, fractional Doppler shifts inevitably arise in practical systems with finite bandwidth and signaling duration, causing channel energy leakage that fundamentally impairs DD domain sparsity. The resulting inter-Doppler interference (IDI) renders accurate channel estimation challenging, as the channel response fails to be directly resolved from received pilot symbols. To address the issue, this paper proposes a novel convolutional block attention module (CBAM) network that directly learns the DD domain channel response from pilot signals. By leveraging channel and spatial attention mechanisms, the proposed network enhances discriminative feature learning, improves sensitivity to fractional Doppler components, and effectively mitigates IDI. Furthermore, a post-estimation thresholding strategy is employed to extract delay and Doppler indices along with corresponding channel gains for signal detection. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed CBAM network significantly outperforms both the CNN and ResNet-CNN machine learning-based approaches, achieving approximately 1.5–3.8 dB normalized mean square error (NMSE) improvement at 30 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

title: Green Full-Duplex AF Cooperative Backscatter Framework with Closed-Form Time Allocation.
abstract: Backscatter communication (BackCom) enables ultra-low-power connectivity but suffers from short range and low data rates. Existing cooperative designs rely on decode-and-forward (DF) relays, incurring high energy costs for decoding and re-encoding, which limits performance under stringent energy budgets. This paper introduces a full-duplex amplify-and-forward (AF) relaying framework for multi-tag BackCom, incorporating constructive combining under phase misalignment and AF-forwarded noise, supported by a timing protocol and energy-aware models for backscattering, relaying, and onboard operations. We formulate two optimization problems: max-min fairness and sum-rate maximization, under energy causality constraints, which capture the trade-offs between fairness and system efficiency. Both are expressed as linear programs and solved analytically, yielding closed-form time allocations, a first for AF cooperative BackCom. Extensive simulations across varying transmit powers, tag distances, and energy budgets validate the framework, revealing up to 51% fairness-aware rate improvement and significant over 90% sum-rate gains over non-cooperative baselines. These results establish AF cooperative BackCom as a timely and energy-efficient solution for green IoT.

title: Channel Estimation in MIMO Systems Using Flow Matching Models.
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems require efficient and accurate channel estimation with low pilot overhead to unlock their full potential for high spectral and energy efficiency. While deep generative models have emerged as a powerful foundation for the channel estimation task, the existing approaches using diffusion-based and score-based models suffer from high computational runtime due to their stochastic and many-step iterative sampling. In this paper, we introduce a flow matching-based channel estimator to overcome this limitation. The proposed channel estimator is based on a deep neural network trained to learn the velocity field of wireless channels, which we then integrate into a plug-and-play proximal gradient descent (PnP-PGD) framework. Simulation results reveal that our formulated approach consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) generative model-based estimators, achieves up to 49 times faster inference at test time, and reduces up to 20 times peak graphics processing unit (GPU) memory usage. Our code and models are publicly available to support reproducible research.

title: Edge-Cloud Pulse Diagnosis Platform: Automated Diagnosis through Mechanized Sampling and Deep Time Series Modelling.
abstract: With the rapid aging of populations and the increasing burden of chronic diseases, scalable and objective tools for early health risk assessment are urgently needed. In this paper, we present an end-to-end, non-invasive pulse diagnostic system that integrates force-controlled robotic palpation, a high-fidelity sensing front end, and a time-series classifier built from a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) encoder followed by an attention-enhanced long short-term memory (Att-LSTM) network. The automated pipeline identifies clinically significant radial pulse patterns without manual intervention. Based on a mechanized palpation platform, we simulated around 6000 high-resolution radial artery pulse recordings based on correlations of pulse patterns summarized from years of clinical research. This dataset was then divided into training, validation and test sets. The proposed method achieves 97.56% test accuracy and demonstrates consistently high precision and recall across ten pulse classes. These findings validate the feasibility of combining traditional palpation with modern machine-learning techniques and highlight the platform’s potential as an objective, scalable screening tool for chronic disease risk assessment.

title: Adaptive Split Federated Learning in Space-Ground Integrated Networks.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) in space-ground integrated networks (SGINs) enables global Internet of things (IoT) devices to access data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) services while preserving privacy. In this paradigm, space-layer devices (e.g., satellites) aggregate locally trained models from ground-layer IoT devices to construct a global model. However, the limited and time-varying computational resources of IoT devices significantly hinder efficient FL. To overcome this challenge, we propose an adaptive split FL framework for SGINs. The framework dynamically profiles device-level computational capacity and partitions the AI model into a device-side sub-model executed locally and a server-side sub-model offloaded to the cloud. Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites relay intermediate data between IoT devices and cloud-enabled ground stations, enabling collaborative sub-model training. A long-term optimization problem is further formulated to minimize total training delay through joint optimization of model splitting, spectrum allocation, and satellite access. To tackle the mixed-integer nonlinear programming problem with time-varying constraints, we reformulate it as a Markov decision process and solve it using deep reinforcement learning with proximal policy optimization. Numerical results validate the superiority of the proposed framework.

title: Stability-Aware Task Offloading for UAV-Assisted Vehicular Edge Computing via Lyapunov-Guided Attention-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: This paper proposes a collaborative offloading paradigm in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-assisted Roadside Unit (RSU)-enabled Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) scenarios. To address the challenge of long-term task queue stability, we propose a Lyapunov-guided Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework. The original delay minimization problem is transformed into per-slot decision-making subproblems. Then, the Multi-Head Attention mechanism is integrated into the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm to learn optimal offloading strategies between RSUs and UAVs. Simulation results demonstrate that under the queue stability constraints, our proposed Lyapunov-guided Attention-based SAC (LA-SAC) algorithm achieves superior performance in key metrics compared to other DRL baseline methods.

title: Cross-Domain Incremental Modulation Recognition with Virtual-Class Contrastive Learning.
abstract: Effective recognition of newly emerging modulation types in cross-domain scenarios is essential for intelligent wireless systems. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for cross-domain class-incremental modulation recognition by learning a robust and separable feature space. In the base-training session, we first introduce a virtual class generalization module that simulates unseen modulation classes from different domains to proactively allocate feature-space capacity. Then, we integrate contrastive learning on both original and virtual samples to learn more compact and discriminative feature representations. Finally, we combine the learned backbone with an analytic incremental classifier to sustain recognition of both newly introduced and previously learned classes. Simulation results show that our method outperforms existing approaches in recognizing both new and previously learned classes and effectively alleviates catastrophic forgetting.

title: Beamforming for Multiuser LEO Satellite Communications with Irregular Tiled Array.
abstract: Due to the large aperture and low grating lobe of irregular tiled array (ITA), we consider the beamforming design for multiuser low earth orbit satellite communications (SatComs) with ITA. We partition the entire ITA into multiple identical super arrays, where each super array is composed of a few subarrays. To maximize the total sum-rate of Sat-Coms, we propose an ITA and beamforming alternating optimization (IBAO) scheme. Specifically, we transform the sumrate maximization problem into a weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) problem, thereby obtaining a closed-form solution for the beamforming design. Subsequently, the binary conversion matrix is introduced to model the subarray layout. For each super array, we relax the binary conversion matrix into continuous variables, which are then optimized within the WMMSE problem. The alternating optimization is iteratively performed between the continuous conversion matrix and beamforming matrix until the convergence. Finally, the binary conversion matrix is recovered via integer programming, which approximates the continuous solution by selecting feasible subarrays from a predefined set. Simulation results show that the IBAO scheme can significantly reduce hardware costs while maintaining competitive SatComs performance.

title: Hermit: A Flow-Collaborative Transport Scheme for Multi-Source Video On-Demand Streaming.
abstract: Today's fast-growing Video-on-Demand (VoD) service needs efficient content delivery to guarantee the user experience. To reduce costs, the industry has been exploring the adoption of unstable, heterogeneous, low-performance edge nodes as cost-efficient alternatives to expensive CDN servers. To compensate for the resulting degradation in user experience, Multi-source Parallel Downloading (MPD) is becoming a new VoD transport paradigm. However, existing transport optimization solutions face performance obstacles when applied to the MPD scenarios. They cannot handle the contention between MPD flows of the same download task, which is likely to occur at the shared last-hop, and lack the ability to quickly adapt to the unstable network environments brought by dynamic, heterogeneous, and low-performance edge nodes. To fill this gap, we propose Hermit, a VoD-oriented MPD transport algorithm. Hermit (1) continuously monitors the state of the flows and makes timely scheduling decisions, and (2) efficiently coordinates across the flows to mitigate self-contention at the shared last hop. As a client-driven scheme, Hermit does not require cumbersome coordination among edge nodes, nor does it increase server complexity. Through extensive experiments on real-world large-scale testbed and locally emulated network conditions, we demonstrate that Hermit can improve the consistent downloading rate by 9.2% to 21.3%.

title: Beyond Clustering: A Hybrid Framework for Target Generation in Sparse IPv6 Networks.
abstract: Over-reliance on clustering causes existing IPv6 scanning methods to fail in sparse regions, creating a biased, incomplete view of the Internet. This paper introduces HGen, a hybrid framework that moves beyond this single-paradigm dependency by synergistically combining mechanisms for broad generalization, isolated seed activation, and deep exploitation. Experiments show HGen outperforms state-of-the-art methods across all sparse scenarios, achieving 3.4x the Autonomous System coverage and more than doubling the discovery efficiency of the best baseline in seedless regions. A large-scale scan of sparse ASes validated HGen’s real-world impact, cutting seedless ASes by over 60%, expanding known hosts more than fivefold, and enhancing asset diversity. Our work delivers a crucial methodological supplement for IPv6 mapping and a vital, bias-corrected dataset for the research community.

title: Lightweight Radio Resource Swapping for Max-Min Fair Allocation in URLLC Systems.
abstract: Ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC) demands resource allocation strategies that balance reliability with computational efficiency. Existing theoretically optimal methods suffer from prohibitive complexity for real-time deployments, while heuristic alternatives remain computationally demanding for large-scale systems. This paper proposes a swapping-based framework that exploits temporal channel correlation and frequency selectivity to distribute allocation overhead across time and frequency domains. The approach selects a limited subset of bottleneck resources, establishes their exchange priorities based on channel quality metrics, and performs selective swaps to enhance user performance. Our evaluation using real-world industrial channel measurements demonstrates that the proposed method achieves comparable reliability to legacy approaches while reducing allocation time by orders of magnitude, with computational complexity that scales gracefully across varying system scales.

title: Secure Bandwidth Allocation via Weighted Nash Equilibrium subject to Geometric-Consistency Constraints in UASNs.
abstract: This paper addresses resource-allocation imbalance in underwater acoustic sensor networks (UASNs) caused by malicious nodes spoofing channel information. We propose a collaborative framework that integrates topology reconstruction with Weighted Nash Equilibrium (WNE)-based bandwidth allocation. At its core is a two-stage approach that first applies channel reciprocity verification for preliminary screening and then performs incremental geometric reconstruction with a mean-squared-error (MSE) closure metric to adaptively identify and exclude malicious nodes. The subsequent bandwidth allocation leverages the detection results to set per-node trust weights for WNE, thereby aligning security with efficiency. Simulations and field trials over time-varying underwater acoustic channels demonstrate robust suppression of malicious behavior and stable topology, while achieving a favorable fairness–throughput trade-off.

title: Time Scaling Effect Analysis and Sensing Algorithm Design for AFDM-based ISAC Systems.
abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) has been treated as a promising candidate waveform for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, particularly in high-mobility scenarios. Although the time scaling effect (TSE) is often neglected in AFDM-based sensing of high-velocity targets, this work demonstrates its significant impact on high-precision range and velocity estimation. To this end, we first derive the theoretical estimation errors of range and velocity for AFDM-based sensing under the conventional TSE-negligible scenarios, where the target’s motion within the coherent processing interval (CPI) does not exceed one range resolution. Based on the derived errors, we show that even when target motion is confined within 0.1 range resolution cell during the CPI, the resulting range and velocity estimation errors can still reach meter and meter-per-second levels, respectively. To achieve precise parameter estimation under TSE, we then propose a low-complexity method based on the phase compensation. Simulation results validate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed estimator.

title: Ambiguity Function Analysis and Sensing Algorithm Design for ODDM-based Multi-user Downlink ISAC Systems.
abstract: In orthogonal delay-Doppler (DD) division multiplexing (ODDM)-based multi-user (MU) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, the statistical properties of ODDM’s ambiguity function differ from the traditional point-to-point (P2P) or single user case due to DD-domain resource allocation among user equipments (UEs) within an ISAC frame, which may consequently influence its sensing performance. To this end, this paper analyzes the expected ambiguity function (EAF) of the ODDM waveform under MU downlink transmissions to evaluate its sensing performance in this context. Unlike the traditional EAF analysis for the P2P scenario, which assumes i.i.d. information symbols and uniform power allocation over DD resource elements, we derive a closed-form expression of ODDM’s EAF for the MU downlink scenario that accounts for variations in constellation diagrams and power levels across those resource elements. Based on this expression, we find that high sidelobes occur in ODDM’s EAF for the MU downlink transmissions. The locations of these sidelobes depend on the DD-domain multiple-access pattern and resource allocation granularity, while their levels are determined by power fluctuations across DD resource elements. To mitigate the false detections caused by these high sidelobes, we propose a CLEAN-based sensing scheme that reduces the complexity of accurate delay-Doppler estimation via Fourier coefficient interpolation. Simulation results confirm the theoretical analysis and the considerable performance of the proposed sensing scheme.

title: AFDM Channel Estimation with Chirped FMCW.
abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is a promising waveform for doubly selective channels because it can efficiently handle Doppler effects and achieve full diversity. Reliable AFDM, however, requires accurate channel estimation. Existing AFDM estimators typically employ guard-banded pilots or superimposed pilots in the affine domain, which either reduce spectral efficiency or incur high receiver complexity. This paper proposes a novel frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW)-assisted channel estimation framework for AFDM. An FMCW pilot is superimposed on the time-domain signal prior to the AFDM post-chirp operation in the inverse discrete affine Fourier transform, eliminating guard intervals and improving spectral efficiency. At the receiver, after the standard AFDM post-chirp dechirping step, FMCW dechirping and reshaping produce a radar-like delay–Doppler response (DDR). A one-dimensional DFT across slow time localizes each path in a unique column, from which delay, Doppler, and complex gain are estimated using low-complexity processing. Analysis characterizes the effective affine-domain pilot structure, the resulting complexity reduction, and the data-to-pilot interference statistics. Also, our simulation results show that the proposed method achieves comparable normalized mean square error (NMSE) and bit-error-rate (BER) performance relative to conventional MMSE estimators while reducing complexity significantly.

title: A Novel One-tap Equalizer for Zero-Padded AFDM System over Doubly Selective Channels.
abstract: Recently, affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) has gained traction as a robust solution for doubly selective channels. In this paper, we present a novel low-complexity one-tap equalizer for zero-padded AFDM (ZP-AFDM) systems. We first select the AFDM parameters, c1and c2, such that c1has a relatively high value, and c2depends on c1, which simplifies the affine domain input-output relation (IOR). This selection also demonstrates that a phase term that varies slowly along the affine domain is experienced by all affine domain symbols and this variation is significantly slower compared to that experienced by the time domain symbols over doubly selective channels. To simplify the equalization, we then introduce zero padding to the transmitted affine domain symbols and reconstruction operation on the received affine domain symbols. By doing so, we convert the effective affine domain IOR of our ZP-AFDM system to be characterized using approximately circular convolution. Next, we transform the resulting affine domain symbols into a new domain called the frequency-of-affine (FoA) domain. We propose our one-tap equalizer in this FoA domain to efficiently recover the transmitted symbols. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed one-tap equalizer, particularly when c1is high, without compromising performance robustness.

title: Performance Optimization of Semantic Communication for Users with Dynamically Evolving Knowledge.
abstract: This paper develops a dynamically evolving knowledge-based semantic communication framework, where the base station (BS) and users possess continuously updating multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) to keep up with the evolving knowledge. In the investigated framework, a BS extracts semantic information based on its own MLLM, and transmits it to the users, who process the received semantic information according to their own MLLMs. Here, the MLLM of the BS is constantly updated to keep up with the newest knowledge. In each transmission period, the BS uses the adaptive low rank method (AdaLoRA) to decompose the updated parameters of MLLM and transmits important parameters to the users. Due to the limited wireless resources, the BS must transmit an appropriate size of semantic information and parameters for each user. We formulate this problem as an optimization problem aimed at maximizing the MLLM synchronization metric (MSM). To solve this problem, we introduce a hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) algorithm to allocate resource blocks (RBs) for the users and subsequently transmit semantic information along with updated parameters to the users. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework can improve the MSM by up to 1.36x compared to the framework without parameter transmission.

title: Decentralized AI Service Placement, Selection and Routing in Mobile Networks.
abstract: The rapid development and usage of large-scale AI models by mobile users will dominate the traffic load in future communication networks. The advent of AI technology also facilitates a decentralized AI ecosystem where small organizations or even individuals can host AI services. In such scenarios, AI service (models) placement, selection, and request routing decisions are tightly coupled, posing a challenging yet fundamental tradeoff between service quality and service latency, especially when considering user mobility. Existing solutions for related problems in mobile edge computing (MEC) and data-intensive networks fall short due to restrictive assumptions about network structure or user mobility. To bridge this gap, we propose a decentralized framework that jointly optimizes AI service placement, selection, and request routing. In the proposed framework, we use traffic tunneling to support user mobility without costly AI service migrations. To consider nonlinear queueing delays, we formulate a non-convex problem to optimize the tradeoff between service quality and the end-to-end latency. We derive the node-level KKT conditions and develop a decentralized Frank–Wolfe algorithm with a novel messaging protocol. Numerical evaluations are used to validate the proposed approach and show substantial performance improvements over existing methods.

title: REVQA: Resource-Efficient MLLM Video Question Answering via Redundant Frame Elimination.
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) extend LLMs by incorporating visual inputs as extra tokens, enabling open-world visual understanding. However, MLLMs encounter serious challenges when visual inputs shift from a single image to a long video, because the massive video tokens may exceed the maximum capacity. Existing solutions typically adopt uniform frame sampling over the long video sequence and feed the frames into the vision encoder as visual inputs, which inevitably introduces redundant frames that are irrelevant to Video Question Answering (VideoQA) tasks, causing excessive waste of inference resources. To address these important challenges, we propose REVQA, a novel Resource-Efficient MLLM VideoQA system via redundant frame elimination, which enables efficient inference by identifying and filtering frames irrelevant to VideoQA tasks before feeding them into MLLMs. Specifically, we first construct a state representation for each frame to record both static attributes and dynamic variations. Next, based on the frame states, user queries, and annotated answer intervals from datasets, we design a redundancy-aware frame selection strategy that performs adaptive frame filtering before uniform sampling. Then, we encode the semantic information of the filtered frames into compressed representations. Finally, we fine-tune MLLMs with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to mitigate potential semantic loss caused by frame elimination. Extensive experiments across multiple MLLMs and VideoQA benchmarks demonstrate that REVQA reduces the average inference latency by 36.20% while maintaining comparable task accuracy with a slight performance drop of only 0.02.

title: TSRO: Traffic-aware Slicing for Resource-efficient DNN Offloading in Multi-edge Systems.
abstract: Network slicing enables customized resource allocation for Deep Neural Network (DNN) inference offloading systems, improving resource efficiency and profits for Edge Service Providers (ESPs). However, the variable and fluctuating traffic patterns across multiple edges and the heterogeneous resource costs of executing inference seriously hinder its widespread adoption. Existing solutions commonly depend on pre-defined configurations or historical patterns, making them less effective in handling the dynamic nature of multi-edge environments, causing degraded QoS and inefficient allocation. To address these important challenges, we propose TSRO, a novel Traffic-aware Slicing framework for Resource-efficient DNN Offloading in multi-edge systems. Specifically, we first incorporate a self-attention-based predictor that learns temporal traffic variations across different edge regions. Next, an adaptive slicing policy with randomized rounding is designed to flexibly reallocate resources. Finally, we design an enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) based optimization framework that leverages dual distillation to accelerate policy learning. Extensive experiments using real-world inference traces validate the superiority of TSRO. The results show that TSRO improves ESP profits, which outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across various scenarios.

title: GEO-Coordinated Service Handover Across LEO Satellites Using Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Frequent service handover is inevitable in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, as the rapid movement of LEO satellites limits their visibility duration to ground users. The dynamic and time-varying topology further complicates the maintenance of seamless service continuity and balanced resource utilization. In view of this, we propose a geostationary orbit (GEO)-coordinated service handover scheme, where GEO satellites, remaining stationary relative to ground users, leverage their continuous and comprehensive visibility to make handover decisions among LEO satellites. A multi-agent deep reinforcement learning-based approach is developed to jointly optimize satellite selection and load distribution. Furthermore, service caching and resource backfill mechanisms are introduced to minimize service interruption and improve resource efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves lower handover latency, better load balance, and higher resource satisfaction compared with baseline methods.

title: Towards Flexible Sensing Ranges: A Novel Framework for OTFS-Based ISAC System.
abstract: Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) waveform, owing to its ability to jointly process communication symbols and sensing parameters in the Delay-Doppler (DD) domain, has recently emerged as a prominent candidate for the next-generation wireless (6G) systems. However, existing OTFS-ISAC systems suffer from a fixed sensing range, due to the doubled delay and Doppler, the paths of sensing echoes can easily fall outside this boundary compared to that of communication. To address this issue, in this paper, a novel framework for flexible sensing ranges in OTFS-based ISAC systems is proposed. This framework adaptively finds a suitable DD domain grid by adjusting the OTFS frame configuration to accommodate dynamic environments. Firstly, we analyze the statistics of MF outputs and design the threshold for the out-of-range target detection. Then, different sensing ranges are achieved by processing the transmitted and received signals with different subcarrier/time slot pairs. Based on this, the overall sensing coverage of the OTFS-ISAC system is extended by iterating through the possible OTFS frame configurations to locate the in-range targets. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through simulations.

title: Spatially Non-Stationary Channel Estimation for XL-RIS-Aided MIMO Systems.
Broadcast Confidential Messages With FASs: Fundamental Limits and Two-Timescale Design.
abstract: With the unprecedented capability of configuring antenna positions, fluid antenna systems (FASs) have been recognized as a key enabler for secure communications. However, it is challenging to optimize the secrecy rate by reconfiguring positions of fluid antennas based on the fast-changing instantaneous channel state information (CSI). Considering the effectiveness of regularized zero-forcing (RZF) and zero-forcing (ZF) precoding in mitigating information leakage in physical layer security, we propose a two-timescale design to maximize ergodic secrecy sum rate (ESSR), where only the statistical CSI is utilized for the port selection of FASs. For that purpose, we first derive the analytical expression for the ESSR of FASs with RZF/ZF precoding by utilizing random matrix theory (RMT). Then, based on the evaluation results, we propose a two-timescale algorithm to maximize the ESSR by optimizing both port selection of FASs and regularization factor of RZF. Numerical simulations validate the accuracy of the proposed ESSR evaluation and show that the proposed two-timescale design could improve the ESSR performance significantly when compared with the uniform port selection.

title: TPFed: A Threshold-Free and Privacy-Preserving Defense for Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training while preserving data privacy, but it remains vulnerable to poisoning attacks. Existing clustering-based defenses under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) settings often rely on assumptions about malicious client ratios, while their scoring mechanisms inadequately capture gradient characteristics and auxiliary datasets raise privacy concerns. To address these challenges, we propose TPFed, a defense framework that introduces a new client scoring mechanism and leverages clustering to transform the non-IID scenario into an approximately IID setting, thereby enhancing the separability between benign and malicious clients. In addition, we integrate secure multi-party computation (SMC) to preserve privacy and design a dynamic reference update mechanism to enhance adaptability to client distribution shifts while mitigating overfitting. Experimental results demonstrate that TPFed achieves strong robustness against representative poisoning attacks in complex FL scenarios.

title: Optimal Minimum Distance-Based Precoders Towards Reliable RSMA Transmission with Joint Detection.
abstract: Recent research identifies Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) as a potential technology for massive connectivity, which enhances the capacity region of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channels with linear precoding. Nevertheless, enhancing the system reliability of RSMA using linear precoding remains an open research problem. To fill this gap, we first employ a joint detection (JD) receiver to replace the conventional successive interference cancellation (SIC) receiver, providing theoretically optimal maximum likelihood (ML) symbol detection. To this end, we formulate a reliability-enhancing optimization problem based on the minimum Euclidean distance of the received constellation to assist linear precoding in improving bit error rate (BER) performance with JD receiver. Considering a practical OFDM-RSMA system, we propose a successive spatial-frequency optimization algorithm by decomposing it across individual subcarriers for separate precoding design. After solving each subproblem via semi-definite programming (SDP), the closed-form solution for optimal power allocation on each subcarrier can be derived. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed minimum distance-based precoder is effective in enhancing the reliability of the RSMA system, achieving a lower BER for RSMA compared to conventional SIC receivers.

title: Holographic Cell-Free MIMO: A Cost-Efficient Paradigm with Low-Complexity Precoding.
abstract: To meet the stringent performance requirements of sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks, cell-free multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) has emerged as a promising paradigm, improving user experience but incurring substantial hardware cost. To address this issue, in this paper, we propose a holographic cell-free MIMO network, where multiple reconfigurable holographic surface (RHS)-enabled APs cooperatively serve UEs in a user-centric manner. To avoid the high computational complexity of large-scale user-centric cooperation, a low-complexity distributed coherent joint transmission (CJT) scheme is developed, in which each AP performs precoding independently using local channel state information, while CJT among multiple APs is achieved via lightweight interAP information exchange and phase compensation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed network significantly improves cost efficiency compared with conventional networks, while achieving a sum rate close to that of conventional phase-array cell-free MIMO. Moreover, the proposed distributed CJT scheme attains sum-rate performance comparable to the high-complexity centralized CJT scheme.

title: Reflections over the Sea: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for Maritime Self-Powered Communications.
abstract: Maritime communication is becoming a vital component of 6G networks, driven by the rapid expansion of the maritime economy. However, existing technologies face critical challenges in signal coverage, availability, and robustness, especially under harsh sea conditions. This paper proposes a novel framework for the maritime Internet-of-Things (IoT) communications that leverages the reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) mounted on offshore infrastructures, such as wind turbines, to enhance coverage and reliability. To capture dynamic maritime environment, a near-ocean-surface channel model is developed considering the impact of sea waves. In addition, a wave energy harvesting (EH) system is designed to self-power IoT sensors for data acquisition, processing, and transmission. To support real-time adaptation, channel state information is continuously measured to optimize RIS reflection parameters and maximize multi-user communication rates. Simulation results show that the proposed system significantly improves IoT communication performance by over 20%, under harsh sea conditions.

title: Differential Space-Time Block Coded Generalized Spatial Modulation: Design and Low-Complexity Detection.
abstract: In this contribution, a novel differential space–time block coded generalized spatial modulation (D-STBC-GSM) scheme is proposed, which integrates space–time block coding into the differential multi-generalized spatial modulation (D-MGSM) framework in order to exploit transmit diversity while preserving flexible system configurations. Such a non-coherent and low-complexity transmission paradigm is particularly appealing for emerging upper mid-band (7–24 GHz) 6G deployments, where rapid channel variations and hardware constraints render accurate channel state information acquisition increasingly challenging. To improve the reliability of frame-based differential detection, a power allocation strategy is further developed to reinforce the reference symbols within each transmission frame. Moreover, a low-complexity detection algorithm is devised by exploiting the inherent orthogonality of the embedded Alamouti structure, achieving near-maximum-likelihood performance with substantially reduced computational complexity. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed D-STBC-GSM scheme consistently outperforms conventional D-MGSM and other differential spatial modulation schemes in terms of bit error rate performance.

title: Accelerate Symbol-Level Precoding Using Tensor Equivariant Neural Network.
abstract: Although Symbol-level precoding (SLP) based on constructive interference (CI) exploitation offers significant performance gains, it is limited by high computational complexity. To address this, we propose a deep learning method with low inference complexity for the CI-constrained signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) balancing problem, leveraging the structure of the optimal solution in the closed-form and its inherent tensor equivariance (TE). First, building upon the optimality condition of the computationally efficient non-negative least squares (NNLS) form, we construct a mapping from the problem formulation to the solution and prove its TE, based on which the designed networks reveal specific parameter-sharing patterns that deliver low computational complexity. Utilizing this inherent property, we develop a lightweight TE neural network (TENN) that incorporates an attention mechanism. Simulation results show that the proposed method retains much of the optimal SLP gains, delivers about 80-times speedup over the conventional method in the typical scenario, and exhibits strong generalization across user numbers and symbol block lengths.

title: Joint Resource Allocation and Active/Passive Beamforming Optimizations Over Integrated Sensing and Symbiotic Radio Networks Using RIS-MIMO.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel joint resource allocation and active/passive beamforming optimization scheme over integrated sensing and symbiotic radio (ISASR) networks equipped with reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) and MIMO techniques. For our considered ISASR networks, a full-duplex (FD) base station (BS) communicates with a multi-antenna user and simultaneously senses multiple internet-of-things devices (IoTDs) with the aid of IoTDs’ equipped RISs. Moreover, each IoTD modulates its own data on the incident signals sent by the BS and passively backscatters its own data to the user with the aid of its RIS. Hence, in our proposed ISASR networks, RISs can not only enhance the performance of target sensing, but also improve the performance of passive backscatter communication. First, we formulate a system throughput maximization problem that jointly optimizes the BS’s throughput and all IoTDs’ throughput, subject to the sensing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and communication constraints. Second, leveraging deep reinforcement learning (DRL), we develop a joint optimization scheme for BS’s active beamforming, RISs’ phase shifts (i.e., passive beamforming), power allocation, and time scheduling to balance the performance of communication and sensing. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the superior convergence, stability, and communication and sensing performance of our developed scheme over the existing baseline schemes.

title: Over-the-Air Federated Compressive Learning with Privacy-Amplified Learnable One-Bit Updates.
abstract: Over-the-air federated learning reduces uplink latency by exploiting waveform superposition, yet high-precision updates strain bandwidth and leak magnitude information. Although one-bit quantization of updates is communication-efficient, it suffers from post-hoc mismatch between learned update directions and the transmitted signs. This work presents PLOFCL, an over-the-air federated compressive learning framework that communicates learnable one-bit updates and removes server-side reconstruction. Each client trains a two-stage compressive learning model, and binarization is enforced per coordinate with a gradient surrogate during local training. Privacy is amplified by single-shot local privatization that clips updates with a scale matched to the quantization range and adds Gaussian noise before discarding magnitudes. Theoretical analysis and experiments show that PLOFCL achieves substantially lower communication cost while maintaining competitive accuracy and reporting lower privacy budgets under the f-differential private framework.

title: MA-Aided Hierarchical Hybrid Beamforming for Multi-User Wideband Beam Squint Mitigation.
abstract: In wideband near-field arrays, frequency-dependent array responses cause wavefronts at different frequencies to deviate from that at the center frequency, producing beam squint and degrading multi-user performance. True-time-delay (TTD) circuits can realign the frequency dependence but require large delay ranges and intricate calibration, limiting scalability. Another line of work explores one- and two-dimensional array geometries, including linear, circular, and concentric circular, that exhibit distinct broadband behaviors such as different beam-squint sensitivities and focusing characteristics. These observations motivate adapting the array layout to enable wideband-friendly focusing and enhance multi-user performance without TTD networks. We propose a movable antenna (MA) aided architecture based on hierarchical sub-connected hybrid beamforming (HSC-HBF) in which antennas are grouped into tiles and only the tile centers are repositioned, providing slow geometric degrees of freedom that emulate TTD-like broadband focusing while keeping hardware and optimization complexity low. We show that the steering vector is inherently frequency dependent and that reconfiguring tile locations improves broadband focusing. Simulations across wideband near-field scenarios demonstrate robust squint suppression and consistent gains over fixed-layout arrays, achieving up to 5\% higher sum rate, with the maximum improvement exceeding 140\%.

title: Fairness-Oriented Strategies for Video Streaming Competition in Shared Network Environments.
abstract: In recent years, the rapid growth in HTTP-based video services has increased bandwidth competition among multiple streaming players in the same LAN. Although Adaptive Bitrate Algorithms (ABRs) are designed to optimize user experience, our observations indicate that they often lead to significant disparities in user experience and cannot coexist fairly in shared network environments.In this paper, we present a regulation mechanism named ABC, which runs as a web service without requiring any modifications to existing DASH servers or video players. To ensure coexistence fairness, ABC adopts a dual-constraint mechanism that enforces bandwidth allocation through transport-layer rate limiting and application-layer ABR guidance, while being aware of each client’s ABR algorithm. We deploy ABC in a network where five popular ABR algorithms coexist and compare it with the state-of-the-art client-side solution FESTIVE, server-side solution Minerva, and network-assisted solution CANE. The results show that ABC improves fairness by 71.11% and reduces time consumption more effectively than all other solutions.

title: LLSC: End-to-End Image Semantic Communication Framework for Low-Light Scenarios.
