abstract: Transmitting images captured under low-light conditions suffers from dual degradation: intrinsic quality loss from poor illumination and extrinsic impairments from bandwidth-limited channels. This paper presents a novel end-to-end semantic communication framework explicitly designed for low-light visual recovery, which jointly optimizes semantic feature extraction, channel transmission, and perceptual reconstruction. The proposed system employs Retinex-based decomposition to extract illumination and reflectance as semantic representations, followed by a content-adaptive pyramid encoder that hierarchically captures multi-scale features across four levels with cross-scale interaction modules. A progressive decoder reconstructs enhanced images through Feature Pyramid Network-inspired fusion and learnable gamma correction. Experiments on the LISU dataset demonstrate superior performance over conventional sequential training approaches, achieving over 30% LPIPS improvement across both AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels, alongside 7% MS-SSIM gains.

title: Design Insights into Partition Placement and Routing for DNN Inference in Multi-Hop Edge Networks.
abstract: Partitioned DNN inference is a promising approach for latency-sensitive edge intelligence, since it enables different parts of a model to be executed across end devices, edge servers, and the cloud. In multi-hop edge networks, however, partition placement and inference traffic routing are inherently coupled: raw inputs, intermediate features, and final outputs may have different sizes, while candidate nodes also differ in computation capability and may experience congestion under load. In this paper, we study fixed-partition DNN inference over heterogeneous multi-hop edge networks, where each partition is placed at exactly one node without replication. We formulate a mixed discrete-continuous optimization problem that jointly captures routing and execution costs, and develop a practical alternating framework that couples partition placement with congestion-aware forwarding updates. Numerical results show that split flexibility is especially important in IoT-edge-cloud settings, while congestion-aware refinement becomes more beneficial as the offered load increases.

title: A Parallel Routing and No-Wait Scheduling Method for Time-Sensitive Networking.
abstract: Routing and no-wait scheduling (RnS) are essential for managing time-triggered (TT) flows in time-sensitive networking (TSN). However, previous work formulated RnS optimization problems with a lot of constraints portraying conflicts between the frames of different TT flows and developed algorithms that required long running times or exhibited low success rates in finding feasible points. This paper aims to design an efficient and effective algorithm for RnS in TSN. We propose a new integer linear programming (ILP) formulation for the RnS problem. In this formulation, whether a frame uses a timeslot on a link is characterized by an indicator variable, and frame conflicts at a timeslot on a link are delineated by a summation of indicator variables. Our ILP formulation not only involves fewer variables and constraints in the scenarios with a large number of flows but also exhibits a decomposition structure. We apply the continuous relaxation and dual decomposition methods to solve our ILP problem and subsequently propose a parallel iterative optimization algorithm that can converge to a dual optimal point and return an optimal integer point of the original ILP problem. We also devise a greedy algorithm to find a feasible point close to an optimal point within a finite number of iterations. Numerical results confirm that our method can achieve shorter running times, 100% success rates, and lower bandwidth consumption than the previous RnS algorithms for TSN.

title: Active Channel Sparsification for FDD Massive MIMO: A Graph Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: While massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) promises high data rates and link reliability, the massive number of antennas introduces critical challenges in downlink (DL) channel estimation and precoding, especially in frequency-division duplex (FDD) systems, due to the lack of instantaneous channel reciprocity. Going beyond compressed sensing-aided approaches, active channel sparsification (ACS) has emerged as a promising candidate to realize joint DL channel estimation and precoding with limited pilot budget, relaxing the reliance of the level of channel sparsity. However, the complex combinatorial optimization problem inherent in the ACS methodology incurs prohibitive computational costs, hindering itself from potential practical deployment. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel ACS-GRL framework to produce sparsified channel representation via a bipartite graph neural network (GNN) architecture together with deep reinforcement learning (DRL). As such, leveraging second-order channel statistics, the proposed ACS-GRL framework generates a sparsifying pre-beamforming matrix that maps the multiuser channels to a sparsified one, which can be estimated effectively with a limited DL pilot budget, and at the same time yields sparsifying DL precoding vectors to maximize the effective multiplexing gain. Preliminary experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed scheme over the existing ACS methods in improving the sum rate performance.

title: Joint Network Slicing and Destination Guaranteed Trajectory Design for UAV Communications.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications effectively enhance network slicing, especially for the coexistence of enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB), ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC), and massive machine-type communications (mMTC). In this paper, the network slicing bandwidth allocation and destination-guaranteed UAV trajectory are jointly optimized to maximize the eMBB throughput while satisfying the URLLC latency and mMTC connectivity requirements. A deep deterministic policy gradient-based algorithm is developed. Specifically, the reward design front-loads the energy depletion penalty in time to ensure that the UAV reaches the destination area before energy depletion. In addition, as the user positions and the number of arriving URLLC packets are included in the state, the trained model can be deployed for any new environments without retraining, enabling strong scalability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm, with reduced computational complexity, achieves even higher eMBB throughput than the greedy algorithm with exhaustive search, and attains 7%–26% improvement over the other benchmark algorithms.

title: Waveform Design for DCO-OFDM with Null-space Sensing Signal in Optical Wireless ISAC.
abstract: Optical wireless integrated sensing and communication (OW-ISAC) is emerging as a complementary and enhancing paradigm to its radio-frequency counterpart. However, integrating both functionalities often degrades communication performance to enhance sensing precision. In this paper, a novel OW-ISAC scheme based on direct-current-biased optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (DCO-OFDM) is presented, which embeds a sensing signal into the channel null space. Subsequently, an optimization problem is formulated to enhance the sensing performance while ensuring the spectral efficiency for communication simultaneously. Then, the non-convex optimization problem is decoupled into subproblems for power allocation and sensing signal design. Moreover, an iterative method is developed, employing the minorization-maximization algorithm, which transforms the waveform design into a solvable second-order cone programming problem. Numerical results demonstrate the convergence of the algorithm and illustrate the trade-off between sensing precision and communication efficiency.

title: Semantic-Aware Co-Design of Spatio-Temporal Focusing and Adaptive Modulation for Wearable Brain-Body Neuro-Interfaces.
abstract: This paper presents a communication-theoretic, semantic-aware co-design for a wearable brain-body neuro-interface that addresses the dynamic somatic dysregulation in Major Depressive Disorder. At the physical layer, we derive an analytical spatio-temporal focusing model for temporal interference (TI) stimulation using a multilayer spherical head formulation. Closed-form envelope metrics enable efficient optimization of focusing gain and mainlobe-to-sidelobe ratio (MSR) under scalp-current safety constraints, yielding a library of high-precision stimulation actions. At the MAC layer, wearable biosignals are abstracted into semantic channel state information, and adaptive modulation is cast as a Markov decision process with energy/safety-aware rewards; the optimal policy is obtained by value iteration. Analytical and simulation results show that the proposed co-design sustains high MSR at deep targets with phase-locked steering, improves long-term therapeutic reward versus static or myopic baselines, and shortens the time to a desired "Calm" state, with multiplicative benefits over isolated layer designs.

title: Efficient Deep Learning-Based mmWave Positioning Through Ray-Tracing Method.
abstract: Deep learning-based positioning methods, known for their ability to process rich scatter signals in complex scenarios, present advantages over conventional methods. However, to achieve accurate positioning for the neural network, a large amount of training data is required, which is very time-consuming and high cost to collect. To address this, our work leverages ray-tracing techniques for efficient channel modeling and real dataset collection. In this paper, we present a practical and scalable alternative, a ray-tracing–driven data generation pipeline combined with a deep-CNN estimator and an SNR-aware multi-resolution grid refinement stage. By utilizing a 3D model of the actual environment, we adopt the ray-tracing method to accurately calculate path information, which is then used to model millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channels and generate received signals for user equipment (UEs) as training data. This efficient approach eliminates the need for physical relocation of UEs and extensive on-site data collection, significantly enhancing the practicality and applicability of deep learning-based positioning techniques. Additionally, we refine the neural network’s coarse positioning results with a grid search technique to further enhance accuracy. Simulation results show that the proposed ray-tracing-based method achieves sub-meter-level positioning precision, even in changing environments, validating the effectiveness of the proposed ray-tracing method for data generation.

title: Joint Optimization of Role Switching and Trajectory Planning for Multi-UAV Assisted Uplink Secure Communications.
abstract: As an aerial base station, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) offer significant potential to enhance terrestrial communications due to their flexible on-demand deployment, enabling rapid and reliable line-of-sight (LoS) wireless connectivity. This paper investigates a multi-UAV-assisted uplink wireless communication network under eavesdropping threats with location uncertainty. The proposed system enhances operational sustainability through energy replenishment stations while introducing multi-role UAVs capable of dynamic role-switching among three functions: communication reception, friendly jamming, and energy replenishment. To maximize worst-case secrecy capacity, we formulate a joint optimization problem encompassing UAV role-switching decisions, power allocation, and trajectory planning. By decomposing this multi-variable optimization problem into tractable subproblems, we derive a globally optimal solution through an iterative framework based on block coordinate descent (BCD) and successive convex approximation (SCA). Simulation results confirm that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing benchmarks in improving secrecy capacity.

title: Exploitating the Wavenumber-Domain MlSO Channel with Uniform Linear Array.
abstract: As sixth-generation (6G) networks move toward higher carrier frequencies and larger antenna apertures, wireless systems increasingly operate in the near-field, demanding a physically consistent model that explicitly highlights the wavenumber-domain channel characteristics. In this paper, we establish an analytical wavenumber-domain channel modeling for multiple-input single-output (MISO) transmissions based on the Weyl expansion. Our model reveals that the effective channel coefficients of uniform linear arrays (ULAs) can be derived as a one-dimensional integral with respect to the zeroth-order Hankel function of the first kind in the wavenumber-domain. This modeling allows us to exploit the channel characteristics directly in the wavenumber-domain. Particularly, we derive the wavenumber-domain expression of multiuser interference, whose value is sensitive to the wavenumber-domain aliasing due to the presence of the Dirichlet kernel. The asymptotical orthogonality condition that eliminates the aliasing is then derived, which requires the antenna spacing is no larger than half of the wavelength. The avoidance of wavenumber-domain aliasing can significantly reduce the multiuser interference (MUI) and improve the communication performance, which is explicitly verified by our numerical results under the same aperture size and transmit power.

title: ISAC-Enabled Multi-UAV and USV Collaborative System for Maritime Inspection.
abstract: This paper investigates a maritime inspection system enabled by the cooperation of an unmanned surface vehicle (USV) and multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) under an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework. UAVs perform target sensing while maintaining communication links with a USV that provides edge computing support. We consider two design objectives: (i) fairness—maximizing the minimum sensing mutual information (MI) across targets, and (ii) throughput—maximizing the sum MI over all targets. The trajectories of the UAVs and the USV, together with UAV transmit power, are jointly designed subject to communication, obstacle avoidance, and inter-UAV interference constraints. To address the fairness and MI maximization problems, we propose an alternating optimization algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate the trade-off between sensing fairness and the maximization.

title: Low-Complexity Frequency-Domain Successive-Interference-Cancellation Equalization for OTFS.
abstract: Frequency-domain (FD) pilot-based channel estimation and equalization are widely adopted due to their implementation efficiency, but their performance degrades in doubly selective channels. In this paper, we propose an FD-based pilot insertion and successive-interference-cancellation equalization framework with an adaptive-length equalizer that dynamically adjusts its effective span according to the channel delay-Doppler characteristics. By exploiting the banded (localized) structure of the FD channel matrix, the proposed method avoids unnecessary equalizer expansion in benign conditions while retaining sufficient degrees of freedom in severe time-frequency dispersion. A low-complexity criterion is developed to determine the equalizer length without requiring full channel knowledge. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive equalizer achieves near-optimal error-rate performance with significantly reduced computational complexity compared to conventional FD equalizers, making it particularly suitable for high-mobility and real-time communication scenarios.

title: Semantic Sensing: A Task-Oriented Paradigm.
abstract: Sensing and communication are fundamental enablers of next-generation networks. While communication technologies have advanced significantly, sensing remains limited to conventional parameter estimation and is far from fully explored. Motivated by this, we propose a novel concept of semantic sensing (SemS), which exploits physical channel samples to extract advanced semantic information, such as target classification and mobility patterns, beyond the traditional parameter-based data, such as channel state information. Specifically, we introduce a semantic sensing paradigm grounded in the information bottleneck (IB) principle to optimize both information acquisition and interpretation for task-oriented sensing. To this end, we develop a deep learning–based optimization framework that jointly designs transmit waveform parameters and receiver representations. The framework is implemented in an OFDM system, where the semantic encoder is implemented through a multilayer perceptron (MLP)-based pilot pattern optimizer, and the semantic decoder is implemented using a lightweight residual network (ResNet) backbone. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed semantic pilot design achieves superior task accuracy and robustness compared to reconstruction-based baselines, particularly under constrained resource budgets.

title: HCBQ: A Hierarchical Clustering-and-Branching Deep Q-Learning Framework for User Scheduling in Cell-Free MU-MIMO Systems.
abstract: Cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) has emerged as a pivotal candidate for 6G wireless networks, driven by its capacity to substantially enhance spectral efficiency, link reliability, and user fairness. In the emerging hierarchical cell-free radio access network (CF-RAN) architecture, the user-centric distributed unit (UCDU) must jointly schedule users associated with multiple edge distributed units (EDUs). However, the resulting inter-user spatial correlation and partial EDU associations lead to a prohibitively large state and action space, making conventional discrete-action deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approaches infeasible. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hierarchical clustering-and-branching deep Q-learning framework, referred to as HCBQ, to enable scalable user scheduling and balance spectral efficiency-fairness trade-off. The proposed framework first employs a clustering-based user pre-grouping module to compress the state representation by exploiting user channel correlation, and then utilizes a branching dueling Q-network agent to decompose the combinatorial scheduling action into parallel sub-decisions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed HCBQ scheduler achieves superior scalability and a better trade-off between system spectral efficiency and fairness compared with conventional baselines such as round robin, max-rate, and proportional fair, as well as advanced DRL methods including TD3 and SAC-KNN.

title: PACE: Predictive and Adaptive Multimodal Cache Enhancement for Cross-Modal Task Chains.
abstract: With the rapid rise of Agentic AI, multimodal generative tasks are increasingly executed through task chains—pipelines of functionally independent yet data-correlated models collaborating to fulfill complex cross-modal requests. However, the isolated execution of these models prevents effective cache sharing, leading to redundant storage and repeated inference, which severely limits end-to-end system efficiency. We present Predictive and Adaptive multimodal Caching Enhancement (PACE), a unified caching framework designed to address cache inefficiency in multimodal task chains. PACE employs a PatchTST-based predictive model to estimate cache entry reuse probability by jointly analyzing request semantics, task attributes, and historical access patterns. This predictive insight drives a value-guided online policy for cache admission and eviction, optimizing performance under strict memory constraints. Experiments on a text-to-video generation workload comprising 10,000 task chain instances demonstrate that PACE achieves a 61.2% cache hit rate, reducing end-to-end latency by 59.2% over no-caching and by 19.3% compared with state-of-the-art baselines. Consistent performance gains were observed across different modalities, with hit rates improving by 1.1% for text, 3.5% for images, and 3.2% for video. These results demonstrate PACE’s effectiveness in eliminating cross-modal cache redundancy and enhancing overall service responsiveness.

title: Prototype of Joint CKM and 3D Environment Reconstruction System via UAV RF Measurements.
abstract: With the rapid development of low-altitude economy (LAE) and the wide application of cellular-connected unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), the three-dimensional (3D) radio frequency (RF) measurements have become readily available as a byproduct of communication. Learning from such historical RF measurements naturally forms a 3D channel knowledge map (CKM), which not only enhances communication performance for subsequent UAV flights, but also supports real-time environment awareness, such as 3D environment reconstruction. To validate and advance this concept, this paper introduces our developed cost-effective UAV-based CKM prototype system. By integrating onboard computing units and 5G user equipment (UE) modules on a UAV, the system achieves fully autonomous largescale 3D channel knowledge acquisition, with all data uploaded to the cloud server in real time. Leveraging the generated CKM and aided by prior knowledge of the 2D satellite map and base station (BS) locations, a 3D environmental map is reconstructed. This framework holds strong potential for future applications in 6G networks, smart cities, and LAE management.

title: Joint Latency-Energy Optimization for Multitask Offloading in 6G Collaborative Robotic Networks.
abstract: In sixth-generation (6G) networks, collaborative robotic networks enable connected robotic agents to perform tasks cooperatively, yet efficiently offloading tasks is critical to limit resource consumption in large-scale deployments. Compared to conventional mobile edge computing (MEC) approaches, collaborative robotic networks encounter unique challenges, including the high optimization computational complexity for large-scale robotic deployments and the necessity for coordinated, autonomous task assignment among agents. To address this, we formulate a multi-agent multitask offloading problem that jointly considers task assignment, resource management, offloading decisions, and computation frequency assignment, resulting in an NP-hard, nonconvex mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem. We then decompose the problem into resource allocation and task offloading subproblems, which are tackled through proximal policy optimization (PPO) and minimum-cost strategies respectively within a block coordinate descent (BCD) framework. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method achieves stable convergence, reducing latency by 61.95% and energy consumption by 11.82%, demonstrating strong applicability for large-scale collaborative robotic networks in future 6G scenarios, such as the industrial metaverse, autonomous swarm systems, and intelligent transportation.

title: Generative AI Based Secrecy Throughput Improvement in IRS-NOMA-Aided FANETs.
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is a promising technology, which can significantly improve channel propagation quality. However, the openness of wireless channels exposes information security risks such as malicious eavesdropping, especially in flying ad hoc networks (FANETs). This paper presents a generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) scheme to optimize the secrecy throughput in the non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-aided FANETs, where the IRS is strategically configured to establish supplementary communication links. Specifically, to prevent eavesdroppers from intercepting signals using serial interference cancellation (SIC), the secrecy throughput maximization is formulated under the constraints on IRS phase control, drone beamforming, and mobility. Then, we utilize the deep retrieval-augmented generation (DRAG)-based GenAI to translate complex security scenarios into rigorous Markov decision process (MDP) formulations, thereby achieving domain knowledge enhancement. Further, a mixture-of-experts (MoE)-based dual-agent proximal policy optimization (DA-PPO) algorithm is proposed to jointly optimize IRS phase shift, drone beamforming and trajectory. Especially, MoE facilitates robust policy learning under diverse channels, and the shared critic mechanism is deployed to guide the dual agents, effectively maximizing the benefits of the joint optimization. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MoE-based DA-PPO algorithm achieves at least a 6.2% secrecy throughput improvement over traditional baselines.

title: Minimizing Task Delay for Mobile Edge Generation in D2D Underlaying Cellular Network.
abstract: A mobile edge generation (MEG) framework is proposed for latency-sensitive tasks in social-aware D2D underlaying cellular networks. User devices (UDs) are organized into socially cohesive communities for cooperative generation via cellular and D2D links. A joint seed-and-content-based (JSCB) protocol is proposed to enable adaptive switching UD association between seed acquisition with local generation and direct content sharing, while a spillover mechanism is incorporated to handle overdue transmissions. An average task delay minimization problem is formulated to jointly optimize UD association, transmission mode, D2D pairing, and beamforming. To address the hybrid, temporally coupled problem, a joint matching and proximal policy optimization (JMPPO) algorithm is developed, in which discrete and continuous actions are decoupled through hierarchical deep reinforcement learning and matching. Numerical results demonstrate that JSCB achieves reduced delay via adaptive scheduling, while JMPPO outperforms learning-based and traditional baselines under diverse conditions.

title: 6DMA-aided Multiple Access Point Coordination: Two-timescale Decentralized Beamforming and Antenna Movement Optimization.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate six-dimensional movable antenna (6DMA)-aided multi-access point (AP) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication systems. To address practical implementation constraints and improve scalability, we propose a two-timescale decentralized optimization framework that jointly designs beamforming, antenna position, and array orientation. In the short timescale, each distributed AP designs its receive beamformer locally based on instantaneous channel state information (CSI). In the long timescale, the central processing unit optimizes the antenna positions and array orientations for all APs to maximize the ergodic sum rate of all users. The reconfiguration of antenna positions and array orientations is based on the statistical CSI, rendering the optimization problem interesting but also challenging to solve. To address this problem efficiently, a constrained random successive convex approximation algorithm is developed. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed 6DMA-aided multi-AP system outperforms the conventional fixed-position antenna and other flexible-antenna schemes.

title: Learning-Based Joint Channel Acquisition and Communication Optimization for Movable Antennas.
abstract: This paper presents an end-to-end deep learning framework for movable-antenna (MA)-enabled multiuser communications. Unlike conventional methods that presume perfect channel state information (CSI), our design explicitly addresses practical CSI acquisition via tailored pilot signals and quantized feedback, while jointly optimizing channel estimation, MA placement, and precoding. An end-to-end framework with a corresponding training paradigm is designed to integrate these key phases of MA systems. The proposed pipeline learns transmission strategies directly from imperfect channel data, overcoming the mismatch of separately performing channel estimation and MAs’ position optimization. Simulation results show consistent gains in achievable sum rate over traditional benchmarks, particularly under limited feedback. Notably, the proposed method obtains performance comparable to widely used gradient-based schemes, yet requires substantially lower feedback overhead. These results underscore the effectiveness and adaptability of learning-based MA system design for future wireless networks.

title: Constructing Knowledge Map for MIMO-OFDM Clustered Channel Estimation.
abstract: Channel knowledge map (CKM) exploits environment information to assist channel estimation during communication. For clustered channels, which represent a typical type of wireless propagation environment, there has been no research devoted to designing an appropriate CKM to enhance their estimation. To exploit environment information for clustered channel, improve channel estimation accuracy and reduce pilot overhead, we propose ClusterCKM, a CKM providing the range of clustered multipath parameters for any pair of transmitter-receiver links in the region of interest. Firstly, we construct ClusterCKM through estimating the spatial range of scatterer clusters from historical channel information. From these spatial range of scatterer clusters, ClusterCKM infers the range of multipath parameters for the target link. Furthermore, a ClusterCKM-based channel estimation algorithm is developed to utilize the parameter range provided by ClusterCKM. Simulation results show that, more accurate channel estimation can be achieved and pilot overhead can also be reduced by ClusterCKM and the ClusterCKM-based estimation algorithm.

title: Predictive Beamforming in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks: A Cross-Attention Approach.
abstract: Accurate beam prediction is essential for maintaining reliable links and high spectral efficiency in dynamic low-altitude wireless networks. However, existing approaches often fail to capture the deep correlations across heterogeneous sensing modalities, limiting their adaptability in complex three-dimensional environments. To overcome these challenges, we propose a multi-modal predictive beamforming method based on a cross-attention fusion mechanism that jointly leverages visual and structured sensor data. The proposed model utilizes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to learn multi-scale spatial feature hierarchies from visual images and a Transformer encoder to capture cross-dimensional dependencies within sensor data. Then, a cross-attention fusion module is introduced to integrate complementary information between the two modalities, generating a unified and discriminative representation for accurate beam prediction. Through experimental evaluations conducted on a real-world dataset, our method reaches 79.7% Top-1 accuracy and 99.3% Top-3 accuracy, surpassing the 3D ResNet-Transformer baseline by 4.4%-23.2% across Top-1 to Top-5 metrics. These results verify that multi-modal cross-attention fusion is effective for intelligent beam selection in dynamic low-altitude wireless networks.

title: Covariance-Based Signal Processing Approach for Over-the-Air Diagnosis of Intelligent Reflecting Surface.
abstract: Due to circuit failures, there may exist defective elements on an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS), which cannot adaptively adjust their reflecting coefficients as desired. In this paper, we will develop a novel over-the-air diagnosis method that can find all the defective elements via processing the signals propagated over the transmitter-IRS-receiver path, instead of via taking away the IRS for circuit check. Specifically, under our proposed signal processing scheme, the receiver can first mitigate the effect of signals reflected by the defective IRS elements in its received signals. Then, the IRS diagnosis problem reduces to detecting which IRS elements are contributing to the above effective signals with the desirable phase shifts. Such a problem can be efficiently solved via exploiting the sample covariance matrix of the effective signals. Via numerical results, it is shown that our proposed over-the-air scheme can find all the defective elements with a very high probability.

title: RIS Phase Optimization for Secure Localization Against Passive Eavesdroppers.
abstract: RIS has emerged as a pivotal enabler for high-precision localization in 6G networks, capable of overcoming blockage and extending sensing coverage. However, the open nature of wireless pilot signals exposes user equipment to location privacy risks from passive eavesdroppers. This paper proposes to thwart malicious localization by exploiting the inherent information asymmetry regarding the RIS configuration. We analyze a scenario where a passive eavesdropper, lacking access to the instantaneous RIS phase shifts, operates under a systematic model mismatch. We theoretically establish that the eavesdropper’s position estimation error is fundamentally governed by the divergence between the true received signal manifold and the adversary’s hypothesized model. Guided by this insight, we formulate a secure phase design optimization problem that maximizes the signal mismatch energy subject to a strict localization accuracy constraint for the legitimate user. To tackle the non-convexity arising from unit-modulus constraints and the nonlinear Fisher information metric, we develop a computationally efficient semidefinite relaxation (SDR) algorithm. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively degrades the eavesdropper’s localization accuracy while guaranteeing high-precision positioning for the legitimate user.

title: Hierarchical Multi-Agent DRL-Based Caching and Resource Allocation Optimisation for Green Low-Altitude Networks.
abstract: Unlike traditional edge networks, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted low-altitude networks (LANs) have raised higher requirements for content fetching and caching capabilities under limited network resources. Considering the complex environment of LANs, this work proposes an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted content caching edge intelligent LAN, where each UAV serves as a mobile caching node and offers dynamic fetching services for user devices. We aim to minimise the long-term delay and energy consumption integrated costs by jointly optimising caching strategy, transmit power, communication resource, and UAV deployment. To solve the joint optimisation problem, we propose a multi-agent hierarchical deep reinforcement learning-based caching and resource allocation optimisation algorithm. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm’s convergence and effectiveness outperform the benchmarks based on the proposed LAN.

title: Enabling High Error Tolerance in Satellite Video Transmissions by Generative Semantic Communication.
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite relays will significantly extend the coverage of mobile networks, enabling users in remote areas to transmit data of real-time events. Nevertheless, the limited power of user devices and the long distance to satellites lead to low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), which results in high error rates and frequent retransmissions, severely hindering the transmissions of high-dimensional data such as videos. In this paper, we propose a novel method to achieve high error tolerance in satellite-relay video transmissions using generative semantic communications (GSC). For the transmitter, we design and optimize a semantic encoder integrating a pre-trained video encoder with a low-density parity-check (LDPC) encoder, efficiently achieving generalizability and enabling forward error correction. For the receiver, we fine-tune a generative video model using an efficient in-context adaptation algorithm, enabling it to reconstruct videos from error-corrupted semantic information. Simulation results show that our method achieves 2.5 dB higher video peak SNR than conventional semantic communications at an error rate of 45%, and remains robust when the error rate exceeds 80%.

title: Stimulation Parameters Scoring and Adaptive Decoding for Vagal Gastrointestinal Axis Communication.
abstract: Vagal–gastrointestinal (vagal–GI) axis communication is an in-body bio-communication mechanism based on vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) to modulate gastrointestinal (GI) peristaltic rhythms. However, the relationship between VNS parameters (voltage, frequency, and pulse width) and the regulation of peristaltic rhythms is nonlinear. Without a quantitative framework to analyze these modulatory effects, it is difficult to select the optimal stimulation parameters for different individuals. This paper proposes a stimulation parameters scoring framework (SPSF) based on response signal separability, along with a dynamic threshold decoding scheme (DTDS). The SPSF quantifies GI peristaltic rhythm changes induced by various VNS parameters from a communication engineering viewpoint, enabling the identification of optimal stimulation parameters. The DTDS achieves adaptive decoding by designing dynamic thresholds based on the separability of response signals. Furthermore, in vivo experiments on rabbits demonstrated that high-scoring stimulation parameters generated more stable and easily decodable GI response signals, while even low-scoring parameters achieved satisfactory decoding performance, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed SPSF and DTDS. This research lays a theoretical foundation for adaptive bio-communication across varying individual and physiological contexts, fostering the transition of neuromodulation from empirical approaches to quantitative and systematic research.

title: Joint Trajectory Optimization and Resource Allocation for Multi-UAV-Enabled Integrated Sensing, Communication and Computation Systems.
abstract: Due to the significant advantages of high mobility and low cost, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have emerged as promising aerial platforms that integrate sensing, communication, and computing, achieving more efficient resource utilization in various applications. In this paper, we propose a multi-UAV-enabled integrated sensing, communication, and computing (ISCC) framework, in which multiple UAVs cooperatively perform sensing and communication tasks while leveraging edge computing capabilities. We aim to maximize the sum of the average sensing and communication rates of the UAVs by jointly optimizing sensing and communication task scheduling, power allocation, and trajectory optimization. To solve the non-convex problem, we propose an alternating iterative algorithm based on successive convex approximation (SCA) and relaxation methods to decompose the problem into three sub-problems for efficient iterative solution. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms other fixed and semi-fixed strategies, verifying the effectiveness of the algorithm.

title: Container-Based Emulation of Laser Inter-Satellite Links with Realistic Link Budget and Dynamic Network Modeling.
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) constellations with optical inter-satellite links (OISLs) enable low-latency, high-capacity communication, but their performance is highly sensitive to path loss and pointing errors. This paper presents a high-fidelity OISL emulation framework that integrates link budget modeling with container-based network virtualization and adopts a decentralized architecture to capture the distributed operational characteristics of large-scale LEO constellations. In the proposed framework, each satellite is instantiated as an independent Linux container and interconnected via point-to-point VETH interfaces in a fully decentralized manner. The Traffic Control (TC) tool is employed to emulate dynamic link characteristics, including delay, bandwidth, and packet loss. The core innovation lies in the dynamic generation of link parameters based on a fine-grained link budget model, which comprehensively accounts for transmit power, aperture diameter, data rate, free-space path loss, and a Gaussian beam-based pointing loss model. The pointing loss is derived from a probabilistic model of radial deviation at the transmitter, accurately capturing power attenuation caused by misalignment. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed platform precisely reproduces variations in key physical-layer performance metrics, including carrier-to-noise density ratio (C/N0), energy-per-bit-to-noise density ratio (Eb/N0), bit error rate (BER), and packet loss rate (PLR), as functions of inter-satellite distance, quantitatively revealing the critical impact of pointing errors on link performance. Overall, the proposed framework provides a lightweight, scalable, and high-fidelity decentralized emulation platform for optical inter-satellite link performance evaluation and network protocol validation in large-scale LEO satellite constellations, offering valuable engineering insights for link management and routing decisions in future constellation systems.

title: Big-Data-Driven ISAR RF Digital Twin for UAV Channel Modeling in 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks.
abstract: This paper extends an ISAR based RF digital twin framework by incorporating big data technologies to model unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication channels in sixth generation non terrestrial networks (6G NTNs). High resolution inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) echoes, vehicle trajectories, network telemetry and environmental context are collected via an edge–cloud data pipeline. Lightweight preprocessing at the edge performs motion and Doppler compensation and compresses radar echoes into compact spectral–temporal descriptors, while distributed storage and processing in the cloud facilitate large scale training and real time decision making. A Transformer backbone fuses ISAR features with trajectory and context signals, and a reinforcement learning engine adapts beamforming, power allocation and scheduling. Novel freshness aware state variables ensure the digital twin remains synchronized with rapid UAV attitude changes and blockage conditions, and anomaly detection triggers recalibration when sensor drift is detected. Simulations across urban, suburban and open environments show that the big data enhanced twin achieves lower outage probability, reduced end to end latency and higher throughput than statistical, CNN based or ray tracing baselines, illustrating the value of combining ISAR detail, big data pipelines and edge intelligence in 6G NTN scenarios.

title: Minimum Required Power for Continuous-Aperture Array Based Secure Transmission.
abstract: A continuous-aperture array (CAPA)-based secure transmission framework is proposed, where continuous current distribution, or beamformer, is designed to minimize the required transmission power for achieving a specific target secrecy rate. On this basis, closed-form expressions for the minimum required power (MRP) and the associate optimal current distribution are derived. These results are further compared with conventional maximal ratio transmission (MRT) and zero-forcing (ZF) beamforming schemes to provide deeper insights. The analytical findings are then specialized to the typical array structures, e.g., planar CAPAs and planar spatially discrete arrays (SPDAs), followed by asymptotic analyses under the assumption of an infinitely large aperture. Numerical results demonstrate that: i) the proposed secure continuous beamforming design outperforms MRT and ZF beamforming; ii) CAPAs achieve superior secrecy performance compared to conventional SPDAs.

title: Distributed MoE-based Uplink Detection for Cell-Free Communication Systems.
abstract: Cell-free Massive multiple input and multiple output (MIMO) is recognized as a key technology for beyond-5G networks, where distributed access points (APs) jointly serve user equipments (UEs) to address the inherent inter-cell interference issue inherent in cellular systems. While conventional distributed signal detection methods offer a practical balance between performance and fronthaul load, they are fundamentally limited by linear processing constraints. In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning based uplink detection framework by introducing the distributed mixture of experts detection network (DMoE-DetNet). In this architecture, each AP acts as a local expert employing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for non-linear feature extraction, and transmits the local minimum mean square error (MMSE) detection results and statistical channel information to the central processing unit (CPU). In the CPU, an attention-based encoder module captures complex spatio-temporal dependencies among users for global feature fusion, with a gating network at the central processor dynamically weighting the contributions from different APs. At last, a linear detector outputs the symbol probability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DMoE-DetNet significantly outperforms conventional linear processing based cell-free signal detection methods in terms of symbol error rate, showcasing the potential of artificial intelligence-enabled communication systems.

title: A Joint Target Sensing and Data Detection Scheme for Multistatic ISAC Networks via Broadcast Transmission.
abstract: The integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) technology leverages full-dimensional resources for simultaneous sensing and communication (S&C), serving as a key enabler of beyond-5G networks. However, most existing monostatic ISAC systems employ separate S&C receivers and primarily focus on transmitter design, which limits the potential of joint processing and cooperative gains. In this paper, we propose a joint target-sensing and data-detection (JTD) scheme for multistatic ISAC under broadcast (BC) transmission, employing superposition coding and successive interference cancellation to exploit the mutual benefits of S&C. Locally, each receiver refines channel estimation or target localization by reusing detected data symbols as virtual pilots, while at the network level, receivers further enhance performance by reusing symbols decoded from others via BC transmission. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme significantly enhances JTD performance and outperforms the time-division multiple access protocol.

title: Perceptually Lossless Haptic Codec for Immersive Communication.
abstract: Haptic coding plays a crucial role in immersive communication, enabling real-time, seamless, and high-fidelity haptic feedback transmission to deliver interactive experience. However, current haptic coding methods are still suboptimal, since they mainly emphasize unimodal data fidelity while neglecting perceptual factors across modalities. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a haptic codec that fully accounts for the visuo-haptic perceptual mechanism, where our highlights are characterized by perceptually lossless reconstruction, high compression efficiency, and low encoding–decoding latency. Specifically, we first proposed a frequency-domain perception weighting strategy for the haptic codec based on the visuo-haptic perception mechanism. This strategy is integrated into an encoder-decoder framework designed for immersive communication scenarios, balancing compression efficiency and low latency. Then, experiments on the IEEE P1918.1 dataset demonstrate that our proposed codec outperforms existing methods in terms of perceptual quality, compression efficiency and latency, demonstrating superior performance in real-time tactile interactions.

title: Multi-Base Station Cooperative Sensing for UAV Parameter Estimation in ISAC Systems.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables reliable transmission by sensing targets in scattering environment. However, a single base station (BS) struggles to accurately detect three-dimension (3D) moving targets. Meanwhile, asynchronicity caused by spatially separated transceivers introduces timing offsets (TOs) and carrier frequency offsets (CFOs), which impair the accuracy of sensing parameter. To address this, this paper studies an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) networked ISAC system, where multiple base stations (BSs) cooperatively sense multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) through a joint active and passive sensing framework. The sensing signals received from the BSs are transmitted through a backhaul-limited link to a fusion center (FC) for sensing parameter estimation. In this context, we propose a novel cooperative sensing scheme for UAV parameter estimation based on quantized signals. The joint active and passive sensing problem is formulated as a problem with imperfect parameters (such as TO and CFO). An efficient algorithm is proposed to solve the resulting problem. Simulation results indicate that the proposed cooperative sensing design achieves higher estimation accuracy than other baselines. The results also confirm the performance advantage of multi-BS cooperative sensing over conventional single-BS sensing.

title: A Spatio-Temporal-Frequency Transformer Framework for Near-Field Target Recognition.
abstract: A target recognition framework relying on near-field integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems is proposed. By exploiting the distance-dependent spatial signatures provided by the near-field spherical wavefront, high-accuracy sensing is realized in a bandwidth-efficient manner. A spatio–temporal–frequency (STF) transformer framework is introduced for target recognition using electromagnetic features found in the wireless channel response. In particular, a lightweight spatial encoder is employed to extract features from the antenna array for each frame and subcarrier. These features are then fused by a time-frequency transformer head with positional embeddings to model temporal dynamics and cross-subcarrier correlations. Simulation results demonstrate that strong target recognition performance can be achieved even with limited bandwidth resources.

title: Statistical Delay Analysis for CSMA/CA in Tactile Communication Networks.
abstract: The Tactile Internet enables real-time interaction between users and remote environments. Unlike conventional services, tactile communication is highly sensitive to latency and reliability, typically requiring millisecond-level delay and 99.999% reliability. To meet such demanding quality of service (QoS) requirements, rigorous theoretical analysis is essential. However, statistical delay-QoS analysis remains challenging due to the randomness of wireless channels and the bursty, heavy-tailed nature of tactile traffic. This paper addresses the problem of statistical delay estimation for tactile communication over WiFi. Specifically, the Pareto distribution is utilized to characterize the heavy-tail feature of tactile traffic and the token bucket mechanism is also utilized to shape the traffic. The carrier sense multiple access with collision avoidance (CSMA/CA) in WiFi is modeled as a three-state Markov-modulated Bernoulli process, capturing transmission, backoff, and idle behaviors. This service process is concise and effecient. Based on martingale theory, we derive an upper bound on the delay bound violation probability. Simulation results verify the proposed framework’s accuracy and effectiveness for evaluating tactile traffic delay over WiFi, and further illustrate how key system parameters influence the delay bound violation probability.

title: Phase Error Resilient Practical Channel Estimation by Special Orthogonal Group Equivariant AI/ML.
abstract: Channel estimation (CE) is an essential part at the receiver impacting the performance of the whole network. It also attracts tremendous study on using artificial intelligence / machine learning (AI/ML) to optimize CE. Despite the focus of these studies is on building the ability to handle additive-noise reduction, interpolation, and generalization, one impact from the multiplicative phase noise has been underestimated. For example, there may be linear phase rotation caused by timing offset or common phase rotation caused by frequency offset or phase noise of oscillators. In the conventional CE process, there is often estimation on that rotation and offset in order to (re-) compensate their impacts. However, such compensation involves estimation or/and interpolation error(s) which may propagate and seriously degrade the CE performance of both AI and non-AI methods. Therefore, an upgraded multi-layer perceptron (MLP) model is proposed with the trainable weights and biases in each layer being projected onto certain subspaces, which is special orthogonal group equivariant (SOGe). Such design facilitates the joint handling of phase rotation, additive-noise, and channel interpolation. Carefully designed algorithms for the projector also exploit the sparsity feature thus leading to low computational complexity. The simulation results show that the proposed AI/ML model achieves more than 10dB gain on NMSE over other AI/ML models, with more than 99% reduction on both computational complexity and model parameter numbers. Compared with conventional CE methods, the proposed method has comparable complexity and achieves up to 5dB gain in terms of BLER and 8 times throughput performance.

title: Comparisons on Ξ-, Λ- and V-Type Atomic Receivers in Wireless Communication and Sensing.
abstract: Atomic receiver based on the Electromagnetically Induced Transparency (EIT) demonstrates its potential in high sensitivity, miniaturization and wide frequency range wireless communication and sensing. Existing experiments have confirmed that EIT can be realized in Ladder(Ξ)-, Lambda(Λ)- and Vee(V)-type, each corresponding to distinct atomic excitation pathways. However, existing research on atomic receiver mainly focuses on the Ξ-type, overlooking the other two types. In this paper, we analyze the four-level configuration of Λ- and V-type atomic receivers under signal field for the first time. In particular, by using the rotating-wave transformation, we extend the three-level Hamiltonian to four-level system under the influence of the external signal field, and analyze how this interaction alters the EIT spectrum. Then, based on the master equation, we analyze and compare the performance of three systems for wireless communication and sensing. Under typical settings in currently reported experiments, result shows that Ξ-type system performs better in sensitivity and available frequency, while V-type system performs better in instantaneous bandwidth and Λ-type exhibits an exceptionally stable EIT window in complex electromagnetic environments.

title: UPSCA-SR: Fast Joint Optimal Resource Allocation for Multi-Cell MIMO-OFDM Networks.
abstract: Fast joint optimal resource allocation is essential for maximizing throughput in practical multi-cell MIMO-OFDM networks, which is a challenging large-scale, nonconvex optimization problem. Unfortunately, existing optimization and deep learning methods cannot simultaneously achieve high throughput and short computation time. To address this issue, we propose a novel data- and model-driven method, referred to as UPSCA-SR, to jointly optimize resource allocation to achieve a large weighted sum rate of all users in a multi-cell MIMO-OFDM network with short computation time. Specifically, we adapt PSCA, a parallel iterative algorithm based on parallel successive convex approximation, to obtain the nonconvex joint resource allocation problem’s stationary points. PSCA features parallel closed-form updates, resulting in a short computation time per iteration. Then, inspired by spectral correlation, we propose UPSCA-SR, which combines a PSCA unrolling module for a condensed system and a super-resolution (SR) module. UPSCA unrolls the proposed PSCA for a condensed system with compressed channel state information (CSI) to achieve low-dimensional resource allocation, accelerating PSCA’s convergence by optimally tuning its parameters over data samples and decreasing the number of optimization variables. Subsequently, SR recovers high-dimensional resource allocation for the original system from the obtained low-dimensional resource allocation. UPSCA-SR can achieve a flexible trade-off between the weighted sum rate and the computation time by adjusting the compression ratio and the number of unrolled iterations of PSCA. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed UPSCA-SR offers a superior trade-off compared to state-of-the-art optimization and deep learning methods, emphasizing its practical importance.

title: A Novel Channel Estimation Method for Stem-connected Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface.
abstract: Stem-connected reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) has been recognized as a promising beyond-diagonal RIS (BD-RIS) that achieves the optimal tradeoff between performance and circuit complexity but poses a significant challenge for channel estimation. In this work, we introduce a novel two-stage channel estimation approach that uses on-off switches on the RIS stems to address this issue. In the first stage, with switches off, the stem-connected RIS reduces to a simple diagonal structure with parameters estimated based on parallel factor (PARAFAC) decomposition. In the second stage, with switches on, we efficiently estimate the remaining with parameters based on alternating least square. Simulation results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior channel estimation accuracy with lower computational cost than existing methods. Furthermore, it is applicable to most beyond-diagonal RIS architectures, enabling the first comprehensive comparison of channel estimation performance across single-, fully-, tree-, and stem-connected RIS architectures.

title: EABA: Edge-Assisted Batch Authentication for Vehicular Cooperative Perception.
abstract: Cooperative perception enables connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs) to enhance environmental awareness by sharing sensor data with neighboring vehicles. However, authenticating high-frequency perception messages poses significant challenges due to stringent latency requirements and increasing vehicle density. This paper presents an Edge-Assisted Batch Authentication (EABA) framework that leverages roadside units (RSUs) as trusted edge authenticators to overcome these limitations. The proposed Verifiable Batch Attestation (VBA) mechanism enables RSUs to perform batch verification and generate compact cryptographic proofs that vehicles verify through single-operation validation. The framework incorporates adaptive scheduling to optimize batch processing under varying traffic conditions while maintaining low latency. A comprehensive security analysis demonstrates the scheme’s ability to preserve message authenticity, vehicle privacy, and batch-level verifiability while defending against common vehicular network attacks. Performance evaluation reveals that EABA significantly reduces authentication overhead, achieving the latency and throughput requirements necessary for real-time cooperative perception.

title: Cache Updating and Task Offloading for Optimizing Task Freshness in VEC Systems.
abstract: This paper studies a cache updating and task offloading problem in a cache-enabled vehicular edge computing system, where an edge server provides computing services that rely on cached sensing data to process tasks generated by vehicles in the system. A concept of Age of Correlated Information (AoCI) is introduced to reflect the freshness of a computing service, and the problem is formulated as an optimization problem aiming to minimize a weighted sum of task AoCI cost and sensor energy consumption in the system. The formulated problem is tackled by decomposing it into two subproblems: cache updating and task offloading. For the cache updating subproblem, a D3QN based cache updating algorithm is proposed to find a near-optimal solution and an action embedding method is designed to reduce the action space of the algorithm. For the task offloading subproblem, it is further decomposed into an offloading ratio subproblem and a resource allocation subproblem, and an alternating optimization-based algorithm is proposed to solve the task offloading subproblem. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithms can improve the system performance in terms of computing service AoCI cost and a weighted sum of the total service delays of all tasks generated in the system.

title: Weighted Sum-Rate Maximization for Fully-Connected Pinching Antenna Systems.
abstract: A fully-connected architecture for pinching antenna systems (PASS) is investigated. In contrast to the conventional sub-connected architecture, where each waveguide is fed by a single radio frequency (RF) chain, the proposed fully-connected design distributes the signal from each RF chain to all waveguides. This approach fully use the overall spatial degrees of freedoms and also enables scalability in the number of RF chains. A phase shifter (PS)-based network is utilized to realize the full connection between the RF chains and waveguides, a configuration that also facilitates a tri-hybrid beamforming architecture. To exploit the reconfigurability of the system, a sum-rate-driven optimization algorithm is proposed. To handle the coupling among design variables in the objective and constraints, the algorithm iteratively updates each variable while keeping the others fixed, with tailored update rules ensuring optimality and convergence. Simulation results verify that the proposed design allows flexible trade-offs between performance and hardware complexity, achieving comparable spectral efficiency to sub-connected PASS systems with fewer RF chains.

title: A High-Accuracy DOA Estimation Method in the Presence of Phase Noise for Switched Antenna Array Systems.
abstract: Direction of arrival (DOA) estimation plays a critical role in wireless localization and sensing applications. Recently, switched antenna array (SAA) architectures have been widely adopted in standards such as Bluetooth low energy (BLE) 5.1 due to their low-cost and low-power characteristics. However, SAA-based systems are highly susceptible to phase noise introduced by local oscillator imperfections and switching delays, which severely degrades the performance of subspace-based high-resolution algorithms such as multiple signal classification (MUSIC). To address this issue, a recursive optimization MUSIC (RO-MUSIC) algorithm is proposed in this work, which formulates a dedicated optimization problem tailored to the phase noise model and iteratively solves it in conjunction with angle estimation. Simulation results demonstrate that RO-MUSIC outperforms expectation maximization MUSIC(EM-MUSIC) and traditional MUSIC in robustness and accuracy for phase noise compensation across various conditions.

title: Model-Free Channel Estimation for Massive MIMO: A Channel Charting-Inspired Approach.
abstract: Channel estimation is fundamental to wireless communications, yet it becomes increasingly challenging in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems where base stations employ hundreds of antennas. Traditional least-squares methods require prohibitive pilot overhead that scales with antenna count, while sparse estimation methods depend on precise channel models that may not always be practical. This paper proposes a model-free approach combining deep autoencoders and LSTM networks. The method first learns low-dimensional channel representations preserving temporal correlation through augmenting a channel charting-inspired loss function, then tracks these features to recover full channel information from limited pilots. Simulation results using ray-tracing datasets show that the proposed approach achieves up to 9 dB improvement in normalized mean square error compared to the least-squares methods under ill-conditioned scenarios, while maintaining scalability across MIMO configurations.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization for Channel Capacity Maximization in Fluid-MIMO Systems.
abstract: This paper proposes a quantum-inspired optimization framework to maximize the channel capacity of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) fluid antenna systems through optimal port selection at both transmitter and receiver sides. The port selection problem is a challenging large-scale black-box binary optimization task whose complexity grows exponentially with the number of ports. We first approximate it as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem with one-hot constraints and design a penalty-based reformulation. We then employ the simulated bifurcation (SB) algorithm, a quantum-inspired solver, as an efficient solution sampler to explore the large search space. Numerical simulations show that our method achieves over 99% of the exhaustive search capacity while maintaining scalability, yielding substantial gains compared with fixed MIMO systems and classical relaxation-based schemes.

title: Factor Graph Optimization Based Data Fusion for Accurate 3-D Positioning Using UWB and IMU.
abstract: With advances in ultra-wideband (UWB) chips, multi-antenna anchors have enabled single-anchor localization using hybrid time-of-arrival (ToA) and angle-of-arrival (AoA) measurements. This paper presents a graph optimization-based UWB/inertial measurement unit (IMU) fusion framework for accurate indoor 3-D positioning. An IMU-prioritized fusion strategy is introduced to handle unreliable UWB observations, particularly those caused by multipath, by discarding outlier factors to ensure robustness. By integrating UWB range and angle measurements with IMU orientation through the Leven-berg-Marquardt algorithm, the proposed method achieves errors below 0.02 m in static and 0.2 m in dynamic scenarios using commercial devices. Compared with an extended Kalman filter-based fusion method, the graph optimization approach yields significantly higher positioning accuracy. A demonstration video is available at: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6SGvrb1-5BQ.

title: Reconfigurable Holographic Surface-Aided SWIPT: Holographic Beamforming and Waveform Design.
abstract: Massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) is widely used for high spatial gain and interference mitigation in simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). However, the high hardware cost and power consumption of conventional phased arrays (PAs) employed in massive MIMO hinder their scalable deployment in massive IoT networks. In this paper, we propose a reconfigurable holographic surface (RHS)-assisted SWIPT system. Implemented with low-cost components, RHSs offer a cost-effective alternative to PAs. By dynamically adjusting the amplitude response of serially connected elements under wave excitation, RHSs enable directional beamforming for SWIPT. Due to power coupling in serially connected elements, the amplitude response of the RHS cannot be explicitly characterized, and conventional deterministic beamforming and waveform design are inapplicable; thus, we construct a statistical characterization of the serially-coupled RHS and further propose beamforming and waveform designs for multicarrier signals under an inherent coupling mechanism. Simulations show that, under equal hardware cost, the proposed scheme achieves a larger rate–energy (R–E) region than PA-based systems, high-lighting the potential of RHSs for cost-effective SWIPT.

title: On the AAST Performance of FAS-Aided Secure Short-Packet Communication Systems for Low-Altitude Economy.
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of a fluid antenna system (FAS) with ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) for enhancing physical-layer security (PLS) in low-altitude economy scenarios. A variable block-correlation model (VBCM) is adopted to accurately characterize the spatial correlation among FAS ports. We consider a two-user short-packet communication system comprising an unmanned aerial vehicle receiver (UR) and a UAV eavesdropper (UE). Closed-form expressions for the average achievable secrecy throughput (AAST) are derived, alongside its asymptotic characterization for high signal-to-noise ratio regimes. Simulation results validate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the performance gains achieved by the proposed FAS-aided secure URLLC framework under VBCM.

title: Maximizing Personalized Energy-efficiency for Swarm Learning in 6G Networks.
abstract: The rise of 6G technology is driving the proliferation of intelligent edge applications that demand scalable, energy-efficient, and personalized distributed learning. However, deploying such learning at scale remains challenging due to energy constraints from geographically dispersed edge agents and the risk of local overfitting caused by non-IID data distributions in heterogeneous environments. To address the challenges of scalable and energy-efficient collaboration in heterogeneous multi-agent systems, we first propose a framework named Graph-based Swarm Learning (GraphSL). GraphSL leverages graph structures to model the communication and collaboration patterns among agents through a two-layer topology. Specifically, agents are first grouped geographically to form intra-cluster graphs, which reduce transmission energy by limiting communication to nearby peers. The cluster heads are then connected through an inter-cluster graph to enable cross-cluster knowledge sharing. This design mitigates local overfitting and enhances global model generalization. Building upon this framework, we design a specific algorithm named Personalized Energy-efficiency Maximization GraphSL (PEM-GraphSL). PEM-GraphSL integrates energy-aware and personalization-sensitive training within the GraphSL framework, where a Stackelberg game is employed to jointly optimize personalization and energy efficiency by scheduling intra-cluster collaboration (transmission energy) and local training (training energy). Experiments on complex heterogeneous simulation and real-world datasets demonstrate that PEM-GraphSL improves personalization accuracy by 5–10% over baselines and simplified variants, while reducing training energy consumption by 1.4–60× and transmission energy consumption by 1.6–250×.

title: Buffer-Guided Online Intrusion Detection under Dynamic Wireless Traffic.
abstract: The dynamic nature of wireless networks, driven by device mobility, protocol diversity, and evolving attack strategies, leads to continuous shifts in traffic distributions. Under such non-stationary conditions, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) trained offline to deteriorate quickly, while current online solutions struggle with the trade-off between expensive human annotation and noisy self-training, and are brittle in large-scale wireless deployments. To address this challenge, we propose an online intrusion detection framework, OB-IDS, that leverages buffer-guided adaptation to decide when autonomous updates are reliable and when human supervision is required. OB-IDS integrates three components: (1) a contrastive autoencoder that learns robust and discriminative traffic representations; (2) a drift-awareness module that evaluates how well new samples conform to the learned embedding distribution and buffers high-uncertainty samples; and (3) a buffer-guided two-stage updating mechanism that performs rapid label-free representation adaptation on confident samples and periodic supervised refinement using selectively annotated buffered samples. Experiments on NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15 demonstrate that OB-IDS outperforms state-of-the-art methods in evolving network conditions while requiring significantly fewer manual labels.

title: System Modeling of Microfluidic Molecular Communication: A Markov Approach.
abstract: This paper presents a Markov-based system model for microfluidic molecular communication (MC) channels. By discretizing the advection-diffusion dynamics, the proposed model establishes a physically consistent state-space formulation. The transition matrix explicitly captures diffusion, advective flow, reversible binding, and flow-out effects. The resulting discrete-time formulation enables analytical characterization of both transient and equilibrium responses through a linear system representation. Numerical results verify that the proposed framework accurately reproduces channel behaviors across a wide range of flow conditions, providing a tractable basis for the design and analysis of MC systems in microfluidic environments.

title: Dynamic Cooperative Cell-Free ISAC: A Secure Design.
abstract: This paper focuses on the security issue in the cell-free (CF) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where multiple targets act as potential communication eavesdroppers. Artificial noise (AN) is transmitted to not only jam the confidential information but also sense the targets so as to achieve the dual-functional role. Different from previous security studies that assume fixed AP operation modes, a dynamic cooperative CF (DC-CF) ISAC network is proposed where different APs are dynamically adjusted as ISAC transmitters or sensing receivers according to different channel conditions and system priorities for sensing and communication (S&C). Therefore, an optimization problem is formulated by jointly designing AP operation modes, transmit beamforming, and receive combining to achieve the tradeoff between S&C, where the minimal sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio and minimal secrecy rate are utilized as performance metrics for S&C separately to achieve fairness. The integer variables and their strong coupling are addressed utilizing the penalty-based method, and an alternative optimization-based algorithm is proposed to find a sub-optimal solution. Numerical results validate the superiority of the proposed DC-CF ISAC network in security and sensing performance enhancement over some existing schemes.

title: Cell-free versus Conventional Massive MIMO : An Analysis of Channel Capacity based on Channel Measurement in the FR3 Band.
abstract: Cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) has emerged as a promising technology for next generation wireless systems, combining the benefits of distributed antenna systems (DAS) and traditional MIMO technology. In this work, we present the first extensive channel measurements for CF-mMIMO in the mid-band (FR3, 6-24 GHz), using a virtual widely distributed antenna array comprising 512 elements in the urban Macrocell (UMa) environment. Based on the measurement data, this paper compares the channel capacity of CF-mMIMO and Conventional mMIMO under both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions across a range of signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs). We then analyze how channel capacity varies with Rx positions from the perspectives of the full array and of individual subarrays. Finally, we conclude that the 64-element array configuration yields the greatest advantage in channel capacity for CF-mMIMO in the measurement environment considered, with gains of 14.02\% under LOS and 24.61\% under NLOS conditions. This in-depth analysis of channel capacity in the FR3 band provides critical insights for optimizing CF-mMIMO systems in next generation wireless networks.

title: A Co-Simulation Platform for Mixed Traffic Flow of Vehicular Networks.
abstract: The development of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and autonomous driving technologies are accelerating the transition of vehicular networks toward mixed traffic scenario, where human-driven, assisted-driving, and fully autonomous vehicles coexist. In such scenarios, traffic dynamics significantly influence communication performance, while the safety and efficiency of transportation systems rely on timely and reliable V2X communication. Accurately capturing this bidirectional interaction requires a model capable of jointly modeling traffic and communication domains. To address this issue, we propose a cross-domain co-simulation platform tailored for mixed traffic vehicular networks. The platform integrates SUMO, OMNeT++, and Veins into a unified architecture that tightly couples vehicular mobility with cellular V2X communications. On one hand, the SUMO module enables customized vehicle mobility patterns to simulate realistic driving behaviors, thereby enhancing the accuracy and realism of traffic dynamics. On the other hand, the OMNeT++ module implements a standardized 5G protocol stack along with multiple service models, significantly improving the system’s fidelity, scalability, and adaptability to diverse service requirements. Leveraging this platform, a traffic load prediction model and a resource allocation mechanism are conducted on the simulation platform to support data-driven decision-making. Simulation results demonstrate that our platform accurately reflects performance dynamics across diverse traffic conditions, provides dependable traffic load forecasting, and achieves efficient resource allocation.

title: Near-Field Wideband Channel Estimation for Extremely Large-Scale RIS-Aided Communication Systems.
abstract: This paper studies wideband channel estimation for OFDM systems assisted by extremely large RIS (XL-RIS). Due to the large aperture of XL-RISs, the user equipment may operate in the near-field region, while the base station–XL-RIS link remains in the far field, leading to a cascaded channel with hybrid near-field and far-field characteristics. Moreover, wideband effects further complicate channel estimation in mmWave/THz systems. To address these challenges, we propose a frequency-independent orthogonal dictionary by augmenting the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) matrix with additional parameters, which enables an efficient representation of the wideband cascaded channel using a two-dimensional block-sparse structure. Based on this property, the considered channel estimation problem is effectively solved within a tailored compressed sensing framework. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms conventional polar-domain channel estimation approaches in terms of estimation accuracy.

title: Joint Routing and Heterogeneity Aware Client Sampling for Efficient Transfer Learning in LEO Satellite Network.
abstract: Deploying machine learning (ML) models on highly dynamic low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites requires rapid model retraining to adapt to continuously changing service coverage range. Transfer learning is a promising solution that enables knowledge sharing among satellites to avoid the high cost of training models from scratch. However, achieving efficient transfer learning within the LEO satellite networks faces several challenges from heterogeneous data distributions, dynamically changing topologies, and high communication overhead. To address these challenges, we propose a joint routing and heterogeneity-aware client sampling framework. The framework quantifies inter-satellite distribution differences through a prototype-based similarity metric and jointly considers link-level energy consumption and transmission delay to optimize the sampling strategy. Based on this modeling, the client sampling problem within the LEO satellite networks is formulated as a constrained multi-objective optimization that simultaneously optimizes model transfer performance and communication cost to identify the optimal set of source satellite clients. A genetic algorithm is utilized to solve the problem tailored to the routing and resource constraints of LEO constellations. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed transfer strategy significantly improves model accuracy by 17.72% and convergence speed by 64.29% for newly deployed satellites while reducing redundant transmission, energy consumption, and communication delay for completing transfer learning.

title: Service Traffic Prediction for Mixed Traffic Scenario: Integrating Vehicular Mobility and Service Spatio-Temporal Attributes.
