abstract: The emergence of autonomous driving technology has ushered in an era of mixed traffic, characterized by the coexistence of connected vehicles (CVs), connected automated vehicles (CAVs), and human-driven vehicles (HDVs). Distinct from conventional vehicular networks, these scenarios exhibit fundamentally different driving behaviors and network service demands, thereby leading to the fact that making accurate service traffic prediction at the base station level is more difficult. However, existing research has often overlooked the influence of key factors like vehicle motion and diverse service characteristics, focusing predominantly on modeling the spatio-temporal correlations of service traffic. To address the issue, this study proposes the Dynamic Weighted Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (DWTGCN), which is a novel service traffic prediction model that combines vehicular mobility and the spatio-temporal attributes of service traffic for mixed traffic flow scenarios. Firstly, in order to consider vehicular mobility, the Capsule network and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network are adopted to predict the trajectories of different vehicles. Then, combined with base station coverage, a transfer probability matrix is constructed to represent the handover behavior of vehicles between base stations. Subsequently, the Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) is employed to capture the spatial correlation of service traffic, and the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) is applied to capture the temporal dependency. In the end, a mixed traffic flow scenario simulation platform was constructed using SUMO, Veins, and OMNeT++. Simulation results show that the proposed method exhibits a reduction in error exceeding 15% for all service types over the baseline.

title: IGP-RFC: A Data Fault-Tolerant Storage Method for Unmanned Clusters Based on Reparable Fountain Codes.
abstract: Unmanned cluster systems feature highly dynamic nodes and frequent failures, which often lead to data loss and corruption in distributed storage. We observe that Repairable Fountain Codes (RFCs) possess strong local repairability and desirable properties, making them suitable for secure and efficient data storage in unmanned clusters. However, directly applying existing RFCs and their variants to clustered unmanned systems still faces challenges such as high cross-group repair overhead and low decoding success rates, making it difficult to achieve both fault-tolerant reliability and low repair and decoding costs. To address the dilemma, we propose a novel Repairable Fountain Code with Intra-Group Parity called IGP-RFC. During the encoding and storage process, each cluster in the unmanned system generates intra-group parity symbols and cross-group parity symbols. The intra-group parity symbols enable local fault recovery within groups, effectively reducing cross-group repair overhead, while the cross-group parity symbols maintain data redundancy across the system, thereby reducing the decoding failure rate and decoding cost. Experimental results show that under the same single-node failure probability and average repair cost, the decoding failure probability of IGP-RFC is significantly lower than that of URL-RFC and PD-RFC. When the decoding success rate reaches 99%, the decoding cost of IGP-RFC is only 18% and 15% of that of URL-RFC and PD-RFC, respectively. IGP-RFC provides a feasible and efficient approach for secure and reliable data fault tolerance in unmanned cluster systems.

title: Joint Design of Positioning and Beamforming for Wideband Multi-User Movable Antenna Systems.
abstract: While Movable Antenna (MA) systems have demonstrated significant performance gains in narrowband scenarios, their application in wideband regimes is less developed. Existing wideband MA studies reveal a performance gap compared to narrowband counterparts and lack a unified optimization framework that concurrently delivers high performance, low complexity, and extensibility. This work identifies a critical bottleneck: in wideband Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM), the requirement for all subcarriers to share the same antenna position intrinsically limits the available degrees of freedom. To overcome this, we introduce a joint MA positioning and beamforming optimization method. Our key innovation lies in reformulating the challenging sumrate maximization problem using a sparse optimization framework. This transforms the problem into one of joint position matching and coefficient calculation, enabling all subcarriers to collectively determine the optimal antenna positions within a matching pursuit algorithm, which ensures convergence within few iterations. Simulations confirm the method’s effectiveness, showing substantial improvements over fixed-antenna systems and providing insights into the performance boundaries of wideband MA configurations.

title: Minimum Error Probability NOMA with Practical Modulation and Coding.
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is a promising technique for enhancing spectral efficiency in 6G wireless networks. However, most existing NOMA designs rely on idealized performance metrics, overlooking or offering limited insight into the error performance under practical modulation and coding schemes (MCSs). Thus, this paper focuses on downlink NOMA systems that employ practical MCSs, with the aim of minimizing the decoding error probability (in terms of bit error rate (BER)) via power allocation. We first analyze the BER of the NOMA users by deriving the error correction capability (ECC) of low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes via curve fitting and combining it with quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) constellation analysis. Based on the resulting expressions, we formulate a power allocation problem that minimizes the average BER of the system and propose a minimum error probability NOMA design. Numerical results verify the accuracy of the analysis and demonstrate the performance gains achieved by the proposed NOMA scheme.

title: RateSniffer: A Lightweight and Robust Website Fingerprinting Defense via Rate-Aware Morphing.
abstract: Website Fingerprinting (WF) attacks pose a serious threat to user privacy in anonymity networks, such as Tor, as attackers can infer visited websites by analyzing encrypted traffic patterns. Existing WF defenses suffer from a persistent trade-off between robustness and efficiency. To address this challenge, we propose RateSniffer, a lightweight and robust WF defense that leverages rate-aware adaptive morphing to efficiently obfuscate traffic patterns. RateSniffer comprises two key components: Rate-Aware Feature Region Extraction, which employs Grad-CAM to identify traffic regions most influential to WF classifiers and construct rate-aware templates; and Rate-Aware Adaptive Morphing, which selectively perturbs live Tor traffic by matching short-term sending rates to these templates. Extensive experiments on a real-world Tor dataset against six representative WF attacks and six state-of-the-art defenses show that RateSniffer reduces the accuracies of different WF attacks down to 13.02%-55.73%, with only 47% bandwidth and 11% time overhead. Notably, RateSniffer further decreases attack accuracy by up to 15 percentage points compared to the strongest existing defense, significantly outperforming all prior methods.

title: 3DCKM: A Large-Scale Multiband 3D Channel Knowledge Map Dataset for Low-Altitude Corridors.
abstract: The emergence of Low-Altitude Corridors (LACs) for unmanned aerial vehicle operations introduces unique challenges for wireless communication, where three-dimensional (3D) air–ground links exhibit strong altitude-dependent channel variations. Accurate modeling of these effects requires 3D channel information that captures the spatial relationship between wireless propagation and the environment. Existing channel datasets remain limited to terrestrial scenarios and lack comprehensive 3D spatial and multiband channel information. To bridge this gap, we propose 3DCKM, a large-scale multiband 3D Channel Knowledge Map dataset designed for LACs. 3DCKM provides extensive coverage across multiple frequency bands from sub-6 GHz to millimeter-wave, capturing detailed channel characteristics at varying altitudes to model altitude-dependent propagation effects. 3DCKM dataset integrates spatially aligned environmental data, including building map, terrain features, and material properties, with rich channel knowledge encompassing path loss, propagation delay, angle of arrival/departure (AoA/AoD), zenith angles (ZoA/ZoD), and multipath interactions. By offering large-scale multiband 3D channel knowledge, 3DCKM enables critical applications such as CKM construction, AI-based channel prediction, and LAC network optimization. The dataset is available at https://github.com/zcy2002zcy/3DCKM-datasets.git.

title: Resisting Cumulative Leakage in Multi-Round Private Sum Retrieval.
abstract: This paper addresses the critical challenge of cumulative privacy leakage in multi-round private summation queries, where multiple queries enable adversaries to infer individual sensitive data. We propose a novel scheme that achieves the first practical solution for this challenge, which synergistically integrates Paillier homomorphic encryption with zero-knowledge arguments and offers both zero precision loss and provable security. The core innovation lies in transforming the data leakage detection problem into the problem of detecting the full rank of query matrix rows and combining it with the constraints of Paillier encryption relations and zero-knowledge circuits. Furthermore, we formally define the "multi-query joint leakage resistance" property, ensuring that even after multiple queries, the probability of inferring any specific data value remains negligible. Theoretical analysis confirms security under semi-honest models, while experiments demonstrate practical efficiency with second-level response times for million-scale datasets.

title: Efficient Split Federated Learning for Foundation Model Fine-Tuning in UAV Networks.
abstract: Deploying foundation models (FMs) on edge devices for uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) promises broad "low-altitude economy" applications. Federated fine-tuning exploits distributed data while keeping raw data on devices, but full-parameter tuning overloads UAVs. Split federated learning (SFL) mitigates this by partitioning a model between client and server; yet, per-round delay is dominated by stragglers. PipeSFL further reduces delay via server-side priority scheduling and intra-round asynchrony, but jointly optimizing the split point selection (SPS) and communication resource allocation (CRA) under PipeSFL is non-trivial, especially with mobile clients and time-varying channels. We develop a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework that (i) performs fine-grained per-slot delay analysis to capture client mobility, (ii) jointly optimizes SPS and CRA (bandwidth and server transmit power allocation) under PipeSFL, and (iii) minimizes a weighted sum of per-round training time and worst-case client energy. The base station agent observes previous-round actions, trajectories, and energy usage, and outputs the SPS and CRA for the current round. We also estimate the lag to refine the priority scheduling and extract the UAV trajectory feature based on the attention. With Swin-L and LoRA fine-tuning, our scheme outperforms DRL-optimized SFL baselines and a fixed-CRA variant, and approaches the best fixed split point scheme.

title: CE-CoLSM: Cloud-Edge Large and Small Models Collaborative Framework for Traffic Prediction.
abstract: Network traffic prediction is essential for efficient resource management and proactive optimization in wireless networks. However, it remains highly challenging due to the dynamic, volatile, and often anomalous nature of real-world traffic patterns, which hinder accurate prediction. Although large models have demonstrated remarkable zero-shot generalization capabilities on complex time-series prediction, their substantial computational overhead renders them impractical for deployment at the resource-constrained network edge. Most approaches rely on lightweight, small models at the edge, which struggle to model abnormal traffic data. To address these limitations, we propose CE-CoLSM, a Cloud-Edge Large-and-Small Model Collaboration framework that synergizes the strengths of both models for traffic prediction at the network edge. CE-CoLSM incorporates two key collaboration modules: prediction collaboration and distillation collaboration. The prediction collaboration module enables on-demand cloud large model inference, triggered by a real-time confidence score, to enhance prediction accuracy for abnormal traffic data. The distillation collaboration module enables the edge SM to learn from cloud LM via cross-architecture knowledge distillation, triggered by the accumulation of these abnormal samples. This dual-module collaboration ensures both immediate accuracy under anomalies without catastrophic forgetting, effectively bridging the gap between edge efficiency and cloud intelligence. Extensive experiments on real-world telecommunications datasets demonstrate that the framework enhances prediction performance while significantly reducing cloud-side large model requests by 41.09% and enables new edge-side small models to adapt to abnormal data distribution quickly and effectively.

title: Knowledge-Infused Diffusion Model for Effective Radio Spectrum Map Construction.
abstract: Radio Spectrum Map (RSM) is crucial for enabling generative communications and dynamic spectrum management in 6G. However, existing RSM construction methods face a persistent trade-off: model-driven methods exhibit low computational complexity but may be limited in complex environments. Conversely, data-driven methods suffer from high model complexity, which significantly reduces inference speed. To address these issues, we propose a Knowledge-Infused Diffusion Model (KIDM) for constructing RSM. Specifically, we design a conditional module that integrates inverse distance weighting (IDW) priors via cross-attention mechanisms, guiding the model to capture fine-grained spatial features. Moreover, we employ a lightweight acceleration strategy to optimize the denoising schedule, significantly expediting the reverse generation process. Extensive experiments on two open-source datasets demonstrate that KIDM outperforms the compared baseline methods in average RMSE across different sampling patterns and rates, and achieves a single inference latency of less than 5 ms, meeting the latency requirements of typical real-time 6G applications.

title: ChannelMamba: Time-Varying Channel Prediction with Near-Linear Complexity via State Space Model.
abstract: Channel prediction is vital to mitigate demodulation degradation due to outdated channel state information (CSI) in fast time-varying channels. However, existing predictors suffer from high computational complexity and degraded accuracy when applied to high-dimensional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channels. This paper proposes ChannelMamba, which leverages the selective state space model (SSM) of Mamba to capture spatial-frequency correlations of channels. The selective SSM adeptly distills hidden patterns within historical time series CSI to forecast future CSI while maintaining near-linear complexity. Most conventional predictors forecast future CSI in a sequential manner, which often leads to error accumulation. To overcome this, we tokenize the time stamp of each CSI through a linear layer as parallel input and employ a lightweight temporal encoding layer to forecast multi-step future CSI in parallel. Meanwhile, the bidirectional Mamba block enables ChannelMamba to capture global correlations across high-dimensional CSI, enhancing accuracy under high-mobility scenarios. Simulation results demonstrate that ChannelMamba outperforms transformer-based counterparts by more than 1.2 dB in normalized mean squared error (NMSE) under 28 GHz urban macrocell scenarios ranging from 30 to 70 km/h.

title: Towards Zero-Trust Security in Healthcare: GCN-Driven DDoS Detection in an Edge-Cloud Architecture.
abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) enables continuous patient monitoring but remains highly vulnerable to distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks that can disrupt critical healthcare services. We propose a Zero-Trust framework that embeds anomaly detection directly into the enforcement loop using a semi-supervised Relational Graph Convolutional Network (R-GCN). IoMT traffic is modeled as temporal graphs that integrate network statistics with physiological signals, allowing the R-GCN to generate device-level risk scores for adaptive actions such as quarantine or re-authentication. The framework is implemented on a physical IoMT testbed comprising 25 devices, multiple gateways, and a cloud-hosted Policy Decision Point. Experiments show a True Positive Rate of 0.90 with a False Positive Rate of 0.07, containment of high-intensity DDoS attacks within 22 seconds, and maintenance of over 94% vital-sign delivery. These results demonstrate that graph-based anomaly detection enhances the resilience of IoMT infrastructures when tightly integrated with Zero-Trust principles.

title: Experimental Study of Delay-Jitter Determinism and Robustness in Visible-Laser Links.
abstract: Delay jitter is a fundamental metric of communication link determinism and stability. This work introduces a path-ablation and timestamp-embedding feedback methodology, supported by a purpose-built static visible light communication (VLC) testbed, to systematically evaluate delay jitter. Two transmission paths are compared: a direct physical-layer connection and a protocol stack-based transmission. Real transmission results show that the direct connection constrains end-to-end average jitter tightly within 0.565–0.789 µs, achieving two-to-three orders of magnitude improvement over the stack-based transmission, where jitter ranges from 22.057 to 200.589 µs. Under diverse environmental perturbations and incidence angles, the direct connection jitter remains stable between 0.588–0.663 µs, confirming robustness and angular insensitivity. Furthermore, optical power sweeps at the receiver reveal a usable-power regime, within which valid-packet jitter converges consistently to 0.594–0.611 µs. Collectively, these results establish the deterministic and robust nature of the direct-connection-based visible-light links, providing experimental evidence for their application in high-reliability optical communications.

title: Semantic Communication Performance Optimization with Channel and Content Preference Feedbacks.
abstract: In this paper, a novel channel and content preference feedbacks enabled semantic communication framework that enables a transmitter to use limited channel and content for efficient and accurate image data transmission is developed. In the proposed framework, a base station (BS) divides an image into several sub-images according to the image content and extracts the semantic information from sub-images. Then the BS allocates the semantic information to different sub-channels and transmits them to a user. After receiving the semantic information, the user regenerates the image and selects to transmit a feedback (i.e., channel state information (CSI) feedback or content preference feedback) to the BS. The BS will use this feedback information to optimize sub-channel allocation and feedback selection. Meanwhile, since the number of feedback that the receiver can transmit is limited, the BS must determine when to receive a feedback as well as which type of the feedback should be transmitted according to the dynamic wireless environment. We formulate this problem as an optimization problem whose goal is to minimize the mean square error (MSE) between the original image and the regenerated image via optimizing sub-channel allocation and feedback selection. To address this problem, an actor-critic based reinforcement learning (RL) with dynamic neighborhood construction (AC-DNC) scheme is proposed. Compared to the current RL methods, the proposed method is more effective in finding better actions in huge discrete action spaces since the designed method approximates the discrete neighboring action space using a continuous action and selects an action with the maximum Q value from the neighboring action space. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can improve the performance by up to 27.14% and 26.87% compared to the proposed scheme without CSI and content preference feedback information and the regular Q actor-critic (QAC) method.

title: QoS-Aware Effective Energy Efficiency Power Allocation for Slow FAMA Systems.
abstract: Fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA) is a promising technology for 6G networks, offering spatial diversity and interference management with low hardware cost. This paper investigates effective energy efficiency (EEE) power allocation in slow FAMA (s-FAMA) systems with Quality of Service (QoS) guarantees. A joint optimization problem is formulated for port selection and power allocation. To solve the non-convex fractional program, we proposed an iterative algorithm combining the Dinkelbach method and quadratic transform (QT). Simulation results show significant EEE gains over baseline schemes.

title: Learnable Constellation Mapping and Attention-based Channel Adaptation for Digital Semantic Communication System.
abstract: Aiming at the problems of semantic distortion caused by multipath fading channels and compatibility between digital communication and semantic communication systems, we propose a learnable constellation mapping and attention-based channel adaptation mechanism for digital semantic communication system. By constructing a semantic encoder-modulator, the mapping probability from the source to discrete constellation symbols is learned, and the non-differentiable problem of digital modulation is avoided. Neural networks are designed to combine non-trainable but differentiable multipath channels and orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) to achieve end-to-end cross-layer joint optimization of the system. A dual attention-based channel state information (CSI) feedback mechanism is used to adjust the semantic coding process to ensure dynamic matching between features and subcarriers. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system enhances robustness against channel variations while ensuring compatibility with conventional digital communication systems, consequently improving image transmission quality.

title: Movable XL-array Enabled Mixed Near-field and Far-field Covert Communications.
abstract: In this paper, we propose to deploy a modular-based movable extremely large-scale array (XL-array) at Alice for enhancing covert communication performance. Compared with existing work that mostly considered either far-field or near-field covert communications, we consider in this paper a more general and practical mixed-field scenario, where multiple Bobs are located in either the near-field or far-field of Alice, in the presence of multiple near-field Willies. Specifically, we first formulate an optimization problem to maximize the achievable sum-rate under covertness constraint. To solve this non-convex optimization problem, we first decompose it into two subproblems, corresponding to an inner problem for beamforming optimization given positions of subarrays and an outer problem for subarray movement optimization. Although these two subproblems are still non-convex, we obtain their high-quality solutions by using the successive convex approximation technique and devising a customized differential evolution algorithm, respectively. Last, numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed movable XL-array in balancing sum-rate and covert communication requirements, as compared to various benchmark schemes.

title: Robust Beamforming for Near-Field Physical Layer Security under Location Uncertainty.
abstract: In this paper, we study robust beamforming design for near-field physical-layer-security (PLS) systems, where a base station (BS) equipped with an extremely large-scale array (XL-array) serves near-field legitimate user (Bob) in the presence of near-field eavesdropper (Eve). Unlike existing works mostly assuming perfect channel state information (CSI) or location information of Eve, we consider the scenario where the location of Bob is perfectly known, while only imperfect location information of Eve is available at the BS. Specifically, we formulate a robust optimization problem to maximize the achievable rate of Bob while guaranteeing a worst-case limit on the eavesdropping rate under location uncertainty. To overcome the limitations of conventional methods, we first establish the conditions for which the first-order Taylor approximation of the near-field channel steering vector under location uncertainty is largely accurate. Then, we propose a two-stage robust beamforming method, which first partitions the uncertainty region into multiple sub-regions, followed by the second stage to formulate and solve a refined linear-matrix-inequality (LMI)-based robust beamforming optimization problem. Finally, numerical results validate that the proposed method achieves a superior trade-off between rate performance and secrecy robustness, hence significantly outperforming existing benchmarks under Eve location uncertainty.

title: Location-Agnostic Channel Knowledge Map Construction for Dynamic Scenes.
abstract: To alleviate the pilot and CSI-feedback burden in 6G, channel knowledge map (CKM) has emerged as a promising approach that predicts CSI solely from user locations. Nevertheless, accurate location information is rarely available in current systems. Moreover, the uncertainty inherent to highly dynamic scenes further degrades the performance of existing schemes that typically assume quasi-static scenarios. In this paper, we propose a novel framework named location-agnostic dynamic CKM (LAD-CKM). Specifically, LAD-CKM is constructed through dynamic radio frequency (RF) radiance field rendering, which takes instantaneous uplink CSI and partial downlink CSI as inputs. To enable effective rendering, a dedicated radiator representation network (RARE-Net) is designed to capture the spatial-spectral correlations within the inputs. Furthermore, an adaptive deformation module is devised to deform the uplink CSI-based queries of RARE-Net according to instantaneous channel dynamics, thereby enhancing CSI prediction accuracy under mobility. In addition, a novel synthetic channel dataset is created in outdoor dynamic scenes via ray-tracing. Simulation results demonstrate that LAD-CKM yields significant performance gains compared with existing baselines in terms of effective data rate.

title: Enhancing Physical Layer Security for SIM-aided Cell-free mMIMO Systems.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the physical layer security of cell-free (CF) massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) systems enhanced by stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIM), which offer promising wave-domain beamforming capabilities. We propose a joint optimization framework that simultaneously designs the AP digital precoding and SIM wave-based beamforming to maximize the weighted sum secrecy rate (WSSR). To address the inherent non-convexity caused by the coupling of power and phase design, we decouple the original problem into two sub-problems and solve them using alternating optimization, where AP precoding is optimized via convex reformulation and SIM phase shifts are updated using an efficient ADMM-based algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves a 50% improvement in secrecy performance compared to MMSE baseline methods.

title: A High-Throughput, Cost-Free Covert Communication Scheme Based on the Bitcoin Lightning Network.
abstract: Blockchain offers a promising platform for covert communication because of its decentralized, pseudonymous, and immutable nature. However, existing blockchain-based covert communication schemes typically rely on on-chain transactions as message carriers and therefore suffer from inherent limitations, including high exposure risk, low throughput, and high cost. To address these limitations, we propose a covert communication scheme based on the Bitcoin Lightning Network (LN), in which messages are embedded within off-chain LN payments. We design a payment-failure mechanism that eliminates message transmission costs and a dynamic-tag authentication mechanism that enables receivers to verify the identities of anonymous senders. Furthermore, we propose a blockchain-based bootstrap-ping method that allows participants to securely and covertly exchange the LN information required for covert communication via on-chain transactions. Our security analysis and experimental results demonstrate that, compared with existing schemes, the proposed scheme significantly improves throughput and reduces costs while maintaining a high level of covertness.

title: Spectral and Energy Efficiency Trade-off: A Pinching Antenna Perspective.
abstract: The trade-off between spectral efficiency (SE) and energy efficiency (EE) for pinching antenna systems (PASS) is investigated. First, the optimization problem is formulated to maximize the weighted product of SE and EE by jointly optimizing the transmit and pinching beamforming. Under the maximum ratio transmission (MRT) strategy, the optimization of transmit beamforming reduces to the design of the scalar transmit power. It is then proved that the design of the pinching antenna (PA) placement is independent of the transmit power, but not vice versa. Based on this insight, a two-stage joint optimization framework is developed: 1) In the first stage, a general multi-waveguide PA placement framework is proposed; 2) In the second stage, a closed-form solution for the optimal transmit power is derived with the given optimized PA positions. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of our approach. Code is available at https://github.com/Zihao-Felix-Zhou/SE-EE-Tradeoff-Pinching-Antenna-Systems.

title: Semantic-Driven Continual Learning for Weather-Adaptive Vision-Aided mmWave Beam Selection.
abstract: Vision-aided millimeter-wave (mmWave) beam selection is pivotal for 6G networks but struggles in non-stationary environments where channel distributions shift with dynamic weather. Existing deep learning models suffer from catastrophic forgetting when adapting to such changes, rapidly losing previously acquired alignment capabilities. To address this, we propose a semantic-driven continual learning framework tailored for weather-adaptive beam selection. We introduce the Experience Replay with Synaptic Intelligence (ERSI) algorithm, which leverages asynchronously and sparsely triggered visual semantic cues to detect environmental drifts and trigger adaptive model updates. ERSI synergizes semanticgated experience replay with importance-weighted parameter regularization to consolidate historical channel knowledge while maintaining plasticity for new domains. Extensive evaluations on the multimodal M3SC dataset demonstrate that ERSI effectively mitigates forgetting during sunny-to-rainy/snowy transitions. The method maintains a Top-5 accuracy of over 81% on previous tasks and restricts the forgetting rate to approximately 11%, significantly outperforming conventional baselines and enabling robust lifelong learning in dynamic wireless networks.

title: Collaborative Edge Inference for Large Language Models with Speculative Decoding.
abstract: Existing edge-based large language model (LLM) serving systems primarily rely on autoregressive decoding (AD) to generate inference results, generating only one output token per forward pass. The AD process underutilizes GPUs’ parallel processing capabilities and inherently introduces high serving latency, thereby hindering efficient LLM serving in resource-constrained edge networks. To address this challenge, we propose a speculative decoding (SD)-based LLM serving framework that coordinates small and large models deployed on heterogeneous edge nodes to accelerate output token generation and thus reduce serving latency. To improve resource utilization of edge nodes, we introduce pipeline parallelism that groups multiple inference tasks into batches and processes them in a pipelined manner. Building on this framework, we derive the total serving latency that jointly considers communication and inference latencies. We then formulate a joint task batching and wireless communication resource allocation problem to minimize the total serving latency under computing and communication resource constraints. To solve this problem, we derive closed-form solutions for wireless communication resource allocation, and develop an efficient algorithm to obtain optimal task batching strategies. Simulation results show that the proposed LLM serving framework outperforms benchmarks, achieving up to 23.1% latency reduction.

title: ScreenAnt: Transparent On-Screen Antennas for 6G.
abstract: 6G will require on-device antenna systems to operate at ultra-high frequency bands, achieve robust beamforming on the compact user devices, and be blockage-robust. Conventional edge-mounted antennas on devices have limited apertures, suffer from the 'death grip' caused by user-induced blockage, and have poor scalability at mmWave and sub-THz bands. To address these issues, motivated by the rapid evolution of transparent materials and antennas, we propose ScreenAnt in this work--which integrates a transparent antenna array onto the screens of future mobile devices. Specifically, we propose using a transparent on-screen uniform planar array and develop a framework to model its electromagnetic property, spatial configuration, and blockage robustness under realistic user-induced blockage. We also design a gradient-ascent-based algorithm to efficiently optimize power and phase control of on-screen antennas to maximize ScreenAnt's spectral efficiency. Our thorough simulations show that the proposed ScreenAnt can increase the uplink spectral efficiency by over 50% compared to edge-mounted antennas at 28 GHz, and by more than 150% at 300 GHz. ScreenAnt also demonstrates strong robustness against user-induced blockage, paving the way for practical and high-capacity 6G user device designs.

title: Waveform-domain NOMA: An Enabler for ISAC in Uplink Transmission.
abstract: According to the recent 3GPP decisions on 6G air interface, orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM)-based waveforms are the primary candidates for future integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. In this paper, we consider a monostatic sensing scenario in which OFDM is used for the downlink and its reflected echo signal is used for sensing. OFDM and discrete Fourier transform-spread OFDM (DFT-s-OFDM) are the options for uplink transmission. When OFDM is used in the uplink, the power difference between this signal and the echo signal leads to a power-domain non-orthogonal multiple access (PD-NOMA) scenario. In contrast, adopting DFT-s-OFDM as uplink signal enables a waveform-domain NOMA(WD-NOMA). Affine frequency-division multiplexing (AFDM) and orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) have been proven to be DFT-s-OFDM based waveforms. This work focuses on such a WD-NOMA system, where AFDM or OTFS is used as uplink waveform and OFDM is employed for downlink transmission and sensing. We show that the OFDM signal exhibits additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN)-like behavior in the affine domain, allowing it to be modeled as white noise in uplink symbol detection. To enable accurate data detection performance, an AFDM frame design and a noise power estimation (NPE) method are developed. Furthermore, a two-dimensional orthogonal matching pursuit (2D-OMP) algorithm is applied for sensing by iteratively identifying delay-Doppler components of each target. Simulation results demonstrate that the WD-NOMA ISAC system, employing either AFDM or OTFS, outperforms the PD-NOMA ISAC system that uses only the OFDM waveform in terms of bit error rate (BER) performance. Furthermore, the proposed NPE method yields additional improvements in BER.

title: Reconfigurable Pinching-Antenna Assisted Full-Duplex Wireless-Powered Networks under Self-Interference.
abstract: In this paper, we focus on reconfigurable pinching-antenna (PA) assisted full-duplex (FD) wireless-powered networks under self-interference (SI), where the hybrid access point (HAP) is equipped with two waveguides, each hosting one active PA. The objective of this work is to maximize the sum communication rate of the reconfigurable PA-assisted FD-wireless-powered networks. We construct a unified optimization framework incorporating three core parameters: time allocation for energy harvesting and information transmission, transmit power of the HAP, and activation positions of the two pinching antennas. Due to the strong coupling and non-convexity of the resulting optimization problem, a penalty-based algorithm is developed to obtain an effective solution. The simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme and demonstrate its superior system performance, especially this system achieved a significant performance improvement compared to the HD-WPCN when the self-interference is well suppressed.

title: Constrained Downlink Scheduling for Minimizing Age of Information with Imperfect Feedback.
abstract: This paper considers downlink scheduling under general imperfect feedback and a constrained long-term average transmission rate. We aim to design scheduling algorithms to minimize the age of information (AoI) based on the theory of Lyapunov optimization. We propose a hybrid Lyapunov function that reflects the transmission rate usage quadratically and the AoI evolution linearly, and prove the queue stability to enforce the considered constraint. Built on this function, we develop a drift-plus-penalty (DPP) policy with a simple threshold structure, which uses the estimated age-based weights together with the transmission rate usage to measure the transmission preference. We further provide a closed-form performance guarantee of this policy. Our work can include several previous results as particular cases. Numerical results verify the AoI advantage of the proposed policies over state-of-the-art policies.

title: Estimating Channels for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface in Near-Field High Frequency Systems.
Resilient and Freshness-Aware Scheduling for Industrial Multi-Hop IAB Networks: A Packet Duplication Approach.
abstract: In industrial millimeter-wave (mmWave) multi-hop Integrated Access and Backhaul (IAB) networks, dynamic blockages caused by moving obstacles pose a severe threat to robust and continuous networks. While Packet Duplication (PD) enhances reliability by path diversity, it inevitably doubles the traffic load, leading to severe congestion and degraded Age of Information (AoI). To navigate this reliability-congestion trade-off, we formulated an optimization problem in a multi-hop IAB scenario that minimizes the average AOI while satisfying strict queue stability constraints. We utilize Lyapunov optimization to transform the long-term stochastic optimization problem into tractable deterministic sub-problems. To solve these subproblems efficiently, we propose a Resilient and Freshness-Aware Scheduling (RFAS) algorithm. Simulation results show that in blockage-prone environments, RFAS significantly outperforms baselines by maintaining a Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) above 95%. Crucially, it strictly guarantees queue stability under hard buffer constraints, whereas baselines suffer from buffer overflows. Furthermore, RFAS reduces the network load imbalance by 19% compared to the baseline in high-frequency traffic scenarios. This confirms RFAS as a robust and sustainable solution for real-time industrial control loops.

title: Structure-Aware NL-to-SQL for SFC Provisioning via AST-Masking Empowered Language Models.
abstract: Effective Service Function Chain (SFC) provisioning requires precise orchestration in dynamic and latency-sensitive networks. Reinforcement Learning (RL) improves adaptability but often ignores structured domain knowledge, which limits generalization and interpretability. Large Language Models (LLMs) address this gap by translating natural language (NL) specifications into executable Structured Query Language (SQL) commands for specification-driven SFC management. Conventional fine-tuning, however, can cause syntactic inconsistencies and produce inefficient queries. To overcome this, we introduce Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)-Masking, a structure-aware fine-tuning method that uses SQL ASTs to assign weights to key components and enforce syntax-aware learning without adding inference overhead. Experiments show that AST-Masking significantly improves SQL generation accuracy across multiple language models. FLAN-T5 reaches an Execution Accuracy (EA) of 99.6%, while Gemma achieves the largest absolute gain from 7.5% to 72.0%. These results confirm the effectiveness of structure-aware fine-tuning in ensuring syntactically correct and efficient SQL generation for interpretable SFC orchestration.

title: Towed Movable Antenna Array for Airborne Secure Communications.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel towed movable antenna (ToMA) array architecture to enhance the physical layer security of airborne communication systems. Unlike conventional onboard arrays with fixed-position antennas (FPAs), the ToMA array employs multiple subarrays mounted on flexible cables and towed by distributed drones, enabling agile deployment in three-dimensional (3D) space surrounding the central aircraft. This design significantly enlarges the effective array aperture and allows dynamic geometry reconfiguration, offering superior spatial resolution and beamforming flexibility. We consider a secure transmission scenario where an airborne transmitter communicates with multiple legitimate users in the presence of potential eavesdroppers. Based on the statistical distributions of locations of users and eavesdroppers, the antenna position vector (APV) of the ToMA array is optimized to maximize the users’ ergodic achievable rate. Analytical results for the case of a single user and a single eavesdropper reveal the optimal APV structure that minimizes their channel correlation. For the general multiuser scenario, we develop a low-complexity algorithm by leveraging Riemannian manifold optimization. Simulation results confirm that the proposed ToMA array achieves significant performance gains over conventional onboard FPA arrays.

title: FedSC: Backdoor Defense in Federated Learning via Model Splitting and Benign Consensus Clustering.
abstract: Federated learning (FL), as a privacy-preserving distributed machine learning paradigm, exhibits great potential in fields like the Internet of Things. However, its distributed nature and invisibility of clients’ local training processes make it highly vulnerable to backdoor attacks by malicious clients. Existing defense methods struggle to effectively mitigate the impact of malicious clients and may even impair model performance, especially when confronting complex real-world scenarios such as diverse data distributions and stealthy backdoor attacks. To address these challenges, we propose FedSC, a novel FL backdoor defense framework that can effectively cluster benign client models before federated aggregation. Specifically, FedSC splits a complete model into a feature extractor and a classifier, and only aggregates the benign feature extractors on the server, thereby blocking backdoor propagation at the structural level. Moreover, we design a novel benign consensus clustering method, which leverages consensus scores to proactively identify a high-confidence benign seed to establish a benign cluster and then iteratively expand it, thus effectively isolating malicious models. Experimental and performance analyses demonstrate that, compared with 9 state-of-the-art defense methods, FedSC suppresses the attack success rate below 2.9%, showing superior and robust defense performance. Additionally, FedSC achieves up to a 5.31% improvement in main task accuracy compared to FedAvg without defense.

title: DTO-aBST: Data Transport Optimization with Precise ABE to Accelerate LLM Training.
abstract: The raising of artificial intelligence (AI) has made the efficiency of large language model (LLM) training increasingly important. This work optimizes data transport to mitigate the bandwidth contention caused by communication phases of LLM training. We propose and prototype DTO-aBST, which realizes accurate and timely available bandwidth estimation (ABE) to let LLM training applications plan their data transfers, such that they can quickly occupy available bandwidth without causing congestion. We first perform theoretical analysis to improve the probing procedure of ABE based on binary-search train (BST), increasing the accuracy of ABE and reducing the rounds of probing simultaneously. Then, we design proactive and reactive ABE schemes based on the newly-developed BST to address transient traffic fluctuations, enabling LLM training applications to always use available bandwidth precisely. Extensive experiments with a real-world testbed highlight the efficiency and effectiveness of our proposal over existing benchmarks. Specifically, DTO-aBST can reduce the average communication time per iteration by 33.7% and accelerate the overall training of GPT-2 by 1.17×.

title: Spatiotemporal Trust Evaluation for Collaborator Selection via Customized GNN-Mamba.
abstract: The successful completion of collaborative tasks relies on the effective selection of trustworthy collaborators. To accurately evaluate the trustworthiness of potential collaborators, it is necessary to combine insights from their past collaborations with assessments of their resource capabilities under specific task contexts. However, the coexistence of diverse trust perspectives, along with complex spatiotemporal dependencies among devices, makes accurate trust evaluation particularly challenging. To address these challenges, we propose a customized Graph Neural Network (GNN)-Mamba (GM) model for trust evaluation and collaborator selection. In this model, the GNN model performs spatial trust fusion by leveraging inter-device spatial dependencies extracted from historical collaborations, while the Mamba-based temporal model captures both short-term fluctuations and long-term evolution of device trust. In addition, task-specific resource trust is incorporated to reflect the practical capabilities of devices under varying task conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed GM model outperforms baseline approaches in terms of the accuracy and stability of trust evaluation.

title: A Closed-Loop Hybrid Beamforming Scheme Using Dynamic Arrays for ISAC.
abstract: Hybrid beamforming (HBF) is a crucial technology in wireless communication networks. To enable persistent communication and sensing of users in mobility scenarios, a HBF scheme with dynamic antenna structures is proposed. Specifically, a HBF structure with overlapped subarrays is designed using orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm for the downlink transmission. A sparse array is constructed to receive the echo signals from users, and a single-snapshot angle estimation algorithm to estimate the directions of the users is employed. The estimated directions are utilized for the next downlink transmission to achieve a reliable communication link and a fine tracking of the users. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed HBF scheme is capable of achieving both effective communication and accurate sensing.

title: UAV-Enabled Short-Packet Communication via Fluid Antenna Systems.
abstract: This paper develops a framework for analyzing UAV-enabled short-packet communication, leveraging fluid antenna system (FAS)-assisted relaying networks. Operating in the short-packet regime and focusing on challenging urban environments, we derive novel, closed-form expressions for the block error rate (BLER). This is achieved by modeling the spatially correlated Nakagami-m fading link via a tractable eigenvalue-based approach. A high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) asymptotic analysis is also presented, revealing the system’s fundamental diversity order. Building on this analysis, we formulate a novel energy efficiency (EE) maximization problem that, unlike idealized models, uniquely incorporates the nontrivial time and energy overheads of FAS port selection. An efficient hierarchical algorithm is proposed to jointly optimize key system parameters. Numerical results validate our analysis, demonstrating that while FAS provides substantial power gains, the operational overhead creates a critical trade-off. This trade-off dictates an optimal number of FAS ports and a non-trivial optimal UAV deployment altitude, governed by the balance between blockage and path loss. This work provides key insights for FAS-aided UAV communications.

title: Throughput Maximization for Wireless Powered Communication Networks with Pinching Antennas.
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on a novel wireless-powered communication network (WPCN) architecture that leverages movable pinching antennas (PAs) on transmitting and receiving waveguides. In the harvest-then-transmit protocol, user devices harvest downlink (DL) energy from a hybrid access point (HAP), which they then use for uplink (UL) information transmission via either time-division multiple access (TDMA) or non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). To maximize the sum throughput of all users, we formulate a challenging joint optimization problem that encompasses the time allocation between DL wireless power transfer (WPT) and UL wireless information transmission (WIT), the users’ transmit power control, and the coordinated positioning of multiple PAs along the waveguides. Due to the problem’s complexity, an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is proposed, decoupling the problem into resource allocation and antenna placement sub-problems. A grid-based sequential search method is designed to efficiently optimize PA positions. Simulation results show that the proposed PA-WPCN significantly outperforms conventional static antenna setups under both TDMA and NOMA protocols, offering superior throughput, scalability, and interference management, especially with increasing numbers of antennas and users.

title: Modular Foundation Model Inference at the Edge: Network-Aware Microservice Optimization.
abstract: Foundation models (FMs) unlock unprecedented multimodal and multitask intelligence, yet their cloud-centric deployment precludes real-time responsiveness and compromises user privacy. Meanwhile, monolithic execution at the edge remains infeasible under stringent resource limits and uncertain network dynamics. To bridge this gap, we propose a microservice-based FM inference framework that exploits the intrinsic functional asymmetry between heavyweight core services and agile light services. Our two-tier deployment strategy ensures robust quality of service (QoS) under resource contention. Specifically, core services are placed statically via a long-term network-aware integer program with sparsity constraints to form a fault-tolerant backbone. On the other hand, light services are orchestrated dynamically by a low-complexity online controller that integrates effective capacity theory with Lyapunov optimization, providing probabilistic latency guarantees under realtime workload fluctuations. Simulations demonstrate that our framework achieves over 84% average on-time task completion with moderate deployment costs and maintains strong robustness as the system load scales.

title: Channel-Adaptive Diffusion Shield for Secure Image Semantic Communications.
abstract: In the era of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), ensuring secure and reliable data transmission over harsh wireless channels is critical for resilient industrial networks. While semantic communication offers a spectral-efficient solution for sustainable industrial connectivity, it exposes sensitive operational data to eavesdropping risks. Existing secure semantic schemes often suffer from weak protection against semantic leakage and lack adaptability to dynamic industrial channel conditions. To address these challenges, we propose a Sustainable and Resilient Semantic Diffusion Shield (SuRe-SDS), which innovatively leverages channel noise—conventionally a detriment—as an effective medium for encryption. First, we design a noise-driven transmission encryption scheme that projects data into latent noise space, turning environmental interference into a security asset for low-overhead protection. Second, we introduce an asymmetric semantic diffusion module that fuses modified source semantics with encrypted noise, ensuring the transmitted signals bear no perceptual resemblance to the original privacy-sensitive imagery. Third, to enhance resilience against time-varying industrial channels, we develop a channel-adaptive diffusion step predictor. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SuRe-SDS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of semantic fidelity, robustness against channel impairments, and resistance to eavesdropping.

title: On the Channel Quality of XL-MIMO Systems.
abstract: Low-complexity schemes have been widely applied in massive MIMO systems to alleviate the complexity burden associated with high-dimensional signal processing. However, in XL-MIMO systems, many traditional low-complexity methods become impractical due to the significant degradation of channel conditions caused by near-field effects. In this paper, we propose the diagonal dominance ratio indicator (DDRI) of the Gram matrix to effectively assess the channel quality in XL-MIMO systems. Building upon this metric, conventional low-complexity schemes can be adaptively selected and reliably deployed for efficient implementation. Specifically, we first derive a closed-form expression for this metric under LoS conditions, and extend the analysis to NLoS conditions through the random matrix theory. Then, according to the derived results, we obtain a closed-form approximation of the proposed DDRI that admits ${\mathcal{O}}(1)$ complexity, enabling efficient evaluation of channel quality. Simulation results validate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed metric.

title: SwinCE-DM: A Big Data-Driven Diffusion-Transformer Framework for Robust Channel Estimation in LEO Satellite Communications.
abstract: Accurate channel estimation remains a key challenge for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications, where rapid orbital motion and low SNR environments severely degrade traditional estimators. To address this, we propose SwinCE-DM, a big data–driven framework that tightly couples a hierarchical Swin Transformer encoder with diffusion-based refinement through a task-oriented co-design of the encoder–denoiser interface for LEO time-varying channels. A large-scale big data channel modeling platform, fully compliant with 3GPP TR 38.811, is developed to simulate massive orbital dynamics, multipath fading, and atmospheric effects, generating terabyte-level datasets across SISO and MIMO Ka-band scenarios. Leveraging these data-rich simulations, swinCE-DM learns high-dimensional temporal–spatial correlations via multi-scale windowed attention and iterative noise inversion. SwinCE-DM achieves consistent gains over Transformer- and diffusion-based baselines, e.g., reaching an NMSE of –11.7 dB at 0 dB SNR in MIMO settings. Comprehensive ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of the Swin backbone, diffusion refinement, and big data–enhanced multi-stage training. These results highlight the promise of combining hierarchical vision transformers, generative diffusion models, and big data channel simulations to advance robust and scalable channel estimation for next-generation LEO satellite communications.

title: On the Age of Information in Random Access without Feedback.
abstract: This paper focuses on a random access system without feedback, where devices with Bernoulli traffic transmit their status updates to a common access point over a shared channel. To achieve low average age of information (AoI) without feedback, we propose two easily measured parameters to jointly trace the change in the value of the conditional expected age gain and design a low-complexity parametric policy that allows each device to adjust its transmission probability reasonably. We provide a Markov modeling approach to evaluate the AoI performance under this policy, which enables one to obtain optimal parameters offline. Simulation results verify the accuracy of the modeling and the AoI advantage over the existing feedback-free schemes.

title: A Data-Friendly Deep Learning Architecture for High-Resolution Radio Map Construction.
abstract: High-resolution radio maps provide rich information about the radio landscape that is useful to a myriad of wireless applications. Although deep learning (DL) methods have shown their effectiveness in radio map construction, existing approaches require massive high-resolution radio maps in the dataset, the acquisition of which is labor-intensive and time-consuming in practice. In this paper, our goal is to devise a data-friendly high-resolution radio map estimation solution via training over a hybrid dataset, under which radio maps associated with a small fraction of the environment maps are of high-resolution, while those corresponding to most environment maps are of low-resolution. To exploit this heterogeneous data structure, we propose a novel two-stage DL framework. Specifically, in the first stage, we predict the low-resolution radio map corresponding to any given environment map via a neural network trained on the the abundant low-resolution radio maps in the dataset; while in the second stage, we refine the obtained low-resolution radio map into a high-resolution one via employing an image super-resolution network trained over the limited high-resolution radio maps in the dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework can achieve almost the same performance as the existing DL methods, but with about 80% reduction in the number of high-resolution radio maps in the dataset.

title: Understanding Communication Backends in Cross-Silo Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a practical means for privacy-preserving distributed machine learning. FL’s versatile design makes it suitable for various training settings, from IoT edge devices in cross-device FL to powerful servers in cross-silo FL. A key consequence of this versatility is the high level of diversity found in the networking configuration of FL applications. Coupled with the rising demand for large-scale models such as large language models, well-informed selection and configuration of communication backends become crucial for ensuring optimal performance in FL systems. This work focuses on cross-silo federated learning, presenting in-depth benchmarks of various communication backends, including MPI, gRPC, and PyTorch RPC. In addition, we introduce gRPC+S3, a hybrid backend designed to overcome the limitations of existing approaches, particularly for transmitting large models across geo-distributed deployments, achieving up to 3.8× end-to-end speedup over gRPC. Our benchmarks examine point-to-point and end-to-end performance for a broad range of model sizes running under realistic network conditions. Our findings provide practical insights for selecting and configuring suitable communication backends tailored to the specific federated learning tasks and network configurations.

title: ComplianceGPT: LLM-driven Context-Aware Agent for Automated Medical Data Privacy Compliance.
abstract: As medical communications increasingly dependent on digital platforms, the systems that manage patient data, from electronic health records to internal messaging, have become more complex. This growing complexity increases the risk of data privacy breaches, potentially impacting not only regulatory compliance but also real people’s lives. To address this challenge, we present ComplianceGPT, a Large Language Model (LLM) based context-aware agent for automated medical data privacy compliance. Instead of requiring deep expertise in regulations such as HIPAA, GDPR and HITECH, it allows users to simply provide the medical text they are concerned about, such as clinical notes, patient related emails, or research data. Users can simply click a button to have the system check the text for privacy risks. ComplianceGPT is distinctive because it gives guidance instead of just a pass or fail result, acting like a knowledgeable compliance officer. Using a specialized, context-aware instruction set, the agent learns using few-shot learning technique to differentiate between a doctor’s name in an email signature and a patient’s name in a diagnosis. It can highlight what data constitutes a violation, which specific regulations are breached, and what can be done to de-identify the text. Whether securing a hospital’s internal communications or ensuring the privacy of clinical research notes, this agent adapts seamlessly to diverse user needs. ComplianceGPT integrates the precision of AI with human judgment to enhance the safety of medical data systems. It is designed to analyze information and to empower healthcare professionals to manage sensitive data with greater confidence and assurance.

title: Cooperative Beamforming for Multi-BS ISAC in the Presence of Time and Phase Asynchrony.
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is pivotal for 5G-Advanced. However, existing multi-base station (BS) cooperative frameworks often rely on idealized synchronization and the limited flexibility of non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), rendering them impractical for real-world deployments. Consequently, modeling the impact of imperfect synchronization and exploring more flexible multiple access (MA) strategies, such as rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA), remain critical yet insufficiently investigated challenges. To address this issue, this paper investigates cooperative ISAC under realistic synchronization imperfections by modeling both the initial phase of BS transmit antennas and the time synchronization (TS) errors among BSs. Based on this model, we further derive the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) to establish the fundamental performance limits of sensing. Moreover, we develop a cooperative beamforming strategy that maximizes sensing accuracy while ensuring the required communication rate. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme enhances the cooperative ISAC performance and exhibits robustness to synchronization imperfections.

title: Trade-off-Oriented Waveform Design for RadCom System with Space-Frequency Constraints.
abstract: This paper focuses on developing space-frequency transmit waveforms for dual-function radcom systems that simultaneously support multiuser communications and radar beampattern requirements. The performance metric incorporates two joint resource allocation formulations, the weighted achieved communication capacity for multiple users and the squared error between the designed and desired radar beampatterns under space-frequency and power constraints. To address the resulting nonconvex optimization framework, we introduce an iterative approach using a double minorization-maximization framework integrated with feasible point pursuit design (DMMFPP). Specifically, the proposed method guarantees monotonic improvement in the objective function and convergence to a stationary solution. Numerical simulations confirm the efficacy of the space-frequency waveform design strategy.

title: PIMV-GNN: A Physics-Informed Multi-View Graph Neural Network for Robust Channel Knowledge Map Construction.
abstract: Channel knowledge map (CKM) is a key enabler for environmental awareness in future wireless systems. However, reconstructing high-fidelity CKM from sparse and noisy measurements poses a significant challenge. While Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as a potent tool for this task, existing methods often lack physical consistency and generalization due to reliance on single graph structures and purely data-driven approaches. To tackle this challenge, in this paper, we propose a physics-informed multi-view graph neural network (PIMV-GNN) framework. This framework innovatively integrates two mechanisms within a unified GNN backbone: a multi-view learning (MVL) module that builds a rich spatial representation of the complex environment by fusing two complementary graph structures, namely a "spatial line-of-sight" graph and a "physical proximity" graph; and a physics-informed neural network (PINN) module that enforces physical consistency by imposing constraints derived from the Helmholtz equation in the graph domain. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our proposed PIMV-GNN framework significantly outperforms baseline models under various levels of data sparsity and measurement noise. Furthermore, the results reveal a profound synergistic effect between the MVL and PINN modules, where high-quality multi-view features significantly improve the regularization efficiency of the physics-based constraints.

title: Seeing Radio: From Zero RF Priors to Explainable Modulation Recognition with Vision Language Models.
abstract: Current radio frequency (RF) machine-learning pipelines rely on task-specific deep networks for modulation classification and related tasks, but these models require custom architectures and labeled datasets for each problem, generalize poorly across channel conditions and signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), and offer little interpretability. In contrast, modern multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can integrate heterogeneous visual and textual data and exhibit strong cross-domain generalization and explanation capabilities. Our goal in this work is to explore whether vision–language models (VLMs) can be adapted to directly perceive RF signals and reason about modulation patterns without redesigning their architectures or injecting RF-specific inductive biases. To achieve this, we convert complex IQ streams into time-series, spectrogram, and joint RF visualizations, build a 57-class RF visual question answering benchmark, and show that lightweight parameter-efficient fine-tuning can enhance the accuracy of a general-purpose VLM from around 10% to nearly 90%, with ensuring robustness to noise and out-of-vocabulary modulations and the ability to produce human-readable rationales. The obtained results show that combining RF-to-image conversion with promptable VLMs provides a scalable and practical foundation for RF-aware AI systems in future 6G networks.

title: Hybrid Offline-Online Robust Beamforming for MU-MIMO with Unknown Channel Statistics.
abstract: Robust beamforming design under imperfect channel state information (CSI) is a fundamental challenge in multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems, particularly when the statistics of channel estimation errors are unknown. To address this difficulty, this paper proposes a hybrid offline–online robust beamforming framework that jointly integrates data-driven covariance learning with meta-learning for robust beamforming, thus bypass the need for prior error statistics. In the offline phase, a shared deep neural network (DNN) is proposed to infer the channel error covariance matrix from observed channel samples, and a sparse augmented low-rank (SALR) approximation method is presented to reduce model complexity with minimal performance loss. In the online phase, the model is efficiently fine-tuned with a few gradient steps for rapid adaptation. In particular, a multiple-basis model-agnostic meta-learning (MB-MAML) strategy is proposed to enhance the generalization capability of the proposed framework under non-stationary channel conditions. Simulation results show that the proposed framework achieves superior robustness and sum-rate performance compared to existing methods, while maintaining low online computational complexity.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Constraint-Aware Control Channel Scheduling in AI-Native 6G Networks: A Queue-Aware Approach.
abstract: As mobile networks evolve towards AI-native 6G, intelligent resource management becomes paramount. Control channel scheduling (e.g., PDCCH) is critically constrained by resource contiguity requirements and blind decoding search space limitations. Traditional heuristic algorithms (e.g., First-Fit) suffer from myopic decision-making, leading to severe resource fragmentation—termed the Cascading Blocking Effect. This paper proposes a protocol-agnostic Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework for AI-native MAC scheduling. Our key innovation is a Queue-Aware Contention Heatmap—a state augmentation mechanism that encodes the aggregate search space coverage of pending users into a one-dimensional contention density vector. Combined with a Hybrid Attention-Based Policy Network and strict validity-aware action masking, our PPO-based scheduler learns to effectively manage resource allocation. Simulation results demonstrate that our method achieves a 50.8% blocking reduction at typical operating load compared to the industry-standard Greedy scheduler. Crucially, it closes 57.1% of the optimality gap between heuristic and theoretical optimal baselines, while maintaining sub-millisecond inference latency, paving the way for autonomous 6G Radio Resource Management.

title: Implementation and transition to post-quantum cryptography of the Minimal IKE protocol.
abstract: This paper concerns the Minimal Internet Key Exchange (IKE) protocol, which has received little attention to date, despite its potential to make the best-known IKE protocol sufficiently lightweight to be also applied in contexts where it is currently prohibitive, due to its large footprint. First, we introduce and describe Colibri, an efficient, open-source implementation of the Minimal IKE protocol, which allows us to quantitatively assess its real advantages in terms of lightness. Then we introduce a post-quantum variant of the Minimal IKE protocol, which is essential to make it contemporary, and assess it through Colibri. We demonstrate that the protocol performance remains excellent even in such a more challenging context, making it suitable for deploying pervasive and quantum-resistant virtual private networks.

title: Joint Precoding and Antenna Movement Design for Movable Antenna-Enabled Multi-Satellite Cooperative Communication System.
abstract: Multi-satellite cooperative communication (MSCC) has emerged as a promising approach to enhance coverage and spectral efficiency, yet its achievable performance is often limited by line-of-sight (LoS)-dominant propagation and fixed arrays geometry, especially when only statistical channel state information (CSI) is available. Meanwhile, movable antennas (MAs) introduce spatial degrees of freedom (DoF) by actively reconfiguring the array geometry, thereby enhancing spatial multiplexing capability and improving spectral efficiency. However, integrating MAs into MSCC has remained largely unexplored. Motivated by this, this paper investigates an MA-enabled MSCC system, where multiple satellites equipped with MAs realize coherent joint transmission under statistical CSI. To maximize the sum-rate, we derive a tractable closed-form expression of the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio and further reformulate the resulting non-convex problem into a unified optimization framework. An alternating optimization algorithm is developed to jointly optimize the precoding and MA positions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms benchmark schemes, highlighting the effectiveness of jointly exploiting spatial DoF and multi-satellite cooperation.
